Ujjvala-nilamani is a supplement to Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu, which describes all the rasa, yet the conjugal one only in brief. Ujjvala-nilamani describes the conjugal rasa in great detail, following the general pattern of analyzing vibhavas, anubhavas, vyabhicari-bhavas, sattvika-bhavas and sthayi-bhavas. Parakiya and svakiya forms of love are discussed. Jiva Goswami in his commentary justifies svakiya whereas Visvanatha Cakravarti accepts parakiya as stronger.

The contents includes chapters such : Types of Heros, Assistants of Krsna, Krsna’s Beloveds, Description of Radha, Varieties of Heroines, Varieties of Group Leaders, Varieties of Messengers of The Heroine, The Sakhis of the Heroine, Uddipanas for Ujjvala-Rasa, Anubhavas, Sattvika Bhavas, Vyabhicari Bhavas, Sthayi Bhavas, Types of Srngara-rasa.

# Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-ṭīka \[BS\]

## Chapter 1 - Types of Hero

## Outline

Ālambana

Kṛṣṇa

- Pati (husband)
- Upapati (paramour)
- Dhīrodātta
- Dhīralalita
- Dhīraśānta
- Dhīroddhata
- Anukūla (favorable)
- Dakṣiṇa (compliant)
- Śaṭha (deceitful)
- Dhṛṣta (impudent)
- Perfect (Dvārakā)
- More perfect (Mathurā)
- Most perfect (Vraja)

2 x 4 x 4 x 3 = 96 types of Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

***nāmākṛṣṭa-rasajñaḥ śīlenoddīpayan sadānandam \|***  
***nija-rūpotsava-dāyī sanātanātmā prabhur jayati \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, the eternal soul whose name attracts the greatest devotees, who stimulates love in his father Nanda by his actions, who gives bliss by his beauty, remains ever glorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The goal of Jīva is Śrī Rūpa, whose elder brother is Sanātana, to whom he is equal to Sanātana, and whose younger brother is Vallabha. This is my commentary on the *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,* “The Brilliant Sapphire,” The other meaning of *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* is “The Sapphire of Conjugal Rasa.”1 previously difficult to gaze upon, arising from the sweet ocean of nectar of the Lord’s bhakti .

Rūpa Gosvāmī, author of *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,* previously wrote a little about *ujjvala-rasa*, the most astonishing among all the *rasas.* Thinking he would fulfill his goal, he then produced the work called *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*, manifesting the non-difference between the means of revelation and the object of revelation, in the manner that *Bhagavatam* reveals *rasa* and is *rasa i*tself. In this work he describes the conjugal *rasa* in detail. He first praises and prays for the mercy of his dear object of worship and, by a play on words, he also praises and prays for the mercy of his guru Sanātana Gosvāmī..

The Lords name has attracted many tasters of bhakti for Kṛṣṇa and his expansions. He has stimulated love in his eternal father Nanda by his natural qualities. He gives joy to all people by the beauty of his form. He has an eternal form (sanātanātmā). This means he undergoes birth and other actions simply to make his appearance in this world. He is called *prabhu* because he is always the supreme controller and because he is the object of service. May he remain victorious, since he possesses superior qualities in all ways. The word jayati indicates not only victory but the state of being. The other meaning is as follows..

Astyosti??

May he whose tongue (*rasa-jñaḥ*) is controlled by the name of the Lord, who increases the joy of the devotees (*sat)* by his good qualities, who gives joy to me, Rūpa, his follower, whose form is called Sanātana, who is my master, my object of service, remain eternally with all superior qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

May the Lord who is agitated and conquered by side glance of Rādhā, who is disturbed and controlled by this mass of beauty other than his own, who, constantly thirsty, is made to drink the nectar of her smile, bestow bliss upon us!

May the divine river of Śrī Rūpa’s sweet words, most pure, with the sound of flowing water, having numerous auspicious ornaments oozing from each phrases, which overwhelms the intelligenc, enter my heart and destroy unlimited pain.

I offer repeated respects to the lotus feet of Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, whose ideas are sweet with mercy, and have the depth of a million oceans. One verse in his commentary, destroying a multitude of doubts, is most excellent and is very clear. He has said “I have written according to my will, but some parts are according to the desires of others. Those views which are consistent are my views and the rest is the opinion of others.”

Giving up the path of respecting one’s parents, which is characteristic of *parakīyā-bhāva* and which is the quality of *mahābhāva*, is praised as the highest goal. Delighted by this parakīyā mood, I constantly desire to explain it, from the beginning, to the middle, and to the end, because of its beauty, though it is difficult it understand. I take a particle of dust from his lotus feet. May those feet, which are oceans of mercy, pardon my incoherent explanations.

The author, Rūpa Gosvāmī, the ornament in all the hearts of all sensible people, the king among the assembly of all poets, the jewel in the crown of tasters of *rasa,* under the control of a great joy, constantly increasing by the association of the highest devotees, and thus swathed in the sweet *rasa* of *bhakti*, in order to satisfy his dear friends, the most intimate devotees, pulled from the casket of his heart the most confidential, secret conjugal rasa (*ujjvala-rasa*), similar to a shining sapphire, and revealed it to those devotees.

He begins by invoking auspiciousness, through praising as most excellent his worshipable Lord and, by a play on words, the topmost devotee, his elder brother Sanātana Gosvāmī.

The Lord remains with all excellence (*prabhuḥ jayati*). This indicates that the author attempts to glorify the Lord, even if his reason for writing the work is most rash. (He thus seeks the Lord’s assistance.) This is similar to using *jayati* in sentence like the following *jayati vraja-rāja-nandanena hi cintākalikābhyudeti naḥ*: All glories to the Lord; may the son of Vraja’s king think of us! *Jayati (*literally “he conquers”) indicates that he offers respects to the Lord, since *namaskāra* means a particular favorable action revealing one’s inferiority.

By his name he attracts the *rasikas.* This indicates he attracts the women of Vraja since they are the chief *rasikas* and the most worthy of being satisfied by him. Moreover, without distinction, he is attractred to the *rasikas*. This indicates that Kṛṣṇa is qualified with all excellence since he, among all the *avataras*, is attracted to all types of devotees including the *gopīs* at the top, because of his sweet nature*.* He produces great love in his father Nanda by his auspicious deeds *(śīlena*). The dictionary says *cucau tu carite celam: śila* means pure activity. Though his quality of parental affection (*vātsalya-rasa*) is the main subject, the mention of activities indicates the *uddīpana* part of *ālambana* (in *vibhāva*). He gives joy to all by his beauty *(nija-rūpa).* *Nija-rūpa* can also mean persons with a similar form, the cowherd boys. He gives joy to the cowherd boys (*sakhya-rasa*). He also gives joy those in *dāsya-rasa* (*nija*) by showing his form (*rūpa*). He has a form of eternity, knowledge and bliss (*sanātana ātmā*) for *śānta-rasa*. Thus Kṛṣṇa is most excellent because he is the loving object for *ujjvala, vātsalya, sakhya, dāsya* and *śānta* devotees. Among those devotees the former are superior to the latter in the list. Thus *ujjvala-rasa* is the best, since just by chanting the name of the *viṣaya (*Kṛṣṇa), the *āśrayas* (*gopīs*) become attracted to him. This indicates the *gopīs’* attainment of intense *prema*, which manifests as *madhura-rati* as the *sthāyi-bhāva*, which then manifests as *prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga, anurāga* and *mahābhāva.*  The general word *rasa-jña* is used because *ujjvala-rasa* is secret. It is not clearly indicated by the general word. This confidential nature will be clear in the next verse.

The other meaning is as follows. He whose tongue is controlled by the names of the Lord such as “Kṛṣṇa,” whose tongue feels no endeavor to chant (which indicates the devotees excellence), who stimulates strong bliss in the learned devotees (sat) by his qualities, who gives bliss to the persons like me (Rūpa), whose form is called Sanātana, remains most excellent!

Caitanya Mahāprabhu is also included in the meaning. This should be explained first. *Sanātana ātmā* refers to Caitanya Mahāprabhu who accepted Sanātana as his own body. This usage is found in Caitanya Caritāmṛta also. He has the quality of giving the excellent *(ut*) sacrifice (*sava*) of chanting to those who are included in himself (*nija-rūpa*) such as Advaitācārya and Svarūpa Dāmodara. *Amara-koṣa* says the words meaning sacrifice are *yajṇa, sava, adhvara* and *yāga*. Another meaning of the phrase *nija-rupotsava-dayī*, but unintentional is that Sanātana gives bliss through his devotee called Rūpa (*nija-rūpa*) since Rūpa is non-different from him.

### Text 2

***mukhya-raseṣu purā yaḥ saṁkṣepeṇodito rahasyatvāt \|***  
***pṛthag eva bhakti-rasa-rāṭ sa vistareṇocyate madhuraḥ \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Madhura-rasa*****, the king of all** ***bhakti-rasas,*** **which was described only briefly in** ***Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*** **among the chief** ***rasas*** **because of its confidential nature, is described in detail here, since this work remains confidential with the devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author has explained that the main reason for not describing it in detail is its confidential nature:

*nivṛttānupayogitvād durūhatvād ayaṁ rasaḥ \|*  
*rahasyatvāc ca saṁkṣipya vitatāṇgo vilikhyate \|\|*

**Though this** ***rasa*** **has many components, it will be described in summary because it is difficult to describe, because it is very confidential, and because it is unsuitable for those who do not have the taste for** ***madhura-rasa--*****since it appears similar to the** ***rasa*** **of mundane love. BRS 3.5.2**

But like any secret, it should be revealed to persons who are qualified. That is the meaning of this verse. The chief *rasas—śanta, prīti, preyo vatsala and ujjvala*--were described in the *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* but *ujjvala-rasa* was described only briefly. This rasa called *madhura* or *ujjvala,* the king of *bhakti-rasas*, is described in detail in *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi.* It was previously described briefly because it is very confidential. This rasa is hidden from persons opposed to the Lord, who are without taste, since they equate it with material conjugal *rasa*. Even highly respected persons are not skilful at understanding the meaning of *Bhāgavatam*. This *rasa* is also difficult for them to understand. Therefore it should be hidden from them as well. What then to speak of materialistic people?

The main reason is that the subject is confidential. However, the reason for explaining *madhura-rasa* in this work is that it has confidential circumstances (*rahasyatvāt*). A secret should be attained (*rahasyatvam prāpya*) by consideration of particular time, place, and candidate. An ablative word (*rahasyatvāt*) can stand for a participle (*prāpya).*  Or, another meaning is that by this work the secret of the *rasa* is removed. This is indicated by the word *pṛthak* (different). But then, what is within this work should not be revealed elsewhere.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author explains how this work is different from *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*. Among the chief *rasas* (*śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya* and *madhura*) *madhura-rasa* which was described there briefly is described here in detail. As well it is the chief *rasa*, the king of *rasas,* and therefore should be described elaborately. The main reason for it being secret has been described clearly:

*nivṛttānupayogitvād durūhatvād ayaṁ rasaḥ \|*  
*rahasyatvāc ca saṁkṣipya vitatāṇgo vilikhyate \|\|*

**Though this** ***rasa*** **has many components, it will be described in summary because it is difficult to describe, because it is very confidential, and because it is unsuitable for those who do not have the taste for** ***madhura-rasa--*****since it appears similar to the** ***rasa*** **of mundane love. BRS 3.5.2**

Three reasons are given in the quotation for not describing the *rasa* in detail; it is unsuitable for those without taste (*nivrttānupayogitvāt*), it is difficult to understand *(durūhatvāt*) and it is secret (*rahasyatvāt*). In the present verse, only its secret nature (*rahasyatvāt)* is mentioned, since it includes the other two reasons. This topic is unsuitable even for those who have given up the material path, and who have taste for *śānta, dāsya, sakhya* and *vātsalya rasa,* but who do not have taste for *ujjvala-rasa* (*nivṛtta*)--since they see it as material, seeing it from the point of view of material lust.

### Text 3

***vakṣyamāṇair vibhāvādyaiḥ svādyatāṁ madhurā ratiḥ \|***  
***nītā bhakti-rasaḥ prokto madhurākhyo manīṣibhiḥ \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When** ***madhura-rati*** **becomes tasty with the presence of** ***vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika*** **and** ***sañcāri bhāvas,***  **to be described subsequently, it is called** ***madhura-bhakti-rasa*** **by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author now describes *madhura-rasa,* the king of *rasas,* instructed in the previous work, by repeating some of the descriptions. There, *bhakti-rasa* was described in a general way. The elements including *vibhāva* were mentioned:

*vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca sāttvikair vyabhicāribhiḥ \|*  
*svādyatvaṁ hṛdi bhaktānām ānītā śravaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*eṣā kṛṣṇa-ratiḥ sthāyi-bhāvo bhakti-raso bhavet \|\|*

**This** ***rati*** **for Kṛṣṇa, called the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****, takes on a pleasurable nature in the hearts of the devotees by the** ***vibhāvas*****,** ***anubhāvas, sāttvika-bhāvas*** **and** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas,*** **through activities such as hearing, and then becomes** ***bhakti-rasa*****. BRS 2.1.5**

*tatra jñeyā vibhāvās tu raty-āsvādana-hetavaḥ \|*  
*te dvidhālambanā eke tathaivoddīpanāḥ pare \|\|*

**In** ***rasa,*** **the** ***vibhāvas*** **should be known as the causes of relishing** ***rati.*** **They take the form of support (*****ālambana*****) of two types and stimuli (*****uddīpana*****). BRS 2.1.14**

*kṛṣṇaś ca kṛṣṇa-bhaktāś ca budhair ālambanā matāḥ \|*  
*raty-āder viṣayatvena tathādhāratayāpi ca \|\|*

**The wise consider the** ***ālambanas*** **to be Kṛṣṇa, as the object of love experienced in** ***rati,*** **and His devotees, as the experiencer (subject) of** ***rati*** **(the five major and seven secondary** ***sthāyi-bhāvas*****). BRS 2.1.16**

*tad-bhāva-bhāvita-svāntāḥ kṛṣṇa-bhaktā itīritāḥ \|\|*

**Those whose hearts are full of attraction for Kṛṣṇa are called the devotees of Kṛṣṇa. BRS 2.1.173**

*uddīpanās tu te proktā bhāvam uddīpayanti ye \|*  
*te tu śrī-kṛṣṇa-candrasya guṇāś ceṣṭāḥ prasādhanam \|\|*

**Those things which nourish the** ***bhāva*** **of the practitioner are called** ***uddīpanas*** **or stimuli. BRS 2.1.301**

*kṛṣna-sambandhibhiḥ sākṣāt kiñcid vā vyavadhānataḥ \|*  
*bhāvaiś cittam ihākrāntaṁ sattvam ity ucyate budhaiḥ \|\|*

**On the topic of** ***rasa*****, when the heart becomes overwhelmed by** ***ratis*** **or** ***bhāvas*** **in relation to Kṛṣṇa, either directly or indirectly, the learned call this** ***sattva.***

*sattvād asmāt samutpannā ye ye bhāvās te tu sāttvikāḥ \|*  
*snigdhā digdhās tathā rukṣā ity amī trividhā matāḥ \|\|*

**The transformations which arise solely from this** ***sattva*** **are called** ***sāttvika-bhāvas.*** **There are three types of** ***sāttvi-ka-bhāvas: snigdha*** **(affectionate, arising from genuine** ***rati*****),** ***digdha*** **(tainted, arising from other emotions) and** ***rukṣa*** **(contami-nated, arising in a person without** ***rati*****). BRS 2.3.1-2**

*te stambha-sveda-romāñcāḥ svara-bhedo ’tha vepathuḥ \|*  
*vaivarṇyam aśru pralaya ity aṣṭau sāttvikāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\|*

**The eight** ***sāttvika bhāvas*** **are paralysis, perspiration, hairs standing on end, choking of the voice, trembling, changing color, tears, and fainting. BRS 2.3 16**

*athocyante trayas-triṁśad-bhāvā ye vyabhicāriṇaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣeṇābhimukhyena caranti sthāyinaṁ prati \|\|*

**Hereafter, the thirty-three** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **will be described. They are called** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **since they move (*****caranti*****) against the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****, while assisting it in a distinctive way (*****viśeṣena abhimukhyena*****)**

*vāg-aṅga-sattva-sūcyā jñeyās te vyabhicāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sañcārayanti bhāvasya gatiṁ sañcāriṇo ’pi \|\|*

**The** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **reveal themselves by words, by eye brows and other bodily parts and by external actions (*****anubhāvas*****) which arise from overwhelming emotions (*****sattva*****). The section on** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **explained that** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **arise solely from deep emotions and** ***anubhāvas*** **arise from deep emotions with the addition of intellect as well. In the description of the various** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*****, some of them are described as producing** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **such as tears or hairs standing on end, and some produce** ***anubhāvas*** **such as dancing. That would mean that a** ***vyabhicāri-bhāva*** **produces** ***sattva*** **(deep emotion) which then produces a** ***sāttvika-bhāva.*** **The external symptoms of** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **as sometimes called the** ***anubhāva*** **aspect of the** ***sāttvika-bhāva.*** **2 Since they set in motion (*****sañcārayant*****i) the course of the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****, they are called** ***sañcāri-bhāvas*****. BRS 2.4.1-2**

*unmajjanti nimajjanti sthāyiny amṛta-vāridhau \|*  
*ūrmivad vardhayanty enaṁ yānti tad-rūpatāṁ ca te \|\|*

**All the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas,*** **rising and falling like waves in the sweet ocean of the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****, increase the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*** **and then merge into the** ***sthāyi-bhāva.*** **BRS 2.4.3**

*Madhura-rati* is described:

*mitho harer mṛgākṣyāś ca sambhogasyādi-kāraṇam \|*  
*madhurāpara-paryāyā priyatākhyoditā ratiḥ \|*  
*asyāṁ kaṭākṣa-bhrū-kṣepa-priya-vāṇī-smitādayaḥ \|\|*

**That** ***rati*** **found in the doe-eyed women and which is the root cause of eight types of enjoyment between the women and Kṛṣṇa is called** ***priyatā-rati*****. It is also called** ***madhura-rati*****. In this** ***rati*****, there are side-long glances, moving the eyebrows, and affectionate words and slight smiles etc. BRS 2.5.36**

Thus *madhura-rasa* should be described in this way. The words “This is called *madhura*” refer to the explanations in the *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.* It is not called *śṛṅgāra* in this verse *(*since this has a material connotation)*.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse begins to describe the king of *rasas.* Becoming tasteful by assistance of *vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika* and *sañcāri-bhāvas*, which act as cause and effect, described by the author in his previous work, the *sthāyi-bhāva* called *madhura-rati* becomes *madhura-bhakti-rasa.*

### Text 4

*tatra* ***vibhāveṣv ālambanāḥ—***  
***asminn ālambanāḥ proktāḥ kṛṣṇas tasya ca vallabhāḥ \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Among the** ***vibhāvas, ālambanas*** **are described: The** ***ālambanas*** **are Kṛsṇa and the women dear to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

In *vibhāva* there are two elements *ālambana* and *uddīpana*. First *ālambana* is described. Kṛṣṇa is the *viṣaya* in *ālambana* and his dear women are the *āśraya* in *ālambana.*

### Text 5

*tatra kṛṣṇo, yathā—*  
***pada-dyuti-vinirdhuta-smara-parārdha-rūpoddhatir***  
***dṛg-añcala-kalānaṭīpaṭimabhir mano-mohinī \|***  
***sphuran-nava-ghanākṛtiḥ parama-divya-līlā-nidhiḥ***  
***kriyāt tava jagat-trayī-yuvati-bhāgya-siddhir mudam \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**May Kṛṣna, whose toe luster defeats the pride of beauty of millions of Cupids, who bewilders the mind by the skillful dancers in the form of his glances, whose form is like a trembling rain cloud, who is an ocean of supreme, divine pastimes, who bestows the result of fortune to the young women of the three worlds, give joy to you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa is to be understood as the obejct of the the particular descriptive terms mentioned in this verse, for in him there is the highest state of those items. This is similar to verses like *ayam udayati mudra-bhaijanau padminenam****:*** the sun is the breaker of the locks of the lotuses. This verse is found in *Sat-ukti-karṇāmṛtam* compiled by Śrīdhara dāsa.

*ayam udayati mudrā-bhañjanaḥ padminīnām*  
*udaya-giri-vanālī-bāla-mandāra-puṣpam \|*  
*viraha-vidhura-koka-dvandva-bandhur vibhindan*  
*kupitakapi-kapola-kroḍa-tāmras tamāṁsi \|\|*

**Breaking the seal on the lotuses, the new Mandara flower on Udaya Mountain, the friend of cuckoo pairs distressed by separation, the sun appears, breaking the darkness, red like the hollow cheek of an angry monkey.**

In that verse the sun is mentioned only by the word ayam, but the descriptive phrases make it clear that the sun is meant.

He is the supreme object of poetic descriptions. That is expressed by describing him as the defeater of millions of Cupids who are proud of their beauty. He enchants the world by the skills of dancers who take the form of his glances. He is the final result of good fortune (*bhāgya-siddhiḥ*) for the young woman of the three worlds, who is first because of her great love and her being the chosen object by Kṛṣṇa, what to speak of being the final result of good fortune are all other women of the three worlds, who have similar love. Or he is the final result of good fortune for all women qualified for such love in the three worlds. The word *yuvati* (young woman) implies women endowed with love. Some women manifest their good fortune by touching him, some by seeing him and and some by hearing about him. Śukadeva has said:

*śruta-mātro ’pi yaḥ strīṇāṁ prasahyākarṣate manaḥ*  
*uru-gāyoru-gīto vā paśyantīnāṁ ca kiṁ punaḥ*

**The Lord, whom countless songs glorify in countless ways, forcibly attracts the minds of all women who simply hear about him. What to speak, then, of those women who see him directly? SB 10.90.26**

Though the word *siddhi* can also refer to mystic powers like becoming small, it means “result” in this case. The word *tava* (your) indicates the hearer of the verse (Rādhā). The singular number is used (*tava*) to indicate the rareness of being qualified to hear about Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is blessing given by Paurṇamāsī to Rādhā, filled with long for Kṛṣṇa before ever meeting him directly (*pūrva-rāga*), bowing to Paurṇamāsī with reverence. The beauty of one of his feet destroys the pride of beauty of millions of Cupids. Kṛṣṇa has beautiful limbs (BRS 2.1.23) This will also be described later. In the qualities of the *viṣaya* Kṛṣṇa, the qualities of his limbs are also included. One ray from his foot produces effects impossible for milions of Cupids. Thus he is able to attract the hearts of all young women, including Lakṣmī, by his beauty, which agitates multitudes of chaste women.

*kasyānubhāvo ’sya na deva vidmahe*  
*tavāṅghri-reṇu-sparaśādhikāraḥ*  
*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya has attained this great opportunity of being touched by the dust of your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. SB 10.16.36**

*kṛṣṇaṁ nirīkṣya vanitotsava-rūpa-śīlaṁ*  
*śrutvā ca tat-kvaṇita-veṇu-vivikta-gītam*  
*devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā*  
*bhraśyat-prasūna-kabarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa’s beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of him and hear his resonant flute-song, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their belts loosen. SB10.21.12**

“My chastity has been destroyed.” Paurnamāsī then speaks. “But you should not regret this. All women are affected in this manner, and thus there is no fault in you. Your emotions should not be hidden from me. He bewilders the hearts of his lovers by displaying the skills of dancing suitable for love on the tips of his eyes which are the dancing arena. He bewilders his lovers’ hearts, which should be their supportive friends, after they have tasted his glances.” This indicates his mental qualities such as being artisic, clever, and intelligent. (BRS 2.1.24) Just by the movement at the edge of his eye, he explains everything about *rasa* as his principle means of communcation What need is there of words from his mouth, which will be unimportant? Thus this phrase also indicates his qualities in speaking

His form is like a new rain cloud. This describes his black color, which showers the *mahā-rasa*.This cloud is tinted by flashes of lightning in the form of his lover (golden Rādhā). This description also indicates that he is the personification of *śṛṅgāra rasa,* since *śyama* is the color of *madhura-rasa.*

He is the ocean of excellent pastimes. This indicates Kṛṣna’s four extraordinary qualities in his relationship with ohers. This also indicates that though he indulges in amorous pastimes, he remains faultless and respected by all, since he is beyond matter. He is the fruition of good fortune for the young women situated in upper, middle and lower planets of the universe. Some of them become fortunate by hearing alone. Others become fortunate by seeing and hearing him. Others become fortunate by seeing and embracing him. Though he gives happiness to all beings, particularly he gives happiness to young women. Thus, though he is the *viṣaya* for *śānta* and other *rasas,* he is principally the viṣaya for *madhura-rasa*. Since he is endowed with qualities like being attached to conjugal actions and being skillful at *rāsa-līlā,* no one in *śānta, dāsya, sakhya* or *vātsalya rasas* can make him the *viṣaya* for their own *rasa* when he displays those qualities. Moreover, since without these young women, these qualities could not be produced and these delightful qualities could not manifest, the verse mentions that they alone have good fortune as the result given by him, since those women give the greater bliss to him than all others. Thus the conjugal *rasa* of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa is established as the main element (*aṅgī*) for all *rasas* whether they are situated as main or secondary elements to other *rasas*. In this description, it should be understood that Kṛṣna is the *viṣaya* or object and the descriptive terms modify him to show his extraordinary nature. This is in the manner of verses like *ayam udayati mudra-bhaijanau padminenam* which describe the sun without indicating the subject because it is well understood***.***

“Because this is a description of the hero acting as *viṣaya* for *śṛṅgāra-rasa*, it is necessary to emphasize the qualities of *madhura* rather than luster (manifesting from his feet).” *Kāvya-prakāśa* says *ahladakatvaa madhuryaa caigare druti-karaeam****:*** in *śṛṅgāra-rasa* there is great sweetness that causes bliss and causes the heart to melt. (*Kāvya-prakāśa* 8.3**)**

*murdhni vargan tyagau sparca aoa-varga raeau lagh****u*** *\|*  
*avattir madhya-vattir va madhurye ghaoana mata \|\|*

**The consonants minus the cerebrals,** ***r*** **and** ***ṇ*** **when short, repetition, lack of compounds, compounds of medium length and harmonious expression suggest sweetness.** ***Kāvya-prakāśa 8.9***

It also says *deptyatma-vistater hetur ojo verya-rasa-sthiti***:** luster (*ojas*) is the cause of spreading of brilliance in the body and it sustains *vīrya-rasa.* (*Kāvya-prakāśa* 8.4)

***y****oga adya-taetyabhyam antyayor eea****-****tulyayou \|*  
*oadiu canau vatti-dairghyaa gumpha uddhata ojasi \|\|*

**The combination of the first and third consonant of a group with the consonant following them, any consonant combined with** ***r*****, the combination of similar consonants, cerebral consonants,** ***ś*** **and** ***ṣ,*** **long compounds, and bombastic diction suggest luster or** ***ojas*****.** ***Kāvya-prakāśa*** **8.10**

In this verse Kṛṣṇa is described as conquering millions of Cupids and conquering a host of other heroes including the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, by his qualify of attracting the hearts of all young women including Lakṣmī. This composition is not improper since it produces *śṛṅgāra-rasa*, though it is being revealed by modifying phrases, like great soldiers, which project Kṛṣṇa’s unequalled qualities (portraying *ojas*). Display of power or luster is present, but is used to support the description of Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness. 4

### Text 6

***ayaṁ suramyo madhuraḥ sarva-sal-lakṣaṇānvitaḥ \|***  
***valīyān nava-tāruṇyo vāvadūkaḥ priyaṁ-vadaḥ \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣna has beautiful limbs, is pleasing to behold, possesses all auspicious marks on his body, is of ideal age, is eloquent and speaks in a pleasing manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now the author shows Kṛṣṇa endowed with qualities suitable for *madhura-rasa* among all the qualities mentioned in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.*  Some of the words have similar meaning to words in the previous work and some words are exactly the same. *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* has the following verse.

*ayaṁ netā suramyāṅgaḥ sarva-sal-lakṣaṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*ruciras tejasā yukto balīyān vayasānvitaḥ \|\|23\|\|*

**For instance** ***suramya*** **is the equivalent of** ***suramyāṅga*** **in** ***Bhakti-rasāmṛta sindhu*** ***Madhura*** **in this verse is the equivalent of** ***rucira*** **in the previous work.** ***Nava-tāruṇya*** **is the same as** ***vayasānvita.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

With what qualities is the *viṣaya e*ndowed, as *alambana* of *madhura-rasa*? This is now explained. The first five terms describe qualities of Kṛṣṇa’s body. *Vāvadūkaḥ* (eloquent) and *priyaṁvada* (pleasing speech) are qualities of his speech.

### Text 7

***sudhīḥ sa-pratibho dhīro vidagdhaś caturaḥ sukhī \|***  
***kṛtajño dakṣiṇaḥ prema-vaśyo gambhīrāmbudhiḥ \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is intelligent, quick-witted, learned, artistic, clever, happy, grateful, skilful, controlled by love and inscrutible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sudhī* is the equivalent of *buddhiman* (intelligent). *Sa-pratibha* is the equivalent of *pratibhānvitaḥ* (quick-witted) in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu. Dhīra* is the equivalent of *supaṇḍitya* (learned). *Gambhīratāmbudhi* is the equivalent of *gambhīra* (inscrutable).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Starting with *sudhi* (intelligent) fourteen qualities of the mind are listed (ending with the first line of the next verse).

### Text 8

***varīyān kīrtimān nārī-mohano nitya-nūtanaḥ \|***  
***atulya-keli-saundarya-preṣṭha-vaṁśī-svanāṅkitaḥ \|\|8\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**He is the best of men, praised by all, attractive to young women, ever surprising to the beholder, and has unprecedented pastimes, beauty, devotees and produces sound with his flute.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nārī-mohana* is the equivalent of *nārī-gaṇa-manohārī* (attractive to women). The last line indicates Kṛṣṇa’s four qualities described in BRS 2.1.42.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Varīyān* means he is the chief among all persons*. Kīrtimān* means he is praised by all people. He is attractive to young women (*nārī-mohanaḥ*). He is astonishing at every moment to the beholder (*nitya-nūtanaḥ*). These four qualities describe his relationship with others. The last line describes Kṛṣṇa’s unique qualities in relation to pastimes, beauty, devotees (*gopīs*) and the sound of his flute. These are described as follows:

*līlā-premṇā priyādhikyaṁ mādhuryaṁ veṇu-rūpayoḥ \|*  
*ity asādhāraṇaṁ proktaṁ govindasya catuṣṭayam \|\|*

**His extraordinary qualities are his special pastimes, his devotees endowed with abundant** ***prema*****, the sweetness of his flute and the sweetness of his form. BRS 2.1.43**

### Text 9

*ity ādayo’sya śṛṅgāre guṇāḥ kṛṣṇasya kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*udāhṛtir amīṣāṁ tu pūrvam eva pradarśitā \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Such qualities of Kṛṣṇa are glorified in** ***madhura-rasa*****. Examples of the qualities were given in** ***Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Generally these qualities are illustrated with examples from other *rasas*. But they may be used here as well, by substituting other speakers of the verses. For instance “having auspicious qualities” is described as follows:

*rāgaḥ saptasu hanta ṣaṭsv api śiśor aṅgeṣv alaṁ tuṅgatā*  
*visāras triṣu kharvatā triṣu tathā gambhīratā ca triṣu \|*  
*dairghyaṁ pañcasu kiṁ ca pañcasu sakhe samprekṣyate sūkṣmatā*  
*dvātriṁśad-vara-lakṣaṇaḥ katham asau gopeṣu sambhāvyate \|\|*

**O friend! I see that your child has twenty-three auspicious marks on his body. How is it possible that such a child could be born in a cowherd’s house? Seven places on his body are red. Six limbs are elevated. Three limbs are broad. Three limbs are short. Three limbs are deep. Five limbs are long. Five limbs are fine. BRS 2.1.49**

The qualities described in verse 5 should be included in the list of qualities, but for fear of enlarging the commentary, they have not been explained here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though the examples given for the qualities in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* often relate to other *rasas,* they can be applied to *madhura-rasa* by changing the speaker, object of description, and the situation. (In the above example of possessing auspicious qualities, instead of an elder speaking about baby Kṛṣṇa, a *gopī* can speak the same words about *kaiśora* Kṛṣṇa.)

### Text 10

***pūrvokta-dhīroddāttādi-catur-bhedasya tasya tu \|***  
***patiś copapatiś ceti prabhedāv iha viśrutau \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The four types known as** ***dhīroddātta, dhīralatlita, dhīraśānta*** **and** ***dhīroddata*** **described in** ***Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*****, have two types in** ***rasa: pati*** **and** ***upapati.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *dhīrodātta* and other are described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*.

*gambhīro vinayī kṣantā karuṇaḥ sudṛḍha-vrataḥ \|*  
*akatthano gūḍha-garvo dhīrodāttaḥ su-sattva-bhṛt \|\|*

**The person who is inscrutable, modest, tolerant, merciful, determined in vows, who obscures others’ pride, is not boastful, and is strong, is called** ***dhīrodātta.***  **BRS 2.1.226**

*vidagdho nava-tāruṇyaḥ parihāsa-viśāradaḥ \|*  
*niścinto dhīra-lalitaḥ syāt prāyaḥ preyasī-vaśaḥ \|\|*

**He is called** ***dhīra-lalita*** **who is clever, endowed with fresh youth (end of** ***kaiśora*** **period), skilful at joking and free of worries. He is controlled by His dear devotees. BRS 2.1.230**

*śama-prakṛtikaḥ kleśa-sahanaś ca vivecakaḥ \|*  
*vinayādi-guṇopeto dhīra-śānta udīryate \|\|*

**The learned say that he who is peaceful, tolerates suffering, uses discrimination, and possesses qualities like modesty is called** ***dhīra-śānta*****. BRS 2.1.233**

*mātsaryavān ahaṅkārī māyāvī roṣaṇaś calaḥ \|*  
*vikatthanaś ca vidvadbhir dhīroddhata udāhṛtaḥ \|\|*

**The wise call** ***dhīroddhata*** **(haughty) the person who shows envy, pride, deceit, anger, fickleness, and boastful nature. BRS 2.1.236**

These are of two types: married and unmarried. The married Kṛṣṇa is husband of the women in Dvārakā. The unmarried Kṛṣṇa is lover of the women of Vraja. This will be explained in this work also:

*laghutvam atra yat proktaṁ tat tu prākṛta-nāyake \|*  
*na kṛṣṇe rasa-niryāsa-svādārtham avatārini \|\|*

**The** ***upapati*** **described in disparaging terms is the materialistic lover and does not apply to Kṛṣṇa, who appeared in the world to taste** ***madhura-rasa*** **in this way.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.21**

This is the opinion of ancient sages as well:

*neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā*  
*tad gokulāmbujadṛśāṁ kulam antarena \|*  
*āśāṁsayā rasavidher avatāritānāṁ*  
*kaṁsāriṇā rasikamaṇḍalaśekhareṇa*

**Poets’ objection to married women enjoying with another man as the main rasa applies only to women other than the women of Gokula, whom Kṛṣna, the topmost among tasters, made appear in this world because of a special desire for** ***madhura-rasa*****.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **5.3**

But looking in t he Skanda Purāṇa the following statement is seen:

*vṛndāraṇye viharatā sadā rāsādi-vibhramaiḥ \|*  
*hariṇā vraja-devīnāṁ viraho’sti na karhicit \|\|*

**Actually Kṛṣṇa eternally enjoys the** ***rasa*** **dance and other pastimes with the goddesses of Vraja in Vṛndāvana forest. Kṛṣṇa and the** ***gopīs*** **are never actually separated at any time.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **15.186**

By this statement it is understood that the *gopīs* have a relationship with Kṛṣṇa without beginning, and never with anyone else. Thus having another husband is out of the question for them. In this work it is explained that when he descends for pastimes on earth, he then approaches Rādhā and others as an *upapati.* The *upapati* is dependent on the eternal *pati* form.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What are the different types of male lovers as *ālambana (viṣaya)*? This verse answers. It is said that there are two types of heroes in *rasa (iha)* in relation to Kṛṣṇa in his four forms starting with *dhīrodatta:* the husband (married) and unmarried lover.

### Text 11

*tatra* ***patiḥ—***  
***uktaḥ patiḥ sa kanyāyā yaḥ pāṇigrāhako bhavet \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***pati*** **(husband) is defined: The husband is he who is married to a young girl.**

### Text 12

***yathā—***  
***rukmiṇaṁ yudhi vijitya rukmiṇīṁ***  
***dvārakām upagamayya vikramī \|***  
***utsavocchalita-paura-maṇḍalaḥ***  
***puṇḍarīka-nayanaḥ kare’grahīt \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa after showing his prowess in battle, defeated the son of Bhīṣmakra, Rukmi and took Rukmiṇī to Dvārakā. He then married her. The assembly of citizens becamse filled with bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa is the husband for the women of Dvārakā. This and the next verse are statements uttered by a friend of Subhadrā to Draupadī.

### Text 13

***yathā vā—***  
***kalita-yugala-bhāvaḥ kvāpi vaidarbhya-putryā***  
***makha-bhuvi kṛta-dīkṣo dakṣiṇārthān dadānaḥ \|***  
***viharati harir uccaiḥ satyayā dīyamānaḥ***  
***kvacid alam alasāṅgaḥ puṇyake nāradāya \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**At one place in Dvārakā Kṛṣṇa remains with Rukmiṇī, at another place he accepts initiation at a sacrificial arena, and at another place he gives donations in charity. With languid limbs, he is given by Satyabhāmā to Nārada during the puṇyaka ritual. In this way Kṛṣṇa enjoys in Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Puṇyake* refers to vow described in *Hari-vaṁśa*. The incident in this verse is described in that work. He has tired limbs because of his emotions.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

His acting as husband has been described but not the *madhura-rasa* in that marriage. Therefore this verse is supplied. With *guru, brahmaṇas, mantra*, and *dharma* as the witnesses, he acts completely like a husband for Rukmiṇī and other wives. Satyabhāmā was the most fortunate since he was controlled by her, since she had possessive affection for him*. Puṇyake* refers to a vow described in *Hari-vaṁśa*. Its story is also related there. His tired limbs indicates his mood after enjoying with his wife. He is controlled by her because of her bold request. “You will give me to a *brāhmaṇa.* But now, stay a moment with me and enjoy.”

### Text 14-15

***yathā vā—***  
***katyayani maha-maye mahayoginy adhecvari \|***  
***nanda-gopa-sutaa devi patia me kuru te namau \|\|14\|\|***  
***iti saikalpam acerur ya gokula-kumarikau \|***  
***tasv eva kiyatenaa tu pati-bhavo harav abhut \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Among the young, unmarried** ***gopīs*** **some among them who made the following vow attained the Lord as their husband:**

**O goddess Kātyāyanī, O great potency of the Lord, O possessor of great mystic power and mighty controller of all, please make the son of Nanda Mahārāja my husband. I offer my obeisances unto you. SB 10.22.4**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author shows the mood of the Lord as a husband in the young girls of Vraja when the Lord performed pastimes on earth. Among all those young girls of Gokula who had such emotions (*kiyatīnām*), those who made the vow, and not the others who remained in their houses, developed the mood of having the Lord as their husband. Kṛṣṇa said:

*yātābalā vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyathā kṣapāḥ*  
*yad uddiśya vratam idaṁ cerur āryārcanaṁ satīḥ*

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. After all, this was the purpose of your vow to worship goddess Kātyāyanī, O pure-hearted ones. SB 10.22.27**

By this it is understood that Kṛṣṇa accepted and fulfilled the desire of those who wanted the Lord as their husband. It will also be said later in the text:

*tatra durgā-vrata-parāḥ kanyā dhanyādayo matāḥ \|*  
*hariṇā pūritābhīṣṭās tena tās tasya vallabhāḥ \|\|*

**These young unmarried girls, headed by the** ***gopī*** **Dhanyā, devotedly followed an austere vow to please the goddess. Kṛṣṇa fulfilled their desire and they are thus called his dear women (wives).** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **3.35**

As well it said *gāndharva-rītyā svīkārāt svīyātvam iha vastutaḥ:* it is true that Kṛṣṇa married the *gopis* by the Gāndharva rite. *(Ujjvala-nīlamaṇī* 3.16)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having given openly known examples of Kṛṣṇa as a husband, the author now gives an example of Kṛṣṇa as a husband, which is hidden from the public. Among the unmarried girls some among them (*kiyatīnām*), desired the Lord as their husband. Not all of them desired Kṛṣṇa as an umarried lover (*upapati*). Dhanyā and others are explained later as having desired Kṛṣṇa as upapati. There were two types of young girls and therefore two meanings to the *mantra* they chanted.

O Kātyāyani! Make the son of Nanda my husband. Kātyāyanī may reply “But by ordering me to do this, are you making me completely independent? I will just urge your parents to do this. Rather you should say ‘May I have him as my husband or make the parents agree.’” Fearing such an answer from her, they say “O great yogī!” This means “Union (*yoga*) with him is possible for you to arrange quickly. There is no need of intervention of parents.” This indicates their impatience with the delay. “O controller (*adhīśvari)*!” Nothing is impossible for you! “O Mahāmāyā!” But you should bewilder my parents with *māyā* so that they do not arrange my marriage with some other cowherd. Seeing the restrictions in meeting Kṛṣṇa from husbands, mothers-in-law and sisters-in-law for married gopīs like Rādhā and Candrāvalī, some young girsl thought, “It will then be impossible to experience confidential relationships with Kṛṣṇa.” Therefore they did not desire to marry some other cowherd.. Thus at the time of worshipping Kātyāyani they were determined to marry Kṛṣna alone, having discerned that having him as a husband was the only way they could meet freely with him. Thus they prayed that he be their husband.

For the young girls who did not want Kṛṣṇa as their husbnad there is another meaning of the prayer. Make the son of Nanda my devi-pati. Devī means “He who plays and gives pleasure.” The root *div* transform with the addition of the suffix to become *devī*, just as *graha* becomes *grāhī.* He is the master and enjoyer. Make the son of Nanda my master who enjoys pastimes. In this interpretation *pati* does not mean a husband who acts according to the rules of *dharma.*  They recite this prayer because they cannot tolerate the delay, having great longing for him as upapati feeling the married form unsuitable for them. O mahā-māyā! O mahā-yogini! Even when my parents get me married to some other cowherd in the future, bewilder my husband and others and protect my from being touched by my husband. You should arrange meetings with Kṛṣna for me. My husband will still think he is my husband. Kṛṣṇa alone is my husband. There is no harm in this arrangement. By association with Rādhā and other married *gopīs* they became fixed in their minds to associate with Kṛṣṇa in the same manner. They took Kṛṣna as their unmarried lover (*upapati*). One should understand that this was the Lord’s intention. After they recited the prayer, Kṛṣṇa answered with SB 10.22.27 promising to fulfil their desires. But he did not say “I will become your husband.” He said, “You will enjoy the future nights with me. With this purpose you chaste girls performed worship.”

One should not say the meaning of this verse is “Among the young girls those who performed the vow developed the mood of being Kṛṣṇa’s husband.” That meaning has three faults. The word *kiyātīnām* is out of order, the possessive case of *kiyatīnām* has no meaning and there is no grammtical rule to put it in the locative case.

Some who were absorbed in the mood of Kṛṣṇa as their husband performed the worship of Umā to have the Lord as their husband. This is described in the section concerning *svakīya* in Chapter 3. *tena kiṁ dīvyaty atra na ced umā-vrata-phalaṁ piñcāvataṁsī patiḥ:* what is the use of performing vows to Katyāyanī if the husband with the peacock does not play here? (*Ujjvala-nīlamāṇi*.3.5)

Those who are qualified for *parakīya* relationship are described in the next section (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 3.17). Dhanyā and others becamse absorbed in the worship of Umā for this purpose. Thus some who performed the vows to Kātyāyani wanted Kṛṣṇa as *upapati.* It must be explained that there were two types of young girls performing the vow. If one explains the phrase *durgā-vrata-parāḥ kanyā dhanyādayaḥ* (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 3.35) to mean that Dhanyā and others desired *svakīya* relationship (married to Kṛṣṇa), it would be meaningless to place an illustration of *svakīya* relationship in the section on *parakīya* relationships.

### Text 16

***mula-madhava-mahatmye cruyate tata eva hi \|***  
***rukmiey-udvahatau purvaa tasaa parieayotsavau \|\|16\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said in the** ***Mūla-mādhava-māhātmya*** **that Kṛṣna married the girls of Vraja (without a ceremony) before he married Rukmiṇī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Not only did the young girls regard Kṛṣṇa as their husband, but they married him. That is explained in this verse. This has been understood by hearing (*śrūyate*) through the disciplic succession, not by direct statements. It appears that the work called *Mūla-mādhava-māhātmya* could not be found at that time.5 Their vow to attain Kṛṣna as their husband was actually fulfilled through a Gāndharva wedding which requires mere acceptance (and no ceremony). This is the meaning of the statement in *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 3.15

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This has been heard through oral tradition only. There are no scriptural proofs.

### Text 17

***athopapatiu—***  
***rageeollaighayan dharmaa parakeya-balarthina \|***  
***tadeya-prema-vasatir budhair upapatiu smatau \|\|17\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***upapa*****ti (paramour) is described: The wise define the** ***upapati*** **or paramour as the man who has love for the wife of another person, while transgressing** ***dharma*** **because of attraction for her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The definition of the *upapati* given here is an analogy only, since the descriptions cannot really be applied to Kṛṣṇa. Though he is absorbed in these pastimes when he descends on earth, controlled by the prema of his devotees, the Lord also has eternal pastimes. But his *līlā-śakti*, in order to nourish the special rasa of the devotees by its power, encourages the *parakīya* mood in them and displays Kṛṣṇa as the unmarried lover (*upapati)*. Being absorbed in his pastimes, he is sometimes not aware of the powers of his *līlā-śakti*:

*ity uktvādri-darī-kuñja-gahvareṣv ātma-vatsakān*  
*vicinvan bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ sapāṇi-kavalo yayau*

**“Let me go and search for the calves,” Kṛṣṇa said. “Don’t disturb your enjoyment.” Then, carrying his yogurt and rice in his hand, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, immediately went out to search for the calves of his friends. To please his friends, he began searching in all the mountains, mountain caves, bushes and narrow passages. SB 10.13.14**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The abode (*vasatiḥ*) of love for another’s wife *(tadīya*), with intentional transgression of excellent *dharma* because of passion for the wife of another person (*parakīya abalā*) is called *upapati.* By the two modifing phrases—*tadīya* (the wife of another) and *premnaḥ vasatiḥ* (abode of prema), the *viṣaya* and *āśraya* of *prema* are indicated.

### Text 18

***yatha padyāvalyām (205)---***  
***saṅketa-kṛta-kokilādi-ninadaṁ kaṁsa-dviṣaḥ kurvato***  
***dvāronmocana-lola-śaṅkha-valaya-kvāṇaṁ muhuḥ śṛṇvataḥ***  
***keyaṁ keyam iti pragalbha-jaratī-vākyena dūnātmano***  
***rādhā-prāṅgaṇa-koṇa-koli-viṭapi-kroḍe gatā śarvarī***

**Перевод:**

**From** ***Padyāvalī:*** **When Lord Kṛṣṇa arrived in Rādhā’s courtyard for their rendezvous, his tinkling ornaments sounded like the cooing of cuckoos. He suddenly heard the door open, and he also heard the continual jingling sounds of conch shell bracelets. When he heard the arrogant Jaratī call out, “Who’s there? Who’s there?” he became pained at heart. He spent that entire night hiding in a tree in a corner of the courtyard.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author gives an example of *upapati* by quoting a verse written by some poet from *Padyāvalī.* It is merely an illustration to show the concept of the *upapati,*  for all the people of Vraja are endowed with all wealth:

*tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān*  
*harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramākrīḍam abhūn nṛpa*

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the home of Nanda Mahārāja is eternally the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and his transcendental qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed with the opulence of all wealth. Yet beginning from Lord Kṛṣṇa’s appearance there, it became the place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune. SB 10.5.18**

The depiction of poor household in the verse is unsuitable. In *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* the author has given a verse of Bilvamaṅgala as an illustration of the wealth:

*cintāmaṇiś caraṇa-bhūṣaṇam aṅganānāṁ*  
*śṛṅgāra-puṣpa-taravas taravaḥ surāṇām \|*  
*vṛndāvane vraja-dhanaṁ nanu kāma-dhenu-*  
*vṛndāni ceti sukha-sindhur aho vibhūtiḥ \|\|*

**In Vṛndāvana, the ornaments on the feet of the women are** ***cintāmaṇi.*** **The flower trees for making decorations are desire trees. The desire cows are the wealth of Vraja. This display of wealth is an ocean of happiness. This verse is not found in present editions of** ***Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta*****.6**

Later in the work it will be said:

*tatrāpi sarvathā śreṣṭhe rādhā-candrāvalīty ubhe \|*  
*yūthayos tu yayoḥ santi koṭi-saṅkhyā mṛgīdṛśaḥ \|\|*

**In all respects Rādhā and Candrāvalī are the best of all the** ***gopīs.*** **Each of them has a group of followers numbering millions of doe-eyed** ***gopīs*****. (*****Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **4.1)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse Vṛṇdā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Sleeplessness and hidden desire with great longing of both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are suggested by the tinkling of his ornaments and the sound of the door opening. The sound of the ornaments gives joy to Rādhā. The sound of the door opening gives joy to Kṛṣṇa. Joy disappears and anxiety appears when they hear Jaratī say, “Who is there?” Their meeting has been prevented and their meeting is difficult. This illustrates *bahu vāryate mitho durlabhata* in the next verse. Then their disappointment, longing and impatience increase to the extreme. Even after some moments, the jingling sound, the opening of the door and Jaratī’s words continue to be heard. This is indicated by the word *muhuḥ.* This indicates their increased emotions. In this way the night (*śarvarī*) passed. “They have been quickly brought together by me in the bower, and now in the daytime enjoy pastimes together.” Thus, the supreme excellence of enjoyment in union in *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is established through the nourishment of love in separation at night caused by Jaratī’s urge to prevent illicit affairs of the *upapati.*

### Text 19

***atraiva paramotkarnau caigarasya pratinohitau \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The supreme position of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa*** **is established in** ***upapati*** **or paramour love.**

### Text 20

***tathā ca muniḥ—***  
***bahu varyate khalu yatra pracchanna-kamukatvaa ca \|***  
***ya ca mitho durlabhata sa manmathasya parama ratiu \|\|20\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bharata Muni says: That love which causes great opposition because of being against normal** ***dharma,*** **which necessitates the love being kept secret, and which makes it hard for the lovers to meet is the highest type of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These particular pastimes of the women of Vraja with Kṛṣna (*atra)* establish the highest position for *śṛṅgāra-rasa*. Why is this? The author quotes Bharata Muni. That attraction which causes great obstacles to union, in which there is hidden desire for union, and which is hard to attain for both, is considered the highest attraction related to love. That is the meaning of his statement. The excellence of *rasa* is established by the presence of the factors mentioned such as being prevented (*bahu vāryate*). In his work, he makes this clear with statements such as the following:

*tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ*  
*govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ*

**Their husbands, fathers, brothers and other relatives tried to stop them, but Kṛṣṇa had already stolen their hearts. Enchanted by the sound of His flute, they refused to turn back. SB 10.29.8**

According to Bharata Muni, this situation creates excellence of *rasa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The excellence of love with the *upapati (atra)*, not the married lover, is established, or gains importance (*pratiṣṭhitaḥ*). First the author proves his point by quoting Bharata Muni, the life of all concepts of *rasa,* the founder of *rasa* theory. This *upapati* causes prevention or opposition (*bahu vāryate*). It is forbidden from the point of view of normal *dharma.* In that attraction there is desires hidden from others. It is hard for the lovers to meet. That attraction related to love is the most excellent. Other forms of love are inferior.

### Text 21

***laghutvam atra yat proktaa tat tu prakata-nayake \|***  
***na kanee rasa-niryasa-svadartham avatarini \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The criticism of the material paramour by the author does not apply to Kṛṣṇa, who appeared in this world to taste the thick** ***madhura-rasa*** **as** ***upapati.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse resolves any doubts about the previous statement. This is an explanation of the doubt: that the paramour or *upapati* is disrespectable *(laghutvam*).

*śṛṅgaṁ hi manmathodbhedas tad-āgamana-hetukaḥ \|*  
*uttama-prakṛti-prāyo rasaḥ śṛṅgāra iṣyate \|\|*

***Śṛṅga***  **means manifestation of desire or the cause of its manifestation. Thus, this rasa with highest nature is called** ***śṛṅgāra.***

This ancient definition describes *śṛṅgāra-rasa* as the highest. In the pure or *ujjvala-rasa*, impure paramour love should not be present as its portion. In the *Tri-khaṇḍa-śeṣa,* the paramour is also called a sinful master (*pāpa-pati*). Thus the paramour is condemned. The paramour is also condemned in literature on dramatics and poetics. What has been said is summarized in *Sāhitya-darpaṇa:*

*upanāyaka-saṁsthāyāṁ muni-guru-patnī-gatāyāṁ ca \|*  
*bahu-nāyaka-viṣayāyāṁ ratau tathānubhava-niṣṭhāyām \|\|*  
*pratināyaka-niṣṭhatve tadvad adhama-pātra-tiryag-ādi-gate \|*  
*śṛṅgāre’anucityaṁ raudre gurv-ādi-gata-kope \|\|*

**In** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa,*** **the paramour is improper, since this person as a secondary character addicted to experiencing love affairs with the wife of a sage or guru, opposed vehemently by the hero, ends up in lower species of life since he is the dedicated enemy of the hero, and, endowed with** ***raudra-rasa*****, shows anger to guru and others.**

Wherever the *upapati* is described, he is condemned. According to the proofs of the ancients it is not the main *rasa.* Married love produces the main *rasa.* As a secondary form, it is derided. Even Kṛṣṇa, who supports this aspect, says:

*asvargyam ayaśasyaṁ ca phalgu kṛcchraṁ bhayāvaham*  
*jugupsitaṁ ca sarvatra hy aupapatyaṁ kula-striyaḥ*

**For a woman from a respectable family, petty adulterous affairs are always condemned. They bar her from heaven, ruin her reputation and bring her difficulty and fear. SB 10.29.26**

It is dismissed as disgusting and faulty. Even the women of Vraja agree when they say *niḥsvaṁ tyajanti gaṇikā jārā bhuktvā ratāṁ striyam:* prostitutes abandon a penniless man, and a lover abandons the woman he has enjoyed, even though she remains attached to him. (SB 10.47.7-8) Parīkṣit also criticizes it. *Āpta-kāmo yadu-patiḥ kṛtavān vai jugupsitam:* the self-satisfied Lord of the Yadus behaved so contemptibly. (SB 10.33.28) Thus, *laghutvam* in the verse means vulgar and censurable.

According to Bharata Muni, the love in marriage is the best, with obstacles created by cowives etc. as in the marriages depicted in *Ratnāvalī-nātīkā* and *Yayāti-carita*. How then can he say that paramour love is the best (verse 20)?

The solution is stated in the present verse. The *upapati* is disgusting when it refers to someone other than Kṛṣṇa. That is what is meant by *prākṛta-nāyaka*. When Kṛṣṇa is the *upapati* it is not disgusting because it produces the essence (*niryāsa*) of *rasa.* This means it produces a special type of *madhura-rasa.*

What has been stated is this. When Kṛṣṇa appears on earth, he displays the mode of the *upapati.* According to the ancients, it is pointed out that both he and the *gopīs* as well appeared for this purpose**.** *Āśaṁsayā rasa-vidher avatārikāṇām:* with the hope of attaining *rasa* the *gopīs* also appeared on earth. (*Nāṭaka-candrikā*) Brahmā also explains this:

*vasudeva-gṛhe sākṣād bhagavān puruṣaḥ paraḥ*  
*janiṣyate tat-priyārthaṁ sambhavantu sura-striyaḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the eternal consorts should also appear in order to satisfy him. SB 10.1.23**

It should be understood that he descended to relieve the earth of its burden because of the desire of the *devatās,* but he came to take the role of *upapati* by his own desire. Śukadeva describes the taste of the essence of *madhura-rasa (*as *upapati)*:

*bhagavān api tā rātṛīḥ śāradotphulla-mallikāḥ*  
*vīkṣya rantuṁ manaś cakre yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa is full in all opulences, yet upon seeing those autumn nights scented with blossoming jasmine flowers, he turned his mind toward loving affairs. To fulfill his purposes he employed his internal potency. SB 10.29.1**

*iti viklavitaṁ tāsāṁ śrutvā yogeśvareśvaraḥ*  
*prahasya sa-dayaṁ gopīr ātmārāmo ’py arīramat*

**Smiling upon hearing these despondent words from the** ***gopīs,*** **Kṛṣṇa, the supreme master of all masters of mystic** ***yoga,*** **mercifully enjoyed with them, although he is self-satisfied. SB 10.29.42**

*evaṁ śaśāṅkāṁśu-virājitā niśāḥ*  
*sa satya-kāmo ’nuratābalā-gaṇaḥ*  
*siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ*  
*sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ*

**Fully attached to the** ***gopīs*****, the Lord, unaffect by any mundane sex desire, but whose mind was absorbed in conjugal love, took advantage of all those moonlit autumn nights, which inspire poetic descriptions of transcendental affairs. SB 10.33.25**

*Rantum manaś cakre,* using the *ātmanepada* form of the verb, to show that this was his personal goal. *Ariramat* however is in the *parasmaipadam* form though it still expresses his personal desire. By the rule *aṇāv akarmakāc cittavat kartṛtvāt* (Pāniṇi 1.3.88) *parasmaipada* forms can have meanings like the *ātmanepada* forms. The word *saurata* refers to feelings and gestures related to love affairs. In the description of talks with Rukmiṇī the phrase *saurata-saṁlāpaiḥ* (SB 10.60.58) also has this meaning. *Saurata* does not mean something related to the *devatās (sura),* since that interpretation has never been given. He held those amorous feelings in his mind (*ātmani*).

The phrase *sura-striyaḥ* in the statement of Brahmā cannot mean the wives of the *devatās*, since one cannot say that Rādhā was the wife of any *devatā.*  Uddhava explains that the *gopīs* are exceptional:

*nāyaṁ śriyo ’ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ*  
*svar-yoṣitāṁ nalina-gandha-rucāṁ kuto ’nyāḥ*  
*rāsotsave ’sya bhuja-daṇḍa-gṛhīta-kaṇṭha-*  
*labdhāśiṣāṁ ya udagād vraja-vallabhīnām*

**When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the** ***gopīs*** **in the** ***rāsa-līlā*****, the** ***gopīs*** **were embraced by the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower. And what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation? SB 10.47.60**

These *gopīs* are most extraordinary and are dearest to Kṛṣna. Thus the term *sura-striyaḥ* (divine women) most suitably refers to the *gopīs*. They appeared because they were dearest to him (*tad-priyārtham*). The phrase does not mean “in order to make him happy, for in that case the phrase *tad-sukhārtham* would have been used. In *Brahma-saṁhitā*, the *gopīs* are called *śriyaḥ* and Lakṣmī. Similarly the Pāṇdāvas are called Kurus. This, however is not the normal manner of addressing them, and they are usually simply called Pāṇḍavas and *gopīs.* Therefore when the Pāṇḍavas are called Kurus it means that they conquered the Kurus. Similarly, when the *gopīs* are called Lakṣmī it means that they surpass Lakṣmī. That is mentioned in SB 10.47.60 quoted above.

By the statements of Uddhava and Brahmā mentioned above, the *gopīs* must have an eternal relationship with the Lord (since they are superior to Lakṣmī). Therefore they cannot actually have a *parakīya* relationship with Kṛṣṇa (since they are eteranlly related to him and not another male). Because such a situation is unsuitable, the perception of their having *parakīya* relationship when he appears as avatāra is not actual. This is shown in the drama *Lalita-mādhava* in the discussion between Paurnamāsī and Gargī. This section is the part which Jīva Gosvāmī later says is the opinion of others and is inconsistent. Viśvanāhta will refute a lot of these arguments. Even if the *gopīs* are eternally related with Kṛṣna, this fact does not rule out an eternal *parakīya* relationship. 7

*gārgī :ṇuṇaṁ goaḍḍhaṇādi-goehiṁ candāalī-pahudīṇaṁ ubbāho bi māāe ṇibbāhido \|*

**Gārgī: It is not that** ***māyā*** **produced the marriage of Govardhana and the other cowherds with Candrāvalī and the other** ***gopīs*****?**

*Paurṇamāsī: atha kim \| patiṁ-manyānāṁ ballavānāṁ mamatā-mātrāvaśeṣā tāsu dāratā \| yad ebhiḥ prekṣaṇam api tāsāṁ atidurghaṭam*

**The** ***gopas*** **simply thought these girls were their wives, with an appearance of attachment to them. In fact, they never even saw them.**

If Kṛṣṇa is their eternal husband and their being married to other cowherds is illusory, *parakīya* must be destroyed in the end. But if it is not destroyed by some magical mantra and is without beginning, then *parakīya* should be eternal. According to this logic, an improper manifestation of *rasa* will arise. Thus, in the later part of the Lord’s appearance on earth, the married condition becomes manifest. That is the final conclusion and will be proved by the explanations given in *Lalita-mādhava.*

Because it has been said that the conclusion is an eternal union in order to resolve the separation which is plentifully described, the *rasas* in the sequence of pastimes on earth do not produce the perfection of *ujjvala-rasa*. Since this is dissatisfying, to counteract separation, an arrangement in the form of marriage in the undisputedly best form of *sambhoga, samṛddhimān,* among the four types of sambhoga (*saṅkṣipta, saṅkīṛṇa, sampanna*, and *samṛddhimān*) will be shown in the examples. Thus Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā at the end of great separation (*samṛddhimān-sambhoga*):

*tavātra parimṛgyatā kim api lakṣma sākṣād iyaṁ*  
*mayā tvam upasāditā nikhila-loka-lakṣmīr asi \|*  
*yathā jagati cañcatā caṇaka-muṣṭi-sampattaye*  
*janena patitā puraḥ kanaka-vṛṣṭir āsādyate \|\|*

**I have been searching for some sign of you, and now I have found you. I worship you, the goddess of fortune who reigns over all worlds. You are a shower of gold raining upon a person fallen and wandering in the universe, searching for a treasure of chick-peas.** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **8.39** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **15.208**

In the drama it is pointed out that *upapati* only exists because of a belief in having *upapati* love. The *gopīs* believed they were married to cowherd men, but those forms were actually illusory. 8 Even writers of material *rasa* have praise this type of *upapati* love with its condemned portion (since it is abelief in *upapati* only.) However in the case of Kṛṣṇa, it is not derided but rather praised because *rasa* of *samṛddhi-sambhoga* is nourished when marriage takes place after separation and the illusion of being *upapati* ends. Thus the text says that the negative aspects of *upapati* do not apply to Kṛṣṇa. The reason is the intensity of *rasa* it produces (*rasa-niryā*sa). But without this arrangement, when the hero is not Kṛṣṇa, where there is actual *upapati* occurring, the relationship is condemned (*laghutvam)*. If one eats healthy food out of greed, thinking it is unhealthy, one still becomes healthy. Ignorant people, thinking the highest truth is something else, still get benefit from hearing about Kṛṣṇa’s *upapati* love.

Moreover, the excellence of the gopīs’ rati does not depend on the presence of excessive obstacles, for it is said:

*yoga eva bhaved eṣa vicitraḥ ko’pi mādanaḥ \|*  
*yad-vilāsā virājante nitya-līlāḥ sahasradhā \|\|*

**During union, mādana takes on unprecedented astonishing qualities, whose effects manifest as thousands of continuous pastimes.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.225**

Even in the absence of obstacles, in union--in *madana,* the summit of *mahā-bhāva--*this is intrinsic excellence is present. It will be shown that *samarthā rati* has an intrinsic excellence. It is not present in the *sādhāraṇī rati* of Kubja, or *samañjasa-rati* of the queens. The qualities of *samarthā rati* will be described:

*sva-svarūpāt tadīyād vā jātā yat-kiṁcid-anvayāt \|*  
*samarthā sarva-vismāri-gandhā sāndratamā matā \|\|*

**Arising from** ***lalanā-niṣṭha-svaṛupa*** **or a slight connection with anything related to Kṛṣṇa,** ***samartha-rati*** **is most condensed, and even a trace of it makes one forget everything else.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.53**

*ratir bhāvāntimāṁ sīmāṁ samarthaiva prapadyante \|\|*

***Samarthā rati*** **alone attains its limit at** ***mahābhāva. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.232**

The word *eva* (alone) with *samarthā* indicates that *sādhāranī* and *samañjasā rati* are not similar to it in terms of being criticized or other qualities. Because of the intrinsic excellence of *samarthā rati,* persons desiring liberation and liberated souls desire the *gopīs*’ type of love. *Vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṁ ca:* their pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as well. (SB 10.47.58) This desire appears in the queens as well.

*vraja-striyo yad vāñchanti pulindyas tṛṇa-vīrudhaḥ*  
*gāvaś cārayato gopāḥ pada-sparśaṁ mahātmanaḥ*

**We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord’s feet that the young women of Vraja, the cowherd boys and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire—the touch of the dust he leaves on the plants and grass as he tends his cows. SB 10.83.43**

But because they do not at all desire censure from others they cannnot think of love with Kṛṣna as *upapati.* And even the *gopīs* in their differing types of *rati* will be described in terms of their unique response when there are obstacles and criticism. The obstacles, like shackles that the hunter tries to put on the mad elephant’s feet, cause the strength of their *rati* to manifest, but do not create it. Thus it is said:

*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopī*****s of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge.. SB 10.47.61**

The characteristics of *parakīya* love are described:

*rāgeṇaivārpitātmāno loka-yugmānapekṣiṇaḥ*  
*dharmeṇāsvīkṛtā yās tu parakīyā bhavanti tāḥ*

**Those women, who out of great attraction, ignoring their fate in this world and the next, not accecting the rites of marriage, offer themselves to Kṛṣṇa, are called** ***parakīya*** **women. .** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **3.17**

The excellence of *rati* is said to shown by means of separation:

*na vinā vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute \|*

**The happiness of conjugal love cannot reach it's fullness without separation of the lovers.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **15.3**

*nāhaṁ tu sakhyo bhajato ’pi jantūn*  
*bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye*  
*yathādhano labdha-dhane vinaṣṭe*  
*tac-cintayānyan nibhṛto na veda*

**The reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they worship me, O gopīs, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he can think of nothing else. SB 10.32.20**

One can judge the excellence of *rati* by toleration of separation. There are various degrees of digestive power in various animals, but the elephant’s and the rabbit’s fire of digestion cannot be measured by how far they jump (but by how much they eat after developing hunger Just as hunger that is produced by walking in a forest is not reduced by crossing the forest, *rati* with a life of constant separation because of constant obstacles (in *upapati* love) is not reduced automatically. However, by periodic separation (followed by union), there is great benefit.

Material *rasa* has been described as highly censured (*bahu vāryate*) in order to understand the manifestation of gopīs’ attachment. That is the intended meaning of the author. Thus what Bharat Muni has said about the material *upapati* is correct. *Rasa-niryāsa-svādārtham avatariṇi*: Kṛṣṇa has appeared in this world to taste the thick *madhura-rasa* as *upapati.* This means that he does not accept the role of *upapati* except in the material world. His eternal position is that of being married.

The proof of this is self evident. In *Brahmā-saṁhitā* (5.48) the *gopīs* are called *nija-rūpatayā.* This means that the *gopīs* are his own portions, who are thus eternally perfect. In explaining the ten syllable mantra, *Gautamīya-tantra* says:

*aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnāṁ patir eva vā \|*  
*nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ \|\|*

**The husband of the perfect** ***gopīs*** **who accompany him for many life times in this world is called Kṛṣṇa. He increases the bliss of the three worlds.**

The phrase *aneka-janma-siddhānām* does not mean that the *gopīs* reached perfection after many lifetimes. The births refers to the many times they have appeared along with Kṛṣṇa in the material world as eternally perfect beings. Kṛṣna also says *bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna:*  you and I have appeared many times in this world in the past. (BG 4.5)

In the phrase *anādi-siddha-veda* this usage is also seen. The words *patir eva vā* (a husband) in the *Gautamīya-tantra* verse indicate that he does not exist in the spiritual world as he does when he appears as an *upapati* during earthly pastimes by illusion. In the same scripture it is said *gopīti prakṛtiṁ vidyāj janas tattva-samūhakaḥ*: the word *gopī* means *prakṛti* and j*ana* means all the elements. *athavā gopī prakṛtir janas tad-aṁśa-maṇḍalam*: or *gopī* refers to *prakṛti* and *jana* refers to a group of expanded forms (*aṁśa*). In these two explanations of the ten syllable *mantra* about Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa is described as the Lord of a group of spiritual *śaktis* and the shelter of the material elements producing the world composed of the three *guṇas.* However these are secondary meanings, since later the conclusion is given.

Thus the Lord is one but has qualities. In the *Vedānta-sūtra* it is said *ahi-kuṇḍalavat*: the lord is both bliss and blissful (or himself and the *gopīs*) like the snake and its coils (3.2.27) *prakāśāśrayavad vā tejastvā:* the Lord is both attribute and substance and is thus said to be the abode of light or has brilliance. (3.2.28) *pūrvavad vā:* the Lord is both attribute and substance just as time both prior and posterior. (3.2.29)

The word *nanda-nandana* makes it clear that Kṛṣṇa alone is being designated. In every *kalpa* he appears as the son of Nanda. *Trailokyānanda-vardhana* with the present participle suffix *ana* indicates his quality of increasing even now the bliss of all the eternal and practicing devotees by seeing and hearing. *Vardhana* indicates the eternal present as does *jayati* in the verse *jayati jana-nivasaḥ* (SB 10.90.48). Similarly, the phrase *nivṛtta-tarṣair upagīyamānād* means that the Lord is being glorified now by persons without material thirst.

In *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* (2.27) Durvasā also describes Kṛṣṇa as married: *sa vo hi svāmī bhavati*: he is the husband. The conventional meaning of the word *svāmī* is husband. *Amara-koṣa* says *svāmi* means husband or husband’s brother. Even Śukadeva reveals Kṛṣṇa as husband when he is absorbed in bliss and speaking indirectly.

*pāda-nyāsair bhuja-vidhutibhiḥ sa-smitair bhrū-vilāsair*  
*bhajyan madhyaiś cala-kuca-paṭaiḥ kuṇḍalair gaṇḍa-lolaiḥ*  
*svidyan-mukhyaḥ kavara-rasanāgranthayaḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo*  
*gāyantyas taṁ taḍita iva tā megha-cakre virejuḥ*

**As the** ***gopīs*** **sang in praise of Kṛṣṇa, their feet danced, their hands gestured, and their eyebrows moved with playful smiles. With their braids and belts tied tight, their waists bending, their faces perspiring, the garments on their breasts moving this way and that, and their earrings swinging on their cheeks, Lord Kṛṣṇa’s young consorts shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds. SB 10.30.7**

The word *kṛṣṇa-vadhvaḥ* can mean Kṛṣṇa’s wives. They are compared to lightning in the cloud of Kṛṣṇa. (They are naturally related.) The relationship of being naturally married has been shown through the use of similes.

*dharma-vyatikramo dṛṣṭa īśvarāṇāṁ ca sāhasam*  
*tejīyasāṁ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā*

**The status of powerful controllers is not harmed by any apparently audacious transgression of morality we may see in them, for they are just like fire, which devours everything fed into it and remains unpolluted. SB 10.33.30**

Though he recognizes such bold approaches in Kṛṣṇa, not satisfied that the *gopīs* are wives of other husbands, Śukadeva breaks the illusion and draws the conclusion:

*gopīnāṁ tat-patīnāṁ ca sarveṣām eva dehinām \|*  
*yo 'ntaś carati so 'dhyakṣaḥ krīḍaneneha deha-bhāk \|\|*

**He who lives as the overseeing witness within the** ***gopīs*** **and their husbands, and indeed within all embodied living beings, assumes forms in this world to enjoy transcendental pastimes. SB 10.33.35**

For the materialists, he crushes the idea of Kṛṣṇa being an *upapati* by introducing the idea that he is the *antaryāmī* in all beings. For the devotees however there is an esoteric meaning that Kṛṣṇa is the eternal and natural husband of the *gopīs.* The meaning can be taken as follows. He who has a playful form (*deha-bhak*) for all the women cowherds, all the cowherd men (*patīnām*) and all persons situated in Vraja, for all those who had bodies suitable for pastimes, and he who is invisible to materialists (*antar=antardhana*) but is sometimes visible to them (*adhyakṣaḥ*), performs pastimes like *rāsa-līlā* eternally. Thus the *gopīs* are not married to someone else, because they have continuous and eternal pastimes such as *rāsa-līlā* suitable only for them.

Some of this has been written by my own will and some by the will of others. What is consistent is my opinion and what is not consistent (a lot of the latter portion) is the opinion of others.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There is no difference of opinion between authorities on *rasa* and persons with apparently contrary views when examining the real substance. That is stated in this verse. The rejection of the *upapati* by the previous *ācāryas* is rejection of the material person only, because that type of *upapati* transgresses *dharma,* because he generates bad *karma* for himself in the future, and because he will end up in hell. He is condemned because he produces only suffering for himself. Because the *upapati’s* actions are depicted in plays and poems, one may develop a taste for them as if the *upapati* had worthy conduct. Even persons of good conduct, absorbed in such depictions, may fall into identification with such a person and becomes tinged with irreligion, in the manner *of yad adharma-kṛtaḥ sthānaṁsūcakasyāpi tad bhavet:* the person who points out the sinner attains the same place as the sinner. (SB 1.17.22) However, the same condemnation cannot be given to Kṛṣṇa, who is the crest jewel controlling all *dharma* and *adharma.* Why does he appear? He appears so that the well bred can taste the essence of his *rasa*. If it is claimed that Kṛṣṇa is also to be condemned, the taste of the essence of *rasa* would have no shelter by which the well bred could experience it. Who is Kṛṣṇa? He is the source of all *avatāras.*  For any *avatāra,* there are no restrictions of proper or improper conduct. That is well known in the *śruti* and *smṛti.* What then can be said of the source of all *avatāras (avatārī)*?

The meaning is this. A taste of the essence of *rasa,* testified by all sensible people, is visible in both married and unmarried love affairs. This is in agreement with Bharata Muni who gives the definition that unmarried love is vehemently opposed (*bahu vāryate*), with Rudra-bhaṭṭa’s *Śṛṅgāra-tilaka* quoted in *Ujjvala–nīlamanī* 3.20, and with *Viṣṇu-gupta-saṁhitā* quoted in *Ujjvala–nīlamanī* 3.21, describing the *parakīyā* woman. As well, *Śṛṅgāra-tilaka* 1.61 says:

*ananya-śaraṇā svīyā dhanāhāryā parāṅganā \|*  
*asyās tu kevalaṁ prema tenaiṣā rāgiṇāṁ matā \|\|*

**A woman completely dedicated, a woman married to oneself, a woman worth a fortune, is the best woman. She has pure love. By that love she is respected among women lovers.**
