Though it is concluded that both the unmarried and married protagonists are topmost, the cause of being called disreputed (*laghutvam*) is that the person is tinged with immorality. But immorality can never touch Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, who is the source of the first *puruṣāvatāra,* who, by the movement of his brow, causes creation, maintenance and destruction of the all things including *dharma* and adharma; who is the highest form of pastimes but possesses a human body, and who is endowed with the *hlādinī-śakti,* the principle energy among all his great energies, which takes the form of Rādhā. The enjoyers of his *upapati* pastimes attain the highest results according to the *Bhāgavatam*:

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. SB 10.33.39**

*tad vāg-visargo janatāgha-samplavo*  
*yasmin prati-ślokam abaddhavaty api*  
*nāmāny anantasya yaśo 'ṅkitāni yat*  
*śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ*

**The use of words in which, though not perfectly composed, there are the names of the Lord and descriptions of his glories which devotes hear, sing, and again receive, destroys the sins of all people. SB 12.12.52**

*mṛṣā giras tā hy asatīr asat-kathā*  
*na kathyate yad bhagavān adhokṣajaḥ*  
*tad eva satyaṁ tad u haiva maṅgalaṁ*  
*tad eva puṇyaṁ bhagavad-guṇodayam*

**Words that do not describe the transcendental Lord but instead deal with temporary matters are simply false, harsh and useless. Only those words that manifest the qualities of the Supreme Lord are actually truthful, auspicious and pure. SB 12.12.49**

Rather it is concluded that he is the highest of all lovers. The author of *Nāṭaka-candrikā* (Rūpa Gosvāmī) says:

*yat-paroḍhopapatyos tu gauṇatvaṁ kathitaṁ budhaiḥ \|*  
*tat tu kṛṣṇaṁ ca gopīś ca vineti pratipāditam \|\|*

**The condemnation of the** ***upapati*** **in his relation with a married woman by the wise does not apply to Kṛṣṇa and the** ***gopīs.***

The author of *Alaṅkāra-kaustubha* (Kavi-karṇapūra) says:

*aprākṛte paroḍha-ramaṇī-ratir eva sarvottamatayā bhūyasī śrūyate \| na tasyām anaucitya-pravartitatvam alaukikaṁ tu siddher bhūṣaṇam eva na tu dūṣaṇam iti nyāyāt tarkāgocaratvāc*

**The love of married women for Kṛṣṇa is said by many to be the highest. It follows the principle beyond logic that the spiritual actions which are normally condemned are an ornament, not a fault, in Kṛṣṇa.**

There is another meaning to the phrase *na kanee rasa-niryasa-svadartham avatarini.* How is Kṛṣṇa described? He appears in the world to taste his intimate devotees in the material world taste the essence of *rasa.* But his tasting the essence of *rasa* eternally exists in both his manifested and unmanifested pastimes. When he shows his pastimes of being born to the people of this world by his mercy, they are called his manifest pastimes. When the pastimes are invisible to the eyes, they are called his unmanifest pastimes. But there is no difference between the manifest and unmanifest pastimes at all. It is said in *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta* 1.5.387*:*

*anādim eva janmādi-līlām eva tathādbhutam \|*  
*hetunā kenacit kṛṣṇaḥ prāduṣkuryāt kadācana \|\|*

**Fire, though a powerful form, remains hidden in wood and jewels, but due to a certain cause, appears from jewels and wood. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa makes his astonishing appearance which is without beginning at a certain time, under certain conditions.**

*tatra śrī-jīva-gosvāmi-caraṇānāṁ tu yan matam \|*  
*svecchābhimatam etan me mānanīyaṁ na cetarat \|\|*

**I give respect to the opinions of Jīva Gosvāmī which are his own, and not to the other opinions he has written.**

It is not a fact that Kṛṣṇa is always married to the *gopīs* in the unmanifest pastimes. His pastimes are all eternal whether his love takes an unmarried (*upapati*) or married form (*paroḍha).* It is not a fact that for some days in his manifest pastimes there is an illusion of Kṛṣṇa being *upapati,* for it is most unsuitable to say that the entire *rāsa-līlā*, the crest jewel of all pastimes, is merely an illusion of an *upapati* having affairs with married women.

The statements of Śukadeva, the Lord, and the *gopīs* announce emphatically the *parakīya* nature of the *rāsa-līlā,* and never say that he was actually married to them.

*tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ*  
*govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ*

**Their husbands, fathers, brothers and other relatives tried to stop them, but Kṛṣṇa had already stolen their hearts. Enchanted by the sound of his flute, they refused to turn back. SB 10.29.8**

*mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ*  
*vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṁ bandhu-sādhvasam*

**Not finding you at home, your mothers, fathers, sons, brothers and husbands are certainly searching for you. Don’t cause anxiety for your family members. SB 10.29.20**

*yat paty-apatya-suhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga*  
*strīṇāṁ sva-dharma iti dharma-vidā tvayoktam*  
*astv evam etad upadeśa-pade tvayīśe*  
*preṣṭho bhavāṁs tanu-bhṛtāṁ kila bandhur ātmā*

**Our dear Kṛṣṇa, as an expert in religion you have advised us that the proper religious duty for women is to faithfully serve their husbands, children and other relatives. We agree that this principle is valid, but actually this service should be rendered to you. After all, O Lord, you are the dearmost friend of all embodied souls. You are their most intimate relative and indeed their very self. SB 10.29.32 (The above quotations are all from the first chapter concerning** ***rāsa-līlā*****.)**

*tan-manaskās tad-alāpās tad-viceṣṭās tad-ātmikāḥ*  
*tad-guṇān eva gāyantyo nātmagārāṇi sasmaruḥ*

**Their minds absorbed in thoughts of him, they conversed about him, acted out his pastimes and felt themselves filled with his presence. They completely forgot about their homes as they loudly sang the glories of Kṛṣṇa’s transcendental qualities. SB 10.30.43 (This is from the second chapter on** ***rāsa-līlā*****.)**

*evaṁ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda*  
*svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye ’balāḥ*  
*mayāparokṣaṁ bhajatā tirohitaṁ*  
*māsūyituṁ mārhatha tat priyaṁ priyāḥ*

**My dear girls, understanding that simply for my sake you had rejected the authority of worldly opinion, of the Vedas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to me. Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. Therefore, my beloved** ***gopīs,*** **please do not harbor any bad feelings toward me, your beloved. SB 10.32.21 (This is from the fourth chapter on** ***rāsa-līlā*****.)**

*kṛtvā tāvantam ātmānaṁ yāvatīr gopa-yoṣitaḥ*  
*reme sa bhagavāṁs tābhir ātmārāmo ’pi līlayā*

**Expanding himself us many times as there were cowherd women to associate with, the Supreme Lord, though self-satisfied, playfully enjoyed their company. SB 10.33.20**

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against him. SB 10.33.37 (The last two quotations are from the fifth chapter on** ***rāsa-līlā*****.)**

Moreover if these pastimes are illusory, the superiority of the *gopīs* over Lakṣmī, expressed in SB 10.47.60, starting with *nāyaṁ śriyo ’ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ* would not be factual. As well Kṛṣṇa’s extraordinary qualities known as extraordinary pastimes of *prema* and extraordinary loving devotees-- two of the four qualities found only in Kṛṣna (BRS 2.1.43) would be without basis.

And no one has every described the *rāsa-līlā* as a pastime of a married Kṛṣṇa. It can never be said that the five chapters on *rāsa-līlā* are commendable if one must reject the portions describing *upapati* love created by illusion. If that were so, then the verses proving the highest level of *prema* in the *rāsa-līlā* would be a lie:

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*  
*yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ*  
*saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā*

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. SB 10.33.22**

If the *gopīs* actually did not cut their ties, then Kṛṣṇa’s quality of being controlled by their *prema,* expressed in his words “I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service” would also not be factual.

All the words of the Lord, the supreme controller of illusion, during the pastimes would amount to mere flattery. But the wisest person, the crown jewel of devotees, Uddhava has said:

*āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ*  
*vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām*  
*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

He has shown that the *gopīs’ prema* is superior to that of the queens of Dvārakā. The reason is that they have given up association of family members. If giving up family members is illusory, then his reason for their greatness is not factual. Therefore his conclusion that they are the greatest devotees is false. It would also mean that the speaker Uddhava is in illusion.

Moreover the meaning of ten and the eighteen syllable *mantras* mentioned in the Pañcarātra and Vedas, which are to be used for worshipping in the eternal state, show Kṛṣṇa as the *upapati* with married women. In the mantra the words *gopī-jana-vallabhāya* cannot refer to Kṛṣṇa who married *brāhmaṇa* women. Though some may give this interpretation it is not accepted by persons knowledgeable of grammar and rhetoric. Only by indiscriminately giving an extraordinary meaning to the power of words, one could give such a meaning. Even then the meaning is: the *brāhmaṇa* women are dear or he is dear to them. This can also indicate *parakīya* relationship. Using the word *brāhmaṇī* to indicate a person’s wife can only be found in colloquial language and cannot be applied in argumentation.

*Brāhmaṇī* can indicate a woman related to a *brāhmaṇa* man, and because of lack of any masculine qualifying word, the word should be taken to mean a woman. *Brāhmaṇī* can also refer to something related to a *bṛāhmaṇa.* Only in a certain context is it used to indicate a married woman. If one says at a temple or *śrāddha* rites, “Make yourself into *a brāhmaṇī (brāhmaṇīm ākāraya)”* it would mean that one should make oneself into a female *brāhmaṇa ācārya*. If the same sentence were to be used for external deity service, it would indicate a female servant. If used in relation to offspring, it would indicate a sister. Used in one’s bedroom it would indicate one’s own wife and used in a solitary forest, it would also indicate one’s wife.

One should not spoil the *mantras* with such meanings, for it is said that what appears to be fault in the Lord is his ornament, not a fault. Thus in meditating on the *mantra* in the *Gautamīya-tantra,* it is said *vicitrāmbara-bhūṣābhir gopa-nārībhir āvṛtam*: he is surrounded by the cowherds’ wives who were ornamented with colorful cloth. The conventional meaning of *gopa-nārībhiḥ* is “by the wives of the cowherds.”

In the *Krama-dīpikā*, in the *mantra* for meditation in the first part of the day it is said *go-gopa-gopa-vanitā-nikaraiḥ parītaṁ sāndrāmbuda-cchavi-sujāta-manoharāṅgam*: Kṛṣṇa is surrounded with groups of cows, cowherds, and cowherds’ wives and has attractive limb the color of a dense rain cloud. In the *mantra* for meditation on the Lord in the morning, noon and evening, after describing Kṛṣṇa’s dark complexion and being covered with dust from the cows, it is said *mahībhāra-bhūtām arārāti-yūthān*

*alaṁ pūtanādīn nihantuṁ pravṛttam*: he is engaged in killing Pūtanā and other hostile demons who are burden to the earth. Then it is said:

*vande taṁ devakī-putraṁ sadyo-jātaṁ dyu-saprabham \|*  
*pītāmbaraṁ kara-lasac-chaṅkha-cakra-gadāmbujam \|\|*  
*evaṁ dhyātvā japen mantraṁ*

**I offer respects to the newly born son of Devakī, with the complexion of the sky wearing a yellow cloth and with arms hold shining conch, wheel, club and lotus. Having meditated thus, one should chant the following** ***mantra*****.** ***Krama-dīpikā*** **6.2-3**

*lambitaṁ bāla-śayane rudantaṁ vallavī-janaiḥ \|*  
*preṅkhamāṇaṁ*

**One should meditate on Kṛṣṇa lying in his bed and crying, he is swung back and forth by the cowherd women.** ***Krama-dīpikā*** **6.11**

*sāsu-cūṣaṇa-nirbhinna-sarvāṅgīṁ rudatīṁ ca tām*

**He sucked out the life air of from all of Pūtanā’s limbs while she screamed.** ***Krama-dīpikā*** **6.14**

*dārayantaṁ bakaṁ dorbhyāṁ*

**One should meditate on Kṛṣna tearing up Baka with his arms. .** ***Krama-dīpikā*** **6.26**

*kālīyasya phaṇā-madhye divyaṁ nṛtyaṁ karoti tam*

**One should meditate on Kṛṣna dancing divinely on the hoods of Kālīya.**

*uddaṇḍa-vāma-dor-daṇḍa-dhṛta-govardhanācalam*

**One should meditate on Kṛṣna lifting up Govardhana with his left arm.** ***Krama-dīpikā*****. 6.40**

*athavā garudārūḍhaṁ bala-pradyumna-saṁyutam \|*  
*nija-jvara-viniṣpiṣṭa-jvarābhiṣṭutam acyutam \|\|*

**One should meditate on Acyuta mounted on Garuḍa, accompanied by Pradyumna and Balarāma, and praised by Bāṇāsura whose fever was defeated by the Lord’s. .** ***Krama-dīpikā*** **6.46**

*dveṣayantaṁ rukmi-balau dyūtāsaktau smaran harim*

**One should remember the Lord who created enmity between Rukmi and Balarāma while they played dice.**

In sequence, the *mantras* describe Kṛṣna’s pastimes on earth from his birth. The worshippers, by meditating with these *mantras,* achieve maturity in meditation by attaining a state of eternal time, and then meet the Lord directly. This result shows that manifested pastimes on earth are eternal (since meditation on them gives that result.)

In his commentary on verses such as 4.5 and 4.9 of the *Gītā,* Rāmānujācārya shows the eternal nature of Kṛṣṇa’s birth, pastimes and associates, using proofs from *śruti* and *smṛti.* Madhusūdana Sarasvatī explains that *divya* in the phrase *janma karma ca me divyam* means “spiritual.” In the *Puruṣa-bodhinī-śruti* of the Pipalāda-śākhā, it is said *devo nitya-līlānurakto bhakta-vyāpī bhakta-hṛdy antarātmā*: the Lord who is engaged in eternal pastimes spreads himself into the devotee, and acts as the soul within the devotee. And Viṭṭhala-Nātha Gosvāmī in his work *Vidvan-maṇḍana* has stated that the pastimes, qualities, name and form of Kṛṇsa are eternal.

In the *Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa*, in the later section, this is stated. Brahmā speaks to Bhṛgu and other sages.

*prākṛte pralaye prāpte vyakte’vyaktaṁ gate purā \|*  
*śiṣṭe brahmaṇi cin-mātre kālam āyātige’kṣare \|\|*  
*brahmānanda-mayo loko vyāpī vaikuṇṭha-saṁjñitaḥ \|*  
*nirguṇo’nādy-anantaś ca vartate kevale’kṣare \|\|*  
*akṣaraṁ paramaṁ brahma vedānāṁ sthānam uttamam \|*  
*tal-loka-vāsī hi janaḥ stuto vedaiḥ parāt paraḥ \|*  
*ciraṁ stutyā tatas tuṣṭaḥ parokṣaḥ prāha tān girā \|\|*  
*tuṣṭo’smi brūta bho prājñā varaṁ yan manasīpsitam \|\|*  
*śrutaya ūcuḥ—*  
*brahmeti paṭhyate’smābhir yad-rūpaṁ nirguṇaṁ param \|*  
*vāṅ-mano-gocarātītaṁ tato na jñāyate tu yat \|\|*  
*ānanda-mātram iti yad vadantīha purāvidaḥ \|*  
*tad-rūpaṁ darśayāsmākaṁ yadi deyo varo hi naḥ \|\|*  
*śrutvaitad darśayāmāsa khaṁ lokaṁ prakṛteḥ param \|*  
*kevalānubhavānanda-mātram akṣaram avyayam \|\|*  
*yatra vṛndāvanaṁ nāma vanaṁ kāma-dughair drumaiḥ \|*  
*manoramaṁ nikuñjāḍhyaṁ sarvartu-rasa-saṁyutam \|\|*  
*yatra govardhano nāma sunirjhara-darī-yutaḥ \|*  
*ratna-dhātu-mayaḥ śrīmān supakṣi-gaṇa-saṅkulaḥ \|\|*  
*yatra nirmala-pānīyā kālindī saritā varā \|*  
*ratna-baddhobhaya-taṭā haṁsa-padmādi-saṅkulā \|\|*  
*nānā-rāsa-rasonmattaṁ yatra gopī-kadambakam \|*  
*tat-kadambaka-madhyasthaḥ kiśorākṛtir acyutaḥ \|\|*  
*darśayitveti ca prāha brūta kiṁ karavāṇi vaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭo madīyo loko’yaṁ yato nāsti paraṁ varam \|\|*  
*śrutaya ūcuḥ—*  
*kandarpa-koṭi-lāvaṇye tvayi dṛṣṭe manāṁsi naḥ \|*  
*kāminī-bhāvam āsādya smara-kṣubdhāny asaṁśayam \|\|*  
*yathā tval-loka-vāsinyaḥ kāma-tattvena gopikāḥ \|*  
*bhajanti ramaṇaṁ matvā cikīrṣājani nas tathā \|\|*  
*śrī-bhagavān uvāca —*  
*durlabho durghaṭaś caiva yuṣmākaṁ sumanorathaḥ \|*  
*mayānumoditaḥ samyak satyo bhavitum arhati \|\|*  
*āgāmini viriñcau tu jāte sṛṣty-artham udyate \|*  
*kalpaṁ sārasvataṁ prāpya vraje gopyo bhaviṣyatha \|\|*  
*pṛthivyāṁ bhārate kṣetre māthure mama maṇḍale \|*  
*vṛndāvane bhaviṣyāmi preyān vo rāsa-maṇḍale \|\|*  
*jāra-dharmeṇa susnehaṁ sudṛḍhaṁ sarvato 'dhikam \|*  
*mayi samprāpya sarve 'pi kṛta-kṛtyā bhaviṣyatha \|\|*  
*brahmovāca—*  
*śrutvaitac cintayanty astā rūpaṁ bhagavataś ciram \|*  
*ukta-kālaṁ samāsādya gopyo bhūtvā hariṁ gatāḥ \|\|*

**Previously, when all matter, meeting final destruction, entered an invisible state, and only pure Brahman remained, absorbing even material time, a pervading planet composed of pure spiritual bliss, known as Vaikuṇṭha, remained beyond the** ***guṇas,*** **with no beginning or end, in that pure Brahman. It was the indestructible, highest Brahman, the highest place mentioned in the Veda. The resident of that planet, superior to all, is praised by the Vedas. After being praised for a long time and being satisfied, he who is invisible to mortals spoke to the Vedas. “I am satisfied with you. O wise ones! Ask for a boon that you desire.”**

**The Vedas said, “If you want to give us a benediction, please show us that form which is pure bliss, which is not understood, which is beyond words and mind, which we understand to be Brahman, which the ancient sages describe and whose form is beyond the** ***guṇas*****.”**

**Hearing that, the Lord showed them the indestructible spiritual planet without miseries, beyond matter, composed of only bliss. In that place there was a forest called Vṛṇdāvana, filled with the pleasures of all seasons, charming with desire trees and dense with bowers. There was a glorious hill named wealthy Govardhana with clean waterfalls, filled with gems, and crowded with beautiful birds. In that place there was the Yamunā River with pure water, whose banks were studded with jewels, and which was filled with swans and lotuses. In that place there were groups of** ***gopīs*** **mad with a taste of various pastimes. In that place Kṛṣṇa, with the form of a youth, was situated among the** ***gopīs.***

**After he showed them this, he said, “Say what I should do for you after you have seen my planet. There is no greater benediction that this.”**

**The Vedas said, “Seeing you with more beauty than millions of Cupids, make our minds, undoubtedly agitated by love, assume the mood of the** ***gopīs.*** **Thinking of that enjoyment, our desire to act in the manner that the** ***gopīs*** **living on your planet serve has manifested within us.”**

**The Lord said “Such desire rarely occurs and is difficult to fulfill, but permitted by me, it should come true. When the future Brahmā is born and rises up to create the universe, when the Sārasvata-kalpa (twelfth day of Brahmā) arrives, you will become** ***gopīs*** **in Vraja. I will appear in Vṛndāvana, within Mathurā area within Bhārata on the earth as your lover in the** ***rāsa*** **arena. Attaining most firm affection for me as the unmarried lover, you will all become successful.”**

**Brahmā said, “Hearing that, the Vedas contemplated the form of the Lord for a long time. When the said time arrived, they became** ***gopīs*** **and attained Kṛṣṇa.”**

Viṭṭala-nātha explains the verses as follows:

The Vedas requested, “Show us your form beyond words and mind, beyond the *guṇas,* ascertained in the Vedānta.” The Lord then showed Gokula and his form situated there, as he performed pastimes. If it is approved by the Vedas, it is actually happening. If this is so, the eternal nature of the pastimes is proven. This is also defined by omniscient Gargācārya at the name giving ceremony described in the Tenth Canto.

*bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te \|*  
*guṇa-karmānurūpāṇi tāny ahaṁ veda no janāḥ \|\|*

**For this son of yours there are many forms and names according to his transcendental qualities and activities. These are known to me, but people in general do not understand them. SB 10.8.15**

“Your son has many names and forms.” The present tense is used. That means they continue to exist. Similarly his qualities like generosity and activities like subduing Kāliya and suitable forms exist eternally.  *Anurūpa* refers to a form suitable for a particular pastime. For instance, in lifting Govardhana, he has a standing form with raised arm while saving the inhabitants and pleasing them. If the actions and forms which produce the actions are continually present, then the names of Kṛṣṇa suitable for the particular pastimes are also continually present. Otherwise, when the action has been completed, the related name would disappear.

Later Viṭṭala-nātha explains as follows. The names of the Lord are eternal sound forms of Brahman. Just as one may perceive the Lord’s body to be material because of faulty perception, so one may perceive his names to be material sound because of faulty perception. Thus, all the names attached to the Lord’s form should be considered eternal.

“How can names which appear only after manifestation of qualities and actions be Brahman, since those names become bound by material time?” The corresponding names just manifest along with the manifestation of the actions of the Lord’s *svarūpa* (since they are eternal). The names are not created after an activity. Kṛṣṇa was bathed by Surabhi after lifting Govardhana and received the name Govinda. But long before this, if the names are not eternal, how could the women of Vraja, placing syllables on Kṛṣṇa’s body after he drank the milk of Pūtanā say *krīḍantaṁ pātu govindaḥ*: may Govinda protect you while you play? They also later said *govinda-veṇum anumatta-mayūra-nṛtyam*: the peacocks dance madly after hearing Govinda’s flute. (SB 10.21.10) Thus the name corresponding to the form doing the activity has an eternal nature describing the activity. These will gradually manifest in this world in order that the devotees experience *rasa* from them. Some portions however may sometimes remain covered.

Thus the Lord eternally lifts Govardhana. The form of Kṛṣṇa lifting Govardhana always exists along with the name Govardhana-dhāra and the action of lifting Govardhana. Even today the devotees can realize this. There is also worship and meditation on deity forms. One commits offense by thinking of the names, forms and activities to be non-eternal. And such offensive worship will not cause joy, for it is said *yo’nyathā santam ātmānam*: he who thinks body is the self (or the Lord is material) is the worst sinner. (*Mahā-bhārata* 1.65.18) By being without offense, the worship will be pure. Thus the names corresponding to the activity are eternal because the name and form are both necessary constituents of the Lord. One should not doubt that this statement is in any way merely figurative.

In *Bhāgavat-sandarbha*, Jīva Gosvāmī has explained the following verse:

*na vidyate yasya ca janma karma vā*  
*na nāma-rūpe guṇa-doṣa eva vā*  
*tathāpi lokāpyaya-sambhavāya yaḥ*  
*sva-māyayā tāny anukālam ṛcchati*

**He who has no birth or activities, no name or form, no qualities or faults, accepts birth and activities as Brahmā and Śiva at the time creation and destruction by his energies of** ***rajas*** **and** ***tamas*** **for creating and destroying the universe. SB 8.3.8**

He explains it as follows:

The Lord has no birth or activities, but by his *svarūpa-śakti (sva-māyayā)* he accepts birth and activities. One may say, “Since he attains birth and activities, those are temporary events.” In answer to this the verse says that the Lord continually (*anukālam*) attains them. This means he never gives up birth and activities. Being manifested through the *svarūpa-śakti* and being eternal are supportive of each other.

“How can birth and pastimes be eternal? They are both actions. An action and each of its parts are defined in terms a beginning and end. Without that, the action’s very form would disappear.”

There is no fault, for the following reasons. Because the Lord always has an eternal form, that form is eternally manifest. Because of this, the Lord’s pastimes with birth and activities are also eternal. Thus the individuality and manifestation of associates in the pastimes and the places in unlimited Vaikuṇṭhas and unlimited universes are also eternal. The beginning and completion of actions revealed by the Lord’s form are located in one place, but when a portion of the birth and actions are completed in that place, that portion begins in another universe. Since the Lord is eternal because of having no destruction, the birth and activities exist elsewhere after being completed in one place. The birth and activities begin somewhere else, sometimes a little different because of differences in details and sometimes exactly the same because of sameness of the details. One form becomes a different seat of action by manifesting separately. This is illustrated when Kṛṣṇa expanded into many forms in Dvārakā.

*citraṁ bataitad ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak*  
*gṛheṣu dvy-aṣṭa-sāhasraṁ striya eka udāvahat*

**It is quite amazing that in a single body Lord Kṛṣṇa simultaneously married sixteen thousand women, each in a separate palace. SB 10.69.2**

Because of doing different actions in each form, the Lord identifies himself differently in the many expanded forms in which he performs those actions. Because of this, awareness of *rasa* arising from the sequence of pastimes manifests in each palace in Dvārakā.

“Why do you say that the birth and activities continue to exist? Because the birth and activities begin separately in different universes, they become new birth and activities.” It must be said that there is oneness of the actions of the same form which appears at different times. Similarly, one can say the word “cow” twice, but that does not mean there are two words to indicate a cow: *dvir-go-śabdobhayam uccarito na tu dvau go-śabdāu*. (This is an example from Śāṅkāra’s *Śārīraka-bhāṣya*) Similarly, one can light the fire in the hearth twice, but there is only one fire. Thus the Lord’s birth and activities have an eternal nature, and thus the meditation on pastimes that Kṛṣṇa previously performed, a meditation which is prescribed in the scriptures, is proper (since the pastimes are actually eternal, not destroyed).

In Madhva’s commentary it is said *paramātma-sambandhitvena nityatvāt trivikramatvādiṣv apy upasaṁhāryatvaṁ yujyate:*  the oneness of all forms like Vāmana is possible because they are actually eternal in relationship with Paramātmā.  *Śruti* agrees with this. *Yad gataṁ bhavac ca bhaviṣyac ca*: the Lord exists in the past, present and future. (*Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad* 3.8) The oneness of the Lord (in his various forms spread over time) is recommended in performing worship. Because of the unrefined nature of Kṛṣṇa’s birth (in a prison), it becomes astonishing. However this is only a likeness to a material birth. In some aspects it does not resemble material birth at all. *Ajāyamānā bahudhā vijāyate*: the Lord, though unborn, is born in many forms. (*Mahā-nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad*)

Though Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, the king of pastimes, is served by his inconceivable *mahā-yoga-śaki* for creating birth and other pastimes, which is most skilful at supplying all ingredients necessary for the various pastimes, it would seem that after destruction of all the universes, pastimes like the bewilderment of Brahmā in which his power of displaying millions of universes was shown, could not take place.

But some authorities explain how it is possible that the pastimes continue even after final devastation of the universes. It is said in Nārada*-pañcarātra asyā āvarikā śaktir mahā-māyākhileśvarī:* the covering potency belonging to *yoga-māyā* is the controller of all material *māyā.*  Thus it is understood that material *māyā* is but a portion of *yoga-māyā.*  This *māyā* has two varieties: one which creates the material universe and another for assisting Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. The products of the first type are temporary, since at the time of final destruction all material objects disappear. The products of the second type *(yoga-māyā*) exist prior to the creation, for at the time of final devastation, this *māyā* supplies the existence of an illusory universe filled with ingredients for Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, with an illusory Kaṁsa and six aborted children. In this way (even when no universe is present), the birth pastime, the battle between the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, the stealing of the *pārijāta* tree, the kidnapping of Rukmiṇī, Kṛṣṇa’s going to Sutala and other lower planets to retrieve the sons of his *guru*, maintain their eternal nature.

Moreover the eternal nature of the pastimes is shown in the following verse:

*ayati jana-nivāso devakī-janma-vādo*  
*yadu-vara-pariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam*  
*sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ su-smita-śrī-mukhena*  
*vraja-pura-vanitānāṁ vardhayan kāma-devam*

**Lord Kṛṣṇa lives eternally among the cowherd men and the Yādavas, and is conclusively both the son of Devakī and Yaśodā. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty and the cowherd men, and with his mighty arms he kills everything inauspicious, in Vraja, Mathurā and Dvārakā. By his presence he destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities, moving and inert, and the suffering of separation of the inhabitants of Vraja and Dvārakā. His blissful smiling face always increases the desires of the** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana and women of Mathurā and Dvārakā. He remains eternally in this situation. SB 10.90.48**

By the strength of his arms (*dorbhiḥ*), by Arjuna and others, he continually destroys *adharma.* This statement shows that even the pastimes of killing the demons, which takes place in the manifested pastimes on earth, continue eternally (even after final destruction, in the illusory universe created by *māyā*).

In the manifested pastimes, the formal wedding between Kṛṣṇa and the *gopīs* with *brāhmaṇas* and fire as the witness is nowhere found by anyone in the ancient scriptures. And even if it is seen in the scriptures, is it approved by Śukadeva? King Parīkṣit asks:

*sa kathaṁ dharma-setūnāṁ vaktā kartābhirakṣitā*  
*pratīpam ācarad Brahman para-dārābhimarśanam*

**He is the original speaker, follower and guardian of moral laws. How, then, could he have violated them by touching other men’s wives?**

*āpta-kāmo yadu-patiḥ kṛtavān vai jugupsitam*  
*kim-abhiprāya etan naḥ śaṁśayaṁ chindhi su-vrata*

**O faithful upholder of vows, please destroy our doubt by explaining to us what purpose the self-satisfied Lord of the Yadus had in mind when he behaved so contemptibly. SB 10.33.27-28**

Śukadeva did not resolve the sin by saying “O King! Do not worry! At one time, they married Kṛṣṇa. Therefore they were not the wives of other men. He had *svakīya* relationships.” Instead he admitted the apparently sinful actions. His opinion should not disrespected.

*dharma-vyatikramo dṛṣṭa īśvarāṇāṁ ca sāhasam*  
*tejīyasāṁ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā*

**The status of powerful controllers is not harmed by any apparently audacious transgression of morality we may see in them, for they are just like fire, which devours everything fed into it and remains unpolluted. SB 10.33.29**

*kuśalācaritenaiṣām iha svārtho na vidyate*  
*viparyayeṇa vānartho nirahaṅkāriṇāṁ prabho*

**O master, when these great persons who are free from false ego act piously in this world, they have no selfish motives to fulfill, and even when they act in apparent contradiction to the laws of piety, they are not subject to sinful reactions. SB 10.33.32**

The words of the sages are respected by the wise, in order to explain the distasteful pastimes such as Kṛṣṇa dropping his bow and Vasudeva getting killed.

Those who maintain that Kṛṣṇa married the *gopīs* emphasize the word *patiḥ* (husband) in the phrase *aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnāṁ patir eva vā nanda-nandana*. (*Gautamīya-tantra*) However, words like *pat*i do not only mean a person who gets married according to the *rasa* scriptures*.* For instance, one sees the word *pati* used in describing *parakīya* relationships of a man with the *svādhīna-pātikā* and the *svādhīna-bhartṛkā* woman.

Another explanation can be given. The phrase *aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnam* can mean *gopīs* who attained perfection after many births, not one birth. It can also refer to eternally perfect *gopī*s who appeared whenever Kṛṣṇa appeared in this world. Thus the phrase has two meanings. Kṛṣṇa is the husband of some *sādhana-siddha gopīs* and he is the *upapati* of all the others. Thus the word *pati* has two meanings. Including both meanings is accepting both points of view. Similarly since the Vedas and Upavedas say that all *devatās* are to be respected, one may simply say “I worship all the *devatās”*. (This includes male and female forms.)

However, it is not possible to say that Kṛṣṇa was the husband of all of the *gopīs*, for the *Bhāgavatam* says *para-dārābhimarśana*: he touched the wives of others (SB 10.33.27) The word *eva* in the phrase *aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnāṁ patir eva vā nanda-nandana* also indicates that he was the *pati* in the sense of being *upapati* since the *gopīs* had no relationship with their husbands in their houses. Otherwise the word *eva* would have no meaning in the phrase. It would have no function of emphasizing anything. It will be said later *na jātu vraja-devīnāṁ patibhiḥ saha saṅgamaḥ*: the *gopīs* had no intimate relationship with their husbands.

It is not possible to explain the words *patir eva* to mean that Kṛṣṇa was an *upapati* by illusion only in the pastimes on earth, for Jīva Gosvāmī himself has established that all of the pastimes that take place on earth are eternal. The words *kṛṣṇa-vadhvaḥ* (SB 10.33.7) mean simply that the *gopīs* were the women of Kṛṣṇa. *Nānārtha-varga* says that *vadhū* means a wife, a daughter-in-law, and a woman. In the Third Canto the word *vadhūḥ* in the phrase *sā tvāṁ brahman nṛpa-vadhūḥ kāmam āśu bhajiṣyati* (SB 3.21.28) simply indicates the unmarried daughter of the king. Bhīṣma says *prakṛtim agan kila yasya gopa-vadhvaḥ*: the cowherd women imitated the characteristic movements of the Lord after his disappearance from the *rāsa* dance. (SB 1.9.40)

Also, the word *svāmī* in the phrase *sa hi vo svāmī bhavati (*he is your master) from *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* does not mean husband. According to Pāṇini, *svāmī* means controller. There is a famous saying “He who becomes one’s *svāmī* becomes one’s enjoyer or lover.” Therefore Kṛṣṇa was not the husband of those women.

Rūpa Gosvāmī says *Lalita-mādhava* (1.22):

*naṭatā kirāta-rājaṁ nihatya raṅga-sthale kalā-nidhinā*  
*samaye tena vidheyaṁ guṇavati tārā-kara-grahaṇam \|\|*

**While dancing on the stage after having killed the ruler of uncivilized men, Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa, master of all arts, will at the proper time accept the hand of Rādhā, who is qualified with all transcendental attributes.**

This states that Kṛṣṇa married Rādhā. When Kaṁsa was in Dvārakā, he married Rādhā who had assumed the secondary form of Satyabhāmā. It does not mean that Kṛṣṇa married Rādhā in Vraja. One cannot say that Rādhā’s marriage with Kṛṣṇa was possible in Vraja out of love by using the argument that their marriage is pointed out in one place in scripture and not refuted elsewhere, for in *Lalita-mādhava* (10.38) it is said at the conclusion:

*yā te līlā-rasa-parimalodgāri-vanyāparītā*  
*dhanyā kṣauṇī vilasati vṛtā māthurī mādhurībhiḥ \|*  
*tatrāsmābhiś caṭula-paśupī-bhāva-mugdhāntarābhiḥ*  
*saṁvītas tvaṁ kalaya vadanollāsi-veṇur vihāram \|\|*

**This fortunate earth, not far from Mathurā, spread with the forests giving the fragrance of your rāsa pastimes is surrounded by sweetness of trees, birds and animals. You, with flute in your mouth, should play here, surrounded by us foolish, unsteady women, identifying ourselves as wives of cowherd men.**

This is a prayer of Rādhā. You are surrounded by us women whose *antaḥkaraṇas (antarābhiḥ*) have no sense of discrimination (*mugdha*) because of having emotions of unsteady cowherd women (*caṭula-paśupī-bhāva*). By describing the women as unsteady, Rūpa Gosvāmī indicates the love of an *upapati.*  In common language mention of an unsteady woman indicates a *parakīya* relationship. Thus he indicates that their *parakīya-bhāva* is accepted. Thus one should not explain that *parakīya* is undesirable in Vraja and that Kṛṣṇa married Rādhā.

Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭta in the third part of *Rasa-taraṅginī*, concerning the *ālambana*, says that Rādhā had a *parakīya* relationship with Kṛṣṇa.

*śānte brāhmaṇa eva syāt prīte dāsaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*preyasi syuḥ sakhāyo hi yaśodā vatsale smṛtā \|\|*  
*madhure rādhikā jñeyā hāsye syān madhumaṅgalaḥ \|*  
*sakhī-yūtho’dbhute jñeyo vīre cāraṇa-govṛṣāḥ \|\|*  
*karuṇe vatsa-vṛkṣādir jaṭilādyās tu raudrake \|*  
*govardhano’bhimanyuś ca bhayānaka udāhṛtau \|\|*  
*tapasvinyādayo hy atra bībhatse parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vrajasthā niyatā jñeyā ālambana-vibhāvakāḥ \|\|*

**The** ***brāhmaṇa*** **is the** ***ālambana*** **in** ***śānta-rasa.*** **The servant is in** ***prêta*** **or** ***dāsya rasa*****. The friends are in** ***sakhya rasa*****. Yaśodā is in** ***vatsalya-rasa.*** **Rādhā is in** ***madhura-rasa*****. Madhumaṅgala is in** ***hāsya-rasa.*** **The groups of** ***sakhīs*** **produce** ***adbhuta-rasa*****. The bulls produce** ***vīra-rasa.*** **The calves and trees produce** ***karuṇa-rasa.*** **Jaṭilā and others produce** ***raudra-rasa.*** **Govardhana and Abhimanyu produce** ***bhāyanaka-rasa.*** **The austere women produce** ***bībhatsa-rasa*****. Persons fixed in Vraja are known as the** ***ālambana*** **in** ***vibhāva*****.**

Elsewhere he says:

*na rādhā-bhartāraṁ kvacid api ca dṛgbhir gṛha-gataṁ*  
*samadrākṣīn nityaṁ tava sarasa-mūrtiṁ vilikhati \|*  
*tavāpy etad-vakṣo vahati rucirāṁ tat-pratikṛtiṁ*  
*tataḥ kṛṣṇa premṇāham api vidadhe dautyam akhilam \|\|*

**He never looked upon the husband of Rādhā in the house by his glances. He constantly touches your beautiful form. His chest carries your attractive likeness. Out of love for Kṛṣṇa, I perform all services as a messenger.**

In *Lalita-mādhava* it is said *goaḍḍhaṇādi-goehiṁ candāalī-pahudīṇaṁ ubbāho bi māāe ṇibbāhido:* did the *māyā* potency cause the marriage of Govardhana and the other *gopas* with Candrāvalī and the other *gopīs*? I will now explain this statement. All *jīvas* in this world, fallen in the midst of *māyā,* identify with the body. One develops possessiveness of material husband and sons. One thinks “This is my husband. This is my son.” This relationship is produced by *māyā.* The cowherds, *gopīs,* animals, and birds living in Vraja, assistants in Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, are all beyond *māyā.* Their identity with their bodies and identity as mothers and fathers is not created by *māyā.* Those identities are filled with eternity, knowledge and bliss. Just as Nanda and Yaśodā identify themselves as the father and mother of Kṛṣṇa, Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā identify themselves as father and mother of Rādhā. This identity is purely spiritual.

Abhimanyu identifying himself as a husband however is not spiritual. It is *māyā.* It is impossible that there could be eternal hatred in spiritual forms of Abhimanyu and other husbands towards the spiritual forms of Rādhā and other *gopīs*. Thus this identity as a husband is *māyā,* a secondary expansion of *yoga-māyā*, and established by her arrangement. This identity as a husband of a material woman is temporary since it is material.

Though the *gopīs* thinking they are married to husbands is also created by *māyā,* it is eternal, because this exists in the center of arrangement for the Lord’s pastimes and because this illusion is supported and encouraged by *yogamāyā*. This is the difference. The bewilderment of the *gopīs* is created by *yoga-māyā,* not by material *māyā,* since it is beyond the *guṇas.* Kṛṣṇa’s thinking that the *gopīs* are his lovers and the *gopīs’* thinking that Kṛṣṇa is their lover are filled with eternity, knowledge and bliss. The *gopīs* thinking they are wives of certain husbands is certainly illusory, but produces their dependence on Kṛṣṇa. This is the version accepted by the wise.

Some commentators say the word *māyā* in the statement from *Lalita-mādhava* means *yoga-māyā.* According to them, the identity of men being married to the *gopīs* is spiritual. By *yogamāya,* skilful at doing the impossible, animosity arises in the husbands.

Other persons do not accept that Rādhā was married to someone else, and claim she was unmarried. But following that idea, she is then inferior to all the other *gopīs* rather than superior to them. The Lord finds the *gopīs* superior to the queens of Dvārakā because of the excellence of their *prema*. Recognizing their superiority, the Lord and Uddhava have also pointed out the reason for this: they have trespassed normal rules of conduct by transgressing their marriages. The Lord has said:

*evaṁ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda*  
*svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye ’balāḥ*  
*mayāparokṣaṁ bhajatā tirohitaṁ*  
*māsūyituṁ mārhatha tat priyaṁ priyāḥ*

**My dear girls, understanding that simply for my sake you had rejected the authority of worldly opinion, of the Vedas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to me. Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. Therefore, my beloved** ***gopīs,*** **please do not harbor any bad feelings toward me, your beloved. SB 10.32.21**

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*  
*yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ*  
*saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā*

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. SB 10.32.22**

Uddhava said:

*āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ*  
*vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām*  
*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

If Rādhā was not married to someone else, prayers to have Kṛṣṇa as her husband would not be trespassing public opinion or the Vedas. If that is so, then her *prema* is not the subject of the words of Kṛṣṇa and Uddhava quoted above. She would be inferior to other *gopīs.* This idea is not approved by my master.

*“*Rādhā is the *hlādinī-śakti* arising from Kṛṣṇa’s *svarūpa.* In reality the *parakīya* condition cannot take place since she eternally belongs to Kṛṣṇa.” That is true. Therefore Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are worshipped together and have pastimes together. They are not devoid of pastimes with each other. Though Śukadeva, Parāśara, Vyāsadeva and others have spoken about the pastimes, the words of Śukadeva are most dear to us. According to him, she is the topmost of all *gopīs*, and has *parakīya-bhāva*, since it is seen in her and the other *gopīs.*

“In married life there is no suffering caused by infamy and no pain arising from opposition from sisters-in-law and mothers-in-law. Such suffering is not seen in Rukmiṇī and other queens. One sees such suffering in the *gopīs.* In that aspect, they have more suffering and thus inferior to Rukmiṇī and others.”

That is not so. Whatever amount of suffering is seen in the *gopīs* possessing *rāga, anurāga* and *mahābhāva* is actually bliss of the same amount. It will be said:

*duḥkham apy adhikaṁ citte sukhatvenaiva rajyate \|*  
*yatas tu praṇayotkarṣāt sa rāga iti kīrtyate \|\|*

**When the intensity of love makes intense suffering shines as happiness in the heart, it is called** ***rāga*****.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.126**

Jīva Gosvāmī speaks concerning the characteristics of *mahābhāva.* The highest amount of suffering from the *gopīs,* most obedient to the rules, is caused by abandonment by their families and respectable society. Fire and death do not cause such suffering for them. Though there appears to be suffering because of this rejection, the relationship with Kṛṣṇa produces happiness. This is the highest condition of *rāga. Rāga* takes shelter of the *gopīs*, and then becomes *anurāga*. This is seen in the *gopīs* from the beginning. It is not possible to occur in the queens of Dvārakā. Indicating the *gopīs*, Uddhava in astonishment said *yā dustyajam ārya-pathaṁ svajanaṁ ca hitvā*: these ladies of Vraja abandoned their families and their advanced religious principles, even though to do so is very difficult. (SB 10.47.61) Taking shelter of the *gopīs*, *anurāga* manifests and then becomes *mahābhāva*. By this explanation it is understood that when *rāga* reaches its highest condition, *mahābhāva* arises. The appearance of *mahābhāva* indicates the highest condition of *rāga.* When that highest condition of *rāga* occurs, the relationship with Kṛṣṇa which causes the *gopīs* to be rejected by family and respectable society, which causes the greatest suffering, produces happiness. No other condition does so. If such rejection by family does not occur in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes in relation to Kṛṣṇa, then the highest condition of *rāga* will also not occur. If that highest condition does not appear, then *mahābhāva* will not appear in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes. This is not an acceptable conclusion.

Therefore in both manifest and unmanifest pastimes Kṛṣṇa acts as an *upapati*, which causes rejection by family and society. This is Jīva Gosvāmī’s personal conclusion. That only married relationships occur in the unmanifested pastimes is the opinion of others. Therefore most merciful Jīva Gosvāmī has properly stated:

*svecchayā likhitaṁ kiṁcit kiṁcid atra parecchayā \|*  
*yat pūrvāpara-sambaddhaṁ tat pūrvam aparaṁ param \|\|*

**Some portions I have written as my own opinions, and some portions are the opinions of others. What is consistent is my view and what is not consistent is the view of others.**

One should not worry that the concept of the *upapati* is rejected by the author of *Sāhitya-darpaṇa*. The author of *Nāṭikā-candikā* does not accept the opinions of *Sāhitya-darpaṇa*:

*nātīva-saṅgatatvād bharata-muner mata-virodhāc ca \|*  
*sāhitya-darpaṇīyā na gṛhītā prakriyā prāyaḥ \|\|*

**The principles mentioned in** ***Sāhitya-darpaṇa*** **have not been generally accepted in this work, since those opinions contradict Bharata Muni and are not generally consistent.**

If it is established that Kṛṣṇa married the *gopīs* with the witness of *guru, brāhmaṇas* and fire, then the whole o*f Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* from the very beginning would be contradicted. If this were so, the *gopīs* who have an awareness of being married to other men (*patnī-bhāvābhimānātmā* 14.48) and have a natural affection which overcomes the heart and makes them indifferent to this world and the next (*rāgeṇaivārpitātmāno loka-yugmānapekṣitāḥ* 3.17) would become inferior to other women and their basic *sthāyī-bhāva* would be unsteady. What would be the use of statements compiled with great effort like *tatraiva paramotkarṣaḥ śṛṅgārasya pratiṣṭhitaḥ*: the excellence of conjugal love is established (1.19)? This commentary has been written in order to give a quick grasp of the characteristics of conjugal love and the examples given in the text. If this commentary does not portray the inner convictions of the author then it can be said to be deceptive cheating of the greatest devotee friends, who have splendid, unlimited mercy. But enough of these manifestations of excessive deliberation!

*tiryag-yonim avāpa karma-vaśato viṣṇuḥ sa cety uktimac*  
*chāstraṁ gāruḍam atyasahyam api na kasyāpi tat-saṁmatam \|*  
*vyāso bhāgavatasya tasya ca bhavet kartā tad apy ādarād*  
*ārādhyaḥ sa gatiś ca tatra nitarām āgo’sti keṣām api \|\|*

**The statement in the** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa*** **that even Viṣṇu takes birth as an animal by the law of** ***karma*** **is intolerable and not accepted by anyone. Vyāsa, the writer of the** ***Bhāgavatam*** **and the** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa,*** **and his intention, should be worshipped with great respect*****.*** **However, some people commit repeated offense by misunderstanding the intent. It is said in** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa*****:**

*brahmā yena kulālavan niyamito brahmāṇḍa-bhāṇḍodare*  
*viṣṇur yena daśāvatāra-grahaṇe kṣipto mahā-saṅkaṭe \|*  
*rudro yena kapāla-pāṇi-puṭake bhikṣāṭanaṁ kāritaḥ*  
*sūryo bhrāmyati nityam eva gagane tasmai namaḥ karmaṇe \|\|*

**I offer respects to the law of** ***karma,*** **by whom Brahmā, like a potter, is regulated within the universe to carry out creation, by whom Viṣṇu is placed into the forms of ten** ***avatāras,*** **full of great danger, by whom Śiva is made to live by begging, using a skull as his bowl, and by whom the sun travels in the sky continually.** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa*** **1.113.15**

This has been quoted in *Bhagavat-sandarbha*. This verse is also found in *Nīti-śakatam* of Bhartṛhari to illustrate *karm*a. It is quoted in the Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha, to illustrate that sometimes inaccurate statements are made to show the force of karma or other principles. Viṣṇu is not under control of *karma*. Similarly Jīva Gosvāmī in his commentary may make statements whose intentions may be misunderstood.9

### Text 22

***tatha ca prāñcaḥ****—*  
***caigara-rasa-sarvasvaa cikhi-piccha-vibhunaeam \|***  
***aigekata-narakaram acraye bhuvanacrayam \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An ancient authority: I take shelter of the totality of** ***rasas,*** **conjugal** ***rasa,*** **which has accepted a human form, which is the object of bliss for the three worlds, and which is decorated with a peacock feather. (*****Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta*** **93)**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author confirms his statement that the purpose of the appearance of Kṛṣṇa was to give a taste of the essence of *rasa* by citing the words of Bilvamaṅgala, a great devotee of Kṛṣṇa from previous times. Though Kṛṣṇa is the shelter of the universe he has taken as his true form (*aṅgīkṛta*) a human form, not a godly form. Or *aigekata-narakaram* can mean that he has accepted a “human” birth when he comes as *avatāra.* He has a peacock feather ornament, suitable for his pastimes as a cowherd. He is the complete shelter (*sarvasvam*) of *śṛṅgāra-rasa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He confirms the purpose mentioned in the previous verse by quoting the words of a previous great devotee with high realization, Bilvamaṅgala. A unique feature of his enjoying the *gopīs* is his peacock feather ornament. His whole property (*sarvasvam*) is *śṛṅgāra-rasa*. Without it, he is poverty-stricken. Or he is the totality of *śṛṅgāra-rasa.* Without him, *śṛṅgāra-rasa* has no meaning. In *śṛṅgāra-rasa*, the type with the *upapati* is the best. How can Bilvamaṅgala take shelter of him if Kṛṣṇa as *upapati* is disrespectable (*laghutvam*)? Or if he is despicable as the *upapati,* how can he be the totality of *śṛṅgāra-rasa*? The original form (*aṅgī*) is a human. This formation is like *śuklīkṛta haṁsaḥ*: a swan made white. The other forms like Matsya, Kūrma, and the godly form in Vaikuṇṭha are his *aṅgas.* Because he is most attractive to the three worlds, the worlds act as the *āśraya* or experiencer of his beauty.

### Text 23-24

***anukula-dakniea-caoha dhanoac ceti dvayor athocyante \|***  
***pratyekaa catvaro bheda yuktibhir ame vattya \|\|23\|\|***  
***caohya-dharnoye paraa naoya-prokte upapater ubhe \|***  
***kanee tu sarvaa nayuktaa tat-tad-bhavasya sambhavat \|\|24\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said by deduction from circumstance that there are fout types of** ***pati*** **and** ***upati*** **according to their behaviour: the favorable, the compliant, the deceitful and the impudent. Each of these four types has four types. Deceitful and impudent forms are found only in the** ***upapati*** **in dramatic literature. However, this does not apply to Kṛṣṇa, because they manifest when he is both** ***pati*** **and** ***upapati.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having expressed his desire, the author now describes the form of Kṛṣna, the *ālamabana*. According to the pastime he takes on particular qualities. The *pati* and *upapati* have these qualities, revealed by action (*vṛtty*ā). This is further explained in verse 24. Even though deceit and impudence do not become the main *rasa* of the *upapati (aṅgini-rasa),* they can be described in a secondary role. They are all present in Kṛṣṇa because he has special *prema* for manifesting pastimes as *p*ati and *upapati (tat-tad-bhāvasya).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The four qualiteis manifest in both the *pati* and *upapati. Vṛttyā* means “by action.” Kṛṣṇa can manifest deceit and impudence both as *pati* and *upapati (tat-tat-bhāvasya).* Or Kṛṣṇa can manifests deceit and impudence in both forms..

### Text 25-26

***tatranukulau—***  
***atiraktataya naryaa tyaktanya-lalana-spahau \|***  
***setayaa ramavat so’yam anukulau prakertitau \|\|25\|\|***  
***radhayam eva kaneasya suprasiddhanukulata \|***  
***tad-aloke kadapy asya nanya-saigau smatia vrajet \|\|26 \|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ānukula*** **is described: He who gives up desire for other women with intense attachment for one woman, like Rāma for Sītā, is called the anukula or well-disposed lover. Kṛṣṇa’s is famous for his** ***anukūla*** **attachment to Rādhā. Whenever he sees her, he forgets other women.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When Kṛṣṇa sees Rādhā, he forgets other women. The phrases “when he sees her” is representative only. It also refers to hearing about or remembering her, One should not think that the example of Rāma’s attachment to Sītā is not appropiate because of lack of complete similarity. Because the desire for other women is improper, since he has a vow of having only one wife, accepting only one wife with complete dedication is not difficult for Rāma. However, in the presence of many other women and in the absence of Rādhā, it is difficult for Kṛṣṇa to forget the other women filled with *prema.* But still he forgets others and thinkgs of Rādhā. Therefore on seeing or thinking of Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa becomes the ideal example of the *ānukūla* hero. That is shown here. Thus when Kṛṣṇa took Rādhā and disappeared during the *rāsa-līlā,* he did not meet the other gopīs, though they were suffering. *Gīta-govinda* (3.1) says *radham adaya hadaye tatyaja vraja-sundareu*: taking Rādhā in his heart, Kṛṣṇa gave up the other women of Vraja.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because of being intensely attrached to one woman, he gives up desire for other women. Because the verse says that desire disappears only at that time and does not say that desire for other women is absent all the time, the theory that Kṛṣṇa should not have attraction to no other women is defeated.

The phrase “when Kṛṣṇa sees Rādhā” also means when he hears or remembers her. It is easy for Rāma to be *ānukūla* to Sīta since he took a vow of having only one wife. Though it is difficult for Kṛṣṇa to be *anukūla* to Rādhā, since he has many women, because of the most astonishing level of prema for her, he forgets all other women who have prema for him. The superiority of Kṛṣṇa’s *ānukūla* sentiments based on his prema to those of Rāma is indicated here. When he takes Rādhā and disappears during the *rāsa-līlā*, though the other *gopīs* were suffering, he did not meet with them. *Gīta-govinda* (3.1) says *radham adaya hadaye tatyaja vraja-sundareu*: taking Rādhā in his heart, Kṛṣṇa gave up the other women of Vraja.

### Text 27

***yathā--***  
***vaidagdhe-nikuramba-cumbita-dhiyau saundarya-sarojjvalau***  
***kaminyau kati nadya vallava-pater devyanti gonohantare \|***  
***radhe pueyavate-cikha-maeir asi knamodari tvaa vina***  
***preikhante na parasu yan madhuripor danoatra danoir maya \|\|27 \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O Rādhā! So many women whose minds are filled with playfulness, whose bodies shine with the essence of beauty, do not play in the courtyard of Nanda at this time. You are the crest jewel of pious women. O slender-waisted girl! I have never seen the glances of Kṛṣṇa fall upon other women when he is separated from you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

After giving the definition the author praises this type of hero. Vṛndā, the controller over the forests for pastimes, speaks this verse. In separation from you (*tvām vinā*), I have never seen his glances move significantly *(preṅkhantī*) to other women.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks this verse. *Tvām vinā* means “in separation from you.” When he remembers you, he thinks of no one else. This is the example of the previous verse which explained that on seeing, hearing or thinking of Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa forgets other *gopīs. Preṅkhantī* means moving.

### Text 28

***dherodattanukulo,*** *yatha—*  
*kuvalaya-dacau saiketa-stha dag-aicala-kaucalair*  
*manasija-kala-naoe-prastavanam abhitanvatam \|*  
*na kila ghaoate radha-raiga-prasaiga-vidhayita*  
*vrata-vilasite caithilyasya cchaoapy agha-vidvinau \|\|28\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***dhīrodatta ānukūla:*** **O lotus-eyed women waiting in the your bowers! By giving signals with skilful glances, you should display skilful introductory dances of love! But Kṛṣṇa does not become slack in executing his vow to make Rādhā become attached to Cupid’s dances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *dhīrodātta* and other type were explained in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindu*. Now according to those descriptions, examples are given of those types mixed with the *ānukūla* and other heroes. This verse is spokjen by Vṛndā to a friend of Rādhā. On the path that Kṛṣṇa takes to meet Rādha, there are many *gopīs* waiting in bowers, giving signals to Kṛṣṇa. *Nāṭī* refers to a type of *drama. Prastāvana* means the introduction to a drama, in which the contents of the drama are summarized. But Kṛṣṇa does not become affected by the women. This illustsrates his inscrutiability. One can only assume what he is thinking. He then lets forth customary praise using conciliating words which hide the particular actions he must do. But he does not do this with rough actions. This shows his modesty. Though they obstruct him with many tricks, he does not become angry at them. This shows his tolerance. He thinks, “they should not become unhappy.” This reveals his compassion. By the clarity of his words, he shows his determined vow. Because of showing modesty, his shows his nature of not boasting. Finally, from attaining his most dear Rādhā he becomes intensely proud. Immediately going to face obstancles shows his strength. In this way his *dhīrodātta* nature comes clear. His *ānukūla* nature is clear from his remembrance of Rādhaā while giving up all tohers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Dhīrodātta and others are described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*. Now he gives examples of the anukūla and others mixed with the dhīrodātta and other types.

*gambhīro vinayī kṣantā karuṇaḥ sudṛḍha-vrataḥ \|*  
*akatthano gūḍha-garvo dhīrodāttaḥ su-sattva-bhṛt \|\|*

**The person who is inscrutable, modest, tolerant, merciful, determined in vows, who obscures others’ pride, is not boastful, and is strong, is called** ***dhīrodātta.*** **BRS 2.1.226**

The *ānukūla* mixed with the *dhīrodātta* is now described. Lalitā speaks words of consolation to Citrā one seeing Kṛṣṇa at some distance remembering Rādhā. *Naṭ*i refers to a drama. *Prastāvanā* is the introductory part of a drama in which the contents of the drama are summarized. “You *gopīs* should engage in introductions while Kṛṣṇa is looking (*abhi*).” The women remain in the bowers near the path that Kṛṣṇa takes to meet Rādhā while making signals to him.

*Prastāvanām* comes from “making.” The phrase can also mean “the playful dance of Cupid prepared by me.” Kṛṣṇa thinks, “Let them display this dance I have prepared.” Having informed each of them about that, let them think that they will dance and make me dance. This shows his inscrutability because they cannot understand his mind even though they are very clever.

“I will dance with you in the dancing arena but now it is necessary to collect the cows over there. Please permit me to go for a moment.” In this way he speaks to each of the *gopīs* with his glances. This shows his modesty.

Though they obstruct him by many devious means, he does not become angry. This shows his tolerance. Because he understands their intolerable pain in separation from him, he is compassionate.

He does not show any slackness in performing (*vilasite*) his vow to produce strong attachment (*prasaṅga*) in Rādhā for attractive dances of Cupid (*raṅga*), and attachment for performing unconventional dances. This shows his strong vows. “O Rādhā! I am most clever at cheating all the *gopīs.* I love only you.” He never boasts in this way since he is controlled by her love. This shows his lack of boasting. “There is no person except me praiseworthy for principles of *dharma*, though I break the vows of the chaste women and get pleasure from enjoying them.” This shows his obscuring other’s pride. He is the killer of Agha. This shows his strength. Kṛṣṇa’s *ānukūla* nature is displayed in all these aspects.

### Text 29

***dheralalitanukulo, yatha—***  
***gahanad anuragatau pitabhyam***  
***apaneta-vyavahara-katya-bharau \|***  
***viharan saha radhaya murarir***  
***yamuna-kula-vanany alaacakara \|\|29\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***dhīralalitānukūla*** **is given: Because of his unfathomable attachment, his parents avoid giving him responsibilities. Playing with Rādhā incessantly, Kṛṣṇa ornaments the forests on the bank of the Yamunā River.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nandīmukhī. *Gananāt* means “attraction that must be deeply pondered.” It is used in a sentence such as “The goal of action is hard to understand (*gahan*a).” *Viśva-prakāśa* says *gahana* means a hole, sorrow, a forest or confusion. Kṛṣṇa has decorated the forests on the river bank. Because the beauty of the foerst in his prsence surpasses its previous beauty, it is said he has ornamented the forest. This shows that Kṛṣṇa is clever and endowed with fresh youth. In comparison to the previous extraordinary beauty of the place, it has become more beautiful by his youthful presence. He plays with Rādhā. This includes the *rasa* of joking. This shows his skill at joking. His parents do not give him responsibilities. This shows his care free nature. He is completely independent and playful. When engaged by his parents and others in herding cows, it should be understood to be part of his carefree activities. He does not take other responsibilities.

It is said *vraje vikreoator evaa gopala-cchadma-mayaya:* with the pretense of herding cows, the two play in Vraja. By *māyā,* the deceiving energy, the pretense of herding cows, the two play in Vraja. Playing is the intention, and herding cows is something else. He plays with Rādhā. This means that he is constantly playing. This indicates that he is controlled by Rādhā. Thus the qualities of the *dhīra-lalita* have been shown. Because he is constantly playing with her, he is completely absorbed in her. This is the quality of the *anukūla* hero. In the definition of *dhīra-lalita* the word *prāyaḥ* is used. He is generally (*prāyaḥ*) controlled by his lover. This is because he does not externally show this.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nandīmukhī. Because of attraction that cannot be explained (*gahanāt*), he is given no responsibilities.

*vidagdho nava-tāruṇyaḥ parihāsa-viśāradaḥ \|*  
*niścinto dhīra-lalitaḥ syāt prāyaḥ preyasī-vaśaḥ \|\|*

**He is called** ***dhīra-lalita*** **who is clever, endowed with fresh youth (end of** ***kaiśora*** **period), skilful at joking and free of worries. He is controlled by his dear devotees. BRS 2.1.230**

Being given no responsibilities shows his care free nature. The word *viharan* in the *parasmaipada* form indicates that he is controlled by Rādhā, since he plays to give pleasure to her. In the present tense, it indicates continuous action of playing, giving up all other *gopīs.* This shows his nature as *ānukūla.* He decorates many forests. Giving up one forest, disappearing in another forest, he stays there. She looks for him and then finds him. She jokes with him. Then they go to another forest. Revealing playful acts shows his joking nature. The word *alam* in the verb *alamcakāra* means competent. This indicates his cleverness. His new youth is indicated by the whole verse, since by clever playing he produces ever fresh results.

### Text 30

***dheracantanukulo.*** *yatha—*  
***bradhnopasti-vidhau tava praeayitapureea vecaa gate***  
***knma-devasya kathaa gueo’py agharipau drag adya saacakrame***  
***buddhiu pacya viveka-kaucalavate danoiu knamodgariee***  
***vag etasya magakni ruoha-vinaya murtic ca dherojjvala \|\|30\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***dhīraśāntānukūla*** **is given: O doe-eyed Rādhā! Coming in the guise of a priest worshipping the sun because of great love for you, how has the enemy of Agha today suddenly attained the qualities of a** ***brāhmaṇa*****? See! His intelligence is skilled in discrimination. His glance emits tolerance. His voice is filled with modesty. His form is shining with peacefulness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dhīraśāntānukūla* is made clear in this verse. *Vradhna* means the sun. Rādhā engages in worshipping the sun. Candrāvaī represents worship of the moon. This is understood from tradition. It will be understood later in the text also.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*śama-prakṛtikaḥ kleśa-sahanaś ca vivecakaḥ \|*  
*vinayādi-guṇopeto dhīra-śānta udīryate \|\|*

**The learned say that he who is peaceful, tolerates suffering, uses discrimination, and possesses qualities like modesty is called** ***dhīra-śānta.*** **BRS 2.1.233**

Viśākhā speaks in the ear of Rādhā while Jaṭilā is nearby. *Vradhnaḥ* means the sun.

“Since you cannot avoid the association of elders, he has assumed the cloth of a priest worshipping the sun in order to see you, while being undetected by others. He glances sweetly at you.” This is hinted This indicates his *anukūla* nature. His intelligence has become most skilful at discrimination. This shows his ability to discrminate. His glance emits tolerance. This indicates his ability to endure suffering. Giving up his fickle nature is suffering for him. He surpresses that to meet Rādhā. His words are humble. This indicates his modesty. His form radiates peacefulenss. This indicates his peaceful nature. He is the epitome of the *ātmārāma* but this is covered by his *prema* in Vraja. The phrase *śama-prakṛtikaḥ* indicates that he is by nature peaceful. How has he attained the qualities of a *brāhmaṇa*? The enemy of Agha, appears to be a *brāhmaṇa* today. Because the *rasas* occurs in a comparison ( he is like a *brāhmaṇa*), there is no contradiciton between the secondary mood of *śānta* and the primary mood of *śṛṅgāra* (which are contrary *rasas).* This is explained in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* 4.8.63.

### Text 31

***dheroddhatanukulo,*** *yatha—*  
***satyaa me parihatya tavaka-sakhea premavadataa mano***  
***nanyasmin pramadajane knaeam api svapne’pi saikalpate \|***  
***sara-grahiei gauri sad-guea-gurau mukta-vyalekodyame***  
***mudraa kia nu mayi vyanakni lalite guohabhyasuya-mayem \|\|31\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Truthfully, even in dreams, my mind, purified by her love, does not give up your friend and desire another woman for a moment. O golden Lalita! Why do you accuse me of great envy, though I am the extractor of the essence, a** ***guru*** **with good qualities, and am free from bad actions?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vyalīka* means offensive. Anger and envy are shown by asking why Lalitā is accusing him of envy. Pride and boasting are shown by describing himself as a *guru* with good qualties, free from bad acts, and extractor of the essence. Deceit is shown by words in the first line which hides his nature. Fickleness is indicated by his faltering. In this way he shows the qualities of the *dhīroddhata.* Faltering also indicates his *ānukūla* nature, for sometimes he shows perpexity in order to destroy his offensive attitude.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *dhīroddhata* is defined:

*mātsaryavān ahaṅkārī māyāvī roṣaṇaś calaḥ \|*  
*vikatthanaś ca vidvadbhir dhīroddhata udāhṛtaḥ \|\|236\|\|*

**The wise call** ***dhīroddhata*** **(haughty) the person who shows envy, pride, deceit, anger, fickleness, and boastful nature. BRS 2.1.236**

The *gopīs* on the path Kṛṣṇa takes to meet Rādhā accuse him. Kṛṣṇa pacifies them superficially with his glances. Lalitā sees this from a distance. Knowing that Kṛṣṇa is dedicated only to Rādhā, she says to him, “O cunning citizen of Vraja! After making my friend happy just now, today you have gathered after a short time women who have given up the proper path with the promise of having fun with you.” Kṛṣṇa answers Lalitā with the above verse. His nature is *ānukūl*a because his mind does not desire any other woman. He shows pride and boasting by listing his qualities of being a guru with good qualities and being the extractor of the essence. He says he is free of doing anything unpleasant to Rād

### Text 32-33

*atha dakṣiṇaḥ—*  
*yo gauravaṁ bhayaṁ prema dākṣiṇyaṁ pūrva-yoṣiti \|*  
*na muñcaty anya-citto’pi jñeyo’sau khalu dakṣinaḥ \|\|32\|\|*  
*yathā—*  
*tathyaṁ candrāvali kathayasi prekṣyate na vyalīkaṁ*  
*svapne’pyasya tvayi madhubhidaḥ prema śuddhāntarasya \|*  
*śrutvā jalpaṁ piśunamanasāṁ tadviruddhaṁ sakhīnāṁ*  
*yuktaḥ kartuṁ sakhi savinaye nātra viśrambhabhaṅgaḥ \|\|33\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The compliant lover: The** ***dakṣiṇa*** **is the person who, though having a new lover, cannot free himself from respect, fear, affection for his previous lover, caused by softness of his nature.**

**An example: O Candrāvalī! You speak the truth. Even in Kṛṣṇa’s dreams one cannot him commit offense to you, since his heart is pure because of his** ***dakṣiṇa*** **love for you. O friend! Do not break your relationship of love with Kṛṣṇa who is modest, by hearing gossip of opposing friends with treacherous minds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In discussing the *dakṣiṇa* lover, first the following should be considerd *Amara-koṣa* says that *dakṣiṇ*a means soft and generous. This is also described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu:*

*sauśīlya-saumya-carito dakṣiṇaḥ kīrtyate budhaiḥ \|\|*

**A person who is mild due to his amiable nature is called compliant by the intelligent. BRS 2.1.137**

The movements of his body etc. are said to be very soft (*saumya*), because of an amiable mentality (*sauśīlya*). Taking this into account in *mādhura-rasa,* the author describes the *dakṣiṇa* lover. He is known as *dakṣiṇa* who, though in love with someone else, does not free himself from respect, fear, love and *dakṣiṇya* (mild nature) for his previous woman. The words describe aspects of his amiable nature (*sauśīlya*). In *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindu*, after describing the general quality of *dakṣiṇya*—his amiable nature, Rūpa Gosvāmī then describes the special quality--softness (*saumya*) in his actions, which is a portion of that general quality. Respect, fear and love for the previous lover follow from *saumya*. Therefore those qualities are not the main quality *dakṣiṇyam.* There would arise lack of meaning with repetitive statements if the secondary and main quality (*saumya* and *sauśīlya*) were regarded as one in meaning in the definition. Therefore this should be meaning.

The *dakṣiṇa,* though bound to some present lover with good qualities because of his particular attachment, but cannot free himself from a previous lover to whom he had strong adoration through *prema* mixed with respect. She was not pleasurable to him by pure attraction without reverence. Thus the verse mentions he cannot give up his respect (*gauravam*) for her. He becomes fearful and unsteady of breaking his love for a woman who loves him. He cannot give his love of affection (*prema*) in which compassion is prominent, because of fear of causing her suffering. Because of that quality of affection he cannot give up his softness or *saumya* nature (*dakṣiṇyam*). This person is called *dakṣiṇa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *dakṣiṇa* cannot give up attachment to woman for whom he had great attachment, though he has a new attachment (*anya-cittaḥ*) to some other woman at a later time. This inictes his great attachment to her.

The verse given as an example is a statement by Nāndīmukhī. “You speak the truth.” However there is abuse intended. *Vyalīkam* means unworthy or offensive. The cause is purity (*dakṣiṇya*) in his love for you. The words *śuddhāntarasya* indicate the *dakṣiṇa. Savinaye* (modesty) indicates respect. The cause being humble is fear.

### Text 34-35

*yad vā---*  
*nāyikāsu āpy anekāsu tulyo dakṣiṇa ucyate \|\|34\|\|*  
*yathā daśa-rūpake—*  
*snātā tiṣṭhati kuntaleśvara-sutā vāro ‘ṅga-rāja-svasur*  
*dyūte rātrir iyaṁ jītā kamalayā devī prasādyādya ca*  
*ity antaḥ-pura-sundarīḥ prati māyā vijñāya vijñāpite*  
*devenā pratipatti-mūḍha-manasa dvitrāḥ stitham nādikāḥ \|\|35\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**There is another definition of the** ***dakṣina*****: It is said that the** ***dakṣina*** **shows equal affection to many lovers.**

**An example from** ***Dāśa-rūpaka*****: The daughter of Kuntaleśvara, having bathed, is waiting for you to come. You are the protector of the sister of the King of Aṅga. The night has been conquered by Kamalā in a dice match. Rukmiṇī must also be satisfied.” Thus I informed Kṛṣṇa, but though I informed him, he remained silent for a few moments, bewildered about how to solve the problems.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Devi* refers to Rukmiṇī in Dvārakā for it is said in *Matsya Purāṇa*:

*vārāṇasyāṁ viśālākṣī vimalā puruṣottame \|*  
*rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṁ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane \|\|*

**In Varaṇāśi Viśālākṣī presides. In Puri Vimalā presides. In Dvārakā Rukmiṇī presides and in Vṛndāvana Rādhā presides.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a statement of a female servant in Dvārakā to one of her friends. According to *dharma-śāstra* you should have relation with her today, bathing after menstrual period. You are the protector of the sister of the king of Aṅga. You have obligation to her according to the custom. Kamalā has defeated the night in playing at dice with you. (They played all night and she won.) Today Kamalā surpasses you! You must please Rukmiṇī. You must show her love. The servant infomed Kṛṣṇa what should be done. O Lord of Dvārakā! Please make arrangements for all the queens. Though he was informed by me, he could not solve the problem (*apratipatti*). Thus his mind became perplexed *(mūḍha*). The four women represent four levels of *prema.*

### Text 36

***yatha va—***  
***padma dag-bhaigir alaa kalayati kamala jambhate saiga-bhaigaa***  
***tara dor-mulam alpaa prathayati kurute karea-kaeoua sukece \|***  
***caivya nevyaa vidhatte karam iti yugapan madhavau preyasebhir***  
***bhavenahuyamano bahu-cikhara-manau pacya kueoho’yam aste \|\|36\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Padmā is glancing at him. Kamalā is yawning while bending her limbs. Tāra is slightly stretching her arms. Sukeśī is scraching her ear. Śaibyā is adjusting her belt with her hand. Look! Being beckoned by his beloved** ***gopīs*** **simultaneously with their love, Mādhava, his mind attracted to all of them, stands in a stunned condition.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

An example from Dvārakā was given for the second defintion of *dakṣiṇa.* Because of the assocation with Rukmiṇī, the author is dissatisfied and gives another example. This illustrates Kṛṣna’s attraction for many women in Vṛndāvana.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Not satisfied with the relationships in Dvārakā, the author gives an example from Vṛndāvana. Padmā and others are all on the same level, because he acts as *dakṣiṇa* to them all. His mind is eager for many women (*bahu-śikhara-manāḥ*).

### Text 37-38

*caohau—*  
*priyaa vyakti puro’nyatra vipriyaa kurute bhacam \|*  
*niguoham aparadhaa ca caoho’yaa kathito budhaiu \|\|37\|\|*  
*yatha—*  
*svapne vyalekaa vanamalinoktaa*  
*palety upakareya vivarea-vaktra \|*  
*cyama viniucvasya madhu-triyamaa*  
*sahasra-yamam iva sa vyanainet \|\|38\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The cheater: The** ***saṭha*** **is defined by the wise as a person who speaks nicely in front of a woman had behind her back does unpleasant acts and commits covered offense to her.**

**An example: When Śyāmā heard Kṛṣṇa utter the upleasant name of Pālī in his dream, her face lost its color and she became breathless. The spring night extended for a thousand night-watches**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *sāṭha* speaks in a pleasing manner in the woman’s presence but acts the opposite behind her back. He also engages in many other excesses *(aparādham*). These are seen as two separate characteristics. Kṛṣna, uttering Pālī’s name in his dearm, is an example of speaking in a displeaisng manner. It is understood that he had previously told Śyāmā, “Even in my dreams I do not see any one other than you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One should not think there is redundancy in the defintion since acting in a displeaing manner and committing offense seem to be the same. Offense means to give treatment opposite to the normal, pleasing conventions of this world, because of lacking long term vision. The offense is committed with knowledge that it will offend the other person. It is not done without knowing. The word *vipriya* means that in the absence of the person one acts unfavorably towards the person. The word *aparādha* means that one acts in a displeasing manner while knowing it will displease the person. The offense will be understood in the example.
