A firend of Śyāmā speaks to Nāndīmukhī. He spoke displeasing words in his dream. While awake, he spoke pleasantly. “I hold no one in my heart but you.” One of the qualiteis of the *saṭha* is to first speaking in a pleasing manner. After private enjoyment with Śyāma; who was pleased, while he was sleeping he dreamed of enjoying with Pālī in Śyāmā’s absence. Thus he spoke well but acted in a displeasing manner. This is the second condition of the *saṭha.* However, when he uttered Pālī’s name in the dream, Śyāmā understood, and became offended. This is committing offense which he tried to cover up, since simply it could be understood only by uttering her name.

### Text 39

***yatha va—***  
***talpitena tapaneya-kantina***  
***kanea kuija-kuhare’dya vasasa \|***  
***abhyadhyāyi tava nirvyalīkatā***  
***muñca sāma-paṭalīpaṭiṣṭhatām \|\|39\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Kṛṣṇa! By your golden cloth used as a bed in the depths of the bower you have claimed innocence. Give up your pleasing words and extreme cunning.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

An example of offense is given.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

As the definition of speaking in a pleasing manner and acting in a displeasing manner is not clear to the unintelligent, another example is given. This is a statement of Padmā.

You claim innocence, no offense (*nirvalīkatā*) when we see your cloth which is stained with eye ointment and dirt. You have actually committed offense, because of the contrary evidence. Giving up offensive acts which you hide from us. Previously you spoke so nicely (*sāma*). This does not mean that your offense has ceased, because you could very well make more offenses. Even without displeasing conduct one can commit offense. This is seen in the seventh part of *Vidaghā-mādhava* in the incident of mentioning the name of the opposing *gopī.*

### Text 40-41

*atha dhṛṣṭaḥ—*  
*abhivyaktānya-taruṇī-bhoga-lakṣmāpi nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*mithyā-vacana-dakṣaś ca dhṛṣṭo’yaṁ khalu kathyate \|\|40\|\|*  
*yathā--*  
*nakhāṅkā na śyāme ghana-ghusṛṇa-rekhā-tatir iyaṁ*  
*na lākṣāntaḥ-krure paricinu girer gairikam idam \|*  
*dhiyaṁ dhatse citraṁ vata mṛgamade’py añjanatayā*  
*taruṇyās te dṛṣṭiḥ kim iva viparīta-sthitir abhūt \|\|41\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The lover who is fearless though bearing the marks of enjoyment with other women on his body, who is skilful at lying is called** ***dhṛṣṭa.***

**An example: O Śyāmā! These are not the marks of a woman’s nails on my body. They are marks of thick** ***kuṁkuma.*** **O cruel hearted woman! Do you not know about lac dye? This is red chalk from the mountain. How amazing ! You mistake musk for a woman’s eye ointment. Your immature eyes seen to have produced an opposite situation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though it is possible that his body may be injured by nails according to this example, the *gopīs* do not do this.

*at te sujāta-caraṇāmburuhaṁ staneṣu*  
*bhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu*  
*tenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṁ svit*  
*kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṁ naḥ*

**O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in You. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as you roam about on the forest path. SB 10.31.19**

However they touch his limbs in a joking way with their nails with gentle gestures. These imitiation of nail marks that appear with color are not considered to be the same as those inflicted by adversarial women. This is how the poets describe it.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Śyāmā who has being defeated. Because of smelling a fragrant lump of musk, it has stuck to my lip.

### Text 42-43

***udāttādyaiś catur-bhedais tribhiḥ pūrṇatamādibhiḥ \|***  
***caturviṁśaty ātmā paty-ādi-yugmataḥ \|\|42\|\|***  
***nāyakaḥ so’nukūlādyaiḥ syāt ṣan-navatidhoditaḥ \|***  
***nokto dhūrtādi-bhedas tu muneḥ sammaty-abhāvataḥ \|\|43\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***pati*** **and** ***upapati,*** **by having divisions of perfect, more perfect and most perfect in the four types starting with** ***dhīrodātta,*** **have a total of twenty-four types. In addition there are four types of heros starting with** ***ānukūla*****. This produces a total of ninety-six forms of Kṛṣṇa. The types such as** ***dhūrta*** **are not mentioned since Bharata Muni does not accept these divisions.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It should be inferred that the *upapati* forms are most perfect (Vṛndāvana forms) and the *pati* forms are perfect and more perfect (Mathurā and Dvārakā). This of course means that the other forms appear in small numbers in the respective places. From the definiton of the *śaṭha,* the category of *dhūrta* should be understood to be a person skilful at speaking in order to cheat to enjoy a woman.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa has twelve forms by multiplying the four forms of *dhīrodātta,* d*heralalita, dherodhatta*, and *dheracanta* by the three forms of perfect (Dvārakā), more perfect (Mathurā) and most perfect (Vraja). All these are also available in both the *upati* and *pati* forms. Most perfect forms of *pati* and *upati* can clearly be seen (in Vṛndāvana). Kṛṣṇa’s relation with Kubja is an example of an *upapati* of the more perfect type (since it was in Mathurā) for it is said *bhāva-yogāt tu sairindhrī parakīyaiva sammatā:* because of her bhāva, she is said to be a *parakīyā* lover of Kṛṣṇa. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 5.8) Kṛṣṇa has a *pati* rlationship with Rukmiṇī. *Gopala-tāpanī Upaniṣad* says:

*prapya mathuraa purea ramyaa sada brahmadi-sevitam \|*  
*caikha-cakra-gada-cariga-raknitaa munaladibhiu \|\|*  
*yatrasau saasthitau kaneas tribhiu caktya samahitau \|*  
*ramaniruddha-pradyumnai rukmieya sahito vibhuu \|\|*

**He attained Mathurā a pleasant city served by Brhamā and others and protected by the conch, cakra, club, bow and pestle. There Kṛṣṇa was situated with his three energies along with Saṅkarśaṇa, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Rukmiṇī.**

In some Purāṇas one also hears of Kṛṣṇa marrying Rukmiṇī in Mathurā. When Uddhava comes from Mathurā to Vṛndāvana, the *gopīs* say:

*asmāt kṛṣṇa ihāyāti prāpta-rājyo hatāhitaḥ*  
*narendra-kanyā udvāhya prītaḥ sarva-suhṛd-vṛtaḥ*

**But why should Kṛṣṇa come here after winning a kingdom, killing his enemies and marrying the daughters of kings? He’s satisfied there, surrounded by all his friends and well-wishers. SB 10.47.45**

(Thus her relatinship could be considered a more perfect *pati* relationship.) The married relationship of Rukmiṇī and other queens in Dvārakā is considered perfect.

Because the inhabitants of Mathurā were brought to Dvārakā, Kubja also lived in Dvāraka. There she had perfect *upapati r*elationship with Kṛṣṇa. In verse 43 the word *muneḥ* refers to Bharata Muni.

Thus ends the chapter on types of heroes.

## Chapter 2 - Assistants of Kṛṣṇa

## Outline

- *Ceṭa* (servant)
- *Viṭa* (rogue)
- *Viḍūṣaka* (buffoon)
- *Pīthāmarda* (impudent companion)
- *Priya-narma-sakha* (intimate friend)
- Messengers  
   Kṛṣṇa  
   \- Glances  
   \- Flute  
   Assigned messengers

### Text 1-2

***athaitasya sahāyāḥ syuḥ pañcadhā ceṭako viṭaḥ \|***  
***vidūṣakaḥ pīṭhamardaḥ priya-narma-sakhas tathā \|\|1\|\|***  
***narma-prayoge naipuṇyaṁ sadā gāḍhānurāgitā \|***  
***deśakālajñatā dākṣyaṁ ruṣṭa-gopī-prasādanam \|***  
***nigūḍha-mantratety ādyāḥ sahāyānāṁ guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***upapati*** **have types of assistants: the** ***ceṭaka*** **(servant),** ***viṭa (*****rogue companion)*****, vidūṣaka (*****clown companion)*****, pīṭhamarda*** **and** ***priya-narma-sakha.*** **They have the following qualities: they are skilful at joking, always endowed with deep attachment for Kṛṣṇa, knoweldgeable of time and place, skillful at pacifying angry** ***gopīs,*** **and able to give intimate counselling.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

There should be assistants—for the pastimes of the apparent *upapati.* However, though they are youths, one should consider them to be without male attitudes, or neuter, in the pastimes of the two lovers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Thought the assistants are youths (*kiśora)* they are without masculine sentiments , as if neuter, except for the *pīṭhamarda*. They manifest this by the *līla-śakti*. This is Jīva Gosvāmī’s explanation..

### Text 3

***sandhāna-caturaś ceṭo gūḍha-karmā pragalbha-dhīḥ \|***  
***sa tu bhaṅgura-bhṛṅgārādikaḥ prokto’tra gokule \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ceṭa:*** **The** ***ceṭa*** **(servant) is skilful at accomplishing tasks, doing things secretly, and is bold in his intelligence. In Gokula Kṛṣṇa has** ***ceṭas*** **like Bhaṅgura and Bhṛṅgāra.**

### Text 4

***yathā—***  
***na punar idam apūrvaṁ devi kutrāpi dṛṣṭaṁ***  
***śaradi yad iyam ārān mādhavī puṣpitābhūt \|***  
***iti kila vṛṣabhānor lambhitāsau kumārī***  
***vraja-nava-yuvarāja vyājataḥ kuñjavīthim \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**“I said to Rādhā, ‘O dear lady! I have seen something most astonishing today, never before seen. The** ***mādhavī*** **plant over there is flowering in the autumn.’ O young prince of Vraja! Rādhā then entered the bower.” The two then went on the path to the bower.**

### Text 5

*atha* ***viṭaḥ—***  
***veśopacārakuśalo dhūrto goṣṭhīviśāradaḥ \|***  
***kāmatantrakalāvedī viṭa ityabhidhīyate \|***  
***kaḍāro bhāratīvandhurityādirviṭa īritaḥ \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Viṭa: One who is skilful at dressing in disguise, who is cunning, who is persuasive, and who knowledgeable of tantric methods to control women is called** ***viṭa*** **(rogue companion). Kaḍāra and Bhāratībandhu are two** ***viṭas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Skill at dressing and knowledge of the arts to control women are useful for a messenger.. Thus the viṭa is not useless in all circumstances and is not without some understanding of the mood of the lovers. In the example following the two characteristics should be inferred because the viṭa goes about in disguise to talk to the *gopīs* and uses mantras to bewilder the women.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *viṭa* knows the arts described in *kāma-śāstra*—using mantras and herbs to control women.

### Text 6

***yathā—***  
***vraje sāraṅgākṣī vitatibhir anullaṅghya vacanaḥ***  
***sakhāhaṁ tad bandhoś caṭubhir abhiyāce muhur idam \|***  
***kala-krīḍad-vaṁśī sthagita-jagatī-yauvata-dhṛtis***  
***tvayā yuktaḥ śyāme na khalu parihartuṁ sakhi hariḥ \|\|6 \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O woman with doe-eyes! I am a friend of your friend. Since the women of Vraja do not disobey my words, I make a request with my profuse words. O Śyāmā! O friend! It is not proper to give up Kṛṣṇa, who destroys the chastity of all the young women of the world by playing on soft, sweet notes on his flute.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

That no one can disobey his orders is an illustration of his skill in persuasion. He destroys the determination of young women by a flute which playfully sounds with a soft sweetness. By this he instills fear. This shows his cunning nature and knowledge of conrolling women by *kāma-tantra.*

### Text 7

*atha* ***vidūṣakaḥ—***  
***vasantādyabhidho lolo bhojane kalahapriyaḥ \|***  
***vikṛtāṅga-vaco-veṣair hāsyakarī vidūṣakaḥ \|***  
***vidagdhamādhave khyāto yathāsau madhumaṅgalaḥ \|\|7 \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The vidūṣaka: The** ***vidūṣaka*** **is fond of eating, likes to make a commotion, and causes laughter by his strange contortions, words and clothing. Madhumaṅgala is famous in** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*** **as a** ***vidūṣaka*** **and Vasanta and others also act as** ***vidūṣakas.***

### Text 8

***yathā—***  
***tuṣṭena smita-puṣpa-vṛṣṭir adhunā sadyas tvayā mucyatām***  
***ārūḍhaḥ kutukī vimānam atulaṁ māṁ gokulākhaṇḍalaḥ \|***  
***ithaṁ devi manorathena rabhasād abhyarthyamāno apy asau***  
***yat te mānini nādharaḥ prayatate tan nādbhutaṁ rāgiṣu \|\|8\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: You should release a shower of smiles and flowers immediately because of satisfaction. O desirous woman! The king of the earth has mounted himself upon me, an incomparable chariot. O goddess! With great desire, I have prayed strongly for this smile. O respectable one! It is not astonishing that your lips do not respond to my request, since that is the nature of those with envy (that is the nature of red lips).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *vidūṣaka* is greedy (*lolaḥ*) for food. These qualities should be understood in the example given. *Vimāna* means a celestial chariot and lack of respect. This is not astonishing for persons with envy (*rāgiṣ*u). The word *rāga* has another meaning in the verse. *Viśva-prakāṣa* says *rāga* means attachment, envy, suffering, red color. Thus the word *rāga* can refer to the red lips as well as envy.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

O respectable (envious) woman! Though I, having desire (manorathena), pray to see your smile, it is not asonishing that your lips do not fulfill that desire, since that is the nature of persons with envy ( or redness). By association with those lips you have also become full of envy (*mānini*).  *Rāga* means attachment envy, suffering and red.

What is desired? O lips! Being satisified, release a shower of flowers in the form of smiles. This means the lips possess smiles that should be released. But they are contained within. At this moment you do not have pride. Why hold up those smiles? Release them, because the king of the earth (*gokulākhaṇḍalaḥ*) or the king of Vraja or the maintainer of your sense by sweetess has put me on a divine chariot *(vimānam*), or has elevated me with knowledge. Or to make her smile, he comes carying Kṛsṇa. This shows how he causes laughter by crooked limbs, words or dress.

*Vimanam* also means lack of respect. He ascend me, a *vidūṣaka*, since I have no respectable position. Or he rides on me who have unequalled glory *(atulam*) because I lack pride. Therefore you should shower flowers on the king on his chariot and reveal a smile to he who destroys pride by showing the highest glory. It is understood that she then smiled.

### Text 9

***yathā vā—***  
***mamopaharati svayaṁ bhavad abhīṣṭadevo naman***  
***navaṁ kamalam ujjvalaṁ kamala-bandhur utkaṇṭhayā \|***  
***mayā tu tad avajñayā bhuvi nirasyate ruṣyatā***  
***na mānayasi mad vacas tad api mānini tvaṁ kutaḥ \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Your worshippable deity, the friend of the lotus (the sun), with eagerness has offered my a splendid, new lotus. But I threw it on the ground in anger since I had been disrespected by the sun. O proud Rādhā! You do not respect my words though I am worshipped by your deity. What is wrong with you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“He is trying to make me laugh, but I will not laugh.” In this way she showed her stubbornness and did not listen to his words. He then thought, “I will have to find some other means that will defeat her.” He then speaks this verse. I have become angry because without bathing the sun brought me the lotus. It has become impure. I became angry. I said “I will keep away from you because of your actions.”

### Text 10

*atha* ***pīṭhamardaḥ—***  
***guṇair nāyaka-kalpo yaḥ premnā tatrānuvṛttimān \|***  
***pīṭhamardaḥ sa kathitaḥ śrīdāmā syād yathā hareḥ \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**He who has qualities equal to the hero and imitates him is called the** ***pīṭhamarda (*****impudent companion)*****.*** **Śrīdāmā is the** ***pīṭhamarda*** **of Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 11

***yathā—***  
***kālindīpuline mukundacaritaṁ viśvasya vismāpanaṁ***  
***draṣṭuṁ gacchati goṣṭhameva nikhilaṁ naikātra candrāvalī \|***  
***brūmas tasya suhṛttamāḥ svayam amī pathyañ ca tathyañ ca te***  
***mā govardhanamalla ghaṭṭaya mudhā govardhanoddhāriṇam \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: All the cowherdmen go to the bank of the Yamunā River to see the actions of Kṛṣna, which astonish the world. Only Candrāvalī does not go. O Govardhana-malla! I, the friend of Kṛṣna, speak what is beneficial and truthful to you. Do not uselessly interfere with the lifter of Govardhana.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

By his speech in the plural form (*brumaḥ*) Śrīdāmā is understood to have qualities like Kṛṣṇa. The supposed husband of Candrāvalī is an outcaste *ksatirya (malla)* named Govardhana. This is descibed in *Lalita-mādhava.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa allures my wife and takes her to the forest. I will take revenge on him. In this way Govardhanamalla spoke many words of opposition. Śrīdāmā then speaks to him. By using the plural he indicates that many people testify for Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Govardhanamalla has no proof for his accusations. By saying he is a friend of Kṛṣṇa, he shows that he knows Kṛṣṇa’s inner feeling of constant love for Candrāvalī. This advice is beneficial for you, because Kṛṣṇa will otherwise kill you as he killed Baka and Ariṣṭa. Do not become agitated like a black snake if you desire your good fortune. *Ghātṭa* meams moving. Do not think falsely that that you are a wrestler (*malla*) of Kaṁsa like Cānūra. By showing that he could lift a huge mountain like Govardhana, he does not give any regard to Kaṁsa. Among the *śṛṅgāra, sakhya* and *raudra rasas* displayed here, *raudra* is the main one in this verse. As a play on words, Śrīdāmā also suggests that you are Govardhana, and Kṛṣṇa, as lifter of Govardhana, will deliver you with your family.

### Text 12

***yathā vā—***  
***taveyaṁ śrīdāman bhaṇitir iha viśrambhayati māṁ***  
***prasādo rudrāṇyāḥ kim iva capalāsu prasaratu \|***  
***vane yāntīṁ durgārcana-ghusṛṇa-mālyāṅkita-karāṁ***  
***vadhūṁ dṛṣṭvā śaṅke prathayati kalaṅkaṁ khala-janaḥ \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O Śrīdāmā! Your speech gives me confidence. How can the mercy of Śiva’s wife spread to fickle persons? Still, seeing her go to the forest, carrying garlands and sandalwood in her hands to worship Durgā, I feel some fear. Some wicked person may spoil her reputation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows Śrīdāma’s intense *prema* for the hero through his intense desire to please Kṛṣṇa**.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“You can send her to the forest or keep her in the house, but you should not be afraid of my friend Kṛṣṇa. He does not know her. If he should enter the forest, I will come. I speak from the authoriites. The nature of Śiva’s wife is that when she is pleased by constant service, she gives her own wealth. Being served, when she does not receive service she becomes angry and takes way all grains and wealth. I have heard this from Bhāṇḍīra”. When Śrīdāmā said this, Bhāruṇḍā then spoke. “We have the mercy of Śiva’s wife otherwise we would not have grains, wealth and cows in the house. By her mercy Candrāvalī is steady and chaste. This is understood. However seeing her in the forest I feel some fear.” .

### Text 13

*atha* ***priya-narma-sakhaḥ—***  
***ātyantika-rahasya-jñaḥ sakhī-bhāva-samāśritaḥ \|***  
***sarvebhyaḥ praṇayibhyo’sau priya-narma-sakho varaḥ \|***  
***sa gokule tu subalas tathā syād arjunādayaḥ \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***priya-narma-sakhā*** **knows the most intimate pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, covets the desire for Kṛṣṇa meeting the** ***gopīs*** **and is the best among all the dear friends of Kṛṣṇa. In Gokula, Subala and Arjuna are** ***priya-narma-sakhas*****. Arjuna is a** ***gopā*** **in Vraja. BRS 3.3.431**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *priya-narma-sakhas* have the desire that Kṛṣṇa and the *gopīs* meet each other. That is the meaning of their *sakhī-bhāva*. By this their masculine sentiments are covered.

### Text 14

***yathā—***  
***pratyāvartayati prasādya lalanāṁ krīḍā-kali-prasthitāṁ***  
***śayyāṁ kuñja-gṛhe karoty agha-bhidaḥ kandarpa-līlocitām \|\|***  
***svinnaṁ bījayati priyā-hṛdi parisrastāṅgam uccair amuṁ***  
***kva śrīmān adhikāritāṁ na subalaḥ sevā-vidhau vindati \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**For what service is fortunate Subala not qualified? He pleases Kṛṣṇa with pleasant words when Kṛṣna returns from playing and fighting. He makes beds for Kṛṣna in the bower which are suitable for the pastimes of Cupid. He intensely fans Kṛṣṇa, whose limbs are fatigued and perspiring as he lies on the heart of his beloved.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He fans the perspiring limbs of exhausted Kṛṣṇa. This is *udātta alaṅkāra*, in which, because describing the main subject becomes secondary to describing his condition in an extreme state. Another version has *śaśvad vījayati priyānvitatayā svinnāṅgam etaṁ rahaḥ.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a friend some words which produce devotion for Subala. He fans Kṛṣṇa who is perspiring. He does this by standing outside the room and using a machine.

### Text 15

***yathā vā—***  
***yābhiḥ sāci-dṛgañcalena caṭulaṁ kaṁsārir ālihyate***  
***dordvandvena kucopapīḍam urasi svairaṁ pariṣvajyate \|***  
***etasyādhara-sīdhur uddhuratayā sāmodam āsvādyate***  
***kiṁ jānāsi sakhe vyadhāyi katarad gopībhir ābhis tapaḥ \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Do you know that the** ***gopīs*** **must have performed severe austerities? While trembling, they lick Kṛṣṇa with the edges of their crooked glances. With abandon, they embrace his chest, pressing him to their breasts. They happily taste the nectar of his lips without restraint.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The speaker is sympathetic to the *gopīs’* sentiments. But he do not desire the same positions, since his desire is that Kṛṣṇa and the *gopīs* meet each other.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse illustrates their *sakhī-bhāva*: the desire to have Kṛṣṇa meet the *gopīs*. Even though the *sakhis* in their their own groups are happy with the intimate meeting of Kṛsṇa and their leaders, and do not desire personal exchanges, thye are of two general types. Those who have extreme *prema* intensely desire Kṛṣṇa, whereas others desire Kṛsṇa to a lesser extent. The first type, the *parama-preṣhṭa-sakhīs* such as Lalitā, desire personal amorous relationships with Kṛṣṇa. The latter type, the *nitya-sakhis* like Kastūrī, never desire to enjoy Kṛṣṇa separately. The example given in the verse describes *gopīs o*f the first type, who desire intimate relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Ujjvala speaks with affection to Subala. *Kucopapīḍam* means he was pressed by their breasts.

### Text 16-17

***caturdhāḥ sakhāyo atra ceṭaḥ kiṅkara īryate \|***  
***pīṭhamardasya vīrādāvapi sāhāyyakāritā \|\|16\|\|***  
***hari-priyā-prakaraṇe vakṣyante yās tu dūtikāḥ \|***  
***atrāpi tā yathāyogyaṁ vijñeyā rasa-vedibhiḥ \|\|17\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These are the four types of friends. The** ***ceṭa*** **assists as a servant (*****dāsya-rasa*****). The** ***pīṭamarda*** **assists in** ***vīra-rasa.*** **The** ***dūtikās*** **(female assistants) will be described in the section called** ***Hari-priyā*****. In this chapter, those who know** ***rasa*** **should understand the messengers who are of suitable type for the hero.**

### Text 18

***tatra svayaṁ, yathā—***  
***sakhi mādhavadṛg dūtyāḥ***  
***karmaṭhatā kārmaṇe vicitrāsti \|***  
***upadhāśuddhāpi yayā***  
***ruddhā tvam citritevāsi \|\|18\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***svayaṁdūtī (*****Kṛṣṇa acting as his own messenger)**

**By his glances: O my friend Rādhā! The glances of Mādhava, his servants, skilful at their job, are amazing in the magical powers. Though you are pure by the tests of** ***dharma,*** **you have become attacked by those glances and become stationary like a figure in a painting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

S*vayam* means the *svayaṁ-dūtī (*natural messenger*). Kārmaṇe* means ‘actions like controlling by use of herbs.”  *Upadhā* means tests by *dharma* etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Svayam* means *svayaṁ-dūtī.* This is Viśākhā speaking to Rādhā. *Kārmaṇ*e means “by herbs which bring a person under control.” You are pure by tests like *dharma.* *Amara-koṣa* says *upadhā* means test by *dharma* and other things**.**

### Text 19

*vaṁśī yathā śrī-lalita-mādhave -*  
*hriyamavagṛhya gṛhebhyaḥ*  
*karṣati rādhāṁ vanāya yā nipuṇā \|*  
*sā jayati nisṛṣṭārthā*  
*varavaṁśajakākalī dūtī \|\|19\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**By his flute, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **1.24: All glory to the excellent sound of the flute, skilful agent of Kṛṣṇa, which. destoying shyness, pulls Rādhā from her house to the forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Avagṛhya* means “taking away.”  *Nisṛṣṭārthā* means “having been given responsibilities.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a statement by Gārgī. *Avagṛhya* means cutting. The flute pulls her from the house in order make her go to the forest. *Nisṛṭārtha* means “having been given responsibilities.”

### Text 20

***āptadūtī—***  
***vīrāvṛndādirapyāptadūtī kṛṣṇasya kīrtitā \|***  
***vīrā pragalbha-vacanā vṛndā cāṭūktipeśalā \|\|20\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***āpta-dūtī (*****assigned messenger): Vīrā, Vṛndā and others are Kṛsṇa’s assigned messengers. Vīrā speaks boldly and Vṛndā is expert at flattery.**

### Text 21

***yathā—***  
***vimukhī mā bhava garviṇi***  
***madgiri giriṇā dhṛtena kṛta-rakṣam \|***  
***mūḍhe samuḍha-vayasaṁ***  
***mādhavam ādhāva rāgeṇa \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O proud woman! Do not turn away from Kṛṣṇa. I say, by lifting the mountain he protected you. O fool! Go with deep attachment to Mādhava, who has now attained youth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of a messenger to a *gopīs* with *pūrva-rāga* and of the *vāmya* mood. Hasten to Mādhava ( *mādhavam ādhāva),* who has attained youth (*samūḍha-vayasam*). He will become attracted to other women at this age. You will regret it if you do not go now. To make the intention clear, she says “Fools!” This is a bold utterance. Though the statement is finished she then says “with great attachemnt (*rāgena*).” This indicates an order to go with a *sthāyi-bhāva* of *rāga.* Also there is a suggestion of “Your husband *(dhava*) is insignificant (*mā)”* by using the word *mādhavam*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The flute mayh be considered a *svayam dūtī* because it cannot be separated from Kṛṣṇa. But the flute may be considered an assigned messenger (*āpta-dūtī*) since it has been entrusted with a role (*nisṛṣṭārthā*). *Rādhā-kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeṣa-dīpikā* says that Vṛndā, Vṛndārikā, music and the flute are messengers. By my words (*mad-giri*) do not turn away from Kṛṣṇa. He has completely attained youth (*samūḍha-vayasam*). While he is still unattached to other women, go to him quickly. Go without delay. He protects you by holding up the mountain. This indicates his power, which is attractive to women. This indicates that he previousy protected you by holding up a mountain, and today you will be protected by two firm mountains (his arms). This indicates comforting them with a promise of meeting him. Go to Mādhava, dear to Lakṣmī (*m*ā). This can be said because Garga said at his birth that he was equal to Nārāyaṇa. Mādhava means the husband (*dhava*) of glory (*mā*). O fool! Why do you turn yourself into an animal? Do not go to your husband *(dhavam*) who is old, as if you were animals. This is rough language.

### Text 22

***yathā vā—***  
***vṛndā sundari vandanaṁ vidadhatī yat pṛcchati tvām asau***  
***cañcan mañjula-khañjarīṭa nayane tatrottaraṁ vyañjaya \|***  
***keyaṁ bhrū-bhujagī tavātiviṣamā baṁbhramyate yad bhiyā***  
***klāntaḥ kāliya-mardano.api kurute nādya praveśaṁ vraje \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O beuatiful woman with sweet eyes like the wagtail! Bow to Vṛṇdā, and answer the questions that I ask you. Why do you move your snake-like brows? It is so distasteful! Fearing that movement, Kṛṣṇa has become fatigued and wanders about. Today he cannot even enter Vraja.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of Vṛndā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks. By moving her brows, which are like snakes, he becomes bitten and fatigued and thus wanders about. Go to him and again move your brows. By again biting him, you will revive him. According to folk lore, if a person is bitten by a snake, if he is bitten again, he recovers. The poison counteracts the poison.

### Text 23

***asyāsādhāraṇā dūtyo vīrādyāḥ kathitā hareḥ \|***  
***liṅginyantāstu vakṣyante yāstāḥ sādhāraṇā dvayoḥ \|\|23\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The extraordinary messengers of Kṛṣṇa such as Vīrā have been described here. The ordinary messengers of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, ending with those called** ***liṅgiṇī,*** **will be described later.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dvayoḥ* means Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vīrā, Vṛndārikā, Melā and the flute are the extraordinary messengers of Kṛṣṇa, not the messengers of the *gopīs.* There are three types of ordinary messengers: the craftswoman, the fortune teller and the ascetic women (*liṅginī*).

## Chapter 3 - Kṛṣṇa’s Beloveds

## Outline

Ālambana

- Svakīya (married to Kṛṣṇa)
- Parakīya (unmarried to Kṛṣṇa)  
   1\. Kanyakā (not married to another man)  
   2\. Paroḍhā (married to another man)  
   A. Sādhana-parā (by practice)  
   a.Yauthikī (in a group)  
   \- Sages  
   \- Upaniṣads  
   b. Auathikī (individual)  
   B. Devī (heavenly women)  
   C. Nitya-priyā (eternal paroḍhā)  
   3\. Groups

### Text 1

***hareḥ sādhāraṇa-guṇair upetās tasya vallabhāḥ \|***  
***pṛthu-premṇāṁ sumādhurya-sampadāṁ cāgrimāśrayāḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The women lovers of Kṛṣṇa are endowed with Kṛṣṇa’s general qualities and possess the highest degree of abundant** ***prema*** **and exquisite beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The women possess qualities equal to Kṛṣṇa’s, as much as is appropriate.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The common qualities are having beautiful limbs, being endowed with auspicious marks etc.

### Text 2

***yathā—***  
***praṇamāmi tāḥ parama-mādhurī-bhṛtaḥ***  
***kṛta-puṇya-puñja-ramaṇī-śiromaṇīḥ \|***  
***upasanna-yauvana-guror adhītya yāḥ***  
***smara-keli-kauśalam udāharan harau \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the women of the highest beauty, the crest jewels of women who executed piles of pure acts, who are expertise in the arts of love from the young teacher Kṛṣṇa whom they have approached, and who show the applications of the lessons taught by him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The women approach him as a guru. However, since they have natural qualities like cleverness, when the situation is appropriate these qualities simply appear without making endeavors to learn. Seeing how he acts, they learn skills at *rāsa d*ance, singing and dancing. They show the application (*udāharan*) of what they have been taught by him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though it is said they have accrued great pious acts, this statement arises from their great love with absorption in pastimes, which gives the appearance that they exist in the ordinary world. This is a statement of the women of Mathurā, taken as an individual statement (I bow down). The *gopīs* do not need to be taught. Actually they are *nitya-siddha* and their excellent qualities manifest at an appropriate time. It is said *upadiṣati kāminīnāṁ yauvana-mada eva lalitāni:* the intoxication of youth manifests skills in women. This statement is found in many traditional scriptures such as *Sāhitya-darpaṇa*. In the commentary it is said that *upadiśati* means “manifests.”1 They develop skill in singing and dancing and *rasa* dance just by seeing, though these skills are hard to develop even for the writers of scriptures. They show the application (*udāharan*) of what they have been taught by him.

### Text 3-4

*svakīyāḥ parakīyāś ca dvidhā tāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\|3\|\|*  
*tatra svakīyāḥ—*  
*kara-graha-vidhiṁ prāptāḥ patyur ādeśa-tat-parāḥ \|*  
*pātivratyād avicalāḥ svakīyāḥ kathitā iha \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

***Svakīyā:*** **There are two types of Kṛṣṇa’s women:**  ***svakīya*** **and** ***parakīya.*** **The** ***svakīya*** **is known as the woman who attains her lover by marriage ceremony, abides by her husband’s orders, and does not deviate from vows to her husband as mentioned in scripture.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *svakīya* woman does not deviate from the *dharma* mentioned in scriptures (*pāti-vratyād*). She follows the order of her husband. This means that if there is some disagreement with the husband, she sacrifices a small portion of *dharma.*

### Text 5

***yathā—***  
***sunirmāṇe dharmādhvani pati-parābhiḥ paricite***  
***mudā baddha-śraddhā giri ca guru-vargasya paritaḥ \|***  
***gṛhe yāḥ sevante priyam aparatantrāḥ pratidinaṁ***  
***mahiṣyas tāḥ śaures tava mudam udagrāṁ vidadhatu \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**All the queens who have firm faith in the words of elders and in the perfect path of** ***dharma*** **known by chaste wives and who daily serve their husband in the house uncontrolled by others should give great joy to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sunirmāṇe dharmādhvani* means “in the path of *dharma* without fault, with all good qualities.” The women have faith in the words of the elders. One can depend on the elders’ advice, but one should not depend on advice which forbids association with Kṛṣṇa, as in the case of those with *parakīya-bhāva.* In this case, the statement holds, since there were no elders who opposed Kṛṣṇa’s marriages in Dvārakā. They served him every day. This indicates that it was not difficult for the queens to associate with Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is Draupadī’s statement to a friend. The queens follow the path produced (sunirmāṇe) by scripture and tradition, not that of the *parakīya* woman, which produces humiliation. They follow the path known by chaste wives (pati-parābhiḥ), not that known by the *parakīya* women or thieves. They are attached following the path known to civilized people. *Dharma adhvani* means “to the scriptures of *dharma* promoting service to the husband.” This produces no fault in this life or the next. On the other hand, *parakīya* is based on passion, not scripture. However, in fact, these three descriptions actually indicate the greater *prema* in the *parakīya* relationship, which produces greater happiness. Therefore the *parakīya* lover is greater. The svakīya woman is dependent on elders’ advice when it does not contradict service to Kṛṣṇa. However in other cases she is independent in her service (*apāra-tantryam*). *Udagrām* means great.

### Text 6

***yathā vā śrī-daśame (10.60.55)–***  
***na tvādṛśīṁ praṇayinīṁ gṛhiṇīṁ gṛheṣu***  
***paśyāmi mānini yayā sva-vivāha-kāle \|***  
***prāptān nṛpān na vigaṇayya raho-haro me***  
***prasthāpito dvija upaśruta-sat-kathasya \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From the Tenth Canto: In all my palaces I can find no other wife as loving as you, O most respectful one. When you were to be married, you disregarded all the kings who had assembled to seek your hand, and simply because you had heard authentic accounts concerning me, you sent a** ***brāhmaṇa*** **to me with your confidential message. SB 10.60.55**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Rahovahaḥ (rahoharaḥ)* means the revealer of the message. The word *me* has a locative meaning (to me.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example is given of the chief among the married women (*yathā vā*).  *Rahovahaḥ* means “one who brings a message.” *Me* means “to me.”

### Text 7-10

***tās tu śrī-yadu-vīrasya sahasrāṇyasya ṣoḍaśa \|***  
***aṣṭottara-śatāgrāṇi dvāravatyāṁ suviśrutāḥ \|\|7\|\|***  
***āsāṁ sakhyaś ca dāsyaś ca pratyekaṁ syuḥ sahasraśaḥ \|***  
***tulya-rūpa-guṇāḥ sakhyaḥ kiñcin nyūnās tu dāsikāḥ \|\|8\|\|***  
***tatrāpi rukmiṇī satyā jāmbavaty arka-nandinī \|***  
***śaivyā bhadrā ca kauśalyā mādrīty aṣṭau gaṇāgrimāḥ \|\|9\|\|***  
***tatrāpi rukmiṇī-satye varīyasyau prakīrtite \|***  
***aiśvaryād rukmiṇī tatra satyā saubhāgyato varā \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The queens numbered sixteen thousand one hundred and eight in Dvārakā. They each had thousands of female friends and female servants. The friends were equal to them in beauty and qualities and the servants were somewhat less in beauty and qualities. Among the queens Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Jāmvavatī, Kalindī, Śaibyā, Bhadrā, Kauśalyā and Mādrī were the best. Among the eight, Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā were the best. Rukmiṇī was superior in power and Satyabhāmā was superior in beauty.**

### Text 11

***tathā hi hari-vaṁśe—***  
***kuṭumbasyeśvarī yāsīd rukmiṇī bhīṣmakātmajā \|***  
***satyabhāmottamā strīṇāṁ saubhāgye cādhikābhavat \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said in** ***Hari-vaṁśa*****: Rukmiṇī, daughter of Bhīṣmaka, was the controller of the families, and Satyabhāmā were supreme in charm among the women.**

### Text 12

***pādme (6.88.28) ca kārttika-māhātmye tāṁ prati śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyaṁ***  
***na me tvattaḥ priyatamā kācid anyā nitambinī \|***  
***ṣoḍaśa-strī-sahasrāṇāṁ priye prāṇa-samā hy asi \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said in** ***Padma Purāṇa, Kārtika Māhātmya,*** **when Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rukmiṇī: No woman is dearer to me than you. Among the sixteen thousand women, you are like my very life.**

### Text 13

***anayoḥ sakalotkṛṣṭāḥ sakhyo dāsyaś ca lakṣaśaḥ \|***  
***svīyā-jātīya-bhāvena nikhilā eva bhāvitāḥ \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The thousands of friends and servants of Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā are the most excellent among all the friends and servants. They have** ***svakīya-bhāva*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Svīyā-jātīya-bhāvena* means they are endowed with mood appropriate (*jātīyā*) to wives.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Svīyā-jātīya-bhāvena* means they are endowed with affections like a wife. *Jātyāntāc cho bandhun*: the ending *jātīyā* means “appropriate to.” (Pāṇini 5.4.9) This means they cannot be separated from Kṛṣṇa. If what is defined in one place in scriptures is not contradicted by statements elsewhere, then it should be used in other cases as well. Thus, though it is not stated explicitly, the servants of the women of Vraja in *parakīya* relationship also had *parakīya* relationship. Some of the servants of Rādhā, who were given at the time of her marriage by Vṛṣabhānu, were not married, and some like Rūpa-mañjarī, were married. For Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī has said:

*tvaṁ rūpa-mañjari sakhi prathitā pure'smin*  
*puṁsaḥ parasya vadanaṁ na hi paśyasīti \|*  
*bimbādhare kṣatam anāgata-bhartṛkāyā*  
*yat te vyadhāyi kim u tac chuka-puṅgavena \|\|*

**O friend Rūpa-mañjarī! Although you are a famous and important person in this town, still you cannot see the face of the Supreme Lord standing before you. Your husband is not here, and yet there is a mark on the** ***bimba*** **fruits of your lips as if someone has bitten them. Did a great parrot bite them?** ***Vilāpa-kusumāñjali*** **1**

It should be understood that the *bhāva* of present day *sādhakas* will bear results according to taste and *sampradāya.* If one becomes fixed on *pati-bhāva* (Kṛṣṇa as a husband) during *sādhana,* then that becomes the *bhāva* in perfection. It will not be something unsuitable. Though simply taking the bride’s hand is considered marriage, the principle marriage here is that one follows marriage rules with the witness of *brāhmaṇas* and fire since following rules has been mentioned in this regard. The *svakīya* relationship of the friends and servants however is secondary to that of the queens (since they did not get married with fire and *brāhmaṇas* present).

### Text 14

***yāś ca gokula-kanyāsu pati-bhāva-ratā harau \|***  
***tāsāṁ tad-vṛtti-niṣṭhitvān na svīyātvam asāmpratam \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**For the unmarried girls of Gokula who were attached to Kṛṣṇa as their husband (worshipping Kātyāyanī),** ***svakīya*** **attainment is not improper, because they were fixed on that mood.**

### Text 15

***yathā—***  
***āryā ced ativatsalā mayi muhur goṣṭheśvarī kiṁ tataḥ***  
***prāṇebhyaḥ praṇayāspadaṁ priya-sakhī-vṛndaṁ kim etena me \|***  
***vaikuṇṭhāṭavi-maṇḍalī-vijayī ced vṛndāvanaṁ tena kiṁ***  
***dīvyaty atra na ced umā-vrata-phalaṁ piñcāvataṁsī patiḥ \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: What value is it if the elders, the leading women of Vraja, are always affectionate to me? What value is it if the host of priya sakhīs is dearer to me that my very life? What value is it if Vṛndāvana is greater than all the forest of Vaikuṇṭha? What is the use of performing vows to Katyāyanī if the husband with the peacock does not play here?**

### Text 16

***gāndharva-rītyā svīkārāt svīyātvam iha vastutaḥ \|***  
***avyaktatvād vivāhasya suṣṭhu pracchanna-kāmatā \|\|16\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because of being married according to the Gāndharva method, these girls are considered to be married to Kṛṣṇa. However, because they cannot reveal this marriage, their desires are well covered.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Desires covered” means they and Kṛṣṇa have to overcome many obstacles to meet. Thus they rarely meet. They evoke a prominent *parakīya* mood since they experience fear and shame since they do not consider their husbands to be their husbands, and were perceived to be unmarried by their parents (before they got them married). One should not have doubts about the fitness of their *bhāva* since it is said that they regarded themselves as wives, since they married other men in front of the *brāhmaṇas* and fire. *patyur no yajña-saṁyoge:* the word *patni* means a woman legitimately who can participate in fire sacrifice with her husband. (Pāṇini 4.1.33)

### Text 17

***atha parakīyā—***  
***rāgeṇaivārpitātmāno loka-yugmānapekṣiṇā \|***  
***dharmeṇāsvīkṛtā yās tu parakīyā bhavanti tāḥ \|\|17\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Parakīyā:*** **Those women, who out of great attraction, ignoring their fate in this world and the next, not accepting the rites of marriage, offer themselves to Kṛṣṇa, are called** ***parakīya*** **women.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Those who offer themselves out of inner attraction (*rāgena*), not out of external arrangements of marriage according to *dharma,* are called *parakīya.* Having mentioned their union, they are further described. They do not accept the man by marriage according to *dharma.* This means they accept him by attraction.

### Text 18

***yathā--***  
***rāgollāsa-vilaṅghitārya-padavī-viśrāntayo’py uddhura-***  
***śraddhā-rajyad-arundhatī-mukha-satī-vṛndena vandyehitāḥ \|***  
***āraṇyā api mādhurī-parimala-vyākṣipta-lakṣmī-śriyas***  
***tās trailokya-vilakṣaṇā dadatu vaḥ kṛṣṇasya sakhyaḥ sukham \|\|18\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The women who have transgressed the path of** ***dharma*** **out of strong love are worshipped and sought by a host of chaste women headed by Arundhatī, who are attached to them with great faith. Though forest dwellers, they surpass Lakṣmī and Śrī in their sweet fragrance. May these friends of Kṛṣṇa, most excellent in the three worlds, bestow happiness upon you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The chaste women give respect to the *parakīya gopīs*. They do not consider it a misfortune to love Kṛṣṇa. The sentiments of Arundhatī and others towards the *gopīs* is general *bhakti*, not *madhura-bhakti.* They regard Kṛṣṇa with motherly affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī and Gārgī when they are first being engaged as messengers. The *gopīs* have transgressed the limits (*viśārntiḥ*) of the path of *dharma* because of intense attraction. What path of *dharma* would they not transgress? Though they have this nature, they are worshipped by chaste women having attachment (*rajyat*) with faith.

### Text 19

***kanyakāś ca paroḍhāś ca parakīyā dvidhā matāḥ \|***  
***vrajeśa-vrajavāsinyah etā prāyeṇa viśrutāḥ \|***  
***pracchanna-kāmatā hy atra gokulendrasya saukhyatā \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***parakīyā*** **women are of two types: unmarried to other men and married to other men. This generally refers to the women living in Vraja. Their love is concealed. They give happiness to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is the conventional view by seeing the pastimes on earth, but is not the actual situation which was established previously. Those unmarried women who worship Kṛṣṇa while being devoid of consideration whether he is their husband or not, out of great attraction, are also called *parakīya* women. Concealed love gives rise to a special happiness. What has previously been shown is here expressed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Unmarried *gopīs* (*kanyakāḥ*) other than those who thought of Kṛṣṇa as their husband while worshipping Kātyāyanī are referred to here. The word *prayena* (generally) is used because some of them arrived from other places and were living in Vraja along with their mothers. They were not born there.

### Text 20

***tathā hi rudraḥ (śṛṅgāra-tilake 2.30)—***  
***vāmatā durlabhatvaṁ ca strīṇāṁ yā ca nivāraṇā \|***  
***tad eva pañca-bāṇasya manye paramam āyudham \|\|20\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rudrabhaṭta says: Coyness, unavailability, and rebuffing in a woman’s behavior are considered to be the ultimate weapon of Cupid.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author gives two statements, similar to those of Bharata Muni, to support his previous statements.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The mixture of genders (*vāmatā durlabhatvam*: feminine and neuter) in the words is correct. Resolving all words into one gender is forbidden in scriptures and common practice.

### Text 21

***viṣṇu-gupta-saṁhitāyāṁ ca—***  
***yatra niṣedha-viśeṣaḥ sudurlabhatvaṁ ca yan mṛgākṣīṇām \|***  
***tatraiva nāgarāṇāṁ nirbharam āsajjate hṛdayam \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***Viśṇu-gupta-saṁhitā*** **it is said: When the woman makes a point of resisting and becoming unavailable, the man becomes more deeply attached.**

### Text 22

***āḥ kiṁ vānyad yatas tasyām idam eva mahāmuniḥ \|***  
***jagau pāramahaṁsyāṁ ca saṁhitāyāṁ svayaṁ śukaḥ \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Ah! What more can be said! For Śukadeva himself, in** ***Bhāgavatam,*** **the book for** ***paramahaṁsas*****, has glorified the** ***parakīya*** **love of the** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“The subject of *parakīya* is not described because it is a cause of great disturbance.” But worry should not worry about that. *Āḥ* is an abuse hurled at the materialists. *Viśva-koṣa* says that *āḥ* is an expression of anger or pain. What more can be said? Is not everything else worthless? Śukadeva praises what is being discussed (*idam*). The word *eva* here means *api* (even). *Ca* means *ca api* (even in the *Bhāgavatam*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author shows anger towards those who support *svakīya* love. *Viśva-koṣa* says that *āḥ* is an expression of anger or pain. Śukadeva has glorified loudly without fear *parakīya* love. Use of the word *svayam* is used because there is no word superior to that of Śukadeva.

### Text 23

***yathā śrī-daśame (10.33.19)—***  
***kṛtvā tāvantam ātmānaṁ yāvatīr gopa-yoṣitaḥ \|***  
***reme sa bhagavāṁs tābhir ātmārāmo ‘pi līlayā \|\|23\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Expanding himself as many times as there were cowherd women, the Supreme Lord, though self-satisfied, enjoyed their company by his** ***līlā-śakti.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though Kṛṣṇa is *ātmārāma,* he enjoys with the *gopīs.* It has been said:

*ātmārāmāś ca munayo nirgranthā apy urukrame \|*  
*kurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim ittham-bhūta-guṇo hariḥ \|\|*

**Some sages who are** ***ātmārāmas,*** **beyond the scriptures, false ego and rules, also practice unmotivated, pure bhakti to the master of pure** ***bhakti,*** **Kṛṣṇa, since he possesses qualities attractive to even them. SB 1.7.10**

Just as Kṛṣṇa has extraordinary qualities (*ittham-bhūta-guṇaḥ)* the *gopīs* also have extraordinary qualities. However at this time there was a special manifestation. One Kṛṣṇa expanded himself into as many forms as there were *gopīs* by *his līlā-śakti (līlayā*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa was unable to neglect even one of the *gopīs* because of his extreme attachment to them. Therefore he expanded into many forms. The word *gopa-yoṣitaḥ* means the wives of the cowherd men. This is *parakīya* love. Another version has *vraja-yoṣitaḥ* (women of Vraja). But since Kṛṣṇa had not married them, and would not marry them in the future, according to Śukadeva, the love is still *parakīya.* Śukadeva says:

*dharma-vyatikramo dṛṣṭa īśvarāṇāṁ ca sāhasam*  
*tejīyasāṁ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā*

**The status of powerful controllers is not harmed by any apparently audacious transgression of morality we may see in them, for they are just like fire, which devours everything fed into it and remains unpolluted. SB 10.33.29**

The word *rarāma* indicates conjugal enjoyment, forbidden in scriptures. Since enjoyment of others’ wives is forbidden in the scriptures, producing *adharma,* it indicates *parakīya* love which was difficult for them to attain. He expanded himself because of his great attachment to them, even though he is *ātmārāma.* This means the *gopīs* had remarkable *prema (itthaṁ-bhūta-guṇaḥ),* as Kṛṣṇa himself has. This is stated in SB 1.7.11.

### Text 24-25

***vartitavyaṁ śam icchadbhir bhaktavan na tu kṛṣṇavat \|***  
***ity evaṁ bhakti-śāstrāṇāṁ tātparyasya vinirṇayaḥ \|\|24\|\|***  
***rāmādivad vartitavyaṁ na kvacid rāvaṇādivat \|***  
***ity eṣa mukti-dharmādi-parāṇāṁ naya īryate \|\|25\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Those who desire auspiciousness should act as devotees, not as Kṛṣṇa. This is discerned as the meaning of the scriptures on** ***bhakti.*** **To act like Rāma and not like Rāvaṇa is the conduct recommended for those seeking liberation or piety.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some people will worry about establishing the nature of *rasa* in Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes with women who are apparently of *parakīya* nature. “Others will realize *rasa* when the meditation on *śṛṅgāra-rasa* gives rise to a vision of one’s non-difference with the hero or heroine as the case may be.” This is the position of scholars of *rasa.* Let that be. In this *rasa,* meditation on non-difference with Kṛṣṇa produces fault. In order to describe *rasa,* the *gopīs* are to be glorified. Therefore the author gives this verse. Not only in considering *parakīya-rasa,* in any *rasa* one should not imitate the sentiments of Kṛṣṇa. That is the meaning here.

Some do not approve of Kṛṣṇa’s *rasa* pastimes because they produce sin. They say, however, in Rāma’s famous pastimes, the parts showing good conduct should be accepted. Those desiring liberation accept the parts about peace, those desiring *dharma* accept the parts about acting according to ones *dharma,* and those desiring *artha* and *kāma* accept the parts about *nīti.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“People will become attracted to bad actions according to the idea that whatever great men do others follow (*Gītā* 3.21).” The answer is given here. *Śam* means auspiciousness. One should act according to the actions performed by the devotee (*bhaktavat*).

“Should one follow the *siddhas* or the *sādhakas*? One should not follow the *siddhas,* since the *siddhas* act similar to Kṛṣṇa. The *siddhas* act independently.

*yat-pāda-paṅkaja-parāga-niṣeva-tṛptā*  
*yoga-prabhāva-vidhutākhila-karma-bandhāḥ*  
*svairaṁ caranti munayo ’pi na nahyamānās*  
*tasyecchayātta-vapuṣaḥ kuta eva bandhaḥ*

**Material activities never entangle the devotees of the Supreme Lord, who are fully satisfied by serving the dust of his lotus feet. Nor do material activities entangle those intelligent sages who have freed themselves from the bondage of all fruitive reactions by the power of yoga. So how could there be any question of bondage for the Lord himself, who assumes his transcendental forms according to his own sweet will? SB 10.33.35**

One should not act like the *sādhaka*, for one can find bad conduct among the *sādhakas.* *Api cet sudurācāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk*: the devotee who commits sinful acts worship me. (BG 7.24)”

This is not correct. The rules of the *bhakti* scriptures should be practiced. That is the meaning of *varitavyam (*should be practiced). The practice is that of the devotees (*bhaktavat*), not the actions of Kṛṣṇa (*kṛṣṇavat*). Some say one should say “I will act like Rāma, since he had good conduct.” That is not the opinion of the devotees. According to the principle that “One becomes whatever *dharma* he follows” the person who imitates Rāma will attain merging with him.

### Text 26

***tathā ca tatraiva —***  
***naitat samācarej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ \|***  
***vinaśyaty ācaran mauṭhyād yathārudro ‘bdhi-jaṁ viṣam \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***Bhāgavatam*** **also says: One who is not a great controller should never imitate the behavior of ruling personalities, even mentally. If out of foolishness an ordinary person does imitate such behavior, he will simply destroy himself, just as a person who is not Rudra would destroy himself if he tried to drink an ocean of poison. SB 10.33.31**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Acting freely produces fault, what to speak of meditating on non-difference with the emotions of Kṛṣṇa towards the *gopīs.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A scriptural example of his previous statement is given.

### Text 27

*anugrahāya bhaktānāṁ mānuṣaṁ deham āśritaḥ \|*  
*bhajate tādṛśīḥ krīḍā yāḥ śrutvā tat-paro bhavet \|\|27\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**To show mercy to his devotees the Lord engages in such pastimes by hearing which the humans become dedicated to him. SB 01.33.36**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Devotees who hear the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa become devoted to him, not non-different from him. Proof is given here. This is the nature of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. It is said:

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopīs of Vṛndāvana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. SB 10.33.39**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The independent activities of the Lord however are for the benefit of the devotee.  
To show mercy to the devotees the Lord performs such pastimes. A person who has taken human body (*mānuṣaṁ deham āśritaḥ*), on hearing these pastimes, becomes completely dedicated to the Lord (*tat-paraḥ bhavet*). The pastimes have a power like that of jewels, mantras or herbs so that they produce complete dedication to the Lord. They do not create sinful effects.

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopīs of Vṛndāvana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. SB 10.33.39**

Another meaning is that after hearing one must become (*bhavet*) a devotee. Otherwise one would be a sinner. As it is said in the Third Canto:

*ko nāma loke puruṣārtha-sāravit*  
*purā-kathānāṁ bhagavat-kathā-sudhām*  
*āpīya karṇāñjalibhir bhavāpahām*  
*aho virajyeta vinā naretaram*

**Using his ears as hands to take the nectar, knowing the essence of all human goals to be bhakti, having drunk the sweet stories of the Lord among all the past narrations, which destroy material existence, what person would then reject them? Only an animal would reject them! SB 3.13.50**

Thus, just from hearing constantly and becoming addicted to any topics of Kṛṣṇa one attains perfection and if one hears topics of the *rāsa-līlā* one attains even higher perfection. One should always hear and become addicted to the five chapters on *rāsa-līlā.*

### Text 28

***śrī-mukhena tu māhātmyam āsāṁ prāha svayaṁ hariḥ \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The Lord himself has glorified the** ***gopīs*** **with his mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“One should meditate on the *bhāvas* of other devotees since those are purifying. The *bhāvas* of the *gopīs* are faulty, since seeing the conduct of the *upapati* is distasteful.” This verse answers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“One should meditate on the *bhāvas* of other devotees since those *bhāvas* purify a person. The *bhāvas* of the *gopīs* are faulty, since seeing the conduct of the *upapati* is distasteful. By meditating on them some become corrupted in mentality and fall into *saṁsāra*.” This verse answers.

### Text 29

***yathā tatraiva (10.32.22)—***  
***na pāraye ‘haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ***  
***sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ \|***  
***yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ***  
***saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā \|\|29\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. SB 10.32.22**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Let the compensation be repaid by your good acts. Let that be my show of gratitude. The materialists will see here the ordinary affairs of an *upapati.* This scripture is not revealed to such persons.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

As was said, the union with the *gopīs (samyujam)* with Kṛṣṇa was without fault (*niravadya*). What is proper compensation? No object which produces what is proper can actually be the correct compensation (*ṣadhu-kṛtyam*). Whatever compensation I give is temporary, in the life of Brahmā. I cannot repay the debt. He blames himself. You have worshipped me (*mā*), cutting ties, throwing at a distance even the slightest bonds of affection for husbands, mother-in laws, fathers-in-law, fathers, mothers, brothers. Another meaning is “Cutting off all ties, you do not respond to family relationships again like immature *yogīs*.” But I have affection for parents, brother, and friends. If I worship you, I cannot follow the method correctly, since the principle is “as you surrender to me I respond.” Another meaning is “I cannot worship you (*mā abhajam)* while cutting off all ties to family.” *Abhajam* becomes *abhajan* before *durjara.* Therefore let your good conduct by the compensation.

### Text 30

***uddhavo’pi jagau suṣṭhu sarva-bhāgavatottamaḥ \|\|30\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava, the best of all devotees has glorified the** ***gopīs.***

### Text 31

***yathā (SB 10.47.61)—***  
***āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ***  
***vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām \|***  
***yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā***  
***bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām \|\|31\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Even the great devotees praise the *gopīs.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The observer should not develop the tendency to act without restrictions devoid of good conduct.” The word j*agau* in verse 30 refers to the *Bhāgavatam* verse:

*dṛṣṭvaivam-ādi gopīnāṁ kṛṣṇāveśātma-viklavam*  
*uddhavaḥ parama-prītas tā namasyann idaṁ jagau*

**Thus seeing how the** ***gopīs*** **were always disturbed because of their total absorption in Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava was supremely pleased. Desiring to offer them all respect, he sang as follows. SB 10.47.57**

This word thus indicates “Everyone should hear that song and my conformity to it.” The *gopīs* have placed their foot dust upon the lowly bushes while going to meet Kṛṣṇa because they cannot understand the proper path. “But you are the chief of Kṛṣṇa’s associates in pastimes. What most remarkable thing do you see in the *gopīs*?” They have given up association of family, hard to give up. This shows their supreme, unconditional *prema*. The *prema of* Rukmiṇī is covered by conventions of *dharma.* Therefore Uddhava prays for their foot dust.

### Text 32

***māyā-kalita-tādṛk-strī-śīlanenānasūyabhiḥ \|***  
***na jātu vraja-devīnāṁ patibhiḥ saha saṅgamaḥ \|\|32\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***gopīs*** **did not marry the cowherd men, who held no animosity, because the cowherd men saw forms of the** ***gopīs*** **made by** ***māyā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“There is not fault if the Lord is actually the husband of the *gopīs*. But to think that they had other husbands is impossible. It becomes disgusting. How can *rasa* be produced by this?” In answer to this, it is explained in this verse that *māyā* produced forms which performed activities like getting married to the cowherd men and which appeared to be faithful to them.

*saha-balaḥ srag-avataṁsa-vilāsaḥ*  
*sānuṣu kṣiti-bhṛto vraja-devyaḥ*  
*harṣayan yarhi veṇu-raveṇa*  
*jāta-harṣa uparambhati viśvam*

**O goddesses of Vraja, when Kṛṣṇa is enjoying himself with Balarāma on the mountain slopes, playfully wearing a flower garland on the top his head, he gives joy to all with the resonant vibrations of his flute. Thus he delights the entire world. SB 10.35.14**

This shows that *māyā* had already accomplished her task of making those forms (since no one complained about his actions). By use of those forms as a practical means, the cowherd men who were exposed to *māyā* did not actually marry the *gopī*s (*na saṅgamaḥ*) who were Kṛṣṇa’s principle consorts, like Rukmiṇī and others in Dvārakā. The *gopīs* did not have an illicit relationship of sleeping with the cowherd men, which need atonement, what to speak of even marrying them.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“What is the solution to the statement that the *gopīs* were married?” The cowherd men did not show hatred because they thought that the *gopīs* were at home while they actually went to meet Kṛṣṇa, since *māyā* had constructed other forms of the *gopīs* to stay at home. This *māyā* is *yoga-māyā,* not external *māyā,* since material *māyā* has no jurisdiction over the perfect associates in the Lord’s abode and since it is impossible that they could be materially bewildered, and thus be opposed to the Lord, and because one never sees the cowherd men hate the Lord. That is because *yoga-māyā* is the *cit-śakti* of the Lord, and therefore her effects must be eternally true. Even when the material world is completely destroyed, the cowherd men continue to identify the *gopīs* as their wives at their side. This is an eternal situation.

### Text 33

***tathā hi śrī-daśame —***  
***nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā \|***  
***manyamānāḥ svapārśvasthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ \|\|33\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said in the Tenth Canto: The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against him. SB 10.33.37**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

This verse is proof of the previous statement. The meaning is this. By Kṛṣṇa’s *māyā* each of the husbands through marriage, thinking that their wives, actually made of *māyā,* were by their made sides and did not hate Kṛṣṇa. This means that whenever there was the need of the gopīs breaking the vow of having one husband, Kṛṣṇa revealed forms of *māyā* to the cowherd men and hid the real forms. The cowherd men did not find fault with the vows of their wives. Though the two forms could not be distinguished, there was a purpose in doing this. Kṛṣṇa’s *māyā* can do anything. Therefore *māyā* assisted the *gopīs.* This explains the statement of verse 32, that *māyā* produced their good conduct *(śīla)* such as marriage. It will also be shown that *māyā’s* actions are the cause of accomplishing the remainder of *rasa*. Some of the *gopīs* were serving their husband and some were inside their houses. Those who could not go had imperfect bodies. But though some were milking cows, they went .This means that though they went, they did not give up their household actions. It is mentioned that they went. *ājagmur anyonyam alakṣitodyamāḥ*: they went, unseen by the others*.* (SB 10.29.4)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“But it is very easy for *yoga-māyā* to produce this conception of the *gopīs* being at the side of their cowherd husbands without having to make some false forms.” That is true. But it is also said:

*tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ*  
*govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ*

**Their husbands, fathers, brothers and other relatives tried to stop them, but Kṛṣṇa had already stolen their hearts. Enchanted by the sound of his flute, they refused to turn back. SB 10.29.8**

At the time of *rāsa-līlā,* the cowherd men felt they must prevent their wives from going and thus brought them back to their house. This was the arrangement. This would not be possible without creating some false forms. Therefore the author says in the text that *māyā* produced false forms of the *gopīs* (*māyā-kalita-tādṛk-strī*). According to *Lalita-mādhava*, even the illusory marriage of the *gopīs* with the cowherd men is eternal.

The cowherd men also did not enjoy with those forms made of *māyā* since it would be improper for them to enjoy other forms which resembled their wives. Therefore Śukadeva says that they thought their wives were at their side, not in their beds. The solution was produced by *yoga-māyā.* Though the cowherd men were men, by *yoga-māyā* they did not develop lust for their wives. Therefore they slept in the cow sheds not in their houses, though requested to do so by their mothers. Thus they did not develop possessiveness of their wives.

### Text 34-35

***tatra kanyakāḥ—***  
***anūḍhāḥ kanyakāḥ proktāḥ sa-lajjāḥ pitṛ-pālitāḥ \|***  
***sakhī-keliṣu visrabdhāḥ prāyo mugdhā-guṇānvitāḥ \|\|34\|\|***  
***tatra durgā-vrata-parāḥ kanyā dhanyādayo matāḥ \|***  
***hariṇā pūritābhīṣṭās tena tās tasya vallabhāḥ \|\|35\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The unmarried girls: Those girls who were unmarried are called** ***kanyakās.*** **They are shy and protected by their parents. They have trust in the pastimes of the** ***sakhīs*** **and are generally** ***mugdhā.*** **Among the** ***kanyakās,*** **some were engaged in worshipping Durgā, such as Dhanyā. Kṛṣṇa fulfilled their desire and they are thus called his dear women (wives).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *kanyakās* have faith in the activities joyfully created by the elder *sakhīs.* Among the *kanyakās*, some such as Dhanyā engaged in worshipping Durgā. Kṛṣṇa fulfilled their desire:

*yātābalā vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyathā kṣapāḥ*  
*yad uddiśya vratam idaṁ cerur āryārcanaṁ satīḥ*

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. After all, this was the purpose of your vow to worship goddess Kātyāyanī, O pure-hearted ones. SB 01.22.27**

Thus they are called his women *(vallabhāḥ)* which means he accepted them as his wives, since the conventional meaning of *vallabhā* is a wife.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among the *parakīya* women are the *kanyakās*. Among the *kanyakās* were Dhanyā and others who performed vows to Durgā. However, these ones were different from those who took themselves as Kṛṣṇa’s wives since they are described in this section concerning *parakīya.* It was said previously:

Among the young, unmarried *gopīs* some among them who made the following vow attained the Lord as their husband. *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 1.15

The *Bhāgavatam* also says:

*hemante prathame māsi nanda-vraja-kamārikāḥ*  
*cerur haviṣyaṁ bhuñjānāḥ kātyāyany-arcana-vratam*

**During the first month of the winter season, the young unmarried girls of Gokula observed the vow of worshiping goddess Kātyāyanī. For the entire month they ate only unspiced** ***khichrī.*** **SB 10.22.1**

From this it should also be understood that there were many other unmarried women, daughters of Vṛṣabhānu, Candrabhānu and others who did not perform the vows to Durgā and who remained situated in *parakīya,* as associates of Rādhā.

### Text 36

***yathā—***  
***visrabdhā sakhi dhūli-keliṣu paṭā-saṁvīta-vakṣaḥ-sthalā***  
***bālāsīti na vallavas tava pitā jāmātaraṁ mṛgyati \|***  
***tvaṁ tu bhrānta-vilocanās tam acirād ākarṇya vṛndāvane***  
***kūjantīṁ śikhi-piccha-mauli-muralīṁ sotkampam āghūrṇasi \|\|36\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! You have confidently involved in the** ***sakhīs’*** **pastimes. You chest is covered with clothing in the form of dust from playing. Because you were a child, your cowherd father did not search for a husband for you. On hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, your eyes quiver and, your body shakes and you turn around dizzily.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a statement by the wife of the elder brother. You have faith in the pastimes of the *sakhīs.* Even though her previous condition has been pointed out, it is in the present tense, since it happened recently.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

These are joking words of some woman of Vraja who has established a relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Your chest is covered with clothing in the form of dust. Thus you are trusting child. The disorder of words caused by necessities of meter should be corrected. The word *vallavaḥ* (cowherd) indicates the father has no great discrimination.

### Text 37

***atha paroḍhāḥ—***  
***gopair vyūḍhā api hareḥ sadā sambhoga-lālasāḥ \|***  
***paroḍhā vallabhās tasya vraja-nāryo’prasūtikāḥ \|\|37\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***paroḍhā:*** **The cowherd women who are married to cowherd men but always desire enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa are called** ***paroḍhā*****. They are dear to Kṛṣṇa and never bear children.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

As was explained previously the idea of their marriage is actually illusory. If they were to bear children, their positions as personalities in *rasa* would be faulty by the disfigurement of pregnancy. Thus *rasa* itself would be destroyed. That their beauty enhanced his beauty is shown in many verses:

*tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*madhye maṇīnāṁ haimānāṁ mahā-marakato yathā*

**In the midst of the dancing** ***gopīs*****, Lord Kṛṣṇa appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire in the midst of golden ornaments. SB 10.3**

*pāda-nyāsair bhuja-vidhutibhiḥ sa-smitair bhrū-vilāsair*  
*bhajyan madhyaiś cala-kuca-paṭaiḥ kuṇḍalair gaṇḍa-lolaiḥ*  
*svidyan-mukhyaḥ kavara-rasanāgranthayaḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo*  
*gāyantyas taṁ taḍita iva tā megha-cakre virejuḥ*

**As the** ***gopīs*** **sang in praise of Kṛṣṇa, their feet danced, their hands gestured, and their eyebrows moved with playful smiles. With their braids and belts tied tight, their waists bending, their faces perspiring, the garments on their breasts moving this way and that, and their earrings swinging on their cheeks, Lord Kṛṣṇa’s young consorts shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds. SB 10.33.7**

By that beauty, *rasa* is accomplished:

*vaṁ śaśāṅkāṁśu-virājitā niśāḥ*  
*sa satya-kāmo ’nuratābalā-gaṇaḥ*  
*siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ*  
*sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ*

**Although the** ***gopīs*** **were firmly attached to Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose desires are always fulfilled, the Lord was not internally affected by any mundane sex desire. Still, to perform his pastimes the Lord took advantage of all those moonlit autumn nights, which inspire poetic descriptions of transcendental affairs. SB 10.33.25**

Thus in pointing out their brothers and sons in the following verse, Kṛṣṇa is just joking with them:

*mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ*  
*vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṁ bandhu-sādhvasam*

**Not finding you at home, your mothers, fathers, sons, brothers and husbands are certainly searching for you. Don’t cause anxiety for your family members. SB 10.29.20**

Actually there would a fault if they had children, since they would be criticizing their husbands and also enjoying with them. *Nindami ca pibāmi ca iti nyāya*2 Śukadeva says *pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ*: they fed the babies milk. He does not say they fed their son’s breast milk. Thus they fed the babies milk that they had taken from the cows, for it is said *duhantyo’bhiyayuḥ:* milking the cows, they *gopīs* departed. In this manner one sees mention of loose mention of the word “son” as when Sāmba stole Lakṣmaṇā. Referring to Balarāma, Sāmba is mentioned as his son, though he was actually Kṛṣṇa’s son:

*pratigṛhya tu tat sarvaṁ bhagavān sātvatarṣabhaḥ*  
*sa-sutaḥ sa-snuṣaḥ prāyāt suhṛdbhir abhinanditaḥ*

**The Supreme Lord, chief of the Yādavas, (Balarām) accepted all these gifts and then departed with his son and daughter-in-law, as his well-wishers bid him farewell. SB 10.68.52**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They never gave birth to children because they never attained menstrual periods. This was arranged by *yoga-māyā* for eternal pastimes.

### Text 38

***yathā padyāvalyām (312)—***  
***kātyāyanī-kusuma-kāmanayā kim arthaṁ***  
***kāntāra-kukṣi-kuharaṁ kutukād gatāsi \|***  
***sadyastana-stana-yuge tava kaṇṭakāṅkaṁ***  
***gopaḥ sukaṇṭhi bata paśyati jāta-kopaḥ \|\|38\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **Why are you eagerly going into the deep, dark forest to pick flowers for goddess Katyāyanī? O beautiful-necked girl! Your angry husband sees the scratches on your new breasts caused by thorns.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a joking statement and therefore a friend makes some conjectures which are actually untruthful. Though the husband is far away, the sound of his breathing is indicated by the use of sibilants. The girl of good family also could not have such developed breasts at this age. .

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Candrāvalī. *Sadyastana* means “newly developed.’ *Kaṇṭakāṅkam* means “signs of injury by thorns.”

### Text 39

***etāḥ sarvātiśāyinyaḥ śobhā-sād-guṇya-vaibhavaiḥ \|***  
***ramādibhyo’py uru-prema-mâdhurya-bhara-bhūṣitāḥ \|\|39\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These** ***paroḍhā*** **women excel all others in beauty, good qualities and power. They are endowed with greater** ***prema*** **and sweetness than Lakṣmī and others.**

### Text 40

***tathā śrī-daśame:***  
***nāyaṁ śriyo ‘ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ***  
***svar-yoṣitāṁ nalina-gandha-rucāṁ kuto ‘nyāḥ \|***  
***rāsotsave ‘sya bhuja-daṇḍa-gṛhīta-kaṇṭha-***  
***labdhāśiṣāṁ ya udagād vraja-vallabhīnām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In the Tenth Canto it is said: When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the** ***gopīs*** **in the** ***rāsa-līlā*****, the** ***gopīs*** **were embraced by the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower. And what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation? SB 10.47.60**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows the supreme qualification and eternal position of the lovers and as well confirms that the temporary appearance of their *parakīya* love was caused by *māyā.* Their love has already been shown to be greater than that of persons desiring liberation, liberated persons and even devotees:

*tāḥ paraṁ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo*  
*govinda eva nikhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ*  
*vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṁ ca*  
*kiṁ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya*

**Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a high-class** ***brāhmaṇa*****, or even as Lord Brahmā himself? SB 10.47.58**

The reason for their greatness is given:

*kvemāḥ striyo vana-carīr vyabhicāra-duṣṭāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇe kva caiṣa paramātmani rūḍha-bhāvaḥ*  
*nanv īśvaro ’nubhajato ’viduṣo ’pi sākṣāc*  
*chreyas tanoty agada-rāja ivopayuktaḥ*

**How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by improper behavior, have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul! Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord Himself awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients. SB 10.47.59**

Uddhava, the speaker of these verses, has given the introduction and conclusion on seeing their great love. By using the word *paramātmani* in the above verse, he discards the idea that there was sinful conduct in the *gopīs* and their husbands. He explains that the *gopīs* gave up worldly *dharma* only for the sake of Kṛṣṇa and this shows that they followed the best conduct. No other meaning can be given.

*āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ*  
*vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām*  
*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

Here is the meaning. There are these women of Vṛndāvana, such as Rādhā, wandering the forest. And there are other unfaithful women having bad conduct, because they do not have such deep attachment to Kṛṣṇa. The *gopīs* have *mahābhāva* known as *rūḍha—bhāva* which no other women have. My Lord distributes the best auspiciousness to these *gopīs* who are ignorant of his greatness. They have exalted nature because they have realized Kṛṣṇa’s form:

*gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṁ*  
*lāvaṇya-sāram asamordhvam ananya-siddham*  
*dṛgbhiḥ pibanty anusavābhinavaṁ durāpam*  
*ekānta-dhāma yaśasaḥ śrīya aiśvarasya*
