**What austerities must the gopīs have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and extremely rare. SB 10.44.14**

Desiring on him, they meditated on him at all times and Kṛṣṇa became their debtor:

*tā man-manaskā tṛṣṭ-prāṇā*  
*mad-arthe tyakta-daihikāḥ*  
*mām eva dayitaṁ preṣṭham*  
*ātmānaṁ manasā gatāḥ*  
*ye tyakta-loka-dharmāś ca*  
*mad-arthe tān bibharmy aham*

**The minds of those** ***gopīs*** **are always absorbed in me, and their very lives are ever devoted to me. For my sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies, renouncing ordinary happiness in this life, as well as religious duties necessary for such happiness in the next life. I alone am their dearest beloved and, indeed, their very self. Therefore I take it upon myself to sustain them in all circumstances. SB 10.46.4**

Referring to that, Uddhava speaks the verse quoted in the text. The word *u i*ndicates amazement. There is no mercy for the dear woman famous as Lakṣmī with great love situated on the chest (*aṅg*e) of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha. She did not have the brilliance of the *gopīs* having *madhurya-prema*, glory and good qualities. Then what to speak of other women of Vaikuṇṭha (*svar-yosītām*) who had beauty and fragrance like gold lotuses and who had all amazing qualities. What to speak of the fortune of others? All other women were much inferior.

Mercy was not constantly given to others. When the occasion arose, it became manifest. Mercy was constantly manifested to those *gopīs* who were blessed with the arms of Kṛṣṇa around their necks. This means that since they were the most remarkable, they were the eternal lovers of Kṛṣṇa who himself was most remarkable. Just as they were the highest devotees of Kṛṣṇa, because of being most remarkable, they were also the best of Lakṣmīs They surpassed other Lakṣmīs. The sages who became *gopīs,* mentioned later, are not considered here, as they are secondary.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lakṣmī, endowed with great love, situated on the chest of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, did not attain such mercy. What to speak of other heavenly women? What to speak of ordinary women? Lakṣmī is most extraordinary in beauty, affection, love, good qualities and glory. Without that qualification she cannot remain on the chest of Nārāyaṇa. She has the utmost love (*nitānta-rateḥ*), endowed with beauty, fragrance, sweet voice, youth, taste and humor, which are relished by Nārāyaṇa, Indra and others. Love cannot become utmost (*nitānta*) without extreme beauty and sweetness. Beauty and fragrance of the lotus indicates all fragrance, beauty, youth etc. There is repetition to make the meaning clear.

### Text 41

***tās tridhā sādhana-parā devyo nitya-priyās tathā \|\|41\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are three types of** ***paroḍhā:*** ***sādhana-parā (*****caused by practice)*****, devī*** **(heavenly women) and** ***nitya-priyā (*****eternal condition)*****.***

### Text 42

***tatra sādhanaparāḥ—***  
***syur yauthikyas tv ayauthikya iti tatrādimā dvidhā \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sādhana-parā*** **is of two types:** ***yauthikī*** **and** ***ayautikī.***

### Text 43

***tatra yauthikyaḥ—***  
***yauthikyas tatra saṁbhūya gaṇaśaḥ sādhane ratāḥ \|***  
***dvividhās tās tu munayas tathopaniṣado matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***yauthikyas*** **are those who practice by mixing with others of a group. There are two types: the sage and the Upaniṣads.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Those who are in groups are *yautikya.* They meet with others and are engaged in *sādhana. Ganaśaḥ* means there are many groups. The *yauthikya* stays in one such group.

### Text 44-46

***tatra munayaḥ—***  
***gopālopāsakāḥ pūrvam aprāptābhīṣṭa-siddhayaḥ \|***  
***cirād udbuddha-ratayo rāma-saundarya-vīkṣayā*** *\|****\|44\|\|***  
***munayas tan-nijābhīṣṭa-siddhi-sampādane ratāḥ \|***  
***labdha-bhāvā vraje gopyo jātāḥ pādma itīritam \|\|45\|\|***  
***kathāpy anyā kila bṛhad-vāmane ceti viśrutiḥ \|***  
***siddhiṁ katicid evāsāṁ rāsārambhe prapedire \|***  
***iti kecit prabhāṣante prakaṭārthānusāriṇaḥ \|\|46\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The sages: Some sages, worshippers of Kṛṣṇa, not having fulfilled their desires after a long time, developed attraction on seeing the beauty of Rāma. Becoming absorbed in attaining their desired perfection, they finally attained the** ***bhāva*** **of** ***gopīs*** **in Vraja. This is related in** ***Padma Purāṇa.*** **Another story of this nature is told in** ***Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa.*** **Among them some attains perfection at the** ***rāsa-līlā.*** **In this way the best authorities clearly explain the statements of the Purāṇas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is said in the *Padma Purāṇa:*

*purā maharṣayaḥ sarve daṇḍakāraṇya-vāsinaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ hariṁ tatra bhoktum aicchan suvigraham \|\|*  
*te sarve strītvam āpannāḥ samudbhūtāś ca gokule \|*  
*hariṁ samprāpya kāmena tato muktā bhavārṇavāt \|\|*

**Previously all the great sages of Daṇḍaka forest, on seeing Rāma, desired to enjoy that beautiful form of Kṛṣṇa. They attained bodies of women and were born in Gokula. Attaining the Lord, they became liberated from the material world by their** ***prema.***

Here is the explanation. On seeing Rāma, the sages’ previous sentiments for Kṛṣṇa became activated, because of some similarity of Rāma with Kṛṣṇa. They then desired to enjoy the beautiful form of Kṛṣṇa (*suvigraham*), and asked for this benediction in their minds. By the mercy of Rāma, a desire tree, who remained silent, they all entered the wombs of cowherd women outside of Vraja as females. When those cowherd women were pregnant they came to Gokula. The sages were born there (*samudbhūtāḥ*). With great desire (*kāmena*), with the consciousness that they were married women, they attained Kṛṣṇa (*harim*). While in their homes they attained him, and became free from the material world. This means that having been confined to their rooms by their husbands, they gave up their material bodies made of *guṇas* and attained association with Kṛṣṇa in their spiritual bodies. It is said that some of them were kept in their homes. That obstacle was created to increase their longing and destroy their remaining *karmas.*

Another story about the sages is famous (*viśrutiḥ*) in the *Vāmana Purāṇa*. Among the sages some attains perfection at the *rāsa-līlā.* This is told in Padma Purāṇa. The best authorities (*kecid*) explain clearly (*prabhāśante*) the meaning of the statements in the two Purāṇas. They do not explain that the sages attained mere liberation. Their insight should be taken with full faith. There is no need of searching for another meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Jīva Gosvāmī explains the quotation from the *Padma Purāṇa.* On seeing Rāma, the sages developed *rati* for Kṛṣṇa. On seeing Sītā they developed devotion like the *gopīs.* Their goal follows what they saw. They followed the process of *rāgānuga-bhakti.* Without that, they could not attain positions as *gopīs.*

### Text 47-48

***atha upaniṣadaḥ—***  
***samantāt sūkṣma-darśinyo mahopaniṣado'khilāḥ \|***  
***gopīnāṁ vīkṣya saubhāgyam asamordhvaṁ suvismitāḥ*** *\|****\|47\|\|***  
***tapāṁsi śraddhayā kṛtvā premāḍhyā jajñire vraje \|***  
***vallavya iti paurāṇī tathaupaniṣadī prathā \|\|48\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**All the major Upaniṣads, which give elevated philosophy, seeing the unequalled good fortune of the** ***gopīs,*** **became very astonished. After performing austerities with faith, filled with** ***prema,*** **they were born in Vraja as cowherd women. This is the statement of the Purāṇas and Upaniṣads.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is mentioned in the *Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa (paurāṇi).* The Upaniṣads prayed to Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana:

*kandarpa-koṭi-lāvaṇye tvayi dṛṣṭe manāṁsi naḥ \|*  
*kāminī-bhāvam āsādya smara-kṣubdhānya-saṁśrayam \|\|*  
*yathā tal-loka-vāsinyaḥ kāmatvena gopikāḥ \|*  
*bhajanti ramaṇaṁ matvā cikīrṣājaninas tathā \|\|*

**Seeing you with more beauty than millions of Cupids, please make our minds, undoubtedly agitated by love, assume the mood of the** ***gopīs.*** **When we think of that enjoyment, our desire to act in the manner that the** ***gopīs*** **living on your planet serve you has manifested within us.**

Kṛṣṇa replied:

*durlabho durghaṭaś caiva yuṣmākaṁ sumanorathaḥ \|*  
*mayānumoditaḥ samyak satyo bhavitum arhati \|\| iti \|*

**Such desire rarely occurs and is difficult to fulfill, but permitted by me, it should come true.**

In the *Padma Purāṇa* it is also explained that Gāyatrī became a *gopī* and attained Kṛṣṇa. He spoke to the elder cowherds when Brahmā was married to her in the form of cowherd girl:

*mayā jñātvā tataḥ kanyā dattā caiṣā viriñcaye \|*  
*yuṣmākaṁ tu kule cāhaṁ deva-kāryārtha-siddhaye \|*  
*avatāraṁ kariṣyāmi mat-kāntā tu bhaviṣyati \|\| iti \|*

**Known by me, this girl has been married to Brahmā. But I will appear as an** ***avatāra*** **in your family to execute activities for the** ***devatās*** **and at that time she will be my lover.**

The Upaniṣads themselves have spoken of their birth in their famous prayers:

*nibhṛta-marun-mano-’kṣa-dṛḍha-yoga-yujo hṛdi yan*  
*munaya upāsate tad arayo ’pi yayuḥ smaraṇāt*  
*striya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo*  
*vayam api te samāḥ sama-dṛśo ’ṅghri-saroja-sudhāḥ*

**Simply by constantly thinking of him, the enemies of the Lord attained the same Supreme Truth whom sages fixed in yoga worship by controlling their breath, mind and senses. Similarly, we** ***śrutis,*** **who generally see you as all-pervading, will achieve the same nectar from your lotus feet that your consorts are able to relish because of their loving attraction to your mighty, serpentine arms, for you look upon us and your consorts in the same way. SB 10.87.21**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(He has the same commentary with the following addition). The desire of the Upaniṣads indicates *rāgānuga-bhakti*. In the *Bṛhat-vāmana Purāṇa*, Kṛṣṇa gives the following benediction:

*jāra-dharmeṇa susnehaṁ sudṛḍhaṁ sarvato’dhikam \|*  
*mayi samprāpya sarve’pi kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyatha \|\|*

**Attaining most firm affection for me as parakīya lovers, you will all become successful.**

They would attain the sentiments of married women in love with Kṛṣṇa, like the inhabitants of Gokula, who were *nitya-siddhas,* since that is what they requested and he could not give something else. The Upaniṣads followed after the *rāgātmika-bhakti* of the *nitya-siddhas* having *paroḍha-bhāva.* Since *rāganuga-bhakti* is defined as following after the *rāgātmika-bhaktas,* this was the nature of their *sādhana*. The Upaniṣads are distinguished by the word *api* to indicate that they revered the *nitya –siddha gopīs* and thus obtained the *gopīs’* consent. Without perfection of *rāgānuga* it is impossible for even Lakṣmī to attain the body of a *gopī* after long intense austerity.

*śrīḥ prekṣya kṛṣṇa-saundaryaṁ tatra lubdhā tatas tapaḥ \|*

**Lakṣmī, seeing the beauty of Kṛṣṇa, desired to attain him.** ***Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta*** **1.351**

But she could not attain Kṛṣṇa according to *Bhāgavatam:*

*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. SB 10.16.37**

*nāyaṁ śriyo ’ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ*  
*svar-yoṣitāṁ nalina-gandha-rucāṁ kuto ’nyāḥ*

**The** ***gopīs*** **received benedictions from the Lord that neither Lakṣmīdevī nor the most beautiful dancers in the heavenly planets could attain. SB 10.47.60**

Since the sages at Daṇḍaka forest attained *gopī* bodies, it can be inferred that they also performed *rāgānuga-bhakti.* It should be understood that *rāgānuga* arises from association with devotees who have similar tendencies.

### Text 49-51

***atha ayauthikyaḥ—***  
***tad-bhāva-baddha-rāgā ye janās te sādhane ratāḥ \|***  
***tad-yogyam anurāgaughaṁ prāpyotkaṇṭhānusārataḥ \|****\|****49\|\|***  
***tā ekaśo'thavā dvi-trāḥ kāle kāle vraje'bhavan \|***  
***prācīnāś ca navāś ca syur ayauthikyas tato dvidhā \|\|50\|\|***  
***nitya-priyābhiḥ sālokyaṁ prācīnāś ciram āgatāḥ \|***  
***vraje jātā navās tv etā martyāmartyādi-yonitaḥ \|\|51\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Individual attainment: Those persons who have great attached for the** ***paroḍhā-bhāva*** **and are absorbed in** ***rāgānuga sādhana,*** **develop intense** ***sādhana*** **arising from their longing. After some time they are born in Vraja singly, or in groups of two or three. There are two divisions of** ***ayauthikyas*****: senior and recent. Long before, the seniors attained the residence with the eternal** ***gopīs.*** **The recent devotees are born in Vraja after taking births as humans or** ***devatās.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They attain intense practice of *rāgānuga bhakti (anurāgaugham).* *Anurāgaugham* does not refer to the level of *anurāga,* for it is impossible to manifest *anurāga* in a *sādhaka* body. Senior devotees are those persons who attained perfection when Kṛṣṇa appeared as *avatāra* in previous *kalpas.* They did not attain perfection in the present *kalpa* when Kṛṣṇa appeared. They attained perfection in *kalpas* previous to the present one, but in the present *kalpa* they also appear along with Kṛṣṇa, and in future *kalpas* they will also appear with him.

The recent devotees will take birth in Vraja after being born as humans, devatās and Gandharvas (martyāmartyadi-yonitaḥ). Another meaning is that they are born from humans and non-humans—such as animals. Hiraṇyāṅgī was born from a deer. *hiraṇyāṅgī haridvarṇā hariṇī-garbha-sambhavā*: Hiraṇyāṅgī is golden in complexion, born of a deer. (*Radhā-kṛṣṇa- gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā*)

Some say there are also two types of *yauthikis.* In future appearances of Rāma, there will also be sages living in Daṇḍaka forest who will see the beauty of Rāma and become worshippers of Kṛṣṇa. It is understood that there should be different sages in the future when Rāma appears. When Kṛṣṇa later appears they will attain forms of *gopī*s, attaining perfection according to their *sādhana.* One cannot say that such sages will not appear in the future. When at the beginning of *rāsa-līlā* they are confined to their houses they will give up their bodies out of separation from Kṛṣṇa. Who are they? They cannot be the previous sages from the previous *kalpa,* for having attained *siddha* bodies it would not be suitable for them to give up those bodies again. One should not say that *yoga-māyā* will arrange for them to give their bodies. Such an arrangement would be unsuitable, since it is disgusting that *siddhas* would give up their spiritual bodies. Since there are unlimited *sādhaka bhaktas,* different sets of *bhaktas* become sages in every *kalpa.* When Kṛṣṇa appears, new sages have become *gopīs.* They give up their bodies when they are confined to their houses during the *rāsa-līlā*

Because the Upaniṣads are unlimited, in every *kalpa* other Upaniṣads perform *sādhana* and attain perfection. Thus there are two types of *yautikis*: accomplished ones and new ones. Apart from these two types of *yautikis*, when Kṛṣṇa appears in the future, others who are not in groups but almost perfect, will give up their bodies when confined to their houses by the līlā-śakti.

“If those present day persons practicing r*āgānuga* attain *prema* in some birth by going through the states of *niṣṭhā, ruci, āsakti,* they become qualified for service to the Lord. At the time of leaving the body, will they attain the positions of associates beyond the material world, or participate when the Lord descends as *avatāra*?” Since it is impossible for the transformations of *prema* such as *sneha, māna , praṇaya* to appear in the body of a *sādhaka,* by the power of associating in *gopī* bodies with *nitya-siddha gopīs* having *mahābhāva*, and by the seeing, hearing , remembering and chanting about the qualities of the Lord, they will certainly attain such a position.

Since these methods are very powerful, without them one cannot attain perfection as a *gopī.*

*gopīnāṁ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane*  
*kṣaṇaṁ yuga-śatam iva yāsāṁ yena vinābhavat*

**The young** ***gopīs*** **took the greatest pleasure in seeing Govinda come home, since for them even a moment was like a hundred** ***yugas.***  **SB 10.19.16**

The meaning is this. Who are the *gopīs?* Those for whom a moment seemed like a hundred *yugas* attained the supreme bliss. *Truṭir yugāyate*: half a second becomes as long as an entire age for us. (SB 10.31.15) This is a characteristic of *mahābhāva.* It is not seen that the *sādhaks* of this world enter into the pastimes of Vṛndāvana unmanifest in this world, whereas it is seen that the *siddhas* enter to those pastimes. Thus it is only a place for *siddhas,* for stages like sneha do not quickly manifest by ones’ own *sādhana.* Thus, by *yogamāyā*, devotees who have developed *prema* join at the time of Kṛṣṇa’s *avatāra* in the manifestation of Vṛndāvana in this world as a preliminary attainment. This can be inferred by seeing that *sādhakas,* various materialistic persons and *siddhās* all enter this earthly Vṛndāvana. It is the place for *sādhakas* and *siddhas*, where they can perfect their *bhāvas* before associating directly with Kṛṣṇa.

“How can the devotees with strong eagerness endure for such a long time?” This is not a long time at all, since there are unlimited universes. The manifest pastimes continue unbroken. The devotee attains a body of a *gopī* in Vṛndāvana of some other universe were the Vṛndāvana pastimes are appearing at that moment. That is the sequence.

To the devotee having great longing for direct service for a long time, who has developed *prema* by intense and constant *rāgānuga-sādhana*, the merciful Lord one time directly shows himself with his associates, with realization of service, even to a person in a *sādhaka* body, in a dream, though he has not developed *sneha* and other stages. He gives a spiritual *gopī* body endowed with proper *bhāvas*, as he gave to Nārada. Then, when Kṛṣṇa and his associates appear in a manifest Vṛndāvana, that body is born in a womb of a *gopī* by the arrangement of *yoga-māyā* in order to perfect *sneha* and other varieties of *prema.*

The pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in human pastimes with *gopīs* born of humans are famous. Without being born as a “human,” there can be no perfection. Though Lakṣmī accepted the exalted position of the *gopīs,* because she did not accept the permission to the *gopīs* to be born in a *gopī* womb, Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes with her could not take place.

### Text 52-53

***atha devyaḥ—***  
***deveṣv aṁśena jātasya kṛṣṇasya divi tuṣṭaye \|***  
***nitya-priyāṇām aṁśās tu yā jātā deva-yonayaḥ*** *\|****\|52\|\|***  
***atra devāvataraṇe janitvā gopa-kanyakāḥ \|***  
***tā aṁśinīnām evāsāṁ priya-sakhyo'bhavan vraje \|\|53\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The women** ***devatās:*** **When Kṛṣṇa in his expansions appear in the heavenly planets among the** ***devatās,*** **expansions of his** ***nitya-priyas*** **also appear to be born among the** ***devatās*** **to satisfy him. When Kṛṣṇa appears on earth, those expansions appear in Vraja as young cowherd girls and become** ***priya-sakhis*** **of the original consorts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This confirms what is said in *Bhāgavatam:*

*vasudeva-gṛhe sākṣād bhagavān puruṣaḥ paraḥ*  
*janiṣyate tat-priyārthaṁ sambhavantu sura-striyaḥ*

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore heavenly women should also appear in order to satisfy him. SB 10.1.23**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa appears as the *Manvantara avatāras* among the *devatās.* “But it is not suitable to say that his consort expansions become his *prāṇa-sakhis*. Those who are expansions enter into Kṛṣṇa when he appears. For instanced the expansions Droṇa and Dhaṛā entered into Nanda and Yaśodā when they appeared on earth.” That is true. There are three types of expansions of *nitya-priyās* situated among the planets of the *devatās.* Some persons in the heavenly planets become devotees of his pastimes by hearing about his pastimes from Nārada and others. These devotees are of three types: those who purely follow the associates in his pastimes; those who follow by identifying themselves as the associates (*ahaṅgrahopāsana*); and those who do not follow the associates. Among the first type are some of the *devatās*, who become *priya-sakhas* of Śridāma and Subala etc. Their wives become *priya-sakhīs* of Rādhā and other *gopīs.* Others become male and female friends of Nanda and Yaśodā and others. The second type (*ahaṁgrahopāsana*) merges into the male or female associates. Just as Dronā and Dharā merged into Nanda and Yaśodā, some sages merge into the cows, calves and birds of Vṛndāvana. The third type, having no desire for following the associates, does not attain the associates, because in order to attain the associates one must follow after them. An example is Lakṣmī. It is said:

*nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ*  
*jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ yathā bhaktimatām iha*

**Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but he is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self. SB 10.9.21**

The meaning is this. He is not available to those who are interested in *artha, dharma* and *kāma (dehinām*), to those interested in liberation (*jñāninām*) and to those *ātma-bhūtas* like Brahmā, Śiva and Lakṣmī. These three persons are mentioned in the previous verse:

*nemaṁ viriñco na bhavo na śrīr apy aṅga-saṁśrayā*  
*prasādaṁ lebhire gopī yat tat prāpa vimuktidāt*

**Neither Lord Brahmā, nor Lord Śiva, nor even the goddess of fortune, who is always the better half of the Supreme Lord, can obtain from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the deliverer from this material world, such mercy as received by mother Yaśodā. SB 10.9.20**

They are called *ātma-bhūta* (identify themselves as the Lord) because Brahmā and Śiva think of themselves as his *avatāras* and Lakṣmī identifies herself as the *śakti* of the Lord. For these three types of people the son of Yaśodā does not give happiness. However the son of Vikuṇṭha or the son of Kauśalya gives them happiness. The son of Yaśodā gives them grief. But he does give happiness to the devotees in Vraja (*iha*), to those with devotion to the son of Yaśodā (*iha*). The type of *bhakti* is described in other verses:

*striya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo*

**These women fully absorbed their minds in meditation on Lord Kṛṣṇa’s powerful arms, which are like the bodies of great serpents. SB 10.87.23**

*yathā tal-loka-vāsinyaḥ kāmatvena gopikāḥ \|*  
*bhajanti ramaṇaṁ matvā cikīrṣājaninas tathā \|\|*

**Thinking of that enjoyment, our desire to act in the manner that the** ***gopīs*** **living on your planet serve has manifested in us.** ***Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa***

The happiness he gives to persons with *bhakti* following the associates (like the Upaniṣads mentioned SB 10.87.23), he does not give to others. It is obtained by accepting the suffering of following humbly after the *gopīs* or other associates. It is difficult for Brahmā, Śiva or Lakṣmī, situated in their own planets, w

### Text 54

***atha nityapriyāḥ—***  
***rādhā-candrāvalī-mukhyāḥ proktāḥ nitya-priyā vraje \|***  
***kṛṣṇavan nitya-saundarya-vaidagdhyādi-guṇāśrayāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The eternal consorts: Rādhā and Candrāvalī are said to be the chief** ***nitya-priyās*** **in Vraja. Like Kṛṣṇa, they are the shelter of eternal beauty, grace and other qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If having one husband is respected in the Upaniṣads, how can Kṛṣṇa become the *upapati* for the *nitya-priyās* unless *māyā* operates? One who is eternally his beloved becomes his *parakīya* lover (when he appears on earth). That is explained here.

### Text 55

*tathā ca brahma-saṁhitāyāṁ (5.48)—*  
***ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhis***  
***tābhir ya eva nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ \|***  
***goloka eva nivasaty akhilātma-bhūto***  
***govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi \|\|55\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Brahma-saṁhitā:*** **I worship the Supreme Lord Govinda who, though regarding all the inhabitants as his very self, resides in Goloka exclusively with the young** ***gopīs,*** **who are embodiments of** ***madhura-rasa.*** **He accepts them as his wives, while they respond to his conjugal affection reciprocally.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Proof of the previous statement is given. Kṛṣṇa resides in Goloka with his *śaktis,* expansions of himself *(kalābhiḥ*), as his wives (*nija-rūpatayā*), not with apparent *parakīya* as in his appearance on earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is Brahmā’s glorification of Kṛṣṇa. The *gopīs* are expansions of Kṛṣṇa who has a form of eternity, knowledge and bliss. The *gopīs* have separate manifestations (*pratibhāvitābhiḥ*) of *rasas* filled with experience of bliss and knowledge. *Hlādinī sandhinī saṁvit tvayy ekā sarva-saṁśrayā:* the three energies *hladinī, samdhinī* and *saṁvit* have their shelter in you. (*Viṣṇu Purāṇa*) Or they possess *śṛṅgāra-rasa (rasa),* purely spiritual *prema (ānanda-cin-maya*) by which Kṛṣṇa manifests love for them and they manifest love for him. The word *prati* indicates the mutual exchange of love. They are his own form (nija-rūpatayā), *śaktis* arising from his *svarūpa. Śruti* says: *parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca*: it is said that the Lord has various intrinsic *śaktis* known as *jñāna, bala* and *kṛiyā. Viṣṇu Purāṇa* says *viṣṇu-śaktiḥ parā proktā*: the *śakti* of Viṣṇu is said to be supreme.

He resides in Goloka by means of sixty-four arts used in *śṛṅgāra-rasa,* in order to play constantly. He has the form of continuous Paramātmā in Kṛṣṇa-loka, above Vaikuṇṭha, and also in Gokula within the material realm as the giver of life to all beings (*akhilātmā-bhūtaḥ*), a form living among humans. The word Goloka is used to indicate both the place in the spiritual world and the place Gokula in the material world. For instance Brahmā-saṁhitā refers to the spiritual realm in the phrase *goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya devī-maheśa-hari-dhāma*. In *Hari-vaṁśa* (2.19.34-35) the following is found:

*gavām eva tu yo loko durāroho hi sā gatiḥ \|\|*  
*sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa sīdamānaḥ kṛtātmanā \|*  
*dhṛto dhṛtimatā vīra nighnatopadravān gavām \|\|*

**But it is very difficult to attain that place. And the planet protected personally by you (Gokula), O hero, and which destroys the suffering of the cows and other inhabitants, is the residence of the determined and disciplined devotees.**

The word *rakṣitaḥ* should be supplied. Since Goloka means both the planet in the spiritual word and the place on earth, in this verse *durārohaḥ hi sā gatiḥ* can mean that Gokula is most excellent. The word *eva* after Goloka indicates that planets in the spiritual world are excluded.

### Text 56-58

***tatra śāstra-siddhās tu rādhā candrāvalī tathā \|***  
***viśākhā lalitā śyāmā padmā śaibyā ca bhadrikā \|***  
***tārā vicitrā gopālī dhaniṣṭhā pālikādayaḥ \|\|\|***  
***candrāvalyeva somābhā gāndharvā rādhikaiva sā \|***  
***anurādhā tu lalitā naitāstenoditāḥ pṛthak \|\|57\|\|***  
***loka-prasiddha-nāmnyas tu ayaḥ \|\|58\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***nitya-priyās*** **mentioned in scriptures are Rādhā, Candrāvalī, Viśākhā, Lalitā, Śyāmā, Padmā, Śaibyā, Bhadrikā, Tārā, Vicitrā, Gopālī, Dhaniṣṭhā, and Pālikā. Somābhā is the same as Candrāvalī, Gāndharvā is Rādhikā and Anurādhā is Lalitā. Thus they are not named separately. Others famous among the people are Khañjanākṣī, Manoramā, Maṅgalā, Vimalā, Līlā, Kṛṣṇā, Śārī, Viśāradā, Tārāvalī, Cakorākṣī, Śaṅkarī and Kuṅkumā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Those famous in scripture are mentioned. Scriptures include *Bhaviṣyottara* and *Prahlāda-saṁhitā* of *Skanda Purāṇa*. In *Bhaviṣyottara* it is said:

*gopālī pālikā dhanyā viśākhā dhyāna-niṣṭhikā \|*  
*rādhānurādhā somābhā tārakā daśamī tathā \|\|*

**Instead of** ***dhyāna-niṣṭhikā*****, the word** ***dhaniṣṭikā*** **is also seen. Daśamī can mean Tārakā the tenth gopī, or Daśamī can be the name of another gopī. In** ***Skanda Purāṇa*** **Lalitā, Padmā, Bhadrā, Śaibyā and Śyāmalā are additionally mentioned.** ***Gopāla-tapanī Upaniṣad*** **mentions Rādhā as Gāndharvā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The proofs and reasoning for alternate names of Candrāvalī and others is given in *Vaiśṇava-toṣanī.*

***ity ādīnān tu śataśo yūthāni vraja-subhruvām \|***  
***lakṣa-saṅkhyāstu kathitā yūthe yūthe varāṅganāḥ \|\|59\|\|***

The numbers given are only representative. There are actually billions of *gopīs* in each group.
