## Chapter 4 - Description of Rādhā

## Outline

Rādhā

- Sixteen śṛṅgāra (accoutrements)
- Twelve ābharaṇa (ornaments)
- Qualities
- Her group:  
   1\. Sakhīs  
   2\. Nitya-sakhīs  
   3\. Prāṇa-sakhīs  
   4\. Priya-sakhīs  
   5\. Parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs

### Text 1-2

***tatrāpi sarvathā śreṣṭhe rādhā-candrāvalīty ubhe \|***  
***yūthayos tu yayoḥ santi koṭi-saṅkhyā mṛgīdṛśaḥ \|\|1\|\|***  
***abhūd ākulito rāsaḥ pramadā-śata-koṭibhiḥ \|***  
***puline yāmune tasminn ity eṣāgamikī prathā \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It was said that Rādhā and Candrāvalī are the best among the leaders. Their groups contain ten million** ***gopīs*** **each. The scriptures say that the** ***rāsa*** **dance took place on the bank of the Yamunā River with one billion** ***gopīs*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In the previous chapter (*tatrāpi)* it was established that the best were Rādhā and Candrāvalī. However, in the chapter on *sthāyi-bhāva* it will also be shown that Candrāvalī’s group is superior to all groups other than Rādhā’s group.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The scripture mentioned is *Krama-dīpikā*.

### Text 3

***tayor apy ubhayor madhye rādhikā sarvathādhikā \|***  
***mahā-bhāva-svarūpeyaṁ guṇair ativarīyasī \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Of the two, Rādhikā is far superior. She is the very form of** ***mahābhāva,*** **and excells in all qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā is the *svarūpa* of *mahābhāva.* *Brahma-saṁhitā* says that the *gopīs* are all filled with *bhakti-rasa*: *ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhiḥ. Bhakti (prema)* was also shown in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* to have the highest bliss (*śuddha-sattva-viśeṣātmā*). *Bhakti’s* condition of *rasa* is also established by this definition. Kṛṣṇa resides with *śaktis (kalābhiḥ)* eternally (*pratibhāvitabhiḥ*) endowed with *bhakti*-rasas full of knowledge and bliss.

*yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā*  
*sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ*  
*harāv abhaktasya kuto mahad-guṇā*  
*manorathenāsati dhāvato bahiḥ*

**The** ***devatās*** **constantly dwell with all good qualities in that person who has pure** ***bhakti*** **for the Lord. There are no good qualities in the non-devotee who chases after temporary material objects with desire for material pleasure. SB 5.18.12**

Thus it should be understood that these devotees, the gopīs, are endowed with the highest qualities. Though all the gopīs have elevated bhakti and are the very form of *bhakti-rasa,* among the *gopīs,* the *svarūpa* of *mahābhāva* and the manifestation of all qualities appear in the best devotee Rādhā. *Gautamīya-tantra,* speaking of the sage and other elements of the mantra says:

*devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā \|*  
*sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā \|\|*

**Rādhikā, filled with love for Kṛṣṇa is the** ***devatā*** **of the mantra. She is the personification of all Lakṣmīs, the most beautiful and most attractive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Prema-bhakti* was shown in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* to be filled with the highest bliss: *śuddha-sattva-viśeṣātmā.* Thus *prema* is established as the condition for *rasa.* *Brahma-saṁhitā* established that the *gopīs* are full of bliss *(ānanda-cin-maya). Mahābhāva* is the essential portion, the highest portion, after the stages of *sneha, praṇaya* and others in *prema-bhakti.* Jīva Gosvāmī has explained that this cannot take place without giving up regard for elders and *dharma*. Thus Rukmiṇī and others, though having *hlādinī-śakti*, do not have *mahābhāva.* The women of Vraja, portions of Rādhā, are portions of *mahābhāva,* but they are not the *svarūpa* of *mahābhāva* since they lack the essential portion of *mahābhāva* called *mādana.* Rivers, streams and ponds, though bodies of water, are not like the ocean. This is the position of Rādhā’s *mahābhāva*.

The highest suffering for the women of Vraja, most respectful to rules, is rejection by their authorities and relatives, not the pain of fire or death. Though they are aware that this will result from their relationship with Kṛṣṇa, their relationship with Kṛṣṇa gives happiness. This is the highest level of *rāga.* Taking shelter of that level, *anurāga* operates and becomes *mahābhāva*. Mahābhāva commences and becomes visible in the women of Vraja. It is not possible for this to manifest in the queens of Dvārakā. Pointing out these women, Uddhava said in amazement *yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā:* these ladies of Vraja abandoned their families and their advanced religious principles, even though to do so is very difficult. (SB 10.47.61)

### Text 4

***gopālottara-tāpanyāṁ yad gāndharveti viśrutā \|***  
***rādhety ṛk-pariśiṣṭe ca mādhavena sahoditā \|***  
***atas tadīya-māhātmyaṁ pādme devarṣiṇoditam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rādhā, known as Gāndharvā, is said to excel all others in** ***Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad*** **and she is described as being in the company of Mādhava in the** ***Rk-pariśiṣṭa*****. Nārada describes her as supreme in the** ***Rādhā-māhātmya*** **of** ***Padma Purāṇa*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā’s position is confirmed by quoting from *Padma Purāṇa* and *śruti.* He explains her name Gāndharvā in the first line. She is best because (*yat*) she is known to excel all other women (*viśrutā*) in the *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad*, going by the name Gāndharvā. In *Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa* she is said to excel all others because she is always with Mādhava. Her superiority is shown by the words *rādhayā mādhavo devo mādhavenaiva rādhikā vibhrājante janeṣv ā*: Mādhava resides with Rādhā, Rādhā resides with Mādhava. In her glorification in *Padma Purāṇa* she is described (*uditam*) as supreme. In another scripture it is said that a sage attained Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi by taking shelter of her glorious form since she was superior to all others.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author supports his statement by proof from scripture. *Tāsāṁ madhye śreṣṭhā gāndharvā hy uvāca:* the best among the *gopīs,* Rādhā, spoke (*Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* 2.6) *Tāṁ hi mukhyāṁ vidhāya pūrvam anukṛtvā tūṣṇīm āsuḥ*: putting the chief *gopī* in front, the *gopīs* then become silent. (*Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* 2.13) *Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa* says *rādhayā mādhavo devo mādhavenaiva rādhikā vibhrājante janeṣv ā*. This means there is no other *gopīs* like her. In order to destroy the doubt that Rādhā is singled out as the dearest among the group only in the sense that a king is singled out when expressing a group, it is then said *ekā advitīyā:* she is without compare.

### Text 5

***tathā hi—***  
***yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṁ priyaṁ tathā \|***  
***sarva-gopīṣu saivaikā viṣṇor atyanta-vallabhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Just as Rādhā is dear to Kṛṣṇa, her** ***kuṇḍa*** **is dear to him. Among all the** ***gopīs*** **Rādhā is dearest to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The word Viṣṇu here means Kṛṣṇa, who is called Viṣṇu because he spreads himself everywhere. The root *viṣ* means to spread. Rādhā is dear to Kṛṣṇa who is spread with *śṛṅgāra-rasa,* since the word *priya* is used in this sentence*.* Just as Rādhā is dear to Kṛṣṇa who spreads out and embraces the soul, intelligence, body and senses of Rādhā--her *kuṇḍa* is dear to Kṛṣṇa (*viṣṇoḥ*), who spreads himself out into the water, steps, groves, gardens, flowers, fruits, birds and their cooing by bathing, sitting, lying down, playing, seeing, smelling, tasting and hearing at that *kuṇḍa.* “But it is said that other *gopīs* are also dear to Kṛṣṇa.” That is true. Embracing them all by manifesting himself in unlimited forms (spreading himself—*viṣṇoḥ*) he shows intense affection. Because it is said *rādhikā-yūtha evāyaṁ modano na tu sarvataḥ*: *modana* exists only in Rādhā’s group (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi.*15.176), her group is also the best among all groups. And then her superiority to all others is established:

*sarva-bhāvodgamollāsī mādano’yaṁ parāt paraḥ \|*  
*rājate hlādinī-sāro rādhāyām eva yaḥ sadā \|\| \[u.nī.15.219\]*

***Mādana,*** **the essence of** ***hḷādinī-śakti,*** **superior to** ***mohana,*** **making all** ***bhāvas*** **shine, is continually present in Rādhā.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.219.**

Her *kuṇḍa* is similar to herself. *Premāsmin bata rādhikeva labhate yasyāṁ sakṛt snānataḥ:* bathing once in that *kuṇḍa* one attains *prema.* (*Govinda-līlāmṛta* 7.102)

### Text 6

***hlādinī yā mahā-śaktiḥ sarva-śakti-varīyasī \|***  
***tat-sāra-bhāva-rūpeyam iti tantre pratiṣṭhitā \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is explained in** ***Gautamīya-tantra*** **that Rādhā is the essence of that great** ***śakti*** **called** ***hlādinī*****, the best of all** ***śaktis.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Viṣṇu Purāṇa* 1.12.68 says:

*hlādinī sandhinī saṁvit tvayy ekā sarva-saṁsthitau \|*  
*hlāda-tāpa-karī miśrā tvayi no guṇa-varjite \|\|*

**In you who are the shelter of all spiritual qualities exist the energies of** ***hlādinī, sandhinī*** **and** ***saṁvit.*** **In you who are devoid of material qualities, the mixture of happiness and distress found in the material world does not exist.**

*Sarvajña-sūkta* says:

*hlādinyā saṁvid-āśliṣṭaḥ sac-cid-ānanda īśvaraḥ \|*  
*svāvidyā-saṁvṛto jīvaḥ saṅkleśa-nikarākaraḥ \|\|*

**The Lord full of eternity, knowledge and bliss is embraced by the** ***hlādinī*** **and** ***saṁvit śaktis.*** **The** ***jīva*****, the very form of suffering, is surrounded by his own ignorance.**

It is well known that the *hlādinī-śakti* is the best of all *śaktis*. Its essence, the peak of *mahābhāva* called *mādana,* is non-different from and takes the form of Rādhā. It is explained in the *Gautamīya-tantra* that Rādhā is the essence of the *hlādinī-śakti*. This is the order of the words. .

### Text 7

***suṣṭhu-kānta-svarūpeyaṁ sarvadā vārṣabhānavī \|***  
***dhṛta-ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgārā dvādaśābharaṇānvitā \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rādhā, the very form of the highest beauty, has sixteen accoutrements and twelve ornaments.**

### Text 8

***tatra suṣṭhu-kānta-svarūpā, yathā śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyam—***  
***kacās tava sukuñcitā mukham adhīra-dīrghekṣaṇaṁ***  
***kaṭhora-kuca-bhāg-uraḥ kraśima-śāli madhya-sthalam \|***  
***nate śirasi dorlate karaja-ratna-ramyau karau***  
***vidhūnayati rādhike tri-jagad eṣa rupotsavaḥ \|\|8\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**She is the form of the highest beauty, in the words of Kṛṣṇa: Your hair is nicely curled. Your face has unsteady, long eyes. Your chest holds to firm breasts. Your waist is thin. Your shoulders are low. Your hands have pleasing, jewel-like fingernails. O Rādhā! This festival of beauty makes the three worlds tremble.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks this verse. *Nate śirasi dorlate* means the two shoulders (tops of the two arms) are lowered. *Bhujā-śiras* (shoulder) is found in the *Amara-koṣa*. Her beauty cannot be equated with other beauty, but makes the three worlds tremble. This means she derides the three worlds by the pride of her beauty. The verb is in the causative. There is another version of this verse:

*kacās tava sukuñcitā mukham adhīra-dīrghākṣi-bhāguraḥ*  
*pṛthu ghana-stanaṁ sphurita-madhyam uccaiḥ kṛśam \|*  
*bhujā niṭilam ānataṁ kara-yugaṁ nakha-śrīdharaṁ vidhūnayati.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks this verse. The upper part of the arms means the shoulders. They are bent over. Her hands are naturally beautiful with the jewels of her finger nails. By wearing ornaments, their beauty would be unlimited.

### Text 9

***atha dhṛta-ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgārā—***  
***snātā nāsāgra-jāgran-maṇi-rasita-paṭā sūtriṇī baddha-veṇī***  
***sottaṁsā carcitāṅgī kusumita-cikura sragviṇī padma-hastā \|***  
***tāmbūlāsyoru-bindu-stavakita-cibukā kajjalākṣī sucitrā***  
***rādhālaktojjvalāṅghriḥ sphurati tilakinī ṣoḍaśā-kalpinīyam \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The sixteen accoutrements: Rādhā, freshly bathed, shines with sixteen accoutrements: a pearl shining at the tip of her nose, a colored cloth, a sash around her waist, tied up braid, ear ornaments, anointed limbs, flowers in her hair, garland around her neck, lotus in her hand, betel nut in her mouth, musk dot on her chin, mascara on her eyes, patterns on her cheeks, lac on her feet, and** ***tilaka*** **on her forehead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ṣūtriṇī* means “wearing a belt.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala speaks to Kṛṣṇa when he is returning to Vraja in the evening and sees Rādhā in a garden. She has a gleaming pearl at the tip of her nose. She has a belt around her waist, or a cord around her neck. She has ornaments in her ears (*uttaṁsa*). She has a musk dots on her chin. She has *makarī* designs on her cheeks (*sucitrā*).

### Text 10

***atha dvādaśābharaṇāśritā—***  
***divyaś cūḍā-maṇīndraḥ puraṭa-viracitāḥ kuṇḍala-dvandva-kāñci-***  
***niṣkāś cakrī-śalākā-yuga-valaya-ghaṭāḥ kaṇṭha-bhūṣormikāś ca \|***  
***hārās tārānukāra-bhuja-kaṭaka-tulākoṭayo ratna-kḷptās***  
***tuṅgā pādāṅgurīya-cchavir iti ravibhir bhūṣaṇair bhāti rādhā \|\|10\|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The twelve ornaments: Rādhā shines like the sun with twelve ornaments: her shining crown jewel, her two gold earrings, her gold belt, her medallion, her two** ***cakī-śalākas*****, her two bracelets, her throat ornament, her rings, her necklace, her arm bands glowing like a constellation, her anklets made of jewels, and her dazzling toe rings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *niṣkā* is an ornament worn over the heart. The *cakrī-śalākā* is an ear ornament with a small wheel design and a pin which pierces the ear hole. Rādhā shines with these twelve ornaments which are like suns.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *cūḍāmaṇi* is a head ornament. *Niṣkā* is a medallion. *Cakrī* and *śaklākā* are worn on the upper part of the ears. *Ūrmikā* are rings. *Tārānukāra* means resembling constellations. *Katakā* are arm bands. *Tulākoti* are anklets. Her toe rings shine greatly.

### Text 11-15

***atha vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ kīrtyante pravarā guṇāḥ \|***  
***madhureyaṁ nava-vayāś calāpāṅgojjvala-smitā \|\|11\|\|***  
***cāru-saubhāgya-rekhāḍhyā gandhonmādita-mādhavā \|***  
***saṅgīta-prasarābhijñā ramya-vāṅ narma-paṇḍitā \|\|12\|\|***  
***vinītā karuṇā-pūrṇā vidagdhā pāṭavānvitā \|***  
***lajjā-śīlā sumaryādā dhairya-gāmbhīrya-śālinī \|\|13\|\|***  
***suvilāsā mahābhāva-paramotkarṣa-tarṣiṇī \|***  
***gokula-prema-vasatir jagac-chreṇī-lasad-yaśāḥ \|\|14\|\|***  
***gurv-arpita-guru-snehā sakhī-praṇayitā-vaśā \|***  
***kṛṣṇa-priyāvalī-mukhyā santatāśrava-keśavā \|***  
***bahunā kiṁ guṇās tasyāḥ saṅkhyātītā harer iva \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The outstanding qualities of Rādhā are glorified. She is beautiful, possesses new youth, has fickle glances, has a bright smile, beautiful lines of fortune, a fragrance that frenzies Kṛṣṇa, is skilful at singing, has pleasant voice, is expert at joking, is humble, compassionate, sly, clever, shy, respects proper conduct, is patient, inscrutable, coy, manifests thirst for Kṛṣṇa with the highest state of** ***mahābhāva,*** **is the abode of** ***prema*** **in Gokula, has lustrous fame, is the object of great affection from elders, is controlled by affection of her friends, is chief of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, and constantly controls Kṛṣṇa. What more can be said? Her qualities, like Kṛṣṇa’s, cannot be counted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā is the queen of Vṛndāvana, for in the *Purāṇa* it said *rādhā vṛndāvane vane*: Rādhā rules in the forest of Vṛndāvana. Her qualities are listed starting with sweetness and ending with having obedience of Keśava at all times. *Āśrava* means “following the words” according to *Amara-koṣa.* Qualities of her limbs are the first six till her fragrance. The three qualities till her joking are qualities of her speech. The qualities will her *mahābhāva* are mental qualities. After that are qualities in relationship to others. Some are not clear in their classification.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pāṭava* means clever. *Vilāsa* (coy) means gestures indicating joy, as well as smiling, goose bumps, change of color and efforts. She has extreme thirst for Kṛṣṇa with the highest manifestation of *mahābhāva*. She has full (*guru)* affection for elders. She makes Kṛṣṇa follow her words.  *Āśrava* means “situated in the words” according to *Amara-koṣa.*  There are six qualities relating to the body. There are three qualities related to speech. There are ten qualities related to the mind starting with humility. There are six qualities related to relationships with others. In all there are twenty-five qualities.

### Text 16-19

***ity aṅgokti-manaḥ-sthās te para-sambandha-gās tathā \|***  
***guṇā vṛndāvaneśvaryā iha proktāś caturvidhāḥ \|\|16\|\|***  
***mādhuryaṁ cārutā navyaṁ vayaḥ kaiśora-madhyamam \|***  
***saubhāgya-rekhā pādādi-sthitāś candra-kalādayaḥ \|\|17\|\|***  
***sādhumārgād acalanaṁ maryādety uditaṁ budhaiḥ \|***  
***lajjābhijātya-śīlādyair dhairyaṁ duḥkha-sahiṣṇutā \|\|18\|\|***  
***vyaktatvāl lakṣitatvāc ca nānyeṣāṁ lakṣaṇaṁ kṛtam \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These are the four types of qualities of Rādhā’s body, speech, mind and relationship with others. The word** ***madhurya*** **means beauty. New youth means she is in the middle of** ***kaiśora*** **period. The auspicious marks such as the crescent moon are on her feet and other limbs.** ***Maryāda*** **means she is firm in following the proper path.** ***Lajjā*** **means both natural and cultivated shyness.**  ***Dhairya*** **means toleration of suffering. Because their meaning is clear, the other qualities are not explained in detail.**

### Text 20

***tatra madhurā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (1.32)—***  
***balād akṣṇor lakṣmīḥ kavalayati navyaṁ kuvalayaṁ***  
***mukhollāsaḥ phullaṁ kamala-vanam ullaṅghayati ca \|***  
***daśāṁ kaṣṭām aṣṭā-padam api nayaty āṅgika-rucir***  
***vicitraṁ rādhāyāḥ kim api kila rūpaṁ vilasati \|\|20\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Beauty, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: How the remarkable beauty of Rādhā shines! The beauty of her eyes devours forcibly the fresh blue lotus. The splendor of her face surpasses a forest of blossoming lotuses. The luster of her body defeats gold.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a statement of Paurṇamāsī*. Aṣṭāpadam* is gold. *Vīra-rasa* is invoked by the conquering nature of her beauty. The sounds used in the third line suggest *ojas* and are not unsuitable for *vīra-rasa.*

### Text 21

***atha nava-vayāḥ—***  
***śroṇiḥ syandanatāṁ kṛśodari kuca-dvandvaṁ kramāc cakratāṁ***  
***bhrūś cāpa-śriyam īkṣaṇa-dvayam idaṁ yāty āśugatvaṁ tava \|***  
***saināpatyam ataḥ pradāya bhuvi te kāmaḥ paśūnāṁ patiṁ***  
***dhunvan jitvara-māninaṁ tvayi nijaṁ sāmrājya-bhāraṁ nyadhāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**New youth: O thin-waisted Rādhā! Your waist is the chariot, your breasts are the** ***cakra*** **weapon, your brow is the bow, and your eyes are the arrows. In order to conquer Kṛṣṇa who thinks he is the victor, Cupid has given you responsibility for his kingdom, giving you the post of commander of his army.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a messenger speaking.  *Cakratām* can refer to a *cakravāk*a bird or a *cakra* weapon. *Āśugatvam* means speed and an arrow. *Paśūnām patim* means Kṛṣṇa and Śiva.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a messenger speaking. *Cakratām* can refer to a *cakravāka* bird or a *cakra* weapon. *Āśugatvam* means speed and an arrow. *Paśūnām patim* means Kṛṣṇa and Śiva.

*Saināpatyam* means being a commander. The intention is “Do not delay in releasing the weapon.”

### Text 22

***atha capalāpāṅgī—***  
***taḍid aticalatāṁ te kiṁ dṛgantād apāṭhīd***  
***vidhu-mukhi taḍito vā kiṁ tavāyaṁ dṛgantaḥ \|***  
***dhruvam iha gurutābhūt tvad-dṛg-antasya rādhe***  
***varam atijavināṁ me yena jigye mano'pi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her fickle glance: O moon-faced Rādhā! Has lightning learned its unsteady nature from your glance? Or has your glance learned this art from the lightning? Your glance is certainly the best teacher, for it has even conquered my quick mind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks this verse*. Apāṭhīt* means “has learned” according to *Ākhyāta-candrikā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Apāṭhīt* means “has learned.” *Gurutā* means “excelling in teaching.” By your glance (*yena)* my mind is conquered. The last line means “Though it is pursued by the very quick mind, the glance surpasses my mind and controls my mind.”

### Text 23

***atha ujjvala-smitā—***  
***tava vadana-vidhau vidhauta-madhyāṁ***  
***smita-sudhayādhara-lekhikām udīkṣya \|***  
***sakhi laghur aghabhic-cakora-varyaḥ***  
***pramada-madoddhura-buddhir ujjihīte \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her dazzling smile: O friend! Spying the thin line of a sweet smile in the pure middle portion of your lips on your moon-like face, the best of** ***cakora*** **birds (who subsists on moonbeams), the destroyer of suffering, with intelligence wild because of bliss and pride, is coming here quickly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Laghu* means quick or attractive. *Ujjihīte* means “manifests.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks this verse. Rādhā has a sweet smile because of her joy on seeing Kṛṣṇa. Though she tried to hide the smile, it still appeared. *Vidhauta-madhyām* means “the smile visible on the middle portion of the lips.” Kṛṣṇa saw this slight smile that appeared for an instant. He began to think. It will spread out to become a kiss. “He will kiss you because he is free of sin (*agha-bhit*) and the lips are pure or cleansed (*vidhauta*), suitable for him. I can see that you also are inclined to this by the sweetness manifest on your lips, since he destroys secret suffering (*agha-bhit*).” This joke is suggested. Or, not seeing the inner purity of the smile, though it is pure, he will destroy its impurity *(agha*). *Agha-bhit* also means the killer of Aghāsura*. Smṛti* says *prāyo vīra-ratāḥ striyaḥ*: women are attracted to bravery. *Laghu* means “he comes quickly.” He has wild intelligence because of bliss and pride (*pramada-mada*). “This is not expected if we were not close by.” Therefore we should quickly leave this place. This joke is hinted.

### Text 24

***atha cāru-saubhāgya-rekhāḍhyā—***  
***aghahara bhaja tuṣṭiṁ paśya yac candralekhā-***  
***valaya kusuma vallī kuṇḍalākāra bhāgbhiḥ \|***  
***abhidadhati nilīnām atra saubhāgyarekhā-***  
***vitatibhir anuviddhāḥ suṣṭhu rādhāṁ padāṅkāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her auspicious marks: O destroyer of suffering! Be satisfied! See here! The marks on Rādhā’s feet, endowed with groups of auspicious lines like the crescent moon, bracelet, flower, vine and earring, tell her hidden nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Abhidadhati* means “they tell.”  *Anuviddhā* means endowed. The marks like moon are only some of the lines. These auspicious marks are described in the *Varāha-saṁhitā*, astrological scriptures, *Kāśī-khaṇḍa, Matsya* and *Garuḍa Purāṇas.* At the base of the big toe is a barley corn. Below that is a *cakra,* a flower and vine with a crescent moon. At the base of the middle down to the middle of the foot is a line. At the base of the little toe is a goad. This makes seven marks. On the right foot, at the base of the big toe is a conch. On the heel there is a fish. At the base of the little toe there is a sacrificial altar. Above the fish are a chariot, hill, earring, club and spear. This makes eight marks on the right foot. The marks on the left hand are now described, there are three other lines which are well know. There is a long life line (heart line) starting from between the forefinger and middle finger, going to the edge of the hand near the little finger. There is another line (head line) from the edge of the hand, ending between the forefinger and thumb. There is another line rising from the wrist close to the base of the thumb, curving and joining the head line, and ending between the forefinger and thumb. Other lines are described. On the tips of the five fingers are *nandyāvartas.* At the base o f the small finger is a temple. At the base of the heart line is an arrow feather. At the base of the middle finger is a bull. At the base of the little finger is a goad. There are also a fan, a desire tree, a post, an arrow, a spear and a garland. This makes eighteen marks on the left hand. On the right hand there are three similar lines. At the tips of the five fingers are five conches. At the base of the forefinger is a *cāmara.* At the base of the little finger is a goad. There are also a palace, drum, thunderbolt, cart yoke, bow, sword and vase. This makes seventeen marks. The left foot has seven, the right foot as eight, the left hand has eighteen and the right hand has seventeen. The total is fifty auspicious marks.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Madhumaṅgala speaks this verse. The foot marks tell about the hidden nature (*nilīnām*) of Rādhā. The foot marks are endowed (*anuviddhāḥ*) with groups of lines indicating auspiciousness. The lines are then described, in a representative way. These auspicious marks are described in the *Varāha-saṁhitā,* astrological scriptures, *Kāśī-khaṇḍa, Matsya* and *Garuḍa Purāṇas.* At the base of the big toe is a barley corn. Below that is a *cakra.* Below that is an umbrella. Below that is a bracelet. From between the second toe and big toe a lines starts and curves down half the foot. At the base of the middle tow is a lotus. Below the lotus is a flagpole with flag. At the base of the little toe is a goad. On the heel is a half moon. Above that is a vine and flower. This makes eleven marks.

On the right foot, at the base of the big toe is a conch. At the base of the little toe is an earring. Between the middle and second toe is a mountain. On the heel is a fish. Above the fish is a chariot. On one side of the chariot is a club and on the other side a spear. This makes eight marks on the right foot. On both feet there are nineteen marks.

On the left hand marks are described for devotee meditation. These are not listed in the text. There is a long life line (heart line) starting from between the forefinger and middle finger, going to the edge of the hand near the little finger. There is another line (head line) from the edge of the hand, ending between the forefinger and thumb. There is another line rising from the wrist close to the base of the thumb, bending, and joining the head line, and ending between the forefinger and thumb. On the tips of the five fingers are *nandyāvartas.* At the base o f the small finger is a temple. At the base of the heart line is an arrow feather. At the base of the middle finger is a bull. At the base of the little finger is a goad. There are also a fan, a desire tree, a post, an arrow, a spear and a garland. This makes eighteen marks on the left hand.

On the right hand there are three similar lines. At the tips of the five fingers are five conches. At the base of the forefinger is a *cāmara.* At the base of the little finger is a goad. There are also a palace, drum, thunderbolt, cart yoke, bow, sword and vase. This makes seventeen marks on the right hand. That makes thirty-five marks on the hands.

### Text 25

*atha gandhonmādita-mādhavā—*  
*vallī-maṇḍala-pallavālibhir itaḥ saṅgopanāyātmano*  
*mā vṛndāvana-cakravartini kṛthā yatnaṁ mudhā mādhavi \|*  
*bhrāmyadbhiḥ sva-virodhibhiḥ parimalair unmādanaiḥ sūcitāṁ*  
*kṛṣṇas tāṁ bhramarādhipaḥ sakhi dhuvan dhūrto dhruvaṁ dhāsyati \|\|25*

**Перевод:**

**Her fragrance which frenzies Kṛṣṇa: O Mādhavī! Do not uselessly try to hide yourself by the leaves of the creepers. O friend! Kṛṣṇa, the king of the gallants, that rascal, making you shake, will certainly enjoy you, who are like a jasmine flower, detected by your fragrance. That fragrance betrays you and wanders about to incite him to madness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa cannot be driven away because of begin controlled by the highest *prema.* Mādhavī refers to Rādhā or the jasmine flower. *Dhāsyati* means “he will drink” from the root *dhe*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks. O jasmine flower (*mādhavi*)! This also means “O Rādhā!” It is impossible for you to avoid Kṛṣṇa even for a moment. Being controlled by her lover Mādhava, she is called Mādhavī. She is addressed as the empress of Vṛndāvana since she is most excellent among all the *gopīs* and creepers. Her fragrance is her enemy, unable to bear the fact that she try to hide herself. It wanders here and there trying to find Kṛṣṇa, and will reveal Rādhā’s identity to him. She hints “I should not be falsely blamed in front of him.” Kṛṣṇa, frenzied by the fragrance because of its excellent and uniqueness in quantity and type, does not distinguish proper time or place. *Dhāsyati* means “will drink, support or nourish.” It comes from the root *dhe*: to drink. *Bhramara* refers to a lusty person and a bee.

### Text 26

***atha saṅgīta-prasarābhijñā—***  
***kṛṣṇa-sāra-hara-pañcama-svare***  
***muñca gīta-kutukāni rādhike \|***  
***prekṣate’tra hariṇānudhāvitāṁ***  
***tvāṁ na yāvad atiroṣaṇaḥ patiḥ \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her skill in singing: O Rādhā, possessing the fifth note which steals the self-control of Kṛṣṇa! Stop singing that attractive song because your angry husband will see you being pursued by him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

O Rādhā who has the fifth note which steals away Kṛṣṇa’s self-control (*kṛṣṇa-sāra*)! It also means a black deer. Your husband will see you being followed by Kṛṣṇa or the deer.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks this verse. *Kṛṣṇa-sara* means the self-control of Kṛṣṇa or the black deer. The husband will see you being followed by a deer or by Kṛṣṇa *(hariṇā*). Chaste women should not sing so that deer become attracted. The hint is that she should to some solitary place way from people if she wants to sing.

### Text 27

***atha ramya-vāk—***  
***suvadane vadane tava radhike***  
***sphurati keyam ihākṣara-mādhurī \|***  
***vikalatāṁ labhate kila kokilaḥ***  
***sakhi yayādya sudhāpi mudhārthatām \|\|27\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her pleasing voice: O Rādhā with a beautiful face! O friend! What is this sweetness of syllables that appears in your mouth? By this, the cuckoo becomes voiceless and nectar becomes useless!**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. The cuckoo loses his sweet voice (*vikalatām*), or becomes silent, and nectar becomes useless (*mudhārthatām*).

### Text 28

***atha narma-paṇḍitā—***  
***vaṁśyās tvam upādhyāyaḥ***  
***kim upādhyāyī tavātra vaṁśī vā \|***  
***kula-yuvati-dharma-haraṇād***  
***asti yayor nāparaṁ karma \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her skill at joking: Do you teach the flute or does the flute teach you? There is no other engagement for both of you than stealing the good conduct of young chaste women.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Does the flute sing, dependent on me? Or do I sing, dependent on the flute? The young women give up *dharma* because they are not chaste. What fault is there in me or the flute?” This is how Kṛṣṇa would answer Rādhā’s questions.

### Text 29

***yathā vā—***  
***deva prasīda vṛṣa-vardhana puṇya-kīrte***  
***sādhvī-gaṇa-stana-śivārcana-nitya-pūta \|***  
***nirmañchanaṁ tava bhaje ravi-pūjanāya***  
***snātāsmi hanta mama na spṛśa na spṛśāṅgam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Lord! Be pleased with me! O increaser of** ***dharma*****! O person famous for good acts! You are purified constantly by worship of Śiva, performed in the hearts of chaste women. I worship you. I have bathed in order to worship the sun, so do not touch my limbs! Do not touch me!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Praising him she says “O increaser of *dharma*!” I am going to worship the sun. You should not touch me since Śiva devotees should not touch worshippers of other *devatās*. As criticism she says “O Lord!” as a joke. O cutter of *dharma (vṛṣa-vardhana)*! She indicates the opposite when she says “you are famous for good acts.” “You are famous for sin*.” Sādhvi* indicates women dedicated to their husbands. “You are eternally purified” means jokingly “You are eternally condemned.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Unsatisfied because Kṛṣṇa answered her cleverly, she takes aim at Kṛṣṇa with this verse. You are the cause of increase of *dharma.* Therefore, you are famous for your good acts. Therefore you have the pious women perform worship of Śiva in their hearts in order to increase their fame and *dharma.* You are daily purified by that worship of Śiva. Not a day goes by without their performing worship. Without being purified in that way, eating and drinking would not be pleasurable for you.

“But I will become successful just by touching you, the devotee of the sun.” I have just bathed. It will be troublesome for me to bathe again and it will take time. Therefore do not touch me. *Vṛṣa-vardhana* also has the opposite meaning: one who is most irreligious. The same phrase means “destroyer of *dharma*” since *vardha* means to cut.

### Text 30

***atha vinītā—***  
***api gokule prasiddhā bhrū-bhramibhiḥ parijanair niṣiddhāpi \|***  
***pīṭhaṁ mumoca rādhā bhadrikām api dūrataḥ prekṣya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her humility: Rādhā, famous in Gokula, though forbidden by her relatives with raised brows, leaves her seat on seeing at a distance Bhadrikā approaching.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Bhadrā is someone of lower status. Someone speaks to Kṛṣṇa about the qualities of Rādhā. When he hears such things and enjoys it because of the strong *madhura-rasa* in her. Other statements later should be understood in the same way. The author also says:

*rāga-raṅgam anugān aparīkṣā-kāriṇi priyatame sati rādhā \|*  
*bhadrikām api vidhāya purastād ātmanānugatatāṁ bata cakre*

**Being most dear, not testing her followers for attachment, Rādhā puts Bhadrikā in front and follows behind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Madhura-rasa* is nourished when the hero relishes the qualities of the heroine. This should be the meditation.

### Text 31

***yathā vā, vidagdha-mādhave (5.15)—***  
***bhūyo bhūyaḥ kali-vilasitaiḥ sāparādhāpi rādhā***  
***ślāghyenāhaṁ yad agharipuṇā bāḍham aṅgīkṛtāsmi \|***  
***tatra kṣāmodari kim aparaṁ kāraṇaṁ vaḥ sakhīnāṁ***  
***dattāmodāṁ praguṇa-karuṇā-mañjarīm antareṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Again and again I have offended Kṛṣṇa by playful quarrels. Praiseworthy, he is still willing to accept me. O slender-waisted girl! What reason is there for his taking me back other than the fragrant blossom of the great quality of mercy of you, my friends?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Unsatisfied because the previous example stimulates *madhura-rasa* with difficulty, the author gives another example. She has had many quarrels with Kṛṣṇa (*bhūyaḥ bhūyah*), because of natural qualities (*kali-vilāsitaiḥ*). The word *rādhā* can mean one who causes offenses (*aparādha*). Thus the line indicates the derivation of her name. Rādhā, whose very name means offender, has offended Kṛṣṇa many times with quarrels arising from her nature. This meaning would not be inferred except for the unfortunate circumstances she expresses. Except for the fragrant (*dattāmoda*) flower of mercy arising from your excellent qualities, using that mercy as my ornament, I have been accepted by him. Because he is controlled by your love, he accepts me after hearing that I am the object of your mercy, when you plead with him to give me some happiness.

### Text 32

***atha karuṇā-pūrṇā—***  
***tārṇa-sūci-śikhayāpi tarṇakaṁ***  
***viddha-vaktram avalokya sāsrayā \|***  
***lipyate kṣatam avāpta-bādhayā***  
***kuṅkumena kṛpayāsya rādhayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her great compassion: Seeing a calf whose mouth was pierced by piece of straw, compassionate Rādhā began to weep. Filled with grief, she applied** ***kuṁkuma*** **to the wound.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The calf belonged to milking cow to be offered to Kṛṣṇa. Instead of *kṛpayā* the word *sahasā* (immediately) is sometimes seen. Here is another verse of the author:

*dhik kaṭhora-hṛdayāsmi rādhikā yac ciraṁ viraham asya hā sahe \|*  
*taṁ saheta kim iyaṁ vraja-prajā komaleti mama hṛd vidīryate \|\|*

**Rādhā says “I am so hard-hearted that I tolerate long separation from Kṛṣṇa.” How can soft Rādhā, resident of Vraja, tolerate this separation? My heart is pierced.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. The calf belonged to milking cow to be offered to Kṛṣṇa. The calf’s mouth was pierced by the tip of a tender piece of grass. Her tears show her great compassion.

### Text 33

***atha vidagdhā—***  
***ācāryā dhātu-citre pacana-viracanā-cāturī-cāru-cittā***  
***vāg-yuddhe mugdhayantī gurum api ca girāṁ paṇḍitā mālya-gumphe \|***  
***pāṭhe śārī-śukānāṁ paṭur ajitam api dyūta-keliṣu jiṣṇur***  
***vidyā-vidyota-buddhiḥ sphurati rati-kalā-śālinī rādhikeyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her cleverness in arts: Rādhā, master of all arts of love, is an authority in painting with minerals, is skilful at cooking a variety of pleasing dishes on her own, makes Kṛṣṇa foolish in word battles, and is master of stringing garlands. She is skilful at understanding the** ***śāri*** **and parrot, defeats Kṛṣṇa at dice, and has sharp intelligence in music.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Girām gurum* can mean Kṛṣṇa or Sarasvatī. The phrase *vāg-devīm apy avācaṁ racayitum adhikā* (she makes Sarasvatī speechless) is sometimes inserted in the verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundalatā speaks to a gopī who asks “How skilful Rādhā has become, though she was born just yesterday!” She is an *ācārya* of painting, with no teacher. Not learning from anyone, she produces a variety of cooked foods by her own creativity. Similarly it is said *veṇu-vādya urudhā nija-śikṣāḥ:* Kṛṣṇa has invented many new styles of flute-playing. (SB 10.35.14) In this way the other items should be understood. She defeats Kṛṣṇa, *guru* of words, or Sarasvatī in a battle of words. She has particularly sharp intelligence (*vidyota*) of singing and musical instruments, and logic, *mīmāṁsa* and other philosophies

### Text 34

*atha pāṭavānvitā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (3.3)—*  
***chinnaḥ priyo maṇisaraḥ sakhi mauktikāni***  
***vṛttāny ahaṁ vicinuyām iti kaitavena \|***  
***mugdhaṁ vivṛtya mayi hanta dṛganta-bhaṅgīṁ***  
***rādhā guror api puraḥ praṇayād vyatānīt \|\|34\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her cunning nature from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Rādhā once said the following words: "O friend, my favorite pearl necklace has broken, and now I must search for the scattered pearls". Using this trick, because of great love, turning her head, she attractively glanced at me in the presence of Jaṭilā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vivrṭya* means turning. Another version has *nivṛtya.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Madhumaṅgala. *Pāṭava* means dexterous. *Vṛttāni* means round pearls. *Mugdham* means attractive. *Vivṛtya* means turning.  *Guroḥ* means Jaṭilā.

### Text 35

*atha lajjā-śīlā—*  
***vraja-narapati-sūnur durabhālokano’yaṁ***  
***sphurati rahasi tāmyaty eṣa tarṣāj jano’pi \|***  
***virama janani lajje kiñcid udghāṭya vaktraṁ***  
***nimiṣam iha manāg apy akṣi-koṇaṁ kṣipāmi \|\|35\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The son of Vraja’s king, difficult to see, appears in a solitary place. Persons like me have become distressed because of desire. O mother shyness! Please desist a little, even for a moment! Uncovering my face I will glance at him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Eśaḥ janaḥ* means “a person like me. Instead of *virama janani* the *phrase uparama sahki* is sometimes found.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to herself.  *Tarṣāt* means because of extreme longing. A person like me (*eṣaḥ janaḥ*) becomes exhausted because of extreme longing. Addressing her friend, she intends to say, “O my enemy, why are you strangling my life airs?” Or, another meaning is “O my friend, shyness, I will teach you what is beneficial as a friend. For a moment withdraw. You should desist; otherwise I give up my life!” She considers this in her mind. Take dominion over the rest of my body but for a moment, a half a moment even, delay your oppression. Do this and I will live.” *Udghātya* (uncovering) is formed from *ghaṭ* and takes the form *udghātya* instead of *udghātva* because of the affix

### Text 36

***atha sumaryādā—***  
***prāṇān akṛtāhārā sakhi rādhā-cātakī varaṁ tyajati \|***  
***na tu kṛṣṇa-mudira-muktād amṛtād vṛttiṁ bhajed aparām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her great perseverance: O friend! It is better that the** ***cātakī*** **bird Rādhā give up her life by not eating. There is no other way of maintaining my life than the nectar released from the cloud of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Maryādā means perseverance by one’s nature, by following rules of the Vedas, or by one’s vows. Examples of each of these are given. This is Rādhā’s private response to an intimate friend who called her for a meal on seeing that she seemed to be hungry. Even in the *prakaṭa* pastimes her taste does not arise except by impressions of her being an eternal beloved. Internally, she identifies herself as his wife but externally she acts differently according to social custom as in the following verse where she herself speaks:

*api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro ’dhunāste*  
*smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṁś ca gopān*  
*kvacid api sa kathā naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṁ gṛṇīte*  
*bhujam aguru-sugandhaṁ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu*

**O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kṛṣṇa resides in Mathurā. Does he remember his father’s household affairs and his friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does he ever talk about us, his maidservants? When will he lay on our heads his** ***aguru*****-scented hand? SB 10.47.21**

There is no way of maintaining my life except by the tasty food remnants (*amṛtāt)* from Kṛṣṇa. In order to hide her relationship because of fear that someone will hear, she calls Kṛṣṇa the black cloud and calls herself a *cātakī* bird which lives by the rain from the cloud.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Maryādā* is a type of perseverance. It is sometimes natural, or learned by training, or by decision. Examples of each will be given in order. Śyāmalā one time called Rādhā privately to eat because of affection on seeing her thinness. Rādhā responds with these words. Or, Nāndīmukhī says to Rādhā “I have tried very hard to arrange a meeting with Kṛṣṇa, but Kṛṣṇa will not agree.” Testing Rādhā’s *prema*, she then thinks there must be some way of maintaining Rādhā’s life, and offers food. Rādhā replies with these words. By the sweet showers of his form, fragrance, voice, taste, softness and grace from the cloud of Kṛṣṇa, I will bring my senses to life. There is no other way. This is my decision. Therefore I will die. This is the intention of her words.

### Text 37

***yathā vā—***  
***āhūyamānā vrajanāthayāsmi yukto'bhisāraḥ sakhi nādhunā me \|***  
***na tādṛśīnāṁ hi gurūttamānām ājñāsv avajñā valate śivāya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I have been called by the queen of Vraja. It is not proper to meet Kṛṣṇa right now. It is not auspicious to disobey the orders of such great superiors.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows Rādhā’s determination to follow Vedic conduct because of her respect for elders arising from previous impressions, as in the previous verse. She does not find it a fault if she does not follow the orders of Jaṭilā, since she does not have the understanding that she should respect the mother-in-law.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Vṛndā. Sometimes Yaśodā would invite Rādhā for an evening meal out of affection. One should not fear any disruption to *prema* by such acts. For *gopīs* with *samartha-ratī,* their natural acts all aim at Kṛṣṇa’s happiness. It is the natural quality of the chaste women to follow the orders of their mothers and others, without at the same time going against Kṛṣṇa’s words. In the long run such acts give rise to happiness for Kṛṣṇa, who relishes their good character. She says she cannot meet Kṛṣṇa right now. She does not say she cannot meet him today. If the opportunity arises, I will meet him when he comes. If not, I will send Lalitā or Viśākhā who are equal to me. This is what the word *adhunā* (now) suggests. It solves the problem.

### Text 38

***yathā vā—***  
***pūrṇāśīḥ pūrṇimāsāv anavahitatayā yā tvayāsyai vitīrṇā***  
***vaṣṭi tvām eva tanvann akhila-madhurimotsekam asyāṁ mukundaḥ \|***  
***diṣṭyā parvodagāt te svayam abhisaraṇe cittam ādhatsva vatse***  
***yuktyāpy uktā mayeti dyumaṇi-sakha-sutā prāhiṇod eva citrām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**This is the full moon, which fulfills all desires. Inattentively, you have supplied Citrā, but Mukunda, spreading his profuse sweetness, desires only you. Dear Rādhā! By fate, the opportunity has arisen. Apply your heart for going to the meeting yourself. Though I said this with reason, Rādhā just sent Citrā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

An old messenger sent by Kṛṣṇa instructs Rādhā and returning to Kṛṣṇa, says this to him. This is full moon which fulfills all desires. “You, being inattentive, have sent Citrā, but Mukunda spreading an abundance of complete sweetness desires you alone, and not her.” Though I said this, Rādhā (the daughter of the friend of the son, Vṛṣabhānu) sent Citrā to you. She personally did not come to meet you. Another version has *citrāyai pūrṇimāsāvanavahitatayā yā tvayā prāg vitīrṇā.* There is no fault in this verse (of repetition) as in *udeti raktaḥ savitā rakta evāstam eti* ca: the red sun rises and the red sun sets.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An elder messenger sent by Kṛṣṇa to instruct Rādhā returns to Kṛṣṇa and speaks. This is the full moon which fulfills all desires. It is understood that it is the full moon of Śrāvaṇa month. It is said:

*prasūnair adbhutaiḥ kāntā kāntena śrāvaṇī-dine \|*  
*prasādhitā prasiddhena saubhāgyena vivardhate \|\|*

**On the full moon of Śrāvaṇa month, the women decorated by her lover with wonderful flowers increases in fame and fortune.**

“Without attention, with considering, you have sent Citrā (who is later named in the verse) by force, though not desiring to come. But on this full moon, Madhava, spreading his intense sweetness, desires you, not her.” I said this but the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu sent Citrā. She did not come herself.

One should not fear some dissipation of the limit of *prema* by this. Rādhā thought as follows. I have been accepted by him for giving him happiness in his pastimes. Lalitā and Viśākhā are also capable of giving him happiness. But Citrā should give pleasure to him as I do today, being enjoyed and decorated by him, since this full moon is so powerful. What can I be on my own to satisfy the longings of Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of love? Not satisfied in himself, by meeting me he gains fulfillment with *prema* directed to me. Therefore I will make arrangements so that his desire will be satisfied with all the *sakhīs.*

Always after enjoying with him, she sends him away on some pretext. Then he enjoys with the *sakhīs.* But her affection for all the *sakhīs* is a secondary cause of her doing that. The primary cause is to fulfill the desires of Kṛṣṇa. Thus the *sakhīs* are assistants of Rādhā who has a nature of giving happiness to Kṛṣṇa. This idea is accepted by the wise *sakhīs.* If it were otherwise, the *gopīs* would not consider it fair that heroine simply derives her happiness by their friendship.

### Text 39

***atha dhairya-śālinī—***  
***tīvras tarjati bhinna-dhīr gṛha-patiś chadma-jñayā padmayā***  
***hāraṁ hārayati hari-praṇihitaṁ kīśena bhartuḥ svasā \|***  
***mallīṁ lumpati kṛṣṇa-kāmya-kusumāṁ śaibyā-priyā varkarī***  
***rādhā paśya tathāpy atīva sahanā tuṣṇīm asau tiṣṭhati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Great tolerance: Her angry husband, his mind disturbed by Padmā’s false word, scolds her. Her necklace is stolen by a monkey under Kuṭilā’s instruction. Śaibyā’s favorite goat eats up the flowers of the jasmine plant pleasing to Kṛṣṇa. Rādhā, most tolerant, sees all this and remains silent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Padmā is a *gopī* in the opposing group of Candrāvalī. *Kiśena* means by a monkey taught by Kuṭilā. Śaibyā is also a *gopī* in Candrāvalī’s group. One version has the line *mallīm priyeṇa nihitaṁ bhartuḥ svasā ḍimbhayeti śaivyā-nirdiṣṭaḥ śiśur*: the sister of Abhimanyu, ordered by Śaibyā, said “Throw away that jasmine plant given by Rādhā’s lover, Kṛṣṇa *(priyena*).” *Bhartuḥ* means one who thinks he is the husband, one who maintains. The author has also written:

*rāse nivṛtte tu sapatnikānāṁ vakroktim ākarṇya nijāli-vaktrāt \|*  
*rādhā vihasyāha bhavatya eva dviṣanti tāsāṁ na tu tādṛśās tāḥ \|\|*

**After the** ***rāsa*** **dance, hearing the crooked words of other** ***gopīs*** **from her friend, Rādhā laughed and said. “Her friends may show envy, but these women are not like them.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. Her angry *(tīvraḥ)* husband, Abhimanyu, scolded her. He has become disturbed in mind by Padmā, who says “Your wife Rādhā is cheating you.” Her necklace given by Kṛṣṇa is stolen by a monkey. “O monkey! I will give you lots of sweets. When alone, open that chest. Take the necklace while no one is looking and give it to me.” Kuṭilā, the sister of the husband, teaches this to the monkey. The goat, dear to Śaibyā, ordered by her, eats the leaves and buds of the jasmine plant*. Varkara* means a young animal, a goat or deer.

### Text 40

***atha gāmbhīrya-śālinī—***  
***kalahāntaritā-pade sthitiṁ***  
***sakhi dhīrādya gatāpi rādhikā \|***  
***bahir udbhaṭa-māna-lakṣaṇā***  
***sudurūhā lalitā dhiyāpy abhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her inscrutability: Though Rādhā is situated in the midst of conflict within her mind, she remains calm. Externally she appears most respectful. By her intelligence she has become indescribably gentle.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to her friend. *Pade* means “in a condition.” Though there is cause for agitation, she does not become disturbed. This is a quality of patience (described previously). In this case there is great tolerance. Since *prema* is nourished by agitation, it may arise internally from some cause and then manifest externally. Not taking revenge in this situation is called *dhairya* or tolerance. However, when the inner agitation does not manifest externally at all it is called *gāmbhīrya* or inscrutability. This is the difference between them.

### Text 41

***atha suvilāsā—***  
***tiryak-kṣipta-calad-dṛgañcala-rucir lāsyollasad-bhrū-latā***  
***kundābha-smita-candrikojjvala-mukhī gaṇḍocchalat-kuṇḍalā \|***  
***kandarpāgama-siddha-mantra-gahanām ardhaṁ duhānā giraṁ***  
***hāriṇy adya harer jahāra hṛdayaṁ rādhā vilāsormibhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Coyness: She has a delightful, moving, crooked glance emanating from the edge of her eye. Her eyebrows are agitated with dancing. Her moon face shines with a smile like a jasmine flower. Her cheeks are lit by her earrings. She manifests half a word from her mouth, which has the effect of all mantras for invoking Cupid’s powers. Beautiful Rādhā steals the heart of Kṛṣṇa by her waves of playful gestures.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The creepers of her brows are agitated with dancing. Another version is *lāsya-bhramad-bhrū-latāḥ:* she has brows moving with dance. Another version describing her smile is *sāndra-śrī-smita-candrikākara-mukhī*: her moon like face as a profound smile. . Her words have the deep power (*gahanām*) of mantras for calling Cupid: they immediately cause bewilderment and inaction. *Duhānā* means “cause to appear.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa is present at a platform strewn with flowers in pastime bower with Rādhā. He brings her forcibly to his left side. Rādhā, surrounded by her friends, sits in front of Kṛṣṇa for a discussion. To help her feel relaxed and in order to see her beauty, he faces her and her friends. Kṛṣṇa said to the seated friends, “Oh! Women the eyes like the *cakora* bird! What can be said! Today my fortune has been great, because I have seen an auspicious omen after meditating with mantra of Parvatī while alone. I saw suddenly the most beautiful chaste, pious women destroying all darkness of the night by their effulgence.”

First, she gave a side long glance from the edge of her eye. The glance was sideways not showing her face by looking in front. The glance was moving, not stationary for a second, by the edge of her eye, not the full eye. By this her beauty became most attractive (*rucī*). By this glance she meant “We are most improper women and you are proper, engaged in remembering enjoyment with worshippable goddess Gaurī.”

He then said, “Moreover an astrologer said that a golden garland, the king of elegance, will decorate my throat today.”

When he said this, her brows trembled with dancing. The meaning is “You say that you will be decorated with a golden garland, but do not try to understand my desires. I stay with my friends. When they go from here, I will also go.”

The *sakhīs* replied, “The son of the king of Vraja has many golden garlands. They are not rare. However today you have attained a desire tree (*surataru)* by good fortune.”

He said, “You have spoken the truth. By the three syllables from the desire tree (*surata*) I will become successful. And the golden garlands also will be successful with that perfection.”

Her face like moonlight then showed a smile like a jasmine flower. Her smile arose from *rati-sthāyi-bhāva*, but was covered, and only showed slightly. The smile had the beauty of a jasmine flower, which spread over her whole face like moonlight.

Kṛṣṇa, not able to control himself, tilted his face and gazed at her face. At that moment, she turned her face to his left side. This caused her earring to move near her right cheek (*gaṇḍocchalat-kuṇḍalā*). Seeing her earring illuminate her right ear, her lock of hair, cheek, forehead and edge of her eye, Kṛṣṇa became stunned with bliss. She covered her face using her cloth held in her right hand.

She replied in a voice indicating a clash of bewilderment, joy, shame, longing, insolence, and inaction. She spoke incomplete words which were spread with mantras of Cupid mentioned in the scriptures--which give control, conquest, insanity, and bewilderment. This indicates that each syllable she uttered in reply was like a mantra for controlling and bewildering him. This is the ornament of *atiśayokti* or hyperbole. They were not syllables but mantras. This is the ornament of *apahnuti.*

She answered, “Those who walk in the forest will perfect the three syllables in the lotuses in the forest, not by me, a desire creeper.”

The meaning is this. Amorous union (*surata--*three syllables) will not be perfected by me, the desire creeper that fulfills desires, but by the many lotus-like women. I give my *sakhīs* to you for this purpose.” This joking answer is for the *sakhīs*.

The *sakhīs* speak. “If you want to give us to your beloved, then we forest lotuses will flee to the forest.” Saying this, they began to depart. Rādhā was also eager to leave. Kṛṣṇa embraced her forcibly around her neck and led her to the flower bed. She stole his heart with the waves of these gestures. She was an ocean agitated into waves by the moon of his face.

Though not intelligent, I can grasp the jewels of meaning from the verse, an ocean of sweetness, weighty with clear suggestions.

### Text 42

*atha mahā-bhāva-paramotkarṣa-tarṣiṇī—*  
***aśrūṇām ativṛṣṭibhir dviguṇayanty arkātmajā-nirjharaṁ***  
***jyotsnī-syandi-vidhūpala-pratikṛti-cchāyaṁ vapur bibhratī \|***  
***kaṇṭhāntas truṭad-akṣarādya-pulakair labdhā kadambākṛtiṁ***  
***rādhā veṇu-dhara pravāta-kadalī-tulyā kvacid vartate \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Thirst for Kṛṣṇa with the highest state of** ***mahābhāva:*** **O holder of the flute! She has doubled the flow of the Yamunā by intense showers of her tears. Her body has a color like moonstone emanating rays of light. Her throat is filled with broken syllables. Her body is like a** ***kadamba*** **flower with goose bumps. She is a like a banana trembling in strong wind. She remains in this state somehow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A friend of Rādhā talks to Kṛṣṇa. This is an example of *udātta alaṅkāra*. *Udātta* means a description with plenty of extreme exaggeration. This is made by taking the extreme nature of objects to describe something. In order, perspiration, being stunned and change of color are indicated in the comparison to a moonstone. *Chāyā* means luster or beauty. *Truṭat* is formed from *truṭ* since it belongs to the *tudādī* class of roots. She is like a banana tree trembling in strong wind (*pravāta*). In order to increase Kṛṣṇa’s longing for her, the friend says with uncertainty that Rādhā somehow (*kvacit*) remains like this, since he is the cause of this condition, by attracting her with his flute (*venu-dhara)*. Actually however she is hidden within a bower close by and is watching him, since the verse says that she flows with moon light. This means she derives great happiness on seeing her beloved from the bower*. Mahābhāva* with *sūddipta-sattvika-bhāvas*, called *rūḍha,* is shown in this description. It will be explained later *sūddīptāḥ sāttvikā yatra sa rūḍha iti bhaṇyate:* when the *sāttvika-bhāvas* become *uddīpta* in *mahābhāva* it is called *rūḍha. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.159)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*modano’yaṁ praviśleṣa-daśāyāṁ mohano bhavet \|*  
*yasmin viraha-vaivaśyāt sūddīptā eva sāttvikāḥ \|\|*

***Modana*** **becomes** ***mohana*** **in the state of separation. Because of the lack of control during separation, the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **become** ***sūddīpta.*** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.179**

### Text 43

*atha gokula-prema-vasatiḥ—*  
***prema-santatibhir eva nirmame***  
***vedhasā nu vṛṣabhānu-nandinī \|***  
***yādṛśāṁ padam itā manāṁsi naḥ***  
***snehayaty akhila-goṣṭha-vāsinām \|\|43\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**All of Gokula has** ***prema*** **for her: Rādhā has been made of a mass of** ***prema*** **by the creator. On seeing her, the minds of all the inhabitants of Gokula are filled with affection.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Yaśodā speaks to a friend who asks about Rādhā as a pretext. *Sneha-santatibhiḥ* is sometimes seen instead of *prema-santatibhiḥ.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Rādhā from far off, coming to her house to cook in the morning, Yaśodā speaks to a friend. Actually a part of the mass of *prema* is *sneha* and other stages. Rādhā is composed of all these parts. *Itā* means “having obtained.”

### Text 44

*atha jagac-chreṇī-lasad-yaśāḥ—*  
***utphullaṁ kila kurvatī kuvalayaṁ devendra-patnī-śrutau***  
***kundaṁ nikṣipatī viriñcī-gṛhiṇī-romauṣadhī-harṣiṇī \|***  
***karṇottaṁsa-sudhāṁśu-ratna-sakalaṁ vidrāvya bhadrāṅgi te***  
***lakṣmīm apy adhunā cakāra cakitāṁ rādhe yaśaḥ-kaumudī \|\|44\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fame which dazzles the whole universe: O Rādhā! The night lotus of your fame makes the lotus of the earth blossom in joy. It makes the white jasmine fall from the ear of Sācī. It makes Sāvitrī’s hairs stand on end. It liquefies all the moonstone ornaments in the ear of Lakṣmī, and makes Lakṣmī, the abode of the day lotus, tremble.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kuvalayam* means a water lily and the earth globe. The night lotus of Rādhā’s fame makes the earth planet or the water lily blossom. Her fame makes the jasmine fall from the ear of Sācī. The jasmine is white, but the lotus of Rādhā’s fame is whiter or purer. The jasmine falls from her ear because of becoming dizzy on seeing the purity of Rādhā’s fame. The lotus of Rādhā’s fame makes the herbs (*devatā* of the hairs) in the form of hairs on the body of Brahmā’s wife stand up. The night lotus (blooming in the moonlight) of Rādhā’s fame makes Lakṣmī, the abode of the day blooming lotus, tremble, melting (*vidrāvya*) her moonstone earrings. The word *vidrāvya* is used by poets to indicate impudence and boldness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks. *Kuvalayam* is the blue water lily and also the earth, including the lower planets. All the inhabitants of those places, hearing of her fame, become joyful. He fame spreads to the seven upper planets as well. The jasmine falls from Sācī’s ear because of getting dizzy. Or it falls when Sācī hears about her fame. The jasmine is the most delicate among flowers, but is defeated by Rādhā’s lotus of fame. It is hinted that Sācī was in some private place absorbed in great sense enjoyment. The lotus of Rādhā’s fame became a jasmine in one of her ears, since it had to enter through the fine lattice holes of the *devatā’s* palace.

Her fame makes Sāvitrī’s hairs, like herbs, stand on end. The phrase “hairs like herbs” suggests that Sāvitrī was standing on the roof, absorbed in *sattva-guṇa*, with disgust for material pleasure, and in that place Rādhā’s lotus or moonlight *(kaumudi*) fame cooled all her limbs and made her hairs stand on end.

Her fame spreads over the material realm and also to the spiritual realm. Her fame melts all the moonstone ear ornaments, turning them into running water and causes Lakṣmī to become filled with doubt, inaction, and surprise. The moonlight of her fame has causes external effects—melting of moonstones, and internal effects—emotions in Lakṣmī. This statement indicates that Lakṣmī was most pure, devoid of any material contamination. First, one hears but this does not quickly produce *sāttvika-bhāvas.* Secondly, hearing about Rādhā produces symptoms in all the body with hairs standing on end. Thirdly, hearing about her produces internal and external effects, in the form of *sañcāri-bhāvas.* According to the degree of a person’s purity Rādhā’s fame will enter a person. It will not enter persons who are proud. This conclusion should be understood.

### Text 45

*atha gurv-arpita-guru-snehā—*  
***na sutāsi kīrtidāyāḥ***  
***kintu mamaiveti tathyam ākhyāmi \|***  
***prāṇimi vīkṣya mukham te***  
***kṛṣṇasyeveti kiṁ trapase \|\|45\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Object of great affection by the elders: You are not the daughter of Kīrtidā. I say that you are my daughter. Seeing your face, I come to life as I do on seeing Kṛṣṇa’s face. Why are you ashamed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Yaśodā speaks. The mood is similar to verse 37. There is the ornament *apahnuti.* *Apahnuti* is defined as *prakṛtaṁ yan niṣidhyānyat sādhyate sā tv apahnutiḥ: apahnuti* is accomplished by denying a normal condition. (Yaśodā denies that Rādhā is Kīrtidā’s daughter.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Yaśodā speaks to Rādhā who remains speechless, covering her face in shame before her. “My affection for you is not less by one degree that your mother’s.” This indicates that Yaśodā and Kīrtidā are equal. I come to life on seeing your face. This is the main reason why she called Rādhā every morning. She hints that Rādhā should know this.

### Text 46

*atha sakhī-praṇayādhīnā—*  
***upadiśa sakhi vṛnde vallavendrasya sūnuṁ***  
***kim ayam iha sakhīnāṁ mām adhīnāṁ dunoti \|***  
***apasaratu saśaṅkaṁ mandirān māninīnāṁ***  
***kalayati lalitāyāḥ kiṁ na śauṭīrya-dhāṭīm \|\|46\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her dependence on her friends’ affection: O friend! Teach the son of Nanda. Why does he afflict me, who am dependent on my friends? He should leave the houses of respectable women in fear. Does he know the heroic assaulting skills of Lalitā?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Does he not know (*kalayati*) about the heroic ( *śauṭīrya*) assaults of Lalitā? Kṣīrasvāmī says *dhāṭī* means assault arising from deceit.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, greatly disturbed, speaks*. Śauṭirya* means heroic.  *Dhāṭī* means a deceitful assault. Many times Lalitā experienced his assaults. The plural is used to indicate many *sakhīs* like her exist. Actually only Lalitā does not agree with him. This means that she must be won over and brought under control by him. “I am not only dependent on her but on other *sakhīs* as well.” Taking shelter of Viśākhā and others she can accomplish her work. This is a private instruction with consolation.

### Text 47

*atha kṛṣṇa-priyāvalī-mukhyā, yathā lalita-mādhave (10.10)—*  
***santu bhrāmyad-apāṅga-bhaṅgi-khuralī-khelābhuvaḥ subhruvaḥ***  
***svasti syān madirekṣaṇe kṣaṇam api tvām antarā me kutaḥ \|***  
***tārāṇāṁ nikurambakena vṛtayā śliṣṭe’pi somābhayā***  
***nākāśe vṛṣabhānujāṁ śriyam ṛte niṣpadyate svaś-chaṭā \|\|47\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The principle woman of Kṛṣṇa’s affection, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: My dear girl with the fascinating eyes! Even if I am attacked by many girls with beautiful eyebrows, who are expert archers with their restless, crooked glances, how can I find happiness for even a moment without you? I am like the sky. Even if the sky is embraced by moonlight and all the stars, it never becomes bright until it is filled with the morning sun.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The third line uses *arthāntara-nyāsa.* There is also another meaning in the words, which nourishes the meaning. *Somābhā* refers to Candrāvalī as well as moonlight and *vṛṣabhānujām śriyam* indicates Rādhā as well as sunlight. *Ākāśe* can mean sky or “in Kṛṣṇa, who completely illuminates.” *Svaśchatā* means lively consciousness. Thus the other meaning is: there can be no lively consciousness in Kṛṣṇa, even if he is embraced by Candrāvalī and her associates. It exists only with Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. Other women are constantly engaged in the practice of aiming their curved, unsteady glances, in order to control Kṛṣṇa. But their efforts are useless. “Without you, Rādhā, I can have no happiness. By seeing some part of your body, like your back, that part produces happiness in me. But even their intentional glances do not affect me.” The example is *arthāntara-nyāsa* (illustrating a particular matter by a general truth). Though the sky is embraced, deeply touched by the full beauty of moon light (*soma ābhayā*) along with the array of stars, without the beauty of the sun in Jyeṣṭha month (*vṛṣabhānujām*), without just one piece of its beauty, absence of darkness *(svacchatā*) does not take place. There is another meaning. Let us exclude the women with beautiful eyebrows. If the most beautiful of them, Candrāvalī, embraces my heart (*ākāśe*), without the beauty of Rādhā, I am not devoid of suffering (*svacchatā*). My heart remains miserable and without brilliance when Rādhā is not present. The word *śrīyam* also suggests morning.

### Text 48

*atha santatāśrava-keśavā—*  
***ṣaḍ-aṅghribhir amarditān kusuma-sañcayān ācinod***  
***akhaṇḍam api rādhike bahu-śikhaṇḍakaṁ tvad-girā \|***  
***amuñca nava-pallava-vrajam udañcad arkojjvalaṁ***  
***karotu vaśago janaḥ kim ayam anyad-ājñāpaya \|\|48\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Her constant control of Kṛṣṇa: O Rādhikā! I have plucked a mass of flowers uncrushed by the bees and have brought many undamaged peacock feathers according to your words. Give up using the fresh leaves brilliant as the rising sun for making the garland. A person like me should act under your control. Give me another order.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. The phrase *bahu-śikhaṇḍakam* means a great variety of peacock feathers. *Ayam* means “a person like me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Bahu-śikhaṇḍakam* is in the singular to indicate a collection of many peacock feathers. The word *tribhuvanam* (three worlds) is a similar construction using a numeral in a *dvigu* compound. *Ayam* means “a person like me.”

### Text 49-50

***yasyāḥ sarvottame yūthe sarva-sad-guṇa-maṇḍitāḥ \|***  
***samantān mādhavākarṣi-vibhramāḥ santi subhruvaḥ \|\|49\|\|***  
***tās tu vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ sakhyaḥ pañca-vidhā matāḥ \|***  
***sakhyaś ca nitya-sakhyaś ca prāṇa-sakhyaś ca kāścana \|***  
***priya-sakhyaś ca parama-preṣṭha-sakhyaś ca viśrutāḥ \|\|50\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In Rādhā’s group, which is the best of all, are beautiful women decorated with all good qualities, who completely attract Kṛṣṇa. The** ***sakhīs*** **of Rādhā are of five types:** ***sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-sakhī*** **and** ***parama-preṣṭha-sakhī*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having described the qualities of the chief lover Rādhā, the author now describes her friends, who assist her. In verse 16 four types of Rādhā’s qualities were described: those concerning her body, speech, mind and relationship with others. The present sentence is related that previous sentence, without the necessity of explicit grammatical connection, since a clause with *yat* need not have a corresponding *tat,* since the relationship is implied. An example is found the verse *sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtaṁ nīlitaṁ yad abhirāmatādhike* of *Kāvya-prakāśa* 7.188.

### Text 51

***sakhyaḥ kusumikā-vindhyā-dhaniṣṭhādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|***  
***nitya-sakhyaś ca kastūrī-maṇi-mañjarikādayaḥ \|\|51\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhīs*** **are women like Kusumikā, Vindhyā, and Dhaniṣṭhā. The** ***nitya-sakhīs*** **include Kastūrī and Maṇi-mañjarikā.**

### Text 52

***prāṇa-sakhyaḥ śaśimukhī-vāsantī-lāsikādayaḥ \|***  
***gatā vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ prāyeṇemāḥ svarūpatām \|\|52\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***prāṇa-sakhīs*** **include Śaśimukhī, Vāsanti, and Lāsikā. All these three types generally have the same qualities as Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Imāḥ* means the *sakhīs, nitya-sakhīs* and *prāṇa-sakhīs.* They generally are almost (*prāyena*) equal to Rādhā in terms of *prema*, beauty and good qualities. This means that they are not completely equal to her. Those who are truly equal are the *priya-sakhīs,* and *parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs*. Though there are five types, one should understand that there are also two types, those with equal affection and those with unequal affection (*sama-sneha* and *asama-sneha*). This will be explained later.

“If you say they are almost equal, then the *sakhīs, nitya-sakhīs* and *prāṇa-sakhīs* are somewhat inferior to Rādhā. This would mean they are servants as defined by the phrase *tulya-rūpa-guṇā sakhyaḥ kiñcin nyūnās tu dāsikāḥ*: the servants are slightly less in qualities than the friends, whose qualities and form equal the queens. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 3.8) That is not so. This statement concerning servants says they are somewhat equal or similar. This means that they are somewhat less than leaders. Thus, “being less” is of two grades. Similarity of qualities may be suitable or unsuitable for gaining respect. Those whose qualities are suitable, who have equal qualities by their nature are *sakhīs.* Those whose qualities are unsuitable, and have fewer qualities by their nature are servants. Thus there is no fault.

### Text 53

***priya-sakhyaḥ kuraṅgākṣī sumadhyā madanālasā \|***  
***kamalā mādhurī mañju-keśī kandarpa-sundarī \|***  
***mādhavī mālatī kāma-latā śaśikalādayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***priya-sakhīs*** **include Kuraṅgākṣī, Sumadhyā, Madanālasā, Kamalā, Mādhurī, Mañjukeśī, Kandarpa-sundarī, Mādhavī, Mālatī, Kāma-latā and Śaśikalā.**

### Text 54

***parama-preṣṭha-sakhyas tu lalitā sa-viśākhikā \|***  
***sa-citrā campakalatā tuṅgavidyendulekhikā \|***  
***raṅgadevī sudevī cetyaṣṭau sarva-gaṇāgrimāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The eight** ***parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs*** **Lalitā, Viśākhā, Citrā, Campaka-latā, Tuṅgavidyā, Indulekhā, Raṅgadevī and Sudevī are the best of all.**

### Text 55

***āsāṁ suṣṭhu dvayor eva premṇaḥ parama-kāṣṭhayā \|***  
***kvacij jātu kvacij jātu tad-ādhikyam ivekṣate \|\|55\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By the influence of the highest level of** ***prema*** **for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa these eight sometimes show more affection for Rādhā and sometimes show more affection for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The meaning of the last sentence is this. Because of the highest level of *prema* for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa (*dvayoḥ*) the eight *sakhīs (āsām)* sometimes show more *prema* for Rādhā and sometime show more *prema* for Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is not correct to say that the best *gopīs* show equal affection for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. That is explained in this verse. Lalitā and other supreme *gopīs* in their *prema* for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, sometimes show more *prema* for Rādhā than Kṛṣṇa because of *prema’s* supreme excellence (*parama-kāṣthayā*). This is because they cannot tolerate Rādhā’s suffering following from Kṛṣṇa’s actions. Sometimes they have more *prema* for Kṛṣṇa than Rādhā because his body withers in separation, caused by her tough pride, since they cannot tolerate Kṛṣṇa’s suffering following from Rādhā’s actions. The word *iva* suggests that even those with great discernment cannot understand the additional *prema* for Rādhā or Kṛṣṇa, since the *sakhīs* cannot tolerate the suffering of either equally. Where there is unequal affection (*asama-sneha*) and the *sakhīs* have more sneha for one of them, when Rādhā or Kṛṣṇa is happy or sad, the *sakhīs* show more happiness or sadness for one of them. This is not so in other cases.
