Total 15 types

I. Eight conditions:

- *abhisārikā (*going for an appointment*),*
- *vāsa-sajjā* (decorating herself)*,*
- *unkanthitā* (anxiety because of delay),
- *khaṇḍitā* (devastated)*,*
- *vipralabdhā* (feeling cheated)*,*
- *kalahāntaritā* (separation by quarrel)*,*
- *proṣita-preyasī (*great separation*)*
- *svādhīna-bharṭrkā* (controlling the lover)

II. Uttamā

III. Madhyā

IV. Kaniṣṭhā

15 x 8 x 3 = 360 types

### Text 1

***yūthe’py avāntara-gaṇās teṣu ca kaścid gaṇas tri-caturābhiḥ \|***  
***iha pañca-ṣābhir anyaḥ saptāṣṭābhis tathety ādyāḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Within a group there are smaller groups of three, four, five, six seven or eight** ***gopīs*** **or more.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The different types of *nāyikās* are now described.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are many diffferent groups within the *yūtha,* such as *sakhī, prāṇa-sakhis, priya-sakhīs* etc. Or in Rādhās’ group there is Lalitā’s group, Viśākhā’s group etc. There are unlimited groups. Three or four *sakhīs* may make one group. Or five may make a group. In this way there hundred, thousands or ten thousands in a sub group.

### Text 2

***nāsau nāṭye rase mukhye yat paroḍhā nigadyate \|***  
***tat tu syāt prākṛta-kṣudra-nāyikādy-anusārataḥ \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The woman married to another man which is not praised in literature. However, that condemnation is according to the nature low, material heroines.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In discussing *parakīya* heroes, finding fault in the parakīya woman has already been dismissed. Again fault is rejected to strengthen the case.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It was already established. in the chapter on the *nāyaka* or hero, that Kṛṣṇaas the *upapati* is most highly praised, though generally the *upapati* is condemned. Now in this chapter discussing the heroine, it is established that married women having a relationship with Kṛṣṇa is most highly praised, though it is condemned for other women.

### Text 3

***tathā coktam—***  
***neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā***  
***tad gokulāmbujadṛśāṁ kulam antarena \|***  
***āśāṁsayā rasa-vidher avatāritānāṁ***  
***kaṁsāriṇā rasika-maṇḍala-śekhareṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said: Poets’ objection to married women enjoying with another man as the main** ***rasa*** **applies only to women other than the women of Gokula, whom Kṛṣṇa, the topmost among tasters, made appear in this world because of a special desire for** ***madhura-rasa*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The author quotes a previous *ācārya* to prove the point. The main *rasa* is that *rasa* which must be continuous in order that it is fulfilled. If the *rasa* with a married woman is secondary, it may not be criticized. This is summarized by the author of *Sāhitya-darpaṇa:*

*paroḍhāṁ varjayitvātra veśyāṁ cānanurāgiṇīm \|*  
*ālambanaṁ nāyikā syur dakṣiṇādyāś ca nāyakāḥ \|\|*

**The heroine, excluding a married woman, a prostitute or a woman with no attraction for the man, becomes the** ***alambana*** **in a drama.**

The word ca indicates a new subject. The married prostitute should be rejected only. If a legitimate wife has no attraction, that also should be rejected. It is said *para-nāyaka-saṁsthāyam.* The groups of Vraja women are excluded from this (*antareṇa*). They are respected. The reason is given by describing them.

The eternal lovers, with an illusion of being married to someone else, appeared in this world (*avatāritānām*), supported by the suitable *līḷā-śakti,* but not supported with much show of omniscience, power and supreme lordship, in order to taste special prema rasa that could be accomplished in the pastimes on earth. Forgetting their eternal nature by taking birth etc. he had them appear, so that a special type of *rasa* (*rasa-vidheḥ*) could take place. The cause of the desire is stated: Kṛṣṇa is the topmost among *rasikas.* The *gopis’* identity as married women was accomplished by the līla-śakti, without their association with another man. Thus these women were most highly qualified for the main *rasa.*

What is said is this. Though there is *rasa* of enjoyment in union without obstacle, separation sometimes is needed since Bharata Muni says *vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṇim aśnute*: union is nourished by separation. If that separation gives variety to the pastimes, then it is excellent. There is not such variety in the love of a married couple. Since Kṛṣṇa is married to them in the spiritual world, by *līlā-śakti,* taking another birth and giving up that condition of husband and wife by illusion, the women seem to be married to someone else, by making an image of a husband. The women, thinking these are their husbands, secretly meet with Kṛṣṇa (their actual husband) out of strong attraction which transgresses *dharma* and public opinion, and have rare opportunities to meet because of constant fear. Later the man goes to a far off place and then meeting becomes impossible for them. Some later they can meet and this produces the most astonishing happiness for the couple when they get married in this world by the arrangement of the *līlā-śakti.* Rādhā says in *Lalita-mādhava* at the last act called Fulfillment of Desires:

*sakhyas tā militā nisarga-madhurāḥ premābhirāmī-kṛtā*  
*yāmīyaṁ samagaṁsta saṁstaravatī śvaśrūś ca goṣṭheśvarī \|*  
*vṛndāraṇya-nikuñja-dhāmni bhavatā saṅgo’py ayaṁ raṅgavān*  
*saṁvṛttaḥ kim ataḥ paraṁ priyataraṁ kartavyam atrāsti me \|\|*

**In this forest of Vṛndāvana I have found my beautiful, charming, and affectionate** ***gopī*** **friends, I have found my sister Candrāvalī, and all her friends. I have obtained Yaśodā the queen of Vraja as my mother-in-law, and I have also attained your company, which brings me the greatest happiness. What can be more pleasing to me than all these things?**

The author himself has thus approved that the supreme level of variety in love is attained when the love is without obstruction. This is shown in his own work. It is also approved when the author says that the supreme leader of *rasikas* has made the *gopīs* appear for special *rasa.* I will show that this is the highest level (called *samṛddhimat*) in *sambhoga,* union for enjoyment, in which the highest result is accomplished.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Previous authorities were already quoted. Now he provides a verse produced by a scholar expert at distilling the opinions of the ancient authorities. The main *rasa* (*aṅginī rase*) means *madhura-rasa*. Love with married women is forbidden according to *Sāhitya-darpaṇa:* *paroḍhām varyayitvā.* But this does not include the women of Gokula. They are approved, whereas other *paroḍha* affairs are condemned. This is the conclusion of previous *ācāryas.* The reason is given. Desiring a method of tasting *rasa (rasa-vidheḥ),* desiring “Let the taste of *śṛṅgāra-rasa* be described in scriptures” Kṛṣṇa himself, the enemy of Kaṁsa, had the women appear on earth.

The meaning is this. In scriptures for liberation, *śānta-rasa* is prescribed since it destroys *saṁsāra* by its nature of decreasing lust. *Śṛṅgāra-rasa* is forbidden since it nourishes *saṁsāra* by its nature of encouraging lust. But attachment to others’ wives is forbidden even in scriptures encouraging material life, since the performer of the act and relisher of the event falls to hell by generating bad karma for himself. However, the Lord himself had the women appear in this world for pastimes of love with married women.

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopīs of Vṛndāvana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. SB 10.33.39**

Thus his pastimes, recorded in *Bhāgavatam,* are the means of tasting this *rasa.* This pastime is not possible for anyone except the women of Vraja. Therefore he personally appeared and has them appear.

Moreover in the *Bhāgavatam,* it is shown that of the three features, Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān, Bhagavān is the principle form (*vadanti tat-tattva-vidaḥ S*B 1.2.11) In *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* (2.1.221), Vraja Kṛṣṇa is recognized as the most perfect form of Bhagavān, the shelter of *dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya* and ultimately *madhura-rasa.* And in this work, as a final conclusion, Kṛṣṇa is shown to reach the highest level by displaying himself as the *upapati* in *madhura-rasa.* It is far superior to the *jñānī’s* realization of *śānta-rasa* depending on Brahman. Ultimately, it is seen to be far superior to all results.

*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**That hearer will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. SB 10.33.39**

This verse indicates that a person on first entering *bhakti (bhaktim pratilabhya)* has material contamination (*hṛd-rogam*) but by *bhakti* quickly destroys that contamination, because though *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is considered inferior, it is also stated to be the highest conclusion by its nature and its results, because of *Bhāgavatam,* the scripture of the *paramahaṁsas*. One experiences *vismaya-rasa* (surprise) because of its unlimited power, which is arranged by the greatest taster of *rasa,* Kṛṣṇa (*rasika-maṇḍala-sekhareṇa*).

“Let this be recognized as *rasa,* but since Bharata Muni excludes it, let it be explained that Kṛṣṇa appeared with a method for experiencing *rasābhāsa* for it is said *sarve ’pi rasanād rasāḥ*: even *bhāvābhāsas* and *rasābhāsas* are *rasa* since they are enjoyable. (BRS 4.9.41)”

Then Kṛṣṇa would be a knower something which is not *rasa (rasābhāsa).* They also explain that with a desire of this type of *rasa (rasa-vidheḥ),* he had the *gopīs* appear. Thus, in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes, does this type of *rasa* not appear?

“Let that be. Because they are married to Kṛṣṇa in *aprakaṭa* pastimes, this married condition is recommended, without the excellence of *rasa* having deep attraction in *parakīya* mood with feelings of great obstacles and transgressing the limits of public opinion and scripture. Thus when Kaṁsa develops the desire for this special type of *rasa,* and has his women appear in this world as wives of others, caused by the *līlā-śakti* making them think they are wives of others, that special taste is accomplished for some time.”

True. Very true. Kṛṣṇa does not taste the excellence of *rasa* at all times, but during the manifest pastimes on earth only. Because those pastimes are occasional, the taste is occasional. The root of the excellence of *rasa* is affairs with other’s wives, produced by illusion. That is most auspicious. This is your conclusion.

Now listen. If the taste for excellent *rasa* caused by Kṛṣṇa is occasional, then it must be simply *māyā,* because material *māyā-śakti* produces temporary appearances, not the *cit-śakti.* If the condition of women being married to other men is created by illusion, then the Lord himself must fall under illusion. This amounts to a condition found in Śaṅkara’s philosophy. In that philosophy it is *jīva* who is in illusion, not the Lord. (Thus Kaṁsa is a jīva.)

“The illusion is caused by *prema* alone, and accomplished by the *līlā-śakti*.” Then, that means *prema* does not exist in the spiritual world since Kṛṣṇa is not in illusion there and the women know they are wives. How can his illusion be temporary if it is caused by *prema?* It should be eternal. It is only objects of *māyā* that are temporary. If his pastimes are *māyā* because of being temporary, Śukadeva, the crest jewel of *ātmārāmas,* could not have been attracted to them.

*nibhṛta-marun-mano-’kṣa-dṛḍha-yoga-yujo hṛdi yan*  
*munaya upāsate tad arayo ’pi yayuḥ smaraṇāt*  
*striya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo*  
*vayam api te samāḥ sama-dṛśo ’ṅghri-saroja-sudhāḥ*

**Simply by constantly thinking of him, the enemies of the Lord attained the same Supreme Truth whom sages fixed in yoga worship by controlling their breath, mind and senses. Similarly, we** ***śrutis,*** **who generally see you as all-pervading, will achieve the same nectar from your lotus feet that your consorts are able to relish because of their loving attraction to your mighty, serpentine arms, for you look upon us and your consorts in the same way. SB 10.87.23**

*pariniṣṭhito ’pi nairguṇya uttama-śloka-līlayā*  
*gṛhīta-cetā rājarṣe ākhyānaṁ yad adhītavān*

**O saintly King, I was certainly situated perfectly in transcendence, yet I was still attracted by the delineation of the pastimes of the Lord, who is described by enlightened verses. SB 2.1.7**

One cannot say that his attraction is for the *aprakaṭa* pastimes for it is said in the above verse that Śukadeva studied the delineation of pastimes of the Lord as *avatāra,* not in the spiritual world. Moreover in *Bhagavat-sandarbha*, when commenting on *na vidyate yasya ca janma karma ca* (SB 8.38), by establishing the eternal nature of all the pastimes, Jīva Gosvāmī has destroyed all mistaken opinions. It has already been said *atra paramotkarṣaḥ śṛṅgārasya pratiṣṭhitaḥ*: the supreme position of śṛṅgāra-rasa is established in paramour love. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 1.19)

The foundation of our philosophy is that Kaṁsa is Svayam Bhagavān, the complete manifestation of all perfection. He is eternally most completely, with completeness of all his *śaktis.* *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta* also agrees. The Lord is endowed with all *śaktis* for producing all excellence, all power, all sweetness, pastimes and for fulfilling all his desires. If there is absence of excellence of *rasa* in the spiritual world pastimes *(aprakaṭa*), the sweetness and fulfillment of all desires arising from his excellent *śaktis* would be absent. With such absence or small manifestation, the completeness of Svayam Bhagavān would not be accomplished. Thus he would be imperfect. What type of goal and *sādhana* could be established by this?

“The excellence of *rasa* is accomplished in the *prakaṭa* pastimes on earth, and in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes it will be experienced by hearing and remembering those pastimes in an assembly.” That is true. There would still be a fault since, with lack of happiness from enjoyment of *parakīya* affairs. There would also be lack of fulfillment of the desire for enjoyment of union arising from remembering those pastimes. This would be the condition. What more can be said on the subject?

### Text 4

***vrajendra-nandanatvena suṣṭhu niṣṭhām upeyayuḥ \|***  
***yāsāṁ bhāvasya sā mudrā sad-bhaktair api durgamā \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The workings of the** ***bhāva*** **of the** ***gopīs*** **who accept Kṛṣṇa, excellently fixed in his form as the son of Nanda, are hard to understand, even for various knowledgeable devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *gopīs* have made statements like the following:

*akṣaṇvatāṁ phalam idaṁ na paraṁ vidāmaḥ*  
*sakhyaḥ paśūn anaviveśayator vayasyaiḥ*  
*vaktraṁ vrajeśa-sutayor anuveṇu-juṣṭaṁ*  
*yair vā nipītam anurakta-kaṭākṣa-mokṣam*

**O friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Mahārāja Nanda are certainly fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by their friends, driving the cows before them, he holds the flute to his mouth and glances lovingly upon the residents of Vṛndāvana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of vision. SB 10.21.7**

Following these statements and the Lalita-*mādhava*, the author shows the fixed nature of the *gopīs* love. Of the two sons of Nanda, they gaze at one with the face having the flute.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The main *rasa, śṛṅgāra-rasa*, has two types of mood: with married and unmarried Kṛṣṇa. The first type manifests with Kṛṣṇa identifying himself as the son of Vasudeva, and the second manifest with Kane identifying himself as the son of Nanda. It is found that the women of Dvārakā married to Kane express desire for Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda, with the mood of the *upapati.*

*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. SB 10.16.36**

*na vayaṁ sādhvi sāmrājyaṁ svārājyaṁ bhaujyam apy uta*  
*vairājyaṁ pārameṣṭhyaṁ ca ānantyaṁ vā hareḥ padam*  
*kāmayāmaha etasya śrīmat-pāda-rajaḥ śriyaḥ*  
*kuca-kuṅkuma-gandhāḍhyaṁ mūrdhnā voḍhuṁ gadā-bhṛtaḥ*

**O saintly lady, we do not desire dominion over the earth, the sovereignty of the King of heaven, unlimited facility for enjoyment, mystic power, the position of Lord Brahmā, immortality or even attainment of the kingdom of God. We simply desire to carry on our heads the glorious dust of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s feet, enriched by the fragrance of kuṅkuma from His consort’s bosom. SB 10.83.41-42**

*vraja-striyo yad vāñchanti pulindyas tṛṇa-vīrudhaḥ*  
*gāvaś cārayato gopāḥ pada-sparśaṁ mahātmanaḥ*

**We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord’s feet that the young women of Vraja, the cowherd boys and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire—the touch of the dust he leaves on the plants and grass as he tends his cows. SB 10.83.43**

Do the women of Vraja desire to experience Kṛṣṇa as the son of Vasudeva married to his consorts? This is the question. The present text answers. The *gopīs* accept that constant form (*niṣṭām*) of Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda alone, which is most excellent (*suṣṭhu*). This means that even in dreams Kṛṣṇa does not think himself to be the son of Vasudeva. The *gopīs* accept that form of Kṛṣṇa. This means that they have the *sthāyi* known as *rati* for that particular form.

“What is this strong favoritism for Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda, since Kṛṣṇa is only one person with two identities due to time and place?” The workings are hard to understand even by various devotees with knowledge. According to the saying *tad vijānanti tad-vidaḥ*, those who experience the taste of that *bhāva* know it by realization.

### Text 5

***yathā lalita-mādhave (6.54)—***  
***gopīnāṁ paśupendra-nandana-juṣo bhāvasya kas tāṁ krtī***  
***vijñātuṁ kṣamate durūha-padavī-sañcāriṇaḥ prakriyām \|***  
***āviṣkurvati vaiṣṇavīm api tanuṁ tasmin bhujair jiṣṇubhir***  
***yāsāṁ hanta caturbhir adbhuta-ruciṁ rāgodayaḥ kuñcati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **When Kṛṣṇa playfully manifested himself as Nārāyaṇa, full of splendor with four victorious hands, the** ***gopīs’*** **love for that form became restricted. Even a learned scholar cannot understand the nature of their love, which moves to a mysterious object, a love which is fixed upon the Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Rādhā was lamenting in separation from Kṛṣṇa who had gone to Mathurā, she bathed at Khelā-tīrtha and went to the sun globe. There Saṁjñā, the wife of the sun god, consoled by having her meet Viṣṇu situated in the sun. Viśākhā speaks to Sāmjñā in this verse. Who can understand the nature (*prakriyām*) of the *gopīs’ bhāva*? No one can. That *bhāva* moves to a place difficult to understand, focusing on (*juṣaḥ*) the son of Nanda, not the son of Vasudeva. Or that *bhāva* moves to a place difficult to understand, composed of affection (*juṣaḥ*) for the son of Nanda. When Kṛṣṇa, to joke with them, showed the form of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha (*vaiśṇavīṁ tanum*) full of splendor (*abdhuta-rucim)* with four glorious arms, attraction for that form by the *gopīs* became restricted. Appearance of attraction for Kṛṣṇa’s form revealed as Viṣṇu did not take place in the *gopīs.* It was previously said:

*rāgollāsa-vilaṅghitārya-padavī-viśrāntayo’py uddhura-*  
*śraddhā-rajyad-arundhatī-mukha-satī-vṛndena vandyehitāḥ \|*

**The women who have transgressed the path of** ***dharma*** **out of strong love are worshipped and sought by a host of chaste women headed by Arundhatī, attached to them with great faith.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamānī*** **3.18**

### Text 6

***bhujā-catuṣṭayaṁ kvāpi narmaṇā darśayann api \|***  
***vṛndāvaneśvarī-premṇā dvibhujaḥ kriyate hariḥ \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Though he shows four arms as a joke, the Lord was forced to revert to two arms because of the** ***prema*** **of Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows the special nature of Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among the *gopīs,* Rādhā‘s *bhāva* is most astonishing.

### Text 7

***yathā—***  
***rāsārambha-vidhau nilīya vasatā kuñje mṛgākṣī-gaṇair***  
***dṛṣṭaṁ gopayituṁ svam uddhura-dhiyā yā suṣṭhu sandarśitā \|***  
***rādhāyāḥ praṇayasya hanta mahimā yasya śriyā rakṣituṁ***  
***sā śakyā prabhaviṣṇunāpi hariṇā nāsīc catur-bāhutā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: At the beginning of the rāsa dance Kṛṣṇa hid himself in a bower. By inspiration he decided to show his form with four arms in order to hide himself from the gopīs. The greatness of Rādhā was such that by the effulgence of her glory he was unable to maintain his form with four arms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A proof from tradition is given.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Gautamīya-tantra* says:

*vasanta-kusumāmoda-surabhi-kṛta-diṅ-mukhe*  
*govardhana-girau ramye sthitaṁ rāsa-rasotuskam*

**He enjoyed the situation of happiness of the** ***rāsa*** **dance, at Govardhana at a place filled with fragrance of spring flowers.**

At a place at the foot of Govardhana called Parāsaulī, the place of the *rāsa* dance, .at the beginning of the dance, Kṛṣṇa hid himself and remained there (*nilīya vasatā*), at a bower in the forest called Praviṣṭakā, commonly known as Peṭha. In order to hide himself from sight (*dṛṣṭam gopayitum*), by inspired intelligent, thinking “I will do this” he showed his form with four arms because it was impossible for him to flee the bower, as it was surrounded by all the *gopīs.* “Oh! That is not Kṛṣṇa. That is the form of Nārāyaṇa with four arms.” All the *gopīs* offered him respects and begged,  
”Please show us Kṛṣṇa.” When Rādhā came, the greatness of Rādhā’s love was so astonishing (*hanta*). By the effulgence (*śriyā)* of that greatness (*yasya*), he could not maintain that four armed form *(sā*).

The following should be considered. Though Brahmā, Indra and Śiva display powers elsewhere, those are restricted in front of the supreme lord Bhagavān. In front of him their powers do not manifest at all. Whatever powers they have do not remain. This is because of their eternal dependence on him. But one should not say that because Bhagavān is dependent on *prema,* in front of *prema* his powers cannot remain, since his powers are eternal. However they can become invisible. *Prema* by its nature is unlimited. However, it is sometimes just a small particle, sometimes the greatest expanse, sometimes a great expanse, and sometimes more or less according to circumstance.

Thus there are four levels of quantity of *prema.* The small particle of *prema* exists in the devotees not having developed *rati.* Because *prema* cannot be detected, the Lord’s dependence also cannot be detected. The greatest amount of *prema* can be found in Rādhā. Kṛṣṇa is absolutely dependent on her since *prema* is most complete. Therefore his powers cannot manifest in her presence. In the Purāṇas there is a story of how his powers manifested in showing the pastime of lying on Śeṣa on the ocean. However, that was because of her desire to see that pastime.

A great amount of *prema* manifests in the inhabitants of Vraja. Kṛṣṇa is dependent on them completely because of the greatness of the *prema*, but not absolutely (as with Rādhā). Sometimes his powers manifest in front of them to some degree, but it cannot restrict their *prema.* When Kṛṣṇa kills Pūtanā or Aghāsura, shows the universe in his mouth, or refuses to be tied up, they do not investigate this show of power because of their devotion to Kṛṣṇa. The greatness of their *prema* is the cause. Even if they notice his powers when he went to Varuṇa and was worshipped, when he swallowed the forest fire, or held up Govardhana, their conception of him as their relative and child is much stronger because of their attachment to him. This is not so in other persons. Vasudeva, Devakī and the Pāṇḍavas have weaker thoughts of their relationship to him.

*ūtī-gṛhe nanu jagāda bhavān ajo nau*  
*sañjajña ity anu-yugaṁ nija-dharma-guptyai*

**Indeed, while still in the maternity room you told us that you, the unborn Lord, had already been born several times as our son in previous ages. SB 10.85.20**

*devakī vasudevaś ca vijñāya jagad-īśvarau*  
*kṛta-saṁvandanau putrau sasvajāte na śaṅkitau*

**Devakī and Vasudeva, now knowing Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to be the Lords of the universe, simply stood with joined palms. Being apprehensive, they did not embrace their sons. SB 10.44.51**

*sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktaṁ*  
*he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti \|*  
*ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ*  
*mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi \|\|*

**I beg pardon from you, for not knowing your greatness. Through want of consideration or through affection, I looked upon you, the immeasurable, as a friend. I beg pardon for whatever I have said rudely, such as addressing you as “O Kṛṣṇa! O Yādava! O friend!” BG 11.41**

In the inhabitants of Vraja, there is complete amount of *prema* and complete dependence. The fourth case, of having less or more *prema* according to circumstance, is seen in Nārada and others. In such cases, the Lord is dependent on the amount of *prema* according to the circumstance.

Thus though Kṛṣṇa is dependent on *prema* in all cases, when there is absolute dependence (on Rādhā), then his powers cannot manifest at all. Among local leaders, because some are dependent on others, they may show their powers, but in front of the head man, they do not show powers at all.

“The independence of the Supreme Lord has been nullified by this. This is not approved by writers of scriptures, since the Lord then becomes like the *jīva.”* This is not a fault in the Lord, but it is a great quality in him. *Māyā* controls the *jīva* and makes him suffer. The dependence of the j*īva* on *māyā* is the cause of his suffering. *Bhakti,* the *śakti* of the Lord, controls the Lord to give happiness to the Lord. Lord becomes dependent on *bhakti* to give him happiness. That is a fact. Similarly Rādhā is dependent on her *sakhīs* for her happiness.

### Text 8

***api ca—***  
***sāmānyāyā rasābhāsa-prasaṅgāt tādṛg apy asau \|***  
***bhāva-yogāt tu sairindhrī parakīyaiva sammatā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kubjā had only a similarity to a prostitute who cannot have** ***rasa*** **with Kṛṣṇa because of relationships with many other men. Because of her** ***bhāva,*** **she is said to be a** ***parakīyā*** **lover of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows that the maid servant Kubjā has a manifestation of *rasa*. She cannot be called *sāmānyā* or a prostitute. Prostitutes never develop *bhāva*. Previously Kubjā did not have *bhāva* for anyone else, since that type of relationship was prevented by her ugly appearance and because she had strong affection for Kṛṣṇa which would manifest in the future. When giving him sandalwood, she is described as having *anurāga*, in a *rasa* for Kṛṣṇa. It did not arise afterwards, from pulling his upper cloth in order to have intimate association with him. With that in mind, this verse is spoken. Because of her possession of *bhāva* she is considered to have a *parakīya* relationship. However the word *eva* means that she had something similar to *parakīya.* *Eva* can mean *iva* (like) according to the grammarian Kātantara. It should be said that her *rati* was less than that of the queens of Dvārakā. The reason her love is called *parakīya* is that her love is hidden from the public. There is another version with *parakīyeva (parakīya iva).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Common women (prostitutes) are either *parakīyā* or *svakīyā.* There are three types of *nāyikās.* Two types have been shown: the *parakīyā* and *svakīyā* types of Vraja and Dvārakā. Is there a third type of *nāyikā* of Kṛṣṇa? This verse explains. Because of *rasābhāsa*, because she is related with many men, the common prostitute is not a *nāyikā* of Kṛṣṇa (though this is not stated explicitly in the sentence). This is the implied meaning. Ablative case (*prasaṅgāt*) gives the reason that it is not possible. There is invariable concomitance, as in the case of transitive verbs necessarily being connected to objects. When we say “enter” we mean “enter the house” and when we say “eat” we mean “we eat the cake.” Because of prostitutes are related to many men, Kubja is only somewhat similar to them.

Though the maid servant Kubjā was similar to a prostitute, she was not a prostitute since she did not the tendency to have union with many men. She was like a prostitute in that she did not have respect for marriage. She had *bhāva,* and because she enjoyed with Kṛṣṇa, without others knowing, her love is called *parakīya.* Because of her *bhāva,* she thought, “Kṛṣṇa alone is my lover in secret.” Though she was most beautiful, she was protected from other men by being a hunch back. Therefore it is said:

*āhūya kāntāṁ nava-saṅgama-hriyā*  
*viśaṅkitāṁ kaṅkaṇa-bhūṣite kare*  
*pragṛhya śayyām adhiveśya rāmayā*  
*reme ’nulepārpaṇa-puṇya-leśayā*

**Calling forward his beloved, who was anxious and shy at the prospect of this new contact, the Lord pulled her by her bangled hands onto the bed. Thus he enjoyed with that beautiful girl, whose only trace of piety was her having offered ointment to the Lord. SB 10.48.6**

### Text 9

***yathā ca prāñcaḥ (śṛṅgārahi-tilake 1.62,64)—***  
***sāmānyā vanitā veśyā sā dravyaṁ param icchatā \|***  
***guṇa-hīne ca na dveṣo nānurāgo guṇiny api \|***  
***śṛṅgārābhāsa etāsu na śṛṅgāraḥ kadācana \|\|9\|\| iti \|***

**Перевод:**

**The ancient authority says: The prostitute does not hate the man with inferior qualities, nor have attraction for the man with superior qualities, but simply desires money. This is a corrupted form of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa,*** **and not** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse proves that that prostitute has rasābhāsa. The prostitute represents others as well, such as maid servants.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author gives proof of the *rasābhāsa* nature of the prostitute by describing the normal prostitute’s nature.

### Text 10-11

***svakīyāś ca paroḍhāś ca yā dvidhā parikīrtitāḥ \|***  
***mugdhā madhyā pragalbheti pratyekaṁ tās tridhā matāḥ \|\|10\|\|***  
***bheda-trayam idaṁ kaiścit svīyāyā eva varṇitam \|***  
***tathāpi sat-kavi-granthe dṛṣṭatvāt tad-anādṛtam \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Previously two types of** ***nāyikās*** **were described: the** ***svakīyā*** **and the** ***paroḍhā.*** **These two types of** ***nāyikās*** **are of three types:** ***mugḍhā, madhyā*** **and** ***pragalbhā*****. Some say that the three types only belong to the** ***svakīya*** **woman*****,*** **but according to the works of expert poets, this opinion should not be accepted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some persons, who do not accept the *rasa* of *parakīya,* say that the three types belong only to *svakīyā* women. The poet’s work says:

*parakīyā dvidāḥ proktā proḍhā kanyakātathā*  
*yātrādi-niratāny oḍhā kulaṭā galita-trapā*  
*kanyā tv ajātopayamā saljjā nava-yauvanā*

**There are two types of** ***parakīyās*****: the** ***paroḍhā*** **(married to another man) and the** ***kanyakā*** **(unmarried). The** ***paroḍhā*** **is engaged in worldly affairs, is unchaste and free of shame. The** ***kanyā,*** **not being married, is shy and blooming with new youth.**

This statement concerning *parakīyā* concerns circumstances where *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is secondary, not the main *rasa,* as was previously explained. Jayadeva does not mention the *parakīya* variety (*upapati* love) as the main *rasa.* Instead he says:

*tām aprāpya mayi ssvayaṁvara-parāṁ kṣīroda-tīrodare*  
*śaṅke sundari kāla-kūṭam apiban mūḍho mṛdānī-paith*

**O beautiful one! When the Lord of Pārvatī (Śiva) could not attain you on the shore of the ocean of milk, bewildered by your beauty, he swallowed the deadly** ***kālakūṭa*** **poison. Then you selected me to be your consort.** ***Gīta-govinda*** **12.27**

By establishing Rādhā as Lakṣmī the possibility of *parakīya* is repudiated. Jayadeva in the first verse depicts Rādhā as unmarried girl in the words of Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some only accept *svakīyā* heroines because *parakīya* destroys *rasa* by its *rasābhāsa* nature. It is thus useless. That is their opinion. However that opinion is not acceptable according to the present verse. This is understood by looking at the works of true poets. This opinion is not respected by real poets, but rejected. Those who are not real poets, who do not accept *rasa* in *parakīyā*, say that the three types are found only in the *svakīyā.*

### Text 12

***tathā prācīnaiś coktam—***  
***udāhṛti-bhidāṁ kecit sarvāsām eva tanvate \|***  
***tās tu prāyeṇa dṛśyante sarvatra vyavahārataḥ \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The authorities have said: Some poets accept the three mentioned types in both the** ***svakīyā*** **and** ***parakīyā*** **woman since they are seen everywhere in ordinary life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Accepting the *parakīyā* heroine in a secondary role, he quotes authorities. They say that these types are seen in both *svakīyā* and *parakīyā* women in ordinary life.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He gives proof by stating the opinion of poets*. Bidhām* means differences. .

### Text 13-14

***tatra mugdhā—***  
***mugdhā nava-vayaḥ-kāmā ratau vāmā-sakhī-vaśā \|***  
***rati-ceṣṭāsu sa-vrīḍa-cāru-gūḍha-prayatna-bhāk \|\|\|***  
***kṛtāparādhe dayite bāṣpa-ruddhāvalokanā \|***  
***priyāpriyoktau cāśaktā māne ca vimukhī sadā \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***mugḍhā:*** **The** ***mugdhā*** **is young, inexperienced in love, uncooperative in love, dependent on** ***sakhīs,*** **shy in love affairs with covered actions, weeps after her lover commits offense, does not reply to the lover with unkind words, and avoids pride.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *mugdhā* is described in her full form, and examples also show the full form of the *mugdhā.* Generally the *mugdhās* are young in years and affairs of love, but *prāgalbhās* are sometimes young also. This generality applies to later definitions also.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nava-vayaḥ* means youthful. *Kāma* means desire for amorous encounters. *Nava-kāma* means that she has only a little skill in the arts of love. The *prāgalbhās* are also sometimes young in years and some *mugdhās* are mature. One also sees inexperience in love in the *madhyās.* In *Vidagdha-mādhava* it is said *pādānte viluṭhaty asau mayi muhur daṣṭādharāyāṁ ruṣā:* if I piteously fall down at his feet, then this enemy of the Madhu demon, in an angry mood, bites my lips. (*Vidagdhā mādhava* 2.21) *Kva vāhaṁ kā vāhaṁ cakara kim ahaṁ vā sakhi tadā*: Where was I? Who was I? What was I doing? Friend, I did not know. (*Vidagdha-mādhava* 2.6) Uncooperativeness in love*,* dependence on friends, shyness, and covered actions are also seen in the *madhyās* and *prāgalbhās.* *Alaṅkāra-kaustubha* says *vārtāyām api surate parāṅmukhī sa-trapā mugdhā*: the *mugdhā* is modest, avoids amorous encounters and rumours.

### Text 15

***tatra nava-vayāḥ—***  
***viramati śaiśava-śiśire, praviśati yauvana-madhau viśākhāyāḥ \|***  
***dīvyati locana-kamalaṁ, vadana-sudhāṁśuś ca visphurati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Youth: When Viśākhā gives up the winter of childhood and entering the spring of youth, her lotus eyes sport and the moon of her face glows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing at a distance Viśākhā who has come to meet him, Kṛṣṇa speaks. The eyes play or the eyes blossom like lotuses. The word *ca* indicates dissension between the lotus and the moon in terms of their joy. In this example *vismaya-rasa* (astonishment) is the main *rasa*, and *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is the secondary *rasa.*

### Text 16

***yathā vā—***  
***bālya-dhvānta sakhe prayāhi tarasā rādhā-vapur-dvīpatas***  
***tāruṇya-dyumaṇer yad eṣa vijayārambhaḥ puro jṛmbhate \|***  
***kṛṣṇa-vyomni rucir darottaralatā tārā-dyutau kāpy uraḥ-***  
***pūrvādrau suṣamonnatiḥ smita-kalā paśyādya vaktrāmbuje \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend, darkness of childhood! Please leave quickly! From the island of Rādhā’s body, the sun of youth is beginning its victory march. See today the beauty in the dark sky, slight trembling in the luster of the stars of her eyes, the increasing beauty in the eastern mountain of her breasts, and a slight smile on the lotus of her face.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tārā* refers to the pupils of the eyes and to the stars.  *Ruci* means desire and beauty.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā is given as an example of the characteristics of the *mugdhā.* Śyāmalā describes Rādhā in a joking mood. The ingredients of *rasa* such as *rati, prema* and *sneha,* and various gestures are established as eternally present in Rādhā in this metaphor. Just as it is understood that objects like pots and cloth when in darkness are not seen but are still present, so the qualities mentioned here are present in Rādhā previous to her manifestation of *śṛṅgāra*, but not visible to anyone because of being covered by childhood. She addresses Rādhā’s childhood in a joking manner. O friend! I am your friend. Rādhā’s youth had not appeared because of your covering nature. Like her, I cannot be mocked by anyone. Go quickly! Otherwise, on coming near you, her youthfulness will destroy you. Out of friendship she gives good advice to childhood. With even a slight appearance of Rādhā’s youth, her childish actions will be suddenly given up. Again she jokes. Her youth makes its appearance (*jṛmbhate*) victoriously, to defeat its enemies. The symptoms are then described. In the dark sky or in the sky taking the form of Kṛṣṇa, beauty or desire appears. The stars tremble in fear or the pupils of her eyes are fickle in movement. Her breasts are raised like mountains. They were not like that in childhood. They are extremely beautiful in the sun’s rays (*suṣamonnatiḥ*) or are raised up with beauty.

### Text 17

***nava-kāmā, yathā—***  
***bāle kaṁsa-bhidaḥ smarotsava-rase prastūyamāne chalāt***  
***prauḍhābhīra-vadhūbhir ānata-mukhī tvaṁ karṇam adhyasyasi \|***  
***savyājaṁ vana-mālikā-viracane’py ullāsam ālambase***  
***raṅgaḥ ko’yam avātarad vada sakhi svānte navīnas tava \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Inexperience in love: O child! As the proud cowherd women make preparations for the enjoyment of the festival of Cupid with Kṛṣṇa using deceptive words, with lowered face you listen. Making a garland on some pretext, you show that you are filled with joy. O friend! Speak up! Some new, extraordinary happiness now manifests in your heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A proud messenger speaks*. Raṅgaḥ* means festivity.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Dhanyā. *Prauḍhābhīra-vadhubhiḥ* refers to Śyāmā, Lalitā, Rādhā and other cowherd women. The women talk using deceptive words.

“O Rādhā! Explain whatever you have learned from the *guru* of pastimes in the bower.” “O Śyāmā, it is difficult to learn this difficult scripture by my feeble intelligence. You must continually teach me. You should tell me the stories in his Purāṇa. I will become successful by your mercy.” “O Rādhā! Enough with pretenses! Today the *guru* of pastimes learns from you. He is coming to learn from you. We should hear the topics from your mouth. We should hear them constantly.” In this way an introduction was made (*prastūyamāne*). When this was talk was taking place, Dhanyā lowers her head, revealing her tolerance. *Anāta* means whirling, curved or bowed. She thinks, “Desiring pious credits, I should make this garland on the pretext of worshiping the *devatās”. Raṅgaḥ* means festivity. *Avātarat* means he will appear.

### Text 18

***ratau vāmā, yathā--***  
***nava-bālikāsmi kuru narma nedṛśaṁ***  
***padavīṁ vimuñca śikhi-piñcha-śekhara \|***  
***viracanti paśya paṭavas taṭīm imā-***  
***maravinda-bandhu-duhitur nata-bhruvaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Uncooperative in love: I am an innocent child. You should not joke with me like that. Get off the road, O peacock feathered boy! See! The clever women with curved brows are wandering on the bank of the Yamunā River.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Going to the bank of the river (verb is omitted), they wander there.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Dhanyā speaks. Kṛṣṇa tries to extort a fake toll from her on the road. “On the pretext of taking a tax, do not try to loosen the knot on my sash!” Give just a little enjoyment to me. “But I am just a young girl.” If the toll remains with you, I will grab it. “See! The clever women are wandering on the bank of the river. I will not agree unless we have a private place.” In describing the women with curved brows, she indicates that they are her friends.

### Text 19

***yathā vā—***  
***yamunā-puline vilokanān me***  
***calitāṁ smera-sakhī-gṛhīta-hastām \|***  
***ayi muñca karaṁ mameti khañjad-***  
***vacanāṁ khañjana-locanāṁ smarāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: I remember her, the bank of the Yamunā, her hand held by a smiling friend, fleeing on seeing me, saying “Let go of my hand” in a choked voice, while her eyes moved about like** ***khañjana*** **birds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When he grasped her hand, she prevented him. *Ayi* indicates an entreaty. *Viśva-koṣa* says *ayi* means a question or entreaty.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since the previous example did not illustrate strongly the *vāma* woman, another example is given. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. Her friend smiles and says “Returning to the forest has been successful for you.” Holding her hand, she says “Why are you going?” When Kṛṣṇa takes her hand she says “Let go! You are not my friend. You are my enemy, because you desire to throw me into danger.” Her voice sounds like the *khañjana* bird. She makes indistinct sounds with her voice. This is choking of the voice, a *sāttvika-bhāva*. Her eyes are fickle like the *khañjana* birds flight. This indicates *cāpalya*, a *sañcari-bhāva*. Because of fear, *sāttvika* and *sañcari-bhāvas* appear in the *sthāyi-bhāva.* The woman is Rādhā. She is ornamented with *vilāsa* (coyness).

### Text 20

***sakhī-vaśā—***  
***vraja-rāja-kumāra karkaśe***  
***sukumārīṁ tvayi nārpayāmy amum \|***  
***kalabhendra-kare navodayāṁ***  
***nalinīṁ kaḥ kurute janaḥ kṛtī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Controlled by her friends: I will not give this tender young girl to harsh person like you. What intelligent person would give a newly blossomed lotus to the trunk of an elephant?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Rādhā comes to a planned meeting with Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa pulls her with force towards him. Seeing the bold gestures of his hands, Lalitā pulls Rādhā back and speaks. The image of the elephant and the lotus is *arthāntara-nyāsa*. This suggests the following words: If you give up you nature as an elephant and become like a bee, I will give her to you.

### Text 21

***yathā vā—***  
***na svīkṛtā sakhi mayā srag ihāsti kaundī***  
***kiṁ dīrgha-roṣa-vikaṭāṁ bhru-kuṭīṁ tanoṣi \|***  
***kṣipteyam atra mama maṇḍana-peṭikāyāṁ***  
***ced vṛndayā caṭulayā kim ahaṁ kariṣye \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O friend! I did not accept this jasmine garland from Kṛṣṇa. Why do you frown at me in anger? If unsteady Vṛndā has put that garland in jewel box, what can I do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous example Lalitā helped her friend, but Lalitā displays extreme *vāma* tendencies (uncooperativeness in love). The sense of Rādhā depending on her friend is therefore minimized. Therefore another example is given. When Kṛṣṇa, pleasing Dhanyā by giving her a garland, departed, a bold friend who teaches how to act arrogantly in front of Kṛṣṇa arrived. Dhanyā became frightened and took off the garland and placed it in her jewel box. Then she spoke. Dhanyā indicates that Vṛndā put the garland there in spite of Dhanyā’s refusal, and thus produced a cause of this friend scolding her. Dhanyā says Vṛndā is her enemy.

### Text 22

***savrīḍa-rata-prayatnā, yathā—***  
***dvitrāṇy etya padāni kuñja-vasater dvāre vilāsonmukhī***  
***sadyaḥ kampa-taraṅgad-aṅga-latikā tiryag-vivṛttā hriyā \|***  
***bhūyaḥ snigdha-sakhī-girāṁ parimalais talpāntam āseduṣī***  
***svāntaṁ hanta jahāra hāri-hariṇī-netrā mama śyāmalā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Shyness in love affairs: Eager for love, Śyāmalā took a few steps at the doorway of the bower. Immediately her vine-like body, erupted in waves of trembling, and in shyness she turned around. By the sweet fragrance of words of tender** ***sakhīs*****, she then came to the edge of the bed. Oh! Śyāmalā with attractive doe eyes attracts my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *mugdhā* is shy in her actions during amorous encounters. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala in the morning. She desired amorous pleasure (*vilāsonmukhī*). The phrase also means that her face was beautiful or attractive. This is ornament called *vilāsa*. The vine of her body was wavy with shaking. Immediately, at that moment, she turned around, because of the sudden force of seeing her beloved. This means with his left hand he removed her veil. This caused her to turn around. At this time simultaneously she experienced apprehension, embarrassment, confusion, and impatience (*vyabhicāri-bhāvas).* The *sakhīs* who were like tender creepers (*snigdha-sakhī*) spoke many affection words in order to bring her inside, using *sāma* (calming) and *dāna* (rewarding) which caused her to come forward or retreat. The word *girām* and *parimalaih* are both in the plural to indicate the many attempts. The words were like flower buds, having fragrance. She was like a female bee, attracted the fragrance, and he was like a male bee. Attracted by the fragrance, she finally came in and was enjoyed by the male bee. The ornaments of *atiśayoki* and *aprastuta-praśaṁsa* are used. She had attractive *(hāri*) doe eyes. He relished the movements of the edges of her eyes at that time.

### Text 23

***roṣa-kṛta-bāṣpa-maunā, yathā—***  
***siddhāparādham api śuddha-manāḥ sakhī me***  
***tvāṁ vakṣyate katham adakṣiṇam uddhateva \|***  
***nemāṁ viḍambaya kadamba-vanī-bhujaṅga***  
***vaktraṁ pidhāya kurutām iyam aśru-mokṣam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Weeping caused by anger when the lover offends her, and silence: How can my pure minded friend speak to an awkward person like you, who have offended her? She is completely disturbed. O snake in a kadamba forest! Do not joke with her. Covering her face, may she continue weeping.**

**Viśvanātha:**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

A friend of Dhanyā who has been insulted by Kṛṣṇa, speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Uddhatā* means disturbed in mind. Do not joke around (*viḍambaya*) by offering respects. You are a snake, or a lecher in the small forest (*vanī*). This implies “She knows that you enjoyed with another girl in the forest at night.” Do not obstruct her weeping. It is her fate that she cries.

### Text 24

***atha māne vimukhī—***  
***mṛdvī tathākṣamā ceti sā māne vimukhī dvidhā \|\|24\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are two types of women who distain pride: the soft woman and the incapable woman.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *akṣamā* (incapable) the word *uddatā* (disturbed) is also seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since “unable to say unkind words to her love” has not been illustrated, it is understood that it is included in the previous example of “silence and tears when the lover offends.” In verse 14 it was said *priyāpriyoktau cāśaktā māne ca vimukhī sadā*. The two words *ca* indicate separate items. “Unable to say unkind words” was generally illustrated in the previous verse, and therefore a separate example has not been given. Avoidance of pride has two types.  *Mṛdvī* means a woman who has mild pride. *Akṣamā* means woman with no pride. The *mṛdvī* (though a *mugdhā*) is touched with a portion of the *madhyā* woman. Th*e akṣamā* is extremely *mugdhā.*

### Text 25

***tatra mṛdvī, yathā rasa-sudhākāre (1.156)—***  
***vyāvṛtti-kramaṇodyame’pi padayoḥ pratyudgatau vartanaṁ***  
***bhrū-bhedo’pi tad īkṣaṇa-vyasaninā vyasmāri me cakṣuṣā \|***  
***cāṭūktāni karoti dagdha-rasanā rūkṣākṣare’py udyatā***  
***sakhyaḥ kiṁ karavāṇi māna-samaye saṅghāta-bhedo mama \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The soft woman, from** ***Rasa-sudhākāra:*** **When I try to go away, my feet return to him. If I frown, my eyes, eager to see him, forget to do this. Though I want to speak to him with rough words, my miserable tongue speaks pleasing words. O friends! What am I to do when showing anger? My senses have rebelled.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vyasmāri cakṣuṣā* means “forgotten by my eyes.” Instead of *cakṣuṣā* the word *cetasā* is also found. *Saṅghāta-bhedaḥ* means “change in the senses.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Dhanyā speaks to her friends who have come to teach her how to be proud and angry, and ask how she is doing. When I turn my back and try to go away, I return to him instead. In front of him the feet do not want to go away. Frowning is forgotten by the eyes because they are attracted to him. The tongue causes misfortune (*dagdha*). There is difference in my senses (*saṅghāta*). Though she wants to leave, frown and scold, after seeing him, their nature changes to the opposite. The senses have become crazy because of some black arts, by throwing of dust invoked with mantras, or some magical ointment.

### Text 26

***akṣamā, yathā—***  
***ābhīra-paṅkaja-dṛśāṁ bata sāhasikyaṁ***  
***yā keśave kṣaṇam api praṇayanti mānam \|***  
***māneti varṇa-yugale’pi mama prayāte***  
***karṇāṅganaṁ vahati vepathum antarātmā \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The incapable woman: What rashness of the women with lotus eyes, that even for a moment they show pride or anger on seeing Kṛṣṇa. If the two syllables** ***māna*** **enter my ears, my heat begins to shake.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Someone speaks to a friend who is teaching her how to show anger. She scolds all angry women. *Sāhisikyam* means audacity*. Keśave* means “on seeing Keśava.” This woman never shows anger at Kṛṣṇa. In giving examples of “showing tears when offended by her lover” the phrase *roṣakṛta-bhāṣpa* (tears arising from anger) is used. However, the moment she sees her lover, she becomes peaceful, the agitation of body, words and mind caused by anger disappear because of the pressure of bliss on seeing him. In the next instance, anger itself disappears.

First, Kṛṣṇa sees the women with tears and anger. However, her anger disappears with just a touch of the bliss of seeing Kṛṣṇa. This is the *akṣamā* woman. Anger does not begin. In the case of the *mṛdvī* however her anger disappears with the pressure of bliss on seeing him. The anger begins but does not become complete. That is the difference.

### Text 27

***atha madhyā—***  
***samāna-lajjā-madanā prodyat-tāruṇya-śālinī \|***  
***kiñcit-pragalbha-vacanā mohānta-surata-kṣamā \|***  
***madhyā syāt komalā kvāpi māne kutrāpi karkaśā \|\|27\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***madhyā:*** **The** ***madhyā*** **woman has equal shyness and desire, is full youth, has somewhat bold speech, has the possibility of love affairs after fainting, is mild in anger and sometimes rough.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *madhyā* has equal amounts of shyness and desire. The *mugdhā* has more shyness and less desire. The *pragalbhā* has less shyness and more desire. The *mugdhā* has slight youth, the *madhyā* has medium youth and the *pragalbhā* has full youth. The *mugdhā* is not bold, the madhyā has slight boldness and the *pragalbhā* has full boldness. *Moha* means fainting because of bliss, arising with the appearance of strong desire. The phrase *mohānta-surata-kṣamā* means that it is possible that the *madhyā* faints and then has her love affair for a moment. She cannot faint afterwards. The *mugdhā* has bliss only because of having very little desire. She does not faint. It is not possible because she has little strength even for exchanges of love. The *madhyā* does not have sufficient strength to faint after the loving exchange. The *pragalbhā* because of her strong passion, can enjoy relationships first, and then faint in bliss because of greater strength. Thus the *mugdhā* is capable of affairs without fainting; the *madhyā* is capable of fainting before loving affairs; and the *pragalbhā* is capable of fainting after an affair.

### Text 28

***tatra samāna-lajjā-madanā, yathā—***  
***vikirati kila kṛṣṇe netra-padmaṁ sa-tṛṣṇe***  
***namayati mukham antaḥ-smeram āvṛtya rādhā \|***  
***nidadhati dṛśam asminn anyataḥ prekṣate’muṁ***  
***tad api sarasijākṣī tasya modaṁ vyatānīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Equal shyness and desire: When Kṛṣṇa, full of desire, glances with his lotus eyes, Rādhā covers her head and lowers it, with a suppressed smile. When he glances away, she glances at him directly, and gives joy to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Anataḥ-smeram* means a smile which is suppressed. She does not glance at him because he is directly gazing at her. The *pragalbhā* smiles explicitly because of little shyness. When she lowers her head she glances at him slightly. When the lover glances at her, the *madhyā* glances back. The *mugdhā* does not glance, because of greater shyness. This is made clear. When he glances elsewhere completely, she then looks at him directly *(prekṣate*). When she knows that he will glance, she does not glance directly.

### Text 29

***prodyat-tāruṇya-śālinī, yathā—***  
***bhruvor vikṣepas te kavalayati mīna-dhvaja-dhanuḥ-***  
***prabhārambhaṁ rambhā-śriyam upahasaty uru-yugalam \|***  
***kuca-dvandvaṁ dhatte ratha-caraṇa-yūnor vilasitaṁ***  
***varorūṇāṁ rādhe taruṇimani cūḍāmaṇir asi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Conspicuous youth: Your eyebrows destroy Cupid’s bow, proud of its splendor. Your two thighs mock the beauty of banana trunks. Your two breasts have the beauty of a pair** ***cakravāka*** **birds. O Rādhā! O jewel of youth! You are the crest jewel of women with beautiful thighs.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. Your brows devour the bow’s pride in its splendor. In front of you, Cupid’s bow has no splendor, what to speak of prowess. The arrows of your glances, which are millions of times more wonderful than Cupid’s arrows, will strike me. This idea is suggested. And I do not know what state I will be in then. This is further suggested. Your breasts have the beauty *(vilāsam*) of a pair of *cakravāka* birds (*ratha-caraṇa)* or they are like a pair of *cakravāka* birds playing together (*vilāsam*). The phrase *ratha-caraṇa-yūnoḥ*, like the phrase *śāka-parthiva*((king who eats spinach), has a missing term and should be *ratha-caraṇa-nāma-pakṣi-yunoḥ* (a pair of birds called *ratha-caraṇa* or *cakravāka* birds).

### Text 30

***kiñcit-pragalbhoktiḥ, yathoddhava-sandeśe (54)—***  
***mad-vaktrāmbhoruha-parimalonmatta sevānubandhe***  
***patyuḥ kṛṣṇa-bhramara kuruṣe kiṁtarām antarāyam \|***  
***tṛṣṇābhis tvam yadi kala-ruta vyagra-cittas tadāgre***  
***puṣpaiḥ pāṇḍu-cchavim aviralair yāhi puṁnāga-kuñjam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Somewhat bold speech from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: O black bee intoxicated by the fragrance of my lotus face, why do you try to stop me from serving my husband? O humming bee, if your heart is pained because of thirst, you should fly over to the** ***punnāga*** **forest thick with white flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some *gopī* indicates a place of meeting to Kṛṣṇa who has come secretly in the darkness of evening after playing his flute in the distance. Why do you create obstacles while I am engaged in serving my husband, doing cooking and other chores? She speaks in this way in order to make family members feel happy that she is a faithful wife.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Out of extreme longing, in some garden near Jaṭilā’s house, Kṛṣṇa plays the flute for a long time but sees that Rādhā does not come. In order to learn what she is doing, he sends a *sakhī.* Rādhā sees the *sakhī* but she is surrounded by mother-in-law and other elders. Speaking to a bee, she indicates a meeting place far off to the *sakhī.* By addressing the bee, she says “you have not considered that it will be difficult to accomplish pastimes in a garden so near the houses of elders. I am engaged in serving my husband by heating water and other chores.” She says this to please her mother-in-law and sister-in-law.

O humming bee! If I am prevented by elders who understand by hearing the sound of your flute, what is going to happen? Do not play the flute. Go to the *punnāga* forest far away. Or, if you cannot go far because of overriding thirst, then leave the garden and go to the bower close by. In that bower, which is pale in color (*pāṇḍu-chhavim*) it will be hard for people to see us, since there is profuse moon light in the night. And because it is thick with flowers, they cannot enter. Because it is fragrant, it is suitable for *śṛṅgāra-rasa*.

### Text 31

***mohānta-surata-kṣamā, yathā—***  
***śrama-jala-niviḍāṁ nimīlitākṣīṁ***  
***ślatha-cikurām anadhīna-bāhu-vallīm \|***  
***mudita-manasam asmṛtānya-bhāvāṁ***  
***rati-śayane niśi gopikāṁ smarāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Amorous pleasure after fainting: I remember that** ***gopī*** **at night on the bed. She was covered with perspiration, her eyes were closed, her hair was slack and her arms were weak. She thought of nothing else. Her mind was joyful.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of Kṛṣṇa as he meditates on Rādhā. *So’pi kām smarāmi* is another version of the last line. Another version has the last line *murajid amuṁ nahi vismrṭiṁ nināya.* Then it would be the words of Subala.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala asks “What are you thinking?” Kṛṣṇa then speaks this verse. Her perspiration is continuous. Her locks of hair are loosened. Her vine-like arms are weak, after amorous pleasure. She does not have thoughts of any other *viṣaya, āśraya* or *uddīpana.* (She thinks only of Kṛṣṇa, herself and the stimulants for *rasa.*) This is the characteristic of happiness in amorous pastimes. The state of fainting is understood from the beauty of her face at that moment. The phrase *mudita-manasam* has a weak meaning. The redundancy is caused by the state of *prema* of the speaker. “Her mind was pained by the fire of desire for me, but by union with me today, her mind is joyful. Therefore I have succeeded.” This reveals his intention.

### Text 32

***māne komalā, yathā—***  
***prāṇās tvam eva kim iva tvayi gopanīyaṁ***  
***mānāya keśi-mathane sakhi nāsmi śaktā \|***  
***ehi prayāva ravijā-taṭa-niṣkuṭāya***  
***kalyāṇi phulla-kusumāvacaya-cchalena \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Soft in showing anger: You are my very life! What can I hide from you? O friend! I cannot show anger towards the killer of Keśi. O auspicious friend, come! We will go to the bank of the Yamunā on the pretext of picking blooming flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is possible to make references to later pastimes (Kṛṣṇa, killer of Keṣi), since it has been established in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* and will be established in this work that Kṛṣṇa returned from Dvārakā to Vraja In the evening after Kṛṣṇa killed Keśi, Akrūra came to Vraja. This caused great disturbance. Thus this present verse is recited much later. “The co-wives will laugh. Therefore let us go to the bank of the Yamunā.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śrī Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. One should not worry that this pastime must have taken place latter, after the killing of Keśi, and that it is not an earlier pastime. Garga said at the time of giving Kṛṣṇa his name that he has many names (*bahūni santi nāmāni*). Those names are used to indicate Kṛṣṇa in Vraja. Thus the people of Vraja use names like killer of Keśi, killer of Mura, and killer of Kaṁsa even before those events occurred.

In the first part of the verse there are strong qualities of the *mugdhā*, but this is countered by the bold speaking typical of the *madhyamā.* Rādhā says, “Come! We will go to the bank of the Yamunā. Though other *gopīs* teach me to be angry, you alone are my life. You have been unjustly deceived by some *sakhī.* I will now go to meet Kṛṣṇa there.” “Are you going to him to beg for amorous pleasure?” Rādhā speaks angrily, “No, we will go there on the pretext of picking flowers.”

### Text 33

***māne karkaśā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (5.30)—***  
***mudhā mānonnāhād glapayasi kim aṅgāni kaṭhine***  
***ruṣaṁ dhatse kiṁvā priya-parijanābhyarthana-vidhau \|***  
***prakāmaṁ te kuñjālaya-gṛha-patis tāmyati puraḥ***  
***kṛpā-lakṣmīvantaṁ caṭulaya dṛgantaṁ kṣaṇam iha \|\|\|***

**Rough behavior in anger, form** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: O hard-hearted girl, why do you uselessly torture your body with this outburst of anger? Why are you angry to hear the prayers of your friends? Right here, the master of the bower abode is gasping for his beloved. For a moment give him a merciful glance from the corner of your eye.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. From an outburst (*unnāhāt)* of anger you give suffering, uselessly to yourself. *Priya-parijana* means “by your friends.” He is gasping (*tāmyati*). “How can I on my own destroy this anger which has come on its own?” Cast a fickle glance with the edge of your eye, full of a wealth of mercy at your lover *(iha*), who is bowing down. Order the glance to manifest externally. Do not suppress it. I say this to you, knowing your inner disturbance.

**When a women becomes angry she is classed in three types:** ***dhīra, adhīra*** **and a combination of both (*****dhīrādhīra*****).**

Because the *madhyās* are being described the *madhyās* who are *dhīra* are now described using the term *dhīra-madhyā*.

After becoming angry (*māna-vṛtteḥ*) women may be classed as *dhīra, adhīra* and *dhīrādhīra.* In order to make the present discussion clear, the word *madhyā* is added to the present subject (*dhīra-madhyā* etc.).  *Uptrāsam* means to deride with bold speech. This is accompanied by ironic laughter.

### Text 36

***yathā—***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because, in addressing Kṛṣṇa as *svāmi* and *paśūnām pate*, she uses somewhat bold words and because she speaks as a blossoming youth, she is considered a *madhyā.* The crooked words make it clear that she is a *dhīrā.* “It is suitable that you are marked with moon lines.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having been disappointed by him, Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. O lord of the animals, Śiva! Or lord of the cows, Kṛṣṇa! You are not very intelligent. Also it is indicated that Kṛṣṇa is master of other women who are like animals. The plural *paśūnām* indicates many women. This type of criticism reveals her knowledge of *śṛṅgāra-rasa,* and thus indicates that she has *prodyat-tāruṇi,* youthfulness manifested. Using the word *paśu* indicates her bold language. Because the words can have double meaning, the boldness is tempered somewhat. Thus she is considered a *madhyā.*

He is suitable because he is marked with digits of the moon --fingernail scratches (*candra-lekhā*). This is *atiśayokti.* All your limbs (*sarvataḥ*) are stained with red lac and collyrium. That is suitable since it indicates that the women were eager to touch all parts of your body. Enough of my fears! You have made me successful as a devotee of Śiva by becoming Śiva, being blue and red and carrying the crescent moon. If you become half-woman (Śiva), and thus make yourself invisible as Kṛṣṇa, my desire would be fulfilled.

Because of not developing patience and skillfulness in crooked words, the *adhīra* uses harsh language.

### Text 38

***yathā—***  
***uttuṅga-stana-maṇḍalī-sahacaraḥ kaṇṭhe sphurann eṣa te***

***dhūrtābhīra-vadhū-pratārita-mate mithyā-kathā-ghargharī-***

**Перевод:**

**An example: This necklace you wear has been the companion of the raised breasts of a great host of girls, and it is now clearly glorifying your nighttime pastimes with them. You mind has been cheated by a rascal** ***gopī!*** **O noisy liar, jingling like a bell! Leave here at once. It is not proper for you to stay here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *adhīrā* and *dhīrādhīra* women and later examples also, should be analyzed in the same way as the *dhīrā.* “Enemy of Kaṁsa” can be explained as previously.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Your necklace has associated with women’s breast, because of the fragrance and the *kuṁkuma* on it. I can confirm this with my eyes and nose. There is no doubt that last night you were enjoying other women. O enemy of Kaṁsa! Kaṁsa, your enemy, resides in Mathurā, but my enemy resides in my midst. Understand the cause of my sense of intolerance by your own experience. But you think that she who is actually without a drop of *prema* is filled with *prema.* Your intelligence has been cheated by a crafty cowherd woman, who shows her lust as *prema,* in the manner of counterfeit money. Kūṭa-kārṣāpaṇa nyāya.1 As you have been cheated by her false show of love, I have been cheated by  
your lies. You say “I do not know any one except you, even in my dreams.” You make a jingling sound of a bell with your lies. By the noise of your lies, like a jingling bell (*ghargharī*), the sound of thunderbolt of true statements by my friend, telling of your affair with my competitor, cannot be covered. Her statement is partially bold, because of the indirect expression. This indicates the *madhyā* woman.

### Text 39

***atha dhīrādhīra-madhyā—***  
***dhīrādhīra tu vakroktyā sa-bāṣpaṁ vadati priyam \|\|39\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***dhīrādhīra-madhyā:*** **The** ***dhīrādhīra-madhyā*** **speaks to her lover with harsh words and tears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *dhīrā* portion of her speaks crooked words and the *adhīrā* portion of her weeps tears. “But the *adhīrā* uses harsh words.” That is true. The following should be considered. Because the *pragalbhā* has full anger, beating the lover is the action—most serious. Because the *madhyā’s* anger is not full, the *madhyā* uses harsh words—a moderate action. Because the *mugdhā* has very little anger, her action is minimal—crying. The *dhīra-madhyā’s* harsh words, covered by self-control, become crooked words with irony. The *adhīra-madhyā’s* harsh words become simply harsh words because of lack of self-control. The *dhīrādhīrā* does not have full qualities of the *dhīrā* or *adhīrā* because of co-existence of self-control and lack of self-control. There are thus two portions of *dhīrādhīra*: one portion being *dhīrā* and one portion being *adhīrā.* Her *dhīrā* portion uses crooked words only. Because the *dhīrā* nature is not complete she does not use irony. Because of her *adhīrā* nature, she does not use rough words. But in her *adhīrā* portion, anger must be expressed, but this is not possible by words. She cannot beat the lover or use harsh words. What remains is a small amount of anger and tears. Thus the *dhīra-adhīrā* uses crooked words and tears.

There is no mixture of *mugdhā* qualities. The *mugdhā* simply weeps. The *madhyā dhīra-adhīrā* speaks with tears. This will be illustrated. The *dhīrādhīrā* by self-control has crooked words only and not sarcasm. But because of some lack of self control, she cries but does not use harsh words because of the presence of some self control. Self-control or *dhīra* means depth (*gāmbhīrya*).

### Text 40

***yathā—***  
***gopendranandana na rodaya yāhi yāhi***  
***sā te vidhāsyati ruṣaṁ hṛdayādhidevī \|***  
***tvan-mauli-mālya-hṛta-yāvaka-paṅkam asyāḥ***  
***pāda-dvayaṁ punar anena vibhūṣayādya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My dear prince of the cowherds, do not make me cry. Go! Go! The queen of your heart will become angry. Today, decorate her feet whose unguents were stolen from her feet by your crown and flower-garland.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Anena* indicates Rādhā pointing to the auspiciousness of lac. It does not become redundant by use in the compound as well. The defect of lack of coordination of words and meaning is not present. The meaning is “decorate her two feet again with the unguents stolen by your crown.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks. What harm is it to you, lover of millions of women, son of a king, if you make persons like me cry? Do not make me cry! Go! Go! When you go, when not seeing you directly, it will be possible for me to forget you, with some effort. “Please excuse my offense.” She then speaks to him when he offers respects. If the woman hears you trying to please me, she will become angry. Therefore I am advising you for your benefit as a friend. Forget about my pleasure. I am not angry. But do not say that she will not hear. She is the deity in your heart, controlling it. Offering yourself to her saying “You are mine and no one else’s” she remains there shining (*devī*). Therefore she will hear. You will commit offense to her by trying to approach me. Another offense to her can be seen in you. You must remove that offense. Decorate again her feet whose lac has been stolen by the garland on your head (when you bowed to her feet), by that lac decorating the garland on your head. You must return the stolen goods to its owner. Why do you bow to me? You should fall at her feet repeatedly. Because she is present as the deity of his heart, the word *asyāḥ* is used, indicating her immediate presence.

There is another meaning to avoid redundancy of words.

Make a special decoration of the lac stolen by the garland in your crown *(vibhūṣaya*). Take the lac from your garland, and place it on your crown. You should quickly use valuable stolen goods for your enjoyment. Or decorate her feet with the lac stuck on your crown. Offer respects to her to obtain forgiveness for your offense. Or, completely enjoy that woman who only desires enjoyment. Both meanings are possible because the word *mauli* can mean crown or valuable article. Enjoyment will be complete if you offer back to her, your mistress, goods stolen from her at the time of enjoying. There is no *adharma* in doing this. The strength of the word *punaḥ* can mean “to decorate many times.” Therefore this meaning is suitable.

She points out the lac with her finger using the word *anena* (that over there). Thus it is not redundant to the compound word. Therefore the fault of lack of coordination of words and meaning does not take place. This is Jīva Gosvāmī’s explanation.

### Text 41

***yathā vā—***  
***tām eva pratipadya kāma-varadāṁ sevasva devīṁ sadā***  
***yasyāḥ prāpya mahā-prasādam adhunā dāmodarāmodase \|***  
***pādālakta-citaṁ śiras tava mukhaṁ tāmbūla-śeṣojjvalaṁ***  
***kaṇṭhaś cāyam uroja-kuṭmala-suhṛn-nirmālya-mālyāṅkitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Go at once to the queen who can fulfill your desires! Continually serve her and attain her mercy! In this way you can enjoy her remnants. Place the red lac from her feet on your head. Make your mouth glisten with the remnants of betel-nuts chewed by her. Decorate your neck with the spotless flower garland that has become the friend of her flower-bud breasts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are two types of *dhīrādhīrā*: one with more *dhīrā* qualities and one with more *adhīrā* qualities. The predominantly *dhīrā* woman was described in the last verse. This verse describes the women with more *adhīrā* qualities. Go to the woman who offers you lust (and not *prema*). There is slight harshness in her words because of more *adhīrā* qualities. There are no tears as a sign of immaturity. Take shelter of her by offering yourself fully (*pratipadya*). Serve her constantly. Do not waste time. You cannot accomplish your goal by temporary service.

### Text 42

***sarva eva rasotkarṣo madhyāyām eva yujyate \|***

**Перевод:**

**All of the excellence of** ***rasa*** **is present in the** ***madhyā*** **heroine since she is mixed with the qualities of the** ***mugdhā*** **and the** ***pragalbhā.***

In the first example the *dhīrādhīrā* was mixed with *mugdhā* qualities clearly. In the present example the *dhīrādhīrā* is mixed with *pragalbhā* qualities. *Dhirādhīra madhyā* is natural to Rādhā. Some say that all three types arise naturally in Rādhā according to the amount of anger. The *adhīrā* nature of Rādhā is illustrated in *Gīta-govinda* with *yāhi mādhava, yāhi keśava, mā vada kaitava-vādam*: go away Mādhava, go Keśava! Stop your lies. (*Gīta-govinda* 8.3)

### Text 43

***atha pragalbhā—***  
***pragalbhā pūrṇa-tāruṇyā madāndhoru-ratotsukā \|***  
***bhūri-bhāvodgamābhijñā rasenākrānta-vallabhā \|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***pragalbhā:*** **The** ***pragalbhā*** **has full youth, is blinded with passion, has a strong desire for enjoying her lover, is skilful in manifesting many emotions, desires to control her lover, is bold in speech and actions, and is very rough when angry.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Uru-ratoskukā* means her *rati* is *sambhogecchā-mayī*, having a desire for enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa. This was mentioned in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*. *Tat-tat-bhāvecchā-mayī* love is considered superior. Kubja was given as an example of the *sambhogecchā-mayī.* The women of Vraja are the latter type. That is explained by the term *rasenākrānta-vallabhā:* she overcomes her lover with *rasa*, composed of *prema.* The *pragalbhā* endeavors to give happiness to her lover because in *prema* the goal is only to give the lover pleasure. This is *tat-tad-bhāvecchā-mayī* love.

### Text 44

***tatra pūrṇa-tāruṇyā, yathā—***  
***muṣṇāti stana-yugmam abhramu-pateḥ kumbha-sthalī-vibhramaṁ***  
***visphāraṁ ca nitamba-maṇḍalam idaṁ rodhaḥ-śriyaṁ luṇṭhati \|***  
***dvandvaṁ locanayoś ca lola-śapharī-visphūrjitaṁ spardhate***

**Перевод:**

**Full youth: My dear Candrāvalī! Your breasts eclipse the charm of the frontal lobes on the elephant Airāvata. Your broad hips steal the beauty of the Yamuna's shore. Your eyes challenge the pride of the** ***śapharī*** **fishes. You are cleansed by the sweet nectar of your youthfulness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Visphūjitam* means pride. Your eyes compete with the pride of *śapharī* fish.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Abhramu-pateḥ* means “of Airāvata.” *Rodhaḥ-śriyam* means the beauty of the bank. *Visphūrjitam* means pride and indicates completion or rivalry.

*kāla-bhādhva-deśānām antar-bhūta-kriyāntaraiḥ*  
*sarvair akarmakaiḥ yoge karmatvam upajāyate*

**When time, distance, activity or place is syntactically connected with an intransitive verb and has another action expressed in it, the time, distance, activity or place takes the accusative case.**

*Dvandvaṁ locanayoś ca lola-śapharī-visphūrjitaṁ spardhate* means literally “your two eyes compete with the pride of the fish.” The intransitive verb is *spardhate* and *visphūrjitaṁ* is in the accusative case.

***sadyaḥ-prodyad-uru-pramoda-laharī-vismāritātma-sthitir***

***uru-ratotsukā, yathā—***

***skhalad-barhākalpāṁ dalad-amala-guñjā-maṇisarām \|***  
***mamānaṅga-krīḍāṁ sakhi valaya-riktī-kṛta-karāṁ***  
***manas tām evoccair maṇita-ramaṇīyāṁ mṛgayate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Strong desire for conjugal pleasure: O friend, my heart yearns to enjoy increasingly bold amorous pastimes with Kṛṣṇa, where our bodies are profusely spread with fingernail marks, where his peacock-feather ornament falls away, my** ***gunja*****-necklace breaks, the bracelets slip from my wrists, and my voice murmurs loudly in conjugal bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vaiyātyam* means boldness. *Amara-kosa* says *viyāta* means proud.  *Manīta* means the sounds of the woman during love making.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Gopīs* with *samartha-rati* have strong desire for enjoyment of love. But we will explain later this is ultimately for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa. One should see the discussion in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* concerning *sambhogecchāmayī* and *tat-tad-bhāvecchātmā* love within *kāma-rūpa-bhakti.* One can conclude the religious or irreligious nature of a king by observing the religious or irreligious nature of his followers. Similarly from seeing these two types in *kāmānuga-bhakti* (part of *rāgānuga-sādhana-bhakti*, following *kāma-rūpa-bhakti*) one can infer these two types in *prema-bhakti*. Because of the woman being the *nāyikā* of Kṛṣṇa, it is reasonable to conclude that such desire for enjoyment is for the pleasure of the lover.

Maṅgalā speaks to a *prāṇa-sakhi* in private. My mind always pursues amorous pastimes of the night, which has spontaneous increase of (*udañcat*) boldness of the two lovers. Even though that boldness is a masculine quality, she has no personal fault since the boldness arises independently, on its own. *Amara-koṣa* says that *viyāta* means bold or confident. *Nakha-pada* means fingernail marks. *Maṇita* means the sounds made during love making.

***bhūri-bhāvodgamābhijñā—***

***kuñje guñja-dalau virājasi cirāt kūjad-vipañcī-svarā***  
***baddhuṁ bandhura-gātri kṛṣṇa-hariṇaṁ śaṅke tvam ākāṅkṣasi \|\|\|***

**Skilful at manifesting many symptoms of love: You are now your crooked sidelong glances like the tips of shackles, and you are also expanding the creepers of your eyebrows. Your face is concealed by the flower-bud of a meaningful smile, and your bodily hairs are standing up in ecstasy like sprouts. Your voice sounds like a** ***vīṇā*****.
