You desire to control (*bandhum)* by friend ship, or control by binding up.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa from far off, her friend Bakula-mālā, laughing internally, speaks to Śyāmā, who has made all preparations and is about to meet Kṛṣṇa. You want to bind up the black deer, or you want to attract Kṛṣṇa with affection. You have a crooked, oscillating (*preṅkan*) glance, which is like the tip of a chain (*śrṅkhala-śikhā*). In anger and speculation she thinks “H is coming after such delay because of having enjoyed some other women.” Her brows are expanded. “I know all about you. You speak the truth when you say that you are late because of collecting the cows.” This indicates pride and envy. Seeing him change color out of worry from her false appearance of anger, her face is concealed with the bud of a meaningful smile. He has been fooled by my false show of anger. This indicates her concealed peace and mercy. Giving up fear, he prays “Give me the treasure of amorous pleasure which I so much desire.” Hearing this, her body erupts in goose bumps. This indicates the appearance of the *sthāyi-bhāva* of *rati.* Her voice sounds like a *vīṇā.* She says “I do not have the wealth of amorous pleasure in my bag now. But the faithful girls like Pālī are there to give it to you in plenty. Leave the bower and beg it from them.” She jokes with longing and impatience.

Spreading her brows, covering her face, scattering the sprouts of goose bumps and making attractive sounds are means of trapping the deer. “But that pleasure is there in your knotted cloth. So, undo the knot on your sash and show me whether it is there or not.” In this way Kṛṣṇa enacts his plan.

### Text 48

***rasākrānta-vallabhā, yathā—***  
***avacinu kusumāni prekṣya cāruṇy araṇye***  
***viracaya punar ebhir maṇḍanāny ujjvalāni \|***  
***madhumathana mad-aṅge kalpayākalpam etair***  
***yuvatiṣu mama bhīmaṁ rautu saubhāgya-bherī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Desires to control her lover: O Kṛṣṇa, looking at the beautiful flowers in the forest, please pick these flowers, make splendid ornaments from them, and then decorate my body with those ornaments. In this way, may the trumpet of my good fortune be loudly sounded among the young** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Picking flowers and making garlands indicate only activities of affection but are only a pretext for having Kṛṣṇa decorate her. Thus these activities indicate her nature of controlling him. This is understood from the statement, “Let the trumpet of my good fortune be sounded loudly to the young women.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The desire of the *pragalbhā* is “My lover should always be satisfied with me because of profuse *rasa*.” Maṅgalā speaks. You should pick the flowers personally, not making someone else do it. Looking at the beautiful flowers, she thinks these are suitable for decorating her. Others should not discover them and take them. She thinks “On seeing your creation of decorations, I will make the young girls become astonished.” If the man is eager to follow the orders of the woman (because of her qualities), she is called *santātāśrava-keśava* (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 4.15) and if she is eager to make him follow her orders she is called *rasākrānta-vallabha*. In special circumstances if the man follows the orders of the woman obediently she is called *svādhīna-bhartṛikā.* Thus there are three types.

### Text 49

***atiprauḍhoktiḥ, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (280)—***  
***kākuṁ karoṣi gṛha-koṇa-karīṣa-puñja-***  
***gūḍhāṅga kiṁ nanu vṛthā kitava prayāhi \|***  
***kutrādya jīrṇa-taraṇi-bhramaṇātibhīta-***  
***gopāṅganā-gaṇa-viḍambana-cāturī te \|\|49\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Very bold speech, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O Kṛṣṇa, O cheater! Disguising yourself with this heap of dried cow-dung, why do you uselessly make such a clamor? Go away! You used to be very expert at tricking the** ***gopīs,*** **frightening them in an old boat.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kākum karoti* means “You make sounds like a cuckoo in making arrangements for meeting.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa come to her house in stealth out of great desire, even without her consent, Śyāmalā became pleased. But then for fun, showing external anger to frighten him, she said “I will reveal your real nature to the elders.” She then speaks this verse.

Cow dung has been piled up at the corner of the house for cooking purpose. Kṛṣṇa smears himself with to disguise himself as an old man. Pointing a finger at his face, he says, “Haha, show them this old man.” Why do you make such sounds (*kākum*)? If you desire your good fortune, please leave this place! Remembering his previous mode of action, and making him recall how he put her is such trouble, she speaks, taking revenge. You used to be so expert at tricking the *gopīs.*

### Text 50

***atiprauḍha-ceṣṭā, yathā—***  
***sakhyās tavānaṅga-raṇotsave’dhunā***  
***nanarta muktā-latikā stanopari \|***  
***utplutya yasyāḥ sakhi nāyakaś calo***  
***dhīraṁ muhur me prajahāra kaustubham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Very bold actions: My friend, when your friend Candrāvalī and I were engaged in our festive amorous battle, the necklace on her breasts danced. During that dancing, the reckless chief pearl on her necklace jumped down and repeatedly beat my innocent Kaustubha jewel.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Padmā coming after Kṛṣṇa has completed his enjoyment with Candrāvalī, Kṛṣṇa speaks, in order to embarrass Candrāvalī. *Utplutya* means jumping down.

*Nāyaka* is the main jewel in the necklace. That jewel repeatedly beat my innocent (*dhīram)* Kaustubha. *Dhīram* also means “learned.” Using the words *cala* and dhīra, Kṛṣṇa makes clear their difference. She replies “Let your Kaustubha beat my jewel having a hundred good qualities” for it is said “He who beats another person is beaten by that person in return.”

### Text 51

***māne’tyanta-karkaśā, yathā uddava-sandeśe (53)—***  
***medinyāṁ te luṭhati dayitā mālatī mlāna-puṣpā***  
***tiṣṭhan dvāre ramaṇi vimanāḥ khidyate padmanābhaḥ \|***  
***tvaṁ connidrā kṣapayasi niśām rodayantī vayasyā***  
***māne kas te nava-madhurimā taṁ tu nālokayāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Very rough in anger, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O beautiful one! The jasmine plant with wilted flowers is suffering on the ground. Kṛṣṇa with the lotus-navel now stands, dejected, at your doorstep. You passed the whole night sleepless, making your friends cry. What new sweetness do you find in this jealous anger? I see no sweetness in it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bakula-mālā speaks to Śyāmalā. What offense has the jasmine plant committed, that you make it suffer by not picking its flowers or watering it? This indicates her extremely rough behavior.

### Text 52

***māna-vṛtteḥ pragalbhāpi tridhā dhīrādi-bhedataḥ \|\|52\|\| (raṣu. 1.103b)***

**Перевод:**

**According to the amount of anger displayed the** ***pragalbhās*** **are divided into three types:** ***dhīrā, adhīrā*** **and** ***dhīrādhīrā.***

### Text 53

***tatra dhīra-pragalbhā—***  
***udāste surate dhīrā sāvahitthā ca sādarā \|\|53\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***dhīra-pragalbhā*****: The** ***dhīra-pragalbhā*** **shows and respect and hides her anger while showing indifference to love affairs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Related to *māna (māna-vṛtteḥ)* there are three types of *pragalbhās*. Because the *pragalbhā* has been defined already, only her *dhīra* characteristics are mentioned here. The *dhīrā* shows respect and hides her anger. Showing indifference to loving affairs (*surate udāste*) the *dhīrā* will deny her anger. “I am not like that.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In showing anger (*māna-vṛtteḥ*), the *pragalbhā* has three types. The *dhīra-pragalbhā* becomes indifferent (*udāste*). Some persons may think that the word *ca* indicates two types of *dhīra-pragalbhā*: one who hides her nature and one who is reverent. On becoming angry, the *pragalbhā,* becoming indifferent to love, becomes *dhīra* in concealing her feelings of anger or in showing respect. The concealment of anger would be because of perfect self-control and the show of respect would be because of imperfect self-control. The examples are given in the opposite order however (the imperfect self-control given first and the perfect self-control given second) because of the predominance of order of the types over the order of words of the present text, to indicate the superiority of the one with perfect self-control.

According to the author’s opinion however, the first type, with complete self-control, is the *dhīra-pragalbhā.* It should be understood that the second type, because of not being completely in control of her self, has some degree of lack of self-control. Therefore she is actually a borderline *dhīrā-pragalbhā,* not a real *dhīra-pragalbhā.* This will be indicated by the words *yathā vā* in verse 56, where the example of a real *dhīra-pragalbhā* is given.

### Text 54

***yathā—***  
***devī nādya mayārciteti na hare tāmbūlam āsvāditaṁ***  
***śilpaṁ te paricitya tapsyati gṛhīty aṅgīkṛtā na srajaḥ \|***  
***āhūtāsmi gṛhe vrajeśitur iti kṣipraṁ vrajantyā vacas***  
***tasyāśrāvi na bhadrayeti vinayair mānaḥ pramāṇīkṛtaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Hari! I have not worshipped Devī today, so I cannot taste your betel nut. I cannot accept your garland because my husband will be pained on seeing your skill. I cannot hear your words because I am being called to Yaśodā’s house and must go quickly. Saying this politely, Bhadrā showed her anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Pālī speaks to her friend. The meaning is clear. This verse in not in all editions.

### Text 55

***yathā vā—***  
***kaṇṭhe nādya karomi durvrata-hatā ramyām imāṁ te srajaṁ***  
***vaktuṁ suṣṭhu na hi kṣamāsmi kaṭhinair maunaṁ dvijair grāhitā \|***  
***kā tvāṁ projjhya calet khaleyam aciraṁ śvaśrūr na ced āhvayed***  
***itthaṁ pālikayā harau vinayato manyur gabhīrīkṛtaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: I cannot put this garland around my neck because I am performing a severe austerity. I cannot speak at all since the strict** ***brāhmaṇa*** **women have made me perform a vow of silence. I would not give you up and go away if the mischievous mother-in-law were not calling me at this moment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse illustrates the dhīra-*pragalbhā*. Her boldness and her self-control are evident. Because she speaks boldly with the words “severe” “strict” and mischievous” in reference to others she is known as *pragalbhā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

I cannot put the garland on my neck because I am performing severe austerity—which I do not care for. This indicates respect and hiding her love. The *brāhmaṇa* women are harsh. They do not know *rasa.* They have made me take this vow of silence. I cannot break this vow even for a moment at your loving request. “At least stay with me for a moment.” Who would not do so? Her use of bold words “severe,” “strict,” and “mischievous” indicate that she is a *pragalbhā.* Her avoidance of amorous pastimes and her hiding her anger on the pretext of vows indicates that her self-control is not complete.

### Text 56

***yathā vā—***  
***kucālambhe pāṇir na hi mama bhavatyā vighaṭito***  
***muhuś cumbārambhe mukham api na sācīkṛtam abhūt \|***  
***parīrambhe candrāvali na ca vapuḥ kuñcitam idaṁ***  
***kva labdhā mānasya sthitir iyam anālokita-carī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: You did not block my hand from touching your breast. You did not turn your mouth away when I kissed you constantly. O Candrāvalī! You did not withdraw your body when I embraced you. What an amazing state your mind has attained!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse shows inscrutability, respect and concealment, but in the mind. Thus she is a *dhīrā*. Because of her hardness in anger, and her full youth, with ability to block his hands, she is a *pragalbhā*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The word *vā* in the phrase *yathā vā* (another example) indicates satisfaction by giving an example of full self-control. According to the author’s opinion there are not actually two varieties of *dhīra-pragalbhā*. This verse indicates the following. My dear Candrāvalī, why are you angry? “No, I am not angry. Do you see some indication in my mind? What opportunity could my mind find, since you are without offense?” If that is so, will you let me touch you? “Of course, I will let you. What doubt is there? This body is yours.” She says this externally. Internally however, she thinks out of anger, “I have given up love for him. Let him know about this body given to him. What is it to me?” This indifference shows her complete self-control as a *dhīrā.*

Kṛṣṇa indicates by the statement *kvā labdhā* “Today I have not obtained even a drop of happiness from enjoying you. How amazing!”

### Text 57

***atha adhīra-pragalbhā—***  
***santarjya niṣṭhuraṁ roṣād adhīrā tāḍayet priyam \|\|57\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***adhīra-pragalbhā*****: The** ***adhīra-pragalbhā*** **attacks her lover out of anger, after scolding him cruelly.**

### Text 58

***yathā—***  
***mugdhāḥ kaṁsaripo vayaṁ racayituṁ jānīmahe nocitaṁ***  
***tāṁ nīti-krama-kovidāṁ priya-sakhīṁ vandemahi śyāmalām \|***  
***mallī-dāmabhir ucchalan-madhukaraiḥ saṁyamya kaṇṭhe yayā***  
***sākṣepaṁ cakitekṣaṇas tvam asakṛt karṇotpalais tāḍyase \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa, enemy of Kaṁsa! Being foolish women, we do not know how to do things properly for you. We offer respects to our dear friend Śyāmalā. She bound you around the neck with garlands filled with buzzing bees and attacked you incessantly with lotus ear decorations, while your eyes trembled.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Gaurī speaks. Considering ourselves *mugdhās* (innocent), we do not know how to behave properly. We offer respects to Śyāmalā. This indicates we want to learn how to act from her. Our minds and words reach perfection by binding you with garlands and attacking you with ear ornaments. To beat directly with the hands is not very pleasant. Thus it is not described here. Some say that Śyāmalā is an example of the *adhīra-pragalbhā.*

### Text 59

***atha dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā—***  
***dhīrādhīra-guṇopetā dhīrādhīreti kathyate \|\|59\|\| (raṣu. 1.105)***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***pragalbhā*** **woman with qualities of the** ***dhīrā*** **and** ***adhīrā*** **is called the** ***dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā.***

### Text 60

***yathā—***  
***sphurati na mama jātu krodha-gandho’pi citte***  
***vratam anu gahanābhūt kintu maune manīṣā \|***  
***aghahara laghu yāhi vyājam āstāṁ yad etāḥ***  
***kusuma-rasanayā tvāṁ bandhum icchanti sakhyaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My heart does not show a speck of anger for you. I have decided to perform a vow of silence. O killer of Agha! Leave this place immediately. Give up all deceit. The** ***sakhīs*** **desire to bind you with cords from the flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

By saying she is not angry she shows her *pragalbhā* nature of the *dhīra* type. I have taken a vow of silence but out of affection for you I am giving up that vow (since I am speaking to you now). Putting *vāyja* in the neuter instead of the masculine is a recording mistake.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Maṅgalā speaks. Go quickly. Give up the pretence of showing your innocence (*vyāja āstām*). They will tie you up with strings for making flower garlands. Or, they want to tie you with bells decorated with flowers and keep you here. Then you will not be able to see your lover.

### Text 61

***yathā vā—***  
***kṛtāgasi harau puraḥ sphurati taṁ bhramad-bhrū-latā***  
***titāḍayiṣur uddhurā śruti-taṭād vikṛṣyotpalam \|***  
***na tena tam atāḍayat kim api yāhi yāhīti sā***  
***bruvaty ajani maṅgalā sakhi paraṁ parāñcan-mukhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! Moving her brows, firmly desiring to beat Kṛṣṇa, who has committed some offense, Maṅgalā took off her earrings. But she did not beat him with them. She said “Leave, leave!” She then simply turned her head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first part of the verse shows her *pragalbhā* nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because of expressing herself with a phrase with a double meaning, indicating the *adhīrā* nature, the author was unsatisfied with the previous verse, and thus gives another verse to express her *dhīrā* nature as well as her *adhīra* nature. The first three lines who her *adhīra* nature clearly. She showed respect to her lover, by simply (*param*) turning her face, having emotions worthy of a true *nāyikā.* The word *añcat* (honor) in parāñcat shows that by receiving his glance she was pleased. Therefore she hid her anger by turning her face.

Turning her head was not unfavorable, but not favorable. This is expressed by the word *ajani (*I do not know.) Though this is so, her *dhīra* nature is indicated because she does not show any signs of agreement with Kṛṣṇa, even though he falls at her feet and makes many attempts to pacify her.

According to Sāhitya-darpaṇa the characteristic of the *dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā* is *dhīrādhīra tu solluṇṭha-bhāṣitaiḥ khedayaty amum*: the *dhīrādhīrā* causes pain with sarcastic words.

*analaṅkṛto ‘pi sundara harasi mano me yataḥ prasabham*  
*kiṁ punar alaṅkṛtas tvaṁ samprati nakhara-kṣatais tasyāḥ*

**O handsome man! Since even without ornaments, you attract my mind strongly, ornamented with that woman’s nail marks, how much more attractive you are.** ***Sāhitya-darpaṇa*** **3.63**

This example is not in agreement with the author, since it reveals the *dhīra-madhyā.*

### Text 62

***kiśorikāṇām apy āsām ākṛteḥ prakṛter api \|***  
***prāgalbhyād iva kāsāṁcit pragalbhātvam udīryate \|\|62\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Among the girls, some are called** ***pragalbhā*** **because of they are older in years.**

### Text 63

***madhyā tathā pragalbhā ca dvidhā sā paribhidyate \|***  
***jyeṣṭhā cāpi kaniṣṭhā ca nāyaka-praṇayaṁ prati \|\|63\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***madhyā*** **and** ***pragalbhā*** **are two types: senior and junior in relation to the amount of affection shown by the man.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some girls are known as *pragalbhā* by maturity of their forms.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is possible to manifest *pragalbhā* nature somewhat simply by being older in years. The women should be classified as senior and junior based on the greater or lesser amount of love shown by the man.

### Text 64

***yathā—***  
***supte prekṣya pṛthak puraḥ priyatame tatrārpayan puṣpajaṁ***  
***līlāyā nayanāñcale kila rajaś cakre prabodhodyamam \|***  
***kṛṣṇaḥ śītala-tāla-vṛnta-racanopāyena paśyāgrata-***  
***stārāyāḥ praṇayād iva praṇayate nidrābhivṛddhi-kramam \|\|64\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Look! While the two women are sleeping separately in front of him, Kṛṣṇa, observing them, is now throwing pollen in Līlā’s eyes to try to wake her up. He is trying to make Tārā sleep more deeply by cooling her skillfully with a palm fan as if out of affection. Līlā is senior and Tārā is junior in this example.2**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tāla-vṛnta* means fanning.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

From far away, concealing herself, Vṛndā speaks to Nāndīmukhī, showing her the scene. He sprinkles pollen in her eye to break her deep sleep, though he could do so simply by pulling her hand. Since the pollen comes from flowers, it would not injure the eyes. He skillfully fans Tārā (*tāla-vṛnta-racana).*

### Text 65

***yathā vā—***  
***dīvyantyau dayite samīkṣya rabhasād akṣais tryahātma-glahair***  
***gaurīṁ ghūrṇitayopadiśya hitavad-dāya-prayogaṁ bhruvā \|***  
***tasyās tūrṇam upārjayann iva jayaṁ śikṣā-vaśenācyutaḥ***  
***śyāmām eva cakāra dhūrta-nagarī-saṅketa-vij jitvarām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Seeing the two girls playing dice passionately with the stake of giving themselves for three continuous days, Kṛṣṇa gave instructions using his brows to Gaurī how to manipulate the dice. But by that instruction, though she seemed to be winning, Kṛṣṇa, master of the skills of deception, made Śyāmā victorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Seeing the two girls playing dice passionately with the stake of giving themselves for three continuous days (*tryahātma-glahaiḥ*), teaching Gaurī how to manipulate the throwing by moving his brows for her advantage (*hitavat*), he made Śyāmā victorious among the two. He knew how to give deceitful instructions—he made a compact with crafty goddess of gambling--by which a person appears to win but actually loses the game.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse illustrated senior and junior *madhyās.* The present verse illustrates senior and junior *pragalbhās.* The word *vā* in *yathā vā* means “and.” Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. The two played at dice *(akṣaiḥ*) with giving oneself for three days with Kṛsṇa as the stake. *Amara-koṣa* says *glaha* means the stake in playing dice. Kṛṣṇa moved his brow to indicate his attraction for Gaurī. *Dhūrta-nagarī* means various deceptions. Kṛṣṇa had an agreement with various deceptions (*saṅketa-vid*). This means he had extraordinary skills at various deceptions or that he knows how to acquire for himself various deceptive skills.

Though it was evident that Kṛṣṇa by showing favor to Śyāmā gave her great fortune, he did it in such a way that she would not refuse out of her friendship to Gaurī. Otherwise Gaurī would feel some suffering in her mind. In showing favor to Gaurī, Śyāmā would not suffer since she was convinced that Kṛṣṇa would never give her up, and that his show of favoritism to Gaurī was only a show. Having affection for both of them, he accomplished his pastime as he desired. The pastime with Līlā and Tārā should be considered in the same way.

### Text 66

***kācit kāñcid apekṣya syāj jyeṣṭhety āpekṣikī bhidā \|***  
***ato bheda-dvayam idaṁ na kṛtaṁ gaṇanāntare \|\|66\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Women are** ***jyeṣṭhā*** **or** ***kaniṣṭhā*** **in comparison to each other. This division is not considered here in enumerating the different types.**

### Text 67

***kanyā mugdhaiva sā kintu svīyānyoḍhe ubhe budhaiḥ \|***  
***mugdhā-madhyādi-bhedena ṣaḍ-bhede parikīrtite \|\|67\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***kanyās*** **are all** ***mugdhās*****. The** ***svīyā*** **(married to Kṛṣṇa) and** ***paroḍhā*** **(married to another man) may be** ***mugdhās, madhyās*** **or** ***pragalbhās.*** **Thus there are six types.**

### Text 68

***madhyā-prauḍhe dviṣaḍ-bhede prokte dhīrādi-bhedataḥ \|***  
***kanyā svīyā paroḍheti mugdhā ca trividhā matā \|***  
***iti tāḥ kīrtitā pañcadaśa bhedā ihākhilāḥ \|\|68\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***madhyās*** **and** ***pragalbhās*** **have three types each:** ***dhīrā, adhīrā*** **and** ***dhīrādhīrā*** **(total of six types) and thus this total multiplied by the** ***svīya*** **and** ***paroḍhā*** **types makes twelve. Since the** ***mugdhās*** **are of three types:** ***kanyā, svīyā and paroḍhā*****, there is total of fifteen types.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *kanyās* (unmarried girls) are all *mugdhās*. Those married to Kṛṣṇa are of seven types: the *mugdhā, dhīra-pragalbhā*, *adhīra-pragalbhā, dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā*, *dhīra-madhyā, adhīra-madhyā, and dhīrādhīra-madhyā*. Those married to other men are of the seven same types. The total of *kanyā, svīyā* and *paroḍhā* is then fifteen. *Dvi-ṣad* means twelve. The three types of *madhyās* and *pragalbhās* are multiplied by the *svīyās* and *parodḥās* to make twelve. Added to this are the three types of *mugdhās.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *kanyās* have one variety called *mugdhā.* There are *svīya-mugdhā, svīya-madhyā svīya-pragalbhā* and *paroḍha-mugdhā, paroḍhā-madhyā* and *paroḍhā-pragalbhā*. This makes seven varieties. However if one takes the three types of *madhyās (dhīrā, adhīrā and dhīrādhīrā* ) in *svīyā* and *paroḍḥā* types it becomes six types, along with similar six types of *pragalbhās.* This makes twelve types. Taking the *kanyā,* and *svīya* and *paroḍhā mugdhās,* it becomes fifteen types.

### Text 69-70

***athāvasthāṣṭakaṁ sarva-nāyikānāṁ nigadyate \|***  
***tatrābhisārikā vāsa-sajjā cotkaṇṭhitā tathā \|\|69\|\|***  
***khaṇḍitā vipralabdhā ca kalahāntaritāpi ca \|***  
***proṣita-preyasī caiva tathā svādhīna-bhartṛkā \|\|70\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**All the women undergo eight conditions:** ***abhisārikā (*****going for an appointment*****), vāsa-sajjā*** **(decorating herself)*****, unkanthitā*** **(anxiety because of delay),** ***khaṇḍitā*** **(devastated)*****, vipralabdhā*** **(feeling cheated)*****, kalahāntaritā*** **(separation by quarrel)*****, proṣita-preyasī (*****great separation*****)*** **and** ***svādhīna-bharṭrkā*** **(controlling the lover)*****.***

### Text 71-72

***tatra abhisārikā, yathā—***  
***yābhisārayate kāntaṁ svayaṁ vābhisaraty api \|***  
***sā jyotsnī tāmasī yāna-yogya-veṣābhisārikā \|\|\|***  
***lajjayā svāṅga-līneva niḥśabdākhila-maṇḍanā \|***  
***kṛtāvaguṣṭhā snigdhaika-sakhī-yuktā priyaṁ vrajet \|\|72\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Going for an appointment: The woman who goes to meet her lover or is met by the lover, wearing clothing suitable for the full moon or dark moon is called the** ***abhisārikā.*** **Out of shyness she covers her body, makes her ornaments soundless and goes in the company of only one intimate friend to meet her lover.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When the night is full of moonlight she wears clothing suitable for that appointment and when the night is without moonlight she wears clothing suitable for that. Because of shyness, she covers herself with her other limbs (*svāṅga-līnā*).

### Text 73

***tatra abhisārayitrī, yathā—***  
***jānīte na harir yathā mama manaḥ-kandarpa-kaṇḍūm imāṁ***  
***māṁ prītyābhisaraty ayaṁ sakhi yathā kṛtvā tvayi prārthanām \|***  
***cāturyaṁ tarasā prasāraya tathā sasneham āsādya taṁ***  
***yāvat prāṇaharo na candrahatakaḥ prācī-mukhaṁ cumbati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The woman makes an appointment: I pray to you that you should act in such a way that he meet me while not knowing that my heart burns with longing. Use your skills with affection and accomplish this, while the rascal moon, taker of life, has not yet risen in the east.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a statement made by some *prāṇa-sakhī* who discerns the situation with positive and negative elements, and while revealing her great longing by her speech, personally prepares to send a messenger. Have him meet me in such a way that he does not know the longing I have in my mind which is like Cupid having an itch, which can be relieved by his touch. Even if peacefulness is lost, I will gain some control of my self-control. You must go since it will be difficult to endure this in front of him. Another version has *manas-tṛṣṇām imam dhṛṣtājām.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. If he finds out the itching of my love, it will be most embarrassing for a decent girl. I will be defamed. He will also laugh at me and become bold. You should describe to him my beauty and good character instead. You know the itching in my mind. I will describe this a little to you. It is the fourteenth lunar day of the dark moon. It is evening. You should go now. My life airs will remain for a few hours and not longer. The rascal named the moon should not rise in the east. The moon is called rascal *(hataka*) because it gives sorrow to others. Therefore has a useless life, like a living dead person. The construction is actually *candra-nāma-hataka* (rascal named the moon) with an omitted term, like *śāka-pārthiva* (king who enjoys spinach).

### Text 74

***atha jyotsnyāṁ svayam abhisārikā, yathā—***  
***indus tundila-maṇḍalaṁ praṇayate vṛndāvane candrikāṁ***  
***sāndrāṁ sundari nandano vraja-pates tvad vīthim udvīkṣate \|***  
***tvaṁ candrāñcita-candanena khacitā kṣaumeṇa cālaṅkṛtā***  
***kiṁ vartmany aravinda-cāru-caraṇa-dvandvaṁ na sandhitsasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Going to meet Kṛṣṇa in the moonlight: The moon has become beautiful in Vṛndāvana with its fullness. O beautiful woman! The son of the master of Vraja looks far off into the distance at the path you will tread. Wearing white flax cloth and anointed with sandalwood and camphor, why do not you put your lotus feet on the path?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kṣauma* is a fine cloth made of flax. It is used because it is white.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. The moon becomes most excellent in Vṛndāvana with it fullness and density*. Prath* means to proclaim. Not having the taste of seeing you, he looks far off *(udvīkṣate*) in the distance for you. Wearing flax cloth and anointed with sandalwood and camphor. This cloth is famous for being white.

### Text 75

***tāmasyāṁ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.22)—***  
***timira-masibhiḥ saṁvītāṅgyaḥ kadamba-vanāntare***  
***sakhi baka-ripuṁ puṇyātmānaḥ saranty abhisārikāḥ \|***  
***tava tu parito vidyud-varṇās tanu-dyuti-sūcayo***  
***hari hari ghana-dhvāntānyetāḥ svavairiṇi bhindate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Going in the darkness, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Friend, covering their limbs with dark cloth, many girls with pious credits go to meet Kṛṣṇa in the** ***kadamba*** **forest. Alas, the lightning splendor of your limbs, appearing through the cloth, dispelling the deep darkness, has become your enemy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. The luster of your body coming through the holes in the cloth pierces the deep darkness, which is your best friend. That luster is your enemy. By this *vyāja-stuti*, her great beauty is indicated.

### Text 76-77

***atha vāsaka-sajjā—***  
***svavāsaka-vaśāt kānte sameṣyati nijaṁ vapuḥ \|***  
***sajjī-karoti gehaṁ ca yā sā vāsaka-sajjikā \|\|\|***  
***ceṣṭā cāsyāḥ smara-krīḍā-saṅkalpo vartma-vīkṣaṇam \|***  
***sakhī-vinoda-vārttā ca muhur dūti-kṣaṇādayaḥ \|\|77\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Decorating her abode and body: The** ***vāsaka-sajjā*** **is a woman who decorates her house and her body when her lover is coming, because of the desire of the lover that she remains there. She is determined to enjoy with her lover, looks constantly at the path, gossips with her friends, and constantly looks anxiously for messengers to arrive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Svavāsaka-vaśāt* means “by the control of her own favorable situation.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sva-vāsakah* means to make her stay since the lover would desire this (*vaśāt).* “Stay in the bower. I will come quickly.” The desire of the lover makes her stay in the bower. Because of this, when the lover comes, she who decorates her body and the bower with things suitable for *śṛṅgāra,* is called a *vāsaka-sajjā*: one who decorates because she stays there. The implied meaning is that she decorates her body and the blower until the lover arrives, by the desire of the lover.

### Text 78

***yathā—***  
***rati-krīḍā-kuñjaṁ kusuma-śayanīyojjvala-ruciṁ***  
***vapuḥ sālaṅkāraṁ nijam api vilokya smita-mukhī \|***  
***muhur dhyāyaṁ dhyāyaṁ kim api hariṇā saṅgama-vidhiṁ***  
***samṛddhyantī rādhā madana-mada-mādyan matir abhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Seeing the brilliant flower bed, the bower for amours pastimes and her nicely decorated body, Rādhā smiles. Constantly thinking of how to meet him, increasing her fortunate at every moment, her mind takes delight in the intoxication of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a friend while observing Rādhā at a distance. Rādhā smiles, indicating to her body, “Today you will have a suitable nature to give enjoyment to my beloved.”

### Text 79-80

***atha utkaṇṭhitā—***  
***anāgasi priyatame cirayaty utsukā tu yā \|***  
***virahotkaṇṭhitā bhāva-vedibhiḥ sā samīritā \|\|\|***  
***asyās tu ceṣṭā hṛt-tāpo vepathur hetu-tarkaṇam \|***  
***aratir bāṣpa-mokṣaś ca svāvasthā-kathanādayaḥ \|\|80\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Anxiety because of delay: She who becomes anxious when her faultless lover has a delay in coming, who becomes filled with longing in separation, is called** ***utkaṇṭhitā*** **by those who know about love. Her actions include pain in the heart, trembling, wondering about the cause of his delay, dullness and tears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If the lover is at fault in the delay then she shows anger. This does not happen when there is a state of *utkaṇṭhitā.* After some time, she becomes anxious in separation (*virahotkaṇṭhitā*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She knows the lover is not at fault in his delay. If he is actually at fault, but she does not think so, then she still displays *utkaṇṭhitā* symptoms. If he is innocent, but she thinks he is at fault, then she becomes angry and remains separate from him.

### Text 81

***yathā—***  
***sakhi kim abhavad baddho rādhā-kaṭākṣa-guṇair ayaṁ***  
***samaram athavā kiṁ prārabdhaṁ surāribhir uddhuraiḥ \|***  
***ahaha bahulāṣṭamyāṁ prācī-mukhe’py udite vidhau***  
***vidhu-mukhi! na yan māṁ sasmāra vrajeśvara-nandanaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! Has Kṛṣṇa been bound by the ropes of Rādhā’s glances? Has he begun fighting with some wild demons? Aah! O moon faced friend! When the moon is rising in the east on the eighth day of the dark moon, the son of the king of Vraja does not remember me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Bahulāstami is the eighth day of the dark moon.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī speaks to Padmā. He did not remember me on eight day of the dark moon. It is not possible for him to remain thinking of my sweetness. Or he does not remember me. What misfortune for me! This expresses her despair.

### Text 82

***vāsa-sajjā-daśāśeṣe mānasya viratāv api \|***  
***pāratantrye tathā yūnor utkaṇṭhā syād asaṅgamāt \|\|82\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intense longing arises after decorating the room and waiting, when the mind is a state of resignation, and when meeting cannot take place because of others.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The resignation of mind is not because of thinking the lover is at fault. She thinks he is innocent.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The three times when longing occurs are described. Resignation of the mind is called *kalahāntaritā.*

### Text 83

***atha vipralabdhā—***  
***kṛtvā saṅketam aprāpte daivāj jīvita-vallabhe \|***  
***vyathamānāntarā proktā vipralabdhā manīṣibhiḥ \|***  
***nirveda-cintā-khedāśru-mūrcchā-niḥśvasitādi-bhāk \|\|83\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Feeling cheated: When the lover cannot make an appointment because of unfortunate circumstances, and the woman feels pain within, she is called** ***vipralabdhā*** **(cheated) by the wise. She shows despondency, contemplation, lamentation, tears, fainting, and heavy breathing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vipralabdhā* means cheated by the lover for some other reason, not intentional on the part of the lover.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She ascertains that he is not coming definitely.

### Text 84

***yathā—***  
***vindati sma divam indur indirā-***  
***nāyakena sakhi vañcitā vayam \|***  
***kurmahe kim iha śādhi sādaraṁ***  
***drāg iti klamam agān mṛgekṣaṇā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “The moon has risen in the sky. O friend! We have been cheated by the husband of Lakṣmī. What shall we do? Give me instructions with attention.” Suddenly Rādhā fainted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. The time for meeting has passed. He has gone away with Lakṣmī. What do we have to do with him? Instruct me concerning respect (*sādaram*). This means “Instruct me so that my respect for remaining alive does not manifest. I do not want to live.”

### Text 85

***atha khaṇḍitā—***  
***ullaṅghya samayaṁ yasyāḥ preyān anyopabhogavān \|***  
***bhoga-lakṣmāṅkitaḥ prātar āgacchet sā hi khaṇḍitā \|***  
***eṣā tu roṣa-niḥśvāsa-tūṣṇīṁ-bhāvādi-bhāg bhavet \|\|85\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Devastated: When the lover breaks an appointment, and enjoys with another woman, and then comes with the marks of enjoyment the next morning, the woman becomes devastated (*****khaṇḍitā*****). She shows anger, breathes heavily, and remains silent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When the time for meeting passes and the lover comes the next day with marks of his encounter, she becomes *khaṇḍitā*. Saying “I will come in the middle of the first part of the evening” but shows up at midnight, the condition of *khaṇḍitā* does not take place. If he does not show up, and comes the next morning, then she becomes *khaṇḍitā.* She will not be devastated if he has signs of enjoyment which are fake, in order to joke with her. Thus it is said here that he has enjoyed with another woman. She becomes devastated if he has had enjoyment with someone else.

### Text 86

***yathā—***  
***yāvair dhūmalitaṁ śiro bhuja-taṭīṁ tāṭaṅka-mudrāṅkitāṁ***  
***saṁkrānta-stana-kuṅkumojjvalam uro mālāṁ parimlāpitām \|***  
***ghūrṇā-kuḍmalite dṛśau vraja-pater dṛṣṭvā prage śyāmalā***  
***citte rudra-guṇaṁ mukhe tu sumukhī bheje munīnāṁ vratam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Seeing Kṛṣṇa in the morning with reddish lac on his body, with the marks of earrings on his shoulders,** ***kuṁkuma*** **from someone’s breast smeared on his body, and a crushed garland on his chest, with eyes rolling, Śyāmalā became angry in her heart, showed a smile on her face, and remained silent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *vraja-pateḥ* the phrase *mura-ripoḥ* is found sometimes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bakula-mālā, a friend of Śyāmā, speaks to a friend who asks. She saw Kṛṣṇa with a body black and red with lac, with earring marks (*tāṭaṅka*) on his shoulder. The word *vraja-pateḥ* (of the master of Vraja) means the enjoyer of many thousands of women according to the context. This is not astonishing for him at all. She became angry. The word *rudra-guṇam* suggests that her face and eyes became red. She was silent. These are the qualities of a *dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā.*

### Text 87

***atha kalahāntaritā—***  
***yā sakhīnāṁ puraḥ pāda-patitaṁ vallabhaṁ ruṣā \|***  
***nirasya paścāt tapati kalahāntaritā hi sā \|***  
***asyāḥ pralāpa-santāpa-glāni-niḥśvasitādayaḥ \|\|87\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Deliberate separation: The woman who rejects her lover in front of her friends and then suffers regret is called** ***kalahāntartitā.*** **She talks idly, feels pain and exhaustion and breathes deeply.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She rejects her lover in front of her friends. If she is alone, she cannot maintain her anger.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Kalahāntaritā* means “excluding quarrel.”  *Antara* means opportunity, limit, undergarment, interim, difference, a hole, other than oneself, an opportunity outside oneself, and the soul within. Another meaning is “separating after quarrel.”

### Text 88

***yathā—***  
***srajaḥ kṣiptā dūre svayam upahṛtāḥ keśi-ripuṇā***  
***priya-vācas tasya śruti-parisarānte’pi na kṛtāḥ \|***  
***namann eṣa kṣauṇī-viluṭhita-śikhaṁ praikṣi na mayā***  
***manas tenedaṁ me sphuṭati puṭapākārpitam iva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: I have thrown the garland he gave far away. I do not hear his pleasing words. I do not look when he bows down with his hair strewn on the ground. My mind is splitting open as if being heated by fire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to herself. *Puṭa* is a crucible, an earthen vessel. My mind is like some gold or silver put in a crucible for heating.

### Text 89

***atha proṣita-bhartṛkā—***  
***dūra-deśaṁ gate kānte bhavet proṣita-bhartṛkā \|***  
***priya-saṁkīrtanaṁ dainyam asyās tānava-jāgarau \|***  
***mālinyam anavasthānaṁ jāḍya-cintādayo matāḥ \|\|89\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lover in distant separation: When the lover goes to a far away place, the woman is called** ***proṣita-bhartṛikā*****. She glorifies her lover, feels miserable, becomes thin, stays awake, fades in complexion, becomes unsettled, becomes stunned and becomes absorbed in contemplation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Proṣita-bhartṛkā* and *svādhīna-bhartṛika* have the word *bhartṛikā* which refers to a married couple with *śṛṅgāra* as the main *rasa*. This is the usage of the writers of scriptures. In the definition of the *vāsaka-sajjā* the word “house” is used. The word *bhartṛkā* never refers to a paramour, since it is not possible to give the same meaning to a thief and a husband. Otherwise the word *svādhīna-jārā* (independent paramour) would be used like the word *svādhīna-pati* (independent married man). However because *jāra* is a vulgar word it is not used. The word *bharṭr* is also used in derogatory way according to context and can produce repulsion. One should not say that a married couple cannot have an appointment. A compliant husband may have problems with many strong cowives or may be bashful in front of many elders. Thus he can go for a meeting in private with his wife at an appointed time. Nor should it be said that everyone would know if a man was called from his own house, what to speak of going from another’s house, because by his cleverness it is possible to hide this. Therefore Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes of meeting in the enjoyment pastimes called *samṛddhimat* (when Kṛṣṇa unites with the gopīs after many years of separation and marries them) are possible. In *Lalita-mādhava,* out of fear of Candrāvalī, Rādhā always goes to the side of Kṛṣṇa in secret. Thus there are similar pastimes for the married man and the apparent *upapati.* One should not think otherwise.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Going far away, means when Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathurā and Dvārakā. Some say that the *proṣita-bhartṛkā* and the *svādhīna-bhartṛkā* cannot have a *parakīya* relationship since the word *bhartṛ* does not mean *jāra* (paramour). By using this word as representative of all eight conditions of the women, some say that these are all *svakīya* relationships. This however is not acceptable for later it is said:

*pūrvaṁ yāḥ pañcadaśadhā proktās tāsāṁ śataṁ tathā \|*  
*viṁśatiś cābhir atra syād avasthābhiḥ kilāṣṭabhiḥ \|\|*

**Multiplying the fifteen types of women previously mentioned by the eight conditions there are a hundred and twenty types of women.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **5.101**

In this verse, without the *parakīya* varieties there could not be fifteen types. Nor can it be said that since Rādhā and Candrāvalī would marry Kṛṣṇa later they are called *bhartṛkā,* since there is clearly no traditional proof that they were married later. Nor by mentioning the *Padma Purāṇa,* after Kṛṣṇa killed Dantavakra, or by quoting the First Canto, can one say that there must have been marriage to fulfill the desires of his parents when he went back to Vraja.

*yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra bho bhavān*  
*kurūn madhūn vātha suhṛd-didṛkṣayā*  
*tatrābda-koṭi-pratimaḥ kṣaṇo bhaved*  
*raviṁ vinākṣṇor iva nas tavācyuta*

**O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever you go away to Mathurā, Vṛndāvana or Hastināpura to meet Your friends and relatives, every moment of your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun. SB 1.11.9**

Previously, when Akrūra came, though Kṛṣṇa was at the end of his *kaiśora* period, his parents saw him as if he were in still in the *paugaṇḍa* age. When he returned after killing Dantavakra, even then they saw him having the same age. This was not the time for marriage and his parents did not have a desire to get him married. And in *Padma Purāṇa* it says *gopa-nārībhir aniśaḥ krīḍayām; āsa mādhavaḥ*: Kṛṣṇa performed pastimes constantly with the cowherd women. The word *nārībhiḥ i*ndicates women, not his wives.

What is the meaning in using the word *bhartṛikā* in *svādhīna-bhartṛikā*? In all scriptures concerning literary ornaments ancient or recent, the word *bhartṛ* is used to mean both husband and unmarried lover. For instance in *Rasa-mañjarī* the following is found. *Iyaṁ parakīyā svādhīna-bhartṛketi iyaṁ veśyā svādhīna-bhartṛkā*: she is a *parakīya svādhīna-bhartṛkā,* she is a *svādhīna* prostitute. There are many other examples as well. Thus it has a broad usage as in saying “All respects to the *devatās*” to indicate all the *devatās* to be worshipped (including male and female forms). This was explained before (in relation to the term *pati*). Uncultured women say to their servants, “You should bring that person who is in my house, called my *bhartā,* who does not know enjoyment of my youth, form, beauty, and skills. He is my *bhartā,* my *pati,* my *svāmī*.” They also use the word *āryaputra* (a word for husband to be used by the wife) to indicate the secondary hero when he is not present.

### Text 90

***yathā—***  
***vilāsī svacchandaṁ vasati mathurāyāṁ madhu-ripur***  
***vasantaḥ santāpaṁ prathayati samantād anupadam \|***  
***durāśeyaṁ vairiṇy ahaha mad-abhīṣṭodyama-vidhau***  
***vidhatte pratyūhaṁ kim iha bhavitā hanta śaraṇam \|\|90\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Kṛṣṇa is now living happily in Mathurā with great enjoyment. But for me, springtime brings pain at every step and from every direction. My enemy, the impossible hope that perhaps he may return, has become a great obstacle in fulfilling my desire to kill myself. Where can I find shelter from this enemy?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. Since he enjoys there, why will he come here? *Abhīṣṭa* means death. *Pratyūham* means obstacle.

### Text 91

***atha svādhīna-bhartṛkā—***  
***svāyattāsanna-dayitā bhavet svādhīna-bhartṛkā \|***  
***salilāraṇya-vikrīḍā-kusumāvacayādi-kṛt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Keeping her lover under control: She who keeps her lover close by and under her control is the** ***svādhīna-bhartṛikā.*** **She has pastimes in the water and forest, and picks flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Svāyattah* means *svādhīna.* She whose lover remains close by (*asanna*).under her control is the *svādhīna-bhartṛkā.*

### Text 92

***yathā—***  
***mudā kurvan patrāṅkuram anupamaṁ pīna-kucayoḥ***  
***śruti-dvandve gandhāhṛta-madhupam indīvara-yugmam \|***  
***sa-khelaṁ dhammillopari ca kamalaṁ komalam asau***  
***nirābādhāṁ rādhāṁ ramayati ciraṁ keśi-damanaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: He happily paints incomparable designs on her full breasts and places blue lotuses which attract the bees by their scent in her two ears. In her braid, he playfully places a delicate lotus. Kṛṣṇa constantly pleases Rādhā without disturbance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This statement can be explained as a pastime after he returned to Vraja many years later, since he killed Keśi just before he went to Mathurā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī.

***ghaṭaya jaghane kāñcīṁ mugdha-srajā kavarī-bharaṁ \|***  
***kalaya valaya-śreṇīṁ pāṇau pade maṇi-nūpurāv***  
***iti nigaditaḥ prītaḥ pitāmbaro’pi tathākarot \|\|\|***

**Another example, from** ***Gīta-govinda*****: “Draw patterns on my breasts and cheeks. Put the belt around my waist and a place pleasing garland in my braid. Put bracelets on my wrists and jeweled anklets on my feet.” Ordered in this way Kṛṣṇa, very pleased, obeyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Dependence on the woman was not fully expressed in the previous verse. Therefore this verse is given.

### Text 94

***ced iyaṁ preyasā hātuṁ kṣaṇam apy atiduḥśakā \|***  
***parama-prema-vaśyatvān mādhavīti tadocyate \|\|94\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**If Kṛṣṇa cannot give up his lover for even a moment because he is controlled by her** ***prema,*** **the** ***svādhīna-bhartṛkā*** **is called** ***mādhavī.***

### Text 95

***hṛṣṭāḥ svādhīna-patikā-vāsasajjābhisārikāḥ \|***

***vāma-gaṇḍāśrita-karāś cintā-santapta-mānasāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***svādhīna-bhartṛikā, vāsa-sajjā*** **and** ***abhisārikā,*** **being happy, are always decorated with ornaments. The other five, in lamentation, are without ornaments, have their hand on their left cheek, and are afflicted with anxiety.**

### Text 96

***uttamā madhyamā cātra kaniṣṭhā ceti tās tridhā \|***  
***vrajendranandane prema-tāratamyena kīrtitāḥ \|\|96\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The previously mentioned heroines can be divided into three types according to the amount of their prema for Kṛṣṇa:** ***uttamā, madhyamā*** **and** ***kaniṣṭhā.***

### Text 97

***bhāvaḥ syād uttamādīnāṁ yasyā yāvān priye harau \|***  
***tasyāpi tasyāṁ tāvān syād iti sarvatra yujyate \|\|97\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**According to the amount of** ***prema*** **and its transformations that the woman shows as** ***uttamā, madhyamā*** **or** ***kaniṣṭhā,*** **Kṛṣṇa responds with similar love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The three types arise from three different types of persons based on their actual nature. But the two divisions of *jyeṣthā* and *kaniṣṭhā* depending on relative considerations are present in all of them only because of their dealings with each other.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are three types of all the types mentioned. The *prema* here means the transformations of *prema* such as *sneha,* up to *mahābhāva.* “The classification of *jyeṣthā* and *kaniṣthā* was previously not accepted, but now the classifications of *uttamā, madhyā* and *kaniṣṭhā* are accepted, according to the amount of *prema* for Kṛṣṇa. There was only apparent difference in love and therefore the two types were not considered since the two had the same qualities. How can you know consider them in three types then?”

If you say “This girl is superior (*jyeṣthā*) to that one in *prema*, and that one is inferior (*kaniṣṭhā*) in *prema*” depending on a relative consideration, it is not possible to classify them all simply as superior or inferior. One must take two particular women in order to show superior and inferior, by showing the results in a particular example.

But one can say “This woman has the highest type of *prema,* and that woman has medium type of *prema*.” This is not based on a comparison of two particular women.

“It is possible to say that this woman is a *madhyamā* compared to that *uttamā* and that *kaniṣṭhā.”* That is not so. One must say that the *madhyamā* woman is inferior to the *uttamā* type and superior to the *kaniṣthā* type. Otherwise, the class of *madhyamā* would be meaningless. Because of the use of the term *madhyamā,* the relative considerations are rejected. Thus all agree that these terms should be used in classifying the types of heroines.

According to the amount of *bhāva* of a particular woman (*yāvān*) Kṛṣṇa responds with the same amount of *bhāva.* The word “amount” includes the different varieties of love since the Lord has said *ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham*: according to the way in which a person surrenders, I respond. (BG 4.11)

### Text 98

***tatra uttamā, yathā—***  
***kartuṁ śarma kṣaṇikam api me sādhyam ujjhaty aśeṣaṁ***  
***cittotsaṅge na bhajati mayā datta-khedāpy asūyām \|***  
***śrutvā cāntarvidalati mṛṣāpy ārti-vārtā-lavaṁ me***  
***rādhā mūrdhany akhila-sudṛśāṁ rājate sad-guṇena \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***uttamā:*** **Rādhā will renounce all her attainments if that will make me happy for a moment. Even if I torment her she never becomes angry with me deep in her heart. If she hears a rumor, even if it is untrue, that I am slightly suffering, her heart cracks. With these good qualities, Rādhā reigns as the best of all the beautiful-eyed** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. Her *rāga* is indicated by that fact that she will give up all spiritual results such as serving *brāhmaṇas* and *devatās* and all material results such as possessions, reputation, daily comforts, sleeping, eating, and even maintaining her life. It is said:

*snehaḥ sa rāgo yena syāt sukhaṁ duḥkham api sphuṭam*  
*tat-sambandha-lave ’py atra prītiḥ prāṇa-vyayair api \|\|*

**That** ***sneha*** **which turns sorrow into happiness by a slight appearance of Kṛṣṇa is called** ***rāga.*** **In this state of** ***rāga,*** **the devotee will do anything for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa, even giving up his life. BRS 3.2.87**

Though I give her pain she does not show anger in her heart. This indicates *prema.*

*sarvathā dhvaṁsa-rahitaṁ saty api dhvaṁsa-kāraṇe \|*  
*yad-bhāva-bandhanaṁ yūnoḥ sa premā parikīrtitaḥ \|\|63\|\|*

**When the relationship of love between the couple remains always without destruction even when there is causes for destroying it, it is called prema.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.63**

*Antar vidalati* (her heart breaks) indicates *rūḍha-bhāva.* In the definition of *rūḍḥa* it is said *khinnatvaṁ tat–saukhye’ py aṛti-śaṅkayā*: fearing Kṛṣṇa is suffering, she becomes depressed. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.161) Thus the verse indicates in order the unlimited nature of Rādhā’s *raga, prema* and *mahābhāva.* The statements with *mayā* and *mrṣā* indicate the high level of these types and the amounts of these three types of love.

### Text 99

***madhyamā, yathā—***  
***durmānam eva manasā bahu mānayantī***  
***kiṁ jñāta-kṛṣṇa-hṛdayārtir api prayāsi \|***  
***raṅge taraṅgam akhilāṅgi varāṅganānāṁ***  
***nāsau priye sakhi bhavaty anurāga-mudrā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***madhyamā*****: O Ranga-devi, your limbs are trembling live waves. You worshipped evil anger with great respect in your mind. Though you know you have pained your lover’s heart you are still leaving. O my friend, this is not the symptom of a beautiful girl's** ***anurāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Raṅge* means “O Raṅgā!”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend of Raṅgā, leader of a group speaks to her. O Raṅgā ,whose whole body is full of waves because of anger! Though she knows that Kṛṣṇa is suffering, her heart does not melt. Thus her *prema* is *madhyamā.* However, in her heart she actually considers the following. “On hearing that he was suffering I completely gave up my anger but I will reveal my mercy after a few moments. Let him experience suffering from separation for that long so that he will not act like this again.” Thus one should not fear some unsteadiness in her *samartha-rati.* But when one has the highest level of type of affection and amount of affection, such thoughts will not arise. Thus she is ranked as a *madhyamā.*

### Text 100

***kaniṣṭhā, yathā—***  
***danujabhid-abhisāra-prastutau vṛṣṭim ugrāṁ***  
***jana-gamana-virāmād uccakaiḥ stauṣi tuṣṭā \|***  
***kathaya katham idānīṁ jṛmbhite megha-ḍimbhe***  
***kutukini bata kuñje prasthitau mantharāsi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***kaniṣṭhā:*** **In preparing to meet Kṛṣṇa, you were jubilantly praising this fierce rain storm, since others will not go out in the rain. Eager girl, please tell me, now that a little cloud is swelling, why you have become reluctant to travel to the bower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *uccakaiḥ* sometimes *anyadā* is seen. The three examples are explained here. Renouncing to make Kṛṣṇa happy is a symptom of *rat.* That is described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu:*

*kṣobha-hetāv api prāpte kṣāntir akṣubhitātmatā \|\|27\|\|*

**Tolerance means “being undisturbed, even when there is cause for disturbance.” BRS 1.3.27**

Or in the First Canto *taṁ mopayātaṁ pratiyantu viprā*: the *brāhmaṇas* and Gaṅgā-devī should know that I am surrendered, and have dedicated my heart to the Lord. (SB 1.19.150) That she does not feel pain in her heart occurs in *prema.*

*hrāsa-śaṅkā-cyutā baddha-mūlā premeyam ucyate \|*  
*asyānubhāvāḥ kathitās tatra vyasanitādayaḥ \|\|*

**When** ***sambhrama-prīti*** **becomes firmly fixed, with no doubt that it will decrease, it is called** ***prema.*** **The** ***anubhāvas*** **are such things as complete attachment to the Lord. BRS 3.2.81**

*aṇimādi-saukhya-vīcīm avīci-duḥkha-pravāhaṁ vā \|*  
*naya māṁ vikṛtir na hi me tvat-padakamalāvalambasya \|\|*

**Since I have taken shelter of your lotus feet, you may throw me into the waves of suffering in the hell called Avīci, or throw me in the waves of happiness by bestowing siddhis like** ***aṇima,*** **but I will not change my** ***prema*** **for you. BRS 3.2.82**

The melting of the heart is a sign of *sneha:*

*sāndraś citta-dravaṁ kurvan premā 'sneha' itīryate \|*  
*kṣaṇikasyāpi neha syād visleṣasya sahiṣṇutā \|\|*

**When** ***prema*** **becomes extremely thick and the heart melts, it is called** ***sneha.*** **In this state, one cannot tolerate even a moment’s separation from the Lord. BRS 3.2.84**

*dambhena bāṣpāmbu-jharasya keśavaṁ*  
*vīkṣya dravac-cittam asusruvat tava \|*  
*ity uccakair dhārayato vicittatāṁ*  
*citrā na te dāruka dāru-kalpatā \|\|*

**O Dāruka! Seeing Kṛṣṇa, your heart used to turn liquid on the pretext of your gushing tears. Now, in separation from Kṛṣṇa, it is not astonishing that you, Dāruka, have become like a doll made out of wood (*****dārukalpatā*****) out of extreme loss of consciousness. BRS 3.2.85**

If this happens naturally, how much more will happen on hearing that Kṛṣṇa is suffering! In the example of the *madhyamā,* she shows anger. Anger is also seen in Rādhā:

*karnante na kṛta priyokti-racana kṣipraṁ maya durato*  
*malli-dama nikama-pathya-vacase rusaḥ kalpitaḥ*  
*ksoni-lagna-sikhanda-sekharam asau nabhyarthayann ikṣitaḥ*  
*svantaṁ hanta mamadya tena khadiraṅgarena dandahyate*

**No sweet words enter my ear. I immediately threw the jasmine garland far away. I was angry with the friend who spoke words for my benefit. I do not see him placing his peacock-feather crown on the ground and begging with many prayers. My heart continually burns because of** ***a khadira*** **cinder.** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*** **5.6**

The anger manifests not only in the mind but in external actions. Rādhā’s internal anger is manifested through action in this verse. If this is so, it will manifest in all the women of Vraja, who have the highest *prema,* and not just in their mind. However, the display of anger is to teach other *sakhīs* the nature of anger in love. It is a somewhat excessively assumed role, and not her real character.

The example of the *kaniṣṭhā* in the present verse is not suitable for the women of Vraja, since in examples of other devotees with *rāga,* such actions would not take place.

*snehaḥ sa rāgo yena syāt sukhaṁ duḥkham api sphuṭam*  
*tat-sambandha-lave ’py atra prītiḥ prāṇa-vyayair api \|\|*

**That** ***sneha*** **which turns sorrow into happiness by a slight appearance of Kṛṣṇa is called** ***rāga*****. In this state of** ***rāga*****, the devotee will do anything for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa, even giving up his life. BRS 3.2.87**

*gurur api bhujagād bhīs takṣakāt prājya-rājya-*  
*cyutir ati-śāyinī ca prāyacaryā ca gurvī \|*  
*atasanuta mudam uccaiḥ kṛṣṇa-līlā-sudhāntar-*  
*viharaṇa-sacivatvād auttareyasya rājñaḥ \|\|*

**Though extremely terrified of the snake Takṣaka, Parīkṣit, son of Uttarā, giving up his great kingdom and undertaking the extreme vow of fasting till death, became most blissful through drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. BRS 3.2.88**

Therefore the example given is certainly not suitable for women who have attained *adhirūḍha* state of *mahābhāva*. It is said that such examples are given for the inquisitive beginners to give a general understanding. For more serious inquirers the section on *sthāyi-bhāva* will give excellent examples of the degrees of love. The example of the *uttamā* shows their aspect of *prema.* The example of the *madhyamā* shows their aspect of fault finding. The example of the *kaniṣṭhā* shows their aspect of non-cooperation (*vāmya)*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā urges a girl who desires to meet Kṛṣṇa to move quickly. She reproaches the girl whose *rāga* is unsteady, in order to dispel her *vāmya* tendency. Actually the girl considers in her mind as follows. “This small rain cloud which is approaching will last for only a moment. It will be unfavorable for enjoying with my lover for it will soak my attractive cloth and ornaments.” The following should be considered on this subject. The act of consideration in *prema, sneha* and *raga* shows the lack of depth of these conditions. Intense *rāga* is shown as follows:

*tīvrārka-dyuti-dīpitair asilatādhārākarālāsribhir-*  
*mārtaṇḍopala-maṇḍalaiḥ sthapuṭite’py adres taṭe tasthuṣī \|*  
*paśyanti paśupendra-nandanam asāv indīvarair āstṛte*  
*talpe nyasta-padāmbujeva muditā na spandate rādhikā \|\|127\|\|*

**Remains on the slope covered with piles of sharp-edged, uneven sun stones heated by the intense rays of the sun at noon, Rādhā, joyfully gazing at the prince of the cowherds, remains motionless as standing with her feet on a bed spread with blue lotuses.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.127**

When her lover is coming, she does not consider whether the stones are hot or cold, whether the stones will injure his tender body or will be pleasing to him. However everything is solved be the power of *yoga-māyā* who is ever watchful.

She praises the fierce rain storm because people will not go out at that time. Because this is also done with consideration, it reveals a lesser type of *rāga.* The *madhyamā* does not think strongly “By good fortune rain has come. No one will go out of the house. I can meet my lover comfortably.” The *kaniṣṭhā* however will go to the extent of covering her body. Thus Vṛndā hints critically that she is a *kaniṣṭhā.* “Though you are actually a *madhyamā*, by your words and actions you reveal qualities of a *kaniṣṭhā*.” When the type and amount of the *sthāyīs* from *rati* to *mahābhāva* are highest the woman is *uttamā.* Lesser than this, she is *madhyamā.* When the type and amount are small, she is *kaniṣṭhā.* If there is no consideration at all, it means the type and amount of the *sthāyī* is at a maximum. If there is slight consideration, then the *sthāyī* is medium in type and amount. If the consideration is profuse, then the *sthāyī* is least in type and amount.

“It is seen in the *rāsa* dance that the *gopīs* did not consider anything else as in the verse *duhanyto bhiyayuḥ kāścid doham nitvā samutsukāḥ:* some of the *gopīs,* milking cows when they heard Kṛṣṇa’s flute, stopped milking and went off to meet him. (SB 10.29.5) Do *madhyamās* and *kaniṣṭhās* exist in Vraja at all?”

The *uttamās* are described in that verse. However, it should be understood that the *madhyamās* and *kaniṣṭhās* also were there, just as when we say that the umbrella carriers go, it includes persons without umbrellas as well. Chatrino gacchanti iti nyāya.3 It is said *pati-sutānvaya-bhrātṛ-bāndhavān antivilaṅghya te’ nty acyuto gatāḥ*: we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors, brothers and other relatives and come to you. (SB 10.31.17) This is a statement of some among the *gopīs*. But some considered the obstacles of husbands while the time of the appointment was passing, just as time passes unaware while one sleeps. Going to meet the lover is characterized by such considerations. The *abhisārikā* is described as *lajjayā svāṅga-līneva niḥśabda-pada-maṇḍanā:* out of shyness she covers her body, makes her ornaments soundless. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 5.72) These actions indicate that she has consideration in the form of fear of elders.

“Should the *uttamās* be described as not having this quality of consideration?” Yes. When the *sthāyī-bhāva* of *rāga* appears in full at the time of meeting and the *sañcāri-bhāva* of *sambhrama (*confusion of mind) appears, consideration of the situation does not manifest in the *uttamās.* In *Vidagdha-mādhava* it is said *kaṁsārer abhisāra-sambhrama-bharān manye jagad-vismṛtam:* I think that because of the great of confusion in meeting Kṛṣṇa, you have forgotten everything. (*Vidagdha-mādhava* 4.2.1) When *rāga* does not appear, then the quality of the *madhyamā* will appear in the form of considering other things. Śyāmā, an *uttamā,* thus considers as follows:

*jānīhi bhrmarākṣi kutra guruavaḥ paśya pradoṣodgame*  
*kuñjābhikramaṇāya māṁ travayati sphārāndhakārāvalī*

**Bhramarākṣi, watch for my elders. Now that evening has arrived, this great blinding darkness will aid my swift journey to the bower.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **8.7**

The arrangement is this. Those who have plentiful qualities of the *uttamā* will never show qualities of the *madhyamā* or *kaniṣṭhā.* They should be considered real *uttamās,* like chief commanders to the king. Those who do not show the qualities of the *uttamā* sometimes and show *madhyamā* or *kaniṣṭhā* qualities are *madhyamās*. Those without *uttamā* or *madhyamā* qualities are *kaniṣṭhā.* In *pūrva-rāga* Rādhā says:

*sā kalyāṇī kula-yuvatibhiḥ śīlitā dharma-śailī*  
*drāg asmābhiḥ katham avinayotphullam ullaṅghanīyā*

**Why do we pious girls disobey the auspicious rules of religion?** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*** **2.14**

However, one should understand that this deep sense of consideration of Rādhā is not a sign of the *kaniṣṭhā.*

### Text 101-102

***pūrvaṁ yāḥ pañcadaśadhā proktās tāsāṁ śataṁ tathā \|***  
***viṁśatiś cābhir atra syād avasthābhiḥ kilāṣṭabhiḥ \|\|101\|\|***  
***punaś ca tri-vidhair ebhiḥ prabhedair uttamādibhiḥ \|***  
***triśatī spaṣṭam uktātra ṣaṣṭyā yuktā manīṣibhiḥ \|\|102\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Multiplying the fifteen types of women previously mentioned by the eight conditions there are a hundred and twenty types of women. Multiplying this by the three types just discussed, there are three hundred and sixty types of women according to the authorities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The previous fifteen types are not again discussed here because the commentary would become too huge.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“How can the *dhīra, adhīra* and *dhīrādhīra* have the seven states such as *abhisārikā* (since they are in relation to anger). They should be related only to the state of *khaṇḍitā,* when Kṛṣṇa breaks his appointment. Because anger arises from the condition of the *khaṇḍitā,* taking support of anger, the woman manifests as the *dhīrā, adhīrā* or *dhīrādhīrā*.”

*Dhīrā, adhīrā* and *dhīrādhīrā* are natural qualities of heroines. They exist at all times as the woman’s nature. At the time of anger, the effects of that nature—crooked words and sarcasm—appear, give pleasure to Kṛṣṇa, and show their nature. In works like *Rasa-mañjarī* types like *mugdhābhisārikā, madhyābhisārikā* and *pragalbhābhisārikā*, and also *dhīrabhisārikā* and *adhīrābhisārikā* are mentioned. Because of self-control the appointment is hard to view. This is the *dhīrābhisārikā.* Because of no self-control, the appointment is clear. This is *adhīrābhisārikā.* By some self-control and some lack of it, the appointment is somewhat visible. This is the *dhīrādhīrābhisārikā.* Other types should be considered in the same way.

### Text 103

***kiṁ ca—***  
***yathā syur nāyakāvasthā nikhilā eva mādhave \|***  
***tathaitā nāyikāvasthā rādhāyāṁ prāyaśo matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Moreover: Just as all the different types of heroes are present in Kṛsṇa, all the different types of heroines are generally present in Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *prāyaśaḥ* (generally) is used to indicate that these types appear in a pleasing way, and not otherwise.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Just as all conditions such as favorable cheating are present in Kṛṣṇa at all times, *dhīra-pragalbhā* and other types are present in Rādhā at all times, not just in some portions. That is indicated by the word *prāyaśaḥ* (for the most part).

## Chapter 6 - Varieties of Group Leaders
