12 types

### Text 1-4

***etāsāṁ yūtha-mukhyānāṁ viśeṣo varṇito’py asau \|***  
***suhṛd-ādau vyavahṛti-vyaktaye varṇyate punaḥ \|\|1\|\|***  
***saubhāgyāder ihādhikyād adhikā sāmyataḥ samā \|***  
***laghutvāl laghur ity uktās tridhā gokula-subhruvaḥ \|\|2\|\|***  
***pratyekaṁ prakharā madhyā mṛdvī ceti punas tridhā \|\|3\|\|***  
***pragalbha-vākyā prakharā khyātā durlaṅghya-bhāṣitā \|***  
***tad-ūnatve bhaven mṛdvī madhyā tat-sāmyam āgatā \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The details of the heads of the groups** ***(yūthas*****) will be described and then the details in the groups’ relationship as friends or enemies will be described to show their dealings. The women of Gokula are described as** ***adhikā, samā*** **or** ***laghu*** **in relation to the great, normal or lesser amount of respect given by Kṛṣṇa due to their** ***prema,*** **qualities and form. In each of these types there are** ***prakharā, madhyā*** **and** ***mṛdvī*** **types. The** ***prakharā*** **speaks boldly and her words cannot be disobeyed. The** ***mṛdvī*** **shows very little of those qualities and the** ***madhyā*** **shows medium qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Saubhāgya* refers to the respect gained from the *prema* of Kṛṣṇa. The word *ādi* refers to qualities, form and other elements. When a woman has these elements in abundance she is called *adhikā.* The *prakharā’s* words cannot be disregarded. This also means her activities cannot be disregarded by others.

If a woman is arrogant (*pragalbhā*) in words only, it would be irregular and unsuitable for *rasa*. *Ūnatve* means lesser as in *ūnaviṁśat*i: twenty minus one. If a woman has lesser degree of the *prakharā* qualities then she is called *mṛdvī.* *Madhyā* means oneness (*sāmya*) as in the phrase *raṣābhyāṁ no ṇaḥ samāna-pade*: directly after *r* and *ṣ* in the same word, n becomes ṇ; they all are “one” in the sense of being cerebral in pronunciation. (Pāṇini 8.4.1) In this verse meaning is that *madhyā* is an equal mixture of the *prakharā* and the *mṛdvī*, a weak form of the *prakharā.* A woman in that state is called *madhyā.* Because she is situated between the two, she is called *madhyā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Suhṛd-ādau* means “in terms of women who are friendly, neutral or members of ones own group.” *Saubhāgya* refers to “being the object of Kṛṣṇa’s *prema.*” *Ādi* means form and qualities. The *prakharā’s* words cannot be defeated by others. Since the word *vākhyā* has been used this excludes arrogant actions. These categories are separate from the *pragalbhā, madhyā* and *mugdhā* previously described. The *mṛdvī* has only a little arrogance. This means she does not have the arrogance in her mood. The *madhyā* has slightly more *prakharā* qualities than the *mṛdvī* and slightly less than the *prakharā. prākharyaṁ mārdavaṁ cāpi yadyapy āpekṣikaṁ bhavet:* the terms *prākharya* and *mārdava* are relative to each other. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 8.91) When it is said that a face is equal to the moon, it means it is slightly less than the moon. The meaning is similar *to īṣad asamāptau kalpa-deśya-deśīyaraḥ*: the words *kalpa, deśya* and *deśīyara* are used to denote slight incompleteness (Pāṇini 5.3.67)

### Text 5-6

***tatra adhikā-trikam—***  
***ātyantikī tathaivāpekṣikī cety adhikā dvidhā \|\|5\|\|***  
***sarvathaivāsamordhvā yā sā syād ātyantikādhikā \|***  
***sā rādhā sā tu madhyaiva yan nānyā sadṛśī vraje \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Definition of the** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **leader*****:*** **There are two types of** ***adhikā*** **leader*****: ātyantikī*** **and** ***apekṣikī.*** **The** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **has no superior or equal. Rādhā alone, a** ***madhyā*****, is** ***ātyantikādhikā,*** **since no women in Vraja is equal to her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ātyantika* and *ādhika* combine as a *karma-dhāraya* compound. Though *ātyantikī* is the feminine, in the compound it takes the masculine form *ātytantika*. Rādhā, a *madhyā,* is the *ātyantikādhikā,* since (*yat*) no one in Vraja equals her. The proof is in the Purāṇas, quoted earlier. Proofs will also be given later. She is a *madhyā* because the *madhyā* is capable of producing the highest type of *rasa.* Thus her extraordinary position is denoted here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One may argue that since the word *adhika* means the best adding adjectives like extreme (*atyantika*) or relative (*apeksika*) are meaningless. That is not so. She surpasses the limits *(ātyantika*) of the best (*adhikā*). Therefore the term is not unsuitable. *Ātyantika* means “going to the limit” according to Pāṇini 4.4.1. *Pāradāra* becomes *pāradārika:* one who goes to another’s wife.

Rādhā is a *madhyā* as distinct from the *mṛdvī* and the *prakharā.* She is *atyantikādhika* because *(yat)* no one in Vraja is equal to her. She is comparable only to herself. Or there is no one even a little less than her. All others are extremely less.

### Text 7

*tatra ātyantādhikā, yathā—*  
***tāvad bhadrā vadati caṭulaṁ phullatām eti pālī***  
***śālīnatvaṁ tyajati vimalā śyāmalāhaṅkaroti \|***  
***svairaṁ candrāvalir api calaty unnamayyottamāṅgaṁ***  
***yāvat karṇe na hi niviśate hanta rādheti mantraḥ \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Example of the supreme leader: Bhadrā may speak charming words, Pālī may blossom with happiness, Vimalā may abandon all shyness, Śyāmalā may become proud, and even Candrāvalī may strut about with her head raised high, only so long as the mantra Rādhā does not enter their ears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse illustrates Rādhā’s *ātyantādhikā* position and her *madhyā* position. Even her name has great power. Rādhā does not display direct arrogance. This indicates her *madhyā* nature.  *Śālīnatvam* means lack of boldness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One time the *gopīs* in a group were showing the excellence of their own group in discussion using ironic praise. Śyāmalā then said, “O women of Vraja! Please here the highest truth. Vimalā gives up all lack of boldness and becomes *pragalbhā*. Candrāvalī raises her head. Śyāmalā may become proud.” She mentions her own name. By criticizing herself she shows the truth of her words. She has made this decision. “Though I am a friend of Rādhā, since I am head of a group superior to others, I should have deep pride. But that cannot remain.” That is her conviction. I think her name is a mantra because by hearing it one sees that it has the power to conquer all people. This is the metaphor used. Or it is not a name, it is a mantra. This is *apahnuti* (statement of denial). If one takes the verse to be spoken by a friend or by Vṛndā, the statement about Śyāmalā would not have such elegance.

### Text 8

***atha āpekṣikādhikā—***  
***madhye yūthādhināthānām apekṣyaikatamām iha \|***  
***yā syād anyatamā śreṣṭhā sā proktāpekṣikādhikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Definition of the relatively superior leader: Any other leader who, compared to others group leaders, is the best among them is called** ***āpekṣikādhikā.***

### Text 9

*atha adhika-prakharā, yathā—*  
***paśya kṣauṇī-dharād upaiti purataḥ kṛṣṇo bhujaṅgāgraṇīs***  
***tūrṇaṁ bhīrubhir ālibhiḥ samam itas tvaṁ yāhi mantrojjhite \|***  
***ācāryāham aṭāmi bhogi-ramaṇī-vṛndasya vṛndāṭavīṁ***  
***kiṁ naḥ kāmini kārmaṇena vaśatāṁ nītaḥ kariṣyaty asau \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***adhika-prakharā:*** **Look! Here comes the serpent-king Kṛṣṇa slithering down Govardhana Hill. O woman without mantra! You and your frightened friends should immediately flee from this place. However, since I am an expert snake charmer who travels around this forest of Vṛndāvana, owned by a group of the snake’s wives, I shall now cast a magical spell and bring this snake under my control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*The āpekṣikādhikās* are now described. *Kārmaṇena* means by actions to defeat him. *Mūlam* means herbs.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The group leaders speak among themselves. Since their names are not given, one among them simply speaks to another. *Bhujaṅgah* means a snake and a lecher. Leave here, otherwise he will bite you. O woman without mantra (*mantrojjhite*)! This means you do not know the best mantra among all mantras. *Bhogī* means snake and Kṛṣṇa. I know the arts of enchanting snakes. I teach skills in *rasa* to the *gopīs.* I will bring him under control by some herbs, and by many words and actions using my body. The bold words and *saubhāgya* are evident. This *adhika-prakharā* belongs to an inimical group.

### Text 10

*atha adhika-madhyā—*  
***ālībhir me tvam asi viditā pūrṇimāyāḥ pradoṣe***  
***roṣeṇāsau prathayasi kathaṁ pāṭavenāvahitthām \|***  
***dhṛtvā dhūrte saha-parijanāṁ mad-gṛhe tvāṁ nirundhyāṁ***  
***vartma-prekṣī guṇayatu sa te jāgaraṁ kuñja-rājaḥ \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***adhika-madhyā*****: I recognize you with your friends this evening of the full-moon day. Why do you advertise yourself while cleverly hiding? Rascal woman! In anger, I will catch you and imprison you and your friends in my house. Let the king of this grove stay awake all night watching for you on the path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa come she speaks boldly, without restriction, to drive another *gopī* away. She also jokes with her at a distance from Kṛṣṇa since it is not actually possible to take the *gopī* to her house and tie her up. This is the *madhyā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *gopī* spoken to is the example. Let the king of the grove stay awake watching for you on the path. This indicates that *gopī’s saubhāgya*. She tries to hide herself. This indicates her lack of *prakharā* qualities. Since she hides cleverly (*pāṭaveṇa*) she is not a *mṛdvī.* Thus she is a *madhyā*. By saying “I will imprison you” the speaker is a *prakharā.* But she is a *laghu-prakharā* because of the lack of words to indicate her great *saubhāgya.* She is an enemy.

### Text 11

*atha adhika-mṛdvī—*  
***nyañcan-mūrdhā saha parijanair dūrato mā prayāsīr***  
***mām ālokya priya-sakhi yataḥ prema-pātrī mamāsi \|***  
***mālā maulau tava paricitā mat-kalā-kauśalāḍhyā***  
***dyūte jitvā danuja-damanaṁ yā tvayā svīkṛtāsti \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***adhika-mṛdvī*****: Seeing me in the distance, do not bow your head and go away with all your friends. Dear friend! I have affection for you. The flower garland worn in your hair and made by my skill was the stake when I defeated Kṛṣṇa in a gambling match.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The girl being addressed is the example of the *adhika-mrdvī*. Bowing her head indicates she is a *mṛdvī.* Wearing the garland in her hair is a sign of her *saubhāgya adhika.* The speaker is a *laghu-madhyā* and a friend.

### Text 12

***atha samā-trikam—***  
***sāmyaṁ bhaved adhikayos tathā laghu-yugasya ca \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***samā*** **arises between the two types of** ***adhikās*** **or the two types of** ***laghus.***

### Text 13

*tatra sama-prakharā—*  
***na bhavati tava pārśve cet sakhī kāpi mābhūt***  
***parihara hṛdi kampaṁ kiṁ haris te vidhātā \|***  
***aham aticaturābhir veṣṭitālī-ghaṭābhiḥ***  
***priya-sakhi puratas te dustarā bāhudāsmi \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***sama-prakharā*****: If a friend is not at your side, do not fear. Give up trembling in your heart. What can Kṛṣṇa do to you? My dear friend! I am accompanied by many intelligent** ***gopīs.*** **I shall now stand before you, and raise my arms to defend you from this Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Bāhudā* means giving arms and is the name of a river.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa came running from far off, shouting, “Who is this who is taking flowers from my garden?” What can he do to you, since I am here with my clever friends? *Bāhudā* means protection with arms and is the name of a river. Because Kṛṣṇa comes for both of the women (thus having *saubhāgya* of Kṛṣṇa’s love), both are *samās.* The speaker is a *prakharā* because of the way she speaks. She is the example of the *sama-prakharā* and is a friend.

### Text 14

*atha sama-madhyā—*  
***lole na spṛśa māṁ tavālika-taṭe dhātur yad ālakṣyate***  
***tvaṁ spṛśyāsi kathaṁ bhujaṅga-ramaṇī dūrād atas tyajyase \|***  
***dhig vāmaṁ vadasi tvam eva kuhaka-preṣṭhāsi bhogāṅkite***  
***yenādya cyuta-kañcukāḥ śuṣirataḥ sakhyo’pi sarpanti te \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of a** ***sama-madhyā*****: First leader: O fickle hearted woman! Don't touch me! Your forehead is marked with mineral pigment smudges from the snake.**

**Second leader: Why should I touch you? The mistress of the snake should keep far away from me.**

**First leader: You are dear to the snake. Your body carries the marks of the snake. You speak crooked words since your friends, casting off their skins, are crawling from the snake hole.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a dialogue. *Kuhaka* is a magician and a snake. *Śuṣirataḥ* means because of the flute or from the snake hole. *Sarpanti* means they go for appointments with Kṛṣṇa or slither about. The description of the marks from minerals indicates amorous relationship with Kṛṣṇa since both the speaker and hearer are dear to Kṛṣṇa, which is understood from the allusions they make.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Two friends, one of whom has been enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa, and the other who has not been enjoyed, talk to each other. The first says, “There is some red clay mark on the edge of your forehead. You are impure, since you are the leftover remnants of Kṛṣṇa after he has enjoyed. The second says “You are the female snake who enjoys with a snake.” The second meaning is “You enjoy with Kṛṣṇa, the lecher. You are the famous instigator of your lover. But I was enjoyed by him today though I did not desire it. Thus you are more impure than I am.” The first says, “You speak with deceit. You are dear to a snake, or to Kṛṣṇa, the magician.” The word *preṣṭhā* indicates an extreme desire for amorous enjoyment. “You are marked with the snake’s hood or with enjoyment (*bhoga*). Your friends slither from the snake hole, having cast off their skins or your friends go for a meeting with Kṛṣṇa because of the sound of his flute, after casting off your bodices.”

The first speaker shows her *saubhāgya* by her humor and scolding when she says “Do not touch me.” The second speaker shows her *saubhāgya* by the marks of enjoyment on her forehead. Because the two women speak in words with double meaning they are considered *madhyās.*

### Text 15

***atha sama-mṛdvī—***  
***pratyākhyātu suhṛjjanaḥ katham ayaṁ tārābhidhatte giraṁ***  
***prāṇās tvaṁ hi mamoccakair urasi śape dharmāya līlāvati \|***  
***kintu tām aham arthaye param idaṁ kalyāṇi taṁ vallabhaṁ***  
***svīyaṁ śādhi yathā sa gauri sarale kuryāj jane na cchalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***sama-mṛdvī*****: How can your friend Tārā deny your words? O Līlāvatī! I swear that you are my life and soul. O auspicious, fair-complexioned friend! One thing I beg from you. Please instruct your cowherd friend Kṛṣṇa that, although it is proper for him to deal with me in this way, he should not abuse others who are honest, simple folk in this fashion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

How can this woman called Tārā reject (*pratyākhyātu*) your words? She says her own name to indicate her soft nature. He should not act deceitfully with innocent girls like me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

How can a person named Tārā reject your words when you say “Give up your anger?” You should instruct your lover Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa sent Līlāvatī, a friend of Tārā, to tell Tārā to give up her anger. This shows Tārā’s *saubhāgyādhika*. When she says “Tell your lover,” Līlāvatī is shown to have *saubhāgya* also. The *mṛdvī* nature of Tārā is evident. But Līlavatī has a *prakharā* nature since she will instruct Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 16

***yathā vā—***  
***prahitya kaṭhine nijaṁ parijanaṁ madāryā tvayā***  
***nikāmam upajapyatāṁ kim u vibhīṣikā-ḍambaraiḥ \|***  
***vrajāmi ravijā-taṭe guru-girā mṛṣā-śaṅkini***  
***pradoṣa-samaye samaṁ savayasā śivāṁ sevitum \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O hard woman! Sending your friends, you may try to instigate my mother-in-law against me with terrible accusations. You worry for nothing. In the evening, I am going to the shore of the Yamunā by the instruction of my elders to worship the goddess Durgā with my friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prahitya* means sending*. Mad-āryā* means “my mother-in-law.” *Upajapyatām* means “become opposed.” I go on the instructions of my elders.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Previously it was said *sāmyaṁ bhaved adhikayos tathā laghu-yugasya ca*: the *samā* leader manifests as an intermediate from the two types of *adhikās* or two types of *laghus.* Three verses illustrated *samā* derived from the two types of *adhikas*. Now *sāmya* derived from the two types of *laghus* is described.

A *mrḍvī* speaks to a *prakharā* “O beautiful girl, do you not fear your elders, because you are obviously going to the forest in the evening?” The *prakharā* replies with this verse. Sending your friends, you may try to create dissension (*upayapyatām*) with my mother-in-law. But I am going on her instruction (*guru-girā*). Why are you angry? Please be content. This answer is understood. This is considered *sāmya* based on *laghu* qualities because no words are uttered to indicate the two types of s*aubhāgyādhika.*

### Text 17

***atha laghu-trikam—***  
***laghur āpekṣikī cātyantikī ceti dvidhoditā \|\|17\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Types of** ***laghu*****: There are two types of** ***laghus: āpekṣikī*** **and** ***ātyantikī.***

### Text 18

***tatra āpekṣikī laghuḥ—***  
***madhye yūthādhināthānām apekṣyaikatamām iha \|***  
***yā syād anyatamā nyūnā sā proktāpekṣikī laghuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Definition of the** ***āpekṣikī laghu*****: The leader who, compared to other leaders, is the lowest among them is called the** ***āpekṣikī laghu*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *āpekṣikī laghu* is comparatively low. The *ātyantikī laghu* has reached the limits of lowness. This should be understood that “inferiority” is relative term only, in comparing certain aspects of the leader. The explanation is similar to that for two types of *adhikās.* Otherwise the fault called *abhavan mata-yoga* (faulty relation of words and content) would take place.

### Text 19

***tatra laghu-prakharā—***  
***tvaṁ mithyā-guṇa-kīrtanena caṭule vṛndāṭavī-taskare***  
***gāḍhaṁ devi nibadhya māṁ kim adhunā tuṣṭā taṭasthāyase \|***  
***hṛtvā dhairya-dhanāni hanta rabhasād ācchidya hrī-vaibhavaṁ***  
***yenāyaṁ sakhi vañcito’pi bahudhā duḥkhī jano vañcyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Example of the** ***laghu-prakharā:*** **O fickle woman! Are you very happy now that you have tightly bound me to the thief who lurks in this forest of Vṛndāvana with this false glorification while you sit by neutrally? He has not only tied me up, but has stolen the great wealth of my self-control and forcibly snatched from me the wealth of my modesty. My friend, suffering persons like me, though cheated, are cheated repeatedly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An angry woman informs her friend. *Dhairya-dhanānī* means a wealth of self-control and many types of self-control. *Hrī-vaibhavam* means “having even more wealth of modesty.” Thus she had the highest level of self-control and modesty. Because all of this self-control and modesty has been destroyed, there is a suggestion of *saubhāgyādhikya* by having great *prema.* Uttering words like “Being cheated” do not indicate a *laghu,* since they are words of a proud woman. The woman being addressed has a *prakharā* nature, since she is described with words like “false glorification” and “fickle woman.” The woman being addressed is a *laghu* since there are no words to indicate her *saubhāgya*. The speaker is also an example of *prakharā* by using words like “fickle woman” but she has slight *saubhāgya,* since she says she has been cheated repeatedly.

### Text 20

***atha laghu-madhyā—***  
***goṣṭhādhīśa-sutasya sā nava-nava-preṣṭhasya yāvad-dṛśoḥ***  
***panthānaṁ vṛṣabhānujā sakhi vaśīkārauṣadhijñā yayau \|***  
***tāvat tvayy api rūkṣam asya balavad-dākṣiṇyam evekṣyate***  
***kā candrāvali evi durbhagatayā dūnātmanāṁ naḥ kathā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***laghu-madhyā*****: O friend! Rādhā, the daughter of Maharaja Vṛṣabhānu, knows a magic potion to bring Kṛṣṇa under her control. While she looks at her ever new lover, the prince of Vraja, his great kindness becomes cruelty towards you. O Candrāvalī! Who can describe the misfortune of us tormented persons?**

### Text 21

***atha laghu-mṛdvī—***  
***apasaraṇam ito naḥ sāmprataṁ syād***  
***yad api hari-cakoraṁ citram ālocayāmaḥ \|***  
***kalayata sahacaryaḥ paryaṭad gaura-dīptis***  
***taṭa-bhuvi nava-śobhāṁ sauti candrāvalīyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***laghu-mṛdvī:*** **My friends, if we see the wonderful** ***cakora*** **bird called Kṛṣṇa, let us leave at once. Look! The golden moon of Candrāvalī wanders about, spreading the shore of the Yamunā with a beautiful splendor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sauti* means “she creates.” Sometimes *prātīti* (she fills) is found instead.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The meaning of the three verses is clear. *Sauti* means “she creates.” Sometimes *prātīti* (she fills) is found instead.

### Text 22

***atha ātyantikī laghuḥ—***  
***anyā yato’sti na nyūnā sā syād ātyantikī laghuḥ \|***  
***traividhya-sambhave’py asyā mṛdutaivocitā bhavet \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Definition of the** ***ātyantikī laghu*****: The leader to whom none is lower in position is called the** ***ātyantikī laghu.*** **Though the three types are possible in the** ***ātyantika-laghu,*** **the** ***mṛdvī*** **is most common.**

### Text 23

***yathā—***  
***nija-nikhila-sakhīnām āgraheṇāgha-vairī***  
***katham api sa mayādya vyaktam āmantrito’sti \|***  
***kṣaṇam uru-karuṇābhiḥ saṁvarītuṁ trapāṁ me***  
***mad-udavasita-lakṣmīṁ goṣṭha-devyas tanudhvam \|\|23\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Because of your strong will, I have been able to invite Kṛṣṇa to my bower this evening. O goddesses of Vraja! Please stay here a while and make my home glorious. By your mercy I will be able to hide my embarrassment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Udavasitam* means house.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

My parents have invited Kṛṣṇa to my house on my birthday for a big feast. But I have invited him to my bower tonight for enjoyment. Since he is dependent on you, without your help my desire cannot be fulfilled. She then speaks. Spread glory in my house. *Udavasitam* means house according to *Amara-koṣa*. If you come and say something you will make me successful. “I have invited him to my bower because of your stubbornness.” This indicates that she cannot do this on her own. She came into the assembly of leaders herself, without being observed by her friends. Being pleased by her humble words, the assembly members acted as messengers for her that day

### Text 24

***na samā na laghuś cādyā bhaven naivādhikāntimā \|***  
***anyās tridhādhikāś ca syuḥ samāś ca laghavaś ca tāḥ \|\|24\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **never becomes equal or inferior to anyone and the** ***ātyantika-laghu*** **never becomes superior to anyone. The other three types can be superior, equal or inferior to others.**

### Text 25

***vinātyantādhikāṁ tena sarvāsu laghutā bhavet \|***  
***sarvāsv adhikatā ca syād vinaivātyantikīṁ laghum \|\|25\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**All except the** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **can be inferior and all except the** ***ātyantika-laghu*** **can be superior to others.**

### Text 26

***ādyaikaivāntimā dvedhā madhyasthā navadhoditāḥ \|***  
***ity asau yūtha-nāthānāṁ bhidā dvādaśadhoditā \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There is one** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **and two types of** ***ātyantika-laghu*****. Those between the extremes are of nine types. Thus there are twelve types of leaders of the groups. The nine are the** ***prakharā, madhyā*** **and** ***mṛdvī*** **varieties of the** ***apekṣikādhika*****,** ***samā*** **and** ***apekṣika-laghu.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The various types are explained. The *ātyantādhikā (ādyā)* never becomes an equal (*sama)* or an inferior (*laghu).* The *ātyantika-laghu (antimā)* never becomes superior to others (*ādhikā)*. There are two types of *ātyantika-laghu: sama* and *laghu.* This makes three types with the *ātyantikādhika*. The middle types—*āpekṣikādhikā, samā* and *āpekṣika-laghu*—mixing with the *prakharā, madhyā* and *mṛdvī* types, becomes nine. With the three just mentioned, the total is twelve.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *ātyantikādhikā (ādyā)* is one type only. The *ātyantikī laghu (āntimā)* never becomes extremely superior to anyone (*adhikā).* Thus she is only a *laghu.* However, there are many others who are quite similar to her. Thus she can take the role of s*amā* being equal. Thus there are two types of *ātyantikī laghu: laghu* and *samā.* The middle types are *āpekṣikādhikā, samā* and *āpekṣika-laghu*. In relation to others in the same category one may be *adhikā* in relation to another, who is *laghu,* and that person is *laghu* in relation to the *adhikā.* In relation to others of those who are equal, one is *samā.* Thus there are three grades of the three types of *āpekṣikādhikā*, the *samā* and the *āpekṣika-laghu.*

### Text 1-2

***athāśrita-sahāyānāṁ kṛṣṇa-saṅgama-tṛṣṇayā \|***  
***etāsāṁ pūrva-rāgādau dūtya-yuktir vilikhyate \|\|1\|\|***  
***dūtī svayaṁ tathāptā ca dvidhātra parikīrtitā \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The duties of the messengers, engaged among the various assistants of the heroine because of extreme desire to meet Kṛṣṇa in conditions like** ***pūrva-rāga*** **will now be described. There are two types of messengers:** ***svayam*** **and** ***āptā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

After describing the different types of heroes, the assistants of Kṛṣṇa engaged as messengers were previously explained. After describing the different types of heroines, the assistants of the heroine should be described. The principle assistants are the messengers. First the messengers are explained, but by explaining them, all the assistants will be explained.

### Text 3-4

***tatra svayaṁ dūtī—***  
***atyautsukya-truṭad-vrīḍā yā ca rāgātimohitā \|***  
***svayam evābhiyuṅkte sā svayaṁ-dūtī tataḥ smṛtā \|\|3\|\|***  
***svābhiyogās tridhā proktā vācikāṅgika-cākṣuṣāḥ \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Acting as one’s own messenger*****:*** **She who, overcoming shyness because of zeal, engages herself as her own messenger and she who, completely overcome by attraction, engages herself as her own messenger, is called the** ***svayaṁ dutī.*** **She has three types of effort: by words, by limbs and by the eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Two types are indicated, she who has destroyed shyness and she who is overcome with rāga. The first type engages herself spontaneously and reveals her love to the hero. The second type does so even more. The zeal of the first is a strong desire for pleasure. The attraction of the second type is *rati.* There are thus two types mentioned here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The word *ca* indicates that the pronoun *yāḥ* should be repeated, thus indicated two cases. The woman who reveals her intentions herself (*sva*) is called *svayaṁ-dūtī.* Generally she has never had personal association with Kṛṣṇa and is filled with *pūrva-rāga.* The second type of woman, though having associated with Kṛṣṇa becomes extremely bewildered by *anurāga*, being unsatisfied. By the *sthāyi-bhāva* she forgets her shyness, self-control and fear. She considers herself like a person who has never directly associated with Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 5

***tatra vācikaḥ—***  
***vāciko vyaṅgya evātra sa śabdārtha-bhavo dvidhā \|***  
***uktau vyaṅgyau ca tau kṛṣṇa-puraḥstha-viṣayau dvidhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Verbal means: Verbal means consists of allusions (*****vyaṅgya*****) of two types: related to words** ***(śabda*****) and related to meaning** ***(artha*****). These two types also have two types each: concerning Kṛṣṇa and concerning objects in front of the person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If the words are direct, then *rasa* would be destroyed. In *rasa* there is a fault of expression by using the direct meanings of words.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*vācikāṅgikāvadhy-ātmāditvāt ṭhag-antau??*

Allusions or suggestive language is used because there would be *rasābhāsa* in using only the direct meaning of words. *Prakaṭa-prārthanādiḥ syāt sambhogādes tu dhṛṣṭatā:* to request for enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa overtly is called boldness (part of *rasābhāsa*). (BRS 4.9.30) There are two types of suggestive language: that arising from the power of words and that arising from the power of meaning. These two types have Kṛṣṇa or objects directly visible as the subject.

### Text 6

***tatra kṛṣṇa-viṣayaḥ—***  
***sa sākṣād-vyapadeśābhyāṁ syāt kṛṣṇa-viṣayo dvidhā \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concerning Kṛṣṇa: Those types concerning Kṛṣṇa are also of two types: direct and by indirect statement (extended metaphor).**

### Text 7

***tatra sākṣāt—***  
***sākṣād bahu-vidho garvākṣepa-yācñādibhir bhavet \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Direct: In relation to Kṛṣṇa this can be accomplished through pride, harsh speech or entreaty.**

### Text 8

***tatra garveṇa śabdottho vyaṅgyo, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.20)—***  
***sādhvīnāṁ dhuri dhāryā lalitā-saṅgena garvitā cāsmi \|***  
***hitam ālapāmi mādhava pathi mādya bhujaṅgatāṁ racaya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion arising from word-play by expressing pride, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: I am the best of all chaste girls. Now that I am in the company of Lalitā, I feel very confident. I give you this good advice. O Mādhava, do not become a snake in my path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sādhvīnām* means “of chaste women or beautiful women.”  *Dhuri* means worthy of being carried on the head. *Lalitā-saṅgena* means with Lalitā or with a mood of playfulness*. Bhujaṅgatām* means a lecher and an embrace. *Mā* means do not and can also stand for *mām* (me).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks. *Sādhvīnām dhuri* means “in enumerating chaste women and of beautiful women.”  *Dhur* means a burden or reflection. Or, among all things to be carried (*dhāryā*), I am to be carried on the top of the head (*dhuri*). I am proud in the company of Lalitā or I am proud with a mood of playfulness or with attraction for you. Do not become licentious or, embrace me in your arms. She knows the words and actions of Kṛṣṇa as expressed in *Vidagdha-mādhava* (2.20). She says “I have not done anything wrong. Even though again and again I struck him with a garland of lotus flowers, that dark rake would not give up the pleasure of embracing my body.” Thus the words have double meaning. This is an example of use of words.

### Text 9

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***tamāla-śyāmāṅgi kṣipasi kim apāṅga-śriyam itaḥ***  
***prasiddhāhaṁ śyāmā trijagati satīnāṁ kula-guruḥ \|***  
***samārabdhe yasyāḥ katham api manāg bādhana-vidhau***  
***mṛgī-mālāpy eṣā prasabham abhito hanti kupitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion from change of meaning, expressed through pride: O Kṛṣṇa, whose limbs are dark like a** ***tamāla*** **tree! Why do you throw these charming sidelong glances at us? I am Śyāmā, famous as the guru of all pious, chaste girls in all three worlds. If you try to even lightly bind me with your sidelong glance, the group of women will become furious and destroy you completely.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Manāg bādhana-vidhāv* is the correct version.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Itaḥ* means “at me.” Though she says her friends will destroy him, her friends are not present. You can do as you please with me since I am alone. “If that is so, then today I will test the strength of your vow of chastity to your husband. How will those friends destroy me?” He then forcibly touched her breasts. By the power of the different meaning of the statement, it is an example of suggestion arising by the meaning of the statement.

### Text 10

***atha ākṣepeṇa śabdottho vyaṅgyo, yathā—***  
***adhvānaṁ vraja-dhūrta mā vṛṇu suraḥ paśyāmbarānte dṛśaṁ***  
***nikṣipyoru-payodharonnatim imāṁ naṣṭendu-lekhā-śriyam \|***  
***navyā kañculikojjvalā tanur iyaṁ rāgeṇa valgu-śriyā***  
***yāvan na stimitā satī kuṭila me vaivarṇyam āpadyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion arising from word-play using harsh speech: O rascal of Vraja, do not block my path. Turn your eyes to the horizon and look at the big clouds that have already covered the splendor of the crescent moon. O crooked cheater! Do not block my path, so that my fine beautiful, effulgent red bodice will not become wet and spoiled.**

**Accept me without making a sound. Turn your eyes and see on the edge of cloth my huge raised breasts without finger nail marks. And my praiseworthy body shining with bodice has not yet become stunned and changed complexion because of** ***prema.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Do not block the path. Or, accept me without making a sound. *Ambara* means the sky and a cloth. *Indulekhā* means the crescent moon and nail marks. *Navyā* means new and worthy of praise. *Rāgena valgu-śriyā* means reddish with great beauty or bright with *prema. Tanu* means fine or a body.  *Stimitā* means moist or stunned. *Vaivarṇyam* is the same in both meanings.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some *prakharā* woman speaks. Do not block the path. Wander around in Vraja.

Take hold of me without a sound. O thief of Vraja. You know the result of doing this. *Ambara* means sky and cloth. *Payodhara* means a cloud and the breast. The clouds have obliterated the crescent moon. Or my breasts are without the beauty of nail marks, since we have not enjoyed together for many days. I have a new, fine, red bodice which will become wet and disfigured. Or, I have a praiseworthy body shining with a bodice, stunned *(stimita*) and transformed by the *sāttvika-bhāva* of changing complexion (*vaivarṇyam*) because of *prema (rāgena).* “Then why are you agitated? Have your two breasts become beautiful with nail marks?” Then Kṛṣṇa took action.

### Text 11

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***kadambāraṇyānāṁ kitava vikacaṁ luṇṭhasi navaṁ***  
***mad-utsaṅgād diṣṭyā vara-parimalaṁ malli-paṭalam \|***  
***ruci-sphāraṁ hāraṁ harasi yadi me ko’tra śaraṇaṁ***  
***vidūre yad-goṣṭhaṁ jana-virahitā ceyam aṭavī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion from word play arising from change of meaning, using harsh speech: Thief of the kadamba forests! In my presence you are stealing many fragrant, fresh, blossoming jasmine flowers. If you try to steal my splendid necklace, who will protect me? The village of Vraja is far away, and I am alone in this forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Even though Kṛṣṇa has made great effort for the meeting, she personally is making the proposal out of great eagerness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

O cheater lurking on the paths in the kadamba forest! This means “I am the guardian of this forest. You are thief. You are stealing the blossoming (*vikacam*) jasmine flowers *(malli*). The village is far off. I am alone.” This means “This is favorable for our union without obstacles.” Kṛṣṇa then said, “If the village is far off, then please accept my hospitality.” He then took her hands and entered the bower.

### Text 12

***atha yācñā—***  
***yācñā svārthā parārtheti dvidhātra parikīrtitā \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Requests may be for oneself or for others.**

### Text 13

***tatra svārtha-yācñayā śabdottho vyaṅgyo, yathā—***  
***puṣpa-mārgaṇa-mano-rathoddhatā kṛṣṇa mañju-latayā tavānayā \|***  
***rakṣitāsmi sa-vikāsayā puro visphurat-sumanasaṁ kuruṣva mām \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion using word-play through a request for oneself: O Kṛṣṇa! I have developed a great desire to search for flowers. I am stopped here with your attractive creeper. On your order make me pick those splendid flowers in front of me. I have developed a great desire to enjoy with you. You have stopped me here by your beauty. As you desire, please give enjoyment so that my mind becomes glorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Puṣpa-mārgana* means “searching for flowers” and desire. *Mañja-latayā* means “by the attractive creeper” or “by attraction.” *Visphurat-sumanasam* means a heart with splendid beauty or a shining, splendid flower.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Puṣpa-margana* means searching for flowers or desire. I have been stopped here by an attractive creeper or by your beauty. Give the order to pick those shining flowers (*visphurat-sumanasam*). Or give me enjoyment with bliss (*visphurat)* so that my mind becomes splendid (*sumanasam*). After Rādhā spoke Kṛṣṇa picked the flowers and placed them in her bodice.

### Text 14

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***vṛndāraṇyaṁ bhujaga-nikarākrāntam aśrāntam asmāt***  
***kātyāyanyai kusuma-paṭalīṁ jāta-bhīr nāharāmi \|***  
***tena krīḍoddhūta-phaṇi-pate śraddhayāsmi prapannā***  
***tvām ekānte diśa viṣa-haraṁ mantram ekaṁ prasīda \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestive language arising from interpreting the meaning, through a plea for oneself: I am afraid of this snake-filled Vṛndāvana forest. Therefore I neglected to offer flowers to the goddess Kātyāyanī. O Kṛṣṇa who played on the raised hoods of Kāliya! I have surrendered to you with faith. In this solitary place, please give me a mantra to counteract the poison of snake-bites.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this solitary place your friends and my friends are not here. Give a mantra which destroys poison. I have been bitten by the snake of lust. It is not proper to chant the mantra loudly. Come near my face and whisper it in my ear. Then on the pretext of giving her mantra, he kissed her on the cheek and grabbed her bodice as the *dakṣina* for giving the mantra.

### Text 15

***yathā vā—***  
***samastam abhirakṣituṁ janam arandhra-vīrud-ghane***  
***vane carasi kīrtyase tvam uru-kīrti-bhājāṁ dhuri \|***  
***prasīda karuṇāṁ kuru tvaritam uddiśādhva-kramaṁ***  
***yadūdvaha vadhū-janaḥ śrayatu vismṛtādhvā vrajam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa! You are glorified as the best of all famous men, and you traverse this dense, creeper-filled forest simply to protect all beings. O best of the Yadus! Please be kind to me. Please be merciful, and immediately show me the path to Vraja. A woman who has forgotten the path should take shelter of you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

You protect everyone—the cows, cowherds, the deer and other animals. The forest is without holes or dense (*arandhra*). You were born in the Yadu dynasty since Nanda is related to the Yadus. This is explained the commentary on the Tenth Canto and in the *Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In expressing the desire for a mantra, Rādhā revealed her intentions. Not satisfied with that example, the author offers another example. Or, having given an example of a *pragalbhā* making a request, he now gives an example of a *mugdhā*. The forest is impenetrable because of the density of the growth. Considering *(dhuri*) those with greatest fame, you are glorified. Nanda was part of the Yadu clan so therefore Kṛṣṇa is addressed as best of the Yadus. *Hari-vaṁsa* says *yādavānāṁ hitārthāya dhṛto govardhano mayā*: I lifted Govardhana to benefit the Yadus (Nanda’s family members). We have forgotten the path. This means “I have come to ask you the path to come close to you.” “Then come by this path.” He led her a little distance. “It is not possible for you, difficult to attain, to get past this path covered with thick creepers.” She had said, “You have come to protect all the inhabitants of Vraja” To make her words come true he then with force raised her up to his chest.

### Text 16

***parārtha-yācñayā śabdottho, yathā—***  
***sakṛt pītvā vaṁśī-dhvani-nava-sudhāṁ karṇa-culukair***  
***madālī vibhrāntā laghima-nikarottānita-matiḥ \|***  
***sadāhaṁ kaṁsāre kam api gadam āsādya viṣamaṁ***  
***vivarṇā tvāṁ dhanvatarim iha paraṁ niścitavatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestive language arising from word play, through a plea for others: When my friend once drank the fresh nectar of your flute music with the cupped hands of her ears, her mind became very light and she at once fainted. Afflicted with a dangerous disease and a burning sensation, she has become pale, and thinks that you are the expert doctor who can cure her.**

**Drinking once the fresh nectar of your flute music with the cupped hands of my ears, I have become completely intoxicated, bewildered, and light-headed. O enemy of Kaṁsa! Pale with** ***sāttvika-bhāva*****, I constantly desire some unequalled amorous play and have decided that you are the cure.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sudhā* is nectar, and a powder made of burned conch shell. *Mad-ālī* means my friend and “swarm of intoxication.’ *Sadāham* means “I always do” and “along with burning.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sudhā* is nectar, and powder made of burned conch shell. *Madālī* means “my friend” or a swarm of intoxication. *Vibhrāntā* means “very bewildered.” *Sadāham* means “existing with burning.” *Sudha* means “completely purged” according to Medinī. *Gadam* means sickness or amorous play. Kṛṣṇa says, “Being in that condition, I know the mantra or medicine. Just as you protect your limbs with a shield of mantras, you will be relieved of internal and external burning by applying a special ointment to the mouth and eyes.”

### Text 17

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***asūryampaśyāpi priya-sahacarī-premabhir ahaṁ***  
***tavābhyarṇaṁ labdhvā madhumathana dūtyaṁ vidadhatī \|***  
***drutaṁ tasyāḥ snehaṁ niśamaya na yāvac chaśi-dhiyā***  
***dhayan vaktra-jyotsnāṁ niśi hata-cakoras tudati mām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestive language arising from meaning, through a plea for others: O killer of the Madhu demon! Though I am wife of a king, I come to you with a message from a dear friend who faithfully loves you. Please try to understand her love for you. She is a** ***cakora*** **bird and she considers your face to be the moon. If tonight she does not get the opportunity to drink the moonlight of your face she will die. Her death will cause me great pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Asūrampaśyā* means a king’s daughter or person difficult to see. By mentioning that her friend thinks of his face as the moon, she indicates that his face is the most beautiful and sweet. Kṛṣṇa says “Therefore I am qualified for enjoyment with you. I will hear about her affection later. Now I am thinking of a way of protecting you. If you stay outside the evil *cakora* bird will not leave you. You are afraid to enter this dark cave in the mountain alone. Hiding you within my chest because you are terribly frightened, stay there awhile. In this way I will fool the *cakora*. Then I will hear about her affection.”

As well as pride, rough words and entreating, humility is also used as vehicle to present suggestive language to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 18

***atha vyapadeśaḥ—***  
***jalpo vyājena kenāpi vyapadeśo’tra kathyate \|\|18\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Chattering on a different subject to convey one’s intentions is called** ***vyapadeśa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a *paribhāśikī* definition given in the *rasa* scriptures. It is defined elsewhere as well.  *Vyapadeśa* means a deceit or pretext. By describing something else one reveals one’s desired intentions. This is the ornament called *aprastuta-praśaṁsa* (indirect expression).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This takes place in speaking to Kṛṣṇa. It is talking using *aprastuta-praśaṁsa (kena vyājena).*

### Text 19

***tena śabdottho, yathā—***  
***tyajan kuvalayādhikāṁ ghana-rasa-śriyollāsinīṁ***  
***puraḥ sura-taraṅgiṇīṁ madhura-matta-haṁsa-svanām \|***  
***malīmasa-payodharām api madāndha-padminn imāṁ***  
***bhajan kim iva paṅkilām ahaha karma-nāśām api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of** ***vyapadeśa,*** **using word play: O elephant blinded with intoxication! Why do you leave the Gaṅgā River in front of you, glistening with beautiful water, and filled with blue lotus flowers and sweetly cooing, intoxicated swans? Why have you taken shelter of this Karmanāśa River, like a soiled cloud, filled with mud?**

**O hero who carries a lotus flower! Why do you, standing in front of me, give up the best of all girls on earth, glistening with the beauty of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa*****, playing in love, sweetly cooing during love? Why do you enjoy this sinful woman with spoiled breasts, who ignorantly destroys the artful actions of love?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word play is clear. The speaker speaks of herself. By speaking she hopes to drive the other woman away. *Sura-taraṅginī* refers to the Gaṅgā and Karmanāśā, a river in Magadha. Though there is word play in this verse the word play itself forms a disguised statement. The word play nourishes the *vyapadeśa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *pragalbhā* demonstrates her excellence and her opponent’s inferiority to Kṛṣṇa who is gazing at some enemy woman. *Kuvalaya* means a blue lotus and the earth. *Ghana-rasa* means water and *śṛṅgāra-rasa. Sura-taraṅginī* means Gaṅgā and a woman playful in amorous acts. *Payodhara* means clouds and breasts. *Padmin* means “O elephant” or “O girl holding a lotus.” *Paṅka* is mud or sin. Karmanāśa is a river or a woman who destroys artful actions by her ignorance. *Puraḥ* means in front you, I am standing. Or it can mean, “You standing in front of me.” Then Kṛṣṇa said, “Enter the bower.”

### Text 20

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***madhupair anavaghrātāṁ vimucya***  
***mākanda-mañjarīṁ madhurām \|***  
***bhrāmyasi madakala-kokila***  
***katham iva vṛndāvane paritaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion by** ***vyapadeśa,*** **using altered meaning of statements: My dear melodious cuckoo bird! Why do you wander about Vṛndāvana forest, ignoring this sweet mango blossom that even the bumble-bees have not smelled?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Madhupaiḥ* means by bees or by the protectors of spring. This refers to the southern breezes. Why do you ignore the mango bud not touched by the bees or the southern breezes, which would carry the fragrance of her body? This indicates her extreme shyness, since she covers here body completely with cloth so that even bees do not detect it and the winds do not carry it. Any other explanation would be unpleasant. Other explanations involving *atiśayokti* and puns are rejects as being material.

One should not think that this is an example of word play because of the one word *madhupaiḥ.* In all texts concerning literary ornaments, *vyapadeśa* arises using both word play and change of meaning. If two, three or four puns or change of meaning are employed however it is not accepted as *vyapadeśa.* But one pun or change of meaning is accepted. O cuckoo! Giving up everything enjoy the mango bud. “In front of me she is giving such instructions!” Kṛṣṇa then forcibly kissed her.

### Text 21

***atha puraḥstha-viṣayaḥ—***  
***śṛṇvato’pi harer matvā vyājāt aśrutivat kila \|***  
***jalpo’grataḥ sthite jantau puraḥstha-viṣayo mataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Addressing animals or plants: This refers to speaking to animals or plants, pretending that Kṛṣṇa is not listening, but knowing that he actually is listening.**

### Text 22

***tatra śabdottho, yathā—***  
***āhūyamānāsmi kathaṁ tvayālināṁ***  
***svanaiḥ sva-puṣpāvacayāya mālati \|***  
***āmoda-pūrṇaṁ sumanobhir āśritaṁ***  
***punnāgam eva pramadena kāmaye \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Addressing others using word play: O** ***mālatī*** **creeper! Why do you call me through the bumble-bees to pick your flowers? I madly desire this fragrant** ***punnāga*** **tree with beautiful flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The pun here is *punnāga* which refers to a flowering tree and to the best of men.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Punnāga* means a tree and Kṛṣṇa, the best of men. Kṛṣṇa then comes.  
”O sakhī! I have heard of your desire. Come here, I will show you the *punnāga* tree.” She takes his hand and comes to the bed made of *punnāga* flowers

### Text 23

***arthottho, yathā—***  
***anavacita-carīyaṁ cāru-puṣpā latālī***  
***tava nikhila-vihaṅgāś cātra nirdhūta-śaṅkāḥ \|***  
***tvayi vicaritum īhe tena govardhanādya***  
***prakaṭaya tam upāyaṁ nirvṛtā yena yāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Addressing others, using altered meanings: O Govardhana Hill! You are decorated with many creepers bearing beautiful flowers unpicked by anyone, and you are the home of many confident birds. I wish to wander on your slope. Please tell me how I may easily do that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Blissful, she becomes fully satisfied. Coming to her, Kṛṣṇa says, “Govardhana in personal form spoke to me directly in that cave. He requested that I bring one of my devotees who had offered prayers to him. Enter that cave to please him.” He then led her into the cave.

### Text 24

***yathā vā—***  
***prasiddhaḥ sādhvīnāṁ vrata-hara-vinode vraja-pateḥ***  
***suto’yaṁ tvaṁ vācāpy alam asi niroddhuṁ na mṛdulā \|***  
***aho dhiṅ mūḍhāhaṁ tad api gahane granthila-latā-***  
***śatākrānte śrāntā yad iha vicarāmy asya purataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: The prince of Vraja is famous for breaking the chastity of pious girls, and I am a delicate girl, unable to resist him, even with words. I am so foolish! Exhausted from walking in this impenetrable tangle of creepers, I have now stumbled on him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In speaking to others, it actually means speaking to plants or to moving beings. This example illustrates moving entities--people. *Na alam* means “I am unable.” The forest is thick with creepers, impossible for others to enter. Since she is tired, he is able to catch her. He comes and says, “O beautiful woman! I have heard you talking to your friend. You are afraid of me. I swear to Viṣṇu that I will not destroy your chastity. Would a person like me desire to be a destroyer of trust? Therefore, go and rest on the flower bed in the bower for a moment. Since you are tired from playing in the forest, I have mercifully supplied this. I will stand guard. Do not fear that others will come.” Becoming excited, he then embraced her, though she was agitated, fearful and shy.

### Text 25-27

***atha āṅgikāḥ—***  
***aṅguli-sphoṭanaṁ vyāja-sambhramādy-aṅga-saṁvṛtiḥ \|***  
***padā bhū-lekhanaṁ karṇa-kaṇḍūtis tilaka-kriyā \|\|25\|****\|*  
***veśa-kriyā bhruvor dhūtiḥ sakhyām āśleṣa-tāḍane \|***  
***daṁśo’dharasya hārādi-gumpho maṇḍana-śiñjitam \|\|26\|\|***  
***dor-mūlādi-prakaṭanaṁ kṛṣṇa-nāmābhilekhanam \|***  
***tarau latāyā yogādyāḥ kṛṣṇasyāgre syur āṅgikāḥ \|\|27\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Using the limbs: In front of Kṛṣṇa, messages are conveyed using the body by cracking the fingers, hastily covering the body; writing on the ground with the toes, scratching the ear, applying** ***tilaka,*** **decorating oneself, moving the eyebrows, embracing a friend, beating a friend, biting the lips, stringing necklaces and garlands, making the ornaments tinkle, showing the shoulders, writing Lord Kṛṣṇa's name, and twining a creeper around a tree.**

### Text 28

***tatra aṅguli-sphoṭanam—***  
***iyaṁ satīnāṁ pravarā varākṣī***  
***kathaṁ nu labhyeti mayi klamāḍhye \|***  
***viśākhayāsphoṭyata pañca-śākha-***  
***śākhāvalī mad-vyasanena sārdham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Cracking the fingers: Beautiful-eyed Viśākhā, the best of all chaste girls, then began to crack her fingers. Even though I was greatly fatigued, this activity drove away my unhappiness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pañca-śakha* means a hand according to *Amara-koṣa*. Thus *pañca-śākha-śākha* means fingers.

### Text 29

***vyāja-sambhramādy-aṅga-saṁvṛtiḥ—***  
***pihitam api pidhatte mat-purastād uro yad-***  
***vṛtam api muhur āsyaṁ yat-paṭenāvṛṇoti \|***  
***vraja-nava-hariṇākṣī tan-manojasya manye***  
***śara-paribhava-ghūrṇāghrāta-citteyam āste \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Covering the body in haste: As she stood before me, this doe-eyed young** ***gopī*** **repeatedly covered her face and breasts with her cloth, though they were already covered. I think her heart is wounded by the arrows of Cupid.**

### Text 30

***padā bhū-lekhanam—***  
***kamraṁ namra-muklī lilekha caraṇāṅguṣṭhena goṣṭhāṅgane***  
***yat kiñcid vraja-sundarī mayi dṛśor vṛtte nava-prāghuṇe \|***  
***tenānaṅga-nideśa-paṭṭa-padavīm āsādya man-mānasaṁ***  
***kṣiptvā tat-kuca-śaila-saṅkaṭa-taṭī-sandhau balāt kīlitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Writing on the ground: As soon as I arrived, this beautiful** ***gopī,*** **her head bowed, began to scratch beautiful designs on the ground with her big toe. These designs became the edicts of Cupid, and as I read them I found my mind tightly bound with ropes and forcibly thrown into the valley between the two mountains of her breasts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. By that writing, a tablet for recording the orders of Cupid was produced. By that contract, my mind was thrown forcibly and bound up between the narrow slopes of her breasts. *Kīlita* means “bound up” according to *Amara-koṣa*. While writing on the ground by bringing her arms together, her breasts came together and trapped his mind.

Here is the explanation. Cupid, being satisfied, has given dominion of Rādhā’s limbs to my eyes. Clear writing was done using the ground as the paper and big toe as the pen in order to confirm my dominion. Seeing the greed in my mind after getting that dominion, in order to undo the mind’s offense, my eyes bound up my mind between her breasts.

### Text 31

***karṇa-kaṇḍūtiḥ—***  
***raktāṅgulī-śikhara-ghaṭṭana-lola-pāṇi-***  
***śiñjāna-kaṅkaṇa-kṛta-smara-turya-śaṅkam \|***  
***līloccalat-kanaka-kuṇḍalam atra karṇa-***  
***kaṇḍūyanaṁ vraja-saroja-dṛśaḥ smarāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Scratching the ear: I am contemplating this lotus-eyed** ***gopī*** **scratching her ear with the tips of her red fingernails, causing the bangles on her wrist to tinkle which sounded perhaps like Cupid’s drums and causing her gold earrings to sway playfully.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

By the movement of the pink tip of the little finger of her left hand as she put it in her ear hole, the movement of her bracelets jingling produced the doubt whether it was the sound of Cupid’s drums.

### Text 32

***tilaka-kriyā—***  
***sānandaṁ śarad-indu-sundara-mukhī sindūra-bindūjjvalaṁ***  
***bandhūka-dyutinā kareṇa tilakaṁ gāndharvikā kurvatī \|***  
***tvām ālokya śikhaṇḍa-śekhara sakṛt karṇoccalat-kuṇḍalā***  
***rūḍhaṁ cetasi rāga-kandalam iva vyaktaṁ vyatānīd bahiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Applying** ***tilaka:*** **O Kṛṣṇa decorated with a crown of peacock feathers! As soon as Rādhā, whose face has the beauty of the autumn moon, saw you, she at once began to apply a splendid dot of vermilion using her hand, as splendid as a** ***bandhuka*** **flower, while her earrings swung to and fro. It appears that the love sprouting in her heart has spread externally.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundavallī speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Simultaneously (*sakṛt)* with seeing you, she began to apply *tilaka.* The earrings moved about when the sides of her face became horizontal in applying the *tilaka.* The sprout of *anurāga* previously growing in her heart seemed to manifest externally in the form of the red *tilaka* mark.

### Text 33

***veśa-kriyā—***  
***harau puraḥsthe kara-pallavena***  
***salīlam ullāsya milan-marandam \|***  
***nālīka-netrā nija-karṇa-pālīṁ***  
***pālī lavaṅga-stavakaṁ nināya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Decorating oneself: As Kṛṣṇa stood before her, lotus-eyed Pālī, showing her playful nature, placed a cluster of nectar-filled clove flowers on her ear lobe using her bud-like hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Pālī* means the ear lobe according to *Viśva-kośa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nālika-netrā* means lotus eyes but also means “not useless eyes,” since those eyes could drink the beauty of his face.

### Text 34

***bhruvor dhūtiḥ—***  
***vidhunvatī madana-dhanur bhayaṅkaraṁ***  
***bhruvor yugalaṁ kathaya kim adya khidyase \|***  
***viśākhike mukha-śaśi-kānti-śṛṅkhalā***  
***babandha te madhuripu-gandha-sindhuram \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Moving the eyebrows: My dear Viśākhā! Moving Cupid's arched bows of your eyebrows in this frightening manner, why do you grieve today? After all, with the chains of the beauty of your moonlike face, you have just tied up the maddened elephant known as Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Gandha-sindhuram* is a rutting elephant.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She moves her eyebrows to indicate “Why does he come near me?”

### Text 35

***sakhyām āśleṣaḥ—***  
***puraḥ kalaya maṇḍalī-kṛta-kaṭhora-vakṣoruhaṁ***  
***calat-kanaka-kaṅkaṇa-kvaṇita-tuṅgitānaṅgayā \|***  
***apāṅgam aghamardane nayana-vīthi-navyātithau***  
***prasārya pariṣasvaje sahacarī ciraṁ citrayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Embracing friends: Look! With a passionate sidelong glance Citrā greets Kṛṣṇa, who has just entered her vision. While the jingling of her moving golden bracelets incites his lust, she embraces a friend for a long time, pressing her to her round, firm breasts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to Rati-mañjarī. The jingling incites Kṛṣṇa’s lust. Citrā says “He is very lusty. I am very soft. He will spoil me. Therefore I will flee.” A *prakharā sakhī* speaks to her. “Do not display fear in front of me! Have faith. I can defeat him by speaking arrogantly.” Citrā then embraced her saying “May you have good fortune.” This is the cause of her embracing her friend.

### Text 36

***sakhī-tāḍanam—***  
***vimuñca nikhilaṁ vaśīkaraṇa-kāraṇānveṣaṇaṁ***  
***manas tvayi viśākhayā muraharopahārīkṛtam \|***  
***muhur yad anayā bhavat-pada-saroja-kakṣā-milat-***  
***taḍic-cala-dṛgantayā sphuṭam atāḍi puṣpaiḥ sakhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Beating a friend: Give up seeking reasons to bring Viśākhā under control. She has offered her mind to you completely. While clearly directing the lightning bolts of her restless sidelong glances at your lotus feet, she repeatedly strikes a friend with flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala speaks to Kṛṣṇa. A friend of Viśākhā said, “O friend! You desire is fulfilled, since here comes Kṛṣṇa. Glance at him!” Then Viśākhā beat her laughing friend with flowers.

### Text 37

***adhara-daṁśaḥ—***  
***bhajati pathi dṛśor vrejandrasunau***  
***madana-madonmuditā puras tavālī \|***  
***iyam iha kupiteva paśya sakhyai***  
***vidhu-vadanā radana-cchadāvadāṅkṣīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Biting the lip: Now that she has seen Kṛṣṇa, your moon-faced friend has become joyous with the intoxication of love. Look! She has bitten her lip as if she has become angry at her friend.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā speaks to Lalitā. The following conversation is implied. “You have thrown me into the hands of the lecher, bringing me far away on the pretext of picking flowers on these bent branches. Just wait! I will take revenge on you.”

### Text 38

***hārādi-gumphaḥ—***  
***keyaṁ puraḥ sphurati phulla-saroruhākṣī***  
***savye yayā subala mām avalokayantyā \|***  
***āvṛtya mauktika-sare parigumphyamāne***  
***ceto-maṇir mama sakhe taralo vyadhāyi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Stringing a necklace: O Subala! Who is this blossoming lotus-eyed girl who has appeared in front of me? By repeatedly gazing at me to the left, with bent head, she has made the jewel of my heart the center of the necklace of pearls she strings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Āvṛtya* means repeatedly. *Taralaḥ* is the center jewel of a necklace. It can also mean fickle. She has made me unsteady.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She turns her neck in order to fix her thieving glance on me, in order to steal my heart. *Mauktika-sare* means a garland of pearls. *Taralaḥ* means the center jewel and fickle.

### Text 39

***maṇḍana-śiñjitam—***  
***vilokya māṁ śyāmalayā vidūrataḥ***  
***saṅkīryamāṇā maṇi-kaṅkaṇāvalī \|***  
***vitanvatī jhaṅkṛta-ḍambaraṁ muhuḥ***  
***śaṅke bravīty aṅgaja-rāja-śāsanam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Jingling ornaments: Seeing me from far away, Śyāmā makes a tumultuous tinkling sound with the clashing of her jeweled bracelets. I think this sound announces the dominion of Cupid.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Saṅkīryamāṇā* means striking together.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The bracelets on her right wrist when adjusted by the left hand make a noise. This is the natural action of a woman with nothing else to do. It is done without particular reason except to attract Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 40

***dor-mūla-prakaṭanam—***  
***śyāme divya-tarāḥ sphuranti parito vṛndāvanāntar-latā***  
***yāḥ kalyāṇi vahanti hanta madhurām agre phalānāṁ tatim \|***  
***citreyaṁ tava dor-latā valayinī yasyās tvayollāsite***  
***mūle nandita-kṛṣṇa-kokilam abhūd āvir varīyaḥ phalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Revealing the shoulder: O Śyāmā! In this forest of Vṛndāvana in front of you there are many splendid creepers bearing beautiful fruit clusters. O fortunate woman! But more astonishing are the creepers of your arm with bracelets, for, when you show your shoulder out of joy, a wonderful fruit appears at the root that delights the black cuckoo bird.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Śyāmā. *Valayinī* means “surrounded” as well as bracelets. If you go near to the *tamāla* tree, it will quickly surround you. That is its nature. *Ullāsite* means “when shown out of joy.” A wonderful form has appeared which gives joy to Kṛṣṇa or the black cuckoo. “Oh! This is most remarkable. I have never seen such a fruit. I must squeeze it with my fingers to see if the fruit is tender or hard.” He then did so.

### Text 41

***kṛṣṇa-nāmābhilekhanam—***  
***dūtyam agre tava tiṣṭhatu vṛnde***  
***tiṣṭhate yad iyam indu-mukhī me \|***  
***nāma me vilikhati priya-sakhyāḥ***  
***paśya gaṇḍa-phalake ghusṛṇena \|\|41\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Writing Kṛṣṇa’s name: O Vṛndā! So much for your messenger service, since the moon-faced girl reveals herself in front of me. See! She has written my name on the surface of her cheek with** ***kuṁkuma.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tiṣṭhate* means “she reveals herself with love.” *Prakāśana-stheyākhyayoś ca*: the *ātmanepada* of *sthā* means “to indicate ones intentions to another person” or to make an award.” (Pāṇini 1.3.23)

### Text 42

***tarau latāyā yogaḥ—***  
***rūpaṁ nirūpya kim api vraja-paṅkajākṣyāḥ***  
***sākṣād bhuvam aham arjuna yāvad ārtaḥ \|***  
***sā mām adhīram adhinot kala-dhauta-yūthyā-***  
***stāvat tamāla-viṭape ghaṭanāṁ vidhāya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Winding a creeper around a tree: O Arjuna! When I saw the beautiful form of this lotus-eyed Vraja woman, I became afflicted. At that moment, by wrapping a golden** ***yūthi*** **creeper around a dark** ***tamāla*** **tree, she delighted me though I had become unsteady.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nirūpya* means seeing. Arjuna is a cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa. *Kala-dauta* means gold.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nirūpya* means seeing. Arjuna is a cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa. “Oh! The golden *yūti* has fallen on the ground. I will raise it up using the *tamāla* tree.” By doing this, she indicated her *prema* for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 43

***atha cākṣuṣāḥ—***  
***netra-smitārdha-mudratve netrānta-bhrama-kūṇane \|***  
***sācīkṣā vāma-dṛk-prekṣā kaṭākṣādyāś ca cākṣuṣāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Using the eyes: Signals sent from the eyes are divided into the following varieties: smiling eyes, half-closed eyes, wandering glances, contracted glances, crooked glances, glancing to the left and repeated glances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Kūṇana* means contracting.

### Text 44

***tatra netra-smitam, yathā—***  
***vibhramaṁ ratipateḥ sthagayantīṁ***  
***keśavasya purataḥ kapaṭena \|***  
***tvām avetya caṭule sakhi jātyā***  
***gūḍham atra hasatas tava netre \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Smiling with the eyes: O friend! Seeing you trying to conceal your amorous agitation in front of Kṛṣṇa deceitfully, your eyes, fickle by nature, are secretly smiling.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sthagayantīm* means covering.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

These gestures for sending messages arise from *anubhāvas* with the thought “My lover will relish these and become attracted to me.” They are not at all artificial. They are full of taste.

### Text 45

***netrārdha-mudrā—***  
***kavayo hari-vaktra-puṣkare’smin***  
***sakhi netre kathayanti puṣpavantau \|***  
***anayoḥ savidhe tavākṣi-padmaṁ***  
***bhavitā nārdha-nimīlitaṁ kathaṁ vā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Half-closed eyes: Poets say that Kṛṣṇa's face is the sky and his eyes are the sun and moon. My friend, is this not perhaps the reason your lotus eyes are half-closed in his presence?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is only a metaphor, not reality, since the Lord’s form is the supreme element beyond all matter.  *Puṣkaram* means a lotus and the sky. *Puṣpavantau* means sun and moon.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundavallī jokes with Rādhā who is standing in front of Kṛṣṇa. His face is the sky and his eyes are the sun and the moon. According to *Amara-koṣa, puspavantau* means sun and moon. Her lotus eyes are half closed because a lotus closes in the night with the moon and opens in the day with the sun. Her eyes are actually half-closed out of shyness which suddenly appeared when her eyes, wide open with joy, met the eyes of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 46

***netrānta-bhramaḥ—***  
***na hṛdye’py adhyastā ratir anaḍuhāṁ saṅgara-rase***  
***na ramye’pi krīḍā-sadasi suhṛdāṁ dhīr upahitā \|***  
***tvayi kṣiptvā dṛṣṭiṁ param iha tamālāyitam abhūn***  
***mukundena śyāme tad api kim apāṅgaṁ naṭayasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Wandering glance from the edge of the eye: Mukunda has now lost interest in the duel between the bulls. His mind is no longer fixed on happily playing with his cowherd friends. O Śyāmā! By glancing at you he has become stunned like a** ***tamāla*** **tree. Why do you make your glance dance?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Anuḍuhām* means of bulls. Because of shyness and zeal, her eyes are closed and open, as in the previous verse. Does he see me or not see me because he is overcome with emotions? Thinking in this way, her eyes wander with their open portion.

### Text 47

***netra-kūṇana-—***  
***kalindajā-kūla-purandare dṛśor-***  
***adhvany avāpte prathamādhvanī-natām \|***  
***trapāñcitaṁ kiñcid akuñci cañcalaṁ***  
***vilakṣayā śyāmalayā dṛg-añcalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Contracting the eyes: When she saw Kṛṣṇa while traveling on the road, astonished Śyāmalā first closed her eyes in shyness, moved them about because of eagerness, and then contracted them in fear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vilakṣayā* means filled with astonishment according to *Amara-koṣa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Adhvanī-natām* means “being a traveler on the road.” Filled with shyness, she closed her eyes. The corner of her eye moved because of zeal and fickleness. At first, her eyes were not contracted, but becoming fearful, they contracted partly*. Vilakṣayā* means filled with astonishment.

### Text 48

***sācīkṣā—***  
***tiryag-vivartita-naṭan-nayana-tribhāgaṁ***  
***praikṣiṣṭa yat taraṇijā-puline mṛgākṣī \|***  
***hṛn-magna-bhagna-makarāṅka-śarāgravan māṁ***  
***sadyas tad adya nitarāṁ vivaśīkaroti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Crooked glances: On the bank of the Yamunā, doe-eyed Rādhā glanced with one third of her eye, which moved horizontally, wandered about, and finally began dance. Like the tip of a broken arrow of Cupid piercing my heart, that glance completely wounded me today.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tiryag-vivartita-naṭan-nayana-tribhāgam* is an adverbial clause. She glanced with one third of her eye. *Tribhāgam* means a third as in the word *tri-piṣṭapa* (one third of the surface--heaven). *Vivaśa* means “injured” according to *Amara-koṣa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. She glanced with one third of her eye, which moved about (*vivartita),* danced, and moved horizontally. *Tribhāgam* means one third even though the usually form would be *tritīya-bhāgam*. Out of shyness, one third of her eye operated with eagerness. But when Kṛṣṇa glanced at her, her glance became horizontal. At that moment, out of increased eagerness, the glance began to wander around. Then because of joy and insolence, it began to dance.

### Text 49

***vāma-dṛk-prekṣā—***  
***pūrṇaṁ pramodottaralena rādhe***  
***śyāmāṁ rasānāṁ nidhim indubhājam \|***  
***savyena netrāñjalinā pibantī***  
***tvam unmanāḥ kumbha-bhavāyitāsi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glancing to the left: O Rādhā! With the cupped hand of your left eye, you have repeatedly drunk the full, dark ocean of nectar in the form of Kṛṣṇa, endowed with the moon and rising with waves of bliss. Filled with desire, you have become Agastya, overflowing with that nectar.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa is a vessel of special *rasas*, or an ocean of *rasa.* *Indu-bhājam* means his face is like a moon. This is *atiśayokti.* By the left portion of her eye, not the full eye, she drinks the nectar with cupped hands. It is as if she has four hands in the form of two eye lids covering each eye. The two eyelids of the left eye drink the nectar. She continuously drinks (*pibantī*). Though he is continually being drunk by her, he still remains there. Thus she continues to drink. Her power is unlimited since she drinks the ocean of nectar and puts it into a pot, but it does not fill the pot. There is another version of the verse:

*pūrṇaṁ pramodottaraleṇa rādhe*  
*mano murāre rasa-vāri-rāśim \|*  
*savyena netreṇa vidhāya pītaṁ*  
*taṁ kumbha-jātaṁ bhavatī jigāya \|\|*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā, who is decorated with marks of love. The ocean produces waves because of joy. He is an ocean of water or special *rasas* like *śṛṅgāra*. The ocean is black or is Kṛṣṇa. That ocean is endowed with the moon or with Kṛṣṇa’s face. The left eye has cupped hands in the form of the two eyelids. *Kumbha-bhava* means a vessel and also Agastya who swallowed the ocean. The left eye operates fully after amorous enjoyment since shyness has gone. It operates as a messenger to Kṛṣṇa when the desire for enjoyment arises again.

### Text 50

***kaṭākṣaḥ—***  
***yad gatāgati-viśrānti-vaicitryeṇa vivartanam \|***  
***tārakāyāḥ kalābhijñās taṁ kaṭākṣaṁ pracakṣate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Repeated glances:** ***Kaṭākṣa*** **is defined by the knower of arts as astonishing, repeated movement of the pupils towards the object, staying a moment and then withdrawing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The pupils go to the object and come back, and remain on the object for a very short time (*viśrānti)* with astonishing, repeated movements.

### Text 51

***yathā—***  
***citraṁ gauri vivartate bhramikarī viśramya viśramya te***  
***dṛk-tārā-bhramarī gatāgatim iyaṁ karṇotpale kurvatī \|***  
***yasyāḥ kelibhir ākulīkṛta-mateḥ padmāli-vārtā kva sā***  
***gāndharve madhusūdanasya nitarāṁ svasyāpy abhūd vismṛtiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O golden-complexioned Rādhā! The bees of the pupils of your eyes, going and coming, with astonishing movement, causing bewilderment, repeatedly rest on the lotus flower in Kṛṣṇa's ear. The playing of this bumble-bee has agitated the mind of Kṛṣṇa. Where is the question of thinking of the friend of Padmā? He has completely forgotten himself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

O golden limbed Rādhā! The friend of Padmā is Candrāvalī. What is the news of her? She is situated far away. *Padmāli* also means a group of lotuses.  *Madhusūdana* is a bee and Kṛṣṇa*. Bhrami* means wandering around.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A messenger speaks to Rādhā or Kṛṣṇa speaks to her. The pupils move to his ear ornament stay there and return. By touching Kṛṣṇa’s face, they become completely pleased. *Padmāli* is a group of lotuses or Candrāvalī. Madhusūdana is a bee or Kṛṣṇa. He forgets himself because of the movements of her eyes bewilder his mind (*bhramikarī*).

### Text 52-53

***ity eteṣām asaṅkhyānāṁ dig eveyaṁ pradarśitā \|***  
***yathocitam amī jñeyā nāyake’py agha-vidviṣi \|\|52\|\|***  
***svābhiyogā iti proktāś ced amī buddhi-pūrvakāḥ \|***  
***svabhāvajās tu bhāvajñair anubhāvāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\|53\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A general view of the unlimited means of the** ***svayaṁ dūtī*** **communicating her intentions towards Kṛṣṇa has been given. These are also used by Kṛṣṇa in suitable cases. These gestures are performed intentionally. But since they arise as natural actions they are also accepted as** ***anubhāvas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This (*amī*) refers to the activities in speaking, use of limbs and eyes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

These are also found in the hero, Kṛṣṇa:

*mad-adhara-viluṭhad-vilocanāntaṁ*  
*mṛdula-latā-nava-pallavaṁ daśantam \|*  
*sakhi harim avalokya bhānujāyās*  
*taṭa-vipine sphuṭad-antarāsmi jātā \|\|*

**When I saw Kṛṣṇa in the forest at the bank of the Yamunā, his sidelong glance plundering my lips while he bit a delicate bud of a creeper similar to my lips, my heart began to blossom. .** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.6**

*kuṭilaṁ mām avalokya navāmbujam upari cucumba sa raṅgī \|*  
*tena haṭhād aham abhavaṁ vepathu-maṇḍala-sañcalad-aṅgī \|\|*  
*bhāmini pṛccha na vāraṁ vāram \|*  
*hanta vimuhyati vīkṣya mano mama vallava-rāja-kumāram \|\|*  
*dāḍima-latikām anu nistala-phala-namitāṁ sa dadhe hastam \|*  
*tad anubhavān mama dharmojjvalam api dhairya-dhanaṁ gatam astam \|\|*  
*adaśad aśoka-latā-pallava-mayam atanu-sanātana-narmā \|*  
*tad aham avekṣya babhūva ciraṁ bata vismṛta-kāyika-karmā \|\|*

**Glancing at me, passionate Kṛṣṇa kissed a bending new lotus. Because of that hint, my whole body is now violently trembling. Beautiful one, please do not ask again and again. Now that I have seen the prince of the cowherds, my heart has become enchanted.**

**When he placed his hand on a pomegranate creeper bowed down with two round fruits, the splendor of my piety and the wealth of my peacefulness vanished. When I saw him bite a red** ***aśoka*** **flower as he continually joked, I at once forgot all my household duties.** ***Gītāvalī*** **6, 8**

*kṛṣṇe karṣati koka-yugmam abalā dorbhyāṁ dadhuḥ svastikaṁ*  
*kaṇṭhe cāru mṛṇālam arpayati tāś cakrur bhujān bhaṅgurān \|*  
*padmaṁ jighrati pāṇibhiḥ pidadhire vaktraṁ jala-krīḍane*  
*tāsāṁ tasya babhūva saurata-rasaḥ ko’pīṅgitair iṅgitaiḥ \|\|*

**When Kṛṣṇa plucked two dates, the girls crossed their hands in front of their bodies. When he put a beautiful water lily on his throat they bent her arms. He smelled a lotus using his hands. They covered their faces. While playing in the water the girls and Kṛṣṇa partook of astounding amorous pleasure by various gestures.** ***Ananda-vṛndāvana-campu***

These devices using words, body movements and eyes are done intentionally with the idea “By hearing and seeing me do this, my lover will become attracted to me.” But these should be understood to be *anubhāvas*. First they arise as *anubhāvas* and then the woman thinks “Seeing this, Kṛṣṇa should become attracted.” They are then known as *abhiyoga* or devices to attract Kṛṣṇa. The word intentionally (*buddhi-pūrvaraḥ)* does not mean that the intention was previous (*pūrvakaḥ*) to the act, but rather “connected to intention.”

### Text 54

***atha āpta-dūtī—***  
***na viśrambhasya bhaṅgaṁ yā kuryāt prāṇātyayeṣv api \|***  
***snigdhā ca vāgminī cāsau dūtī syād gopa-subhruvām \|***  
***amitārthā nisṛṣṭārthā patra-hārīti sā tridhā \|\|54\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Trusted messengers (*****āpta-dūtī):*** **Those who are faithful to the end of their life in this service, who are affectionate and who are skilful at words are known as the commissioned messengers among the cowherd women. There are three types:** ***amitārthā (self-appointed), nisṛṣṭārthā*** **(appointed) and** ***patra-hārā (*****message bearer)*****.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Since the messenger is well known to bring about a meeting between two lovers, it is not mentioned in the definition of the *āpta-dūtī.* The particular qualities of the messenger are mentioned.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since it is clear that the duty of the messenger is bringing about a meeting of the couple it is not mentioned. The qualities of the messenger are mentioned.

### Text 55

***tatra amitārthā—***  
***jñātveṅgitena yā bhāvaṁ dvayor ekatarasya vā \|***  
***upāyair melayet tau dvāv amitārthā bhaved iyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Self-appointed messenger: The woman who, knowing the desires of the man and woman or the desires of one of them, brings them together by some means is called the** ***amitārthā*** **(performer of unlimited actions).**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She who does unlimited actions is called *amitārthā.* Knowing the desires of the man and the woman or knowing the desires of one of them, she brings them together by some means (without specific instructions).

### Text 56

***yathā—***  
***sā te bakāntaka kaṭākṣa-śarārditāpi***  
***jīrṇaṁ trapā-kavacam eva vṛthā vahantī \|***  
***varṇair nunoda mukha-candra-vigāhibhir māṁ***  
***gamyair dṛśāṁ guṇatayā na kila śrutīnām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O killer of the Baka demon! Rādhā, pained by the arrow of your glance, futilely carrying the shattered amour of her modesty, had dispatched me with words from her moon-like face, which cannot be understood by hearing, but only by seeing her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**
