*Dṛśāṁ guṇatayā* means “by being the object of your sight.” This meaning of the word is seen for example in *guṇā guṇeṣu vartante*: the senses are engaged in sense objects. (BG 3.28)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A letter carrier, understanding the signs given by the heroine, reveals to her lover her condition on the pretext of delivering a letter. O killer of Baka! Though she suffers from your glance of love, since she is modest, protected by shyness, she sent me with the words contained in her letter.

“What has been written? Give me the letter. Having read it aloud, I will understand. You are a letter carrier.” No, the words came from her mouth, not written down “Then tell me what she said. Please tell me. I want to hear. Are you a letter carrier or an appointed messenger?” No, her words can be understood only by seeing her, not by hearing her words. Seeing the messenger with a grey face, Kṛṣṇa understood that the heroine had not sent her. In this way, she revealed she was an *amitārthā,* acting on her own.

### Text 57

***atha nisṛṣṭārthā—***  
***vinyasta-kārya-bhārā syād dvayor ekatareṇa yā \|***  
***yuktyobhau ghaṭayed eṣā niṛṣṭārthā nigadyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Assigned messenger: The woman who has been assigned by the couple or by one of them to bring about their meeting by some means is called** ***nisṛṣtārthā*** **(agent).**

### Text 58

***yathā—***  
***aghadamana jagaty anargha-rūpā***  
***vilasati sā guṇa-ratna-rāśir ekā \|***  
***dhig apaṭu-matir asmi yat purastāt***  
***kaṭhina-maṇes tava vaktum udyatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O destroyer of Aghāsura! She has qualities like a pile of jewels and her beauty has no price in the universe. Fie on me! I have a diseased mind for trying to describe these jewels to a person like you, hard-hearted as a diamond.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The speaker is revealed to have natural affection for Rādhā by her words of praise. Though it is possible she has been sent, she dispels this idea by saying “I am foolish. I have on my own tried to say something.” But this indicates she has been given the responsibility to arrange a meeting, through false representation, in order to show her dedicated desire to benefit Rādhā. Though a diamond shows itself off by its brilliance, it is also very hard. It is not like the moonstone. It remains the same in heat or moister. Having seen his intentional indifference, she speaks with anger, out of love.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Her beauty is priceless, pure white in the three worlds, since it cannot be found anywhere there. Her limbs have beauty, youth, fragrance, proper firmness and shape. Her words are also well endowed. But her mental qualities such as patience and inscrutability are also incomparable. Thus the messenger talks of her qualities as a pile of jewels. No price can be given for seeing her form with your eyes, what to speak of smelling her with your nose or hearing her with your ear. Then what to speak of a price for appreciating her qualities!

“But my beauty is unequalled in the world. Ask all the towns everywhere and come and tell me. Give my beauty to her eyes, and in exchange I will accept all of her beauty.”

“Oh! I am so foolish to try this!”

“Why do you criticize yourself?”

“I have tried to speak in front of you. There is no one existing who can say that your and her beauty are equal. There is a great difference.”

“Since you know the oath of justice, tell the truth. I will accept it.”

“You are hard-hearted like a diamond. By this one quality all your qualities become valueless. But she is decorated with affection and softness, and is most excellent.”

The previous example showed the messenger delivering her own message secretly. Since this verse shows none of the unique qualities of the *amitārthā* or the *patrahārī* it illustrates the *nisṛṣtārthā.*

### Text 59

***atha patrahārī—***  
***sandeśa-mātraṁ yā yūnor nayet sā patra-hārikā \|\|59\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The woman who simply delivers a message from the man or the woman is called the** ***patra-hārikā.***

### Text 60

***yathā—***  
***tayā nibhṛtam arpitā mayi mukunda sandeśa-vāg***  
***vrajāmbuja-dṛśādya yā śruti-puṭena tāṁ svīkuru \|***  
***praviśya mama nirbhaye yad iha sāndra-nidrotsave***  
***kadarthayasi dhūrta māṁ kim iva yuktam etat tava \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Mukunda! Please hear this message your lotus-eyed** ***gopī*** **gave me in a secluded place. “O rascal! Why do you enter into my peaceful, deep sleep and cause me pain? Is this proper?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sent by one woman of Vraja, this messenger approaches Kṛṣṇa in private and tells him what she said. Please hear the message which (*yā*) was give by her to me. *Kadarthayasi* means “You give me pain.”

### Text 61

***tāḥ śilpa-kārī daivajñā liṅginī paricārikā \|***  
***dhātreyī vana-devī ca sakhī cety ādayo vraje \|\|61\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These messengers in Vraja may be artisans, fortune tellers, ascetics, servants, nurses, presiding deities of the forest, or friends.**

### Text 62

***atra śilpa-kārī—***  
***tvām āhuḥ pramādākṛtiṁ bhagavatas tvaṣṭur dvitīyāṁ tanuṁ***  
***tat tūrṇaṁ likha rūpam atra bhuvane yad vetsi lokottaram \|***  
***ity abhyarthitayā mayādya phalake tvāṁ prekṣya sā citritaṁ***  
***citrā citra-daśāṁ gatā sahacarī-netreṣu citrīyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Artisans: “You are a second Viśvakarmā, appearing in a female form. Please quickly draw a picture of the most handsome man you know in this world.” Requested in this way, I drew a picture of you on a slate. When Citrā saw you on the slate, she became struck with wonder and became motionless like a picture, which surprised her friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Citrīyate* means causing astonishment.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tvaṣṭuḥ* means “of Viśvakarmā.” You are Viśvakarmā incarnated as a woman. Requested by Citrā, I drew a picture. She became stunned like a picture (*citra-daśām*). *Citra* means a picture or astonishing according to *Amara-koṣa.* Her friends became astonished also. Citra becomes a verb form (*citrīyate*) by the following rule. *Namo-varivaś-citra-ṅaḥ kyac* (Pāṇini 3.1.19)

### Text 63

***daivajñā—***  
***tavādya śubha-rohiṇī-vṛṣabha-rāśi-bhājaḥ parām***  
***avetya gaṇanād ahaṁ sukha-samṛddhim atrāgatā \|***  
***tad ehi mudirākṛte parama-citra-kodaṇḍa-bhāg***  
***akhaṇḍa-vidhu-maṇḍalā bhavati vidyud uddyotatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Astrologer: From calculations I see that today that you, having the auspicious constellation of Rohiṇī in Vṛṣabha, will attain great wealth. O Kṛṣṇa, whose form is like a dark rain-cloud! Come quickly! May lightning flash, a full moon and a colorful rainbow illuminate you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The bow, moon and lightning represent Rādhā’s eyebrow, face and golden limbs.

This is the first type of *atiśayokti* (hyperbole). The definition is *upamānenāntar-nigīrṇasya svopameyasya yad adhyavasānaṁ saikātiśayoktiḥ:* the subject is suppressed by not mentioning it and the objects of comparison alone are mentioned. *Bhavati* means “to you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Bhavati* means “in you.” This is an example of the first type of *atiśayokti.* The bow is Rādhā’s brows and the full moon is her face.

### Text 64

***liṅginī—***  
***liṅginā tāpasī-veśā paurṇamāsīvad īritā \|\|64\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The ascetic is a woman wearing the dress of renunciation like Paurṇamāsī.**

### Text 65

***yathā—***  
***sarale na vidhehi putri cintāṁ***  
***vaśagas te bhavitā vrajendra-sūnuḥ \|***  
***yad ahaṁ caturātra siddha-mantrā***  
***jaratī pravrajitā tavāsmi dūtī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Honest daughter! Do not worry. The prince of Vraja will be brought under your control because I am an old ascetic, very clever and have the power of reciting mantras. I shall become your messenger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

First she will try to bring him under control by her cleverness. Then if that is not possible she will control him by chanting mantras—by chanting his name. The results of chanting his name are well known. “When did she get the power of mantras?” I am now elderly. This indicates “From a young age I have been chanting mantras. In order to get a proper opportunity I have renounced everything.” By her cleverness she will get control of his mind. By the mantras she will externally control him. By old age and renunciation, he must obey her orders since she has more respect than his parents (who are not renounced).

### Text 66

***paricārikā—***  
***lavaṅga-mañjarī-bhānumaty-ādyāḥ paricārikāḥ \|\|66\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Servants: Some servant girls like Lavaṅga-mañjarī and Bhānumatī act as messengers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among all the servants, Lavaṅga-mañjarī is the most respected. This fact is not to be concealed. In the *Gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā she* is also mentioned as one of the foremost. This has been kept secret.

### Text 67

***yathā—***  
***sahacara-pariṣattaḥ kṣipram ārād vikṛṣtas***  
***tava guṇa-maṇi-mālām īśvari grāhitaś ca \|***  
***madhuripur ayam akṣṇoḥ prāpitaś cābhikakṣāṁ***  
***bhaṇa punar api seyaṁ kiṅkarī kiṁ karotu \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: I have pulled him away from his group of friends and made him accept your jeweled necklace. He has come close to you eyes. O my queen, please tell me what else may this maidservant do for you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lavaṅga-mañjarī speaks.

### Text 68

***dhātreyī—***  
***dhātreyikāsmi madhumardana rādhikāyās***  
***tvayy adbhutaṁ kim api vaktum ihāgatāham \|***  
***niṣpadya kṛṣṇa-rucir adya hiraṇya-gaurī***  
***sadyaḥ sudhākara-kalā-dhavaleyam āsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Nurse’s daughter: O Kṛṣṇa! I am the daughter of Rādhā’s nurse. I have come here to tell you something very astonishing. Although hers complexion is golden, now that she has a taste for you, she has suddenly become thin and pale, just like the white crescent moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Dhātreyī* means the daughter of a nurse. *Kṛṣna-ruci* means black color or having a taste for Kṛṣṇa. With that taste, she has suddenly changed color and become thin. But she is also extraordinarily beautiful, since she is like the moon.

### Text 69

***vanadevī—***  
***jātyāhaṁ vana-devatāpi bhaginī kutrāpi te premataḥ***  
***kvāpy ambā jananī kvacit priya-sakhī kutrāpi bhartuḥ svasā \|***  
***grīvām unnamaya prasīda racaya bhrūr iṅgitād īṅgitaṁ***  
***kuryād vallava-kuñjaraḥ pariṇatiṁ vakṣoja-kumbhe tava \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Goddess of the forest: I was born as a goddess in this forest. Out of love for you I have appeared to you at different times as your sister, mother-in-law,** ***priya-sakhī*** **and sister-in-law. Now please lift your head towards me. Be pleased, move your eyebrows and reveal what is on your mind. In this way Kṛṣṇa, the elephant among the cowherd boys, will be able to touch your breast with his hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Show indication of your love (*īṅgitam*) by moving (*iṅgitāt)* your eyebrows. . He will transform your breasts into an elephants’ frontal lobes (*kumbha*). Surrounded by the elephant, she will be marked by his tusks. This indicates that she will be embraced intensely by him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A messenger who takes many forms, sent by Vṛndā to break Rādhā’s anger, reveals to Rādhā her extraordinary power in order make her words come true. At one time I became your sister Anaṅga-mañjarī and I fed and dressed you. I became your mother Mukharā and I teach you for your benefit. I became your *priya-sakhī,* Lalitā, and teach you how to show anger. I have become your sister-in-law, Kuṭilā, and scold you. At that time you did not recognize me. Now, out of friendship, while being a messenger, I am revealing everything. Therefore, lift your head in my direction. Then you will know if you have seen me before or not. Out of respect for me, be pleased. If you will not speak, then move your eye brow. By that you will reveal your mind, so that Kṛṣṇa will touch your breast with his hand. She suggests that Rādhā becomes an elephant, suitable for the elephant named Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 70

***atha sakhī—***  
***svātmano’py adhikaṁ prema kurvāṇānyonyam acchalam \|***  
***viśrambhiṇī vayo-veṣādibhis tulyā sakhī matā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Friends acting as messengers: The woman who gives up pretense and show great affection for the heroine, who shows great trust, and who has a similar age and dress as the heroine is known as friend.**

### Text 71

***yathā—***  
***na me śokas tasyāṁ yad iyam atipūtaiḥ priya-sakhī***  
***hatā te dṛg-bhaṅgīṣubhir anupamāṁ yāsyati gatim \|***  
***paraṁ śocāmy uccair jagad idam ahaṁ yan madhuripo***  
***vinā tasyāḥ prekṣām ahaha bhavitā vyartha-nayanam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O enemy of Madhu! I do not lament now that my dear friend Rādhā, wounded by the arrows of pure your glances, is about to attain her final destination. I only lament that the eyes of this entire material world will become useless for the lack seeing her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā describes to Kṛṣṇa the final state of Rādhā. If you delay in meeting her, she will attain this state. In stating that the whole world will be unfortunate with her loss, she points to all her friends using her forefinger. This indicates that everyone in Vraja will be in sorrow. I do not lament for you since you are just a woman killer. I do not lament for myself, since I will die along with her.

### Text 72

***vācyaṁ vyaṅgyam iti dvedhā tad dūtyam ubhayor api \|\|72\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These friends as messengers communicate to the hero and heroine by direct words or by suggestion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tad-dūtyam* means being a messenger as a friend. The words are directed to the hero or the heroine (*ubhayoḥ*).

### Text 73

***tatra kṛṣṇa-priyāyāṁ vācyaṁ, yathā—***  
***śapa prahara tarja māṁ kṣipa bahiṣkuruṣvādya vā***  
***kadāpi matir āgrahān na sakhi me viraṁsyaty ataḥ \|***  
***prayāmi tad ahaṁ harer upanayāya satyaṁ bruve***  
***na sā śvasitu yā na vām anubhaven navāṁ saṅgatim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Direct words to the heroine: Curse me, hit me, rebuke me, throw me about or throw me outside. Still my mind does not waver from its resolve. I shall now go to bring Kṛṣṇa here. O friend, I speak the truth. She who will not work to see you reunited with Kṛṣṇa should no longer breathe.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Kṣipa* means “throw around.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks to Rādhā. She speaks in the next verse also. She who does not accomplish a new meeting of the two lovers should die (*śvasitu*).

### Text 74

***vyaṅgyaṁ, yathā—***  
***sakhi tarkitāsi kāmita-***  
***kṛṣṇāguru-saurabhā tvam iha \|***  
***bhavad-abhimatārtha-vidhaye***  
***naigama-savidhaṁ gamiṣyāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suggestion: My friend, I can guess that you desire to be anointed with black** ***aguru*** **perfume. I shall now go to the market to fulfill your desire.**

**I can guess that, so heavily perfumed, you desire to meet Kṛṣṇa. I shall go and get the lecher.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first meaning is “You desire black *aguru* perfume.” The second meaning is “You, heavily perfumed, desire Kṛṣṇa.” *Naigama* means merchant and townsman (*nāgara*) according to *Viśva-koṣa.* However the word *nāgara* also means a lecher. Thus *naigama* means Kṛṣṇa. *Savidham* means near.

### Text 75

***yathā vā—***  
***tvam asi kim iva bāle vyākulā tṛṣṇayoccaiḥ***  
***śṛṇu hitam avilambāṁ tatra yātrāṁ vidhehi \|***  
***vilasad-amala-rāgaḥ pūrva-śailasya tiṣṭhan***  
***vidhur upari cakori tvat-pratīkṣāṁ karoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: My child, why are you so afflicted with thirst? Listen for your benefit. Go immediately to that place. O** ***cakora*** **bird! The splendid, pure red moon waits for you on the eastern horizon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having given an example of indirect expression through word play, the author gives an example based on meaning. Since the phrase “on the eastern horizon” is used, *vidhu* refers only to the moon, and is not a pun (*vidhu* also means Viṣṇu), since the vocative “O *cakorī*!” indicates the ornament of *atiśayokti* (Rādhā is like the *cakorī*). And mentioning the moon (*vidhu*) produces the *vyaṅga.* The word *rāga* (red) should not be given another meaning (passion) for the same reason. The designation of an ornament of speech does not depend on one word, since the final affect depends on the taking the total meaning into account.

### Text 76

***atha kṛṣṇe vācyam—***  
***tayāsmi kṛṣṇa prahitā tavāgre***  
***saundarya-sarojjvalayā trilokyām \|***  
***abhūta-pūrvāṁ racayan vidhir yāṁ***  
***svasyāpi vismāpakatām ayāsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Direct expression to Kṛṣṇa: O Kṛṣṇa! Rādhā has sent me with a message for you. Rādhā is the most beautiful girl in all the three worlds. After Brahmā had created her, he became struck with wonder at her unprecedented beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In order to describe her beauty she describes how Brahmā created her. This is indirect expression (*vyaṅgya*). However “I have been sent by her” is direct expression (*vācyam*). Thus this verse is given as an example of direct expression. Brahmā himself became astonished (*svasyāpi vismāpakatām*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks. Her beauty astonished Brahmā. How much more it astonished others! He thought “I did not know I had such powers of creation!” The indirect suggestion (*vyaṅgam)* is “Enjoying her, make your life successful.” However, “She has sent me” is a direct statement. Thus this verse is given as an example of direct expression. If the messengers of the heroine speak directly at all times there would be lack of *rasa* through lack of show of skill.

### Text 77

***atha vyaṅgyam—***  
***tat-priyāyāḥ puraḥ paścāt kṛṣṇe vyaṅgyaṁ dvidhā bhavet \|***  
***tat sākṣād vyapadeśābhyāṁ dvividhaṁ ca dvidhoditam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Indirect expression to Kṛṣṇa: Two kinds of indirect messages are sent to Lord Kṛṣṇa: spoken in the presence of the beloved and spoken in her absence. These messages may again be divided into direct and using another subject (*****vyapadeśa)*****.**

### Text 78

***tatra tat-priyāyāḥ puraḥ kṛṣṇe sākṣād vyaṅgyaṁ, yathā—***  
***mādhava kalāpinīyaṁ na savidham āyāti me durārādhā \|***  
***nija-pāṇinā tad enāṁ prasīda tūrṇaṁ gṛhāṇādya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Spoken in the presence of the beloved directly: O Madhava! This peahen is very difficult to please. She will not come near me. Please be kind and quickly take her with your hand.**

**Mādhava! This well ornamented woman does not come close since she is soft and respectable. Take her by the hand and please her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kalāpinī* is a peahen and a decorated woman according to *Amara-koṣa.* It is difficult for me to make her favorable (*durārādhā*). The locative of the word *me* (in me) has the sense of an instrumental (by me). The phrase *me durarādhā* can be taken as *medura ārādhā.* She is soft and respectful.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks. *Kalāpinī is* a peahen and a decorated woman according to *Amara-koṣa.*  She does not come to me because she cannot be controlled. Or she does not come close because she is soft and respectable.

### Text 79

***yathā vā uddhava-sandeśe (51) --***  
***santi sphītā vraja-yuvatayas tvad-vinodānukūlā***  
***rāgiṇi agre mama sahacarī na tvayā ghaṭṭanīyā \|***  
***dṛṣṭvābhyarṇe śaṭha-kula-guruṁ tvāṁ kaṭākṣārdha-candrān***  
***bhrū-kodaṇḍe ghaṭayati javāt paśya saṁrambhiṇī iyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O Kṛṣṇa! Many girls in Vraja yearn to enjoy pastimes with you. My friend is not agitated by you. Whenever she sees you, the guru of all cheaters, she becomes angry and places in the two bows of her eyebrows many half-moon arrows of sidelong glances to attack you. See! She is now angry.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Many girls are eager for you. This is a joke. My friend is not agitated by you. “Then what is the worry?” Seeing you close by she becomes angry (*rāginī*) and on the bow of her eyebrows strings half moon glances and fires them. “Then what?” She becomes overcome with anger. See! “I cause agitation to give her bliss, not to give her suffering. Why should she become angry?” You are the *guru* for cheaters. All you do is cheat.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

And example of indirect expression using word play was given. Now an example of changed meaning is given. Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa in front of Rādhā. These plump (*sphītā*) women are suitable for your pleasure or are without obstinacy. Rādhā is filled with envy or attraction. *Viśva-kośa* says *rāga* means attraction or envy. She cannot be agitated by you. She is filled with anger. You will have no opposition to enjoying other young women, but if you agitate my friend there will a war of love since she is skilful in the arts of Cupid and cannot be defeated by you, even though you are a formidable enemy. The meaning does not depend on the pun in the word *rāginī.* Without that word the intended meaning is accomplished.

### Text 80

***vyapadeśena—***  
***dhavam upekṣya kaṭhoram iyaṁ puraḥ***  
***parimalollasitā kila mādhavī \|***  
***śrayitum utkalikā-valitādbhutaṁ***  
***nanu bhavantam upaiti hali-priya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By reference to other objects: O kadamba-tree! This fragrant** ***mādhavī*** **creeper laden with buds has now ignored the hard** ***dhava*** **tree. She comes to take shelter of you, a wonderful** ***kadamba*** **tree.**

**O friend of Balarāma! This girl, controlled by you, joyous because of your fragrance, endowed with all excellence, has given up her harsh husband and comes to take shelter of you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dhavam* means husband and a type of tree. *Mādhavī* means type of jasmine and a woman controlled by Kṛṣṇa.  *Utkalikā* means having an excellent blossom or having great longing. *Hali-priya* means “O Kṛṣṇa, pleasing to Balarāma” and “O *kadamba* tree!”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks. *Dhavam* means husband and a type of tree. *Mādhavī* means type of jasmine and d a woman controlled by Kṛṣṇa. *Utkalikā* means having an excellent blossom or having great longing. *Hali-priya* means “O Kṛṣṇa, pleasing to Balarāma” and “O kadamba tree!” *Valita* means “endowed with.”

### Text 81

***tat-priyāyāḥ paścāt sākṣād vyaṅgyaṁ, yathā—***  
***sphurat-sura-maṇi-prabhaḥ suramaṇī-ghaṭā-ślāghitāṁ***  
***sadābhimata-saurabhaḥ prakaṭa-saurabhodbhāsinīm \|***  
***mukunda mudira-cchavi-nava-taḍic-chriyaṁ tām asau***  
***bhavān api na campakāvalim ṛte kila bhrājate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Speaking while not in the presence of the heroine using direct expression: O Mukunda! You are eternally fond of the** ***surabhi*** **cows and you are splendidly decorated with the radiant Kaustubha jewel. Campakalatā is glorified by all the beautiful and charming** ***gopīs,*** **and she is brilliant with fragrance. O Kṛṣṇa! You do not appear glorious without the company of Campakalatā, beautiful as fresh lightning in the beautiful cloud**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Without Campakalatā you do not shine. She is suitable by being very similar to you. This is accomplished by similarity of words. He is radiant with the sparkling Kaustubha jewel.(*sura-maṇi-prabhaḥ*). He has many *surabhi* cows or he has fragrance. She is suitable also because of her qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend speaks about Campakalatā. He has the radiance of the Kaustubha. She is praised by groups of splendid women (*suramaṇī-ghaṭā*). He has many *surabhi* cows. You should remain with her because you have similar qualities to hers.

### Text 82

***vyapadeśena vyaṅgyaṁ, yathā—***  
***śailas tuṅga-śirā virājati saras tasyottare vistṛtaṁ***  
***tat tīre vanam unnataṁ tad-udare hārī latā-maṇḍapaḥ \|***  
***tasya dvāri gabhīra-saurabha-bharair āhlādayantī diśaḥ***  
***phullā te madhusūdanādya padavīm ālokate mālatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Speaking in the absence of the heroine, using** ***vyapadeśa:*** **My dear bumble-bee, north of this lofty mountain is a great lake. On the northern shore of that lake is a large, tall forest, and in the midst of that forest is a charming cottage of creepers. At the door of that cottage is a blossoming jasmine creeper that delights the directions with its intense fragrance. O bumble-bee! That jasmine-creeper is now gazing at the path waiting for you to arrive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mālatī* is a jasmine and also the name of a *gopī.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The mountain is Govardhana; the lake is Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Madhusūdana is a bee and Kṛṣṇa. *Mālatī* is a jasmine and Rādhā by *atiśayokti.*

### Text 83

***yathā nāyikayā dūtye vayasyāyā niyojanam \|***  
***kṛṣṇāya kriyate tasya prakāro’yaṁ vilikhyate \|***  
***niyojanaṁ kriyāsādhyaṁ vācikaṁ ceti tad dvidhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When the heroine engages friends as messengers for meeting Kṛṣṇa, there are two methods of engaging them: by action and words.**

### Text 84

***tatra kriyā-sādhyam—***  
***divi vīkṣya navāmbudaṁ tathāsau***  
***parirambhodyamam atatāna tanvī \|***  
***api kiñcid ihānudīrya vācā***  
***prajighāyāghabhide yathā vayasyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Engaging the messenger by actions: Slender Rādhā stares at a new rain-cloud in the sky, and stretches her arms as if to embrace it. It seems that, without speaking a word, she is sending her friend to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Parirambhodyamam* is described in dramatic literature. It is a slight imitation of embracing.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Rādhā stretches her hands to imitate an embrace. It seems that by not speaking a word she sends (*prajighāya*) her friend to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 85

***yathā vā—***  
***muhur api vidhurāntar-veṇum ākarṇya mugdhā***  
***svayam iha na vayasyāṁ mādhavāya nyayuṅkte \|***  
***api tu viśadam asyāḥ sveda-śāliny-aruddhā***  
***tanum anu vikasantī kaṇṭaka-śreṇir eva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Briefly hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute, innocent Rādhā did not ask her friend to bring Kṛṣṇa. She perspired and the hairs of her body stood on end.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She could not stop (*aruddhā*) perspiration. Similarly *parāheṛ asoḍha* means impossible to conquer. *Kaṇtakāḥ* is hairs standing on end.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The heroine performs actions indicating her eagerness for meeting Kṛṣṇa. The activities are of two types: *anubhāvas* and *sāttvika-bhāvas.* *Anubhāvas* were previously illustrated. This verse illustrates *sāttvika-bhāvas.* *Mugdhā* means very youthful. Therefore she was unable to speak directly to her friend. *Aruddha* means that she perspired and part of her body was uncovered by movement of her cloth. “My friend should see this so that she understands my eagerness and brings Kṛṣṇa.” In this way she engages her friend as a messenger. *Sveda-śālini* means covered with perspiration. *Kaṇṭakāḥ* means hairs standing on end.

### Text 86

***atha vācikam—***  
***vācyaṁ vyaṅgyam iti proktaṁ pūrvavad vācikaṁ dvidhā \|\|86\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Verbal indications: Just as the messengers speak either directly or indirectly, the heroine engages her messengers directly or indirectly.**

### Text 87

***tatra vācyaṁ, yathā—***  
***tvam asi mad-āsavo bahiś carantas***  
***tvayi mahatī paṭutā ca vāgmitā ca \|***  
***laghur api laghimā na me yathā syān***  
***mayi sakhi rañjaya mādhavaṁ tathādya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Direct speech to engage a friend as a messenger: O friend, you are my life-breath moving outside my body. Within you reside great cleverness and eloquence. Please make Kṛṣṇa attracted to me so that I do not become even more insignificant than I already am.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. *Asavaḥ* means life airs. I have faith in you. You are clever and skilful with words. On the pretext of picking flowers you should wander in the forest and unseen by him come near him. While he is listening, talk to your friends and describe how I have greater love for him than all other women. When he comes close he will ask “O friend, who is this sweet person that you are describing?” Then you should say with reverence, “I speak of no one.”

“O friend do not be afraid. There will be no fault in speaking. Tell me whom you were describing.”

“O Mādhava, what will you do by knowing this?”

“O friend! That is a great secret.”

“Mādhava, please go away! She is very different from you, by her very nature. You should have nothing to do with her.”

“O friend! Why is she so different?”

“You are lusty for women. She is a chaste wife. You are unsteady. She is most controlled. You are devoid of religious acts. She is devoted to worship. You are impure and she is bathes three times a day, wearing washed cloth.”

“O friend! I am a *brahmacārī.* Durvāsa can testify. By the order of my father I have taken mantra *dīkṣā* from *guru* Bhāguri. You can ask Nāndīmukhī and Paurṇamāsī. I am the personification of purity. You can testify to that.”

“O Mādhava! You are a male. She comes from a good family and will not see you.”

“O friend! She does not have to see me. I will be satisfied by seeing her, so exalted in *dharma,* at a distance.”

“Mādhava! How can that be done?”

“O friend! I will establish a deity of the sun today in a cave temple at Govardhana. After cleaning the temple I will remain at a distance. You should bring her to see the deity and perform worship of this deity which you have not yet seen. When she enters to perform worship I will be successful just by seeing her back. If you mercifully agree to this, go there unseen by others and with very soft foot steps.”

“O Mādhava! What bribe will you give?”

“O friend! I sell myself into your hands. Why speak of bribes?”

“Mādhava! Take comfort. I will fulfill your desire.”

“After saying this, come and take me there.” Rādhā then revealed this heart-felt instruction to her friend Viśākhā.

### Text 88

***atha vyaṅgyam—***  
***atra śabdārtha-mūlatvād vyaṅgyaṁ ca dvividhaṁ bhavet \|\|88\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vyaṅgyam:*** **The indirect request is through word play and altered meaning of the statement.**

### Text 89

***tatra śabda-mūlaṁ, yathā—***  
***na hi śikṣituṁ vara-kalāsu kauśalaṁ***  
***guṇa-cāturīṁ ca na mṛgākṣi kāmaye \|***  
***tam ahaṁ samabhyasitum eva subhruvāṁ***  
***sakhi keśa-bandhana-viśeṣam arthaye \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Word play: My dear doe-eyed friend, I do not wish to become skill in the best of arts or become skilled in qualities. I only wish is to learn the art of tying braids of beautifully browed** ***gopīs.***

**My dear doe-eyed friend, I do not wish to skill in the best of arts or become skilled in qualities. I only wish to attend to Keśava, the wealth of the beautiful women.**

### Text 90

***yathā vā—***  
***ṇa paumarāa-ppamuhaṁ raaṇaṁ kāmei goi me hiaaṁ \|***  
***kintu sadā hīra-baraṁ vāñchai hārantare kāduṁ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example:**

**na padma-rāga-pramukhaṁ ratnaṁ kāmayate gopī me hṛdayam \|**  
**kintu sadā hīra-varaṁ vāñchati hārantare kartum \|\|**

**O** ***gopī*****! My heart has no desire for the best ruby. It only desires to put a beautiful diamond in the middle of this necklace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sadā hīra-varam* (best diamond) can also be *sadā ahīra-varam* (best cowherd).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having given an example of a *mugdhā* engaging a friend as a messenger, the author now gives an example of a bold woman engaging a friend. *Hīra-varam* means the best diamond and also the best cowherd (*ahīra-varam*).

### Text 91

***atha artha-mūlam—***  
***ākṣepeṇa svapatyāder govindādeḥ praśaṁsayā \|***  
***vaiśiṣṭyena ca deśāder artha-mūlam anekadhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Changed meaning: Engaging a friend using indirect language by changing of meaning may take place by many means, such as rebuking a husband, praising Kṛṣṇa or describing a place.**

### Text 92

***tatra svapatyādy-ākṣepeṇa, yathā—***  
***vidhātur daurātmyān na hi vahati ghora-prakṛtaye***  
***ruciṁ cetaḥ patye hata-vapur idaṁ dīvyati rucā \|***  
***bhajat-kakṣām akṣṇor viṣamam idam ugraṁ praharate***  
***yamī-tīrāraṇyaṁ kim iha sakhi śikṣāṁ na tanuṣe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Criticizing the husband to incite a messenger: Because of Brahmā’s cruelty, my heart is not at all attached to my husband. My unfortunate body sports with the beauty of youthfulness. When I see the forest by the bank of the Yamunā, I feel terrible, unequalled pain. O friend, why do you not instruct me during this calamity?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of some woman who has developed *pūrva-rāga* (attraction to Kṛṣṇa before directly meeting him). Because of the creators cruelty he produced a husband with cruel nature. Thus my heart has no attraction for him. She resolves the objections of a friend by rationalizing in this way. She actually simply desires to say “I have no attraction for my husband.” Following her statement about Brahmā she then says her body is unfortunate for showing youthful beauty. If this body were more unsuitable, it would be possible to remain in isolation. But the opposite is the case. The forest on the river bank causes suffering. It strikes at my heart, making me attracted to some other man, famous for causing suffering. What are you going to teach me so that I can remain indifferent as before? It is difficult to tolerate this suffering. You should unite me with he who is playing in the forest. This is the deep meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā in *pūrva-rāga* speaks to Viśākhā. What offense have I committed that a cruel husband was given to me? That is the cruelty of the creator. Is it my fault if I have no taste in my heart for him? This is an explanation given to her friend. But if the creator had given me a beautiful husband she still would not have taste since her heart has become attached only to Kṛṣṇa. This is her internal thought.

“You may not like your husband, but it is not proper to develop attraction for another man.” But my unfortunate body day by day sports with beauty arising from youth (*rucā).* It is the fault of having such a youthful body, not the fault of my heart.

“But considering your duty as a woman with utmost shyness and fame, you should have self-control.” The forest on the bank of the Yamunā, attaining closeness to my eyes, gives me pain. It ignites the fire of lust, but does not burn me up completely. And there is no method to obtain relief. It is ferocious (*ugram*). Even jewels, mantras or herbs have no effect. It is unusually strong *(viṣama*). In this calamity (*iha*) you do not give me instruction. This means “There is no possibility of instruction on how to get relief.” Saying farewell to family duty, shyness and reputation, quickly take me to Kṛṣṇa if you desire to maintain my life.

### Text 93

***govindādeḥ praśaṁsayā, yathā—***  
***kula-strīṇāṁ neṣṭā para-puruṣa-rūpa-stuti-kathā***  
***tathāpi tvaṁ prāṇāḥ sakhi mama bahiṣṭhāḥ svayam asi \|***  
***kiyān āste tasmin vraja-pati-kumāre madhurimā***  
***cchaṭāpy ārād yasya mradayati dṛśor dvandvam amṛtaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Inciting a messenger indirectly by praising Kṛṣṇa, using altered meaning: O friend! A chaste girl will never glorify another man. Since you are my life air situated apart from my body, I say this. How much sweetness resides in Kṛṣṇa! Even his effulgence from a far distance makes my eyes affectionate by its flood of nectar.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Since you are my friend, I will tell you this. *Ārāt* means “at a distance.” His effulgence makes my two eyes soft. It produces affection in my eyes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. You are my friend and therefore I speak this *(tathāpi*). This is the hint. Because you are my life air, what I say cannot be kept hidden from life airs. His effulgence even from a distance softens my eyes with nectar, taking away their hardness. His effulgence makes my eyes full of affection. I may resolve not to look at him, but the eyes have developed affection for him and therefore favor looking at him.

### Text 94

***yathā vā—***  
***dūtya-cakra-caturāsi cañcale***  
***nandano vrajapateḥ sa nāgaraḥ \|***  
***māṁ jahāti śiśutā ca rakṣiṇī***  
***mā kṛthāḥ sakhi tataḥ pramāditām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O fickle friend! You are very expert at delivering messages. Kṛṣṇa is just a lecher. Now I have given up my foolhardy nature. You must be my protector. O friend! Do not be inattentive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some woman angrily speaks about Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness indirectly. Do not become inattentive. Do not have lapses because of lack of foresight.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Praising Govinda also includes praising messengers. That is illustrated here. O fickle woman! This nature is difficult to give up, since one requires cleverness in performing the duties of a messenger. Kṛṣṇa is a lecher. If he had not been born, it would make no difference to me. My childishness by whose influence I was very rash in maintaining my self-control has now left me. Therefore do not be inattentive. By inattention, in carrying out messenger services in front of me, my chastity will not remain. Both you and I will be condemned by the public. You should conceal your nature since you have foresight. However, internally you are actually very skilful at being a messenger. This is praise for her. That cleverness will bear fruit, since he is just a lecher. Now I do not have an obstinate, aggressive nature. Therefore do not be lax in being a messenger. Otherwise, by repeated wounds from the arrows of Cupid taking away my life airs, someone will be responsible for killing a woman. Cupid who is dedicated as a hunter will not be responsible. Kṛṣṇa is not responsible since he is not opposed to meeting me, since he is a lecher at heart. Youthfulness is not responsible since it has not arrived for that purpose. You should conclude that the responsibility falls on you, since you are full of *dharma* and capable of protecting me by your messenger activities, by staying close to me.

### Text 95

***deśādi- vaiśiṣṭyena, yathā—***  
***vṛndāraṇye vratati-paṭalī-saṅkaṭe puṣpa-hetor***  
***bhrāmaṁ bhrāmaṁ sahacari ciraṁ śrāntim abhyāgatāsmi \|***  
***tad-viśrāntiṁ kṣaṇam iha karomy ekikāhaṁ nikuñje***  
***tvaṁ kālindī-taṭa-parisarād āharethāḥ prasūnam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Inciting a messenger by mentioning a place, using statements with other meanings: O friend! Because of wandering and wandering about to collect flowers in Vṛndāvana forest filled with trees and creepers, I am very tired. I shall now go alone into this grove and rest for a moment. In the meantime please go and bring me a flower from the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *gopī* who has understood that Kṛṣṇa is near by smelling his fragrance, sending a friend to make an appointment on the pretext of picking flowers, speaks to her friend.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Saṅkaṭe* means spread. For picking flowers, I have wandered about so long, since I have not found the right flowers. With the flowers you gather at the Yamunā I will decorate my breasts here while I am alone. “You should pick a flower” indicates that she should bring Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 96

***yathā vā—***  
***madhuritā madhunā vidhunāpy asau***  
***sakhi pataṅga-sutā-pulināṭavī \|***  
***sa-vayasā vayasā ca vibhūṣitā***  
***tanur iyaṁ kim iha kṣamam ucyatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: The spring season and the moon have made this forest on the Yamunā's shore very beautiful. My body is also nicely decorated with ornaments and youthfulness. My friend, what more is needed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One *sakhī*, after being decorated by a friend, sends the friend to bring Kṛṣṇa on the pretext of picking flowers but the friend does not return quickly. The *sakhī* speaks to another friend. I am decorated with my friend and youthfulness. What more than this is need?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous example did not particularly show the special quality of inciting a meeting by mentioning place. Therefore another example is given. Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā saying as it were “Today I will test your intelligence.” The forest has been made beautiful by the spring and moon. Similarly by two elements--by friends such as *tilaka* and ornaments, and my youthfulness (such as gestures and playfulness)--my body has become beautiful. The friend, ornaments, is the secondary element and the youthfulness is the primary element in making the body beautiful. What other object is to be desired (*kṣamam ucitam*)? The friend says, “I will show you by bringing another object.” Then the friend goes to bring Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 1

***prema-līlā-vihārāṇāṁ samyag vistārikā sakhī \|***  
***viśrambha-ratna-peṭī ca tataḥ suṣthu vivicyate \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhīs*** **who, as their very nature, reveal and increase the pleasure and pastimes of** ***prema,*** **who are casket of jewels of intimacy, will be described in detail.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

All the *sakhīs* within the groups will be described.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The various types of *sakhīs* will be described according to their various services as messengers, since the variety of *sakhīs* is best understood from their interactions. First they are glorified. Not only do they play a major role as messengers, but all of them are the possessors and causes of *rasa.* That is explained in this verse. The word *sakhī* is in the singular to express a class. They increase and make known (*vistārikā*) the pastimes of *prema.* The *prema* of the hero for the heroine and the *prema* of the heroine for the hero is made known by the *sakhī* and inceased by the *sakhī*. The *sakhī* increases the pastime by causing non-cooperation of the heroine, by joking, and by having the couple meeting through appointments,. The *sakhī* broadcasts the pastimes in other places and other times. The *sakhī* increases the pleasure *(vihāra*) of amorous union by resolving problems of elders and husbands by her great efforts. This union is revealed by the *sakhī* afterwards from the emanation of *rasa* her interactions with the heroine who has been enjoyed. The *sakhī* does not feel complete *(samyak*) without the activities such as *abhiyoga.*

### Text 2

***eka-yūthānuṣaktānāṁ sakhīnām eva madhyataḥ \|***  
***adhikāder bhidā jñeyā prakharādeś ca pūrvavat \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Among the** ***sakhīs*****, those who are attached to only one group are divided into the types** ***adhikā, samā*** **and** ***laghu,*** **and** ***prakharā, madhyā*** **and** ***mṛdvī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They have differences in *svarūpa* which are naturally revealed though their various interactions. What about their different natures for performing service as messengers? That is described in this verse.

### Text 3

***prema-saubhāgya-sādguṇyādy-ādhikyād adhikā sakhī \|***  
***samā tat-sāmyato jñeyā tal-laghutvāt tathā laghuḥ \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhī*** **is** ***adhikā*** **because of greater amount of** ***prema-saubhagya*** **and good qualities. The** ***sakhī*** **with a medium amount of these is called** ***samā*** **and the** ***sakhī*** **with least amount is called** ***laghu.***

### Text 4

***durlaṅghya-vākya-prakharā prakhyātā gauravocitā \|***  
***tad-ūnatve bhaven mṛdvī madhyā tat-sāmyam āgatā \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhī*** **whose words cannot be ignored is called** ***prakhāra*** **and is to be respected. The** ***sakhī*** **with least respect is the** ***mṛdvī*** **and the one with medium respect is the** ***madhyā.***

### Text 5

***ātyantikādhikatvādi-bhedaḥ pūrvavad atra saḥ \|***  
***sva-yūthe yūtha-nāthaiva syād atrātyantikādhikā \|***  
***sā kvāpi prakharā yūthe kvāpi madhyā mṛduḥ kvacit \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The divisions of** ***ātyantikā*** **and** ***apekṣikā*** **are also found as previously. The leader of the group is called** ***ātyantikādhikā. This ātyanikādhiika sakhī*** **with a group should be distinguished from the** ***ātyantikādhika*** **leader among all group leaders, who is Rādhā alone. This was described in Chapter Six.1 In some groups she may be a** ***prakharā*** **and in other groups a** ***madhyā*** **or** ***mṛdvī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Even the leader acts as a messenger for her *sakhis* and takes on *sakhī-bhāva* (rather than being the *nāyikā*). This will be explained in this chapter.

### Text 6

***tatra ātyantikādhikā-trikam—***  
***tat trikaṁ sakalāpekṣyaṁ nātīvānyavaśaṁ tathā \|***  
***sva-yūthe tad-vyavahṛti-vyaktaye punar ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***ātyantikādhikā*** **who may be** ***prakharā, madhyā*** **or** ***mṛdvī*** **is to be respected by all others in the group. The leader is usually not under the control of anyone. These three** ***ātyantikādhikās*** **will be described in order to show the dealings in the group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The leader is to be most highly respected. Sometimes, in special circumstances and because she is soft, she is dependent on her *sakhīs*, though she is most independent.

### Text 7

*tatra* ***ātyantikādhika-prakharā—***  
***nīle nīla-nicolam artpaya maghe dehi srajaṁ dāmanīṁ***  
***tvaṁ kālāguru-kardamaiḥ sakhi tanuṁ limpasva campe mama \|***  
***jānīhi bhramarākṣi kutra guravaḥ paśya pradoṣodgame***  
***kuñjābhikramaṇāya māṁ tvarayate sphārāndhakārāvalī \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***ātyantikādhika-prakharā*****: Nīlā, give me this black cape. Maghā, give me this garland of** ***damanaka*** **flowers. My friend Campā, anoint my body with this dark** ***aguru*** **paste. Bhramarāksī, watch for my elders. Now that evening has arrived, this great blinding darkness will hasten me to the meeting in the bower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dāmanīm* means “made of *damanaka* flowers.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā speaks. This describes the decoration of the leader by the *sakhīs*. Since she gives orders she is the *ātyantikādhikā.* Others give her great respect and she is not dependent on anyone. *Dāmanīm* means “made of *damanaka* flowers.”

### Text 8

***adhika-prakharāḥ śyāmā-maṅgalādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\|8\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Śyāmā and Maṅgalā are among the** ***adhika-prakharās.***

### Text 9

***tatra ātyantikādhika-madhyā—***  
***anaṅga-śara-jarjaraṁ sphuṭati cen mano vas tadā***  
***mad-arthana-kadarthanaiḥ kṛtam itaḥ svayaṁ gacchata \|***  
***dṛśāṁ pathi bhavādṛśī-praṇayitānurūpaḥ sukhaṁ***  
***yad atra rata-hiṇḍakaḥ sa kila pāti go-maṇḍalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***ātyantikādhika-madhyā:*** **When my heart is torn open by Cupid's arrows, enough of your actions causing me suffering! Go from here for an appointment. Not far off, the debauchee Kṛṣṇa, object of love for persons like you, is herding the cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kṛtam* means “enough of this.”  *Rata-hiṇḍakaḥ* means a love thief.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks with the anger of love and a hidden smile to her *sakhīs* while constantly saying “O friend, do not delay in arranging a meeting.” The apparent *prakharā* speech is concealed and therefore she is a *madhyā.* *Kṛtam* means “enough of this.” *Dṛśām pathi* means “at a short distance.” *Rata-hiṇḍukaḥ* is a lecher. *Go-maṇḍalam* means a group of cows, but also the group of senses. Kṛṣṇa is herding your senses.

### Text 10

***bhavanty adhika-madhyās tu śrī-rādhā-pālikādayaḥ \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rādhā and Pālikā and others are** ***ātyantikādhika-madhyās.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Adhika-madhyāḥ* means *ātyantikādhika-madhyā* since that is the subject. The *āpekṣikas* will be decribed later.

### Text 11

***tatra ātyantikādhika-mṛdvī—***  
***śṛṇu sakhi vacas tathyaṁ māna-grahe mama kā kṣatiḥ***  
***sphurati muralī-nāde ko vā śramaḥ śravaṇāvṛtau \|***  
***atikaṭhinatā-durvādaṁ te niśamya mayā vraje***  
***damayitum amuṁ kintu kṣipraṁ dṛg-ardham agha-dviṣi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Listen, friend to the truth. If I show pride, what is the loss? Do my ears become tired from drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's flute? I have heard you are spreading the rumor among all the** ***sakhīs*** **that I am too harsh. To dispel that rumor, I will half glance at Kṛṣṇa very quickly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vraje* means “among all the *sakhīs*.” The word *sakhī* is not mentioned in order to convey the idea they act as a group.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī, separated from Kṛṣṇa because of a quarrel, speaks to Padmā. You keep saying, “You are too harsh, you are too harsh.” This has become known among many *sakhīs.* In order to dispel the rumor you have started, I will glance at him. There is no harshness is be removed by me. Because of my half-glance without speaking, you still become angry.

### Text 12

***adhikā mṛdavaś candrāvalī-bhadrādayo matāḥ \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Candrāvalī and Bhadrā are some of the** ***adhika-mṛdvīs*****.**

### Text 13

*atha* ***āpekṣikādhikā-trikam—***  
***yauthikīṣu sakhīṣv eva yūtheśāto laghuṣv iha \|***  
***yādhikaikām apekṣānyā sā syād āpekṣikādhikā \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The three types of** ***āpekṣikādhikās*****: She who are less than the leader, but who is superior to others in the group of** ***sakhīs*** **is called** ***āpekṣikādhikā.***

### Text 14

***tatra adhika-prakharā—***  
***sumadhye mā yāsīs tvam adhikam amībhir mṛdulatāṁ***  
***madasyopādānaiḥ śaṭha-kula-guror jalpa-madhubhiḥ \|***  
***ayi krīḍā-lubdhe kim u nibhṛta-bhṛṅgendra-bhaṇite***  
***kuḍuṅge rādhāyāḥ klamam api visasmāra bhavatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***āpekṣikādhika-prakharā*****: Sumadhyā! Do not become soft by the intoxicating honey talks of this Kṛṣṇa, the guru of cheaters. O girl greedy to enjoy pleasant pastimes! Have you forgotten that Rādhā is languishing in this grove full of the humming of kings of bees?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a group related to Rādhā. The attitude here is fault finding and anger of the *prakharā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks with censure to the *priya-sakhī* Sumadhyā who has become controlled by Kṛṣṇa’s cleverness, since he wants to break Rādhā’s pride.  *Nibhṛtam* means “full of.” Rādhā is in a bower filled with the humming of bees.

### Text 15

***yathā vā—***  
***mugdhe tūṣṇīṁ bhava śaṭha-kalā-maṇḍalākhaṇḍalena***  
***tvaṁ mantreṇa sphuṭam iha vaśīkṛtya tenānuśiṣṭā \|***  
***kuñje govardhana-śikhariṇo jāgareṇādya rādhāṁ***  
***dṛṣṭvāpy uccaiḥ sakhi yad asi me cāṭu-vāde pravṛttā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fool! Be quiet! You have become controlled by the mantras of Kṛṣṇa, the king of the rogues and have taken lessons from him. Even though you can see Rādhā sleepless in this garden on the summit of Govardhana Hill, you speak sweet words to me in a loud voice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since the words *kridā-lubdha* in the last verse were spoken in a joking way (it could mean the opposite *krīdā alubdha*—not desiring enjoyment), the woman could be a *madhyā.* Therefore another verse is given. Lalitā speaks to Citrā. Kṛṣṇa is the king of all skills in cheating. You have been taught by him. He has said, “Go and please Lalitā.” Seeing Rādhā who is sleepless, you talk to me in this pleasing manner.

### Text 16

***lalitādyās tu gāndharvā-yūthe’tra prakharādhikāḥ \|\|16\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lalitā is the** ***apekṣikādhika-prakharā*** **in Rādhā’s group.**

### Text 17

***atha adhika-madhyā—***  
***dāmārpyatāṁ priya-sakhī-prahitāṁ tvayaiva***  
***dāmodare kusumam atra mayāvaceyam \|***  
***nāhaṁ bhramāc caturike sakhi sūcanīyā***  
***kṛṣṇaḥ kadarthayati mām adhikaṁ yad eṣaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**My dear friend Caturikā! Please give this garland made by a** ***priya-sakhī*****, for which I picked the flowers, to Dāmodara. Do not by mistake reveal me to him since he will make me suffer greatly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to a *sakhī* named Caturikā

### Text 18

***yathā vā—***  
***giro gambhīrārthāḥ katham iva hitās te na śṛṇuyāṁ***  
***nigūḍho māṁ kintu vyathayati murārer avinayaḥ \|***  
***mayollāsāt tasmai svayam upahṛtā hanta sakhi yā***  
***kuraṅgākṣī-keśopari paricitā sā srag adhunā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**My friend, why do I avoid hearing your beneficial, profound words? The intense rudeness of Murāri simply causes me pain. The garland that I gave Kṛṣṇa is now decorating the head of Kuraṅgākṣī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When she says “He will make me suffer” she indicates her desire for enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa. This indicates a head of a group, not a *sakhī.* Therefore another example is now given. Viśākhā talks to Campakalatā. Your words have deep meaning. “O Viśākhā! Tomorrow is the full moon. Rādhā’s anger is giving happiness to the *sakhīs* in the opposite camp.” O Campakalatā! Why do I not hear your words, so that today I can make Rādhā give her anger at Kṛṣṇa? Kuraṅgākṣī is a *sakhī* in Candrāvalī’s group. It is understood that Kuraṅgākṣī took a garland that fell from Kṛṣṇa’s limbs and put it on her head to agitate Rādhā’s *sakhīs.*

### Text 19

***atra yūthe viśākhādyā bhavanty adhika-madhyamāḥ \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In Rādhā’s group, Viśākhā is the leading** ***adhika-madhyā.***

### Text 20

***atha adhika-mṛdvī—***  
***darāpi na dṛg-arpitā sakhi śikhaṇḍa-cūḍe mayā***  
***prasīda bata mā kṛthā mayi vṛthā purobhāgitām \|***  
***naṭan-makara-kuṇḍalaṁ sapadi caṇḍi līlā-gatiṁ***  
***tanoty ayam adūrataḥ kim iha saṁvidheyaṁ mayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**My dear angry friend! Even a little I have not seen Kṛṣṇa. Be kind to me. Don't uselessly become angry at me. If this Kṛṣṇa suddenly displays his dancing shark-shaped earrings and his playful gait close by, what should I do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

O my *sakhī* Citrā! You have consoled Kṛṣṇa, telling him that Rādhā’s anger has been destroyed. Thus he is coming and going from here. I will inform Lalitā all about your actions. Citṛā speaks humbly to that *prakharā prāṇa-sakhī* of Rādhā who is trying to frighten her. I have not even glanced a little at him from far off. You are accusing me of comforting Kṛṣṇa by speaking to him. *Amara-koṣa* says *purobhāgitā* means finding fault. When you go and he by chance shows his playful gait from far off for some purpose, I want to know what I should do? O angry *sakhī*! Since he is the prince, with independent character, should I flee with my friends or stay here?

### Text 21

***adhikā mṛdavaś cātra citrā madhurikādayaḥ \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Citrā and Madhurikā are the main** ***āpekṣikādhikha-mṛdvīs*** **in Rādhā’s group.**

### Text 22

*atha* ***samā-trikam—***  
***gāḍha-viśrambha-nirbheda-prema-bandhaṁ samā-trikam \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***samā*** **has slightly less** ***saubhāgya,*** **strong sense of friendship, and deep attachment to others in the group. There are three types.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Gādhā* means less *saubhāgya* than the *adhikā*. The *samā* has deep friendship (*viśrambha*) and strong attachment to others in the group (*nirbheda-prema*).

### Text 23

***tatra sama-prakharā—***  
***praviśati harir eṣa prekṣya nau hṛṣṭa-cetāḥ***  
***sakhi sapadi mudhā tvaṁ sambhramān mā prayāsīḥ \|***  
***pṛthu-bhuja-parighābhyāṁ skandhayor arpitābhyāṁ***  
***taṭa-bhuvi sukham āvāṁ maṇḍite paryaṭāvaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**My friend! Seeing us, Kṛṣṇa enters in a happy mood. Do not foolishly leave out of confusion. We will stroll on the bank of the Yamunā, decorated by the great bolts of his huge arms upon your shoulders.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The huge arms are Kṛṣṇa’s arms.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Two *prakharā samā prāṇa-sakhīs*, sent by Rādhā to arrange a meeting with Kṛṣṇa at her request, speak. The two huge arms are Kṛṣṇa’s. They do not mention that they are his arms out of shyness and sense of concealment.

### Text 24

***atha sama-madhyā—***  
***śyāme gauri hariḥ kva dīvyati sakhi kṣauṇībhṛtaḥ kandare***  
***kiṁ pañcāsya-nakhāḥ sva-vikramam adhur vakṣoja-kumbhe tava \|***  
***ākarṣaty abhitaḥ sa nāga-mathanas tvām eva kṛtvā ravaṁ***  
***mithyā lāsya-naṭi tvam eva ramase tasmin sukaṇṭhī-rave \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***sama-madhyā sakhī*****:**

**Śyāmā: Gaurī! At this moment where does Hari enjoy pastimes?**

**Gaurī: Śyāmā! My friend, the lion is in the cave of Govardhana Hill.**

**Śyāmā: Did his five nails boldly touch your breasts?**

**Gaurī: I think you have become attracted by the roar of this lion.**

**Śyāmā: False actress! It is you who find pleasure in this lion's roaring.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The two girls call out to each other. Śyāmā says “Where is Hari playing, O friend?” Gaurī says “He plays in a mountain cave.” Hari means Kṛṣṇa and a lion. Jokingly Śyāmā replies “Have his five nails held your breasts?” Gaurī says “The lion (*nāga-mathanaḥ*) has attracted you by his roaring.” *Nāga-mathanaḥ* also means Kṛṣṇa, controller of Kāliya. Śyāmā says “False actress! You enjoy the melodious roaring.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Two *priya-sakhīs* joke with each other in a conversation. First each calls the other. Śyāmā says “Where does Hari play?” Gaurī takes the word *hari* to mean a lion. By this she indicates “I do not know Kṛṣṇa.” “The lion is in a cave in the mountain.” Śyāmā thinks “Yes, I spoke about a lion.” Acting fearfully she says “Did he boldly place his five claws on the frontal lobe of your elephant body (your breast)? If he did, then pull up your cloth and show me the wound, because I will heal you by touching it.” Or, because of the singular case of “five nails” Kṛṣṇa took her left breast in his right hand and, surrounding her head with his left hand, strolled off. Whatever others may think, only this enjoyment could have taken place.

I think that you are curious about the lion’s actions. You always experience them. Thinking in this way, Gaurī says “I think you have been attracted by the lion’s roar. The conqueror of elephants has attracted you, who are a she-elephant. But he does not attract me, a deer.” *Nāga* also refers to Kāliya. *Ravam* also means the sound of the flute. Śyāmā says “O false actress! You said that I am an elephant and you are a deer. Both statements are false. But you enjoy the lion with the pleasant roar. Therefore you are a lioness since you remain healthy even by the touch of his nails. This I can infer.” Another meaning is “You have a beautiful voice. Therefore because you know singing, you enjoy the sound of his flute.”

### Text 25

***atha sama-mṛdvī—***  
***prālambam indumukhi yādṛśam eva dattaṁ***  
***kṛṣṇena tubhyam aparaṁ sakhi tādṛśaṁ me \|***  
***tvaṁ cen madīyam api ditsasi nādya mā dā***  
***hāsyaṁ vimuñca calitā tava pārśvato’smi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***sama-mṛdvī:*** **O Indumukhī! I have a garland similar to the one given to you by Kṛṣṇa. If you take mine and do not want to give it to me, then show a smile. I shall leave your company at once.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prālambam* is a long straight garland.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *prāṇa-sakhī* speaks to Indumukhī, an equal. This long garland is mine. If you think my garland is better, then you take it and give you your inferior garland. If you do not give your own garland and do want to give mine, you may say “I will not give anything, I do not want to. Let’s go. We will go again to Kṛṣṇa and I will decorate your neck with a garland given by him.” Smile and take both garlands. Laughing, she says “I am leaving this place.”

### Text 26-28

***atha laghu-trikam—***  
***laghu-trikaṁ priya-sakhī-saukhyotkarṣārtha-ceṣṭitam \|\|26\|\|***  
***yad apy anyonya-niṣṭhaṁ syāt sakhyaṁ tad api yujyate \|***  
***sadā sāhāyya-hetutvān mukhyaṁ tat tu laghu-trike \|\|27\|\|***  
***laghur āpekṣikī cātyantikī ceti dvidheritā \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***laghu sakhī*** **broadcasts the superior happiness of the leader of the group and has strong friendship with the leader. There are three types—*****prakharā, madhyā*** **and** ***mṛdvī.*** **Because they are always engaged in assisting the leader, their relationship as a** ***sakhī*** **is their chief role. There are two types of** ***laghus: āpekṣikī*** **and** ***ātyantikī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The three types of *laghu* are *prakharā, madhyā and mṛdvī.* The *priya-sakhīs* are by nature *adhikās.* The *laghus* perform bodily actions for showing their excellent happiness. Although the *adhika-prakharās* and other *adhikās* are friends with the *laghu-prakharās, madhyās and mṛdvīs--*since the messenger service cannot be performed without their coming and going, the *laghus* have a relationship as *sakhī* to the *adhikās* of their group.

### Text 29

***tatra āpekṣika-laghuḥ—***  
***āpekṣika-laghuś cātra kathitā lalitādikā \|\|29\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lalitā is an example of an** ***āpekṣika-laghu.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā and others are *laghus* depending on Rādhā.

### Text 30

***tatra laghu-prakharā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (5.32)—***  
***dhārā bāṣpa-mayī na yāti viratiṁ lokasya nimitsataḥ***  
***premāsminn iti nanda-nandana-rataṁ lobhonmanā mā kṛthāḥ \|***  
***itthaṁ bhūri nivāritāpi tarale mad-vāci sācīkṛta-***  
***bhrū-dvandvā na hi gauravaṁ tvam akaroḥ kiṁ nādya rodiṣyasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***laghu-prakharā*****: Do not allow your heart to fall in love with Nanda's son, for anyone desiring to establish a loving relationship with him will shed a stream of unending tears. I have prevented you many times, but ignoring my advice, fickle girl, you are knitting your eyebrows at me. Will you not cry forever today?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another version has *prema-khinna-jite tad atra sahasā lobhān mano mā kṛthāḥ*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā revealing her deep *anurāga* for Rādhā speaks to Rādhā who is pretending to be angry in front of Kṛṣṇa. *Prema* is the object of the sentence. .By showing her crooked brows at Lalitā, Rādhā expresses her anger.

### Text 31

***sā laghu-prakharā dvedhā bhaved vāmātha dakṣiṇā \|\|31\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***laghu-prakharās*** **are of two types:** ***vāmā*** **(obstinate) and** ***dakṣiṇā (*****compliant).**

### Text 32

***tatra vāmā—***  
***māna-grahe sadodyuktā tac chaithilye ca kopanā \|***  
***abhedyā nāyake prāyaḥ krūrā vāmeti kīrtyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***vāmā*****: The** ***vāma*** **is always proud. When pride slackens it becomes anger. She cannot be controlled by the hero and is generally harsh towards him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Generally she is harsh (*krūrā)* with the hero.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She cannot be controlled by the hero (*abhedyā nayake*). Generally she is harsh to him. If they were completely harsh, then it would contradict the equal affection that Lalitā and others show to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. When *māna* slackens it becomes anger. There is no question of giving it up completely.

### Text 33

***tatra māna-grahe sadodyuktā, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (222)—***  
***kañcana vañcana-cature***  
***prapañcaya tvaṁ murāntake mānam \|***  
***bahu-vallabhe hi puruṣe***  
***dākṣiṇyaṁ duḥkham udvahati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of always being engaged in pride: You should be angry with this expert cheater, killer of Mura. Being gentle to a lecher will bring only suffering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *vāma sakhī* speaks to a group leader who is *dakṣiṇā* (compliant).

### Text 34

***māna-śaithilye kopanā, yathā—***  
***sarabhasam abhivyaktiṁ yāte navāvinayotkare***  
***caṭu-paṭimabhir nītā mṛdvī prasādam agha-dviṣā \|***  
***asarala-sakhī-cillī-vyālī-paribhrama-kampitā***  
***vimukhita-mukhī bhūyo bhadrā haṭhād bhrukuṭiṁ dadhe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Slackening of** ***māna*****, turning to anger: After Kṛṣṇa had impetuously offended Bhadrā, gentle Bhadrā at first remained pleased with his clever words. However, when she noticed her friends moving their eyebrows at him, Bhadrā immediately showed anger on her face, and knitted her eyebrows also.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Navāvinayotkare* means a new pile of offenses.

### Text 35

***nāyakābhedyā, yathoddhava-sandeśe (52)—***  
***kāmaṁ dūre vasatu paṭimā cāṭu-vṛnde tatrāyaṁ***  
***rājyaṁ svāmin viracaya mama prāṅgaṇaṁ mā prayāsīḥ \|***  
***hanta klāntā mama sahacarī rātrim ekākinī iyaṁ***  
***nītā kuñje nikhila-paśupī-nāgarojjāgareṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Being uncontrolled by the hero, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: O master, give up your clever flatteries. Make your own kingdom. Don't come near me. Ah! My friend is now completely exhausted. Having gone to the bower at night alone, she stayed awake waiting for a rake who enjoys with all the other** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prāṅganam* means “close.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

May your cleverness (*paṭimā*) with all sorts of pleasing words (*cāṭu-vṛnde*) remain far away! This means “they cannot stand in my presence.” Do not come to my yard. Single handed, because I am your enemy, I will leave my yard and destroy your kingdom. Please believe that. “But Rādhā is in your yard. Without her, what use is my kingdom?” You are really the best of liars! My friend is exhausted. Going to the bower, she stayed awake all night waiting for the enjoyer of many cowherd women. What will you do to Rādhā?

### Text 36

***nāyake krūrā, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyāṁ (57)—***  
***amūr vraja-mṛgekṣaṇāś catur-aśīti-lakṣādhikāḥ***  
***pratisvam iti kīrtitaṁ savayasā tavaivāmunā \|***  
***ihāpi bhuvi viśrutā priya-sakhī mahārghyety asau***  
***kathaṁ tad api sāhasī śaṭha! jighṛkṣur enām asi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Harshness to the hero, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: There are eight million four hundred thousand** ***gopīs*****. Even your friend has praised them. But it is well known in the world that my dear friend Rādhā is the most valuable among them all. Cheater! How can you grab her so boldly?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Priya-sakhī* here means the dearest *sakhī* in the group.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Pratisvam* means each and each totally. Madhumaṅgala has just glorified the *gopīs* in relation to some suggestive words spoke by Nāndīmukhī. Among all of them (*iha)*, Rādhā is most valuable. No one is equal to this leader of a group. You try to grab her so boldly. Will you not fear the screams of the king on taking Rādhā for a greater price than eight million four hundred thousand girls paid as tax? O cheater! On the logic of destroying cheating with cheating, śaṭhe śāṭhyaṁ prakurvīta iti nyāya2 she says “You should bring the best horses from the king.” .

### Text 37

***yūthe ‘tra vāma-prakharā lalitādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\|37\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In Rādhā’s group Lalitā is famous as a** ***vāma-prakhara-laghu*****.**

### Text 38

***atha dakṣiṇā—***  
***asahā māna-nirbandhe nāyake yukta-vādinī \|***  
***sāmabhis tena bhedyā ca dakṣiṇā parikīrtitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***dakṣiṇa-prakharā-laghu*****: She who is intolerant of the heroine’s attempts to show** ***māna*****, uses skilful words in talking to the hero and who is controlled by his sweet or clever words of consolation is called** ***dakṣiṇā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *dakṣiṇā* cannot tolerate attempts (*nirbnadhe*) to display *māna* by the heroine. She is controlled by consoling, sweet words uttered by the hero (*tena*).

### Text 39

***tatra māna-nirbandhāsahā, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (9.10)—***  
***snigdhe yat paruṣāsi praṇamati stabdhāsi yad rāgiṇi***  
***dveṣasthāsi yad unmukhe vimukhatāṁ yātāsi tasmin priye \|***  
***tad yuktaṁ viparīta-kāriṇi tava śrī-khaṇḍa-carcā viṣaṁ***  
***śītāṁśus tapano himaṁ hutavahaḥ krīḍā-mudo yātanāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intolerance of** ***māna,*** **from** ***Gīta-govinda*****: When your lover shows affectionate for you, you are harsh to him, when he bows down to offer respects you remain indifferent, when he shows love, you show hatred, when he is friendly, you are averse to him. O reverser! Your sandalwood paste burns like poison, the cooling moon is like the blazing sun, your camphor ointment is like fire, and the happiness of pastimes is torture. This is suitable to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks to Rādhā who has separated from Kṛṣṇa because of a quarrel. Because you, who make everything opposite, are harsh when your lover Kṛṣṇa is affectionate, sandalwood burns like poison. This is according to the logic of “As you do to others that you experience yourself.” yathā kriyate tathā bhujyate iti nyāya.3 *Rāgini* means *anurāgini* (great love). Joy in pastimes is pain. What gave happiness in pastimes now gives you pain.

### Text 40

***nāyake yukta-vādini, yathā padyāvalyām (297)—***  
***adoṣād doṣād vā tyajati vipine tāṁ yadi bhavān***  
***abhadraṁ bhadraṁ vraja-kula-pate tvāṁ vadatu kaḥ \|***  
***idaṁ tu krūraṁ me smarati hṛdayaṁ yat kila tayā***  
***tvad-arthaṁ kāntāre kula-tilaka nātmāpi gaṇitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Use of skilful words to the hero, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O prince of Vraja, who can say whether you abandoned her because she was faultless or faulty? Who can say whether your actions are auspicious or inauspicious? O** ***tilaka*** **of your family! My cruel heart remembers that this girl entered the dangerous forest for you, without caring for herself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Bhāgavatam* describes Rādhā’s plight:

*anvicchantyo bhagavato mārgaṁ gopyo ’vidūritaḥ*  
*dadṛśuḥ priya-viśleṣān mohitāṁ duḥkhitāṁ sachem*

**While continuing to search out Kṛṣṇa’s path, the** ***gopīs*** **discovered their unhappy friend close by. She was bewildered by separation from her lover. SB 10.30.40**

Seeing that Rādhā had fainted after being given up by Kṛṣṇa, one of her *sakhīs* entered a forest to search for him. She found him very apologetic. She then scolds him with this verse. Rādhā is faultless because it is proper that the *svādhīna-bhartṛkā* shows pride as follows:

*tato gatvā vanoddeśaṁ dṛptā keśavam abravīt*  
*na pāraye ’haṁ calituṁ naya māṁ yatra te manaḥ*

**As the two lovers passed through one part of the Vṛndāvana forest, the special gopī began feeling proud of herself. She told Lord Keśava, “I cannot walk any further. Please carry me wherever you want to go.” SB 10.30.38**

O perhaps she was at fault since you, the king of great pride, could not tolerate her words. You are the son of the master *rasikas* of Vraja but you are also the controller of Vraja’s people (*vraja-kula-pate*), for you, as the evil prince, can destroy or protect it, doing what is inauspicious or auspicious. And you are responsible for killing Rādhā. I have a cruel heart. This is a statement with opposite meaning. You are the *tilaka* of the family (*kula-tilaka*). The word *kula* is repeated but this is not a fault since the last use of *kula* refers to his whole *gotra.* Though the verse indicates a *madhyā* speaking, her bold words such as “you give her up” “cruel” and “she does not consider herself” indicate a *prakharā* tendency.

### Text 41

***nāyaka-bhedyā, yathā—***  
***na vyarthāṁ kuruṣe mamaiva bhaṇitiṁ madhye sakhīnām iti***  
***śrutvā khyātim asau kṛtī madhuripur māṁ bāḍham āśiśriye \|***  
***dṛṣṭvā mad-vadanaṁ prasīda rabhasād enaṁ puraḥ kātaraṁ***  
***kalyāṇībhir alaṁ kṛśodari dṛśor bhaṅgībhir aṅgīkuru \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Subject to the hero’s solicitations: O slender-waisted Rādhā! The** ***sakhīs*** **are saying that you heed what I say. Hearing that rumor, expert Kṛṣṇa took shelter of me. Look into my face and be happy. He is in front of you, filled with despair. Quickly accept him with your auspicious glances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks to Rādhā after a separation from Kṛṣṇa because of quarrelling. Viśākhā will say when you are angry “Give up anger.” Lalitā will say when you are longing for Kṛṣṇa “Show anger.” But I never say speak to you like that. I am not like them. Therefore you should listen to me, not to them. He is clever (*kṛtī)*. Thus he took shelter of me to test my fame. Look at my face. You will destroy my fame which has been given by you. Till next birth my face remains withered and silent in front of you, for *sambhāvitasya cākīrtir maraṇād atiricyate*: dishonor is worse than death for one who has been honored. (BG 2.33) What are you telling me to do without proper reflection? He is there in despair. Then Rādhā quickly showered Kṛṣṇa, who was at her feet, with her tears. With his hand he wiped her face and kissed her.

### Text 42

***tuṅgavidyādikā cātra dakṣiṇa-prakharā bhavet \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Tuṅgavidyā and others are** ***dakṣiṇa-prakhara-laghus*** **in Rādhā’s group.**

### Text 43

***atha laghu-madhyā—***  
***tvayā racita-saṁkathāṁ pathi samīkṣya māṁ māninī***  
***sakhī mama viṣaṇṇa-dhīḥ kṛta-kaṭākṣam ākṣepyati \|***  
***vrajādhipati-nandana tvam avadhehi mantraṁ bruve***  
***vinātra lalitāśrayaṁ bhavad-upakramo’yaṁ vṛthā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***laghu-madhyā*****: If my proud friend sees me talking with you in this pathway, in disappointment she will attack me with angry glances. O prince of Vraja, listen! I will give you good advice. Without taking shelter of Lalitā, all your plans will be useless.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Campakalatā talks to Kṛṣṇa with sweet words. If from far off, one of her friends sees us speaking, she will scold me. “O Campakalatā! What secret bribe did you get from Kṛṣṇa?” O prince of Vraja, Lalitā gives respect to you--who give bliss to Vraja. Please consider in your mind (*avadhehi)* that after thinking, whatever methods you obtain from your own mind, or whatever you hear from others’ mouths, will not be successful. I will give you advice (*mantram*). This also means “This is secret. Do not mention my name in front of anyone.” *Bruve* is the *ātmanepada* form to indicate that she speaks for her own benefit, to cover her own fault in revealing the secret to him. There is a suggested meaning as in the following verse:

*tvām asmi vacmi viduṣāṁ samavāyo’tra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*ātmīyāṁ matim āsthāya sthitim atra vidhehi tat \|\|*

**I tell you that there is an assembly of learned people here. Therefore after gathering your intelligence, stay here.** ***Kāvya-prakāśa***

In the *Kāyva-prakāśa* verse the suggestion is “Since I am your friend, you must stay here.”

### Text 44

***atha laghu-mṛdvī—***  
***sakhi tava muhur mūrdhnā pāda-graho’pi mayā kṛtas***  
***tad api ca harau jātāsi tvaṁ prasāda-parāṅ-mukhī \|***  
***bhavatu yamunā-tīre veṇor udañcati pañcame***  
***vicalita-dhṛtis tvaṁ lolākṣī mayāpi hasiṣyase \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of the** ***laghu-mṛdvī*****: My friend! I repeatedly place my head at your feet. You should forgive Kṛṣṇa. Anyway, when his flute sounds on the bank of the Yamunā, you will lose you composure and your eyes will show greed for him. I will smile at you then.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

I repeatedly beg you, give up this bad intelligence! But you do not consider the scolding you have given him. Desire as you wish, since it will manifest eventually as agreement with me! If you do not become pleased with him, I will make that scolding into a welcome. I, though gentle, will give to you the result of that scolding. Not respecting us *sakhīs* who are unable to help him, she will surrender to his flute. You should not say that your determination cannot be defeated. It will become unsteady. How do I know that? Your eyes are full of greed. That greed of your eyes tells everything. You yourself will make an appointment with him and will be enjoyed by him. There is no doubt. Though the speaker is touched by the *madhyā’s* qualities because of her particular duty, she is by nature a *mṛdvī.* Thus this is an example of a *laghu-mṛdvī*

### Text 45

***atha ātyantika-laghuḥ—***  
***ātyantika-laghus tatra proktā kusumikādikā \|***  
***sarvathā mṛdur eveyaṁ yan nitānta-laghīyasī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***ātyantika-laghu*****: Kusumikā is an example of an** ***ātyantika-laghu.*** **Since this person is completely soft, she is called the** ***laghu*** **to the extreme (*****atyāntika-laghu*****).**

### Text 46

***yathā—***  
***vande sundari sandiśa priya-sakhīṁ mānaṁ vimuñcatv asau***  
***sotkaṇṭhāpi manasvinīva vasati tvac-chaṅkayā veśmani \|***  
***dūre tvan-mukham īkṣate harir iyaṁ maunaṁ śukaḥ śikṣate***  
***lāsyaṁ necchati candrakī savayasaḥ kvāsmīti na svaṁ viduḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O beautiful Lalitā! Send someone to tell Rādhā to abandon her anger. Although she longs to meet Kṛṣṇa, she puts on an air of anger, and remains at home, fearing to come out lest she meet you. Kṛṣṇa is gazing at your face from a distance. Struck with wonder, the parrot has become silent, the peacock no longer wish to dance, and our friends, wondering “Who am I?” do not remember who they are.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sundari* is an address to a chief *sakhī.* *Priya-sakhīm* refers to the head of the group.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kusumikā speaks to Lalitā. “I should go to her, fall at her feet and beg her to give up her pride.” No, remain here and send either me or another *sakhī.* Give the order not to Rādhā but to a skilful *sakhī:* “Rādhā should give up her pride. She should not have fear of me.” I would an obstacle in doing that. She will welcome your order since she puts on an appearance of anger but has great longing within.
