But without your order everyone will remain unhappy. The peacock does not dance. The *sakhīs* and *sakhas* do not know who they are. They have all fainted.

### Text 47

***prakharādiṣv anyatamā yūtheśaikaiva kīrtitā \|***  
***madhyasthā navadhaivantyā samā laghur iti dvidhā \|\|47\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***atyantikādhikā*** **leader who is either** ***prakharā, madhyā*** **or** ***mṛdvī*** **has been described. There are nine varieties of** ***āpekṣikādhikas, samās*** **and** ***āpekṣika-laghus.*** **There are two varieties of** ***atyantika-laghus: samā*** **and** ***laghu.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *ātyantikādhikā (yūtheśā)* may be *prakharā, madhyā* or *mṛdvī* (*anyatamā*). There is only one *ātyantikādhikā* in a group. There are nine types of those in the middle—*āpekṣikādhikās, samās* and *āpekṣika-ḷaghus*: *adhikā-prakharā, adhikā-madhyā* and *adhika-mṛdvī; sama-prakharā, sama-madhyā* and *sama-mṛdvī*; *āpekṣiki-laghu-prakharā, āpekṣiki-laghu-madhyā* and *āpekṣiki-laghu-mṛdvī.* The last group, the *ātyantika-laghu* has two types: *samā* and *laghu.*

### Text 48

***ekaikasminn ato yūthe bhidā dvādaśadhā bhavet \|***  
***atha dūtyārtham etāsāṁ viśeṣaḥ punar ucyate \|\|48\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Thus in one group, there are twelve types. They are distinguished by their service as messengers.**

### Text 49

***dūtyam atra tu tad-dūrād yūnor yad abhisāram \|***  
***tatra tu prathamā nitya-nāyikāvātra kīrtitā \|\|49\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Uniting the couple who are situated far apart is called** ***dūtya.*** **The head of the group is always a** ***nāyikā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The head of the group never becomes a *sakhī* since she never takes a lesser role.

### Text 50

***syur nāyikāś ca sakhyaś ca tisro madhyasthitās tataḥ \|\|50\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***āpeksīkādhikā*****, the** ***samā*** **and** ***the āpekṣika-lāghu*** **can be a** ***nāyikā*** **(enjoying with Kṛṣṇa) or a** ***sakhī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

These *nāyikās* depend on those who are lesser, and when they are *sakhīs* they depend on those who are higher.

### Text 51

***tatrādyā nāyikā-prāyā dvitīyā dvi-samā tataḥ \|***  
***tṛtīyā tu sakhī-prāyā nitya-sakhyeva pañcamī \|\|51\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***āpekṣikādhikā*** **is generally a** ***nāyikā.*** **The** ***samā*** **plays the role of the** ***nāyikā*** **or the sakhī. The** ***āpekṣika-laghu*** **is generally a** ***sakhī*****. The** ***ātyantika-laghu*** **is always a** ***sakhī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Adyā* means the *āpekṣikādhikā*. She is generally the *nāyikā,* but sometimes becomes a sakhī even for the *laghus.* The *samā (dvitīyā)* plays two roles: as *nāyikā* and as *sakhī.* The *āpekṣiki-laghu (tṛtīyā)* is generally a *sakhī*. *Ātyantika-laghu* is always a *sakhī*: she depends on the *ātyantikādhikā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among these three types (*tatra*) the *āpekṣikādhikā* is generally a *nāyikā* for those in a lesser position, since she is superior to the others, and because she would not at all be respected for taking the role of an inferior. But because of her nature of producing friendship out of love for the others she may act as a *sakhī.* Therefore the word *prāya* (generally) is used. The *samās* play the role of *nāyikā* or *sakhī* equally, since because of their intermediate nature they become *sakhīs* because of their affection for another and they become *nāyikās* because of others’ *affection.* Because of their inferior nature, the *āpekṣikī-laghus* are generally *sakhīs* for superiors, having only a little respect as a *nāyikā.* But sometimes they become *nāyikas* because of others’ affection. Thus the word *prāya* (generally) is used. The *ātyantika-laghu (pañcamī*) is always (*nitya*) a *sakhī.* No one is lower than her. Because of no respect since they cannot be a *nāyikā,* all of them are *sakhīs.* The *ātyantikādhikā* is classed as *prathamā* (first) since she should not be classed with the other three types.

### Text 52

***ādyāyāṁ nikhilāḥ sakhyo dūtya eva na nāyikāḥ \|***  
***pūrvoktā nāyikā eva pañcamyāṁ na tu dūtikāḥ \|\|52\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The lower four types serve as messengers for the** ***āytantikādhikā*** **(leader) not as her** ***nāyikā.*** **The higher four types become** ***nāyikās*** **for the** ***ātyantika-laghu*****, and they never become the messenger for the** ***ātyantika-laghu.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

For the *ātyantikādhikā,* the other four types act as messengers and never as her *nāyikā* since she is superior to all others. For the *ātyantika-laghu* the other four types are *nāyikās* and never her messengers, since she is the lowest of all. The *āpekṣikādhikas, samās* and *āpekṣika-laghus* act as *nāyikās* or messengers for each other according to their status.

### Text 53

***tatra nitya-nāyikā—***  
***yātra yūtheśvarī proktā sā bhaven nitya-nāyikā \|***  
***apekṣyatvād atīvāsyā mukhyaṁ dūtyaṁ na vidyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Where the leader of the group is mentioned, she is always the** ***nāyikā*****. Because of the great respect for her, she does not serve as a major messenger.**

### Text 54

***svayauthikya-sakhī-madhye yā yatrātīva rāgiṇī \|***  
***niyuktair asti tad dūtye suṣṭhu sā yūtha-mukhyayā \|***  
***tathāpi praṇayāṁ kvāpi kadācid gauṇam īkṣyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**She, as the head of the group, engages those within her group, who have intense attachment to her as messengers. Sometimes out of affection she becomes a minor messenger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because of being highly respected, the leader does not serve as a messenger. She says from the first day “O *sakhī*! You will serve as a messenger.” That *sakhī* then serves as a messenger at the appropriate time. It is not necessary to show this by example.

### Text 55

***dūre gatāgatam ṛte yad dūtyaṁ gauṇam atra tat \|***  
***gauṇaṁ hareḥ samakṣaṁ ca parokṣaṁ ceti tad dvidhā \|\|55\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Messenger service excluding traveling back and forth at a distance is called minor. The minor messenger service has two types: visible and invisible.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

Though messenger service is accomplished by her *sakhīs* as their ideal service, sometimes the leader also performs this service. For her, all the *sakhīs* are messengers and her *sakhīs* do not become the *nāyikā.* However seeing her *sakhīs* as equals out of affection she cannot help but perform that service. Minor messenger service will include going short distances unnoticed by others.

### Text 56

***tatra samakṣam—***  
***sāṅketikaṁ vācikaṁ ca samakṣaṁ dvividhaṁ matam \|\|56\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Visible messenger service consists of two types: gestures and speech.**

### Text 57

***tatra sāṅketikam—***  
***tatrādyaṁ syād dṛgantādyaiḥ kṛṣṇaṁ prerya sva-nihnutiḥ \|\|57\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Gestures: Gesture consists of signaling to Kṛṣṇa using the edge of the eye etc. while concealing oneself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Gesture refers to moving the edge of the eye, the brow, or the forefinger.

### Text 58

***yathā—***  
***priya-sakhi viditaṁ te karma yat prerayantī***  
***tvam aghadamanam akṣṇā kṣipram antarhitāsi \|***  
***ahaha na hi latāḥ syus tatra cet kaṇṭakinyo***  
***mama gatir abhaviṣyat tat-karāt kā na vedmi \|\|\|***  
***--idam adhika-mṛdvī-dūtyam***

**Перевод:**

**Dear friend! I know that you are glancing at Kṛṣṇa, hiding it from me. If it were not for the thorny creepers, I would not been able to get here, free from his hands.**

**This example also shows the messenger service of the** ***ātyantikādhika-mṛdvī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She speaks while hiding the truth. By this, her secret is revealed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One *sakhī* scolds her leader while hiding her enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa. The *sakhī* speaks his verse. The leader answers “Oh! Fleeing in fear and in confusion you were injured by some thorns. Come near me and lift your cloth, and show me. Out of my ignorance you have fallen into difficulty. What should I do? He has done that to you by making a request to you out of great lust. You have been protected by your pious acts. Do not be angry. I will not do this again.”

### Text 59

***atha vācikam—***  
***mithaḥ puro vā paścād vā vākyam ekatra vācikam \|\|59\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Speech: The message of a leader may be spoken in front of Kṛṣṇa and a** ***sakhī*** **or while one of them is behind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mithaḥ puraḥ* mean while the *sakhī* and Kṛṣṇa both hear. Sometimes the messenger speaks to a *sakhī,* while Kṛṣṇa can be seen. Both are called verbal messages.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The verbal message is in front of two of them or behind in the same place. This means the messenger speaks in front of Kṛṣṇa and the *sakhī*. *Mithaḥ* suitably indicates Kṛṣṇa and the leader of the group. Because of the word *ekatra* (in one place) the message may be spoken behind Kṛṣṇa, to the *sakhī*, or spoken behind the *sakhī*, to Kṛṣṇa. Thus there are actually three types.

### Text 60

***tatra mithaḥ puraḥ kṛṣṇe vācikam—***  
***mayāpalapanaṁ kiyat tvayi kariṣyate yā sakhī***  
***mamāniśam upendra te kusuma-mañjarīr luñcati \|***  
***iyaṁ guṇavatī kare tava vidhṛtya dattādya sā***  
***yathecchasi tathā kuru svayam ito gṛhaṁ gamyate \|\|\|***  
***--idam adhika-prakharā-dūtyam***

**Перевод:**

**A messenger speaks to Kṛṣṇa in front of both: How can I tell a lie to you? My friend constantly picks your flower blossoms. This girl is full of good qualities. I give her to you. Take her hand. Do whatever you like with her. I am going home.**

***An ātyantikādhika-prakharā*** **speaks as a messenger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What is done is done. It is impossible to do later.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa says “O Śyāmalā! When you are asked you always say ‘I did not steal the flowers.’ Please stay. One day in the garden, concealing myself I will remain there. Grabbing your friend, I will put her in Cupid’s prison. Then you will know.” Śyāmalā then speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Apalapanam* means a lie. *Guṇavatī* means “She has qualities of a thief which will now bear results.” What can I do? This is a reason for not helping her. *Guṇavatī* can also be the name of the *sakhī.*

### Text 61

***kṛṣṇasya paścāt sakhyaṁ, yathā—***  
***mat-kaṇṭhād iha mauktikāni vicinu tvaṁ vīrudārodhataḥ***  
***srastāny eṣa kilāsti mālya-racanā vyāsakta-citto hariḥ \|***  
***diṣṭyā kṣemam upasthitaṁ sumukhi naḥ sānau yad asya cyuto***  
***hastād veṇur iti prayāmi kapaṭān nihnotum enaṁ girau \|\|\|***  
***--idam adhika-madhyā-dūtyam***

**Перевод:**

**Leader giving a message behind Kṛṣṇa to a** ***sakhī:*** **The creepers rubbing against my neck have broken my necklace. Please pick up the scattered pearls while Kṛṣṇa is busy making a garland. O friend with a beautiful face! Good fortune has now appeared to us. Kṛṣṇa has accidentally dropped the flute from his hand on the peak of Govardhana Hill. To fool him, I shall go and hide it on the hill.**

**An** ***ātyantikādhika-madhyā*** **speaks.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The flute has fallen from his hand. Good fortune has arrived. Therefore I will go. *Upātagatam* is also seen instead of *upasthitam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Citrā. “I am afraid of Kṛṣṇa.” Do not worry. He is busy making a garland. This shows that Kṛṣṇa is not in front of them. The sakhī says “But you also did not pick up any of the pearls.” I have found his flute instead.

### Text 62

***sakhyāḥ paścāt kṛṣṇe, yathā—***  
***vicakilam avacetuṁ sā sakhī mad-vacobhiḥ***  
***katham api taṭa-puṣpāraṇyam ekā gatāsti \|***  
***aghahara mama gehād yāntam abhyarthaye tvāṁ***  
***punar iyam atimugdhā na tvayā khedanīyā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Message given to Kṛṣṇa, with a** ***sakhī*** **behind: According to my request, my friend has gone alone to the flower garden to the bank of the Yamunā to pick jasmine flowers. O Kṛṣṇa! I implore you as you leave my cottage, please do not torment my innocent young friend Citrā again.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vicakilam* is a jasmine flower

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa says “Rādhā! Today all your *sakhīs* have extraordinary beauty. I do not see Citrā. Where is she?” Rādhā speaks this verse. *Vicakilam* is jasmine. I had to speak a lot to her (*vacobhiḥ*). She almost did not agree to go, since she fears you. However, I sent her on a mission. No one accompanied her. O killer of Agha (sorrow)! You should extinguish her fire created by the arrow of Cupid. *Amara-koṣa* says that *agha* means sin, suffering and pain. After enjoying her, do not give her up again.

### Text 63

***atha hareḥ parokṣam—***  
***tat parokṣaṁ hareḥ sakhyāḥ sakhī-dvārā yad arpaṇam \|***  
***vyapadeśādinā vāpi tat-pārśve preṣaṇādikam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Parokṣa*** **message means offering a** ***sakhī*** **to him through another** ***sakhī*****, or sending a message by other means such as** ***vyapadeśa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When a *sakhī* offers a *sakhī* to Kṛṣṇa (*hareḥ*) it is called *parokṣa-dūtyam.*

### Text 64

*tatra sakhī-dvārā, yathā—*  
***ruddhāṁ viddhi guror girā śaśikalām ātma-dvitīyām atas***  
***tvām udyamya nayāmi śarmaṇi sadā jāgarti te rādhikā \|***  
***bhṛṅgāḥ subhru tad-aṅga-saurabha-bharair ākṛṣyamāṇāḥ kramāt***  
***panthānaṁ prathayanti te kuru puraḥ kuñja-praveśe tvarām \|\|64\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Offering a** ***sakhī*** **by a** ***sakhī:*** **Śaśikalā, who is like a second self to you, has been locked at home by the order of her elders. Therefore with effort I am taking you for the appointment. Rādhā is always alert to your welfare. These bumble-bees, attracted by the sweet fragrance of Kṛṣṇa's body, are revealing the path to go to him. Quickly enter the bower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

You said that we will see the moon in the forest. Thus you lead me far off. Then you said “After seeing the moon, go on the path to the bower without the moon. Go further.” Where have you led me? Raṅgadevī speaks in this way with fear. Kalāvatī speaks to her this verse. Śaśikalā is your second self, your friend, who always helps you keep your appointments. I am taking you to the appointment. “You have destroyed my faith. I follow your order but why did you take me? I will turn and go home. “Rādhā thinks of your welfare.” The statement has the opposite meaning. She is alert for your misfortune, for fooling you. She never sleeps. She is the destroyer of your faith. She is your enemy. I will follow your order. “Very well, I will do as you wish. But why have you made me associate with her? You want to get lost. Let’s go ahead further.” When Raṅgadevī speaks like this, Kalavatī then says “The bees are attracted to his scent. The bees will be your associates now. Follow behind them. O woman with beautiful brows! Make your brows auspicious.” This means, “Good fortune is coming to you.” Hearing them talk, and understanding that Raṅgadevī, a *nāyikā,* was there, Kṛṣṇa left the bower, accepted Raṅgadevī, and made Kālavatī joyful This illustrates the previous statement “Among the *sakhīs* of the group, she who has great attachment is engaged as a messenger by the leader.” Śaśikalā was prevented from doing this service.

### Text 65

***atha vyapadeśaḥ—***  
***vyapadeśo harau lekhopāyanādy-arpaṇa-kriyā \|***  
***nija-prayojanāścarya-darśanādiś ca kīrtitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vyapadeśa*** **means using the pretext of giving Kṛṣṇa letters, gifts, other purposes of the leader or seeing something astonishing.**

### Text 66

***tatra lekhya-vyapadeśena, yathā—***  
***dūtī-paddhatim uddhate parihara tvaṁ sāci kiṁ prekṣase***  
***vāmākṣi svayam āhṛtaṁ priya-sakhī-lekhaṁ puro vācaya \|***  
***śayyā puṣpamayī nikuñja-bhavane saurabhya-puñjāvṛtā***  
***mṛdvī tvām iyam āhvayaty ali-ghaṭā kolāhala-vyājataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Arranging** ***sakhīs*** **to meet Kṛṣṇa by having them deliver written messages: O violent girl! Give up this letter-carrying. O crooked eyes! Why do you look at me with that crooked glance? Read that letter written by Rādhā. In this hut in the grove there is a soft, fragrant couch made of flowers. This flower bed is calling you to lie down upon it through the loudly buzzing bees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rasāla-mañjarī says “I am Rādhā’s letter carrier. Why are you looking at me with lust? The messengers offer their lives, not their bodies. You know the nature of the messenger.” Kṛṣṇa replies with this verse. Give up this business of carrying letters. O violent woman! What irrelevant words are you speaking? You are not a messenger. If you do not give the letter, then read aloud the letter written by Rādhā (*svayam āhṛtam*). I have not done anything devious. “Coming to you, Rasāla-mañjarī will reveal the whole letter. Today O Kṛṣṇa, lover of the forest, do not violate my *dharma.”*

When you mention your friend Rasāla-mañjarī (mango bud) and that I am a lover of the forest, there is another meaning. That you should consider. *Dharma* can also be taken *adharma* by *sandhi* rules. Thus your statement is unclear. But *dharma* is the quality of her messengers and therefore all her followers have *prema* for me. The meaning is true. Then having defeated her, he took her hand and led her to the bed.

### Text 67

***upāyana-vyapadeśena, yathā—***  
***prasīda vasanāñcalaṁ mama vimuñca nirmañchanaṁ***  
***vrajāmi nanu nirdaya sphurati paśya sandhyorjitā \|***  
***vidaty api tavonnataṁ guṇam upāharaṁ manda-dhīḥ***  
***srajaṁ priya-sakhī-girā vrajapate na te dūṣaṇam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By sending gifts: Merciless boy, be kind to me. Let go of my cloth. Look! The frightening twilight has appeared. I have to go to evening** ***arati*** **now. It is not your fault. O master of Vraja! Knowing your violent nature, I have foolishly come to give you a gift of a garland on my leader’s orders.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sandhyorjitā* means the challenge of the twilight. Instead of *vrajapate* sometimes *calamate* (fickle minded) is seen. However in conjunction with the statement “you are not at fault” *calamate* could also mean *acalamate* (without a fickle mind) after *hā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rati-mañjarī speaks to Kṛṣṇa when he grabs her cloth. O merciless one! I have a sick body now. The evening has reached its middle portion (*sandhyorjitā*). In the twilight the associates of Śiva wander about and can see you attack women. But you do not fear them. The word *ūrjita* also implies *oja* which indicates “terrible.” He does not leave her. It is my fault however. Knowing your elevated quality, I brought the garland. She means the opposite however. He has degraded qualities. I am foolish. I cannot understand the meaning of words of my dear friend. O lord of Vraja! She should actually say “O son of the lord of Vraja! However because of her fear and confusion these words come from her mouth.

### Text 68

***nija-prayojana-vyapadeśena, yathā—***  
***muktāvalī niśi mayā dayitā kadamba-***  
***vāṭī-kuṭīra-kuhare sakhi vismṛtāsti \|***  
***tām āhareti vṛṣabhānujayā niyuktā***  
***tāṁ projjhya kiṁ śaśikale gṛham āgatāsi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**On the pretext of another task: “Last night I absent-mindedly left my favorite pearl-necklace in the cottage in the grove of** ***kadamba*** **trees. My friend, please go and fetch it for me.” Engaged in this way, O Śaśikalā, why have you come home empty-handed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Śaśikalā in a joking mood. Śaśikalā would reply, “Just as you have engaged me in getting the necklace, now you ask me what happened to the necklace. All respects to the youthful couple!”

### Text 69

***āścarya-darśana-vyapadeśena, yathā—***  
***sakhi vyālīṁ vaktre dyumaṇi-paṭalaṁ kaṇṭha-savidhe***  
***dadhac-candrān mūrdhopari sakala-ratnāni vamati \|***  
***ali-śyāmo haṁsaḥ sphuṭam iti mad-uktāsi calitā***  
***tad āścaryaṁ draṣṭuṁ kim iva kupitevātra milasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**On the pretext of seeing something astonishing: O friend! I saw a swan as black as a bee. On his face was a snake, and on his neck were many suns. On his head were many moons. He was vomiting many jewels. My words have made you go there to see this wonder. Why have you returned in an angry mood?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Explaining the mission she has sent Śyāmalā on when the *sakhīs* eagerly come and sit down, Rādhā jokes with Śyāmalā.  *Vyālīm* is a female snake. It means by *atiśayokti* the flute, since the flute poisons the women like a snake bites a person. “Many suns” means the Kaustubha. “Many moons” means peacock feathers. “Many jewels” means many attractive words. The phrase “I saw this today” should be supplied. Because of acting as if confused because of astonishment, she omits this phrase. The word *iva* indicates that the friend has actually become blissful by associating with Kṛṣṇa. It will be said:

*āsāṁ madhye bhavet kācin nāyikātve darāgrahā \|*  
*tasminn anāgrahā kācit sakhya-saukhyābhilāṣiṇī \|\|*

**Among the** ***āpekṣika-laghus,*** **some have a slight desire to be a** ***nāyikā.*** **Others do not desire this, and instead simply desire the happiness of being a** ***sakhī. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **8.84**

Having gone and seen the swan, I saw him falling in the dust and rising after fainting, calling out for Rādhā. When asked he explained to me his devastated condition. “When Rādhā sprinkled lotus pollen on me I became insane. If she revives me, then I will live.” Therefore I am angry at you. Why do you delay after doing that to him? Please go and bring him back to life!

### Text 70

***atha nāyikā-prāyātrikam—***  
***āpekṣikādhikānāṁ yat tisṝṇāṁ laghuṣu sphuṭam \|***  
***kadācid eva dūtyaṁ tā nāyikā-prāyikās tataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The three types** ***of āpekṣikādhikās*** **who sometimes serve as messengers for** ***laghus*** **are called** ***nāyikā-prāyikās. The ātyantādhika*** **acting as a secondary messenger was just described. 4**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If the *āpekṣikādhikās* engage as arrangers for *laghus* then the *nāyikās* of three types are called *nāyikā-prāyikaṣ.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The verb *kathyante* (are called) should be added.

### Text 71

***tatra adhika-prakharā-dūtyam—***  
***pāṇau me patitāsi śambhali cirād atyākulaṁ mā kṛthāḥ***  
***kākuṁ te karavāṇi niṣkrayam ahaṁ śīrṇābhisāraiḥ sadā \|***  
***tvaṁ diṣṭyātra nikuñja-sīmani samānītā kim u stambhase***  
***muktās tvat-kuca-kumbhagāḥ kṣapatu śyāmaḥ sa siṁhī-patiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***adhika-prakharā*** **as an arranger: O Śambhalī! Now you have fallen into my hands. Please do not be so disturbed. I will reward you for making all the appointments. You are exhausted from the work. Coming to the edge of the grove, why are you now stunned? The dark-complexioned lion will now tear away the pearl-decorated bodice covering your breasts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śambhalī is a messenger. Do not lament (*kākum*) in a confused state (*ākulam*). Let me give you some compensation for your difficult work in arranging meetings (*abhisāraiḥ*). Instead of *samānīta* sometimes *mayā nītā* is seen. He is like a lion (*siṁhi-patiḥ*). However the meaning can be “he is a husband who is like a female lion.” This indicates the speaker’s *prakharā* nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to a *laghu sakhī* in her group. O Śambhalī! Do not lament in a confused state. I will reward you in plenty for undertaking difficult work on my behalf. You are withered because of arranging the meetings. Why are you stunned? According the logic of “Enjoy what is given” I am giving you the reward now. I am showing you such mercy. Let him tear the pearls off and scatter them around. He is arrogant like a lion. Instead of saying *siṁha* she says *siṁhi-patiḥ* (husband of a lioness). She thus indicates the *laghu’s* very young age, and that Kṛṣṇa will make her especially suffer in his amorous actions. Or, you are like a female elephant but today you will become like a lioness. Or, because he is so lusty for women, like a lion with many lionesses, he will enjoy you, even if you are an elephant. All of this indicates arrangements for her to enjoy amorous pastimes with Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 72

***tatra adhika-madhyā-dūtyam—***  
***vyathayasi sadā māṁ vāg-bhaṅgyā śanair anuśiṣya yaṁ***  
***chalayasi ca māṁ bhrū-nartakyā vinudya yam uddhate \|***  
***ayam iha vaśīkṛtya svairī mayāpy upalambhitas***  
***tvayi vitanutāṁ kṛṣṇaḥ padmī sa padmini vibhramam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***adhika-madhyā*** **as an arranger: By giving the black elephant instructions to meet me with your clever words, you have given me pain. By moving your eyebrows to drive him away, you have cheated me. O proud woman! Controlling him, though he is independent, I have made him yours. O she elephant! Display your coquetry now.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Anuśiṣya* means “giving instruction.” *Upalambhitaḥ* means “has been attained.” With a pretense of fearlessness you cheat me and then give me pain through him. This is the order of the words. *Padmī* means best of elephant. O female elephant (*padmini*)!

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā bring her *laghu-sakhī* to Kṛṣṇa on some pretext speaks. Giving him instructions by your clever words to meet with me, you give me pain, or you make me suffer from wounds on the lip and breast because of Kṛṣṇa. You should pick flowers there and Kṛṣṇa will not come there. Or if he comes, then I will protect you. This is a truthful oath I make. Having faith in me, drive him away by moving your brows. “O Kṛṣṇa! Touch her limbs without fear. I am your assistant.” Your brows give him instructions in this way and thus you cheat me. Kṛṣṇa, controlled by me, is obtained by you. I should repay you with this gift for all the wicked assistance you have given me. But he is independent. He does not want you. He wants me. This indicates the *laghu* nature of the *sakhī* being addressed. The cause of his independent choice however is her eyebrow but she conceals her own *saubhāgya. Padmī* means an elephant. *Vibhramam* means amorous gestures. The word *padmini* taken as *kamalini,* indicates a woman who is fond of amorous affairs.

### Text 73

***tatra adhika-mṛdvī-dūtyam—***  
***anudinam abhisāraṁ kāritāsmi tvayāhaṁ***  
***kusumita-ravi-kanyā-tīra-vanyā-kuṭīṣu \|***  
***sakṛd aham akṛtajñā tvāṁ puraḥ kuñja-madhye***  
***yad iyam upanaye kā niṣkṛtis te tato’bhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***adhika-mṛdvī*** **making arrangements for the** ***laghu:*** **Every day you arrange for me to meet Kṛṣṇa at the cottages in the flower-filled groves on the bank of the Yamunā. I am very ungrateful. If I bring you into this bower just once, I can repay the debt.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Te* means “your*.” Niṣkṛitḥ* means repayment. There is another version:

*anudinam abhisāraṁ kāritāhaṁ tvayā yā*  
*harim anu ravi-kanyā-tīra-vanyā-kuṭīṣu \|*  
*sakṛd iyam akṛtajñāṁ tvāṁ tadīyaṁ samīpaṁ*  
*samanayam kāsmin niṣkṛtis te mamāsti \|\|*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bringing from the house on the pretext of picking flowers, you say “Now enter the bower.” In this way make arrangements for me to meet Kṛṣṇa. Oh! I am your servant. Is it proper that you make arrangements for me? Citrā then speaks to this humble *sakhī.* *Niṣkṛtiḥ* means repayment.

### Text 74

***atha dvi-samā-trikam—***  
***samānāṁ prakharā-madhyā-mṛdvīnāṁ tu parasparam \|***  
***dūtyaṁ ca nāyikātvaṁ ca samaṁ tā dvisamās tataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***samās*** **of three types—*****prakharā, madhyā*** **and** ***mṛdvī*****—who act as messengers and as** ***nāyikās*****,--are called** ***dvisamās,*** **equally performing both roles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because they take the role of messenger and *nāyikā* equally they are called *dvisamās.*

### Text 75

***tatra sama-prakharā-dūtyam—***  
***prāg ekāntaram eva niścitam abhūd anyonya-dūtyaṁ hi nau***  
***vāras tatra tavāyam astu karavai dūtyaṁ tathāpy adya te \|***  
***bhrū-bhaṅgaṁ sakhi muñca maṇḍaya tanuṁ yad yācate mām asau***  
***savyā te sphuratī dṛg adya mṛgaye goṣṭhāṅgane mādhavam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sama-prakharā*** **acting as arranger: In the past we have always acted as each other's messenger. Here is the opportunity. Today I will become your messenger. O my friend! Decorate your body and set your eyebrows dancing. Because the twitching of your left eye is begging me to do this, I will go to the cow pens and find Mādhava.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

They take turns acting as messengers. *Vāraḥ* means opportunity. Therefore I am going to Mādhava near the cow shed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Samā sakhīs* under one leader are always engaged by the leader in serving each other as messengers. In this verse two *sama-prakharās* speak to each other. *Ekadināntaram* means every other day. The meaning is understood even without adding the word *dina* (day) as in the expression *ekāntropavāsa* (every other day of fasting). Or it can mean “each service as messenger being separated *(ekāntaram*). Though today is my turn for meeting Kṛṣṇa, let it be yours. Her father’s house had suddenly sent to him ingredients such as scents, cloth, ornaments, and foods suitable for his enjoyment. He developed a desire to meet with her because of this. This was understood by the second *sakhī*. Since your left eyebrow request this, I am going to find him.

### Text 76

***atha sama-madhyā-dūtyam—***  
***tvaṁ nyastāsi muradviṣaḥ śaśikale pāṇau mayā gamyate***  
***dūtī hanta tavāham eva kamale kiṁ dhiṅ mṛṣā jalpasi \|***  
***ity anyonya-vikṣepaṇa-praṇayitā-mādhurya-mugdho harir***  
***dorbhyāṁ te hṛdaye nidhāya yugapat paśyonmadaḥ khelati \|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sama-madhyā*** **as an arranger: “O Śaśikalā! You have fallen into the hands of Kṛṣṇa. I am leaving.” “O Kamalā! Why do you speak these lies! I am your messenger.” Kṛṣṇa has become charmed by the sweet love exchanged between these two** ***sakhīs.*** **Look! He embraces them both to his chest, and passionately enjoys amorous pastimes with them both.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

I am your messenger and you are not my messenger.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a conversation between Kamalā and Śaśikalā, two sakhīs of Raṅgadevī. Rūpa-mañjarī reveals this conversation to Rati-mañjarī and then says “See! He is embracing them both!”

### Text 77

***yathā vā—***  
***kva mālatikayārpitā calasi mādhavi tvaṁ mama***  
***kva mādhavikayārpitā tvam api yāsy alaṁ mālati \|***  
***asambhava-sahodgame rahasi kṛṣṇa-bhṛṅgo yuvā***  
***yuvām iha dhayann ayaṁ vahatu kañcid ānandathum \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Mādhavī! You belong to me, after being offered by Mālatī to me. Where are you going? O Mālatī! Having been offered by Mādhavī to me, where are you going? The dark-complexioned young bumble-bee shall now take you both, approaching at the same time, to a secluded place, while drinking the honey of your kisses, to enjoy amorous pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Mama* means “to me.” According to the poets the *mālatī* flower blooms in the autumn and the *mādhavī* flowers in the spring. Thus they are never seen together. That is the meaning of *asambhava-sahodgame* (impossibly blooming together).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having given an example of two *samā sakhīs* speaking sweetly, now the author gives a statement of Kṛṣṇa about this. Kṛṣṇa speaks to two *sakhīs* of Viśākhā engaged as messengers for each other. O Mādhavī! Where are you going, since you belong to me *(mama*)? “But why do I belong to you?” Mālatī has given you. She said, “O Kṛṣṇa! I give this *sakhī* Mādhavī to you.” Then he speaks to Mālatī in the same way. He will drink (*dhayan*) you two, who have come to him impossibly at the same time (*asambhavasahodgame).* Two *nāyikās* approach the hero in a secluded place at the same time. In terms of flowers the *mādhavī* and *mālatī* bloom in the spring and autumn respectively and the bee cannot drink their nectar at the same time. This is according to the poets’ view. However in the common view, the bee takes both flowers in the spring.

### Text 78

***atīvābheda-madhuraṁ sauhṛdaṁ sama-madhyayoḥ \|***  
***viralaṁ śakyate jñātuṁ kintu prema-viśeṣibhiḥ \|\|78\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**One those who are expert in** ***prema*** **can understand the rare, extremely pure sweetness of friendship between** ***sama-madhyās.***

### Text 79

***atha sama-mṛdvī-dūtyam—***  
***drutam anusaran mandārākṣīṁ mukunda nivartaya***  
***vrajati nibhṛtaṁ yā kuñjāntaḥ-kuṭīm upanīya mām \|***  
***iti tava sakhī-vākyena tvām ahaṁ sukham āhvaye***  
***sphurati hi muhur madhye tiṣṭhan vidhuḥ sama-tārayoḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sama-mṛdvīs*** **acting as arrangers: On Rādhā’s order I am happily calling you. She said, “O Mukunda! After bringing me to the bower, Mandārākṣī is quietly leaving. Follow her and quickly bring her back.” Kṛṣṇa then shone like a moon between two stars.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Mandārākṣi, a *sakhī* of Rādhā. Quickly follow her and bring her back. Out of affection I am acting as her messenger, but cannot bring her myself. She brought me to the cottage. She did her job well. By Rādhā’s words I am calling you. She who engaged you as a messenger now is acting as a messenger for you out of affection. It is not my fault. “But the hero avoids two women at once in the same room.” This is the opinion of some. However I will attain an extraordinary beauty lying between these two young women on the same bed.

### Text 80

***atha sakhī-prāyātrikam—***  
***laghūnāṁ prakharā-madhyā-mṛdvīnāṁ prāyaśaḥ sadā \|***  
***dūtyaṁ bhavati tenemāḥ sakhī-prāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The three types of** ***āpekṣika-laghus*****—*****prakharā, madhyā and mṛdvī*****—usually act as messengers and are therefore called** ***sakhī-prāyās*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here the *laghu* means the *āpekṣika-laghu.* Generally they are messengers, but sometimes the *ātyantikādhikā* or the *āpekṣikādhikā* will act as their messengers and make them *nāyikās* as described previously

### Text 81

***tatra laghu-prakharā-dūtyaṁ, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (11.22)—***  
***tvāṁ cittena ciraṁ vahann ayam atiśrānto bhṛśaṁ tāpitaḥ***  
***kandarpeṇa ca pātum icchati sudhā-sambādha-bimbādharam \|***  
***asyāṅkaṁ tad alaṅkuru kṣaṇam iha bhrū-kṣepa-lakṣmī-lava-***  
***krīte dāsa ivopasevita-padāmbhoje kutaḥ sambhramaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Laghu-prakharā*** **as an arranger: Exhausted by continually carrying you in his heart, he therefore desires to drink from the nectar-filled** ***bimba*** **fruits of your lips. He is afflicted by the arrows of Cupid. Decorate his lap for a moment. What is the problem for you? A drop of the treasure of your moving eyebrows has purchased him, and he serves your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks to Rādhā. Exhausted because of carrying you in his heart, he desires to drink your nectar saturated lips. Give him some food for his exhaustion. “No, he is afflicted by the five poisonous arrows of Cupid.” Tired and afflicted he still carries you. See the determination of his *prema*. “What is the cause of his being afflicted by Cupid?” He has carried you in his heart for a long time. Cupid’s intention is as follows. “The heart is my birth place. How can you carry her there? If you desire your own good, then give her up or carry her on your chest.” He has become stubborn in carrying you in my heart and thinks “Better that I give up my life than stop carrying you.” Showing compassion, as your friend, I pray, “Sit on his lap.” May he carry you on his chest! Then Cupid will be merciful and stop the burning affliction.

Uttering harsh words like “Go Mādhava, go Keśava!” and ant then uttering a hundred sweet words I cannot find in you any mercy. I have become agitated by shame and fear. By a small particle of the treasure of the movement of your eye brows he sells himself. You have given the complete wealth of eyebrow movements. Therefore he has become useless, being a debtor and paying the price. This is indicated by the word *iva.* What can be said of your generosity? The state of debt does not give him qualification to exist as a slave. He can only serve the lotuses of your feet, given by you. That means he san only smell them. At least extend your feet so he can hold them with his hands and smell them. May he ornament his locks with the red lac from you feet! This is the esoteric hint. Then let him taste your lips, embrace you and enjoy with you. These are the three requests that Tuṅgavidyā makes.

### Text 82

***atha laghu-madhyā-dūtyam—***  
***kim iti kuṭilita-bhrūś caṇḍi vṛttādya sadyas***  
***tvam iha kusuma-hetoḥ sauhṛdād āhṛtāsi \|***  
***vraja-nara-pati-putraṁ santam antar nilīya***  
***priya-sakhi taṭa-kuñje hanta jāne kathaṁ vā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Laghu-madhya*** **acting as arranger: My angry friend! Out of friendship, I brought you here for picking flowers. Why are you suddenly arching your eyebrows in anger? How did I know that Kṛṣṇa was hiding in the bower on the bank of the river?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. This proves the saying that “One who does not give a donation considers the requestor to be a *non-brāhmaṇa*.” You are simply criticizing me after I have done you favors. The other suggestions in the verse are clear.

### Text 83

***atha laghu-mṛdvī-dūtyam—***  
***kuñja-geham avagāhya mādhavaṁ***  
***suptam atra sicayena vījaya \|***  
***phullam indu-kiraṇaiḥ kumudvatī-***  
***koraka-prakaram āharāmy aham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Laghu-mṛdvī*** **as an arranger: Mādhava has entered the bower. Fan him with the edge of your cloth as he sleeps, and I shall bring bunches of lotus flowers which have blossomed in the moonlight.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śaibyā speaks to Candrāvalī.

### Text 84

***āsāṁ madhye bhavet kācin nāyikātve darāgrahā \|***  
***tasminn anāgrahā kācit sakhya-saukhyābhilāṣiṇī \|\|84\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Among the** ***āpekṣika-laghus*****, some have a slight desire to be a** ***nāyikā.*** **Others do not desire this, and instead simply desire the happiness of being a** ***sakhī.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among the three types of *āpekṣika-laghus* some have a slight insistence to be a *nāyikā.* But this is always with the compliance of the group leader. Eagerness has two types: to fulfill the desires of the lover and to express affection for one’s *sakhīs*. There are two types of *sakhīs*: those whose limbs are greatly desired by Kṛṣṇa and those whose limbs are not greatly desired by Kṛṣṇa. First type has eagerness to fulfill the desires of Kṛṣṇa and the second type has eagerness to express affection for her *sakhīs.* “We will engage ourselves in this way because it is impossible for a young girl to completely satisfy Kṛṣṇa’s desires for love. We will assist her.” In this way the first type acts as *nāyikās* with a slight eagerness. Knowing that Kṛṣṇa has less greed for them and thinking they cannot help Kṛṣṇa by the above method, the second type of *sakhī* arranges by her efforts for their leader and her *sakhīs*, who have great *saubhāgya* to meet with Kṛṣṇa. They desire to please the leader. They do not desire to be *nāyikās.*

### Text 85

***tatra ādyā, yathā—***  
***lekhām āhara nīpa-kuñja-kuharāt tvaṁ candrakāṇāṁ mayā***  
***nyastānām iti mad-girā sarabhasaṁ smerā svayaṁ prasthitā \|***  
***tām unmucya mad-īritāṁ śaśikale kiṁ candralekhā-śataṁ***  
***celenāvṛtam anyad eva dadhatī labdhāsi namrā gṛham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Eagerness to be a** ***nāyikā:*** **I said “Please bring me a bunch of peacock feathers from within this grove of** ***kadamba*** **trees.” Śaśikalā! Quickly you departed with smile. Not bringing one bunch as I directed, why do you cover a hundred bunches with your cloth and go to the cottage with a bowed head?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Letting Lalitā and others hear, Rādhā speaks to Śaśikalā. *Lekhām* is a bunch. Since Śāśikalā leaves in haste with smile, she is eager to be a *nāyikā.* I told you to bring one bunch of feathers but you have brought a hundred bunches. Why are you embarrassed? These are words of a *pragalbhā.*

### Text 86

***dvitīyā, yathā—***  
***māṁ puṣpāṇām avacayam iyād vṛndaśo mā prahaiṣīr***  
***vṛndāraṇye param iha bhavad-duḥkha-bhītyā prayāmi \|***  
***satyaṁ satyaṁ sumukhi sakhitā-saukhyatas te mama syān***  
***na svādīyān agha-vijayinaḥ keli-śayyādhirohaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Do not repeatedly send me to pick flowers in Vṛndāvana forest. I go there only because of fear of making you suffer. O beautiful-faced friend, I tell you the truth. Your happiness is my happiness. I have no desire to mount Kṛṣṇa’s bed of pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vṛndaśaḥ* means again and again.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* who cannot tolerate her leader acting as a go-between for her speaks to her leader. *Vrndaśaḥ* means many times.

### Text 87

***atha nitya-sakhī—***  
***sakhyenaiva sadā prītā nāyikātvānapekṣiṇī \|***  
***bhaven nitya-sakhī sā tu dvidhaikātyantikī laghuḥ \|***  
***āpekṣika-laghūnāṁ ca madhye’nyā kācid īritā \|\|87\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Those who are not interested in being a** ***nāyikā*** **and who have attachment to being a** ***sakhī*** **are called** ***nitya-sakhīs.*** **There are** ***ātyantika-laghus*** **of two types:** ***sama*** **and** ***laghu*****. Among the** ***āpekṣika-laghus*** **also some are** ***nitya-sakhīs.*** **These were previously described.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some were previously described (*īritā)* in verse 84. These are also *nitya-sakhīs.*

### Text 88

***yathā—***  
***tvayā yad upabhujyate murajid-aṅga-saṅge sukhaṁ***  
***tad eva bahu jānatī svayam avāptitaḥ śuddha-dhīḥ \|***  
***mayā kṛta-vilobhanāpy adhika-cāturī-caryayā***  
***kadāpi maṇi-mañjarī na kurute’bhisāra-spṛhām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Maṇi-mañjarī attains much greater happiness from your association with Kṛṣṇa than from attaining Kṛṣṇa for herself. She is very pure. Though I allured her with clever arguments, Maṇi-mañjarī has no desire at any time for a conjugal meeting with Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though one *sakhī* engaged by Rādhā to arrange a meeting of Maṇi-mañjarī with Kṛṣṇa, she was unable to make her meet him, even though she used logically arguments. The *sakhī* returned to Rādhā and reported what happened. She derives greater happiness from Rādhā meeting Kṛṣṇa that from herself meeting Kṛṣṇa. I have allured her saying, “There is no greater happiness than associating directly with Kṛṣṇa. Just one time you should do this. Lalitā and others play roles as both *nāyikā* and *sakhī* at various times. You should be like that. Why do you always desire to be a *laghu*?” With this clever logic she tried to convince her.

### Text 89

***yathā vā—***  
***rādhā-raṅga-lasat-tvad-ujjvala-kalā-sañcāraṇa-prakriyā***  
***cāturyottaram eva sevanam ahaṁ govinda samprārthaye \|***  
***yenāśeṣa-vadhū-janodbhaṭa-mano-rājya-prapañcāvadhau***  
***nautsukyaṁ bhavad-aṅga-saṅgama-rase’py ālambate man-manaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Govinda! I request that you please engage me in excellent service where you expertly stimulate the spread of dazzling conjugal arts on the dancing stage of Rādhā. This service is the topmost treasure in the exalted kingdom of all the** ***gopis'*** **hearts. My heart has no desire for your intimate association since by this service countless women reach the limit of their desires.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The second type (*samā*) is illustrated. The *ātyantikī-laghu-sakhīs* as *laghu* and *sama* are not defined in the text anywhere. This is also the case of the *ātyantikī-laghu* group leader who is *laghu* or *sama* in Chapter 6. It probably means that the sakhīs with lowest *saubhāgya* interact as the lowest (*laghu*) in comparison to all others or as equal to others (*sama)* who are also in the lowest catetory. 5 Kṛṣṇa says, “Come and lie with me in the bower. Your birth will be successful.” A *sakhī* who came to pick flowers for making a garland, not showing skill at v*āmya* qualities characteristic of women, spoke frankly to him, convincing him of her feelings as follows. “I pray for the principal service in which you show skill in instigating the spread of beauty of glowing conjugal love in the arena where Rādhā performs the dance of love. By that service, in reaching the limit of satisfying the excellent desires of countless women, my mind does not derive happiness from intimately associating with you. I derive greater bliss in my mind by seeing your association with Rādhā through the lattice holes than from personally association with you. Having attained greater happiness, a person is not attracted to lesser happiness.” Being advised by Rādhā he then said “But you should not think of your happiness. Think of my happiness.” The young girl then enjoyed with Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 90

***tatra tad-dūtyaṁ, yathā—***  
***antaḥ praviśati na sakhī***  
***kupyati me kuñja-dehalī-līnā \|***  
***tad imāṁ bhaṅgurita-bhruvam***  
***anunaya vṛndāṭavī-candra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Their service as arrangers: My** ***sakhī*** **does not enter within. She stands on the threshold of the bower, anger at me. O moon of Vṛndāvana! Please bring this girl knitting her eyebrows within!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The service of the two types of *laghus* is mentioned together as one, and illustrated in one verse. By the description, the *sakhī* brought to Kṛṣṇa is a *mṛdvī-laghu,* for it is said *traividhya-sambhave’py asyā mṛdutaivocitā bhavet*: though the three types are possible in the *ātyantika-laghu*, the *mṛdvī* is most common. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 6.22)

### Text 91-92

***prākharyaṁ mārdavaṁ cāpi yadyapy āpekṣikaṁ bhavet \|***  
***tathāpi vistara-bhayāt tad viśeṣo’tra neritaḥ \|\|91\|\|***  
***prākharyādi-svabhāvo’yaṁ yathāyatham udīritaḥ \|***  
***deśa-kālādi-vaiśiṣṭye syād asyāpi viparyayaḥ \|\|92\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The terms** ***prakharā*** **and** ***mṛdvī*** **are relative terms. For fear of enlargement of the text, I have not discussed this in detail. The natures of the different types have been described as they are. But according to time and place, these qualities may be reversed in a particular person.**

### Text 93

***tatra prākharyasya viparyayo, yathā—***  
***dhvāntair gāḍhatamāṁ tamīm agaṇayan vṛṣṭiṁ ca dhārā-mayīṁ***  
***caṇḍaṁ cānila-maṇḍalaṁ sakhi harir dvāraṁ tavāsau śritaḥ \|***  
***hā krodhaṁ visṛja prasīda tarasā kaṇṭhe gṛhāṇa priyaṁ***  
***mūrdhnāyaṁ lalitābhidhas tava padaṁ natvā jano yācate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***prakharā*** **showing opposite tendencies: Not considering the night filled with darkness, thick showers of rain and the fierce winds, Kṛṣṇa now stands at your door. Give up your anger. Be kind. Embrace him. This person named Lalitā bows down at your feet, and begs you to accept him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Lalitā speaks. The anger of Rādhā is made unsteady out of fear of Lalitā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā who is angry with Kṛṣṇa.  *Tamīm* means night.

### Text 94

***mārdavasya viparyayo, yathā—***  
***guṇa-stavana-kūṭataḥ kuṭila-dhīḥ sakhi tvām asau***  
***kaṭākṣitavatī kathaṁ tad api nojjhasi praśrayam \|***  
***ruṣaṁ kuru karoṣi cen mṛdutarādya citrāpy asau***  
***vidhāsyati tadaucitīṁ hima-ghaṭeva padmopari \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A** ***mṛdvī*** **showing** ***prakharā*** **nature: Crooked Padmā has glanced at you and glorified you with false praise. Why do you not give up your politeness? Show anger towards her. Even gentle Citrā, though soft, will take appropriate action on Padmā, throwing a pot of snow on lotuses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“O Padmā! Where did you come from?”

“I came from my house.”  
”What is your friend doing?”

“She is crying.”

“Why is that?”

“You may be a deep ocean of self-control, and do not shed tears in separation from your lover.”

After this conversation Padmā left. Citrā heard about this from another *sakhī*. She went to Rādhā who was repentant and scolded her with this verse. Padmā has made a show (*kuṭataḥ*) praising your qualities. According to Medinī *kūtā* means neuter, noise, pile, an iron mallet, projecting bone, illusion, peak of a mountain, insignificant, plough, limb and device. Padmā has a devious mind. While pretending to praise you she made you the object of her glance—she criticized you. By her praise she criticized you. By saying that you do not weep she indicates that you have very little *prema,* since you can conceal tears. *Praśrayam* means politeness. She has left this place, but I will find her and do what is appropriate. It is unsuitable for Citrā who is soft with coolness (*hima-ghaṭa*) to show heat. Therefore she will throw a pot of her coolness on Padmā, the *sakhī* of Candrāvalī, like throwing snow on lotuses. In this way Padmā will suffer.

### Text 95

***dūtyaṁ tu kurvatī sakhyāḥ sakhī rahasi saṅgatā \|***  
***kṛṣṇena prārthyamānāpi syāt kadāpi na sammatā \|\|95\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhī*** **engaged as a matchmaker by another** ***sakhī,*** **though sometimes requested by Kṛṣṇa for intimacy in a solitary place, refuses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Na sammatā* means “she does not at all consent.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa may request amorous enjoyment but the *sakhī* do not agree.

### Text 96

***yathā—***  
***dūtyenādya suhṛj-janasya rahasi prāptāsmi te sannidhiṁ***  
***kiṁ kandarpa-dhanur bhayaṅkaram amuṁ bhrū-guccham udyacchasi \|***  
***prāṇān arpayitāsmi samprati varaṁ vṛndāṭavīcandra te***  
***na tv etām asamāpita-priya-sakhī-kṛtyānubandhāṁ tanum \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I have met you in this secluded place because of delivering a message for my dear friend. Why do you raise the fearful bow of Cupid, your eyebrows, in this way? O moon of Vṛndāvana, it is better that I offer my life to you than my body, which has not fulfilled its duty to Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

I have come as a messenger. Therefore you should not make advances. Why do you raise the cluster of your brows? They are more fearful than the bow of Cupid. He thinks, “Fearing the affliction of Cupid she may give up her stubbornness.” But such fear does not occur in my heart because of the strength of my friendship with my friend. “But I will do this by force.” I will give up my life. You are the moon of Vṛndāvana, spotless, supposedly. If you desire to be tarnished with the death of a woman, then go ahead. I will go and fulfill this appointment which you so desire for your *sakhī* in a few seconds. But now, give me association with your body, which I desire. If you say you have no love for me, then I naturally I have no love for you but then my *priya-sakhī* will come for enjoyment. The duty to my priya-sakhī has not been completed. As long as she does not associate with you and my duty is not accomplished I cannot give my body to you.”

This reason is this. Their friendship is based on trust. The *nāyikā* trusts her messenger. If the *sakhī* enjoys with Kṛṣṇa secretly, the trust will be broken and the friendship will be lost. With *prema* uprooted, how can *rasa* be accomplished*? Kāvya-prakāśa* (1.4) gives an example of a heroine detecting her friend’s illicit connection with her lover saying *niḥśeṣa-cyuta-candanaṁ stana-taṭam:* the sandalwood has vanished from your breast. The enjoyment of the messenger is discovered by the angry *nāyikā,* but still there is friendship and *rasa*. Let the poets enjoy this, but not us!

### Text 97-99

***mithaḥ prema-gunotkīrtis tayor āsakti-kāritā \|***  
***abhisāro dvayor eva sakhyāḥ kṛṣṇe samarpaṇam \|\|97\|\|***  
***narmāśvāsana-nepathyaṁ hṛdayodghāṭa-pāṭavam \|***  
***chidra-saṁvṛtir etasyāḥ paty-ādeḥ parivañcanā \|\|98\|\|***  
***śikṣā saṅgamanaṁ kāle sevanaṁ vyajanādibhiḥ \|***  
***tayor dvayor upālambhaḥ sandeśa-preṣaṇaṁ tathā \|***  
***nāyikā-prāṇa-saṁrakṣā prayatnādyāḥ sakhī-kriyāḥ \|\|99\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The activities of the** ***sakhīs*** **consist of excellently glorifying the love and qualities of the Kṛṣṇa to the** ***nayikā***  **and of the** ***nāyikā*** **to Kṛṣṇa ; creating attachment between the couple; arranging meetings of the couple, offering the** ***sakhī*** **to Kṛṣṇa; joking, consoling, dressing the couple, expertly revealing the feelings of one lover to the other; hiding faults of the woman; cheating the husbands and others; advising; associating with the couple after they meet; serving the couple by fanning etc.; scolding the couple; delivering messages; and protecting the life of the** ***nāyikā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *sakhīs* glorify the qualities and love of *nāyikā* to Kṛṣṇa and of Kṛṣṇa to the *nāyikā.* They serve them during the meeting.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *sakhīs* excellently glorify the qualities and love of one to the other. They have the ability to create attachment between the couple. All the activities are performed at the appropriate time. .The total of activities is seventeen. Other activities are arguing with the opposing group’s *sakhīs* and getting knowledge of and revealing the plans that opposing *sakhīs* or the elders have made or desire to make.

### Text 100

*tatra kṛṣṇe sakhī-premotkīrtiḥ, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (189)—*  
***murahara sāhasa-garimā***  
***katham iva vācyaḥ kuraṅga-śāvākṣyāḥ \|***  
***khedārṇava-patitāpi***  
***prema-madhurāṁ te na sā tyajati \|\|100\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glorifying the** ***sakhī’s*** **love to Kṛṣṇa, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O Kṛṣṇa, how can I describe the greatness of fawn-eyed Rādhā’s love for you? Even though she has fallen into the ocean of suffering, she does not give up her sweet love for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She suffers because your indifference.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Rādhā suffers because of your indifference. She has passed your test and should be acknowledged by giving yourself to her. Thinking this love more valuable than her life, she carries it. Otherwise she would give up her life. If a person fell in the ocean carrying this great burden without letting go, that person would not live.

### Text 101

***sakhyāṁ kṛṣṇa-premotkīrtiḥ, yathā tatraiva (191)—***  
***kelikalāsu kuśalā nagare murārer***  
***ābhīra-nīraja-dṛśaḥ kati vā na santi \|***  
***rādhe tvayā mahad akāri tapo yad eṣa***  
***dāmodaras tvayi paraṁ paramānurāgaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glorifying Kṛṣṇa’s love to the** ***sakhī*****, from** ***Padyāvalī*****: O Rādhā! In Murāri’s Vraja are there not many lotus-eyed gopīs expert in amorous pastimes? You must have performed great austerities to make Dāmodara love you so much.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The village mentioned is Vraja. However, *nāgara* also means a person with cunning behavior. Kṛṣṇa is most expert in such behavior.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Campakalatā speaks to Rādhā.

### Text 102

***tatra tasyā guṇotkīrtiḥ, yathā—***  
***nininda nijam indirā vapur avekṣya yasyāḥ śriyaṁ***  
***vicārya guṇa-cāturīm acalajā ca lajjāṁ gatā \|***  
***aghārdana tayā vinā jagati kvānurūpāsti te***  
***paraṁ parama-durlabhā milatu kasya sā me sakhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glorifying the** ***nāyikā’s*** **qualities to Kṛṣṇa: Seeing Rādhā’s beauty Lakṣmī became disgusted with her own body. Considering Rādhā’s qualities Durgā became ashamed. O Kṛṣṇa! Who else except Rādhā is suitable for you in this universe? Who else can my most rare friend meet?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *acalajā ca lajjāṁ gatā* sometimes *hriyam avāpa padmāly api* is seen. This means the followers of Lakṣmī become ashamed, or the friend of Padmā, Candrāvalī becomes ashamed. *Kasya* has an accusative meaning as in *māsānām aśnīyāt*: he ate beans.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Qualities of Rādhā are glorified to Kṛṣṇa. Lalitā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Indirā is Lakṣmī. *Acalajā* is Durgā. “If Rādhā is suitable for me, she should be my lover. You should strive for that.” Lalitā says “She is most rare (*parama-durlabhā*).” Though she is suitable she cannot be attained. But if you have accrued austerity from past lives, then she can be yours. *Kasya* has an accusative meaning. However using the genitive hints at another meaning.

“She is said to be the wife of Abhimanyu.”

“She is my friend, and no one’s (*kasya).* She cannot be attained by marriage.”

“How should I attain her?”

“The best thing is the *parakīya* man *(param*).”

The imperative is used in *milatu.* Because of her suitability she should unite with you in a *parakīya* manner. *Param* also means she is extremely rare to attain. However by my endeavors, she is easily attained.

### Text 103

***tasyāṁ tasya guṇotkīrtiḥ, yathā lalita-mādhave (1.49)—***  
***mahendra-maṇi-maṇḍalī-mada-viḍambi-deha-dyutir***  
***vrajendra-kula-candramāḥ sphurati ko ‘pi navyo yuvā***  
***sakhi sthira-kulāṅganā-nikara-nīvi-bandhārgala-***  
***cchidākaraṇa-kautukī jayati yasya vaṁśī-dhvaniḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glorifying Kṛṣṇa’s qualities to the heroine, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O friend! All glories to the moon of Vraja women, the fresh youth, whose bodily luster mocks the pride of all the jewels of the Mahendra mountain, and the sound of whose flute eagerly breaks the lock of the sashes of the most chaste girls.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. The flute is intent on break in two (*chidākaraṇa*) the locks on the sashes of the women. This means the sashes are like door panels of Cupid’s house. A person shows his strength by pounding on the door and breaking the inner bolt. Similarly the air from Kṛṣṇa’s mouth enters the hole of the flute, becomes the musical notes, and somehow breaks the locks on the sashes. This shows his extraordinary strength.

### Text 104

***kṛṣṇe sakhyā āsakti-kāritā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.10)—***  
***sā saurabhormi-paridigdha-digantarāpi***  
***bandhyaṁ januḥ sutanu gandha-phalī bibharti \|***  
***rādhe na bibhrama-bharaḥ kriyate yad-aṅke***  
***kāmaṁ nipīta-madhunā madhusūdanena \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Producing a** ***sakhī’s*** **attraction to Kṛṣṇa, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: O beautiful, slender Rādhā! Even if it anoints the directions with waves of sweet fragrance, a c*****ampaka*** **lives in vain if a playful bumblebee does not drink its honey and perform pastimes there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā and Viśākhā speak to Rādhā. The *campaka* (*gandhaphalī*) spreading *(digdha*) its aroma in all directions has useless birth if the bee, drinking honey, or Kṛṣṇa, does not drink the nectar of your lips, and does not perform pastimes there.

### Text 105

***tasyāṁ tasyāsakti-kāritā, yathā—***  
***yady etasyāṁ vara-parimalārabdha-viśvotsavāyāṁ***  
***na tvaṁ kṛṣṇa-bhramara ramase rādhikā-mallikāyām \|***  
***arthaḥ ko vā nava-taruṇimodbhāsinas te tataḥ syād***  
***vṛndāṭavyām iha viharaṇa-prakriyā-cāturībhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Producing Kṛṣṇa’s attraction for Rādhā: O black bumble-bee Kṛṣṇa, if you decline to enjoy the jasmine flower Rādhā, whose fine fragrance produces joy in the universe, then what is the purpose of your splendid youthfulness and what is the purpose of your expertise in enjoying pastimes in the Vṛndāvana forest?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.  *Parimala* means fragrance and the spreading of the fame of her beauty, qualities and skills. Her fragrance brings joy to the universe, or brings all joy. Therefore she is yours*. Arthaḥ* means purpose.

### Text 106

***kṛṣṇasyābhisāraṇaṁ, yathā—***  
***avaruddha-sudhāṁśu-vaibhavaṁ***  
***vinudantaṁ sakhi sarvato-mukham \|***  
***iha kṛṣṇa-ghanaṁ pragṛhya taṁ***  
***lalitā-prāvṛḍ iyaṁ samāgatā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bringing Kṛṣṇa to a meeting: O friend! The attractive monsoon season, grasping the dark cloud which expels rain and derides the splendor of the moon, is coming here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The cloud expels rain or Kṛṣṇa moves his face in all directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to Rādhā who is dressing herself. That cloud derides the glory of the moon by his face or covers the splendor of the moon. The cloud rains water in all directions. *Sarvatomukham* means water according to *Amara-koṣa*. The phrase also means he turns his face in all directions out of fear that other *nāyikās* will see him. The indication is that this cloud will bring into blossom the jasmine of Rādhā, burnt by the fire of separation.

### Text 107

***sakhyā abhisāraṇaṁ, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (5.18)—***  
***tvad-vāmyena samaṁ samagram adhunā tigmāṁśur astaṁ gato***  
***govindasya manorathena ca samaṁ prāptaṁ tamaḥ sāndratām \|***  
***kokānāṁ karuṇa-svanena sadṛśī dīrgha-mad-abhyarthanā***  
***tan mugdhe viphalaṁ vilambanam asau ramyo’bhisāra-kṣaṇaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bringing the** ***sakhī*** **to Kṛṣṇa, from** ***Gīta-govinda*****: The sun whose heat is similar to your anger, has completely set, and, deep darkness, similar to Kṛṣṇa’s desires, has spread everywhere. Just as the** ***cakravākas*** **cry in misery at night, I repeatedly appeal to you. O charming girl, to delay is fruitless. Now is the time for your delightful meeting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sudevī speaks to Rādhā. The anger, being hot like the sun, is opposed to Kṛṣṇa’s desires. The darkness is impenetrable, not allowing any light within it. It is compared to Kṛṣṇa’s desires, which will destroy the hot sun of her anger. The sound of the *cakravāka* bird, repeated without rest many thousands of times, is similar to Sudevī’s pleas. What is the use of your anger? As soon as the sun sets, it does not rise immediately. Anger is similar. “Oh! My friend anger has suddenly disappeared. Go to him quickly, for the anger, like the hot sun, will appear again.”’ She consoles and jokes with her.

### Text 108

***kṛṣṇe sakhyāḥ samarpaṇaṁ, yathā—***  
***yad-antaram upāsituṁ kamala-yonim ījur guṇā***  
***yad-aṅgam upasevituṁ taruṇimāpi cakre tapaḥ \|***  
***nava-praṇaya-mādhurī-pramada-medureyaṁ sakhī***  
***mayādya bhavataḥ kare muraharopahārīkṛtā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Offering the** ***sakhī*** **to Kṛṣṇa: A host of virtues have worshipped Brahma for the right to serve this girl's heart, and youthfulness has performed austerities to serve her body. She is now completely filled with bliss arising from the sweetness of constant love for you. O killer of the Mura demon, I now gift this girl to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ijuḥ* means they worship.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Good qualities worship Brahmā to serve her heart *(antaram*). This means that qualities like self-control, dignity, and skill in the arts, worship Brahmā to dwell in her heart. This means she has attained many good qualities as a blessing because of the mercy of many people. Youthfulness, by performing austerities has been able to enter her body. What is the cause of her greatness? She has a great amount of *prema*: she is dense with bliss and intoxicating pride (*pramāda)* caused by constant (*nava*) sweet affection.  *Upahāra* means a gift.

### Text 109

***narma, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (1.33)—***  
***dehaṁ te bhuvanāntarāla-virala-cchāyā-vilāsāspadaṁ***  
***mā kautūhala-cañcalākṣi latikā-jāle praveśaṁ kṛthāḥ \|***  
***navyām añjana-puñja-mañjula-ruciḥ kuñjecarī devatā***  
***kāntāṁ kāntibhir aṅkitām iha vane niḥśaṅkam ākarṣati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Joking from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O girl with restless eyes! Your body is the temple of splendor rare in the three worlds. Do not enter that tangle of tender creepers. A** ***devatā*** **whose beautiful complexion is like lamp black moves in that forest. He fearlessly attracts a woman marked with beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. This girl is the abode of pastimes (*vilāsa*) of beauty (*ccchāyā*) rare in the three worlds. The word *latikā* indicates compassion. The creepers are tender. It is possible to enter but impossible to get out, since they are a network (*jāla*).

### Text 110

***āśvāsanaṁ, yathā—***  
***mā gāḥ klamaṁ sakhi muhur vṛṣabhānu-putri***  
***bhānuṁ pratīhi caramācala-caṅkramotkam \|***  
***ānandayan nayanam uddhura-dhenu-dhūlī-***  
***dhvāntaṁ vidhūya vidhur eṣa purojjihīte \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Consolation: O daughter of Vrṣabhānu! Do not repeatedly become fatigued. The sun desires to move crookedly while setting in the west. See! Delighting your eyes and dispelling the darkness of the dust raised the cows, the moon is now rising.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks, when Rādhā says “Though a thousand *yugas* have passed today, why has the sun not set?” This verse answers. “See! The sun has now moved crooked before it sets, out of desire to see Kṛṣṇa for a longer time.” Though the sun actually moves on a straight course, their seeing it as such is not unusual, because of their *prema.* The affix *cam* in *caṁkramotkam* denotes crookedness, according to the rule *nityam kauṭilye gatau.* (Pāṇini 3.1.23) One should also consider the word *caṅkṛama* found in the following Vedic rule:

*vyāyāmaṁ ca vyavāyaṁ ca snānaṁ caṅkramaṇaṁ tathā \|*  
*jvara-mukto na seveta yāvan na balavān bhavet \|\|*

**While he is not strong the person free of fever should not exercise, have sex, bathe or stroll about.**

If the sun acts in such a contrary manner, how will I live? The moon, Kṛṣṇa (*vidhuḥ*), is rising nearby (*purā). Purā* means “near” according to *Nānārtha-varga*.

### Text 111

***nepathyaṁ, yathā—***  
***bhāle mayā te mṛga-nābhināsau***  
***yaḥ patra-bhaṅgo’sti viracyamānaḥ \|***  
***sa bindu-rūpeṇa patac-chramāmbu-***  
***lipto harer vaktram alaṅkarotu \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Dressing: May the patterns I am drawing on your forehead with musk, when washed away by drops of perspiration, fall upon the face of Kṛṣṇa and decorate it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *harer vaktram alaṅkarotu* sometimes *harer vaktram upaskarotu* (same meaning) is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While decorating Rādhā, Lalitā jokes. She indicates her desire to have Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa reverse their positions in their amorous encounter. By this the labor of her painting the patterns will become successful.

### Text 112

***hṛdayodghāṭa-pāṭavaṁ, yathā—***  
***tathyaṁ vadādya na hi saṅkuca paṅkajābhaṁ***  
***dvandvaṁ dṛśor iha kiśori nimīlayantī \|***  
***kā rajyate sakhi vivoḍhari gokule’smin***  
***kṣuṇṇā na vīthir iyam ekikayā tvayaiva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Having the heroine reveal her heart: Tell me the truth. Today you close your eyes. Do not be shy! What woman in Gokula has a husband? This path is not tread by you alone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Who in Gokula has a husband? No one does. This joking statement is included in “revealing the heart” since it remove the girl’s reservations. However the intention is to show what is usual. This path of having attraction for your husband has not been destroyed by you alone.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā questions Rādhā, who is embarrassed to speak to her friend, about her inner feelings of love in *pūrva-rāga*. Though you close your eyes, do not be shy. Open your eyes and tell me the truth. Tell me the reason for your heart’s affliction. “The cause of my distress is attraction to another man. How can I not be shy to tell her that?” What woman in Gokula has a husband? None have. Therefore this famous path of being faithful to the husband has not been crushed by your feet alone. All the women have done this. Destroying the path of faithfulness to the husband by your feet, you have instituted the path of the *upapati* by your acceptance of it. Your reservations should not be so reserved according to the logic of *na duḥkham pañcabhiḥ saha*: five people gathered together cannot be unhappy. (*Gopāla-campu* 24.84)

### Text 113

***yathā vā—***  
***vayas te sāmrājyaṁ sakhi vitanute puṣpa-dhanuṣo***  
***jihīte saundaryaṁ tribhuvana-dṛg-āsecanakatām \|***  
***na dāsye’py aucityaṁ vahati pariṇetā pariṇatas***  
***tvam ekā hrī-dagdhe bata vimuṣitāsi vraja-kule \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: My friend! Your youthfulness has enlarged the kingdom of Cupid, and your beauty is such that the eyes of all the three worlds can never be fully satisfied. That aged husband is not suitable for your service. O my friend, destroyed by your shyness! Among all the girls of Vraja, you are the only one who has been cheated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Youth and beauty are the subjects of the sentences. *Jihīte* means “goes.” *Āsecanakaṁ* means “from seeing your beauty the eyes of all in the universe cannot be fully satisfied.”  *Parinetā* means husband. *Pariṇatah* means old. O shy girl! You have been stolen (*vimuṣitāḥ*). You are a stolen treasure. But this also means “You alone have stolen or captivated Kṛṣṇa on being attaining by him”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous example “revealing the heart of the heroine" is not without fault since the fault of being attached to another man is revealed to be common among the women. Therefore another example is given. Previous to the appearance of your youth, Cupid had conquered the world. Except for conquering Kṛṣṇa his victory was complete. But now, with the appearance of your youthfulness, Kṛṣṇa has been conquered. Therefore, Cupid’s victory is complete. But one should not only glorify your present beauty. Before your youth, when you were a child you had beauty. Your beauty attains the position of never completely satisfy the eyes of the people of the universe.  *Āsecanakam* means “seeing whom one is not fully satisfied” according to *Amara-koṣa*. Glorification of her youth and beauty also indicate the great sweetness of all her qualities. The speaker says that all that beauty and youth are wasted since she has a husband. Such servitorship to a husband is of no value. It is not proper to accept this. The husband is also ugly and without good qualities. He is like an animal and has no youth. Starting from the time of marriage he has been old. After his *bālya* and *paugaṇda* ages he simply became an aged person.

“What am I to do? Such is my fate.” O girl, destroyed by shyness! Kṛṣṇa, who has qualities suitable for you, full of desire, resides in Vraja. Because you have not endeavored for his association because of shyness you have been destroyed. It is not because of your fate. “Which woman is doing this?” Ah (*bata*)! This is said in pain. Among the women of Vraja (*vraja-kule*), you alone are cheated. Others, giving up their husbands, attained association with Kṛṣṇa, enjoy with him and have made their beauty and youthfulness successful. You think that the desire to give attachment to another man is good. But it is a great fault, since the beauty, qualities and youth given by the creator would be useless. You have committed offense against the creator. Considering all this tell me what you want to do. Revealing her heart and saying “Yes, let me also try this” she also says tearfully that cultured women should not praise having affairs with other men.

### Text 114

***chidra-saṁvṛtir, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.1)—***  
***mudā kṣiptaiḥ parvottarala-hṛdayābhir yuvatibhiḥ***  
***payaḥ-pūyaiḥ pītīkṛtam atiharidrā-drava-mayaiḥ \|***  
***dukūlaṁ dor-mūlopari paridadhānāṁ priya-sakhīṁ***  
***kathaṁ rādhām ārye kuṭilita-dṛgantaṁ kalayasi \|\|114\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Covering faults of the heroine, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: O noble lady, why do you stare at my dear friend Rādhā from the corners of your crooked eyes? The cloth she wears on her shoulders has become yellow because water mixed with turmeric thrown by the young girls in joy, whose minds were excited by the festival.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Jaṭilā, the so-called mother-in-way of Rādhā, being near-sighted, was wondering if it was Kṛṣṇa’s cloth, when she saw suddenly Rādhā wearing yellow cloth. A *sakhī* of Rādhā speaks to her to mislead her. She mentioned that the color is covering her shoulders not her arms in order to suggest that Rādhā is about to give up the cloth since it has been stained with colors. This is to cheat Jaṭilā. Some disrespect is also indicated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā deceives Jaṭilā who recognized Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth on the body of Rādhā, her daughter-in-law and began to scold her in anger. “Rādhā, wearing white cloth stayed up all night with many other girls performing vows in a temple. After the night was over in order to complete the festival in joy they threw turmeric water on each other. After a while the cloth on her limbs dried and become yellow. Please understand this.”

### Text 115

*paty-ādeḥ parivañcanā, yathā—*  
***śyāmāṅgaḥ paṭur eṣa karmaṇi baṭur gargasya śiṣyo mayā***  
***rādhām arcayituṁ prage dina-karaṁ sadmany ayaṁ prāpitaḥ \|***  
***tenābhīra payas tvam āgamaya gāṁ dugdhvā pataṅga-priyāṁ***  
***piṅgākṣīm aruṇām ahaṁ tu karavāṇy ebhiḥ sarojaiḥ srajam \|\|115\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Cheating husbands: This dark-complexioned** ***brāhmaṇa*** **boy is Garga's student, and is very expert at performing rituals. I have brought him to this home so he may direct Rādhā's worship of the sun-god. O cowherd Abhimanyu, milk a brown-eyed, red cow, dear to the sun-god and then return with the milk. Meanwhile I shall make a garland from these red lotus flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The black *brāhmaṇa* is Kṛṣṇa.  *Arcayitum* is a causative form “have Rādhā worship.” Since others were going elsewhere the *brāhmaṇa* accepted to come here. *Prage* means early morning. A cowherd (*abhira*)! This is an address to Rādhā’s so-called husband Abhimanyu. After milking a special breed of brown cow, since this is dear to the sun-god, bring the milk.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā, concealing Kṛṣṇa dressed as a *brāhmaṇa,* has faithful Abhimanyu leave on a pretext. *Arcayitum* is a causative form with Rādhā as the commissioned doer (he had Rādhā worship the sun god). *Bhāṣā-vṛtti* gives the *rule gaty-arthādi-vyatirikta-nāmānau kartur ṇāv ubhayaṁ bhavati kartṛkatvaṁ karmatvaṁ ca*: in the case of verbs other than expressing “going” the subject becomes both an object and subject when the verb is made causative.

O Abhimanyu! After milking the brown cow bring the milk. Milk from a brown cow is necessary for bathing the sun-god. The cow must be red in all its limbs and have brown eyes. This cow is very dear to the sun god. Anyone else cannot recognize such a cow. No one else can be sent. Therefore she calls for him to go. The purpose is to delay him in returning.

### Text 116

***śikṣā, yathā—***  
***tvam īraya samīraṇaṁ vara-saroja-vallī-dalair***  
***vidhehi sakhi mantharaṁ caraṇa-padma-saṁvāhanam \|***  
***mukhe ghaṭaya vīṭikām avadalayya karpuriṇīṁ***  
***harer iti navāṅganā praṇayinī-padaṁ vindati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Instructing other** ***sakhīs*****: First fan Kṛṣṇa with a fan made of lotus-petals and vine-flower petals, then gently massage his lotus feet, then cut up some betel-nuts, mix them with camphor, and place them in his mouth. Acting in this way, a young girl can become the intimate friend of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first two actions are those of a new wife. You should cut up the betel nut completely (*avadalayya*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* takes another *sakhī* who is to directly associate with Kṛṣṇa for the first time to Kṛṣṇa and instructs her. One prepares betel nut by removing the skin and chopping it. Place it in his mouth.

### Text 117

***yathā vā—***  
***kurvīthāḥ param ādaraṁ priya-suhṛd-varge sadā preyasaḥ***  
***kāmaṁ tasya rahasya-saṁvṛti-vidhau nirbandham aṅgīkuru \|***  
***mā cetas tad asammate sakhi nijābhīṣṭe’pi kṛtye kṛthāḥ***  
***prāpsyaty evam anargalo’pi sa haris tūrṇaṁ tavādhīnatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! Be very respectful to your lover's cowherd friends, strictly keep secrets, and do not press your own desires on him when they conflict with his wishes. Then you will quickly bring Kṛṣṇa, who cannot be controlled, under your control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The instructions given to the *nāyikā* were not so sweet in the last example. Therefore another example is given. Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. The dear friends of Kṛṣṇa are Subala and others. Kṛṣṇa is not controlled by anyone (*anargalaḥ)* but can be controlled by you.

### Text 118

***atha kāle saṅgamanaṁ, yathā—***  
***vāsarīya-viraha-klama-biddhāṁ***  
***locanotpala-valad-bhramarālim \|***  
***rādhikā-kumudinīṁ vidhuneyaṁ***  
***saṁyunakti lalitottara-sandhyā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Uniting the lovers at the appropriate time: The beautiful twilight has united the pond of night lotuses, Rādhā, pained by the separation caused during the day, filled with bees enjoying the delightful lotuses, with the moon.**

**Lalitā has united Rādhā, pained by separation during the day, whose lotus eyes are covered by locks of hair, with Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Brahmarāḥ* means bees and locks of hair.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rati-mañjarī speaks to Rūpa-mañjarī.  *Vidhunā* means with the moon or with Kṛṣṇa. Lalitā means graceful or the *sakhī* Lalitā. *Locanotpala-valad-bhramarālim* means the bees enjoy in the beautiful lotuses or the locks of hair cover her lotus eyes. *Bhrama* means locks on the forehead according to *Amara-koṣa.*

### Text 119

***atha vyajanādinā sevā, yathā—***  
***cāmarī-kṛta-latā-camarīkā***  
***kuñja-dhāmni lalitā lulitāṅgīm \|***  
***svidyad ākṛtim abījayad enāṁ***  
***petuṣīm aghaharorasi rādhām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Serving by fanning etc.:**
