**In the forest grove, Lalitā, making a** ***cāmara*** **from buds of a creeper, fanned Rādhā, exhausted and perspiring, who had fallen on the chest of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Camarī* is a flower bud Instead of *petuṣīm* sometimes *saṅgatām* is found.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Camarī* is a flower bud. *Petuṣīm* (fallen) indicates their position after love making in reverse position. Because of exhaustion she fell upon Kṛṣṇa’s chest.

### Text 120

***atha tayor dvayor upālambhaḥ \| tatra harer upālambho, yathā—***  
***saumya-mūrtir upanīya nirbharaṁ***  
***śāradārka iva rāgam agrataḥ \|***  
***tvaṁ bhajan sapadi tīvratāṁ kutaḥ***  
***pūtanārdana dunoṣi me sakhīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Scolding Kṛṣṇa: First showing yourself to be very gentle like the autumn, showing great attraction for her, red like the rising sun, you immediately show harshness. O killer of Pūtanā! Why do you afflict my friend?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

After Rādhā has been devastated, Lalitā scolds Kṛṣṇa, who has become gentle. In order to arouse faith in all innocent people, you show gentleness. I do not know such gentleness even in my dreams. She speaks a lie.  *Rāga* means *anurāga*, attraction, but also red. When the sun has risen and has not set, it exists in front of us (*agrataḥ*). The sun is red. The gentle form of the sun in Āśvina month (autumn) has become harsh because it creates *pitta* in the body and injures innocent people who serve it. You are like that. It is said:

*śuṣkaṁ māṁsaṁ striyo vṛddhā bālārkas taruṇaṁ dadhi*  
*prabhāte maithunaṁ nidrā sadyaḥ prāṇaharāṇi ṣaṭ*

**Dried meat, an old wife, the morning sun, unripe yogurt, sex after dawn or sleep after dawn quickly takes away life.** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa*** **1.114.30**

O killer of Pūtanā! If, from childhood creating that impression, your nature is killing women, then there are many women with false love like Pūtanā. You should exclude my friend from your list. Why do you afflict her? I think you cannot recognize the difference between real love and false love.

### Text 121

***sakhyā upālambho, yathā—***  
***vipakṣe dākṣiṇyaṁ praṇayasi paraṁ keli-kutuke***  
***mukundenārabdhe kalayasi pṛthuṁ vepathu-bharam \|***  
***mudhaivābhyasyantī sahacari sadā maṇḍana-kalāṁ***  
***kuto maugdhyena tvaṁ samayam anabhijñe gamayasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Scolding the** ***nāyikā:*** **O friend! Although you tremble with eagerness to enjoy amorous pastimes with Mukunda, you are nevertheless friendly to the rival party. Therefore, your attempt to skillfully decorate yourself is useless. O ignorant woman! Why are you so wasting your time in gentle dealings?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā, not able to tolerate Rādhā giving respect with sweet words to Padmā, whom Rādhā met accidentally, speaks to Rādhā while she is decorating herself with skillfully strung groups of pearls. What conduct of love are you considering? If you recognize the opposing party which should be condemned, by giving respect to that party you denigrate your position. How can your superiority be maintained? If you give up your verbal and bodily *pragalbhā* nature suitable for amorous interaction with Kṛṣṇa, and tremble just by the touch of his hand, how can your major pastimes take place? Therefore you are engaged in useless decoration of your body. If you distance yourself from your own excellence by respecting inferior people, what is your plan? O ignorant woman! Actually this reveals Rādhā’s supreme position by *vyāja-stuti* (censure conveying the opposite).

### Text 122

*atha sandeśa-preṣaṇaṁ, yathā haṁsadūte (75)—*  
*tvayā goṣṭhaṁ goṣṭhītilaka kila ced vismṛtam idaṁ*  
*na tūrṇaṁ dhūmorṇāpatir api vidhatte yadi kṛpām \|*  
***ahar vṛndaṁ vṛndāvana-kusuma-pālī-parimalair***  
***darālokaṁ śokāspadam iva kathaṁ neṣyati sakhī \|\|122\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sending messages, from** ***Haṁsadūta*****: O** ***tilaka*** **marking of the people! If you forget Vraja, and if death does not come soon, how will my friend pass her days which are the object of lamentation and difficult to behold, though filled with the fragrance of Vṛndāvana’s flowers?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dhūmorṇa-patiḥ* means Yama.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā sends a message to Kṛṣṇa, living in Mathurā, by means of a swan, in two verses. You are the *tilaka* of your people. This has the opposite meaning: you give suffering to your people. Or, as mentioned in this verse, you are the *tilaka* of Yama. If death does not bestow mercy quickly means “If death comes quickly” However this is happening slowly. If you come quickly you will see her, but not otherwise. You must appear in Vṛndāvana as the object of love.

### Text 123

***atha nāyikā-prāṇa-saṁrakṣā-prayatno, yathā—***  
***tvām āyāntaṁ kathayati mṛṣā kurvatī divyam ugraṁ***  
***mūrcchārambhe tava maṇimayīṁ darśayaty āśu mūrtim \|***  
***vanye veṇau dhvanti marutā karṇa-rodhaṁ vidhatte***  
***rakṣaty asyāḥ katham api tanuṁ mādhavī yādavendra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Efforts to protect the life of the** ***nāyikā:*** **When Rādhā faints, Mādhavī, making a false, terrible oath, tells her that you are coming. When Rādhā faints, she restores Rādhā’s consciousness by showing her a jeweled form of you, or plugs Rādhā’s ears when Rādhā hears the sound of the bamboos rattling in the wind, since it resembles the sound of your flute. O king of the Yadavas, in this way Mādhavī keeps her alive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Divyam* means an oath. *Venau* means in hollow bamboo. Mādhavī *gopī* tries to comfort Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa who has asked for news of Rādhā. *Mūrcchārambha* should be understood to be related with two statements. Otherwise it would be a fault called “breaking the symmetry of composition.” since it would not relate to the first phrase but would relate to the second of the two statements.

Or there is another meaning. “O friend! Tell me how many days have passed. I will now give up my life.” When Rādhā says this, Mādhavī says, “Kṛṣṇa is coming.” Mādhavī makes a great oath. Rādhā says “O friend! By this oath you are just cheating because when you said this previously he did not appear even after a long time.” When she is about to faint, then Mādhavī shows her a jewel form of you. Developing faith that you will actually come, when the bamboos in the forest suddenly make a sound, Mādhavī blocks her ears with her hands. Thinking it is the sound of the flute Rādhā will think the *rāsa-līlā* is about to beginning and will run off in madness. Not seeing Kṛṣṇa she will again faint. Fearing this Mādhavī blocks her ears. Mādhavī is the name of a *sakhī.*

This ends the discussion of activities of the *sakhīs.*

### Text 124

***athāsām aparaḥ ko’pi viśeṣaḥ punar ucyate \|***  
***asamaṁ ca samaṁ ceti snehaṁ sakhyaṁ svapakṣagāḥ \|***  
***kṛṣṇe yūthādhipāyāṁ ca vahantyo dvividhā matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another unique feature among the** ***sakhīs*** **will be described. There are two types of** ***sakhīs*** **in a group--*****asama*** **and** ***sama*****--according to the amount of affection they show to Kṛṣṇa and the particular leader of the group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Āsām* means “among the *sakhīs*.”

### Text 125

***atha asama-snehāḥ—***  
***adhikaṁ priya-sakhyās tu harau tasyāṁ tatas tathā \|***  
***vahantyaḥ sneham asama-snehās tu dvividhā matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Unequal affection: There are two types unequal affection: a** ***sakhī*** **who has more affection for Kṛṣṇa than for her leader and a** ***sakhī*** **who has more affection for her leader than Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tataḥ* means “than Kṛṣṇa.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* who has more affection for Kṛṣṇa than for her leader (*priya-sakhyāh*) and a sakhī who has more affection for the leader than for Kṛṣṇa are the two types.

### Text 126-127

***tatra harau snehādhikāḥ—***  
***ahaṁ harer iti svānte gūḍhām abhimatiṁ gatāḥ \|***  
***anyatra kvāpy anāsaktyā sveṣṭāṁ yūtheśvarīṁ śritāḥ \|\|\|***  
***manāg evādhikaṁ snehaṁ vahantyas tatra mādhave \|***  
***tad dūtyādi-ratāś cemā harau snehādhikā matāḥ \|\|127\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**More affection for Kṛṣṇa: She who carries out her services such as match-making, while deep within identifying herself as belonging to Kṛṣṇa, while taking shelter of her leader without attraction for other leaders, and while having slightly more affection for Kṛṣṇa, is called the** ***sakhī*** **with more affection for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Abhimatam* means “identity.” Her identity as Kṛṣṇa’s is deep within. Externally however she shows equal affection for Kṛṣṇa and her leader. She has no attachment to other group leaders. “If she identifies herself as Kṛṣṇa’s then why does she have attachment for the group leader?” She has full affection for the group leader but compared to that, she has slightly more affection to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 128

***yathā—***  
***na me cetasy anyad vacasi punar anyaṁ katham api***  
***sthavīyān mānas te sakhi mayi sukhaṁ prathayati \|***  
***raves tāpeneva kṣaṇam udayatā yena janito***  
***bakārer vaktrendu-cchavi-śavalimā māṁ glapayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I have nothing else in my heart and my words. O my friend, your great anger does not indicate happiness to me. The moon-like face of Kṛṣṇa made defective by your anger, like the heat of the rising sun, gives me pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

There is nothing else in my mind and nothing else in my words, nothing at all. They are concentrated on one thing. “Please tell me.” Your great anger does not indicate happiness to me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Dhaniṣṭhā speaks to Rādhā who is angry. I do not speak to you like other friends who speak to please you so that they can see your face. Your solid anger does not reveal happiness to me. By that anger (*yena*), Kṛṣṇa’s face has become disfigured.

### Text 129

***yathā vā—***  
***sura-kulam akhilaṁ praṇamya mūrdhnā***  
***pravaram amuṁ varam arthaye varāṅgi \|***  
***muhur abhimata-sevayā yathāhaṁ***  
***subala-sakhaṁ sukhayāmi rādhikāṁ ca \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O beautiful friend! Bowing my head before you and before all the** ***devatās*****, I appeal to you so that I can constantly please Subala's friend Kṛṣṇa and also Rādhā with my chosen service.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous statement could be an example of equal affection to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, for it has been said:

*āsāṁ suṣṭhu dvayor eva premṇaḥ parama-kāṣṭhayā \|*  
*kvacij jātu kvacij jātu tad-ādhikyam ivekṣate \|\|*

**By the influence of the highest level of prema for Rādhā and Kṛṣna these eight sometimes show more affection for Rādhā and sometimes show more affection for Kṛṣṇa.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **4.55**

Therefore another example is given to show the unique definition. This is very confidential. Some *sakhī s*peaks to a *sakhī* of similar nature about the kind of *sakhī* mood taught to her. The word *ca* indicates that she also desires to serve Rādhā but it is less than for Kṛṣṇa. Therefore she has more affection for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 130

***yāḥ pūrvaṁ sakhya ity uktās tās tu snehādhikā harau \|\|130\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhīs*** **previously described in** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **4.51 had more affection for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *sakhīs* in Rādhā’s group previously described in *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 4.51 in relation to the five types of *sakhīs* are Kusumikā, Vindyā and others. They have more affection for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 131

***atha priya-sakhyāṁ snehādhikāḥ—***  
***tadīyatābhimāninyo yāḥ snehaṁ sarvadāśritāḥ \|***  
***sakhyām alpādhikaṁ kṛṣṇāt sakhī-snehādhikās tu tāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhīs*** **with more affection for their leader: She who continually identifies herself as the property of the group leader and whose has slightly more affection for her group leader than Kṛṣṇa is the** ***sakhī*** **who has more affection for the** ***sakhī.***

### Text 132

***yathā—***  
***viramatu tava vṛnde dūtya-cāturya-caryā***  
***sahacari vinivṛtya brūhi goṣṭhendra-sūnum \|***  
***viṣama-viṣadhareyaṁ śarvarī prāvṛṣeṇyā***  
***katham iha giri-kuñje bhīrur eṣā praheyā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Vṛndā! Give up this skilful service of carrying messages. O friend! Tell Vraja's prince Kṛṣṇa not to come to this rendezvous. This monsoon night is filled with poisonous snakes. Why should this frightened girl be sent to the bower on Govardhana Hill?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some *sakhī* speaks to her leader being taken to Kṛṣṇa by Vṛndā as evening approaches without a proper means of going. *Prāvṛsenyā* means “during the monsoon.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some *prāṇa-sakhī* of Rādhā, with *prakharā* mood, opposing Rādhā’s meeting with Kṛṣṇa, speaks to Vṛndā. *Prāvṛsenyā* means related to the monsoon. *Visadharāh* means snake. *Praheyā* means “being sent.” Kṛṣṇa, who defeated Kāliya, who has no fear of this, is secretly trying to meet with her.

### Text 133

***yathā vā—***  
***vayam idam anubhūya śikṣayāma***  
***kuru cature saha rādhayaiva sakhyam \|***  
***priya-sahacari yatra bāḍham antar-***  
***bhavati hari-praṇaya-pramoda-lakṣmīḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Caturā! Let me teach you what I have learned from my experience. Make friends with Rādhā. That friendship includes Kṛṣṇa’s love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In that love for Rādhā *(yatra*) a wealth of bliss from love for Kṛṣṇa will be included.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous example could be taken as an example of equal affection for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Therefore another example is given. Maṇi-mañjarī gives instruction to a new *sakhī.* “You say to make friendship with only Rādhā. Should there be no love for Kṛṣṇa?” Where there is love for Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa’s love for you, an abundance of bliss, will also be included. What more needs to be said? Your love for Kṛṣṇa is included in your love for Rādhā.

The meaning is this. When you have friendship with Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa will have more affection for you, thinking “This is the *sakhī* of my beloved Rādhā.” He must make friendship with you first because he depends on you to attain her when she becomes proud or angry. Thus your friendship with him will arise without extra effort.

### Text 134

***yāḥ pūrvaṁ prāṇa-sakhyaś ca nitya-sakhyaś ca kīrtitāḥ \|***  
***sakhī-snehādhikā jñeyās tā evātra manīṣibhiḥ \|\|134\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Those who were previously described as** ***prāṇa-sakhis*** **and** ***nitya-sakhīs*** **are known by the wise as** ***sakhīs*** **with more love for the leader of the group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Previously the order of *sakhīs* was stated:

*sakhyaś ca nitya-sakhyaś ca prāṇa-sakhyaś ca kāścana \|*  
*priya-sakhyaś ca parama-preṣṭha-sakhyaś ca viśrutāḥ \|\|*

**The** ***sakhīs*** **of Rādhā are of five types:** ***sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-*****sakhī and** ***parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **4.50**

In order of greater excellence there are *sakhīs, nitya-sakhīs, prāṇa-sakhīs, priya-sakhīs* and *parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs*. The verse states *prāṇa-sakhīs* and then *nitya-sakhīs*. This indicates that mainly the *prāṇa-sakhīs* have more affection for the leader of the group than the *nitya-sakhīs*. The same meaning is indicated in verse 137 by mentioned *parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs* and then *priya-sakhīs.*

### Text 135

***atha sama-snehāḥ—***  
***kṛṣṇe sva-priya-sakhyāṁ ca vahantyaḥ kam api sphuṭam \|***  
***sneham anyūnatādhikyaṁ sama-snehās tu bhūriśaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sakhī*** **who shows quite clearly equal affection for Kṛṣṇa and her group leader are called the** ***sakhī*** **with equal affection.**

### Text 136

***yathā—***  
***vinā kṛṣṇaṁ rādhā vyathayati samantān mama mano***  
***vinā rādhāṁ kṛṣṇo ‘py ahaha sakhi māṁ viklavayati \|***  
***janiḥ sā me mā bhūt kṣaṇam api na yatra kṣaṇa-duhau***  
***yugenākṣṇor lihyāṁ yugapad anayor vaktra-śaśinau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: If she is not together with Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā brings great pain to my heart. O my friend! If he is not accompanied by Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa also brings me great pain. I pray that I shall never take a birth where even for a moment I shall not have the opportunity to drink with my eyes the festive, moon-like faces of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sakhī* with equal affection speaks to a *vāma sakhī* of Rādhā who is angry. *Kṣaṇa-duhau* means “filled with festivity.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Campakalatā speaks to Bakulamālā, a *sakhī* of Śyāmā who has suddenly come while Rādhā is angry.  *Yatra* means “in that birth” *Kṣaṇa-duhau* means “filled with festivity.”

### Text 137

***tulya-pramāṇakaṁ prema vayantyo’pi dvayor imāḥ \|***  
***rādhāyā vayam ity uccair abhimānam upāśritāḥ \|***  
***parama-preṣṭha-sakhyaś ca priya-sakhyaś ca tā matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Those who have equal love for Kṛṣṇa and the group leader, who identify themselves belonging to Rādhā, are** ***parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs*** **and** ***priya-sakhīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

They identify themselves as belonging to Rādhā. This means they identify themselves as belong to their group leader. All other leaders are included in the word “Rādhā.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“If there are three types of *sakhīs*—with more affection for Kṛṣṇa, more affection for Rādhā and equal affection for both—then why was it explained previously that there five types? There are two varieties corresponding to their amount of love for those with more affection for the group leader (*prāṇa-sakhī* and *nitya-sakhī*) and for those with equal affection (*parama-preṣṭha-sakhī* and *priya sakhī*). Why is there only one variety (*sakhī*) for those with more affection for Kṛṣṇa? There should be two varieties also for those with more affection for Kṛṣṇa. Do those *sakhīs* also not have grades of *prema*? And if those with equal affection are the best, then those with more affection either for the group leader or for Kṛṣṇa should be equally inferior. Why are those with more affection for Kṛṣṇa such as Kusumikā and Vindyā placed at the bottom? If you say that Kṛṣṇa is attracted to those who have more affection for the group leader, since she is dear to him, then Rādhā should be attracted to those who have more attraction for Kṛṣṇa, since he is dearest to her. If you say that the names are given by Kṛṣṇa because he is satisfied with them, why cannot Rādhā give the names?”

One should understand the conclusion to these points. *Sakhīs, nitya-sakhīs, prāṇa-sakhīs, priya-sakhīs,* and *priya-narma-sakhīs* actually all have successively greater *prema* for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. This is the significance of those names. Those who have more affection for Kṛṣṇa are the *sakhīs.* The *nitya-sakhīs* have more affection than them for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa but they are called *sakhīs* with more affection for the group leader because they have slightly more affection for Rādhā than for Kṛṣṇa. The *prāṇa-sakhīs* have more affection for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa than the *nitya-sakhīs*, and slightly more affection for Rādhā. They are also called *sakhīs* with more affection for the group leader. Those who have more affection for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa than the *prāṇa-sakhīs* but also equal affection for both are the *priya-sakhīs.* They are called *sakhīs* with equal affection. The *priya-narma-sakhīs (parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs)* have even more affection than the *priya-sakhīs* for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, but equal affection for both. They are also called *sakhīs* with equal affection.

“Let that be. I do not object to the successively higher statues. But just as those with more affection for the *sakhī* have two varieties—*nitya-sakhīs* and *prāṇa-sakhīs*, so those with more affection for Kṛṣṇa should have two varieties--*sakhī* and *snigdha-sakhī*. Why not? Because of this, I am bewildered.”

That is true. It has previously been explained in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* that attaining the position of a *gopī* cannot take place without *rāgānuga-bhakti*. And without following after the *nitya-siddha-gopīs, rāgānuga* cannot be perfected.  *Rāgānuga* means to follow after those *gopīs* who have *rāga.* Those three types who follow the *nitya-siddhas* attain perfection like the *nitya-siddha gopīs* but they exist externally in a slightly lesser position than the *nitya-siddha gopīs* that they follow. Having loyalty to group leaders and their *sakhīs* according to their own desires, the three types This probably means the *prakharā, madhyā*, and *mṛdvī.* 6 who follow the *parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs* with equal affection for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa become *priya-sakhīs* with similar type of affection. The three types who follow *prāṇa-sakhīs* with more affection for Rādhā become situated eternally as *nitya-sakhīs* with more affection for Rādhā. But there are not three types who follow after *sakhīs* with more affection for Kṛṣṇa. Because there is no one following after those *sakhīs* having only one type, there is no lesser type than them.

“Why should they not be followed?” According to the principles of *rāgānuga-bhakti* a person should follow a desired *gopī* while having affection for her not less than one’s affection for Kṛṣṇa. If one follows a *gopī* while having less affection for her than for Kṛṣṇa, it would not be much different from *vaidhi-bhakti.* Even *vaidhi-bhakti* cannot be perfected without following devotees. Therefore in *rāgānuga-bhakti*, persons who desire to follow a *sakhī* with more affection for Kṛṣṇa must not have less affection for that *sakhī* than for Kṛṣṇa.

However, that person would also have to have slightly less affection for Rādhā and other group leaders than for Kṛṣṇa (since there is preference for stronger affection for Kṛṣṇa than Rādhā). But it is very improper to consider the group leaders to be inferior to the *sakhī.* Therefore one does not follow such a *sakhī* and therefore there is one variety of those who have more affection for Kṛṣṇa.

## Chapter 9 - The Groups

## Outline

I. Sva-pakṣa (ones own group)

II. Suhṛt-pakṣa (friendly group)

III. Taṭastha-pakṣa (neutral group)

IV. Vipakṣa (hostile group)

1. deception
2. malice
3. insolence
4. envy
5. jealousy
6. anger
7. pride

- *ahaṅkāra*
- *abhimāna*  
   \- *darpa*  
   \- *uddhasita*  
   \- *mada*
- *auddhatya*

### Text 1

***āsāṁ caturvidho bhedaḥ sarvāsāṁ vraja-subhruvām \|***  
***syāt sva-pakṣaḥ suhṛt-pakṣas taṭasthaḥ pratipakṣakaḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The women of Vraja may be divided in four groups: one’s own group, the favorable group, the neutral group and the opposing group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another type of distinction among the women of Vraja is now made.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author now will briefly discuss difference based on different *bhāvas* of the *sakhīs* and leaders.

### Text 2

***suhṛt-pakṣa-taṭasthau tu prāsaṅgikatayoditau \|***  
***dvau sva-pakṣa-vipakṣākhyau bhedāv eva rasa-pradau \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The friendly and the neutral groups were incidentally mentioned previously. One’s own group and the opposing group give rise to** ***rasa.***

### Text 3

***proktas tatra sva-pakṣasya viśeṣaḥ pūrvam eva hi \|***  
***suhṛt-pakṣādi-bhedānāṁ dig eva kila darśyate \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Details of one’s own group were described previously. Now the difference between the friendly, neutral and opposing groups will be described briefly.**

### Text 4

***tatra suhṛt-pakṣaḥ—***  
***suhṛt-pakṣo bhaved iṣṭa-sādhako’niṣṭa-bādhakaḥ \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The friendly group: The friendly group accomplishes what is favorable to one’s group and prevents what is unfavorable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The friendly group gives whatever help it can for fulfilling the goals of one’s own group, while being completely friendly. Or, the qualifying factor is being friendly. It has friendship with deep affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The friendly group is that which helps the party accomplish its goals, and prevents obstacles to that goal. Thought this is a common characteristic within one’s one group as well, it is the distinguishing quality of the friendly group. The distinguishing quality within one’s group is the extreme sense of having one mind and one purpose.

### Text 5

*tatra iṣṭa-sādhakatvam, yathā—*  
***adyākarṇaya mad-giraṁ parijanair ebhiḥ samaṁ śyāmale***  
***rādhāyās tvayi sauhṛdaṁ sakhi jagac citteṣu citrīyate \|***  
***ullāsād bhavad ākhyayā yad aniśaṁ tasyāṅgarāgas tayā***  
***sāndraś candraka-śekharasya samaye candrānvitaḥ preṣyate \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Assisting a group in accomplishing their goal: My friend Śyāmalā! Please hear my impartial words along with your associates. Your friendship with Rādhā is such that the heart of the universe is astonished. Constantly calling your name in bliss, she gives you this thick ointment mixed with camphor for giving to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The genitive in *candraka-śekharasya* expresses “for the purpose of Kṛṣṇa.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundavallī, going to the house of Śyāmā; and sitting amongst their group, speaks. Hear my words today. Actually every day we relish Rādhā’s words. Today I will let you relish Rādhā’s words. My words are impartial (*samam*). Do not think the words are false. Even some among this group will be witnesses to this. Rādhā’s friendship with you shines like a painted picture on the wall of the hearts of the women dwelling in the universe. This means that anyone who experiences the friendship will experience most astonishing bliss in their heart. Constantly calling your name she has sent special ointment prepared by herself of sandalwood, *aguru, kuṁkuma* and musk mixed with camphor for Kṛṣṇa’s limbs. “My lover Kṛṣṇa should give *saubhāgya* to Śyāmā as he does to me.” With that intention Rādhā calls one of your members and says, “O friend! Take this ointment and go to Kṛṣṇa. When he asks, say that Śyāmalā has made it with her own hands for him and that you are delivering it.”

### Text 6

*aniṣṭa-bādhakatvaṁ, yathā—*  
***gīrbhir mūḍha-janasya khaṇḍita-matir bhāṇḍīra-mūle mudhā***  
***kiṁ gantāsmi tavodite balavatī śyāme pratītir mama \|***  
***nirvyājaṁ baṭa-rāja-rodhasi vadhū-veśa-kriyodbhāsinā***  
***kaṁsāriḥ subalena goṣṭha-nagarī-vaihāsikaḥ krīḍati \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Preventing misfortune for the other group: I was misled by the words of a foolish girl. Why should I go to Bhāṇḍira-baṭa? By your words I have understood everything. It is clear. The clown who jokes with the cowherd women is playing with Subala dressed as Rādhā beneath the banyan tree.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The old woman Jaṭilā speaks. There was no relationship between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā but only a joke being enacted by Kṛṣṇa and Subala. Therefore Kṛṣṇa is called a clown.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Instigated by Padmā, Jaṭilā angrily goes to Bhāṇḍīra. By chance Śyāmalā comes and deceives her on the way, so that she is satisfied. She then speaks to Śyāmalā. I have been misled by the words of Padmā who does not know the truth. Why should I go there? “If you want to, go there.” You have explained everything. Baṭarāja is Bhāṇḍīra. Subala appears radiate with the clothing and actions such as movements of the hands, eyes and neck of Rādhā. There is no relationship between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā. It is only a joke on old women of Vraja like us. Kṛṣṇa will say, “O Jaṭilā! Seeing your daughter-in-law with unhappy mind, I quickly made her happy by giving her my touchstone. Seeing its direct effect, consider your house fortunate. Please give me something as a reward.” He will abuse me with joking in this way. Therefore I will not go there.

### Text 7

***atha taṭasthaḥ—***  
***yo vipakṣa-suhṛt-pakṣaḥ sa taṭastha ihocyate \|\|7\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The group which is friendly with the opposing group is called borderline.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The borderline or neutral group, because it is friendly with the opposing group, but does not do anything to create hostility to one’s group, does not show hatred to the group as the opposing group does.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The neutral group is friendly to the opposing group. *Udāsīno ‘ri-vad varjya*

*ātma-vat suhṛd ucyate*: one who is neutral may be avoided like an enemy, but a friend should be considered like one’s own self. (SB 10.24.5) This means that the neutral party is like an enemy, but not an enemy. The friend is like the self, but not the self. The friend is not a wife, son or servant (same as self), but is beneficial for the self. Thus the friendly party is different from one’s own party, but performs beneficial acts for it. This is the quality of the friendly party. There is similarity of one’s own party and the friendly party since both give one benefit. Thus the ending *vat* (like) is used (*ātmavat*). Since the neutral party is beneficial to the enemy party it is called a friend to it. Therefore one cannot put one’s faith in it. One disregards it. Because the friendly party gives benefit one gives respect to it.

### Text 8

***yathā—***  
***khedaṁ na vyasane tanoṣi vahase nollāsam asyāḥ śubhe***  
***doṣāṇāṁ prakaṭīkṛtau na hi dhiyaṁ dhatse guṇānām api \|***  
***avyākṣipta-mano-gatiḥ suvadane dveṣeṇa rāgeṇa ca***  
***tvaṁ śyāme muni-vṛttir atra satataṁ candrāvalau dṛśyase \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My dear beautiful-faced Śyāmā! You feel neither joy in Candrāvalī’s good fortune nor distress at her misfortune. You take no account of her virtues or faults. Your mind is not moved by either love or hatred for her. You appear just like a silent sage, neutral in relation to her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā scold Śyāmā, criticizing her in the guise of praise. When Candrāvalī meets misfortune you do not lament. The hint is that she rejoices. When Candrāvalī has good fortune, Śyāmā is not happy, but rather laments. She does not consider Candrāvalī’s faults by expressing them, but secretly acts against her, since she is the helper of Rādhā. She does not name her good qualities but only alludes to them. In order to hide her emotions she creates a false impression. She does not show that she notices her good qualities, but does so secretly. Your mind is not subject to self derision in love or hatred, or by anger and hatred. You have no repentance such as “I hate Candrāvalī though she is innocent. What a mind I have!” O woman with a smiling face! You are full of glee. Your face reveals your nature. You are like a sage. Without saying a word, you achieve all your intended plans.

The neutral party appears to be neutral while showing signs of benefiting the opposing group. This neutral group does not have internal and external neutrality, with actions neither beneficial nor harmful to one’s group. This would not produce *rasa.*

### Text 9

***atha vipakṣaḥ—***  
***mitho-dveṣī vipakṣaḥ syād iṣṭahāniṣṭa-kārakaḥ \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The enemy: A group which hates another group is the opposing party, blocks accomplishment of the other’s goals and causes it problems.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Persons who mutually hate each other become mutually opposing groups. They then block the goals of the other party and cause problems.

### Text 10

*tatra iṣṭa-hantṛtvaṁ, yathā—*  
***rādhe tvat-padavī-niveśita-dṛśaṁ kuñje hariṁ jānatī***  
***padmā tatra nināya hanta kuṭilā candrāvalīṁ chadmanā \|***  
***ity ākarṇya mukunda sā subalataḥ stabdhā tathādya sthitā***  
***dṛṣṭvā nīla-paṭīṁ tanau jaṭilayā prātar yathā tarjitā \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Obstructing the other party’s goals: "O Rādhā, Padmā saw Kṛṣṇa as he gazed at the path on which you would come, and by a trick she has now brought Candrāvalī to this place." Ever since Rādhā heard that from Subala, she remains silent, even today in the morning, just as if Jaṭilā were to see her wearing blue cloth in the early morning and started scolding her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Jaṭilā began scolding her because she thought Rādhā was wearing blue cloth in order to meet Kṛṣṇa in the dark or she was wearing cloth of his complexion out of attraction to him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. From the previous night until today Rādhā remains stunned as if being scolded by Jaṭilā. This was caused by fear, without her being aware of it. Wearing blue cloth indicates an appointment in the dark and she as well was wearing ornaments. “O cause of blackness on our two families! Can you live in our house while wearing cloth and ornaments indicating some appointment? Did you not meet your messengers like Lalitā today? Get up. I say, go to your illicit lover and do not come back to my house. I will go to Mathurā right now with my son to find a cure for you two.”

### Text 11

*atha aniṣṭa-kāritvaṁ, yathā—*  
***kutaḥ padme putri kṣiti-dhara-taṭād amba jaṭile***  
***vadhūr dṛṣṭā kva nu ravi-niketasya purataḥ \|***  
***ciraṁ nāyāty eṣā katham iva niruddhātra hariṇā***  
***tavādhvānaṁ paśyaty ahaha bhavatī dhāvatu ruṣā \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Causing problems:**

**My dear daughter Padmā, where have you been?**

**Padmā: Mother Jaṭilā, I have come from Govardhana Hill.**

**Jaṭilā: Did you see Rādhā? Where?**

**Padmā: She was in front of the sun-god's temple.**

**Jaṭilā: Why has Rādhā not come here after so long?**

**Padmā: Kṛṣṇa stopped her coming here. She is on the lookout for you. You must run there in anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Jaṭilā and Padmā talk. The meaning is clear. You must run there to catch them, since Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will go to another place after their enjoyment.

### Text 12

***chadmerṣyā-cāpalāsūyā-matsarāmarṣa-garvitam \|***  
***vyaktiṁ yāty ukti-ceṣṭābhiḥ pratipakṣa-sakhīṣv idam \|\|12\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The party shows the following qualities in their words and actions toward the opposing party: deception, malice, insolence, envy, jealousy, anger and pride.**

### Text 13

*tatra chadma, yathā—*  
***śrutvā kīcakam adri-mūrdhni paśavaḥ śyāmaṁ ca dṛṣṭvāmbudaṁ***  
***dhāvantv alpa-dhiyaḥ kathaṁ tvam api dhig dhīrādhikaṁ dhāvasi \|***  
***ity uccair anṛtottareṇa taralāṁ pratyāyya padmām asau***  
***prāptā paśya gṛhaṁ karoti lalitā rādhā-prayāṇe tvarām \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Deception: Thinking the sound of bamboos in the wind to be Kṛṣṇa’s flute and thinking the rain-cloud on the peak of Govardhana Hill to be dark-complexioned Kṛṣṇa, these unintelligent cows are now running towards him. O Padmā! You are also running there. So much for your great intelligence! Speaking in a loud voice some expert lies, Lalitā deceived fickle Padmā, and then quickly ran to Rādhā's house to bring her to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Lalitā went to Rādhā’s house (*gṛhaṁ prāptā*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhānumatī speaks to Maṇimañjarī. *Kīcaka* is a type of bamboo that makes a sound. According to *Amara-koṣa* this bamboo makes a sound in the wind. Thinking the sound of bamboos to be Kṛṣṇa’s flute and the cloud to be Kṛṣṇa, the cows come running. O Padmā! You are also running. How unfortunate for you and your intelligence. Making her perceive Kṛṣṇa as a cloud (*pratyāyya*), she went to bring Rādhā.

### Text 14

*atha īrṣyā, yathā—*  
***udghaṭayya kuṭilaṁ kaca-pakṣaṁ***  
***devi darśayasi kiṁ vana-mālām \|***  
***nīla-yaṣṭivad amuṁ mad-alinde***  
***lokayāli vana-mālinam eva \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Malice: Why do you push aside your hair and show off this garland of flowers? O friend! Look at this person wearing a garland stretched out like a blue stick on my porch.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kaca-pakṣam* means all her hair. *Pakṣa* means hair according to *Amara-koṣa*. The statement is made out of malice.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā was flaunting her good fortune with Kṛṣṇa by showing off her garland given by him. Seeing her on the path, Lalitā speaks. *Kaca-pakṣam* means all her hair. We know your hair is curled. You are showing off the beauty of those curls. They are fine and glossy, not like ours. “Kṛṣṇa is like a blue stick.” This indicates he is stunned with *sāttvika-bhāva* on her porch. He has fallen into that state because of joy on seeing Rādhā or because of fear that Padmā has come near. She becomes envious. “Look friend! See! He has come to my house. Only if you can get close to him, I suppose he could give you that garland. You must have picked up from the path an old garland that fell from his neck and put it on your head. This is what I think happened.” In this way she shows her malice.

### Text 15

***yathā vā—***  
***nirbandha-pravaṇena kaṁsa-ripuṇā prāg arpyamāṇo’pi yaḥ***  
***prājyaṁ doṣam avekṣya nāyaka-maṇau na svīkṛto’bhūn mayā \|***  
***hāraḥ samprati so’yam eva viṣamo lubdhe kva labdhas tvayā***  
***drāg iṣṭo’py uraga-kṣatāṅguli-nibho duṣṭaḥ sakhi tyajyatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example of malice: Kṛṣṇa begged me to take this necklace, but I refused because the jewel in the center is seriously flawed. Such a flawed necklace is dangerous. What will it benefit you? Though it has been given by him, you should throw the evil thing away, just as a finger bitten by a snake must be cut off.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prājyam* means grave.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pure malice was described. Now malice rooted in envy is described. Padmā speaks to some *sakhī* she meets on the path. Though he is eager to have you accept the necklace using clever words and humility, saying “Please take it,” though he offers it, you should not accept it. Why? There is a serious flaw in the main jewel. That is bad luck for the wearer. That is known to me. Though it has been given by Kṛṣṇa, you should throw it away. Though it is painful to give up, you should be tolerant. A finger bitten by a snake is cut off even though it is part of the body. If one does not do so, one will die. I am instructing you confidentially.

### Text 16

***atha cāpalam—***  
***nātmānaṁ vyathaya vṛthā nikuñja-madhye***  
***khadyoti dyutim iha kurvatī sa-rāgam \|***  
***kṛṣṇābhre girivara-saṅgate’ nurūpā***  
***somābhā vilasitum atra vidyud eva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Insolence: You are performing services with passion in this grove. Do not needlessly trouble yourself. At Govardhana the lightning Candrāvalī is suitable to engage in pastimes with the dark cloud Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The lightning named Somābhā is suitable to enjoy with Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One *sakhī* of Rādhā brought her to the appointed bower but not seeing Kṛṣṇa there went to the side of Govardhana to search for him. Seeing Kṛṣṇa with Candrāvalī in a bower there, she began to think of the consequences. Recognizing her as Rādhā’s *sakhī*, Padmā spoke to her with envy, calling her a firefly. You are giving off light with color (you are doing match making with passion). Do not bring sorrow to yourself. Your desires will not be accomplished today. The lightning named Somābhā-- she who has the complexion of golden Durgā--is suitable to engage in pastimes with the black cloud Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 17

***atha āsūyā—***  
***yad bhāṇḍīre tava sahacarī tāṇḍavaṁ sā vyatānīt***  
***padme śaivyā samajani na tat kasya vismāpanāya \|***  
***sā cet tanvī prakṛti-laḍahā śikṣitā cābhaviṣyan***  
***manye sarvaṁ jagad api tataḥ prekṣayāmohayiṣyat \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Envy: O Padmā! No one is astonished by your friend Śaibyā dancing at Bhāṇḍīra. If slender Saibyā had learned dancing from you, I think she would have charmed the entire world just by her glance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prakṛti-laḍahā* means naturally beautiful.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Raṅgadevī speaks to Padmā. If that naturally beautiful woman has been taught by you, or if she were skilful (*śikṣitā*) like you, she would have enchanted the whole world.

### Text 18

***atha matsaraḥ—***  
***alaṁcakre rādhā-hṛdayam uru-hāreṇa hariṇā***  
***srajā dhūrteneyaṁ tava tu kavara-śrīr avarayā \|***  
***mano dvandvātītaṁ munivad avikalpaṁ ca dadhatī***  
***tathāpi tvaṁ mugdhe na vipina-vinodād viramasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Jealousy: O charming girl, although Kṛṣṇa decorated Rādhā's heart with a valuable necklace, and decorated your braided hair with an inferior garland, your mind is situated beyond all dualities, and, like a great sage, you do not make distinctions between good and bad. O innocent girl! You do not refuse pastimes with him in the forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Your braid is decorated with an inferior garland. Or he decorates Rādhā’s heart with a garland of precious jewels, and decorates your braid with a cheap, ugly one. Instead of *dhūrteneyam* sometimes *kṛṣṇeneyam* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Candrāvalī. Rādhā is decorated with a necklace of great value, and Candrāvalī with one worth a few pennies, and one which is ugly as well.

### Text 19

***atha amarṣaḥ—***  
***sphuṭadbhir iva korakair alaghubhiś ca guñjā-phalair***  
***mayādya viracayya yan muraharāya viśrāṇitam \|***  
***tvayātra sakhi rādhikā-śravasi vīkṣya tat-kuṇḍalaṁ***  
***manaḥ svam udaghāṭi yat tad atilāghavāyaiva naḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Anger: My friend, I have made earrings from ripe bunches of large** ***guñja*** **berries, and you have personally presented them to Kṛṣṇa. When I see that earring on Rādhā's ear, it makes my mind grieve since we are so insignificant to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Viśrāntam* means given.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī scolds her *sakhī* out of love.  *Viśrāntam* means given. That earring produces great sorrow in my mind. It makes us insignificant. In order to kill her pride, appearing very gracious, you should make something up by indirect hints. Though it is a lie you should to say, “Candrāvalī is skilful and this is known by all the young girls of Vraja. O Rādhā *(sakhī*)! Kṛṣṇa has given you this earring to astonish you. “ Or you could say, “O friend! Seeing an earring that had fallen on the bank of the Yamunā, one *sakhī* has taken it and put it in your ear.” She has disturbed your mind completely.

### Text 20

***atha garvitam—***  
***ahaṅkāro’bhimānaś ca darpa uddhasitaṁ tathā \|***  
***mada auddhatyam ity eṣa garvaḥ ṣoḍhā nigadyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pride: Pride is said to have six types:** ***ahaṅkāra, abhimāna, darpa, uddhasita, mada*****, and** ***auddhatya*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Garvitam* means pride. The common characteristic is disregard for others.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Garvitam* means pride. The common characteristic is disregard for others. The six items listed are varieties of this.

### Text 21

***atra ahaṅkāraḥ—***  
***ahaṅkāraḥ parākṣepaḥ svapakṣa-guṇa-varṇanāt \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ahaṅkāra*** **means to deride others by glorifying one’s own group’s qualities.**

### Text 22

***yathā—***  
***ākāśe ruci-lavam indra-nīla-śobhe***  
***somābhā janayati tāvad-asphuṭa-śrīḥ \|***  
***netrāṇāṁ timira-harā vareṇya-dīptiḥ***  
***sā yāvan na hi vṛṣabhānujābhyudeti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The moon giving off faint beauty produces a drop of splendor in the sky, dark as a sapphire, until the brilliant sun of Jyeṣṭha month, having the greatest brightness, rises in the sky and destroys darkness for our eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Candrāvalī has indistinct beauty because Rādhā has the highest beauty. The *sakhī* speaks with *ahaṅkāra* to unsettle her opponent. Using the phrase “particle of brilliance” conveys the same. Candrāvalī produces only a drop of splendor in the sky, in the huge expanse (ā + kāś), Kṛṣṇa. The light of the moon conquers the stars. Candrāvalī is greater than Tārakā. She can do this as long as the sun (Rādhā) does not appear.

Instead of *vṛṣabhānujā* sometimes *sakhī bhānujā* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One time Lalitā went to the assembly of Candrāvalī. Padmā said “Candrāvalī makes the sky of Kṛṣṇa splendorous.” Lalitā replies. Her indistinct beauty produces a little splendor in the sky having the brilliance of a blue sapphire. This also means “She produces a speck of satisfaction in Kṛṣṇa who is completely manifested *(ākāśe*). Her beauty is indistinct because it is covered by Kṛṣṇa’s beauty. Or her beauty is covered by the darkness. *Vṛṣabhānujā* means the light produced by the sun during Jyeṣṭha month. It also means Rādhā. When Rādhā makes her appearance, the sky of Kṛṣṇa becomes most auspicious.

### Text 23

***abhimānaḥ—***  
***abhimāno nija-premotkarṣākhyānaṁ tu bhaṅgitaḥ \|\|23\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhimāna*** **means showing the superiority of one’s own love using inferences.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Reciting the great love that one’s party holds for him. The word *nija* indicates one’s own group. This is understood from the previous definition.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This means “recounting the excellence of one’s own group’s *(nija) prema*”.

### Text 24

***tatra kṛṣṇe svapakṣa-premākhyānaṁ, yathā—***  
***tvaṁ dhīra-dhīḥ phaṇi-hrade hari-jhampa-gāthāṁ***  
***niṣkampam eva yad iyaṁ gadituṁ pravṛttā \|***  
***tatrānuṣaṅgikatayāpy udite kadambe***  
***vakṣaḥ pinaṣṭi rudatī taralā sakhī me \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Announcing one’s group’s** ***prema*** **for Kṛṣṇa: O Candrāvalī! When you recite the story of Kṛṣṇa jumping into the Kāliya Lake, you remained calm. My friend Rādhā, having an unsteady mind, wails and pounds her breasts in lamentation as soon as she hears the word** ***kadamba*** **in an unrelated discussion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In using praise to criticize the secondary *rasa* of *hāsya* is covered because of the appearance of pride. The word “jump” indicates that he entered the water with force from a high place. Just by uttering a word related to the jump, Rādhā begins crying. Taking this opportunity Lalitā speaks with malice, because of the highest level of prema in Rādhā among all the Vraja women.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Candrāvalī. Kṛṣṇa jumped from a high place, from the *kadamba* tree into the water. Rādhā, hearing the word *kadamba* in relation to some other matter, not even saying it herself, cries and beats her chest. I do not know what would happen if she heard the whole story of Kāliya. This is because she is very emotional. Though you have *prema*, in chanting about the story of Kāliya you do not change. You have complete control. This statement shows the superiority of Rādhā in her love of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 25

***svapakṣe kṛṣṇa-premākhyānaṁ, yathā—***  
***dhanyāsi kṛṣṇa-kara-kalpita-patra-vallī***  
***ramyālikā viharase mada-mantharāṅgī \|***  
***hā vañcitāsmi kalite lalitā-mukhendau***  
***jāḍyaṁ sa yāty akhila-śilpa-dhurandharo’pi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Announcing Kṛṣṇa’s love for one’s own group: You are fortunate. You are wearing** ***tilaka*** **painted by the hand of Kṛṣṇa on your forehead. Your limbs are languid with passion. I have been cheated. Seeing the moon-like face of Lalitā, Kṛṣṇa, the chief of all artisans, simply becomes stunned.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Alikā* is forehead.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Ratnaprabhā, a s*akhī* of Lalitā, speaks to Padmā whom she meets her on a path.  *Alikā* means forehead. “You are fortunate.” Padmā says “You are well known as independent lovers. Why do you speak like this?” “We have been cheated. Seeing (*kalite*) the face of Lalitā, Kṛṣṇa becomes stunned.” This shows the superiority of Kṛṣṇa’s love for Lalitā compared his love for the opposing party.

### Text 26

***darpaḥ—***  
***garvam ācakṣate darpaṁ vihārotkarṣa-sūcakam \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pride which shows the superiority of one’s pastimes with Kṛṣṇa is called** ***darpa.***

### Text 27

***yathā—***  
***vidmaḥ puṇyavatī-śikhāmaṇim iha tvām eva harmye yayā***  
***nīyante śaradindu-dhāma-dhavalāḥ svāpotsavena kṣapāḥ \|***  
***ko’yaṁ naḥ phalati sma karma-viṭapī vṛndāṭavī-kandare***  
***śyāmaḥ ko’pi karī karoti hṛdayonmādena nidrā-kṣayam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Padmā! I think you must be the crest jewel of all pious girls, for only you are able to sleep peacefully on the rooftop during these autumn nights, white with moonlight. The tree of** ***karma*** **is fructifying. This dark-complexioned elephant with maddened heart breaks my sleep in the Vṛndāvana forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The elephant breaks my sleep. Actually she pretends to sleep and remains awake. The word *śyāma* indicates she is actually speaking of Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Once Nāndīmukhī was reciting Purāṇic stories somehow related to Kṛṣṇa in an assembly of young women and Lalitā was listening. Seeing Lalitā’s eyes rolling, Padmā began to laugh. Lalitā speaks to her. You have done pious acts in previous births that we have not done. The tree of *karma* has given its fruit. Otherwise how is it possible that we suffer from staying awake in mountain caves covered with darkness, depending on full moon nights? It is impossible to have the good fortune of hearing pious stories in the day because of our tiredness. By this she indicates that her group has enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa and the opposing party does not.

### Text 28

***uddhasitam—***  
***upahāso vipakṣasya sākṣād uddhasitaṁ bhavet \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Laughing at the opposing party is called** ***uddhasitam.***

### Text 29

***yathā—***  
***noccair niḥśvasihi prasīda parame muñca grahaṁ durlabhe***  
***mlāniṁ te sakhi vīkṣya hanta kṛpayā mac-cittam uttāmyati \|***  
***baddhaḥ paśya vibhaṅgure’tra lalitā-vāg-vāgurāḍambare***  
***jānīte na kila svam eva sarale śyāmaḥ kuraṅgī-patiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My friend, please do not sigh in this way. Be content. Give up striving for the unattainable. When I see you so faded, my heart becomes tortured with compassion. O honest, pious friend! Look, the black deer of Kṛṣṇa has fallen into the great snare of Lalitā's crooked words. He is not aware of himself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vāgura* is a trap.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā had brought Candrāvalī to meet Kṛṣṇa and then went to find Kṛṣṇa. She saw at a distance Lalitā talking to Kṛṣṇa. Viśākhā then speaks to disappointed Padmā. Considering this your fate, cutting lamentation by discrimination, become happy. Become free from the desire for rare things such as taking Kṛṣṇa. “Why do you say this?” Your face is faded. “There is no solution for this.” See with your eyes. He is caught in the effort of the trap of her very crooked (*vibhaṅgura*) words. *Viśva-koṣa* says *āḍambara* means an undertaking. Padmā says, “Remembering my *sakhī*, and cheating Lalitā, I will bring him to her.” He is not aware of himself, what to speak of recognizing your *sakhī.* He has forgotten everything concerning his body because of intoxication with her sweet words. You should no longer reflect on this at all.

### Text 30

***madaḥ—***  
***sevādy-utkarṣakṛd garvo mada ity abhidhīyate \|\|30\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pride arising from excellence of service is called** ***mada.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sevā* means serving Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 31

***yathā—***  
***jagati lalite dhanyā yūyaṁ sugandhibhir adbhutai***  
***ravir aviratiṁ yābhiḥ puṣpair amībhir upāsyate \|***  
***bata vidhi-vaśāj jātaṁ vanya-sraji vyasanaṁ tathā***  
***dalam api na naḥ kātyāyanyai yathā pariśiṣyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Lalitā! I think you are the most fortunate girl in the entire universe, for you constantly worship the sun-god with these fragrant, wonderful flowers. I am not so fortunate. When we make garlands of flowers, Candrāvalī and my friends take them all and do not leave even a single petal to offer to goddess Katyāyanī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Lalitā who is picking flowers for worshipping the sun god. “Why do you not worship Katyāyanī?” We do not have such good fortune. We are attached (*vyasanam*) to making flower garlands. Whatever flowers and leaves the *sakhīs* pick are used for making a garland for Candrāvalī. She does not have devotion to her deity as Rādhā does.

### Text 32

***auddhatyam—***  
***spaṣṭaṁ svotkṛṣṭatākhyānam auddhatyam iti kīrtyate \|\|32\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Clearly speaking of one’s own excellence is called** ***auddhatya.***

### Text 33

***yathā—***  
***kas tāvad vraja-maṇḍale sa valate gāndharvikā spardhatāṁ***  
***sārdhaṁ hanta janena yena jagatī-jaṅghāla-kīrti-dhvajā \|***  
***kulyāyāḥ kṛpaṇāvalīṣu kṛpayā kāmaṁ dravac-cetaso***  
***yasyāḥ preraṇayā kṣaṇaṁ bhavati vaḥ padme niṣevyo hariḥ \|\|33\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Who in Vraja can compete with Rādhā, whose victory flag dominates the world? O Padmā, it is only because her heart melts with compassion for you wretches that you are able to serve Kṛṣṇa for even a moment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā has a flag of fame swiftly traveling the universe. By mercy to wretches like you among noble women, you can approach Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“O Nāndīmukhī! The time has come for Rādhā to compete with Candrāvalī. We compare Rādhā to star and Candrāvalī to the moon.” When Lalitā hiding in the bushes heard Padmā say this, she emerged from the creepers and spoke with zeal. Who in Vraja has this ability? She has the flag of fame, spreading quickly throughout the universe. *Jaṅghāla* means very fast. The goal is to conquer all fame while going fast. While Rādhā is in Vraja, it is not possible for you to touch Kṛṣṇa’s limbs.

“Not attaining association with Kṛṣṇa, burning with the fire of great desire, they will die.” Thinking in this way, having a soft heart, Rādhā is merciful to these miserly women from noble families.

### Text 34

***kiṁ ca—***  
***śliṣṭoktiś ca kvacit tāsāṁ nindā-garbhopajāyate \|\|34\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Some** ***sakhīs*** **use puns to criticize.**

### Text 35

***yathā—***  
***govindāhita-maṇḍanā vidhuratāvāpti-prasaṅgojjhitā***  
***dakṣānalpa-kalā vayo-ghana-ruciṁ tanvā muhus tanvatī \|***  
***sarvānuttama-sādhutā-pada-kṛtir bhavye bhavatyāḥ sakhī***  
***nāsau bhāgya-bharāt kadāpi viratiṁ prāpnoti saudāminī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My dear Bhavyā! Your friend Saudāminī is decorated with ornaments presented to her by Govinda. She becomes very unhappy when she is separated from him. She is very expert in the arts. Her body displays the intense beauty of youthfulness. Her actions contain the highest good conduct. Her good fortune will never end.**

**Your friend’s ornaments are disliked by Kṛṣṇa. He enjoys with other women when he is not in her presence. She is expert at quarrelling and radiates the beauty of an iron hammer. Her low actions give pain to the good people. She never ceases to have misfortune.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She is decorated with ornaments given by Kṛṣṇa or her decorations are disliked by Kṛṣṇa. She becomes sad in separation from him, or when she is separated from him he enjoys with others. She is expert in many arts and radiates the beauty of youth (*vayo-ghana-rucim*), or she is expert in many quarrels (*dakṣā analpa-kalau*) and radiates the beauty of an iron hammer (*ayo-ghana-rucim*). She is the best or is the least among all. Saudāmanī does not cease to possess abundant good fortune (*asau sakhī bhāgya-bharāt*), or she does not cease to have abundant misfortune (*asaubhāgya-bharāt*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Campakalatā speaks to a *sakhī* of Candrāvalī names Bhavyā concerning judging beauty, qualities and prema of sakhīs in an assembly. Saudāmanī is decorated with ornaments given by Kṛṣṇa, or her decorations are disliked by Kṛṣṇa. In separation she grieves or he enjoys with others when they are separate. She has intense beauty of youth with full skills or she has the beauty of an iron hammer and is expert in many quarrels.  *Ghana* means a hammer according to *Amara-koṣa.* Her actions are the abode of the highest good conduct, or her actions which are the worst give pain to good people. O Bhavyā *sakhī*! That person (*asau*), your *sakhī* Saudāmanī does not cease to have good fortune or your *sakhī* does not cease to have misfortune.

### Text 36

***yathā vā—***  
***samasta-jana-locanotsava-vinoda-niṣpādinī***  
***vilakṣaṇa-gati-kriyā-vicalitāṅga-hāra-sthitiḥ \|***  
***nirasya haritālajaṁ ruci-taraṅgam ātmorjitaiḥ***  
***sakhī naṭati te rasa-skhalitam atra khelāvatī \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Your friend Khelavatī produces pleasure and joy for the eyes of all people by her dancing. Her necklace becomes stunned by those extraordinary movements. By the power of teaching, she defeats waves of beauty arising from yellow** ***haritāla*** **ointment. She dances with special steps.**

**Your friend destroys joy in the eyes of all people by her dancing. Her necklace becomes displaced by her awkward movements. By her fickle nature she drives away the waves of beauty derived from Kṛṣṇa’s keeping the rhythm. She dances with deviation from** ***rasa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Her dancing is a pleasant joy for the eyes of all people or her dancing drives away the eyes of all people. Her movements are so remarkable that her necklace on her limbs do not move, or her movements, against those prescribed in the scriptures, move her bodily ornaments out of place. She defeats the beauty of yellow *haritāla* paste or she drives away the pleasant performance created by Kṛṣṇa’s rhythms in dancing. By the *śakti* of teaching the body, Khelavatī dances with special dance steps, or by her fickle nature she dances with deviation from *rasa.* The word *khelatvaī* also indicates that she is frivolous like a child.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Criticism is of two types: criticizing *prema* and criticizing qualities. The previous verse criticized *prema.* This verse criticizes qualities. Raṅgadevī speaks to Śaibyā. *Vinoda* means pleasure and driving away. She dances so remarkable by cause of skill in learning, that her necklace on her body does not move from its place, or she moves her limbs so that she stumbles around with confused gestures (*aṅga-hāra*) because of making movements which are not according to scriptures. *Aṅga-hāra* means “throwing the limbs around” according to *Amara-koṣa.* She defeats waves of beauty from *haritāla,* by the power of beauty of her body (*ātmorjjitaiḥ),* or she destroys the pleasure of rhythms produced by Kṛṣṇa by the fickle life airs of her body.  *Ūrja* means strength and life air. She dances with special steps, without deviating from *rasa* or she dances while deviating from *rasa.*

### Text 37

***yās tu yūthābhināthāḥ syuḥ sākṣān nerṣyanti tāḥ sphuṭam \|***  
***vipakṣāya sva-gāmbhīrya-maryādādi-guṇodayāt \|\|37\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because the heads of the groups have qualities such as profundity and sense of propriety, they do not personally express hatred of the opposing group in a clear manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous descriptions concerned the *sakhīs*. Do the leaders also act in this way towards the opposing party? This verse answers.

### Text 38

***yathā—***  
***vipakṣa-ramaṇī-sakhīṁ piśunitorugarvacchaṭāṁ***  
***vilokya kila maṅgalā virala-hāsa-phenojjvalam \|***  
***tatāna tam anākulaṁ vinaya-nirjharaṁ yena sā***  
***nije tarasi majjitā sapadi lajjitā vivyathe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When she sees the excessive pride of a rival** ***gopī,*** **Maṅgalā shows a beautiful form with a rare smile like the foam of a river produced by its calmness. By that cascade of modesty, she becomes inundated in its current. She now feels pain because of her shyness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Piśunita* means showing. She becomes drowned in current of the cascade of modesty.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Seeing a *sakhī* of the opposing group manifesting excessive pride, understanding it by some symptoms, the *sakhī* shows a beautiful but slight smile. By the cascade of modesty she became submerged in its current. Being shy, she was later pained by remorse.

### Text 39

***vipakṣa-yūtha-nāthāyāḥ purataḥ prakaṭaṁ na hi \|***  
***jalpanti laghavaḥ serṣyaṁ prāyaśaḥ prakharā api \|\|39\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Though** ***sakhīs*** **may be** ***prakharā*** **they do not generally speak with hatred in front of the leader of the opposing group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Laghavaḥ* means the *sakhīs,* who are inferior to the leaders.

### Text 40

***yathā—***  
***diṣṭyā dustarato mad-ukti-nigaḍān muktāsi mugdhe kṣaṇād***  
***abhyarṇe vṛṣabhānujā vijayate yad bhānujāyās taṭe \|***  
***nātathyaṁ prathayāmi devy api girāṁ vāg-dyūta-kelīṣu me***  
***nirdhūta-pratibhodgamā bhagavatī lajjārṇave majjati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O charming girl! Luckily, you have been released from the great shackles of my words, difficult to overcome, for Rādhā has now come to the nearby shore of the Yamunā River. I do not reveal what is untrue. During a contest of words Sarasvatī, the goddess of eloquence, who has spotless genius, sinks in the ocean of shame at my sport.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mugdhe* means “O innocent girl.” Taking this moment (*kṣaṇāt*) you have been freed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

At a distance Padmā, with anger, respect and trembling, speaks to Campakalatā who criticizes her clearly with false praise. O young girl! By fate for a moment you are free from the chains of my words. If you stay a little longer, when Rādhā leaves I will give you exactly what you deserve. Rādhā is nearby (*abhyarṇe*). I cannot boast in front of her. It is improper. Hear about my skill in words. I do not reveal (*prathayāmi*) what is untrue. *Girām devī* is Sarasvatī.

### Text 41

***hari-priya-jane bhāvā dveṣādyā nocitā iti \|***  
***ye vyāharanti te jñeyā apūrva-rasikāḥ kṣitau \|\|41\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There is no one inferior in** ***rasa*** **on earth to those who say that the followers of the Lord should not indulge in qualities like hatred.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Apūrva-rasikāḥ* is a pun which actually means “those who are not rasikas.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Apūrva-rasikāḥ* means persons who unprecedented *rasa.* However this is a pun and actually means “persons who have not had *rasa* previously.”

### Text 42

***yathā vā—***  
***saṁmohanasya kandarpa-vṛndebhyo’py agha-vidviṣaḥ \|***  
***mūrto narma-priya-sakhaḥ śṛṅgāro vartate vraje \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The personification of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa,*** **the great friend of Kṛṣṇa, killer of Agha, who is more charming than a multitude of Cupids, exists in Vraja.**

### Text 43

***kṣipen mitho vijātīya-bhāvayor eṣa pakṣayoḥ \|***  
***īrṣyādīn sva-parivārān yoge sva-preṣṭha-tuṣṭaye \|***  
***ata eva hi viśleṣe snehas tāsāṁ prakāśate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa is present,** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa*** **creates hatred and jealousy between the two camps of rival** ***gopīs*** **in order to please Kṛṣṇa. When Kṛṣṇa is absent, it produces affection amongst them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ordinary *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is accepted in scriptures as most brilliant because of the relationships of the man and woman. How much more brilliant is the *śṛṅgāra-rasa* of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Kṛṣṇa is more enchanting than a multitude of Cupids. This shows the extreme greed of all the *gopīs* for enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa. He bewilders even Cupid: *sākṣād manmatha-manmathaḥ*. (SB 10.32.2) Though the great Cupid and the associates of *śṛṅgāra* exist in Vraja, enjoyment with the women cannot take place simultaneously, unlike the services of other devotees. Therefore, there is hatred between the women. However, Kṛṣṇa, the killer of Agha, is the shelter of all beings and possesses the highest powers, since he can give liberation. Just as one should take a *devatā* body to act among the *devatās* one should take a human body to act among humans. Thus *śṛṅgāra-rasa* takes the role of *priya-narma-sakha* in Vraja, taking into consideration the dearest of *sakhīs.* Existing there, he instigates his associates--hatred, jealousy and other traits. But if he does not make distinctions, then how can friendship between *sakhīs* take place at all? It takes place mutually between parties with different types of love. Just as ordinary people with differing qualities form opposing parties, so the groups of *gopīs* with differing types of love for Kṛṣṇa form opposing parties. Because they mutually have no appreciation, it is possible for hatred to take place between them. Similarly young couples appreciate each other but not other couples.

Similarity and differences in the type of love are shown. One should not say that Kṛṣṇa would not tolerate this. This is done for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. Enmity between groups nourishes Kṛṣṇa’s attraction for them. When his attraction is nourished, he is satisfied. *Vyabhicāri-bhāvas*, though opposing elements, nourish the *sthāyi-bhāva.* Hatred and other emotions appear externally in the *gopīs,* but not internally.

Just as the senses live for themselves, this enmity takes place when Kṛṣṇa is present, but not when he is not in Vraja. The senses in waking state compete for their own enjoyment and desire their own selfish satisfaction. In deep sleep, indifferent to their own endeavors, they all merge together and simply follow the *atman.* They do not compete in that state. Thus it is explained that hatred takes place when Kṛṣṇa is present, but when he is absent. When Kṛṣṇa is present, they do not experience his absence simultaneously. When he leaves Vraja however, they all experience separation at the same time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“How can someone whose mind is afflicted by lamentation and anger have a realization of Kṛṣṇa? How can hatred and other negative emotions which are said to be unfavorable for *sādhana* be favorable for persons who have reached perfection?” True, the transformations of mind such as attachment and hatred in the state of *sādhana* are material and are contrary to *bhakti.* However in the perfected state, the *antaḥkaraṇa* takes a form of *prema* and its functions of lamentation, bewilderment, attachment and hatred become forms of *prema* and do not impede *bhakti.*

*unmajjanti nimajjanti sthāyiny amṛta-vāridhau \|*  
*ūrmivad vardhayanty enaṁ yānti tad-rūpatāṁ ca te \|\|*

**All the** ***vyabhicāri- bhāvas*****, rising and falling like waves in the sweet ocean of the** ***sthāyi bhāva,*** **increase the** ***sthāyi bhāva*** **and become the svarūpa of the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****. BRS 2.4.3**

Thus, though *nirveda* and other *vyābhicāri-bhāvas* are qualities of the mind, and appear to forms of the material *guṇas*, they are actually beyond the *guṇas.* *The sthāyi-bhāva* is *prema,* and the *vyābhicāri-bhāvas* appear as forms of the *sthāyi-bhāva.* “Then perhaps *prema* is also material. What is the proof that *prema* is beyond the *guṇas*?” It is said *akṣaṇaṁ bhakti-yogasya nirguṇasya hy udāhṛtam*: *bhakti-yoga* is said to be beyond the *guṇas*. (SB 3.29.12*) Prema* is a transformation of that *bhakti. Bhaktyā sañjātayā bhaktyā bibhraty utpulakāṁ tanum*: one develops ecstatic symptoms by *prema* arising from *bhakti.* (SB 11.2.31) Moreover, if *prema* were material, then the statements in all scriptures that the Lord is dependent on *prema* would be meaningless. *Harir hi nirguṇaḥ sākṣāt puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ*: the Lord is beyond the *guṇas,* beyond *prakṛti.* (SB 10.88.5) Thus it is not suitable to say that the Lord beyond the *guṇas* is controlled by *prema* within the *guṇas.*

“Let that be. *Prema* is beyond the *guṇas.* But how can the functions of the mind also be beyond the *guṇas,* since the there is a relationship between the receptacle and what is in the receptacle. The *antahkaraṇa* is a receptacle of *bhakti* for those who begin the process of *bhakti,* with a slight taste for worship, and without the development of *rati.* If it is filled with *bhakti,* how then can attachment and hatred act unfavorably for *bhakti*?”

That is true, but there is no unity of the receptacle and what it holds, but rather the opposite. As soon as *bhakti* enters the ear there is no mixing with the *antaḥkaraṇa.* By repeated practice of *bhakti,* one rises from *anartha-nvṛtti,* to *niṣṭhā, ruci* and *āsakti* stages. After that, the mixing takes place. As along as there is no mixing of *bhakti* with the *antaḥkaraṇa*, the functions of the mind such as attachment and hatred will remain as material *anārthas.* When sulfur is added to mercury there is no immediate mixing, but after repeatedly rubbing, after a long time, they mix. Sulfur then gives up its original nature and takes a different form. Similarly the material nature of the *antaḥkaraṇa* is gradually destroyed and becomes spiritual. Just as sulfur and mercury eventually become one substance as collyrium, so *bhakti* and the *antaḥkaraṇa* become one as *prema.* Though mercury does not combine with other substances, sulfur, pleasing to Pārvatī, transforms by rubbing into another form, and by heating, it gradually matures and takes on a unique form and name. The uncontaminated Lord, in the form of chanting or other processes enters the *antaḥkaraṇa* endowed with attraction through the ears or other senses and rubbing against it by its *śakti,* makes the *antaḥkaraṇa* take on a spiritual form. By heating that combination till it matures to higher and higher states, it then attains the unique forms and names of *prema, sneha, praṇaya, raga*, *anurāga* and *mahābhāva.* Just as the mature combination takes on varieties by mixing with favorable elements, so *prema* takes on forms such as *dāsya* or *sakhya* by mixing with *bhāvas* of a servant, friend, parent or lover. The *prema* of the *sādhana-siddhas* has been described in this way. What doubt is there then about the *prema* of the *nitya-siddhas?*

Now let us return to the text. “So let there be no fault in the *siddhas* for displaying hatred and other negative emotions. But cannot *śṛṅgāra-rasa* carry on with such negative emotions?” Only one Cupid bewilders the material world. By seeing the scriptures of *rasa* written by Bharata Muni concerning *śṛṅgāra-rasa* related to Cupid, in the description of breaking appointments, it is understood that *śrṅgāra-rasa* is maintained and nourished by material anger, hatred and other emotions. How can the *śṛṅgāra-rasa* of Kṛṣṇa, who is more attractive than a multitude of Cupids be maintained and nourished without spiritual anger and hatred? *Agha vidviṣaḥ* indicates that Kṛṣṇa destroys all sins (*agha)* of those who taste this *rasa,* whereas material cupid increases sin. The *śṛṅgāra-rasa* of that Kṛṣṇa exists in personification in Vraja as *ujjvala-śṛṅgāra.* That *rasa* offers the *vyabhicāri-bhāvas* such as malice, which nourish *rasa* and which are associates of the *sthāyi-bhāva*, to the inimical parties, for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa, for happiness in pastimes where he displays impudence and other qualities. These negative emotions occur when there is possibility of meeting with the heroine. But in that condition, these emotions are also seen in separation from the heroine. For instance, malice is shown in the following. *Tasyā amūni naḥ kṣobhaṁ kurvanty uccaiḥ padāni yat:* these footprints of that special *gopī* greatly disturb us. (SB 10.30.30) However, when there is no possibility of meeting Kṛṣṇa for any of the *sakhīs,* these emotions do not occur.

*anvicchantyo bhagavato mārgaṁ gopyo ’vidūritaḥ*  
*dadṛśuḥ priya-viśleṣān mohitāṁ duḥkhitāṁ sakhīm*

**While continuing to search out Kṛṣṇa’s path, the** ***gopīs*** **discovered their unhappy friend close by. She was bewildered by separation from her lover. SB 10.30.40**

In this verse she is addressed as a friend (*sakhīm*). The nature of attempts at simultaneous enjoyment of *śṛṅgāra-rasa* produces the hatred and other emotions. It should be understood that these devotees of the Lord do not have continuous hatred for each other.

### Text 44

***yathā lalita-mādhave (3.39)—***  
***sāndraiḥ sundari vṛndaśo hari-pariṣvaṅgair idaṁ maṅgalaṁ***  
***dṛṣṭaṁ te hata-rādhayāṅgam anayā diṣṭyādya candrāvali \|***  
***drāg enāṁ nihitena kaṇṭham abhitaḥ śīrṇena kaṁsa-dviṣaḥ***  
***karṇottaṁsa-sugandhinā nija-bhuja-dvandvena sandhukṣaya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example for** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O beautiful Candrāvalī, suffering Rādhā can see how your body has become auspicious from Kṛṣṇa's many tight embraces. Please bring her back to life by embracing her with your thin arms fragrant from the touch of Kṛṣṇa's flower-earrings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā speaks in separation. *Sandhukṣaya* means “bring back to life.” This is also described in the five chapters on *rāsa-līlā* in the *Bhāgavatam*, where one *sakhī* is separated from Kṛṣṇa. However both parties are separated from him:

*anvicchantyo bhagavato mārgaṁ gopyo ’vidūritaḥ*  
*dadṛśuḥ priya-viśleṣān mohitāṁ duḥkhitāṁ sakhīm*

**While continuing to search out Kṛṣṇa’s path, the** ***gopīs*** **discovered their unhappy friend close by. She was bewildered by separation from her lover. SB 10.30.40**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Separated from Kṛṣṇa who has gone to Mathurā, Rādhā laments. She sees her reflection on a stone on Govardhana and thinks it is Candrāvalī. She begins speaking to that reflection. *Vṛndaśaḥ* means many times. Bring me to life by your arms, thin because of separation, offered (*nihitena*) around my neck. Those arms are fragrant with his ear ornament. After enjoying with you, taking your two arms, he slept on the right and then on the left side. I will also experience happiness by the embrace of your arms which have had such good fortune.

### Text 45

***yūtheśāyāḥ sva-pakṣādi-bheda-hetur athocyate \|***  
***bhāvasya sarvathaivātra sājātye syāt sapakṣatā \|\|45\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The cause of differences between the leader’s groups will be described. Members of one’s own group always possess identical type of love.**

### Text 46

***manāg etasya vaijātye suhṛt-pakṣatvam īritam \|***  
***sājātyasya tathālpatve sati jñeyā taṭasthatā \|***  
***sarvathā khalu vaijātye niścitā pratipakṣatā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The friendly group has slight difference in the type of love. The neutral group has a slight similarity in the type of love. The opposing group has completely different type of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The difference between the groups is described in terms of differing types of love. The word *bhāva* here refers to a particular type of *prema.* One can think “I belong to Kṛṣṇa” or “Kṛṣṇa belongs to me.” If two persons have the same type of love they belong to the same group. Those who are similar (*etasya*) with slight difference are in friendly groups. If there is great difference, they do not enter this category. If there is little similarity, there will be disrespect, and if there is great difference there will be limitation of relationships. This produces the neutral party. If there is complete difference the party is opposing.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“There is one *rasa, śṛṅgāra,* and one *viṣaya*, Kṛṣṇa. The *āśrayas* are the women of Vraja. Why do they have enemy and friendly groups?” The following should be considered.

In mixing the modesty of the *antaḥkaraṇa* with the sweet form of love, the quantity and type of the love may become much greater than the modesty and the modesty becomes swallowed by the love. “Kṛṣṇa is mine.” This is the possessive type of love called *madhu-sneha.* It is a *sthāyi-bhāva* which is devoid of show of respect. If the love does not become greater than the modesty, with the appearance of both love and modesty, one will think “I belong to Kṛṣṇa.” This mood of being Kṛṣṇa’s is called *ghṛta-sneha sthāyi-bhāva*, filled with respect for Kṛṣṇa. These two moods, like honey and ghee, are not of the same type. Thus mixing them in equal amounts creates something disharmonious. Women possessing these different types of love will thus not have a taste for each other. This results in opposing groups. The two main heroines are Rādhā and Candrāvalī. Though they have equal amounts of modesty, between them Rādhā’s modesty is devoured by her love (*prīti*) and thus does not show externally. Her modesty is not less than Candrāvalī’s though Lalitā’s and Viśākhā’s modesty is less than Rādhā’s and Candrāvalī’s, their *prīti* is much greater than their modesty. The modesty is devoured by their *prīti* and they show *madhu-sneha.* Though Lalitā and others possess less *prema* than Rādhā, because their *prema* is of completely the same type, they belong to the same group. The cause of being a *sakhī* or a leader is in all cases the amount of *prema.* Padmā and others have less modesty than Rādhā and Candrāvalī, and their *prīti is* not greater than their modesty. Thus they have *ghṛta-sneha.* They become part of Candrāvalī’s group and become enemies of Lalitā’s group.

If there is slight difference and great similarity, and even in absence of great similarity, if there is little difference, then they are a friendly group. If modesty is almost completely devoured by *prīti,* and there is a slight manifestation of modesty, then the *madhu-sneha* is tinged with *ghṛta-sneha*. Thus Śyāmalā’s group is friendly to Rādhā’s. If the similarity is little and the difference is great, if there is a little similarity, then the group is neutral. The modesty is only slightly devoured by the *prīti.* Generally modesty becomes evident. This is *ghṛta-sneha* with a slight tinge of *madhu-sneha.* Thus Bhadrā’s group is neutral to Rādhā and friends with Candrāvalī’s group.

### Text 47

***mitho-bhāvasya vaijātye na bhāvo rocate mithaḥ \|***  
***arocakatayaivāyam akṣāntiṁ janayet parām \|\|47\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because of the difference in the type of love, those types of love do not appreciate each other. They produce extreme intolerance by that lack of taste for each other.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse establishes the position of the enemy group.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mitho vaijātye* means completely opposite in quality.

### Text 48
