***yathā—***  
***yā madhyastha-padena saṅkulatarā śuddhā prakṛtyā jaḍā***  
***vaidagdhī-nalinī-nimīlana-paṭur doṣāntarollāsinī \|***  
***āśāyāḥ sphuraṇaṁ harer janayituṁ yuktātra candrāvalī***  
***sāpi syād iti locayan sakhi janaḥ kaḥ soḍhum īṣṭe kṣitau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Candrāvalī is prominently neutral, without sweetness of love, devoid of intelligence, joyful in thinking her faults are good qualities. She makes the beautiful lotus flower close its petals because of her incompetence. She longs only for a brief appearance of Kṛṣṇa. She should take another form. Considering this, on this pleasant earth, who is able to tolerate the sight of this Candrāvalī?**

**The moon is flawed, is marked with spots and by its nature gives suffering because of its coolness. It closes the petals of the beautiful lotus and shows joy only at night. It appears in the east and should take another form. Seeing the moon, what person on earth can tolerate it?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā speaks. Candrāvalī is prominently neutral since she shows great respect for Kṛṣṇa. Or the moon is at its middle phase. She is devoid of intense sweetness (*śuddha*). Or the moon is white. She is devoid of intelligence concerning dealings of the lover and beloved. Or the moon is cool. She hates persons like us with superior natures. Or the moon delights in the night (*doṣa*). She has a thirst for Kṛṣṇa. Or the moon appears in the eastern direction. See this, or consider this.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A follower of Vṛndā, a deity of the forest, curious about the conclusions of *prema*, asks “If Kṛṣṇa attains happiness by enjoyment with Candrāvalī, which is also your goal—to give him happiness--then why are you inimical to her? Why do you get angry when he frustrates your desires and meets with her?” Rādhā teaches her the principle. Candrāvalī can also mean the moon in the twelve months. The moon is always endowed with faulty marks. Or, she deals with Kṛṣṇa as a neutral party, because of having great respect. The moon is impure, having marks on its surface. She is devoid of the natural crookedness of *prema*, which moves crooked like a snake. By its nature the moon gives suffering, being cool. Or she is without intelligence. Or by her respect, friendliness is lost. The moon or she is skilful at closing the beautiful lotuses. Or the word *vaidagdhi* can mean the opposite. She is skilful at closing lotuses because of incompetence. She, the lotus, does not give happiness to Kṛṣṇa, the bee. The moon is brilliant in the night, not the day. In her mind *(antara*) she is joyful at seeing her faults as good qualities. She does not see her neutral nature as a fault. The moon appears *(sphuraṇam*) in the eastern direction (*harer āśāyāḥ*). Or she has a slight appearance of desire for Kṛṣṇa, but not an actual desire. She should produce another form. Seeing the moon, or considering Candrāvalī, who can tolerate this? One can tolerate her on earth, but all will discover her malice. Therefore she should not criticize again. Let her be like that. Her relationship with Kṛṣṇa will be finished. It is not unsuitable that I hate her. What is tasty to eat, one takes and prepares. If someone produces occasions for taking things which are tasteless, then will one become angry or not at that person? Consider this and then tell me. In this way she revealed the truth about *prema.*

### Text 49

***ṣoḍaśyās tvam uḍor vimuñca sahasā nāmāpi vāmāśaye***  
***tasyā durvinayair muner api manaḥ śāntātmanaḥ kupyati \|***  
***dhig goṣṭhendra-sute samasta-guṇināṁ maulau vrajābhyarcite***  
***pādānte patite’pi naiva kurute bhrū-kṣepam apy atra yā \|\|49\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Give up saying the name of the sixteenth constellation. O abode of misfortune! The mind of even a peaceful sage will become angry by her lack of modesty. Even though Kṛṣṇa, the summit of all who possess good qualities, and worshipped in Vraja, falls at her feet, she does not even move her eyebrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Candrāvalī speaks. Give up speaking of the sixteenth constellation, Viśākhā, also called Rādhā. If one utters her name directly then one thinks of anger. Because of her anger, though she is a *madhyā* she is well known for her *prakharā* nature. Though a sage is silent, he will speak, in order to reveal her faults.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The love of Candrāvalī is not appealing to Rādhā. That was shown. Rādhā’s love is not appealing to Candrāvalī. That is shown in this verse. Candrāvalī speaks with harsh language to one of her *sakhīs* who has been speaking about Rādhā’s character on some occasion. The sixteenth constellation has the same name as Rādhā. Touching her name directly makes my tongue bitter. Give up speaking of her name immediately, on any occasion, what to speak of speaking of her character! O abode of misfortune! I think you have lost your intelligence, since you bring up topics relating to her suddenly. “But you do not hate or criticize anyone in the universe. Your good character is famous for bring most compliant and soft.” That is true, but it is very difficult to give up criticizing her. The peaceful mind of the silent sage, whose nature is not praising or criticizing others nature or actions becomes angry at her. Therefore since I am a daughter of the cowherd with fixed behavior and uncontrolled speech, why should I not become angry and criticize her? Who becomes angry at her lack of modesty? To hell with her! To hell with her actions! And to hell with you for mentioning her! Even when he falls at her feet she does not react. What woman would make her lover fall at her feet? The proud woman should be pleased on seeing her lover offer pleasing words and gifts, rejecting others, putting his hands on his head, bowing down and lamenting. This is the perfection of *prema-rasa*. That may be so, but a woman with real love should lament in her mind on seeing him fall at her feet. Oh! She does not even move her eyebrow! How can she possess a trace of *prema*? Let there not even be *prema*. But he is at least respected by the intelligent person, since he is the crest jewel among persons with good qualities and is respected in Vraja. “If that is so, why does your lover go again and again to her by his own will, though she is devoid of *prema*? If he prefers her, then why do you, filled with *prema,* hate her?” She has beauty and extreme desires. He goes to her in order to make her attain good qualities by his personal teaching and just to give her pleasure from amorous play. But since her nature is determined by fate, she can never have good character. What happiness can he then derive from her amorous pleasure when she is so contaminated? Considering all this, I hate her. In this way she reveals her own realization of *rasa* to her *sakhī.*

### Text 50

***yatra syān nija-bhāvasya prāyas tulya-pramāṇatā \|***  
***pakṣaḥ sa eva maitrāya vidveṣāya ca yujyate \|\|50\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Where there are others with love in almost equal amount to one’s own love that constitutes a group. Some groups are friendly and others are inimical according to the difference in type of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Where there is love almost equal in amount to one’s own love for Kṛṣṇa, up to the same levels of *rati, prema, praṇaya* etc. as one’s own, that is called a group. The word *prāyaḥ* (almost) is used because exact similarity is not possible. There is an appearance of similarity.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Are there not other *gopīs* with *ghṛta-sneha,* completely different from Rādhā, since Rādhā’s hatred of Candrāvalī alone is well known? And for Candrāvalī are there not others besides Rādhā? What is the reason?” This verse answers. The word *prāyaḥ* means that the amount can be slightly less. Where there is a slight different in the predominant similarity, there is friendship. Where there is complete difference, there is hatred. This is from the material viewpoint.

### Text 51

***nāṁśo’py anyatra rādhāyāḥ premādi-guṇa-sampadām \|***  
***rasenaiva vipakṣādau mithaḥ sāmyam ivārpyate \|\|51\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Even one part of the wealth of Rādhā’s qualities and** ***prema*** **do not exist elsewhere. However** ***rasa*** **produces apparent equality with her in opposing group, her own group and the friendly group.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The opinion of those who bathe in the ocean of Rādhā’s greatness is presented. *Vipakṣadau* means the opposing group, one’s own group, and the friendly group. On hearing the activities of Hanumān, agitated by *vīra-rasa*, a knower of *rasa* contemplate an attempt to jump over the ocean. Similarly, because of *rasa*, other groups make a how equality with Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Do Candrāvalī and Śyāmalā have amounts of *prema* equal to Rādhā’s, since the two show hatred and friendliness towards Rādhā?” No one can compare to Rādhā even in part. However *rasa,* in order to nourish itself, creates apparent equal amounts of love in other groups, even though Rādhā and Candrāvalī are extremely different in their type of love.

### Text 52

***bhāvasyātyantikādhikye sājātyaṁ sarvathā dvayoḥ \|***  
***tathā tulya-pramāṇatvam evaṁ prāyaḥ sudurghaṭam \|\|52\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Two leaders having completely the same type and amounts of love is almost impossible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“There may be two *ātyantādhikās* with the same type of love. They would then be in the same group even though they are supposed to be leaders.” It is almost impossible to find two group leaders with *ātyantikādhikā* status with the same type of love for Kṛṣṇa, with the same sentiment of “I am Kṛṣṇa’s” or “Kṛṣṇa is mine.” They will be partly similar. If there were complete similarity of type of love there could be no leader. “If there are equal amounts of *prema,* then independent groups should be possible.” Exactly equal amounts of *prema* are very rare. One may say that Lalitā and Viśākhā have equal amounts of love of the same type as Rādhā. However this is rare. Therefore the word *prāyaḥ* (almost) is used.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“If two leaders have very different types of love and equal amounts of love, they are inimical. If two leaders have completely the same type of love (and equal amounts of love) do they reside in the same group? Or would she have another group?” This verse answers. If there are two group leaders *(ātyantikādhike*), complete similarity in the type of love is impossible. Without some difference there would not be different group leaders at all. Having exactly the same type of love is the cause of extreme affection between two persons, and that extreme affection causes them to stay together continually giving bliss to each other. When they live together how can there be difference of views? Here is the arrangement for that. Among many who have the same type of love, the woman with the greatest among of that type of love becomes the leader. The others become her sakhīs. It had been said:

*yūthādhipātve ‘py aucityaṁ dadhānā lalitādayaḥ \|*  
*sveṣṭa-rādhādi-bhāvasya lobhāt sakhya-ruciṁ dadhuḥ \|\|*

**Though Lalitā, Viśakhā, Padmā and Śaibya are capable of being leaders, because of their mood of serving other leaders like Rādhā, they have a taste as friends of leaders.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **3.61**

“Since Rādhā and Candrāvalī are in the highest position as *ātyantādhikās*, there are others like Lalitā and Padmā with less amount love than those two. It is proper that they become their *sakhīs.* But are there many other leaders other than those two with equal amounts of love of the same type or are there no others like that?” The answer is given in the verse. Among all the others, even two having exactly the same type of love and the same quantity is very rare. If they have exactly the same type of love and one has more and the other has less in amount, then one becomes the leader and the other becomes the *sakhī.* If two have different type of love, that difference is the cause of being two leaders of different groups, since the difference becomes a cause of being separate. It does not dependent on their having equal amounts of love. If two have the same type of love, having different groups based on equal amounts of the same type of love would very rarely happen, since the same type of love is not a cause of becoming a separate group. Thus the same type of love in one group and the same type of love in different groups has been described.

### Text 53

***syāc ced ghuṇākṣra-nyāyāt suhṛttaiveha sammatā \|***  
***rasa-svabhāvād atrāpi vaipakṣyam iti kecana \|\|53\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There could be friendship between two such leaders in different groups, though this is a rare case, in the manner of worm holes being similar by chance to letters of the alphabet. Others say that inevitably there will be hostility between them because of the nature of** ***rasa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Other than Rādhā and Candrāvalī there may be others having the same type of *prema*. Those two are the topmost *ātyantikādhikās*. There could be friendship between *ātyantādhikās* of groups headed by Lalitā, Padmā or others with others of equal status and same type of love, what to speak of others.” This verse answers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse explains the word *prāyaḥ* in the previous verse*.* When a certain type of insect eats up old wood it creates patterns that by chance resemble letters of the alphabet. Thus it could happen rarely that there are two leaders with similar love of the same amount. For such a leader *(iha*), having the same type of love but not being in the same group (*suhṛttā*) is permitted (*sammatam*), since it would be impossible to perform their activities while living together. This however is as rare as worms making patterns resembling letters. But there is another opinion. Because of the nature of *rasa,* not because of *prema,* there will be some animosity with any other group, even (*api*) with a friendly group or within one’s own group.

The meaning of this chapter will be summarized. Among the billions of gopīs the chief among those with pure *ghṛta-sneha* is Candrāvalī. Her *s*are Padmā and others. Rādhā, Lalitā and others in the group have hatred to them, and not to others, since there is not such extreme difference with other groups. Similarly Candrāvalī, Padmā and others of their group have hatred of Rādhā and her group, who have pure *madhu-sneha*, and do not have such hatred of others. Rādhā and her group have friendship with many other group leaders with impure *madhu-sneha*, such as Śyāmalā and Maṅgalā. Candrāvalī and her group regard them as a neutral party because of being impure, having varieties of little, very little, and extremely little *ghṛta-sneha*. Rādhā and her group regard others like Bhadrā as neutral since they have impure *ghṛta-sneha*. However Candrāvalī and her group regard Bhadrā and others as friendly groups. This is how one should understand the different types of groups. Those with the same type of lover belong to one’s own group. The opposing group consists of one group leader and many followers of similar nature. There are many friendly and neutral groups with their many leaders.

### Text 1

***atha vibhāveṣūddīpanāḥ—***  
***uddīpana-vibhāvā hares tadīya-priyāṇāṁ ca \|***  
***kathitā guṇa-nāma-carita-maṇḍana-sambandhinas taṭasthāś ca \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***uddīipanas:*** **The stimuli among the** ***vibhāvas*** **are said to be the Lord’s and his dear lovers’ qualities, names, activities, and decorations as well as related items and neutral elements like the wind or full moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is said:

*tad vraja-striya āśrutya veṇu-gītaṁ smarodayam*  
*kāścit parokṣaṁ kṛṣṇasya sva-sakhībhyo ‘nvavarṇayan*

**When the young ladies in the cowherd village of Vraja heard the song of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, which arouses the influence of Cupid, some of them privately began describing Kṛṣṇa’s qualities to their intimate friends. SB 10.21.3**

In *ujjvala-rasa* as in other *rasas, rasa* is explained in terms of *rasa* directed to Kṛṣṇa, not to his beloved *gopīs,* and Kṛṣṇa’s qualities should be called the *uddīpanas*, not their qualities. Their beauty and youth act as *uddīpanas* for Kṛṣṇa. These *uddīpanas* manifest along with manifestions of love at a particular moment

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *ālambana* portion of *vibhāva* has been described in terms of the hero, heroine and their assocaites. Now the *uddīpana* portion of *vibhāva* is described. In this *rasa* because the hero and heroine are both *viṣaya* and *āśraya* in relation to each other, there qualities of one become *uddīpana* for the other. The *sādhakas* however taste the mood of the women of Vraja directed to Kṛṣṇa as the main item and taste Kṛṣna’s love directed to the women of Vraja as the secondary item. That is the conclusion.

### Text 2

***tatra guṇāḥ—***  
***guṇās tridhā mānasā syur vācikāḥ kāyikās tathā \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are three types of qualities: mental, verbal and bodily.**

### Text 3

***tatra mānasāḥ—***  
***guṇāḥ kṛtajñatā-kṣānti-karuṇādyās tu mānasāḥ \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Mental qualities: Mental qualities are such things as gratitude, tolerance and compassion.**

### Text 4

***yathā—***  
***vaśam alpikayāpi sevayāmum***  
***vihite’py āgasi duḥsahe smitāsyam \|***  
***para-duḥkha-lave’pi kātaraṁ me***  
***harim udvīkṣya manas tanoti tṛṣṇām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Kṛṣṇa become controlled by one who performs even the slightest service. He smiles patiently even if an intolerable offense is committed to him. His heart becomes tormented if he sees others suffering even slightly. When I consider the Lord, my heart becomes thirsty for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is statement of someone in Dvārakā in *pūrva-rāga* in continual anticipation of realizing his qualities. “Considering him” indicates the beginning of *ruci* or taste. The speaker should be understood to be Satyabhāmā. She does not state any of the extraordinary *uddīpanas* of *madhura-rasa* because she is hiding her emotions somewhat from a friend.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Rādhā speaks to another *sakhī* having the same type of love with more love for Kṛṣṇa (*asama-sneha*) and a predominance of being a servant. He has the highest amount of gratitude, tolerance and compassion and therefore can be served happily by girls like us. This mood is included in *śṛṅgāra-rasa.*

### Text 5

***atha vācikāḥ—***  
***vācikās tu guṇāḥ proktāḥ karṇānandakatādayaḥ \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Verbal qualities are things like giving bliss to the ears.**

### Text 6

***yathā—***  
***karṇāpahāri-varṇām***  
***aśruta-cara-mādhurībhir abhyastām \|***  
***āli rasālāṁ mādhava-***  
***vācaṁ nācamya tṛpyāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My friend, I am not satisfied by having just once sipped the Mādhava's words, which produce** ***rasa*** **and which are filled with an unprecedented sweetness that enchants the ears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is also a statement in *pūrva-rāga.* These are words of a Vraja kumarī, so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa that she cannot even move, to a *sakhī* inquiring from her. His words are sweet because of their colorful meaning*. Rasālām* means that which deposits *rasa*. I am not satisfied by sipping his words which produce *rasa* in me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā, who asks “You are behind the creepers and cannot see your lover. Why are you lingering there?” As long as Kṛṣṇa is here speaking with Subala, I will also stay here. *Rasālā* is a kind of sweet drink. It is used as a comparison not a metaphor. *Karṇāpahāri-varṇām* modifies *mādhava-vācam* not *rasālām* since the meaning would be impossible (a drink which attracts the ears). *Kāvya-prakāśa* gives the following example*. Pādāmbujaṁ bhavatu no vijayāya mañju mañjīra-śiñjita-manoharam ambikāyāḥ:* may the lotus feet of Ambikā, lovely because of jingling of her anklets, ordain our victory. The jingling is unfavorable to the description of the lotus as feet, since lotuses do not jingle. Therefore lotus it is not used as a metaphor.

### Text 7

***atha kāyikāḥ—***  
***te vayo rūpa-lāvaṇye saundaryam abhirūpatā \|***  
***mādhuryaṁ mārdavādyāś ca kāyikāḥ kathitā guṇāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bodily qualities: Bodily qualities are such things as youth,** ***rūpa, lāvaṇya, saundarya, abhirūpatā, mādhurya*** **and** ***mārdava.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The items will be explained.

### Text 8-9

***tatra vayaḥ—***  
***vayaś caturvidhaṁ tv atra kathitaṁ madhure rase \|***  
***vayaḥ-sandhis tathā navyaṁ vyaktaṁ pūrṇam iti kramāt \|\|\|***  
***vayo-mukhā guṇāḥ pūrvam uktāḥ keśava-saṁśrayāḥ \|***  
***tena te’tra pravakṣyante prāyaśas tat-priyānugāḥ \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Youth: Youth is divided into the following four parts:** ***vayah-sandhi, navya, vyakta*** **and** ***purna*****. Previously in** ***Bhakti-rasāmṛtta-sindhu*** **these qualities have been described in relation to Keśava. In the following portions of the present book these same qualities will be generally described in relation to Kṛṣṇa's** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vayah* means youth. It is a separate item. This has been explained in *Bhakti-rasāmrta-sindhu,* but here another definition is given. What was called the first part of *kaiśora* is here divided into *vayaḥ-sandhi* and *navya.* *Madhya-kaiśora* and *śeṣa-kaiśora* are here called *vyakta* and *pūrṇa.* Generally these terms are used in relation to the *gopīs* but sometimes they are applied to Kṛṣṇa as well in this book.

### Text 10

***tatra vayaḥ-sandhiḥ—***  
***bālya-yauvanayoḥ sandhir vayaḥ-sandhir itīryate \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vayaḥ-sandhi*** **is the joining of** ***paugaṇḍa*** **and** ***kaiṣora*** **ages.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This means the first part of *kaiśora* only, since the whole of *kaiśora* is between *paugaṇḍa* and *yauvana. Bālyam* means *paugaṇḍa.*

### Text 11

***sa kṛṣṇasya, yathā—***  
***yāntī śyāmalatāṁ vimucya kapiśa-cchāyāṁ smara-kṣmāpater***  
***adyājñā-lipi-varṇa-paṅkti-padavīm āpnoti romāvalī \|***  
***vāñchaty ucchalitaṁ manāg abhinavāṁ tāruṇya-nīra-cchaṭāṁ***  
***labdhvā kiñcid adhīram akṣi-śaphara-dvandvaṁ ca kaṁsadviṣaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s** ***vayaḥ sandhi:*** **The hairs on Kṛṣṇa’s body, giving up their brown color and becoming black, have become letters written in Cupid's edict. The two restless** ***śaphara*** **fish of Kṛṣṇa's eyes, attaining the waters of fresh youthfulness spreading everywhere, are filled with desire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of a young girl of Vraja desiring to have an amorous relationship with Kṛṣṇa*. Lipi* means writing letters of the alphabet. His hairs are arranged (*padavīm)* in rows revealing the written orders of Cupid. The phrase “enemy of Kaṁsa” suggests his powers which manifest during this age.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A messenger describes Kṛṣṇa standing at the base of tree in the distance to Rādhā who is looking through the holes in the tangle of creepers. Kṛṣṇa’s hairs have given up their brownish color and become a line of letters, like the orders of a king which cannot be disobeyed.

*varṇasyojjvalatā kāpi netrānte cāruṇa-cchaviḥ \|*  
*romāvali-prakaṭatā kaiśore prathame sati \|\|*

**At the beginning of youth, the** ***kaiśora*** **age, the complexion becomes indescribably effulgent, the edges of the eyes become reddish and fine hairs appear on the body. BRS 2.1.313**

*kharatātra nakhāgrāṇāṁ dhanur āndolitā bhruvoḥ \|*  
*radānāṁ rañjanaṁ rāga-cūrṇair ity ādi ceṣṭitam \|\|*

**At the beginning of youth, the activities consist of sharpening his nails, quivering of the bow-like eye brows, and staining the teeth with dyes. BRS 2.1.217**

*Uccahlita* means spread out and *kaṁsa-dviṣaḥ* (enemy of Kaṁsa) indicates Kṛṣṇa’s abilities.

### Text 12

***tan-mādhuryam—***  
***daśārdha-śara-lubdhakaṁ calam avekṣya lakṣyecchayā***  
***viśantam iha sāmprataṁ bhavad-apāṅga-śṛṅgopari \|***  
***sadāśru-nikarokṣitā vraja-mahendra vṛndāvane***  
***kuraṅga-nayanāvalī dara-pariplavatvaṁ gatā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sweetness of Kṛṣṇa during the first part of** ***kaiśora:*** **O king of Vraja! The fickle hunter Cupid with his five arrows has attained the summit of your sidelong glance. Seeing this hunter in Vṛndāvana forest, pierced by his arrows of desire, the frightened does of the** ***gopīs'*** **eyes have now become filled with tears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“His sweetness” means his power of delighting, or his extreme attractiveness. *Kuraṅga-nayanāvalī* means the groups of women with deer-like eyes, or the groups of eyes of the deer. Their eyes are slightly (*dara*) restless, or the deer’s eyes are restless with fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sweetness means the special taste realized on seeing his form. Using double meanings, Nāndīmukhī consoles Kṛṣṇa as he meditates full of *pūrva-rāga*, thinking “How can I attain those beautiful women of Vraja?” Seeing the hunter Cupid with five arrows, the *gopīs* become pierced with the arrows of desire (*laksya icchayā*). *Lakṣya* means attained. The groups of doe-eyed women, seeing the hunter who has attained the jeweled top of the mountain of your glances, tremble slightly, or in fear.

### Text 13

***tat-priyāṇāṁ, yathā—***  
***vādyaṁ kiṅkiṇim āharaty upacayaṁ jñātvā nitambo guṇī***  
***svasya dhvaṁsam avetya vaṣṭi-balibhir yogaṁ hrasan madhyamam \|***  
***vakṣaḥ sādhu-phala-dvayaṁ vicinute rājopahāra-kṣamaṁ***  
***rādhāyās tanu-rājyam añcati nave kṣauṇī-patau yauvane \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The first stage of youth of the women: When young king of youthfulness enters the kingdom of Rādhā’s body, Rādhā’s beautiful hips, thinking of making an offering, greet him with the tinkling sounds of a sash of bells. Fearing it's destruction at his hands, because of its lesser qualities, her waist contracts with three folds of skin. Her chest with two ripe fruits selects a gift adequate for the king.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first part of youth of Kṛṣṇa’s *gopīs* is described. A messenger speaks to Kṛṣṇa. By those words she makes Kṛṣṇa understand that Rādhā has extreme desire for him at this age. This is should be understood in later verses also. The sound of her bells is like music. Her hips are suitable (*guṇi)* for a king, or her hips are tied with a cord. The waist feels unqualified because it is thin (*madhyama* is of medium quality) or the waist is in the middle between the stomach and hips.  *Sadhu* modifies *vakṣa. Añcati* means going. The king of new youth (*nave yauvane kṣauṇī-patau*) enters the kingdom of Rādhā’s body.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa, on seeing Rādhā at a distance, speaks to Subala. When the new king of youth attains his kingdom her beautiful hips produce music in the form of her bells in order to welcome him. They produce music skillfully, while thinking of making an offering *(upacayam*) “I should give my wealth to the king who knows good qualities.” Or, her hips are bound with a cord (*guṇī*). Knowing the cord’s strength (*upacayam),* her waist with the cord plays music. Her waist sees that she will be destroyed. “I will be destroyed because I do not have qualities like the waist and cannot pay taxes like the breasts to the king. I have only medium qualities (*madhyamam*), not the best qualities. I continue to live (*vaṣti*) by offerings made the help of others (*yogam)”* Or the waist contracts with three lines.

### Text 14

***tan-mādhuryam—***  
***āśāste patituṁ kaṭākṣa-madhupo mandaṁ dṛg-indīvare***  
***kiñcid vrīḍa-visāṅkuraṁ mṛgayate ceto-marālārbhakaḥ \|***  
***narmālāpa-madhu-cchaṭādya vadanāmbhoje tavodīyate***  
***śaṅke sundari mādhavotsava-karīṁ kāñcid daśām añcasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The sweetness of Rādhā during the first part of** ***kaiśora:*** **The bumble-bee of your glances now desires to land on the blue lotus flower of your eyes, the young swan of your heart is now searching for the lotus sprout of your shyness, and a flood of the honey of joking words now raises itself on the lotus of your mouth. O beautiful Rādhā! I think you are now preparing a great festival of happiness for the pleasure of Mādhava.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One *sakhī* speaks to another *sakhī* about her appearance which stimulates Kṛṣṇa’s love.  *Mandam* is an adverb*. Udīyate* is a reflexive verb formed from affix *ut* and the verb *i.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā jokes with Rādhā. Her glances like bees desire to fall on the blue lotus of her eyes. The glances did not know your eyes. But now they will know. *Vṛḍa* is shyness but when not in the neuter it means passion as well as in *vrīḍam eti na tava priyaṁ vadan*: (*Māgha-kāvya 14.2*) *Mādhava* means spring and Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 15

***atha navyam—***  
***darodbhinna-stanaṁ kiñcic-calākṣaṁ manthara-smitam \|***  
***manāg abhisphurad-bhāvaṁ navyaṁ yauvanam ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Nayva*** **age: The age when a girl's breasts slight appear, when her eyes become a little restless, when she smiles mildly, and when the full sentiment of amorous love begins to manifest slightly, is called the second state of** ***kaiśora.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

During the first part of kaiśora (*vayaḥ-sandhi*) there is soft flesh and the breasts are not formed. During *navya* the breasts begin to grow. The eyes are slightly restless, whereas during *vayaḥ-sandhi* the eyes are not visibly restless. The smile does not come out of the mouth but lingers. During *vayaḥ-sandhi* the smile is within the mouth. Full manifestation (*abhisphrad*) is slight. During *vayaḥ-sandhi* the first symptoms of changes because of love are not visible, whereas in *navya* they are visible.

A line of hairs is now slightly visible above your navel. O beautiful-faced girl, your fresh youthfulness is now suitable for serving Kṛṣṇa.**

Vṛndā speaks. The waist is somewhat thin *(apacitam*).

A bold woman, joking with her sister-in-law, attempting to turn her into a messenger, speaks. Wandering around indicates her fickle nature. Being disturbed by the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa is a sign of *āvega* (agitation). Glancing about is a sing of *autsukya* (eagerness). These are vyabhicāri-bhāvas.1

### Text 20

***tan-mādhuryam—***  
***bhrājante varadanti mauktika-gaṇā yasyollikhadbhir nakhaiḥ***  
***kṣiptāḥ puṣkara-mālayāvṛta-rucaḥ kuñjeṣu kuñjeśv amī \|***  
***śauṭīryābdhir uroja-pañjara-taṭe saṁveśayantyā kathaṁ***  
***sa śrīmān hariṇekṣaṇe harir abhūn netreṇa baddhas tvayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The sweetness of** ***vyakta*****: O girl with very beautiful teeth! By Kṛṣṇa scratching your breasts, your pearl-necklace has been scattered through the bowers and have lost their brilliance, being covered by cast off lotus garlands. O doe-eyed Rādhā! How were you able to bind with a glance the ocean of strength, and put him to rest near the cage of your breasts?**

**By the claws of the lion wounding the elephant’s temple, the elephants’ pearls have been scattered in the bowers and have lost their brilliance, being crushed by the elephants’ trunks. How were you able to bind with a churning rope the ocean of strength, and put him to rest near the cage of your breasts?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

O woman with the best teeth (vara-danti)! Or, as part of a compound, vara-danti with mauktika-gaṇā means the pearls from the best of elephants. Puskara-māla means a lotus garland or many tips of elephants’ trunks. Saṁveśayantyā means “make him lie down.” How have you bound him with your eyes or a churning rope?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā speaks to Rādhā. O doe-eyed woman! Giving up a male deer, how have you bound up the lion with your eyes? This is a statement of wonder. Or, how have you bound a lion with a churning rope, since you are a cowherd girl and such a rope is suitable. Why have you made him rest beside the cage on your breast? Present participle form is used to indicate a reason. *Saṁveṣa* means a sleep or a dream according to *Amara-koṣa.* This is not an ordinary lion. It is and ocean of strength, or because of his strength, how can you, who are so tender, tolerate his rough behavior during love making, since he is very strong? This joke is hinted.

The pearls of her necklace are scattered about by the nails of Kṛṣṇa as he scratches her breast. Heaps of the best pearls from the elephants (*vara-danti*) forehead are scattered about by the lion’s claws making deep wounds in the elephant. Or *vara-danti* can be a separated word: O woman with beautiful teeth! In either case, the elephant’s temple or the breast of the girl is indicated with the appropriate image of the lion attacking the elephant’s head or Kṛṣṇa scratching Rādhā’s breast. The pearls from the elephant’s temples have lost their beauty by being crushed by the tips of elephants’ trunks, or the pearls of the girl’s necklace on her breast have their beauty covered by a lotus garland. *Puṣkara* means the tip of an elephant’s trunk according to *Amara-koṣa.*

Vṛndā speaks. *Yayasi* means “in youth.”  *Kandalayatah* means “have sprouted” or “appear to be.”

### Text 27

***nītaṁ te punar uktatāṁ bhramarakaiḥ kastūrikā-patrakaṁ***

***hāraś ca smita-kānti-bhaṅgibhir alaṁ piṣṭānupeṣīkṛtaḥ***  
***kiṁ rādhe tava maṇḍanena nitarām aṅgair asi dyotitā \|\|\|***

What is the use of you wearing all these decorations? You are already made splendid by the beauty of your limbs.**

*Punar uktatāṁ (*redundant repetition of words) means “made useless.” The verse becomes more attractive by use of words with other meanings.

The previous verse described how her body without ornaments appears ornamented. Not satisfied, since the words were unsuitable, the author gives another example. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā while she is being decorated*. Bhramarakaiḥ* means “with locks of hair.”

### Text 28

***atha lāvaṇyam—***  
***muktāphaleṣu chāyāyās taralatvam ivāntarā \|***  
***pratibhāti yad aṅgeṣu lāvaṇyaṁ tad ihocyate \|\|28\|\|***

*Chāyāyāḥ taralatvam* means “waves of beauty.” The word *lāvaṇya* comes from the *lavaṇa,* beauty. Medinī says *lavaṇa* means a salty taste, the name of river and beauty. That which has beauty is called beautiful (*lavaṇa*). That state is called *lāvaṇya* or beauty or *lavaṇimā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Chāyāyāḥ taralatvam* means “waves of beauty.” When waves of beauty create reflections (*pratibhāti*) coming from within (*antarā*) the limbs it is called *lāvaṇya.* Because of its purity and its abundance the beauty radiates at every moment.

*Vyadhita* means “did.” *Viḍambyanti* means “they criticize.” Your limbs criticize a jeweled mirror because having such beauty.

Kṛṣṇa speaks. Brahmā collected all the flawless beauty that existed in the universe. But he did not find anything in the universe like your limbs. The affix *ka* on *aṅga* indicates compassion. Her limbs have mercifully been given beauty and youthfulness.

***marakata-mukurābhe bimbitāsi tvam eva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

A *sakhī* consoles Rādhā who is showing envy. “No one is like you with the highest beauty even in your reflection.”

Having shown the beauty fixed in Rādhā’s limbs, the author now gives an example of the beauty fixed in Kṛṣṇa. Where two examples are given later for one point, the reason is the same. Rādhā, anger playing within her, sat in front of Kṛṣṇa. Advising her and then mocking her, Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā to enlighten her.

*Aṅgas* are arms etc. and *pratyāṅgas* means wrists, upper arm and forearm. Each of these should be of proper fatness, thinness, roundness, in the proper place, and wrinkled at the joints such as the elbow. .

Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Aṁse* means “to the shoulder*.” Srastau* means hanging Her waist is the width of the hand in all directions (*abhitaḥ*). This means that the hand can grasp her waist.  *Abhitaḥ* means around and in the midst. It takes the accusative case.

*Yat* is the subject and *anyad vastu* is the object. That which produces similar beauty *(sārūpyam*) in a nearby object is called *abhirūpatā.*

**An example: O golden** ***gopī*****! When it touches his splendid teeth, Kṛṣṇa's flute looks like a crystal. When it touches his red lotus palm it looks a ruby, and when it touches his blue lotus cheek it looks like a sapphire. Look! Kṛṣṇa's flute looks like three different jewels.**

### Text 35

***yathā vā--***

***rādhe kokanada-śriyaḥ karatale sindūrataḥ sundare \|***  
***drāg indindira-bandhureṣu cikureṣv indīvarābhāṁ vahann***

In *śṛṅgāra-rasa* the hero becomes the *viṣaya* for the heroine, and the heroine becomes the *viṣaya* for the hero. Therefore the *uddīpanas* can be described in relation to either of them. Here there is no rule of who will be described first or second. Kṛṣṇa speaks. *Kairava-korakaḥ* means a bud of a white lotus. *Avaṣṭambha* means gold. *Kokanadam* is a red lotus. *Indindirā* is a bee. *Indīvara* is a blue lotus.

*Rūpa* has been described as being beautiful even without ornaments. When that *rūpa* becomes impossible to describe, and no words can express it, though it can be experienced by the mind it is called *mādhuryam. Kim api* means “somehow beautiful” though indescribable.

**An example: O beautiful faced woman! The indescribable splendor of Kṛṣṇa, the color of a rain cloud, chokes up the hearts of the women of Vraja. His bodily gestures steal away the eyes, and the fresh perfection of sweetness makes pious girls falter in their vow of chastity.**

The word “of the women of Vraja” should be added to all the objects of the sentences. *Dhāma* is the subject and *hṛdayam* is the object of the first sentence. *Vivarta* means perfection. The indescribable perfection of his sweetness makes the girls falter.

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. That effulgence obstructs the heart. Surrounding the heart, it then becomes fixed in the heart. His gestures forcibly steal the eyes. In the absence of mind and eyes being obstructed, how can *dharma* be fixed? The fresh perfection of his beauty makes the *dharma* of the women unsteady.

***Mārdavam:*** **When one cannot tolerate even the softest touch, it is called** ***mārdavam. Mārdavam*** **is of three kinds: great, medium and least.**

Rūpa-mañjari speaks to Rati-mañjarī. From today, we should not pick fresh jasmines, but search out and pick *yūthikā* or land lotus petal tips or other flowers for the bed. *Adhiśī* is the verb meaning to lie upon.

Lalitā speaks. *Cīnasya* means very fine cloth from China. *Lohita-candanena* means “with red sandalwood paste.”

### Text 41

***kaniṣṭhaṁ, yathā rasa-sudhākare (1.186f)—***  
***āmodam āmodanam ādadhānaṁ***  
***nilīna-nīlālaka-cañcarīkam \|***  
***kṣaṇena padmā-mukha-padmam āsīt***  
***tviṣā raveḥ komalayāpi tāmram \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kaniṣṭha mārdavam:*** **The delightful, fragrant lotus flower of Padmā's face, decorated with the bumble-bees of her locks of hair, black as bees, by exposure to even the softest rays of the sun, instantly becomes red.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Amodam* is fragrance. *Amodanam* is bliss.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Padmā speaks to Padmā. Her face, offered to others (*ādadhānam)* gives bliss (*āmodanam*) and fragrance (*āmodam*). She has locks of hair like bees (*cañcarīkam*) touching her forehead because of being sprinkled with perspiration.

“It would seem that all the girls, dressed finely and having ornaments, would be touched by the sun’s rays while having pastimes with Kṛṣṇa in the forest during the day. They would all become extremely discolored because of their softness. This would be a disgusting *uddīpana*.” That is not so. Since they have all generally awakened *rāga,* suffering becomes the highest happiness. That being so, what disfigurement could take place? They become most beautiful on meeting Kṛṣṇa.

*tīvrārka-dyuti-dīpitair asilatādhārākarālāsribhi-*  
*rmārtaṇḍopala-maṇḍalaiḥ sthapuṭite’py adres taṭe tasthuṣī \|*

**Remains on the slope covered with piles of sharp-edged, uneven sun stones heated by the intense rays of the sun at noon, Rādhā, joyfully gazing at the prince of the cowherds, remains motionless as standing with her feet on a bed spread with blue lotuses.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.127**

Though she was burning in the sun and had pain in her soft feet she did not become lazy. Rather she sought the best dress and ornaments to give pleasure to Kṛṣṇa. In the state of separation after disagreement, because of the impossibility of meeting Kṛṣṇa, the stage of *rāga* manifests in them. Then they become discolored because of the softness of their bodies. In the present examples of highest, medium and least sensitivity, softness arises from a relationship with Kṛṣṇa, and it is not in anyway ugly. Some explain that the degree of sensitivity depends up on the sensation such as touching or seeing.

### Text 42

***atha nāma, yathā—***  
***taṭa-bhuvi ravi-putryāḥ paśya gaurāṅgi raṅgī***  
***sphurati sakhi kuraṅgī-maṇḍale kṛṣṇasāraḥ \|***  
***iti bhavad-abhidhānaṁ śṛṇvatī sā mad-uktau***  
***sutanur atanu-ghūrṇā-pūra-pūrṇā babhūva \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The name as a stimulus: “O golden-complexioned friend, look at this happy Kṛṣṇa-sāra deer surrounded by these female deer on the shore of the Yamunā.” When beautiful Rādhā heard your name uttered by me, she at once became flooded with amorous passion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 43-44

***atha caritam—***  
***anubhāvāś ca līlā cety ucyate caritaṁ dvidhā \|***  
***agre’nubhāvā vaktavyā līleyaṁ kathyate’dhunā \|\|\|***  
***līlā syāc cāru-vikrīḍā tāṇḍavaṁ veṇu-vādanam \|***  
***godohaḥ parvatoddhāro gohūtir gamanādikā \|\|44\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Actions as stimulus: Actions are divided into two kinds:**  ***anubhāva*** **and** ***līlā. Anubhāva*** **actions will be described in the related chapter. Now activities of** ***līlā*** **will be described. The** ***līlās*** **include charming play, dancing, playing the flute, milking the cows, lifting Govardhana Hill, calling the cows, and walking.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *anubhāvas* consist of *alaṅkāra, udbhāsvara* and *vācikā* types.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *anubhāvas* consist of *alaṅkāra, udbhāsvara* and *vācikā* types.

### Text 45

***atha cāru-vikrīḍā—***  
***rāsa-kandūka-khelādyā cāru-krīḍātra kīrtitā \|\|45\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Charming play: The** ***rāsa*** **dance and playing games with a ball are known as charming play.**

### Text 46

***tatra rāsaḥ—***  
***taṁ vilāsavati rāsa-maṇḍale***  
***puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ surāṅganāḥ \|***  
***prekṣya sambhṛta-vihāra-vibhramaṁ***  
***babhramur madana-sambhramormibhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Rāsa*** **dance: O charming Rādhā! When the wives of the** ***devatās*** **see lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, filled with the beauty of pastimes, in the circle of the** ***rāsa-*****dance, they become overwhelmed with waves of amorous passion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā speaks to Rādhā. O charming Rādhā (*vilāsavati*)! By hearing the description of the *rāsa-līlā,* Rādhā remembers the pastime and this becomes an *uddīpana* for *rati.*

### Text 47

***kandūka-krīḍā—***  
***aruṇa-rucim udasya kṣepaṇīṁ kuñcitāgrāṁ***  
***sarabhasam abhidhāvan vibhramad-dīrgha-veṇiḥ \|***  
***viracayati mukundaḥ kandukāndola-nṛtyad-***  
***vipula-nayana-bhaṅgī-vibhramaḥ kautukaṁ naḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Playing with a ball: Swinging his red bat with a narrow handle and swiftly pursuing the ball, his braid moving about playfully, Kṛṣṇa, attractive by the movements of his wide eyes following the ball, produces joy in us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sakhī* speaks to another *sakhī.* By knowing these activities, the *gopīs* are stimulated in their love. Thus it acts as *uddīpana.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, watching through the network of creepers, sees Kṛṣṇa playing with his friends. She speaks to her *sakhīs.* The bat is dyed with vermilion and is used to hit the ball. Kṛṣṇa has a braid of hair which moves about wonderfully as he chases the ball. He displays special charm by the movements of his wide eyes dancing about because of the movements of the ball.

### Text 48

***tāṇḍavam—***  
***pracala-pracalāka-kuṇḍalo’yaṁ***  
***sva-suhṛn-maṇḍala-carcarī-parītaḥ \|***  
***harir adya naṭan pataṅga-putrī-***  
***taṭa-raṅge mama raṅgam ātanoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Dancing as a stimulus: As Kṛṣṇa dances, surrounded by his friends moving to the rhythm of** ***carcarī*** **on the bank of the Yamunā, while his earrings and peacock-feather sway, he stimulates my love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Pracalāka* is a peacock feather. *Carcarī* is a type of beat.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, looking through the network of creepers, speaks to her sakhīs. *Pracalāka* is a peacock feather*. Carcarī* is a type of beat.

### Text 49

***veṇu-vādanaṁ, yathā lalita-mādhave (4.27)—***  
***jaṅghādhas-taṭa-saṅgi-dakṣiṇa-padaṁ kiñcid vibhugna-trikam-***  
***sāci-stambhita-kandharaṁ sakhi tiraḥ-sañcāri-netrāñcalam \|***  
***vaṁśīṁ kuṭmalite dadhānam adhare lolāṅgulī-saṅgatāṁ***  
***riṅgad-bhrū-bhramaraṁ varāṅgi paramānandaṁ puraḥ svīkuru \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Playing the flute, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: O most beautiful friend! Please accept Kṛṣṇa, standing before you full of bliss. The edges of his eyes roam to the side, and his eyebrows move slowly like bumblebees. Standing with his right foot placed below the knee of his left leg, his body bent at the waist, and his neck firmly positioned to the side, he holds his flute to his pursed lips and moves his fingers upon it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a description of a likeness of Kṛṣṇa seen by Rādhā at the time of arranging for her to attain Kṛṣṇa as her husband during a drama.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. This form is bliss, since the person possessing it and the object are non-different. Please accept it with a glance. His right foot is touching the left leg below the knee. His waist is slightly bent. His neck is firmly positioned sideways. *Trikam* means joint of the back and lower part of the body according to *Amara-koṣa*. His neck is firm, not moving.

### Text 50

***go-doho, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (262)—***  
***aṅguṣṭhāgrima-yantritāṅgulir asau pādārdha-nīruddha-bhūr***  
***āpīnāñcalam ārdrayann iha puro dvitraiḥ ārdrīkṛtya payodharāñcalam alaṁ sadyaḥ in Padyāvalī. 2 payo-bindubhiḥ \|***  
***nyag-jānu-dvaya-madhya-yantrita-ghaṭī-vaktrāntarāla-skhalad-dhārādhvāna-manoharaṁ sakhi payo gāṁ dogdhi dāmodaraḥ \|\|50\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Milking cows from** ***Padyāvaī:*** **Resting on half his feet, grasping the udder between his thumb and finger, first moistening the udder with two or three drops, and making a charming stream of milk pour into the pail firmly fixed just below his knees, Dāmodara milks a cow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viṣākhā, watching Kṛṣṇa, speaks to Rādhā. He presses the upper portion of his thumb to his other fingers. The word “portion” should be understood in the compound. *Bhāṣā-vṛtti* says *kvacid uttara-padasya vṛttāv antarbhāvaḥ suvarṇa-vikāro'laṅkāro'sya suvarṇālaṅkāraḥ*: sometimes the second word of a phrase to give meaning is dropped as in the case of *suvarṇālaṅkāra* (gold ornament) which actually means an ornament made from gold. First, he moistens the edge of the udder (*āpīna*). This is the first action in milking a cow. The pail is firmly placed *(yantrita*) slightly down from the large joints of his knees. He milks the cow of its milk which flows in streams in the mouth of the pail. The verb *doghi* has two objects: cow and milk.

### Text 51

***parvatoddhāraḥ—***  
***udyamya kandukita-mandara-sodarādriṁ***  
***savyaṁ karaṁ kaṭim anu sthagayann asavyam \|***  
***smerānanaś cala-dṛg-añcala-cañcarīkaś***  
***cittāmbujaṁ mama hariś caṭulīcakāra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lifting the mountain: Placing his right hand on his hip, and raising his left hand right, smiling Kṛṣṇa lifts Govardhana Hill equal to Mandara Mountain, as if it were a ball. The restless bumble bee of his sidelong glance makes the lotus flower of my heart tremble.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kandukitaḥ* means “made like a ball.” Govardhana is equal to Mandara Mountain (*sodara*). Lifting his left hand, he keeps his right hand on his waist.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. *Kandukitaḥ* means “made like a ball.” He lifts the mountain playfully. Govardhana is equal to Mandara Mountain. Lifting his left hand, he covers his waist with his right hand keeping it there. The verb *sag* or *sthag* means to cover.

### Text 52

***go-hūtiḥ—***  
***piśaṅgi maṇika-stani praṇata-śṛṅgi piṅgekṣaṇe***  
***mṛdaṅga-mukhi dhūmale śabali haṁsi vaṁśī-priye \|***  
***iti sva-surabhī-kulaṁ muhur udīrṇa-hīhī-dhvanir***  
***vidūra-gatam āhvayan harati hanta cittaṁ hariḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Calling the cows: To the cows straying away Kṛṣṇa constantly calls “O Piśaṅgī! Maṇikastanī! Praṇata-śrṅgī! Pingekṣaṇa! Mṛdaṅgamukhī! Dhūmalā! Śabalī! Haṁsī! Vaṇṣī-priyā! Hīhī!” By this calling, Kṛṣṇa has stolen my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā.

### Text 53

***gamanam—***  
***anupada-mada-mandāndoli-dor-argala-śrīḥ***  
***sura-gaja-guru-garva-stambhi-gambhīra-keliḥ \|***  
***sahacari dara-cañcac-cāru-cūḍā-rucir māṁ***  
***madayati gati-mudrā-mādhurī mādhavasya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Walking: As Kṛṣṇa walks the great bolts of his arms slowly swing back and forth as if intoxicated, and his beautiful crown moves slightly. His profound sporting stuns the pride of the leaders of the elephants in the heavenly planets. O my friend! The sweetness of Mādhava's walking intoxicates me.**

### Text 54

***atha maṇḍanam—***  
***caturdhā maṇḍanaṁ vāso-bhūṣā-mālyānulepanaiḥ \|\|54\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Decoration as** ***uddīpana:*** **There are four kinds of decoration: garments, ornaments, garlands and cosmetics.**

### Text 55

***atha vastraṁ, yathā—***  
***ambaraṁ racita-dhairya-saṁvaraṁ***  
***ramyam ambara-maṇi-prabhojjvalam \|***  
***subhru kiṁ na hi kaṭīra-maṇḍale***  
***puṇḍarīka-nayanasya paśyasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Garments: O Lalitā with beautiful eyebrows! Do you not see on lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa's hips a beautiful garment shining from the light of the sun? This garment destroys my composure.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a description made by one *sakhī* to another *sakhī,* while she gazes at Kṛṣṇa secretly out of *vāmya.* Do you not see this? It is self-evident. *Prabhojjvalam* should actually be *prārabdhābhojvvalam.* It is just shining from the light of the sun. Another version has *prodyad-ambara-maṇi-prabhāmbarām*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This suppresses my composure. The cloth sparkles with the light of the sun which is attached to it. *Ambaram* can also mean yellow or pink.

### Text 56

***yathā vā—***  
***amala-kamala-rāga-rāgam etat tava***  
***jayati sphuṭam adbhutaṁ dukūlam \|***  
***mama hṛdi nija-rāgam atra rādhe***  
***dadhad api yad dviguṇaṁ babhūva raktam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Rādhā! All glories to your wonderful, ruby-red silk cloth, which, inciting my** ***anurāga,*** **has doubled my attachment to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kamala-rāga-rāgam* means the color of a ruby. My attraction has doubled in attachment or color. This shows the great attachment in his heart. Here *rāga* stands for *anurāga,* produced by the excellence of the *viṣaya,* Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā. Your cloth is red like a ruby. It has produced *(dadhat) anurāga* in me (*nija-rāgam*). The nature of *anurāga* is that it makes one experience newer beauty at every moment in the *viṣaya.* Thus he says that it has doubled his attachment.

### Text 57

***bhūṣā, yathā—.***  
***praharatu hariṇā kadamba-puṣpaṁ***  
***priya-sakhi śekharitaṁ yad aṅgajāstram \|***  
***bata katham amunāvataṁsito’sau***  
***mama hṛdi bidhyati nīlakaṇṭha-pakṣaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Ornaments as stimuli: O friend! Why has the** ***kadamba*** **flower made into a chaplet by Kṛṣṇa become Cupid's weapon and attacked me? Why has the ornament made by Kṛṣṇa and ornamented with a peacock feather pierced my heart? How can the friend of Śiva do this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nīlakaṇṭha-pakṣaḥ* is a peacock feather. Nīlakaṇṭha is also Śiva, who is famous as Cupid’s enemy. Here Cupid is called the friend (*pakṣaḥ*) of Śiva. .

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. *Śeksharitam* means being an ornament in the hair. *Amara-koṣa* says *śekhari* means an ornament in the hair. It is the weapon of Cupid. It strikes me constantly, since it is his flower arrow. Why does the friend of Śiva pierce my heart? Medinī says *pakṣaḥ* means friend or helper. *Nīla-kaṇṭha-pakṣaḥ* is also a peacock feather. *Amara-koṣa* says *nīlakaṇṭha* means a peacock.

### Text 58

***yathā vā—***  
***hāreṇa tāra-dyutinā kapolaḥ***  
***preṅkholinā kuṇḍalayor yugena \|***  
***uttuṅga-bhāsā kanakāṅgadena***  
***māṁ lāliteyaṁ lalitā dhinoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: With her bright pearl necklace, the pair of earrings swinging at her cheeks, and her glistening golden armlets, Lalitā, served by** ***sakhīs,*** **enchants and delights me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa praises Lalitā. This acts as an *uddīpana* for Lalitā who directly or indirectly hears Kṛṣṇa’s statement. As in previous examples the ornaments act as an *uddīpana* for *rati.* She has a necklace of pure pearls (*tāta-dyutinā*). Lalitā served by *sakhīs (lalitā)* delights me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala speaks to Kṛṣṇa about Lalitā who is walking. She has a necklace of special pearls which shine. *Viśvak-kośa* says *tāra* means a center jewel or a special pure pearl. Lalitā means desirable, from the verb *lal,* to desire.

### Text 59

***mālyānulepane, yathā rasa-sudhākare (1.186a)—***  
***ālolair anumīyate madhukaraiḥ keśeṣu mālya-grahaḥ***  
***kāntiḥ kāpi kapolayoḥ prathayate tāmbūlam antargatam \|***  
***aṅgānām anubhūyate parimalair ālepana-prakriyā***  
***veṣaḥ ko’pi vidagdha eṣa sudṛśaḥ sūte sukhaṁ cakṣuṣoḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Garlands and cosmetics, from** ***Rasa-sudhākara:*** **One can guess that she has a garland in her hair by the buzzing bees. The beauty of her cheeks proclaims that she has betel in her mouth. By the fragrance one can guess that she has cosmetics on her limbs. These indescribable decorations of Rādhā bring great delight to my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This can also be taken as an *uddīpana* for Kṛṣṇa, if a *sakhī* hears from someone what Kṛṣṇa says. Other verses can be taken in a similar way.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. Though her head is covered, it can be established that she is wearing a garland in her hair because of the bees.

### Text 60

***yathā vā—***  
***anaṅga-rāgāya babhūva sadyas***  
***tavāṅga-rāgo’pi kim aṅganāsu \|***  
***uddāma-bhāvāya tathā kim āsīd***  
***dāmāpi dāmodara tāvakīnam \|\|60\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Dāmodara, are your bodily cosmetics being used for arousing love in the** ***gopīs*****? Are you using your garland for producing the purest love in them?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sakhī* jokes with Kṛṣṇa in front of Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A messenger speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Aṅga-rāga* is sandalwood and *kuṁkuma* ointment. Is your garland (*dāma*) for producing extremely pure (*uddāma) bhāva*? *Ud* can also have a negative meaning such as misfortune as in *udvartmanā gacchati*: he goes by the wrong road. Are you using your garland to produce dangerous emotions in the *sakhīs*?

### Text 61

***atha sambandhinaḥ—***  
***lagnāḥ sannihitāś ceti dvidhā sambandhino matāḥ \|\|61\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Related objects as** ***uddīpana:*** **Thee two types of related objects: attached objects and close objects.**

### Text 62

***tatra lagnāḥ—***  
***vaṁśī-śṛṅgī-ravau gītaṁ saurabhyaṁ bhūṣaṇa-kvaṇaḥ \|***  
***padāṅkādyā vipañcyādi-nikvāṇāḥ śilpa-kauśalam \|***  
***ity ādayo’tra kathitā lagnāḥ sambandhino budhaiḥ \|\|62\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Attached objects: The sound of the flute and horn, songs, fragrance, the sound of ornaments, foot prints, the sound of a vīṇā, and skill in arts are said to be attached objects by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *uddīpanas* listed, from qualities to decorations, exist directly on the hero and heroine. Related objects are those which exist indirectly. Attached objects like the sound of the flute cannot exist without the hero. Objects which exist without the hero or heroine are called close objects. However the sound of the flute could be included with calling the cows, walking etc. since they are all directly connected to the hero or heroine. Those which exist without direct relation are called related objects *(sambandhinaḥ*) Thus the sound of the flute could be included with the activities known as *līlā* (verse 43).

### Text 63

***tatra vaṁśī-ravo, dānakeli-kaumudyāṁ (32)—***  
***veṇor eṣa kala-svanas taru-latā-vyājṛmbhaṇe dohadaṁ***  
***sandhyā-garja-bharaḥ pika-dvija-kuhu-svādhyāya-pārāyaṇe \|***  
***ābhīrendu-mukhī-smarānala-śikhotseke salīlānilo***  
***rādhā-dhairya-dharādharendra-damane dambhohlir unmīlati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The sound of the flute, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **The soft sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute is the medicine for making the trees and vines burst into flower. That sound is the evening thunder that drowns out the cuckoos’ cries and brāhmaṇas' chanting the Vedas. It is a playful breeze that fans the flames of love in the moon-faced** ***gopīs*****. It is a thunderbolt that shatters Rādhā's mountain of self-control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The flute is the cause of all the items mentioned. *Pārāhyaṇe* means “in chanting the Vedas.” *Vyājṛmbhaṇe* means “making flowers bloom.” *Dohadam* means desirable.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Rādhā and others. The sound of the flute is the special medicine giving bliss that makes the flowers bloom. The sound of the flute overshadows completely the chanting of the Vedas and the warbling of cuckoos. The rumbling in the evening is thunder.

### Text 64

***yathā vā rasa-sudhākare (1.100) \[padyāvalyāṁ (246)\]—***  
***mādhavo madhura-mādhavī-latā-***  
***maṇḍape paṭu raṭan-madhuvrate \|***  
***saṁjagau śravaṇa-cāru gopikā-***  
***māna-mīna-vaḍiśena veṇunā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Rasa-sudākara*****: As Mādhava wanders in this pavilion of** ***mādhavī*** **creepers filled with buzzing bees, he expertly plays on his flute music pleasing to the ear. That flute is like a hook to catch the fish of the** ***gopīs'*** **hearts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse illustrated the sound of the flute acting as an *uddīpana* for Rādhā. Now an example is given as an uddīpana for all the *gopīs. Gopikā* here means all the *gopīs* who become Kṛṣṇa’s lovers.

### Text 65

***kṛṣṇa-vaktrendu-niṣṭhyūtaṁ muralī-ninadāmṛtam \|***  
***uddīpanānāṁ sarveṣāṁ madhye pravaram īryate \|\|65\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Of all the** ***uddīpanas,*** **the sweet flute music from the moon of Kṛṣṇa's mouth is said to be the best.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Niṣṭhyūtam* means “coming from.”

### Text 66

***śṛṅgī-ravaḥ—***  
***kaṁsārāteḥ pibatu muralī tasya sad-vaṁśa-janmā***  
***sā vaktrenduṁ sphuṭam akuṭilā pañcamodgāra-gurvī \|***  
***āsvādyāmuṁ tvam api viṣamā bhaṅgurāṅgāra-kālī***  
***tuṅgaṁ śṛṅgi dhvanasi yad idaṁ tat tu duḥkhākaroti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sound of his horn: Let Kṛṣṇa's flute, born in a family of pious bamboos, very straight, playing the fifth note with great virtuosity, drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's mouth. O buffalo-horn! You have crooked curves, are as black as coal and make discordant sounds. Even though you also drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, the sound you make brings us great pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks. The horn is big, but uneven. It is famous, but gives pain. The ending *duḥkhā* in *duḥkhā karoti* comes from the rule *duḥkhāt prātilomye* (Pāṇini 5.4.64)

### Text 67

***atha gītam—***  
***mānānalaṁ me śamayan samiddhaṁ***  
***gānāmṛtaṁ varṣati kṛṣṇa-meghaḥ \|***  
***mā krudhya vātyāsi sakhi prasīda***  
***dūre nayāmuṁ nija-vibhrameṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Singing: The black cloud of Kṛṣṇa rains the nectar of his singing to extinguish the blazing fire of my anger. O friend resembling the wind! Do not become angry with me. Be kind to me and, by your charm, send him far away from here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, after quarrelling with Kṛṣṇa, speaks to Lalitā. *Śamayan* means “in order to extinguish.” You are like the wind, since you make me move. If you are able, why do not make him move?

### Text 68

***saurabham—***  
***milati parimalormiḥ kasya roma-śriyāsau***  
***mama tanu-latikāyāṁ kurvatī kuḍmalāni \|***  
***sakhi viditam ihāgre mādhavaḥ prādurāsīd***  
***bhuvi surabhitayā yaḥ khyātim aṅgīkaroti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fragrance: What wealth of fragrance is now causing the hairs on the creeper of my body to stand up like flower buds? O friend! I think Mādhava must have come here, since only he has become famous in the world for his fragrance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another version has as the first line *milati parimala-śrīḥ kasya vā roma-mūle mama.* *Surabhitayā* means by his fragrance or by spring.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the forest for an appointment, Rādhā speaks. *Roma-śriyā* means “by the beauty of hairs standing on end.” Just as in the phrase *dadhy-odana* the word *utsika* is dropped, so in the phrase *roma-śriyā* the meaning is actually *roma-udgama-śriyā.* When Lalitā does not reply, she gives the answer. O friend! I suddenly know. *Surabhiḥ* means spring. Kṛṣṇa is fragrant. *Amara-koṣa* says that *surabhi* means spring and flowers.

### Text 69

***yathā vā—***  
***madayati hṛdayaṁ kim apy akāṇḍe***  
***mama yad idaṁ nava-saurabhaṁ varīyaḥ \|***  
***tad iha kusuma-saṁgrahāya rādhā***  
***śikhari-taṭe śikhara-dvijā viveśa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: A fresh, excellent fragrance has unexpectedly brought joy to my heart. Rādhā, whose teeth are as beautiful as pomegranate seeds, has come near the peak of Govardhana to collect flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is Kṛṣṇa’s statement while Rādhā secretly listens after wondering if Kṛṣṇa is nearby, since she has come to meet him. *Ākāṇde* means “unexpected.” *Śikhara* means a ruby, or the ripe seed of the pomegranate.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks.  *Śikhara* means a ruby, or the ripe seed of the pomegranate.

### Text 70

***bhūṣaṇa-kvaṇaḥ—***  
***kalahaṁsa-nādam iha haṁsa-gāminī***  
***niśamayya haṁsa-duhitus taṭāntare \|***  
***tava nūpura-dhvani-dhiyā pariplavā***  
***kalasīṁ na veda śirasaś cyutām api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sound of ornaments: While walking along the Yamunā's shore as gracefully as a swan, Rādhā, hearing the cooing of swans nearby, thought that the sound was your tinkling ankle-bells. She began to tremble. Forgetting the water pot on her head, it fell on the ground.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Pariplavā* means fickle or unsettled. She had the water for carrying water with devotion for worshipping the *devatās.* It was not because others were absent in her house that she was doing household chores, for it is said:

*ata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān*  
*harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramākrīḍam abhūn nṛpa*

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the home of Nanda Mahārāja is eternally the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and his transcendental qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed with the opulence of all wealth. Yet beginning from Lord Kṛṣṇa’s appearance there, it became the place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune. SB 10.5.18**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Pariplavā* means fickle or unsettled. *Amara-koṣa* says *pariplava* means fickle or trembling. Rādhā went to the shore of the Yamunā for a moment, thinking “I will personally carry these pots of water for *devatā* worship, even though we have servants. I will see Kṛṣṇa at a distance.”

### Text 71

***yathā vā lalita-mādhave (1.51)—***  
***madhurima-laharībhiḥ stambhayaty ambare yā***  
***smara-mada-sarasānāṁ sārasānāṁ rutāni \|***  
***iyam udayati rādhā-kiṅkinī-jhaṅkṛtir me***  
***hṛdi pariṇamayantī vikriyāḍambarāṇi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **By its waves of its sweetness, the tinkling of Rādhā's ankle-bells, which derides the cooing of the cranes maddened with passion and which makes me attain perfection, produces the highest transformations of love in my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks while Rādhā can hear, since she is not far away. *Pariṇamayantī* means “makes one attain perfection.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Desiring to see Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa begins to speculate. *Stambhayati* means derides. *Pariṇamayantī* means “make one attain perfection.”

### Text 72

***padāṅkādyāḥ, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyāṁ (13)—***  
***pada-tatibhir alaṅkṛtojjvaleyaṁ***  
***dhvaja-kuliśāṅkuśa-paṅkajāṅkitābhiḥ \|***  
***nakhara-luṭhita-kuṭmalā vanālī***  
***kim api dhinoti dhunoti cāntaraṁ me \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Foot marks, from** ***Dana-keli-kaumudi*****: The resplendent forest, decorated with his footprints marked with flag, thunderbolt, elephant goad, and lotus, whose flower buds are touched by his nails, gives me extraordinary delight and makes me tremble within.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks. The forest range *(vanālī*) is decorated with many foot prints marked with the flag, thunderbolt, elephant goad, and lotus.  *Pada* here means foot print, not foot. Or *pada* can be sign. Or the beautiful forest women (*ālī*) are decorated with marks by Kṛṣṇa. The forest has buds touched (*luṭhita)* by his nails, when he picks flowers using his hands. Or the women have breasts which are scratched by his nails, with Kṛṣṇa in an inferior position. That forest gives me pleasure (*dhinoti*) by seeing the marks of his feet and his nails and makes me tremble (*dhunoti*), since I develop pain out of long to see him directly. Or, the *sakhī (ālī)* who has been enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa gives me pleasure since I have affection for her and she makes me tremble because of the marks of enjoyment on her body. Seeing those marks, I develop desire.

### Text 73

***vipañcī-nikvāṇo, yathā lalita-mādhave (1.36)—***  
***smara-keli-nāṭya-nāndīṁ***  
***śabda-brahma-śriyaṁ muhur duhatī \|***  
***vahati mudaṁ mama mahatīm***  
***iha mahitā śyāmalā-mahatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sound of the** ***vīṇā,*** **from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **Filled with prologues to a drama of Cupid’s sports and fulfilling the wealth of sound in the form of the Vedas, Śyāmalā's glorious** ***vīṇā*** **brings me great happiness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse is similar to verse 71. *śabda-brahma-śriyam* means “that which makes full the wealth of Vedic sound.” The vīṇā *(vipañcī)* is filled with prologues to a drama of Cupid’s play.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa, wanting to see Śyāmalā, speaks. Her *vīṇā* produces great joy in me. *Amara-koṣa* says *mahatī* is a type of *vīṇā.* The sound completes the wealth of sound, which is the Vedas. It is the dramatic prologue for Cupid’s sports.

### Text 74

***śilpa-kauśalaṁ, yathā—***  
***vara-kusuma-niveśa-prakriyā-sauṣṭhavena***  
***prakaṭita-hari-śilpā paṭṭa-sūtrojjvala-śrīḥ \|***  
***hṛdi vinihita-kampā nirmimīte srag eṣā***  
***niśita-śara-parīta-smāra-tuṇīr aśaṅkām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Skilful crafts: This brilliant garland, strung with great skill by Kṛṣṇa on a silken string and revealing expertise in arranging the best flowers, produces the doubt that perhaps it is Cupid's quiver filled with sharpened arrows-- since it makes my heart tremble.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing a garland given by Kṛṣṇa through a forest deity, Rādhā begins to think. One would mistake it for the quiver of Cupid. The phrase *hṛdi vinihita-kampā* is an example of a compound where a word (*hṛdi*) retains its ending instead of dropping it as is normally done.

### Text 75-76

***atha sannihitāḥ—***  
***nirmālyādyāḥ sannihitā barha-guñjādri-dhātavaḥ \|***  
***naicikīnāṁ samudayo laguḍī-veṇu-śṛṅgīkāḥ \|\|\|***  
***tat-preṣṭha-dṛṣṭir godhūlir vṛndāraṇyaṁ tad-āśritāḥ \|***  
***govardhano ravisutā tathā rāsa-sthalādayaḥ \|\|76\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Close objects: Things closely related by the beloved are remnants of flowers and other things offered to the beloved; peacock feathers;** ***guñja*** **berries; mineral pigments from the hills and mountains; the herd of cows; the stick; flute; buffalo-horn bugle; the sight of his friends; dust raised by the cows; Vṛndāvana forest; the inhabitants of the forest; Govardhana Hill; the Yamunā River; the** ***rāsa-*****dance arena and other places of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Items which are near” means items which are related to those items by type, since simply by seeing any peacock feather, not just the one on Kṛṣṇa’s head, one’s *bhāva* is aroused.

### Text 77

***tatra nirmālyādyāḥ, yathā vidagdha-mādhavādau (2.42)—***  
***aṅgottīrṇa-vilepanaṁ sakhi samākṛṣṭi-kriyāyāṁ maṇir***  
***mantro hanta muhur vaśīkṛti-vidhau nāmāsya vaṁśī-pateḥ \|***  
***nirmālya-srag iyaṁ mahauṣadhir iha svāntasya sammohane***  
***nāsāṁ kas tisṛṇāṁ gṛṇāti paramācintyāṁ prabhāvāvalīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Remnants: O friend! The sandal paste from Kṛṣṇa's forehead is a jewel that draws people to it. The name of Kṛṣṇa, the husband of the flute, is a mantra that brings people under its control. Kṛṣṇa's flower-garland is a great herb that charms people's hearts. Who does not speak of the inconceivable power of these three things?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Who will not speak of these three—the ointments, the name and the garland remnants?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Who will not speak of the gem, mantra and herbal power of the ointments, name and garland? Because *nāma* is neuter the word *āsām* in the feminine is wrong. The word should be *eṣām* according to the rule *napuṁsakam anapuṁsakena*: in a series of words with mixed gender, the neuter prevails. (Pāṇini 1.2.69) That is true. However at the end of the description of the three, *oṣadhi* is mentioned. This is a feminine noun. For consideration of the continuity and to avoid interruption of the poetic meaning by breaking the order, they can be considered as *dvandva* compounds: *vilepana-nāma-srajām* and *maṇi-mantra-mahauṣadhīnām*. Thus they take the feminine ending of the last item. This is poetic knowledge, not grammatical proficiency. Kṛṣṇa is called the husband of the flute. The flute is his legitimate wife, but also the messenger to bring married women. Kṛṣṇa becomes strong because of the flute and these three methods. Therefore his desires must be fulfilled.

### Text 78

***yathā vā lalita-mādhave (6.26)—***  
***dukūle’smin kārtasvara-mahasi vistārita-dṛśo***  
***vapuḥ kiṁ te phullair vahati tulanāṁ nīpa-kusumaiḥ \|***  
***truṭantībhiḥ kiṁ vā sphaṭika-maṇi-mālābhir upamāṁ***  
***labhante’mī kṣāmodari nayanayos toya-pṛṣatāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O slender-waisted girl! As you stare with wide eyes at this splendid golden cloth, why does your body become covered with upright hairs like blossoming kadamba flowers, and why do the tears flow from your eyes like broken strands of crystal?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Toya-pṛṣatāḥ* means drops of water.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī questions Rādhā, who does not know about the stories of a new Vṛndāvana in Dvārakā. *Kārtasvaram* means gold. *Toya-pṛṣatāḥ* means drops of water.

### Text 79

*atha barha-guñje, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.16)—*  
***agre prekṣya śikhaṇḍa-khaṇḍam acirād utkampam ālambate***  
***guñjānāṁ ca vilokanān muhur asau sāsraṁ parikrośati \|***  
***no jāne janayann apūrva-naṭana-krīḍā-camatkāritāṁ***  
***bālāyāḥ kila citta-bhūmim aviśat ko ‘yaṁ navīna-grahaḥ \|\|79\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Peacock feathers and** ***guñja*** **berries, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **Upon seeing peacock feathers in front of her, this girl suddenly begins trembling. When she sees** ***gūnjā*** **berries, she constantly cries with tears in her eyes. I do not know if some young demon had possessed her heart, causing astonishment by unprecedented dancing**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mukharā* informs Paurṇamāsī about the activities of Rādhā.

### Text 80

***adri-dhātur, yathā—***  
***ābhīra-vṛndādhipa-nandanasya***  
***kalevarālaṅkaraṇojjvala-śrīḥ \|***  
***kṣiptendra-gopāṁśur apāṁśulo’yaṁ***  
***tanoti rāgaṁ mama dhātu-rāgaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Minerals from the mountain: These uncontaminated, bright mineral pigments that decorate the body of the prince of the cowherds and that deride the color of the cochineal insect make me thirsty to see him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Apāṁśula* means uncontaminated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, in separation, seeing the red minerals of Govardhana, speaks. Those minerals are uncontaminated (*apāṁśula*) and defeat the red color of cochineal bug. *Rāga* means “thirst to see him.”

### Text 81

***naicikī-samudayo, yathā—***  
***sandhyā-dyote vilasati gatāḥ prekṣya goṣṭha-prakoṣṭhe***  
***hambārambhonmukharita-mukhī-naicikīs tvad-vihīnāḥ \|***  
***antaś-cintā-culukita-matir yādavendrādya mandā***  
***kaṣṭaṁ candrāvalir iha kathaṁ prāṇa-bandhaṁ karotu \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The cows: When Candrāvalī sees the cows in the pen at sunset, mooing in separation from you, she becomes miserable, absorbed in thought. O king of the Yādavas, in this circumstance, how will she be able to remain alive?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā somehow sends a message to Kṛṣṇa when he is residing in Mathurā. When twilight appears (*sandhyā-dyote*), when she sees the cows moo in the yard near the cow pens, she becomes miserable. O king of the Yādavas! You are king of the cowherds by birth, but have become king of the Yadus. How will you remember us cowherd women? We have such bad fortune!

### Text 82

***laguḍī, yathā—***  
***viṣṭabhya yāṁ bhuvi puraḥ śikharārpitena***  
***vinyasta-cāru-cibukena kara-dvayena \|***  
***dīvyan harir giri-taṭe mudam ādadhān naḥ***  
***sā hanta yasṭir adhunā hṛdayaṁ pinaṣṭi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The stick: Support the stick on the ground, Kṛṣṇa, attractive on Govardhana Hill with his hand and charming chin resting on its tip, gave us great joy. Now that stick thrashes my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *gopī* laments for Kṛṣṇa who has gone to Mathurā. Supporting the stick on the earth in front of him, he appears attractive with his hands making a fist or with palms turned down on the tip.

### Text 83

***veṇur, yathā—***  
***hṛdi nyastā vaṁśī tad-adhara-sudhā-bhāg iti mayā***  
***durantaṁ viśleṣa-jvara-garalam asyāḥ śamayitum \|***  
***vitene sā tūrṇaṁ śata-guṇam idaṁ yādava-pate***  
***virakto yatreśas tam iha na hi vā kaḥ praharati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The flute: Because your flute contains the nectar of your lips, I placed it against Rādhā’s heart to counteract the unbearable poison of separation from you. Instead of counteracting the poison, that flute increased the poison by hundreds of times. O king of the Yadavas, if the master is disinterested in her, can not the servant then attack her?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā sends a message through a swan to Kṛṣṇa. I placed the flute on her heart since it was burning with the poison of separation from you, because it is well known that nectar counteracts poison, and that flute has the nectar of your lips. But my strategy had the opposite effect. The flute (*sā*) produced a hundred times the poison of fever in separation. There is *arthāntara-nyāsa* in this verse. When the master is a little detached from a person, cannot anyone related to him attack the person? Thus the nectar of your lips in the flute’s holes increases the poison because of hatred for her (following your example).

### Text 84

***śṛṅgikā, yathā—***  
***valitaṁ vilocanāgre, śavalaṁ dhūlibhir idaṁ balāvaraja \|***  
***balavat kuvalaya-nayanās tava gavalaṁ kavalayaty adya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The horn: O brother of Balarāma! Your bent, dust-spotted buffalo-horn devours the lotus eyed** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Gavalam* is the horn of a wild buffalo. This is not the only type of horn. There are rhinoceros and other horns as well.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Uddhava returns from Vraja to Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa ask him about his horn and stick. Uddhava answers*. Valitam śavalam dhūlibhiḥ* means covered with spots of dust. That buffalo horn devours the lotus-eyed *gopīs*. Though the horn was kept in a safe place because he did not use it, it is covered with dust.

### Text 85

***tat-preṣṭha-dṛṣṭir, yathā—***  
***sakhi mṛgamada-lekhayā viśākhā-***  
***hṛdi makarīr api rādhikā likhantī \|***  
***subalam avakalayya ghūrṇitāgre***  
***pulakavatī vana-mālinaṁ lilekha \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Kṛṣṇa’s friends: When Rādhā was drawing dolphins in musk on Viśākhā's breasts, she happened to see Subala nearby. Agitated with love, the hairs of her body standing on end, she drew a picture of Kṛṣṇa. .**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a *sakhī.*

### Text 86

***yathā vā lalita-mādhave (6.43)—***  
***nikhila-suhṛdām arthārambhe vilambita-cetasā***  
***masṛṇita-śikho yaḥ prāpto'bhūd manāg iva mārdavam \|***  
***sa khalu lalitā-sāndra-sneha-prasaṅga-ghanībhavan***  
***punar api balād indhe rādhā-viyoga-mayaḥ śikhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**
