**Another example, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: As I was busy pleasing my friends, the fire of separation from Rādhā remained subdued and peaceful for a moment, but now because of Lalitā's intense love for her, that fire has suddenly begun to blaze strongly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is comedy in *Lalita-mādhava*. Lalitā of Vraja was Jāmbavatī. Born in Vraja as Lalitā, by the power of *yoga-māyā* she became Jāmbavatī in Jāmabavān’s house for bringing her back to Kṛṣṇa and protecting her as a child. She was given to Kṛṣṇa at the time of stealing the Syamantaka gem. Similarly, Rādhā by *yoga-māyā’s* power appeared in Satrājit’s house as Satyabhāmā. She was not known by Kṛṣṇa in the beginning. This verse describes Kṛṣṇa’s feeling of separation from her on attaining Lalitā. In the section on *sthāyi-bhāva* the contradictions will be resolved. When Lalitā sees herself as Jambavatī attaining Kṛṣṇa, she remembers the feelings of separation of her friend Rādhā, instead of remembering Kṛṣṇa. In remembering Rādhā, she criticizes her own happiness of enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa at the present. Finally the feeling of separation caused by the illusion of having illicit love produces the enjoyment of love in being married to Kṛṣṇa

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Madhumaṅgala. Because my mind became absorbed (*vilambita*) in efforts of fixing my friends like Vasudeva and Ugrasena in their positions while quelling Jarāsanda and other demons, my fire of separation from Rādhā, burning slowly, became mild. It has now become intense because of the intense prema Lalitā has for her. Or it has become intense because of the *ghṛta-sneha*. “Oh! Why has that friend of Lalitā gone away from me?” *Śikhī* means fire.

### Text 87

***godhūlir, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (37)—***  
***ā-pratyūṣād api sumanasāṁ vīthibhir grathyamānā***  
***dhatte nāsau sakhi katham aho vaijayantī samāptim \|***  
***dhinvan gopī-nayana-śikhinaḥ vyoma-kakṣām jagāhe***  
***so’yaṁ mugdhe niviḍa-dhavalo dhūli-cakrāmbuvāhaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Cow dust, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: My friend, since morning you have been stringing these flowers. Why have you not completed the** ***vaijayantī*** **garland by now? O beautiful one, the dense white cloud of dust raised by the cows has now entered the sky, to the great delight of the peacocks of the** ***gopī's*** **eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Candrāvalī. *Śikhinaḥ* means peacocks. *Vyoma-kakṣām* means a place in the sky. *Ambuvāhaḥ* means clouds.

### Text 88

***vṛndāraṇyaṁ, yathā tatraiva (83)—***  
***āśā-pāśaiḥ sakhi nava-navaiḥ kurvatī prāṇa-bandhaṁ***  
***jātyā bhīruḥ kati punar ahaṁ vāsarāṇi kṣayiṣye \|***  
***ete vṛndāvana-viṭapinaḥ smārayantaḥ vilāsān***  
***utphullās tān mama kila balān marma nirmūlayanti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Vṛndāvana forest, from the same work: O friend! With newer and newer ropes of hope I keep my life tightly bound. By nature I am a timid woman. How many days can I endure in this way? Reminding me of his pastimes, the blossoming trees of Vṛndāvana violently uproot my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, feeling separation when Kṛṣṇa is in Mathurā, laments. How many days will I hope that today or tomorrow he will come? How many days will I tolerate this great difficulty, tying my life airs to this hope? But please hear of another problem. The trees are flowering. I am reminded of the pastimes with flowers that we experienced.

### Text 89

***tad-āśritāḥ—***  
***tad-āśrityāḥ khagā bhṛṅgā mṛgāḥ kuñjā latās tathā \|***  
***tulasī karṇikāraś ca kadambādyāś ca kīrtitāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of the forest: The living entities which have taken shelter of Vṛndāvana forest that act as** ***uddīpanas*** **are birds, bumble-bees, deer, bowers, creepers,** ***tulasī, karnikāra*****,** ***kadamba*** **and other flowers.**

### Text 90

***tatra khagāḥ, yathā lalita-mādhave (10.16)—***  
***kas tān paśyan bhavad-upahṛta-snigdha-piñchāvataṁsān***  
***kaṁsārāte na khalu śikhinaḥ khidyate goṣṭhavāsī \|***  
***unmīlantaṁ nava-jaladharaṁ nīlam adyāpi matvā***  
***ye tvām antar-mudita-matayas tanvate tāṇḍavāni \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Birds, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O enemy of Kaṁsa! Observing those peacocks which have offered you their feathers for your head ornaments, and which, seeing an approaching rain cloud, think that you have come back, and begin to dance with joy in their mind, what person of Vraja would not become disturbed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurnamāsī speaks to Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā.

### Text 91

***bhṛṅgāḥ, yathā—***  
***vṛndāvane śravasi ye ninadaṁ vipañcī-***  
***niṣṭhyūta-pañcama-manoharam āharantaḥ \|***  
***te ṣaṭpadāḥ kuliśa-ghaṭṭana-ghoram etaṁ***  
***daive virodhini bhavanti na ke vipakṣāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bees: These bumble-bees of Vṛndāvana which produce for the ear the attractive fifth note resounding from a** ***vīṇā*** **now produce the terrible sound of a thunder clap. Who will not become the enemy of one with bad destiny?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks in separation. The bees produce an attractive sound of the fifth note coming from a *vīṇā* but now they produce the sound of terrifying thunder

### Text 92

***mṛgāḥ, yathā tatraiva—***  
***hari hari bhavatībhiḥ svāntahārī hariṇyo***  
***harir iha kim apāṅgātithya-saṅgī vyadhāyi \|***  
***yad anuraṇita-vaṁśī-kākalībhir mukhebhyaḥ***  
***sukha-tṛṇa-kavalā vaḥ sāmi-līḍhāḥ skhalanti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Deer, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: O does! Has he who steals hearts become the guest of your glances? I think it is so because on hearing the echoing sound of his flute, the grass is falling, half-eaten, from your mouths.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sāmi* means half.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In *Lalita-mādhava*, Rādhā, in madness, searches for Kṛṣṇa after he has left for Mathurā. *Hari hari* indicates lamentation. The mouthfuls of grass which give happiness remain half-swallowed.

### Text 93

***kuñjāḥ, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (125)—***  
***labdhāndolaḥ praṇaya-rabhasād eṣa tāmrauṣṭhi namraḥ***  
***pramlāyantīṁ kim api bhavatīm yācate nanda-sūnuḥ \|***  
***premoddāma-pramada-padavī sākṣiṇī śaila-kakṣe***  
***draṣṭavyā te katham api na sā mādhavī kuñja-lekhā vīthī3 \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Bowers, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: O girl with red lips! Agitated by passionate love, Nanda's son in all humility begs you who are withering from grief. You should not look at the many jasmine bowers of Govardhana Hill, witness to our great joy of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a message sent by Kṛṣṇa to Rādhā. Śaila-kakṣe means “in the mountain forest.” According to Dharani-kośa, kakṣa means a forest, armpit or shrub.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa sends a message to Rādhā through Uddhava. Because of his strong love for her, he has become agitated *(labhdāndolanaḥ*). *Śaila-kakṣe* mean at Govardhana or in a forest there. *Dharaṇi-kośa* says *kakṣa* means a forest or shrub. She should not look at the rows (l*ekhā*) of bowers. They will make her remember the pastimes and cause her to die.

### Text 94

***latādir, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (295)—***  
***tulasi vilasasi tvaṁ malli jātāsi phullā***  
***sthala-kamalini bhṛṅge saṅgatāṅgī vibhāsi \|***  
***kathayata bata sakhyaḥ kṣipram asmāsu kasmin***  
***vasati kapaṭa-kandaḥ kandare nanda-sūnuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Creepers, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O** ***tulasī*****! You are very beautiful. O jasmine vine! You are filled with splendid blossoms. O land-growing lotus flower! You shine with all these bumble-bees. O friends! Please tell me at once in which cave Kṛṣṇa, the king of cheaters, is staying?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

As previously (verse92) Rādhā speaks.

### Text 95

***karṇikāro, yathā lalita-mādhave (7.15)—***  
***rāsāt tirohita-tanuḥ sakhi yasya puṣpaiś***  
***cūḍāṁ cakāra cikure mama piñcha-cūḍaḥ \|***  
***kūle kalinda-duhitur dhṛta-kandalo’yaṁ***  
***māṁ dandahīti sa muhur nava-karṇikāraḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***karnikāra*** **flower, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: O friend! These new** ***karṇikāras*** **coming from shoots on the Yamunā's shore, the same kind of flowers peacock-feather-crowned Kṛṣṇa placed in my hair when he left the arena of the rāsa dance with me, now make me burn with pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, wandering in Nava-vṛndāvana, laments. *Dhṛta-kandalaḥ* means “coming from shoots.”

### Text 96

***kadambo, yathā—***  
***sakhi ropito dvipatraḥ***  
***śatapatrākṣeṇa yo vraja-dvāri \|***  
***so’yaṁ kadamba-ḍimbhaḥ***  
***phullo vallava-vadhūs tudati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kadamba:*** **O my friend, at the gateway of Vraja village, lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa planted this** ***kadamba*** **tree when it was a sapling with only two leaves. Now this** ***kadamba*** **tree in full bloom causes the** ***gopīs*** **great pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Someone separated from Kṛṣṇa when he went to Mathurā speaks.

### Text 97

***govardhano, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.42)—***  
***govardhana tvam iha gokula-saṅgi-bhūmau***  
***tuṅgaiḥ śirobhir abhipadya nabho vibhāsi \|***  
***tenāvalokya haritaḥ parito vadāśu***  
***kutrādya vallava-maṇiḥ khalu khelatīti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Govardhana, from** ***Lalita-Mādhava*****: O Govardhana! You shine very splendidly in this land around Gokula, touching the heavens with your many lofty peaks. Please look in all directions from your height and tell me where the jewel of the cowherd boys plays today.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, in the madness of separation, asks this question while searching for Kṛṣṇa. Govardhana touches the sky (*nabhah*) with its peaks. *Haritaḥ* means “in the directions.”

### Text 98

***ravi-sutā, yathā padyāvalyām (368)—***  
***mathurā-pathika murārer***  
***upageyaṁ dvāri vallavī-vacanam \|***  
***punar api yamunā-salile***  
***kāliya-garalānalo jvalati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Yamunā, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O traveler to Mathurā! At Lord Kṛṣṇa's door you should sing this message from the** ***gopīs:*** **The fire of Kāliya's poison again burns in the Yamunā's water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Rādhā sends a message. Previously the poison affected Kāliya’s lake. Now the whole Yamunā is affected.

### Text 99

***rāsa-sthalī, yathā—***  
***goṣṭhād apy avalokyamāna-śikharocchrāya-śriyā dūrataḥ***  
***sadyaḥ khedini citta-catvara-taṭe vaṁśī-vaṭenārpitā \|***  
***kurvāṇā hṛta-vṛttim indriya-gaṇaṁ sā yādavendrādya te***  
***kaṣṭaṁ rāsa-vihāra-bhur viharati prāṇaiḥ kuraṅgī-dṛśām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The place of the** ***rāsa*** **dance: O king of the Yādavas! When the beautiful doe-eyed** ***gopīs*** **glance from Vraja at the beautiful top of Vaṁśī-baṭa far away, it places the** ***rāsa*** **arena in their suffering hearts. Having robbed the** ***gopīs*** **of their senses, the** ***rāsa*** **arena pulls out their life airs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The famous Vaṁśī-batā is a banyan tree situated in Vṛndāvana. “Playing with life airs” is an expression taken from *Gīta-govinda*. This means “plays in the form of pulling out their life airs.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava, returning to Mathurā from Vraja, speaks to Kṛṣṇa, who has asked about the place of the *rāsa* dance. O king of the Yādavas! Now you give happiness to the Yādavas. The place of the *rāsa* dance now plays with the live airs of the doe-eyed *gopīs.* Previously it played with their eyes. It pulls the life airs from their bodies and plays with them. “Suffering in separation from me they stay in the village. The place of the *rāsa* is far away. How do they happen to meet with the place?” Vaṁśī-baṭa places the *rāsa* arena in the courtyard of their hearts, in order to pull out their life airs. “How does it do this?” By the beauty of the top of Vaṁśī-batā, which is situated at the edge of the *rāsa* arena, which is seen from Nandīśvara, the *rāsa* arena enters their hearts. Vaṁśī-baṭa, a cause of misfortune, enters their eyes and brings the *rāsa* arena into their hearts. The *rāsa* arena then pulls out their life airs.

### Text 100

***atha taṭasthāḥ—***  
***taṭasthāś candrikā-megha-vidyuto mādhavas tathā \|***  
***śarat-pūrṇa-sudhāṁśuś ca gandhavāha-khagādayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Ordinary objects: Prominent among the ordinary objects that act as** ***uddīpanas*** **are the moonlight, clouds, lightning, springtime, autumn, the full-moon, the breeze, and the birds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Taṭasthāḥ* means ordinary objects.

### Text 101

***tatra candrikā, yathā rasa-sudhākare (1.87)—***  
***durāsade candrikayā sakhī-gaṇair***  
***latāli-kuñje lalitā nigūhitā \|***  
***cakora-cañcu-cyuta-kaumudī-kaṇaṁ***  
***kuto’pi dṛṣṭvā bhajati sma mūrcchanām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Moonlight, from** ***Rasa-sudhākara*****: Lalitā was hidden by her friends in a bower of creepers so thick that even the moonlight could not enter. Seeing a single drop of moon light, as if falling from a cakora bird's beak, Lalitā fainted**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She saw a beam of moonlight, which looked as if it had fallen from a *cakora’s* beak.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Lalitā speaks this news when asked by some other *sakhī.* Lalitā was kept hidden in a bower that could not been penetrated by moon light, in order to maintain her life, since she was suffering separation. However, she saw a particle of moon light coming through a hole in a leaf of a creeper.

### Text 102

***megho, yathā rasa-sudhākare—***  
***vāsaḥ pītaṁ kutukini kutaḥ kutra barhaṁ madāndhe***  
***kaṁsārir vā kva nu sakhi mudhā sambhramān mā prayāhi \|***  
***paśyottuṅge kṣaṇa-ruci-ghaṭāliṅgitaḥ śaila-śṛṅge***  
***navyaḥ śakraṁ dadhad udayate kārmukaṁ vār-mug eṣaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A cloud, from** ***Rasa-sudhākara*****: Where is that yellow garments? Where is the peacock feather? Where is the enemy of Kaṁsa? O eager friend, blind with passion! Please do not fall into illusion because of your agitation. Look! On the high peak of the mountain is a fresh cloud embraced by a lightning flash, and supporting a rainbow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā says “Oh! Kṛṣṇa, with his yellow garment and peacock feather, desires to grab me on the peak of Govardhana. I will not go that way.” Lalitā speaks to Rādhā who has turned to go. O Rādhā full of desire (*kutukini)!* You are always meditating on him, desiring pastimes with him at all times. Thus you see him everywhere. .*Kṣaṇa-ruci* means lightning. *Vār-muk* is a cloud.

### Text 103

***vidyut, yathā rasa-sudhākare (1.98)—***  
***varṣāsu tāsu kṣaṇa-ruk-prakāśād***  
***gopāṅganā mādhavam āliliṅga \|***  
***vidyuc ca sā vīkṣya tad-aṅga-śobhāṁ***  
***hrīṇeva tūrṇaṁ jaladaṁ jagāhe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lightning, from** ***Rasa-sudhākara*****: During the monsoon rain when lightning flashed, the** ***gopī*** **embraced Mādhava. When a lightning flash saw the beauty of her form, it quickly merged with the cloud in shyness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kṣaṇa-ruk* means lightning. Another version has *varṣāsu vidyud valaya-prakāśād. Iva* indicates a comparison.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Nāndīmukhī about what happened the night before. The *gopī* embraced Kṛṣṇa so that Kṛṣṇa would not see her uncovered body when the lightning flashed. She did this out of shyness. The lightning then disappeared immediately. The reason is given. Out of shyness on seeing her form, it merged with the cloud immediately.

### Text 104

***vasanto, yathā—***  
***ṛtu-hatakaḥ sakhi bhuvane***  
***kim avatatīrṣur babhūvādya \|***  
***mandādaram ali-vṛndaṁ***  
***vṛndāvana-kunda-saṅgame yad abhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Spring season: O friend! Why would this wretched spring season want to come into this world now? Even bees show little enthusiasm to meet with the** ***kunda*** **flowers of Vṛndāvana.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Ṛtu-hatakaḥ* means “the wretched person called the season.” This means the season has no sense of discrimination.

### Text 105

***śarat, yathā—***  
***kalahaṁsojjvala-jalpā***  
***prakaṭita-vṛndāvanoru-mādhuryā \|***  
***dhṛtim apahartuṁ sakhi me***  
***dūtīva hareḥ śaran militā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Autumn season: Has the autumn, revealing the intense sweetness of Vṛndāvana, filled with the attractive murmuring of swans, come like a messenger of Kṛṣṇa to steal my composure?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* describes the autumn season.  *Kalahāmsa* should be in the plural.

### Text 106

***pūrṇa-sudhāṁśur, yathā—***  
***rākā-sudhāṁśur abhavan na tamāṁsi hartuṁ***  
***vṛndāṭavī-jaṭharagāny adhunāpi śaktaḥ \|***  
***rākā-sudhāṁśu-mukhi tāni tavonnatāni***  
***hṛt-kandarāntara-carāṇi kathaṁ jahāra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The full moon: This full moon has no power to remove the darkness completely from Vṛndāvana. O moon-faced Rādhā! How is it then able to remove the more intense darkness of anger residing in the cave of your heart?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tāni* refers to darkness or suffering in the form of anger. O Rādhā with a face like the full moon! This address indicates the doubling of doubt that the anger can be removed, since that brilliant face does not meet and destroy the darkness of the heart. .

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tāni* refers to anger. O Rādhā with a face like the moon! Seeing your face, one can understand that the regular moon cannot remove your anger.

### Text 107

***gandhavāho, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (7.39)—***  
***mano-bhavānandana-candanānila***  
***prasīda re dakṣiṇa muñca vāmatām \|***  
***kṣaṇaṁ jagat-prāṇa vidhāya mādhavaṁ***  
***puro mama prāṇa-haro bhaviṣyasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The wind, from** ***Gīta-govinda*****: O breeze filled with the fragrance of the sandalwood! O bestower of Cupid’s bliss! O compliant wind! Please give up your contrary nature. O life of the universe! Please place Mādhava before me for a moment. Then you can take away my life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

On being cheated, Rādhā laments. O wind! You give bliss to Cupid (*manobhava*) since you help him by taking away my life air (part of wind element) while I am so compliant. O wind filled with sandalwood fragrance! Why do you not cool me? “I am the servant of the king, Cupid. I do as he orders. I do not do otherwise.” Ah (*re*)! This is a sign of contempt. If you want to kill me, then what courtesy do you need to do it? *Dakṣina* means wind coming from the south and also a person who is gentle. For a moment give up your contrary attitude (*vāmatām*) to me. If you are engaged in Cupid’s service, do not give up your inborn nature. But give it up for a moment. “Tell me what act should I perform according to my nature?” O life of the universe! *Jagat-prāṇa* is a synonym for wind. I am also living in the universe, but if you want to take my life, then at least for a moment place Mādhava in front of me. Since you are his friend you can bring him. Mādhava means the spring season as well as Kṛṣṇa. Do not fail to do this, so that one time before I die I can see him.

### Text 108

***khagāḥ, yathā—***  
***mānena sārdhaṁ paśupāla-subhruvāṁ***  
***marāla-mālā calitā ghanāgame \|***  
***kadamba-kuñje vijihīrṣayā samaṁ***  
***samāgatā nāgari cātakāvalī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Birds: O clever woman! Now that the clouds have come, the swans have left with the anger of** ***gopīs*** **and a flock** ***cātakā*** **birds Cātaka birds subsist on rain drops. 4 have come to enjoy in this** ***kadamba*** **forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā.

### Text 109

***ādi-śabdāt sakhī-sneha ātmany uddīpano varaḥ \|\|109\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Word** ***ādi*** **(etc.) in text 100 indicates a** ***sakhī’s*** **affection acting as a person’s** ***uddīpana*** **for Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 110

***yathā—***  
***harim avekṣya puro guruto bhiyā***  
***muhur abhūn mukulan-nava-vibhramā \|***  
***lalitayā vivṛte nija-sauhṛde***  
***cala-dṛg-añcalam ādhita rādhikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Looking at Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā became frightened because her elderly relatives were nearby and hid her fresh agitation. When Lalitā’s friendship became manifest in her, Rādhā glanced at Kṛṣṇa from the corner of her restless eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā and Lalitā had made some separate agreement out of friendship. *Ādhita* means “she offered.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to her *sakhī.* On glancing at Kṛṣṇa she developed fear of her elders. She thought that her husband or mother-in-law would come. Out of great fear or out of fear of elders she restricted her agitation. Her agitation became like a bud. Her agitation became invisible. Lalitā understood that Kṛṣṇa wanted to see her agitation. She said, “O dear *sakhī*! He who has given up Candrāvalī, who has affection for elders, has taken shelter of me, since I am great friends with you. I comforted him, telling him you were close by. Enough with fear! Listening to me today and ignoring your elders, accept him by giving him a glance of your mercy.”

## Chapter 11 - Anubhāvas

## Outline

I*. Anubhavās*

A. *Alaṅkāra*

1\. Bodily

- *Bhāva*
- *Hāva*
- *Helā*

2\. Without effort

- *śobhā*
- *kānti*  
   \- *dīpti*  
   \- *mādhurya*  
   \- *pragalbhatā*  
   \- *audārya*  
   \- *dhairya*

3\. from their nature

- l*īlā*
- *vilāsa*
- *vicchiti*  
   \- *vibhrama*  
   \- *kilakiṅcita*  
   \- *moṭtāyita*  
   \- *kuṭtamita*  
   \- *bibboka*
- *lalita*  
   \- *vikṛta*
- *maudghyam*
- *cakitam*

B*. Udbhāsvara*

- loosening of the undergarment
- loosening of the bodice
- loosening of the dressed hair
- crushing the limbs
- yawning
- expansion of nostrils
- sighing

C*. Vācika*

- *Ālāpa*  
   \- *Vilāpa*
- *Saṁlāpa*  
   \- *Pralāpa*
- *Anulāpa*
- *Apalapa*  
   \- *Sandeśa*  
   \- *Ātideśa*  
   \- *Apadeśa*  
   \- *Upadeśa*  
   \- *Nirdeśa*  
   \- *Vyapadeśa.*

### Text 1

***anubhāvās tv alaṅkārās tathaivodbhāsvarābhidhāḥ \|***  
***vācikāś ceti vidvadbhis tridhāmī parikīrtitāḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are three types of** ***anubhāvas: alaṅkāra, udbhāsvara*** **and** ***vācika.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These names are given according to convention, but can also be understood by etymology.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *alaṅkāras* are twenty-two, starting with *bhāva* and ending with *cakita.* *Udbhāsvaras* are seven starting with *nīvy-uttarīya sambhāvana*. The *vācika alaṅkāras* are twelve starting with *ālāpa.*

### Text 2

***tatra alaṅkārāḥ—***  
***yauvane sattvajās tāsām alaṅkārās tu viṁśatiḥ \|***  
***udayanty adbhutāḥ kānte sarvathābhiniveśataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Alaṅkāras:*** **In the youth of the girls, twenty remarkable** ***alaṅkāras*** **manifest from** ***sattva*****, because of complete absorption in Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sattva* refers to the heart subjected to *bhāvas* arising from actions in relation to Kṛṣṇa. Thus the *alaṅkaṛas* are called *sattva-jā.*

### Text 3

***bhāvo hāvaś ca helā ca proktās tatra trayo’ṅgajāḥ \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Three** ***alaṅkāras--bhāva, hāva*** **and** ***helā*****—are perceived by bodily movement.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Different limbs such as movements of edges of the eye, eyebrow, or neck are used to indicate something. These are perceived by bodily movement. They are not produced by the body but from *sattva*—a state of the heart.

### Text 4

***śobhā kāntiś ca dīptiś ca mādhuryaṁ ca pragalbhatā \|***  
***audāryaṁ dhairyam ity ete saptaiva syur ayatnajāḥ \|\|4\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Seven** ***alaṅkāras-- śobhā, kānti, dīpti, mādhurya, pragalbhatā, audārya*** **and** ***dhairya*****-- arise without effort.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Without any efforts such as dressing these *alaṅkāras* arise.

### Text 5

***līlā vilāso vicchittir vibhramaḥ kilakiñcitam \|***  
***moṭṭāyitaṁ kuṭṭamitaṁ bibboko lalitaṁ tathā \|***  
***vikṛtaṁ ceti vijñeyā daśa tāsāṁ svabhāvajāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Ten** ***alaṅkāras—līlā, vilāsa, vicchiti, vibhrama, kilakiṅcita, moṭtāyita, kuṭtamita*****,** ***bibboka, lalita*** **and** ***vikṛta*** **arise from the natures of the** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though efforts are made for these activities, these *alaṅkāras* of the women arise from natural efforts.

### Text 6

***tatra bhāvaḥ—***  
***prādurbhāvaṁ vrajaty eva raty-ākhye bhāva ujjvale \|***  
***nirvikārātmake citte bhāvaḥ prathama-vikriyā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Bhāva:*** **When the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*** **called** ***rati*** **makes its appearance because of** ***ujjvala-rasa*****,** ***bhāva,*** **the first transformation, takes place in the heart undisturbed by all except Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The locative case in *ujjvale i*ndicates purpose as in *carmaṇi dvīpinaṁ hanti*: they kill the tiger for his skin. When there is *rati* which is another name for *bhāva* or specifically *madhura-bhāva,* for producing *ujjvala-rasa,* in the heart devoid of any indications such as inscrutability and shyness, the first appearance of transformations that cannot be suppressed, such playfully moving the eyes, is the *anubhāva* called *bhāva.* This *bhāva* is not a *sthāyi-bhava* or *vyabhicāri-bhava*. The word *bhāva* can mean transformation, state of mind or *anubhāva* according to *Amara-koṣa.* That by which something is made known is called *bhāva.* The *vṛddhi* of the vowel in the word *bhāva* indicates its causative nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When the *sthāyi-bhavā* called *rati* appears in *śṛṅgāra-rasa* in the heart, the first transformation, not previously present in *vayaḥ-sandhi*, an experience of agitation caused by love, is called *bhāva.* That heart was without transformations previously (*nirvikāra*)m since in *paugaṇḍa* age feeling of love did not arise.

“How can this be *anubhāva,* since *anubhāvas* means understanding the presence of *bhāva* by appearance of external qualities*? Anubhāvās tu cittastha-bhāvānām avabodhakaḥ: anubhāvas* reveal the state of the heart. (BRS 2.1.1)” That is true. *Sāttvika-bhāvas* like being stunned or perspiring have an *anubhāva* aspect in that they are external.  *Bhāva* and *hāva* are simultaneously internal and external transformations and are thus called *anubhāvas*. When, at the beginning of *vayaḥsandhi* there is an experience of agitation of love not present previously by seeing or hearing about Kṛṣṇa, there is internal transformation of the heart. Externally this is perceived as moving the eyes etc. Therefore these are the symptom that should be discussed. When the heart is without any transformation, the appearance of *rati* is the first transformation. What is in the heart becomes reflected in the body. What is indicated is a complete transformation of heart. The genitive case should be understood (*cittasya nirvikārasya*). Thus the meaning is “The first agitation of the heart (manifested externally also) previously unaffected by love is called *bhāva.”* The writer of *Alaṅkāra-kaustubha* (124) however has distinguished this *bhāva* from the *anubhāvas.*

“*Hāva* and *helā* are transformations of this *bhāva* just described. There three will not occur after *vayaḥsandhi* in the young women (since they would show more advanced symptoms.” That is true, they will not occur. In *Sāhitya-darpaṇa* (3.105) it is said *janmataḥ prabhṛti nirvikāre manasi udbuddha-mātro vikāro bhāvaḥ:* the transformation consisting of mere awakening of love in a mind which has been free of agitation of love from birth is called *bhāva*. That is one opinion. Others say that because all the conditions of all the women of Vraja are eternal, the state of full *vayaḥsandhi* even after the appearance of youth exists eternally. Some explain as follows. This first transformation is not a final state, but only a preliminary one. That first, slight transformation when there is an appearance of the *sthāyi-bhāva* called *rati* by seeing Kṛṣṇa, in a person previously without feelings of love which was a temporary state, because of being attached to other modes of living, is called *bhāva.*

However, others say that this *bhāva* cannot arise from a state of lack of *bhāva.* Therefore, the first transformation, difficult to suppress, in the heart devoid of disturbance such as shyness, profundity etc., which appears externally as moving the eyes etc., is called *bhāva.*

However the intention of the author is different. It is should be understood and explained according to the example in verse 8. The heart is like the qualities of the Lord who is without *guṇas* because he is without material *guṇas.* The heart is untransformed (*nirvikārātmake*) in the sense that it has not been agitated by any man except Kṛṣṇa. Thus the meaning is “The first transformation which appears slightly in the mind and the body from seeing Kṛṣṇa when the heart has not been agitated by any man except Kṛṣṇa is called *bhāva.”*

### Text 7

***tathā hy uktaṁ (rasa-sudhākare 1.192)—***  
***cittasyāvikṛtiḥ sattvaṁ vikṛteḥ kāraṇe sati \|***  
***tatrādyā vikriyā bhāvo bījasyādi-vikāravat \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Though there are symptoms of the appearance of** ***bhāva,*** **when there are no external symptoms it is called** ***sattva*****. Its first transformation with external symptoms is called** ***bhāva,*** **just as a sprout is the first transformation of a seed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Thought there are symptoms of the arousal of *bhāva (vikṛteḥ kāraṇe),* the absence of external symptoms *(cittasya avikṛtiḥ)* is called *sattva.* When *sattva* exists *(tatra),* the first external indication is called *bhāva.* *Rati* is like the seed and *bhāva* is the transformation into the sprout.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One should not say that the literary writes have not explained *bhāva* in this way, since the ancient authorities have said as follows. Though there is cause for transformation, such as seeing a handsome man, (*vikṛteḥ kāraṇe*), if the heart is not agitated, it is called *sattva—śuddha-sattva* with no trace of *rajas* or *tamas*. This is because the person’s nature is to remain without agitation. In that state, that first transformation, a spiritual event, arising from seeing Kṛṣṇa, who is full of knowledge and bliss, is called *bhāva.*

A particular seed such as a vegetable seed, by particular cause of transformation such as rain, transforms, but does not transform by the touch of snow in winter. Gold however remains unaffected by the touch of ice. In this way the first transformation takes place. It is not improper to use a material example for a spiritual subject, since people cannot realize spiritual objects directly. Thus Kṛṣṇa is compared to a cloud.

“If this does not apply to material heroines like Damayantī, your desired goal is thwarted. *Śruti* says *raso vai saḥ rasaṁ hy evāyaṁ labdhvānandī bhavati*: the Lord is *rasa*; attaining *rasa* one becomes blissful. You have applied this explanation of *rasa* full of knowledge and bliss to the spiritual consorts of the Lord. If foolish material poets apply this *rasa* to material women having flesh, blood, stool, urine, old age and death, what are we to do?” The following has been said in explaining *rasa: tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye muhyanti yat sūrayaḥ, tejo-vāri-mṛdāṁ yathā vinimayaḥ:* that knowledge of *mādhura-rasa* was imparted unto Bharata Muni, and about that *rasa* those who write poetry on *śṛṅgāra-rasa* are bewildered. (SB 1.1.1) This is because they think it is material *rasa* by error. An example is given. It is like mistaking light or earth for water.

### Text 8

***yathā—***  
***pitur goṣṭhe sphīte kusumini purā khāṇḍava-vane***  
***na te dṛṣṭvā saṅkrandanam api manaḥ spandanam agāt \|***  
***puro vṛndāraṇye viharati mukunde sakhi mudā***  
***kim āndolād akṣṇaḥ śruti-kumudam indīvaram abhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When you saw Indra in the Khāṇḍava forest filled with flowers in your father's pasture-land, your heart did not tremble. O friend! When Kṛṣṇa dances blissfully before you in Vṛṇdāvana, why does the white lotus in your ear become blue by the rolling of your eyes?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first line is presented as a joke. The third line expresses astonishment. The word *api* indicates possibility. Actually, on seeing him, she wept and her mind became unsteady. By the playful words in the last two lines, the special sweetness of Mukunda is indicated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī,* though knowing the truth, expert at having others reveal their hearts, questions her leader as if she does not know. Now for two or three days you have come to your father-in-law’s house from your father’s place in Kāṇḍhava forest. You have come to Nanda’s cow pastures. Previously you were in Khāṇḍava forest filled with flowers. This acts as *uddīpana.* Though you saw Indra (*saṅkrandanam*), who is very handsome, your mind did not waver at all. I saw this, as your associate. Though there was cause for agitation, you did not become agitated. When Mukunda plays before you, and you see him with your glances, your eyes began to sway so that the white ornament in your ear became blue. The first transformation is movement of the eyes. This is *bhāva.*

### Text 9

***atha hāvaḥ—***  
***grīvārecaka-saṁyukto bhrū-netrādi-vikāśa-kṛt \|***  
***bhāvād īṣat-prakāśo yaḥ sa hāva iti kathyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**That stage where there is a slight manifestation because of** ***bhāva,*** **where the neck becomes tilted, and the eyebrows, eyes, and other bodily features blossom with happiness, is called** ***hāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Grīvā recaka* means bending the neck sideways.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When there is slightly more manifestation than in *bhāva,* where only the eyes become unsteady, it is called *hāva.* This means there are more transformations. *Grīvā recaka* means bending the neck sideways.

### Text 10

***yathā—***  
***sāci-stambhita-kaṇṭhi kuḍmalavatīṁ netrālir abhyeti te***  
***ghūrṇan karṇa-latāṁ manāg vikasitā bhrū-vallarī nṛtyati \|***  
***atra prādurabhūt taṭe sumanasām ullāsakas tvat-puro***  
***gaurāṅgi prathamaṁ vana-priya-bandhuḥ sphuṭaṁ mādhavaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Your neck has turned sideways and remains in that position. The bees of your eyes, roving here and there and becoming wide, move towards the creeper of your ears. The creepers of your eyebrows are dancing. O golden-complexioned Rādhā! Spring, the friend of the cuckoos, which gives joy to the jasmine, has appeared before you on the bank of the Yamunā. Kṛṣṇa, giving joy to good women, friend of the forest women, has appeared here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sumanasām* means “persons with good hearts” or flowers. *Vana-priya-bandhuḥ* means friend of the Vṛndāvana women or friend of the female cuckoos. *Mādhava* means Kṛṣṇa or spring.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmā speaks to Rādhā. Your neck is turned sideways and does not move. Out of longing, your neck is turned sideways because of your side glances, but you remain unsatisfied. And the neck remains in that position because of bliss and becoming senseless. This is a joke. The bees of your eyes go towards the creepers of your ears. *Kuḍmalavatīm* means having buds or having an ornament. The reason is given.

The spring season, which brings joy to the jasmine (*sumanasām*), or Kṛṣṇa who gives joy to the beautiful women, has appeared. *Amara-koṣa* says *sumanā* means jasmine. It also means women with good hearts. *Vana-priya* is the cuckoo or the women who like the forest. Clearly therefore I think it is because of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 11

***atha helā—***  
***hāva eva bhaved dhelā vyakta-śṛṅgāra-sūcakaḥ \|\|11\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Hāva*** **becomes** ***helā*** **when there are clearly indications of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa.***

### Text 12

***yathā—***  
***śrute veṇau vakṣaḥ sphurita-kucam ādhmātam api te***  
***tiro-vikṣiptākṣaṁ pulakita-kapolaṁ ca vadanam \|***  
***skhalat-kāñci svedārgalita-sicayaṁ cāpi jaghanaṁ***  
***pramādaṁ mā kārṣīḥ sakhi carati savye gurujanaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**As you listen to the sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute, your breasts heave like bellows, your eyes glace to the side, your cheeks develop goose bumps, your belt slips from your hips, and your garments become damp with perspiration. O my friend, do not become inattentive. Your elders are now approaching on your left.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ādhmātam* means like breathing like bellows. Your breast heaves from the passage of air and your hips heave by walking. *Pramādam* means inattention.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. Your breathing is like a bellows by the movement of air. By walking your hips move up and down. *Pramādam* means inattention. Elders are on the left. Therefore go to the appointment by the right quickly through the side door. I will handle the elders and will come later.

### Text 13

***atha ayatnajāḥ \| tatra śobhā—-***  
***sā śobhā rūpa-bhogādyair yat syād aṅga-vibhūṣaṇam \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Śobhā:*** **The state called** ***śobhā*** **when the body is decorated with beauty and amorous enjoyment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Bhogaḥ* means amorous enjoyment.

### Text 14

***yathā—***  
***dhṛtvā raktāṅguli-kiśalayair nīpa-śākhāṁ viśākhā***  
***niṣkrāmantī vratati-bhavanāt prātar udghūrṇitākṣī \|***  
***veṇīm aṁsopari viluṭhatīm ardham uktāṁ vahantī***  
***lagnā svānte mama na hi bahiḥ seyam adyāpy ayāsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Grasping a** ***kadamba*** **branch with the budding reddish twigs of her fingers, Viśākhā left the cottage of creepers at daybreak. Her eyes were rolling and her braid fell on her shoulder, half undone. Viśākhā now sticks in my heart and will never leave it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to a *sakhī* of Viśākhā. The hint is “Even though it is day, make another appointment with her.”

### Text 15

***atha kāntiḥ--***  
***śobhaiva kāntir ākhyātā manmathāpyāyanojjvalā \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kānti:*** **When** ***śobhā*** **becomes bright with increased desire it is called** ***kānti.***

### Text 16

***yathā—***  
***prakṛti-madhura-mūrtir bāḍham atrāpy udañcat-***  
***taruṇima-nava-lakṣmī-lekhayāliṅgitāṅgī \|***  
***vara-madana-vihārair adya tatrāpy udārā***  
***madayati hṛdayaṁ me rundhatī rādhikeyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Rādhā, with a form sweet with naturally deep** ***anurāga*****, whose limbs are embraced by the lines of fresh beauty of youth, is exalted today with the best pastimes of Cupid. Rādhā stops my heart and drives me mad with love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā has a form sweet with naturally deep *anurāga (prakrtyā).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. Rādhā stops my heart: now I do not desire anything else.

“You are an ocean of love. How can that one person do this to you?” She is exalted (*udāra*) with best pastimes of love: that one person fulfills all my desires

### Text 17

***atha dīptiḥ--***  
***kāntir eva vayo-bhoga-deśa-kāla-guṇādibhiḥ \|\|***  
***uddīpitātivistāraṁ prāptā ced dīptir ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dīptī:*** **When** ***kānti*** **becomes intensely filled with youth, amorous enjoyment, place, time and qualities, it is called** ***dīpti.***

### Text 18

***yathā—***  
***nimīlan-netra-śrīr acaṭula-paṭīrācala-marun-***  
***nipīta-svedāmbus truṭad-amala-hārojjvala-kucā \|***  
***nikuñje kṣiptāṅgī śaśi-kiraṇa-kirmīrita-taṭe***  
***kiśorī sā tene hari-manasi rādhā manasijam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Lying in bower on the bank of the Yamunā lit by the moon, beautiful with sleepy eyes, decorated with drops of perspiration sipped by the steady the Malaya winds, her breast gleaming with the splendid broken necklace, youthful Rādhā aroused Cupid in the mind of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to her *sakhī. Nimīlad* means sleepy. *Paṭirācala* means the wind from Malaya Hills. Her broken necklace and her lying down indicate her fatigue after intense enjoyment. She arouses Cupid in his mind as he sees her limbs made beautiful by the rays of the moon falling through the lattice holes of the creepers. He then wakes her up in order to again enjoy with her. There is also the hint that “She did not sleep all that night. I will go in order to let her sleep for a moment now.”

### Text 19

***atha mādhuryam—-***  
***mādhuryaṁ nāma ceṣṭānāṁ sarvāvasthāsu cārutā \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mādhuryam: Mādhuryam*** **means beauty of actions in all circumstances.**

### Text 20

***yathā—***  
***asavyaṁ kaṁsārer bhuja-śirasi dhṛtvā pulakinaṁ***  
***nija-śroṇyāṁ savyaṁ karam anṛju-viṣkambhita-padā \|***  
***dadhānā mūrdhānaṁ laghutara-tiraḥ-sraṁsinam iyaṁ***  
***babhau rāsottīrṇā muhur alasa-mūrtiḥ śaśimukhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Placing her right hand on Kṛṣṇa's shoulder and her left hand, full of goose bumps, on her hip, supporting herself on crooked feet, her head hanging slightly to the side, the moon-faced** ***sakhī*** **appears fatigued from the** ***rāsa*****-dance**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

From a distance Rati-mañjarī points out her *sakhī*. *Asavyam* means the right hand. *Bhuja-sirasi* means on the shoulder. *Śaśimukhi* refers to Rādhā or her *sakhī.*

### Text 21

***atha pragalbhatā—-***  
***niḥśaṅkatvaṁ prayogeṣu budhair uktā pragalbhatā \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Pragalbhatā: Pragalbhatā*** **refers to fearlessness in amorous actions.**

### Text 22

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (7.40)—***  
***prātikūlyam iva yad vivṛṇvatī***  
***rādhikā rada-nakhārpaṇoddhūrā \|***  
***keli-karmaṇi gatā pravīṇatāṁ***  
***tena tuṣṭim atulāṁ harir yayau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Expert in the actions of love play, Rādhā without restraint attacks Kṛṣṇa with her teeth and nails as if he were an enemy. These activities bring Kṛṣṇa incomparable pleasure.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pragalbhaṭa* means boldness in amorous actions. Vṛndā speaks. Seeing the splendour of her actions (*tena)* he is satisfied. Though Rādhā is not by nature *pragalbhā* because of great passion there is temporary *pragalbhā* without her effort.

### Text 23

***atha audāryam—***  
***audāryaṁ vinayaṁ prāhuḥ sarvāvasthāgataṁ budhāḥ \|\|23\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Audāryam: Audāryam*** **is kind nature in all circumstances.**

### Text 24

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.13) —***  
***nyaviśata nayanānte kāpi sāralya-niṣṭhā***  
***vacasi ca vinayena stotra-bhaṅgī nyavātsīt \|***  
***ajani ca mayi bhūyān sambhramas tena tasyā***  
***vyavṛṇuta hṛdi manyuṁ suṣṭhu dākṣiṇyam eva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Sincerity has entered the corners of Candrāvalī’s eyes, there is modest entreaty in her words, and she is very respectful to me. Somehow, her kindness has completely checked the anger in my heart.**

### Text 25

***yathā vā—***  
***kṛtajño’pi premojjvala-matir api sphāra-vinayo’-***  
***py abhijñānāṁ cuḍāmaṇir api kṛpānīradhir api \|***  
***yad antaḥ-svaccho’pi smarati na harir gokulabhuvaṁ***  
***mamaivedaṁ janmāntara-durita-dusṭa-druma-phalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Hari is naturally grateful, his mind shines with** ***prema,*** **he is extremely humble, he is the crest-jewel of the wise, he is an ocean of mercy and his heart is pure. If he does not remember Gokula, it is only the result of my past sins.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī is generally gentle by nature. However, in the previous verse in order to show her humility she puts forth effort in glancing with the edge of her eye and other acts. Therefore it cannot really be an example of modesty as defined in this list. Thus another example is given. A woman laments to Rādhā after Kṛṣṇa has left Vraja. This humility in a naturally *vāma* associate of Rādhā has arisen without effort through *vyabhicāri-bhāvas* like humility and self-deprecation. In the previous example concealment was accomplished with effort, rather than actions being generated by concealment. Her humility arose from effort.

### Text 26

***atha dhairyam—***  
***sthirā cittonnatir yā tu tad dhairyam iti kīrtyate \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dhairyam*** **or self-control: Increase of a steady heart is called** ***dhairyam.***

### Text 27

***yathā lalita-mādhave (7.7)—***  
***audāsīnya-dhurā-parīta-hṛdayaḥ kāṭhinyam ālambatāṁ***  
***kāmaṁ śyāmala-sundaro mayi sakhi svairī sahasraṁ samāḥ \|***  
***kintu bhrānti-bharād api kṣaṇam idaṁ tatra priyebhyaḥ priye***  
***ceto janmani janmani praṇayitā dāsyaṁ na me hāsyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O friend! Even though Śyāmasundara may become indifferent, hurtful, or hard for thousands of years, he is dearer that the dearest. Because of my love for him, my heart cannot give up service to him for even a moment out of illusion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Nava-vṛndā. Because of *prema* I cannot give up serving him. Rādhā who is by nature of *adhīra* nature, because of separation, because of a strong manifestation of the *vyabhicāri-bhāva* called *rati, There could be a mistake in calling rati* a *sañcāri-bhāva.*1 manifests *dhairyam* without effort. mati?//The items from *śobhā* to *mādhurya* arise from the nature of the body, but because they arise without effort to produce those effects they are said to be “without effort.” The three items *pragalbhā, audhārya* and *dhairyam* do not arise from the nature of the person (*svabhāvajā—*see the next verse), but by the individual reasons for each given above, they are not produced by effort. Thus they are said to be “without effort.”

### Text 28

***atha svabhāvajāḥ \| tatra līlā--***  
***priyānukaraṇaṁ līlā ramyair veśa-kriyādibhiḥ \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rising from their nature,** ***līlā:*** **Imitating the lover by attractive garments and actions is called** ***līlā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sometimes these actions take place intentionally with effort and sometimes without intention, arising from *vyabhicāri-bhāvas.* They are called “arising from nature” because nature is evident in all of them. Imitating the beloved is done with intention or sometimes without intellectual intention. This is natural for women having *prema*.

### Text 29

***yathā viṣṇu-purāṇe (5.13.27)—***  
***duṣṭa-kāliya tiṣṭhādya kṛṣṇo’ham iti cāparā \|***  
***bāhum āsphoṭya kṛṣṇasya līlā-sarvasvam ādade \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Viṣṇu Purāṇa:***  **Wicked Kāliya! Stand still! I am Kṛṣṇa. Moving her arms, she imitated all of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She imitated (*ādade*) whatever pastimes existed.(*līlā sarvasvam*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Parāśara speaks to Maitreya. *Āsphoṭya* means making a sound by pressing the left armpit with the palm of the right hand. Because this action arises from madness out of great separation, it is done with effort but without intellectual intention.

### Text 30

***yathā vā chando-mañjaryām—***  
***mṛgamada-kṛta-carcā pīta-kauṣeya-vāsā***  
***rucira-śikhi-śikhaṇḍā baddha-dhammilla-pāśā \|***  
***anṛju-nihitam aṁse vaṁśam utkvāṇayantī***  
***kṛta-madhuripu-veṣā mālinī pātu rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Chando--mañjarī*****: Rādhā anointed her body with black musk, dressed in yellow silk garments, wore a garland of flowers, placed a charming peacock feather in her hair, and placing a piece of bamboo on her crooked shoulder, made sweet sounds. May this Rādhā dressed as Kṛṣṇa protect us!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This gives an example with intention and effort. Rati-mañjarī speaks to her *sakhī. Mālinī* means she wore a garland, or it is the name of a poetic meter.

### Text 31

***atha vilāsaḥ—***  
***gati-sthānāsanādīnāṁ mukha-netrādi-karmaṇām \|***  
***tātkālikaṁ tu vaiśiṣṭyaṁ vilāsaḥ priya-saṅgajam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vilāsa:*** **The immediate gestures of the face, eyes, walking, sitting, and standing, to cause union with the lover, are called** ***vilāsa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tātkālikam* means that these actions are done at the start of meeting the lover.

### Text 32

***yathā—***  
***ruṇatsi purataḥ sphuraty aghahare kathaṁ nāsikā-***  
***śikhagrathita-mauktikonnamanakaitvena smitam \|***  
***nirāsthad aciraṁ sudhā-kiraṇa-kaumudī-mādhurīṁ***  
***manāg api tavodgatā madhura-danti danta-dyutiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Rādhā with the beautiful teeth! When Kṛṣṇa stands before you, why do you hide your smile, by pretending to move the pearl decorating the tip of your nose? When you manifest a slight smile, the splendor of your charming teeth quickly defeats the beauty of the moon’s rays.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nirāsthat* means “it defeats.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vīrā speaks to Rādhā who is showing her *vāma* nature in front of Kṛṣṇa when they meet. When she smiles, the beauty of the details of her moon-like face defeats the beauty of the moon.

### Text 33

***yathā vā—***  
***adhyāsīnam amuṁ kadamba-nikaṭe krīḍā-kuṭīra-sthalīm-***  
***ābhīrendra-kumāram atra rabhasād ālokayantyāḥ puraḥ \|***  
***digdhā dugdha-samudra-mugdha-laharī-lāvaṇya-nisyandibhiḥ***  
***kālindī tava dṛk-taraṅgita-bharais tanvaṅgi gaṅgāyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When you gaze in front of you at the youthful prince of the cowherds sitting in the pastime-cottage near the** ***kadamba*** **tree, the Yamunā River, covered by the waves of your glances which are flowing with the beauty of charming waves of the milk ocean, turns into the Gaṅgā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The milk ocean indicates her smiles. The Yamunā appears to become the Gaṅgā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This describes actions of her eyes. The previous verse described her smile. Vṛndā speaks to Rādhā. The Yamunā becomes covered (*digdhā*) with her glances which make it flow with the beauty of waves of the milk ocean. This indicates her smile.

### Text 34

***atha vicchittiḥ—***  
***ākalpa-kalpanālpāpi vicchittiḥ kānti-poṣa-kṛt \|\|34\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vicchitti*** **(dressing up): Increasing beauty by just a little dressing up is called** ***vicchitti.***

### Text 35

***yathā—***  
***mākanda-patreṇa mukunda-cetaḥ***  
***pramodinī māruta-kampitena \|***  
***raktena karṇābharaṇīkṛtena***  
***rādhā mukhāmbhoruham ullalāsa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Delighting the heart of Kṛṣṇa by making an ornament of red mango shoots, which quivered in the breeze, Rādhā causes delight to the lotus of her face.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Nāndīmukhī.

### Text 36

***yathā vā hari-vaṁśe—***  
***ekenāmala-patreṇa kaṇṭha-sūtrāvalambinā \|***  
***rarāja barhi-patreṇa manda-māruta-kampinā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Hari-vaṁsa:*** **Decorated with a garland of** ***āmalak*****ī leaves around his neck and a peacock feather moving in the gentle breeze, Kṛṣṇa appeared most splendid.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example of Kṛṣṇa becoming beautiful by a little decoration is given. Vaiśampāyana describes Kṛṣṇa sporting in Vraja. He was decorated with a peacock feather and around his neck *āmalakī* petals strung on a thread made of a creeper, spreading beauty in all directions.  *Āmala* means *āmalakī* in medical usage, as in the phrase *āmalaṁ kamalaṁ kuṣṭham.*

### Text 37

***sakhī-yatnād iva dhṛtir maṇḍanānāṁ priyāgasi \|***  
***serṣyāvajñā vara-strībhir vicchittir iti kecana \|\|37\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Some authorities define** ***vicchitti*** **as the best of women who was ornamented with great effort by** ***sakhīs*** **showing contempt and anger when the lover who has offended her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When the lover has done some offense (*priyāgasi*) she becomes angry and full of contempt.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When the lover has done some offense (*priyāgasi),* she remains with anger and contempt.

### Text 38

***yathā—***  
***mudrāṁ gāḍhatarāṁ vidhāya nihite dūrīkuruṣvāṅgade***  
***granthiṁ nyasya kaṭhoram arpita-matiḥ kaṇṭhān maṇiṁ bhraṁśaya \|***  
***mugdhe kṛṣṇa-bhujaṅga-dṛṣṭi-kalayā durvārayā dūṣite***  
***ratnālaṅkaraṇe manāg api manas tṛṣṇāṁ na puṣṇāti me \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Throw away these arm bands fastened tightly. Tear this tightly tied jewel necklace from my neck. O foolish friend! These jeweled ornaments have been ruined by the poisonous glan e of the black snake. I have no desire at all for them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, angry, speaks to Viśākhā. Since the arm bands are fastened tightly and the necklace is tied tightly, I can not take them off by myself. You are also ignoring me, and have become my enemy. “What offense have the ornaments committed?” O foolish friend! You do not have any knowledge. By glancing at them, he has showered them with poison. I should not again offer poison to my limbs which have already been poisoned by his glance.

### Text 39

***atha vibhramaḥ—***  
***vallabha-prāpti-velāyāṁ madanāveśa-sambhramāt \|***  
***vibhramo hāra-mālyādi-bhūṣā-sthāna-viparyayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vibhrama:*** **When, at the time of going to meet her lover, the heroine places necklaces, flower-garlands and other ornaments in the wrong places, when agitated by the onslaught of intense passion, it is called** ***vibhrama.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Placing the ornaments in the wrong place the time of going to meet the lover is called *vibhrama.*

### Text 40

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.21)—***  
***dhammillopari nīla-ratna-racito hāras tvayāropito***  
***vinyastaḥ kuca-kumbhayoḥ kurvalaya-śreṇī-kṛto garbhakaḥ \|***  
***aṅge carcitam añjanaṁ vinihitā kastūrikā netrayoḥ***  
***kaṁsārer abhisāra-sambhrama-bharān manye jagad vismṛtam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **You have placed the sapphire necklace in your braided hair, the lotus flower hair decoration on your full breasts, mascara for your eyes on your arms and legs, and musk perfume for the body around your eyes. In great haste to meet Kṛṣṇa, you have forgotten everything.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. *Garbhakaḥ* is a garland meant for the hair.

### Text 41

***yathā vā, śrī-daśame (10.29.7)—***  
***limpantyaḥ pramṛjantyo’nyā añjantyaḥ kāś ca locane \|***  
***vyatyasta-vastrābharaṇāḥ kāścit kṛṣṇāntikaṁ yayuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the Tenth Canto: Some** ***gopīs*** **were putting on cosmetics or applying mascara to their eyes. But all the gopīs stopped these activities at once and, though their clothes and ornaments were in complete disarray, rushed off to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example is given from an authorized text.

### Text 42

***adhīnasyāpi sevāyāṁ kāntasyānabhinandanam \|***  
***vibhramo vāmatodrekāt syād ity ākhyāti kaścana \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Some say that** ***vibhrama*** **takes place when, out of apparent contrariness, the heroine becomes displeased with her lover even though he is submissive and eager to serve her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Externally she is displeased, but internally she is pleased with him, because of extreme crookedness using words only. This is the special nature of *praṇaya*. It is *said aher iva gatiḥ premṇa:* the movement of *prema* is like that of a snake. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 15.102)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Externally she is displeased, but internally she is pleased with him. Others explain in this way, but others say this is called *bibboka.*

### Text 43

***yathā—***  
***tvaṁ govinda mayāsi kiṁ nu kavarī-bandhārtham abhyarthitaḥ***  
***kleśenālam abaddha eva cikura-stomo mudaṁ dogdhi me \|***  
***vaktrasyāpi na mājjanaṁ kuru ghanaṁ gharmāsu me rocate***  
***naivottaṁsaya mālatīr mama śiraḥ khedaṁ bhareṇāpsyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Govinda! Did I ask you to braid my hair? It is too much trouble. The unbound hair gives my joy. Do not wipe the perspiration from my face. It pleases me. Do not garland my head with these jasmine flowers. They give me pain by their weight.**

### Text 44

***atha kilakiñcitam—***  
***garvābhilāṣa-rudita-smitāsūyā-bhaya-krudhām \|***  
***saṅkarī-karaṇaṁ harṣād ucyate kila-kiñcitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kilakiñcita:*** **When pride, desire, weeping, smiling, envy, fear and anger manifest together because of joy, these symptoms are called** ***kilakiñcita.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A simultaneous mixture (*saṅkarīkaraṇam*) of the seven items starting with pride is called *kilakiñcita.* The cause is joy.

### Text 45

***yathā—***  
***mayā jātollāsaṁ priya-sahacarī locana-pathe***  
***balān nyaste rādhā-kuca-mukulayoḥ pāṇi-kamale \|***  
***udañcad-bhrū-bhedaṁ sapulakam avaṣṭambhi valitaṁ***  
***smrāmy antas tasyāḥ smita-rudita-kānta-dyuti mukham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: While her dear friends were watching, when I forcibly placed my lotus hands on Rādhā's bud-like breasts, her eyebrows rose, the hairs of her body stood up in ecstasy, she rested on a** ***sakhī*** **and turned around, and her face shone with smiles and crying. In my heart I remember this Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Avaṣṭambhi* means she had to be supported by a *sakhī,* since she was falling. This indicates pride. Her hairs standing on end indicate her desire. Her face was beautiful with smiling and crying. These are the items “smiling and crying” among the seven. Her raised brow indicates envy and anger. Turning back indicates fear. All these items describe Rādhā. The symptoms are rarely seen in others.

### Text 46

***yathā vā dāna-keli-kaumudyāṁ (1)—***  
***antaḥ-smeratayojjvalā jala-kaṇa-vyākīrṇa-pakṣmāṅkurā***  
***kiñcit pāṭalitāñcalā rasikatotsiktā puraḥ kuñcatī \|***  
***ruddhāyāḥ pathi mādhavena madhura-vyābhugna-tārottarā***  
***rādhāyāḥ kilakiñcita-stavakinī dṛṣṭiḥ śriyaṁ vaḥ kriyāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: May the sight of the flower cluster of** ***kilakiñcita*** **in Rādhā, who was blocked by Kṛṣṇa, bring you a wealth of** ***prema!*** **The spouts of her eyelids were scattered with tears and those eyes shone with an inner smile, proud because of pleasure but somewhat contracted, while her excellent pupils were downcast but exuding sweetness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Proud or swelling with pleasure indicates her pride. *Utseka* means swelling of the heart. Her sweetness (*madhura)* indicates her desire. Her pupil turned down indicates her envy. Smiling and crying are clear. *Puraḥ kuñcatī (*joined with shrinking) indicates fear. Red edges of the eye indicate anger. This cluster of flowers in the form of *kilakiñcita* indicates that some of the symptoms are unclear because of their profundity, as all flowers in cluster are not clearly visible.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Kilakiñcita* not only occurs by touching the body. It can also appear if Kṛṣṇa obstructs the path or other actions. Thus another example is given. Someone gives bliss to the assembly of *rasikas* by use of praise. The sight of Rādhā blocked by Kṛṣṇa on the pretext of taking a toll on the way to *dāna-ghaṭta* should give you the splendor *(śriyam*) of trembling and being stunned, arising from *prema.* What is that sight?

It is a cluster of flowers of various *bhāvas* called *kilakiñcita.* The sight is like a desire creeper which yields wealth. The internal smile indicates smiling. The tears indicate crying. The slightly red eyes indicate anger. Highly soaked (*utsikta*) with pleasure indicates her desire. Contraction indicates fear. The best (*uttara*) pupils moving crookedly *(vyābhugna*) indicates pride and envy*. Uttara* means above, north and best according to *Amara-koṣa.*

### Text 47

***atha moṭṭāyitam—***  
***kānta-smaraṇa-vārtādau hṛdi tad-bhāva-bhāvataḥ \|***  
***prākaṭyam abhilāṣasya moṭṭāyitam udīryate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Moṭṭāyitam:*** **The appearance of desire in the heart caused by** ***sthāyi-bhāva*****, on hearing about or remembering the beloved, is called** ***moṭṭāyitam.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The appearance of desire caused by *(bhāvataḥ*) the *sthāyi-bhāva* of *rati* is called *moṭṭāyitam.*

### Text 48

***yathā—***  
***na brūte klama-bījam ālibhir alaṁ pṛṣṭāpi pālī yadā***  
***cāturyeṇa tad-agratas tava kathā tābhis tadā prastutā \|***  
***tāṁ pītāmbara jṛmbhamāṇa-vadanāmbhojā kṣaṇaṁ śṛṇvatī***  
***bimboṣṭhī pulakari viḍambitavatī phullāṁ kadamba-śriyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa! When Pālī, asked by her friends, did not say the cause of your unhappiness, they eloquently described you to her. As Pālī listened, the lotus flower of her face blossomed with happiness, her lips became red like** ***bimba*** **fruits, and the hairs of her body stood up, rivaling the beauty of** ***kadamba*** **blossoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 49

***atha kuṭṭamitam—***  
***stanādharādi-grahaṇe hṛt-prītāv api sambhramāt \|***  
***bahiḥ krodho vyathitavat proktaṁ kuṭṭamitaṁ budhaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kuṭṭamitam:*** **When a woman becomes pained with external anger out of agitation, though she still has affection, when her lover grabs her breast or tries to kiss her, it is called** ***kuṭṭamitam*** **by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When he tries to touch her breast or lips when she is alone, she shows external anger.

In the sight of a *sakhī,* these actions are *kilakiñcita.*

### Text 50

***yathā—***  
***karauddhatyaṁ hanta sthagaya kavarī me vighaṭate***  
***dukūlaṁ ca nyañcaty aghahara tavāstāṁ vihasitam \|***  
***kim ārabdhaḥ kartuṁ tam anavasare nirdaya madāt***  
***patāmy eṣā pade vitara śayituṁ me kṣaṇam api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa! Stop those impudent hands. Though my braid and cloth slip out of place, you simply laugh. O merciless one! What are you madly trying to do at this unsuitable time? I fall at your feet. Let me sleep for a while.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā who has been enjoyed and dressed by Kṛṣṇa speaks to him when he desires to enjoy her again.

### Text 51

***yathā vā—***  
***na bhrū-latāṁ kuṭilaya kṣipa naiva hastaṁ***  
***vaktraṁ ca kaṇṭakita-gaṇḍam idaṁ na rundhi \|***  
***prīṇātu sundari tavādhara-bandhu-jīve***  
***pītvā madhuni madhure madhusūdno’sau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Please don't knit your eyebrows. Don't hit me with your hand. Don't block your face, whose cheeks have goose bumps. O beautiful, sweet Rādhā! Let the bumble-bee enjoy by drinking the honey of your** ***bandhujīva*** **lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous example, because Rādhā wanted to sleep from tiredness after enjoyment, she did not have affection. Thus another example is given. When Kṛṣṇa embraces Rādhā’s neck on finding her alone, he speaks. The goose bumps on her cheeks are a sign of the affection in her heart. The bee is Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 52

***atha bibbokaḥ—-***  
***bibboko māna-garvābhyāṁ syād abhīṣṭe’py anādaraḥ \|\|52\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Bibboka:*** **Disrespect towards the lover or articles given by the lover out of anger or pride is called** ***bibboka.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Iṣṭe* means to the lover or to articles given by him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Iṣṭe* means to the lover or to articles given by him.

### Text 53

***tatra garveṇa, yathā—***  
***priyokti-lakṣeṇa vipakṣa-sannidhau***  
***svīkāritāṁ paśya śikhaṇḍa-maulinā \|***  
***śyāmātivāmā hṛdayaṅgamām api***  
***srajaṁ darāghrāya nirāsa helayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of pride: Look! Śyāmā has accepted a garland offered by Kṛṣṇa who speaks to her with many words in the presence of her rivals. Contrary Śyāmā, though pleased with it, smells it slightly, and then throws it away indifferently.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While picking flowers, Rūpa-mañjarī points out in the distance a garland of lotuses and speaks. On a festive day for worshipping Sandhya-devī, in a gathering of all the women of Vraja except for Rādhā and Candrāvalī, in the presence of the opposing party, this took place. He speaks to his beloved Śyāmā (*priyokti-lakṣeṇa*) with many words. “I have made this garland with my own hand and it has amazing craftsmanship. Put it on your throat and be successful.” If he had offered it to her when she was alone she would have accepted it, since she admired it (*hrḍayaṅgamām*). Though I have smelled it at your request, actually this type of garland is not worn by my followers. This is what she indicates by throwing it away *(nirāsa*).

### Text 54

***yathā vā—***  
***sphuraty agre tiṣṭhan sakhi tava mukha-ksipta-nayanaḥ***  
***pratīkṣāṁ kṛtvāyaṁ bhavad-avasarasyāgha-damanaḥ \|***  
***dṛśoccair gāmbhīrya-grathita-guru-helā-gahanayā***  
***hasantīva kṣīve tvam iha vanamālāṁ racayasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Kṛṣṇa stands before you, gazing at your face, and waiting for an opportunity. O intoxicated girl! You seem to mock him with a glance like a garland of great neglect strung with flowers of inscrutability, and string a flower garland with your hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse shows disrespect to the beloved. Śyāmalā speaks to Rādhā. “She has come from the forest and entered that garden. When will she finish making that garland? When will I get an opportunity? Will the opportunity arise when my desire will be fulfilled or not?” Kṛṣṇa waits, thinking in this way. You seem to laugh with your eyes. “Oh! A lusty person cannot be love sick!” In this way she mocks Kṛṣṇa. Her eyes are an impassable garland of great neglect strung with flowers of profundity. She cannot be understood. “Is she merciful to me or harsh with me?” O intoxicated Rādhā! There is no mercy in intoxicated persons. You make a flower garland with your hands and you make an incomprehensible garland of *bhāvas* with your eyes. You do not show mercy to Kṛṣṇa. What astonishing actions you have! They are unsuitable. This is *vyāja-stuti,* praise meant as criticism.

### Text 55

***mānena, yathā—***  
***hariṇā sakhi cāṭu-maṇḍalīṁ***  
***kriyamāṇām avamanya manyutaḥ \|***  
***na vṛthādya suśikṣitām api***  
***svayam adhyāpaya gauri śārikām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of pride: O Gaurī! Angrily despising Kṛṣṇa's many sweet words, do not waste your time personally teaching your** ***śarikā*** **bird that is already nicely trained.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* speaks to Gaurī who has separated from Kṛṣṇa after a quarrel. On the pretext of teaching your *śārikā* bird, because you are burning with repentance, after this you say “O parrot! Say Hare Kṛṣṇa, Govinda!” In order to maintain your life you take support of his sweet name. This is the indication of the words *svayam* (yourself) and *suśikṣitām* (well taught).

### Text 56

***atha lalitam—***  
***vinyāsa-bhaṅgir aṅgānāṁ bhrū-vilāsa-manoharāḥ \|***  
***sukumārā bhaved yatra lalitaṁ tad-udīritam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Lalitam:*** **Where there are actions involving movement of the limbs, attractive movement of the eyebrows and tenderness, it is called** ***lalitam.***

### Text 57

***yathā—***  
***subhrū-bhaṅgam ananaṅga-bāṇa-jananīr ālokayantī latāḥ***  
***sollāsaṁ pada-paṅkaje diśi diśi preṅkholayanty ujjvalā \|***  
***gandhākṛṣṭa-dhiyaḥ kareṇa mṛdunā vyādhunvatī ṣaṭ-padān***  
***rādhā nandati kuñja-kandara-taṭe vṛndāvana-śrīr iva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Frowning at the creepers because they are the source of flowers which are Cupid’s arrows, beautiful Rādhā joyful moves her two lotus feet in various directions. With her delicate hand brushing aside the bumble-bees attracted by her fragrance, she delights in the wealth of Vṛndāvana at the edge of the bower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Preṅkholayantī* means she moves.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa, picking flowers for decorating Rādhā, looks at her from a distance and describes her. She sees with hatred the creepers while frowning, because the flowers are Cupid’s arrows. “You flowers become arrows and with those arrows Cupid shoots me. You are therefore my enemies.” She moves about (*preṅkholayantī*) and delights in the wealth of Vṛndāvana.

### Text 58

***atha vikṛtam—***  
***hrī-mānerṣyādibhir yatra nocyate sva-vivakṣitam \|***  
***vyajyate ceṣṭayaivedaṁ vikṛtaṁ tad vidur budhāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vikṛtim:*** **When one does not utter what one wants to say because of shyness, pride or anger and hints at this by actions only, it is called** ***vikrtam*** **by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In *moṭṭayitam* the desire is clearly manifest in hearing news about the beloved. In *vikṛtam* one’s intentions are not clearly stated. They are expressed by actions.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In *moṭṭayitam* the desire is clearly stated. In *vikṛtim* the desire is only indicated. If the desire is manifest in an example, then it is an example in the part which shows the desire indicating the object. An example of only desiring to express the object is verse 61.

### Text 59

***tatra hriyā, yathā—***  
***niśamayya mukunda manmukhād-***  
***bhavad-abhyarthitam atra sundarī \|***  
***na girābhinanda kintu sā***  
***pulakenaiva kapola-śobhinā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of shyness: O Mukunda, listen to what you requested from my mouth. Beautiful Rādhā greeted you, not with words, but with the goose bumps on her shining cheeks.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala speaks to Kṛṣṇa. You prayed “O dear Rādhā! Today you must go to see the picture I made in the cave of Govardhana. If you are merciful to me, you should indicate that you will go there by showing goose bumps.”

### Text 60

***yathā vā—***  
***na para-puruse dṛṣṭi-ksepo varākṣi tavocitas***  
***tvam asi kulajā sādhvī vaktraṁ prasīda vivartaya \|***  
***iti pathi mayā narmaṇy ukte harer nava-vīkṣaṇe***  
***sadayam udayat-kārpaṇyaṁ mām avaikṣata rādhikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: “It is not proper for you to look at another man. You are a chaste girl, born in a respectable family. Please turn your face from ant other man.” When I said these words jokingly to Rādhā on the path, on seeing Kṛṣṇa for the first time, she looked at me pitifully asking for mercy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She looked at me pitifully, asking for mercy.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since the goose bumps mentioned in the last verse are *sāttvika-bhāva* arising by nature, they are not indistinct intentional actions of the heroine. Therefore another example is given. Viśākhā informs Lalitā about the actions of Rādhā. Please turn your face away from a man. It was said jokingly to make her reveal her heart. She looked at me with a plea for mercy (*sadayam*) praying “Make me happy.” She glanced at me with a pitiful look (*udayat-kārpaṇyam*). That glancing was an action saying “I have one request. Order me to look at Kṛṣṇa. Otherwise I cannot live.”

### Text 61

***mānena, yathā—***  
***mayāsaktavati prasādana-vidhau vismṛtya candra-grahaṁ***  
***tad-vijñapti-samutsukāpi vijahau maunaṁ na sā māninī \|***  
***kintu śyāmala-ratna-sampuṭa-dalenāvṛtya kiñcin mukhaṁ***  
***satyā smārayati sma vismṛtam asau mām auparāgīṁ śriyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of anger: When I was absorbed in trying to please her, Satyabhāmā, in an angry mood, remained silent, though she wanted to inform me of the eclipse of the moon I had forgotten. By covering her face slightly with the lid of the sapphire jewellery box, she reminded me of it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Uddhava. She wanted to say “There is an eclipse of the moon now. You should go outside, bathe and perform acts of charity.” Her face was like the moon and the jewel box was like Rāhu. “Oh! She has the ultimate intelligence. By informing me in this way she has defeated me.”

### Text 62

***īrsyayā, yathā—***  
***vitara taskari me muralīṁ hṛtā-***  
***miti mad-uddhura-jalpa-vivṛttayā \|***  
***bhrū-kuṭi-bhaṅguram arka-sutā-taṭe***  
***sapadi rādhikayāham udīkṣitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of anger: “Thief, return the flute you stole from me!” Responding to my firm words, Rādhā simply stared at me with frowning eyebrows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vivṛttayā* means “by response.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. She frowned, indicating “You have called me a thief. I will tell my elders all about this and give you the result you deserve.”

### Text 63

***alaṅkārā nigaditā viṁśatir gātra-citta-jāḥ \|***  
***amī yathocitaṁ jñeyā mādhave’pi manīṣibhiḥ \|\|63\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Twenty** ***alaṅkāras*** **arising from the body and mind have been described. The wise understand that these are also present in Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 64

***kaiścid anye’py alaṅkārāḥ proktā nātra mayoditāḥ \|***  
***muner asammatatvena kintu dvitayam ucyate \|***  
***maugdhyaṁ ca cakitaṁ ceti kiñcin mādhurya-poṣaṇāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Other** ***alaṅkāras*** **mentioned by others are not described here by me since they are not approved by Bharata Muni. However, I will describe two of them,** ***maugdhyam*** **and** ***cakitam*****, which slightly nourish sweetness.**

### Text 65

*tatra maugdhyam—*  
***jñātasyāpy ajñavat pṛcchā priyāgre maugdhyam īritam \|\|65\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Maugdhyam:*** **Asking the beloved something one already knows, as if one does not know, is called** ***maugdhyam.***

### Text 66

***yathā muktā-carite—***  
***kās tā latāḥ kva vā santi kena vā kila ropitāḥ \|***  
***nātha mat-kaṅkaṇa-nyastaṁ yāsāṁ muktāphalaṁ phalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Muktā-carita:*** **What is the name of these creepers whose fruits are like the pearls on my bracelet? Where do they exist and who has planted them?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Satyabhāmā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 67

***cakitam—***  
***priyāgre cakitaṁ bhīter asthāne’pi bhayaṁ mahat \|\|67\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Cakitam:*** **Showing great fear in front of the lover when there is no cause for fear is called** ***cakitam.***

### Text 68

***yathā—***  
***rakṣa rakṣa muhur eṣa bhīṣaṇo***  
***dhāvati śravaṇa-campakaṁ mama \|***  
***ity udīrya madhupād viśaṅkitā***  
***sasvaje hariṇa-locanā harim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “Save me! Save me! This frightening creature is constantly heading for my** ***campaka*** **earring!” Saying this, the doe-eyed** ***sakhī,*** **frightened of a bumble-bee, was embraced by Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though the bee did not desire the *campaka* flower, out of playfulness she said this. Therefore it is unfounded fear. Another version has *hallakam* instead of *campakam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One *sakhī* speaks to another.  *Eṣaḥ* refers to a bee. Though the bee was not coming for her *campaka* she said this because she understood that bee would come towards her by smelling the fragrance of her face.

### Text 69-70

***atha udbhāsvarāḥ***  
***udbhāsante svadhāmnīti proktā udbhāsvarā budhaiḥ \|\|69\|\|***  
***nīvy-uttarīya-dhammilla-sraṁsanaṁ gātra-moṭanam \|***  
***jṛmbhā ghrāṇasya phullatvaṁ niśvāsādyāś ca te matāḥ \|\|70\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Udbhāsvaras:*** **What appears in the body of a person with** ***bhāva*** **is called** ***udbhāsvara*** **by the wise. These are loosening of the undergarment, loosening of the bodice, loosening of the dressed hair, crushing the limbs, yawning, expansion of nostrils, and sighing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Udbhāsante* means “manifest.” *Udbhāsvara* is formed by the rule *stheśa-bhāsa ity ādinā varac:* the suffix *vara* meaning “having this habit” after *sthā, iś, bhās, piṣ* and *kas.* (Pāṇini 3.2.175) *Sva-dhamni* means in the body of a person having *bhāva.* The word *ādi* (etc.) indicates rolling on the ground, singing, yelling, disregarding others, whirling about and hiccups.

### Text 71

***tatra nīvi-sraṁsanaṁ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave(7.41)—-***  
***nairañjanyam upeyatuḥ parigalan-modāśruṇī locane***  
***svedoddhūta-vilepanaṁ kila kuca-dvandvaṁ jahau rāgitām \|***  
***yogautsukyam agād uraḥ sphurad iti prekṣyodayaṁ saṅgināṁ***  
***rādhe nīvir iyaṁ tava ślatha-guṇā śaṅke mumukṣāṁ dadhe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Loosening of the undergarment, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O Rādhā! Your eyes full of tears of joy have washed away your mascara. Your breasts covered with perspiration have given up their red** ***kuṁkuma.***  **Your trembling chest produces desire for union with Kṛṣṇa. Your undergarment has also become loosened. Seeing all this, I think you are fixed in falling from** ***dharma.***

**Your tears of joy have dissipated material** ***upādhis.*** **Your perspiration has destroyed attachment for** ***samsāra.*** **Trembling of your chest has produced eagerness for yoga practice. Your undergarment is devoid of the material** ***guṇas.*** **Seeing these symptoms, I surmise that you are fixed in liberation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In the double meaning there is lesser qualification as the items are listed in sequence. Loosening of the undergarment was the first symptom. *Udayam* means the appearance of qualification in each of the elements.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**
