Seeing at a distance Rādhā playing with Kṛṣṇa at Gaurī-tiṛtha, Vṛndā describes the scene, addressing her in soft tones. *Nairañjanyam* means without *upādhis,* liberation from *saṁsāra*, or without mascara. Tears of joy arising from the happiness of *bhakti* have caused liberation or tears of joy arising from lust have caused the mascara to disappear. *Rāga* means material attachment or redness because of *kuṁkuma.* Perspiration arising from *bhakti* has caused material attachment to disappear and perspiration from lust has caused the *kuṁkuma* and sandalwood to disappear. Yoga refers to *aṣṭāṅga-yoga* and to touching Kṛṣṇa. Trembling (*sphurad)* of the chest produces eagerness for yoga. Trembling shows desire to unite with Kṛṣṇa. *Guṇa* refers to *sattva, rajas* and *tamas* or to a string. *Mumukṣām* means desire for liberation or desire to fall off. Your undergarment shows a slackening of the *guṇas,* or has a loose string. Seeing the manifestation of these four items, a wealth of happiness from liberation or a wealth of happiness from material love, I think you have a desire for liberation or for your garment falling off. Because of increasing lack of knowledge in the eyes, breasts and undergarment, there is gradually lesser qualification for the happiness of liberation or happiness of material love in the items listed.

### Text 72

***uttarīya-sraṁsanaṁ, yathā—***  
***tava hṛdi mama rāgāt ko’pi rāgo gariṣṭhaḥ***  
***sphurati tad apasṛtya vyaktam etaṁ karomi \|***  
***iti khalu hṛdayāt te rādhike rodhakāri***  
***cyutam iva purato me mañju māñjiṣṭha-vāsaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Loosening of upper cloth: O Rādhā, covering your heart with your cloth! The** ***rāga*** **in your heart is greater than my** ***rāga.***  **I shall show this to all by making it leave your heart. It is like the attractive red upper cloth falling away from your heart in front of me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa seeing Rādhā’s upper garment become loose, jokes with her. O Rādhā! Your cloth died with *mañjiṣṭha,* after consideration (i*ti*), is falling from your heart in front of me.  *Iva* indicates a comparison. Compared to the attachment in my heart, or the anger in my heart, the *rāga* in your heart, like the red cloth, is indescribable. Therefore (*tataḥ*) pulling it from here (*itaḥ*), I will show the world this *rāga.* O dear Rādhā! If your cloth goes way in anger and no longer covers you, why worry? Now my heart should cover that *rāga* in friendship. Then he suddenly embraced her.

### Text 73

***dhammilla-sraṁsanaṁ, yathā—***  
***sphurati mura-dviṣi purato***  
***durātmanām api vimuktide gauri \|***  
***nādbhutam idaṁ yadīyuḥ***  
***saṁyaminas te kacā muktim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hair coming undone: O golden-complexioned Rādhā! Since Kṛṣṇa grants liberation to the demons it is not at all surprising that your bound hair has also become undone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Rādhā in a joking mood. *Samyaminaḥ* means one who has controlled the senses or bound up hair.

### Text 74

***gātra-moṭanaṁ, yathā—***  
***vrajāṅgane vallava-puṅgavasya***  
***puraḥ kuraṅgī-nayanā salīlam \|***  
***apy aṅga-bhaṅgaṁ kila kurvatīyam***  
***anaṅga-bhaṅgaṁ tarasā vyatānīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Contorting the body: In this courtyard of Vraja, as this beautiful doe-eyed** ***gopī,*** **playfully contorting her body in front of the best of the cowherd boys, has quickly spread waves of Cupid.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Aṅga-bhaṅgam* means *gātra-moṭanam. Anaṅga-bhaṅgam* means the waves of Cupid.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Vṛndā. *Aṅga-bhaṅgam* means *gātra-moṭanam.* *Anaṅga-bhaṅgam* means the waves of Cupid.

### Text 75

***jṛmbhā, yathā—***  
***puṣpair avetya viśikhair bhavatīm asādhyāṁ***  
***sādhvīm adhītya madanaḥ kila jṛmbhaṇāstrām \|***  
***candrāvali prasabham eva vaśīcakāra***  
***yad goṣṭha-sīmani muhuḥ sakhi jṛmbhase’dya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Yawning: Noticing that his flower-arrows have no effect on you, since you are chaste, Cupid has studied the art of throwing the yawning weapon. O Candrāvalī! I think he must have violently attacked you with that weapon, for you are constantly yawning in the outskirts of Vraja.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *adhītya* sometimes the word *prayujya (*employing) is found.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Candrāvalī. *Asādhyām* means “cannot control.” *Adhītya* means learning from the teacher of that scripture, or learning by oneself.

### Text 76

***ghrāṇa-phullatvaṁ, yathā—***  
***racita-śikhara-śobhārambham ambhoruhākṣī***  
***śvasita-pavana-dolāndolinā mauktikena \|***  
***puṭa-yugam atiphullaṁ bibhratī nāsikāyāṁ***  
***mama manasi vilagnā darśanād eva rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Widened the nostrils: Lotus-eyed Rādhā, with flared nostrils which produced the beauty of a ruby because of the pearl swinging with her breathing, sticks in my mind after seeing her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This describes the thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. *Ārambha* means arrangement. The pearls are attached to the edge of each nostril in the center.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. How are the two nostrils described? By the pearl ornament reflecting the red of her lips, it produced the beauty of a ruby similar to a ripe pomegranate seed *(sikhara*), because of white of the nostrils and the red color reflected in the pearl.

### Text 77

***yadyapy ete viśeṣāḥ syur moṭṭāyita-vilāsayoḥ \|***  
***śobhā-viśeṣa-poṣitvāt tathāpi pṛthag īritāḥ \|\|77\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Even though the above items may be included in** ***moṭtayitam*** **and** ***vilāsa,*** **because they increase beauty intensely, they are glorified separately as** ***udbhāsvaras.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They are considered separately as *udbhāsvaras.* Examples of other items such as rolling on the ground are given in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*:

*navānurāgeṇa tavāvaśāṅgī*  
*vana-srag-āmodam avāpya mattā \|*  
*vrajāṅgane sā kaṭhine luṭhantī*  
*gātraṁ sugātrī vraṇayāñcakāra \|\|*

**O Kṛṣṇa! Because of her new attraction for You, Rādhā is not in control of her limbs. On smelling the fragrance of your forest garland, becoming intoxicated, has fallen on the hard ground of Vraja and injured her beautiful body. BRS 2.2.6**

### Text 78-79

***atha vācikāḥ—***  
***ālāpaś ca vilāpaś ca saṁlāpaś ca pralāpakaḥ \|***  
***anulāpo’palāpaś ca sandeśaś cātideśakaḥ \|\|\|***  
***apadeśopadeśau ca nirdeśo vyapadeśakaḥ \|***  
***kīrtitā vacanārambhā dvādaśāmī manīṣibhiḥ \|\|79\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Verbal** ***Anubhāvas:*** **The wise describe twelve types of speech:** ***ālāpa, vilāpa,saṁlāpa, pralāpa, anulāpa, apalapa, sandeśa, ātideśa, apadeśa, upadeśa, nirdeśa*** **and** ***vyapadeśa.***

### Text 80

***tatra ālāpaḥ—***  
***cāṭu-priyoktir ālāpaḥ \|\|80\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Flattery:** ***Ālāpa*** **refers to pleasing words of flattery.**

### Text 81

***yathā śrī-daśame(10.29.40)—***  
***kā stry aṅga te kala-padāyata-mūrcchitena***  
***sammohitā ‘ryapadavīṁ na calet trilokyām \|***  
***trailokya-saubhagam idaṁ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṁ***  
***yad go-dvija-druma-mṛgān pulakāny abibhrat \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from the Tenth Canto: Dear Kṛṣṇa, what woman in all the three worlds wouldn’t deviate from religious behavior when bewildered by the sweet, drawn-out melody of your flute? Your beauty makes all three worlds auspicious. Indeed, even the cows, birds, trees and deer manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair standing on end when they see your beautiful form.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Abibhrat* should be *abibharuḥ.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The women of Vraja speak to Kṛṣṇa. This is from *Venu-gītā.* The *gopīs* are enchanted with Kṛṣṇa’s qualities. Women of the three worlds deviate from *dharma*. They see him from far off. Others see (*nirīkṣya*) his form and qualities from nearby.

“Is there only enchantment in my form and qualities? Even women with *kāma* have attraction for friendship, charity and other qualities.” The cows, birds and deer are also enchanted. What is the question of their having *kāma*? Please accept us also. This is the intention of that statement.

“It is *rasābhāsa* for heroines to utter flattering words praying for enjoyment with me? Should I accept you, since you are *arasika*?” Sarasvatī solves the problem. By the sound of your flute, women become bewildered and their nature becomes opposite. It is not a fault to pray for enjoyment without shame if the women are intoxicated with alcohol. Rather it adds *rasa* and is a good quality. We are in the same position.

### Text 82

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (5.31)—***  
***kaṭhorā bhava mṛdvī vā prāṇās tvam asi rādhike \|***  
***asti nānyā cakorasya candralekhāṁ vinā gatiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O Rādhā! Whether you are harsh or gentle to me, you are my very life, just as the** ***cakora*** **bird takes shelter of the crescent moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse is given to show that the flattering words of the hero are very pleasant to the heroine by their nature. Without the moon, even on the *dvitīya tithi,* the cakora bird has no other shelter than the moon. What to speak of the full moon?

### Text 83

***atha vilāpaḥ—***  
***vilāpo duḥkhajaṁ vacaḥ \|\|83\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lamentation:** ***Vilapa*** **means words expressing sorrow.**

### Text 84

***yathā śrī-daśame (10.47.47)—***  
***paraṁ saukhyaṁ hi nairāśyaṁ svairiṇy apy āha piṅgalā \|***  
***taj jānatīnāṁ naḥ kṛṣṇe tathāpy āśā duratyayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from the Tenth Canto: Indeed, the greatest happiness is to renounce all desires, as even the prostitute Piṅgalā has declared. Yet even though we know this, we cannot give up our hopes of attaining Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *gopīs* speak when Uddhava comes. It is impossible to give up desire for Kṛṣṇa. Piṅgalā did not have desire centered on Kṛṣṇa. She did not have to suffer like us.

### Text 85

***saṁlāpaḥ—***  
***ukti-pratyuktimad-vākyaṁ saṁlāpa iti kīrtyate \|\|85\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Conversation: Statements with replies are called** ***saṁlāpa.***

### Text 86

***yathā padyāvalyāṁ (269)—-***  
***uttiṣṭhārāt tarau me taruṇi mama taroḥ śaktir ārohaṇe kā***  
***sākṣād ākhyāmi mugdhe taraṇim iha raver ākhyayā kā ratir me \|***  
***vārteyaṁ nau-prasaṅge katham api bhavitā nāvayoḥ saṅgamārthā***  
***vārtāpīti smitāsyaṁ jita-girim ajitaṁ rādhayārādhayāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Padyāvalī:***

**Kṛṣṇa: My dear young girl (*****taruṇi),*** **please step into my boat (*****tarau*****).**

**Rādhā: What power do I have to climb trees (*****taroḥ*****)?**

**Kṛṣṇa: O bewildered girl, I do not mean tree, I mean a boat** ***(taraṇim*****).**

**Rādhā: What affection do I have for the sun (*****taraṇim*****)?**

**Kṛṣṇa: All these words I have used mean boat (*****nau*****).**

**Rādhā: There is no question of us (*****nau)*** **coming together.**

**I worship unconquerable Lord Kṛṣṇa, who happily smiled when defeated by Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tarau uttiṣṭha* means “get up on the boat.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa, during boat pastimes on Mānasa-gaṅgā speaks to Rādhā. Please get into my boat. Rādhā replied by giving another meaning to *tarau* (in the boat). How can I get up into a tree (*tarau*)? Kṛṣṇa said “O foolish girl! You do not understand my words. I meant a boat (*taraṇim*). Why do you reply about a tree? Rādhā then said “What attraction do I have for the sun?” The word *taraṇi* means the sun. Kṛṣṇa said “I am talking about a boat *(nau*). There is no other meaning of *nau.* How can you find another meaning?” Rādhā replied “Why do you speak about us (*nau)* meeting? He then smiled since he could not give a further answer. He smiled to hide his defeat.

### Text 87

***pralāpaḥ—***  
***vyarthālāpaḥ pralāpaḥ syāt \|\|87\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Chatter: Useless talk is called** ***pralāpa.***

### Text 88

***yathā—***  
***karoti nādaṁ muralī ralī ralī***  
***vrajāṅganā-hṛn-mathanaṁ thanaṁ thanam \|***  
***tato vidūnā bhajate jate jate***  
***hare bhavantaṁ lalitā litā litā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Hari! The sound of your flute churns the** ***gopīs’*** **hearts. Afflicted Lalitā worships you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Intoxicated with wine, Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. The syllables *ralī ralī, thanam thaṇam, jate jate,* and *litā litā* are meaningless.

### Text 89

***anulāpaḥ—***  
***anulāpo muhur vacaḥ \|\|89\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Repetition:** ***Anulapa*** **means repetition of words.**

### Text 90

***yathā—***  
***kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇo nahi nahi tāpiñcho’yaṁ***  
***veṇur veṇur nahi nahi bhṛṅgodghoṣaḥ \|***  
***guñjā guñjā nahi nahi bandhūkālī***  
***netre netre nahi nahi padma-dvandvam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: This is not Kṛṣṇa, but a tamāla tree. This is not flute music, but the buzzing bees. This is not a** ***guñja*** **necklace, but a cluster of** ***bandhūka*** **flowers. These are not two eyes, but two lotus flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One *sakhī* speaks to another, on seeing a *tamāla tree*, land lotus and flowering b*andhūka* and mistaking them for something else.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing a *bandhūka* flower and land lotus together with a young *tamāla* tree, Rādhā pointing them out to Lalitā speaks with joy, longing and agitation. On consideration however, she corrects herself. The three statements are doubts ending in confirmation. Or she could also be confirming first: it is Kṛṣṇa, it is not a *tamāla* tree; it is his *guñja* necklace, not a *bandhūka* flower; those are his eyes, not land lotuses.

### Text 91

***apalāpaḥ***  
***apalāpas tu pūrvoktasyānyathā yojanaṁ bhavet \|\|91\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Interpreting meaning: Giving new meanings to previous statements is called** ***apalāpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Giving another meaning to a first statement is called *apalāpa.*

### Text 92

***yathā—***  
***phullojjvala-vana-mālaṁ kāmayate kā na mādhavaṁ pramadā \|***  
***haraye spṛhayasi rādhe nahi nahi vairiṇi vasantāya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “What girl would not yearn for this spring season, filled with forests bright with flowers?” “O Rādhā! You desire Kṛṣṇa.” “Never! Never! O enemy! I desire the spring.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā in separation because of a quarrel speaks to Viśākhā in a solitary spot with longing. Then Lalitā comes suddenly and says jokingly “You desire Kṛṣṇa.” Rādhā replies to her “No. O enemy! You are capable of starting rumours. I desire the spring.” I desire the spring because it has groups of forests bright with flowers. By the word *mādhava* I meant spring.

### Text 93

***sandeśaḥ—***  
***sandeśas tu proṣitasya sva-vārtā-preṣaṇaṁ bhavet \|\|93\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sending messages: Sending a message to a lover who is far away is called** ***sandeśa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sandeśa* is sending a message to a lover who has gone far away (*proṣitasya*).

### Text 94

***yathā—***  
***vyāhara mathurā-nāthe mama sandeśa-prahelikāṁ pāntha \|***  
***vikalā kṛtā kuhūbhir labhate candrāvalī kva layam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O traveler! Please speak the following riddle to Kṛṣṇa, lord of Mathurā. How is the phase of the moon destroyed after decreasing by the new-moon night?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sakhī* of Candrāvalī speaks. *Kuhūḥ* is the sound of the cuckoo and the dark moon. Candrāvalī is the name of a *gopī* and the phases of the moon. *Vikalā* means imperfect and without phases (moon). How are the phases of the moon destroyed after waning to the dark moon? Who does Candrāvalī embrace after becoming disfigured by the cries of the cuckoo? The answer is the sun destroys the phases and Candrāvalī is embraced by Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā sends a message to Kṛṣṇa. Deliver a message to the lord of Mathurā. What loss is it to him if Gokula is destroyed? However he thinks he is very intelligent. Let him answer my riddle. Decreasing by the new moon, where does the moon attain destruction? Becoming disfigured by the cry of the cuckoo, where does Candrāvalī attain destruction. Kṛṣṇa sent the following answer.

*candrāvalī ced vikalīkṛtā syāt*  
*kuhūbhir āpnoti harau layaṁ sā \|*  
*harir vivasvān aghamardanaś ca*  
*layaḥ kṣayaḥ syād upagūhanaṁ ca \|\|*

**If Candrāvalī is disfigured by the cry of the cuckoo she will be embraced by the Lord. If the moon is depleted by the dark moon, it meets destruction by the sun.**

Informing me of the condition of your *sakhī* on the pretext of a riddle, are you rebuking me? I will go there soon and eternally I enjoy and give enjoyment to your friend. She considers this a dream or appearance in her mind. You should ask Candrāvalī the truth in private.

### Text 95

***atideśaḥ—***  
***so’tideśas tad uktāni mad-uktānīti yad vacaḥ \|\|95\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Substitute speaking: Words stating “My words are her words” is called** ***atideśa***

### Text 96

***yathā—***  
***vṛthā kṛthās tvaṁ vicikitsitāni***  
***mā gokulādhīśvara-nandanātra \|***  
***gāndharvikāyā giram antarasthāṁ***  
***vīṇeva gītiṁ lalitā vyanakti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O prince of Gokula! Do not have useless doubts. Lalitā repeats the words that Rādhā thinks in her mind, just as the tune in the mind of a musician manifests externally in playing the vīṇā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though Rādhā makes the words, Lalitā says them. Your doubts (*vicikitsitāni)* about this are useless.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa, who was trying to please Rādhā who was angry, by offering respects. He was expecting some words from the mouth of Rādhā who has come, even though Lalitā had scolded him harshly. “Why do you offer respects to Rādhā. Go away immediately. When she comes here, fall at her feet repeatedly. Do not uselessly doubt that Rādhā says some sweet words to me from her mouth.’” According to *Amara-koṣa* the word *vicikitṣa* means doubt. Lalitā reveals the words in the heart of Rādhā by her words. Those words are like a song in the heart of a musician which manifested externally as the melody of a *vīṇā.*

### Text 97

***atha apadeśaḥ—***  
***anyārtha-kathanaṁ yat tu so’padeśa itīritaḥ \|\|97\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Statements with secret meaning: Making a statement with another intended meaning is called** ***apadeśa.***

### Text 98

***yathā—***  
***dhatte vikṣatam ujjvalaṁ pṛthu-phala-dvandvaṁ navā dāḍimī***  
***bhṛṅgeṇa vraṇitaṁ madhūni pibatā tāmraṁ ca puṣpa-dvayam \|***  
***ity ākarṇya sakhī-giraṁ guru-janāloke kila śyāmalā***  
***cailena stanayor yugaṁ vyavadadhe danta-cchadau pāṇinā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “The pomegranate tree has two effulgent fruits injured by a parrot and two red flowers injured by a bee drinking their honey.” Hearing these words of a** ***sakhī*** **while servants observed from afar, Śyāmalā covered her breasts with her cloth and covered her lips with her hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When her husband was absent, Śyāmalā was smearing oils on her body. Suddenly a *sakhī,* announcing his arrival so that she would restrict herself, spoke with clever words. *Vikṣata* means the birds had scarred the fruit. She heard these words while the elders, who were servants, were watching at a distance.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. The new pomegranate tree supports two damaged fruits, and two red flowers damaged by a bee. *Vraṇitam* means having some damage. Hearing these words skillfully contrived by her *sakhī,* while her mother-in-law was looking (*guru-janāloke),* she covered her breasts with her cloth. According to *Amara-koṣa* the word *dvyavadhā* means disappear or cover.

### Text 99

***upadeśaḥ—***  
***yat tu śikṣārtha-vacanam upadeśaḥ sa ucyate \|\|99\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Giving instruction: Words given as instruction are called** ***upadeśa.***

### Text 100

***yathā chando-mañjaryām—***  
***mugdhe yauvana-lakṣmīr vidyud-vibhrama-lolā***  
***trailokyādbhuta-rūpo govindo’tidurāpaḥ \|***  
***tad-vṛndāvana-kuñje guñjad-bhṛṅga-sanāthe***  
***śrī-nāthena sametā svacchandaṁ kuru kelim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Chando-mañjarī:*** **Charming Rādhā! You are filled with the beauty of youth, which flashes like fickle lightning. Govinda, with a form astonishing to the three worlds, is hard to attain.**

**In this grove of Vṛndāvana filled with the buzzing of bees, meet Kṛṣṇa and freely enjoy pastimes with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tuṅgavidyā speaks to Rādhā who is angry.

### Text 101

***nirdeśaḥ—***  
***nirdeśas tu bhavet so’yam aham ity ādi-bhāṣaṇam \|\|101\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Indicating oneself: Statements saying “This is me” are called** ***nirdeṣa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*So’yam* in the masculine instead of feminine, it is because it is referring to a person in general

### Text 102

***yathā—***  
***seyaṁ me bhaginī rādhā laliteyaṁ ca me sakhī \|***  
***viśākheyam ahaṁ kṛṣṇa tisraḥ puṣpārtham āgatāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa, this is my fortunate friend Rādhā, this is my friend Lalitā, and I am Viśākhā. We three have come here to collect flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This person is Rādhā. Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa, introducing herself. “I have made this flower garden for this purpose, so that every day I will be able to see you chaste girls who worship the *devatās.* And after picking flowers, relax in this flower cottage and leave after giving me a little satisfaction.” This response of Kṛṣṇa should be understood.

### Text 103

*vyapadeśaḥ—*  
*vyājenātmābhilāṣoktir vyapadeśa itīryate \|\|103\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Statements with double meaning: Statements made to reveal ones desires with tricky words are called vyapadeśa.**

### Text 104

***yathā—***  
***vilasan-navaka-stavakā kāmya-vane paśya mālatī milati \|***  
***katham iva cumbasi tumbīm athavā bhramaro’si kiṁ brūmaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Look! There is a splendid** ***mālatī*** **creeper with fresh flowers in Kāmyavana!**

**Why do you prefer to kiss this mediocre** ***tumbī*** **flower? You are just a bumble-bee. What more can I say?**

**Look! There is Mālatī with new shining breasts suitable for maintaining your lust. Why do you kiss the lowly gourd? You are just a lecher. What more can be said?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Mālatī, seeing that Kṛṣṇa was looking at the *gopīs* of the opposing group with great greed, speaks to a bee in front of her. Mālatī refers to the *gopī* of that name and to the jasmine flower. *Stavaka* refers to a bunch of flowers and to the breast. *Kāmya-vane* refers to the forest of that name and to a forest suitable for love pastimes. It can also mean “for the maintenance (*āvana*) of your lusty nature.” *Bhramaraḥ* means a bee or a lusty person. It also implies “You produce bewilderment.” In kissing the *tumbī* (gourd) his madness is suggested, since the *tumbī* has no beauty at all. Though *nirdeśa* and *vyapadeśa* are instruments of the messenger, they have been described here in order to show the *anubhāvas* in the *prema* of the *sakhī.*

### Text 105

***anubhāvā bhavanty ete rase sarvatra vācikāḥ \|***  
***mādhuryādhikya-poṣitvād ihaiva parikīrtitāḥ \|\|105\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These** ***vācika-anubhāvas*** **are possible in all** ***rasas,*** **but because they particularly nourish** ***mādhura-rasa, they*** **are mentioned here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vācika anubhāvas* are seen in *śānta, dāsya* and other *rasas* as well.

## Chapter 12 - Sāttvika-bhāvas

## Outline

I. Stambha (stunned)

1. From joy
2. From fear
3. From astonishment
4. From depression
5. From indignation

II. Sveda (perspiration)

1. From joy
2. From fear
3. From anger

III. Romañca (hair standing on end)

1. From astonishment
2. From joy
3. From fear

IV. Svara-bhaṅga (choked voice)

1. From depression
2. From astonishment
3. From indignation
4. From joy
5. From fear

V. Vepathu (trembling)

1. From terror
2. From anger
3. From joy

VI. Vaivarṇya (changing color)

1. From lamentation
2. From anger
3. From fear

VII. Aśru (tears)

1. From joy
2. From anger
3. From depression

VIII. Pralaya (fainting)

1. From happiness
2. From grief

IX. Intensity

1. *Dhūmāyita-sāttvika-bhāva*
2. *Jvalita-sāttvika-bhāva*
3. *Dīpta-sāttvika-bhāva*
4. *Uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāva*
5. *Sūddīpta-sāttvika-bhāva*

### Text 1

***tatra stambhaḥ, sa harṣād, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (36)—***  
***abhyukṣya niṣkaṁ patayālunā muhuḥ***  
***svedena niṣkampatayā vyavasthitā \|***  
***pañcālikā kuñcita-locanā kathaṁ***  
***pañcālikā-dharmam avāpa rādhikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Being stunned out of joy, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **Rādhā, accompanied by five friends, bathes her locket in falling perspiration and remains motionless. How has she assumed the form of a wooden doll?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *sāttvika-bhāvas* are now described. She bathes her locket with falling perspiration. She with five friends has attained the nature of a doll.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Now the *sāttvika-bhāvas* are described. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Madhumaṅgala. Bathing her locket with falling perspiration, she remained motionless. Accompanied by her five friends, she has become like a doll. *Amara-koṣa* says *pañcālikā* means a doll.

Because of she has strong *rati,* this is en example of *snigdha-sāttvika* (concentrated) arising from a primary *rasa.*

### Text 2

***bhayād, yathā—***  
***ghana-stanita-cakreṇa cakiteyaṁ ghana-stanī \|***  
***babhūva harim āliṅgya niścalāṅgī vrajāṅganā \|\|\|***  
***digdho’yam \|***

**Перевод:**

**Being stunned from fear: Frightened by rumbling in the clouds, the firm-breasted Vraja** ***gopī,*** **embracing Kṛṣṇa, remained stunned in his arms.**

**This is** ***digdha-sāttvika-bhāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This *bhaya* is actually *trāsa* (sudden terror—a *vyabhicār-bhāva*). It is of the *digdha* variety. One should consult *Bhakti-rasāmrta-sindhu* to understand this term.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here *bhaya* means *trāsa* (a *vyabhicāri-bhāva*, not a secondary *rati*). Looking at the actions of angry Rādhā from a distance, Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. By all the rumbling (*stanita-cakreṇa*) of the cloud (*ghana*), Rādhā has become terrorized (*cakitā*). The rumbling was like the vibration of a bowstring. *Ghana* can also mean “concentrated.” Since this is an example of *digdha-sāttvika-bhāva* it should arise from a *vyabhicāri-bhāva* according to the definition:

*rati-dvaya-vinābhūtair bhāvair manasa ākramāt \|*  
*jane jāta-ratau digdhās te ced raty-anugāminaḥ \|\|9\|\|*

**When the heart of a person who possesses genuine** ***rati*** **is overcome by an emotion other than the primary or secondary** ***ratis,*** **if this emotion accompanies genuine** ***rati,*** **it is called** ***didgha-sāttvika-bhāva*****. BRS 2.3.9**

The two types of *rati (rati-dvaya)* are primary (*śānta, dāsya etc.)* and secondary *ratis (hāsya, adbhuta etc.).*

### Text 3

***āścaryād, yathā—***  
***tava madhurima-sampadaṁ vilakṣa***  
***trijagad-alakṣya-tulāṁ mukunda rādhā \|***  
***kalaya hṛdi balavac-camatkriyāsau***  
***samajani nirnimiṣā ca niścalā ca \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From astonishment: Mukunda! Look! As she gazes at your sweetness, which has no equal in all the three worlds, she becomes wonder struck in her heart, stands motionless, with unblinking eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pointing out Rādhā, Madhumaṅgala speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 4

***viṣādād, yathā—***  
***vilambam ambhoruha-locanasya***  
***vilokya sambhāvita-vipralambhā \|***  
***saṅketa-gehasya nitāntam aṅke***  
***citrāyitā tatra babhūva citrā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of depression: Noticing lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa's delay and feeling great separation, Citrā became stunned within the cottage allotted for meeting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Citrā speaks to another of her *sakhīs.* In separation she thought, “He has cheated me today!”

### Text 5

***amarṣād, yathā—***  
***mādhavasya parivartita-gotrāṁ***  
***śyāmalā niśi giraṁ niśamayya \|***  
***deva-yoṣid iva nirnimiṣākṣī***  
***chāyayā ca rahitā kṣaṇam ayāsīt \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Out of indignation: Hearing Kṛṣṇa utter some other** ***gopī’s*** **name while he slept at night, Śyāmalā for a moment became pale and stopped blinking her eyes like a** ***devatā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Gotra* means name. *Chyāyayā* means “with beauty.” Or it can mean in separation she was without shade. *Amara-koṣa* says *chāya* means beauty, the sun, graceful, reflection and shade.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā’s *sakhī* speaks to Rādhā. *Gotra* means name. In his sleep he said, “O dear Pālī!” *Chāyayā* means “of beauty.”

### Text 6

***atha svedaḥ, sa harṣād, yathā viṣṇu-purāṇe (5.13.55)—***  
***gopī-kapola-saṁśleṣam abhipatya harer bhujau \|***  
***pulakodgama-śasyāya svedāmbu-ghanatāṁ gatau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Perspiration out of joy, from** ***Viṣṇu Purāṇa:*** **When Kṛṣṇa’s arm touched the** ***gopī's*** **cheek, his arms became two clouds raining perspiration which caused sprouting of the crops--his hairs stood on end.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Abhipatya* means attaining. The arms became like clouds containing drops of perspiration causing the crops of hairs to stand on end. *Ghana* also means dense in ordinary language.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Parāśara speaks to Maitreya. The arms became like clouds containing drops of perspiration causing the crops of hairs to stand on end. Or his arms became dense with drops of perspiration.

### Text 7

***yathā vā—***  
***dhruvam ujjvala-candra-kānta-yaṣṭyā***  
***vidhinā mādhava nirmitāsti rādhā \|***  
***yad udañcati tāvakāsya-candre***  
***dravatāṁ sveda-bhara-cchalād bibharti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Mādhava! I have concluded that the creator made Rādhā out of a rod of moonstone, because whenever the moon of your face rises, she turns liquid because of profuse drops of perspiration.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā becomes liquid (*dravatām*). She does not actually become liquid but becomes similar because of the intense perspiration.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Rādhā is compared not to moonstone, but to a moonstone stick. This indicates she has a slender body at the beginning of *kaiśora* age.

### Text 8

***bhayād, yathā—***  
***mā bhūr viśākhe taralā vidūrataḥ***  
***patis tavāsau niviḍā latā-kuṭi \|***  
***mahā prayatnena kṛtāḥ kapolayoḥ***  
***svedoda-bindur makarīr vilumpati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Perspiration out of fear: O Viśākhā! Please do not tremble with fear. Your husband is far away, and the jungle of trees and creepers is dense. Your drops of perspiration have completely washed away the** ***makarī*** **patterns I carefully drew on your cheeks.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Viśākhā whom he enjoyed in the bower, and who became frightened on hearing that her husband was coming.

### Text 9

***krodhād, yathā—***  
***khinnāpi gotra-skhalanena pālī***  
***śālīna-bhāvaṁ chalato vyatānīt \|***  
***tathāpi tasyāḥ paṭam ārdrayantī***  
***svedāmbu-vṛṣṭiḥ krudham ācacakṣe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Perspiration out of anger: When Pālī heard Kṛṣṇa accidentally address her as Śyāmalā, though pained, she maintained mild behavior superficially. Nevertheless, the shower of perspiration that moistened her cloth revealed her anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Śālīna-bhāvam* means mild behavior.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Addressing Pālī Kṛṣṇa uttered “O dear Śyāmalā!” Though pained, she remained gentle by hiding her emotions *(avahitthā*).

### Text 10

***atha romāñcaḥ \| sa āścaryād, yathā—***  
***cumbantam ālokya camūru-cakṣuṣāṁ***  
***camūr amūṣāṁ yugapan mura-dviṣam \|***  
***vyomāṅgane tatra surāṅganāvalī***  
***romāñcitā vistṛta-dṛṣṭir ābabhau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hairs standing on end, because of astonishment: When the women of Svarga in the sky saw Kṛṣṇa simultaneously kiss a host of doe-eyed** ***gopīs,*** **they became struck with wonder. Their eyes opened wide and their hairs stood on end.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Gārgī who asked about Kṛṣṇa’s *rāsa-līlā.*

### Text 11

***harṣād, yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.8)—***  
***taṁ kācin netra-randhreṇa hṛdi-kṛtya nimīlya ca \|***  
***pulakāṅguly-upaguhyās te yogīvānanda-samplutā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hairs standing on end because of joy, from the Tenth Canto: One** ***gopī*** **took the Lord through the aperture of her eyes and placed him within her heart. Then, with her eyes closed and her bodily hairs standing on end, she continuously embraced him within. Thus immersed in transcendental ecstasy, she united with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Yogī iva* means “as if uniting with him.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śuka speaks to Parīkṣit. One *gopī* placed the Lord in her heart, but feared that having attained him, he would disappear. Therefore she closed her eyes.

### Text 12

***yathā vā śrī-rukmiṇī-svayaṁvare—***  
***romāṇi sarvāṇy api bāla-bhāvāt***  
***priya-śriyaṁ draṣṭum ivotsukāni \|***  
***tasyās tadā korakitāṅga-yaṣṭer***  
***udgrīvikā-dānam ivānvabhuvan \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Rukminī-svayaṁvara*****: As if eager to behold the beauty of her beloved, all the hairs on her neck stood up, being young in nature, stood up on as her body blossomed like a branch of a tree.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Her hairs were childlike (*bāla-bhāvāt*), having a trusting nature. *Udgrīvikā-dānam ivānvabhuvan* literally mans “the hairs accepted the offering of appearing on her neck.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Svayaṁvara* means the marriage to Kṛṣṇa through a letter that Rukmiṇī personally wrote. The author of the work, Īśvara-purī, speaks to his disciples. Because Rukmiṇī was like a child it is said that her hairs were childlike and she was childlike. This indicates her deep nature. She was anxious to see the beauty of Kṛṣṇa who was coming. She had heard this news from the *brāhmaṇa* Sunanda. *Grīvikā* indicates the neck of a young girl. The hairs stood out from her young neck. The hairs stood up on her neck as if to see Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 13

***bhayād, yathā—***  
***parimala-caṭule dvirepha-vṛnde***  
***mukham abhidhāvati kampitāṅga-yaṣṭiḥ \|***  
***vipula-pulaka-pālir adya pālī***  
***harim adharīkṛta-hrī-dhūr āliliṅga \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hairs standing on end out of fear: When, agitated by the sweet aroma, a swarm of bees raced to Pālī's mouth, she trembled and the hairs of her body stood up. Today, her shyness vanished and she embraced Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Pālī speaks to a friend.

### Text 14

***atha svara-bhaṅgaḥ, sa viṣādād yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (6.10)—***  
***vipula-pulaka-pāliḥ sphīta-sīt-kāram antar-***  
***janita-jaḍima-kāku-vyākulaṁ vyāharantī \|***  
***tava kitava vidhāyāmanda-kandarpa-cintāṁ***  
***rasa-jala-nidhi-magnā dhyāna-lagnā mṛgākṣī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Choking of voice because of lamentation, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **O cheater! Meditating upon you, intensely thinking of love, doe-eyed Rādhā has drowned in an ocean of poison. The hairs of her body stand up, she breathes long sighs, her heart is stunned, and she mutters broken, emotion-charged appeals to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The order of words is “Meditating upon you, intensely thinking of love, doe-eyed Rādhā has sunk in the ocean of *rasa*.” The symptoms of having sunk in the ocean are described.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Rādhā, who is ready to receive Kṛṣṇa, informs him of Rādhā’s repentance caused by not meeting him, while at the same time scolding him. O cheater! Your cheating acts have yielded fruit. You will be responsible for killing a woman. *Jaḍima-kāku-vyākulam* means she speaks painfully in a choked voice. “This is the result of not giving up shyness and normal *dharma.* Therefore I suffer.” *Rasa-jala-nidhi* means an ocean of poison.

### Text 15

***vismayād, yathā—***  
***guru-sambhrama-stimita-kaṇṭhayā mayā***  
***kara-saṁjñayāpi bahudhāvabodhitā \|***  
***na punas tvam atra hari-veṇu-vādane***  
***pulakān vilokitavatī latāsv api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Choking voice out of astonishment: Because my voice became choked up out of great agitation, I tried to inform you by hand signals many times. But because of hearing Kṛṣṇa’s flute, all the creepers broke out in goose bumps with their buds, and you could not see me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. My voice choked up because of agitation on the upcoming meeting with Kṛṣṇa. Because I could not clearly speak I tried to communicate (*sañjñayā*) using my hands. According to *Amara-koṣa*, the word *saṁjñā* means consciousness, name, and communicating using the hands.

### Text 16

***amarṣād, yathā—***  
***preyasyaḥ paramādbhutāḥ kati na me dīvyanti goṣṭhāntare***  
***tāsāṁ nojjvala-narma-bhaṅgibhir api prāpto’smi tuṣṭiṁ tathā \|***  
***dvitrair adya muhus taraṅgad-adhara-grastārdha-varṇair yathā***  
***rādhāyāḥ sakhi roṣa-gadgada-padair ākṣepa-vāg-bindubhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Choking of voice out of indignation: So many astonishing girls sport with me in Vraja, but I am not as satisfied by their brilliant jokes and play as I am by hearing two or three drops of Rādhā’s broken syllables, censuring words arising out of anger, with half syllables indistinct because of trembling lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *roṣa-gadgada-padaiḥ* sometime *jāta-gadgada-padaiḥ* is seen. *Padaiḥ* here means “by employing.” *Amara-koṣa* says *padam* means undertaking.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

After enjoying privately with Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa speaks to Viśākhā with great relish. She scolds him. “O *naptṛka* bird in the *karālikā* tree! O crooked stage director of pet deer! Do not contaminate my eyes. Please leave quickly!” These words are like drops from a river of nectar (*ākṣepa-vāg-bindubhiḥ*), unclear in their inflected endings because of her voice begin choked up in anger, with half syllables indistinct because of her trembling lips.

One should not think it is a fault to name the *vyābhicārī*-bhāva such as *roṣa*, Mention of emotions is considered a literary fault. Rather than mention names, the actions which indicate those emotions should be described. (Kāvya-prakāśa 7.60)1 since it nourishes the sense of great astonishment by establishing the *bhāva* which causes external manifestations such as choking of voice. In the alternate version, with *jāta-gadgada-padaiḥ* one should not think that the astonishment has been expressed amply by those words. Nor is it a universal rule that mentioning the *vyabhicāri* or *sthāyi-bhavā* is a fault. *Kāvya-prakāsa* (7.62) says *na dosaḥ sva-padenoktāu api sañcāriāḥ kvacit:* in some cases mentioning the *vyabhicāri-bhāva* is not a defect.

### Text 17

***harṣād, yathā śrī-rukmiṇī-svayaṁvare—***  
***paśyema taṁ bhūya iti bruvāṇāṁ***  
***sakhīṁ vacobhiḥ kila sā tatarja \|***  
***na prīti-karṇe-japatāṁ gatāni***  
***vidāmbabhūva smara-vaikṛtāni \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Choked voice from joy: When a friend said to her “We shall see Kṛṣṇa again" Rukmiṇī rebuked her with many words, but was unaware that her choked words revealed her love for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

”We will see him again. Do not feel pain.” The word “again” indicates that previously she had seen him. *Karṇe japatām gatāni* means “acting as an informer.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author speaks this verse. “O friend Rukmiṇī! Why do you suffering? Come here. By some means we will see him again.” “We” here indicate “the two of us.” Rukmiṇī rebuked her with many words. “O lusty friend! You are making me fall from *dharma* to the lowest level. See for yourself clearly.” She concealed her desires by saying that she had no desire to see Kṛṣṇa, but was not aware that her choked words revealed her affection for him. She hid her *prema* by her words, but her words revealed clearly her *prema.* She was not aware of this. *Amara-koṣa* says *kareṇejapa* means an informer. The perfect tense is formed according to the rule *uṣa-vid-jāgṛbhyo’ nyatarasyām:*  the affix *ām* is added to *uṣ* (to burn), to *vid* (to know) and to *jāgṛ* (to wake) to form the perfect tense. (Pāṇini 3.1.36)

### Text 18

***bhīter, yathā—***  
***prathama-saṅgama-narmaṇi sādhvasa-***  
***skhalitayāpi girā sakhi rādhikā \|***  
***nava-sudhā-hradinīṁ madirekṣaṇā***  
***śruti-taṭe mama kāñcid avīvahat \|\|18\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Choked voice from fear: O** ***sakhī*****! Rādhā, with eyes like a wagtail bird, has caused a lake of fresh nectar to flow into my ears by her choked words arising from fright, when I joked with her at our first meeting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Viśākhā. On the first day of our enjoyment together, I joked in requesting enjoyment. “Please be merciful to this intensely thirsty bee by giving your honey.” She replied with words choked with fear. “No! No!” She gave permission however by her glances resembling the movements of the wagtail bird. In this way she brought nectar to my ears.

### Text 19

***atha vepathuḥ, sa trāsena, yathā—***  
***keśavo yuvati-veśa-bhāg ayaṁ***  
***bāliśaḥ kila patis tavāgrataḥ \|***  
***rādhike tad api mūrtir adya te***  
***kiṁ pravāta-kadalī-tulāṁ dadhe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Trembling, arising from terror (*****trāsa*****): Keśava has disguised himself as a young girl, and your husband Abhimanyu is a childish fool. O Rādhā! Why are you trembling like a plantain tree in the wind?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Bāliṣaḥ* means a fool. Your husband will not understand what is happening. You are like a banana tree in a strong wind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One day Rādhā was unable to meet Kṛṣṇa since Jaṭilā prevented her. Kṛṣṇa then put on a woman’s dress and entered her house. She became afraid that Abhimanyu would enter the house for doing some job. Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā in a low voice. “Abhimanyu is without intelligence. He will not be able to comprehend.” She began trembling like a banana tree in a strong wind.

### Text 20

***amarṣeṇa, yathā—***  
***yadi kupitāsi na padme***  
***kiṁ tanur utkampate prasabham \|***  
***vicalati kuto nivāte***  
***dīpa-śikhā nirbhara-snigdhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Trembling because of anger: If you are not angry, why is your body trembling so strongly? Why should a flame with plentiful ghee flicker in a windless place?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nivāte* means “where wind cannot enter.” It is used in words like *nivaṭa-kavaca*. *Gītā* says *yatha dīpo nivaṭa-stho neṅgate*: the controlled mind is comparable to a flame in a windless place. (BG 6.19)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Padmā who is angry. *Nivāte* means in a windless place. *Ni* sometimes has a negative meaning, as in *yathā dīpo nirvāta-stho neṅgate* or *nivāta-dīpa-stimitena cakṣuṣa* (*Raghu-vaṁsa-kāvya).* Doctors say *nivāṭe ye guṇaḥ proktās te guṇaḥ karṇa-bandhane:* shelter from wind can be produced by covering the ears.

### Text 21

***harṣeṇa, yathā—***  
***vallava-rāja-kumāre***  
***milite purataḥ kim ātta-kampāsi \|***  
***tava peśalāsmi pārśve***  
***laliteyaṁ pariharātaṅkam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Trembling out of joy: Why do you tremble so when you meet the cowherd-prince? Give up your fear. I, clever Lalitā, am by your side.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Peśalā* means clever.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā who is picking flowers*. Peśalā* means clever.

### Text 22

***atha vaivarṇyam, tad-viṣādād, yathā—***  
***madhurima-bharair muktasyālaṁ kalaṅkita-kuṅkumair***  
***dvirada-radana-śyeṇīm ābhāṁ cirāya vitanvataḥ \|***  
***vidhur api tulām āptas tasyā mukhasya bakī-ripo***  
***vada param ataḥ sāraṅgyākṣyāḥ kim asti viḍambanam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Changing color, out of lamentation: O killer of Pūtanā! Since Rādhā’s face for a long time has had the appearance of ivory spotted with** ***kuṁkuma*****, devoid of beauty, what use is it to compare the moon to her face?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Śyenī* means white. By mentioning Rādhā having eyes like a doe, the comparison to the moon is negated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A s*akhī* of Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa after Rādhā has been cheated by him. Her faced is white like elephant tusks, but its natural beauty has vanished, becoming pale. You can compare Rādhā to many things like “The moon which is the color of lightning cannot compare to your beauty.” But now, in front of you, she is dying. O killer of Pūtanā! You have no fear of killing women. There is the ornament called *pratīpa* (reversed comparison).

### Text 23

***roṣād, yathā—***  
***vilasati kila vṛndāraṇya-līlā-vihāre***  
***kathaya katham akāṇḍe tāmra-vaktrāsi vṛttā \|***  
***prasarad-udaya-rāga-grasta-pūrṇendu-bimbā***  
***kim iva sakhi niśīthe śāradī jāyate dyauḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Change of color out of anger: Please tell me why, as we enjoy amorous pastimes in the middle of the night in Vṛndāvana forest, your face has turned red. How is it possible that the sky with the full moon in the autumn season can be tinged with red at midnight?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

While wandering around and engaging in pastimes of happiness in the forest of Vṛndāvana, how have you become red in complexion at the wrong time? How can the sky with a red moon appear at midnight? It is impossible. It cannot happen unless there is lightning or some other cause.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks after Rādhā becomes angry on mistaking her reflection on Kṛṣṇa’s chest to be another woman. You have become red at the wrong time, *(ākāṇḍe*) after amorous pastimes in Vṛndāvana. You are angry. How can the sky at midnight be red with the moon? It cannot happen. Since it is the full moon, not a half moon, and it is in the autumn season after the raining season, when there is no lightning, how is it possible?

### Text 24

***bhīter, yathā—***  
***krīḍantyās taṭa-bhuvi mādhavena sārdhaṁ***  
***tatrārāt patim avalokya viklavāyāḥ \|***  
***rādhāyās tanum anu kālimā tathāsīt***  
***teneyaṁ kim api yathā na paryacāyi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Change of color out of fear: As Rādhā was enjoying pastimes with Kṛṣṇa on the shore of the Yamunā, she saw what appeared to be her husband in the distance and became disturbed. Her body became black, so that she could not even be recognized.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She could not be recognized by him (*tena). Kim api* means *kiñcid api* (not at all). Sometimes *dara ca* (slightly) is seen instead of *kim api.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Tanum anu* means “in her body.” She could not be recognized at all (*kim api*). The characteristics of Rādhā were not seen by her husband.

### Text 25

***atha aśru, tatra harṣād, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (11.32)—***  
***atikramyāpāṅgaṁ śravaṇa-patha-paryanta-gamana-***  
***prayāsenevākṣṇos taralatara-tāraṁ gamitayoḥ \|***  
***idānīṁ rādhāyāḥ priyatama-samāloka-samaye***  
***papāta svedāmbu-prasara iva harṣāśru-nikaraḥ \|\|25\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Tears, from joy, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **When Rādhā saw her beloved Kṛṣṇa, a host of joyful tears fell from her eyes and spread like a stream of perspiration since her eyes had with great effort extended to the ears, as her trembling pupils fell upon Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When seeing her beloved, a host of tears of joy fell from Rādhā’s eyes, like streams of perspiration, caused by eyes spreading to her ears. *Gamitayoḥ* means “falling upon.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Jayadeva speaks. Now groups of joyful tears have fallen from her eyes like streams of perspiration. The cause of the eyes perspiring from exertion is given. Going beyond the tips of the eyes, the eyes, with flittering pupils falling upon (*gamitayoḥ*) the moon-like face of Kṛṣṇa, have spread to the ears with great effort (*prayāsena*). The object, Kṛṣṇa’s face is understood, just as when we say “I enter” we mean “I enter a house.”

### Text 26

***phulla-gaṇḍaṁ saromāñcaṁ bāṣpam ānandajaṁ matam \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Full cheeks and bodily hairs standing up along with tears are considered to arise from bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The tears of the heroine are indicated here.

### Text 27

***roṣād, yathā—***  
***prātar muradviṣam uraḥ-sphurad-anya-nārī-***  
***patrāṅkura-prakara-lakṣmaṇam īkṣamāṇā \|***  
***aprocya kiñcid api kuñcita-dṛṣṭir eṣā***  
***roṣāśru-bindu-bharam indumukhī mumoca \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Tears arising from anger: Seeing Kṛṣṇa at daybreak, Indumukhī, with crooked eyes, stared at his chest, which bore the** ***tilaka*** **pictures and decorations drawn by some other girl. Not saying a word, she released a flood of angry tears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Indumukhī speaks to her friend.

### Text 28

***yathā vā bilvamaṅgale—***  
***rādhe’parādhena vinaiva kasmād***  
***asmāsu vācaḥ paruṣā ruṣā te \|***  
***aho kathaṁ te kucayoḥ prathante***  
***hārānukārās taralāśru-dhārāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, given by Bilvamaṅgala: Rādhā! Though I have not offended you, why do you speak these harsh, angry words to me? Why do streams of tears spread over your breasts like a jewel-necklace?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example is given of Rādhā showing tears of anger. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā, who is angry.

### Text 29

***śiraḥ-kampi sa-niśvāsaṁ sphurad-oṣṭha-kapolakam \|***  
***kaṭākṣa-bhrū-kuṭī-vaktraṁ strīṇām īrṣyottha-rodanam \|\|29\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When women shed tears out of anger, they shake their heads, sigh, display trembling lips and cheeks, cast sidelong glances, and frown.**

### Text 30

***viṣādād, yathā padyāvalyām (349)—***  
***malinaṁ nayanāñjanāmbubhir***  
***mukha-candraṁ karabhoru mā kuru \|***  
***karuṇā-varuṇālayo haris***  
***tvayi bhūyaḥ karuṇāṁ vidhāsyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Tears from disappointment, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O Rādhā with beautiful thighs! Do not stain your moonlike face with these tears. Kṛṣṇa, an ocean of mercy, will be merciful to you again.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā, when Kṛṣṇa has left.

### Text 31

***atha pralayaḥ, sa sukhena, yathā—***  
***jaṅghe sthāvaratāṁ gate parihṛta-spandā dvayī netrayoḥ***  
***kaṇṭha kuṇṭhita-nisvano vighaṭita-śvāsā ca nāsā-puṭī \|***  
***rādhāyāḥ parama-pramoda-sudhayā dhautaṁ puro mādhave***  
***sākṣātkāram ite mano’pi munivan manye samādhiṁ dadhe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fainting, out of happiness: Now that Rādhā has directly met Mādhava, her legs have become paralyzed, her eyes have given up all motion, her throat has become restricted, and her breath has stopped coming from her nostrils. Her mind is washed by the highest bliss. Therefore I think that she has attained** ***samādhi*** **like a sage.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā along with Viśākhā relishes Rādhā’s bliss on seeing Kṛṣṇa. *Ite* means “attaining.” *Manye* is related to all the statements.

### Text 32

***duḥkhena, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.61)—***  
***daṁśaḥ kaṁsa-nṛpasya vakṣasi ruṣā kṛṣṇorageṇārpyatāṁ***  
***dūre goṣṭha-taḍāga-jīvanam ito yenāpajahre hariḥ \|***  
***hā dhik kaḥ śaraṇaṁ bhaven mṛdi luṭhad gātrīyam antaḥ-klamād***  
***ābhīrī-śapharī-tatiḥ śithilita-śvāsormir āmīlati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fainting, out of sorrow, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **May the serpent Kṛṣṇa angrily bite the chest of King Kaṁsa! Because of Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa took away the life from the pond of Vraja. Alas! Who will give them shelter? The** ***śaphari*** **fish of the** ***gopīs*** **are now rolling about on the dry ground in agony. With restricted waves of their breathing, they approach death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks. The pond of the village is a metaphor and *jīvana* has a double meaning. In terms of the village, *jīvanam* means living. In terms of the pond it means water. The village means all the people living in Vraja. When their life (water) in Vraja has gone away and their state of life has gone, there will not even be any breathing of the *śapharī* fish (*gopīs*). They will not breathe at all. Since all life forms will disappear without water, they will not be especially selected to live. The village also means the place where they live and *jīvanam* means those staying there.  *Jivanam* refers to the inhabitants and Kṛṣṇa staying there. When he is no longer there, the inhabitants can remain there some time. But the *gopīs* cannot remain, since they are very tender, like the *śaphari* fish.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī curses Kaṁsa. *Jīvanam* means life and water. *Āmīlati* means attaining death.

### Text 33

***atha eṣu dhūmāyitāḥ—***  
***surāṅgane sakhi madhurāpur āṅgane***  
***puraḥ purātana-puruṣasya vīkṣayā \|***  
***tavākṣiṇī jala-kaṇa-sākṣiṇī kutaḥ***  
***kathaṁ punaḥ pulaki ca gaṇḍa-maṇḍalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dhūmāyita-sāttvika-bhāva:*** **My dear friend, heavenly goddess! Why do your eyes become filled with tears and your cheeks full of goose bumps by gazing on the Supreme Lord in the courtyard of Mathurā?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *dhūmāyita sātttvika-bhāva* is described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu:*

*advitīyā amī bhāvā athavā sa-dvitīyakāḥ \|*  
*īṣad-vyaktā apahnotuṁ śakyā dhūmāyitā matāḥ \|\|*

**Any** ***sāttvika bhāva*** **which appears alone or with others, manifests slightly and can be hidden, is called** ***dhūmāyita-sāttvika bhāva.*** **BRS 2.3.71**

Actually everyone on seeing the Lord will have tears in the eyes. People have different *bhāvas* for the Lord. What is your *bhāva,* O heavenly woman! This indicates she has special love, like an Apsarā. There is also a joke by saying *purāṇa-puruṣa.* Though this means the Lord, it also means an old man. Your eyes have tears. The word *sākṣī* can mean “present.” However, it also means the witness. Your eyes have become the witness of the Lord and therefore filled with tears.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*prāyo dhūmāyitā eva rukṣās tiṣṭhanti sāttvikāḥ \|*  
*snigdhās tu prāyaśaḥ sarve caturdhaiva bhavanty amī \|\|*

**All the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **in the** ***rūkṣa*** **state remain generally at the** ***dhūmāyita*** **level. The** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **in the** ***snigdha*** **state appear in all four levels (*****dhūmāyita, jvalita, dīpta*** **and** ***uddīpta*****). BRS 2.3.68**

It is therefore not possible for the *gopīs* to have *dhūmāyita-sāttvika-bhāvas*, since they never have a *rūkṣa* condition. Therefore an example of the *devatā* women is given.

The *dhūmāyita-sātttvika-bhāva* is described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu:*

*advitīyā amī bhāvā athavā sa-dvitīyakāḥ \|*  
*īṣad-vyaktā apahnotuṁ śakyā dhūmāyitā matāḥ \|\|*

**Any** ***sāttvika-bhāva*** **which appears alone or with others, manifests slightly and can be hidden, is called** ***dhūmāyita-sāttvika-bhāva*****. BRS 2.3.71**

A *siddha* woman speaks jokingly to a heavenly woman in her aircraft. You are a heavenly woman, but you have love on seeing Kṛṣṇa. “What symptoms of love do you see in me?” Your eyes are the witness of tears. Even though you try to repress the tears, you eyes reveal tear drops on their interior by their excessive sparkling. Your attempt at concealment shows your amorous desire. That attempt at concealment makes you an object of laughter--not your tears and hairs standing on end.

### Text 34

***jvalitāḥ—***  
***sakhi stabdhībhāvaṁ bhajati nitarām uru-yugalaṁ***  
***tanu-jālī harṣaṁ yugam api tavākṣṇoḥ sarasatām \|***  
***tad unnītaṁ dhanye rahasi kara-paṅkeruha-talaṁ***  
***prapannas te diṣṭyā nalina-mukhi nīlo nidhir abhūt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Jvalita-sāttvika-bhāva:*** **O Dhanyā! Your thighs are stunned, your bodily hairs stand on end, and your eyes are filled with tears. O lotus-faced friend! By good fortune, the dark treasure of Kṛṣṇa has secretly fallen into the palms of your lotus hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*te dvau trayo vā yugapad yāntaḥ suprakaṭāṁ daśām \|*  
*śakyāḥ kṛcchreṇa nihnotuṁ jvalitā iti kīrtitāḥ \|\|*

**When two or three of the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **appear very clearly, and can be concealed only with difficulty, they are called** ***jvalita-sāttvika bhāvas*****. BRS 2.3.73**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*te dvau trayo vā yugapad yāntaḥ suprakaṭāṁ daśām \|*  
*śakyāḥ kṛcchreṇa nihnotuṁ jvalitā iti kīrtitāḥ \|\|*

**When two or three of the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **appear very clearly, and can be concealed only with difficulty, they are called** ***jvalita-sāttvika bhāvas*****. BRS 2.3.73**

A *sakhī* talks to Dhanyā. *Stabdhī-bhāva* means being stunned. *Tanujālī* means groups of hairs. *Harṣam* means hairs standing on end. *Sarasatām* means tears. *Nīlo nidhi* means a blue treasure or Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 35

*atha dīptāḥ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (1.36)—*  
***kṣauṇiṁ paṅkilayanti paṅkaja-rucor akṣṇoḥ payo-bindavaḥ***  
***śvāsās tāṇḍavayanti pāṇḍu-vadane dūrād urojāṁśukam \|***  
***mūrtiṁ danturayanti santatam amī romāñca-puñjāś ca te***  
***manye mādhava-mādhurī-śravaṇayor abhyāsam abhyāyayau \|\|35\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dīpta-sāttvika-bhāva,*** **from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O fair-faced Rādhā! The tears from your lotus eyes are turning your black mascara into mud; your sighs are making your bodice dance; and a network of erect hairs make your body prickly. I think the sweetness of Mādhava must have approached your ears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*prauḍhāṁ tri-caturā vyaktiṁ pañca vā yugapad-gatāḥ \|*  
*saṁvarītum aśakyās te dīptā dhīrair udāhṛtāḥ \|\|*

**When three, four or five** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **appear strongly and cannot be concealed, they are called** ***dīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas.*** **BRS 2.3.76**

*Danturayanti* means “they make the body uneven.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*prauḍhāṁ tri-caturā vyaktiṁ pañca vā yugapad-gatāḥ \|*  
*saṁvarītum aśakyās te dīptā dhīrair udāhṛtāḥ \|\|*

**When three, four or five** ***sāttvika- bhāvas*** **appear strongly and cannot be concealed, they are called** ***dīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas*****. BRS 2.3.76**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. *Danturayanti* means “they make the body uneven.” This is according to *Amara-koṣa. Abhyaśam* means near.

### Text 36

***uddīptāḥ—***  
***snātā netraja-nirjhareṇa dadhatī svedāmbu-muktāvaliṁ***  
***romāñcotkara-kañcukena nicitā śrī-khaṇḍa-pāṇḍu-dyutiḥ \|***  
***khañjan-mañjula-bhāratī savayasā yuktā sphuratīty asau***  
***sajjā te nava-saṅgamāya lalitā stambhāśritā vartate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāva:*** **Lalitā is bathed in a waterfalls of tears, is ornamented with the pearl-necklace of her perspiration, is dressed in the garment of her bodily hairs standing up, is pale as sandalwood, and converses with her friends with choked words. Lalitā, decorated in this manner for a new meeting with you, remains stunned.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*ekadā vyaktim āpannāḥ pañca-ṣāḥ sarva eva vā \|*  
*ārūḍhā paramotkarṣam uddīptā iti kīrtitāḥ \|\|79\|\|*

**When five, six or all the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **manifest at once, in their most extreme form, they are called** ***uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas.***

*Stambhā* means she has to take support of a pillar and also that she is stunned.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*ekadā vyaktim āpannāḥ pañca-ṣāḥ sarva eva vā \|*  
*ārūḍhā paramotkarṣam uddīptā iti kīrtitāḥ \|\|79\|\|*

**When five, six or all the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **manifest at once, in their most extreme form, they are called** ***uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas.***

Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa, describing the state of Lalitā in separation from Kṛṣṇa. As a woman in separation, she is decorating herself with symptoms of *sāttvika-bhāvas* for meeting you again. Just as a woman before she decorates herself bathes, so she bathes in tears. She puts on ornaments of perspiration drops and anoints her limbs with the sandalwood of her pale complexion, or, out of separation, her sandalwood ointment has become discolored. Sweet words limp, or come out in half-syllables as a message, on seeing your temporary manifestation internally.  *Stambha* means the *sāttvika-bhāva* of being stunned or taking support of a tree trunk in the bower.

### Text 37

*uddīptānāṁ bhidā eva sūddīptāḥ santi kutracit \|*  
*sāttvikāḥ paramotkarṣa-koṭim atraiva bibhrati \|\|37\|\|*

**Перевод:**

***Sūddīpta-sāttvika-bhāva:*** **The** ***uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas*** **appear sometimes as** ***sūddīpta*****. This is the highest level of the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*****.**

### Text 38

***yathā—***  
***svedair darśita-durdinā vidadhatī bāṣpāmbubhir nistṛṣo***  
***vatsīraṅga-ruhālibhir mukulinī-phullābhir āmūlataḥ \|***  
***śrutvā te muralīṁ tathābhavad iyaṁ rādhā yathārādhyate***  
***mugdhair mādhava bhāratī-pratikṛtir bhrāntyādya vidyārthibhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When Rādhā heard the sound of your flute, she became a rainstorm of perspiration. Her streams of tears slaked the calves’ thirst, and her body became covered from head to feet with the blossoming flowers of erect hairs. Because she became stunned and pale, persons desiring knowledge began worshipping her, thinking she was a statue of Sarasvatī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse is an example of *udātta alaṅkāra,* showing the state of *sūddīpta.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā left her house in the morning and was on the forest path. On hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, she developed *sūddīpta* symptoms. A messenger saw this, and quickly went to Kṛṣṇa and described her situation. Her perspiration was like a cloud, constantly producing showers. The calves satisfied their thirst with the streams of her tears.  *Vatsī* means a female calf or the feminine form can indicate a small animal. She was like a flowering tree from head to foot with groups of hairs standing on end. Hearing the sound of the flute, she became stunned and pale in color. Some persons desiring knowledge happened to approach. Seeing her in a stunned condition and pale in color, they thought she was a deity form of Sarasvatī. They began worshipping her with foot water, *arghya* and other items. In the first moment, she became stunned, and simultaneously five *sāttvika-bhāvas* appeared—perspiration, tears, hairs on end, being stunned and discoloration. This is the condition of *sūddīpta.* The next moment being stunned and fainting became much stronger, and then perspiration, tears and hairs standing on end disappeared. Thus she appeared like a statue of Sarasvatī. Then those desiring knowledge approached and worshipped her. The presence of tears and hairs standing on end would be unsuitable for a statue form.

## Chapter 13 - Vyabhicāri-bhāvas

### Text 1

***nirvedādyāstrayastriṁśad-bhāvā ye parikīrtitāḥ \|***  
***augryalasye vinā te’tra vijñeyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The thirty-three** ***bhāvas*** **starting with** ***nirveda,*** **excluding** ***augrya*** **and** ***ālasya*** **are known as the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **of** ***ujjvala-rasa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Augrya* is unsuitable because of its violence and cruelty. *Ālasya* is unsuitable because it is disinclination to service though being capable. They are visible in relationship between two males.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The thirty-three *bhāvas* were described in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* with examples. In *ujjvala-rasa, augrya* and *ālasya* are not suitable, since *augrya* involves violence and *ālasya* indicates disinclination to service though having the capacity. These two are possible between two males in conflict with each other.

### Text 2

***sakhyādiṣu nija-premāpy atra sañcāritāṁ vrajet \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***prema*** **of the** ***sakhīs*** **and others are pervaded by these** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sañcāritām* means *vyabhicāritām.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *prema* in the *sakhīs,* messengers and others is filled with *vyabhicāri-bhāvas.*

### Text 3

***sākṣād-aṅgatyā neṣṭā kintv atra maraṇādayaḥ \|***  
***vardhyamānās tu yuktyāmī guṇatām upacinvate \|\|3\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Though death and other** ***bhāvas*** **are not desirable, they increase and become visible as good qualities in** ***ujjvala-rasa*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Death and other symptoms, increasing and appearing in them, attain (*upacinvate*) a positive nature.

### Text 4

***tatra nirvedaḥ, sa mahārtyā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.41)—***  
***yasyotsaṅga-sukhāśayā śithilatā gurvī gurubhyas trapā***  
***prāṇebhyo’pi suhṛttamāḥ sakhi tathā yūyaṁ parikleśitāḥ \|***  
***dharmaḥ so’pi mahān mayā na gaṇitaḥ sādhvībhir adhyāsito***  
***dhig dhairyaṁ tad-upekṣitāpi yad ahaṁ jīvāmi pāpīyasī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Self-condemnation (*****nirveda*****) arising from great pain, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O friend! Desiring the happiness of his embraces, I relax my great shyness in front of elders. Although you are my best friend, dearer than my own life, I have given you so much trouble. I even put aside my great vow, kept by the most elevated women. What evil self-control I have! Although he has now neglected me, I, most sinful, am still living.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

As per *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, nirveda* means self-condemnation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nirveda* means self-condemnation. Rādhā, condemning herself, speaks on seeing the withered face of *sakhī* who has come from Kṛṣṇa, and after inferring that he has ignored her. “With a desire for happiness from his association, since he is happiness personified, my shyness in front of elders has slackened.” Though by her declaration, her desire for her own happiness is clear, a mental quality of all the women of Vraja who have *samartha-rati* is that they desire to give Kṛṣṇa happiness by their beauty and grace, what to speak of Rādhā, the jewel of all *vāma* women in Vraja. They do not generally speak about this happiness, but Kṛṣṇa, who is the crest jewel of knowledge, knows about this. Thus he says:

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. SB 10.32.22**

It must only be explained that he falls under their control. *Asyāṁ kṛṣṇa-saukhyārtham eva kevalam udyama*: their only endeavour is to make Kṛṣṇa happy. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.55)

The queens of Dvārakā, having *samañjasa-rati,* are clearly without desire for their own happiness:

*ātmārāmasya tasyemā vayaṁ vai gṛha-dāsikāḥ*  
*sarva-saṅga-nivṛttyāddhā tapasā ca babhūvima*

**Thus, by renouncing all material association and practicing austere penances, we queens have all become personal maidservants of the self-satisfied Supreme Lord. SB 10.83.39**

*tapaś carantīm ājñāya sva-pāda-sparśanāśayā*  
*sakhyopetyāgrahīt pāṇiṁ yo ’haṁ tad-gṛha-mārjanī*

**The Lord knew I was performing severe austerities and penances with the hope of one day touching his lotus feet. So he came to me in the company of his friend and took my hand in marriage. Now I am engaged as a sweeper in his palace. SB 10.83.11**

However, in their mind there is a slight desire. “May Kṛṣṇa make me happy by touching me or embracing me!” Kṛṣṇa knows that. Thus Śukadeva says:

*uddāma-bhāva-piśunāmala-valgu-hāsa-*  
*vrīḍāvaloka-nihato madano ’pi yāsām*  
*sammuhya cāpam ajahāt pramadottamās tā*  
*yasyendriyaṁ vimathituṁ kuhakair na śekuḥ*

**Although the queens’ beautiful smiles and furtive glances were all spotless and exciting, and signified deep love, and although they could conquer Cupid himself by making him give up his bow in frustration, those who approached him with false smiles and glances could not agitate the senses of the Lord. SB 1.11.36**

### Text 5

***viprayogeṇa, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (81)—***  
***na kṣodīyān api sakhi mama premagandho mukunde***  
***krandantīṁ māṁ nijaśubhagatākhyāpanāya pratīhi \|***  
***khelat-vamśī-valayinam anālokya taṁ vaktrabimbaṁ***  
***dhvastālambā yad aham ahaha prāṇa-kīṭam bibharmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Self-condemnation arising from separation, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O friend! I have not the slightest fragrance of love for Mukunda. When you see me crying, you should know that I cry only to announce my good fortune, for even though I can no longer see Kṛṣṇa, who plays the flute melodies enriched with a variety of musical ornaments on his crooked lips, I still maintain my life, which continually bites me like an insect.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā in separation from Kṛṣṇa speaks to Lalitā. I cry to announce to the world that I was previously the object of his love more than all others. Though I do not see Kṛṣṇa with crooked lips, playing groups of notes (*valaya*) on his flute which sports with a variety of *rāgas,* notes, rhythms and vibratos *(khelat*), I maintain and prolong my life, which is an insect which continually bites me.

### Text 6

***īrsyayā, yathā—***  
***nātmānam ākṣipa tvaṁ mlāyad-vadanā gabhīra-garimāṇam \|***  
***sakhi nāntaraṁ kṣitau kaś candrāvali-tārayor vetti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Self-condemnation out of envy: O friend! Your face appears wilted. Please do not rebuke yourself. You are most important to Kṛṣṇa. After all, who on this earth does not know Candrāvalī and Rādhā?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Tāra means Rādhā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Candrāvalī, who is criticizing herself saying “O I am so foul, not tolerating Rādhā on seeing her great good fortune, which is famous everywhere.” You have great importance, given by Kṛṣṇa himself. “But my fame is not as great as Rādhā’s.” True, but her fame is false. Know that she is only famous as you competitor. Since who does not know you and Rādhā in this world? *Tāra* is another name for Rādhā and Viśākhā.

### Text 7

***atha viṣādaḥ \| sa iṣṭānavāptito, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.56)—***  
***pītaṁ na vāg-amṛtam adya harer aśaṅkaṁ***  
***nyastaṁ mayādya vadane na dṛg-añcalaṁ ca \|***  
***ramye cirād avasare sakhi labdha-mātre***  
***hā durvidhir virurudhe jaratī cchalena \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Remorse, on not attaining desires, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: I did not get the chance to drink without fear the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's words, or to gaze at his face from the corner of my eyes. After a long time I finally obtained this delightful opportunity, and now unkind fate, in the form of old Jaṭilā has obstructed this.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Viṣāda* means remorse.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Viṣāda* means remorse or repentance. Longing to see Kṛṣṇa for the first time, Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā in a low voice while Jaṭilā is present*. Jaratī* means Jaṭilā, her mother-in-law.

### Text 8

***yathā va śrī-daśame (10.21.7)—***  
***akṣaṇvatāṁ phalam idaṁ na paraṁ vidāmaḥ***  
***sakhyaḥ paśūn anuviveśatayor vayasyaiḥ \|***  
***vaktraṁ vrajeśa-sutayor anuveṇu-juṣṭaṁ***  
***yair vā nipītam anurakta-kaṭākṣa-mokṣam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from Tenth Canto: O friend! We think there is no greater object of vision for those who have eyes that the face of Kṛṣṇa, which they relish, and which holds his flute and releases glances at those who are attracted to him, as these two sons of Nanda enter the forest after the cows, surrounded by their friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

We do not know of a greater fruit for those with eyes, who drink the form of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma entering the forest after the cows with their friends as Kṛṣṇa plays the flute in his mouths. We cannot see, though we have eyes. Thus we are useless.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having given an example of Rādhā experiencing remorse on one occasion, now an example of remorse experienced daily by all the *gopīs* is given. The women of Vraja speak among themselves. We do not know a greater fruit for those with eyes *(akṣaṇvatām*). What is that fruit? It is the face of Kṛṣṇa with the favorable flute as Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma enter the forest after forest after the cows, along with friends. This face, throwing glances at those with attraction, or the face which inspired those who are attracted to glance upon him, is drunk or tasted (*nipītam*) by the eyes. Though we have given up our traditions, shame and fear, how can we go there at this time? This is their remorse. O friends! Getting their permission, following after them, let us try to attain a small portion of his sweetness.

### Text 9

***prārabdha-kāryāsiddher, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (2.10)—***  
***gaṇayati guṇa-grāmaṁ bhrāmaṁ bhrāmād api nehate***  
***vahati ca paritoṣaṁ doṣaṁ vimuñcati dūrataḥ \|***  
***yuvatiṣu balat-tṛṣṇe kṛṣṇe viharati māṁ vinā***  
***punar api mano vāmaṁ kāmaṁ karoti karomi kim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Repentance for previous actions, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **My mind only considers Kṛṣṇa's virtues, and completely discounts even one of his faults. It moves even a great fault to a great distance and remains completely pleased with him. Even though he passionately enjoys with other young girls in my absence, still my obstinate mind desires him. What shall I do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

After she has quarreled with Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. Though my mind desires him, I have also checked my mind. My mind acts against me, being obstinate (*vāmam*). The unfavorable acts of the mind are listed. Though Kṛṣṇa enjoys with others in by absence, my mind considers a host of his good qualities, not like the voice, which can consider all qualities as one. It does not consider even one manifestation of his anger (*bhramam*) out of illusion. Though he has a host of bad qualities which are directly visible, the mind is fully satisfied with him. Moreover, if some great fault cannot be hidden, and very clearly manifests, the mind moves it far away, so that it cannot come close by. The fault is stated: he has a great thirst for other young women and enjoys with them. The suggestion of repentance is “I am sorry I got angry with him for anything.” And a further suggestion is “I should no longer take instructions from you on how to show anger.”

### Text 10

***vipattito, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.26)—***  
***nipītā na svairaṁ śruti-puṭikayā narma-bhaṇitir***  
***na dṛṣṭā niḥśaṅkaṁ sumukhi mukha-paṅkeruha-rucaḥ \|***  
***harer vakṣaḥ-pīṭhaṁ na kila ghanam āliṅgitam abhūd***  
***iti dhyāyaṁ dhyāyaṁ sphuṭati luṭhad antar mama manaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Repentance for misfortune, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O beautiful-faced friend! I was not able to fully drink Kṛṣṇa's joking words with the cups of my ears, I was not able to fearlessly gaze on his lotus face, and I was not able to embrace his chest firmly. Remembering this repeatedly in my** ***antaḥkaraṇa,*** **my mind falls down and splits open.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śrī laments when separated from Kṛṣṇa. Because of the *sthāyi-bhāva* of *anurāga*, she has continuous experience of Kṛṣṇa’s joking words. Meditating on this within the antaḥkaraṇa, her mind falls down and splits open.

### Text 11

***aparādhād, yathā—***  
***harer vacasi sūnṛte na nihitā śrutir vāmayā***  
***tathā dṛg api nārpitā praṇati-bhāji tasmin puraḥ \|***  
***hitoktir api dhik-kṛtā priya-sakhī muhus tena me***  
***jvalaty ahaha murmura-jvalana-jāla-ruddhaṁ manaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Repentance for offense: I did hear Kṛṣṇa's sweet, truthful words. I did not look at Kṛṣṇa when he bows down before me. His beneficial instructions I constantly rejected. Surrounded by a network of chaff fires, my heart burns.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Murmura-jvalana* is fire from husk. Like the word *dāvāgni*, such words have their special uses in literature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, after quarrelling and separating, laments*. Sūnṛte* means sweet and truthful. *Vāmayā* means “with cruelty.” *Hitoktiḥ* means words of good instruction. *Murmura-jvalana* is fire from husk.

### Text 12

***atha dainyam \| tad duḥkhena, yathā bilvamaṅgale—***  
***ayi murali mukunda-smera-vaktrāravinda-***  
***śvasan-rasa-rasajñe tvāṁ namaskṛtya yāce \|***  
***madhuram adhara-bimbaṁ prāptavatyāṁ bhavatyāṁ***  
***kathaya rahasi karṇe mad-daśāṁ nanda-sūnoḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Wretchedness (*****dainyam*****) out of suffering, by Bilvamaṅgala: O flute, who know the taste of the sweet breath blowing from Mukunda's smiling lotus mouth! I offer my obeisance unto you. When you touch the charming** ***bimba*** **fruit of Kṛṣṇa's lips, please whisper in his ear about my condition.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dainyam* means “offering flattering words with a mentality of being in a low condition.”  *Rasa* means sweet, and used the second time means taste.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Dainyam* means a mentality of being low. The devotee Bilvamaṅgala prays for his mind to be filled with the mood of the Vraja women. O flute, you are the knower of taste of the sweetness of the air blowing from his mouth. Please inform him of my condition: I am burning in the fire of longing to attain him.

### Text 13

***yathā vā, śrī-daśame (10.29.38)—***  
***tan naḥ prasīda vṛjinārdana te ‘ṅghrimūlaṁ***  
***prāptā visṛjya vasatīs tvadupāsanāśāḥ \|***
