***tvat-sundara-smita-nirīkṣaṇa-tīvra-kāma-***  
***taptātmanāṁ puruṣa-bhūṣaṇa dehi dāsyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the Tenth Canto: O vanquisher of all distress, please show us mercy. To approach your lotus feet we abandoned our families and homes, and we have no desire other than to serve you. Our hearts are burning with intense desires generated by your beautiful smiling glances. O jewel among men, please make us your maidservants.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example was given of a *sādhaka-bhakta* with *dainya.* Now an example of *siddha* devotees is given. The *gopīs* speak, suffering because of Kṛṣṇa’s indifferent words at the beginning of the *rāsa* dance.

### Text 14

***trāsena, yathā—***  
***api kara-dhutibhir mayāpanunno***  
***mukham ayam añcati cañcalo dvirephaḥ \|***  
***aghadamana mayi prasīda vande***  
***kuru karuṇām avarundhi duṣṭam enam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dainyam*** **out of fright: Even though I repeatedly brush him away with my hand, this restless bumble-bee still wanders around my face. O killer of Agha! I offer my respects to you. Please be kind and merciful to me. Stop this wicked bee.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While playing in the forest, Rādhā addresses Kṛṣṇa. Though I have driven it away *(apanunnah*) by moving my hand, he lingers around my face.

### Text 15

***aparādhena, yathā—***  
***āli tathyam aparāddham eva te***  
***duṣṭa-māna-phaṇi-daṣṭayā mayā \|***  
***piñcha-maulir adhunānunīyatāṁ***  
***māmakīnam anavekṣya dūṣaṇam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dainyam*** **out of offense: My friend! Bitten by the wicked serpent of pride, I have actually offended you. May Kṛṣṇa, wearing a peacock feather, overlooking my offense, be pleased with me!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

I have offended you, friend, by not listening to your words, because I was bitten by the snake of pride.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā who says “Why do you come to me now. You already rejected me by saying I was a fool and should go far from you, when I advised you to forgive his offense once when he begged you, since he is dearer than a million lives to you.” O friend! I have offended you (*te*). A person bitten by a snake speaks madly because of the poison, and should not be scolded by friends. “Kṛṣṇa has now given up interest in you.” May Kṛṣṇa, not seeing my offense, be pleased with me!

### Text 16

***atha glāniḥ, sā śrameṇa, yathā—***  
***vyātyukṣīm aghamathanena paṅkajākṣī***  
***kurvāṇā kim api sakhīṣu sasmitāsu \|***  
***kṣāmāṅgī maṇi-valayaṁ skhalat karāntāt***  
***kālindī-payasi rurodha nādya rādhā \|\|16\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Weakness (*****glani*****) because of exertion: After Rādhā engaged in a water-splashing battle with Kṛṣṇa while the** ***sakhīs*** **smiled, she became weak and could not prevent her jeweled bracelet from sliding off her wrists into the Yamunā's water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Glāniḥ* means weakness, having no strength. *Vyātyukṣīm* means splashing each other.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Glāni* means having no strength. Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Vyātyukṣiṁ* means splashing water on each other. Scolding her *sakhīs,* she personally engaged in battle. Seeing her unable to withstand his attack, with only her pride remaining, they smiled. The reason is she was weak (*kṣāmāṅgī*).

### Text 17

***ādhinā, yathā haṁsadūte (95)—***  
***pratīkārārambha-ślatha-matibhir udyat-pariṇater***  
***vimuktāyā vyakta-smara-kadana-bhājaḥ parijanaiḥ \|***  
***amuñcantī saṅgaṁ kuvalaya-dṛśaḥ kevalam asau***  
***balād adya prāṇān avati bhavāśā-sahacarī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Weakness because of mental pain, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **Though abandoning her friends who have found no remedies, since she is approaching the final state, tortured by memories of you, lotus-eyed Rādhā has one friend—her hope that you will return. That hope, not leaving her, has today strongly maintained her life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Her friend—the hope for your coming--gives life to the airs of lotus-eyed Rādhā, full of pain on remembering you (*vyakta-smara-kadana-bhājaḥ*), abandoning her friends have who can find no remedy for her. Why has this happened? Her special state is described. She has reaches the final state (*udyat pariṇateḥ*). The friend called hope does not give her up. Lalitā, scolding her friends, praises that hope. “You should not give up keeping your hope.” Today that hope strongly maintains her life. But tomorrow we do not know whether that hope will remain. Thus you should not delay, and go to her.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā, speaking to a swan, instructs Kṛṣṇa. Rādhā’s only friend, hope in you, maintains her life by force. It does not leave her body. This friend is stronger than the life airs. She experiences pain arising from her *prema* for you, which is clearly visible. That pain can be measured.  *Smara* or *kāma* also means *prema*. *premaivagopa-rāmāṇāṁ kāma ity agamat prathām*: the *kāma-rūpa-bhakti* of the *gopīs* has become famous simply as *prema.* (BRS 1.2.285) She has reached the final state (*udyat pariṇateḥ)*. People like us, understanding that she will not live, with no enthusiasm to find a remedy for her pain, have been given up by her. She simply lies on the ground. Hope however has made its own cure by its powers, though the sickness is incurable. It does not leave her (*amuñcatī saṅgam*). That dear friend hope keeps her alive. You cannot know if that hope will remain tomorrow. Therefore, you should quickly go there.

### Text 18

***ratena, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (12.12)—***  
***mārāṅke rati-keli-saṅkula-raṇārambhe tayā sāhasa-***  
***prāyaṁ kānta-jayāya kiṁcid upari prārambhi yat-sambhramāt \|***  
***niṣpandā jaghana-sthalī śithilitā dor-vallir utkampitaṁ***  
***vakṣo mīlitam akṣi pauruṣa-rasaḥ strīṇāṁ kutaḥ sidhyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Weakness because of amorous play, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **Rādhā, boldly desiring to defeat Kṛṣṇa in the passionate battle thick with amorous play, began to fight with zeal. However, after only a brief struggle, her hips began trembling, the creeper of her arms slackened, her chest quivered and her eyes closed. How can women achieve the bold powers of men?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *sakhīs* relish the confidential pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. *Māraḥ* means Cupid and beating.  *Mārāṅka* means the marks of Cupid or beating. At the commencement of the battle spread (*saṅkula*) with amorous play, Rādhā (*tayā*) started with a desire for victory. *Kiñcid upari* means confidential.

### Text 19

***atha śramaḥ \| so’dhvano, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (211)—***  
***dvitraiḥ keli-saroruhaṁ tri-caturair dhammilla-mallī-srajaṁ***  
***kaṇṭhān mauktika-mālikāṁ tad anu ca tyaktvā padaiḥ pañcamaiḥ \|***  
***kṛṣṇa prema-vighūrṇitāntaratayā dūrābhisārāturā***  
***tanvaṅgī nirupāyam adhvani paraṁ śreṇībharaṁ nindati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Exhaustion from walking, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O Kṛṣṇa! Her heart agitated with love, Rādhā has become exhausted from walking on the path to the far-away rendezvous. After taking two or three steps, she abandons her toy lotus flower. After three or our steps she abandons the garland of jasmine flowers decorating her hair. After five steps, she removes the pearl-necklace from her neck. After this she rebukes her hips for being so heavy, but she cannot abandon them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Śrama* means pain (caused by exhaustion). Possibly *kleśa* should be *kheda* in the commentary.1 A messenger speaks to Kṛṣṇa. O Kṛṣṇa! Rādhā becomes pained because she is unable to go the great distance. *Nirupāyam* means “without remedy.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sakhīs* relish the pastime of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa meeting. Taking two or three steps (*dvitraih*) she abandons her lotus. Having discarded all her ingredients for amorous play, she thinks “How can I move more quickly?” Reflecting, she sees her hips. “Ah! The hips are very heavy. But they cannot be given up. You are useless! Your creator is useless! If I did not have the weight of my hips I could quickly go and meet Kṛṣṇa. It is not my fault.”

### Text 20

***nṛtyād, yathā—***  
***śithila-gati-vilāsās tatra hallīśa-raṅge***  
***hari-bhuja-parighāgra-nyasta-hastāravindāḥ \|***  
***śrama-lulita-lalāṭa-śliṣṭa-līlālakāntāḥ***  
***pratipadam anavadyāḥ siṣvidur vedimadhyāḥ \|\|20\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Exhaustion from dancing: The impeccable thin-waisted** ***gopīs*** **moved slowly, resting their lotus hands on Kṛṣṇa's shoulders. Their curling locks of hair hanging slack, stuck on their foreheads, and they perspired at every step.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī.  *Hallīśa* means the *rāsa* dance. The tips of their playful locks of hair hanging slack on their foreheads were covered with perspiration. The women with slender waists (*vedikmadhāḥ*) perspired at every step.

### Text 21

***ratād, yathā—***  
***ahaha bhujayor dvandvaṁ mandaṁ babhūva viśākhike***  
***samajani ghana-svedaṁ cedaṁ yugaṁ tava gaṇḍayoḥ \|***  
***dhṛta-madhurima-sphūrti-mūrtis tathāpi varānane***  
***pramada-sudhayākrāntaṁ svāntaṁ mama praṇayaty asau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Exhaustion from amorous enjoyment: My dear beautiful-faced Viśākhā! Your arms move awkwardly and your cheeks are covered with perspiration. Your form with this charming appearance has filled my heart with the nectar of pleasure.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mandam* means awkward. *Praṇayati* means “makes.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Viśākhā after having enjoyed her. *Mandam* means awkward. *Amara-koṣa* says *manda* means foolish, awkward and unfortunate. Your appearance makes my heart become filled with the nectar of joy. Because of the repetition of meaning (*praṇayati*—cause affection, *pramada*—joy) the meaning of *praṇayati* should be corrected to mean simply “makes.”

### Text 22

***atha madaḥ \| sa madhupānajo, yathā—***  
***yā hriyā hari-puro mukha-mudrāṁ***  
***bhaṅktum adhyavasasau na kadāpi \|***  
***sa papāṭha caṭulaṁ madhu pītvā***  
***śārikeva paśupāla-kiśorī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rapture, from drinking liquor: Without desire to produce clear words in shyness in front of Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā drank the liquor and spoke quivering words like a** ***śārika*** **bird.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mada* means joy which gives rise to loss of discrimination. She did not take care to pronounce her words properly.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse describes losing discrimination by intoxication with liquor. Kundavallī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. *Nādhyavasasau* means “did not desire.”  *Mada* arising from extreme transformations of love generally requires great effort. Therefore it is not illustrated here.

### Text 23

***atha garvaḥ \| sa saubhāgyena, yathā—***  
***muñcan mitra-kadamba-saṅgam abhajann apy utsukāḥ preyasīr***  
***eṣa dvāri haris tvad-ānana-taṭī-nyastekṣaṇas tiṣṭhati \|***  
***yūthibhir makarākṛtiḥ smita-mukhī tvaṁ kurvatī kuṇḍalaṁ***  
***gaṇḍodyat-pulakā dṛśo’pi na kila kṣīve kṣipasy añcalam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pride, or disregard, at ones good fortune: Leaving his cowherd friends and ignoring many** ***gopīs,*** **Kṛṣṇa stands at the door, gazing at your face with longing. O Rādhā! Making** ***makara*** **earrings out of** ***yūthi*** **flowers, while goose bumps rise on your cheeks, you do not even glance at him with the corner of your eye, though you smile.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Garva* means disregarding others.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Garva* means disregarding others. Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā sitting in a bower. She does not even desire (*abhajan)* her friends. You make *makara* earrings for Kṛṣṇa, but you do not even glance at him. You can suppress your joyful smile however. You goose bumps indicate your eagerness. Both these symptoms indicate affected indifference (*bibboka*).

### Text 24

***rūpeṇa, yathā—***  
***candrāvalī-vadana-candra-marīci-puñjaṁ***  
***kaḥ stotum apy atipaṭu kṣamate kṣamāyām \|***  
***yenādya piñcha-mukuṭo’pi niketa-vāṭī-***  
***paryanta-kānana-kuṭira-caraḥ kṛto’yam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Disregard, from beauty: On this earth what skilful person is able to praise the profuse moonlight of Candrāvalī's face, for she makes Kṛṣṇa comes to this forest cottage near her house?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā with excitement speaks to Lalitā who was gazing at Candrāvalī’s beauty in an assembly. By her profuse beauty (*yena)* she makes Kṛṣṇa come to her bower.

### Text 25

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (7.27)—***  
***sahacari vṛṣabhānujayā prādurbhāve vara-tviṣopagate \|***  
***candrāvalī-śatāny api bhavanti nirdhūta-kāntīni \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **My friend! When brilliance of the sun in Jyeṣṭha month appears, a hundred moons lose their beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example of Rādhā is given to show pride in beauty. Lalitā, hearing Padmā’s words, speaks with pride. When the appearance takes place with the great brilliance of the sun in Jyeṣṭha month (*vṛṣabhānujayā*), the light of hundred moons loses its beauty. The other meaning is by the great beauty of Rādhā, a hundred Candrāvalī’s lose their beauty.

### Text 26

***guṇena, yathā—***  
***ramayantu tāvad amalair***  
***dhvanibhir gopī-kapotikā kṛṣṇam \|***  
***iha lalitā-kala-kaṇṭhī***  
***kalaṁ na yāvat prapañcayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Disregard because of qualities: The singing of the** ***gopīs*****, who are like doves, pleases Kṛṣṇa only so long as Lalitā, the cuckoo, does not sing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Lalitā speaks, praising the singing of Lalitā in a gathering of the opposing party. Lalitā is like the cuckoo (*kala-kaṇṭhī*) who sings sweeter than all other birds.

### Text 27

***sarvottamāśrayeṇa, yathā śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe (5.30.51)***  
***jānāmi te patiṁ śatruṁ jānāmi tridaśeśvaram \|***  
***pārijātaṁ tathāpy enaṁ mānuṣī hārayāmi te \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Disregard, by taking shelter of the Lord, from** ***Viṣṇu Purāṇa:*** **I know your husband is Indra, king of the** ***devatās.*** **Still, even though I am only a human girl, I shall now take this** ***pārijāta*** **tree from you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Satyabhāmā speaks.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Satyabhāmā instructs Śacī, Indra’s wife.

### Text 28

***iṣṭa-lābhena, yathā—***  
***namrā na bhavatu vaṁśī mukunda-vaktrendu-mādhurī-rasikā \|***  
***tvaṁ durlabha-tad-gandhā laguḍi vṛthā stabdhatāṁ vahasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Disregard, on attaining the desired goal: Let the flute not bow humbly since it is expert at tasting the sweetness of the moon of Mukunda's mouth. O stick! You uselessly remain straight, though you can never experience even the fragrance of his mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though the statement is metaphorical, pride, as if their own, appears in the hearts of the listeners.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Privately, in an assembly of her *sakhī,* Rādhā scolds Kṛṣṇa’s stick which she has stolen from him. She praises the pride of the flute and criticizes the pride of the stick.

### Text 29

***yathā vā śrī-daśame (10.83.29)—***  
***unnīya vaktram uru-kuntala-kuṇḍala-tviḍ-***  
***gaṇḍa-sthalaṁ śiśira-hāsa-kaṭākṣa-mokṣaiḥ \|***  
***rājño nirīkṣya paritaḥ śanakair murārer***  
***aṁse ‘nurakta-hṛdayā nidadhe sva-mālām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the Tenth Canto: I lifted my face, which was encircled by my abundant locks and effulgent from the glow of my earrings reflected from my cheeks. Smiling coolly, I glanced about. Then, looking around at all the kings, I slowly placed the necklace on the shoulder of Murāri, who had captured my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Lakṣmaṇā relates how she came to the *svayamvara* ceremony. She lifted her face in order to see Kṛṣṇa who was the only person worthy of choosing and placed the garland she had made on the shoulders of Kṛṣṇa, while looking slowly at the kings with disregard. Looking at them, she then gave up looking. Not only did she place the garland on Kṛṣṇa but did so with a shower of glances smiling with joy, like moonlight. The reason is given. Her heart was attracted to the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

All the *vyabhicāri-bhāvas* appear in the queens of Dvārakā as well. That is illustrated in this verse. At Kurukṣetra, Lakṣmaṇā relates the story of her *svayaṁvara* to Draupadī. She glanced at the kings situated all around. Where is Kṛṣṇa who I heard had all wonderful qualities and beauty? She glanced around to find him. Raising her face encircled her locks, she offered a garland indicating her choice to his shoulders while glancing with smiles, cool as the moonlight. This indicates her pride.

### Text 30

***atha śaṅkā, sā cauryeṇa, yathā—***  
***harantī nidrāṇe madhubhidi karāt keli-muralīṁ***  
***latotsaṅge līnā ghana-tamasi rādhā cakitadhīḥ \|***  
***niśi dhvānte śānte śarada-amala-candra-dyuti-muṣām***  
***asau nirmātāraṁ sva-vadana-rucāṁ nindati vidhim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Apprehension, from theft: Desiring to steal the flute from Kṛṣṇa's hand while he was sleeping, Rādhā, merged in the dense darkness of the network of creepers became frightened when she noticed that the darkness of night had dissipated. She cursed the creator of her effulgence of her face which eclipsed the light of the spotless autumn moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Śaṅkā* means anticipation of misfortune. Fear is the effect.

*bhayaṁ cittāticāñcalyaṁ mantu-ghorekṣaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*ātma-gopana-hṛcchoṣa-vidrava-bhramaṇādikṛt \|\|*

**When the heart manifests extreme unsteadiness at seeing offense or fearsome creatures, or other such things, it is called** ***bhaya*** **or fear. BRS 2.5.67**

Rādhā hid in the dense creepers where it was very dark. When the darkness was dissipated by the effulgence of her face, she criticized the creator of effulgence which defeated that of the moon. This follows after the first three lines.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Śaṅkā* means anticipation of misfortune. The *sakhīs* mutually relish the pastime of Rādhā stealing Kṛṣṇa’s flute. “Stealing his flute while he was sleeping” means “desiring to steal the flute while he was sleeping.” When the darkness dissipated, she became frightened (*cakita-dhīḥ*). “Oh! Who has the darkness suddenly disappeared?” Her heart began to tremble in fear. Then on considering the matter, she understood that the cause of destruction of darkness was the rays from her face. She then criticized the creator for making the effulgence of her face. “If the creator had not made my face effulgent like this, I could have stolen the flute today. He has created an obstacle to my desire. To hell with the creator!”

### Text 31

***aparādhād, yathā lalita-mādhave (2.4)—***  
***uttāmyantī viramati tamastoma-sampat-prapañce***  
***nyañcan-mūrdhā sarabhasam asau srasta-veṇīvṛtāṁsā \|***  
***manda-spandaṁ diśi diśi dṛśor dvandvam alpaṁ kṣipantī***  
***kuñjād goṣṭhaṁ viśati cakitā vaktram āvṛtya pālī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Apprehension from offense: When the dense darkness had lifted, in great distress head bent down, she quickly undid her braids. Throwing small glances in all directions with eyes closed from fatigue, in great fear, Pālī covered her face and left the bower for the village.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Oh! Morning has come! How will I enter the village?” In this manner she was distressed *(uttāmyantī*). She bent her head. “From a distance no one will see or recognize me.” *Sarabahsam* means quickly. Because she was up all night her eyes closed with tiredness. She covered her face. “If persons approach close, they should not recognize me.”

### Text 32

***śaṅkā tu pravara-strīṇāṁ bhīrutvād bhaya-kṛd bhavet \|\|32\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because timidity is natural to the best of women, apprehension produces fear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Why is the last verse an example of *śaṅkā*? *Śaṅkā* does not act against fear. Rather, in the best of women it produces fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The cause of apprehension in the previous example was offense—that she was trespassing *dharma*. The *sthāyi-bhāva* of *bhāyānaka-rasa* is *bhaya*. Its cause is offense.

*bhayaṁ cittāticāñcalyaṁ mantu-ghorekṣaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*ātma-gopana-hṛcchoṣa-vidrava-bhramaṇādikṛt \|\|*

**When the heart manifests extreme unsteadiness at seeing offense or fearsome creatures, or other such things, it is called** ***bhaya*** **or fear. BRS 2.5.67**

When *bhaya* becomes condensed it becomes the *sthāyī-bhāva*. When it is weaker, it is the *vyabhicāri-bhava* called *śaṅkā.* That is the difference. Because the best of women are by nature timid, *śaṅkā* becomes the cause of fear. When fear is less it is called *śaṅkā.* When the same emotion becomes strong, it becomes the *sthāyi-bhāva* called *bhaya*, of *bhayānaka-rasa.*

### Text 33

***para-krauryād, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (5.23)—***  
***vyaktiṁ gate mama rahasya-vinoda-vṛtte***  
***ruṣṭo laghiṣṭha-hṛdayas tarasābhimanyuḥ \|***  
***rādhāṁ nirudhya sadane vinigūhante vā***  
***hā hanta lambhayati vā yadu-rājadhānīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Apprehension about others’ cruelty, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Learning of my confidential pastimes with her, this fool Abhimanyu may force Rādhā to stay at home, or else he may take her to Mathurā, the capitol of the Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

How can he take away our enjoyment? That is the apprehension.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Subala wears Rādhā’s dress, and Jaṭilā thinks that he is Rādhā. Kṛṣṇa, unaware of this, speaks with remorse.

### Text 34

***atha trāsaḥ, sa taḍitā, yathā—***  
***sphūrjite nabhasi bhīrur udyatāṁ***  
***vidyutāṁ dyutim avekṣya kampitā \|***  
***sā harer urasi cañcalekṣaṇā***  
***cañcaleva jalade nyalīyata \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Terror, from lightning: When lightning appeared in the rumbling sky, seeing the flash, Rādhā began to tremble. With restless eyes she flung herself on Kṛṣṇa’s chest, just as a lightning flash enters a dark rain cloud.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*trāsaḥ kṣobho hṛdi taḍid-ghora-sattvogra-nisvanaiḥ \|*

**The disturbance which arises in the heart from lightning, fearful creatures or a loud sound is called** ***trāsa*** **(terror). BRS 2.4.54**

*gātrotkampī manaḥ-kampaḥ sahasā trāsa ucyate \|*  
*pūrvāpara-vicārotthaṁ bhayaṁ trāsāt pṛthag bhavet \|\|*

**Disturbance of the heart which suddenly produces shaking of the limbs is called** ***trāsa.*** **This is different from fear. Fear arises after considering previous and subsequent events. BRS 2.4.58**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Trāsa* is sudden trembling of the mind from lightning or other causes.  *Śaṅkā* involves consideration of past and future. When *śaṅkā* becomes strong it is fear. That is the difference. Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to Kundavallī. When lightning appeared (*udyatām*) in the thundering (*sphūrjite*) sky, seeing the flash, Rādhā trembled. Rādhā is compared to the fickle lightning, which merges with the cloud.

### Text 35

***ghora-sattvena, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (5.44)—***  
***karṇottaṁsita-rakta-paṅkaja-juṣo bhṛṅgīpater jhaṅkriyā***  
***bhrāntenādya dṛgañcalena dadhatī bhṛṅgāvalī-vibhramam \|***  
***trāsāndolita-dor-latānta-vilasac-cūḍā-jhaṇat-kāriṇī***  
***rādhe vyākulatāṁ gatāpi bhavati modaṁ mamādhyasyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Terror, from fierce animals, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Because of the buzzing bee attracted to your red lotus ornament, your wandering side glances produce the beauty of a swarm of bees with, and your bracelets jingle because of swinging your creeper-like arms in fear. O Rādhā! Your agitation gives me bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks*. Cūḍā* means bracelet. *Adhyasyati* means offers. *Mama* means “to me” but is in the genitive case to express a general state of existence.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Dṛg-añcalena* is in the singular to express a type. She produces the beauty of a swarm of bees with her many glances from the side of her eyes. The creepers of her arms swing about because of *trāsa.* She makes jingling noise when her bracelets moving by the movement of her arms. *Viśva-koṣa* says *cūḍā* means a flame, topknot, a turret or bracelet. The word *bādhu* (arm) indicates the whole arm up to the hand as in a phrase like *ājānu-bāhu* (arms reaching the knee). *Adhyasyati* means offer. Your difficulties give me pleasure. Genitive case of *mama* is used to express “my pleasure.” Your difficulties are my pleasure.

### Text 36

***ugra-nisvanena, yathā—***  
***tvam asi mama sakheti kiṁvadantī***  
***mudira cirād bhavatā vyadhāyi tathyā \|***  
***mad-urasi rasitair nirasya mānaṁ***  
***yad udita-vepathur arpitādya rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Terror from thunder: O cloud! It is rumored that you are my friend. That has come true after a long time, since today Rādhā, trembling in fear and giving up pride because of your rumbling, has placed herself on my chest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. The rumor is this:

*prema-pravṛddha uditaḥ kusumāvalībhiḥ*  
*sakhyur vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapatram*

**The cloud in the sky has expanded himself out of love. He is rising high and constructing out of his own body, with its multitude of flower-like droplets of water, an umbrella for the sake of his friend. SB 10.21.16**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. The rumour is this:

*prema-pravṛddha uditaḥ kusumāvalībhiḥ*  
*sakhyur vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapatram*

**The cloud in the sky has expanded himself out of love. He is rising high and constructing out of his own body, with its multitude of flower-like droplets of water, an umbrella for the sake of his friend. SB 10.21.16**

*Kiṁ-vadantī* means a rumour according to *Amara-koṣa.* O cloud (*mudira)! Tathyā* means truth and *rasitaiḥ* means “by the sound of thunder.”

### Text 37

***atha āvegaḥ, sa priya-darśanajo, yathā lalita-mādhave (2.11)—***  
***sahacari nirātaṅkaḥ ko’yaṁ yuvā mudira-dyutir***  
***vraja-bhuvi kutaḥ prāpto mādyan-mataṅgaja-vibhramaḥ \|***  
***ahaha caṭulair utsarpadbhir dṛga-aṅcala-taskarair***  
***mama dhṛtir-dhanaṁ cetaḥ-koṣād viluṇṭhayatīha yaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitation, by seeing the loved, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O friend! Who is this fearless young man with the complexion of a cloud? From where has he come to Vraja, wandering around like a maddened elephant? Alas, by the thieves of his restless glances he is plundering from the vault of my heart the treasure of my self-control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Āvega* means agitation of the heart. Seeing him at every moment becoming newer, Rādhā speaks.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Āvega* means agitation of the heart, or not knowing what to do. Having the *sthāyi-bhāva* of *anurāga*, Rādhā wonders about Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 38

***yathā vā tatraiva (6.40)—***  
***upataru lalitāṁ tāṁ pratyabhikṣāya sadyaḥ***  
***prakṛti-madhura-rūpāṁ vīkṣya rādhākṛtiṁ ca \|***  
***maṇim api paricinvan śaṅkha-cūḍāvataṁsaṁ***  
***muhur aham udghūrṇaṁ bhūriṇā sambhrameṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the same work: Now I understand that this girl Jāmbavatī under the tree is actually Lalitā, that this beautiful statue is Rādhā, and that this Syamantaka jewel is the crest-jewel of Saṅkhacūḍa. These facts have made me become dizzy with extreme confusion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is also from *Lalita-mādhava.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous example, not knowing what to do was not clearly depicted. Thus another example is given from *Lalita-mādhava*. There it is related that Rādhā, along with Viśākhā immersed herself in Khelā-tiṛtha out of madness of separation when Kṛṣṇa went to Mathurā. She then attained the sun planet, and offered the Śaṅkhacūḍa gem to the sun god. Lalitā jumped from the peak of Govardhana in the madness of separation, but was caught by the hands of Jāmbavān who took her to his city and became known as his daughter Jāmbavatī. She made statues of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa out of gold and sapphire and spent her time looking at those forms. The sun god gave Rādhā to his devotee Satrājit, giving her the name Satyabhāmā, and as well gave him the Śaṅkacūḍa’s jewel which was called Syamantaka. When defamed by Satrajit, Kṛṣṇa went to the city of Jāmbavān. Recognizing his master after a fight, Jāmbavān sat Kṛṣṇa down on a jeweled seat and entered his city to get the jewel. At that moment, hearing the news from an old woman, Lalitā gave the statues of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa to the old woman and stood near a tree to see Kṛṣṇa. After seeing Lalitā and recognizing her, he took her to Dvārakā and related this to Madhumaṅgala. H recognizes her near the tree (*upataru*) as Lalitā and sees the statue (*ākṛtim*) of Rādhā

### Text 39

***priya-śravaṇajo, yathā lalita-mādhave (1.25)—***  
***dhanye kajjala-mukta-vāma-nayanā padme padoḍhāṅgadā***  
***sāraṅgi dhvanad-eka-nūpura-dharā pāli skhalan-mekhalā \|***  
***gaṇḍodyat-tilakā lavaṅgi kamale netrārpitālaktakā***  
***mādhāvottaralaṁ tvam atra muralī dūre kalaṁ kūjati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitation arising from hearing about the beloved, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O Dhanyā! The mascara has fallen from your left eye. O Padmā!, you are wearing your bracelet on your ankle. O Sāraṅgī! You decorated one foot with tinkling ankle-bells. O Pālī! You belt is falling off. O Lavaṅgī! You have decorated your cheeks with** ***tilaka*** **intended for your forehead. O Kamalā! You decorated you eyes with the red lac meant for your feet. Please do not run while trembling. The flute is sounding in a far off place.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Do not run off. This is addressed to each *gopī.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundavallī speaks. Do not run off! This is addressed to each *gopī.*

### Text 40

***apriya-darśanajo, yathā tatraiva (3.18)—***  
***kṣaṇaṁ vikrośantī viluṭhati śatāṅgasya purataḥ***  
***kṣaṇaṁ bāṣpa-grastāṁ kirati kila dṛṣṭiṁ hari-mukhe \|***  
***kṣaṇaṁ rāmasyāgre patati daśanottambhita-tṛṇā***  
***na rādheyaṁ kaṁ vā kṣipati karuṇāmbhodhi-kuhare \|\|40\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitation on not seeing the beloved, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **One moment shouting, she rolls about on the ground before the chariot. The next moment she gazes with tear-filled eyes upon his face. The next moment, she places a blade of grass between her teeth and falls before Balarāma. Will this condition of Rādhā not throw everyone into the ocean of pity?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā described the actions of Rādhā when she sees Kṛṣṇa mounting the chariot to depart for Mathurā. *Śatāṅgasya* means “of the chariot.”

### Text 41

***apriya-śravaṇajo, yathā—***  
***vraja-narapater eṣa kṣattā karoti girā prage***  
***nagara-gataye ghoraṁ ghoṣe ghanāṁ sakhi ghoṣaṇām \|***  
***śravaṇa-padavīm ārohantyā yayā kuliśograyā***  
***racitam acirād ābhīrīṇāṁ kulaṁ muhur ākulam \|\|\|***  
***—evam anye’py ūhyāḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitation caused by hearing unwelcome news: O friend! When gatekeeper, on instructions of Nanda, loudly announced the terrible news the village that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma would leave for Mathurā city at dawn, those words, sharper than a thunderbolt, entered the ears of the** ***gopīs*** **and caused continuous pain immediately.**

**Other similar examples may be given.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundavallī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. The gate keeper, on instructions (*girā)* of Nanda, announced in a frightening way (*ghoram*) in a loud voice that Kṛṣṇa would go to Mathurā (*nagara-gataye).*

### Text 42

***atha unmādaḥ, sa prauḍhānandād, yathā—***  
***prasīda madirākṣi māṁ sakhi milantam āliṅgituṁ***  
***nirundhi mudira-dyutiṁ nava-yuvānam enaṁ puraḥ \|***  
***iti bhramarikām api priya-sakhī-bhramād yācate***  
***samīkṣya harim unmada-pramada-viklavā vallavī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Madness out of deep bliss: When this** ***gopī*** **saw Kṛṣṇa, she became mad with bliss. Addressing a bumble-bee as a dear friend she said, “My dear beautiful-eyed friend! Please be kind and stop this young boy, the color of a cloud, who has come here to embrace me.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Unmāda* means madness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Unmāda* means madness. Vṛndā speaks. *Bhramarikām* is a bee.

### Text 43

***virahād, yathā—***  
***kvāpy āndolita-kuntalā viluṭhati kvāpy āṅgulī-bhaṅgatas-***  
***tvaṅgad-bhrūr daśanair vidaśya daśanān kaṁsaṁ śapaty uddhūrā \|***  
***kutrāpy adya tamālam uttarala-dhīr ālokya dhāvaty alaṁ***  
***rādhā tvad-viraha-jvareṇa pṛthunā dūnā yadūnāṁ pate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Madness out of separation: Her disheveled hair swinging to and fro, Rādhā sometimes rolls about on the ground, cracking her finger-joints, and, moving her eyebrows, gnashes her teeth. Sometimes she curses Kaṁsa without restraint. Sometimes she becomes very agitated by seeing a** ***tamāla*** **tree, and swiftly runs toward it. O king of the Yadus! In this way Rādhā is burning in a great fire of separation from you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tvaṅgad-bhrūḥ* means “with two moving eyebrows.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava describes to Kṛṣṇa the scene on returning from Vraja. She cracks her fingers and moves her eyebrows. *Tvañc* means to move. She curses Kaṁsa. “O Kaṁsa! May your desire for afterlife be useless as chaff, because you have given me such sorrow.” *Dūnā* means burning. O lord of the Yadus! Now you protect the Yadus. What is the use of your former lover?

### Text 44

***atha apasmāraḥ, yathā—***  
***aṅga-kṣepa-vidhāyibhir niviḍatottuṅga-pralāpair alaṁ***  
***gāḍhodvartita-tāra-locana-puṭaiḥ phena-cchaṭodgāribhiḥ \|***  
***kṛṣṇa tvad-virahotthitair mama sakhīm antarvikārormibhir***  
***grastāṁ prekṣya vitarkayanti guravaḥ sampraty apasmāriṇīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Apasmāra:*** **O Kṛṣṇa! Her heart transformed by waves of separation from you, my friend flails her limbs, shouts loudly, rolls the pupils of her eyes, and foams at the mouth. Observing all this, her elders think she has become an epileptic.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Apasmara* means disturbance of mind caused by disturbed *dhātus*, caused by grief. Her elders think she has become epileptic (*apasmāriṇīm*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Apasmara* means disturbance of mind caused by disturbed *dhātus*, caused by grief. Lalitā instructs Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā through some agent. Seeing my friend afflicted by inner waves of transformation caused by separation from you, the elders, her mother-in-law and father-in-law, think she has epilepsy.

### Text 45

***atha vyādhiḥ, sa yathā rasa-sudhākare (2.52)—***  
***śayyā puṣpa-mayī parāga-mayatām aṅgārpaṇād aśnute***  
***tāmyanty antika-tāla-vṛnta-nalinī-patrāṇi gātroṣmaṇā \|***  
***nyastaṁ ca stana-maṇḍale malayajaṁ śīrṇāntaraṁ lakṣyate***  
***kvāthād āśu bhavanti phenila-mukhā bhūṣā-mṛṇālāṅkurāḥ \|\|45\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sickness, from** ***Rasa-sudhākara:*** **Her bed made of flowers turns to powder on contact with her limbs. The lotus leaf fans all wither from the heat of her body. Sandalwood applied to her breasts dries up and peals off. When water lily stems are placed on her body to cool it, they cook and produce foam at the end of their stems.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vyādhi* means transformations of the body similar to fever etc.  *Parāga* means powder.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vyādhi* means transformations of the body similar to fever etc. A *sakhī* of Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa about Rādhā’s feelings of separation. All the treatments applied to her limbs have reverse effects. By the heat of her body, the petals dry up and become powder. Both the flowers and her limbs have *parāga* (pollen) however, since they have fragrance. *Tala-vṛtna* means a fan. *Malayajam* means sandalwood. When sandalwood paste is applied it falls apart, and becomes dry power in a moment. The word *ca* means certainly and indicates that as soon as the paste is applied, it dries up. Ornaments such as bracelets made of water lily stems, to cool the heat of the body, are applied. By contact with the heat of her body, they cook and produce foam at the ends of the stems.

### Text 46

***atha mohaḥ, sa harṣād, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.6)—***  
***daronmīlan nīlotpala-dala-rucas tasya niviḍād***  
***virūḍhānāṁ sadyaḥ kara-sarasija-sparśa-kutukāt \|***  
***vahantī kṣobhāṇāṁ nivaham iha nājñāsiṣam idaṁ***  
***kva vāhaṁ kā vāhaṁ cakara kim ahaṁ vā sakhi tadā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Derangement, from joy, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Enflamed by desire from the touch of the lotus hand of Kṛṣṇa, with complexion of a slightly blossomed blue lotus petal, immediately I develop a host of contrary disturbances. O friend! I do not know where I am, who I am, or what I have done.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Moha* means degeneration of the mind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mohan means fainting. Rādhā speaks to Lalitā and Viśākhā who question her. By the eagerness generated by touch of the lotus hand of the dark youth, she immediately displays a host of contrary disturbances. I cannot discern where I am. Am I in the yard, on the road or on the flower bed? Who am I? Am I the daughter-in-law of Jaṭilā or am I to be enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa at all times? What did I do? Did I enjoy with Kṛṣṇa as *vāmya* or *dakṣiṇya* or did I play the role of a male? Did I sleep or babble in madness?

### Text 47

***yathā va śrī-daśame (10.21.12)—***  
***kṛṣṇaṁ nirīkṣya vanitotsava-rūpa-śīlaṁ***  
***śrutvā ca tat-kvaṇita-veṇu-vicitra-gītam \|***  
***devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā***  
***bhraśyat prasūna-kavarā mumuhur vinīvy \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the Tenth Canto: Kṛṣṇa’s beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of him and hear his resonant flute-song, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their belts loosen.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Examples of *moha* in *samarthya-rati* were given. Now an example of *moha* in ordinary *abhāsa* form is given. The *gopīs* speak among themselves. Their self-control *(sārā*) becomes completely thrown (*nunna*) from their hearts by Cupid.

### Text 48

***viśleṣād, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (117)—***  
***sā palyaṅke kiśalaya-dalaiḥ kalpite tatra suptā***  
***guptā nīra-stavakita-dṛśāṁ cakravālaiḥ sakhīnām \|***  
***draṣṭavyā te kraśima-kalitā kaṇṭhanālopa-kaṇṭha-***  
***spandenāntar-vapur anumita-prāṇa-saṅgā varāṅgī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Moha*** **from separation, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **Sleeping on a bed of blossoming sprouts, and protected by a circle of friends with tears in their eyes, beautiful Rādhā is now emaciated. The quivering in her throat implies that there is still life in her body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Uddhava, who has asked how he can recognize Rādhā among all the women of Vraja? She is protected (*guptā*) by a group of *sakhīs* eyes having clusters of tears. (*nīla-stavakita-dṛśām*). She is pervaded (*kalitā)* with thinness (*kraśima*). By the slight movement near her throat, it can be inferred that she has life in her body.

### Text 49-50

***viṣādād, yathā śrī-daśame (10.35.16-17)–***  
***nija-padābja-dalair dhvaja-vajra-***  
***nīrajāṅkuśa-vicitra-lalāmaiḥ \|***  
***vraja-bhuvaḥ śamayan khura-todaṁ***  
***varṣma-dhurya-gatir īḍita-veṇuḥ \|\|49\|****\|*  
***vrajati tena vayaṁ sa-vilāsa-***  
***vīkṣaṇārpita-manobhava-vegāḥ \|***  
***kuja-gatiṁ gamitā na vidāmaḥ***  
***kaśmalena kavaraṁ vasanaṁ vā \|\|50\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Moha*** **caused by disappointment, from the Tenth Canto: As Kṛṣṇa strolls through Vraja with his lotus-petal-like feet, marking the ground with the distinctive emblems of flag, thunderbolt, lotus and elephant goad, he relieves the distress the ground feels from the cows’ hooves. As he plays his renowned flute, his body moves with the grace of an elephant. Thus we** ***gopīs,*** **who become agitated by Cupid when Kṛṣṇa playfully glances at us, stand as still as trees, unaware that our hair and garments are slackening.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Lalāmam* means mark. The earth with its grass gets relief from the marks made by the cows’ hooves by the touch of his lotus petal feet, which produces new sprouts. He walks like an elephant (*varṣma-dhurya-gatiḥ*). Playing the flute is his special quality. *Kuja* means trees.  *Kaśmalena* means “by *moha*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some *gopīs* who relish the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and his friends returning with the cows in the afternoon speak among themselves in great *moha*, giving up all family *dharma,* shyness and self-control, and regretting that they cannot associate with Kṛṣṇa like Subala and others. *Lalāmam* means mark. He immediately relieves the suffering of the earth and grass caused by the marks of the cows’ hooves, by the touch of his lotus petal feet after the cows have passed, by making new leaves and sprouts appear. He has the walk of an elephant and plays the flute as he walks. Because of that, we have attained the condition of trees (*kuja*) because of *moha.* The *sthāyi-bhāva* does not completely disappear since *moha* is a *sañcāri-bhāva.* The *sañcāri-bhāva* is only an assistant to the *sthāyi-bhāva:*

*asyānyatrātma-paryante syāt sarvatraiva mūḍhatā \|*  
*kṛṣṇa-sphūrti-viśeṣas tu na kadāpy atra līyate \|\|*

**When the devotees develop** ***mohā*** **they lose awareness of objects including their own bodies, but awareness of Kṛṣṇa never disappears. BRS 2.4.98**

### Text 51

***atha mṛtiḥ—***  
***mṛter adhyavasāyo’tra varṇyaḥ sākṣād iyaṁ na hi \|\|51\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mṛti*** **means an effort to die, but not death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mṛt*i means giving up life. *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇi* explains the verse

*antar-gṛha-gatāḥ kāścid gopyo ’labdha-vinirgamāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ tad-bhāvanā-yuktā dadhyur mīlita-locanāḥ*

**Some of the** ***gopīs*****, however, could not manage to get out of their houses, and instead they remained home with eyes closed, meditating upon Him in pure love. SB 10.29.9**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mṛti* means a zeal for death. It cannot be said to be actual death, since it is impossible that *nitya-siddha gopīs* of Kṛṣṇa with *samartha, samañjasa* or *sādhāraṇa sthāyi-bhāvas* to die. The explanation of SB 10.29.9 and SB 11.31.20 (which describes the queens of Dvārakā entering fire) is found in *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.* Though death is possible for some who are approximately *sādhakas* it is not described because it is inauspicious.

### Text 52

***yathā uddhava-sandeśe (69)—***  
***yāvad vyaktiṁ na kila bhajate gāndineyānubandhas***  
***tāvan natvā sumukhi bhavatīṁ kiṁcid abhyarthayiṣye \|***  
***puṣpair yasyā muhur akaravaṁ karṇa-pūrān murāreḥ***  
***seyaṁ phullā gṛha-parisare mālatī pālanīyā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of** ***mṛti*** **from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O My beautiful-faced friend! As long as Akrūra’s intentions are not clear, I bow down before you and beg you to take care of that jasmine creeper near my house from whose flowers I always used to make ear ornaments for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. *Gāndineyaḥ* is Akrūra. Since I will die on learning that it is true that Kṛṣṇa is going to Mathurā, words will not be available at that time. Therefore I speak now.

### Text 53

***atha ālasyam—***  
***sākṣād aṅgaṁ na cālasyaṁ bhaṅgyā tena nibadhyate \|\|53\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ālasya*** **is not a direct** ***vyabhicāri-bhava*** **but is considered in an indirect way.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ālasya means showing incapacity though one is capable. It is not possible to occur in the gopīs. Rādhā says “I cannot walk any further. Please carry me wherever you want to go.” (SB 1030.37) But this is false ālasya. From such a description, it is therefore employed to nourish the sthāyi-bhāva.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Ālasya* means to have no desire to act for a certain object though one has capacity. If there is *ālasya* towards an object of attachment, that attachment will disappear. This is impossible to occur for persons with *prema,* in relation to Kṛṣṇa or related objects. However it is present in some old people, and nourishes their *sthāyi-bhāva*.

### Text 54

***yathā—***  
***niravadhi dadhi-pūrṇāṁ gargarīṁ loḍayitvā***  
***sakhi kṛta-tanu-bhaṅgaṁ kurvatī bhūri jṛmbhām \|***  
***bhuvam anupatitā te patyur āste savitrī***  
***viracaya tad-aśaṅkaṁ tvaṁ harer mūrdhni cūḍām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of lethargy: My friend! Your mother-in-law was churning a pot filled with yogurt constantly. Then stretching her body and yawning, she has fallen on the ground. Do not have fear. Continue to tie Kṛṣṇa’s hair.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī, who has suddenly come, comforts Rādhā who was enjoying with Kṛṣṇa and who became frightened on hearing from the mouth of *śārika* bird instructed by Padmā that Jaṭilā was coming

### Text 55

***atha jāḍyaṁ, tad-iṣṭa-śrutyā, yathā—***  
***gopure ruvati kṛṣṇa-nūpure***  
***niṣkramāya dhṛta-sambhramāpy asau \|***  
***kīliteva parimīlitekṣaṇā***  
***sīdati sma sadane manoramā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Absence of awareness, from hearing something pleasant: Hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa's ankle-bells at the gate of the village, she was eager to go outside, but the attractive** ***gopī*** **remained sitting in the house with closed eyes like a pole.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Jādya* means not being aware.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Jāḍya* means not being aware. Kundavallī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. *Gopure* is the gate to the town.

### Text 56

***aniṣṭa-śrutyā, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.10)—***  
***ālī-vyālīka-vacanena muhur vihastā***  
***hastāravinda-vigalad-grathitārdha-mālyā \|***  
***hā hanta hanta kim api pratipanna-tandrā***  
***candrāvalī kila daśāntaram āruroha \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lack of awareness, from hearing the unpleasant, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **Hearing from her friend the unpleasant news, Candrāvalī, became overwhelmed. The half-strung flower-garland slipped from her lotus hand, she became exhausted and appeared to be almost dead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is from *Lalita-mādhava*. *Vyalīka* means unpleasant.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks with grief at the departure of Kṛṣṇa for Mathurā. By the unpleasant news given by her friend Padmā, she became agitated *(vihastā*). *Vihasta* means “disturbed” according to *Amara-koṣa.* The unpleasant news is described there:

*ajjhārūḍho raham iha purā saṅga-raṅgī rahaṅgī*  
*hā pupphāṇaṁ tuhabi caḍule gaṇṭhanukkaṇṭhidāsi*  
*āhīrīṇaṁ bahiri gahirukkosa-dīhā vīlāba*  
*kiṁ de candā-alī na parido kaṇṇa-kū-aṁ viśanti*

**Even though Kṛṣṇa, who carries the** ***cakra,*** **and who is very affectionate to his associates, has already climbed the chariot, you are still intent on stringing this flower garland. O fickle, deaf Candrāvalī! Has the deep, sustained, tumultuous wailing of the** ***gopīs*** **not entered your ears?** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **3.19**

*Daśāntaram* means the tenth state, death.

### Text 57

***iṣṭekṣaṇena, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (3.29)—***  
***aho dhanyā gopyaḥ kalita-nava-narmoktibhir alaṁ***  
***vilāsair āmodaṁ dadhati madhurair yā madhubhidaḥ \|***  
***dhig astu svaṁ bhāgyaṁ yad iha mama rādhā priya-sakhī***  
***puras tasmin prāpte jaḍima-niviḍāṅgī viluṭhati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lack of awareness, on seeing Kṛṣṇa, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Because the** ***gopīs*** **please Kṛṣṇa by speaking charming joking words, they are very fortunate. But my fortune is useless because Rādhā becomes completely senseless and rolls about on the ground in ecstasy when she sees Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though Rādhā has such a nature as depicted in contemporary dramas with pastimes, it is very rare. *Svam* means “my.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks of the superior *prema* of Rādhā on meeting Kṛṣṇa. *Āmodam* means bliss.

### Text 58

***aniṣṭekṣaṇena, yathā—***  
***rādhā vanānte hariṇā vihāriṇī***  
***prekṣyābhimanyuṁ stimitābhavat tathā \|***  
***krudyāsya tūrṇaṁ bhajato’pi sannidhiṁ***  
***yathā bhavānī-pratimābhramaṁ dadhe \|\|58\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lack of awareness, on seeing the undesirable: As she was enjoying pastimes with Kṛṣṇa at the edge of the forest, Rādhā suddenly saw Abhimanyu. She appeared to be a statue of the goddess Durgā to angry Abhimanyu when he approached.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against him. SB 10.33.37**

According to the *Bhāgavatam* verse, to remove the husbands having ill feeling for Kṛṣṇa, they were covered by *māyā* and perceived things differently. Therefore the description in the present verse of Rādhā becoming like Durgā was created by *māyā* also, since her form and that of a statue are actually very different. The same should be understood for other means of fooling the husbands, though it is unstated. One should not think that there is any contradiction or untruth in the Bhāgavatam statement.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Rādhā became stunned because of j*āḍya*, and became like a pillar. Abhimanyu thus thought she was a golden statue of Durgā, not Rādhā. “O Kṛṣṇa! Why are you standing near that statue of Durgā?” He then turned his back to Kṛṣṇa and decorated the deity with sandalwood, flowers and scents, and saying “All respects of Durgā,” offered respects to Rādhā (whom he thought was the deity) and went home.

### Text 59

***viraheṇa, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (187)—***  
***gṛhītaṁ tāmbūlaṁ parijana-vacobhir na sumukhī***  
***smaraty antaḥśūnyā murahara gatāyām api niśi \|***  
***tathaivāste hastaḥ kalita-phaṇi-vallī-kisalayas***  
***tathaivāsyaṁ tasyāḥ kramuka-phala-phālī-paricitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lack of awareness out of separation, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O Kṛṣṇa! Beautiful-faced Rādhā, with a vacant mind, on the advice of her friends, takes betel nut, but cannot remember to chew it. As the whole night passes, she simply holds the leaves filled with spices in her hand, and keeps the minced nuts in her mouth, without chewing them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though the ripe nuts are tasty, she was offered buds in order to cool her fire of separation. *Phālī* means cut.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa, conveying to him Rādhā’s pain in separation. Though she accepts the betel nut, she does not know whether it is in her hand or not. She is advised by friends to take it, since she has no desire on her own. They comfort her many times, trying to make her take it. *Phaṇi-valli-kiśalaya* are the leaves of the betel nut. She holds *(kalita*) them in her hand. Her jaw is full of the minced (*phalī*) nuts (*kramuka-phala*). Though her friends put the betel wrapped in the leaf in her mouth she does not chew it. Though they place in her hand *khadira* powder, cardamom and clove wrapped in a leaf, she does not put it in her mouth. Though the night passes three *praharas* (9 hours) she remains stunned.

### Text 60

***atha vrīḍā, sā navīna-saṅgamena, yathā—***  
***vidhumukhi bhaja śayyāṁ vartase kiṁ natāsyā***  
***muhur ayam anuvartī yācate tvāṁ prasīda \|***  
***iti caṭubhir analpaiḥ sā mayābhyarthyamānā***  
***vyarucad iha nikuñja-śrīr iva dvāri rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Shyness on newly meeting: “O moon-faced girl, come sit on this bed. Why do stand with bowed head? Repeatedly a person such as I begs you. Be pleased.” Though I pleaded with many flattering words, she remained standing in the doorway shining like a goddess of the bower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *vyarucad iha* sometimes *lasati bata* is found.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vrīḍā* means shyness. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. *Ayam anuvartī* means “a person like me.” I beg you, I am eager to massage your limbs. She remained at the door, and did not go to the bed out of shyness.

### Text 61

***akāryeṇa, yathā—***  
***paṭuḥ kim api bhāgya-tattvam asi putri vittārjane***  
***yad etam atulyaṁ balād apajahartha hāraṁ hareḥ \|***  
***gabhīram iti śṛṇvatī gurujanād upālambhanaṁ***  
***maṇi-srag-avalokanān mukham avāñcayan mālatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Shyness on doing what is forbidden: My daughter! You are skilful in gaining wealth, for you have certainly stolen this priceless necklace from Kṛṣṇa. Hearing the scolding from elders, Mālatī turned her face from the jeweled necklace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A leader of the opposing group disguised as Mālatī’s maternal grandmother speaks to Mālatī in a joking mood. You are indescribably skilful at earning wealth. *Guru-janāt* here has a secondary meaning, since the scolder was actually not old.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Mālatī speaks. Hearing the scolding from her great grandmother (*guru-janāt)*, she became shy.

### Text 62

***stavena, yathā—***  
***saṅkuca na tathya-vacasā***  
***jaganti tava kīrti-kaumudī mārṣṭi \|***  
***urasi harer asi rādhe***  
***yad akṣayā kauṅkumī-carcā \|\|62\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Shyness on being praised: O Rādhā! Please do not shrink from these truthful words. The moonlight of your glory illuminates the universe, since you are the eternal** ***kuṁkuma*** **anointing the chest of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

After their marriage as described in *Lalita-mādhava,* someone praises Rādhā in this verse. Therefore it is actually praise. If she were not married, it would be taken as a fault.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī was describing the glories of Rādhā to Gārgī when Rādhā happened to come there. She became shy on hearing her glorification. Vṛndā then speaks to her with pride in this verse.

### Text 63

***avajñayā, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (8.10)—***  
***tavedaṁ paśyantyāḥ prasarad-anurāgaṁ bahir iva***  
***priya-pādālakta-cchuritam aruṇa-dyoti-hṛdayam \|***  
***mamādya prakhyāta-praṇaya-bhara-bhaṅgena kitava***  
***tvad-ālokaḥ śokād api kim api lajjāṁ janayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Shyness by being slighted, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **Cheater! When I see your chest reddened by lac from some other** ***gopīs'*** **feet, announcing publicly your attraction for her, that sight of you produces more shame than the lamentation produced by your breaking our love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

O cheater! My seeing you creates shame indescribably surpassing the lamentation produced by breaking the great affection between us. The cause of shame is mentioned. I see your heart tinted red, produced *(churtiam*) by the lac on the feet of another lover advertising your attraction for her.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, disappointed, scolded Kṛṣṇa. O cheater! When I see your heart, the sight of what you did gives me shame more than lamentation caused by breaking our famous profusion of love. This cannot be explained (*kim api*). This shame is a cause of even greater sorrow. This is indicated by the ablative ending (*śokāt*). Or there is another meaning. By my nature I am always shy to see you. But now, I am even shier because of the lamentation produced by breaking our relationship. Your chest, red like the dawn, smeared with the lac of another lover, announces your attachment to someone else. The dawn also indicates the rising of the sun, which used to cause me pain because at that time we had to separate. Until today, your attraction for my competitor was hidden in your heart. Now that attraction has manifested openly, in order to kill me.

### Text 64

***atha avahitthā, sā jaihmyena, yathā śrī-jagannātha-vallabhe—***  
***amuṣyāḥ pronmīlat-kamala-madhu-dhārā iva giro***  
***nipīya kṣībatvaṁ gata iva calan-maulir adhikam \|***  
***udañcat-kāmo’pi sva-hṛdaya-kalā-gopana-paro***  
***hariḥ svairaṁ svairaṁ smita-subhagam ūce katham ayam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment because of deceit, from** ***Jagannātha-vallabha:*** **Drinking the words of Śaśimukhī like a stream of honey from a blossoming lotus, he became almost insane and his head shook. Though his passion increased, he concealed the thoughts in his heart. Smiling slightly, he said, “What is this?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Avahitthā* means hiding one’s form.  *Kṣībatvam* means madness.  *Iva* is an ornament. *Kalā* means thoughts. *Svairam svairam* means very slowly according to *Amara-koṣa.* *Katham uce* means “he said ‘What is this?’” Please tell me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Avahitthā* means hiding one’s form. A forest goddess named Madanikā speculates. He drinks the words of Śaśimukhī who delivers Rādhā’s love letter. In order to test her love, he hides his desire for enjoyment with her and his cleverness. He smiles slightly (*svairam*). *Svairam* means slight according to *Amara-koṣa.* He says “What is this?” while smiling slightly. Though his speech indicated indifference, his smile indicated otherwise.

### Text 65

***jaihmya-lajjābhyāṁ, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (52)—***  
***mā bhūyas tvaṁ vada ravi-sutā-tīra-dhūrtasya vārtāṁ***  
***gantavyā me na khalu tarale dūti sīmāpi tasya \|***  
***vikhyātāham jagati kaṭhinā yat pidhatte mad aṅgaṁ***  
***romāñco ayaṁ sapadi pavano haimanas tatra hetuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment because of deceit and shyness, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O Taralā! Don't speak further about this rascal on the bank of the Yamunā. I won't go near his messenger. I am famous in this world for being hard. My bodily hairs are now standing on end only because of cold wind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Why are your hairs standing on end?” To this challenge, she says “It is because of the cold winter *(haimanaḥ*) wind.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Why are your hairs standing on end?” To this challenge, she says “It is because of the cold winter (*haimanaḥ*) wind.”

### Text 66

***hriyā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.16)—***  
***bhajantyāḥ sa-vrīḍaṁ katham api tadāḍambara-ghaṭām***  
***apahnotuṁ yatnād api navamadāmoda-madhurā \|***  
***adhīrā kālindī-pulina-kalabhendrasya vijayaṁ***  
***sarojākṣyāḥ sākṣād vadati hṛdi kuñje tanuvanī \|\|66\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment out of shyness, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **While Rādhā attempts to hide the trumpeting of the elephant wandering on the bank of the Yamunā in the forest of her body, which is sweet with fragrance of new musk and fickle because of shyness, that body announces victory to the elephant in the bower of her heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī thinks to herself. The body of Rādhā with lotus eyes, which is like a small forest, announces the coming victory of Kṛṣṇa, the elephant king on the bank of the Yamunā, in the bower of her heart. The extraordinary qualities of the body are described. It is sweet with the fragrance of new musk (*madāmodena*) or sweet with extreme madness. It is fickle. She tries to hide the trumpeting of the king of elephants.  *Āḍambara* means great noise of elephants or drums according to *Amara-koṣa.* The roaring indicates victory.

### Text 67

***dākṣiṇyena, yathā lalita-mādhave (7.38)—***  
***uddhūtā smita-kaumudī na madhurā vaktrendu-bimbāt tayā***  
***mṛdvīnāṁ na nirākṛtā nija-girāṁ mādhurya-lakṣmīr api \|***  
***koṣṇair adya durāvarair nija-mano-gūḍha-vyathā-śaṁsibhiḥ***  
***śvāsair eva daroddhūta-stana-paṭais tasyā ruṣaḥ kīrtitāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment because of compliant nature, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **She has not stopped the moonlight of her smile from sweet moon of her face, and has not stopped the abundant sweetness of her soft words. Still, the warm sighs slightly raising the cloth on her breasts, proclaiming the pain deep in her heart that cannot be removed, reveal her anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Madhumaṅgala. *Tayā* means by Candrāvalī. *Durāvaraiḥ* means “hard to remove.”

### Text 68

***hrī-bhayābhyāṁ, yathā—***  
***hṛdaye tvadīya-rāgaṁ, mādhava dadhatī śamīva sā dahanam \|***  
***antarjvalitāpi bahiḥ, sarasā sphurati kṣamā-guṇataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment from shyness and fear: Within her heart, Rādhā burns with love for you, although externally she shows charm, because of her quality of tolerance. She is like a** ***śami*** **tree that burns within and blossoms without.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kṣamā* means peace or the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A selfless messenger of Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Śamī* is a famous tree. That tree burns at every moment on the inside by its nature, while externally it shows beauty with followers and leaves. She has the quality of the earth (*kṣamā*) or she is tolerant of the fire of love because of shyness and fear of people knowing she has love for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 69

***bhayena, yathā—***  
***candrāvalī mandira-maṇḍalāni***  
***patuyḥ prastāc ciram ācarantī \|***  
***vaṁśī-ninādena virūḍa-kampā***  
***nininda dhūrtā ghana-garjitāni \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment because of fear: Performing household chores in her husband's presence, Candrāvalī began to tremble on hearing Kṛṣṇa's flute. She cleverly rebuked the thunder for making her tremble.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sakhī* of the leader of the opposing party speaks. The flute and thunder sounded at the same time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Lalitā, hearing from somewhere the glories of Candrāvalī, speaks of this in gathering of *sakhī.* The flute sounded at the same time as thunder. “Ah! The rumbling of thunder has made be tremble with fear!” In this way she blamed the thunder.

### Text 70

***gaurava-dākṣiṇyābhyāṁ, yathā—***  
***svakara-grathitām avekṣya mālāṁ***  
***viluṭhantīṁ pratipakṣa-keśa-pakṣe \|***  
***malināpy aghamardanādarormi-***  
***sthagitā candramukhī babhūva tūṣṇīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Concealment because of respect and compliant nature: Seeing the flower garland she strung with her own hand stolen and placed in a rival** ***gopī's*** **braided hair, Candramukhī, though angered, covered her agitation with waves of respect for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to a *sakhī* of Candramukhī. *Keśa-pakṣa* means a braid according to *Amara-koṣa. Sthagitā* means covered agitation.

### Text 71

***atha smṛtiḥ \| sā sadṛśekṣayā, yathā haṁsadūte (23)—***  
***tamālasyālokād giri-parisare santi capalāḥ***  
***pulindyo govinda-smaraṇa-rabhasottapta-vapuṣaḥ \|***  
***śanais tāsāṁ tāpaṁ kṣaṇam apanayan yāsyati bhavān***  
***avaśyaṁ kālindī-salila-śiśiraiḥ pakṣa-pavanaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Recollection by seeing a similar object, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **When the Pulinda girls see a** ***tamāla*** **tree near Govardhana Hill, remembering Govinda, they become unsteady and their bodies burn with love. You should go there for a moment and gently remove their suffering with the wind from your wings, cooled by the water of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Smṛti* means awareness of previous experience.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Smṛti* means awareness of previous experience. Lalitā prays to a swan going to Mathurā to deliver a message, pointing out the path to Mathurā the swan.

### Text 72

***dṛdhābhyāsena, yathā—***  
***te pīyūṣakirāṁ girāṁ parimalāḥ sā piñcha-cūḍojjvalā***  
***tās tāpiñcha-manoharās tanurucas te kelayaḥ peśalāḥ \|***  
***tad-vaktraṁ śarad-indu-nindi nayane te puṇḍarīka-śriṇī***  
***tasyeti kṣaṇam apy avismarad idaṁ ceto mamāghūrṇate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Recollection by determined repetition: Even for a moment my mind cannot forget the perfume of his words flowing with nectar, his splendid peacock feather crown, his complexion attractive as a tamāla tree, his charming pastimes, his face that rebukes the autumn moon, and his eyes as white as lotuses. My heart whirls about constantly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Pīyūṣa-kirām is a genitive form from the neuter stem kir.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā, lamenting in separation, speaks to Uddhava. *Pīyūṣa-kirām* is a genitive form from the neuter stem *kir*. His words are like flowers with pleasant fragrance. His eyes have the splendid whiteness of lotuses.

### Text 73

***atha vitarkaḥ, sa vimarśād yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.29)—***  
***vighūrṇantaḥ pauṣpaṁ na madhu lihate’mī madhulihaḥ***  
***śuko’yaṁ nādatte kalita-jaḍimā dāḍima-phalam \|***  
***vivarṇā parṇāgraṁ carati hariṇīyaṁ na haritaṁ***  
***pathānena svāmī tad-ibha-vara-gāmī dhruvam agāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Conjecture because of reflection, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **These restless bumble-bees, disturbed in mind, do not drink the nectar of these flowers. This stunned parrot does not eat the pomegranate fruit. This pale doe refuses to eat the tips of green grass. Certainly Kṛṣṇa, who walks like the best of elephants, has traveled this path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vitarka* means considering a universal concomitance from previous experiences.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vitarka* means excessive deliberation caused by considering various reasons. *Vimarśa* means “considering various reasons.” When Kṛṣṇa hides himself in the forest, Rādhā begins to conjecture. *Carati* means eat.

### Text 74

***saṁśayād, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.40)—***  
***vidūre kaṁsārir mukuṭita-śikhaṇḍāvalir asau***  
***pure gaurāṅgībhiḥ kalita-parirambho vilasati \|***  
***na kānto’yaṁ śaṅke surapatidhanur dhāma-madhuras***  
***taḍil-lekhāhārī girim avalalambe jaladharaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Conjecture from doubt, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **There, in the far distance, Kṛṣṇa, decorated with a peacock-feather crown, embraced by the golden-complexioned gopīs, is enjoying. No. That is not my lover. I think it is only a cloud with lightning and a rainbow resting on Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

After doubt, one concludes the opposite. Instead of *na kānto ‘yam* sometimes *na kaṁsāriḥ* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Doubt means taking two opinions and not being able to decide the truth. Rādhā in separation, bewildered by *divyonmāda*, seeing a cloud on Govardhana, speaks. Looking closely she determines it is not Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 75

***atha cintā, sā iṣṭān avāptyā, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (238)—***  
***āhāre viratiḥ samasta-viṣaya-grāme nivṛttiḥ parā***  
***nāsāgre nayanaṁ yad etad aparaṁ yac caikatānaṁ manaḥ \|***  
***maunaṁ cedam idaṁ ca śūnyam akhilaṁ yad viśvam ābhāti te***  
***tad brūyāḥ sakhi yoginī kim asi bhoḥ kiṁ viyoginy api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pondering** ***(cintā),*** **on not attaining ones desires, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **You have no desire to eat. You have given up interest in all sense objects. Your eyes are fixed on the tip of your nose, and your minds fixed on a single thought. You are now silent, and you see the entire world as vacant. O friend! Please tell me, have you become** ***yoginī*** **or** ***viyoginī*** **(a person in separation)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Cintā* means thinking to order to attain a desired object or avoid an undesirable object. Though she knows the truth, Viśākhā inquires from Rādhā, full of *pūrva-rāga*, who is thinking “How can I attain association with Kṛṣṇa?” The symptoms indicate that she is contemplating. *Eka-tānam* means concentration on one point.

### Text 76

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (3.4)—***  
***akṣṇor dvandvaṁ prasarati darodghūrṇa-tāraṁ murāreḥ***  
***śvāsāḥ kḷptāṁ kila vicakilair mālikāṁ mlāpayanti \|***  
***keyaṁ dhanyā vasati ramaṇī gokule kṣipram etāṁ***  
***nītas tīvrām ayam api yayā kām api dhyāna-niṣṭhām \|\|76\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: The pupils of Kṛṣṇa’s eyes move restlessly, and his repeated sighs have wilted his jasmine garland. What fortunate beautiful girl in Gokula has put him into such difficult, indescribable meditation?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Not satisfied with the previous example, the author gives another.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Just as the *sañcāri-bhāvas* appear in the heroines, they should also appear in Kṛṣṇa. An example is given in this verse. Paurṇamāsī conjectures on seeing at a distance Kṛṣṇa in *pūrva-rāga,* who is thinking “How will I attain Rādhā?” *Vicakilaiḥ* means jasmine flowers.

### Text 77

***aniṣṭāptyā—***  
***bālyasyocchiduratayā yathā yathāṅge***  
***rādhāyā madhurima-kaumudī didīpe \|***  
***padmāyā mukha-kamalaṁ viśīrṇamantaḥ***  
***santāmyad bhramaram idaṁ tathā tathāsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pondering, on attaining bad results: Just as the moonlight of Rādhā's sweetness illuminates her body and separates itself from her childhood, the lotus flower of Padmā's face begins to wilt, and within it the bumble-bee of her heart languishes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ucchidura* is a reflexive verb form meaning “separating itself from her childhood.” Padmā’s face wilts. Her limbs become wilted by manifestation of imperfection. Within the lotus is a bee of dejection, the mind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Her beauty separates itself from childhood. Within the face is the antaḥkaraṇa, like a languishing bee. *Āsīt* should be *abhūt.*

### Text 78

***yathā vā—***  
***mā candrāvali malinā bhava rādhāyāḥ samīkṣya saubhāgyam \|***  
***jyotir-vido’pi vidyuḥ kṛṣṇe kila balavatī tārā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Candrāvalī! Do not become unhappy on seeing Rādhā's good fortune. Astrologers know that the constellation has great power only during the dark moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A *sārī* bird taught by a *sakhī* of Rādhā speaks. In front of leaders of groups, such bold speaking by *sakhīs* would not be proper. *Saubhāgya* means having such beauty that the lover shows great love. Candrāvalī does not have such beauty. This is not illogical, for astrologers know that during the dark moon, the stars are strong. Or Rādhā has control over Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example of Padmā expressing *cintā* at the beauty of Rādhā was given. Now and example of Candrāvalī expressing *cintā* at Rādhā’s beauty is given. A *sārī* bird sent by Lalitā speaks to Candrāvalī. *Kṛṣṇe* means the dark moon and Kṛṣṇa. *Tārā* means a constellation and Rādhā.

### Text 79

***atha matiḥ, yathā padyāvalyām (337)—***  
***āśliṣya vā pāda-ratāṁ pinaṣṭu mām***  
***adarśanān marma-hatāṁ karotu vā \|***  
***yathā tathā vā vidadhātu lampaṭo***  
***mat-prāṇa-nāthas tu sa eva nāparaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Determining the meaning, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **As I am attached to his lotus feet, let Kṛṣṇa crush me in his embrace. Let him mortally wound me by not being visible to me. Let him do whatever he likes with me, but he, and no one else, is the lord of my life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mati* means to determine the meaning after consideration. One *sakhī* speaks to test the emotions of another lover of Kṛṣṇa. “He is young. You think that he can bring you happiness, but you are inexperienced. You are completely attached to him. But I am giving you instruction. Give up your attachment to him.” In response, the other *sakhī* recites this verse. The word *pāda-ratām* (attached to his feet) indicates her expression of lowness out of fear of being rejected.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mati* means to determine the meaning after consideration. One time, Paurṇamāsī, sseing Rādhā with withered limbs because of pain of separation when Kṛṣṇa went to Mathurā, gives her instruction out of affection. “O child! I instruct you to worship the Lord Nārāyaṇa with service, *japa* and praise. Absorbing your mind in this, you will pass this difficult time until Kṛṣṇa returns. This method will bring happiness in this life and the next. Become a devotee of Nārāyaṇa.”

Rādhā said, “If that is so, why do you not instruct me to worship Kṛṣṇa, since he is equal to Nārāyaṇa according to the statement of omniscient Garga? If I worship by that method, he will appear and show himself to me.”

“But he cannot give up his nature. He will again cause you suffering by leaving.”

Rādhā then replies with this verse. Let him embrace me, who have fallen at his feet, raise me up with his hands, place me on his chest and crush me with his arms. Let him embrace me deeply and drown me in an ocean of bliss! Or not showing himself to me (*adarśanāt)*, let him wound me mortally. The ablative *adarśanāt* includes a missing participle so the meaning is “not giving his *darśana*.” Let him drown me in a greater ocean of suffering! Let him do what he wants. In front of me, let him enjoy with other women, since he is a lecher. He has no sense of judgment. But whether considering this life or the next, he is the lord of my life. No other person is my lord. I cannot serve Nārāyaṇa for attaining a position in the next world, since I am solely dedicated to Kṛṣṇa.

Explaining the last words *sa eva nāparaḥ* in another ways (he who does not have inferiority), is not correct, since these explanations do not account for the word *eva* which indicates distinction of Kṛṣṇa from others. Other explanations lead inevitably to *rasābhāsa.* Taking the words as *nā paraḥ* (he is not the Supreme Lord) would also be faulty. One could take the phrase to mean “But he is the lord of my life, and is nothing less.” But then the words *tu* and *eva* would have to be reversed in the verse. The meaning is not unsuitable, but there would be the fault of wrong placement of words. Therefore the first meaning should be taken. One should be aware that this verse came from the mouth of Mahāprabhu. Therefore it represents the words of Rādhā and no one else. The word *lampaṭaḥ* is the version of the previous *ācāryas*, not the version with *tadīya.*

### Text 80

***yathā vā—***  
***bhavāmbuja-bhavādayas tava padāmbujopāsanām***  
***uśanti sura-vanditāḥ kim uta manda-puṇyā nṛpāḥ \|***  
***atas tava jagatpate madhurimāmbudher mad-vidho***  
***na dāsyam iha vaṣṭi kaḥ puruṣa-ratna kanyā-janaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Brahma, Śiva and other** ***devatās*** **desire to worship your lotus feet, what to speak of ordinary kings, who possess less pious results. O lord of the universe! O ocean of sweetness! O jewel among men! What unmarried young girl like me would not yearn to serve you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rukmiṇī speaks after Kṛṣṇa has joked with her. Instead of *kim uta* sometimes *ka iha* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse illustrated persons with *samartha-rati.* Now an example of a person with *samañjasa-rati* is given. Rukmiṇī word a letter and sent a *brāhmaṇa* names Sunanda to Kṛṣṇa with it. *Ambuja-bhavaḥ* means Brahmā. *Uṣanti* means “they desire.” *Madhurimāmbhudheḥ* means an ocean of sweetness or an ocean of *śṛṅgāra-rasa.* *Tava dāsyam* means “to be a servant.”

### Text 81

***atha dhṛtiḥ \| sā duḥkhāhāvena, yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.13)—***  
***tad-darśanāhlāda-vidhūta-hṛd-rujo***  
***manorathāntaṁ śrutayo yathā yayuḥ \|***  
***svair uttarīyaiḥ kucakuṅkumāṅkitair***  
***acīklpann āsanam ātmabandhave \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Determination, caused by disappearing sorrow, from the Tenth Canto: Their heartache vanquished by the ecstasy of seeing Kṛṣṇa, the** ***gopīs,*** **like the personified Vedas before them, felt their desires completely fulfilled. For their dear friend Kṛṣṇa they arranged a seat with their shawls which were smeared with the** ***kuṁkuma*** **powder from their breasts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Dhṛti* means completeness with no unsteadiness of mind. Not only did they fulfill their desire, but attained the highest goal in the same way as the *śrutis* by describing the qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Thus they made a seat for Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Dhṛti* means a feeling of completeness which produces steadiness of the mind. Seeing Kṛṣṇa who had disappeared during the *rāsa* danced and then appeared again, the women of Vraja felt complete bliss with complete destruction of sorrow. Śukadeva describes this bliss and their actions arising from it. The women of Vraja, with all sorrow removed by the bliss of seeing Kṛṣṇa, offered him a seat. They attained the highest goal, beyond which there is not desire, like the great Upaniṣads. The Upaniṣads desired “Being born in Vraja as *gopīs,* we should enjoy pastimes with Kṛṣṇa by offering him our cloth tinged with the *kuṁkuma* from our breasts.” The Upaniṣads then performed great penance of following the *gopīs’* mood to attain the position of *gopīs.* This is related in the *Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa*. In *Bhāgavatam* the *śrutis* say:

*triya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo*  
*vayam api te samāḥ samadṛśo ’ṅghri-saroja-sudhāḥ*

**These women fully absorbed their minds in meditation on Lord Kṛṣṇa’s powerful arms, which are like the bodies of great serpents. We want to become just like the** ***gopīs*** **and render service to his lotus feet. SB 10.87.23**

The Upaniṣads, desiring in this way in a previous *kalpa* when they had seen Kṛṣṇa, attained their desire in this *kalpa* and became *gopīs.* In this *kalpa* other Upaniṣads, having the same desire, will become *gopīs* in future *kalpas*, since the number of *śrutis* is unlimited.

### Text 82

***uttamāptyā, yathā—***  
***navyā yauvana-mañjarī sthiratarā rūpaṁ ca vismāpanaṁ***
