***sarvābhīra-mṛgī-dṛśām iha guṇa-śreṇī ca lokottarā \|***  
***svādhīna puruṣottamaś ca nitarāṁ tyaktānyakāntā-spṛho***  
***rādhāyāḥ kim apekṣaṇīyam aparaṁ padme kṣitau vartate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Determination caused by attaining the ultimate: O Padmā! Rādhā is eternally situated in the full bloom of youth. Her beauty astonishes all the doe-eyed** ***gopīs.*** **Her extraordinary virtues surpass those of the three worlds. Though the supreme lord is independent, he is attached to her and desires no other girl. What more could she desire in the world?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Among all the doe-eyed *gopīs,* Rādhā is the praiseworthy (*navya*) bud of youth. She has the best youthfulness. Among them all, she has astonishing beauty. She has the best beauty. Among them she has the most extraordinary qualities, which causes astonishment to all people (*lokottarā*). The lord who is independent of them all has given up desire for any other lover. “Any other lover” means all the other *gopīs.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā met Viśākhā on the path and asked, “With what desire does Rādhā daily perform worship?” Viśākhā replies with this verse. All the *gopīs* have youthfulness, but Rādhā is the budding flower of youth who attracts the bee of Kṛṣṇa. It is continually fresh (*navyā sthiratarā)* or it is praiseworthy. You all have beautiful forms, but hers is most astonishing among all the beautiful women. She astonishes Candrāvalī your leader, what to speak of others. The other statements have similar implication. Therefore she performs worship only to cheat the elders.

### Text 83

***atha harṣaḥ \| so’bhīṣṭekṣaṇena, yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.4)—***  
***taṁ vilokyāgataṁ preṣṭhaṁ prīty-utphulla-dṛśo ’balāḥ***  
***uttasthur yugapat sarvās tanvaḥ prāṇam ivāgatam***

**Перевод:**

**Exuberance, on seeing the beloved, from the Tenth Canto: When the** ***gopīs*** **saw that their dearmost Kṛṣṇa had returned to them, they all stood up at once, and out of their affection for him their eyes bloomed wide. It was as if the air of life had reentered their bodies.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Harṣa* means happiness in the heart. *Tanvaḥ* means their limbs. Their life airs had previous left them. Now their life airs returned.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śukadeva describes the scene. *Tanvaḥ* means the limbs of their bodies.

### Text 84

***yathā vā lalita-mādhave (1.53)—***  
***sa eṣa kim u gopikā-kumudinī-sudhā-dīdhitiḥ***  
***sa eṣa kim u gokula-sphurita-yauvarājyotsavaḥ \|***  
***sa eṣa kim u man-manaḥ-pika-vinoda-puṣpākaraḥ***  
***kṛśodari dṛśor dvayīm amṛta-vīcibhiḥ siñcati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Exuberance, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **Is this the moon which makes the lotuses of the** ***gopīs*** **blossom? Is this a festival of kingdom of youthfulness appearing in Gokula? Is this the spring season delighting the cuckoo bird of my heart? O slender-waisted Lalitā! This person I see now is sprinkling my eyes with waves of bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The lines have a specific order of understanding (from distant to close, from general to Rādhā’s heart).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse described joy on seeing the Lord in a general way. The present verse is more specific. Rādhā describes Kṛṣṇa. *Sudhā-dīdhitiḥ* means the moon. He gives joy to all the *gopīs* like me. The festival of the prince or a festival of the kingdom of youthfulness has appeared in Gokula. Having described how he gives happiness, pleasure and love, she describes him as the spring which has special attraction for the amorous play of her mind, like a cuckoo bird. That festival and the spring sprinkle the eyes with waves of bliss.

### Text 85

***abhīṣṭa-lābhena, yathā tatraiva (8.11)—***  
***āloke kamaleṣaṇasya sajalāsāre dṛśau na kṣame***  
***nāśleṣe kila śaktibhāg atipṛthu-stambhā bhujā-vallarī \|***  
***vāṇī gadgada-kuṇṭhitottara-vidhau nālaṁ ciropasthite***  
***vṛttiḥ kāpi babhūva saṅgamanaye vighnaḥ kuraṅgī-dṛśaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Exuberance, at attained her beloved, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **When Rādhā saw lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, her eyes became flooded with tears, and she could not see him at all. The creepers of her arms became stunned and had no power to embrace him. Her voice became chocked up and could not to reply his words. These symptoms of doe-eyed Rādhā became obstacles in her meeting, which had occurred after a long, long time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because her voice choked up, she was not able to answer (*uttara-vidhau*). These symptoms because an obstacle in her meeting after a long time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nava-vṛndā describes the uncontrolled nature arising from bliss in Rādhā at the commencement of enjoyment in the form called *samṛddimat* (attaining the Lord after a long absence). Her eyes had no capacity for objects of seeing (*āloke*) since they were filled with streams of tears. Since her voice was choked up she could not answer. Attaining meeting after a long time, the transformations of *prema* caused obstacles.

### Text 86

***atha autsukyam \| tad-iṣṭekṣā-spṛhayā, yathā haṁsadūte (36)—***  
***asavyaṁ bibhrāṇā padam adhūta-lākṣā-rasam asau***  
***prayātāhaṁ mugdhe virama mama veśaiḥ kim adhunā \|***  
***amandād āśaṅke sakhi pura-purandhri-kala-kalād***  
***alindāgre vṛndāvana-kusuma-dhanvā vijayate \|\|86\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Impatience, with desire to see the beloved, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **Stop! Let my right foot remain undecorated with red lac! O fool! What is the use of all this decoration? I shall now go outside. By the sweet discussion of the women, I think that perhaps the Cupid of Vṛndāvana is now walking past my doorstep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ausukyam* (impatience) means intolerance of time because of desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Ausukyam* (impatience) means intolerance of time because of desire. When Kṛṣṇa was in Mathurā one woman spoke to her friend who has decorating her. *Asavyam* means right. O fool! I am always being decorated, but seeing Kṛṣṇa is most rare. You do not know that.

### Text 87

***iṣṭāpti-spṛhayā, yathā śrī-gīta-govinde (6.11)—***  
***aṅgeṣv ābharaṇaṁ karoti bahuśaḥ patre’pi sañcāriṇī***  
***prāptaṁ tvāṁ pariśaṅkate vitanute śayyāṁ ciraṁ dhyāyati \|***  
***ity ākalpa-vikalpa-talpa-racanā-saṅkalpa-līlā-śata-***  
***vyāsaktāpi vinā tvayā vara-tanur naiṣā niśāṁ neṣyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Impatience with a desire to meet the beloved, from** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **Rādhā constantly decorates her limbs and carefully prepares the bed. Whenever a leaf flutters she imagines you have come. Sometimes she engages in long contemplation. Though engaged actions like dressing, arranging the bed, imagining and contemplating pastimes, she does not desire to spend the night without you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Rādhā, who is dressing herself in expectation, speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Rādhā engages in dressing herself up. In this way she dresses up *(ākalpa*), speculates (*vikalpa*), makes the bed *(talpa*), and meditates on hundreds of pastimes (*saṅkalpa*). She meditates as follows. “When he comes today and grabs my bodice, I will deflect his hand with mine and move away from him. When he takes my hand and makes some request, I will smile and refuse.” Though she acts in this way, without you, if you do not go, she cannot spend (*na neṣyati*) the night. As her fire of separation becomes stronger her hope becomes weaker. She will eventually die.

### Text 88

***atha augryam \|***  
***augryaṁ na sākṣād aṅgaṁ syāt tena vṛddhādiṣūcyate \|\|88\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Augryam*** **is not a direct type of** ***vyabhicāri-bhāva*** **for the** ***gopīs.*** **Thus it is seen only in old people and others.**

### Text 89

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.50)—***  
***navīnāgre naptrī caṭula na hi dharmāt tava bhayaṁ***  
***na me dṛṣṭir madhye-dinam api jaratyāḥ paṭur iyam \|***  
***alindāt tvaṁ nandātmaja na yadi re yāsi tarasā***  
***tato’haṁ nirdoṣā pathi kiyati haṁho madhupurī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Ferocity, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Restless Kṛṣṇa! Right in front of you is my young grand-daughter. You have no fear of violating religious principles. I am old and even at noontime cannot see very well, but I am clever. O son of Nanda! If you do not leave my doorstep at once, then I am not to be blamed. Mathurā is not far away.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Augryam* means violent. *Naptrī* means grand-daughter, for it is said naptrī *pautrī sutātmajā*: *naptrī* means a grand-daughter. The word is found in the following

*yatra putraiś ca pautraiś ca naptṛbhiḥ saha gotrajaiḥ*  
*prajā vicitrākṛtaya āsan yābhir idaṁ tatam*

**O my lord, I think that the process manifest in the forms of sons, grandsons and family members has spread all over the universe in different varieties and species. SB 3.7.25 3**

It is not possible for anyone in Vraja to show real hatred for Kṛṣna.

*eṣāṁ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṁ deva rāteti naś*  
*ceto viśva-phalāt phalaṁ tvad-aparaṁ kutrāpy ayan muhyati*  
*sad-veṣād iva pūtanāpi sa-kulā tvām eva devāpitā*  
*yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte*

**My mind becomes bewildered just trying to think of what reward other than you could be found anywhere. You are the embodiment of all benedictions, which you bestow upon these residents of the cowherd community of Vṛndāvana. You have already arranged to give yourself to Pūtanā and her family members in exchange for her disguising herself as a devotee. So what is left for you to give these devotees of Vṛndāvana, whose homes, wealth, friends, dear relations, bodies, children and very lives and hearts are all dedicated only to you? SB 10.14.35**

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against him. SB 10.33.37**

However, showing affection for her grand-daughter, Mukharā scolds Kṛṣṇa, thinking “There should not be anything inauspicious in the form of attraction to others’ wives.”

Therefore her violent nature is only a semblance or *ābhāsa* of *augryam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mukharā suddenly appears and sees Kṛṣṇa trying to approach Rādhā to pacify her anger. “O Kṛṣṇa! You should not be mingling with women. Go from here.” When she boldly says this, he does not leave. She then angrily speaks this verse. She is my grand-daughter (*naptrī*). The usage is found in SB 3.7.24. It is not my fault seeing you stand there in front of me. I do not have good sight even in the day. He laughs. She then becomes violent and threatens him. Mathurā is not far (*kiyati pathi*). I will bring horseman from Kaṁsa to punish you.

### Text 90

***atha amarṣaḥ \| so’dhikṣepād, yathā śrī-daśame (10.60.44)—***  
***tasyāḥ syur acyuta nṛpā bhavatopadiṣṭāḥ***  
***strīṇāṁ gṛheṣu khara-go-śva-viḍāla-bhṛtyāḥ \|***  
***yat-karṇa-mūlam ari-karṣaṇa nopayāyād***  
***yuṣmat-kathā mṛḍa-viriñca-sabhāsu gītā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intolerance from being abused, from the Tenth Canto: O infallible Kṛṣṇa, let each of the kings you named become the husband of a woman whose ears have never heard your glories, which are sung in the assemblies of Śiva and Brahmā. After all, in the households of such women these kings live like asses, oxen, dogs, cats and slaves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Amarṣa* means intolerance when abused or disrespected. Rukmiṇī speaks this verse when afflicted by Kṛṣṇa with his rough jokes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Amarṣa* means intolerance when abused or disrespected. Rukmiṇī who has been abused by Kṛṣṇa in a joking way, replies with criticism. Let these kings like Śiśupāla and Śālva and even *devatās* who act like animals in the inner chambers of women accept wives who have never heard your glories in the slightest Such persons are disgusting even if they follow *dharma.*

### Text 91

***apamānād, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.39)—***  
***bāle vallava-yauvata-stana-taṭī-dattārdha-netrāditaḥ***  
***kāmaṁ śyāma-śilā-vilāsi-hṛdayāc cetaḥ parāvartaya \|***  
***vidmaḥ kiṁ na hi yad vikṛṣya kulajāḥ kelibhir eṣa striyo***  
***dhūrtaḥ saṅkulayan kalaṅka-tatibhir niḥśaṅkam unmuñcati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intolerance of disrespect, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: My child! Withdraw your heart from Kṛṣṇa who is addicted to gazing at the breasts of young** ***gopīs*****, and whose heart is a glistening black stone. Do we not know that he attracts us chaste girls by his play, contaminates us, and then, without worry, simply throws us away?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Actually this verse expresses the intolerance of the *sakhī,* not the heroine. However by the *sakhī’s* intolerance, the heroine’s *rati* is nourished. Thus it is given as an example. This should be understood in previous and later examples as well. He fills us with loads of contamination. This means he contaminates us.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā, encouraging Rādhā’s anger, speaks. He looks at the women’s breasts with lust, not *prema*. His heart shines strongly (*vilāsa*) with color of a black stone. His heart does not melt on seeing those who love him. Previously you placed your consciousness in him without judgment. Now, withdraw it from him since you have changed your perspective. Do not have doubt about my words, for we know what he does. He fills us with contamination. He does not worry. “Oh! I have destroyed the *dharma* of these women for this world and the next! What will be my destination after I die by doing intense penance?” He has no such fear.

### Text 92

***atha asūyā \| sā saubhāgyena, yāthā śrī-daśame (10.30.32)—***  
***imāny adhikamagnāni padāni vahato vadhūm \|***  
***gopyaḥ paśyata kṛṣṇasya bhārākrāntasya kāminaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Envy at the good fortune of another, from the Tenth Canto: Please observe, my dear** ***gopīs*****, how in this place lusty Kṛṣṇa’s footprints are pressed more deeply into the ground. Carrying the weight of his beloved must have been difficult for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Asūyā* (envy) means hatred because of someone else’s advancement.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Asūyā* means hatred because of someone else’s advancement. Among the *gopīs* looking for Kṛṣṇa when he disappeared during the *rāsa* pastime, Padmā and others speak. *Vadhūm* refers to Rādhā. O *gopīs*! That lusty boy has given up persons like you with *prema* and is carrying Rādhā. This indicates their amorous pastimes.

### Text 93

***yāthā vā tatraiva (10.21.9)—***  
***gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur***  
***dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām \|***  
***bhuṅkte svayaṁ yad avaśiṣṭa-rasaṁ hradinyo***  
***hṛṣyat-tvaco ‘śru mumucus taravo yathāryāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from the Tenth Canto: My dear** ***gopīs*****, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopīs, for whom that nectar is actually meant! The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are standing like hair on her body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

O *gopīs*! This flute performed skilful pious acts. He enjoys the great treasure of the nectar of Dāmodara’s lips. A woman can enjoy the nectar of the lips of a man married to other women out of attraction. But this flute is a male. How can he enjoy that nectar? This is a joke. The flute enjoys by itself without giving a drop to any of the *gopīs.* That is astonishing. Let that be. The very pure rivers enjoy the left over nectar from his mouth, and, relishing it, become joyous. Let that be. Seeing the greatness of the flute, the trees, his limbs, are filled with goose bumps in the form of sprouts shooting up and release tears in the form of honey. They do not consider it improper for the flute to enjoy Kṛṣṇa’s lips. Just as some respectable ancestors develop such symptoms on seeing the glory of their descendent, these trees and rivers which are not respectable have symptoms.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Envy of other women who are attracted to one’s husband is famous. In the previous verse some envy of Kṛṣṇa was expressed by the word *kaminaḥ* (lusty boy). Dissatisfied with this example, the author gives another example. The *gopīs,* hearing the flute of Kṛṣṇa as he herds the cows in the morning, talk among themselves. O *gopīs*! The flute must have performed great pious acts. Or, did the flute perform something auspicious or not? The flute comes from a tree which has an impious birth. But it enjoys the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lips. How can we tolerate this? That nectar belongs to us, since he is a *gopa* and a male and we are *gopīs,* females. He should be enjoyed by us every night. The flute is a different species, but thinking itself pleasurable for Kṛṣṇa, identifies itself as dearest to Kṛṣṇa. And showing boldness, it enjoys. Moreover, it enjoys illicit wealth, our wealth. Moreover the flute does not keep this secret, but announces by blowing air to us, who are the actual owners of that wealth. Or it is perhaps not blowing but expressing its enjoyment. It makes us hear that. Moreover, it enjoys without leaving any remnants.  *Avaśiṣṭa* here can have a negative meaning (no remnants). *Avaśiṣṭa* can be taken as *vaśiṣṭa* according to the the rule *vaṣṭi bhāgurir al-lopam*: the grammarian Bhāguri considers that the initial varṇa of *ava* and *api* should be deleted in all cases (as in *ava-śiṣṭa*). Thus *vaśiṣṭa* means remnants and *avaśiṣṭa* means no remnants. It does not leave any remnants for us, the rightful owners of the treasure. What audacity! Moreover, the local inhabitants are similar, because from the flute’s enjoyment of the nectar, on seeing that enjoyment, the rivers (*hradinyaḥ*) become full of goose bumps in the form of blooming lotuses and the trees release tears in the form of honey. Just as devotees (*yathā āryāḥ*) become full of tears and goosebumps from reciting the qualities of the Lord, so the trees and rivers, by the talks of the flute, develop ecstatic symptoms. The rivers are female friends and the trees are male friends, the messengers. The flute, rivers and trees are our enemies.

### Text 94

***yathā vā,***  
***kṛṣṇādhara-madhu mugdhe pibasi sadeti tvam unmadā mā bhūḥ \|***  
***muralī-bhukta-vimukte rajyati bhavatīva kā tatra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example of envy: O fool! Do not become proud, thinking you are constantly drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. Since those lips are only the remnants of what Kṛṣṇa's flute drinks, what value are they?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This statement is made out of *anurāga* and as in the previous example uses the image of the flute drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lips.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since inanimate objects like the flute should not really be objects of envy, another example is given. One *gopī* intoxicated with liquor sees on the path another woman of the opposing party. Out of intoxicated madness, guessing that she has enjoyed with Kṛṣṇa, she speaks with envy. “O fool! Do not be so proud (*unmadā*) thinking that you are always drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lips. Knowing those lips are impure we have rejected them.” The flute has enjoyed those lips first and then thrown them out. O fool! You are foolish since you have such pride, though you are taking leftovers.

### Text 95

***guṇena, yathā—***  
***tvatto’pi mugdhe madhuraṁ sakhī me***  
***vanya-srajaḥ sraṣṭum asau pravīṇā \|***  
***nāsyāḥ karau siñcati ced udīrṇā***  
***nirudhya dṛṣṭiṁ praṇayāśru-dhārā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Envy because of qualities: O fool! My friend is more expert than you at making beautiful garlands of forest flowers, unless a flood of her tears blinds her eyes and wets her hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Viśākhā speaks to Padmā who is proud of the garland she has made. Viśākhā is more expert at making flower garlands. Just on hear the word “forest garland” she remembers the wearer of forest garlands, Kṛṣṇa, because of her great *prema.* Thus tears come to her eyes. But you have no *prema*. This is the hint.

### Text 96

***atha cāpalyam \| tad rāgeṇa, yathā—***  
***phullāsu gokula-taḍāga-bhavāsu keliṁ***  
***niḥśaṅkam ācara ciraṁ vara-padminīṣu \|***  
***mṛdvīm alabdha-kusumāṁ nalinīṁ tvam enāṁ***  
***mā kṛṣṇa-kuñjara kareṇa parispṛśādya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Insolence, arising from passion: O black elephant! As long as you like, play without worry with the other blossoming lotus flowers growing in this lake of Gokula, but do not touch with your hand this delicate lotus not yet blooming.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Cāpalya* means lack of seriousness. *Alabdha-kusumām* is a pun meaning without blossoms or without menses. It is an example of *cāpalya* of the speaker. Or the verse can be taken as an example of *cāpalya* in Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Cāpalyam* means lack of seriousness. Lalitā, obstructing Kṛṣṇa who desires amorous sports in the forest pastimes during the *mahā-rāsa*, speaks. The lotus is without flowers. What is the use of taking a lotus with only leaves and no flower? In reference to Rādhā it means that she has not reached the age of youth fully. What is the use of taking Rādhā when you are passionate with full youth yourself? Though Rādhā had attained full youth Lalitā makes this statement because of her nature as a woman. This is the emotion of concealment (*avahitthā*). The other meaning of *kusuma* (menses) is disgusting so is not intended. By the power of *yoga-māyā,* all the young women of Vraja, in order to associate with Kṛṣṇa daily, did not have menses though it is natural for women. The forbiddance of enjoyment during menses which is seen in the material world does not even apply.

### Text 97

***yathā vā, śrī-gīta-govinde (1.49)***  
***rāsollāsa-bhareṇa vibhrama-bhṛtām ābhīra-vāma-bhruvām***  
***abhyarṇaṁ parirabhya nirbharam uraḥ premāndhayā rādhayā \|***  
***sādhu tvad-vadanaṁ sudhā-mayam iti vyāhṛtya gīta-stuti-***  
***vyājād udbhaṭa-cumbitaḥ smita-manohāri hariḥ pātu vaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Gīta-govinda*****: Surrounded by many beautiful** ***gopīs*** **in the midst of the jubilant** ***rāsa*** **dance, blinded with love, Rādhā tightly embraced Kṛṣṇa's chest. Saying “Your face is made of nectar,” on the pretext of praising his singing, she passionately kissed him. May Kṛṣṇa with his enchanting smile protect you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because of so many women, it was impossible for them to detect Rādhā’s actions. As if in private, she could then embrace and kiss Kṛṣṇa. This illustrates her *cāpalya.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example of the hero’s *cāpalya* towards the heroine was given. Now the *cāpalya* of the heroine towards the hero is illustrated. The great poet Jayadeva gives this description. All the beautiful *gopīs* with graceful eyebrows were absorbed in the bliss of tasting the tumult of the dancing, singing and music of the *mahā-rāsa*, and contributed their individual charms with a show of dexterous qualities, and were nourished by that. They sought nothing else. Near them, Rādhā tightly embraced Kṛṣṇa’s chest on the pretext of praising his singing. “O you are most fortunate since you sing with unheard of sweetness. What reward can I give you?” With her politeness, telling how she relished the singing, to satisfy him, she embraced him. She then passionately kissed him. Since she was most shy, how could she do this? She was blinded by *prema.* Her *cāpalya* arose from *prema.*

### Text 98

***dveṣeṇa, yathā—***  
***yātu vakṣasi harer guṇa-saṅga-***  
***projjhitā layam iyaṁ vana-mālā \|***  
***yā kadāpy akhila-saukhya-padaṁ naḥ***  
***kaṇṭham asya kuṭilā na jahāti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Cāpalya*** **arising from hate: This crooked-hearted garland refuses to leave Kṛṣṇa's neck, the abode of all our happiness. May this garland, free of the** ***guṇas*****, situated on Kṛṣṇa's chest, to meet destruction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Layam yātu* means “let it be destroyed.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa at a distance, Rādhā, filled with the *mahā-bhāva* called *mādana*, speaks to Lalitā, expressing her hatred of the garland. May the garland meet destruction or get liberation. The garland is devoid of the *guṇas*, or devoid of a string. Cursing the garland out of hatred is a sign of *cāpalya* arising from deep emotion.

### Text 99

***atha nidrā \| sā klamena, yathā—***  
***śvāsa-spandana-bandhurodara-talaṁ puṣpāvalī-srastara-***  
***nyañcan-mauktika-hāra-yaṣṭi kalayan nīvīṁ manāg ākulām \|***  
***klāntaḥ keli-bharād uroja-kalasīm ābhīra-vāma-bhruvaḥ***  
***kalyāṇīm upadhāya sāndra-pulakām adrau nidadrau hariḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sleep, from exhaustion: Exhausted from enjoying many amorous pastimes, his abdomen rising as he breathes, holding Rādhā’s disarrayed garment and resting on the pillow of her beautiful, auspicious breasts covered with goose bumps, Kṛṣṇa sleeps on a flower bed strung with hanging with pearls on Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Bandhuram* means “rising and falling.” *Srastara* is a type of bed. *Nivi* is a cloth bound around the waist of a woman. He touches (*kalayan*) the waist cloth of the woman and uses her breast as a pillow.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nidrā* means extinguishing the consciousness. Vṛndā speaks to Nāndīmukhī.  *Bandhuram* means “rising and falling.” *Srastara* is a bed. The garment around the wais *(nīvi)* belongs to Rādhā. He holds the cloth in his hand, pulling it from her thighs. Rādhā’s breasts are full of goose bumps because of bliss either in waking state or in sleep.

### Text 100

***yathā vā haṁsadūte (115)—***  
***alinde kālindī-kamala-surabhau kuñja-vasater***  
***vasantīṁ vāsantī-nava-parimalodgāri-cikurām \|***  
***tvad-utsaṅge nidrā-sukha-mukulitākṣīṁ punar imāṁ***  
***kadāhaṁ seviṣye kiśalaya-kalāpa-vyajaninī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **When will I, fanning Rādhā with a cluster of buds, serve her as she lies on the terrace of the bower cottage, fragrant with Yamunā’s lotuses, her hair emanating the fresh fragrance of** ***mādhavī*** **flowers, and her eyes closed in blissful sleep on your lap?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse gives an example of the heroine sleeping. Expressing her desire, Lalitā speaks to Kṛṣṇa living in Mathurā. “Please bring us to life by coming to Vṛndāvana quickly.” When will I, fanning with clusters of buds, serve Rādhā? *Vāsantī* means a *mādhavī* creeper.

### Text 101

***atha suptir, yathā—***  
***puraḥ panthānaṁ me tyaja yad amunā yāmi yamunām-***  
***iti vyākṣāṇā cucuka-vicarat-kaustubha-ruciḥ \|***  
***hareḥ savyaṁ rādhā bhujam upadadhaty ambuja-mukhī***  
***darī-kroḍe klāntā niviḍam iha nidrā-bharam agāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Lotus-faced Rādhā, using Kṛṣṇa’s right arm as a pillow, out of fatigue fell into deep sleep in the cave house, while her swollen tip of the breast shone like the Kaustubha jewel. She uttered, “Don't follow me. I will go to the Yamunā alone.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Supti* is dreaming.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Supti* is dreaming. Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to Rati-mañjarī who is picking flowers. She describes the sleep of Rādhā.  *Cūcuka* is the tip of the breast. This may also have a short vowel (*cucuka*) according to the commentators.

### Text 102

***yathā vā—***  
***ābhīrendra-sutasya gaṇḍa-mukure svāpnībhir ullāsitaṁ***  
***līlābhiḥ pulakaṁ vilokya cakitā niścinvatī jāgaram \|***  
***sā veṇor haraṇotsave dhṛta-navotkaṇṭhāpi talpāñcale***  
***visrastaṁ karato’pi nādhyavasasau taṁ hartum eṇekṣaṇā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Though doe-eyed Rādhā, desired to steal the flute which had fallen from Kṛṣṇa’s hand to the edge of the bed, when she saw the goose bumps on his cheeks as he enjoyed pastimes in sleep, she became frightened, and thought he must be awake. She gave up the attempt.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is an example of Kṛṣṇa’s dreaming. Vṛndā speaks to Nāndīmukhī. Kṛṣṇa was dreaming of kissing Rādhā. She though he was awake because otherwise, why would he have goose bumps on his cheek. She decided not to steal the flute which had fallen on the edge of the bed because of his sleeping state.

### Text 103

***prabodhaḥ, yathā—***  
***nidrā-pramoda-haram apy uru-kaṇṭha-nādaṁ***  
***kaṇṭhī-ravasya śitikaṇṭha-patatra-mauliḥ \|***  
***tuṣṭāva satvara-vibuddha-pariplavākṣa-***  
***rādhā-payodhara-girindra-nipīḍitāṅgaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Awaking: Even though it interrupted the pleasure of his sleep, peacock-feather crowned Kṛṣṇa praised the lion's loud roar, for he was tightly embraced by the mountain-like breasts of Rādhā, who suddenly awoke with darting eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kaṇṭhi-ravasya* means “of a lion. The lion roared on a distant mountain. It could not harm Kṛṣṇa by coming close. The sweetness was not diminished by fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Prabodha* means waking from sleep. Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Kṛṣṇa with the peacock feather in his crown praised the roar of the lion, because he was embraced by Rādhā*. Paripalvākṣī* means unsteady eyes.

### Text 104

***sakhyāṁ sva-sneho, yathā—***  
***śaila-mūrdhni hariṇā viharantī***  
***roma-kuḍmala-karmabita-mūrtiḥ \|***  
***rādhikā salalitaṁ lalitāyāḥ***  
***paśya mārṣṭi lulitālakam āsyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Affection for her** ***sakhīs:*** **Even though the hairs of her body were standing on end as she enjoyed pastimes with Kṛṣṇa on the summit of Govardhana, Rādhā affectionately wiped Lalitā's face, decorated with beautiful hanging locks of hair.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The affection of the leader for her *sakhīs* is a *vyabhicāri-bhāva*. It is said:

*sañcārī syāt samāno vā kṛṣṇa-ratyāḥ suhṛd-ratiḥ \|*  
*adhikā puṣyamāṇā ced bhāvollāsā ratiḥ \|\|128\|\|*

**If the** ***rati*** **directed to Rādha or another** ***sakhī*** **is equal or less than their** ***rati*** **directed to Kṛṣṇa, the** ***rati*** **directed to Rādhā or the** ***sakhī*** **is called** ***sañcāri-rati*****, nourishing the** ***rati*** **to Kṛṣṇa. If the** ***rati*** **directed to Rādhā or the** ***sakhī*** **is greater than that directed to Kṛṣṇa, and is constantly increasing, though it is still a** ***sañcāri-bhāva*****, it is called** ***bhāvollāsa-rati.*** **BRS 2.5.128**

This is the meaning. If the *rati* directed to a friend is equal or less than that directed to Kṛṣṇa it is a *sañcāri-bhāva*. That affection to the friend nourishes the *rati* for Kṛṣṇa. If that affection for the friend is greater than for Kṛṣṇa and is nourished affection for him, it is called *bhāvollāsa*. It is not a *sañcāri-bhāva* or a *sthāyi-bhāva.* Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a *sakhī* of Lalitā. Rādhā wiped the perspiration from the face of Lalitā. Rādhā has *rati* for Lalitā. This is a *sañcari-bhāva,* nourishing her *rati* for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 105

***atha utpattyādi-daśā-catuṣṭayam, tatra utpattir, yathā—***  
***mṛdur iyam iti vādīr mā tvam asyā kuḍuṅge***  
***śaśimukhi tava sakhyāḥ pauruṣaṁ dṛṣṭam asti \|***  
***iti bhavad-upakaṇṭhe mad-girā bhugna-dṛṣṭeḥ***  
***sthapuṭita-vadanāyā rādhikāyāḥ smarāmi \|\|\|***  
***atrāsūyotpattiḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**The four state of the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāva*****:**

***Utpatti*** **(appearance) of the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāva,*** **envy: O Śaśimukhī! Do not say this girl Rādhā is gentle. In this bower I saw your friend’s great boldness. I remember Rādhā with her face and her glance made crooked by my words.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a message sent by Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā to Lalitā. *Rādhikāyāḥ* has an accusative meaning though expressed in the genitive form as an option. *Utpatti* means a prior condition.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*bhāvānāṁ kvacid utpatti-sandhi-śābalya-śāntayaḥ \|*  
*daśāś catasra etāsām utpattis tv iha sambhavaḥ \|\|*

**Sometimes four stages are seen in the manifestation of** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*****: appearance, conjunction, conflict and disappearance. Appearance (*****utpatti*****) means the initial manifestation of the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāva.*** **BRS 2.4.232**

Tasting the sweetness of Rādhā’s face which had already tasted, Kṛṣṇa speaks to her *sakhī* Śaśimukhī, telling her what he had witnessed. Or it can be the words of Uddhava relating a message to Lalitā from Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā. *Mā vādīḥ* means *mā vada* (do not say this).  *Kuḍaṅge* means in the bower. In the bower she took the male role during amorous action. Her face became crooked *(sthapuṭita*). The genitive case of *rādhikāyāḥ* has an accusative meaning. This is according to the rule *adhīgartha-dayeśāṁ karmaṇi:* verbs having the sense of remembering, giving, pitying, protecting moving and controlling take the genitive case for the object. (Pāṇini 2.3.52) I remember Rādhā with her crooked face. This is the beginning stage (*utpatti*) of envy in Rādhā. Her crooked brow indicates the clear manifestation of envy.

### Text 106

***atha sandhiḥ \| tatra sarūpayor, yathā—***  
***cirābhīṣṭe prekṣe danujadamane vindati dṛśoḥ***  
***padaṁ patyau cārdha-sphuṭa-vacasi rakta-tviṣi ruṣā \|***  
***iyaṁ nispandāṅgī nimiṣa-kalanonmukta-nayanā***  
***babhūvāvaṣṭambha-pratikṛtir ivābmhoja-vadanā \|\|\|***  
***atreṣṭāniṣṭekṣaṇa-kṛtayor jāḍyayoḥ sandhiḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**The same** ***bhāva*** **of** ***jāḍya*** **from different sources: Seeing Kṛṣṇa who desired her for a long time and seeing her husband Abhimanyu stuttering and red with anger, lotus-faced Rādhā stopped blinking her eyes and became stunned. She appeared just like a golden statue.**

**This is being stunned from two sources: seeing the desirable and seeing the undesirable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Avaṣṭambha-pratikrṭiḥ* means she looked like a golden statue.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*sarūpayor bhinnayor vā sandhiḥ syād bhāvayor mūrtiḥ \|\|*

**When two versions of the same** ***bhāvas*** **or two differing** ***bhāvas*** **mix it is called** ***bhāva-sandhi*****. BRS 2.4.235**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. She saw Kṛṣṇa desiring her for a long time. She also saw her husband Abhimanyu by chance who was wandering in the forest looking for a bull. *Nimeṣa-kalana* means actions of closing the eye. She appeared like a golden statue. Not seeing Rādhā, and going for a distance, cheated by Lalitā’s collection of words, Abhimanyu gave up his anger and went home.

### Text 107

***atha bhinnayoḥ \| tatra ekahetujayor, yathā lalita-mādhave (9.39)—***  
***śikhari-bhara-vitarkataḥ prataptaṁ***  
***samaham aharniśam īkṣayā priyasya \|***  
***hṛdayam iha samasta-vallavīnāṁ***  
***yugapad apūrva-vidhaṁ dvidhā babhūva \|\|\|***  
***atra viṣāda-harṣayoḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**Two different** ***bhāvas,*** **remorse and exuberance, from one source: When he lifted Govardhana Hill, the hearts of all the** ***gopīs*** **burned with pain thinking that Kṛṣṇa must be carrying a heavy burden, and at the same time they became filled with happiness to see their beloved continuously day and night. In this way the** ***gopīs'*** **hearts were inconceivably divided in two.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kṛṣṇa was the cause of both emotions.  *Samaham* means “with joy.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśvakarmā paints a picture, recording the utterances of Paurṇamāsī recollecting the time when Kṛṣṇa lifted Govardhana. This verse describes the reaction to the picture. The *gopīs* were filled with pain, thinking “Oh! The arms of our beloved, soft as a *śirīṣa* flower must suffer this great burden.” But they also became a joyful festival *(samaham*) as in the phrase *utsavaṁ śrama-rucāpi dṛśīnām*: he was a festival of joy for their eyes. (SB 10.35.23) Happiness on seeing Kṛṣṇa was their natural quality. The cause of their pain and joy was one cause, Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 108

***bhinna-hetujayor, yathā—***  
***sthavayati nava-rāgaṁ mādhave rādhikāyāṁ***  
***giram atha lalitāyāḥ sāvahelāṁ pratītya \|***  
***calatara-caraṇāgreṇālikhantī dharitrīṁ***  
***vidhṛta-vadana-padmā tatra siṣveda padmā \|\|\|***  
***atra cintāmarṣayoḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**Two** ***bhāvas,*** **pondering and indignation, from differing causes: When Kṛṣṇa’s established his deep love for Rādhā, and Lalitā disrespected Padmā with insults, lotus-faced Padmā scratched the ground with her big toe and began to perspire with anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sthavayati* means “making solid.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

On the auspicious full moon day, Lalitā went from Gaurī-tīrtha to look for Kṛṣṇa. She saw him with Candrāvalī, Padmā and Śaibya on the bank of Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa. She then went to the assembly and spoke. Vṛndā tells this to Kundalaṭa.

Kṛṣṇa speaks in *Vidagdha-mādhava* in the presence of Candrāvalī to Lalitā with a message for Rādha:

*harinābhilasyamana*  
*saraṅga-ramanī sadā tvam atrāsi*  
*tad amum tvad-vaśa-hṛdayam*  
*hṛdayaṅgama-locane viddhi*

**O lover of Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa always desires you. O girl whose eyes penetrate the heart! Please know that Kṛṣṇa's heart is under your control.** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*** **7.11**

Lalitā’s disrespectful words are described in *Vidagdha-mādhava:*

*sahacari vṛṣabhānujāyā prādurbhāve vara-tviṣopagate \|*  
*candrāvalī-śatāny api bhavanti nirdhūta-kāntīni \|\|*

**My friend, the beauty of Rādhā eclipses the splendor of hundreds of Candrāvalīs.** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*** **7.26**

Writing on the ground with her foot, Padmā showed *cintā,* caused by Kṛṣṇa. Her perspiration arising from anger was caused by Lalitā.

### Text 109

***atha śāvalyam, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (5.7)—***  
***dhanyās tā hariṇī-dṛśaḥ sa ramate yābhir navīno yuvā***  
***svairaṁ cāpalam ākalayya lalitā māṁ hanta nindiṣyati \|***  
***govindaṁ parirabdhum indu-vadanaṁ hā cittam utkaṇṭhate***  
***dhig vāmaṁ vidhim astu yena garalaṁ mānābhidhaṁ nirmame \|\|\|***  
***atra cāpala-śaṅkautsukyāmarṣāṇāṁ śāvalyam \|***

**Перевод:**

**Conflict of** ***bhāvas,*** **from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Fortunate are the doe-eyed girls with whom the new youth enjoys. When Lalitā sees my fickle nature, she will rebuke me. Oh! My heart longs to embrace moon-faced Govinda. I curse crooked destiny that has created the poison named anger.**

**Conflict of** ***cāpalya, śaṅkā, autsuka*** **and** ***amarṣa***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The order of lines is faulty. The third line should actually be placed first and the first line should be placed in the third place. A verse maker should be consulted. In that way the word *saḥ* will be understood to mean Govinda.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Śāvalya* means increasing conflict of *bhāvas*. Rādhā after quarreling and separating speaks. The first line indicates *cāpalya* arising from impatience (*autsukya*). The second line indicates worry (*śaṅkā*) arising from remembering Lalitā. This conflicts with *cāpalya.* The third line reveals *ausukya* arising from disappointment. This conflicts with worry. The fourth line indicates her indignation (*amarṣa*) at the creator for producing anger which will arise on seeing Kṛṣṇa and obstruct her love. This conflicts with *autsukya.*

### Text 110

***atha śāntiḥ, yathā—***  
***ālī-yukti-kuṭhārikā-paṭimābhir yo na prapede chidāṁ***  
***dūtī-jalpita-nirjhareṇa ca ciraṁ yaḥ kvāpi noccālitaḥ \|***  
***vaṁśi-nāda-marul-lavena kamalācetas taṭī-veṣṭano***  
***mānākhyaḥ prabalonnatis tarur ayaṁ na kṣipram unmūlyate \|\|\|***  
***atrerṣyākhya-bhāvasya śāntiḥ \|***

**Перевод:**

**Disappearance of a** ***bhāva:*** **The tall, strong tree of anger growing on the shore of Kamalā's heart which would not be cut by the sharp axe of the** ***gopīs'*** **logical arguments and could not be moved by the torrents of the messengers' pleading words, it was uprooted by a faint breeze from Kṛṣṇa's flute immediately.**

**This is the disappearance of malice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Śāntī* means the disappearance of a *bhāva* (such as malice). Nāndīmukhī speaks. Just by the beginning of the sound of the flute, her anger was destroyed. This shows the strength of the flute over all other methods.

## Chapter 14 - Sthāyi-bhāva

## Outline

I. Madhura-rati

II. Causes:

A. Abhiyoga (showing manifestations of love)

B. Visāya (sense objects)

C. Sambandha (qualities in the lover)

D. Abhimāna (possessiveness)

E. Tadīya-viśeṣa (beloved’s articles)

1. his feet
2. cow pastures
3. associates

F. Upamāna (objects with similarlity)

G. Svabhāva (ones nature)

H. Nisarga (through previous practice)

1. Svarūpa  
   a. Kṛṣṇa-niṣṭha  
   \- Lalanā-niṣṭha  
   \- Ubhaya-niṣṭḥa

III. Types:

A. Sādhāraṇī

B. Samañjasa

C. Samartha

IV. Stages:

A. Rati

B. Prema remains in spite of causes for its destruction

1. Prauḍha
2. Madhyā
3. Manda

C. Sneha melting the heart never fully satisfied on seeing the Lord

1. Strength  
   a. Kaniṣṭha  
   b. Madhyama  
   c. Śreṣṭha
2. Types  
   a. Ghṛta-sneha with deep respect “I am his.”  
   b. Madhu-sneha “He is mine.”

D. Māna (anger):

1. Types:  
   a. Udātta from ghṛta-sneha gentle  
   b. Lalita from madhu-sneha, crooked, joking

E. Praṇaya (intimacy):

1. Types:  
   a. Maitra from ghṛta-sneha, modesty  
   \- Sumaitrya mixing with udātta  
   b. Sakhya from madhu-sneha, no fear  
   \- Susakhya mixing with lalita

F. Rāga:

1. Types:  
   a. Nīlimā (from ghṛta-sneha)  
   \- Nīlī  
   \- Śyāma  
   b. Raktimā (from madhu-sneha)  
   \- Kusmubha  
   \- Manijiṣṭḥa

G. Anurāga:

H. Mahābhāva:

1. Types  
   a. Rūḍhā  
   b. Adhirūḍha  
   \- Modana (in Rādhā’s group only)  
   \- Mohana in separation (in Rādhā)  
   \- Divyonmada  
   a. Udgūrṇa  
   b. Citra-jalpa  
   \- Prajalpa  
   \- Parijalpa  
   \- Vijalpa  
   \- Ujjalpa  
   \- Saṁjalpa  
   \- Avajalpa  
   \- Abhijalpa  
   \- Ājalpa  
   \- Partijalpa  
   \- Sujalpa
2. Mādana (in Rādhā only continuously)

### Text 1

***sthāyi-bhāvo’tra śṛṅgāre kathyate madhurā ratiḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sthāyi-bhāva*** **of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa*** **is** ***madhura-rati.***

### Text 2

***sā, yathā govinda-vilāse—***  
***kālāhi-vaktra-vilasad-rasanāgrajāgrad-***  
***gopī-dṛg-añcala-camatkṛti-biddha-marmā \|***  
***śarmādiśatv aruṇa-ghūrṇita-locanāntaḥ-***  
***sañcāra-cūrṇita-satī-hṛdayo mukundaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From** ***Govinda-vilāsa:*** **May Mukunda, who is mortally wounded by the astonishing powerful glances of the gopīs like the tip of the tongue of a black snake, who pulverizes the hearts of the chaste** ***gopīs*** **with his wandering, red, rolling eyes, bestow auspiciousness to you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Now *sthāyi-bhāva* will be discussed.

*namaś caitanya-rūpāya mādhurya-sthāyine sadā \|*  
*sva-sāmarthye’py aho sāmya-sāmañjasyānuvartine \|\|*

**I offer eternal respects to the form of consciousnss (Caitanya Mahāprabhu), the** ***mādhurya-sthāyi-bhāva,*** **which by nature is** ***samartha,*** **but contains with it** ***sādhāraṇī*** **and** ***samañjasa*** **types.**

The author begins with an introductory prayer of auspiciousness. He is bitten just by the astonishment of the glances of the *gopīs,* revealing their prowess, like the tip of the tongue of black snake. Kṛṣṇa has a *sthāyi-bhāva* for the *gopīs.* Being bitten implies that he has attained *rasa.* The *gopīs* are the *viṣaya* and their glances are the *uddīpana*. The *anubhāvas* includes standing of hairs on end and yawning. The *vyabhicāri-bhāvas* are *autsukya* and *cāpalya.* He grinds the hearts of the chaste women by the wandering of the edges of his red eyes which roll about. The *gopīs’ sthāyi-bhavā* has Kṛṣṇa as the *viṣaya*. Grinding their hearts indicates they have attained *rasa.* The *vibhāvas* are Kṛṣṇa and his glances. The *anubhāvas* and *vyabhicāri-bhāvas* are similar to those mentioned above. *Madhura-rati* with Kṛṣṇa as the *viṣaya* and the *gopīs* as the *viṣaya* has been described in this verse.

*mitho harer mṛgākṣyāś ca sambhogasyādi-kāraṇam \|*  
*madhurāpara-paryāyā priyatākhyoditā ratiḥ \|*  
*asyāṁ kaṭākṣa-bhrū-kṣepa-priya-vāṇī-smitādayaḥ \|\|*

**That** ***rati*** **found in the doe-eyed women which is the root cause of eight types of enjoyment between the women and Kṛṣṇa is called** ***priyata-rati*****. It is also called** ***madhura-rrati*****. In this** ***rati,*** **there are side-long glances, moving the eyebrows, and affectionate words and slight smiles etc. BRS 2.5.36**

### Text 3

***yathā vā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (30)—***  
***govardhana-girim upetya kaṭākṣa-bāṇān***  
***karṇa-sphuran-maṇi-śilopari saṅkṣuvānā \|***  
***kā bhrū-dhanur-dhuvana-sūcita-luñcaneyaṁ***  
***vyagrīkaroty ahaha mām api sambhrameṇa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **Who is this girl near Govardhana Hill who, firing arrows of glances above her ruby earrings and indicating theft by the movement of her bow-like eye brows, agitates me with confusion?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having indicated the *sthāyi-bhāva* of the *gopīs* in general, the author now indicates the *sthāyi-bhāva* of Rādhā, the best of the *gopīs*, as the best example. Kṛṣṇa, obstructing the *gopīs* at Govardhana on the pretext of taxing them, sees Rādhā and speaks. She sharpens the arrows of her glances above her ruby earrings. This indicates that the edges of her eyes spread to her earrings because of desire to see Kṛṣṇa. This indicates her *rati* for him. Who is she? This question is directed by Kṛṣṇa to Madhumaṅgala. She indicates theft by the movement of her eye brows. Since I am pierced by the arrows of her glances, she will make me unconscious, and will steal the wealth of my self-control and memory. My heart has become disturbed just by seeing the movement of her bow-like brows and the arrow shafts. I do not know what will happen after actually being pierced by those arrows, even though I am the best of warriors. Rādhā is the *viṣaya* of his *rati.*

### Text 4

***abhiyogād viṣayataḥ sambandhād abhimānataḥ \|***  
***sā tadīya-viśeṣebhya upamātaḥ svabhāvataḥ \|***  
***ratir āvirbhaved eṣām uttamatvaṁ yathottaram \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In order of greater strength,** ***rati*** **arises from manifestation of love (*****abhiyoga*****), from sense objects (*****viṣaya*****), from qualities in the object of love (*****sambandha),*** **from one’s possessiveness (*****abhimāna*****), from dear objects of the beloved (*****tadīya-viśeṣa*****), from objects having some similarity (*****upamāna*****), and from nature (*****svabhāva).***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The causes of *rati* according to material perception are listed. The causes according to the authorities will be listed in vere 42.

### Text 5

***tatra abhiyogaḥ—***  
***abhiyogo bhaved bhāva-vyaktiḥ svena pareṇa ca \|\|5\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhiyoga*** **means a manifestation of emotion by oneself or conveyed through another person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Abhiyoga* is the manifestation of a *bhāva,* by oneself or conveyed through others, such as an *amitārthā* messenger. Ujjvala-nilamaṇi 7.541 When the hero shows his *bhāva,* this is a cause of *rati* in the heroine. When the heroine shows her *bhāva* this is a cause of *rati* in the hero.

### Text 6

***tatra svenābhiyogād, yathā—***  
***mad-adhara-viluṭhad-vilocanāntaṁ***  
***mṛdula-latā-nava-pallavaṁ daśantam \|***  
***sakhi harim avalokya bhānujāyās***  
***taṭa-vipine sphuṭad-antarāsmi jātā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The lover’s directly manifesting the** ***bhāva*****: When I saw Kṛṣṇa in the forest at the bank of the Yamunā, his sidelong glance plundering my lips while he bit a delicate bud of a creeper similar to my lips, my heart began to blossom.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā who asks the news. Not only did he touch my lips with his glance but his glance became intoxicated with the nectar of my lips so that he fell down and could not raise himself. His eyes were satisfied but his tongue and teeth did not get to taste my lips. Therefore he bit a flower bud which was similar to my lips. Seeing that, my heart blossomed. This indicates appearance of her *rati.* Also her compassion for him and the flames of love blazing because of that sight are hinted. She informed her *sakhī* of the compassion, but kept the flames of love secret. The next suggestion is “Quickly make an appointment with him for me.”

### Text 7

***yathā vā—***  
***kuvalaya-vipināny asau sṛjantī***  
***diśi diśi locana-cāpalāc calākṣī \|***  
***harati taraṇijā-taṭe puraḥ kā***  
***subala balān mama citta-cañcarīkam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Subala, who is this girl on the bank of the Yamunā, whose restless glances create lotus flowers everywhere, and who has enchanted the bee of my heart?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse illustrated the arousal of *rati* in the heroine, by the hero’s show of emotion. Now an example of the *rati* arising in the hero, on seeing the heroine’s love, is given. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. In this verse the restless eyes are the display of Rādhā’s love.

### Text 8

***pareṇābhiyogād, yathā—***  
***tvadīyam āpīya gatāvalambā***  
***saṁvāda-mādhvīkam atīva sādhvī \|***  
***āghūrṇamānā vraja-rāja-sūno***  
***nīvīṁ skhalantīṁ na vidāñcakāra \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhiyoga*** **produced by others: O prince of Vraja! When extremely chaste Rādhā drank the nectar of your words, she lost control, became indifferent to everything, and was unaware that her garment is slipping.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When I deliver the news that you had love for her, Rādhā, though self-controlled, began relishing it, lost interest in all else (*gatāvalambā*), became devoid of steadiness, and was unaware that her garment was slipping.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A messenger who has delivered a letter to Rādhā from Kṛṣṇa speaks to Kṛṣṇa who has *anurāga* for Rādhā. Hearing of Kṛṣṇa’s love from a messenger, Rādhā develops *rati,* shown by her slipping garment.

### Text 9

***atha viṣayāḥ—***  
***śabda-sparśādayaḥ pañca viṣayāḥ kila viśrutāḥ \|\|9\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The five sense objects are sound, touch, form, taste, and fragrance.**

### Text 10

***tatra śabdād, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (1.34)—***  
***nādaḥ kadamba-viṭapāntarato visarpan***  
***ko nāma karṇa-padavīm aviśan na jāne \|***  
***hā hā kulīna-gṛhiṇī-gaṇa-garhaṇīyāṁ***  
***yenādya kām api daśâṁ sakhi lambhitāsi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From sound, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: My friend, what is this sound that has emerged from the interior the** ***kadamba*** **forest and has entered my ears? I cannot understand it. Oh! It has forced me into a condition very abominable for a respectable woman.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The sound is the sound of the flute, understood from the context.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā asks “Why are you losing your self-control?” Rādhā answers.  *Nādaḥ* means the sound of the flute. It has forced me to a condition condemned for married women. It destroys my vow of chastity.  *Rati* for the person who plays the flute arises from the sound of the flute.

### Text 11

***yathā vā, tatraiva (2.2)—***  
***ekasya śrutam eva lumpati matiṁ kṛṣṇeti nāmākṣaraṁ***  
***sāndronmāda-paramparām apanayaty anyasya vaṁśī-kalaḥ \|***  
***eṣa snigdha-ghana-dyutir manasi me lagnā sakṛd-vīkṣaṇāt***  
***kaṣṭaṁ dhik puruṣa-traye ratir abhūn manye mṛtiḥ śreyasī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example from the same work: On hearing only once the name Kṛṣṇa, I have lost my intelligence. On hearing another person playing a flute, I have developed intense madness. And seeing a person with dark complexion in a picture, my mind becomes attached to him. How unfortunate! I have become simultaneously attached to three persons. It would be better for me to die.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse also comes from *Vidagdha-mādhava.* Rādhā, first hearing Kṛṣṇa’s name, experiences its great sweetness and develops *rati* for that name. Then relishing the sound of the flute for its intense sweetness, she develops *rati* for the flute player. Then relishing Kṛṣṇa’s form in a picture with her eyes once, she develops *rati* for him. Though they are three persons, they manifest as Kṛṣṇa, who is their shelter, and she develops *rati* for Kṛṣṇa. Without the manifestation of Kṛṣṇa, *rati* will not arise. This will be explained in verse 16. Though Kṛṣṇa is one form expressed in three ways in her mind, because she experiences them separately she is not aware that they are one person. Since she cannot understand how they can be one person, she says “I have developed *rati* for three persons.” To develop *rati* for one man is bad, what to speak of having attraction for three men. Therefore death would be best. Without dying that despicable attraction cannot be driven away.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to a *sakhī* who inquires. I ask “Who does Vṛndāvana belong to?” Lalitā answers “It belongs to Kṛṣṇa.” Hearing one syllable of the name of Kṛṣṇa, what to speak of the whole name, that syllable enters the ears and then the heart. It then steals my intelligence. I have developed *rati* for that person. The verb *lumpati* is in the present tense, to suggest that the impression, entering into its corresponding object (Kṛṣṇa himself) does not leave. The flute sound of another person produces intense madness. First intelligence was lost by the name. Then the remainder of my mind has become insane. The present tense is again used for the same purpose. *Rati* for that second person also arose. She then sees a form in a picture shown by Viśākhā. She develops *rati* for that person. It is improper for a person like me to have attraction for another man, what to speak of three men. Her *nitya-siddha-rati* recognizes Kṛṣṇa as the *viṣaya* but she thinks there are three men—Kṛṣṇa, the flute player and the dark figure in the picture. Then she laments. Her friends then inform her of the truth and pacify her.

### Text 12

***sparśād, yathā—***  
***vrajaṁ muṣṭi-grāhye tamasi nigiraty aṅgam iha me***  
***sakhi sparśaṁ daivād yad-avadhi paraṁ kasyacid agāt \|***  
***gṛhītā jāgaryā tad-avadhi sadaivāṅgaja-gaṇaiḥ***  
***sa-śaṅkair yā paśya kṣaṇam api na sādyānpy uparatā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From touch: O friend! While darkness was swallowing up Vraja in its fists, suddenly a body touched me. At that touch, the hairs of my body stood on end. But look! What was this? Because of this doubt, even today my hairs continue to stand on end.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A new girl who has suddenly come from far away speaks to a *sakhī* who came with her. *Gṛhītā jāgaryā* can mean “my hairs stood on end.” It can also mean “woke up.” *Aṅgaja-gaṇa* means body hairs, but also means Cupid’s assistants. *Sa-śaṅkaiḥ* means having doubt or apprehension of the form “What was that touch which brought happiness?” The mental reaction (*śaṅkā)* then effects various parts of the body because intense astonishment.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When a friend asks the cause of disturbance a *gopī* explains what happened the day before. The bold poetic expression *tamasi muṣṭyā grāhye* (darkness grabbing in its hands) means dense darkness. When the dense darkness swallowed up Vraja, and it was therefore impossible to identify who touched me, while I was going along the path, someone touched me with his body, and all my body hairs stood on end. The hairs continue to remain in this state, because of apprehension. This apprehension is also concealment (*avahitthā).* The mental action of apprehension or doubt produces effects on the body in the form of hairs standing on end. This indicates extreme apprehension.

### Text 13

***rūpād, yathā haṁsadūte (77)—***  
***kṛtākṛṣṭi-krīḍaṁ kim api tava rūpaṁ mama sakhī***  
***sakṛd dṛṣṭvā dūrād ahita-hita-bodhojjhita-matiḥ \|***  
***hatā seyaṁ premānalam anu viśantī sarabhasaṁ***  
***pataṅgīvātmānaṁ murahara muhur dāhitavatī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From form, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **O Kṛṣṇa! By seeing your form of blissful** ***prema*** **from a distance only once, my friend, forgetting what is auspicious and what is not, devoid of all hope, like a moth, blissfully enters the fire of** ***prema*****, and burns in its flames repeatedly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Krṭākṛṣṭi-krīḍaṁ rūpam* means a form of blissful *prema*. Seeing that form, she enters the fire repeatedly. Not only are her hopes destroyed, but she gets burned repeatedly, trying to get away, but falling back into the fire.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā informs Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā of the state of Rādhā in separation through a swan messenger. *Kṛtākṛṣṭi-krīḍaṁ rūpam* means a form with attractive pastimes. That is the fault of your form. What can my friend do? Because of her simplicity she does not know what to do. She has lost all hope. Since it is fate alone that she is in this position, what is your fault in this? She blissfully (*sarabhasam*) enters the flame of *prema.* A moth goes towards the flame and leaves two or three times. Similarly Rādhā in anger many times decides to give up her love for you, and again enters into *prema.*

### Text 14

***rasād, yathā—***  
***pulakayati yad aṅgaṁ sevate gātra-bhaṅgaṁ***  
***vahati hṛdi taraṅgaṁ sadya evādya mugdhā \|***  
***tad aghadamana-vaktrodgīrṇa-tāmbūlam alpaṁ***  
***sphuṭam aviditam āsye nyastam asyās tvayāli \|\|14\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From taste: O charming friend! Because her bodily hairs are standing on end, her limbs are trembling, and waves of** ***anurāga*** **appear within her heart, it is clear that, unobserved by anyone, you must have placed a small portion of Kṛṣṇa’s betel-nut in her mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One *sakhī,* seeing the fresh stains of betel on another *sakhī’s* mouth, and assuming it was given by Kṛṣṇa who was nearby, and was taken with his permission, and seeing the transformations taking place in the *sakhīs’* body, speaks to the *sakhī* who gave the friend the betel nut, understanding the power of the betel from Kṛṣṇa’s mouth. *Pulakayati* means literally “became possessed of hair standing up (*pulakavat karoti*).” The affix *vat* is dropped according to the rule *vin-mator luk* (Pāṇini 5.3.65)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One *sakhī,* desiring the type of *rati* that her leader had for Kṛṣṇa, and understanding the happiness produced by taking his chewed betel, secretly ate some after wrapping it in a leaf. Another *sakhī,* inferring that she had developed *rati* by the transformations taking place in her body, speaks to the one who gave her the betel. *Pulakayati* means her hairs stood on end. Waves of *anurāga* developed in her heart. Because of these symptoms (*tat)* you must have places betel in her mouth.

### Text 15

***gandhād, yathā—***  
***vibhrājante kva sakhi sukhinaḥ śākhino mohanās te***  
***yeṣāṁ puṣpair iyam anupamā vaijayantī kṛtāsti \|***  
***paśyākṛṣṭa-bhramara-paṭalā yāta-yāmāpi kāmaṁ***  
***yā bhūyobhir mama parimalaiḥ stambhayaty adya cetaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From smell: O friend! Where are the beautiful and blissful trees whose flowers have made this incomparable** ***vaijayantī*** **garland? See! Even though it is old, it attracts swarms of bees, and it stuns my heart with its fragrance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Yātayāmam* means withered or enjoyed according to *Amara-koṣa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Being shown by her friend something she did not previously know, a *sakhī* smells Kṛṣṇa’s used garland and, after fainting and wakening, speaks with amazement. The *sakhī* speculates that the trees attain unlimited bliss since the trees’ flowers faint in bliss. *Yātayāmam* means worn out or used according to *Amara-koṣa.*

### Text 16

***lokottara-padārthānāṁ prabhāvaḥ ko’py anargalaḥ \|***  
***ratiṁ tad-viṣayaṁ cāsau bhāsayet tūrṇam ekadā \|\|16\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because the power of extraordinary objects is inconceivable,** ***rati*** **and the** ***viṣaya*** **of** ***rati*** **simultaneously appear immediately.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One may are that what is the capacity of sound or smell to produce *rati*? Objects such as jewels and herbs have special powers, what to speak of things related to Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“It is reasonable that knowing the object supporting the form (or smell*), rati* for that object should develop. But how can *rati* arise if one does not know the object which is the source of the sound or form?” This verse gives the answer to that doubt. Astonishing objects, spiritual objects, related to Kṛṣṇa have extraordinary powers. Those powers reveal *rati* and the *viṣaya* of rati *(tad-viṣayam),* at the same time, immediately.

### Text 17

***atha sambandhaḥ—***  
***sambandhaḥ kula-rūpādi-sāmagrī-gauravaṁ bhavet \|\|17\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Related items:** ***Sambandha*** **refers to excellence of the aggregate of noble family, beautiful form, and other good qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sambandha* means causes of a relationship. *Gauravam* means “excelling in.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sambandha* means excellence in family, beauty, bravery, good conduct all together, complete excellence in all these.

### Text 18

***tato yathā—***  
***vīryaṁ kandukitādir-rūpam akhila-kṣmā-maṇḍalī-maṇḍanaṁ***  
***janmābhīra-purandarasya bhavane pāre parārdhaṁ guṇāḥ \|***  
***līlā kvāpi jagac-camatkṛti-karīty etasya lokottarā***  
***vṛttir veṇu-dharasya durmukhi dhṛtiṁ kasyāḥ kṣaṇaṁ rakṣati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: By his strength he treated Govardhana like a ball. By his beauty he decorates the whole earth. He took birth in the house of the king of the cowherds. His qualities cannot be enumerated. His pastimes astonish the universe. O foul-mouthed friend! What girl is able to keep her peaceful composure for a moment in meeting the extraordinary qualities of the flute player?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“A woman of your family has no right to have *rati* for the supreme person.” When one *sakhī* tests another by saying this, the other *sakhī* replies with this verse. O foul-mouthed friend! You say whatever comes into your mouth. You have no intelligence. He has an extraordinary nature *(vṛttiḥ*). Because he treated the mountain as a toy ball, he has great prowess. His qualities cannot be enumerated (*parārdham pāre guṇāḥ*). Though I protect my self-control by not meditating on the qualities just mentioned, I am forced to remember them on hearing the flute, and those qualities produce *rati* in me.

### Text 19

***atha abhimānaḥ—***  
***santu ramyāṇi bhūrīṇi prārthyaṁ syād idam eva me \|***  
***iti yo nirṇayo dhīrair abhimānaḥ sa ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The conviction “I desire only him, without regard for pleasant objects” is called** ***abhimāna*** **by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The essence of *abhimāna* is constant possessiveness which is deep and long-standing. It produces *rati* without dependence on beauty or other items. Other things are disregarded.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Abhimāna* is a precise decision filled with extraordinary exclusiveness for the object of possessiveness. It produces *rati* without regard for beauty or other items. Though it is distinguished from *svabhāva,* which will be explained later, one should think of the difference as follows. *Abhimāna* has dependence on external causes whereas *svabhāva* is independent of external causes. Among *sādhaka* devotees one may have exclusiveness for the Lord arising from appropriate association and teachings whereas another devotee may have natural attraction.

### Text 20

***tato yathā—***  
***sphurantu bahavaḥ kṣitau madhurimormi-dhaureyakā***  
***vidagdha-maṇayo guṇāvali-patiṁ-varābhir vṛtāḥ \|***  
***na yasya śikhi-candraṁ śirasi naiva veṇur mukhe***  
***na dhātu-vacanā tanau sakhi tṛṇāya manye na tam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: On this earth there may be many men with the highest waves of sweetness, who are jewels of cleverness, and who accepted by virtuous girls. O friend! I consider anyone without the peacock-feather on his head, without the flute in his mouth, and without mineral pigments on his body to be less than a blade of grass.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is shown by showing the opposite. By showing what she does not accept, she indicates that only Kṛṣṇa can be accepted. By giving mentioned some of his qualities, she indicates Kṛṣṇa. But these are not given exhaustively. Even if Kṛṣṇa does not have these characteristics, as when eating or sleeping, her *rati* does not stop. But if another person does not have these characteristics, he is not suitable as an object of *rati.* O friend! I do not consider such a person as much as a blade of grass. By her particular type of utterance (expressing her *abhimāna) rati* appears. These are words to a *sakhī* who understands her mind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

O friend! Rādhā speaks to Nāndīmukhī who jokes with her, testing her *prema.* “You should give up Kṛṣṇa, who has many lovers, has no love for you, indulges in rough behavior and is lusty.” There may be many men possessing *(dhaureyakā*) sweet waves of love or who are the best among the clever, who marry women with the best qualities. These men do not expect great qualities but all qualities take shelter of them. There are the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Rāmacandra and others as well. Among them, I have taste for none. What to speak of taste, hear what is on my mind. They are all less than grass.

### Text 21

***atha tadīya-viśeṣāḥ—***  
***tadīyānāṁ viśeṣāḥ syuḥ pada-goṣṭha-priyādayaḥ \|\|21\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Dear objects include his feet, the cow pastures and associates.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Among the special items these are some.

### Text 22

***tatra padāni—***  
***padāny atra padāṅkāḥ syuḥ \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Whe word “feet” means footprints.**

### Text 23

***tato yathā—***  
***sphurati sakhi rathāṅgāmbhoja-dambholi-bhājāṁ***  
***taṭa-bhuvi viśadeyaṁ kasya paṅktiḥ padānām \|***  
***hṛdayam aghṛṇa-ghūrṇāghrātam udghāṭayantī***  
***mama tanu-latikāyāṁ kuḍmalaṁ yā tanoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! Whose bright footprints are these on the bank of the Yamunā, marked with the signs of the chariot-wheel, lotus and thunderbolt? These footprints cause painful agitation in my heart and make the hairs on the creeper of my body blossom.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some newly married woman, coming for the first time to Vraja, enters Vṛndāvana and speaks with wonder. Those footprints make the heart full of disturbance *(ghūrṇa)* which is merciless or causes pain *(aghṛṇa).* That is possible, but that pain produces buds on the creeper of my body. My hairs stand on end. Buds on a creeper do not blossom from pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. Those footprints fill my heart with great disturbance without mercy (*aghṛṇā*) and make it visible to others. They make my hairs stand on end out of bliss. This is astonishing. In this way she informs her *sakhī* that her *rati* has appeared since her *sakhī* has asked about her condition.

### Text 24

***atha goṣṭham—***  
***goṣṭhaṁ vṛndāvanāśritam \|\|24\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Goṣṭha*** **refers to Vṛndāvana.**

### Text 25

***tato, yathā—***  
***madayati hṛdayaṁ sakhi vrajo’yaṁ***  
***madhurimabhiḥ kvacid apy adṛṣṭa-pūrvaiḥ \|***  
***iha viharati ko’pi nāgarendaras***  
***tribhuvana-maṇḍala-mūrtir ity avehi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! This land of Vraja intoxicates my heart with unprecedented sweetness. In this place, an indescribable king of cunning, the ornament of the three worlds, sports.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A new bride form another place brought to Nanda-vraja to live after being married with a cowherd developed *bhāva* just by touching the land of Vraja. She speaks to her friend. This land gives joy (*madayati*) to my heart, making me insane. Experiencing an appearance of Kṛṣṇa in her heart, unseen by others, knowing the truth, she informs this to her *sakhī* by saying “In this place a certain cunning boy sports.” The place has a special power. It is thus a cause of *rati.* It was said “the power of objects produces *rati* and the *viṣaya* of *rati* at the same time, immediately.” (verse 16)

### Text 26

***atha priyajanaḥ—***  
***prauḍha-bhāvānubiddho yas tasya priya-jano’tra saḥ \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Priyajana*** **refers to a person who is overcome with the deepest love.**

### Text 27

***tato, yathā—***  
***gurubhir niṣiddhā tām ahaṁ yāvad akṣṇoḥ***  
***padam anayam ananta-śreyasāṁ sadma rādhām \|***  
***tṛṣitam iva mano me prekṣate tanvi tāvad***  
***diśi diśi viharantīṁ śyāmalāṁ śālabhañjīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O slender friend! My elders have forbidden me to see Rādhā, but whenever my eyes see Rādhā, the abode of all auspiciousness, my thirsty heart sees the dark form of Kṛṣṇa sporting everywhere.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are the words of someone who is coming for the first time to her father-in-law’s house near Vṛṣabhānu’s house. Nanda’s house however is far off, since the place measures eight *krośas.* Because they see that her heart becomes agitated on mentioning Kṛṣṇa, the elders forbid her seeing him. Fearing she will become stunned in meeting anyone who associates with Kṛṣṇa, they also forbid her to see Rādhā, when she comes to her father’s house. But having seen her on some occasion, she speaks to her friend. Rādhā has unlimited good qualities. She spreads her beauty everywhere. How astonishing! My thirsty mind sees Kṛṣṇa. *Śālabhañjī* means a statue.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“O my daughter-in-law! Though Rādhā was born in a great family, she is now insane. Do not associate with her.” Thus forbidden by her mother-in-law and others who are afraid of Kṛṣṇa, the girl managed to see Rādhā and developed *bhāva.* She speaks to a friend who asks the reason for her disturbed behavior. Experiencing the happiness of *prema* for Rādhā she praises her infinite goodness. She hints at Rādhā’s powers. “My mind sees Kṛṣṇa.” She has developed *anurāga* for Kṛṣṇa.  *Śālabhañjīm* means an image or statue.

### Text 28

***atha upamā—***  
***yathā kathañcid apy asya sādṛśyam upamoditā \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When an object has some similarity to another it is called** ***upamā*** **(resembling object).**

### Text 29

***tato, yathā—***  
***navāmbudhara-mādhurī sphurati mūrtir urvī-tale***  
***kṛśodari dṛśor iyāt pathi kim īdṛśo vā yuvā \|***  
***puraḥ sumukhi gopateḥ sadai sanniviṣṭasya me***  
***pitur vitanute naṭo yam anukṛtya nṛtya-kramam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O slender-waisted friend! He has a form with the sweetness of a fresh cloud! Have you ever seen the youth on earth whom this actor is portraying with dance in the assemply in front of my father, leader of the cowherds?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rati, to be aroused from previous intense *sādhana*, taking an object which is similar as a step, brings that love into awareness and gives pleasure.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A young girl, daughter of a cowherd leader in another province, seeing some actor dancing in the assembly through the lattice holes, speaks with astonishment to a friend. *Kim* indicates a question. O slender-waisted friend! Have the path of your eyes attained *(iyāt*) such a youth. If you know him, take me to his place. After seeing him only I can live. This indicates appearance of her *rati.* The actor, showing through acting Kṛṣṇa’s nature and actions (*anukṛtya*), dances.

### Text 30

***yathā vā—***  
***sphuraty eṣa preyān iva nava-ghanas tasya subhage***  
***śikhaṇḍīnāṁ śreṇīṁ tulayati surendrāyudham idam \|***  
***asau vāso lakṣmīr iva viharate vidyud iti sā***  
***niśamyodasrākṣī tvayi nihita-buddhir nivasati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Anotherr example: “O beautiful friend! This new cloud appears like my lover. This rainbow is like his peacock feathers. The lighting plays like his brilliant cloth.” Saying this with tears in her eyes, she remains with her heart fixed on you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The actor imitating Kṛṣṇa can never be compared with Kṛṣṇa. Such comparisons are only means to an end. What to speak of comparing material objects, as in this verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having shown an example of deliberate imitation, now the author gives an example of similarity of common objects. Vṛndā informs Kṛṣṇa of a girl of Vraja in whom she has produced *rati* for Kṛṣṇa. She lives with her heart dedicated to you (*tvayi nihita-buddhiḥ*). What are the qualities of that lover? He appears like a new cloud, like Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 31

***atha svabhāvaḥ—***  
***bhair hetv-anapekṣī tu svabhāvo’rthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|***  
***nisargaś ca svarūpaṁ cety eṣo’pi bhavati dvidhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**That which does not depend on external causes but appears on its own is called** ***svabhāva*** **or nature. There are two types of** ***svabhāva: nisarga*** **and** ***svarūpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If it gradually appears on its own, it is called *svabhāva.*

**Комментарий. Автор :**

Among the causes of *rati* starting with *abhiyoga* is *svabhāva.* But as a cause it is like comparing an object to itself (causelessness as a cause). *Svabhāva* indicates that *rati* in this case has no cause. Since it is said there is no natural *rati,* a cause of *rati* is sought. However, it will later be explained that causes like *abhiyoga* are not really causes. All types of *rati* have no cause. That is the correct conclusion. The causes have been mentioned only for conventions’ sake.

### Text 32

***atra nisargaḥ—***  
***nisargaḥ sudṛḍhābhyāsa-janyaḥ saṁskara ucyate \|***  
***tad-udbhodhasya hetuḥ syād guṇa-rūpa-śrutir manāk \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An impression created by firm practice is called** ***nisarga*****. Hearing about the qualities and form of the Lord are a slight cause for its appearance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The general characteristic in relation to *madhura-rati* is given, since this *rati* reaches perfection only after many births. That very firm practice of *madhura-rati* which appears repeatedly with increased strength, and which, though disappearing for many lifetimes, remains as a subtle impression to produce *rati* later on, is called *nisarga*. This is similar to the good and bad *karmas* which remain dormant during deep sleep. With awakening and strengthening of *madhura-rati* which was situated in the state of impressions, hearing about the qualities and form of Kṛṣṇa become insignificant as the cause of its arousal. It does not depend on external causes. Thus this does not contradict the general definition of *svabhāva.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“External causes of *rati* are qualities (*sambandha*), similar items (*upamā*) or dear objects of the Lord (*tadīya*). Internal causes are hearing about the Lord and other processes. Though *rati* is said to be without cause and not dependent, it depends on these internal causes.” That is true. In the portion called *nisarga* there is some dependence on a semblance of internal cause. Thus the verse says “the cause of its arousal, the cause of *nisarga*, is hearing about the Lord.”

The impression is created by firm practice, but it is actually *nitya-siddha.* The impressions created by this practice are actually a continuous stream (not created). The impressions bring about hearing of Kṛṣṇa’s form and qualities by means of the *līlā-śakti.* Thus it is caused in name only. Therefore the word *manag* (slight) is added.

### Text 33

***tato, yathā—***  
***sa tarjatu batāgrajaṁ tyajatu māṁ suhṛn-maṇḍalaḥ***  
***pitā kila vilajjatāṁ ghana-dṛg-ambur ambāstu me \|***  
***manaḥ sakhi samīhate śruta-guṇa-śriyaṁ sarvathā***  
***tam eva yadu-puṅgavaṁ na tu kadāpi caidyaṁ nṛpam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! My elder brother may rebuke me, my friends may reject me, my father may become embarrassed, and my mother may cry. But my mind has become attracted to the best of the Yadus, whose profuse glories I have heard. It can never be attracted to Śiśupāla.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Hearing Kṛṣṇa’s qualities is an *uddīpana* not a cause of *rati.* The cause is Kṛṣṇa himself. The word *yadu-puṅgavaṁ* is both an *uddīpana* and a cause of *rati.* This is a statement made by Rukmiṇī.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rukmiṇī expresses her firmness to her friend who tests her *prema* by saying, “It is not proper for a girl of good family, with extreme shyness to write love letters expressing your attachment to a man not approved by your friends.” While hearing topics of *dharma* from Nārada, she heard about Kṛṣṇa’s qualities. This awakened her *nitya-siddha* nature.

### Text 34

***yathā vā—***  
***asundaraḥ sundara-śekharo vā***  
***guṇair vihīno guṇināṁ varo vā \|***  
***dveṣī mayi syāt karuṇāmbudhir vā***  
***śyāmaḥ sa evādya gatir mamāyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Śyāma may be ugly or may be best of handsome men. He may be devoid of all good qualities or be the best of men with good qualities. He may hate me or he may be an ocean of mercy to me. Today he is my goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The *rati* of Rukmiṇī is *svarūpa-siddha-rati* of an eternal consort. Now the author shows *nisarga* that produces *rati* in other women, where hearing about the qualities and form of the Lord are unnecessary.  *Abhimāna* was shown in verse 20. Without *rati* such statements would depend on eagerness arising from instructions from *guru.* By that *abhimāna, rati* arose.
