Though Kṛṣṇa and Śyāmalā both have *sneha* for each other, because his heart become stunned, he has more *sneha.* That is Śyāmalā’s good fortune. This is also hinted.

### Text 85

***śravaṇe, yathā—***  
***śruti-parisara-kakṣāṁ yāti nāmnas tavārdhe***  
***muradamana dṛgambhodārayā dhauta-gātrī \|***  
***madana-mada-madhūlī-mugdha-medhā-samṛddhiḥ***  
***skhalati kuvalayākṣī jṛmbhate stambhate ca \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Heart melting by hearing: O Kṛṣṇa! When the sound of half your name enters her ears, tears at once stream from her lotus eyes wash all her limbs. Her great intelligence is destroyed by the liquor of intoxicating love, and lotus-eyed Rādhā stumbles about, yawns, and becomes stunned.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. The symptoms of *sneha* are the melting of the mind and the tears flowing from her eyes. She has a wealth of intelligence which loses its discrimination by the liquor of intoxicating love.

### Text 86

***ādi-śabdena smaraṇe, yathā—***  
***kṛṣṇa-vartmani kṛtābhiniveśo***  
***sāmprataḥ tvam asi kampita-gātrī \|***  
***sneha-pūra-paripāka-mayaṁ te***  
***kiṁ bhaviṣyati mano na vilīnam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The word** ***ādi*** **indicates melting of the heart by remembrance: Now you have approached the path traveled by Kṛṣṇa, since your limbs have begun to tremble. Has your mind, ripe with profuse affection, not melted with love?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī, seeing Rādhā suddenly covered in tears, speaks. *Kṛṣṇa-vartmani* means “in fire” or “on the path of Kṛṣṇa.” You have entered fire because your limbs are trembling out of feeling cold or you have entered Kṛṣṇa’s path because your limbs are trembling from *sāttvika-bhāva*. Will such a mind not be destroyed? Entering fire means she is burning with love. You should take precautions about staying in that condition. Or, has such a mind not melted, since this is inferred by the tears flowing externally?

### Text 87

***sa ghṛtaṁ madhu cetyuktaṁ sneho dvedhā svarūpataḥ \|\|87\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sneha*** **has two essential forms: ghee** ***(ghṛta*****) and honey (*****madhu*****).**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sneha* takes on different names with different tastes because of different types. *Sneha* can be like ghee or like honey. Since *sneha* means melting of the heart, that melting can be like ghee melting or honey melting. Thus the names are given. This *sneha* has two types, ghee and honey, because of their natures (*svarūpataḥ*). The word *svataḥ* should be understood. Some have melting of the heart like ghee and some have melting of the heart like honey. Because of difference in hearts, *sneha* is different. This is the simple way to understand this. Though something may be tasty, by cooking, it becomes tastier. One can say that the specialty of the food becomes apparent by the cooking. Similarly the author, with desire to describe the specialty of *sneha* in its aspect of melting the heart, has described that taste as tasty like ghee or tasty like honey. When food is cooked and becomes like nectar. Similarly, the object *sneha,* and its quality of taste, become equivalent on melting.

### Text 88

***tatra ghṛta-snehaḥ—***  
***ātyantikādara-mayaḥ sneho ghṛtam itīryate \|\|88\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sneha*** **filled with great respect is called** ***ghrṭa-sneha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

There is respect in *madhu-sneha* also.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Gṛhta-sneha* has more respect than *madhu-sneha*. There some amount of respect in *madhu-sneha* also. Rādhā has slightly more respect for Kṛṣṇa than her *sakhīs* or the *priya-sakhīs* or Subala.

### Text 89

***bhāvāntarānvito gacchan svādodrekaṁ na tu svayam \|***  
***ghanībhaven nisargāti-śītalān mitha ādarāt \|***  
***gāḍhādara-mayas tena snehaḥ syād ghṛtavad ghṛtam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When** ***ghṛta-sneha*** **mixes with a shadow of** ***madhu-sneha*** **it becomes tasty, a quality that it does not have on its own.**

**From the respect in the woman, with equal respect from the man, it becomes thick because of its natural extreme coolness.** ***Sneha*** **filled with deep respect takes on qualities like ghee.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though *rati* was described as most sweet in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,* this *rati* is called sweet to show its very intense sweetness. But by seeing Rādhā and Lalitā who taste the highest sweet *sneha,* it is understood that the *sneha* with great respect is not as attractive. That is explained in this verse.

*Bhāvāntara* refers to a temporary shadow of *madhu-sneha.* When *ghṛta-sneha* mixes with that shadow of *madhu-sneha,* it becomes tastier because of its new superiority. It is said that great respect found in the woman is the *aṅga* of this type of *sneha*. When the man sees that respect, because of the respect in the woman who is endowed with that strong respect as a woman, it becomes thick. But it is desirable that the respect of the hero be great as well. *Mithaḥ* means “attains equality.” This happens because of *ghṛta-sneha’s* natural coolness. The hero’s respect for the woman has natural coolness and does not have a portion of heat such as anger at all, which is seen in women. This is the opinion of Bharata Muni. Because of this, *sneha* filled with great respect is like ghee. It becomes ghee. This means it appears to have the nature of ghee.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse shows how the *sneha* is like ghee. When there is a mixing with a shadow of *madhu-sneha*, because of a slight appearance of heat in the form of passion, as in mixing sugar with ghee, it becomes very tasty. This means that ghee alone is tasty but this mixture is tastier. When both the man and the woman have respect for each other, *sneha* becomes thick. Otherwise it is dilute.

### Text 90

***yathā—***  
***abhutthāya vidūrato madhubhñdā yāśliṣyate sādaraṁ***  
***yā snehena vaśīkaroti guruṇā pāvitrya-pūrṇena tam \|***  
***kṣipraṁ yāti sitopaleva vilayaṁ tat-keli-vṛṣṭyā ca yā***  
***yuktā hanta kayopamātum api sā candrāvalī me sakhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Seeing her from afar, Kṛṣṇa at once respectfully rises and embraces Candrāvalī. With her very pure** ***sneha*** **she brings Kṛṣṇa completely under her control. By the shower of her playfulness she quickly melts him just as rock candy dissolves. Oh! Who can be compared to Candrāvalī?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Candrāvalī’s *sneha* is pure, without the fault of passion, which is heating. This is a statement of envy directed to the *madhu-sneha* of her friend.  *Sitopalā* is rock candy, white candied sugar, appearing like sea salt. Though he is hard, by the absence of anger in us, he becomes soft.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks in the assembly of young women, while glancing angrily at Lalitā, while indicating her good fortune. Candrāvalī has great quantity of *sneha* which is pure, without mixture of the heat of passion. This is a criticism of *madhu-sneha. Sitopalā* is rock candy which quickly dissolves. This statement indicates the oneness of heart and body of the couple.

### Text 91

***yathā vā—***  
***nijam agharipuṇāṁse nyastam ākṛṣya savyaṁ***  
***bhujam iha nidadhānā dakṣam asrokṣitākṣī \|***  
***pada-yugam api baṅkaṁ śaṅkayā vikṣipantī***  
***pratiyuvati-vayasyāṁ smerayāmāsa gaurī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When Kṛṣṇa placed Candrāvalī's left arm around his shoulder, Candrāvalī, thinking her left arm impure, with tearful eyes retracted it and placed her right arm there. But in moving to do so, her feet became bent out of fear that they would touch Kṛṣṇa. She caused Rādhā’s** ***sakhīs*** **to smile.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The previous verse showed the excellence of *ghṛta-sneha* through the words of a *sakhī* having that *sneha.* Now the superiority of *madhu-sneha* over *ghṛta-sneha* is shown through the experience of Rādhā’s *sakhī*. *Baṅkam* means crooked. The opposing party of young girls is actually the party of the speaker, but to distinguish herself from them she speaks in this way to hide her animosity to them. The meaning is “It is slander of the other party, done by us.” *Smerayam āsa* can be replaced by *smārayām āsa* (made laugh), which is easily understood.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse clearly shows the respect given to Kṛṣṇa in the pastimes of the women with *ghṛta-sneha* through actions. Vṛndā describes to Nāndīmukhī how Kṛṣṇa took Candrāvalī among the group to dance after dancing with her alone in the *rāsa-līlā*. When Kṛṣṇa put her left arm on his shoulder, Candrāvalī thought her left arm was inauspicious. How can I put my left arm on his shoulder?” She withdrew her left arm and placed her right arm on his shoulder, going from his right side to his left side to do so. But in going, her two feet became bent. She became afraid that her feet would touch Kṛṣṇa’s body. Some of Rādhā’s *sakhīs,* seeing this from a distance, smiled.

### Text 92

***ādaro gauravotthaḥ syād ity anyonyāśrita-dvayam \|***  
***ratyādau sad api snehe suvyaktatvād ihocyate \|\|92\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Respect (*****ādara*****) arises from thinking a person is respectable (*****gauravam).*** ***Ādara*** **and** ***gauravam*** **take shelter of each other. Though respect arises in** ***rati*****, because it becomes evident in** ***sneha*****, it has been described in** ***sneha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What is respect? *Gauravam* means thinking the person is respectable. The *bhāva* arising from that is called *sambhrama* or respect (*ādara*). Why is it not simply called *gauravam*? It is because *(iti)* of this: *ādara* and *gauravam* take shelter of each other. Therefore *gaurava* also comes from *ādara.* They cannot be separated. “But *gauravam* and *ādara* must exist in *rati* since the qualities in the cause produce qualities in the effect. Why should we say it appears in *sneha*? ” It becomes distinct in *sneha.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“What is the cause of *ādara* (respect)?” It arises from *gauravam.* “What is the cause of *gauravam*? Candrāvalī does not think Kṛṣṇa is great (*gauravam*) from being God. Where does her respect come from?” Because Kṛṣṇa is respected in all of Vraja, that respect gives rise to *gauravam*. They arise from each other (*anyonyāśrita-dvayam*). “If that is so, then respect must be present in *rati* and *prema*.” That is true. It exists in *rati.* The meaning is this. When it is well recognized, respect *(ādara*) becomes designated. Then it is considered. Though it exists in *rati* and *prema* it may not be perceived because of not being recognized by Kṛṣṇa. Thus it is not described. However, it is recognized very well in *sneha.* It is seen that Candrāvalī’s respect (*ādara*) for Kṛṣṇa is very strong. It is very evident there.

### Text 93-94

***Atha madu-sneha***  
***madīyatātiśaya-bhāk priye sneho bhaven madhu \|***  
***svayaṁ prakaṭa-mādhuryo nānā-rasa-samāhṛtiḥ \|\|93\|\|***  
***mattatoṣma-dharaḥ sneho madhu-sāmyān madhūcyate \|\|94\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Madhu-sneha*****:** ***Sneha*** **is called** ***madhu*** **when the lover thinks “You are mine.” This** ***sneha*** **is called** ***madhu*** **because it is similar to honey in that it is naturally sweet, it possesses various** ***bhāvas,*** **it intoxicates with bliss and it causes heating.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This has extreme possessiveness. The following should be understood. The appearance of *rati* has two types: “I am his” and “he is mine.” *Ghṛta-sneha* has the thought “I am his.” *Madhu-sneha* has the very strong thought “He is mine.” Both types of *sneha* have intense feeling, but the possessiveness in *madhu-sneha* overshadows the intense feelings in *ghṛta-sneha*. Therefore the word “very” was not used in describing *ghrṭa-sneha.* However the very strong feeling of respect (*ādara*) in *ghṛta-sneha* is the cause of thinking “I am his.”

There are various tastes in *madhu-sneha*. In *madhu-sneha* there exists subtly various *bhāvas* such as *lalitā* which will be explained later, which are not available in *ghṛta-sneha. Bhāva* is considered *rasa* here (*nānā-rasa-samāhṛtiḥ)* since it is said:

*bhāvāḥ sarve tad-ābhāsā rasābhāsāś ca kecana \|*  
*amī prokta-rasābhijñaiḥ sarve’pi rasanād rasāḥ \|\|*

**Some experts in** ***rasa*** **say that all** ***bhāvas,*** **even** ***bhāvābhāsas*** **and** ***rasābhāsas*** **are** ***rasa*** **since they are enjoyable. BRS 4.9.41**

Or, there is variety in *rasa* because of nourishment from various causes. *Mattatā* means transformations because of bliss. “Warmth” will be discussed. This *sneha* creates warmth (*uṣma-dharaḥ*) and intoxication of bliss (*mattatā*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Madhu-sneha* is endowed with extreme possessiveness of Kṛṣṇa. “He is mine.” *Ghṛha-sneha* has the mood “I am his.” It was said:

*sarvathā dhvaṁsa-rahitaṁ saty api dhvaṁsa-kāraṇe \|*  
*yad-bhāva-bandhanaṁ yūnoḥ sa premā parikīrtitaḥ \|\|*

**When the relationship of love between the couple remains always without destruction when there are causes for destroying it, it is called** ***prema.*** **14.63**

This relation of love is either “I am his” or “He is mine.” When the former thought is stronger, and the heart melts, it is *ghṛta-sneha*. When the second thought is stronger and the heart melts it is called *madhu-sneha*. Actually both exist simultaneously in a person, but according to the prominent factor the name is given. *Ghṛta-sneha* is “I am his” and *madhu-sneha* is “He is mine.” The cause of both is described in the section of the difference between one’s party and the opposing party.

Sweetness appears on its own in *madhu-sneha*. This is unlike *ghṛta-sneha* which becomes tasty by mixing with other *bhāvas.* In terms of *sneha* there are various tastes like crookedness and joking. In terms of honey, there are various tastes by taking nectar from various flowers. *Madhu-sneha* is filled with bliss (*mattatā*) because there are no obstructions of other things and creates heat or pride. And by drinking honey it is well known that one becomes hot and intoxicated.

### Text 95

***yathā—***  
***rādhā snehamayena hanta racitā mādhurya-sāreṇa sā***  
***saudhīva pratimā ghanāpy uru-guṇair bhāvoṣmaṇā vidrutā \|***  
***yan-nāmany api dhāmani śravaṇayor yāti prasaṅgena me***  
***sāndrānandamayī bhavaty anupamā sadyo jagad-vismṛti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Though Rādhā is like a statue of nectar fashioned from** ***sneha,*** **the essence of sweetness, and is thick with many qualities, burning with longing with thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, she remains completely liquid. When her name enters my ears by accident, I become immediately filled with incomparable concentrated bliss and I forget the existence of the entire world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though she is thick with many excellent *bhāvas* like *lalitā,* she is burning with longing to please Kṛṣṇa by thoughts about his qualities. By that she remains in liquid form. Kṛṣṇa forgets everything except her.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. She is concentrated like a statue of nectar but is liquid by the heat of longing. How much is that? I have my experience to witness it. Just hearing her name it transforms me. *Śravaṇayor dhāmani* means the ear holes.  *Yāti* is a participle equivalent to *gacchati sati.*

### Text 96

***atha mānaḥ—***  
***snehas tūtkṛṣṭatāvāptyā mādhuryaṁ mānayan navam \|***  
***yo dhārayaty adākṣiṇyaṁ sa māna iti kīrtyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Māna:*** **When, attaining excellence,** ***sneha,*** **melting of the heart, takes up** ***vāmyam*** **(non-cooperation) to hide one’s intentions, and gives the experience of fresh sweetness, it is called** ***māna.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Non-cooperation (*adakṣiṇyam)* is external. When *sneha* manifests crookedness it is called *māna*. What does it do? It reveals or gives the experience (*mānayan)* of a special taste of sweetness previously unexperience (*navam*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When, attaining excellence, *sneha,* melting of the heart, takes up *vāmyam* to hide one’s intentions, and gives the experience of fresh sweetness, it is called *māna.*

### Text 97

***yathā—***  
***sravad-asra-bhare kṛte dṛśau me***  
***tava godhūlibhir eva gopa-vīra \|***  
***adhunā vadanānilaiḥ kim ebhir***  
***virameti bhrūkuṭiṁ babhāra subhrūḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Rādhā with beautiful eyebrows frowned and said, “My eyes are full of tears because of the dust raised by the cows. O hero of the cowherds! Please stop blowing on my eye.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Playing with Kṛṣṇa in the forest, Rādhā became covered with tears because her heart melted to the extreme. She scolds Kṛṣṇa about the dust raised by cows in the distance to hide her feelings (*avahitthā*). “Then come to me. By blowing wind from my mouth I will cool your eyes.” When he was about to do this, she answered, “Stop that.” How can I be pleased with that (*false) prema* manifesting in your face?

### Text 98

***udātto lalitaś ceti māno’yaṁ dvividho mataḥ \|\|98\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Māna*** **has two types:** ***udātta*** **and** ***lalita.***

### Text 99

***tatra udāttaḥ—***  
***udāttaḥ syād ghṛta-sneho dhārayan gahana-kramam \|***  
***dākṣiṇya-bhāga-adākṣiṇyaṁ vāmya-gandhaṁ ca kutracit \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Udātta: Udātta*** **is** ***ghṛta-sneha*** **which either hides its non-cooperation (*****adākṣiṇyam*****) and shows gentleness, or which manifests non-cooperation as slight** ***vāmya.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ghṛta-sneha* which hides the anger with gentleness, which covers the real state of mind out of profundity (*gāmbhīrya*) or which is *ghṛta-sneha* with a touch of *vāmya,* a slight display of anger externally, is called *udātta.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

From the definition of *sneha,* two types of *māna* occur. *Udātta* takes two forms. It appears gentle, hiding the real state of mind, non-cooperation (a*dakṣiṇyam*). By hiding feelings (*avahitthā*) the woman shows gentleness but lacks this internally. That is one type. When the non-cooperative attitude is hidden but mainfests as slight *vāmya*—outward slight *vāmya* and inside full non-cooperation (*sampuṛṇa adākṣiṇyam)*—it is the second type. *Adākṣiṇyaṁ* means non-cooperation. This takes two forms: with external show cooperation *(dākṣiṇyam*) and with external show of slight *vāmya*. One should not say that only the latter type is *udātta* since the main characteristic of *udātta* is having non-cooperation *(adākṣiṇyam*) (which may show externally or not). As well because it is suitable that the external show of slight *vāmya* is present in the best women during *rati, prema* and *sneha,* it is understood that they must have complete non-cooperation (*sampuṛṇa adākṣiṇyam*).

Manifestation of non-cooperation (*adākṣiṇyam*) takes place in *madhu-sneha* and non-manifestation takes place in *ghṛta-sneha.* Unmanifested non-cooperation takes two forms of *dākṣinyodātta* (hiding it completely) and *vāmya-gandhodātta* (slight manifested as *vāmya).*

### Text 100

***tatra dākṣiṇyodātto, yathā—***  
***rādheti skhalitābhidhe mayi haṭhād biddhāntarāpy ārtibhir***  
***mad-vailakṣya-śamāya sā dviguṇayanty āsyāravinde smitam \|***  
***jalpe ca mradimānubiddham adhikaṁ mādhuryam ātanvatī***  
***citrāṇīva cakāra mat-priya-suhṛd-vṛndāni candrāvalī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of hiding** ***māna*** **by gentleness: When I accidentally said the word “Rādhā,” Candrāvalī was wounded internally with pain. However, in order to quell my confusion, she doubled the smiled and spoke tender words which produced sweetness. In this way she astonished my cowherd friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vailakṣya* means disturbance. She suddenly doubled the smile on her face. Instead of *mat-priya-suhṛd-vṛndāni* sometimes *sā priya-sakhī-vṛndāni* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Dākṣiṇyodātta* means *udātta* related *dākṣīṇya* and *vāmya-gandhodātta* means *udātta* related to *vāmya-gandha*. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Kundavallī. *Vailaksya* means disturbance. Suddenly her smile doubled. His friends became astonished. “Is she pleased with breaking the family traditions or not?” They became stunned, appearing like painted pictures. *Amara-koṣa* says *citra* means astonishing and a picture. This is an example of *māna* with cause. Causeless and causal *māna* will be discussed later. First her heart melted, because of pain, and developed *māna*. She hid both pain and *māna* by her smile.

### Text 101

***atha vāmya-gandhodātto, yathā śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe (5.13.45)***  
***kācid bhrū-bhaṅguraṁ kṛtvā lalāṭa-phalakaṁ harim \|***  
***vilokya netra-bhṛṅgābhyāṁ papau tan-mukha-paṅkajam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Manifesting slight** ***vāmya,*** **from** ***Viṣṇu Purāṇa:*** **Frowning with her eyebrows on her forehead, a** ***gopī*** **stared at Kṛṣṇa, and the two bees of her eyes drank his lotus face.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Drinking his face with her eyes indicates her *dākṣīnya* nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Parāśara describes the actions of an angry *gopī* when she sees Kṛṣṇa after he had disappeared during the *rāsa* dance. Her frowning indicates her slight *vāmya* mood and her eyes drinking the nectar of his face indicate her external *dākṣiṇya.* The past participle *kṛtvā* indicates that her frowning occurred first and was slight. She then glanced at his face. This is in the past tense, indicating a continuous action of drinking, that her eyes like bees were attached to the lotus of his face. This indicates the fullness of her *dākṣiṇya.* This is thus an example *vāmya-gandhodātta*. In the following verse internal *adākṣīnya* is illustrated since the *gopī* goes to Kṛṣṇa’s side and touches his body (in spite of her anger):

*kācit karāmbujaṁ śaurer jagṛhe ’ñjalinā mudā*  
*kācid dadhāra tad-bāhum aṁse candana-bhūṣitam*

**One** ***gopī*** **joyfully took Kṛṣṇa’s hand between her folded palms, and another placed his arm, anointed with sandalwood paste, on her shoulder. SB 10.32.4**

In the present verse, seeing him after a long time, out of anger her heart melted. This is thus *māna.*

### Text 102

***yathā vā—***  
***akṣa-saṁsadi jitāpi mṛgākṣī***  
***mādhavena parirambha-paṇena \|***  
***bhugna-dṛṣṭir iha vipratipannā***  
***taṁ kareṇa rurudhe pariripsum \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Though she lost the dice-game, the doe-eyed** ***gopī*****, opposing this, frowned and stopped Mādhava with one hand when he tried to embrace her as the prize.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

She stopped him with one hand instead of two. This indicates s light *vāmya.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Since the inner *adākṣiṇyam* was not clear in the last verse, another example is given. A *sakhī* of Candrāvalī speaks to someone. At the gambling match with dice, whose prize was an embrace, though she was defeated by Kṛṣṇa, she frowned. This is her external show of a trace of *vāmya.* She stopped him with one hand, not two hands. This shows her *dākṣiṇyam.* Even though it is not possible to stop the man with both hands, it would be proper concealment of her *dākṣiṇya* tendency. Stopping him with one hand she does not conceal herself properly, and shows *dākṣiṇyam.* She was opposed (*vipratipannā).* This indicates inner non-cooperation.

### Text 103

***atha lalitaḥ—***  
***madhu-snehas tu kauṭilyaṁ svātantrya-hṛdayaṅgamam \|***  
***bibhran-narma-viśeṣaṁ ca lalito’yam udīryate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Lalita:*** **When** ***madhu-sneha*** **takes on crookedness, flooding the heart with an independent nature, and displays joking, it is called** ***lalita.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Independence means the *svādhīna-bhartṛka* nature. By this the heart of the woman is flooded.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What is the crookedness? It floods her heart with an independent nature. *Ghṛta-sneha* does not flood the heart with an independent nature, but only partial affects the heart. Crookedness first manifests in the mind and body. Finally it appears in words as joking.

### Text 104

***tatra kauṭilya-lalito, yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.6)—***  
***ekā bhrū-kuṭim ābaddhya prema-saṁrambha-vihvalā \|***  
***ghnatīvaikṣat kaṭākṣepaiḥ sandaṣṭa-daśana-cchadā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Crookedness in** ***lalita*****, from the Tenth Canto: One** ***gopī,*** **agitated with loving anger, bit her lips and stared at him with frowning eyebrows, as if to wound him with her harsh glances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kaṭākṣepaiḥ* means with frowning glances.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śukadeva describes the actions of the *māna* of Rādhā; who sees Kṛṣṇa after he disappeared during the *rāsa* dance. She frowned heavily (*ābaddhya*) not lightly, as if stringing a bow. She was agitated with angry love. This indicates melting of the heart. She looked (*aikṣata*) at him by throwing glances, which were like arrows

### Text 105

***yathā vā—***  
***adatta me vartmani manmathonmadā***  
***svayaṁ grahāśleṣam asau sakhī tava \|***  
***ity uktavantaṁ kuṭilībhavan mukhī***  
***kṛṣṇaṁ vataṁsena jaghāna maṅgalā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Kṛṣṇa said, “Your passionate friend embraced me on this path.” Mangalā turned her head in shyness and struck him with her flower diadem.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse shows that *kauṭilya-lalita* arising from *madhu-sneha* exists in Rādhā’s *sakhīs.* A *sakhī* of Maṅgalā speaks to one of her friends. *Adatta* stands for *dadau* (gave). He said “Your friend gave me an embrace which I accepted.” By his was saying this, her heart melted. Her head became crooked out of shyness. This means she turned her head. Because she did not frown, she manifested very slight *dākṣiṇyam*. This small portion internal *dākṣiṇyam* indicates *kauṭilya-lalita.*

### Text 106

***yathā vā—***  
***citraṁ cira-sparśa-sukhāya cucuke***  
***kurvantam akṣipram iyaṁ calekṣaṇā \|***  
***svinnāṅgulīkaṁ pulakāñcita-śriyā***  
***savyena cikṣepa kucena keśavam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When, in order to taste the happiness of touching Rādhā’s breasts for a longer time, Keśava dallied in painting pictures on her breasts with perspiring fingers, restless-eyed Rādhā suddenly pushed him away using her left breast, which was covered with goose bumps.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This example is given to show that though there is some *dākṣiṇyam* in Rādhā’s *māna,* because she has pure *madhu-sneha*, it is filled with crookedness, and does not show a trace of *ghṛta-sneha*. Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to Rati-mañjarī. *Citram* refers to drawn patterns. His slowness in painting caused her *māna.* Her eyes were restless. She was worried that some intruder would see this. She drove him away by the force of her left breast. The left limbs of a woman are stronger than their right limbs. Not showing frowns or angry glances shows lack of crookedness or some *dākṣīṇyam.* Though pushing him with her breast shows boldness, it is not crookedness. She indicates “I will not let you paint my breasts since you do not know how to paint, but simply use your eyes. I will have my *sakhīs* do it.” She shows disrespect, and thus does not have *ghṛta-sneha*. Thus this *māna* is caused by pure *madhu-sneha* and though a small portion of *dākṣiṇya* is present, it is still pure *madhu-sneha* and most pleasurable.

### Text 107

***atha narma-lalito, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (90)—***  
***mithyā jalpatu te kathaṁ nu rasanā sādhvī-sahasrasya yā***  
***bimboṣṭhāmṛta-sevanād agharipo puṇyā prayatnād abhūt \|***  
***kasmād eva balāt-karotu ca karaḥ soḍhuṁ kṣamaḥ subhruvāṁ***  
***raktaḥ suṣṭhu na nivi-bandham api yaḥ kā vānya-bandhe kathā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Joking in** ***lalita,*** **from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: Kṛṣṇa! How can your tongue, which has been purified by touching the lips of nectar of thousands of chaste women, tell lies? How can your hand act with brutal force? Very attached, it simply cannot tolerate the bondage of the women’s garments. What to speak of tolerating other tied items!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Oh! What shall I do? My tongue does not know how to speak lies to anyone. My hand is opposed to violent action. You make my truthfulness and compassionate nature useless. These women refuse to pay the king’s tax.” When Kṛṣṇa’s says this, Lalitā replies with this verse. By drinking the nectar of thousands of women’s lips your tongue has become pure. It cannot speak lies, just like the *devatās* who drink nectar do not speak lies. Why should your hand act with such force? Your hand is simply most merciful. Filled with attachment (*rakta)* it cannot tolerate the tied-up garments of the women. The hand says“Oh! The waists of the women are suffering by being tied. I will free them.” The meaning is “Coming quickly, and though scolded and beaten by the women, not considering their insults, free our waists from the tied up clothes.” And what to speak of undoing other knots such as those in their braids. He unties those knots first just by his glance. These words are actually harsh criticism by taking the opposite meaning of the crooked words. Thus the words indicate his lying, mercilessness, and lust.

### Text 108

***atha praṇayaḥ—***  
***māno dadhāno viśrambhaṁ praṇayaḥ procyate budhaiḥ \|\|108\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When** ***māna*** **exhibits intimacy it is called** ***praṇaya*** **by the wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The characteristics of *praṇaya* are described. *Visrambha* means not making distinctions between oneself and the beloved.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Visrambha* means confidentiality, without reverence. This is caused by uniting one’s life airs, mind, intelligence, body and clothing with those of the beloved. In spite of this, anger and other emotions are not unsuitable, because of the nature of *rasa*.

### Text 109

***yathā—***  
***kucopānte spṛṣṭā mura-vijayinā tad-bhuja-śira-***  
***stiro-nyasta-grīvā bhruvam anṛju-dṛṣṭir vibhujatī \|***  
***paṭenāsya mlānīkṛta-puraṭa-bhāsā pulakinī***  
***pramodāsrair dhautaṁ nija-mukham iyaṁ mārṣṭi sumukhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When Kṛṣṇa touched her breast, she tilted her neck to rest on his shoulder. The hairs of her body standing on end, beautiful-faced Rādhā glanced sideways and wiped her face which was washed with tears of joy, using his yellow cloth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks on seeing from far the pastime of Rādhā experiencing happiness in the yard of the bower with Kṛṣṇa after being enjoyed and decorated by him. Her neck was turned, supporting itself on the left shoulder of Kṛṣṇa. She gazed with a crooked glance. This means that she looked at Kṛṣṇa from the side of her eye. She frowned. This shows *māna* because of her intolerance. Her tears of joy indicate melting of the heart. She wiped her face with Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth. This shows lack of reverence and their intimacy. Thus it is an example of *praṇaya.*

### Text 110

***svarūpaṁ praṇayasyāsya viśrambhaḥ kathito budhaiḥ \|***  
***viśrambho’pi dvidhā maitraṁ sakhyaṁ ceti nigadyate \|\|110\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The cause of** ***praṇaya*** **is said to be intimacy by the wise. Intimacy has two types:** ***maitra*** **and** ***sakhya.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse describes the cause of *praṇaya.* *Svarūpa* means cause. The meaning is this. It was already said that *māna* with intimacy was *praṇaya.* That meant that familiarity is one of its portions. It was not its cause. When vermilion is added to *haritāla,* it takes on an astonishing color. This is called *praṇaya. Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* explained the following, but that is a *taṭasha* quality:

*prāptāyāṁ sambhramādīnāṁ yogyatāyām api sphuṭam \|*  
*tad-gandhenāpy asaṁspṛṣṭā ratiḥ praṇaya ucyate \|\|*

**When** ***sakhya-rati*** **is completely free of any touch of respect, though there are clear opportunities to show respect, it is called** ***praṇaya.*** **BRS 3.3.108**

The two types are discussed as one. The two types of *visrambha* are discussed without differentiating the two types in order to show that they are both *praṇaya.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“It was just said that *māna* with intimacy becomes *praṇaya.* But it will later be explained that *sneha* produces *praṇaya* which produces *māna* (verse 119).” That is true. There are different types of *praṇaya.* Thus this verse points out the other type of *praṇaya.* In the first type *māna* manifests before *praṇaya* and in the second type, mentioned in this verse, it manifest after *praṇaya.*

### Text 111

***tatra maitraṁ—***  
***bhāvajñaiḥ procyate maitraṁ viśrambho vinayānvitaḥ \|\|111\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The wise say that intimacy endowed with modesty is called** ***maitram.***

### Text 112

***yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.4)–***  
***kācit karāmbujaṁ śaurer jagṛhe’ñjalināṁ mudā \|***  
***kācid dadhāra tad-bāhum aṁse candana-rūṣitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from the Tenth Canto: One** ***gopī*** **joyfully took Kṛṣṇa’s hand between her folded palms, and another placed his arm, anointed with sandalwood paste, on her shoulder.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śukadeva describes the actions of Candrāvalī who sees Kṛṣṇa after he disappeared from the *rāsa* dance. She took Kṛṣṇa’s hand, with intimacy. She put it between her palms. This indicates modesty.  *Māna* is present but in unclear form, because of the *dākṣiṇyam* present. It was explained in SB 10.32.15 that she has been slightly angry previously. It should be understood that on seeing Kṛṣṇa, her heart melted. The first *gopī* described in the present verse is Candrāvalī, and the second *gopīs* is Śyāmalā according to *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.* The other *gopī* places her hand on Kṛṣṇa’s shoulder, though he had previously withdrawn it. This shows lack of modesty.

### Text 113

***yathā vā—***  
***na hi saṅkuca paṅkajekṣaṇaḥ***  
***pādayos te nidadhātu nūpurau \|***  
***anayor dhvanibhir vilajjatāṁ***  
***kalahaṁsīva vipakṣa-kāminī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Do not shyly move back when lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa places bells around you ankles. The tinkling sounds of those bells should shame all your swanlike rivals.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Praṇaya (maitram)* manifesting after *māna* was illustrated. Now *praṇaya* appearing before *māna* is illustrated. A servant of Candrāvalī speaks to Candrāvalī, a *svādhīna-kāntā*. Give up modesty. Stop thinking “How can Kṛṣṇa’s hands touch my feet?” “But my respect for Kṛṣṇa will be destroyed. You do not keep that in mind.” “But the sound of those bells will shame your rivals since it will show your great fortune of having Kṛṣṇa’ put on your ankle bells.” *Praṇaya* is evident (without *māna*). It is understood that her heart melts on being touched by Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 114

***atha sakhyam—***  
***visrambhaṁ sādhvasonmuktaḥ sakhyaṁ sva-vaśatā-mayaḥ \|\|114\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intimacy free of fear is called** ***sakhya.*** **This** ***sakhya*** **controls Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 115

***yathā—***  
***sarabhasam adhikaṇṭham arpitābhyāṁ***  
***danuja-ripor nija-bāhu-vallarībhyām \|***  
***niṭilam avanamayya tasya karṇe***  
***sakhi kathitaṁ kim iva tvayā rahasyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! What secret did you whisper in Kṛṣṇa’s ear when you made him bend his head by strongly embracing his sides with your creeper-like arms?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vallarī* means a creeper. *Sāhitya-darpana* gives an example of the word. *Dīrghaṁ roditi nikṣipaty ata itaḥ kṣāmāṁ bhujā-vallarīm*: she cries out a long time, throwing her thin, creeper-like arms here and there.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā. You made him lower his head *(niṭilam)* by placing your creeper-like arms at his waist (*adhikaṇṭham*).

### Text 116

*yathā vā śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe (5.30.34)–*  
***yadi te tad-vacaḥ satyaṁ satyātyarthaṁ priyeti me \|***  
***mad-geha-niṣkuṭārthāya tadāyaṁ nīyatāṁ taruḥ \|\|116\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Visṇu Purāṇa:*** **If your words “You are dear to me” are really true, then to prove that, you should bring this** ***pārijāta*** **tree to decorate the garden in my palace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The tree mentioned is the *pārijāta* tree.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse was an example of *praṇaya (sakhya)* before *māna.* The present verse illustrates *praṇaya* after a display of *māna*. Satyabhāmā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. The tree is the *pārijāta.* That will please me and nothing else. Her order indicates *sakhya.*

### Text 117

***yathā vā—***  
***vinyasya vakṣoruha-koraka-dvayīṁ***  
***vakṣaḥ-sthale kaṁsa-harasya hāriṇīm \|***  
***patrāṅkuraṁ kuṅkuma-bindunālike***  
***likhaty asau candra-mukhī sakhī mama \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Resting the two flower-buds of her breasts on his charming chest, my friend Candrāvalī paints many patterns with** ***kuṁkuma*** **dots on the forehead of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Alike* means on the forehead.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There is not only *sakhya* in Rādhā and Satyabhāmā but also in the *sakhīs.* That is shown in this verse. A *sakhī* of Candrāvalī speaks to one of her associates.

### Text 118

***yathā vā śrī-daśame (10.30.38)—***  
***tato gatvā vanoddeśe dṛptā keśavam abravīt \|***  
***na pāraye’haṁ calituṁ naya māṁ yatra te manaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from the Tenth Canto: As the two lovers passed through one part of the Vṛndāvana forest, the special** ***gopī*** **began feeling proud of herself. She told Lord Keśava, “I cannot walk any further. Please carry me wherever you want to go.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Praṇaya* of *sakha* variety manifesting before *māna* was described. Now an opposite example is given with some thinking involved. Even though *praṇaya* appears, it is mixed with crookedness. *Praṇaya* arising with crookedness is a special attribute of the heroine’s *prema*. It is said:

aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet \|

ato hetor ahetoś ca yūnor māna udañcati \|\|

The movement of *prema* is crooked by nature, like that of a snake. Thus the *māna* of the two lovers appears with or without cause. *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 15.102

But it was said in the beginning of the discussion on *praṇaya* that *māna* endowed with intimacy (*visrambha*) is called *praṇaya.* That is the opinion of the author.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A statement of Śukadeva is given as proof. *Dṛptā* means *māna.*

### Text 119

***janitvā praṇayaḥ snehāt kutracin mānatāṁ vrajet \|***  
***snehān mānaḥ kvacid bhūtvā praṇayatvam athāśnute \|\|119\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes** ***praṇaya*** **arises from** ***sneha*** **and** ***praṇaya*** **produces** ***māna.*** **But sometimes** ***māna*** **arises from** ***sneha*** **and produces** ***praṇaya.***

### Text 120

***kārya-kāraṇatānyon’nyam ataḥ praṇaya-mānayoḥ \|***  
***ity atra pṛthag evāsau viśrambhodāhṛtiḥ kṛtā \|\|120\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Praṇaya*** **and** ***māna*** **produce each other. But in this chapter** ***visrambha*** **was illustrated both ways.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The second type of *praṇaya* is defined.  *Aśnute* means attains. In the chapter of *sthāyi-bhāva (atra) praṇaya* has been shown to arise differently, after explaining it arises after *māna.*

### Text 121

***udātta-lalitābhyāṁ tu maitrya-sakhye susaṅgate \|***  
***dve sumaitrya-susakhyākhye yathā-saṅkhyam udīrite \|\|121\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When** ***maitrya*** **mixes thoroughly with** ***udātta*****,** ***sumaitrya*** **arises. And when** ***sakhya*** **mixes thoroughly with** ***lalita, susakhya*** **arises.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When *maitrya* mixes thoroughly with *udātta, sumaitrya* arises. And when *sakhya* mixes thoroughly with *lalita, susakhya* arises.

### Text 122

***tatra sumaitryam—***  
***ālīpuraḥ kathayituṁ rajanī-rahasyaṁ***  
***tatrodyate madhuripau mṛdulā bhramad-bhrūḥ \|***  
***utkṣipya tan mukha-puṭāvaraṇāya hastaṁ***  
***nyañcan-mukhī samavariṣṭa punar varākṣī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of** ***sumaitryam*****: When Kṛṣṇa was eager to recount the secret of their nocturnal pastimes in front of the** ***sakhīs*****, mild Candrāvalī with beautiful eyes moved her eyebrows and thrust out her hand to cover his mouth, but then, hanging her head, withdrew her hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Candrāvalī talks of the actions of Candrāvalī in the morning. Her moving eyebrows indicate *vāma-gandha*. She put out her hand to cover his mouth but then withdrew it. She thought in shyness and shrinking “I cannot act like this to the prince of Vraja.” She hung her head. She became ashamed of her audacity. She displayed *vāmya-gandha* related to *madhu-sneha.* Just as she displayed *vāmya-gandha udātta* of *māna,* so by first thrusting out her hands without restriction she showed *sakhya-gandha* in *maitrya.* Because of *maitrya* expressed internally and externally with *udātta,* this is *sumaitrya*. In the quotation from *Bhāgavatam* in verse 112, because there is no external display of *dākṣiṇya udātta-māna*, there is no really mixture with internal and external *vinaya* of *maitrya.* Thus that is only *maitrya* and not *sumaitrya.*

### Text 123

***yathā vā—***  
***kṣipte varṇaka-bhājane taraṇijā-pure parīhāsataḥ***  
***kṛṣṇena bhruvam āracayya kuṭilām ālokayantī tiraḥ \|***  
***tārā vakṣasi citram ardha-likhitaṁ śrī-vatsa-vibhrājite***  
***kāśmīreṇa ghana-śriyā nija-kucākṛṣṭena pūrṇaṁ vyadhāt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When Kṛṣṇa threw her paint box in the waters of the Yamunā, Tārā frowned but then glanced away. She finished the half-completed picture on his chest shining with Śrīvatsa by using her kuṁkuma-anointed breast.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though there may be *dākṣīṇya-māna* with a portion of “Kṛṣṇa is mine” in some *gopīs,* if there is *ghṛta-sneha* in greater quantity, it is *sumaitrya,* not *susakhya*. That is shown now. It is understood the lovers were sitting on stairs near the water. Frowning at Kṛṣṇa, she thought that it is improper to show hatred to the prince of Vraja though he was misbehaving. Therefore she glanced to the side. By showing this side glance, she showed him that she had no *māna.* She painted on Kṛṣṇa’s chest. This is understood from the modifying phrase “shining with Śrīvatsa.” She completed the painting using her breast covered with *kuṁkuma.* This shows a portion of *madhu-sneha* to Kṛṣṇa, without arousal of *gaurava* (respect). But one should not think that this is *vāmya-gandha udātta* mixing with *maitrya* that has a touch of *sakhya* internally and externally since there seems to be a lack of modesty by using her breast. Actually the breast is honoured most among all the limbs. Kṛṣṇa also did not find any fault in her finishing her job in this way. This is amazing.

### Text 124

***atha susakhyam—***  
***dyūte sakṛt pāna-vidhau paṇī-kṛte***  
***jitvā dviroṣṭhaṁ pibati svam acyute \|***  
***babandha kaṇṭhe kuṭilī-kṛtekṣaṇā***  
***taṁ vāmayā dorlatayāsya vallavī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of** ***susakhya:*** **Defeated by Kṛṣṇa in the gambling match where a kiss had been wagered as the prize, when he kissed her twice, Śyāmalā gazed at him with crooked eyes and bound his neck with the creeper of her left arm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā describes the actions of Śyāmalā to Nāndīmukhī. Though as a wager in gambling one kiss was the prize, when Kṛṣṇa drank her lips twice, she could not tolerate his wrong act and bound him up with her arms. Because there is simultaneous crooked glances and embracing him, there is thorough mixture of *kauṭilya-lalita* with *sakhya*. Thus it is *susakhya.*

### Text 125

***yathā vā—***  
***āviṣkurvati visphuran navanakhollekhaṁ sva-vakṣas-taṭaṁ***  
***kṛṣṇe pīta-dukūla-saṅkalanayā smitvā sakhīnāṁ puraḥ \|***  
***abhraśyāmam uro rurodha valita-bhrūr ānanaṁ dhunvatī***  
***romāñcodgama-kañcukena kucayor dvandvena gāndharvikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When Kṛṣṇa removed his yellow cloth and revealed bright, fresh scratch-marks on his chest to the** ***gopīs,*** **Rādhā, shaking her head and frowning, covered his dark chest with her breasts covered with goose bumps.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse stated that Śyāmalā bound him up because he kissed her twice. It follows that if he had kissed her only once, she would not have bound him up. Thus she has a portion of *dākṣiṇya* and *ghṛta-sneha.* That is proper of Rādhā’s friend Śyāmalā. There are variations within her group. However by preponderance there is *madhu-sneha* in the group. Now an example of pure *madhu-sneha* in Rādhā is given.

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a friend. Revealing marks by pulling off his upper cloth, he smiled, showing their leader’s nature to her *sakhīs.* This showed her intimacy. This gave bliss to her confidential *sakhīs* who thought “Our dear *sakhī* had experienced such separation recently.” First she frowned, showing anger and hatred. Shaking her head as if agreeing with him, she meant the opposite. When he would not stop, she then covered his chest to hide her anger, using her breasts since she could not hide all the marks with her two hands. She also had no under garments during sleeping since Kṛṣṇa had taken her garments previously. Or this can be a cause of great *susakhya* (intimacy). The combination of her goose bumps and frowning brow indicate extreme *kauṭilya-lalita*. Hiding his scratches with her breasts indicates extreme *sakhya.* Thus the combination of *kauṭilya-lalita* with extreme *sakhya* produces extreme *susakhya.*

### Text 126

***atha rāgaḥ—***  
***duḥkham apy adhikaṁ citte sukhatvenaiva rajyate (vyajyate)\|***  
***yatas tu praṇayotkarṣāt sa rāga iti kīrtyate \|\|126\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Rāga:*** **When** ***praṇaya*** **reaches a high state and suffering is removed by happiness in the heart (on meeting Kṛṣṇa), it is called** ***rāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When Kṛṣṇa is attained, then suffering turns to happiness and when Kṛṣṇa leaves, then happiness turns to suffering.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When *praṇaya* reaches a high state it is called *rāga.* This means many people do not reach that state. Causes for suffering are removed (*vyajyate*) by causes for happiness because of attaining Kṛṣṇa. Causes of happiness are removed by causes of suffering on not attaining Kṛṣṇa. Suffering is removed by qualities of happiness. Where one experiences qualities of happiness in situations of suffering, it is not suffering. When vermilion is applied to bee’s wax, it takes up the qualities of vermilion and one does not experience the qualities of bee’s wax. If a cloth is dyed with red dye, one experiences redness, not the white color of the cloth. Another version has *rajyate,* which means “becomes colored.”

### Text 127

***yathā—***  
***tīvrārka-dyuti-dīpitair asilatādhārākarālāsribhir-***  
***mārtaṇḍopala-maṇḍalaiḥ sthapuṭite’py adres taṭe tasthuṣī \|***  
***paśyanti paśupendra-nandanam asāv indīvarair āstṛte***  
***talpe nyasta-padāmbujeva muditā na spandate rādhikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Remaining on the slope covered with piles of sharp-edged, uneven sun stones heated by the intense rays of the sun at noon, Rādhā, joyfully gazing at the prince of the cowherds, remains motionless as if standing with her feet on a bed of blue lotuses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Rādhā in the distance, Lalitā relishes her *rāga* with her friends. Rādhā remains on the side of the mountain having groups of uneven sun stones, hot with the rays of the noon day sun in Jyeṣṭha month *(tīvrārka*), having sharp edges like lines of knives.

*Asri* means an edge according to *Amara-koṣa. Āstṛte* means covered. Though there is suffering caused by touching the hot, sharp, hard rocks on the slope of the mountain, she experiences bliss by qualities of happiness, such as Kṛṣṇa’s youthfulness. She does not experience the heat, sharpness, and hardness of the slope though she remains there.

“While sleeping one does not experience the pain of mosquitoes biting but in the morning on waking up, one sees blood coming out from the bites. Similarly, she does not experience pain on her tender feet now, but later she will feel pain.” That is not so. By seeing Kṛṣṇa she is submerged in bliss. Her body from head to foot becomes cool like million moons. It is not possible to burn her. The moon can never be heated by the suns rays. Since a piece of cotton cannot defeated by a sharp rock, her feet which are softer than cotton cannot be defeated by the rocks. Or *yoga-māyā*, solver of all problems, remains always awake in the pastimes.

### Text 128

***yathā vā padyāvalyāṁ (179)—***  
***tārābhisāraka caturtha-niśā-śaśāṅka***  
***kāmāmbu-rāśi-parivardhana deva tubhyam \|***  
***argho namo bhavatu me saha tena yūnā***  
***mithyāpavāda-vacasāpy abhimāna-siddhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **O excellent arranger of meetings! O moon on the fourth night of the month of Bhadrā! O increaser of the ocean of** ***kāma*****! O lord! I offer** ***arghya*** **to you. May my desire to be with the youth be fulfilled even if accompanied by false accusations!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some women have attraction to seeing the moon on the fourth *tithi.* O *caturthi* moon!

You cannot fulfill the desire to attain him, but you are famous for producing false accusations. If I can attain him with a fulfillment of a false accusation, I will be happy. You, the moon, are suitable as the object of this request. It is seen that desire increases intensely for us by expert meetings. You can accomplish this. O excellent arranger of meetings! Of increaser of the ocean of love! This indicates the moon in Bhadrā month. I offer *argha* to you. “Why do you offer me *arghya,* since on seeing me one receives defamation?” Let me have identity with the youth Kṛṣṇa. “He is my lover, and I am his lover.” Let that be accomplished even with false accusations.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

With the attainment of *ṛāga*, suffering becomes filled with happiness. When the women with *rāga* pray for the cause of their suffering, then that cause of suffering becomes a cause of happiness. That is shown in this verse. One young girl of Vraja with *rāga,* on not attaining Kṛṣṇa, thought herself unqualified out of humility. To rectify the situation she decided on her own to pray for defamation to the *caturthī* moon of Bhadrā month, famous for bestowing defamation. You make appointments with the stars (traveling in each constellation over the month). You know the suffering caused by not attaining the lover. O *caturthi* moon! Make me successful by giving me defamation, since I am unqualified to attain Kṛṣṇa otherwise. O increaser of the ocean of *kāma*! You are well known for increasing the ocean. The ocean is filled with *kāma* not water, from our realization. Thus it is not my fault if I have increased desire. O *deva*! Since you are a *devatā* you know the solution for my suffering.

With longing I offer *arghya* to you, who give defamation just by being seen. Do not delay in doing this. “Being defamed, you will suffer criticism of the public. But you will not suffer if you do not associate with Kṛṣṇa.” I pray for a relationship with that youth even with false accusations. If I do not attain Kṛṣṇa, but just have a shadow of his association, the suffering will become happiness. This shows the ultimate height of *rāga.*

### Text 129

***nīlimā raktimā ceti rāgo’yaṁ dvividho mataḥ \|\|129\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are two types of** ***rāga: nīlimā*** **(blue) and** ***raktimā*** **(red).**

### Text 130

***tatra nīlimā—***  
***nīlī-śyāmā-bhavo rāgo nīlimā kathyate budhaiḥ \|\|130\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Nīlimā*****:** ***Nīlī-rāga*** **has two forms like the** ***nīlī*** **and** ***śyāma*** **trees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having explained *rāga*, the types are shown according to ancient authorities. They say:

*na cātiśobhate yan nāpaiti prema mano-gatam \|*  
*tan nīlī-rāgam ākhyānti yathā śrī-rāma-sītayoḥ \|\|*  
*kusumbha-rāgaṁ taṁ prāhur yad apaiti ca śobhate \|*  
*māñjiṣṭha-rāgaṁ tat prāhur yan nāpaity atiśobhate \|\|*

***Prema*** **in the mind which is not too brilliant and which does not decrease is called** ***nīlī-rāga*****. An example is the** ***rāga*** **of Rāma and Sīta. When** ***prema*** **is brilliant and decreases it is called** ***kusumbha-rāga*** **and when it is very brilliant and does not decrease it is called** ***māñjiṣṭha-rāga.***

To show that there are two types of *nīlī-rāga* two examples are given.  *Nīlī* and *śyāma* are two different plants. There are two different *bhāvas, nīlī-bhāva* and *śyāmā-bhāva*. That is the meaning. They are considered one in general discussions.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having defined *rāga* as that which turns suffering to happiness, the types are pointed out in order to understand with examples the meaning of the word *rāga. Nīlī* and *śyāmā* are a tree and creeper. There are two types of *nīlī-rāga, nīlī-bhāva* and *śyāmā-bhāva.*

### Text 131

***tatra nīlī-rāgaḥ—***  
***vyaya-sambhāvanā-hīno bahir nātiprakāśavān \|***  
***sva-lagna-bhāvāvaraṇo nīlī-rāgaḥ satāṁ mataḥ \|***  
***yathāvalokyate caiṣa candrāvali-mukundayoḥ \|\|131\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Nīlī-rāga:*** **When** ***rāga*** **is devoid of decrease, is not clearly distinguishable, and covers** ***bhāvas*** **attached to it, it is called** ***nīlī-rāga*****. This is seen in Candrāvalī and Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having given the example, the object of the example, *rāga* is characterized by two qualities. *Nilī-rāga* aspect of *rati* is characterized with likeness to blue coloring. It does not decrease. Decrease of color or *rāga* caused by its inherent qualities cannot take place. This should not be confused with the qualities of *prema.* Externally it is not clearly distinguished from *śyāmā-rāga*. In terms of colors it means that *nīla* color cannot be distinguished clearly from *śyāma* color. It covers *bhāvas* in contact with it. In terms of colors, the blue covers up other colors which may be applied to the cloth. In terms of *rati, nīlī-rāga* covers up *māna* and other *bhāvas.* As well, the definition of *rāga* from the previous section—being the excellence of *praṇaya* and transforming suffering into happiness, also applies.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Nīlī-rāga* related to *prema* is described in terms of the blue dye. *Nīlī-rāgaḥ* in the verse actually means *nīlī-rāgaḥ iva* (like the blue dye). It cannot be decreased by *sañcāri-bhāvas.* The quality of *prema* is that, in the presence of causes of destruction, it is not destroyed. In that definition of *prema*, “causes of destruction “refers to dependence on *dharma* and other factors and not the *sañcāri-bhāvas*. Since this *rāga* cannot be destroyed even by *sañcāri-bhāvas,* it is not possible for them to mix with it. The color *nīla* is not clearly distinguished from the color *śyāmā.* In terms of *rati,* since *ghṛta-sneha* lacks intense taste by itself, the *rāga* arising from it is not so outstanding. Dark blue color covers all other colors applied to the cloth. Similarly, *nīlī-rāga* covers all emotions like hatred or jealousy.

### Text 132

***yathā—***  
***prasanna-viśadāśayā vividha-mudrayā nirmitaṁ***  
***pratāraṇam api tvayā guṇatayā sadā gṛhṇatī \|***  
***tathā vyavajahāra sā vraja-kulendra candrāvalī***  
***sakhībhir api tarkitā tvayi yathā taṭasthety asau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O king of Vraja! Though you have cheated her by various gestures, Candrāvalī accepts you as a person full of good qualities, since she is the abode of joy and purity. In behavior, even her friends wonder if she is indifferent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though he cheats her, because of her purity, she accepts him as a cause of happiness. This is the general characteristic of *rāga.* It also shows the quality or *nīlī-rāga* of not decreasing at all. That *nīlī-rāga* covers up the quality of purity. Her actions reveal her neutral nature. Because this takes place with effort, other *bhāvas* cannot enter. Being under the control of her *sakhīs,* she still does not do otherwise. This shows the extreme case of covering other *bhāvas* such as purity.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhadrā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Since she is pleased with everything she is compassionate. Because she does not see others’ faults, she is pure (*viśāda*). She has such a heart. Though she has these sweet qualities a flickering greed is perceived in Kṛṣṇa. “Instead of appreciating her good qualities, you desire to make her suffer by cheating her many times.” She has been cheated by you by many methods. “Oh! Even so, she does not become unhappy, but becomes most joyful.” She is pleased with your good qualities. She thinks “Kṛṣṇa, appreciating great qualities, and enjoying them, attains happiness with those women who are fortunate. He gives me happiness by announcing his happiness. How clever he is! This is not cheating.” O Kṛṣṇa! Though you attempt to make her suffer, your desire is not fulfilled. This exclamation of her purity is hinted. The quality of r*āga* to make suffering into happiness is evident.

Hear the clever, confidential method that her *sakhīs* create to solve their leader’s problem. The *sakhīs* become joyful in announcing her indifference. She keeps her *prema* hidden. This shows her good quality. This shows the quality of *rāga* not being covered by apprehension of her *sakhīs,* a *sañcāri-bhāva*. The *sakhīs* speculate about this. That shows it is not clear. It is slightly revealed since Bhadrā understands her mind. Her *nīlī-rāga* covers her anger towards Kṛṣṇa. As well her *ghṛta-sneha* with the thought that “I am his” is evident.

### Text 133

***atha śyāmā-rāgaḥ—***  
***bhīrutauṣadhi-sekādir ādyāt kiñcit prakāśa-bhāk \|***  
***yaś cireṇaiva sādhyaḥ syāt sa śyāmā-rāga ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Śyāmā-rāga:*** **When the first infusion of timidity takes place and reveals more qualities than** ***nīlī-rāga*****, but takes a along time to reach perfection, it is called** ***śyāmā-rāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The qualities of *śyāmā-rāga* are similar to the *śyāmā* creeper. The color depends on a preliminary infusion of the herb *bhīru.* In terms of *rati* it is *bhīrutā* or timidity. Fright is feigned to conceal things. It will become clear in the example. It is the first mixing (*seka*) of the herb.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This color *śyāma* is the first infusion (*seka*) of the herb *bhīrutā.* In *rati* this *rāga* has fear or timidity. “Timidity is naturally present in all women. How does it arise from *praṇaya*?” That is true. For women with *ghṛta-sneha* mixed with a little *madhu-sneha,* at the time of *vayaḥ-sandhi* when *rati* appears, timidity also appears strongly, as a distinguishing quality for them. If *madhu-sneha* is full, it produces full intoxication (*mattatā*). This produces full pride, by which the affection for the beloved becomes “He is mine.” If there is only a portion of *madhu-sneha,* the intoxication is only partial as well. The pride generated from that is also partial. The woman will show full *dākṣiṇya* arising from *ghṛta-sneha*, and extreme timidity (*bhīrutā*). This transforms into timidity mixed with concealment. This *bhīrutā* is akin to *cakita.* It was explained that showing great fear in front of the lover when there is no cause for fear is called *cakitam. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 11.67) It appears internally. It cannot be seen due to misfortune, but appears in the presence of the lover. In *śyāmā-rāga*, this fright appears in front of all people. Compared to *nīlī-rāga* it is more known. This is well known as far as colors are concerned. As far as *rati* is concerned, a portion of *madhu-sneha* is the cause of its appearance. It is accomplished over time. The dying takes a long time. As for *rati,* if a small portion of *madhu-sneha* and greater portion of *ghṛta-sneha* are mixed together, it will take a long time just as thoroughly mixing a small portion of honey with a large portion of cool ghee takes a long time.

### Text 134

***yathā—***  
***purā kuñje mañjuny avatamasa-yukte’pi cakitā***  
***murārer yā pārśve na taruṇi divāpy antaram agāt \|***  
***tamālaiḥ saivādya dviguṇita-tamisre’pi muditā***  
***tamisrārdhe māniny ahaha bhavatī taṁ mṛgayate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O young girl! Previously you were frightened of an attractive bower if was slightly dark. And even in the daytime, with Kṛṣṇa by your side, you would not enter. Proud woman! Now at midnight when it is twice as dark because of** ***tamāla*** **trees, you joyfully search him out.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A messenger jokes with a proud woman who first requested a meeting but then out fear did not keep the appointment, but later out of great longing made her own arrangements. *Avatamasam* means slight darkness. *Divāpy antaram* means “up to the middle of the day.” Because of immediate proximity of time and place, the accusative is used. She was joyful because she had confirmed his presence. Then she searched for him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* jokes with Bhadrā who has separated because of a quarrel. Even though the bower was slightly dark she was afraid. *Amara-koṣa* says *avatamasa* means slight darkness. *Cakitā* means frightened. O young girl! You did not enter even in the middle of the day. But you enter at midnight during the dark phase of the moon, made doubly dark by the *tamāla* trees. Now you are not frightened, but joyful. Though making an appointment in the dark was difficult, now it is joyful. This is the quality of *rāga.* O proud woman! This indicates separation because of quarrelling. Now you make the grief of Kṛṣṇa cheating you into happiness. This verse illustrates *bhīrutā* in her previous state, reaching maturity after a long time , and strong manifestation of *rāga*.

### Text 135

***atha raktimā—***  
***rāgaḥ kusumbha-mañjiṣṭhā-sambhavo raktimā mataḥ \|\|135\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Raktimā:*** **There are two types of** ***raktima-ṛaga*****: arising from** ***kusumbha*** **and arising from** ***mañjiṣṭhā.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

There are two types of *raktima-rāga*: arising from *kusumbha* and arising from *mañjiṣṭhā.* Because of common qualities they are mentioned together.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are two types of *raktima-rāga.*

### Text 136

***tatra kusumbha-rāgaḥ—***  
***kusumbha-rāgaḥ sa jñeyo yaś citte sajjati drutam \|***  
***anya-rāga-cchavi-vyañjī śobhate ca yathocitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kusumbha-rāga:*** **That** ***rāga*** **which quickly attaches itself to the heart and reveals and intensifies the beauty of** ***mañjiṣṭḥa-rāga*** **is called** ***kusumbha-rāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The example of *kusumbha* color is famous. *Rāga* is compared to it. The heart is compared to cloth. Quickly it becomes fixed in the heart. This means that, by practice, it easy awakens in the minds of persons desiring to enter as consorts of the Kṛṣṇa with *gopī* bodies. *Sajjati* means “becomes fixed. This description should apply to *nitya-siddhas* since this *rāga* is their nature. By other *rāgas,* the first three types become beautiful. However *mañjiṣṭhā* dye, once appearing, has the highest beauty. *Kusumbha-rāga* takes shelter of *mañjiṣṭha-rāga*. After a long time however it becomes fixed and develops its own beauty. It appears beautiful in all persons (*yathocitam*). Or it appears beautiful in suitable persons. This indicates that it is not equal to *māñjīṣṭha-rāga.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Kusumbha-ṛaga* means it is like *kusumbha* dye. The example of *kusumbha* dye is famous. This is applied to *rāga.* Just as the cloth quickly becomes colored, the heart quickly becomes fixed with this *rāga.* A little *ghṛta-sneha* mixes with great amount of *madhu-sneha* very quickly, just as a little liquid ghee and a lot of honey mix quickly. Other colors like *mañjiṣṭha* or lac intensify its beauty. By this, the *rāga* of Śyāmalā becomes similar to Rādhā’s. This takes place according to the good qualities in the experiencer (*yathocitam*).

### Text 137

***yathā—***  
***tvayy eva śravaṇāvadhi priya-sakhī yā kṛṣṇa-baddhāntarā***  
***yā dṛṣṭe bhujage’pi tāvaka-bhujā-sāmyāt pramodonmadā \|***  
***prekṣya tvāṁ purato’dya kām api daśāṁ prāptāsti seyaṁ tathā***  
***na jñāyeta yathā kim eṣa balavān rāgo virāgo’thavā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When my dear friend hears your name, she binds you in her heart, and when she sees a snake she becomes mad with happiness, being reminded of your arms. Seeing you, she has attained an indescribable condition. I do not know if this is great** ***rāga*** **or great detachment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first half of the verse describes general qualities of this *rāga*. When she hears your name her heart becomes fixed in you. That indicates *rāga* quickly fixing itself in the heart. When she sees a snake she thinks of your arms. This indicates becoming beautiful on mixing with other *rāgas.* Though touch is not mentioned, it is the step.before seeing. Then, seeing you, she attains an indescribable state. This indicates “assuming suitable beauty.” That condition indicates *praṇaya* and *māna*. Though she is praised by her *sakhīs,* she does not have frowning and other symptoms as in women with *mañjiṣṭha-rāga.* She covers these symptoms. Thus she does not show as much beauty. This is the intention of the poet.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Śyāmalā, an *amitārtha* messenger, speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Just on hearing, the *rāga* is fixed in her heart. Seeing a snake she thinks of Kṛṣṇa’s arms. This indicates mixture with other *rāgas.* Touching is not mentioned. This indicates that she does not have the *mañjiṣṭha-rāga* of Rādhā, difficult to attain. She becomes mad with bliss. This is a general quality of *rāga.* Seeing him she attains an indescribable state. This indicates attaining beauty (*śobhate yathocitam*). Because she has a heavy load of longing within, it seeks to come out. She thus attains an indescribable state.

This shows the strength of the *rāga.* When *rāga* and *virāga* becomes strong, one gives up thinking of “I and mine.” If you do not meet her today, she will give up her life.

### Text 138

***sadādhāra-viśeṣeṣu kausumbho’pi sthiro bhavet \|***  
***iti kṛṣṇa-praṇayiṣu mlānir asya na yujyate \|\|138\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Kusumbha-rāga*** **becomes fixed through special mediums. Thus, it does not fade in suitable devotees of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One should not think that like *kusumbha* dye, this *rāga* will fade with time. It becomes fixed in persons with special qualities. In terms of cloth, it becomes fixed by mixing with special ingredients. In terms of the heart, it becomes fixed by association with persons with *māñjiṣṭha-rāga.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the example it was hinted that *kusumbha-rāga* had more beauty than the *māñjiṣṭha-rāga* of Rādhā. Actually because *kusumbha-rāga* is not steady, this is not a proper description. That is explained in this verse.  *Kusumbha* color becomes fixed in cloth by certain chemical combinations. Then it does not fade in the groups headed by Śyāmalā and others, who associate with *gopīs* having *māñjiṣṭha-rāga.*

### Text 139

***atha mañjiṣṭha-rāgaḥ—***  
***ahāryo’nanya-sāpekṣo yaḥ kāntyā varddhate sadā \|***  
***bhaven māñjiṣṭha-rāgo’sau rādhā-mādhavayor yathā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mañjiṣṭhā-rāga*****:** ***Rāga*** **which never vanishes, does not depend on other elements, and increases its beauty constantly is called** ***māñjiṣṭha-rāga*****. It is seen in Rādhā and Mādhava.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This ṛāga can never be depleted *(ahāryaḥ*). *Kusumbha-rāga* becomes permanent contact with certain qualities, but *māñjiṣṭha-rāga* by nature is permament. It is not dependent on other things. *Kusumbha* by mixed with other *rāgas* became beautiful. *Māñjiṣṭha-rāga* is beautiful in all its portions. This is true also of *māñjiṣṭha* dye. It increases in beauty. That is well known concerning the dye. In terms of *rāga,* that it manifests the beauty of *anurāga,* but it does not mix with the qualities of *anurāga.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Māñjiṣṭha* dye cannot be removed by water *(ahāryaḥ*). In terms of *prema, māñjiṣṭha-rāga* cannot be agitated by *sañcāri-bhāvas.* It is *svataḥ-siddha,* independent. It is not like *śyāmā-rāga*, dependent on herbs (or timidity). It increases its beauty. *Kusumbha-rāga* has limited beauty. It increases its own beauty. It does not change by mixing with *anurāga.*

### Text 140

***yathā—***  
***dhatte drāg anupādhi janma vidhinā kenāpi nākampate***  
***sūte’ty āhita-sañcayair api rasaṁ te cen mitho vartmane \|***  
***ṛddhiṁ sañcinute camatkṛti-karoddāma-pramodottarāṁ***  
***rādhā-mādhavayor ayaṁ nirupamaḥ premānubandhotsavaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: The incomparable festival arising from the** ***prema*** **of Rādhā and Mādhava appears quickly without cause, is not at all moved by any means, produces great taste if met by heaps of opposing elements, and increases with the greatest, unlimited, astonishing bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Its indestructible nature is clear. Without hearing or other means, it suddenly appears, unlike *kusumbha-rāga* which appears gradually in portions. It appears quickly. It was said that *kusumbha* was quickly fixed in the heart, but that it did not indicate its appearance. It does not waver because of any rules. It is fixed. The affix *ā* in *ākampate* means that there is no movement at all. There is no possibility of its wavering, unlike *kusumbha-rāga*. The two types of dye also have this nature: *kusumbha* dye can be altered but *māñjīṣṭha* cannot. In terms of *prema, kusumbha-rāga* is manifest in neutral parties and *māñjiṣṭha-rāga* is manifest in *svādhīna-bhartṛkās. Ahita* means great fear or indifferent to action and life. If these obstacles appear on their path they produce happiness. Instead of *te cen mitho vartmane* sometimes *te cen mitho lambhakāḥ* is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī when she inquires about the qualities of *rāga*. Their *rāga* appears without limitations (*upādhi*). It does not depend on anything (*ananya-sāpekṣatvam)*. It does not waver by any means (*vidhinā*), such as mixing with differing *bhāvas.* The affix *ā* in *ākampate* indicates that it does not move in the slightest. This indicates its indestructible nature (*āharya).* It attains special taste (*rasam*) by all the difficulties and fears related to elders (*atyāhita-sañcayaiḥ*). This means the *rāga* is not disturbed by all of this. If these obstacles happen to block the way, the taste increases. This is a general characteristic of *rāga. Amara-koṣa* says *atyāhita* means great fear. This *rāga* increases. This indicates the quality of increasing in beauty (*sadā kānti-vṛddhiḥ*).

### Text 141

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (3.17)—***  
***mayā te nirbandhān murajayini rāgaḥ parihṛtya***  
***mayi snigdhe kintu prathaya paramāśīs tatim imām \|***  
***mukhāmododgāragrahilamatir adyaiva hi yataḥ***  
***pradoṣārambhe syāṁ vimala-vana-mālā-madhu-karī \|\|141\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **You advise me to give up** ***rāga*** **for Kṛṣṇa. My affectionate friend! Bestow a great benediction to me. Please bless me so that this evening, I may become a bumble-bee resting in Kṛṣṇa's spotless garland, with my mind engaged in the perfume emanating from his mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā with *pūrva-rāga* speaks to Paurṇamāsī. She manifests extreme *rāga* because of great fear caused by Paurṇamāsī discouraging her. Let me be a bee in his spotless garland. If I give up this body, I could be happy. This shows complete independence of *rāga.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous example was merely a description of the form of *mañjīṣṭha-rāga* (rather than an incident). Unsatisfied with that the author gives another example. Rādhā speaks to Paurṇamāsī who speaks logically, testing her *prema* in *pūrva-rāga* by saying it was not advisable to attain Kṛṣṇa. Paurṇamāsī’s insistence reveals that Rādhā cannot give him up in spite of the advice. You advise me to give up aspiring to attain him. O affectionate one (*snigdhe*)! Since you are affection to me, the pile of blessings (*aśīs-tatim*) from you who have done great austerities will certainly bring results.

“May you life long! Is that the blessing I should give?” It should be this (*imam),* what I have been speaking of, not some other thing. You are weakening my aspirations. Thus my loosened life airs are now leaving my body. Your pile of blessings cannot keep my life airs now.

“If you are not going to live, then why do you need my blessings?” You should bless me so that I can be a bee on his flower garland. Give me qualification to attain his garland. *Jaratyās tvaṁ naptrī sa tu kamalayā lālitapadaḥ*: why do you, who are only Jaratī's granddaughter, yearn to attain a person who is very difficult to attain, a person whose feet the goddess of fortune personally massages? (*Vidagdha-mādhava* 3.16) You cannot say that his garland will be hard to attain when I am a bee.

“What is the benefit you get from this?” I will have a mind inclined to the perfume coming from his mouth internally and externally by desire will be fulfilled in that birth or birth as an animal. Do that today, as the delay is intolerable. This evening I am leaving my body. You have a pile of blessings. You should give them again and again.

Extend your blessings. May your blessings be mine! This verse shows the indestructibility of this *rāga* since it does not disappear by the strength of the *sañcāri-bhāva* of *dainya* arising from Paurṇamāsī’s words. The *rāga’s* independence is clear. It increases in beauty for she prays for an insect birth to fulfill that love. General characteristics of *rāga* are found in her request for blessings, showing her suffering transforming into bliss.

### Text 142

***pūrva-pūrvas tu yo bhāvaḥ somābhādau sa rājate \|***  
***tathā bhīṣma-sutādau ca śrī-harer mahiṣī-gaṇe \|\|142\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***bhāvas*** **first mentioned in** ***sneha, māna*** **and** ***rāga (ghṛta-sneha, udātta, matiram sumatiram and nīlimā)*** **manifest in Candrāvalī, Rukmiṇī and the other queens in Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Again all of the aspects are established. *Pūrva-pūrvaḥ* means *ghṛta-sneha, udāatta, matiram sumatiram* and *nīlimā.* Somabhā is Candrāvalī.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *āśrayas* of the two different types of *sneha, māna* and *rāga* arising from two different types of *prema* are described. *Pūrva-pūrvaḥ means ghṛta-sneha, udāatta, matiram, sumatiram* and *nīlimā*. Candrāvalī has *nīlī-rāga* and her friend Bhadrā has *śyāmā-rāga.* Though these differences exist in *sneha* and in *praṇaya* also, they were not mentioned because they are very subtle. These *bhāvas* are also found in other women with *samartha-rati* or *samañjasa-rati.* These women are also described.

### Text 143

***ya uttarottaro dviyo rādhikādau sa dīvyati \|***  
***tathā śrī-satyabhāmāyāṁ lakṣmaṇāyām api kvacit \|\|143\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***bhāvas*** **mentioned in the second place in** ***sneha, māna*** **and** ***rāga (madhu-sneha, lalita, sakhya, susakhya*** **and** ***raktimā*****) appear in Rādhā, Satyabhāmā, Lakṣmaṇā and others.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Uttarottara* means *madhu-sneha, lalita, sakhya, susakhya* and *raktima-rāga.* Rādha and Lalitā have *mañjiṣṭha-rāga*. Their friend Śyāmalā has *kusumbha-rāga*. In Dvārakā Lakṣmaṇā represents Śyāmalā. Thus the first *bhāvas* of each type are found in Candrāvalī and her group and the second type of *bhāvas* are found in Rādhā and her group. *Nīlī-rāga* is found in Candrāvalī and *śyāmā-rāga* is found in her friend Bhadrā. *Kusumbha-rāga* is found in Śyāmalā and *mañjiṣṭha-rāga* is found in Rādhā.

### Text 144

***itthaṁ bhedena bhāvānāṁ sarva-gokula-subhruvām \|***  
***ātma-pakṣa-vipakṣādi-bhedāḥ pūrvam udīritāḥ \|\|144\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The different groups such as one’s own and opposing groups for the various** ***bhāvas*** **of all the women of Gokula have been described previously.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The various *bhāvas* are *ghṛta-sneha* etc. In a previous chapter the different groups were described.

### Text 145

***yā bhāvāntara-sambandhāj jāyante vividhā bhidāḥ \|***  
***aparā api bhāvānāṁ jñeyās tāḥ prajñayā budhaiḥ \|\|145\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The wise by their intelligence know other** ***bhāvas*** **which become of great variety from relation to other** ***bhāvas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The other *bhāvas* are forty-one in number: one *sthāyi-bhāva,* thirty-three *vyabhicāri-bhāvas*, and seven items starting with *hāsya.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are not only four types of groups--*svapakṣa, suhrṭ-pakṣa, taṭastha* and *partipakṣa*. However, for fear of enlarging the text, these have not been described. Many other varieties exist. The meaning is this. Just as white, blue, red and yellow mix together to form various colors, so *ghṛta-sneha* and *madhu-sneha* can mix in various proportions, and the various *rāgas* can mix in various proportions. They then have different names and forms and *sthāyi-bhāvas.* Similarly there are these varieties of women in Vraja.

### Text 146

***sadānubhūtam api yaḥ kuryān nava-navaṁ priyam \|***  
***rāgo bhavan nava-navaḥ so’nurāga itīryate \|\|146\|\|***

**Перевод:**
