**R*****āga*** **which makes the object of love experienced in ever fresh ways and itself becomes ever fresh is called** ***anurāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Rāga*, previously described, which gives an experience of the hero with his form, qualities and sweetness, as if previously inexperienced, and which itself transforms by special thirst, and is experienced as if not experienced before, is called *anurāga*. There are two types: in which on a portion of the object of love is ever fresh and in which all aspects of the object are ever fresh.

### Text 147

***yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (28)—***  
***prapannaḥ panthānaṁ harir asakṛd asman-nayanayor***  
***apūrvo’yaṁ pūrvaṁ kvacid api na dṛṣṭo madhurimā \|***  
***pratīke’py ekasya sphurati muhur aṅgasya sakhi yā***  
***śriyas tasyāḥ pātuṁ lavam api samarthā na dṛg iyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **I have seen Kṛṣṇa many times. But I have never before seen such sweetness as today. My eyes cannot drink even a drop of the beauty in one portion of one limb.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Pratīke* means in a limb or one portion of that.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

At Dāna-ghaṭta near Govardhana, seeing Kṛṣṇa at a distance, Rādhā speaks to Vṛndā. *Asakṛd* means many times. Today his beauty is unique. The sweetness is described. I cannot drink even on drop of the beauty in one portion of one limb like the hand or foot. *Amara-koṣa* says *pratīka* means a limb. Though his sweetness has been seen many times, experiencing it as never before, with extreme thirst, is *anurāga*.

### Text 148

***yathā vā—***  
***ko’yaṁ kṛṣṇa iti vyudasyati dhṛti yas tanvi karṇaṁ viśan***  
***rāgāndhe kim idaṁ sadaiva bhavatī tasyorasi krīḍati \|***  
***hāsyaṁ mā kuru mohite tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā***  
***satyaṁ satyam asau dṛgaṅganam agād adyaiva vidyun-nibhaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example:**

**Rādhā: O slender friend! Who is this Kṛṣṇa, whose name, on entering my ears, makes me lose my composure?**

**Lalitā: O girl blinded by love! What are you saying? You continually play on his chest.**

**Rādhā: Don't make fun of me!**

**Lalitā: O bewildered girl! I have now placed you in the hand of that person.**

**Rādhā: It is true, but a flash of lightning has today landed in the courtyard of my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This verse is composed of questions and answers between two *sakhīs,* one of who is asking questions after forgetting her recent association with Kṛṣṇa out of longing.

*Ko’yam* are the first words of the first speaker. *Rāgādhe* is the beginning of the second speaker’s words. *Hāsyam mā* is the first speaker. *Mohite* is the beginning of the second speaker’s words. *Satyam satyam* are the first speaker’s words. *Kim idam* means “What are you saying?” *Tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā* means “I have now placed you in his hand.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse described *anurāga* in one portion. Now *anurāga* in all portions is described. One time in talking about Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā in great longing developed *anurāga* in her heart. She began conversing with Lalitā. Who is the person represented by the two syllabled word *kṛṣṇa*?

“Let him be. Why are you asking this question?”

“Just on beginning to enter one of my ears, that sound makes me completely lose (*vyudasyati)* my self-control. What will I do if he enters my eyes? I should know who he is. We should contemplate means of protecting our chastity from him.”

“Oh! You are blinded by *rāga* and extreme longing. What are you saying? How is it that you do not know him?”

“I am speaking the truth. I do not know him.”

“You are always playing on his chest.”

“Do not joke with me.” Impossible words end in laughter.

“O bewildered girl! Out of great thirst you have not lost your memory.”

“Then you should help me remember.”

“I have placed you in his hands today. It was not long ago. I did this, not some other person. I put you in his hands, for enjoyment.”

“That is true. You have made me remember.”

“Why do you say that you do not recognize him?”

“Now, on this day in my life, a flash of lightning, very quick, struck the courtyard of my eyes, not completely inside. How is it possible to recognize him at all?”

### Text 149

***paraspara-vaśībhāvaḥ prema-vaicittyakaṁ tathā \|***  
***aprāṇiny api janmāptau lālasā-bhara unnataḥ \|***  
***vipralambhe’sya visphūrtir ity ādyāḥ syur iha kriyāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***anubhāvas*** **of** ***anurāga*** **are mutually being controlled by the lover,** ***prema-vaicittya*****, desiring to be born as an insentient being, and sudden manifestation of Kṛṣṇa during separation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though being controlled by the lover is a quality of *prema,* it is outstanding in *anurāga.* The special nature is that being controlled becomes newer and newer every second.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *anubhāvas* of *anurāga* are described. Controlling the hero is clear in *prema* and other levels of love. However, the hero is not controlled by the shyness, concealment etc. of the heroine in these *bhāvas.* In *anurāga* however, because of no opportunities for concealment, pride and envy, because of great thirst, the control by the heroine is very evident. In *ujjvala-rasa*, control by the hero and control by the heroine are both evident. In dāsya and other *rasas* however, only when there is absence of *sañcāri-bhāvas* is there mutual control by each other, starting with *prema*. It has been said:

*sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham*  
*mad-anyat te na jānanti nāhaṁ tebhyo manāg api*

**The pure devotee is my very heart: what pains him pains me. I am the heart of the pure devotee: what pleases him pleases me. My devotees do not know anything else but me, and I do not know more than they do. SB 9.4.68**

That the Lord is controlled by his devotee, and that the Lord controls the devotee is famous in all scriptures.

### Text 150

***atra paraspara-vaśībhāvo, yathā—***  
***samārambhaṁ pārasparika-vijayāya prathayator***  
***apūrvā keyaṁ vām aghadamana saṁrambha-laharī \|***  
***mano-hastī bandhas tava yad anayā rāga-nigaḍais***  
***tvayāpy asyāḥ premotsava-nava-guṇaiś citta-hariṇaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Being controlled by each other: O Kṛṣṇa! What is this unprecedented wave of passion absorbing you two who broadcast this undertaking of trying to defeat each other? She has firmly chained the elephant of your heart with the shackles of** ***rāga*** **and you have bound the deer of her heart with fresh ropes of blissful** ***prema.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What is this wave of enthusiasm of you two youths engaging in the attempt to defeat each other? We do not know. The cause of not knowing is described. She has bound up the elephant of your mind. You have bound up the deer of her heart. Why are you making these efforts? From this arise newer and newer manifestations of the couple. His mind like an elephant is difficult to control. Her heart, like a deer, is easy to control. A small amount of criticism is suggested.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kundalatā, suddenly coming, tasted the astonishing sweetness that arose from the couple bathing in streams of bliss as they searched for each other with great longing on the road to a bower. She speaks with bliss. You are trying to defeat each other, like trying to control an elephant. You are spreading or broadcasting to the world this undertaking with great attachment, without shame or anger. What is this unprecedented wave of passion, of seeing, touching and kissing between you two. Out of eagerness you are both completely absorbed.

### Text 151

***prema-vaicittya-saṁjñas tu vipralambhaḥ sa kathyate \|\|151\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Prema-vaicittya*****, imagined separation, will be discussed later.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This will be discussed in the next chapter (verse 147).

### Text 152

***aprāṇiny api janma-lālasā-bharo, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (17)—***  
***tapasyāmah kṣāmodari varayitum venuṣu janur***  
***vareṇyam manyethāḥ sakhi tad akhilānāṁ sujanuṣām \|***  
***tapah-stomenoccair yad iyam urarīkṛtya muralī***  
***murārāter bimbādhara-madhurimānam rasayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Desiring birth as an insentient object, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: O slender-waisted friend! We will perform austerities to get the blessing of birth among the bamboos since you consider it the best of all pious births—since this flute, accepting great heaps of austerity, tastes the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa’s red lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though they attained him in the story, it is indicated that they are can never be completely satisfied. This indicates the newness of the experience.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Thinking herself unsuccessful, Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. *Var* is a verb of the fourth class meaning “to desire to obtain.” We will perform austerities with the desire to obtain birth among the bamboo species. O thin-waisted woman! If we do not attain Kṛṣṇa, what is the use of taking birth as a human with our beauty? “Would you reject birth as a *devatā* and pray for birth in a lower species?” You consider it the best among births. The reason is given. This flute born among the bamboos, having done great austerities, tastes his lips. Though Rādhā had enjoyed splendid pastimes with him day and night according to the story, because of her great thirst she thinks in this way because of her experiences. This is the sign of *anurāga.*

### Text 153

***atha vipralambhe visphūrtir, yathā—***  
***brūyās tvaṁ mathurādhvanīna mathurānāthaṁ tam ity uccakaiḥ***  
***sandeśaṁ vraja-sundarī kam api te kācin mayā prāhiṇot \|***  
***tatra kṣmāpati-pattane yadi gataḥ svacchanda gacchādhunā***  
***kiṁ kliṣṭām api visphuran diśi diśi kliśnāsi hā me sakhīm \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Manifestation of the lover during separation: O traveler to Mathurā! Please recite this message in a loud voice before Kṛṣṇa, the king of Mathurā. A beautiful girl of Vraja has sent this message through me. If you have gone to the royal city, go there. But now, why do you torture my suffering friend by appearing before her here and there?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ever freshness is evident in the verse with freshness in every momentary appearance of Kṛṣṇa. Giving the message to the traveler shows she has lost her discrimination, since the traveler may not be able to go there and is unsuitable. This shows the disturbed state of her friend influencing the speaker. The characteristics of *anurāga* are similar to the previous verse. *Kliśnāsi* means “you cause pain.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Visphūrti* means a special appearance of Kṛṣṇa-- since normal *sphūrtis* (momentary appearances) take place even in *rati.* Bilvamaṅgala, filled with *rati,* said:

*hastam utkṣipya yāto ’si balāt kṛṣṇa kim adbhutam \|*  
*hṛdayād yadi niryāsi pauruṣaṁ gaṇayāmi te \|\|*

**O Kṛṣṇa! Is it astonishing if you can give up holding my hand? I will consider you a real man if you can take yourself from my heart. BRS 2.4.43**

It has also been said in describing the *sādhaka:*

*utpanna-ratayaḥ samyaṅ nairvighnyam anupāgatāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇa-sākṣāt-kṛtau yogyāḥ sādhakāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\|*

**Those are called practitioners** ***(sādhaka*****) who have developed** ***rati*** **for Kṛṣṇa but have not completely extinguished the** ***anarthas,*** **and who are qualified to see Kṛṣṇa directly. BRS 2.1.276**

It is also said in *Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta*:

*agre samgrayati kām api keli-lakṣmīm*  
*anyāsu dikṣv api vilocanam eva sākṣi \|*  
*hā hanta hasta-patha-dūram aho kim etad*  
*āśā-kiśoram ayam amba jagat-trayaṁ me \|\|*

**He has directly manifested in front of me an indescribable wealth of his pastimes. He is in other directions also. My eye is the witness. Oh! What misfortune! He is out of reach of my hand. Is that him? Ah! For me, the three worlds have become filled with this youth of my aspiration.** ***Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmrta*** **60**

Lalitā sends a message to Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā. Rādhā sends some message to you through me. Say this to the lord of Mathurā. “What message is this?” She then speaks. The meaning is this. Though you appear to her, thinking you are directly present for embracing and kissing, she at first becomes joyful. After a second, when the form disappears, she drowns in an ocean of suffering. Simple separation is better than a momentary appearance in separation, just as simple darkness is better than having a lightning flash in the darkness.

### Text 154

***atha bhāvaḥ—***  
***anurāgaḥ svasaṁvedya-daśāṁ prāpya prakāśitaḥ \|***  
***yāvad-āśraya-vṛttiś ced bhāva ity abhidhīyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Bhāva:*** **When** ***anurāga*** **attains state of being perceived by itself, is revealed externally through** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*****, takes shelter of the highest** ***rāga*****, and spread its influence in all devotees, it is called** ***bhāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The previously described *anurāga,* if it takes shelter of *rāga* and attains a state of self-knowledge, is called *bhāva.* The word *bhāva* indicates the supreme state of this function, just as the word Bhagavān indicates Kṛṣṇa. Sometimes the word *mahābhāva* is used just as the word svayam bhagavan is also used. The meaning is this. *Yāvad-āśrayam* is an *avyayī-bhāva* compound indicating quantity, just one says *yāvat-pātraṁ brāhmaṇānām āmantrayasva:* invite brāhmaṇas who are fully qualified.  *Aśraya* means *rāga*, and *anurāga* takes shelter of it, attaining its qualities. This will be considered and explained in the example in the next verse describing coloring the heart with profuse *kuṁkuma* composed of new *rāga.*

*rāgo’nurāgatām ādau snehaḥ prāpyaiva satvaram \|*  
*mānatvaṁ praṇayatvaṁ ca kvacit paścāt prapadyate \|\|*  
*ata eva prabandheṣu śrūyate rādhikādiṣu \|*  
*pūrva-rāga-prasaṅge’pi prakaṭaṁ rāga-lakṣaṇam \|\|*

**However sometimes** ***rāga*** **turns to** ***anurāga*****, then** ***sneha, māna*** **and** ***praṇaya.*** **It is said in the scriptures that Rādhā and others, in** ***pūrva-rāga,*** **attained** ***rāga*** **directly.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇī*** **14.227-8**

*Anurāga* refers to attaining the full quantity of its *āśraya, rāga.* The meaning of the sentence is as follows. When *anurāga,* which has attaining fullness of *rāga*, attains the perceptible state in women with *anurāga* who are about to attain *bhāva,* and becomes evident by *sāttvika-bhāvas* through appropriate *uddīpanas*, it is called *bhāva.*

*Bhāva* is also *rāga.*

*duḥkham apy adhikaṁ citte sukhatvenaiva rajyate (vyajyate)\|*  
*yatas tu praṇayotkarṣāt sa rāga iti kīrtyate \|\|*

**When** ***praṇaya*** **reaches a high state and suffering is removed by happiness in the heart (on meeting Kṛṣṇa), it is called** ***rāga. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.126**

The height of suffering is destruction of high respect of the chaste women by their own elders, not fire or death. Though this is perceived as accomplished, the relation with Kṛṣṇa produces happiness. This is the highest level of *rāga.* *Anurāga* taking shelter of this height of *rāga* becomes *bhāva.* This is seen in the women of Vraja with newness. It is not possible in the queens of Dvārakā. The word *nava* in the next verse indicates that newness in the Vraja women. Speaking of them Uddhava says in astonishment:

*āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ*  
*vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām*  
*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

Though it was imposible to give up their families, they did so. This indicates the high sense of propriety in the women of Vraja.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When *anurāga* attains the state of being understood only by *anurāga(sva-saṁvedya*), and becomes manifested, and attains *yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti*, it is called *bhāva.* Without being manifested, *yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti* does not take place. *Anurāga,* though it is underestood only by itself, is then not *bhāva.* The condition mentioned (*daśā)* follows after *anurāga,* since that condition must manifest for *bhāva* to take place.

*āruhya paramāṁ kāṣṭhāṁ premā cid-dīpa-dīpanaḥ \|*  
*hṛdayaṁ drāvayann eṣa sneha ity abhidhīyate \|*

**When** ***prema*** **ascends to its highest excellence, illuminates the object of love and liquifies the heart it is called** ***sneha. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.79**

“Of all states mentioned, are all states understood by themselves, or only *anurāga* or *mahābhāva*?”  *Anurāga* and *bhāva* are not different. From *rati* to *mahābhāva* all are undestood by themselves. “Then it can be said that by being understood by itself *anurāga* attains a state of high excellence.” That is true. *Bhāvas* have three states: self-awareness by the *hlāda* portion, awareness of Kṛṣṇa by the *saṁvid* portion, and being aware, by both portions. It is said:

*vastutaḥ svayam āsvāda-svarūpaiva ratis tv asau \|*  
*kṛṣṇādi-karmakāsvāda-hetutvaṁ pratipadyate \|\|*

**Though in its essential nature** ***bhāva*** **is taste itself, it also acts as a cause of tasting the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, his associates and his pastimes. BRS 1.3.5**

When it is said that *anurāga* attains the state of self-awareness, it means it has attained a state of being, the state of causing action and the state of receiving action. In this condition, *anurāga* reaches its excellence and becomes realization of Kṛṣṇa (state of being). This is the first happiness. Though Kṛṣṇa is realized by *prema* and other *bhāvas*, he is then experienced by the excellence of *anurāga* (*anurāga* as cause). This is the second happiness. From that realization of Kṛṣṇa, the excellence of *anurāga* is realized (*anurāga* realized). This is the third happiness. Attaining a state of self-awareness means that *anurāga* attains these three types of happiness.

In *Taittirīya Upaniṣad* after the words *raso vai saḥ,* it is said *saiṣānadasya sīmā bhavati:* this is the limit of bliss. (2.7.1) The limit of bliss is the height of *anurāga.* Just as the moon and the sun become the limits of excellence of the words cold and hot, and make objects near or far from them take up their qualities of cold and hot, when the excellence of *anurāga* appears in the heart of Rādhā, it causes all persons having love of Kṛṣṇa to become full of the bliss of *prema.*

*Yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti* thus means that *anurāga* acts upon (*vṛtti*) all types (*yāvad*) of devotees (*āśraya*)-- *sādhakas* and *siddhas.* *Yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti* should mean *yāvad-āśraya-tāvad-vṛrti.* In *Bhāśā-vṛtti* it is said *dadhnā upasikta odano dadhy-odana itivat kvacid antarbhāvaḥ:* sometimes words are understood but omitted within compounds: yogurt rice means rice soaked with yogurt.  *Vṛrti* in this sentence does not mean a state but rather action, since a state would imply *mahābhāva* already existed in all types of devotees. It will be said *āsanna-janatā-hṛd-viloḍanam*: it affects the hearts of all people approaching (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 15.161) and *brahmāṇḍa-kṣobha-kāritvam*: the whole universe becomes affected. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.181) Therefore the phrase should have this meaning by placing an extra word in the compound. According to the degree of the *āśraya*, so there are degrees of action of *anurāga*. Though the moon cools the whole world by its rays, it does so in various degrees. Thus *mahābhāva* acts in various ways according to various conditions such as separation and union. It is said in *Prema-sampuṭa:*

*āhlādayann amṛta-raśmir iva trilokīṁ*  
*santāpayan prabala-sūrya ivāvabhāti*

**The moon gives bliss to the three worlds by its rays of nectar, just as the strong sun shines everywhere, causing pain.**

### Text 155

***yathā—***  
***rādhāyā bhavataś ca citta-jatunī svedair vilāpya kramāt***  
***yuñjann adri-nikuñja-kuñjara-pate nirdhūta-bheda-bhramam \|***  
***citrāya svayam anvarañjayad iha brahmāṇḍa-harmyodare***  
***bhūyobhir nava-rāga-hiṅgula-bharaiḥ śṛṅgāra-kāruḥ kṛtī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O my Lord, master elephant of the forest on Govardhana Hill! Expert in the craft of** ***śṛṅgāra,*** **you have melted your and Rādhā’s shellac hearts. by the heat of** ***prema*** **so that they cannot be distinguished and have made those hearts red with fresh** ***kuṁkuma*** **to producing astonishment within the palace of the universe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

At the end, an example of *bhāva* is given. Perspiration indicates special *sāttvika-bhāvas,* which indicate internal and external liquidity, or *svedaiḥ* can mean “by heat of fire (in terms of lac melting).” *Citrāya* can mean “causing astonishment” or drawing a picture. Because the couple’s hearts have become inseparable, nothing else can enter. This indicates “known by itself (*sva-samvedya*).” The later verses give similar indications.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, their bodies ornamented with the *uddīpta-sāttvika-bhāvas* were absorbed in tasting each other’s sweetness in a bower. Vṛndā, enjoying the sweetness of their *mahābhāva*, speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Just as all the qualities of all the *avatāras* exist in Svayam Bhāgavan, all the qualities of *rati* and other *bhāvas* exist in *mahābhāva. Śṛṅgāra-kāruḥ kṛtī* means a craftsman expert in his work of *śṛṅgāra-rasa*. This indicates *rati.* Since Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are together they ignore the criticism of the public. This indicates *prema*. Their hearts are like lac, melted by the heat of *prema,* or have become liquid by the heat of fire. This indicates *sneha.* The hearts merge (*yuñjan*). This indicates *praṇaya*. “Gradually” indicates some steps between. This indicates *māna.* The hearts appear to be one. This indicates *susakhyam.* O elephant king of the bowers of Govardhana! You perform pastimes like a mad elephant. The sufferings of the couple in making appointments day and night to meet in the bowers and mountain caves, though their feet are so soft, becomes happiness. This indicates *rāga*. You have tinted those hearts with quantities of *kuṁkuma* colored fresh red. This indicates *anurāga.* You have done this in great quantity. This indicates *mahābhāva.* “Coloring bright red” also means producing fresh *rāga*. “Coloring the lac hearts” means internally and externally the lac becomes red. This indicates that both hearts have attained *mahābhāva* and self-awareness of the excellence of *anurāga.* This is done to make a picture in the palace of the universe or to cause astonishment in the hearts of the wealthy—in the hearts of the devotees. This is done to create realization of the agitating actions of *mahābhāva.* This indicates acting upon the devotees (*yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti).* In later examples the qualities of *mahābhāva* are represented partially or wholly.

### Text 156

***mukunda-mahiṣī-vṛndair apy asāv atidurlabhaḥ \|***  
***vraja-devy eka-saṁvedyo mahābhāvākhyayocyate \|\|156\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**This** ***bhāva*** **is rare even in the queens of Dvārakā. It is only realized by the women of Vraja. It is also called** ***mahābhāva*****.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mahābhāva* takes place in the women of Vraja, not in the women of Dvārakā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though *prema* and *sneha* are rare even for the inhabitants of Vraja, it is very rare for those having *samañjasa-rati*, with slightly less quantity and type of love. *Mahābhāva* is rarest of all since it is realized only by the women of Vraja. Because the queens with *samañjasa-rati* have desire for enjoyment, they lack complete *prema.* Thus from the beginning, by nature of their love (*jāti*), they do not have complete portion of the bliss of *prema.* The quantity of their *anurāga* does not reach the limits of excellence. Thus *mahābhāva* is not possible for them. Jīva Gosvāmī has said (comment on verse 154):

“The height of suffering is destruction of high respect of the chaste women by their own elders, not fire or death. Though this is perceived as accomplished, the relation with Kṛṣṇa produces happiness. This is the highest level of *rāga*. *Anurāga,* taking shelter of this height of *rāga* becomes *bhāva.* This is seen in the women of Vraja with newness. It is not possible in the queens of Dvārakā. The word *nava* in the next verse indicates that newness in the Vraja women.”

Just as four special qualities fixed only in Kṛṣṇa were mentioned previously, *mahābhāva* is fixed only in the women of Vraja. Thus it is called *mahābhāva.* The first state of *prema* is *rati* or *bhāva.* This highest *bhāva* is called *mahābhāva* to announce its highest state. Just as Matsya is the Supreme Lord, so Kṛṣṇa is also the Supreme Lord, though he is also Svayam Bhagavān.

### Text 157-158

***varāmṛta-svarūpa-śrīḥ svaṁ svarūpaṁ mano nayet \|\|157\|\|***  
***sa rūḍhaś cādhirūḍhaś cety ucyate dvividho budhaiḥ \|\|158\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mahābhāva*** **is the wealth of the essence of the best nectar and the mind takes up its nature. The wise say it has two forms** ***rūḍha*** **and** ***adhirūḍha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Mahābhāva* is explained in terms of its greatness. Having the treasure of the essence of the highest sweetness, it has the highest influence. Thus it transforms the mind into *mahābhāva.* Nothing else can do this. It is said *patnyaḥ ṣoḍaśa-sahasram anaṅga-bāṇair yasyendriyaṁ vimathituṁ na śekuḥ:* his senses could not be agitated by the arrows of Cupid thrown by his sixteen thousand wives. (SB 10.61.4) Thus its most astonishing nature is shown. This is its supreme quality.

*Yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti* cannot mean “it spreads itself into all observers.” Adding the missing word *tāvat* would give this meaning. However, this would contradict the quality of “attaining a state of being understood only by itself (*sva-saṁvedya*).” Even *rati* has a state of being understood only by itself. The excellence of *mahābhāva* is shown by the steps in its appearance, consisting of *rūḍha* and *adhirūḍha.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among all common substances there is nothing as tasty as nectar. Similarly among all types of *prem*a there is nothing as tasty as *mahābhāva.* The mind takes on the nature of *mahābhāva.* The mind’s condition does not differ from that of *mahābhāva*. Because the senses are functions of the mind, the women of Vraja’s senses and mind become the form of *mahābhāva.* By the actions of their minds and senses which are *mahābhāva,* Kṛṣṇa becomes controlled to the extreme. However because the queens of Dvārakā have the desire for enjoyment, their minds do not even become the form of *prema.* What is the question of their minds taking the form of *mahābhāva*?

### Text 159

***tatra rūḍhaḥ—***  
***uddīptā sāttvikā yatra sa rūḍha iti bhaṇyate \|\|159\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **become** ***uddīpta*** **in** ***mahābhāva*** **it is called** ***rūḍha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first stage of *mahābhāva* is called *rūḍha.*

### Text 160

***yathā—***  
***unmīlat-kalahaṁsa-gadgada-ravā kampātivikṣobhataḥ***  
***saṅkīrṇā pṛthu-romaharṣa-gatir bāṣpa-cchaṭodgāriṇī \|***  
***jāḍyotseka-pariplutā kuvalayollāsaṁ muhur bibhratī***  
***gopīnām anurāgitā-sarid iyaṁ rāse vitene rasam \|\| 60 \|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When the** ***gopīs’*** **voices choked up like swans cooing, their movements became restricted by agitated trembling, their hairs stood on end, their eyes flowed with tears, their bodies perspired and they became stunned, their** ***rasa,*** **overflowing with** ***anurāga,*** **giving joy to the world, spread out during the** ***rāsa*** **dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The river was filled with the cooing of swans. Or the *rasa* of the *gopīs* was filled with choked voices like swans. It was restricted by their shivering agitation, or the river’s waters quivered from the landing of winged birds. The *rasa* made their hairs stand on end to the extreme, or the river gave joy to the fish (*pṛthu-roma*). Their *rasa* had clusters *(cchaṭa*) of tears of joy, or the river had water drops like tears splashing. The *rasa* made them stunned, or the river was cool. The *rasa* gave joy to the earth (*kuvalaya),* or the river gave joy to the lotuses. The river of *anurāga* indicates abundance.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Women riding in their airplanes, seeing the *rāsa* dance spoke to each other. *Anurāgita* means “abaundance of *anurāg*a” according to the following rule.

*bhūma-nindā-praśaṁsāsu nitya-yoge’tiśāyane \|*  
*saṁsarge’sti vivakṣāyāṁ bhavanti matub-ādayaḥ \|\| iti \|*

**Words ending in** ***mat*** **or other suffixes express abundance, cricticism, praise, contant connection, excess, or combination.**

Thus this indicates *mahābhāva.* *Sarit* means a river and water, or taste. That taste spreads out. The river has swans, or the women sounded like swans cooing. The river was filled with the disturbed water caused by the winged birds landing on it, or the taste of *mahābhāva* was filled with trembling and agitation. The flowing of the river gave joy to the fish, or the *rasa* of *mahābhāva* had actions making the hairs stand on end. The river had mist because of the speed of the flowing water. Or the *rasa* produced beauty of tears of joy. The river was cool, or the *rasa* made them stunned. The river gave joy to blue lotuses or the *rasa* gave joy to the earth. The metaphor of the river indicates the extreme flowing nature of the *bhāvas.* The general characteristics of *mahābhāva* cannot be described in one verse. As far as possible these have been conveyed.

### Text 161-162

***nimeṣāsahatāsanna-janatā-hṛd-viloḍanam \|***  
***kalpa-kṣaṇatvaṁ khinnatvaṁ tat-saukhye’py ārti-śaṅkayā \|\|161\|\|***  
***mohādy-abhāve’py ātmādi-sarva-vismaraṇaṁ sadā \|***  
***kṣaṇasya kalpetyādyā yatra yoga-viyogayoḥ \|\|162\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***rūdhā-bhāva*****, the** ***anubhāvas*** **are intolerance of a moment, agitation of the heart of onlookers, a** ***kalpa*** **becoming a moment, distress when Kṛṣṇa is happy because of fearing he is in pain, forgetting oneself in the absence of fainting, and a moment becoming a** ***kalpa.*** **These appear during meeting and separation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having shown *rūḍha-bhāva* by manifestation of *sāttvika-bhāvas,* now manifestations of *anubhāvas* are shown. Symptoms during meeting and separation will be understood in the examples.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Anubhāvas* of *rūdha* and *adhirūḍha-bhāva* are described with characteristics. From the examples, cases of separation and union will be understood.

### Text 163

***tatra nimeṣāsahatā, yathā śrī-daśame (10.82.38)—***  
***gopyaś ca kṛṣṇam upalabhya cirād abhīṣṭaṁ***  
***yat-prekṣaṇe dṛśiṣu pakṣma-kṛtaṁ śapanti \|***  
***dṛgbhir hṛdī-kṛtam alaṁ parirabhya sarvās***  
***tad-bhāvam āpur api nitya-yujāṁ durāpam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intolerance of a moment, from the Tenth Canto: While gazing at their beloved Kṛṣṇa, the young gopīs used to condemn the creator of their eyelids, which would momentarily block their vision of him. Now, seeing Kṛṣṇa again after such a long separation, with their eyes they took him into their hearts, and there they embraced him to their full satisfaction. In this way they became totally absorbed in** ***mahābhāva*** **unattainable by the queens who constantly associated with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“In *anurāga, vaicittya-vipralambha* was mentioned. This is a vision of separation even though the lovers are together. *Nimeṣāsahatvam* in *rūḍha-bhāva* means there is intolerance of a very short period of separation. In the former type, imagining separation though it has not taken place, one cannot tolerate it. In the latter type, one shows intolerance by thinking a very short separation is very long period, without imagining the lover’s absence. Intolerance of a moment in *mahābhāva* does not seem more remarkable than *vaicittya-vipralambha* of *anurāga*.”

The quotation from *Bhāgavatam* resolves this doubt. The verse describes the *gopīs’* seeing Kṛṣṇa for the first time in Kurukṣetra. They curse Brahmā who made lids on their eyes.

*yasyānanaṁ makara-kuṇḍala-cāru-karṇa-*  
*bhrājat-kapola-subhagaṁ savilāsa-hāsam*  
*nityotsavaṁ na tatṛpur dṛśibhiḥ pibantyo*  
*nāryo narāś ca muditāḥ kupitā nimeś ca*

**The joyful** ***gopīs*** **and** ***priya-narma-sakhas*** **drank with their eyes Kṛṣṇa’s face, a continual festival of delight, with its playful smile, attractive with beautiful cheeks and ears shining from his** ***makaras*** **earrings. But they could not be fully satisfied, and became angry with the creator who made their eyes blink. SB 9.2.65**

The meaning is that some women became angry at the creator of blinking, though ordinary women also saw Kṛṣṇa. Ordinary women however did not have special *prema.* The *gopīs* imagined (*hṛdi-kṛtam*) embracing him and attained transformations of *mahābhāva (tad-bhāvam āpur).* Such a mood was not available to the queens of Dvārakā who thought “We are eternally united with Kṛṣṇa (*nitya-yujām*) and those *gopīs* are not.” One should not say that this *bhāva* is rare for yogīs (*nitya-yujām*), since that interpretation rejects what is close at hand and gives respect to *yogīs* as if they were eternally related with Kṛṣṇa.

*etāḥ paraṁ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo*  
*govinda eva nikhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ*  
*vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṁ ca*  
*kiṁ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya*

**Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a high-class** ***brāhmaṇa,*** **or even as Lord Brahmā himself? SB 10.47.58**

The *gopīs* had that *bhāva* previously, whereas the yogīs did not. The *bhāva* of the *gopīs* and yogīs should not be equated at all.

What was said is this. *Vaicittya-vipralambha* has lack of awareness because of the confusion arising from fear during *prema,* according to the logic of “longing to see when not present, and fearing separation when present.” Intolerance of a moment means that one imagines a long extension of time for a period of time which is actually very short. Thus, inattention by mental confusion out of fear is seen in common life. One cannot even experience the duration of a *nimeṣa* since it is so short. Since the case of impossibility is stronger in intolerance of a moment in *mahābhāva, vaicittya-vipralambha* in *anurāga* is not as intense. This intolerance of the shortest separation shows the intensity of the mood of trespassing respect of the public and *dharma*

This special nature will also be shown later. Such qualities as intolerance of a moment are also found in the great devotees:

*arva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyed bhagavad-bhāvam ātmanaḥ*  
*bhūtāni bhagavaty ātmany eṣa bhāgavatottamaḥ*

**The most advanced devotee sees Supreme Lord, one’s object of worship, within everything, and sees everything in the Supreme Lord. SB 11.2.45**

In the eight verses at the end of SB 11.2, eight qualities of the great devotees are shown in eight verses, such as:

*gṛhītvāpīndriyair arthān yo na dveṣṭi na hṛṣyati*  
*viṣṇor māyām idaṁ paśyan sa vai bhāgavatottamaḥ*

**Even while engaging his senses in contact with their objects, one who sees this whole world as the energy of Lord Viṣṇu is neither repelled nor elated. He is indeed the greatest among devotees. SB 11.2.48**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śukadeva describes the bliss of the Vraja women on seeing Kṛṣṇa when they went to Kurukṣetra. The *gopīs* experienced Kṛṣṇa. This means that they tasted the sweetness according to their *prema.* The long vowel in *hṛdīkṛtam* is poetic license. Bringing him into their hearts, they embraced him strongly (*alam*) and attained *mahābhāvam (bhāvam).* This means they attained bliss arising from *mahābhāva,* which was not attained by the queens who thought “we are eternally with him (*nitya-yujām*) and they are not.” Or they attained oneness with Kṛṣṇa (*bhāvam*). “Then how are they different from *jñānīs*? *Jñānīs* become one with Kṛṣṇa as Paramātmā.” The verse answers. This state is not possible for the *ārūḍha-yogīs (nitya-yujām*) because they merge by *jñāna.* The merging arising from fainting during *prema* is very special in its type and quantity of bliss. Śukadeva criticizes the *jñānīs* in Parīkṣit’s assembly. Who are these *gopīs*? There special qualities are described. On seeing Kṛṣṇa, they cursed Brahmā who made lids on their eyes. They could not tolerate separation for a very small, undetectable duration of time. Though they were very tolerant and were devotees of all *devatās,* they cursed Brahmā. “O Brahmā! Since you give such suffering, you should quickly die. Let another Brahmā be born who will not create eyelids for us.” In a similar verses SB 9.24.65, the women mentioned are the *gopīs* and the men mentioned are the *priya-narma-sakhas* like Subala.

### Text 164

***āsanna-janatā-hṛd-viloḍanaṁ, yathā—***  
***sakhyaḥ prokṣya kurūn guru-kṣiti-bhṛtām āghūrṇayantī śiraḥ***  
***svasthā viślathayanty aśeṣa-ramaṇīr āplāvya sarvaṁ janam \|***  
***gopīnām anurāga-sindhu-laharī satyāntaraṁ vikramair***  
***ākramya stimitāṁ vyadhād api parāṁ vaikuṇṭha-kaṇṭha-śriyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitating of the hearts of persons who approach: O friends! The waves of the ocean of the** ***gopīs’ anurāga*** **flooded the Kuru dynasty, made the heads of the great kings roll, inundated all people, unsettled the chaste women, attacked the heart of Satyabhāmā and stunned Rukmiṇī.**

**The waves of the ocean flowed in the Kuru province, made the mountain peaks shake, inundated Janaloka, caused worry to the women in Svarga, attacked the center of Satyaloka and made the highest beauty of Vaikuṇṭha limp.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kurūn* means the Kuru dynasty or the province Kuru. *Guru-kṣiti-bhṛtām* means the great kings or mountains. *Svasthāḥ* means health persons or persons situated in Svarga. The *gopīs’* love made unlimited women lax. *Janam* means people or Jana-loka. *Satyantaram* means the mind of Satyabhāmā or the inner part of Satyaloka. *Stimitām* means stunned or soft. *Vaikuṇṭha-kaṇṭha-śriyam* means Rukmiṇī or the ultimate beauty of Vaikuṇṭha. Though Kṛṣṇa hid the *gopīs* from the Kurus, their *bhāvas* though hidden, were beneficial for them and created taste in them. By a bold, poetic statement indicating their exalted position using *udāttālaṅkara* pleasure is created, just as by hearing good qualities everything is purified.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some devotee women inhabitants of Dvārakā, relishing *rasa,* meeting at Kurukṣetra, talk to each other. The waves of the *gopīs* love floods the Kuru dynasty and the Kuru province. It sprinkles them with tears. It makes the heads of the great kings or the tops of the mountains roll about, because of the speed of the currents and the astonishment arising from seeing the *gopīs*’ love. The waves of their love flood all mankind and Janaloka, and give disturbance to unlimited women situated in Svarga, because they feared drowning. Or the waves of the *gopīs’* love make the women who are chaste to their husbands *(svasthāḥ*) become unsteady. The waves moisten the heart of Satyabhāmā or the center of Satyaloka and the beauty of Vaikuṇṭha. The waves make Rukmiṇī, who embraces Kṛṣṇa’s neck, stunned out of joy.

“Agitating the hearts of those who approach” means it agitates those who hear about or see persons with *mahābhāva.* There is no story relating how the queens like Satyabhāmā who were confined to their inner chambers or the great kings who came there met personally with the women of Vraja.

### Text 165

***kalpa-kṣaṇatvam, yathā—***  
***śaraj-jyotsnī rāse vidhir ajani-rūpāpi nimiṣā-***  
***datikṣudrā tāsāṁ yad ajani na tad vismaya-padam \|***  
***sukhotsekārambhe nimiṣa-lava-kalpām iva daśāṁ***  
***mahā-kalpākalpāpy ahaha labhate kāla-kalanā \|\|165\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A** ***kalpa*** **passing in a moment: That the autumn moonlit night lasting the night of Brahmā became shorter than a moment for the** ***gopīs*** **is not astonishing. When they were inundated with bliss, the duration of even Brahmā’s life became a few seconds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śrīdhara Svāmī says that the night became lengthened in commenting on the following verse:

*kṛṣṇa-vikrīḍitaṁ vīkṣya mumuhuḥ khe-cara-striyaḥ*  
*kāmārditāḥ śaśāṅkaś ca sa-gaṇo vismito ’bhavat*

**The wives of the demigods, observing Kṛṣṇa’s playful activities from their airplanes, were entranced and became agitated with lust. Indeed, even the moon and his entourage, the stars, became astonished. SB 10.33.19**

This should be consolidated with the following verse to show that it happened:

*brahma-rātra upāvṛtte vāsudevānumoditāḥ*  
*anicchantyo yayur gopyaḥ sva-gṛhān bhagavat-priyāḥ*

**After an entire night of Brahmā had passed, Lord Kṛṣṇa advised the** ***gopīs*** **to return to their homes. Although they did not wish to do so, the Lord’s beloved consorts complied with his command. SB 10.32.38**

This was possible because the planets, like the rivers, became stunned.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. The night with the autumn moon, equal to Brahmā’s night became short, because when they experienced happiness. A hundred years of Brahmā, becoming impossible (*akalpa*) or very short in terms of measuring time (*kāla-kalanā*), attained the state of a short moment. The root *kala* means counting.

### Text 166

***tat-saukhye’py ārti-śaṅkayā khinnatvam, yathā śrī-daśame (10.31.19)—***  
***yat te sujāta-caraṇāmbu-ruhaṁ staneṣu***  
***bhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu***  
***tenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṁ svit;***  
***kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṁ naḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Suffering on thinking that Kṛṣṇa is suffering, though they try to please him, from the Tenth Canto: O beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in you. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as you roam about on the forest path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is said *aniṣṭhāśaṅkīnīva bandhu-hṛdayāni*: a relative or intimate friend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved. (*Abhijñāna-śakuntalā-nāṭaka*) The *gopīs* are always enager to do anything for Kṛṣṇa’s happiness. Since this tendency appears even in *rati,* it is not unique to *mahābhāva.* But the uniqueness is confirmed in *Bhāgavatam* in this verse. The meaning is this.

“O beloved! You are the object of love that cannot be given up. Your lotus feet which are very soft, we gently place on our breasts.” The plural is used because of their understanding is that they had all reached perfection. It cannot be explained otherwise. They do this gently because their breasts are hard. The verb *dadhimahi* is in the *atmanepada* form to express the result of the action accruing to the doer. One may worry that this shows they have personal desire. However the word *priya* next to the verb refutes this. Because you are dear to us, we do this. It is said that the knowers of happiness recognize the happiness from the touch of the beloved, which touches the heart. Thus, they do not have personal desire (they desire to give happiness to Kṛṣṇa by having him receive their touch). Stating the reason for touching his feet, they ask as if criticizing. “If you wander in the forest, does it hurt or not because of the pebbles? It must hurt. You are cruel to your own limbs.” Let it hurt. What is that to you? “Our minds become agitated because of your pain.” Why is that? “You are our life (bhavad-āyuṣām). If we have separate lives, then what you say is reasonable. If you are our life, then how can we bear even a slight injury to our life?” There will be anxiety for the object of regard, as was stated earlier. “A relative or intimate friend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved.” Those with *rati* do not worry as the *gopīs* do about his feet touching rocks. Though those with *rati* also worry for Kṛṣṇa’s happiness, this tendency becomes most clear in *mahābhāva*. Like the sweetness of sugar cane reaching perfection in rock candy, the tendency in *mahābhāva* is extreme.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is said “A relative or intimate friend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved.” A person become completely disturbed and will even die on seeing a little harm to the beloved. “Though I know the great happiness of Kṛṣṇa, and that there is no possibility of him suffering at all, I still do not know. Perhaps he suffers.” The person worries by attributing suffering though it is useless. This quality becomes outstanding in *mahābhava.*

The women of Vraja lament after Kṛṣṇa disappeared during the *rāsa* dance. “Let us place your very soft lotus feet on our breasts.” They also have fear. “Why do they fear?” They explain. Our breasts are hard. “Then why do place his feet there?” O beloved! You will be pleased in having your feet on our breasts. It is for your happiness. “But placing his feet on your breasts indicates your happiness, though it is painful for his feet.” They become distressed. We will place those feet gently. In uniting with you, we must suffer. That is written on our foreheads by fate. This is the hint. What austerity must we do? If we pray to the creator for soft breasts, this will not give you happiness. And because they are hard, your feet suffer. Either way we are stuck. Let that be. Both meeting and separation are problematic for us. Though you are carefree, you endure such suffering. With those feet you wander in the forest. What great rashness! Are those lotus feet suitable for the walking in the forest? The question is meant as criticism. You suffer, but are cruel to your own limbs just as you are cruel to us.

Or, Kṛṣṇa thinks “They suffer by my suffering. In order to make them suffer I should create suffering for myself and tolerant it.” That is why you tolerate your suffering. Or, seeing our suffering you become blissful. Therefore you consider your suffering to be happiness. Or, it is said that natural faults become good qualities. Previously your heart was as soft as a flower, but by association with our hard breasts it has become hard. Similarly, your feet have become hard by association with our breasts. Thus they do not feel pain from the stones.

Or, because of the blessing of getting touched by your feet, the stones also become soft. Or, because the earth is very merciful, or because of greed to taste your sweetness, the earth has placed her tongue wherever you place your feet. Or, you, being an ocean of mercy to us, pained by separation from us by fate, have become bewildered, and attained a state of *unmada.* Thus you are not aware of the pain in your feet. In this way, considering many reasons, our minds have come distracted. We cannot be sure of anything.

“You express your suffering in this way. I do not consider that suffering because your life remains.” You are our life. Our lives are in you. Because of being situated in you who are auspicious, our lives are not destroyed by these calamities. The meaning is this. Like you, the creator is inclined to make us suffer. He considers “If I establish their lives in pain now, then they will immediately die on being burned by intense pain given by me. Then who can I give suffering to? Placing their lives in Kṛṣṇa, my friend, who is like me in being cruel, they will not die, but experience more suffering.” Thus we do not die.

Or, not discerning the cause, our minds become disturbed, but we are not destroyed by that disturbance. The reason is that our lives continue to exist (*bhavad āyusām*) properly, since life protects the vital organs. Or, not determining the cause, our minds are disturbed, but our life airs, understanding the cause, leave the body. You should see this. Or, “If your life remains, how can you die?” Our lives have been given to you. Play with them in Vraja.

### Text 167

***mohādy-abhāve’pi sarva-vismaraṇaṁ, yathā ekādaśe (11.12.12)—***  
***tā nāvidan mayy anuṣaṅga-baddha-***  
***dhiyaḥ svam ātmānam adas tathedam***  
***yathā samādhau munayo’bdhi-toye***  
***nadyaḥ praviṣṭā iva nāma-rūpe \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Forgetting everything, even without fainting, from the Eleventh Canto: My dear Uddhava, just as great sages in yoga trance merge into self-realization, and just as rivers merging into the ocean, and are thus not aware of material names and forms, similarly, the** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana were so completely attached to me within their minds that they could not think of their own bodies, or of this world, or of their future lives. Their entire consciousness was simply bound up in me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Without fainting, after Kṛṣṇa’ disappears, the *gopīs* forget everything. These two elements go together. They were attached to Kṛṣṇa within their minds because they had seen him suddenly one time (a *sphūrti*). They then became unaware of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Moh*a means fainting. The word *ādi* indicates agitation, depression and other emotions. The cause of their forgetting themselves and objects around them is intense remembrance of the form and qualities of Kṛṣṇa with possessiveness. Unless there is no attachment to husband and mother-in-law they cannot have such possessiveness of Kṛṣṇa. That is seen in this example.

Kṛṣṇa informs Uddhava of the supreme qualities of love and gentleness in the *gopīs* by describing some of their special qualities. Their intelligence was bound by continuous association with me. The word “bound” indicates they became stunned by the wonderful pastimes which astonished the three worlds, that they were tied strongly with association, and that Kṛṣṇa became like a desire cow yielding all desires for their minds. They did not know their bodies (*ātmānam*). During the *rāsa* dance they did not know where they were or where they were going. They were not aware of the next world (*adaḥ*), because they had trespassed *dharma* without worry, and they were not aware of this world (*idam*) because they overcame shyness and fear. Just as the yogīs forget everything and realize Brahman, the *gopīs* forget everything and realize Kṛṣṇa. This example shows forgetting everything. Just as rivers enter the ocean and their names and forms cannot be recognized, so the *gopīs* cannot recognize their names or forms when entering intense experience of *rasa*. This example shows the intense experience of *rasa.*

### Text 168

***kṣaṇa-kalpatā, yathā tatraiva (11.12.11)—***  
***tās tāḥ kṣapāḥ preṣṭha-tamena nītā***  
***mayaiva vṛndāvana-gocareṇa \|***  
***kṣaṇārdha-vat tāḥ punar aṅga tāsāṁ***  
***hīnā mayā kalpa-samā babhūvuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A moment seems like a** ***kalpa*****, from the Eleventh Canto: Dear Uddhava, all of those nights that the** ***gopīs*** **spent with me, their most dearly beloved, in the land of Vṛndāvana seemed to them to pass in less than a moment. Bereft of my association, however, the** ***gopīs*** **felt that those same nights dragged on forever, as if each night were equal to a day of Brahmā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks. In this verse a moment seems like a *kalpa* due to separation, and *kalpa* seems like a moment during meeting.

### Text 169

***ādya-śabdād iha proktā kṛṣṇāvirbhāva-kāritā \|***  
***sambhoga-bhede vispaṣṭaṁ sā purastāt pravakṣyate \|\|169\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The word** ***ādyaḥ*** **in verse 162 indicates** ***anubhāvas*** **which cause Kṛṣṇa to appear. These will be described later, in the type of enjoyment called** ***sampanna.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *ādyaḥ* in verse 162 indicates other symptoms which cause Kṛṣṇa to appear. His appearance is described in the following verses:

*gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur*  
*dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām*  
*bhuṅkte svayaṁ yad avaśiṣṭa-rasaṁ hradinyo*  
*hṛṣyat-tvaco ‘śru mumucus taravo yathāryaḥ*

**My dear** ***gopīs,*** **what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lips independently and leave only a taste for us** ***gopīs*****, for whom that nectar is actually meant! The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are standing like hair on her body. SB 10.21.9**

*tāsām āvirabhūc chauriḥ smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ*  
*pītāmbara-dharaḥ sragvī sākṣān manmatha-manmathaḥ*

**Then Lord Kṛṣṇa, a smile on his lotus face, appeared before the** ***gopīs.*** **Wearing a garland and a yellow garment, he directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, who himself bewilders the minds of ordinary people. Sb 10.32.2**

*tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*madhye maṇīnāṁ haimānāṁ mahā-marakato yathā*

**In the midst of the dancing** ***gopīs,*** **Lord Kṛṣṇa appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire in the midst of golden ornaments. SB 10.33.6**

He is realized according to hearing, but only by devotees.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa’s appearance takes place in a type amorous enjoyment called sampanna (*sambhoga-bhede).* The appearance of Kṛṣṇa, producing all types of happiness in amorous enjoyment, will be understood by consulting later parts of the work. “The appearance of Kṛṣṇa” means close association with him which takes place only in devotes with *prema.*

### Text 170

***atha adhirūḍhaḥ—***  
***rūḍhoktebhyo’nubhāvebhyaḥ kām apy āptā viśiṣṭatām \|***  
***yatrānubhāvā dṛśyante so’dhirūḍho nigadyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When the a*****nubhāvas*** **attain an inconceivably greater excellence than those** ***of rūḍha-bhāva*****, the condition is called** ***adhirūḍha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kām api* means inconceivable.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Anubhāva* here means *sāttvika-bhāvas.* They become special, beyond *sūddīptā,* since they are present during *mohana* state.

### Text 171

***yathā śiva-vākyam—***  
***lokātīatam ajāṇḍa-koṭigam api traikālikaṁ yat sukhaṁ***  
***duḥkhaṁ ceti pṛthag yadi sphuṭam ubhe te gacchataḥ kuṭatām \|***  
***naivābhāsa-tulāṁ śive tad api tat kuṭa-dvayaṁ rādhikā-***  
***premodyat-sukha-duḥkha-sindhu-bhavayor vindeta bindvor api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Śiva speaks: O Parvatī, if all the happiness and pain in the spiritual worlds of Vaikuṇtha, and in the millions of material universes in past, present and future, were added together, they would barely equal two drops in the oceans of bliss and pain that spring from Rādhā's love for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śiva speaks to Pārvatī, when she asks about symptoms of Rādhā. The suffering beyond the material world refers to suffering caused by separation from Kṛṣṇa. *Kūṭatām* means piled up.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śiva speaks to Pārvatī when she asks him about the special *prema* of Rādhā. The happiness of Vaikuṇṭha (*lokātītam*) is the happiness of liberation. The suffering there is produced by devotees’ longing in *prema.* All the happiness and distress in the spiritual world and the millions of universes of *māyā* or Brahmā (*aja),* in past, present and furure, if piled up together, making two mountains, would not become even two drops in the ocean of happiness and suffering swelled by the *prema* of Rādhā, having only some slight similarity.

One should not imagine that *mahābhāva* is not the ultimate goal on hearing that it involves suffering and lacks prudent behavior, since this suffering is the essence of the *hlādinī* and *saṁvit śaktis,* arising from the *svarūpa-śakti.* It is *bhakti* only.

*brahmānando bhaved eṣa cet parārddha-guṇīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*naiti bhakti-sukhāmbhodheḥ paramāṇu-tulām api \|\|*

**If the bliss of Brahman realization were accumulated by** ***samādhi*** **lasting from half of Brahmā’s life, it cannot compare to one drop of the ocean of the happiness of** ***bhakti.*** **BRS 1.1.38**

It is also said *muktiṁ dadāti karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam*: the Lord gives liberation but not even *bhāva-bhakti* to those who worship him. (SB 5.6.18) These verses show that the happiness of *bhakti* is much great than that of millions of universes. That happiness, which produces heat in the form of suffering, is tastier than millions of moons. Thus, how much more tasty will be *mahābhāva*! In the material world, in the presence of heat, coolness gives happiness. In the presence of coolness, heat gives happiness. Thus if both are present happiness arises. If one is absent, the other becomes suffering.

Hunger and an object to be eaten together produce happiness. Without the object to be eaten, hunger produces suffering. Without hunger, the edible object does not produce happiness. In *rati* and other *bhāvas*, even in union, because the anxiety of separation cannot be completely removed, which prevents the feeling of having enough, the union produces happiness. In separation, since the separation has continuous meeting through dreams or in the mind because of his sudden appearance through remembrance (*sphūrti),* the separation becomes filled with happiness.

In *adhirūḍha-bhāva* however there is simultaneous, incomparable happiness and suffering caused by union and separation. This produces an incomparable happiness.

But we do not see simultaneous happiness and distress in Svarga or hell in the material world. Though one can observe simultaneous happiness and suffering at the beginning of eating for instance, because this is limited, it cannot be accepted as a rule. In impersonal liberation, because of the absence of suffering, one experiences happiness. It depends on suffering however. Some say however that liberation means complete absence of happiness and suffering. Thus *prema* and nothing else is the supreme goal of human life. This is the conclusion. Actually, the devotees say that actually *prema* functions not by seeing one’s own happiness, but by seeing Kṛṣṇa’s happiness.

### Text 172

***modano mādanaś cāsāv adhirūḍho dvidhocyate \|\|172\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Adhirūḍha-bhāva*** **has two types:** ***modana*** **and** ***mādana*****.**

### Text 173

***tatra modanaḥ—***  
***modanaḥ sa dvayor yatra sāttvikoddīpta-sauṣṭhavam \|\|173\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Modana*** **is the condition in which the couple exhibits all** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **in extreme** ***uddīpta*** **state.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Modana* and *mādana* indicate by the root meaning of the words amorous enjoyment. Mādana comes from the root *mad,* meaning joy and trembling. He quotes *mitām hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4 92). *Mad* does not retain a short vowel as other verbs of that class do.3 Modana means joy.??? *Mādana* means a type of wine which causes intoxication.

### Text 174

***yathā lalita-mādhave (8.9)—***  
***ātanvan kala-kaṇṭha-nādam atulaṁ stambha-śriyojjṛmbhito***  
***bhūyiṣṭhocchalad-aṅkuraḥ phalitavān svedāmbu-muktā-phalaiḥ \|***  
***udyad-bāṣpa-maranda-bhāg-avicalo’py utkampavān vibhramai***  
***rādhā-mādhavayor virājati cirād ullāsa-kalpa-drumaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: The desire tree of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's bliss eternally shines, spread with the choked voices like warbling of cuckoos, revealing beauty in its stunned trunk, bursting with abundant buds, bearing fruit in the form of pearls of perspiration, being steady with tears of honey, and trembling with grace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kala-kaṇṭha-nādam* means sounds from the throat, or songs of the cuckoo*. Stambha* means being stunned or a tree trunk. The tree or their *adhirūḍha-bhāva* strongly reveals the beauty of its trunk or the beauty of being stunned. Another version has *śriyā jṛmbhitaḥ*. Their hairs standing on end are like buds abuandantly emerging. *Avicala* means unmoving. The tree shakes with grace (*vibhramaiḥ*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nava-vṛndā describes the meeting of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa after a long time. The desire tree of bliss of the couple together exists as the fulfillment of the desires of friends. The tree of that bliss is described in terms of the symptoms of *modana-bhāva.* *Kalakaṇṭha* is a cuckoo or the choked voice which sounds sweet. The sound spreads everywhere completely *(ā*). This is *uddīpta-sauṣṭhavam*, excellence of *uddīpta.* The other symptoms are also understood to be extreme. *Stambha* is the tree trunk, the *sāttvika-bhāva* of being stunned.  *Ankūra* are buds or hair standing on end. The tree is unmoving but trembles because of the birds’ (*vīna*) movement or because of various gestures.

### Text 175

***harer yatra sa-kāntasya vikṣobha-bhara-kāritā \|***  
***premoru-sampad-vikhyāta-kāntātiśayitādayaḥ \|\|175\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***modana,*** **intense agitation of Kṛṣṇa along with his lovers becomes greater than the love of other women who are famous as a treasure of the greatest** ***prema.*** **Many other symptoms also appear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sa-kāntasya* means “along with his lovers.” He exhibits more *prema* that his lovers who are famous as a wealth of the greatest *prema.* This is the quality of *modana.* *Ādayaḥ* means other unlimited qualities also appear in him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Where *modana* exists between himself and his lovers, it exhibits greater love than that possessed by women such as Candrāvalī who are famous for a wealth great *prema.* Other qualities *(ādayaḥ*) in persons with differeing natures are also indicated.

### Text 176

***rādhikā-yūtha evāsau modano na tu sarvataḥ \|***  
***yaḥ śrīmān hlādinī-śakteḥ suvilāsaḥ priyo varaḥ \|\|176\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Modana*** **appears in Rādhā’s group and not in all** ***gopīs.*** ***Modana*** **is ultimate activity of the** ***hlādinī-śakti.***  **It is affectionate, endowed with all auspiciousness and most excellent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Where is *modana* visible? It is found in Rādhā’s group. It is the highest manifestation which starts with *madhu-sneha.* The commentary on *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* 1.2.59 and *Bhāgavatam* 10.3.41, and 10.21.17 show Rādhā’s supreme position.

*pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāya-padābja-rāga*  
*śrī-kuṅkumena dayitā-stana-maṇḍitena*  
*tad-darśana-smara-rujas tṛṇa-rūṣitena*  
*limpantya ānana-kuceṣu jahus tad-ādhim*

**The aborigine women of the Vṛndāvana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass marked with reddish kuṅkuma powder. Endowed with the color of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts of his beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they feel fully satisfied and give up all their anxiety. SB 10.21.17**

*na vayaṁ sādhvi sāmrājyaṁ svārājyaṁ bhaujyam apy uta*  
*vairājyaṁ pārameṣṭhyaṁ ca ānantyaṁ vā hareḥ padam*  
*kāmayāmaha etasya śrīmat-pāda-rajaḥ śriyaḥ*  
*kuca-kuṅkuma-gandhāḍhyaṁ mūrdhnā voḍhuṁ gadā-bhṛtaḥ*

**O saintly lady, we do not desire dominion over the earth, the sovereignty of the King of heaven, unlimited facility for enjoyment, mystic power, the position of Lord Brahmā, immortality or even attainment of the kingdom of God. We simply desire to carry on our heads the glorious dust of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s feet, enriched by the fragrance of kuṅkuma from his consort’s bosom. SB 10.83.41-42**

In these verses Rādhā is indicated by use of the word *śrī*. *Śrī* cannot refer to Lakṣmī since the Lord’s feet related to Vaikuṇṭha is rejected. *Śrī* cannot mean Rukmiṇī because the Pulindya women did not know her. Among all the women of Vraja, Rādhā is the most fortunate. *Anayārādhito nūnaṁ*: Kṛṣṇa is worshipped by her. (SB 10.30.28) This refers only to Rādhā. This is also understood from *Matsya Purāṇa*: *rukmiṇī dvāravatyām tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane:* as Rukmiṇī is the chief queen in Dvārakā, Rādhā is the chief *gopī* in Vṛndāvana. It is also said:

*devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā \|*  
*sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā \|\|*

**Dear Rādhā, filled with thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, is the supreme goddess. She is the embodiment of all women, possesses all beauty, and is the supreme bewilderer.** ***Gautamīya-tantra***

*Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa* says:

*rādhayā mādhavo devo mādhavenaiva rādhikā \| vibhrājante janeṣvā*

**Mādhava is revealed to the people through Rādhā and Rādhā is revealed through Mādhava.**

Let us return to the topic. Modana is the form of the highest activity (*suvilāsa)* of *hlādinī-śakti.* It is none other than the Lord’s *bhāva.* It is *priyaḥ* or dear, the limit of sweetness in *mahā-bhāva* and the best *(varaḥ).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This means that it does not appear in others like Candrāvalī.  *Modana* is the form of the highest activity (*suvilāsa*) of the *hlādinī-śakti.*  This is *modana’s* aspect as *prema-bhakti.* It is *priya* or dear by residing in his dear women as *madhura-rasa*. It is *śrīmān* or *mahā-bhāva*, residing only in the *gopīs.* It is *vara* (best) by residing in Rādhā’s group.

### Text 177

***tatra sakāntasya hareḥ kṣobha-bhara-kāritā, yathā—***  
***hanta stambha-karambitā bhuvi kuror bhadrā sarasvaty abhūd-***  
***bāṣpaṁ bhāskarajā mumoca tarasā satyābhraman narmadā \|***  
***bheje bhīṣma-sutā ca varṇa-vikṛtiṁ gāmbhīrya-bhāg apy asau***  
***kṛṣṇodanvati rādhikādbhuta-nadī-premormibhiḥ saṁvṛte \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Agitation of Kṛṣṇa with his lover: When the astonishing river of Rādhā with its waves of** ***prema*** **entered the sea of Kṛṣṇa at Kurukṣetra, fluent (Sarasvatī) Bhadrā became stunned and could not speak, Kalindī (Yamunā) shed many tears, joking (Narmadā) Satyabhāmā became bewildered, and grave Rukmiṇī (Gaṅgā) turned white.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

At Kurukṣetra after Kṛṣṇa met the women of Vraja, wondering about Kṛṣṇa’s concealed *bhāvas,* Uddhava began to reflect on seeing the astonishment in Bhadrā and others. The words (*vāṇī*) of Bhadrā) stopped or the auspicious Sarasvatī River stopped. Yamunā realsed torrents of water or Kalindī released tears. The pure Narmadā River wandered about, or joking Satyabhāmā became bewildered. Bhiṣma-sutā is Rukmiṇī or Gaṅgā River.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rukmiṇī and other queens, greatly astonished by the news of Kṛṣṇa meeting with the women of Vraja at Kurukṣetra, desired to see these women, but were isolated in their tents. But they managed to see them. A friend of Rukmiṇī had seen the great agitation in Rukmiṇī and other queens and in Kṛṣṇa when they saw Rādhā’s *modana-bhāva* which arose from seeing Kṛṣṇa. The friend of Rukmiṇī describes to another friend what she saw.

In beginning to speak she expresses amazement (*hanta*). Rādhā is an amazing river, with waves of *prema.* The ocean of Kṛṣṇa has been obstructed by the river of Rādhā’s *prema.* It is amazing that the river can block the ocean. The waves of the river have conquered the waves of the ocean, or the ocean’s water has become petrified. Or, Rādhā’s *prema* is greater than Kṛṣṇa’s *prema.* The words (*vāṇī*) of Bhadrā) stopped or the auspicious Sarasvatī River stopped. Yamunā released torrents of water or Kalindī released hot tears. The pure Narmadā River wandered off course, or joking Satyabhāmā developed *apasmāra.* Bhīṣma-sutā is Rukmiṇī or Gaṅgā River. After some moments her *modana-bhāva* slightly slackened. The queens, having recovered, praised her, offered her respects, and returned to their tents. Rādhā, not in control of her senses, was not aware that they had come.

### Text 178

***premoru-sampadvatī-vṛndātiśayitvaṁ, yathā—***  
***advaitād girijāṁ harārdha-vapuṣaṁ sakhyāt priyoraḥ-sthitāṁ***  
***lakṣmīm acyuta-citta-bhṛṅga-nalinīṁ satyāṁ ca saubhāgyataḥ \|***  
***mādhuryān madhureśa-jīvita-sakhīṁ candrāvalīṁ ca kṣipan***  
***paśyāruddha hariṁ prasārya laharīṁ rādhānurāgāmbudhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Surpassing the wealth of great** ***prema*** **of other women: Look! Rādhā, spreading waves from her ocean of** ***anurāga*****, has stopped Durgā, half of Śiva’s body because she is equal to him. She has obstructed Lakṣmī situated on Viṣṇu’s chest because of her affection. She has surpassed Satyabhāmā, a lotus for the bee of Kṛṣṇa’s mind, because of her good fortune. And she has surpassed Candrāvalī, the life of Kṛṣṇa because of her sweetness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Uddhava speaks. Hearing them speak in *unmāda* (SB 10.47.12) and pointing out the excellence of the Vraja women (SB 10.47.60), Uddhava indicates Rādhā as the supreme form of love. Kṛṣṇa, with no self-control, had said, “Go to Vraja and free the *gopīs* from their pain of separation from me by delivering my message.” Remembering the sweetness of that inconstant form of Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava addresses him as *madhureśa.* Absorbed in *bhāva,* he speaks to himself when he utters “See.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The same friend speaks. *Girijām* means Durgā.  *Satyām* means Satyabhāmā. Kṛṣṇa has been covered by the ocean of Rādhā’s *anurāga.*

### Text 179

***modano’yaṁ praviśleṣa-daśāyāṁ mohano bhavet \|***  
***yasmin viraha-vaivaśyāt sūddīptā eva sāttvikāḥ \|\|179\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Modana*** **becomes** ***mohana*** **in the state of separation. Because of the lack of control during separation, the** ***sāttvika-bhāvas*** **become** ***sūddīpta.***

### Text 180

***yathā—***  
***udyad-vepathu-vādyamāna-daśanā kaṇṭha-sthalāntar luṭhaj-***  
***jalpā gokula-maṇḍalaṁ vidadhatī bāṣpair nadī-mātṛkam \|***  
***rādhā kaṇṭakitena kaṇṭaki-phalaṁ gātreṇa dhik-kurvatī***  
***citraṁ tad-ghana-rāga-rāśibhir api śvetī-kṛtā vartate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Overwhelmed with intense** ***rāga*** **for you, Rādhā loudly clatters her teeth from trembling, stutters with a choked up voice, with her tears makes Gokula a well-watered field, eclipses the jack fruit with her hairs standing on end, and stands like a painting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Uddhava informs Kṛṣṇa after returning from Vraja to Mathurā. *Nadī-mātṛkā* means a watered rice field. Though such tears of separation cannot fill a rice field, the statement shows the greatness of her *prema.* Uddhava says to the gopīs:

*sarvātma-bhāvo ’dhikṛto bhavatīnām adhokṣaje*  
*viraheṇa mahā-bhāgā mahān me ’nugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ.*

**You have rightfully claimed the privilege of unalloyed love for the transcendental Lord, O most glorious** ***gopīs.*** **Indeed, by exhibiting your love for Kṛṣṇa in separation from him, you have shown me great mercy. SB 10.47.27**

*Kaṇṭaki-phalam* is jack fruit. You have turned a picture white with heaps of thick red. The word *api* is added since this seems impossible. The normal meaning is “She surprisingly turned white, by abundant, condensed rāga.” Acccording to scriptures, when rāga for the Lord produces bliss, one becomes bright, not white, which is produced by sorrow. Thus her color is surprising.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

On returning from Vraja to Mathurā, Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa, who asks the news. Her teeth, because of trembling, sound like instruments playing. Her voice is choked up. She floods Vraja with tears, making it a flooded paddy field. *Amara-koṣa* says *nadi-mātṛka* means moistened by rain. “How can the shower of tears nourish the rice, since the tears are hot?” Yes, the tears are hot for a moment, but by falling on the earth they immediately become cool. Actually this is a bold poetic expression and it general meaning should be taken. *Kaṇṭaki-phalam* is jack fruit. *Ghana-rāga-rāśibhiḥ* means “by concentrated redness” or “by concentrated *anurāga.”* The symptoms described are *sūddīpta-bhāvas* because of their extent. For instance the shivering makes the teeth chatter.

### Text 181-183

***atrānubhāvā govinda kāntā-śliṣṭe’pi mūrcchanā \|***  
***asahya-duḥkha-svīkārād api tat-sukha-kāmatā \|\|181\|\|***  
***brahmāṇḍa-kṣobha-kāritvaṁ tiraścām api rodanam \|***  
***sva-bhūtair api tat-saṅga-tṛṣṇā mṛtyu-pratiśravāt \|***  
***divyonmādādayo’py anye vidvadbhir anukīrtitāḥ \|\|182\|\|***  
***prāyo vṛndāvaneśvaryāṁ mohano’yam udañcati \|***  
***samyag-vilakṣaṇaṁ yasya kāryaṁ sañcāri-mohataḥ \|\|183\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***mohana,*** **the** ***anubhāva*****s are as follows. Kṛṣṇa faints during the embrace of another lover. Desiring Kṛṣṇa’s happiness, the beloved accepts intolerable suffering. The universe becomes disturbed. Animals weep. Accepting death, the elements of the body long for Kṛṣṇa’s association.**  ***Divyonmāda*** **which has many symptoms appears. Generally** ***mohana*** **appears in Rādhā. These effects with unique qualities arise from the** ***sañcāri-bhāva*** **called** ***moha.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Fainting during embraces is seen elsewhere. One will see such transformations in people who have great affection and remember a loved one in great separation. One sees people tolerating great suffering. For instance Rāntideva desired the happiness of all beings and suffered for that. Causing disturbance in the universe takes place by the great power of *mohana.* But the disturbance in the universe does not take place by a positive contact with that *bhāva,* but rather because of the pain in that *bhāva.* By association with that *bhāva* one gets disturbance:

*dadhati sakṛn manas tvayi ya ātmani nitya-sukhe*  
*na punar upāsate puruṣa-sāra-harāvasathān*

**Anyone who even once turns his mind toward you, the ever-blissful soul of all existence, no longer dedicates himself to serving family life at home, which simply robs a man of his good qualities. SB 10.87.35**

Animals weep because of the pain. Giving up life is seen in normal life also, like bearing intolerable pain for the beloved. *Unmāda-van nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ*: he sings and dances like a madman, for he is indifferent to public opinion. (SB 11.2.40) This *unmāda* can be seen in Prahlāda and others. Thus it is not a unique quality of *mahābhāva.* How can it be called *divya*?

Such criticisms may be raised. However there are unique qualities in *mohana.* From a predominance of *moha* belonging to the *sañcāri-bhāvas,* the effects of *mohana* are completely unique (*samyag vailakṣaṇam*). These qualities do not exist elsewhere. By contact with *mohana,* disturbance takes place in the whole universe. An example *nāraṁ cukrośa cakram* is given in verse 186. By seeing this *mohana*, all are affected with this *bhāva.*

*nadyas tadā tad upadhārya mukunda-gītam*  
*āvarta-lakṣita-manobhava-bhagna-vegāḥ*

**When the rivers hear the flute-song of Kṛṣṇa, their minds begin to desire him, and thus the flow of their currents is broken and their waters are agitated, moving around in whirlpools. SB 10.21.15**

The description of animals weeping is not repetition of the universe being disturbed. It has unique qualities. Accepting death also has its unique qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Speaking of *anubhāvas*, their characteristics are now described. When embraced by his lovers, during amorous pastimes with Rukmiṇī and others in Dvārakā, on recalling mohana*-bhāva* of Rādhā in Vraja, Kṛṣṇa faints, even in his Dvārakā form. The components of his body match the five gross elements in material bodies. Thus elements are mentioned in relation to Kṛṣṇa’s body. *Pratiśravāt* means “because of acceptance.”

*Mohana* has four states: *prakṛti-sthiti, unmāda, prakopa*, and *mūrcchā.* Intolerable suffering and accepting death and the elements of the body longing for Kṛṣṇa’s association arises from *prakṛti-sthiti*. From *unmāda* arises *citra-jalpa.* In *prakope,* Kṛṣṇa’s fainting during the lover’s embrace and agitation of the universe take place. With slight *prakopa* the nearby animals weep. With extreme *prakopa,* there is also fainting, but because it is hard to endure it is not described.

### Text 184

***tatra kāntāśliṣṭe’pi harau mūrcchā-kāritvaṁ, yathā padyāvalyām (371)—***  
***ratna-cchāyā-cchurita-jaladhau mandire dvārakāyā***  
***rukmiṇyāpi prabala-pulakodbhedam āliṅgitasya \|***  
***viśvaṁ pāyān masṛṇa-yamunā-tīra-vānīra-kuñje***  
***rādhā-kelī-parimala-bhara-dhyāna-mūrcchā murāreḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Fainting when embraced by another lover, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **Even though tightly embraced by Rukmiṇī in a palace in Dvārakā within the sea, colored by the reflection of gems, Kṛṣṇa, remembering the fragrance of Rādhā's pastimes in the forest bower on the lovely shore of the Yamunā, suddenly fainted. May that fainting protect the universe!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a verse by Umāpati-dhara. The ocean was colored by the reflection of gems. *Kelī* is in the feminine for easy understanding*. Mūrccchā* means fainting.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some woman, having come from Mathurā, entered the assembly of *sakhīs* headed by Lalitā in Vraja and gave the following blessing. They were in a palace within the ocean which was colorful with reflections of rubies and other jewels attached to the columns, turrets and towers. This was an *uddīpana*. Kṛṣṇa was embracing Rukmiṇī, the *ālambana-vibhāva*, and his hairs stood on end strongly. The *sthāyi-bhāva* of enjoying, *sañcāri-bhāvas* such as joy, and *anubhāvas* and *sāttvika-bhāvas* manifested clearly. Rukmiṇī is indicated as the embracer, acting as in the masculine role during enjoyment. May the fainting of Kṛṣṇa in this situation protect the universe! This indicates that he should protect Vraja. If Kṛṣṇa protects Vraja with its *kadamba* trees and residences, and all the *śaktis* such as *hlādinī,* the whole universe is protected. But he can only do this by coming to Vraja. The intention is “Make Kṛṣṇa come to Vraja quickly.” He remembered the fragrance of pastimes of Rādhā. This indicates a desire creeper which could fulfill all of Kṛṣṇa’s desires. Though there were all ingredients for happiness in Dvārakā, Kṛṣṇa in anxiety for attaining his desires, was inclined to go to Vṛndāvana. That is conveyed by the messenger. The verse is by the poet Umāpati-dhara.

### Text 185

*asahya-duḥkha-svīkārāt tat-sukha-kāmatā—*
