***syān naḥ saukhyaṁ yad api balavad goṣṭham āpte mukunde***  
***yady alpāpi kṣatir udayate tasya māgāt kadāpi \|***  
***aprāpte’smin yad api nagarād ārtir ugrā bhaven naḥ***  
***saukhyaṁ tasya sphurati hṛdi cet tatra vāsaṁ karotu \|\|185\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Enduring the greatest suffering for Kṛṣṇa’s happiness: If Mukunda returns to Vraja we would be very happy, but if his return makes him slightly unhappy, he should not come. If Krishna does not come here from Mathurā city, we will suffer intensely, but if that brings happiness to his heart, let him remain there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

We will suffer severely. This indicates *moha,* fainting.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Uddhava who asks “What message should I deliver to your beloved?” when he is about to leave for Mathurā. *Nagarāt* means from Mathurā. By direct and opposite statements it shows desiring Kṛṣṇa’s happiness while enduring great suffering. Though in the material world a woman sends messages to her beloved in a distant land, it does not invoke *prema*, what to speak of *mohana* in *mahā-bhāva.* Though there may be desire for such statements, there is lack of the same intensity. If a person gives up all possessiveness of body, house, wealth and sons, that becomes a cause of possessiveness for his beloved. If that happens, then intensity of *prema* would arise. It will not be generated by renunciation and inquiry into truth through *jñāna.* Rādhā accepted suffering. Rāntideva’s suffering cannot be compared to it. Previously Śiva said that the suffering of the universes cannot compare to Rādhā’s suffering. The intense pain that takes place in the variety of *mahābhāva* called *mohana,* on the seventh stage of *prema,* will be clear in verse 187. Though she experiences intolerable suffering within, Rādhā sends this message to Kṛṣṇa. This is most exceptional in the material and spiritual worlds.

### Text 186

***brahmāṇḍa-kṣobha-kāritvaṁ, yathā—***  
***nāraṁ cukrośa cakraṁ phaṇi-kulam abhavad vyākulaṁ svedam ūhe***  
***vṛndaṁ vṛndārakāṇāṁ pracura-mudam amucann aśru vaikuṇṭha-bhājaḥ \|***  
***rādhāyāś citram īśa bhramati diśi diśi prema-niḥśvāsa-dhūme***  
***pūrṇānande’py uṣitvā bahir idam abahiś cārtam āsīd ajāṇḍam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Causing disturbance in the whole universe: O Lord! When Rādhā’s vapor from her breath of** ***prema*** **wondrously traveled in all directions, all men shouted, the snakes suffered pain, the** ***devatās*** **perspired, and the inhabitants of Vaikuṇṭha shed tears. Though the inside and outside of the universe was filled with bliss, there was also suffering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Someone coming from Vraja speaks to Kṛṣṇa, informing him of the disturbance caused by Rādhā’s strong *bhāva*. This transformation of *mahābhāva* is occasional, not constant. Thus the description is in the past tense. The perfect tense is used to show completion. The shouting of the population indicates their *moha.* Though it was natural to have bliss from *prema,* this caused suffering because of a portion of it was tinged with separation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mention of the universe being disturbed also included Vaikuṇṭha. Since *mohana* is the essence of the *cit-śakti,* it has power in the spiritual world. When Rādhā in Vraja during separation experienced extreme *mohana-bhāva,* Nāndīmukhī saw and experienced the disturbance as if it were illness in all the spiritual and material worlds. She quickly went to Dvārakā and informed Kṛṣṇa.

All humanity shouted or cried loudly. The snakes and all the inhabitants of the seven lower planets experienced pain. The inhabitants of the seven upper planets perspired. The inhabitants of Vaikuṇṭha such as Lakṣmī shed profuse tears. When? O Lord! You know since you are the Supreme Lord. What are you asking? This happened when Rādhā’s breathe of *prema* wandered in all directions wondrously. Her breathing arose from *mohana*. Outside the universe in Vaikuṇṭha, and within the universe in the fourteen planetary systems, all experienced pain and disturbance.

Hear what was amazing. Though there was full bliss, this happened. The word *pūrṇa* indicates it was not material bliss. The universe enjoyed (*uṣitvā*) this spiritual bliss. The verb ending *tvā* indicates simultaneous action. While enjoying bliss, they suffered. This is astonishing. Actually the suffering is an expression of full bliss. The past tense of “they shouted” indicates extreme *mohana,* which is not continuous. The perfect tense indicates their *moha* or fainting*.*

Kṛṣṇa answered, “Nāndīmukhī! You are fortunate. You speak the truth. Now I am embraced by Rukmiṇī on my flower bed but feel pain in all my limbs. I am fainting. She also is suffering.” In this example the quality of *mahābhāva* known as *yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti (*affecting all the devotees*)* is shown. Any living entity can be come the shelter of *bhakti.* For instance, in *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī* and the *sandarbha,* the explanation of *praṇava* is explained as follows:

*a-kāreṇocyate viṣṇuḥ śrīr u-kāreṇa kathyate \|*  
*ma-kāras tu tayor dāsaḥ pañcaviṁśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\|*

**The letter a is Visṇu, u is Lakṣmī, and m is their servant (*****jīva),*** **glorified as the twenty-fifth element.** ***Padma Purāṇa*** **6.226.22**

“Since the Lords place, pastimes and associates are all eternal, why does the *mohana* of *mahābhāva* arising from separation with Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā not arise even now in a different form? Why do we humans now not experience that suffering which is a form of spiritual bliss?” Yes, all pastimes are eternal. When the pastimes appear in the material world the disturbance of the world caused by *mohana* appears in the material world. When the pastimes disappear, it also disappears. That disturbance will be present in the universe experiencing separation because of Kṛṣṇa going to Mathurā and not in others. Thus all doubts are resolved.

### Text 187

***yathā vā—***  
***aurva-stomāt kaṭur api kathaṁ durbalenorasā me***  
***tāpaḥ prauḍho hari-virahajaḥ sahyate tan na jāne \|***  
***niṣkrāntā ced bhavati hṛdayād yasya dhūma-cchaṭāpi***  
***brahmāṇḍānāṁ sakhi kulam api jvālayā jājvalīti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: I don't know how this weak chest is able to bear this great fire of suffering harsher than a host of fires in the ocean. If the smoke from this fire were to emerge from my heart, it would set the entire universe ablaze.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous verse, the vapor or smoke of the breath was mentioned. This indicates that *mohana* is a fire. What is that fire of *mohana* which just by a particle of its smoke burns up the whole universe including the sun, moon and fire? This verse answers. Rādhā is separation speaks to Viśākhā. This pain is sharper than the fire under the ocean. It would completely burn up (*jājvalīti*) the universe if the smoke came out of my body. This indicates that it does not always emerge. When *mohana* becomes intense, then that smoke emerges from her nostrils. Then it disturbs the universe, as described in the previous verse. *Mohana-bhava* however remains in Rādhā’s heart during Kṛṣṇa’s stay in Mathurā. Or taking the principle meaning of *jājvalīti,* turning everything to ashes, the dense smoke should never come out. *Yogamāyā* keeps it within Rādhā’s body in order to protect the universe and Vaikuṇṭha. But it comes out when she breathes, according to the previous verse. So, the smoke of one portion of *prema* which is included in *mohana* comes out of her nostrils when the *mohana* is extreme.

### Text 188

***tiraścām api rodanam, yathā padyāvalyām (373)—***  
***yāte dvāravatī-puraṁ muraripau tad-vastra-saṁvyānayā***  
***kālindī-taṭa-kuñja-vañjula-latām ālāmbya sotkaṇṭhayā \|***  
***udgītaṁ guru-bāṣpa-gadgada-galat-tārasvaraṁ rādhayā***  
***yenāntarjalacāribhir jalacarair apy utkam utkūjitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Animals weeping, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **When Kṛṣṇa left for Dvārakā, , Rādhā, in great longing, wrapped herself in his yellow cloth and, taking support of a charming creeper in a grove on the bank of the Yamunā, shed tears. She sang in a high, choked-up voice. When the fish and water birds in the heard her song, they began to wail plaintively.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Her type of singing indicates her *mohana*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Going from Vṛndāvana to Dvārakā, Nāndīmukhī, while crying, informs Paurṇamāsī of Rādhā’s actions. *Yāte dvāravatī-puraṁ muraripau* means “when she heard that Kṛṣṇa had gone to Dvārakā.” She wrapped herself in his yellow upper cloth *(saṁvyānayā*) in order to smell the fragrance of his body. She loudly sang a song which resembled the sound of sobbing (*udgītam*). By that song there was plaintive wailing by the fish, *makaras* and crocodiles what to speak of the swans and ducks.

### Text 189

***mṛtyu-svīkārāt svabhūtair api tat-saṅga-tṛṣṇā, yathā tatraiva (336)—***  
***pañcatvaṁ tanur etu bhūta-nivahāḥ svāṁśe viśantu sphuṭaṁ***  
***dhātāraṁ praṇipatya hanta śirasā tatrāpi yāce varam \|***  
***tad-vāpīṣu payas tadīya-mukure jyotis tadīyāṅgana-***  
***vyomni vyoma tadīya-vartmani dharā tat-tāla-vṛnte’nilaḥ \|\|189\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Longing of the elements of the elements of the body to unite with Kṛṣṇa when accepting death: May the elements of this dead body enter their original elements! Offering respects to the creator with my head, I pray for a benediction. May the water of my body fill his water hole, may the fire of my body become the light in his mirror, may the ether of my body be the ether in his yard, may the earth of my body become the path under his feet, and may the air of my body become the air for fanning him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Svāṁśe* means “in its origin.” The order of the elements is not proper because of *moha.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. *Amara-koṣa* says *cañcatā* means death. If Kṛṣṇa does not come, certainly I cannot attain him and he cannot attain me. What is the use of your maintaining my body with such difficulty? Do not take care to protect my dead body out of affection. The components of the body (*bhūta-nivahāḥ*) should enter their elements such as earth. For that purpose, I have a desire. What is impossible for the creator? Entering the elements, the bodily parts should become things used by Kṛṣṇa. May water in the body fill the water hole he uses for bathing and playing! The elements are listed out of order because of her bewildered mind. May the fire of my body be the light in his mirror! May he see his face in my light! May the *ākāśa* of my body become the *ākāśa* in his yard! In the form of *ākāśa* I can embrace all his limbs plentifully when he sits, walks, breathes and yawns. May the earth of my body become the path where he walks! He will place his feet upon me. May the air of my body become air used for fanning him! My air will become fragrant by the fragrance of his perspiration. When I leave, why should you weep?

### Text 190-191

***atha divyonmādaḥ—***  
***etasya mohanākhyasya gatiṁ kāmapy upeyuṣaḥ \|***  
***bhramābhā kāpi vaicitrī divyonmāda itīryate \|\|190\|\|***  
***udghūrṇā-citra-jalpādyās tad-bhedā bahavo matāḥ \|\|191\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Divyonmāda:*** **When** ***mohana*** **attains an indescribable state similar to complete bewilderment with remarkable symptoms, it is called** ***divyonmāda.*** **It has many forms such as** ***udghūrṇā*** **and** ***citra-jalpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When *mohana* attains (*upeyuṣaḥ)* an indescribable (*kām api)* mode *(vṛtti)* similar to complete bewilderment with astonishing (*kāpi)* symptoms it is called *divyonmāda.*

### Text 192

***tatra udghūrṇā—***  
***syād vilakṣaṇam udghūrṇā nānā-vaivaśya-ceṣṭitam \|\|192\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Udghurṇā*** **refers to various actions with no control taking on a remarkable nature.**

### Text 193

***yathā—***  
***śayyāṁ kuñja-gṛhe kvacid vitanute sā vāsa-sajjāyitā***  
***nīlābhraṁ dhṛta-khaṇḍitā vyavahṛtiś caṇḍī kvacit tarjati \|***  
***āghūrṇatyabhisāra-sambhramavatī dhvānte kvacid dāruṇe***  
***rādhā te virahodbhrama-pramathitā dhatte na kāṁ vā daśām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Agitated with excitement by your absence, what astonishing condition has Rādhā not attained? Sometimes, she dresses up and carefully arranges a bed in cottage bower. Feeling abandoned, she sometimes angrily criticizes the dark cloud. Yearning to meet you, she staggers out in the frightening darkness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The verse borrows from a *Bhāgavatam* description:

*kācin madhukaraṁ dṛṣṭvā dhyāyantī kṛṣṇa-saṅgamam*  
*priya-prasthāpitaṁ dūtaṁ kalpayitvedam abravīt*

**One of the** ***gopīs,*** **while meditating on her previous association with Kṛṣṇa, saw a honeybee before her and imagined it to be a messenger sent by her beloved. Thus she spoke as follows. SB 10.47.9**

*Kācit* in the *Bhāgavatam* verse means Rādhā, since her supreme position was established in the *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.* One can also see *Vāsanā-bhāṣya.* Because this *bhāva* is the supreme one, one should consider that all other verses previously discussed dependent on this *bhāva.* According to this *bhāva, citra-jalpā* will show its remarkable features. This is not similar to the speech of the queens of Dvārakā illustrated in verses like SB 10.90.24.

*haṁsa svāgatam āsyatāṁ piba payo brūhy aṅga śaureḥ kathāṁ*  
*dūtaṁ tvāṁ nu vidāma kaccid ajitaḥ svasty āsta uktaṁ purā*  
*kiṁ vā naś cala-sauhṛdaḥ smarati taṁ kasmād bhajāmo vayaṁ*  
*kṣaudrālāpaya kāma-daṁ śriyam ṛte saivaika-niṣṭhā striyām*

**Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendant of Śūra, dear one. We know you are his messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words he spoke to us long ago? Why should we go and worship him? O servant of a petty master, go tell him who fulfills our desires to come here without the goddess of fortune. Is she the only woman exclusively devoted to him?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa about the condition of Rādhā when he asked.

### Text 194

***mathurā-nagaraṁ kṛṣṇe labdhe lalita-mādhave \|***  
***udghūrṇeyaṁ tṛtīyāṅke rādhāyāḥ sphuṭam īritā \|\|194\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***Lalita-mādhava,*** **Act Three, when Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathurā the** ***udghūrṇā*** **of Rādhā is clearly depicted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This description is also dependent on the *Bhāgavatam* description.

### Text 195

***atha citra-jalpaḥ—***  
***preṣṭhasya suhṛdāloke gūḍha-roṣābhijṛmbhitaḥ \|***  
***bhūri-bhāva-mayo jalpo yas tīvrotkaṇṭhitāntimaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Citra-jalpa:*** **The excessive chatter that arises out of great, deep anger, in the presence of a friend of the lover, filled with various** ***bhāvas*** **and finally ending with intense longing, is called** ***citra-jalpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

From the context, this takes place at the time of great separation. *Antima* means “at the very end.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This *bhāva* finally ends in *bhāva* with intense longing.

### Text 196-198

***citra-jalpo daśāṅgo’yaṁ prajalpaḥ parijalpitam \|***  
***vijalpojjalpa-saṁjalpā avajalpo’bhijalpitam \|***  
***ājalpaḥ pratijalpaś ca sujalpaś ceti kīrtitāḥ \|\|196\|\|***  
***eṣa bhramara-gītākhyo daśame prakaṭīkṛtaḥ \|\|197\|\|***  
***asaṅkhya-bhāva-vaicitrī camatkṛti-sudustaraḥ \|***  
***api cec citrajalpo’yaṁ manāk tad api kathyate \|\|198\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Citra-jalpa has ten limbs:** ***prajalpa, parijalpa, vijalpa, ujjalpa, saṁjalpa*****,** ***avajalpa, abhijalpa, ājalpa, partijalpa*** **and** ***sujalpa*****. These are famous in the song of the bee in the Tenth Canto of** ***Bhāgavatam*****. Though the** ***bhāvas*** **are countless, marevelous, astonishing and difficult to penetrate, they will be slightly described.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Api cet* means “even though.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā spoke this *citra-jalpa.* Śukadeva described it. Following him, I will describe that *citra-jalpa* which he explained was the highest formof *mahābhāva.*

### Text 199

***tatra prajalpaḥ—***  
***asūyerṣyā-mada-yujā yo’vadhīraṇa-mudrayā \|***  
***priyasyākauśalodgāraḥ prajalpaḥ sa tu kīrtyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Prajalpa:*** **When a woman utters rough words filled with envy, hatred and pride, with indications of insult, it is called** ***prajalpa.***

### Text 200

***yathā (10.47.12)—***  
***madhupa kitava-bandho mā spṛśāṅghriṁ sapatnyāḥ***  
***kuca-vilulita-mālā-kuṅkuma-śmaśrubhir naḥ \|***  
***vahatu madhu-patis tan-māninīnāṁ prasādaṁ***  
***yadu-sadasi viḍambyaṁ yasya dūtas tvam īdṛk \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O honeybee, O friend of a cheater, don’t touch my feet with your whiskers, which are smeared with the** ***kuṅkuma*** **that rubbed onto Kṛṣṇa’s garland when it was crushed by the breasts of a rival lover! Let Kṛṣṇa satisfy the women of Mathurā. One who sends a messenger like you will certainly be ridiculed in the Yadus’ assembly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The ten verses starting with this verse are explained with *rasa* in *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī*. For fear of lengthening the commentary, the verses are not explained here in detail, but only to understand the meaning. The words *madhupati* (lord of honey) with *kitava-bandho* (cheating friend) indicate envy. *Sapatnyā* indicates rough words. *Mā spṛśāṅghriṁ* (do not touch me) shows hatred and insult. Pride is indicated by “Let him please the women of Mathurā.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava, dear friend of Kṛṣṇa, who has come from Mathurā with his message, approaches Rādhā, offers respects, and sits down. She sees him and does not see him. Seeing a bee wandering about out of greed for the fragrance of her lotus feet, with rising anger, she scolds the bee in *divyonmāda*, thinking “This bee, a messenger sent by my offending lover to pacify me, is offering respects at my feet.” She begins to speak.

O bee, friend of a cheater! He is a cheater because of his lies.

*evaṁ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda*  
*svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye ’balāḥ*  
*mayāparokṣaṁ bhajatā tirohitaṁ*  
*māsūyituṁ mārhatha tat priyaṁ priyāḥ*

**My dear girls, understanding that simply for my sake you had rejected the authority of worldly opinion, of the Vedas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to me. Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. Therefore, my beloved** ***gopīs*****, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward me, your beloved. SB 10.32.21**

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*  
*yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ*  
*saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā*

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. SB 10.32.22**

*tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāṇe yadūttamaḥ*  
*sāntvayām asa sa-premair āyāsya iti dautyakaiḥ*

**As he departed, that best of the Yadus saw how the** ***gopīs,*** **were lamenting, and thus he consoled them by sending a messenger with this loving promise: “I will return.” SB 10.39.36**

“As a friend, you are playing the role of a messenger. Do not touch my feet!”

The bee, making a buzzing sound, seemed to say, “What is this? Will you not let me offer obeisances to you?”

Rādhā said, “Oh one who drinks liquor (*madhu pa*)! By contact with intoxicants, my feet will become impure. If you just want to offer obeisances, do that from far off.”

According *Amara-koṣa* the word *madhu* means wine and nectar of a flower.

The bee seemed to reply, “Why are you accusing me of being drunk, when I have no fault?”

Rādhā said, “This is not just an accusation, it is true. Do not touch me with your whiskers tinged by the *kuṁkuma* of the garland from another woman’s breasts which has been crushed by contact with Kṛṣṇa’s chest or the garland worn by Kṛṣṇa which has been crushed by another woman’s breasts.” Rādhā here puts blame on the natural color of the bee’s yellows hairs, thinking them to be tinged with *kuṁkuma*.

“That you have come to praise me when I am in a state of anger without even washing your whiskers shows that you are without judgment, that you did drink some liquor. Understand that seeing you in that condition will only increase my anger, not decrease it.”

The bee continued to hum. “Whatever the case may be, you should be happy.”

Rādhā answered, “O protector of the liquor! Go to Mathurā and protect the liquor to be drunk by your master, and drink it yourself. That is a good job for you, because you are unsuitable to be a messenger, being so stupid.”

The bee seemed to be saying, “If this is how you act, what can I do? Now I am going to Mathurā. Let Kṛṣṇa himself come and make you happy.”

Rādhā said, “Now he is sitting as the king of the Yadus (*madhu-pati*). Though a cowherd, born to the queen of Vraja, by some good fortune, he has become a *kṣatriya*. Let him give happiness to those angry *kṣatriya* women. All the cowherd women mean nothing to him now. Let him continuously satisfy them.”

By the use of the plural, she indicates the following. “There are unlimited numbers of angry women in Mathurā who were devoted to him. Thus he is responsible for them (*vahatu*, as in *yoga-kṣemam vahāmy aham*). But when he satisfies one of them, another becomes angry. When he satisfies that woman, another one becomes angry. Thus he will have to continuously satisfy them one after the other. Thus he will have no opportunity to come to see us.”

The bee seemed to say, “You are an ocean of good fortune for him. You should not speak like this. If he does not keep you in his mind, why did he send me here as a messenger?”

She answers, “You, as his servant, are carrying the clues of his love affairs. And he, exhibiting those clues, will be scorned in the assembly of Yadus. When the news of his transgressions with the Yadu women becomes known, the husbands will hurl abuse on him. (Or, with such a messenger as you, all the assembly of Yadus will get scorned in all countries by other *kṣatriyas,* because their women were enjoyed by a cowherd man.) And sending a messenger like you with the clues of his illicit affairs, he must certainly be intoxicated, being the master of liquor (*madhu pati*).”

The word "cheater" indicates her indignation *(asūyā*). The word “co-wife” indicates jealousy *(īrṣyā*). “Do not touch my feet” indicates pride (*mada*). “Let him please them” indicates disrespect. “Scorned in the assembly of Yadus” indicates the urge to spit out harsh words. This constitutes *prajalpa.*

### Text 201

***atha parijalpitam—***  
***prabhor nirdayatā-śāṭhya-cāpalādy-upapādanāt \|***  
***sva-vicakṣaṇatā-vyaktir bhaṅgyā syāt parijalpitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Parijalpa:*** **When the woman reveals her cleverness with wit by revealing her lover’s cruelty, cunning, unsteadiness, and other qualities as well, it is called** ***parijalpa.***

### Text 202

***yathā (10.47.13)—***  
***sakṛd adhara-sudhāṁ svāṁ mohinīṁ pāyayitvā***  
***sumanasa iva sadyas tatyaje’smān bhavādṛk \|***  
***paricarati kathaṁ tat-pāda-padmaṁ nu padmā***  
***hy api bata hṛta-cetā hy uttamaḥ-śloka-jalpaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**After making us drink the enchanting nectar of his lips only once, Kṛṣṇa suddenly abandoned us, just as you might quickly abandon some flowers. How is it, then, that Goddess Padmā willingly serves his lotus feet? Alas! The answer must certainly be that her mind has been stolen away by his deceitful words.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first line indicates his cunning. The second line indicates his cruelty. The third line reveals the stupidity of Lakṣmī, using a metaphor about his lotus feet. Wherever he stays, she, the form of great wealth also stays. But even now she stays there. The reasons should be investigated. The fourth line illustrates her cleverness. She finds the cause by seeing a reflection of the cause using joking words. He, master of praise (*uttama-śloka*) has stolen her heart by praising her.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The bee seemed to say, “This yellow color is my natural color as a bee. It is not the *kuṁkuma* from Kṛṣṇa’s alliance with another woman. He thinks only of you, and does not see another woman in Mathurā even while dreaming. What offense has Kṛṣṇa committed that you become so angry?”

“After making us drink the nectar of his lips just once, he has given us up. That is his offense.” Though Kṛṣṇa had actually kissed the *gopīs* many times, by saying that he kissed them only once she expresses her extreme thirst for him out of *anurāga*. “And because his lips are nectar, in spite of our great suffering, we do not die. Kṛṣṇa previously considered, ‘If they all die of such torment, then who will be left whom I can torture? Thus I will make them drink the nectar of my lips so that this does not happen.’ Then after making us drink, he immediately left us. You should consider that if he really wanted to give us happiness, he would have forcibly made us drink the nectar repeatedly. Please consider that.” By saying “He made us drink “in the causative form, she indicates his use of force.

The buzzing bee said, “But if that is so, why do you chaste women still desire him?”

Rādhā said, “That nectar destroys our intelligence. By tasting that nectar our hopes in this and next life have all been destroyed. Kṛṣṇa does not consider the saying, ‘One should not cut down with one’s own hand tree that one has planted and raised oneself even if it is poisonous.’ What he likes and dislikes is astonishing. Just as Viṣṇu (Mohinī) made the *devatās (sumanasaḥ)* drink nectar churned from the ocean, Kṛṣṇa has made us drink nectar (*adhara-sudhām*), yet he abandons us just as someone like you, a bee, abandons a jasmine flower.”

The sentence has a double meaning in terms of the Viṣṇu letting the *devatās* drink nectar and the Kṛṣṇa making the *gopīs* drink the nectar of his lips. In the analogy with the *devatā, adhara* can be taken as an address to the bee “O vile fellow!” In relation to Kṛṣṇa it is taken as a compound *adhara-sudhām* (nectar of his lips). According to *Amara-koṣa* the word *sumanasaḥ* can mean respectable persons as well as jasmine.

The bee said, “But when he abandons you, are you at fault or is he?”

Rādhā answered, “He gives us up, like the bee gives up the jasmine. You should consider whose fault that is. We are also famous in Vraja as *sumana*, being like the jasmine *(sumanasa*) in fragrance, softness, purity and attractiveness, and because we have splendid minds (*su manas),* whereas he is famous in Vraja as being fickle like the bee, only interested in his own pleasure. I am not just reciting poetry. The bee, because of his fickleness, after giving up many jasmine flowers, may become attracted to inferior flowers, or may not. Why should we not become angry with Kṛṣṇa, just as we would with the bee?”

The bee argued, “It is well known from the scriptures that Kṛṣṇa is without fault. Garga, knowledgeable of scriptures, has said that he is equal to Nārāyaṇa.”

Rādhā thought, “Well, let him be Nārāyaṇa, but how can that cover up what we see in real life--- the way he cheats others?” Pondering this, she said “Lakṣmī serves him, because her mind is attracted to the glorification given to Uttama-śloka (he who is glorified) by his own men. Laksmi however is very simple whereas we have been endowed by the creator with skill, intelligence, slyness, and beauty. How can we be like her?”

“By making us drink, we lose our intelligence” shows Kṛṣṇa’s deceptive nature. “He instantly gives them up” indicates his mercilessness. “Like you the bee (*bhavadrk)”* indicates Kṛṣṇa’s fickleness. By revealing Lakṣmī as simple, Rādhā indicates her own cleverness. The word *ādi* in the definition indicate Kṛṣṇa’s ungrateful nature and lack of love for them.

### Text 203

***atha vijalpaḥ—***  
***vyaktayāsūyayā gūḍha-māna-mudrāntarālayā \|***  
***aghadviṣi kaṭākṣoktir vijalpo viduṣāṁ mataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vijalpa:*** **The wise consider** ***vijalpa*** **to be leering statements directed to Kṛṣna with evident indignation containing indications of deep pride.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The explicit indignation contains within it deep signs of pride.

### Text 204

***yathā (10.47.14)—***  
***kim iha bahu ṣaḍaṅghre gāyasi tvaṁ yadūnām***  
***adhipatim agṛhāṇām agrato naḥ purāṇam \|***  
***vijaya-sakha-sakhīnāṁ gīyatāṁ tat-prasaṅgaḥ***  
***kṣapita-kuca-rujas te kalpayantīṣṭam iṣṭāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O bee, why do you sing here so much about the Lord of the Yadus, in front of us homeless people? These topics are old news to us. Better you sing this in front of women of your friend who has conquered those women, whose burning desire in their breasts he has now relieved. Those ladies will surely give you the charity you are begging.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first half of the verse shows indignation and pride. The second half shows leering statements with mocking. *Vijaya* suggests that he is victorious in the war of love with the women of Mathurā. These topics should be sung in front of those women (*sakhīnām*) belonging to your friend who has conquered them (*vijaya-sakha*). By doing that, these women, whose desire has been relieved by his conquest, thinking themselves respected by his love, thinking themselves worshipped, will give you what you desire now. The present tense is used because of closeness to the present time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing the bee constantly buzzing due to his nature, Rādhā thought, “Agitated by my criticism, he is singing his own glories.” She then spoke. “Why are you singing this to us *gopīs?* The songs of an ignorant bee will not please the *gopīs*. Again and again you are singing. And as well, in those songs you are publicizing the glories of the leader of the Yadus. You are doing that in front of us---who were made by Kṛṣṇa to give up our homes and are now sitting at the edge of the forest. We are so poor we cannot even give you a fistful of chickpeas in charity.”

“Then just give me the old clothing and garlands discarded from your bodies.”

“You are completely ignorant of this. I will not give you anything. Reciting the Purāṇas, you are trying to prove that Kṛṣṇa is the lord of the Yadus. O six legged creature! A normal animal has four legs. You have six legs. You are one and a half animals, and thus lack intelligence to know where to sing. Being an animal, how do you know the Purāṇas? And how will you receive charity? But since you are an animal, we are not angry with you. We will give instructions on where you should sing to support your existence. Please listen. You should sing in front of the girl friends of that friend of yours who is preeminently victorious or defeated by them in the battle of love (*vijaya sakha*). You should sing all about those victories and defeat in love.”

*Vijaya sakha* can also mean the friend of Arjuna who is also known as Vijaya. Previously Kṛṣṇa was known as the friend of Subala, but after he left Vraja, he became known as the friend of Arjuna. Rādhā therefore refers to Kṛṣṇa in the future.

“These women of Mathurā, relieved of the pain in their breasts, being respected by you by your letting them hear your songs, will fulfill your desires.”

The first half of the verse shows indignation concealing within it deep-seated anger. In the second half of the verse there are leering inferences, mocking Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 205

***atha ujjalpaḥ—***  
***hareḥ kuhakatākhyānaṁ garva-garbhitayerṣyayā \|***  
***sāsūyaś ca tad-ākṣepo dhīrair ujjalpa īryate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ujjalpas:*** **The wise say** ***ujjalpa*** **is abusing Kṛṣna with indignation for his deceptioin, through jealousy and pride.**

### Text 206

***yathā (10.47.15)—***  
***divi bhuvi ca rasāyāṁ kāḥ striyas tad-durāpāḥ***  
***kapaṭa-rucira-hāsa-bhrū-vijṛmbhasya yāḥ syuḥ \|***  
***caraṇa-raja upāste yasya bhūtir vayaṁ kā***  
***api ca kṛpaṇa-pakṣe hy uttamaḥ-śloka-śabdaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In heaven, on earth or in the subterranean sphere, what women are unavailable to him? He simply arches his eyebrows and smiles with deceptive charm, and they all become his. The supreme goddess herself worships the dust of his feet, so what is our position in comparison? But at least those who are wretched can chant his name, Uttamaḥśloka.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first half of the verse shows his deception with malicious abuse. The second half shows pride with details. *Api ca* means “or.” He talks as a praiser. “Those who are wretched” refers to the *gopīs.* This also shows pride.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Hearing the bee buzzing, Rādhā thought he was saying, “Crown jewel of the dear most of Kṛṣṇa! In Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa is meditating on you day and night, pierced by the arrow of love. If you are pleased, then he will be delivered from his pain.”

Rādhā then speaks with indignation. “Who is difficult for Kṛṣṇa to attain in Saga, Marty and Patella? I know very well that Kṛṣṇa cannot pass his time without the presence of young women. If there are no women in Mathurā, then let him meditate on us, satisfy us, and send a messenger such as you to bring us there. Do not tell us that the *nutria* women will not accept a person of cowherd birth, for there is no one unavailable to him in all the three worlds. If he goes to Saga there are the divine women, if he goes to Recital there are the wives of the Nags. They all give up their husbands for him. What to speak then of the women of Mathurā? For obtaining women he does not have to depend on *pūrṇa*. Being deceptive, with his dancing eyelashes and charming smile, who can resist him? They no longer belong to their husbands. For the price of his deceptive smile they have been purchased, giving up their husbands. He is deceptive because, though attaining them, enjoying them once, he gives them up and goes after new women. What to speak of the heavenly women, even Lakṣmī, situated on the chest of Nārāyaṇa, serves Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet in order to get his association. We have heard this in the prayers of Kailua’s wives from the mouth of Paurṇamāsī. Therefore how can we remain unaffected? We are only humans, moreover simple cowherd women, moreover cowherd women of Vṛndāvana.”

These humble words reveal jealousy latent with pride through the inflection of her voice and nodding of her head. Through that jealousy, she reveals thoughts of her superiority to Lakṣmī in *prema* and beauty, and similarity of caste to Kṛṣṇa.

"He is supposed to favor the miserable. He who is merciful to the suffering and fallen is called Uttama-śloka. But as Kṛṣṇa lacks this quality, that name is a lie.”

Another abusive implication is “If he did not make miserable people like us suffer in the first place, then how could get that name?”

The first half of the verse describing Kṛṣṇa's attraction to all women shows his deceit. The third line indicates jealousy (*īrṣyā)* filled with pride *(garva*). The last line shows abuse (*ākṣepa*) mixed with indignation (*asūya).*

### Text 207

***atha saṁjalpaḥ—***  
***solluṇṭhayā gahanayā kayāpy ākṣepa-mudrayā \|***  
***tasyākṛtajñatādy-uktiḥ saṁjalpaḥ kathito budhaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Samjalpa:*** **The wise say** ***saṁjalpa*** **is utterances about Krsna’s ungratefulness and other bad qualities, through deeply sarcastic words with indications of censure.**

### Text 208

***yathā (10.47.16)—***  
***visṛja śirasi pādaṁ vedmy ahaṁ cāṭu-kārair***  
***anunaya-viduṣas te’bhyetya dautyair mukundāt \|***  
***sva-kṛta iha visṛṣṭāpatya-paty-anya-lokā***  
***vyasṛjad akṛta-cetāḥ kiṁ nu sandheyam asmin \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Keep your head off my feet! I know what you’re doing. You expertly learned diplomacy from Mukunda, and now you come as his messenger with flattering words. But he abandoned those who for his sake alone gave up their children, husbands and all other relations. He’s simply ungrateful. Why should I make up with him now?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Take your head from my feet. Why become angry at his conciliatory gestures? You have learned this from Mukunda. I know what is in the heart of you, an expert at conciliation with flattering words. You say “Reconciliation is in my heart.” But he gave up those who gave up everything for his purpose (*sva-kṛte*). The first half of the verse indicates sarcasm. The second half indicates criticism and ungratefulness. His heart has no kindness (akṛta).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While the bee was flying around it landed on Rādhā’s foot, out of greed for her fragrance, and still buzzing, seemed to say, “O lady, worshipable by millions of Lakṣmīs! Truly Kṛṣṇa has made offense to you. You should forgive him.”

Thinking that the bee was saying this and offering respects, she said, “Why are you touching your head to my foot. Please go away! I know you. You cannot cheat me like you cheat Lakṣmī and others. You have got lessons from Mukunda. You are very skilful at humble entreaties, sending messages with sweet words. You have learned it all from him. I know your character! I know you!” The object is in the genitive (*te).*

“O mistress! What is the use of fighting with him, who is dearer to you than millions of lives? Rather you should make peace with him through me.”

“For his sake, we gave up children, husbands, mothers and fathers, and he gave us up and left. The *gopīs* who were prevented from going to the *rāsa* dance gave up their children and went to meet him. We gave up husbands. The unmarried girls gave up their mothers and fathers. He, who is ungrateful (*akṛta-cetasaḥ*), gave up all these women. Should one make peace with such a cruel hearted person? Never!"

The first half of the verse shows sarcastic abuse and the second half shows the lover's ungratefulness and other qualities (*adi)* like mercilessness, violence to others and lack of love.

### Text 209

***atha avajalpaḥ—***  
***harau kāṭhinya-kāmitva-dhaurtyād āsaktya-yogyatā \|***  
***yatra serṣyaṁ bhiyevoktā so’vajalpaḥ satāṁ mataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Avajalpa:*** **Statements which show that attachment to him is unadvisable because of his hard nature, his lust and his cheating behavior, along with expressions of malice and fear is called** ***avajalpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kāṭhinya-kāmitva-dhaurtyād* is a compound in which the elements are treated as one object.

### Text 210

***yathā (10.47.17)--***  
***mṛgayur iva kapīndraṁ vivyadhe lubdha-dharmā***  
***striyam akṛta virūpāṁ strī-jitaḥ kāma-yānām \|***  
***balim api balim attvāveṣṭayad dhvāṅkṣa-vad yas***  
***tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-kathārthaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Like a hunter, he cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because he was conquered by a woman, he disfigured another woman who came to him with lusty desires. And even after consuming the gifts of Bali Mahārāja, he bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us give up all friendship with this dark-complexioned boy, even if we can’t give up talking about him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Enough with his methods of friendship, which are contaminated! Among them even one is enough. One fault is that he acted like a hunter and shot the king of the monkeys. *Kapīndram* refers to Bāli. *Striyam* refers to Śūrpaṇakhā. *Kāmayānām* means filled with lust. He was conquered by a woman. By her order he went to kill a golden deer. Then he bound up Bali. How can you be my well-wisher? You praise his deeds. Do not praise him. But it is hard to give up talking of him. You have spoken correctly. It is difficult to give up talking about him. His faults as listed always appear in the mind. But it is useless talking about his faults.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The bee seemed to say, “O Rādhā, tender-hearted Kṛṣṇa meditates on you in Mathurā. I have seen it with my eyes.”

“You are a new servant in Mathurā, so you do not know the truth. Not only in this life has he been cruel hearted, but in previous lives also. I have heard this from Paurṇamāsī. When he appeared as a *kṣatriya* in the form of Rāma, he gave up *kṣatriya dharma* and, like a hunter he killed Bāli, the king of the monkeys mercilessly, by hiding behind a tree. In the events of this story there is more impiety, for he transgressed the rules of the hunter. The hunter does not kill monkeys because their flesh is inedible and cannot even be sold to anyone. Hear about some more of his impiety. The woman Śūrpanakhā, overcome with lust, desired Rāma, but Rāma disfigured her by cutting off her nose, so that no one else would want to enjoy with her. That was simply because of his cruel nature. He did not do this cruel act to protect his vow of celibacy while wearing matted locks and dress of a renunciate, but because of being controlled by a woman—Sītā. Similarly, he appeared as Vāmana, as a *brāhmaṇa,* but rejected the qualities of the *brāhmaṇa* such as peacefulness and straightforwardness. After enjoying the offerings made by the pious king Bali, he threw him from his rulership of the three worlds (*pisthapat aksipat*), into a hole in the earth.”

Alternative reading is *avesthayat dhvanksavat* instead of *pisthapat.* In that case the meaning is: “He, like a crow, bound him up by trickery. Just as the crow after devouring offerings meant for worship, calls other crows and surrounds a woman and annoys her, Vāmana called his own people who surrounded Bāli, and tormented him. Enough with friendships with that black complexioned man! Not one of the many types of friendship of us gold complexioned women with that black complexioned man has proved auspicious. We have developed impure hearts. \\We should fear even one friendship with him.”

The bee seemed to say, “Do you who go around criticizing others constantly have pure hearts?”

Rādhā said, “Talking about his activities in so many past lives is hard to give up, though it gives us sorrow. Though we should not be discussing those activities, we cannot give up discussing them, whether it is criticism or just telling the stories as they are.”

Another meaning is as follows. “Though we have given him up, that particular form (*arthaḥ*) cannot be given up by sages and others.”

Killing Vali indicates his ruthless nature, being controlled by a woman indicates his lust, accepting offerings of Bali indicates fraud, and give up friendships with the black fellow indicates fear and malice (*irsya*), and unsuitableness of attachment.

### Text 211

***atha abhijalpitam—***  
***bhaṅgyā tyāgaucitī tasya khagānām api khedanāt \|***  
***yatra sānuśayaṁ proktā tad bhaved abhijalpitam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhijalpa:*** **Remorseful statements to give up Krsna because of his inflicting pain on innocent people treating them like birds are called** ***abhijalpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Speaking with remorse (*sānuśayam*) to give up Kṛsṇa because of giving pain to people who are made to act like birds is caleld *abhijalpa.*

### Text 212

***yathā (10.47.18)--***  
***yad-anucarita-līlā-karṇa-pīyūṣa-vipruṭ-***  
***sakṛd-adana-vidhūta-dvandva-dharmā vinaṣṭāḥ \|***  
***sapadi gṛha-kuṭumbaṁ dīnam utsṛjya dīnā***  
***bahava iha vihaṅgā bhikṣu-caryāṁ caranti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**To hear about the pastimes that Kṛṣṇa regularly performs is nectar for the ears. For those who relish just a single drop of that nectar, even once, their dedication to material duality is ruined. Many such persons have suddenly given up their wretched homes and families and, themselves becoming wretched, traveled here to Vṛndāvana to wander about like birds, begging for their living.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is in the form of an instruction. This is spoken on seeing the birds and thinking of them as beggars. Kṛṣṇa is the cause of people being beggars. That is a fault. By showing that, he is criticized. He inspires improper conduct in the mind through his pastimes. But the topics are like powdered seeds of a poisonous plant. Being purified of household enjoyment (*dvandva-dharmā*), people are destroyed. Immediately they give up their houses and perform begging for grains in Vṛndāvana *(iha*), like birds taking seeds from trees. The characterisitcs of *abhijalpa* are clear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

But what is so remarkable about our suffering after establishing a relationship with him? Discussion of his pastimes gives sorrow to the whole world. The pastimes which he performed at every moment (*anucaritam*) are nectar for the ears. The sound itself gives joy, what to speak of the joy on understanding the meaning. By tasting just one drop, just once, friendship between men and women (*dvandva-dharmā*) is immediately cut (*vidhāta*). If a wife hears, then she gives up affection for her husband. If a husband hears, he gives up affection for his wife. If a son hears, he gives up affection for mother and father. If a mother hears she gives up affection for her son. In this way each person attains complete destruction by such rejection.

It is not the same suffering as in renunciation, but worse. The proof is the experience of common people. Though the people who develop a taste for Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are soft-hearted, they also become hard-hearted, merciless and ungrateful, on hearing the pastimes of hard-hearted Kṛṣṇa. Just on hearing about him, they give up fathers and mothers, in-laws who are suffering because they do not have enough money for the next day’s food, having no other means of support. Or they give the family members suffering due to separation as if they were dead people. Wife and children may die, but they themselves cannot be happy. They are penniless for, having left home with a disturbed mind, they have forgotten to tie up in their cloth even a few coins. This is not the case of one man, or two, or three or four people. This has been the case with hundreds and thousands of people.”

If the alternate reading *dhīrāḥ* (instead of *dīnāḥ*) is taken, it means that in spite of seeing the wife cry, they are unmoved or are hard-hearted.

“How do they maintain their lives?”

“Like (*iva*) birds, they survive on grains by begging, not by some big donation.”

Sometimes alternate reading "iha" is seen instead of "iva." In that case it means: “They come and beg here, in Vṛndāvana, the place of suffering and suffer even more in our association.”

Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are is like a poisonous mixture of sugar candy and powered seeds of the *dhatura* plant. The speaker of his pastimes is a murderer in the dress of a saint. The Purāṇas are a net. The speaker may be seen wandering from forest to forest with the Purāṇas under his arm. Vyāsa and others are the makers of the net which teaches that Kṛṣṇa is supreme. This is accepted by Kṛṣṇa, who then thinks, “I will make all people like the *gopīs* fall in the ocean of suffering.” Seeing others suffering is his happiness. So he must bear the consequence of giving others such misery, not Vyāsa or anyone else.

In this verse, through indirect praise through condemnation, the excellence of *bhakti* is established. This is the conclusion of the verse.

### Text 213

***atha ājalpaḥ—***  
***jaihmyaṁ tasyārtidatvaṁ ca nirvedād yatra kīrtitam \|***  
***bhaṅyānya-sukhadatvaṁ ca sa ājalpa udīritaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Ājaḷpa:*** **Where there is discussion of his crooked nature and how that gives sorrow, whereas other persons give happiness, with disgust, it is called** ***ājalpa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Other things give happiness whereas he gives grief.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He gives sorrow and other things give happiness.

### Text 214

***yathā (10.47.19)--***  
***vayam ṛtam iva jihma-vyāhṛtaṁ śraddadhānāḥ***  
***kulika-rutam ivājñāḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo hariṇyaḥ***  
***dadṛśur asakṛd etat tan-nakha-sparśa-tīvra-***  
***smara-ruja upamantrin bhaṇyatām anya-vārtā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Faithfully taking his deceitful words as true, we became just like the black deer’s foolish wives, who trust the cruel hunter’s song. Thus we repeatedly felt the sharp pain of lust caused by the touch of his nails. O messenger, please talk about something besides Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

We saw his deceit. They describe themselves. We do not remember the touch of his other limbs but by the forceful touch of his nails we developed pain of desire, just as the arrow gives pain on touching the deer. O messenger, jester! He is like the counselor to the king. Speak some other topic. This will bring happiness. The qualities of *ājalpa* are clear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The bee said, “Why did such intelligent ladies as you establish friendship with such a person as Kṛṣṇa?”

Rādhā said, “He said that he could not repay us when we offered ourselves to him. (SB 10.32.22) We fools had faith in this cheater’s statements, thinking them true, just as the wives of the black deer have faith in the song of the hunter. Just as the deer saw his song (saw the result-- the striking of the arrow), so we also experienced the sharp pangs of love with the touch of his nails. Not once, but many times, the deer, having faith, and again seeing the result, has been shot. This shows its extreme stupidity. And we also, repeatedly suffering in the mind from relationship with him, are also extremely stupid. Therefore, O jester, speak of other things, which will make us happy, for news of Kṛṣṇa simply brings us suffering." The qualities of *ājalpa* are clear.

### Text 215

***atha pratijalpaḥ—***  
***dustyaja-dvandva-bhāve’smin prāptir nārhety anuddhatam \|***  
***dūta-sammānanenoktaṁ yatra sa pratijalpakaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Pratijalpa*****: Humble statements expressing respect for the messenger, but with refusal to meet Kṛṣṇa, who has permanent relationships with other women is called** ***pratijalpa.***

### Text 216

***yathā (10.47.20)--***  
***priya-sakha punar āgāḥ preyasā preṣitaḥ kiṁ***  
***varaya kim anurundhe mānanīyo’si me’ṅga \|***  
***nayasi katham ihāsmān dustyaja-dvandva-pārśvaṁ***  
***satatam urasi saumya śrīr vadhūḥ sākam āste \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O friend of my dear one, has my beloved sent you here again? I should honor you, friend, so please choose whatever boon you wish. But why have you come back here to take us to him, whose conjugal love is so difficult to give up? After all, gentle bee, his consort is the goddess Śrī, and she is always with him, staying upon his chest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a refusal with breaking of pride. In separation, Rādhā speaks with wit to the bee which has returned after disappearing. You have returned. Have you come because you have been sent by my beloved? What do you desire *(anurundhe*)? Are you going to ask me to go to Mathurā? Will you take us to him, who has a conjugal relationship hard to give up? Why is it hard to give up? Śrī in the form of a line is seen on his chest. At night she becomes the enjoyer. The qualities of *pratijalpa* are clear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though the bee was buzzing around that place, Rādhā, out of the madness of *prema,* could not find him. Not seeing him for a moment, she began to consider in grief. “Because of my sharp words, that messenger, being afflicted, has gone off to Mathurā, and must have told everything to Kṛṣṇa. Now he has become indifferent to me.”

Attaining the state of a lover in separation after a quarrel, Rādhā stared at the path and said, “Perhaps my beloved, the ocean of love, and crown of good qualities, will again send his messenger here.”

Suddenly seeing the bee, she said respectfully, “O friend of the dear most of my life! Though wounded by the arrows of my words, by your own good qualities, you have forgotten my offenses and returned here. Can I understand that my dear most has sent you here again, not considering my thousands of offenses? If that is so, then you should pray for one boon from me. What do you desire? I will fulfill your request. O bee, if you say you want me to go to Mathurā, then I will agree.”

After saying that she thought, “If I see my beloved surrounded by other women in Mathurā, I will get uncontrollably jealous.” She said, “Why are you taking me to Kṛṣṇa, who cannot give up loving another woman?”

“I swear that he is alone in Mathurā.”

“O one of pure intelligence! Lakṣmī is by his side. Not only that, she is constantly there. Not only that, she is right on his chest, acting as a dominating male.”

As Lakṣmī has the power to take many forms, when Kṛṣṇa enjoys with other women, Lakṣmī sits on his chest as a golden line. But when other women are not present, she gives up the form as a golden line and, taking the form of a young woman, enjoys with him. The qualities of *pratijalpa* are clear.

### Text 217

***atha sujalpaḥ—***  
***yatrārjavāt sa-gāmbhīryaṁ sa-dainyaṁ saha-cāpalam \|***  
***sotkaṇṭhaṁ ca hariḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sa sujalpo nigadyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sujalpa: Sujalpa*** **refers to asking about Kṛṣṇa with simplicity, gravity, humility, unsteadiness and eagerness.**

### Text 218

***yathā (10.47.21)--***  
***api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro’dhunāste***  
***smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṁś ca gopān \|***  
***kvacid api sa kathāṁ naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṁ gṛṇīte***  
***bhujam aguru-sugandhaṁ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kṛṣṇa resides in Mathurā. Does the respectable son remember his father’s household affairs and his friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does he ever talk about us, his maidservants? When will he place on our heads his aguru-scented hand?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ārya-putraḥ* indicates that they regarded him as their husband. The external false situation was not understood by others. This was revealed by Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava.

*tā man-manaskā tṛṣṭ-prāṇā mad-arthe tyakta-daihikāḥ*  
*mām eva dayitaṁ preṣṭham ātmānaṁ manasā gatāḥ*  
*ye tyakta-loka-dharmāś ca mad-arthe tān bibharmy aham*

**The minds of those** ***gopīs*** **are always absorbed in me, and their very lives are ever devoted to me. For my sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies, renouncing ordinary happiness in this life, as well as religious duties necessary for such happiness in the next life. I alone am their dearmost beloved and, indeed, their very self. Therefore I take it upon myself to sustain them in all circumstances. SB 10.46.4**

*Adhāsyat* means *dhāsyati* (place).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Oh, in my madness I have been talking, but did not ask the questions I should have.” With repentance she spoke with respect. “Is the noble son in Mathurā now? Just as he left Vraja, will he also leave Mathurā?” By this she hints that he may develop the desire to come here, because it is not so far from Mathurā. She did not ask if he was happy there, but simply asked if he was there. This revealed her thoughts.

He is the son of Nanda, who is so innocent, being cheated by the cruel Yadus, for whom Kṛṣṇa is their life (*ārya-putraḥ*).

He is thinking, “Even my father cannot bring me to Vraja. By what means can I go to Vraja?” Not tolerating his own delay, he has sent you here as a messenger. Therefore there is no fault if he is still in Mathurā, because he is the son of Nanda. Nanda is noble, simple minded, and without keen foresight of the consequences, and his son is similar. Who could know that such a father could leave such a son and return to Vraja empty-handed? If she had known, the queen of Vraja Yaśodā would have climbed up on Akrūra’s chariot, sat there, hugging her child, and gone off to Mathurā. The *gopīs* would have followed after him. The father's good nature has been the cause of our destruction.

"When the cheater Vasudeva snatched away the son of simple-hearted Nanda, Nanda returned to Vraja and remained in a stunned state. Does Kṛṣṇa sometimes remember those rooms, the storeroom, the kitchen, and the bedroom, which now are empty, unclean, and filled with grass, dust, leaves and spider webs? Does he remember his friends like Subala who now remains stunned in other houses?

"Sometimes, when other women cannot please him by their service and they cannot understand how to make him happy, and they ask what will make him happy, does he speak about us servants to them? Does he say, 'You cannot please me as do my *gopīs* in Vraja, in stringing flower garlands, smearing ointments, putting on ornaments, preparing betel nut, playing the *vīṇā,* creating wonderful melodies and beats, in singing and dancing, in beauty and youthfulness, in exchanging questions and answers, in union, and in all the stages of *prema, sneha, māna* and *praṇaya.* Oh Yadu women, you should go to your husbands. I do not need you at all. I will go to Vraja tomorrow morning.' Having said this, when will he come here, when will he place his arms, fragrant with aguru on our heads? He will console us saying, 'O *gopīs* dear to my life, I make this vow before you. I will never give you up and go elsewhere. I have not found even a particle of anyone like you in the three worlds.' “

The first line of the verse shows simplicity. The second line shows gravity in not mentioning oneself, the third line shows humility and fourth line show unsteadiness and longing. Eager to hear the sweetness of utterances in *citra-jalpa,* Kṛṣṇa went there as a bee. This is the version for persons in *aiśvarya* mood. Some persons from other states say that the ten verses are not *unmāda,* but on the pretext of the bee, are spoken to Uddhava, dark in color, with yellow cloth.

### Text 219

***atha mādanaḥ—***  
***sarva-bhāvodgamollāsī mādano’yaṁ parāt paraḥ \|***  
***rājate hlādinī-sāro rādhāyām eva yaḥ sadā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mādana,*** **the essence of** ***hlādinī-śakti,*** **superior to** ***mohana*****, making all** ***bhāvas*** **shine, is continually present in Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

When the essence of *hlādini* shines with the manifestation all the *bhāvas* it is called *mādana.* This is the supreme condition, which always manifests in Rādhā. Sometimes it manifests internally and sometimes externally.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mādana* shines by the manifestation of all *bhāvas* from *rati* to *mahābhāva*, since *mādana* is without separation from Kṛṣṇa. Or *mādana* makes the manifestation of all *bhāvas* shine. Does *mādana* become *mohana*, another type of *mahābhāva*? This is superior to mohana (*parātparaḥ*). Understood by the *anubhāvas* to be discussed, it is endowed with the general qualities of *mahābhāva* and special qualities also. It is impossible to describe in detail. It will be said *na nirvaktuṁ bhavec chakyā tenāsau munināpy alam;* even the sages cannot describe this (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.226)

### Text 220

***yathā—***  
***āsṛṣṭer akṣayiṣṇuṁ hṛdaya-vidhu-maṇi-drāvaṇaṁ vakrimāṇaṁ***  
***pūrṇatve’py udvahantaṁ nija-ruci-ghaṭayā sādhvasaṁ dhvaṁsayantam \|***  
***tanvānaṁ śaṁ pradoṣe dhṛta-nava-navatā-sampadaṁ mādanatvād-***  
***advaitaṁ naumi rādhā-danuja-vijayinor adbhutaṁ bhāva-candram \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**I praise the astonishing moon of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's** ***mādana,*** **which is indestructible in all time, melts the moonstone of the heart, is crooked though full, destroys frightening darkness by its abundant light, spreads happiness amidst suffering or twilight, holds a wealth of ever-freshness, is incomparable because of its supreme qualities as** ***mādana,*** **and is most astonishing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Its creation spreads over past, present and future and is indestructible. With this astonishing quality it unites everything. This indicates *prema.* It melts the moonstone of the heart. This indicates *sneha.* It is crooked. This indicates *māna*. It eradicates fear by its luster. This indicates *praṇaya.* It spreads happiness even if there is serious offense (*pradoṣe*), or unhappiness due to time and place. This indicates *rāga*. It has a wealth of increasing newness. This indicates *anurāga*. All of this appears from *mādana,* since it is the complete condition of *bhāva.* In terms of the moon, *āsṛṣṭe* refers to the full moon. *Prodoṣa* refers to the evening. Other terms are clear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī.  *Āsṛṣṭeḥ* means *mādana* spreads over all material and spiritual creation. *Mādana* spreads over all time. It is indestructible. This refers to the appearance of *prema.* Melting the heart refers to *sneha* and crookedness refers to *māna.* Destroying fear indicates *praṇaya* and spreading happiness even in suffering indicates *rāga.* Newness indicates *anurāga.* Giving joy to the universe indicates *bhāva.* Because of all these manifestations, *mādana* is incomparable (*advaitam*). It is incomparable (*advaitam)* because of this definition of *mādana*, having a continuous experience of happiness in the form of kissing and embracing in *mādana*. It does not have reduplication elsewhere (*advaitam*) since it only exists with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

*Rādhā-danuja-vijayinor* indicates the *āśraya* and *viṣaya* of *mādana*. Even though both of them are *āśraya* and *viṣaya* in the various *bhāvas,* in *mādana* it is not so. In *mādana* Rādhā alone is the *āśraya.* This is also indicated by the word *advaitam* as explained above. I praise (*naumi)* the moon of this *bhāva. Mādana* is *bhāva* because it makes the night lotuses of our desires bloom. It is astonishing because it is full *(pūrṇatve*) but crooked, spreads over all time (*āsṛṣṭeḥ*), and is ever new. These qualities distinguish it from the moon. Qualities common with the moon’s qualities are it melts moonstone, give happiness in the evening, and destroys darkness.

### Text 221

***atrerṣyāyā ayogye’pi prabalerṣyā-vidhāyitā \|***  
***sadā-bhoge’pi tad-gandha-mātrādhāra-stavādayaḥ \|\|221\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***mādana,*** **hatred arise great strength, directed to inappropriate objects. Because of a state of continual enjoyment in** ***mādana*****, one praises even someone having the slightest contact with Kṛṣṇa. One exhibits thousands of other** ***anubhāvas*** **as well*****.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Jealousy is unsuitable because it is directed to objects without consciousness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The word *ādi* indicates thousands of *anubhāvas* appearing simultaneously from the happiness of seeing, kissing, embracing and union with Kṛṣṇa, just as materialists sometimes enjoy a conglomerate in one form of all happiness and distress experienced over millions of *kalpas.* However the experience in the materialist takes place with expansions of the body, whereas in *mādana* it takes place in one body. Because of the nature of *mādana,* at the time of seeing one limb of Kṛṣṇa, there arise thousands of enjoyments such as embracing and kissing Kṛṣṇa. Because this does not arise in separation it is inconceivable. That is indicated by the word *api.*

### Text 222

***atha ayogye’pīrṣyā, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (92)—***  
***viśuddhābhiḥ sārdhaṁ vraja-hariṇa-netrābhir aniśaṁ***  
***tvam addhā vidveṣaṁ kim iti vanamāle racayasi \|***  
***tṛṇīkurvaty asmān vapur agharipor āśikham idaṁ***  
***pariṣvajyāpāda mahati hṛdaye yā viharasi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Expressing hatred to inanimate objects, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: O garland of forest flower, why do you constantly hate these pure-hearted doe-eyed** ***gopīs*****? As you embrace Kṛṣṇa's body from his head to his feet, you sport on his broad chest, while considering us lower than blades of grass.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks in derogatory terms with jealousy to the garland of Kṛṣṇa, who is asking for tax at Govardhana. Why do you hate us? We never hate you. “What symptoms of hatred to you see in me?” You disregard us when you embrace Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 223

***sadā-bhoge’pi tad-gandha-mātrādhāra-stutir, yathā śrī-daśame (10.21.17)—***  
***pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāyapadābjarāga-***  
***śrīkuṅkumena dayitāstanamaṇḍitena \|***  
***taddarśanasmararujas tṛṇarūṣitena***  
***limpantya ānanakuceṣu juhus tadādhim \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Praise for someone who has slight contact with Kṛṣṇa, from the Tenth Canto: The aborigine women of the Vṛndāvana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass marked with reddish kuṁkuma powder. Endowed with the color of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts of his beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they feel fully satisfied and give up all their anxiety.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks, following after some Pulinda women she happened to see.

The Pulinda women, Śabara women, have reached perfection, but we have not. We desire to inquire about their austerities. This indicates her *anurāga.* Why are they perfect? They smear on their faces and breasts with the *kuṁkuma* which has dyed the feet of Kṛṣṇa. Where did this *kuṁkuma* come from? It came from the breast of his beloved, from enjoyment with his lover. Though I desire to praise her good fortune, not being able to be so bold, I instead praise the Pulinda women. Though that is indeed the *kuṁkuma* of Rādhā, out of *anurāga,* she was not aware of this.

What did they do? They saw the *kuṁkuma* which was smeared on the grass, after Kṛṣṇa had enjoyed with Rādhā and was playing in the forest. They developed lust just from that. I do not know what would happen if they saw Kṛṣṇa. Then, with a desire to receive the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa’s body, they smeared it on their faces and their breasts. Then the pain of lust disappeared, and they experienced the happiness of a direct embrace by Kṛṣṇa. That *kuṁkuma* has a special power in it. It is because of their *prema.* Smearing it on their faces to obtain beauty and fragrance indicates their rustic nature.

### Text 224

***yathā vā—***  
***duṣkaraṁ katarad āli mālatī***  
***komaleyam akarot tapaḥ purā \|***  
***hanta goṣṭha-pati-nandanopamaṁ***  
***yā tamālam amalopagūhate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! What severe austerities must this delicate, pure-hearted jasmine have performed in her previous births so that she is now able to embrace this** ***tamāla*** **tree that so resembles Kṛṣṇa, the prince of Vraja?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Since the last example of Pulinda women was not so appropriate, another example is given. This is an example of thinking the slightest contact with Kṛṣṇa is praiseworthy. In this case it is similarity alone of the *tamāla* tree and the jasmine that is the contact with Kṛṣṇa which arouses praise.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Slightest contact extends even to slight similarity of enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa. That is shown in this verse. Rādhā speaks to Lalitā.

### Text 225

***yoga eva bhaved eṣa vicitraḥ ko’pi mādanaḥ \|***  
***yad-vilāsā virājante nitya-līlāḥ sahasradhā \|\|225\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**During union,** ***mādana*** **takes on unprecedented astonishing qualities, whose effects manifest as thousands of continuous pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The eternal pastimes are famous as objects of meditation in the ten syllable mantra. Though *mādana* is defined in terms of Rādhā, in her absence it takes on many forms, because it spreads to others. It was already said *āsanna-janatā-hṛd-viloḍanam*: *mahābhāva* disturbs the hearts of anyone approaching. (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.223)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This takes place in union, not separation. “In the last two examples *of mādana* union was not evident.” This verse answers. The *anubhāvas* or effects of *mādana* manifest (*virājante)* in a special way-- as thousands of types of pastimes and continuous *bhāvas,* such as embracing and kissing. The special quality of appearing as *sphūrti* is shown by the word *virājante.* When Rādhā praises the Pulinda women or the austerities of the jasmine, at that time, thousands of types of pastimes, such as Kṛṣṇa’s embraces and kissing, manifest.

The meaning is this. From the conclusions of *Bhāgavatāmṛta,* union and separation take place simultaneously in different *prakāśas*, or different dimensions of awareness. In the *prakāśa* of union one identifies with uniting with Kṛṣṇa. In the *prakāśa* of separation, one identifies with being separate from Kṛṣṇa. This is the consciousness of Rādhā. But when the *sthāyi-bhāva* called *mādana* manifests, at the very moment of experiencing union by kissing and embracing, there is an experience of separation. In one *prakāśa* there is an experience of two *prakāśas*. That is the unique feature of *mādana.*

“But how is it possible that at the time of union one would have intense thirst for Kṛṣṇa?” This is astonishing (*vicitra*). At the time of union, there are thousands of types of longing. This means that there is a *sphūrti* of separation. By the *anuṛaga* described, one should not think there would a confusing mixture. First one experiences separation. Then by repeatedly remembrance of the beloved, Kṛṣṇa appears as *sphūrti.* On attaining that *sphūrti,* and on embracing him, one does not make statements about longing. The experiences are spaced apart.

### Text 226

***mādanasya gatiḥ suṣṭhu madanasyeva durgamā \|***  
***na nirvaktuṁ bhavec chakyā tenāsau munināpy alam \|\|226\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The movement of** ***mādana*****, like Kṛṣṇa, is difficult to understand. Thus even sages cannot describe it properly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The movement of *mādana,* and of its object of worship Kṛṣṇa (*mādansya iva*), is difficult to understand. The sages like Bharata or Śukadeva cannot understand it.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

I offer respects to the form of consciousness, the *mādhurya-sthāyi-bhāva,* in which there are *samartha, sādhāraṇī* and *samañjasa* types.

“Calling to a jasmine is unfavorable during union with Kṛṣṇa, and seeing jasmine is difficult at that time. Mādana also includes all other *bhāvas* including union, separation and other varieties of *bhāvas.* If all the *bhāvas* appear simultaneously *mādana* takes on a very strange quality. One must clarify the qualities of *mādana*.” This verse answers. It is incomparable, though difficult to understand, comparable only to itself.

*gaganam gaganākāram sāgaraḥ sāgaropamaḥ*  
*rāma-rāvaṇayor yuddhaṁ rāma-rāvaṇayor iva:*

**Incomparable is the sky, which is one of a kind; incomparable too is the ocean, like which there is no other; so too was the battle between Rāma and Rāvaṇa – matchless, unsurpassed, beyond compare.** ***Rāmāyaṇa***

It is difficult to understand like Kṛṣṇa, who is worshipped the *kāma-bīja* (*madanasya iva*), even for Bharata or Śukadeva.

### Text 227-229

***kiṁ ca—***  
***rāgānurāgatām ādau snehaḥ prāpyaiva satvaram \|***  
***mānatvaṁ praṇayatvaṁ ca kvacit paścāt prapadyate \|\|\|***  
***ataevātra śāstreṣu śrūyate rādhikādiṣu \|***  
***pūrva-rāga-prasaṅge’pi prakaṭaṁ rāga-lakṣaṇam \|\|228\|\|***  
***sphuranti vraja-devīṣu parā bhāva-bhidāś ca yāḥ \|***  
***tās tarkāgocaratyā na samyag iha varṇitāḥ \|\|229\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**However sometimes** ***rāga*** **turns to** ***anurāga*****, then** ***sneha, māna*** **and** ***praṇaya.*** **It is said in the scriptures that Rādhā and others, in** ***pūrva-rāga*****, attained** ***rāga*** **directly. All the different** ***bhāvas*** **that appear in the women of Vraja are not described here because they are inconceivable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Various *bhāvas* appear in the women of Vraja that are not described here. For instance, they imitated Pūtanā during the *rāsa* dance. These are inconceivable *bhāvas* for how is it possible for them to fight? In order to understand it with effort, this state of *unmada* when Kṛṣṇa disappeared was described in *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī*. They inquired from the trees, sang about Kṛṣṇa’s birth, and while singing, developed *unmāda.* They became absorbed in Pūtanā and imitated Pūtanā, out of fear for Kṛṣṇa. It is similar to a person is afraid of a tiger attack. In madness, he will imitate the tiger. In that state of *unmāda,* p*rema* for Kṛṣṇa, as if he were themselves, was the cause. Without that, fear and other *bhāvas* could not take place. There is also imitation of Yaśodā. Kuntī said:

*gopy ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvad*  
*yā te daśāśru-kalilāñjana-sambhramākṣam*  
*vaktraṁ ninīya bhaya-bhāvanayā sthitasya*  
*sā māṁ vimohayati bhīr api yad bibheti*

**My dear Kṛṣṇa, Yaśodā took up a rope to bind you when you committed an offense, and your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears, which washed the mascara from your eyes. And you were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of you. This sight is bewildering to me. SB 1.8.31**

The *gopīs* took up the mood of Kṛṣṇa being afraid of Yaśodā. But they did not imitate Yaśodā by that identity of being Dāmodara, because of non-compliance of Dāmadara. When he complied they finally imitated Yaśodā. This is the particular cause for enacting the scene. Other enactments should be understood in a similar way.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The order of the *bhāvas* is not absolutely fixed. *Rāga* attains to *anurāga*, and becoming *sneha,* attains *māna* and *praṇaya.* In relation to *pūrva-rāga*, without the appearance of *māna* and *praṇaya*, *rāga* appears. The characteristics of this *rāga* are as follows:

*tārābhisāraka caturtha-niśā-śaśāṅka*  
*kāmāmbu-rāśi-parivardhana deva tubhyam \|*  
*argho namo bhavatu me saha tena yūnā*  
*mithyāpavāda-vacasāpy abhimāna-siddhiḥ \|\|*

**O excellent arranger of meetings! O moon on the fourth night of the month of Bhadrā! O increaser of the ocean of kāma! O lord! I offer arghya to you. May my desire to be with the youth be fulfilled even accompanied by false accusations!** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.126**

Various exalted *bhāvas* are not described. For instance, in the *rāsa-līlā* imitation of Pūtanā arose from *sādhāraṇi-rati*, not from *sāmañjasya* or *samartha rati*. In comparison to those *ratis,* it is less in type and quantity, and thus the *bhāva* is usually *dhūmāyitā.* However, though that was *sādhāraṇi-rati,* of inferior type, it became exalted because it had a great quantity in the state of *prema*.

### Text 230

***sādhāraṇyāṁ ratāv eva dhūmāyitatayā matāḥ \|***  
***jvalitās tu rati-premṇor dīptāḥ snehādi-pañcasu \|***  
***rūḍhe bhāve tathoddīptāḥ sudīptā mohanādiṣu \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***sādhāraṇi-rati*** **the** ***bhāva*** **is** ***dhūmayitā*****. The** ***rati*** **and** ***prema*** **of** ***samañjasa*** **and** ***samartha*****, the** ***bhāva*** **is** ***jvalita.*** **In** ***sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga*** **and** ***anurāga*** **it is** ***dīpta*****. In** ***rūḍha-bhāva*** **it is** ***uddīpta*** **and in** ***mohana*** **and** ***mādana*** **it is** ***sūdīpta.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

These are general statements. According to the depth of the *bhāva* the symptoms manifest. Sometimes the opposite is seen because of excellence of place and other reasons.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because *samañjasa* and *samartha ratis* are superior in type and quantity, they manifest *jvalitā* symptoms. *Samartha* is more j*valita* than *samañjasa.* Compared to *rati, prema* is more *jvalitā*. In *sneha, māna, praṇya, rāga* and *anurāga*, gradually the *dīpta* nature increases. And *samaratha* manifests more *dīpta* nature than *samañjasa. Mohana* and *mādana* manifest *sūdīpta* nature.

### Text 231

***iyaṁ prāyikatā kintu śreṣṭha-madhyādi-bhāvataḥ \|***  
***deśa-kāla-janādīnāṁ kvāpy eṣāṁ syād viparyayam \|\|231\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**This happens generally, but according to best, medium and inferior natures of place, time, person and association, this may be altered.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This description cannot be universally applied. *Sneha, māna* and other levels may appear as j*valitā* instead of *dīpta* because of time, place or persons with superior, medium or inferior nature. *Ādi* means association.

### Text 232

***ādyā premāntimāṁ tatrānurāgāntāṁ samañjasā \|***  
***ratir bhāvāntimāṁ sīmāṁ samarthaiva prapadyante \|\|232\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sādhāraṇi-rati’s*** **limit is** ***prema. Samañjasa-ratī’s*** **limit is** ***anurāga. Samartha’s*** **limit is** ***mahābhāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ādya* means *sādhāraṇi-rati.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *āśrayas* of the *bhāvas* mentioned are determined. *Sādhāraṇī* ends with *prema*. Rati and *prema* are the *sthāyi-bhāvas* of Kubja and others. *Samañjasa-rati’s* limit is *anurāga.* The queens of Dvārakā have seven *sthāyi-bhāvas: rati, prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga* and *anurāga.*

### Text 233

***ratir narma-vayasyānām anurāgāntimāṁ sthitim \|***  
***teṣv eva subalādīnāṁ bhāvāntām eva gacchati \|\|233\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***rati*** **of the** ***narma-vayasyas These are priya-narma-sakhas*** **mentioned in Chapter Two.4 extends to** ***anurāga*****, but among them, Subala’s** ***rati*** **extends to** ***bhāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Rati* here means *rati* extremely pleasing to Rādhā’s *rati.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Narma-vayasyas* are devotees like Kokila.

### Text 1

***sa vipralambhaḥ sambhoga iti dvedhojjvalo mataḥ \|\|1\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are two types of** ***sṛṅgāra-rasa*****:** ***vipralambha*** **(separation) and** ***sambhoga*** **(union).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having explained *madhura-rati (sthāyi-bhāva), madhura-rasa* or *śṛṅgāra-rasa* is now described.

*vakṣyamāṇair vibhāvādyaiḥ svādyatāṁ madhurā ratiḥ \|*  
*nītā bhakti-rasaḥ prokto madhurākhyo manīṣibhiḥ \|\|*

**When** ***madhura-rati*** **becomes tasty with the presence of** ***vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika*** **and** ***sañcāri bhāvas,*** **to be subsequently described, it is called** ***madhura-bhakti-rasa*** **by the wise.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.3**

First the elements such as *vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika-bhāva* and *sañcāri-bhāvas* were described. Then *rati,* and after that, *prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga, anurāga* and *bhāva* were described.
