The combination of these elements produces *rasa.* According to the degree of *sthāyi-bhāva* from *rati* upwards, the *rasa* also varies in degrees. *Rasa* very evident by nourishment of the various elements was described in the section on *bhāva* in order to show the degrees of *bhāva.* It is definitely filled with *rasa.* Where the mixture is not clearly perceived but is included in the chapter of *rasa*, it should be understood to also be filled with *rasa* because of being nourished by the ingredients, by their respective manifestations, as mentioned in verse 1.3.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having described *madhura-rati* or *madhura-bhāva,* the author now describes *madhura-rasa* or *śṛṅgāra-rasa.*

*vakṣyamāṇair vibhāvādyaiḥ svādyatāṁ madhurā ratiḥ \|*  
*nītā bhakti-rasaḥ prokto madhurākhyo manīṣibhiḥ \|\|*

**When** ***madhura-rati*** **becomes tasty with the presence of** ***vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika*** **and** ***sañcāri bhāvas*****, to be subsequently described, it is called** ***madhura-bhakti-rasa*** **by the wise.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.3**

In the above verse *rati* stands for *prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga, anurāga* and *mahābhāva.* By these seven degrees of the *sthāyi-bhāva* there are various degrees of *madhura-rasa.* *Ujjvala-rasa* is another name for *madhura-rasa.*

### Text 2

***tatra vipralambhaḥ—***  
***yūnor ayuktayor bhāvo yuktayor vā tayor mithaḥ \|***  
***abhīṣṭāliṅganādīnām anavāptau prakṛṣyate \|***  
***sa vipralambho vijñeyaḥ sambhogonnati-kārakaḥ \|\|2\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vipralambha:*** **The** ***bhāva*** **that strongly manifests in the couple when they cannot attain their desire of embracing and other actions either before or after meeting for the first time is called** ***vipralambha (*****separation)*****.*** **It acts to nourish** ***sambhoga*** **(union)*****.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prakṛṣyate* is a transitive verb but has a causative meaning. For instance the root *jan* is used as follows. Similar is the use of the verb *jan* as in *samām samām vijayate*: it produces evenness. An alternative version has *prakarṣate* which is easier to understand. The *bhāva* between the couple either when together or separate manifests in not attaining desired embraces. It is produced by the mixture of the ingredients of the various *bhāvas* with the object of producing taste. This type of *madhura-rasa* is known as *vipralambha* or separation. . If this special element of the *bhāva* of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds is present it is called *vipralambha-rasa,* since it has already been called *bhakti-rasa* and follows the quality of favorable cultivation of Kṛṣṇa (*ānukūyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanam*). It is called *vipralambha* because of that predominance. It is also called *vipralambha-bhāva* like the words *pūrva-rāga, māna, samañjasa or sādhāraṇī* since there is no confusion of terms. It is considered in this way later as well.

Now the last part of the verse is explained. “*Sambhoga* should be called *rasa* because it is pleasurable. *Vipralambha* should not be called *rasa* because it is painful. Why is it called *rasa?* Is it accepted by Kṛṣṇa?” It produces increase in *sambhoga*. Even at the time of separation it attains the nature of rasa because of causing the increase of sambhoga. It is filled with the thought of having finally attained one’s aspiration. What to speak of being a cause after actually attaining one’s desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *sthāyi-bhāva* of the hero and heroine either before ever meeting or after having met the first time becomes evident *(prakṛṣyate*) when not attaining embraces. The verb has a causative sense. The agent of the passive verb is “by great longing.” This *sthāyi-bhāva* becomes *vipralambha* by mixing with *vibhāva* and other elements. It is called a *rasa*. It is said:

*dīrghānuraktayor yūnor asamāgama-hetutaḥ*  
*bhāvo yadā ratir nāma prakarṣaṁ adhigacchati*  
*nātigacchati cābhīṣṭaṁ vipralambhas tad ucyate*

**When** ***rati*** **becomes evident because a couple who have long attraction cannot meet and when that** ***rati*** **does not attain its goal, it is called** ***vipralambha.***

“*Sambhoga* should be called *rasa* because it is pleasurable. Why is *vipralambha* called *rasa*?” It is called *rasa* because it nourishes *sambhoga.*

### Text 3

***tathā coktam--***  
***na vinā vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute \|***  
***kāṣāyite hi vastrādau bhūyān evābhivardhate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sambhoga*** **is not strong without** ***vipralambha.*** **it increases in strength just as cloth increase in beauty by repeatedly dying with red color.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A logical proof is given. Accepting this, Kṛṣṇa himself has made the following conclusion:

*nāhaṁ tu sakhyo bhajato ’pi jantūn*  
*bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye*  
*yathādhano labdha-dhane vinaṣṭe*  
*tac-cintayānyan nibhṛto na veda*

**The reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they worship Me, O** ***gopīs,*** **is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he can think of nothing else. SB 10.32.20**

The meaning of the quoted verse is as follows. O friends! Please listen. I do not respond to any living entity who worships me, what to speak of responding to person like you with great devotion. I wait, standing a little distant. “Why do you not respond?” I do not respond in order increase that tendency (*vṛtti*) of *prema* which thinks only of me in these women who think “My life belongs to him.” The dative case is used (*vṛttaye*) to indicate a missing verb form (to increase). This means that the attainment of the desired goal after intense hardship will never be given up by that person with great thirst.

“Will not *prema* increase on its own in a most excellent object?” That is true, but that tendency will increase more by my not responding, because of the nature of that tendency. This is explained through an example. A pauper on attaining wealth which is his life support, on losing it, not seeing it at all, becomes obsessed with the possibility of regaining it, what to speak of actually gaining it, and is not aware of anything else. Similarly persons like you, think continuously of me, the supreme wealth, and I think continuously of you, who are my treasure.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Puṣṭim* here means excellence. “If something causes excellence of *sambhoga*, it should be considered part of *sambhoga.* It should be considered a separate *rasa*.” That is true. But not only *vipralambha* nourishes *sambhoga. Sambhoga* is nourished by contact with unlimited astonishing combinations of amorous contact, kissing and embraces, using the eyes and mind, by means of *sphūrti* through remembrances by the hero and heroine endowed with the *sthāyi-bhāvas* of *rati, prema sneha etc*. It is said of separation by those who experience it:

*saṅgama-viraha-vikalpe varam iha viraho na saṅgamas tasyāḥ*  
*saṅge saiva tathaikā tribhuvanam api tanmayaḥ virahe*

**Separation is better than meeting. In meeting there is only one woman, but in separation the three worlds become filled with the woman.** ***Sāhitya-darpaṇa*** **8.58, also another version in the masculine in** ***Padyāvalī*** **240**

One should not say that a person experiences pain because of the intolerable situation on breaking of the vibhāva of a sphūrti or One should not say that a person experiences pain because of the intolerable situation on breaking of the vibhāva of a sphūrti or actual appearance of the lover, because the hlādinī and saṁvit śaktis act spiritually. The suffering is actually a form of bliss. This is illustrated in the following verse. Pūrṇānande’py uṣitvā bahir idam abahiś cārtam āsīd ajāṇḍam: though the inside and outside of the universe was filled with bliss, there was also suffering. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.186)actual appearance of the lover, because the hlādinī and saṁvit śaktis act spiritually. The suffering is actually a form of bliss. This is illustrated in the following verse. Pūrṇānande’py uṣitvā bahir idam abahiś cārtam āsīd ajāṇḍam: though the inside and outside of the universe was filled with bliss, there was also suffering. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.186)

### Text 4

*pūrva-rāgas tathā mānaḥ prema-vaicittyam ity api \|*  
*pravāsaś ceti kathito vipralambhaś catur-vidhaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**There are four types of** ***vipralambha*****: prior to ever meeting (*****pūrva-rāga*****), due to anger (*****māna*****), imagined separation (*****prema-vaicittyam*****), and actual separation after meeting (*****pravāsa*****).**

### Text 5

***tatra pūrva-rāgaḥ—***  
***ratir yā saṅgamāt pūrvaṁ darśana-śravaṇādi-jā \|***  
***tayor unmīlati prājñaiḥ pūrva-rāgaḥ sa ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Pūrva-rāga: Rati*** **which arises from hearing, seeing or other means previous to ever meeting, tasty with a mixture of** ***vibhāvas*****, is called** ***pūrva-rāga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Unmīlati* means “with a special taste by mixing of elements like *vibhāva.”*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Rati* before meeting mixed with *vibhāvas* is *pūrva-rāga.* Later this mixture will be explained.

### Text 6

***tatra darśanāt—***  
***sākṣāt kṛṣṇasya citre ca syāt svapnādau ca darśanam \|\|6\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From seeing: Seeing takes place by directly seeing, or seeing in a picture or in a dream.**

### Text 7

***tatra sākṣāt, yathā padyāvalyām (159)—***  
***indīvarodara-sahodara-medura-śrīr***  
***vāso dravat-kanaka-vṛnda-nibhaṁ dadhānaḥ \|***  
***āmukta-mauktika-manohara-hāra-vakṣāḥ***  
***ko’yaṁ yuvā jagad-anaṅga-mayaṁ karoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Directly seeing, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **With the delicate beauty of a blue lotus, with a necklace of strung pearls on his chest, wearing yellow garments the color of molten gold, this youth now fills the entire universe with passion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa wandering on the road with a few *priya-narma-sakhas* through the lattice, Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā. *Sahodara* means “like.”  *Āmukta* means strung.

### Text 8

***citre, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.23)—***  
***śiśiraya dṛśau dṛṣṭvā divyaṁ kiśoram itīkṣitaḥ***  
***parijalpana-girāṁ viśrambhāt tvaṁ vilāsa-phalāṅkitaḥ \|***  
***śiva śiva kathaṁ jānīmas tvām avakra-dhiyo vayaṁ***  
***niviḍa-baḍavā-vahni-jvālā-kalāpa-vikāsinam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Pūrva-rāga*** **from a picture, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **Having faith in the words of friends, who told me to look upon a youth to soothe my eyes, I looked at your picture drawn in jest. Ah! How could we simple-minded women know you would manifest the intense flames like the fire in the ocean?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Her friends had jokingly drawn a picture of Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks concerning Kṛṣṇa. I looked at your picture drawn in jest. One cannot disbelieve the words of friends since they do not act against me. “So if you had faith in the words that I would soothe your eyes, how did this become a cause of your whole body burning?” I, like my friend, am simple minded. How could my friends know that first you would appear to be very soothing and later manifest the flames of the underwater fire?

### Text 9

***svapne, yathā—***  
***svapne dṛṣṭvā sahacari sarit-kāsarī-śyāma-nīrā***  
***tīre tasyāḥ kvaṇita-madhupā mādhavī-kuñja-śālā \|***  
***tasyāṁ kāntaḥ kapiśa-jaghano dhvānta-rāśiḥ śarīrī***  
***citraṁ candrāvalim api sa māṁ pātum icchann arautsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Pūrva-rāga,*** **seeing the lover in a dream: My friend! In a dream I saw a river that flowed with water as dark as a buffalo. On the river's shore I saw a grove of** ***mādhavī*** **creepers filled with buzzing bees. In that grove I saw a handsome dark-complexioned youth wearing a yellow garment on his hips. How astonishing! Desiring to drink me, he shouted to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Candrāvalī speaks to Padmā. *Kāsarī* means a buffalo. The buffalo gives immediate remembrance of cowherds and young boys, His hips were yellow. This means he wore a yellow cloth*. Pātum* means he desired to drink me.

### Text 10

***atha śravaṇam—***  
***vandi-dūtī-sakhī-vaktrād gītādeś ca śrutir bhavet \|\|10\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing: Hearing consists of hearing songs from the mouth of bards, messengers or friends.**

### Text 11

***tato vandi-vaktrāt, yathā—***  
***paṭhati magadha-rāja-nirjayārthāṁ***  
***sakhi virudāvalim atra vandivarye \|***  
***vada katham iva lakṣmaṇe tanute***  
***pulaka-kulena vilakṣaṇā kilāsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from minstrels: O Lakṣmaṇā! Tell me why the hair of your body stood up in this extraordinary way when this expert bard recited a** ***virudāvali*** **poem narrating Kṛṣṇa's victory over Jarāsandha?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A friend speaks to Lakṣmaṇā. Generally women are attracted to heroism. She listened to Kṛṣṇa’s victory over Jarāsandha in a *virudāvali* poem, during which his form, name and qualities were described. This became a cause of her *rati* appearing.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend speaks to Lakṣmaṇā. Generally women are attracted to heroism. She listened to Kṛṣṇa’s victory over Jarāsandha in a *virudāvali* poem, during which his form, name and qualities were described. This became a cause of her *rati* appearing.

### Text 12

***dūtī-vaktrāt, yathā—***  
***āviṣkṛte tava mukunda mayā prasaṅge***  
***tārāvalī pulakitāṅga-latā natākṣī \|***  
***śuśrūṣur apy alaghu-gadgada-ruddha-kaṇṭhī***  
***praṣṭuṁ tavākṣamata sā na kathā-viśeṣam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from a messenger: O Mukunda! When I spoke about you, Tarāvalī lowered her head. Her hairs stood on end. Desiring to hear, her throat became choked up and she could not speak in order to inquire further.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 13

***sakhī-vaktrāt, yathā—***  
***yāvad unmada-cakora-locanā***  
***man-mukhāt tava kathām upāśṛṇot \|***  
***tāvad añcati dinaṁ dinaṁ sakhī***  
***kṛṣṇa śārada-nadīva tānavam \|\|13\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from a friend: O Kṛṣṇa! As my friend Rādhā, with eyes like an intoxicated** ***cakora*** **bird, hears about you from my mouth, day after day, she becomes thinner and thinner like a river drying up in autumn.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa*. Añcati* means attain.

### Text 14

***gītāt, yathā—***  
***nayane praṇayann udaśruṇī***  
***mama sadyaḥ sadasi kṣitīśituḥ \|***  
***upavīṇayati pravīṇa-dhīḥ***  
***kam udaśruḥ sakhi vaiṇiko muniḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from songs: With tears in his eyes, Nārada sang the glories of someone as he played the** ***vīṇā*** **in the royal assembly, and immediately produced tears in my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lakṣmaṇā speaks to her friend. Nārada sang with the *vīṇā* in the assembly of the king, her father Bṛhatsena. This is *sneha-sthāyi* (melting the heart) in *pūrva*-rāga.

### Text 15

***puroktā ye’bhiyogādyā hetavo rati-janmani \|***  
***atra te pūrva-rāge’pi jñeyā dhīrair yathocitam \|\|15\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The learned recognize the causes of** ***pūrva-rāga*** **to be the causes of** ***rati*** **previously mentioned such as** ***abhiyoga.***

### Text 16

***api mādhava-rāgasya prāthamye sambhavaty api \|***  
***ādau rāge mṛgākṣīṇāṁ prokte syāc cārutādhikā \|\|16\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Though** ***pūrva-rāga*** **arises in Kṛṣṇa first, great beauty in** ***pūrva-rāga*** **arises first in the doe-eyed women.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This statement is a generalization. Because the women’s *rāga* is very deep in the form of impressions and the Lord’s *rāga* follows that of the devotee, their *rāga* should appear first.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This *rāga* appears in Kṛṣṇa first at the beginning of *vayaḥsandhi.*

*prādurbhāvaṁ vrajaty eva raty-ākhye bhāva ujjvale \|*  
*nirvikārātmake citte bhāvaḥ prathama-vikriyā \|\|*

**When the** ***sthāyi-bhāva*** **called** ***rati*** **makes its appearance because of** ***ujjvala-rasa,*** **it is called** ***bhāva,*** **the first transformation in previously unagitated heart.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **11.6**

Though the man and woman may seek each other mutually after the appearance of agitation of the heart, because the woman is covered by shyness, fear, self-control and good conduct, *pūrva-rāga* does not immediately appear in her. Because the man is not covered in this way, the moment that the first agitations take place, he seeks out women. Thus it is said that pūrva-rāga appears in Kṛṣṇa first. However the *pūrva-rāga* of the women which is to be described first is more attractive. Because the women’s *prema* is greater it is described first. The greater *prema* is shown by its power to destroy shyness and other restrictions. *Sāhitya-darpaṇa* (3.195) says *ādau rāgaḥ striyā vāchyaḥ paścāt puṁsas tad-iṅgitaiḥ*: the *rāga* of women will be described first and later that of the man by indications. However some say that *pūrva-rāga* first appears in the women since *bhakti* is *rasa* and takes shelter of the devotee, since the Lord’s *rāga* follows after that of the devotee, and since the women of Vraja are the greatest devotees.

### Text 17-18

***atra sañcāriṇo vyādhiḥ śaṅkāsūyā śramaḥ klamaḥ \|***  
***nirvedautsukya-dainyāni cintā-nidrā-prabodhanam \|\|17\|\|***  
***viṣādo jaḍatonmado moha-mṛty-ādayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|***  
***prauḍhaḥ samañjasaḥ sādhāraṇaś ceti sa tu tridhā \|\|18\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **of** ***vyādhi, śaṅkā, āsūya, śrama, klama, nirveda, autsukya, dainya, cintā, nidrā and prabodhana, viṣāda, jaḍatā, unmāda, moha*****, and** ***mṛti*** **appear in** ***pūrva-rāga.***

***Pūrva-rāga*** **has three types:** ***prauḍha, samañjasa*** **and** ***sādhāraṇa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Atra* means “in *pūrva-rāga*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Prauḍha* should actually be called *samartha.* However it is called *prauḍha* to indicate that *samañjasa* has only a little *prauḍha* aspect and *sādhāraṇa* has none.

### Text 19

***tatra prauḍhaḥ—***  
***samartha-rati-rūpas tu prauḍha ity abhidhīyate \|***  
***lālasādir iha prauḍhe maraṇāntā daśā bhavet \|***  
***tat-tat-sañcāri-bhāvānām utkaṭatvād anekadhā \|\|19\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***pūrva-rāga*** **of** ***samartha-rati*** **is called** ***prauḍha.*** **The ten** ***bhāvas*** **from** ***lālasa*** **to** ***mṛtyu*** **appear though there should be many more because of the excessive nature of these** ***sañcāri-bhāvas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The meaning should be “The *bhāvas* from *lālasa* to *maraṇa* appear though they should be many more because of the excessive nature of these *sañcāri-bhāvas*.”

### Text 20-22

***tathāpi prāktanair asya daśāvasthā samāsataḥ \|***  
***proktās tad-anurodhena tāsāṁ lakṣaṇam ucyate \|\|20\|\|***  
***lālasodvega-jāgaryās tānavaṁ jaḍimātra tu \|***  
***vaiyagryaṁ vyādhir unmādo moho mṛtyur daśā daśa \|\|21\|\|***  
***prauḍhatvāt pūrva-rāgasya prauḍhāḥ sarvā daśā api \|\|22\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The authorities have described ten states in summary. According to that, they will be described. The ten states are** ***lālasa, udvega, jāgrya, tānavam, jaḍimātra, vaiyagryam, vyādhi unmāda, moha,*** **and** ***mṛtyu.*** **Because of** ***pūrva-rāga’s*** **strength, all ten states appear in the** ***prauḍha*** **form of** ***pūrva-rāga.***

### Text 23

***tatra lālasaḥ—***  
***abhīṣṭa-lipsayā gāḍha-gṛdhnutā lālaso mataḥ \|***  
***atrautsukyaṁ capalatā ghūrṇā śvāsādayas tathā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Lālasa:*** **Great desire for attaining a desired object is called** ***lālasa*** **(greed). In this state** ***autsukya*** **(longing),** ***capalatā*** **(fickleness),** ***ghūrṇa*** **(rolling about) and** ***śvāsa*** **(sighing) and other symptoms appear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Lālasaḥ* is in the masculine, since *Amara-koṣa* says it can take either a masculine or feminine ending. *Gāḍha-gṛdhnutā* means having great desire. This is not a desire for killing enemies, but a desire to attain one’s cherished lover. A desire to attain that person starts as a sprout and then increases to great desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Lālasa* means a great longing to attain either the man or the woman. *Lālasaḥ* is in the masculine, since *Amara-koṣa* says it can take either a masculine or feminine ending.

### Text 24

***yathā—***  
***tvam avasitān niṣkrāmantī punaḥ praviśanty asau***  
***jhaṭiti ghaṭikāmadhye vārāñchataṁ vraja-sīmani \|***  
***agaṇita-guru-trāsā śvāsān vimucya vimucya kiṁ***  
***kṣipasi bahuśo nīpāraṇye kiśori dṛśor dvayam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: My dear young friend! You leave the house a hundred times, going quickly to the end of Vraja in half an hour and then returning. In fear of elders you do not respect, why do you repeatedly sigh, and throw glances repeatedly at the** ***kadamba*** **forest?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Udvasitāt* means “from the house.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā speaks to Rādhā. *Udvasitāt* means “from the house” according to *Amara-koṣa.*

### Text 25

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (3.24)—***  
***dūrād apy anuṣaṅgataḥ śrutim ite tvan-nāma-dheyākṣare***  
***sonmādaṁ madirekṣaṇā viruvatī dhatte muhur vepathum \|***  
***āḥ kiṁ vā kathanīyam anyad asite daivād varāmbhodhare***  
***dṛṣṭe taṁ parirabdhum utsuka-matiḥ pakṣa-dvayīm icchati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **When, even from far away, lovely-eyed Rādhā hears one syllable of your name, she trembles, becomes insane and shouts. When she happens to see a beautiful dark cloud, eager to embrace it, she desires two wings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Āḥ* is an indeclinable indicating agitation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse is given to show the mature state of *lālasa*.

### Text 26

***atha udvegaḥ—***  
***udvego manasaḥ kampas tatra niḥśvāsa-cāpale \|***  
***stambhaś cintāśru-vaivarṇya-svedādaya udīritāḥ \|\|26\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Udvega: Udvega*** **(agitation) means trembling of the mind with heavy breathing, fickleness, being stunned, worry, tears, change of color and perspiration.**

### Text 27

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.2)—***  
***cintā-santatir adya kṛntati sakhi svāntasya kiṁ te dhṛtiṁ***  
***kiṁvā siñcati tāmram ambaram ati-svedāmbhasāṁ ḍambaraḥ \|***  
***kampaś campaka-gauri lumpati vapuḥ-sthairyaṁ kathaṁ vā balāt***  
***tathyaṁ brūhi na maṅgalā parijane saṅgopanāṅgīkṛtiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **O friend! How has this host of anxieties broken the steadiness of your heart? Why has your red cloth become excessively wet with perspiration? How has trembling forcibly stolen away the stiffness of your body? O Rādhā as golden as a** ***campaka*** **flower! Please tell the truth. It is not auspicious to conceal things from friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Ḍambaram* means excess. *Vapuḥ sthairyam* means stiffness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Though Viśākhā knows the truth, she asks Rādhā so that she will reveal her heart. *Cintā-santatiḥ* means when a worry arises, it leads to another worry, and to another. *Santati* literally means a lineage. This is the meaning given in *Amara-koṣa*. The mass of worries cuts her self-control, the tree of *dharma.* Having lost your sense of *dharma*, you are without doubt thinking about meeting your lover. This is the suggestion of her words. *Tāmram* means red. *Ḍambaram* means excess.

### Text 28

***atha jāgaryā—***  
***nidrākṣayas tu jāgaryā stambha-śoṣa-gadādikṛt \|\|28\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Jāgaryā: Jāgarya*** **means inability to sleep and the symptoms are being stunned, drying up and sickness.**

### Text 29

***yathā—***  
***śyāmaṁ kañcana kāñcanojjvala-paṭaṁ sandarśya nidrā kṣaṇaṁ***  
***mām ājanma sakhī vimucya calitā ruṣṭeva nāvartate \|***  
***cintāṁ prohya sakhi prapañcaya matiṁ tasyās tvam āvartane***  
***nānyaḥ svāpnika-taskaropaharaṇe śakto janas tāṁ vinā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O friend! Sleep momentarily showed me a certain dark-complexioned person dressed in shining yellow garments, and then at once left as if angered and has not returned. O friend! Give up worrying and find the means to bring this girl named sleep me. No one except she has the power to bring the thief who acts during my sleep.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another version has *taṁ svāpnika-taskaraṁ valayituṁ śakto’paras tāṁ vinā.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Oh! Viśākhā is depressed, worrying “How can I bring Kṛṣṇa to the chambers of the elders? How can I take you, confined to your chambers, near him?” Rādhā speaks to her. My friend sleep momentarily showed me Kṛṣṇa and then left. Use your intelligence to bring back sleep, by medicine, mantra or other methods, so that sleep will pacify me momentarily. “Then what will happen?” No one except she can bring the thief who acts in my dreams. She is able to bring him. Without him I cannot live. Therefore you must find the means. Let me have sleep. Then I will have Kṛṣṇa’s association. This will keep me alive.

### Text 30

***atha tānavam—***  
***tānavaṁ kṛśatā gātre daurbalya-bhramaṇādi-kṛt \|\|30\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Tānavam: Tānavan*** **means thinness of the body and the symptoms are weakness and staggering.**

### Text 31

***yathā—***  
***cyute valaya-sañcaye prabala-riktatā-dūṣaṇa-***  
***vyayāya nihitormikāvalir api skhalaty añjasā \|***  
***niśamya muralī-kalaṁ sakhi sakṛd viśākhe tanus-***  
***tavāsita-caturdaśī-śaśikalā kṛśatvaṁ yayau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Viśākhā! The bracelets have fallen from your wrists, and your rings worn to avoid the fault of empty hands are quickly falling off. By once hearing the sweet sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute, you have become thin and emaciated like the waning moon in its fourteenth phase.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because of their natural *rati* for Kṛṣṇa by thinking of him as their husband in their hearts and thinking only of his benefit, their bodies become thin, not because of their husbands showing attraction and then hatred from them.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend speaks to Viśākhā. The rings take the place of the bracelets because of the bracelets’ conspicuous absence. But quickly these also fall off because of her thinness. She becomes thin like the moon. The moon says, “Do not fear your elders. Quickly go and meet him. I will lead you to him, for I will die on the dark moon day.”

### Text 32

***kaiścit tu tānava-sthāne vilāpaḥ paripaṭhyate \|\|32\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Some replace the symptom of** ***tānava*** **with** ***vilāpa*** **(lamentation).**

### Text 33

***yathā—***  
***atrāsīn navanīpa-bhūruha-taṭe kurvan vihāraṁ haris-***  
***cakre tāṇḍavam atra mitra-sahitaś caṇḍāṁśujā-rodhasi \|***  
***paśyantī latikāntare kṣaṇam ahaṁ vyagrā nilīya sthitaṁ***  
***sakhyaḥ kiṁ kathayāmi dagdha-vidhinā kṣiptāsmi dāvopari \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Dancing with his friends, Kṛṣṇa played under this** ***kadamba*** **tree on the bank of the Yamunā. Hiding behind some creepers, I watched him for a moment with agitation. O friends, what shall I say? Inauspicious fate has cast me into a blazing fire of lamentation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā laments. I am dying in the fire because I no longer see him.

### Text 34

***atha jaḍimā—***  
***iṣṭāniṣṭā-parijñānaṁ yatra praśneṣv anuttaram \|***  
***darśana-śravaṇābhāvo jaḍimā so’bhidhīyate \|***  
***atrākāṇḍe’pi huṅkāra-stambha-śvāsa-bhramādayaḥ \|\|34\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Jaḍimā:*** **When one is not aware of favorable or unfavorable conditions, cannot answer questions, and cannot see or hear, the condition is called** ***jaḍima.*** **In this state, groaning, being stunned, heavy breathing and dizziness appear unexpectedly.**

### Text 35

***yathā—***  
***akāṇḍe huṅkāraṁ racayasi śṛṇoṣi priya-sakhī-***  
***kulānāṁ nālāpaṁ dṛtir iva muhur niḥśvasiṣi ca \|***  
***tataḥ śaṅke paṅkeruha-mukhi yayau vaiṇava-kalā-***  
***madhulī te pāli śruti-caṣakayoḥ prāghūṇikatām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: You suddenly grunting without any reason, you do not hear the words of your friends, and you constantly breathe like a bellows. O lotus-faced Pālī! I think the honey-nectar of the sweet sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute has become the guest of the drinking-cups of your ears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Akāṇḍe* means unexpectedly. Grunting expresses angry words in the mind at remembering Kṛṣṇa’s boldness. *Viśva-koṣa* says *hum* expresses conjecture, questioning, anger talk and conciliation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend talks to Pālī. *Akāṇḍe* means unexpectedly. *Hum* expresses refusal when thinking of enjoyment with Kṛṣṇa in the mind. *Viśva-koṣa* says *hum* expresses conjecture, questioning, anger talk and conciliation. *Dṛtiḥ* means a bellows. *Vaiṇava-kalā* means the expertise of the flute. *Prāghūṇikatām* means “treating as a guest.”

### Text 36

***atha vaiyāgryam—***  
***vaiyāgryaṁ bhāva-gāmbhīrya-vikṣobhāsahatocyate \|***  
***tatrāviveka-nirveda-khedāsūyādayo matāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vaiyāgryam:*** **Intolerance of disturbance caused by depth of emotions is called** ***vaiyagryam*** **(perplexity). In this condition there is lack of discrimination, disgust, depression and envy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Intolerance of disturbance caused by the depth of *bhāva* is called *vaiyagryam.*

### Text 37

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.17)—***  
***pratyāhṛtya muniḥ kṣaṇaṁ viṣayato yasmin mano dhitsate***  
***bālāsau viṣayeṣu dhitsati tataḥ pratyāharantī manaḥ \|***  
***yasya sphūrti-lavāya hanta hṛdaye yogī sumutkaṇṭhate***  
***mugdheyaṁ kila tasya paśya hṛdayān niṣkrāntim ākāṅkṣati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **The yogī withdraws his consciousness from the objects of the senses and desires to fix it on Kṛṣṇa in the heart. This young girl, however, withdraws Kṛṣṇa from the heart and desires to fix her heart on the objects of the senses. The great yogī yearns to see him for a brief moment in the heart, and this charming girl wishes that he may leave her heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī speaks to Nāndīmukhī. *Praytāhāra* for the yogīs means the fifth *aṅga* in *aṣṭāṅga-yoga,* withdrawing the senses. The sage refers to a yogī with some *bhakti*. Rādhā desires to offer her mind to sense objects, but she cannot do that perfectly. She desires to have him leave but he is firmly established in her heart after she has had a *sphūrti* of Kṛṣṇa.  *Māna* is the *sthāyi-bhāva* and *pūrva-rāga* is the *rasa.*

### Text 38

***atha vyādhiḥ—***  
***abhīṣṭālābhato vyādhiḥ pāṇḍimottāpa-lakṣaṇaḥ \|***  
***atra śīta-spṛhā-moha-niḥśvāsa-patanādayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Vyādhi: Vyādhi*** **means paleness and heat in the body. Dullness, desire, fainting, heavy breathing and falling down are the symptoms.**

### Text 39

***yathā—***  
***dava-damanatayā niśamya bhadrā***  
***madana-dava-jvalitā dadhe hṛdi tvām \|***  
***dviguṇita-davathu-vyathā vidagdhā***  
***murahara bhasmamayīva pāṇḍurāsīt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Kṛṣṇa! When wise Bhadrā heard that you had extinguished a forest-fire, she placed you in her heart. She now knows the pain of two forest fires, and is as white as ashes, because of the heat.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Nārada speaks to Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā. Bhadrā was a princess. Being inspiring by Kṛṣṇa, her mind became disturbed. Nārada advised her to hear the story of Kṛṣṇa delivering the people of Vraja from the forest fire to relieve her burning pain. It would serve as a stimulus to her love. She then heard it, and held the details of the story in her heart. But her fire doubled. Nārada personally told this to Kṛṣṇa. That is the story behind his words.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A friend of Bhadrā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Vidagdhā* means knowing or really burned. It can also be taken separately, not in the compound: wise Bhadrā.

### Text 40

***atha unmādaḥ—***  
***sarvāvasthāsu sarvatra tan-manaskatayā sadā \|***  
***atasmiṁs tu tad iti bhrāntir unmāda iti kīrtyate \|***  
***atreṣṭa-dveṣa-niḥśvāsa-nimeṣa-virahādayaḥ \|\|40\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Unmāda:*** **By absorption in Kṛṣṇa, mistaking an object for something else in all places and circumstances is called** ***unmāda.*** **In this state there is desire, hatred, heaving breathing, unblinking eyes and separation.**

### Text 41

***yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.3)—***  
***vitanvānas tanvā marakata-rucīnāṁ rucivatāṁ***  
***paṭān niṣkrānto’bhūd dhṛta-śikhaṇḍo nava-yuvā \|***  
***bhruvaṁ tena kṣiptvā kim api hasatonmādita-mateḥ***  
***śaśī vṛtto vahniḥ param ahaha vahnir mama śaśī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **A new youth whose body emanated the attractiveness of a beautiful sapphire and was decorated with a peacock feather came out of the picture and laughed at me while moving his eyebrows at me. I have become insane. To me the moon is now fire and fire is the moon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Paṭāt* means from a picture.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Rādhā was shown a picture of Kṛṣṇa by Viśākhā, she became completely disturbed in mind. When asked by her friends what happened, she speaks to them. His body spread out profusely the attractiveness of a sapphire. Having been thrown a movement of the eyebrow by him (*tena)* who was laughing (*hasatā*) with indescribable sweetness (*kim api*), she became insane. For me, the moon is fire, since in separation from him, it also produces pain. *Ahaha* indicates depression and astonishment. Fire is like the moon. Because I cannot tolerate the separation, I desire to give up my life by throwing myself in the fire. (Then I will be peaceful and cool.)

### Text 42

***atha mohaḥ—***  
***moho vicittatā prokto naiścalya-patanādi-kṛt \|\|42\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Moha: Moha*** **means unconsciousness, with symptoms of falling down and no movement.**

### Text 43

***yathā—***  
***nāsāśvāsa-parāṅmukhī vighaṭite dṛṣṭī snuṣāyāḥ kathaṁ***  
***hā dhik kṛṣṇa-tilān mamārpaya kare kuryām apāmārjanam \|***  
***ity ārohati karṇayoḥ parisaraṁ kṛṣṇeti varṇa-dvaye***  
***kampenācyuta tatra sūtritavatī tvām eva hetuṁ sakhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Jaṭilā said “Why does my daughter-in-law Rādhā stop breathing. Why do her eyes roll? Misfortune! Give me some black sesame seeds so I can drive away inauspiciousness.” O infallible Kṛṣṇa! Because she trembles on hearing the two syllables “Kṛṣṇa,” she has informed me confidentially that you are the cause.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sūtritavatī* means in the manner of a brief theatrical declaration, revealing something confidential to me.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā informs Kṛṣṇa of Rādhā’s *prema,* when he says that he is not the cause of her madness in which she acts abnormally. Jaṭilā first speaks. By trembling on attaining the two syllables Kṛṣṇa in her ears, you must be the cause.

### Text 44-45

***atha mṛtyuḥ—***  
***tais taiḥ kṛtaiḥ pratīkārair yadi na syāt samāgamaḥ \|***  
***kandarpa-bāṇa-kadanāt tatra syān maraṇodyamaḥ \|\|44\|\|***  
***tatra svapriya-vastūnāṁ vayasyāsu samarpaṇam \|***  
***bhṛṅga-mandānila-jyotsnā-kadambānubhavādayaḥ \|\|45\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Mṛtyu:*** **If she cannot meet with Kṛṣṇa by any means, she becomes desirous of dying because of the pain from Cupid’s arrows. The actions at this time are giving her treasured items to her friends, and experiencing the sound of bees, the gentle breeze, moon light and** ***kadamba*** **trees.**

### Text 46

***yathā—***  
***rādhā rodhasi ropitāṁ mukulinīm āliṅgya mallī-latāṁ***  
***hāraṁ hīramayaṁ samarpya lalitā-haste praśasta-śriyam \|***  
***mūrcchām āpnuvatī praviśya madhupair gītāṁ kadambāṭavīṁ***  
***nāma vyāharatā hareḥ priya-sakhī-vṛndena sandhukṣitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Rādhā gave an embrace to the budding jasmine creeper she had planted on the Yamunā's shore, placed her very beautiful golden necklace in Lalitā's hand, and desiring to faint, entered a** ***kadamba*** **grove filled with buzzing of bees, only to be revived by a group of** ***priya-sakhīs*** **who chanting the name of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This happens in *pūrva-rāga.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Asked by Paurṇamāsī, Vṛndā describes Rādhā’s condition. She embraced a *mālatī* creeper she had planted on the bank of the Yamunā. “O my dear jasmine! I am going to the next world. You will be watered in Vṛndāvana by my *sakhīs* and will blossom. You will sport on the chest of that rare person as a garland made from your flowers. In this way you will make your lover happy.” She offered her necklace to the hand of Lalitā, not to her neck. Because her hair was undone and scattered, she understood it would take time to take off the necklace, she pulled the necklace and broke the string and put it in Lalitā’s hand, saying to herself, “O Lalitā! Place this necklace giving memories of me around your neck and embrace that rare person. May you live long!” She desired (*āpnuvatī*) to faint. She was revived by Kṛṣṇa’s name because it acts as a medicine to bring the dead to life, since it is *amṛta.*

### Text 47

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (2.47)—***  
***akāruṇyaḥ kṛṣṇo yadi mayi tavāgaḥ katham idaṁ***  
***mudhā mā rodīr me kuru param imām uttara-kṛtim \|***  
***tamālasya skandhe vinihita-bhuja-vallarir iyaṁ***  
***yathā vṛndāraṇye ciram avicalā tiṣṭhati tanuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **If Kṛṣṇa is unkind, what fault do you have? Do not weep uselessly. Please perform the funeral rites afterwards. Please arrange so my body will remain forever in Vṛndāvana undisturbed with its creeper-like arms embracing a** ***tamāla*** **tree.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Verse 45 mentioned the actions when having the desire to die. The word *ādayaḥ* indicates desires which indicate treatment of the dead body. Noticing Kṛṣṇa’s indifference, Rādhā desired to throw her body in Kāliya Lake. She speaks with tears to weeping Viśākhā. “O my friend Viśākhā! This body had a long cherished desire to embrace the neck of Kṛṣṇa. If that desire cannot be fulfilled because of ill-fated hope, let that body be successful by having it embrace something like Kṛṣṇa, a *tamāla* tree.” This is *mohana* touched with a little *mādana.*

### Text 48-49

***atha samañjasaḥ—***  
***bhavet samañjasa-rati-svarūpo’yaṁ samañjasaḥ \|\|48\|\|***  
***atrābhilāṣa-cintā-smṛti-guṇa-saṅkīrtanodvegāḥ \|***  
***savilāpā unmāda-vyādhi-jaḍatā mṛtiś ca tāḥ kramaśaḥ \|\|49\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Samañjasa pūrva-rāga:*** **That whose** ***svarūpa*** **is** ***samañjasa-rati*** **become** ***samañjasa-pūrva-rāga-rasa*****. In this** ***rasa*** **there is** ***abhilāṣa, cintā, smṛti,*** **chanting the qualities of the lover*****, udvega, vilāpa, unmāda, vyādhi, jaḍatā*** **and** ***mṛti*** **in succession.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

That whose *svarūpa* is *samañjasa-rati* before having met the lover becomes *samañjasa-pūrva-rāga-rasa* by mixture with the *vibhāvas* and other elements. This will be explained later.

### Text 50

***tatra abhilāṣaḥ—***  
***vyavasāyo’bhilāṣaḥ syāt priya-saṅgama-lipsayā \|***  
***svamaṇḍanāntika-prāpti-rāga-prakaṭanādi-kṛt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhilāṣa:*** **Strenuous effort with a desire to meet the lover is called** ***abhilāṣa.*** **Activities are decorating the body, coming near the lover, and showing one’s attraction.**

### Text 51

***yathā—***  
***yad iha sakhi subhadrā-sakhyam ākhyāya dhūrte***  
***vrajasi pitur agārād devakī-mandirāya \|***  
***racayasi bata satye maṇḍane ca prayatnaṁ***  
***sphuṭam ajani tad antar vastu gūḍhaṁ tavādya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O deceitful Satyabhāmā! On the pretext of friendship with Subhadrā you are going from your father’s house to the house of Devakī and you take great endeavor to decorate yourself. I have clearly understood there is deep secret in your heart today.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *prakharā sakhī* speaks to Satyabhāmā in an inquisitive manner.

### Text 52

***atha cintā—***  
***abhīṣṭāvāpty-upāyānāṁ dhyānaṁ cintā prakīrtitā \|***  
***śayyā-vivṛtti-niḥśvāsa-nirlakṣa-prekṣaṇādi-kṛt \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Cintā:Meditating on various methods to obtain the object of desire is called cintā, which causes tossing about on the bed, sighing, and gazing blankly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vivṛtti* imeans constantly turning.

### Text 53

***yathā—***  
***niḥśvāsas te kamala-vadane mlāpayatyoṣṭha-bimbaṁ***  
***śayyāyāṁ ca kraśima-kalitā ceṣṭate deha-yaṣṭiḥ \|***  
***dvandvaṁ cākṣṇor vikirati ciraṁ rukmiṇi śyāma ambho***  
***na śvo-bhāviny upayama-vidhau śobhate vikriyeyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O lotus-faced Rukmiṇī! Your sighs wilt your bimba-like lips, your body, thin like a stick, moves about on the bed, and your eyes constantly sprinkle mascara-blackened tears. Such agitation does not beautify tomorrow’s marriage.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A neighbor speaks to Rukmiṇī. *Śyāma ambhaḥ* means tears black with collyrium. *Upayama* means marriage.

### Text 54

***atha smṛtiḥ—***  
***anubhūta-priyādīnām arthānāṁ cintanaṁ smṛtiḥ \|***  
***atra kampāṅga-vaivaśya-bāṣpa-niḥśvasitādayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Smṛti:*** **Remembrance of things related to the lover is called** ***smṛti.***  **Actions are trembling, lack of control of the limbs, tears and heavy breathing.**

### Text 55

***yathā—***  
***plutaṁ pureṇāpāṁ nayana-kamala-dvandvam abhito***  
***dhṛtotkampaṁ sātrājiti kuca-rathāṅga-dvayam api \|***  
***ślathārambhaṁ caitad bhuja-visala-yugaṁ tat tava manas-***  
***taḍāge’smin kṛṣṇa-dvirada-patir antar viharati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Satyabhāmā! The lotus flowers of your eyes are filled water, the lotus stems of your arms have become slack and the** ***cakravāka*** **birds of your breasts are trembling. The king of black elephants sports in the lake of your mind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Things related to the lover are his objects, qualities, form, clothing and actions. A friend talks to Satyabhāmā. *Plutam* means “covered with.” *Ślathārambham* means “have become slack.” *Dvirada* is an elephant.

### Text 56

***atha guṇa-kīrtanam—***  
***saundaryādi-guṇa-ślāghā guṇa-kīrtanam ucyate \|***  
***atra vepathu-romāñca-kaṇṭha-gadgadikādayaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Glorifying his qualities: Glorifying the handsomeness and other qualities of the beloved is called** ***guṇa-kīrtanam.***  **In this activity the lover trembles, her bodily hairs stand up, and her voice becomes choked.**

### Text 57

***yathā—***  
***yāntyas tṛṣṇāpi yuvatayo yeṣu ghūrṇāṁ bhajante***  
***yāny ācamya svayam api bhavān romaharṣaṁ prayāti \|***  
***gandhaṁ teṣāṁ tava madhupate rūpa-sampan-madhūnāṁ***  
***dūre vindan mama na hi dhṛtiḥ citta-bhṛṅgas tanoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O king of Mathurā! All young girls, developing a desire for the sweet wealth of your beauty, roll about on the ground. Tasting that beauty, the hairs stand on end. Smelling that sweet fragrance from far away, the bee of my mind has lost self-control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a letter from Rukmiṇī.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rukmiṇī writes a letter. Developing a desire for that sweetness, they roll about, what to speak of actually drinking it.

### Text 58

***ṣaḍ-udvegādayaḥ pūrvaṁ prauḍhe tasminn udāhṛtāḥ \|***  
***sāmañjasyād rater atra kintu tāḥ syur yathocitam \|\|58\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Examples of the six items,** ***udvega, vilāpa, unmāda, vyādhi, jaḍatā*** **and** ***mṛti*** **were given for the** ***prauḍha*** **woman in** ***pūrva-rāga.*** **These also appear suitably in** ***samañjasa-pūrva-rāga*** **because of its suitable nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because of the fitting nature of *samañjasa-rati,* these symptoms appear.

### Text 59

***atha sādhāraṇaḥ—***  
***sādhāraṇa-rati-prāyaḥ sādhāraṇa itīritaḥ \|***  
***atra proktā vilāpāntāḥ ṣaḍ-daśāntāś ca komalāḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sādhāraṇa-pūrva-rāga:*** **Related** ***to sādhāraṇa-rati*****, the** ***pūrva-rāga*** **is called** ***sādhāraṇa.*** **The sixteen items** ***lālasa, udvega, jāgrya, tānavam, jaḍimā, vaiyagryam, vyādhi, unmāda, moha, mṛtyu, abhilāṣa, cintā, smṛti, guṇa-kīrtana, udvega,*** **and** ***vilāpa*** **appear but in weak form.**

### Text 60

***atha abhilāṣo, yathā prathama-skandhe (1.10.30)—***  
***etāḥ paraṁ strītvam apāstapeśalaṁ***  
***nirasta-śaucaṁ bata sādhu kurvate \|***  
***yāsāṁ gṛhāt puṣkara-locanaḥ patir***  
***na jātv apaity āhṛtibhir hṛdi spṛśan \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Abhiḷāsa,*** **from the First Canto*****:*** **Those who had been impure, had lost all auspiciousness and were women became most purified, because lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, increasing the bliss in their hearts by bringing things to them, never left their houses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The women of Kuru and Puru families speak about the queens. Though they could not enjoy with Kṛṣṇa, they are given as an example of *abhilāṣa* in that they have a taste for Kṛṣṇa. He made the queen’s womanhood the best, he purified them all. *Apasta-peśalam* means “without fitness.” They were without purity since they associated with material bodies.

*tvak-śmaśru-roma-nakha-keśa-pinaddham antar*  
*māṁsāsthi-rakta-kṛmi-viṭ-kapha-pitta-vātam*  
*jīvac-chavaṁ bhajati kānta-matir vimūḍhā*  
*yā te padābja-makarandam ajighratī strī*

**A woman who fails to relish the fragrance of the honey of your lotus feet becomes totally befooled, and thus she accepts as her husband or lover a living corpse covered with skin, whiskers, nails, head-hair and body-hair and filled with flesh, bones, blood, parasites, feces, mucus, bile and air. SB 10.60.45**

He pleased them with various gifts given with love.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When the women of the Kuru and Puru dynasties saw Kṛṣṇa they desired him by praising his wives. The queens had lost independence (being imprisoned), had lost purity (because of *kāma*), but he made them glorious (*sādhu*). “The female form has become fortunate because women like Rukmiṇī have appeared.” This was the praise. He pleased them with gifts like the *pārijāta* tree. If the Kuru women were enjoyed by other men, they did not enjoy with Kṛṣṇa. How can they have *pūrva-rāga*? They enjoyed in their minds and in dreams. In future lives they would directly enjoy. Thus it is not unsuitable as an example of *pūrva-rāga.*

### Text 61

***cintādīnāṁ tathānyāsām ūhyā dhīrair udāhṛtiḥ \|\|61\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The wise give examples of items such as** ***cintā.***

### Text 62

***pūrva-rāge prahīyeta kāma-lekha-srag-ādikam \|***  
***vayasyādi-kareṇātra kṛṣṇenāsya ca kāntayā \|\|62\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***pūrva-rāga*** **Kṛṣṇa and his lovers make friends deliver love letters and garlands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa sends letters to his beloved through friends, and his lovers send letters to him.

### Text 63-64

***tatra kāma-lekhaḥ—***  
***sa lekhaḥ kāma-lekhaḥ syāt yaḥ sva-prema-prakāśakaḥ \|***  
***yuvatyā yūni yūnā ca yuvatyāṁ saṁprahīyate \|\|63\|\|***  
***nirakṣaraḥ sākṣaraś ca kāma-lekho dvidhā bhavet \|\|64\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Love letter: A letter which reveals one’s love is called a** ***kāma-lekha*** **(love letter). The woman sends these to the man and the man sends these to the woman. There are two types: without alphabet and with alphabet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The letter reveals one’s love. It is dispatched out of necessity (*samprahīyate*).

### Text 65

***tatra nirakṣaraḥ—***  
***surakta-pallava-mayaś candrārdhādi-nakhāṅkabhāk \|***  
***varṇa-vinyāsa-rahito bhaved eṣa nirakṣaraḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Without letters: Crescent shaped nail marks on red buds, without any alphabetical letters is called the** ***nirakṣara*** **love letter.**

### Text 66

***yathā—***  
***kisalaya-śikhare viśākhikāyā***  
***nakhara-śikhā-likhito’yam ardha-candraḥ \|***  
***dadhad iha madanārdha-candra-bhāvaṁ***  
***hṛdi mama hanta kathaṁ haṭhād viveśa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: With the tip of her fingernail Viśākhā scratched a half-moon on the tip of this shoot. How has this letter like the half-moon arrow of Cupid entered my heart?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Holding a letter give by a friend of Viśākhā to his heart with affection, Kṛṣṇa speaks after a moment to Subala. *Madanārdha-candra-bhāvam* means “like the half-moon arrow of Cupid.”

### Text 67

***atha sākṣaram—***  
***gāthāmayī lipir yatra svahastāṅkaiṣa sākṣaraḥ \|\|67\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A letter with alphabet symbols: A message written in letters in the** ***prākṛta*** **language in the author's own hand is called** ***sākṣara.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Gāthā* means in *prākrṭa* language, in the *āryā* meter. It is written by hand.

### Text 68

***yathā jagannātha-vallabhe—***  
***suiraṁ vijjhasi hiaaṁ lambha-i maaṇo kkhu dujjasaḥ baliaṁ \|***  
***dīsasi saaladisāsuṁ dīsa-i maaṇo ṇa kuttābi \|\|\|***  
***suciraṁ bidhyasi hṛdayaṁ labhate madanaḥ khalu duryaśo balīyaḥ \|***  
***dṛśyase sakala-diśāsu dṛśyate madano na kutrāpi \|\|\]***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Jagannatha-vallabha*****: Over a very long period you repeatedly wounded my heart, and Cupid has been defamed. Now I see you everywhere and cannot see Cupid anywhere.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Over a very long period you repeatedly wounded my heart, and Cupid has been defamed. Now I see you everywhere and cannot see Cupid anywhere.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a love letter sent by Rādhā through Śaśimukhī to Kṛṣṇa. “Wounded by the arrow of Cupid, Rādhā has become exhausted.” This rumor perpetrated by the *sakhīs* is false. Thus she writes the letter.

### Text 69

***bandho’bja-tantunā rāgaḥ kiṁ vā kastūrikā-masī \|***  
***pṛthu-puṣpa-dalaṁ patraḥ mudrā-kṛt kuṅkumair iha \|\|69\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The written letters are bound by lotus fibers and with minerals or musk as ink on wide flower petals or leaves and stamped with** ***kuṁkuma.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Masī* is a material for making ink. These should be known as *uddīpanas.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Rāga* is a substance like vermilion. Musk and something like ink are used, or musk is used as ink.

### Text 70

***atha mālyārpaṇam—***  
***suśliṣṭāṁ nija-śilpa-kauśala-bhara-vyāhāriṇīm adbhutāṁ***  
***goṣṭhādhīśvara-nandanaḥ srajam imāṁ tubhyaṁ sakhi prāhiṇot \|***  
***ity ākarṇya giraṁ saroruha-dṛśaḥ svedoda-bindūcchalād***  
***aṅgebhyaḥ kula-dharma-dhairyam abhitaḥ śaṅke bahir niryayau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Offering a garland: “My friend! Kṛṣṇa sends you this astonishing, tightly strung, skillfully made garland.” When Rādhā heard these words she began to perspire. I think that, on the pretext of perspiration, all her self-control and chastity flowed out of her limbs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa, when he asks her about Rādhā, after having sent her a garland.

### Text 71

***kecit tu—***  
***nayana-prītiḥ prathamaṁ cintā-saṅgas tato’tha saṅkalpaḥ \|***  
***nidrā-cchedas tanutā viṣaya-nivṛttis trapānāpa \|***  
***unmādo mūrcchā mṛtir ity etāḥ smara-daśā daśaiva syuḥ \|\|71\|\|***  
***ity ācakṣate \|***

**Перевод:**

**Some authorities say there are ten stages of developing love in** ***pūrva-rāga*****: pleasure to the eyes, association by contemplation, vows, sleeplessness, thinness of the body, disinterest in other objects, destruction of shyness, madness, fainting, and death-like symptoms.**

### Text 72

***evaṁ krameṇa vijñeyaḥ pūrva-rāgo harer api \|***  
***nidarśanāya tatraikam udāharaṇam ucyate \|\|72\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In the manner as it arises in the women, one should understand** ***pūrva-rāga*** **in Kṛṣṇa. One example is given here to illustrate this.**

### Text 73

***yathā—***  
***upāraṁsīd vaṁśī-kala-parimalollāsa-rabhasād***  
***visasmāra sphārāṁ vividha-kusumākalpa-racanām \|***  
***jahau kṛṣṇas tṛṣṇāṁ sahacara-camū-cāru-carite***  
***sakhi tvad-bhrū-vyālī-culukita-calac-citta-pavanaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of Kṛṣṇa’s** ***pūrva-rāga:*** **My friend! Because the serpents of your eyebrows are drinking the restless wind of his heart, he has lost a taste for the intense bliss arising from the fragrant sound of his flute. He has forgotten to decorate himself profusely with various flower ornaments. He has given up the desire for charming activities with a host of friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Rādhā. The sound of the flute is compared to a flower garden giving fragrance to indicate the various charms in the rhythms and improvisations. *Ullāsa* means prominence and *rabhasa* means bliss. Kṛṣṇa gave up interest in the strong bliss arising from the various fragrances of his flute playing.

Māna (Separation caused by anger)

### Text 74

***dampatyor bhāva ekatra sator apy anuraktayoḥ \|***  
***svābhīṣṭāśleṣa-vīkṣādi-nirodhī māna ucyate \|\|74\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***bhāva*** **of the couple who are attached to each other and are either together or apart, which hinders their actions such as embraces and glances is called** ***māna*** **(anger).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This *bhāva* should also have strong sweetness by being endowed with *vibhāva* and other elements. The word *api* indicates being separate as well as being together.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

That quality which prevents embracing, glancing and other actions desired by the couple-- a type of anger--endowed with *vibhāva* and other elements, is called *māna.* In *rasa* scriptures the word *dampati* simply means a man and woman (not a married couple). One will see the use of *bhartṛkā* in the same way, to indicate an unmarried relationship. The word *abhiṣṭa* excluded obstacles due to laziness, sleep, time, place, vows in a temple etc. as sometimes the embraces of the man and woman are not desired. The obstacle of *māna* may be present while they are together or separate.

### Text 75

***sañcāriṇo’tra nirveda-śaṅkāmarṣāḥ sa-cāpalāḥ \|***  
***garvāsūyāvahitthāś ca glāniś cintādayo’py amī \|\|75\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In this conditon** ***sañcāri-bhāvas*** **such as** ***nirveda, śaṅkā, amarṣa, cāpalatā, garvā, asūya avahitthā, glāni*** **and** ***cintā*** **occur.**

### Text 76

***ahetor neti nety uker hetor yan māna ucyate \|***  
***asya praṇaya eva syān mānasya padam uttamam \|\|76\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The highest level of** ***māna*** **is** ***praṇaya*****. It has two types: caused and uncaused.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Māna’s* best shelter is *praṇaya.* Otherwise it is restricted. Where the *bhāva* called *māna* was described previously, it appears before or after *praṇaya.* The present *māna* as *rasa* cannot appear before *praṇaya* since without *praṇaya* it does not appear with brilliance.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

How does this *māna* arise? This verse answers. *Praṇaya* is the best place for *māna.* Where *praṇaya* exists *māna* will exist. It is the best, because *māna* appearing in *sneha* is not the best. It was said:

*janitvā praṇayaḥ snehāt kutracin mānatāṁ vrajet \|*  
*snehān mānaḥ kvacid bhūtvā praṇayatvam athāśnute \|\|*

**Sometimes** ***praṇaya*** **arises from** ***sneha*** **and** ***praṇaya*** **produces** ***māna.*** **But sometimes** ***māna*** **arises from** ***sneha*** **and produces** ***praṇaya. Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.119**

### Text 77

***tatra sa-hetuḥ—***  
***hetur īrṣyā-vipakṣāder vaiśiṣṭye preyasā kṛte \|***  
***bhāvaḥ praṇaya-mukhyo’yam īṛṣā-mānatvam ṛcchati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Caused** ***māna:*** **The cause of** ***māna*** **is jealousy (*****īrṣā*****) of a rival when the lover praises the rival.** ***Praṇaya*** **then becomes** ***māna*** **caused by jealousy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Māna* has a cause, jealousy. *Māna* without a cause will be explained later.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The cause in this case is jealousy. What is the cause of jealousy? When the lover praises a rival woman or her friends, the woman becomes jealous. The dominant mood of *praṇaya* then becomes *māna* by jealousy.

### Text 78

***tathā coktam (śṛṅgāra-tilaka 2.53)--***  
***snehaṁ vinā bhayaṁ na syān nerṣyā ca praṇayaṁ vinā \|***  
***tasmān māna-prakāro’yaṁ dvayoḥ prema-prakāśakaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Thus it is said: Without** ***sneha,*** **fear will not occur. Without** ***praṇaya*****, jealousy will not occur. Thus both types of** ***māna*** **caused by these two reveal a type of** ***prema.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Without a man feeling affection for a woman, fear will not arise in him. Without *praṇaya* in the woman, jealousy will not occur. From these two arises two types of *māna* which is a type of *prema.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

If a man offends a woman then he fears the woman. If he offends her, she develops hatred or jealousy of him. This *māna* caused by the man and the woman becomes *rasa*. The cause of fear is *sneha* and the cause of hatred is *praṇaya*. Without a melted heart or *sneha* towards the woman, his fear will not arise. Without *praṇaya* of the woman for the man, her hatred will not arise.

### Text 79-80

***ataeva harivaṁśe (2.66.4, 2.65.50)—***  
***ruṣitām iva tāṁ devīṁ snehāt saṅkalpayann iva \|***  
***bhīta-bhīto’tiśanakair viveśa yadu-nandanaḥ \|\|\|***  
***rūpa-yauvana-sampannā sva-saubhāgyena garvitā \|***  
***abhimānavatī devī śrutvaiverṣyā-vaśaṁ gatā \|\|80\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Hari-vaṁsa:*** **Kṛṣṇa, who is feared by fear itself, and who is the descendant of Yadu, while respecting out of affectionate seemingly angry Satyabhāmā, entered the palace gently. Meanwhile, hearing how her rival Rukmiṇī had obtained a** ***pārijāta*** **flower, endowed with beauty and youthfulness, Satyabhāmā, very proud of good fortune, became overwhelmed with special** ***māna.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because she had *praṇaya* her anger was apparent only (*iva*). He thought “Her affection for me has slackened somewhat. But actually that is not really possibly in her. It is apparent (i*va*).” She was proud, thinking that she was the best because Kṛṣṇa adored her the most. She had the special *bhāva* called *māna*, described in the chapter on *bhāva (abhimānavatī).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Her anger was a transformation of *praṇaya (ruṣitām iva).* He respected her out of affection. Or he wanted to make her fall at his feet and speak flattery. She was fortunate because of her happiness fixed on Kṛṣṇa. Because of her pride, she showed hatred. She was filled with *madhu-sneha* (Kṛṣṇa is mine) (*abhimānavatī).* The special feature here is that Kṛṣṇa had supported her rival.

### Text 81-82

***tatrāpi ca susakhyâdi hṛdi yasyā virājate \|***  
***tasyā vipakṣa-vaiśiṣṭye na syād eva sahiṣṇutā \|\|81\|\|***  
***ataḥ satyāṁ vinānyāsāṁ susakhyāder abhāvataḥ \|***  
***śrute’pi pārijātasya dāne māno na cābhavat \|\|82\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**If the woman has** ***susakhya*** **in her heart she cannot tolerate the glorification of her rival. Since** ***susakhya*** **was absent in all queens except Satyabhāmā. On hearing that Rukmiṇī got a** ***pārijāta*** **they did not develop** ***māna.***

### Text 83

***śrutaṁ cānumitaṁ dṛṣṭaṁ tad-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ tridhā matam \|\|83\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The glories of the rival come from hearing, inferring and seeing.**

### Text 84

***atha śravaṇam—***  
***śravaṇaṁ tu priya-sakhī-śukādīnāṁ mukhād bhavet \|\|84\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From hearing: Hearing about the rival comes from the mouth of the lover, a friend or a parrot etc.**

### Text 85

***tatra sakhī-mukhāt, yathā—***  
***śaśimukhi mṛṣā jalpaṁ śrutvā kaṭhora-sakhī-mukhāt***  
***praṇayini harau mā viśrambhaṁ kṛthāḥ śithilaṁ vṛthā \|***  
***parihara manaḥ-klāntiṁ devi prasīda manorame***  
***tava mukham anālocya preyān vane’dya viśīryati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from a friend: Śaśimukhī! Do not weaken your faith in Kṛṣṇa who loves you by hearing false gossip from the mouth of foul-mouthed friends. Give up your mental depression. O goddess Manoramā! Become happy! Not seeing you, he now lies shattered in the forest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Manoramā who is angry at Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 86

***yathā vā—***  
***ahaha gahanā keyaṁ vārtā śrutau patitādya me***  
***viditam anṛtaṁ hāsyād brūṣe vimuñca kadarthanām \|***  
***sahacari kuto jīvaty asmin jane’pi janārdano***  
***dyutaru-kusumaṁ tasyai hā dhik kṛtī vitariṣyati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Alas! What ominous news has fallen on my ears! You are speaking lies as a joke. Give up torturing me. O friend! While I am alive, Kṛṣṇa, who knows place, time and worthy recipient, gives the flower of the heavenly** ***pārijāta*** **tree to Rukmiṇī. What misfortune!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Gahana* means “boding ill fortune.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This gives an example of *māna* in a queen.  *Satyabhāmā* speaks to a friend who tells her about Rukmiṇī getting a *pārijāta* flower. *Keyam adbhūta* means “never heard before.” This means it breaks the ears. Considering for a moment she says, “I know. For a joke you are lying in order to torture me.” While someone with my qualities is alive (*asmin jane*), he who knows place, time and worthy recipient (*krtī),* gives the flower to her, Rukmiṇī.

### Text 87

***śuka-mukhā, yathā—***  
***āste kācid dayita-kalahā krūra-cetāḥ sakhī te***  
***kīro vanyaḥ sphuṭam iha yayā śyāmale pāṭhito’sti \|***  
***atha vyarthe vihaga-lapite suṣṭhu viśrambhamāṇā***  
***mānārambhe na kuru hṛdayaṁ kātaro’smi prasīda \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hearing from a parrot: O Śyāmalā! You have a cruel-hearted, quarrelsome friend. She has taught this wild parrot to speak clearly. You uselessly put all your faith in a chattering parrot. Please do not immerse your heart in this jealous anger. I am very distressed. Please be happy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to angry Śyāmalā with reasoning and pleasing words. The parrot has been made to recite in order to give pain to you and me.

### Text 88

***anumitiḥ—***  
***bhogāṅka-gotra-skhalana-svapnair anumitis tridhā \|\|88\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From inference: There are three types of inference of a lover’s infidelity: marks of enjoyment, calling the wrong name by mistake, and utterances in dreams.**

### Text 89

***atra bhogāṅkaḥ—***  
***bhogāṅko dṛśyate gātre vipakṣasya priyasya ca \|\|89\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Marks of enjoyment: The woman sees marks of enjoyment on the limbs of the lover or the rival woman.**

### Text 90

***tatra vipakṣa-gātre bhogāṅka-darśanaṁ, yathā—***  
***kālindī-taṭa-dhūrta cāṭubhir alaṁ nidrātu candrāvalī***  
***khinnākṣī kṣaṇam aṅganād apasara kruddhāsti vṛddhā gṛhe \|***  
***kiñcid bimbita-dhātu-patra-makarī-citreṇa tatrādhunā***  
***sarvā te lalitā lalāṭa-phalakenodghāṭitā cāturī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Seeing marks on the rival: O cheater who sports on the Yamunā! What is the use of your sweet words? Let tired-eyed Candrāvalī sleep. Leave this yard at once. Anger is increasing in this house. Your cheating is revealed by that woman’s musk patterns marked with the minerals from your forehead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Some fault-finding *gopī* previously painted pictures on his chest with minerals in order to test him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Kṛṣṇa came to the bower of frustrated Candrāvalī, Padmā scolded him with anger. Enough of your flattery! We know the reason for your sweet words, but be silent now. “What harm is there if I speak?” Candrāvalī, having fainted from the pain of the fire of anger, is sleeping. Let her sleep. Your chattering should not awaken her. Her eyes are exhausted. She was awake all night because of pain of separation. “Then I will stand here silently for a moment.” Get out of here! “You who are so merciful will know my innocence, pleasing speech and politeness when she awakens.” Your cheating is revealed in the pictures made of musk on other women which are slightly tinged with the minerals from the decorations on your forehead.

### Text 91

***priya-gātre bhogāṅka-darśanaṁ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.40)—***  
***muktāntar-nimiṣaṁ madīya-padavīm udvīkṣamāṇasya***  
***jāne keśara-reṇubhir nipatitaiḥ śoṇīkṛte locane \|***  
***śītaiḥ kānana-vāyubhir viracito bimbādhare ca vraṇaḥ***  
***saṅkocaṁ tyaja deva daiva-hatayā na tvaṁ mayā dūṣyase \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Seeing marks of enjoyment on the beloved, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **You gave up blinking your eyes to gaze constantly at the path I would tread. I know your eyes are red because of the pollen, and you have been injured on your red lips by the cold forest wind without being aware, because of** ***prema*** **for me. Give up fear. O Lord! Since I am struck by fate, I will not criticize you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Sañkocam* means fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Disappointed Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa who is trying to pacify her. She speaks with opposite meaning in her words. You gave up internal blinking while looking at the path I would come on, what to speak of external blinking, what to speak of what will happen on seeing me directly? Your eyes are red because of your unblinking eyes getting filled with pollen, caused by *prema* for me. I realize this at all times, so what is the need of you informing me of this? You are not even aware of the wounds on your lips because of your *prema* for me. Give up your fear. For a person with *prema,* what is the possibility of offense, by which you are so reserved? O Lord! He cannot even make the *prema* of humans like you. *Deva* also indicates “O Kṛṣṇa engaged in playing! Why are you reserve red? Enjoy with her in front of me!” “If that is ok, why do you criticize me in front of your friends? I must have committed real offense.” Knowing the truth I do not criticize you. I forgive whatever you did wrong previously. “Then why are you lamenting?” If my misfortune is written on my forehead, what can you do?

### Text 92

***tatra gotra-skhalanam—***  
***vipakṣa-saṁjñayāhvānam īrṣyātiśaya-kāraṇam \|***  
***āsāṁ tu gotra-skhalanaṁ duḥkhadaṁ maraṇād api \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Uttering a rival’s name by accident:** ***Gotra-skhalanam*** **means calling the rivalṣ name. It is a cause of great hatred and gives more sorrow than death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Saying the other woman’s name (*gotra*) by mistake is called *gotra-skhalanam.* The dictionary of *Ajaya* says *gotra* means a family, wealth, name and mountain.

### Text 93

***tena yathā bilvamaṅgale—***  
***rādhā-mohana-mandirād upagataś candrāvalīm ūcivān***  
***rādhe kṣemam iheti tasya vacanaṁ śrutvāha candrāvalī \|***  
***kaṁsa kṣemam aye vimugdha-hṛdaye kaṁsaḥ kva dṛṣṭas tvayā***  
***rādhā kveti vilajjito nata-mukhaḥ smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, by Bilvamaṅgala: Leaving the grove named Rādhā-mohana, Kṛṣṇa came to Candrāvalīi and said, “O Rādhā, are you well?” Hearing this Candrāvalī said, “O Kaṁsa, are you well?” Kṛṣṇa said, “Bewildered at heart! Where did you see Kaṁsa?” Candrāvalī said, “Where did you see Rādhā?” May Kṛṣṇa who bowed his head and smiled with embarrassment protect you all!**

### Text 94

***yathā vā—***  
***ahaha vilasaty agre candrāvalī vimala-dyutiḥ***  
***kitava kalitā tārā sātra tvayā kva nu ṣoḍaśī \|***  
***timira-malinākāra kṣipraṁ vrajāruṇa-maṇḍalā***  
***mama sahacarī yāvan manyu-dyutiṁ na vimuñcati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Ah! Candrāvalī with spotless splendor shines before you. O cheater! Where do you see the sixteenth star named Rādhā? O black, contaminated form! You should leave this place at once, as long as my angry friends do not give their complexion of anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The sixteenth constellation is named Rādhā. *Aruṇa-maṇḍalā* means the sun at dawn and Candrāvalī with an assembly (*maṇḍala)* of angry friends.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The anger of the leader was shown when the lover inadvertently mentions another woman’s name. Now an example is give of *sakhīs* becoming angry at the mention of the rival woman’s name. In Candrāvalī’s assembly enjoying the riddles, music, song and dance, Kṛṣṇa remembered Rādhā in the *rūḍha-bhāva* stage and uttered her name when addressing Candrāvalī. Padmā then angrily spoke. *Ahaha* expresses astonishment and lamentation. Candrāvalī means many moons. Learned men know only one moon which they glorify. But she is many moons. Moreover she has spotless light, not covered by clouds. She mentions the sixteenth constellation instead of uttering Rādhā’s name because of her hatred. Just as the moon and darkness are friends, the sun and darkness are enemies. None of her *sakhīs* will forgive you. That you should know. She has her group of *sakhīs* who are angry, or are like a red halo at dawn.

### Text 95

***atha svapnaḥ—***  
***harer vidūṣakasyāpi svapnaḥ svapnāyitaṁ mataḥ \|\|95\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Inference through dreams: Kṛṣṇa’s or a joker’s revelations during dreams is called** ***svapna.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Svapnāyitam* means activity during dreams. This is called *svapna.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Evidence from dreams is called *svapna*. The formation of *svanāyita* follows words like *lohita.*

### Text 96

***tatra hareḥ svapnāyitam, yathā—***  
***śape tubhyaṁ rādhe tvam asi hṛdaye tvaṁ mama bahi-***  
***stvam agre tvaṁ pṛṣṭhe tvam iha bhavane tvaṁ girivane \|***  
***iti svapne jalpaṁ niśi niśamayantī madhuripor***  
***abhūt talpe candrāvalir atha parāvartita-mukhī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa speaking in a dream: “Rādhā! I swear to you that you are in my heart. You are everything outside me. You are in front of me, behind me, you are in this cottage, and you are in the forest by Govardhana Hill.” Hearing these words at night while Kṛṣṇa slept on the bed, Candrāvalī turned her face away.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kundavallī. Kṛṣṇa’s words while dreaming indicate his greater love for Rādhā.

### Text 97

***vidūṣakasya, yathā—***  
***avañci caṭupāṭavair aghabhid ādya padmā-sakhī***  
***tatas tvaraya rādhikāṁ kim iti mādhavi dhyāyasi \|***  
***niśamya madhumaṅgalād iti giraṁ puraḥ svapnajāṁ***  
***vidūna-vadanā sakhi jvalati paśya candrāvalī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**A jester speaking in a dream: “O Mādhavī! Why do you worry? Kṛṣṇa has deceived Padmā with flattering words today. Make Rādhā hurry to the meeting!” Hearing Madhumaṅgala say this in a dream, Candrāvalī with afflicted face is blazing with anger. Look at her!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śaibyā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Padmāyāḥ sakhī* is Candrāvalī.  *Avañci* means cheated. Hasten Rādhā to the meeting!

### Text 98

***atha darśanam, yathā—***  
***mithyā mā vada kandare mama sakhīṁ hitvā tvam ekākinīṁ***  
***niṣkrāntaḥ pṛthu-sambhrameṇa kim api prakhyāpayan kaitavam \|***  
***dūrāt kiñcid añcitena rasanāśabdena sātaṅkayā***  
***niṣkramyātha tayā śaṭhendra puline dṛṣṭo’si rādhā-sakhaḥ \|\|98\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Māna*** **from seeing: Don't lie. You left my friend Candrāvalī all alone in that cave and left in great haste, announcing your deceit. O king of cheaters! Having doubt about the sound of small bells, she came out of the bower and saw Rādhā with you on the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Padmā speaks to Kṛṣṇa who is trying to pacify her. Your haste has announced your deceit. You said, “Today, at the twilight, I have not found one of the cows which have become separated. I hear her mooing in the distance. Stay her while I will bring the cow here.” In the distance with some fear she heard the sound of small bells. “Ah! What is that sound of bells? It is not from my *sakhīs*.” Then she came out of the bower.

### Text 99

***yathā vā—***  
***sahacari parigumphya prātar evārpitāsīd***  
***braja-pati-suta-kaṇṭhe yā mayotkaṇṭhayādya \|***  
***api hṛdi lalitāyās tasthuṣī hanta hṛn me***  
***dahati dahana-dīptiḥ paśya guñjāvalī sā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! This morning I strung this** ***guñja*** **berry necklace and with great love placed it around the neck of the prince of Vraja. Look! Lalitā now wears that same necklace over her heart! That garland, blazing like fire, burns my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tasthuṣī* indicates a completed action. This shows her hatred of Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous example showed the woman seeing the rival with Kṛṣṇa. The present verse shows the woman seeing the rival’s members. Candrāvalī, seeing Lalitā in the distance, reveals to Padmā the pain in her heart. The word eve indicates that the same morning that she gave the garland, she saw it on Lalitā. *Tasthuṣī* is a completed action. She saw it at the time of seeing Lalitā in the distance. I put the garland on Kṛṣṇa’s neck in the morning, and came here. But this same morning, Kṛṣṇa gave it to Lalitā. Oh! It did not remain on his neck of a moment. How can I bear this! This shows her strong hatred of Kṛṣṇa but not of Lalitā. What misfortune! I strung this garland in order to give myself pain.

### Text 100-101

***atha nirhetuḥ—***  
***akāraṇād dvayor eva kāraṇābhāsatas tathā \|***  
***prodyan praṇaya evāyaṁ vrajen nirhetu-mānatām \|\|\|***  
***ādyaṁ mānaṁ parīṇāmaṁ praṇayasya jagur budhāḥ \|***  
***dvitīyaṁ punar asyaiva vilāsa-bhara-vaibhavam \|***  
***budhaiḥ praṇayamānākhyaṁ eṣa eva prakīrtitaḥ \|\|101\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Causeless** ***māna:*** **When** ***māna*** **arises in a couple without cause or by a shadow of cause, the** ***māna*** **is called** ***nirhetu.*** **The wise say that the first type of** ***māna*** **is a transformation of** ***praṇaya (sahetu).*** ***Nirhetu māna*** **is the glory of** ***praṇaya*** **filled with beauty. The learned call this** ***praṇaya-māna.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first type, *īrṣyā-māna,* is a transformation of *praṇaya.* By combination with *īṛṣyā* it attains an equivalent condition, just as crystal becomes red by closeness to a red object.

Snake’s coils can be dissolved or can be formed again. It is not like milk changing to yogurt. Yogurt cannot change back to milk. The second type arises without contact with *īrṣyā*. It is a special form of *praṇaya’s* splendor, like perceiving a garland as a snake. This form is without cause.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Akaraṇāt* means without cause. The first type is called *īrṣyā-māna*, which was previously described. It is with cause. The second type of *māna* is without cause or with apparent cause only. It is the glory of *praṇaya (asya)* filled with *vilāsa.*

### Text 102

***tathā coktam (sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇe 5.48)—***  
***aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet \|***  
***ato hetor ahetoś ca yūnor māna udañcati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**It is said: The movement of a snake is naturally crooked.** ***Prema*** **has the same nature (in** ***māna). Māna*** **between couples arises either with cause or without cause.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a proof of causeless *māna.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Udañcati* means manifests. Also it is said:

*nadīnāṁ ca vadhūnāṁ ca bhujagānāṁ ca sarvadā \|*  
*premnām api gatir vakrā kāraṇaṁ tatra neṣyate*

**The movement of** ***prema,*** **like the movement of a river, a woman or a snake, is always crooked. There is no cause for this.** ***Alaṅkāra-kaustubha*** **5.77**

### Text 103

***avahitthādayo hy atra vijñeyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ \|\|103\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In causeless** ***māna*** **the** ***sañcāri-bhāvas*** **like** ***avahitthā*** **appear.**

### Text 104

***tatra kṛṣṇasya, yathā—***  
***avyakta-smita-dṛṣṭim arpaya puraḥ svalpo’pi mantur na me***  
***patyur vañcana-pāṭavād vrajapate jyotsnī-niśārdhaṁ yayau \|***  
***śubhrālaṅkṛtibhir drutaṁ pathi mayā dūraṁ tataḥ prasthite***  
***sāndrā cāndram arundha bimbam acirād ākasmikī kālikā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s causeless anger: Look at me without smiling, but I have not committed any fault. O master of Vraja! I have come here after half the night is over because I had to expertly cheat my husband. With white cloth and ornaments I came quickly on the path a great distance. Suddenly a thick mass of clouds covered the moon in an instant.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Māna arising from cause cannot appear in Kṛṣṇa. Skipping that, *māna* causes by a shadow of cause is described for Kṛṣṇa. One woman of Vraja had an appointment made by her friend to meet Kṛṣṇa. When she came to him after three hours of the night, she saw that he was angry. She shows that she is innocent. Gaze at me without a clear smile. If you have real anger, do not smile. Just look at me. No male can remain without looking at a young woman standing in front of him. She says this to make him laugh. She describes her innocence.

O king of Vraja! She should say “prince of Vraja” but because of agitation and fear this comes from her mouth.  *Jyotsnī* means moonlit. “Did you not go elsewhere for half the night?” I had to put on white clothing. Then a mass of clouds covered the moon. *Kālikā* means a mass of clouds according to *Amara-koṣa.* This happened suddenly. I had no time to think. Because of the darkness, I could not go out since I was wearing white clothing. I had to change my clothes and come. Thus I am late. I am not at fault.

### Text 105

***yathā vā—***  
***puṣpebhyaḥ spṛhayā vilambitavatīm ālokya mām unmanāḥ***
