***kaṁsāriḥ sakhi lambitānana-śaśī tūṣṇīṁ nikuñje sthitaḥ \|***  
***ātaṅkena mayā tad-aṅghri-nakhare kṣipte prasūnāñjalau***  
***tasyālīka-ruṣā bhruvaṁ vibhujato’py āvirbabhūva smitam \|\|105\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: Seeing me delay as I picked flowers with a desire for the best ones, Kṛṣṇa became angry, hung his head and remained silent in the bower. I became frightened and placed a handful of flowers at his toenails. With false anger he moved his eyebrow and then smiled.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In shadow of cause, Kṛṣṇa may become angry because of lateness by accident or intention. Rādhā come to her house she reveals to Śyāmalā the *rasa* of noon pastimes. First Kṛṣṇa decorated me. Then to decorate him with flowers I went out alone to the garden. Picking the flowers I saw he was standing angrily in the bower. I offered handfuls of flowers to his toenails. Seeing him without movement and silent I thought, “Kṛṣṇa is not in the bower. This is a blue statue of two-armed Nārāyaṇa. To please Kṛṣṇa I will offer this deity a handful of flowers.” When I did this, he smiled.

### Text 106

***kṛṣṇa-priyāyāḥ, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (44)***  
***tiṣṭhan goṣṭhāṅgaṇabhuvi muhur locanāntaṁ vidhatte***  
***jātotkaṇṭhas tava sakhi harir dehalī-vedikāyām \|***  
***mithyā-mānonnati-kavalite kiṁ gavākṣārpitākṣī***  
***svāntam hanta glapayasi bahiḥ prīṇaya prāṇanātham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The woman causeless anger, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **Kṛṣṇa stands in the yard, gazing at the threshold of your house with longing from the corner of his eyes. O friend devoured by false anger! Gazing through the lattice work window, why do you torture your heart? Come outside and please the lord of your life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This verse shows anger without cause in the heroine. Seeing Kṛṣṇa coming to the cow shed from the forest Śyāmalā speaks to Rādhā who has causeless anger. *Dehalī-vedikāyām* means the cleaned ground in front of the courtyard.

### Text 107

***yathā vā—***  
***aham iha vicinomi tvad-giraiva prasūnaṁ***  
***kathaya katham akāṇḍe caṇḍi vācaṁ yamāsi \|***  
***viditam upadhinālaṁ rādhike śādhi kena***  
***priya-sakhi kusumena śrotram uttaṁsayāmi \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O impetuous Rādhā! By your order I picked these flowers. Please tell me why you remain silent? I have understood. Give up this pretense. Dear friend! Order me! With which flower should I decorate your ear?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Upādhinā* means “by pretense.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is an example of anger with a shadow of cause. Having come from picking flowers by the order of Rādhā, a *svādhīna-bhartṛkā*, Kṛṣṇa speaks on seeing Rādhā’s anger. O impetuous one, having anger without cause (*caṇḍi*)! You remain silent. Pausing a moment, he then spoke happily, ignoring her signs of anger. I understand. This is like flowers in the sky (false). Your anger is for the purpose of showing your intense attraction for me. Enough of pretense (*upādhinā).* Give me an order (*śādhi*).

### Text 108

***dvayor eva yugapad, yathā—***  
***kuñje tuṣṇīm asi nata-śirāḥ kiṁ cirāt tvaṁ murāre***  
***kiṁ vā śyāme tvam api vimukhī mauna-mudrāṁ tanoṣi \|***  
***jñātaṁ jñātaṁ smita-vimuṣite kāpi vām āsti yogyā***  
***krīḍā-vāde balavati yayā na dvayor eva bhaṅgaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Simultaneous causeless anger in both: Kṛṣṇa, why do you bow your head in silence for such a long time! Rādhā! Why are you silent and averse to Kṛṣṇa? I have understood. This is an intense practice of yours in not smiling, by which your mutual anger does not break, though it is a great interruption to play.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Smita-vimuṣite* means “whose smiles have gone.” The order of the words in the compound is reversed as in *āhitāgni*: placing fire on the altar. Another version has *smita-virahite.* *Yogyā* means practice according to *Trikāṇḍa-śeṣa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks while relishing the sweetness of causeless anger occurring simultaneously in Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa while they played in the bower. “Suddenly I am becoming angry at the time of happiness. Today I will see how she behaves.” Thinking in this way he became angry. Rādhā thought “If he is becoming falsely angry, then can I not also become angry? Anger is our nature. Today I will see whose anger will break first.” She then showed anger. This is a type of causeless anger. This is some inconceivable practice of the couple *(vām*) in which they stop smiling. By this practice your anger does not break, being an intense obstacle to play (*krīḍā-vāde*). This does not produce joy in the pastimes of the bower, but is an interruption to the play. This is Vṛndā’s critical analysis, but since they did it by their free will, there was no alternative.

### Text 109

***yathā vā—***  
***kuñja-dvāri niviṣṭayos taraṇijā-tīre dvayor eva nau***  
***tatrānyonyam apaśyatoḥ sakhi mudhā nirbandhataḥ klāntayoḥ \|***  
***haste drāg atha dāḍimī-phalam abhinyaste mayā nistalaṁ***  
***rādhām udbhidura-smitāṁ parihasan phullāṅgam āliṅgiṣam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! Having arrived at the entrance to the bower on the bank of the Yamunā, we remained there, not looking at each other. Out of stubbornness, we were both uselessly exhausted. Quickly I grabbed a round pomegranate in my hand. She smiled. Laughing, I embraced her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Nistalam* means round.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because simultaneous anger with a shadow cause is not possible, another example of anger with no cause is given along with the pacification of anger. Kṛṣṇa reveals to Viśākhā the *rasa* of confidential pastimes with Rādhā. First I thought it was not necessary to give up this useless, stubborn anger. Then afterwards, when I saw a pomegranate fruit and took it in my hand, she spontaneously broke into a smile (*udbhiduram smitām*). She smiled to indicate the fruit. “Give enjoyment to your mind by holding the pomegranate.” Kṛṣṇa said, “Beloved! You have broken your anger first by smiling. You have been defeated.” Rādhā said, “O Kṛṣṇa! Your anger was broken first. Taking the pomegranate in your hand was a sign that your anger was finished. You have been defeated.” Then she laughed. In *Amaru-śataka* such causeless anger is also described:

*paśyāmo mama kiṁ prapadyata iti sthairyammayālambitaṁ*  
*kiṁ māmālapatīty ayaṁ khalu śaṭhaḥ kopas tvayāpy āśritaḥ*  
*ity anyonya –vilakśa-dṛṣṭi-cature tasminn avasthantare*  
*sa-vyājaṁ hasitaṁ māyā dhṛti-haro bāṣpas tu muktas tayā*

**I decided to see what she would do. She thought “Why does he speak to me?” “You are cunning and angry.” While we spoke and glanced at each other, I smiled deceitfully and she, losing her composure, wept.**

Elsewhere it is said:

*adatta me vartmani manmathonmadā*  
*svayaṁ grahāśleṣam asau sakhī tava \|*  
*ity uktavantaṁ kuṭilībhavan mukhī*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ vataṁsena jaghāna maṅgalā \|\|*

**When Kṛṣṇa said “Your friend, passionate with desire, gave me an embrace on the road,” Maṅgalā, turning her head in shyness, struck him with a garland.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.105**

*Māna* of the pure *vāmya* type is not considered in *vipralambha-rasa.*

### Text 110

***nirhetukaḥ svayaṁ śāmyet svayaṁgrāha-smitādibhiḥ \|\|110\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Causeless anger disappears on its own, by smiles and other reactions of the man and woman.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It disappears by smiles by the two parties.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

First the disappearance of causeless anger is described. The easy subject is explained before the more difficult according to the logic of the needle and the cauldron. Sūcī-kaṭāha-nyāya.1 Causeless anger disappears on its own---not by effort. When does this happen? It happens when the woman smiles or cries, and the man embraces and kisses her.

### Text 111

***yathā—***  
***roṣas tavābhūd yadi rādhike’dhika-***  
***stathāstu gaṇḍaḥ katham ucchvasity asau \|***  
***sva-narmaṇetthaṁ durapahnava-smitāṁ***  
***priyām acumbat paśupendra-nandanaḥ \|\|111\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O Rādhikā! If you are so angry with me, then why do your cheeks swell with happiness? When she was unable to conceal a smile, the prince of the cowherds proceeded to kiss her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā. Her cheeks became full because of an inner smile.

### Text 112-113

***hetur yas tu śamaṁ yathāyogyaṁ prakalpitaiḥ \|***  
***sāma-bheda-kriyā-dāna-naty-upekṣā-rasāntaraiḥ \|\|112\|\|***  
***mānopaśamanasyāṅkā bāṣpa-mokṣa-smitādayaḥ \|\|113\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Anger with a cause is destroyed suitably by use of** ***sāma*** **(pacification),** ***bheda*** **(division),** ***kriyā*** **(action),** ***nati*** **(offering respects),** ***upekṣā*** **(disrespect) and** ***rasāntara*** **(change of** ***rasa*****). The symptoms are tears, and smiles etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Prakalpitaiḥ* means “by using.”  *Aṅkāḥ* means symptoms. The seven items will be explained with examples. The symptoms of disappearance of *māna* are tears and smiles. The word *ādi* indicates glancing with affection as friends.

### Text 114

***tatra sāma—***  
***priya-vākyasya racanaṁ yat tu tat sāma gīyate \|\|114\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sāma*** **means speaking nicely.**

### Text 115

***yathā—***  
***jātaṁ sundari tathyam eva pṛthunā rādhe’parādhena me***  
***kintu svārasiko mamātra śaraṇaṁ snehas tvadīyo balī \|***  
***ity ākarṇya giraṁ harer natamukhī bāṣpāmbhasāṁ dhārayā***  
***sānaṅgotsava-raṅga-maṅgala-ghaṭau pūrṇāvakārṣīt kucau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: O beautiful Rādhā! Though by my serious offense you are rightfully angry, your affection for me is my sweet shelter. When Rādhā heard these words she bowed her face, and the stream of her tears filled the auspicious pots of Cupid’s festival.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa pleases Rādhā when she is angry. Her approval is indicated by establishing the pots used in worshipping Cupid.

### Text 116

***atha bhedaḥ—***  
***bhedo dvidhā svayaṁ bhaṅgyā sva-māhātmya-prakāśanam \|***  
***sakhyādibhir upālambha-prayogaś ceti kīrtyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There are two types of divisive ploy: praising one’s intelligence by showing wit in speech, and** ***sakhīs’*** **scolding.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

One displays one’s cleverness by wit. “No woman can find a young man like me.” In this way he glorifies himself.

### Text 117

***tatra bhaṅgyā svamāhātmya-prakāśanaṁ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (4.41)—***  
***cañcan-mīna-vilocanāsi kamaṭhotakṛṣṭa-stanī saṅgatā***  
***kroḍena sphuratā tavāyam adharaḥ prahlāda-saṁvardhanaḥ \|***  
***madhyo’sau bali-bandhano mukha-rucā rāmās tvayā nirjitā***  
***labdhā śrī-ghanatādya mānini manasy aṅgīkṛtā kalkitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Bheda*** **through self-praise by clever speech, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Your eyes are as playful as restless fishes, your breasts are like two handsome turtles on your splendid chest, your lips increase bliss, your waist is marked with three lines, and the loveliness of your face defeats a host of goddesses of fortune. Though you possess intense beauty, you mind is polluted with anger.**

**Your eyes support Matsya, your breast supports Kūrma, with Varāha, and you increase the joy of Prahlāda as Nrṣiṁha. You have bound Bali on your waist as Vāmana, and have defeated Rāma, Paraśurāma and Balarāma by the beauty of your face. You are also Buddha and will become Kalki.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Bali-bandhanaḥ* means binding up gifts or “surrounded at the waist by three natural lines.” *Śrī-ghanatā* means thick with beauty or thick with intelligence. *Kalkitā* means deceived or appeared.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā who is angry. *Sphuratā krodeṇa* means with a brilliant lap or with Varāha. You increase bliss or as Nṛsiṁha, increase Prahlāda’s joy. You bound up Bali as Vāmana, or your waist has three lines. You have defeated Lakṣmī, or you have defeated Rāma, Paraśurāma and Balarāma. You are thick with beauty or you are Buddha *(śrīghana*). Your mind is polluted with anger or you have become Kalki. *Amara-koṣa* says *kalka* means sin or impurity. In this way the ten *avatāras* I assume are dependent on you. How can your glory be described? This is the external hint. Actually I am the Supreme Lord worshipped by Brahmā and others but I give pleasure to that cowherd girl. But you do not consider your fortune and do not withdraw your anger.

### Text 118

***athavedaṁ priyoktitvāt sāmodāharaṇaṁ bhavet \|***  
***nāyakasya sva-vacasā bhaṅgyāyaṁ bheda īryate \|\|118\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By the words of the lover, this becomes an example of** ***sāma*** **as well.** ***Bheda*** **is defined by word play in the speech of the man.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The verse quoted does not follow the definition of *bheda,* since it did not solely depend upon the ironic use of words to destroy the anger. *Ayam* means “the definition being discussed.”

### Text 119

***yathā—***  
***rūkṣā yan mayi vartase tvam abhitaḥ snigdhe’pi te dūṣaṇaṁ***  
***tatrāste na hi kintu tat kila mamānaucitya-jātaṁ phalam \|***  
***yena svastaruṇīr upekṣya caramām apy āśrayantīr daśāṁ***  
***premārtaṁ vraja-yauvataṁ ca sumukhi tvaṁ kevalaṁ sevyase \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: It is not a fault for you to be harsh towards me. It is not your fault, since you are filled with affection. It is the result of my unworthy actions since I ignored the heavenly women, who are now dying. O beautiful faced Rādhā! You are absorbed in youthfulness in Vraja filled with the pain of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Since the previous example illustrated *sāma* as well, another example is given to establish the word play of the man. The *gopīs* had said:

*kṛṣṇaṁ nirīkṣya vanitotsava-rūpa-śīlaṁ*  
*śrutvā ca tat-kvaṇita-veṇu-vivikta-gītam*  
*devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā*  
*bhraśyat-prasūna-kabarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa’s beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of him and hear his resonant flute-song, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their belts loosen. SB 10.21.12**

Thus the *devatā* women give up their bodies.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā who is angry. *Svas-taruṇiḥ* means the *devatā* women, who have taken shelter of the tenth state, death. This is described in SB 10.21.12.

### Text 120

***sakhyādibhir upālambha-prayogo, yathā—***  
***kartuṁ sundari śaṅkhacūḍa-mathane nāsminn upekṣocitā***  
***sarveṣām abhaya-pradāna-padavī-baddha-vrate preyasi \|***  
***ity ālībhir alakṣitaṁ murabhidā bhadrāvalī bheditā***  
***nāsāgre vara-mauktika-śriyam adhād asrasya sā bindunā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Bheda*** **through scolding by** ***sakhīs:*** **O beautiful Bhadrā! You should not ignore dear Kṛṣṇa who killed Śaṅkhacūḍa and who has vowed to protect all people from fear. Unseen by Kṛṣṇa, when Bhadrā was scolded by her friends, her nose became beautiful with a tear drop appearing like the best pearl.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Friends partial to Kṛṣṇa speak to Bhadrā who is angry. If he had not killed Śaṅkhacūḍa, where would we be? Bhadrāvalī means Bhadrā.

### Text 121

***atha dānam—***  
***vyājena bhūṣaṇādīnāṁ pradānaṁ dānam ucyate \|\|121\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Dānam:*** **Deceptively giving ornaments and other items is called** ***dāna.***

### Text 122

***yathā—***  
***kāmo nāma suhṛn mamāsti bhavatīm ākarṇya mat-preyasīṁ***  
***hāras tena tavārpito’yam urasi prāpnotu saṅgotsavam \|***  
***ity unnamya karaṁ muradviṣi vadaty udbhinna-sāndra-smitā***  
***padmā māna-vinigrahāt praṇayinā tenodbhaṭaṁ cumbitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “I have a friend named Cupid. When he heard you were my beloved, he gave me a sapphire necklace to give it to you. May that necklace enjoy the happiness of association on your chest!” When Kṛṣṇa, saying this, raised his hand, Padmā abandoned her anger and smiled broadly. Out of love, Kṛṣṇa boldly kissed her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Padmā. She smiled, thinking, “It is true. Cupid gave me a sapphire necklace and gave you a golden one.”

### Text 123

***atha natiḥ—***  
***kevalaṁ dainyam ālambya pādapāto natir matā \|\|123\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Nāti: Nati*** **means to fall at the feet of the beloved while feeling completely helpless.**

### Text 124

***yathā—***  
***kṣiti-luṭhita-śikhaṇḍāpīḍam ārān mukunde***  
***racayati rati-kānta-stoma-kānte praṇāmam \|***  
***nayana-jaladharābhyāṁ kurvatī bāṣpa-vṛṣṭiṁ***  
***varatanur iha māna-grīṣma-nāśaṁ śaśaṁsa \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: When Kṛṣṇa, more handsome than a host of Cupids, offered obeisance with his peacock feather touching the ground very close to her, beautiful Rādhā, showering tears from the clouds of her eyes, proclaimed the end of the summer season of anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kundavallī. *Ārāt* means close.

### Text 125

***atha upekṣā—***  
***sāmādau tu parikṣīṇe syād upekṣāvadhīraṇam \|***  
***upekṣā kathyate kaiścit tūṣṇīmbhāvatayā sthitiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Upekṣā*** **or disrespect: When other methods fail,** ***upekṣā*** **or disrespect is used. Others say that** ***upekṣā*** **means to stand by silently.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Avadhīranam* means disrespect.

### Text 126

***tad dvayaṁ, yathā—***  
***sūnur vallabha eṣa vallavapates tatrāpi vīrāgraṇīs-***  
***tatrāpi smara-maṇḍalī-vijayinā rūpeṇa vibhrājitaḥ \|***  
***sakhyaḥ samprati rūkṣatā pṛthur iyaṁ tenātra na śreyase***  
***dūre paśyata yāti niṣṭhura-manāḥ kā yuktir atrocitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Disrespect: The son of the cowherd king is dear to us. He is the foremost of heroes, and he is more handsome than a host of Cupids. My friends! Because Rādhā has been so harsh with Kṛṣṇa, she has lost her good fortune. Look, filled with cruel anger, she is going away. What reasoning is possible?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another reading of the third line is *sakhyaḥ samprati rūkṣatā prṭhur iyam kāryā tathāpi sphutam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Śikhā and other *sakhīs*. The son of Nanda is dear to the cowherd women (*vallabha*). Because Rādhā has been so rough with Kṛṣṇa it is not auspicious for her. She has fallen from good fortune.

### Text 127

***Standing by silently:***  
***māne muhur nitibhir apy atidurnivāre***  
***vācaṁyama-vratam ahaṁ tarasāgrahīṣam \|***  
***bāṣpaṁ tato vikiratī nijagāda padmā***  
***pauṣpaṁ rajaḥ patitam atra dṛśor mameti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**When I could not dissipate her anger by offering respects, I quickly took a vow not to speak to her. Padmā, with tears in her eyes, said “Some pollen has fallen in my eyes.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala.

### Text 128

***athavā—***  
***prasādana-vidhiṁ muktvā vākyair anyārtha-sūcakaiḥ \|***  
***prasādanaṁ mṛgākṣīṇām upekṣeti smṛtā budhaiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another meaning of** ***upeksā:*** **The wise say that** ***upekṣā*** **means “pleasing a woman by speaking words with other meanings, after giving up other means.”**

### Text 129

***yathā—***  
***dhammille nava-mālatī paricitā savye ca śabda-grahe***  
***mallī sundari dakṣiṇe tu katarat puṣpaṁ tava bhrājate \|***  
***āghreyaṁ paricetum ity upahite vyājena nāsā-puṭe***  
***gaṇḍodyat-pulakā vihasya hariṇā candrāvalī cumbitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: “I am familiar with the fresh jasmine that is in your braid and the jasmine flower in your left ear. What flower is that in your right ear? I should smell it to find out its species.” While smiling, with this pretext using his deceptive nose, he kissed Candrāvalī whose cheeks developed goose bumps.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Candrāvalī. *Śabda-grahe* means “in the ear.” *Upahite* means deceptive.

### Text 130

***atha rasāntaram—***  
***ākasmika-bhayādīnāṁ prastutiḥ syād rasāntaram \|***  
***yādṛcchikaṁ buddhi-pūrvam iti dvedhā tad ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sudden change of** ***rasa:*** **Production of sudden fear and other things is called** ***rasāntram*****. It has two types: accidental and intentional.**

### Text 131

***tatra yādṛcchikam—***  
***upasthitam akasmād yat tad yādṛcchikam ucyate \|\|131\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Accidental: That which arrives unexpectedly is called accidental.**

### Text 132

***yathā—***  
***api gurubhir upāyair adya sāmādibhir yā***  
***lavam api na mṛgākṣī māna-mudrām abhāṅkṣīt \|***  
***harim iha parirebhe sā svayaṁgrāham agre***  
***nava-jaladhara-nādair bhīṣitā paśya bhadrā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Even though Kṛṣṇa tried many intensive means such as pacifying words, Bhadrā would not give up her anger one bit. Look! Frightened by the sound of thunder, Bhadrā has embraced him with her arms right here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The friends of Bhadrā speak amongst themselves. *Svayaṁgrāham parirebhe* means “she has embraced him, accepting him with her arms.

### Text 133

***yathā vā—***  
***upāyeṣu vyarthonnatiṣu bata sāmādiṣu sakhe***  
***sakhīnāṁ cāturye gatavati ca sadyaḥ śithilatām \|***  
***viśākhāyāḥ kopa-jvara-haraṇa-mantra-pratinidhiṁ***  
***sacītkāraṁ rūkṣa-svanitam akarod ukṣa-danujaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: My friend! When all my sweet words and other expert tactics proved useless and her** ***sakhīs’*** **skills all became powerless, suddenly the demon Ariṣṭa roared loudly. This was the incantation to remove Viśākhā’s fever of anger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The sound of thunder naturally reduces anger since it is an *uddīpana* for amorous desire. Thus another example is given. Kṛṣṇa speaks to Subala. The roar was like a mantra. Ukṣa-danujā is Ariṣṭāsura. *Amara-koṣa* says *ukṣā* means a bull.

### Text 134

***atha buddhi-pūrvam—***  
***buddhi-pūrvaṁ tu kāntena pratyutpanna-dhiyā kṛtam \|\|134\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intentional: When the event is arranged intentionally by the lover it is called intentional.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pratyutpanna-dhiyā* means “by inspired intelligence.”

### Text 135

***yathā—***  
***pāṇau pañcamukhena duṣṭa-kṛmiṇā daṣṭo’smi roṣād iti***  
***vyājāt kūṇita-locanaṁ vraja-patau vyābhujya vaktraṁ sthite \|***  
***sadyaḥ projjhita-roṣa-vṛttir asakṛt kiṁ vṛttam ity ākulā***  
***jalpantī smita-bandhur āsyam amunā gāndharvikā cumbitā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Contracting his eyes and contorting his face, Kṛṣṇa said, “I have been bitten on the hand by a ferocious five-headed insect!” Rādhā became very agitated and, immediately giving up her extreme anger, said “What happened?” With smiling face, Kṛṣṇa suddenly kissed her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of *vraja-patau* sometimes the phrase *vraja-vidhau* (moon of Vraja) is seen.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Standing silently in front of Rādhā who was angry, he faked fear and pain, crying out loudly. As he contorted his face and closed his eyes, she immediately gave up her anger. What happened? She raised Kṛṣṇa who had fainted in her arms and in front of his face spoke. With a smiling face, he kissed her.

### Text 136

***yathā vā—***  
***nyastaṁ dāma kṛtāgasādya hariṇā dṛṣṭvā puro rādhayā***  
***kṣiptenābhihataḥ sa tena kapaṭī duḥkhīva bhugnānanaḥ \|***  
***mīlann eva niṣedivān bhuvi tataḥ sadyas tayā vyagrayā***  
***pāñibhyāṁ dhṛta-kandharaḥ sthita-mukho bimboṣṭham asyāḥ papau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: After offending her, Kṛṣṇa gave Rādhā a garland. When he saw she angrily throw the garland at him, he pretended to become overwhelmed with grief from the pain of the garland hitting him. Closing his eyes, he fell to the ground. Agitated Rādhā immediately held his neck with both her hands. With her face in front of him, Kṛṣṇa suddenly kissed her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Niṣedivān* means located.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Like *sāma* and *ḍāna* there are many types of *rasāntara* because of the opportunities for it. There will different *rasāntaras* with different manifestations of anger. That is shown in this verse. Nāndīmukhī speaks to Paurṇamāsī. Kṛṣṇa acted as if he were injured by the blow of the garland hitting him.

### Text 137

***deśa-kāla-balenaiva muralī-śravaṇena ca \|***  
***vināpy upāyaṁ māno’sau līyate vraja-subhruvām \|\|137\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Other than the means mentioned, the causeless anger of the women of Vraja is destroyed by place, time and hearing the flute.**

### Text 138

***tatra deśa-balena, yathā—***  
***alaṅkīrṇaṁ candrāvalir ali-ghaṭā-jhaṅkṛti-bharaiḥ***  
***puro vṛndāraṇyaṁ kim api kalayantī kusumitam \|***  
***hariṁ ca smerāsyaṁ priyaka-taru-mūle priyam itaḥ***  
***skhalan-mānā sakhyām adiśata satṛṣṇaṁ dṛśam asau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By the power of place: When Candrāvalī saw Vṛndāvana filled with extraordinary flowers and swarms of buzzing bees, and when she saw smiling Kṛṣṇa under a** ***kadamba*** **tree, she lost all her anger, and glanced at her** ***sakhī*** **with longing for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Kalayantī* means seeing. She saw Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana *(itaḥ*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Bhadrā who asks about Candrāvalī’s anger. She saw Vṛndāvana spread abundantly (*alaṁkīrṇam*) with swarms of bees. *Priyaka* means a *kadamba* tree. She glanced at her *sakhī* with longing. She indicated “O friend! My anger has been destroyed by this forest. What shall I do? Do what you should do.” It was said that the symptoms that anger was gone were smiles and embraces. The word *ādi* there means giving glances at a *sakhī.*

### Text 139

***kāla-balena, yathā—***  
***śaradi madhura-mūrtiḥ paśya kānti-cchaṭābhiḥ***  
***snapayati ravikanyā-tīra-vanyāṁ sudhāṁśuḥ \|***  
***iti niśi niśamayya vyāhṛtiṁ dūtikāyāḥ***  
***smita-rucibhir atānīt tatra rādhā prasādam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By the power of time: “Look! The charming moon in autumn bathes the forest on the bank of the Yamunā with splendid moonlight.” When Rādhā heard a messenger say this, she emanated joy everywhere by the splendor of her smile.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 140

***muralī-śabdena, yathā—***  
***yadi roṣaṁ na hi muñcasi***  
***na muñca mama devi nātra nirbandhaḥ \|***  
***phutkṛti-vidhūta-mānaḥ***  
***sa bhavatu vijayī harer veṇuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**By the sound of the flute: If you do not give up anger, then don’t. O devī! I will not Endeavour. May Kṛṣṇa’s flute, which destroys anger by its sound, be victorious!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* speaks to Rādhā who is angry. O *devī!* Human women are easily pleased but not a *devatā* woman like you! I will not Endeavour. “Today I will make Rādhā pleased and bring her. See my intelligence.” I have made this decision in front of Kṛṣṇa. Let that Endeavour fail, but I will make a means to defeat you who ignore my advice. I will instruct Kṛṣṇa, “O Kṛṣṇa! Now use your unfailing flute.”

### Text 141

***yathā vā—***  
***mānasyopādhyāyi prasīda sakhi rundhi me śruti-dvandvam \|***  
***ayam uccāṭana-mantraṁ siddho veṇur vane paṭhati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend, teacher of anger! Kindly block both my ears. In this forest the powerful flute is now reciting a destructive mantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The previous verse it was stated that the flute sound destroys anger. However the effects were not shown. This verse shows the effects. Rādhā speaks to Lalitā with anger.

### Text 142-143

***tāratamyaṁ tu mānasya hetoḥ syāt tāratamyataḥ \|***  
***syāl laghur madhyamaś cāsau mahiṣṭhaś cety atas tridhā \|\|142\|\|***  
***susādhyaḥ syāl laghur māno yatna-sādhyasya madhyamaḥ \|***  
***duḥsādhyaḥ syād upāyena mahiṣṭhaḥ preyasāpy ayam \|\|143\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**According to the strength of the cause, the anger may be light, medium or intense. Anger which is easily subdued is called light. Anger which is subdued with effort is medium. Anger which is subdued with difficulty by the best of means is called intense.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Intense anger is subdued with great difficulty by the best of means.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

According to the cause, jealousy, the anger has various strengths.

### Text 144-146

***kṛṣṇe roṣoktayas tāsāṁ vāmo durlīla-śekharaḥ \|***  
***kitavendro mahā-dhūrtaḥ kaṭhoro nirapatrapaḥ \|\|144\|\|***  
***atidurlalito gopī-bhujaṅgo rata-hiṇḍakaḥ \|***  
***gopikā-dharma-vidhvaṁsī gopa-sādhvī-viḍambakaḥ \|\|145\|\|***  
***kāmukeśas tamisraughaḥ śyāmātmāmbara-taskaraḥ \|***  
***govardhana-taṭāraṇya-bāṭa-pāṭac-carādayaḥ \|\|146\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In anger the women call Kṛṣṇa many names. He is Cupid, the summit of evil acts, king of cheaters, great rascal, hard-hearted, ungrateful, most ill-mannered, lecher for** ***gopīs*****, stealer of women, destroyer of the young** ***gopīs’ dharma*****, profaner of cowherds’ wives, lord of the lusty, flood of darkness, black man, stealer of clothing, and thief on the forest path near Govardhana.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

According to Dharaṇi, the word *vāṭa* means path. *Pāṭacara* is a thief.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Araṇya-vāta* means a forest path.  *Pāṭa* means thief. According to *Amara-koṣa* the following are words for thief:

*Cauraikāgārika-stena-dasyu-taskara-moṣakāḥ*  
*Ptatirodhita-parāskandi-pāṭacara-maliṁlucaḥ*

### Text 147

***atha prema-vaicittyam—***  
***priyasya sannikarṣe’pi premonmāda-bhramād bhavet \|***  
***yā viśleṣa-dhiyārtis tat prema-vaicittyam ucyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Prema-vaicittyam:*** **Pain because of thinking of separation even though the lover is present, out of bewilderment of madness in** ***prema*** **is called** ***prema-vaicittyam.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vaicittyam* refers to false perception in *prema.* When it is filled with this *bhāva* it is called *prema-vaicittyam*. This takes place in the presence of the lover. *Gopāla-campu* says:

*sāṅgāliṅgana-laṅgime’ṅga-valayā-saṅge’pi śārṅgī tadā*  
*gopīnāṁ sphurati sma dūra-gatayā premāpagā-pūrataḥ \|*  
*yasmād utkalikā-kalāpa-valanā-vṛttiṁ bahir lumpatī*  
*svapnābhāṁ diśatī śatīm api dṛśi sphūrtiṁ muhur lumpati \|\|*

**Though sweetness manifested fully with embraces, with clothing and ornaments, Kṛṣṇa manifested himself at a distance from the waves of the river of** ***prema*** **of the** ***gopīs*****, because when the external functions of consciousness disappeared because of great longing, though he was present, that presence before the eyes repeatedly disappeared as in a dream.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The excellence of *prema* is the *sthāyi* called *anurāga*. It is based on extreme strength of thirst and produces the perception of an object’s absence when it is present. A *brāhmaṇa* who is voracious by nature after being fed is addressed as follows. “O *brāhmaṇa*! You have eaten well!” The *brāhmaṇa* answers “I did not eat at all.” This has been illustrated:

*ko’yaṁ kṛṣṇa iti vyudasyati dhṛti yas tanvi karṇaṁ viśan*  
*rāgāndhe kim idaṁ sadaiva bhavatī tasyorasi krīḍati \|*  
*hāsyaṁ mā kuru mohite tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā*  
*satyaṁ satyam asau dṛgaṅganam agād adyaiva vidyun-nibhaḥ \|\|*

**Rādhā: O slender friend! Who is this Kṛṣṇa, whose name, on entering my ears, makes me lose my composure?**

**Lalitā: O girl blinded by love! What are you saying? You continually play on his chest.**

**Rādhā: Don't make fun of me!**

**Lalitā: O bewildered girl! I have now placed you in the hand of that person.**

**Rādhā: It is true, but a flash of lightning has today landed in the courtyard of my eyes.**

***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.148**

This special reaction called *prema-vaicittyam* is the highest level of thirst, in which, though Kṛṣṇa is present, and even though he is directly and continually experienced, the person’s intelligence ceases to function, so that the person thinks “I do not experience Kṛṣṇa.”

Similarly, when a person arrives, though constantly drinking water, he may say “Ah! Let me drink water!”

The reasoning is as follows. In *anurāga* the functioning of intelligence becomes very subtle so that the intelligence does not simultaneously make Kṛṣṇa and the sweetness of his qualities the object of experience. Thus in experiencing Kṛṣṇa, intelligence is not aware of his qualities, and when it is aware of his qualities, it is not aware of Kṛṣṇa. A fine needle pierces one thread of cloth while sewing, not two threads. Similarly, in the *sambhoga-rasa* the woman thinks “He has enjoyed me.” She becomes absorbed in his exalted qualities such as amorous play, speaking, cunning, singing, playing instruments and dancing. A moment later giving up absorption in those qualities her intelligence says “Where is he?” The intelligence then experiences separation and does not perceive him, though he is present.

### Text 148

***yathā—***  
***ābhīrendra-sute sphuraty api puras tīvrānurāgotthayā***  
***viśleṣa-jvara-sampadā vivaśa-dhīr atyantam udghūrṇitā \|***  
***kāntaṁ me sakhi darśayeti daśanair udgūrṇa-śasyāṅkurā***  
***rādhā hanta tathā vyaceṣṭate yataḥ kṛṣṇo’py abhūd vismitaḥ \|\|148\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: Even though Kṛṣṇa stood before her, Rādhā’s uncontrolled intelligence became unsteady by a great fever of separation caused by intense** ***anurāga.*** **Grinding a blade of grass with her teeth she said, “O friend, show me my lover.” When Rādhā displayed such actions, Kṛṣṇa became astonished.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Puraḥ sphurati* means “though he was present.”  *Udgūrṇa* means “raising up.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. *Puraḥ sphurati* means “though he was present.” *Udghūrṇa trṇāṅkurā* means “she raised up grass with her teeth.” *Gur* means to raise.

### Text 149

***yathā vā vidagdha-mādhave (5.46)—***  
***samajani davād vitrastānāṁ kim ārta-ravo gavāṁ***  
***mayi kim abhavad vaiguṇyaṁ vā niraṅkuśam īkṣitam \|***  
***vyaraci nibhṛtaṁ kiṁ vāhūtiḥ kayācid abhīṣṭayā***  
***yad iha sahasā mām atyākṣīd vane vanajekṣaṇaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **I think there must have been painful cries of the cows frightened of a forest fire. Or did he see unlimited faults in me, for he has suddenly abandoned me in the forest? Was he called by some** ***śakhī*****? Shall I stay here alone?**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The principle *prema-vaicittyam* which is causeless was shown. Now an example of secondary *prema-vaicttyma* arising from a shadow of a cause is given. When bothered by a bee, Rādhā, on hearing from Madhumaṅgala that Kṛṣṇa had arrived, did not see him, even though he was standing in front of her, because of the appearance of *prema-vaicittyam*. She laments with fear and depression. Was he called by a rival through indications of a bird’s call?

### Text 150-151

***vilāsam anurāgas tu kutracit kam api vrajam \|***  
***pārśve santam api preṣṭhaṁ hāritaṁ kurute sphuṭam \|\|150\|\|***  
***suṣṭhūdāharatā paṭṭa-mahiṣī-gīta-vibhramam \|***  
***spaṣṭaṁ muktā-phale caitad vopadevena varṇitam \|\|151\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes** ***anurāga*** **attains a transformation. This causes the lover who is present to appear as if absent. This is well illustrated in the song of the queens in** ***Bhāgavatam*** **and in the story of** ***Muktā-phala*** **by Vopadeva.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prema-vaicittyam* is explained.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The song of the queens is in *Bhāgavatam* 10.90.15. *Mukta-phala* is a work by Vopadeva.

### Text 152-154

***atha pravāsaḥ***  
***pūrva-saṅgatayor yūnor bhaved deśāntarādibhiḥ \|***  
***vyavadhānaṁ tu yat prājñaiḥ sa pravāsa itīryate \|\|\|***  
***taj-janya-vipralambho’yaṁ pravāsatvena kathyate \|***  
***harṣa-garva-mada-vrīḍā varjayitvā samīritāḥ \|\|153\|\|***  
***śṛṅgāra-yogyāḥ sarve’pi pravāse vyabhicāriṇaḥ \|***  
***sa dvidhā buddhi-pūrvaḥ syāt tathaivābuddhi-pūrvakaḥ \|\|154\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Absence by leaving: The wise say that obstacles to the couple meeting such as place, it is called** ***pravāsa.*** **The feeling of separation caused by these obstacles is also called** ***pravāsa*****. All the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*** **except** ***harṣa, garva, mada*** **and** ***vrīdā*** **manifest in** ***pravāsa-vipralambha*** **of** ***śṛṅgāra-rasa*****. There are two types of** ***pravāsa*****: intentional and unintentional.**

### Text 155-156

***atra buddhi-pūrvaḥ—***  
***dūre kāryānurodhena gamaḥ syād buddhi-pūrvakaḥ \|***  
***kāryaṁ kṛṣṇasya kathitaṁ svabhakta-prīṇanādikam \|\|155\|\|***  
***kiñcid dūre sudūre ca gamanād apy ayaṁ dvidhā \|\|156\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Intentional absence: Intentional** ***pravāsa*** **takes place when the man goes way because of duties, when Kṛṣṇa performs actions to please other devotees. There are two types: somewhat far separation and very far separation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Somewhat far” means going from Vraja to some place in Vṛndāvana. “Very far” means going from Vraja to Mathurā and Dvārakā.

### Text 157

***tatra ādyaḥ—***  
***dṛṣṭiṁ nidhāya surabhī-nikuramba-vīthyāṁ***  
***kṛṣṇeti varṇa-yugalābhyasena rasajñām \|***  
***śuśrūṣaṇe murali-nisvanitasya karṇau***  
***cittaṁ sukhe tava nayaty ahar adya rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, of somewhat far departure: Fixing her eyes on the path where the herd of cows will return, engaging her tongue in repeating the two syllables “Kṛṣṇa,” engaging her ears in hearing the sound of your flute, she spends her day with heart fixed in your happiness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *muralī* also has a form *murali.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One messenger gives news of Rādhā to Kṛṣṇa when he is herding the cows. She fixes her eyes on the path where the cows will return.

### Text 158

***atha dvitīyaḥ—***  
***bhāvī bhavaṁś ca bhūtaś ca trividhaḥ sa tu kīrtyate \|\|158\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Going a great distance: Going a great distance has three types: future, present and past.**

### Text 159

***tatra bhāvī, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (67)—***  
***eṣa kṣattā vraja-narapateḥ ājñayā gokule asmin***  
***bāle prāto nagara-gataye ghoṣaṇām ātanoti \|***  
***duṣṭam bhūyaḥ sphurati ca balād īkṣaṇaṁ dakṣiṇaṁ me***  
***tena svāntaṁ sphuṭati caṭulam hanta bhāvyaṁ na jāne \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Future, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: My dear girl, following the king of Vraja's order, the gatekeepers in Gokula have announced the departure for Mathurā early tomorrow morning. Oh! My right eye is now quivering with inauspiciousness. Because of that, my unsteady heart is trembling. I do not know the future.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A woman of Vraja speaks with fear, lamentation and depression to a friend. *Kṣattā* means door keepers. *Nagara-gataye* means going to Mathurā. The right eye trembles, signifying some disaster. According to *Amara-koṣa* the word *ksāttā* means two guards standing at the door.

### Text 160

***bhavan, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.7)—***  
***bhānor bimbe tvaritam udaya-prasthataḥ prasthite’sau***  
***yātrānandīṁ paṭhati muditaḥ syandane gāndineyaḥ \|***  
***tāvat tūrṇaṁ sphuṭa khura-puṭaiḥ kṣauṇi-pṛṣṭaṁ khananto***  
***yāvan nāmī hṛdaya bhavato ghoṭakāḥ sphoṭakā syuḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Present departure, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: With the sun quickly rising over Udaya-giri, Akrūra stands on the chariot, happily reciting prayers for a safe journey. O heart! You should immediately burst, before the horses digging the earth with their hooves make it burst.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Prasthaḥ* means a mountain top. *Yātrānandīm* means auspicious prayers. She addresses her heart.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmā laments. The sun is traveling over the top of Udaya Mountain. *Yātrānandīm* means auspicious prayers.  *Syandane* means “on the chariot.”  *Gāndineyaḥ* is Akrūra. O heart! Please break quickly. “But I am very reserved.” Do not say that. Why are you steadier than the earth? The horses of the chariot dig the earth with their hooves. It is better I die this way than from the blows of the horses’ hooves. It is better to die while seeing the lord of my life in Vraja than to watch him leave Vraja.

### Text 161

***bhūto, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (85)—***  
***kāmaṁ dūre sahacari varīvarti yat kaṁsavairī***  
***na idam lokottaram api vipad-durdinaṁ me dunoti \|***  
***āśākīlo hṛdi kila vṛtaḥ prāṇa-rodhī tu yo me***  
***so’yaṁ pīḍāṁ niviḍa-vaḍavā-vahni-tīvras tanoti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Past departure, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O friend! The extraordinary cloudy day of disaster--Kṛṣṇa's leaving us on his own-- does not cause me pain. But the hope that he will return is a spike in the heart which destroys my life. It inflicts pain like the intense fire of the fire beneath the sea.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā talks to Viśākhā. The cloudy day (*durdinam)* was a disaster.

### Text 162

***atra śrī-yadu-siṁhena preyasīhir amuṣya ca \|***  
***preṣaṇaṁ kriyate premṇā sandeśasya parasparam \|\|162\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**During intentional long distance separation, Kṛṣṇa and his beloveds send messages to each other because of their** ***prema.***

### Text 163

***yathā uddhava-sandeśe (115)—***  
***soḍhavyaṁ te katham api balāc cakṣuṣī mudrayitvā***  
***tīvrottāpam hata-manasijoddāma vikrāntacakram \|***  
***dvitrair eva priya-sakhi dinaiḥ sevyatāṁ devi śaibye***  
***yāsyāmi tvat-praṇaya-caṭula-bhrū-yugāḍambarāṇām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O Śaibyā! Somehow or other you must tolerate the intense pain caused by many bold attacks of worthless Cupid. Dear friend! In a few days I will come to partake of the exploits of your eyebrows trembling out of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā sends a message to Śaibyā through Uddhava. I will make the exploits of your eyebrows my object *(sevyatām*). The subject is expressed in the genitive form. The word s*evyatām* suggests that in Mathurā he suffers by not being worshipped by such exclusive devotees, event though he is regarded as the Lord there.

### Text 164

***tathā padyāvalyām (376)—***  
***kālindyāḥ pulinaṁ pradoṣa-maruto ramyāḥ śaśaṅkāṁśavaḥ***  
***santāpaṁ na harantu nāma nitarāṁ kurvanti kasmāt punaḥ \|***  
***sandiṣṭaṁ vraja-yoṣitām iti hareḥ saṁśṛṇvato’ntaḥpure***  
***niḥśvāsāḥ prasṛtā jayanti ramaṇī-saubhāgya-garva-cchidaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **“The charming moonlight, the evening breezes, and the shore of the Yamunā are not able to cool our burning suffering but rather intensify it.” When Kṛṣṇa heard this message from the women of Vraja within his palace, he sighed. May the sighs he released at that time, which crushed the queens who were proud of their good fortune, be ever victorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The women of Vraja sent messages by parrots which usually went undelivered. May the sighs be victorious!. This means “May his desire to return be fulfilled.” This usage of *jayati* is permitted by poets.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī in Dvārakā, relishing the message sent by the women of Vraja, describes the state of Kṛṣṇa. This message was read by some traveler. The women of Dvārakā are Rukmiṇī and others. The suggestion is clear.

### Text 165

***atha abuddhi-pūrvaḥ—***  
***pāratntryodbhavo yas tu proktaḥ so’buddhi-pūrvakaḥ \|***  
***divyādivyādi-janitaṁ pāratantryam anekadhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Unintentional departure: When the separation takes place beyond one’s will, it is called unintentional. Such unintentional causes are many, such as fate or mundane situations.**

### Text 166

***yathā lalita-mādhave (2.27)—***  
***ānītāsi mayā manoratha-śata-vyagreṇa nirbandhataḥ***  
***pūrṇaṁ śārada-purṇimā-parimalair vṛndāṭavī-maṇḍalam \|***  
***sadyaḥ sundari śaṅkhacūḍa-kapaṭa-prāptodayenādhunā***  
***daivenādya virodhinā katham itas tvaṁ hanta dūrīkṛtā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O beautiful Rādhā! Because I was agitated with hundreds of desires, I brought you to this forest of Vṛndāvana filled with the fragrance of the new moon. Nevertheless, destiny disguised as this demon Śaṅkhacūḍa has arrived and taken you away.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śārada means new according to *Amara-koṣa.* After Śiva-rātri s the journey to the Ambikā took place temple. Then Horikā Pūrṇimā came. Because of lack of *rasa* by dancing in Balarāma’s presence, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma danced in separate places. After the full moon, the new moon of the spring season started.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

To fool Mukharā, Kṛṣṇa hid in a bower. Suddenly Śaṅkhacūḍa arrived and took Rādhā off her throne. “O Kṛṣṇa! Where are you?” Hearing the painful cries of Lalitā and others, he quickly left the bower. Kṛṣṇa then began lamenting. Fate has struck in the form of the demon coming.

### Text 167

***cintātra jāgarodvegau tānavaṁ malināṅgatā \|***  
***pralāpo vyādhir unmādo moho mṛtyur daśā daśa \|\|167\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In** ***pravāsa-v ipralambha*** **ten conditions arise;** ***cintā*** **(thinking),** ***jāgara*** **(sleeplessness),** ***udvega*** **(agitation),** ***tānavam*** **(thinness),** ***malinatā*** **(soiled body),** ***pralāpa*** **(meaningless chatter),** ***unmāda*** **(madness),** ***vyādhi*** **(sickness),** ***moha*** **(fainting) and** ***mṛtyu*** **(death).**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Atra* means in *pravāsa-vipralambha.*

### Text 168

***tatra cintā, yathā haṁsadūte (2)—***  
***yadā yāto gopī-hṛdaya-madano nanda-sadanān***  
***mukundo gāndinyās tanayam anuvindan madhupurīm \|***  
***tadāmāṅkṣīc cintā-sariti ghana-ghūrṇā-paricayair***  
***agādhāyāṁ bādhā-maya-payasi rādhā virahiṇī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Absorption in thinking, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **When Kṛṣṇa, the Cupid who enchanted the** ***gopīs'*** **hearts, left Nanda's home and followed Akrūra to Mathurā city, Rādhā, overwhelmed by separation, became plunged in a river of** ***cintā*****, deep with water of affliction and many powerful whirlpools.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *rasika* speaks. When Kṛṣṇa left Nanda’s house and went to Mathurā, according to instructions of Akrūra, then Rādhā became absorbed in a river of thought *(cintā*). “Should I protect myself by binding my life airs, burning with pain of separation, by the ropes of hope, or should I free myself from hope and give up life? Should I enter the fire or the Yamunā? But if he returns and does not see me, what will happen? He will give up his life by lamenting for me. Or will he maintain his life by some means? Ah! Since he has great love for me, how can he remain alive? Therefore I will not die. I will see his beautiful lotus face. If the fire of pain does not burn me, then I can live.” She became absorbed in such thoughts. The water was thick with whirlpools, or the thoughts were thick with unsteadiness arising from *mohana* in *mahābhāva.* The river had water in the form of pain (*bādhā*).

### Text 169

***atha jāgaraḥ, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (322)—***

***asmākaṁ tu gate kṛṣṇe gatā nidrāpi vairiṇī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Wakefulness, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **Girls who can see their lover in dreams are very fortunate. As for me, since Kṛṣṇa left, my enemy sleep has also left me.**

Rādhā speaks to Viśākhā.

### Text 170

***atha udvegaḥ, yathā haṁsadūte (104)—***  
***mano me hā kaṣṭaṁ jvalati kim ahaṁ hanta karavai***  
***na pāraṁ nāvāraṁ kim api kalayāmy asya jaladheḥ \|***  
***iyaṁ vande mūrdhnā sapadi tam upāyaṁ kathaya māṁ***  
***parāmṛṣye yasmād dhṛti kaṇikayāpi kṣaṇikayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Udvega,*** **from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **Alas! My heart burns with pain! What should I do? I cannot see how to cross to the shore of this ocean of suffering. I offer my respects to you with my head. Reflect, and tell me how I can be touched by a little peacefulness for a moment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Parāmṛśye* means “I will be touched.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. I cannot see the shore of the ocean of suffering *(asya*). I should be touched (*parāmṛśye*) by a particle of self-control.

### Text 171

***atha tānavaṁ, yathā—***  
***udañcad-vaktrāmbhoruha-vikṛtir antaḥ-kaluṣitā***  
***sadāhārābhāva-glapita-kuca-kokā yadupate \|***  
***viśuṣyantī rādhā tava viraha-tāpād anudinaṁ***  
***nidāghe kulyeva kraśima-paripākaṁ prathayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Thinness: O lord of the Yadus! Her lotus face rising in the river is now without color and her heart is contaminated with mud. Because of not eating, the** ***cakravāka*** **birds of her breasts have withered. Because of the fire of separation, Rādhā, day by day drying up, has reached the perfection of thinness, like a small river in the summer heat.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa two verses when he asks him for news of Rādhā and Viśākhā. Her face has lost its color (*vikṛtiḥ*). Her heart is full of mud (*antaḥ-kaluṣitā)* or is suffering from lamentation and wretchedness. The *cakravāka* birds have withered because of no food like water lilies to eat. Or her breasts without a necklace (*sadā hāra abhāvāt*) are withered. *Kulyāḥ* is a small river.

*Visara* means all.

Rādhā in separation speaks to Lalitā. *Puṭa-pāka* is heating gold and other substances in clay pots. The pain is greater than that. *Dambholeḥ* means “than a thunderbolt.” *Viśūcikāni* is a type of disease.

Uddhava speaks to Kṛṣṇa. Two types of madness are illustrated: intense and most intense (illustrated in the next verse.

***yathā vā—***

***atha mohaḥ—***

***idānīṁ kaṁsāre kuvalaya-dṛśaḥ kevalam idaṁ***

**Перевод:**

**Fainting: O enemy of Kaṁsa! The friend called “fainting in separation from you” is now assisting lotus-eyed Rādhā. That friend has stopped the ocean of her wretchedness, removed the disgrace of elders’ thoughts, stolen away her madness, and blocked the waves of her tears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā writes a letter to Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā. *Nirundhe* means suppress. The friend fainting is now assisting lotus-eyed Rādhā. In this condition you do not have to worry about her. Stay there happily. But today or tomorrow you will be responsible for killing a great ocean of women.

### Text 178

***atha mṛtyuḥ, yathā haṁsadūte (96)—***  
***aye rāsakrīḍārasika mama sakhyāṁ navanavā***  
***purā baddhā yena praṇaya-laharī hanta gahanā \|***  
***sa cen muktāpekṣas tvam api dhig imāṁ tula-śakalaṁ***  
***yad etasyā nāsā-nihitam idam adyāpi calati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Death, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **O enjoyer of the** ***rāsa*** **dance! Previously you bound up my friend with profuse, deep waves of newer and newer pastimes of love. If you neglect her now, she will meet misfortune, for a cotton swab placed to her nose moves only a little today.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lalitā scolds Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā through the swan messenger. You alone know the *rasa* of the *rāsa* dance because you have made Rādhā the recipient of suffering. This is *vyāja-stuti*, praise meant as condemnation. Since the main cause of the *rāsa* dance is Rādhā, an ornament of cause is also hinted. If you do not give regard to her, she will meet misfortune since she depends on you. “What are the signs of her regard for me?” A cotton swap applied to her nose to find out whether she is dead or alive moves today. Today she maintains life with great difficulty.

**In** ***pravāsa-vipralambha*** **the conditions described also apply to Kṛṣṇa. One example is given to represent this.**

***proktānāṁ prema-bhedānāṁ vividhatvād daśā api \|***

**Перевод:**

**Because of varieties of** ***prema*** **which were described in the last chapter, the conditions of** ***vipralambha*** **will also be of great variety. For fear of the great volume of the work, they have not been described here.**

The varieties of *prema* are *prauḍha, madhya* and *manda, madhu-sneha* and *ghṛta-sneha*, and *nīlima, raktimā* and *mañjiṣṭa rāga.* These types have not been described in relation to *vipralambha* because of fear of the great volume of the work.

**Перевод:**

**The states of** ***vipralambha*** **described are ordinary for the different types of** ***prema*****. The extraordinary states have not been described for fear of great volume of the work.**

### Text 183

*kintv atraivādhirūḍhasya mohanatvam apeyuṣaḥ \|*

**However, the extraordinary forms of** ***adhirūḍha*** **attaining** ***mohana*** **(in separation) were previously described in relation to** ***vipralambha.***

*Mohana* in the previous chapter on *bhāva* should be considered in this regard for its *rasa.*

These were described because they are not seen in anyone except in Rādhā.

***vipralambhaṁ paraṁ kecit karuṇābhidham ucire \|***

*Vipralambham* here means a different *vipralambha.* Because it is filled with unsteadiness and worry they say it is called *karuṇā.* Because it does not have substantial unsteadiness, it is a simply a variety of *pravāsa.* Therefore it is not described separately.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There is another type of *vipralambha* different (*param)* from those described. For instance, when Kṛṣṇa enters Kāliya Lake, there is *vipralambha*. But it is only a type of *pravāsa.*

***atha saṁyoga-viyoga-sthitiḥ***  
***harer līlā-viśeṣasya prakaṭasyānusārataḥ \|***  
***varṇitā virahāvasthā goṣṭha-vāma-bhruvām asau \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The condition of union and separation: The condition of separation of the Vraja women from Kṛṣṇa has been described according to the** ***prakaṭa*** **pastimes of Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 186

***vṛndāraṇye viharatā sadā rāsādi-vibhramaiḥ \|***  
***hariṇā vraja-devīnāṁ viraho’sti na karhicit \|\|186\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**There is no separation at all of the Vraja women from Kṛṣṇa, who eternally enjoys in the forests of Vṛndāvana with pastimes like the** ***rāsa*** **dance.**

### Text 187

***tathā ca pādme pātāla-khaṇḍe mathurā-māhātmye—***  
***go-gopa-gopikā-saṅge yatra krīḍati kaṁsahā \|\|187\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From the** ***Padma Purāṇa, Pātāla-khaṇḍa, Mathurā-māhātmya:*** **There Kṛṣṇa plays in the association of the cows, cowherds and** ***gopīs.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having described the separation of Kṛṣṇa and his associates, the author now speaks in order to dispel the unhappiness of that situation. Separation is the special feature of the pastimes on earth. Verses 186 describe the special nature of the *aprakaṭa* pastimes, where the pastimes of enjoyment are continuous. The word *vṛndāraṇye* refers to the *aprakaṭa* place.

The scriptural proof is given in verse 187. Kṛṣṇa plays with the cows, cowherds and *gopīs*. The present tense is used to the continuous nature of this act. As with the previous verse a distinction from the *prakaṭa* pastimes on earth is established. Without that distinction, the events could not take place eternally. Since the meaning of scripture cannot be denied, in these pastimes the *acintya-śakti* enables these two types to take place. *Śrutes tu śabda-mūlatvāt:* knowledge of God comes from the scripture. (*Vedānta-sūtra* 2.1.27)

Some may say that this statement is simply a glorification of the Yamunā, since the previous line is *aho abhāgyam lokasya na pītaṁ yamunā-jalam*: unfortunate people do not drink the water of the Yamunā. But this verse is part of a glorification of Mathurā. Thus the verse does not mean “Kṛṣṇa always plays in the water of Yamunā” since the sensible meaning is “Kṛṣṇa eternally plays on the bank of the Yamunā.”

Another objection to accepting the eternal nature stated in the verse is as follows. “If this eternal quality is accepted, then it can mean that Kṛṣṇa appears in every *kalpa* of Brahmā and performs pastimes. These pastimes should be understood to take place at the appropriate time repetitively. Therefore the present tense is used just as one says ‘The rays of the sun enter through the lattices of my house.’ And one may take the word *sadā* to mean always instead of eternal as in ‘This always (*sadā)* happens in my house.’”

The meaning of the statement of scripture just mentioned could be taken in such a limited way, if one were to take the meanings of “supreme” and “eternal” in the same way and if Bhagavān did not exist. One could accept the limited meaning if statements such as the following did not exist:

*rājadhānī tataḥ sābhūt sarva-yādava-bhūbhujām*  
*mathurā bhagavān yatra nityaṁ sannihito hariḥ*

**Since that time, the city of Mathurā had been the capital of all the kings of the Yadu dynasty. The city and district of Mathurā are very intimately connected with Kṛṣṇa, for Lord Kṛṣṇa lives near there eternally. SB 10.1.28**

The verb *sannihitaḥ* is intransitive, belonging to the *saṅkīrṇa* group. Svāmī-kṣīra says *samnidhā* means “being near.” Since the verb is intransitive, it is used with a subject to indicate present existence. Existence is understood to be continuous, not repeatedly appearing, as an *avatāra*. Though it is said he goes to other places such as Mathurā, that meaning can not be applied to this statement. Even the past participle will indicate the same continuous action as in the statement “This state is protected *(rakṣitam*) by a king versed in the four *varṇas.”* No break is indicated. If this is so, how much more emphatic is the statement by using the word *nityam* (eternal) along with the present tense. It is seen in the scriptures that the past participle (such as *sannihitaḥ* from *sannidhā*) is used without the word *nityam* to indicate a continuous states. *Ayam ātmāpahata-pāpmā*: the soul is free of sin. (Here the past participle *ahapata* is used with a continuous sense.)

But *sannidhā* means nearness. Thus there is glorification of a particular place nearby. Thus this statement is not meant to glorify Mathurā. As well a place distant from Mathurā is not famous for such qualities. Thus other meanings are rejected. One may say that the word *yasyāḥ* should be used instead of *yatra* if the indication is a place near to Mathurā. However use of the locative (*yatra*) indicates a relationship, a place near to the residents of Mathurā. Or, accepting the fact that Kṛṣṇa exists in two forms, one could say that this sentence simply means Kṛṣṇa resides nearby in the *prakaṭa* Mathurā as well as in the *aprakaṭa* Mathurā.

“How can these statements about Mathurā actually indicate Vṛndāvana?” Since the statement is part of the glorification of Mathurā in which Vṛndāvana is a part of Mathurā area, and since there is mention of cows and cowherd women, it is reasonable. Thus the statement in the glorification of Mathurā concerns the eternal pastimes of an *aprakaṭa* Vṛndāvana.

Similarly the *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* describes the forests of Mathurā:

*bhū-gola-cakre sapta-pūryo bhavanti tāsāṁ madhye sākṣād brahma gopāla-purī. yathā sarasi padmam tiṣṭhati tathā bhūmyāṁ cakrena rakṣitā hi mathurā tasmād gopālapurī hi bhavati brhad vṛndāvanaṁ madhor madhuvanam. etaih evāvṛtā purī bhavati tatra teṣu eva gahaneṣv evam*

**There are seven cities on the earth. Among them the city of Kṛṣṇa is directly Brahman. Just as a lotus resides in a pond, Mathurā protected by the circle of the earth, and near that place, city of Gopāla exists. Vṛndāvana is large. Madhuvana is sweet. The city exists surrounded by these forests.**

The difference from the *prakaṭa* manifestation is described in the *Varāha Purānā* in order to show suitability for living there.

*tatrāpi mahad āścaryaṁ paśyanti paṇḍitāḥ narāḥ*  
*kāliya-hrada pūrveṇa kadambo mahito durmaḥ*  
*śata-śākhaṁ viśālākṣi puṇyaṁ surabhi gandhi ca*  
*sa ca dvādaśa-māsātimanojña śubha-śītalaḥ*  
*puṣpāyati viśālākṣi prabhāsante diśo disaḥ*

**O large-eyed woman! The wise see something very astonishing there. In front of the lake of Kāliya, there is a huge, pure** ***kadamba*** **tree with hundreds of branches and sweet fragrance. All year, attractive and cool, it continues to flower. All the directions are illuminated by this tree.**

In this and other quotations poetic license is used in the verses. In the *Varāha Purāṇa* also this is found in the description of Brahma-kuṇḍa:

*tatrāścaryam pravakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu tvaṁ vasundhare*  
*labhante manujāḥ siddhiṁ mama karma parāyaṇāḥ*  
*tasya tatrottare pārśve ‘śoka-vṛkṣaḥ śita-prabhaḥ*  
*vaiśākhasya tu māsasya śukla-pakṣasya dvādaśī*  
*sapuṣpati ca madhyāhne mama bhakta-sukhāvahaḥ*  
*na kaścid api jānāti vinā bhāgavataṁ śucim*

**O earth! Listen as I explain something astonishing there. Being absorbed in service to me, men attain that place. Near, to the north of that place, there is an** ***aśoka*** **tree emanating coolness. On the twelfth day of the waxing phase of Vaiśākha month, the tree blooms at noon, giving bliss to my devotees. Except for my pure devotee, no one knows this.**

*Śucim* in the above verse means “having exclusive devotion.” This means that this place is not known on earth. That Kṛṣṇa’s associates are eternally situated there is stated in the *Bṛhad-gautamīya-tantra* in the questions and answers between Nārada and Kṛṣṇa.

*kim idaṁ dvādaśābhikhyaṁ vṛndāranaṁ viśāmpate*  
*śrotum icchāmi bhagavan yadi yogyo ‘smi me vada*  
*idaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ ramyaṁ mama dhāmaiva kevalaṁ*  
*tatra ye paśavaḥ pakṣi mṛgāḥ kīṭā narāmaraḥ*  
*ye vasanti mamādhiṣṇye mṛtā yanti mamālayam*  
*tatra yā gopakanyāś ca nivasanti mamālaye*  
*yoginyastā mayā nityaṁ mama sevā parāyaṇāḥ*  
*pañca yojanam evāsti vanaṁ me deha-rūpakam*  
*kālindīyaṁ suṣumnākhyā paramāmṛta vāhinī*  
*atra devāś ca bhūtāni vartante sūkṣma-rūpataḥ*  
*sarva-devamayaś cāhaṁ na tyajāmi vanam kvacit*  
*āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me ’tra yuge yuge*  
*tejomayam idam ramyam adṛśyaṁ carma-cakṣuṣā*

**O master of the people I desire to hear about the twelve forests of Vṛndāvana. If I am qualified please tell me. Kṛṣṇa then spoke. This pleasant Vṛndāvana is my only abode. There, all cows, animals, birds, insects and humans are without death. Those who live under my mercy come to my abode on dying. The daughters of the cowherd men live in my abode. Completely giving up all connections, they serve me continually. This place, measuring five** ***yojanas,*** **is non-different from my body. The Yamunā, flowing with the sweetest nectar, is the** ***suṣumnā*** **(central nerve) of that body. All the** ***devas*** **and the elements exist there in a spiritual form. I, the embodiment of all** ***devas,*** **do not leave that forest for a moment, though I appear and disappear in this world age after age. But this radiant forest full of pleasure is invisible to the material eye.**

In *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad*, Brahmā says *govindam sac-cid-ānandaṁvṛndāvana-sura-bhūruha-tlāsīnam satatam sa-marud-gan ‘ham tosaāmī*: along with the Maruts I continually satisfy Govinda full of eternity, knowledge and bliss, sitting at the base of a desire tree in Vṛndāvana. In various mantras in the Yamalas, Pañcarātra and Saṁhitās, the Lord and his associates are described as objects of meditation (for attaining an eternal goal). Therefore the statement has been made in the present verse “Kṛṣṇa plays in Vṛndāvana eternally performing the *rāsa* dance and other pastimes.”In their respective places, there are different forms seen in the *prakaṭa* pastimes. For instance there is the manifestation of the four-armed form shown temporarily to Brahmā and the form seen continuously by the cows, birds and deer. Or, in Dvārakā there is a manifestation of thousands of palaces measuring two *krośas* each, though the whole place measures only twelve *yojanas*. By the power of *yogamāyā* seen by Nārada, Kṛṣṇa simultaneously showed his pastimes of morning, noon and evening in various forms. What Nārada saw is famous.

*citraṁ bataitad ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak*  
*gṛheṣu dvy-aṣṭa-sāhasraṁ striya eka udāvahat*

**It is quite amazing that in a single body Lord Kṛṣṇa simultaneously married sixteen thousand women, each in a separate palace. SB 10.69.2**

It is explained in the marriage with sixteen thousand maidens there was a manifestation of various forms of his associates. It is said by the commentator that simultaneously at each house Devakī and his other relations also were present. In this case the consciousness of each associate is separate in each form (unaware of simultaneously being present in many places.) By the power of *yogamāyā,* this took place in one palace:

*dīvyantam akṣais tatrāpi priyayā coddhavena ca*  
*pūjitaḥ parayā bhaktyā pratyutthānāsanādibhiḥ*

**There he saw the Lord playing at dice with his beloved consort and His friend Uddhava. Lord Kṛṣṇa worshiped Nārada by standing up, offering him a seat. SB 10.69.20**

Simultaneously in other places this occurred:

*mantrayantaṁ ca kasmiṁścin mantribhiś coddhavādibhiḥ*  
*jala-krīḍā-rataṁ kvāpi vāramukhyābalāvṛtam*

**Somewhere Kṛṣṇa was consulting with royal ministers like Uddhava, and somewhere else he was enjoying in the water, surrounded by many society girls and other young women. SB 10.69.27**

Thus according to the different *bhāva,* there is a separate identity in these forms in which the Lord thinks “He is in that situation and I am here.” In the marriage with sixteen thousand maidens, Devakī and others derived happiness from seeing Kṛṣṇa while they performed the auspicious rites in his presence in each palace. If he were absent, then they would long to see him. By the power of *yogamāyā* Uddhava sometimes saw union and sometimes separation of Kṛṣṇa. That is the amazing feature of the pastimes. Thus, in the manifestation of these different forms, the difference is not actual difference. Thus also there is no separation at all from Kṛṣṇa because of the union with Kṛṣṇa taking place in another form, for instance in the verse of the text describing Kṛṣṇa playing eternally in Vṛndāvana. This is explained in the commentary of *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī* on SB 10.47.29 with the words *bhavatīnāṁ viyogo me na hi sarvātmanā kvacit:* you are never actually separated from me, for I am the soul of all creation.

One should simply perform worship to that particular form which brings happiness. Thus all contradictions are resolved.

“However, in those forms where separation in *pūrva-rāga* and other varieties arises, union should also be described later for that form. What is the use if eternal *sambhoga* (union) takes place in another form for those persons in separation in the *prakaṭa* pastimes? Without final union, those descriptions will be disagreeable, especially if they miss the happiness found in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes. Thus there should be no separation. Why are these descriptions given? Why has Kṛṣṇa himself said the following?

*dhārayanty ati-kṛcchreṇa prāyaḥ prāṇān kathañcana*  
*pratyāgamana-sandeśair ballavyo me mad-ātmikāḥ*

**Simply because I have promised to return to them, my fully devoted cowherd girlfriends struggle to maintain their lives somehow or other. SB 10.46.6**

Therefore after great separation finally there must be a description of meeting. This should be without any interference. If there is happiness in a particular expansion, that happiness should not disappear, like the elephant bathing and again becoming dirty. Unresolved separation is not the method of *prema,* but rather would be a sign that Kṛṣṇa is interested in his own happiness, since he disregards his dear devotees.”

What to speak of Kṛṣṇa’s dear devotees, even material *rasa* texts say *na vinā vipralambhena:* joy does not exist without separation. (*Sarasvatī-kanthābharaṇa* 5.52) There is agreement that separation exists for the perfection of union. Following from this, union without obstacles should be the final result of many separations. *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* and other works like *Nāṭaka-candrikā,* and types of worship as well, taking shelter of the *prakaṭa* manifestations, show this understanding. The agreement of Śukadeva and others in this also is clear. Brahmā said:

*prapañcaṁ niṣprapañco ’pi viḍambayasi bhū-tale*  
*prapanna-janatānanda-sandohaṁ prathituṁ prabho*

**My dear master, although you have nothing to do with material existence, you come to this earth and imitate material life just to expand the varieties of ecstatic enjoyment for your surrendered devotees. SB 10.14.37**

This is the intention of the verse: the “imitation of the material world” consists of the birth pastime and others as well, and though there are eternal pastimes, the birth pastime is a cause of great bliss for the surrendered souls. If the author were not insistent on the eternal pastimes, but only on the *prakaṭa* pastimes, what would be the value of the description of the *prakaṭa* pastimes since they are composed of the suffering of separation? With that worry in mind, after showing the suffering produced by transformations of *prakaṭa* pastimes and not showing the *prakaṭa* pastimes maturing into the happiness of the eternal pastimes, the author now speaks of the types of union and enjoyment which lead to *samṛddhimān* as the final result, the fulfillment of all *rasas.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“*Vipralambha* consists of four types of separation: in *pūrva-rāga*, in *māna*, in *prema-vaicittyam* and in close and distant *pravāsa.* These are experienced as happiness by the *sādhakas,* the *siddhas*, the eternal associates in his pastimes, the dear women, and Kṛṣṇa. Because the heroines as *āśraya* and *viṣaya* stay in Vraja, the distant separation caused by Kṛṣṇa leaving and going to Mathurā is intolerable.” Thus the author begins to speak.

This condition of separation has been described according to the *prakaṭa* pastimes *(prakaṭasyānusārataḥ*). This means that both *prakaṭa* and *aprakaṭa* pastimes exist but in the material world the *prakaṭa* pastimes are visible and the *aprakaṭa* pastimes are invisible. This has been explained in the commentary on *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 1.21

The details are now discussed, taking into account *Laghu-bhāgavatāmrṭa.* Because there are unlimited forms of one Vraja just like there are unlimited forms of the Lord, the pastimes such as birth in one manifestation are seen by people of this world, and these pastimes are not seen in the other countless manifestations by those particular people. But the pastimes of birth, infancy, childhood and youth, going to Mathurā, performed by Kṛṣṇa who is in a particular manifested form seen by the people, are also seen in unlimited other universes at various times in sequence and also become invisible at certain times there. In a similar manner, the rising, morning, noon and afternoon of the sun in the zodiac are seen in one place, but is not seen simultaneously at another place in the same way. But the sun rising in the zodiac is not real and not eternal, whereas the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in Vraja are real and eternal. This has been shown by previous scripture evidence, and more will be supplied.

Just as the sun always produces morning and then noon by being located in different places, Kṛṣṇa, by being located in different universes, continually shows birth, infancy, killing Baka, youth, and going to Mathurā. Thus all the *prakaṭa* pastimes are eternal. Just as the suns movement over twenty-four hours (*sixty ghaṭikās*) is perceived sequentially in all countries, so Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes from birth are perceived in all universes till the end of Brahmā’s life. At the time of final devastation when the material universes are all destroyed, the *prakaṭa* pastimes continue in universes made by *yogamāyā.*

The *prakaṭa* pastimes, visible in the material world, appear according to time and place. This is understood from Uddhava’s statement:

*kṛṣṇa-dyumaṇi nimloce gīrṇeṣv ajagareṇa ha*  
*kiṁ nu naḥ kuśalaṁ brūyāṁ gata-śrīṣu gṛheṣv aham*

**My dear Vidura, the sun of the world, Lord Kṛṣṇa, has set, and our house has now been swallowed by the great snake of time. What can I say to you about our welfare? SB 3.2.7**

The *prakaṭa* pastimes of Mathurā and Dvārakā, and the birth pastimes in Vraja in other manifestations in other universes are not seen at all by the people of the material world. The unlimited manifestations are kept separate. This is understood from *the Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta:*

*kṛṣṇa-bālyādi-līlābhir bhūṣitāni samantataḥ \|*  
*śaila-goṣṭha-vanādīnāṁ santi rūpāṇy anekaśaḥ \|\|513\|\|*

**All around there are innumerable forms for the mountains, cow pens and forests in which Kṛṣṇa performs his** ***kaumāra, paugaṇḍa*** **and** ***kaiśora*** **pastimes.** ***Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta*** **1.5.513**

Because of the unlimited manifestations of Kṛṣṇa, his pastimes and associates, each with their separate identities which do not overlap, separate pastimes of birth, infancy, boyhood and youth take place one after the other in different universes or simultaneously, but in any case they are fixed. But the departure to Mathurā does not exist in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes of eternal Mathurā, since Kṛṣṇa and his associates must be eternally present for their pastimes there.

It is said:

*tatra prakaṭa-līlāyām eva syātāṁ gamāgamau \|*  
*gokule mathurāyāṁ ca dvāravatyāṁ ca śārṅgiṇaḥ \|\|*

**In the revealed pastimes, Kṛṣṇa will come and depart from Gokula, Mathurā and Dvārakā.** ***Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta*** **1.5.439**

Going (*gama)* in this verse means going from the *prakaṭa* Vraja to *prakaṭa* Mathurā. Coming (*āgama*) means coming back to Vraja after killing Dantavakra. This takes place in the *prakaṭa* pastimes and not in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes. Going from the village to the forest and from the forest and coming from the large forest to Vṛndāvana takes place in both the *prakaṭa* and *aprakaṭa* pastimes since both the village and forest are within Vraja. It has been shown that all the *prakaṭa* pastimes of both places are eternal by the reasoning mentioned above.

“Then it must be concluded that in the *aprakaṭa* manifestation, some portions of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes do not exist, since the birth pastime depends on previously not being born. And if there is no going from Vraja to Mathurā in the *aprakaṭa* manifestation, how can Mathurā pastimes starting with killing the washer man and ending with the coming of Kālayavana take place in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes? Killing the washer man could only take place after Kṛṣṇa leaves Vraja.”

That Kṛṣṇa has been born from the womb of Yaśodā is eternally understood by all the associates in his pastimes situated in the *aprakaṭa* manifestation, but they do not inquire about past time. It is not possible to inquire about time in the past or what existed then. This happens by the great influence of inconceivable *yogamāyā.* Similarly, even those knowledgeable of scriptures cannot detect the initial relationship with *karma,* the cause. They do not find answers for the question “For the *jīvas* wandering in various bodies, appearing repeatedly in every *kalpa* in the world of material pastimes, what was the point in time that they contacted ignorance, and what form did the *jīvas* have at that time?” The cause for this is the inconceivable power of *māyā.*

Nevertheless those knowledgeable of scripture speak of the *jīva’s* beginningless relationship with ignorance. Similarly those knowledgeable of *bhakti* speak of the beginningless of Kṛṣṇa’s birth pastime. Just as one hears that the spiritual waters of the Virajā River called the Causal Ocean, the moat around Vaikuṇṭha, arose from the Vedas in the *Padma Purāṇa*, so one hears of the birth of Kṛṣṇa. *Vedāṅga-sveda-janita-toyaiḥ prasrāvitā*: the causal ocean flowed by the water generated from the perspiration of the limbs of the Vedas. (*Padma Purāṇa* 6.255-257)

The associates in pastimes in the *aprakaṭa* Mathurā are aware that Kṛṣṇa came from Vraja and killed the washer man or is killing the washer man, but they are not aware that previously to the killing Kṛṣṇa was not there. Similarly Gaṅgā is famous for been brought to the earth by Bhagīratha. However Gaṅgā always existed on earth before Bhagīratha. This is understood from the activities of Pṛthu. *Gaṅgā-yamunayor nadyor anatrā kṣetram āvasan*: King Pṛthu lived in the tract of land between the two great rivers Ganges and Yamunā. (SB 4.21.11) Similarly, before the sons of Sagara and before the reign of Priyavrata, the ocean existed, since the sons of Prācīnabhrih, the Pracetās performed austerities there.

Thus the attitude is “It is not possible for us to understand even our own condition previous to Kṛṣṇa’s coming to Mathurā.” It is alike the awareness of the maid servants of Devahūtī. “We cannot understand who and what form we had and where we were previous to *vayaḥsandhi.* We are like the servants of Devahūtī, all with new youth, who rose from the water by the powers of Kardama Muni.” The associates in the *aprakaṭa* Mathurā pastimes know that Kṛṣṇa is in Mathurā and not in Vraja, and similarly the associates in Vraja think that Kṛṣṇa is playing in Vraja and Kaṁsa is in Mathurā. The inhabitants of Dvārakā also think in this way. Kṛṣṇa simultaneously exists eternally in Vraja, Mathurā and Dvārakā with his associates in unlimited forms, with separate consciousness in each place, though he has only one body. This is the conclusion.

Thus, in the *prakaṭa* pastimes there is separation when Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathurā, whereas in the *aprakaṭa* pastimes the arrival of Akrūra in Vraja, Kṛṣṇa going to Mathurā and the lamentation of the Vraja *gopīs* does not exist. That is expressed in verse 186. Separation accompanies the many a*prakaṭa* manifestations as previously discussed (*prakaṭasyānusārataḥ*).

The scriptural proof follows. The present tense is used *(krīḍati*) to show the eternal nature of the action. One should not say that this statement is made only in relation to the glorification of the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa used to play in the water of the Yamunā.

*aho ābhāgasysya lokasya no pītaṁ yamunā-jalam*  
*go-gopa-gopikā-saṅge yatra krīḍati kaṁsahā*

*Yatra* should mean “of the Yamunā” rather than “in the Yamunā” since it is unreasonable to say he always plays in the water of the Yamunā.
