Similarly, one should not take “village on the Gaṅgā” to mean “a village floating on the Gaṅgā.” Rather the mean is “Kṛṣṇa always plays on the bank of the Gaṅga with the cows, cowherd, and *gopīs.”*

“But the present tense is used with the *nitya* (always) in sentences like ‘the rays of the sun always enter the windows of the house,’ or ‘he always eats in the house’ or ‘one should always perform the *sandhyā* rites.’ But this only refers to a particular time. Similarly the statement that Kṛṣṇa always plays means that at the time of his appearance as *avatāra* Kṛṣṇa plays.”

That is not so, since one cannot equate *jīvas* bound by karma in the material world with the Lord, his abode, his pastimes and his associates.  *Jīvas* with pious acts on the earth and other planets appear again and again and enjoy in every *kalpa* of Brahmā.

“Please explain the difference between material and non-material objects. Since it is impossible that there be eternality in the momentary existence of the pastimes of the Lord, there is great similarity between material and non-material objects.”

It was already stated, according to *Bhagavat-sandarbha* that nothing is impossible for the Lord and his unlimited associates and pastimes such as birth revealed with eternity, knowledge and bliss. And there is no situation where there is the experience of separation with Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā but at the same experiencing performing pastimes in Vraja, since the *prakaṭa* pastimes take place continually in different universes, as previously explained.

“Then to avoid separation from Kṛṣṇa completely, there must be other pastimes, *aprakaṭa* pastimes.” That is explained in the verse. Kṛṣṇa plays eternally in Vṛndāvana (*yatra*) in association with the cows, cowherds and *gopīs,* not in separation from them. This excludes the *prakaṭa* pastimes. The word *yatra* (in Vṛndāvana) should play a double function, in relation to Kṛṣṇa playing and to associating with the cowherds and *gopīs.* “Kṛṣṇa plays eternally in Vṛndāvana, in association with the cows, cowherds and *gopīs* in Vṛndāvana.” In this manner slight absence and separation within Vraja is not excluded. Thus Kṛṣṇa has association of the cows, cowherds and *gopīs* though he goes from the village to the forest or from the forest to the village, producing slight separation within Vṛndāvana.

Some explain that the word “killer of Kaṁsa” indicates that after killing Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa later killed Dantavakra and again entered Vraja pastimes (*prakaṭa* form) and this verse is the proof. How this is not acceptable. The word *kaṁsahā* in that interpretation would mean “One who killed Kaṁsa.” However, that is not the meaning. The word *han* is used with a limited number of words to indicate the past tense as found in the rule *brahma-bhrūṇa-vṛtreṣu kvip* (Pāṇinī 3.2.87) The *Bhāsya-vṛrti* says the same thing. Thus *Kaṁsa-hā* means only “he who is killing Kaṁsa or will kill Kaṁsa.” Therefore in this verse it means that he has not gone to Mathurā. Thus it can mean that he will kill Kaṁsa in the near future or that he hates Kaṁsa. It is understood that in the *dāna* and other pastimes that he is aware of Kaṁsa in Mathurā. *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta* quotes the Yāmala:

*kṛṣṇo ’nyo yadu-sambhūto yaḥ pūrṇaḥ so ’sty ataḥ param \|*  
*vṛndāvanaṁ parityajya sa kvacit naiva gacchati \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa, who was also born in the Yadu dynasty (as Vāsudeva), being Svayam Bhagavān, and superior to that Vāsudeva form, never gives up Vṛndāvana to go elsewhere.** ***Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta*** **1.5.461**

Even though there are many scriptural proofs stating the eternal nature of the Vṛndāvana pastimes, the extraordinary nature of the *aprakaṭa* pastimes are presented by Jīva Gosvāmī, crest jewel of great realization. These statements are found in the *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.* First the *śruti* is given.

govindaṁ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaṁ6 sura-bhūr-ruham āsīnaṁ satataṁ samarudgaṇo’ṁ paritoṣayāmi tam ekaṁ govindaṁ sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham pañca-padaṁ vṛndāvana-sura-bhūruha-talāsīnaṁ satataṁ sa-marud-gaṇo’haṁ paramayā stutyā toṣayāmi ity ākare.2 \[go.tā.u. 1.33\] iti \| janma-jarābhyāṁ bhinnaḥ sthāṇur ayam acchedyo’yaṁ yo’sau saurye tiṣṭhati yo’sau goṣu tiṣṭhati yo’sau gāḥ pālayati \| yo’sau gopeṣu tiṣṭhati \[go.tā.u. 2.22\] iti gopāla-tāpanī \|

I along with the Maruts satisfy Govinda, the form of eternity, knowledge and bliss, who sits beneath a desire tree in Vṛndāvana. He is unchanging, free from birth and old age. He who stays in the Yamunā is indestructible. Death fears Govinda who stays with the cows, who protects the cows and who resides with the cowherd people. *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad*

In this verse it is stated that he is free from birth and old age. Birth like a material person is rejected along with old age. He is not born even from Yaśodā or Devakī. Kṛṣṇa himself says *janma karma ca me divya evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ:* he who knows my sacred birth and activities in truth does not take birth again. (BG 4.9) *Sthāṇuḥ* means existing at all times. *Saurye* indicates the water of the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa plays with the *gopīs. Goṣu* indicates he stays with the cows to herd them. He protects the cowherds by lifting Govardhana. He stays with the cowherds such as Śrīdāma and plays with his friends.

“How will he exist at the base of the desire tree in Vṛndāvana at the time of devastation?”

He is *acchendya.* This means he cannot be destroyed by the power of time like the material world.

bhū-gola-cakrea sapta-puryo bhavanti \| tāsāṁ madhye sākṣād brahma gopāla-purīti \| yathā hi vai sarasi padmaṁ tiṣṭhati tathā bhūmyāṁ tiṣṭhatīti cakreṇa rakṣitā hi mathurā tasmād gopāla-purī bhavati \| bṛhad bṛhad-vanaṁ madhor madhu-vanaṁ

On earth there are seven cities. Among them the city of Gopāla is Brahman itself. Just as a lotus resides in a pond, Mathurā protected by the circle of the earth, and then city of Goal exists. Vṛndāvana is large. Madhuvana is sweet. The city exists surrounded by these. *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* 2.26-28

*tato vṛndāvanaṁ puṇyaṁ vṛndā-devī-samāśritam \|*  
*hariṇādhiṣṭhitaṁ tac ca brahma-rudrādi-sevitam \|*  
*vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sadā krīḍati mādhavaḥ \|*  
*vṛndāvanāntara-gataḥ sa-rāmo bālakair vṛtaḥ \|\|*

**Vṛndāvana, the abode of the Lord, is pure, served by Vṛndā-devī, worshipped by Brahmā and Śiva. Kṛṣṇa plays with the calves and older calves within Vṛndāvana, surrounded by Balarāma and other boys.** ***Skanda Purāṇa***

*yamunā-jala-kallole sadā krīḍati mādhavaḥ*

**Kṛṣna eternally plays in the waves of the Yamunā.** ***Padma Purāṇa***

The eternal nature of Mathurā pastimes is shown:

*prāpya mathurāṁ purīṁ ramyāṁ sadā brahmādi-sevitam \|*  
*śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-śārṅga-rakṣitāṁ muṣalādibhiḥ \|\|*  
*yatrāsau saṁsthitaḥ kṛṣṇas tribhiḥ śaktyā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*rāmāniruddha-pradyumnai rukmiṇyā sahito vibhuḥ \|\|*

**He attained attractive Mathurā always worshipped by Brahmā and others and protected by the conch, cakra, club and bow. There Kṛṣṇa lives with his three** ***śaktis,*** **along with Balarāma, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Rukmiṇī.** ***Gopala-tāpanī Upaniṣad*** **2.35-36**

The *smṛti* says:

*rājadhānī tataḥ sābhūt sarva-yādava-bhūbhujām*  
*mathurā bhagavān yatra nityaṁ sannihito hariḥ*

**Since that time, the city of Mathurā had been the capital of all the kings of the Yadu dynasty. The city and district of Mathurā are very intimately connected with Kṛṣṇa, for Lord Kṛṣṇa lives there eternally. SB 10.1.28**

Dvārakā pastimes are also described.

*jayati jananivāso devakī-janma-vādo*  
*yadu-vara-pariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam \|*  
*sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ susmita-śrī-mukhena*  
*vraja-pura-vanitānāṁ vardhayan kāma-devam \|\|*

**Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa lives among the cowherd men and the Yādavas, and is conclusively both the son of Devakī and Yaśodā. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty and the cowherd men, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious, in Vraja, Mathurā and Dvārakā. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities, moving and inert, and the suffering of separation of the inhabitants of Vraja and Dvārakā. His blissful smiling face always increases the śṛṅgāra-rasa of the** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana and women of Mathurā and Dvārakā. He remains eternally in this situation. SB 10.90.48**

The word *jayati* is in the present to express the eternal. It does not have an imperative meaning, to give blessings. Śukadeva, the crest jewel of devotees, knowing the eternal excellence of everything related to the Lord, would never give blessings. By stating that Kṛṣṇa plays with the women of Vraja and the cities, and increase their *kāma-deva, samartha, samañjasa* and *sādhaṛaṇa rati* women are indicated. *Kāma-deva* indicates *śṛṅgāra-rasa* filled with *prema.* Their love increases by meeting and separation. He produces *sambhoga* with *saṅkṣipta, saṅkīrṇa, sampanna* and *samṛddhimān* varieties and *vipralambha* with *pūrva-rāga, māna*, and *pravāsa.* The verse indicates the eternal nature of the pastimes of meeting and separation in Vṛndāvana, Mathurā, Dvārakā and Indraprastha and the song of the bee in *divyonmāda* in lamentation produced when Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathurā.

*Susmita-śrī-mukhena* means that he increases their love by his smiling face which is seen (in meeting), heard about and remembered (in separation). He destroys obstacles for all creatures. He destroys the obstacle of Indra and others for immovable objects Govardhana and Raivataka. He destroyed *saṁsāra* of moving beings like the deer, horses, cows, humans filled with devotion suitable for pastimes by showing his form. This shows the eternal nature of pastimes of delivering many people by going to Mithila to see Śrutadeva, and pastimes like lifting Govardhana. He destroys *adharma* by Arjuna and Bhīma who are like his arms. This shows the eternal nature of killing demons like Keśi, Kaṁsa and Jarāsandha in the *prakaṭa* pastimes because of their *adharma*. He stays with the Yadus. This indicates the eternal nature of his infancy, childhood and youth pastimes with his associates Vasudeva, Nanda, Vṛṣabhānu, Uddhava, Śrīdāmā, Subala and others. Devakī indicates the wife of Vasudeva and the wife of Nanda.

He is fixed (*janma-vāda*) as the child of Devakī and Yaśodā. The Purāṇa says *dve nāmnī nanda-bhāryāyā yaśodā devakī:* Devakī is the name of Yaśodā as well as Vasudeva’s wife. *Vādaḥ pravadatām aham*: among types of debate, I am *vāda*, which attempts to discern actual truth with the goal of coming to a conclusion. (BG 10.32) Thus the word *vāda* means a fixed conclusion. This indicates the eternal nature of his birth pastime. The eternal nature of unlimited other pastimes which are not mentioned are also indicated, since the meaning of scriptures includes items which are not contrary, though not specifically stated. Thus the eternal nature of all the pastimes which are proved in many *śruti* and *smṛti* statements is seen in this jewel of a verse from *Bhāgavatam.*

Now the proofs for the eternal nature of the *prakaṭa* pastimes are given. For this, one must rely on the meaning obtained from the practitioners of mantras like Bāla-gopala-mantra found in the *Gautamīya-tantra* and other works. At the stage of *sādhana* the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa waking up, washing his mouth, eating butter, crawling, playing, laughing and sleeping eternally exist for one who meditates at different times of the day upon the Lord in a particular form. In the *siddha* stage the pastimes also eternally exist for the person who directly experiences those pastimes in particular manifested forms. It is said *yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhir bhavati tādṛśī*: one achieves a perfection of the type practiced during meditation.

For those who have a *bhāva* like *vātsalya* in the visible pastimes on earth, that strong taste is not contradicted by the secondary nature of other pastimes within the manifestation since Kṛṣṇa gives that strong taste desired by the devotee.

Since temporal states in the visible pastimes on earth are ephemeral, states like crawling are not permanent in the manifestation. The Lord’s pastimes are similar to those of this world. But in the *prakaṭa* pastimes taken all together in the countless manifestations, without mixing with each other, actions like crawling are permanent (since they continue in one universe after another). This is according to *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta.*

Some of these pastimes are permanent, by being spread over day and night repetitively, and others are permanent as seasonal events occurring repetitively. The pastimes with the associates like Yaśodā, who cares for baby Kṛṣṇa, start in the morning by waking him up and finish each the day and night, and then come again the next day. Even though millions of lifetimes of Brahmā pass, there is no reason for the going and coming of these pastimes to change. Thus the infant age of Kṛṣṇa is fixed and his associates in those pastimes and his friends in that period are fixed. The seasons such as spring, with pastimes of throwing colors, *dāna* and swinging during day and night also go and come again repeatedly. The beginning and end of Kṛṣṇa’s *kaiśora* period are also fixed. In all these universes taken together, Kṛṣṇa may be two years, three years, five years or eight years. This is arranged by *yogamāyā.*

The proofs of the eternal nature of Vṛndāvana with visible pastimes (*prakaṭa* pastimes) will be given. In the *Rudra-yāmala* in the discussion between Rudra and Gaurī it is said:

*vīthyāṁ vīthyāṁ nivāso’dhara-madhu-suvacas tatra santānakānāṁ*  
*eke rākendu-koṭyā upaviśada-karās teṣu caike kamante \|*  
*rāme rātrer virāme samudita-tapana-dyoti-sindhūpameyo*  
*ratnāṅgānāṁ suvarṇācita-mukura-rucas tebhya eke drumendrāḥ \|\|*  
*yat kusumaṁ yad mṛgyaṁ yat phalaṁ ca varānane \|*  
*tat tad eva prasūyante vṛndāvana-suradrumāḥ \|\|*

**O Gaurī, whose words are like honey on the lips! In Vṛndāvana, among the divine coral trees are the kings of trees, more brilliant than a million full moons. They are comparable to an ocean of rising suns at the end night, surpassing all other trees, splendid with buds of gold, shine brilliantly. O Rāmā with a beautiful face! Its flowers and fruits are desirable. Thus the desire trees of Vṛndāvana arise.**

*aho vṛndāvanaṁ tatra keli-vṛnāvanām ca*  
*vṛkṣāḥ; kalpa-drumāc caiva cintāmani-mayī sthali*  
*krīḍā-vihaṅga-lakṣaś sa surabhīnāṁ anaekaśaḥ*  
*nana-citra vicitra-śṛī-rāsa-maṇḍala-bhūmayaḥ*  
*keli-kuñja-nikuñjāni nana-sakukya-sthalaṇi ca*  
*prācīra-cchatra-ratnāni kalāḥ śeṣasya bhānty aho*  
*yac-chiro-ratna-vṛndānāma-tulya-dyuti-vaibhavam*  
*brahmaiva rājate tatra rūpah ko vaktum arthati*

**Oh Vṛndāvana! In that place are forests for pastimes. There are desire trees and land made of touchstone. There are thousands of playing birds and unlimited desire cows. There are many colorful** ***rāsa*** **areas for dancing, bowers and groves for pastimes, and spots for making friendship. Walls and roofs are made of jewels. The hoods of Śeṣa, whose host of head jewels have unequalled luster, shine there. The lord resides there. Who can describe its beauty?**

Thus the eternal nature of the pastimes of to be experienced in the material world and the spiritual world have been established with their details.

“If Kṛṣṇa performs pastimes with his associates eternally in different manifestations in Vṛndāvana, Mathurā and Dvārakā in one body simultaneously as illustrated in the verse *citraṁ bataid ekena vapuṣā* (SB 10.69.1) in both *prakaṭa* and *aprakaṭa* pastimes, then how can there be separation from Kṛṣṇa with *udghūrṇa* and *citrajalpa* at all?”

In order to accomplish various pastimes and in order to accomplish the various *bhāvas* of the *sādhaka* and *siddha* devotees, by the power of the Lord’s *līlā-śakti,* separate identities of the Lord and his associates in each manifestation of pastimes and in each form, and different activities following from those identities, are established. An example of different forms is Rāma meeting with Paraśurāma after breaking the bow. The Lord appeared in two forms Rāma and Paraśurāma who met each other, with different identities.3 An example of different manifestation of pastimes is what Nārada saw in Dvārakā, by the power of *yogamāyā.*

*īvyantam akṣais tatrāpi priyayā coddhavena ca*  
*pūjitaḥ parayā bhaktyā pratyutthānāsanādibhiḥ*

**There he saw the Lord playing at dice with his beloved consort and his friend Uddhava. Lord Kṛṣṇa worshiped Nārada by standing up, offering him a seat, and so on. SB 10.69.20**

*mantrayantaṁ ca kasmiṁścin mantribhiś coddhavādibhiḥ*  
*jala-krīḍā-rataṁ kvāpi vāramukhyābalāvṛtam*

**Somewhere he was consulting with royal ministers like Uddhava, and somewhere else he was enjoying in the water, surrounded by many society girls and other young women. SB 10.69.27**

In these instances, according to the different *bhāva,* Kṛṣṇa has a different identity. “He is there and I am here.” At the marriage with sixteen thousand maidens Devakī became happy by performing rites of auspiciousness in the presences of Kṛṣṇa in some palaces. In other palaces she had longing, not being present. By the power of *yogamāyā,* sometimes Uddhava and others have the happiness of meeting and sometimes the grief of separation.

When the women of Vraja experience separation from Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā, they maintain their lives in great pain in a particular *prakaṭa* manifestation, since they are unaware of the happiness of union with Kṛṣṇa in other *prakaṭa* manifestations. In meeting with Kṛṣṇa in *aprakaṭa* pastimes there is great joy, since the associates are unaware of the pain of separation of Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā manifested in *prakaṭa* manifestations.

### Text 188

***atha sambhogaḥ***  
***darśanāliṅganādīnāṁ ānukūlyān niṣevayā \|***  
***yūnor ullāsam ārohan bhāvaḥ sambhoga ucyate \|\|188\]\|***

**Перевод:**

**Union: That** ***bhāva*** **which increases joy of a couple by engaging in seeing each other, embraces and other exchanges of love out of favorable attitude is called** ***sambhoga*** **(enjoyment in union).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *ānukūlyāt* indicates that enjoyment based on lust is excluded.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This *bhāva* called *sambhoga* should increase the joy of the couple, the hero and heroine, who are mutually *viṣaya* and *āśraya*, by activities (*sevayā*) which are according to the scriptures on fine arts written by Vātsyāyana and Bharata (*ni* for *nitarām*). This excludes animalistic actions in love. The actions should be for the purpose of mutual happiness (*ānukūlyāt*). Since actions should be mutually favorable (*ānukūlyan*), other types of amorous enjoyment are excluded. Thus material enjoyment filled with lust such as the verse starting *niḥśeṣa-cyuta-candanam* (the sandalwood has vanished from your breast) from *Kāyva-prakāśa* (1.4) is excluded.

### Text 189

***manīṣibhir ayaṁ mukho gauṇaś ceti dvidhoditaḥ \|\|189\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The wise say that there are two types of** ***sambhoga*****: primary and secondary.**

### Text 190-191

***tatra mukhyaḥ—***  
***mukhyo jāgrad-avasthāyāṁ sambhogaḥ sa caturvidhaḥ \|\|190\|\|***  
***tān pūrva-rāgato mānāt pravāsa-dvayataḥ kramāt \|***  
***jātān saṁkṣipta-saṅkīrṇa-sampanna-rddhimato viduḥ \|\|191\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Primary union: Primary** ***sambhoga*** **takes place in the waking state. There are four varieties. From** ***pūrva-rāga*** **arises** ***saṁkṣipta-sambhoga,*** **from** ***māna*** **arises** ***saṅkīrṇa-sambhoga,*** **from close** ***pravāsa*** **arises** ***sampanna-sambhoga*** **and from distant** ***pravāsa*** **arises** ***samṛddhimat-sambhoga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is a general statement since from *prema-vaicittyam* arises the fifth type.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The four types of separation lead to four kinds of *sambhoga*. After *pūrva-rāga* there is *saṅkṣipta-sambhoga.* After *māna* there is *saṅkīṛṇa-sambhoga.* After somewhat distant *pravāsa* there is *sampanna-sambhoga* and after very far *pravāsa* there is *samṛddhimat-sambhoga.* The *sambhoga* from *prema-vaicittyam* was not mentioned. Some say it is *samṛddhimat-sambhoga* because it is said to arise from the power of *anurāga* and to take place after separation at a great distance. Some say *prema-vaicittyam* produces *sampanna-sambhoga*.

### Text 192

***tatra saṅkṣiptaḥ—***  
***yuvānau yatra saṁkṣiptān sādhvasa-vrīḍitādibhiḥ \|***  
***upacārān niṣevete sa saṁkṣipta itīritaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Saṅkṣipta-sambhoga:*** **That** ***sambhoga*** **in which the couple utilizes very few for the facilities for enjoyment because of fear and shyness is called** ***saṁkṣipta*** **(abbreviated).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Fear and shyness manifest because it comes after *pūrva-raga,* when the couple have met for the first time. *Upacārān* means the facilities available.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Upacārān* means the objects used for enjoyment. *Ādi* means intolerance. This is because such a meeting occurs after *pūrva-rāga.*

### Text 193

***tatra nāyakena kṛtaḥ, yathā saptaśatyām—***  
***līlāhituliaselo rakkha-u vo rāhiātthaṇapphaṁse \|***  
***hariṇo paḍhama-samāgama-sajjhasabebellio hattho \|\|\|***  
***\[līlābhitulita-śailo rakṣatu vo rādhikā-stana-sparśe \|***  
***hareḥ prathama-samāgama-sādhvasa-vevellito hastaḥ \|\|\]***

**Перевод:**

***Saṅkṣipta*** **in the hero, from** ***Saptaśatī:*** **May the hand which lifted Govardhana, which trembled with fear to touch the breast of Rādhā at their first meeting, protect you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is an example of *saṅkṣipta-sambhoga* in the hero. The meaning is “May the hand (haṭtho) of Kṛṣṇa which easily lifted the mountain (līlāhitulia-selo) but trembled (bebellio) with fear (sajjhasa) because of the first (paḍhama) meeting, protect you.” Though the hand lifted Govardhana, it trembled with fear because of the *parakīya* relationship.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nāndīmukhī speaks to Rādhā’s sakhīs. That hand which lifted Govardhana effortlessly (*līlā*) trembled (*vevellitaḥ*) out of fear. Since birth he had never done such a thing. His thought was “How should one enjoy a woman?”

### Text 194

***nāyikāyāḥ, yathā—***  
***cumbe paṭāvṛta-mukhī nava-saṅgame ’bhūd***  
***āliṅgane kuṭilitāṅga-latā tadāsīt \|***  
***avyakta-vāg ajani keli-kathāsu rādhā***  
***modaṁ tathāpi vidadhe madhusūdanasya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In the heroine: When they first met, she covered her face when he tried to kiss her. She retracted the creeper of her body when he tried to embrace her. She did not speak when he tried to frivolously converse with her. Still Rādhā delighted Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Fright was shown in the previous verse. Now shyness is shown. Though such reactions in Rādhā always take place, at the first meeting they were extreme.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

At the first meeting, where there was kissing, she covered her face.

### Text 195

***atha saṅkīrṇaḥ—***  
***yatra saṅkīryamāṇāḥ syur vyalīka-smaraṇādibhiḥ \|***  
***upacārāḥ sa saṅkīrṇaḥ kiñcit taptekṣu-peśalaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Saṅkīrṇa*** **(contaminated)** ***sambhoga:*** **When the actions of love are mixed with remembrance of displeasing actions of the lover, it is called** ***saṅkīrṇa-sambhoga*****, tasting like hot sugar cane juice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Valīka* means displeasure.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Displeasing remembrances means remembrance of the lover cheating and glorification the excellence of a rival woman. When the kissing and embraces (*upacārāḥ*) are mixed *(saṅkīrṇā*) with these displeasing remembrances, it is called *saṅkīrṇa-sambhoga.* The taste (*peśalaḥ*) is like hot sugar cane juice, with an experience of simultaneous hotness and sweetness.

### Text 196

***yathā—***  
***sāsūya-jalpita-sudhāni samatsarāṇi***  
***manoparāma-ramaṇīya-dṛg-iṅgitāni \|***  
***kaṁsa-dviṣaḥ sphurad-amanda-mukhāny anaṅga-***  
***vikrīḍitāni saha rādhikayā jayanti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example: All glories to the love pastimes of Kṛṣṇa with Rādhā, containing a great abundance of bliss, nectar of envious words filled with jealousy, peaceful minds, and pleasant glances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another version has *kaṁsa-dviṣā sama* and *vṛsabhānujayā* instead of *kaṁsa-dviṣaḥ sphurad* and *saha rādhikayā*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Paurṇamāsī on her own arranged a meeting of Rādhā with Kṛṣṇa and from a distance saw their pastimes through the spaces in a creeper bower. She gives blessings in this verse. Rādhā’s words of envy were finding faults in the qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Her jealousy (*samatsarānī*) took the form of hatred of the qualities of the rival woman.

### Text 197

***yathā vā—***  
***vaktraṁ kiñcid avāñcitaṁ vivṛṇute nātiprasādodayaṁ***  
***dṛṣṭir bhugna-taṭā vyanakti śanakair īrṣyāvaśeṣa-cchaṭām \|***  
***rādhāyāḥ sakhi sūcayaty aviśadā vāg apy asūyākalāṁ***  
***mānantaṁ bruvatī tathāpi madhurā kṛṣṇaṁ dhinoty ākṛtiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O friend! Her crooked face did not indicate she was pleased. Her contracted eyes showed remaining mass of hatred. Her impure words showed her jealousy. Still her sweet form showing the end of anger pleased Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vaktram* (face) is the subject of the first sentence.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Saṅkīrṇa* is possible at the beginning and middle of *sambhoga* but not at the end. The previous verse showed *saṅkīrṇa* in the middle of *sambhoga.* The present verse shows *saṅkīrṇa* at the beginning of *sambhoga.* Gārgī speaks to Nāndīmukhī, relishing the *rasa.* *Vaktram* is the subject of the first sentence. Her form indicating *(bhruvatī*) the end of *māna* pleased Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 198

***atha sampannaḥ—***  
***pravāsāt saṅgate kānte bhogaḥ sampanna īritaḥ \|***  
***dvidhā syād āgatiḥ prādurbhāvaś ceti sa saṅgamaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sampanna-sambhoga*** **(complete union)*****:*** **When the lovers meet after being separated a short distance, it is called** ***sampanna*****. There are two types of meeting: coming and manifestation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Saṅkṣipta* (abbreviated) and *saṅkīrṇa* (contaminated) are surpassed by the *sampanna* (excellent) by the very meaning of the words.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pravāsa* here means a short distance. When the lovers meet after a separation caused by some short distance it is called *sampanna*. This has two varieties.

### Text 199

***tatra āgatiḥ—***  
***laukika-vyavahāreṇa syād āgamanam āgatiḥ \|\|199\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Coming: Arriving through regular actions is called coming.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Every morning going from Vraja to the forest and every evening returning from the forest to Vraja is regular actions (*laukika-vyavahāreṇa).*

### Text 200

***yathā uddhava-sandeśe (40)—***  
***mā mandākṣaṁ kuru gurujanād dehalīṁ geha-madhyād-***  
***ehi klāntā divasam akhilam hanta viśleṣato ’si \|***  
***eṣa smero milati mṛdule vallavī-citta-hārī***  
***hārī guñjāvalibhir alibhir līḍha-gandho mukundaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa:*** **O delicate Rādhā! Do not contract your eyes because your elders. Come from inside the house to terrace. You have been fainting all day from separation. Smiling Kṛṣṇa, who enchants the** ***gopīs*****' hearts, who is decorated with garlands of** ***guñja*** **seeds, and whose fragrance is licked by the bees, is now softly approaching.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Rādhā, informing her that Kṛṣṇa has come from the forest to the cow sheds.

### Text 201

***atha prādurbhāvaḥ—***  
***preṣṭhānāṁ prema-saṁrambha-vihvalānāṁ puro hariḥ \|***  
***āvirbhavaty akasmād yat prādurbhāvaḥ sa ucyate \|\|201\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Manifestation: The sudden manifestation of Kṛṣṇa in front of his beloveds who are agitated with** ***rūḍha-bhāva*** **is called** ***prādurbhāva*** **(manifestation).**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is a sudden appearance without coming by normal means from another place, because of the intensity of *rūḍha-bhāva (prema-saṁrambha).*

### Text 202

***yathā śrī-daśame (10.32.2)—***  
***tāsām āvirabhūc chauriḥ smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ \|***  
***pītāmbara-dharaḥ sragvī sākṣān manmatha-manmathaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example from the Tenth Canto: Then Lord Kṛṣṇa, a smile on his lotus face, appeared before the** ***gopīs.*** **Wearing a garland and a yellow garment, he directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, who himself bewilders the minds of ordinary people.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śukadeva describes the appearance of Kṛṣṇa after *vipralambha-rasa.* *Tāsām āvirabhūt* means he appeared directly to their vision.

### Text 203

***yathā vā haṁsadūte (107)—***  
***ayi svapno dūre viramatu samakṣaṁ śṛṇu haṭhād***  
***aviśvastā mā bhūr iha sakhi manovibhramadhiyā \|***  
***vayasyas te govardhana-vipinam āsādya kutukād***  
***akāṇḍe yad bhūyaḥ smara-kalaha-pāṇḍityam atanot \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **It was not a dream. Friend, hear me. I was awake. Do not disbelieve me in haste, thinking my mind has become bewildered. Your friend unexpectedly entered the forest near Govardhana Hill and once again displayed his expertise by have a lover's quarrel with me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rādhā in separation speaks to Lalitā about enjoying with Kṛṣṇa in a dream and then describes how Kṛṣṇa suddenly appeared. This manifestation is described in *Haṁsadūta.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some will argue that the previous example shows that Kṛṣṇa came from another place and appeared before the *gopīs.* Rādhā in separation speaks to Lalitā about enjoying with Kṛṣṇa in a dream and then describes how Kṛṣṇa suddenly appeared. *Samakṣam* means in the waking state.

“You are here and Kṛṣṇa is in Mathurā. How is it possible for you two to meet now, unless it is an illusion in your mind?” When Lalitā says this, Rādhā replies, “Do not think this is some sudden illusion in the mind.” Though it is *samṛddhimān* because Kṛṣṇa has gone far away, this example shows *sampanna* because the qualities of *samṛddhimān* are not complete, since the two not seeing each other is not caused by others for both parties (since he makes such an appearance by his free will ) as in *samṛddhimān.* Though there is experience of meeting after long distance separation according to her statement, there is no indicate that Kṛṣṇa is prevented from seeing her by others. Thus, it is not *samṛddhimān* but *sampanna.* This is the intention of the author. Thus after killing Dantavakra and coming to Vraja, the meeting of Kṛṣṇa with Rādhā is also *sampanna*, not *samṛddhimān. According to Viśvanātha the condition of Kṛṣṇa being under others’ control is the situation in Lalita-mādhava where Kṛṣṇa promises King Bhiṣmaka that he will not marry anyone else except Rukmiṇī unless Candrāvalī agrees. At the end of the drama, Candrāvalī recognizes that Satyabhāmā is Rādhā, and agrees to the marriage. 4*

Some explain as follows. One should not think this is an example of *sambhoga* after long distance separation since it is in this section on *sampanna.* In common people, past states appear to be present states because of lack of control during sleep or fainting. Usually it happens in dreams and occasionally in fainting. Even without *mohana* in *rūḍha-bhāva* there is constant forgetfulness of the self: *ātmādi-sarva-vismaranaṁ sadā* (*Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 14.162) Thus, because of Rādhā’s great lack of control arising from separation from Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā, suddenly, in a moment of complete forgetfulness of self, Kṛṣṇa manifested. “He is my lover. Entrusting the cows to his friends, by some pretext, overcome with love for me, he has come alone to give enjoyment to me in this grove at Govardhana.” Because of manifestation of identity with the pastimes before the coming of Akrūra, the *sambhoga* element is like that when Kṛṣṇa has left only a slight distance, not a great distance. Thus from the above one can understand that it is a union after slight separation in a dream. This would then be classed as secondary sambhoga, which is explained later. 5

### Text 204-205

***rūḍhākhya-bhāva-jāto’yaṁ sambhogo vaipralambhikaḥ \|***  
***nirbharānanda-purāṇāṁ paramāvadhir iṣyate \|\|204\|\|***  
***dviguṇā virahārtiḥ syāt sphuraṇe anurāgaje \|***  
***prādurbhāve bhavaty atra sarvābhīṣṭa-sukhotsavaḥ \|\|205\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***sambhoga*** **arising from** ***rūḍha-bhāva,*** **arising from separation, is the pinnacle of perfect, excessive bliss. The doubled pain of separation becomes the most greatly desired happiness with a** ***prādurbhava*** **of Kṛṣṇa after a** ***sphūrti*** **in** ***rūḍha-bhāva.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

That *sambhoga* which arises from *rūḍha-bhāva,* which accompanies separation, is the height of bliss.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vaipralambhikaḥ* means “created in *vipralambha.”* The ending *ka* follows words like *adhyātmika.* The words *nirbhara, parama* and *avadhi* indicate that one should not fear *sampanna-sambhoga* is inferior to *samṛddhimat-sambhoga*. Rather it is greater. “But how can the *sambhoga* produced by a momentary appearance (*sphūrti)* of Kṛṣṇa in separation be superior?” This is not a momentary manifestation (*sphūrti)* but something greater that a *sphūrti.* After there is a *sphūrti* arising from *anurāga*, there is happiness of associating with the lover. *Anurāga* here means arising from *rūḍha-bhāva. Sphūrtis* arise in *anurāg*a and *prādurbhāva* (manifestion) arises in *mahābhāva (rūḍha-bhāva).*

### Text 206

***atha samṛddhimān—***  
***durlabhālokayor yūnoḥ pāratantryād viyuktayoḥ \|***  
***upabhogātireko yaḥ kīrtyate sa samṛddhimān \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The great enjoyment of lovers uniting, who have been separated and who find it most difficult to meet because of others’ control is called** ***samṛddhimān.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The four resolutions of the four types of *vipralambha* are being described in succession. Amongst the four *sambhogas* to destroy the pain, the pain of *pūrva-rāga* is destroyed by *saṅkṣipta-sambhoga*. The destroyer of pain of *māna* is *saṅkīrṇa-sambhoga.* The extinguisher of the fire of slightly far departure from Vraja to the forest is *sampanna*. Destruction of intolerable long separation constantly described is *samṛddhimāt-sambhoga*. This *sambhoga* should now be described.

This *samṛddhimāt sambhoga* is greater than the others since *saṅkṣipta* is endowed with fear and shyness, *saṅkīrṇa* is endowed with negative memories and *sampanna* is devoid of great obstacles. Since *saṅkṣipta* has only a sprout of closeness, *saṅkīrṇa* with intimate contact is superior. *Sampanna* is superior to *saṅkīṛṇa.* From the special taste of *saṅkīrṇa* which is like hot sugar cane juice, the superior taste in *sampanna* can be understood. Separation which is like extreme hunger, though overlooking the quality of taste, is actually the cause of taste, since in the absence of hunger hot sugar cane juice is not attractive. The separation from *pūrva-rāga* and *māna* are causes of taste since that separation is like hunger. If that is so, how much more will be the taste caused by *pravāsa* combined with increased *rāga?*

*gopīnāṁ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane*  
*kṣaṇaṁ yuga-śatam iva yāsāṁ yena vinābhavat*

**The young** ***gopīs*** **took the greatest pleasure in seeing Govinda come home, since for them even a moment without His association seemed like a hundred ages. SB 10.19.16**

Since *sampanna* is considered superior to the first two types of *sambhoga,* it is clear that there is a very special taste in *samṛddhimat-sambhoga* because of the greater hunger caused by long separation over great distance. Its superiority over the other *sambhogas* which destroy the pain in *pūrva-rāga, māna* and slightly distant *pravāsa* must be described.  *Ṛddhi* means completion and *sam* means additional. The suffix *mat* indicates a continual connection, signifying great praise. Thus it indicates excellence.

*Samṛddhiman-sambhoga* is shown to attain the highest excellence by the power of *yogamāyā.* The couple can see each other with the greatest difficulty (*durlabhālokayoḥ*). They are separated because of being controlled by obstacles to seeing each other (*pāratantryāt*). The extreme enjoyment of seeing each other that arises after that condition, surpassing (*atirekaḥ*) *saṅkṣipta, saṅkīṛṇa* and *sampanna sambhoga*, caused by the hunger or taste arising from distant and long separation, is called *samṛddhimān.* They are separated because of both being controlled by others. This is a special feature of *samṛddhimān.* That type of separation does not occur in the other three types of *sambhoga*. They find it difficult to see each other. They are eager to meet. The difficulty in doing so however indicates that their separation has been caused by others, not by their will.  *Pāratantryāt* thus means “not by their own will.” The opposite is shown in this example: the wives serve their husband daily by their free will (*aparatanryaḥ).* Those who are separated beyond their control are different from those who separate by their will.

This will be illustrated according to the reasoning of the phrase *na vinā vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute*: *sambhoga* is not nourished unless there is separation. *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 15.3

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The great enjoyment in meeting experienced by a hero and heroine who are separated because of great distance and who can see each other only with great difficulty because of others’ control is called *samṛddhimān sambhoga*. In the other *sambhogas* the cause of not seeing each other is not both parties being under others’ control. Rather only one of them, the woman, is under the control of the mother-in-law, husband and elders, who prevent her from meeting her lover. There is of course great enjoyment when the couple rarely meets because the woman is prevented. The evidence was given earlier with *bahuvāryate yataḥ* and*yatra niṣedha-veśeṣaḥ sudurlabhatvaṁ ca yan mṛgākṣīn:*

*bahu vāryate khalu yatra pracchanna-kāmukatvaṁ ca*  
*yā ca mitho durlabhatā sā manmathasya paramā ratiḥ*

**That love which causes great opposition because of being against normal** ***dharma,*** **which necessitates the love be kept secret, and which makes it hard for the lovers to meet is the highest type of love.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.20**

*yatra niṣedha-viśeṣaḥ sudurlabhatvaṁ ca yan mṛgākṣīṇām \|*  
*tatraiva nāgarāṇāṁ nirbharam āsajjate hṛdayam \|\|*

**When the woman makes a point of resisting and becoming unavailable the man bcomes more deeply attached.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **3.21**

Thus it is proved that there is greater pleasure derived from rare contact because of others’ prevention. This is also seen in *Lalita-mādhava.*

The word *paratantryāt* in this verse means the inability to see each other is caused by others factors, beyond their control. This excludes separation and difficulty in seeing each other caused by *māna* (which is caused by oneself).

The word *pāratantryāt* in the ablative cannot mean “without dependence on others” since the two examples following in the text do not show absence of dependence on others, but rather show complete dependence on other factors for not seeing each other. It is seen in that story that Navavṛndā, who has made an oath, cannot tell the secret of Rādhā’s identity.

It is also not suitable to say that because of being under others’ control that they were separated (rather than finding it difficult to see each other). The separation is caused only by going to a distant place *(pravāsa*), by going to Mathurā. That others are the cause of his going to Mathurā can be discarded as insignificant.

In the example given here, *samṛddhimat sambhoga* occurs once in the *prakaṭa* pastimes according to the story in *Lalita-mādhava.* Its eternal nature however has been shown before (since such pastimes continue in other universes.) Some persons explain that since, after the distant separation they get married and are not under others’ control, *samṛddhimān, saṅkṣipta, saṅkirṇa* and *sampanna* can only be parts of *upapati* love. However this is not at all the intention of the author. There is *samṛddhimān* even in the married state, without control by others. This is clear from the following verse:

*sakhyas tā militā nisarga-madhurāḥ premābhirāmī-kṛtā*  
*yāmīyaṁ samagaṁsta saṁstaravatī śvaśrūś ca goṣṭheśvarī \|*  
*vṛndāraṇya-nikuñja-dhāmni bhavatā saṅgo’py ayaṁ raṅgavān*  
*saṁvṛttaḥ kim ataḥ paraṁ priyataraṁ kartavyam atrāsti me \|\|*

**In this forest of Vṛndāvana I have found my beautiful, charming, and affectionate** ***gopī*** **friends, I have found my sister Candrāvalī, In Lalita-mādhava, Candrāvalī and Rādhā were the daughters of Vindhya Mountain.6 and all her friends. I have obtained Yaṣodā the queen of Vraja as my mother-in-law, and I have also attained your company, which brings me the greatest happiness. What can be more pleasing to me than all these things?** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **10.36**

This verse shows married life without dependence on others. However, why does the author give the next two verses in the text as examples of *samṛddhimān,* since those verses show dependence on others in *upapati* love? In the drama, Rādhā in Dvārakā was not married. But though Rādhā identifies herself as the daughter of Satrājit given to him by the sun god she still has *upapati bhāva* with Kṛṣṇa as previously. Thus “being controlled by others” reaches its highest state (since Rādhā feels she is married and Kṛṣṇa is controlled by Rukmiṇī.) There should be some satisfaction by this (*smṛddhimān* with *upapati* love).

“But when Rādhā speaks the verse 10.36 in *Lalita-mādhava,* this indicates the highest bliss in married life, free from others’ control.” This is not so. In the same work later she says:

*yā te līlā-rasa-parimalodgāri-vanyā parītā*  
*dhanyā kṣauṇī vilasati vṛtā māthurī mādhurībhiḥ \|*  
*tatrāsmābhiś caṭula-paśupī-bhāva-mugdhāntarābhiḥ*  
*saṁvītas tvaṁ kalaya vadanollāsi-veṇur vihāram \|\|*

**This fortunate earth, not far from Mathurā, spread with the forests giving the fragrance of your rāsa pastimes is surrounded by sweetness of trees, birds and animals. You, with flute in your mouth, should play here, surrounded by us foolish, unsteady women, identifying ourselves as wives of cowherd men.** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **10.38**

The meaning of the verse is this. *Mathurī* means not far from Mathurā, a place called Vṛndāvana. Nava-vṛndāvana in Dvārakā is excluded. That place near Mathurā is spread with many forests emanating the fragrance of marks of the *rāsa* pastimes, surrounded by the sweetness of mountains, rivers, trees, animals and birds. Our hearts are foolish with the identity of unsteady *gopīs. Caṭula* indicates unsteadiness in women because of *upapati* love. The fickle woman is famous in the world for such love. We are the wives of cowherds (*paśupī).* The word *paśupī* should not be taken simply as a generic term like *gopī* from *gopā* by convention. Words like *paśupa* are not well known, not used by the common to people. The word *caṭula* indicates *parakīya* state. Fickleness of unmarried or married women indicates attachment to another man. *Mugdha* means without intelligence. This indicates their trespassing *dharma* for this life and the next. How are you described? You have a flute in your mouth that attracts the women and perform pastimes such as the *rāsa* dance, playing in the forest, boat pastimes and toll gate pastimes. Now you are the king and I am your wife, a queen, a chaste woman. This married life is unfavorable for such desirable things. Kṛṣṇa then said “O beloved! Let this be.” This refers to the *upapati* love in Vraja, not to married life in Dvārakā. This is the intention of the author. (Therefore even in Dvārakā she is also feeling *upapati* love.)

“Why does the author describe the marriage of the Vraja women with Kṛṣṇa in Nava-vṛndāvana within Dvārakā in *Lalita-mādhava?* If the marriage is described there, then one can assume his marriage with the Vraja women also takes place when Kṛṣṇa returns to Vraja in other *kalpas* after killing Dantavakra, as described in the *Padma Purāṇa* as quoted in the *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta*.” True, the marriage with the Vraja women in Dvārakā is not without proof. In *Padma Purāṇa,* Thirty-second Chapter, in the glorification of Kārtika month, it is said *kaiśore gopa-kanyās tā yauvane ṛaja-kaṇyakāḥ:* those who were unmarried *gopīs* in *kaiśora* age became kings’ daughters in their youth. In the *Skanda Purāṇa, Prabhāsa-khanda,* in the glorificaiton of *Gopyāditya,* speaking of the queens, it is said *śoḍaśaiva sahasrāṇi gopyas tatra samāgatāh:* sixteen thousand *gopīs* were gathered there.

However, Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana is *pūrṇatama.* He is *pūrṇa* as the lord of Dvārakā. Similarly the women of Vraja are *pūrṇatama* forms of the *hlādinī-śakti,* and in Dvārakā, in marriage, they are *pūrṇa* forms as Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā and others, as the daughters of Bhīsmaka, Satrājit and others. It is not possible to describe this marriage taking place in the *pūrṇatama dhāma* of Vraja, since there is fault of *samañjasa-rati* mixing with *samartha-rati.* It is a contradiction to the prayer uttered by Rādhā expressing fickleness, cowherds’ wives and their foolishness in trespassing *dharma.*

Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā, though the son of the king of Vraja, thinks “I am now the son of Vasudeva in Dvārakā” and his queens, for instance Candrāvalī, daughter of Candrabhānu, think “I am Rukmiṇī, daughter of Bhīṣmaka, the wife of Kṛṣṇa.” But Kṛṣṇa identifies the pastimes of Vṛndāvana as the best and similarly the queens identify the women of Vraja as the best, because of their greater amount of *rasa.*

### Text 207

***yathā lalita-mādhave (7.18)—***  
***dagdhaṁ hanta dadhānayā vapur idaṁ yasyāvalokāśayā***  
***soḍhā marma-vipāṭane paṭur iyaṁ pīḍātivṛṣṭir mayā \|***  
***kālindīya-taṭī-kuṭīra-kuhara-krīḍābhisāra-vratī***  
***so’yaṁ jīvita-bandhur indu-vadane bhūyaḥ samāliṅgitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example, from** ***Lalita-mādhava*****: O Nava-vṛndā! Having maintained this body burned up by the desire to see him and tolerating an intense shower of sharp pain which destroys my vital organs, I again am embraced by this friend of my life who is intent on meeting for pastimes in the bower on the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“*Samṛddhimān* has been said to the final result of all the *bhāvas* in *vipralambha* and *sambhoga.* But it is not the highest happiness. It cannot be the all in all for the women of Vraja, for it was shown that Kṛṣṇa gave up these women who feared others because of their *parakīya* relationship, went to Mathurā, after a long time met them again at Kurukṣetra and then quickly left them. Thus they again suffered separation in absence of Kṛṣṇa. This is not fitting for the highest happiness. How can it be the highest happiness for them?”

To dispel this doubt, this verse shows the nature of their *samṛddhimān.* The arrangement is this. Candrāvalī, Rādhā and others were born to the wives of Bhīsmaka and other kings. By the power of *māyā* they had previously been placed in the wombs of wives of cowherd men like Candrabhānu. Their marriage to other cowherd men was arranged by *māyā.* By that arrangement, association of the cowherds with those women was through shadow forms of those women while they associated with Kṛṣṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks with bliss and astonishment to Nava-vṛndā, on seeing a sapphire form of Kṛṣṇa made by Viśvakarmā, which she thinks is actually Kṛṣṇa and desires to meet directly.

*Dagdhām* means burned by the fire of separation. She tolerated an intense shower of pains from the coming Akrūra to Vraja to being controlled by Rukmiṇī. O moon-faced Nava-vṛndā! Other *gopīs* had been given such as Rukmiṇī as young unmarried girls and their marriage with Kṛṣṇa was described. And the marriages to the sixteen thousand girls stolen by Naraka were done according to normal custom. Rādhā, given the name Satyabhāmā by Satrājit, was gifted to Kṛṣṇa.

This is not a concocted story. There are traditional proofs for it. In the Thirty-second Chapter of *Padma Purāṇa* in the glorification of Kārtika month, it is said *kaiśore gopa-kanyās tā yauvane rāja-kanyakāḥ*: those who were daughters of cowherds in their *kaiśora* age became daughters of kings in their youth. In *Skanda Purāṇa, Prabhāsa-khanda,* in the glorification of the *gopīs* the queens are described as sixteen thousand *gopīs* gathered together: *ṣoḍaśaiva sahasrāṇi gopyas tatra samāgatāḥ*. In the *Bhāgavatam* the meeting between the *gopīs* and the queens shows them with separate identities. That is a description from a different *kalpa.*

The verse from the *Lalita-mādhava* is thus used as an example of Rādhā’s *samṛddhimān.* Rādhā, given by Satrājit to Kṛṣṇa, was hidden by him for some time in a Vṛndāvana constructed within Dvārakā because of fear of Candrāvalī. Not knowing that the lord of Dvārakā is the Kṛṣṇa of Vraja, she thinks the statue of him in the forest is Kṛṣṇa. She speaks this verse.

### Text 208

***yathā vā (8.10)—***  
***tavātra parimṛgyatā kim api lakṣma sākṣād iyaṁ***  
***mayā tvam upasāditā nikhila-loka-lakṣmīr asi \|***  
***yathā jagati cañcatā caṇaka-muṣṭi-sampattaye***  
***janena patitā puraḥ kanaka-vṛṣṭir āsādyate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: I have been searching for some sign of you, and now I have found you. I worship you, the goddess of fortune, who reigns over all worlds. You are a shower of gold raining upon a person who has fallen in the universe and is wandering about for a treasure of chick-peas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

**When Kṛṣṇa went among the Yadus in order to kill Kaṁsa, by some means the women of Vraja were brought to the houses of Bhīṣmaka and others, and were identified as their daughters with names like Rukmiṇī. Rādhā in the previous verse still identifies the other women as queens and Kṛṣṇa as lord of Dvārakā.7 The author therefore was not satisfied with the previous example from the Seventh Act. When Rādhā realizes Kṛṣṇa as lord of Dvārakā, Kṛṣṇa speaks the present verse from Act Eight. Fulfillment of Desires, Act Ten, where all things are accomplished, is expressed in these words (though this verse is from the Eighth Act.).**

When Rādhā went to Dvārakā, Candrāvalī finally recognized Rādhā as her sister in Gokula, the wedding of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa was performed (with Candrāvalī’s permission), and then Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa began conversing. Kṛṣṇa at that time (Tenth Act) said *prāpṇeśvari prārthayasva kim ataḥ param te priyam karavāni*: O controller of my life, please ask for something so I may please you. Rādhā then said:

*sakhyas tā militā nisarga-madhurāḥ premābhirāmī-kṛtā*  
*yāmīyaṁ samagaṁsta saṁstaravatī śvaśrūś ca goṣṭheśvarī \|*  
*vṛndāraṇya-nikuñja-dhāmni bhavatā saṅgo’py ayaṁ raṅgavān*  
*saṁvṛttaḥ kim ataḥ paraṁ priyataraṁ kartavyam atrāsti me \|\|*

**In this forest of Vṛndāvana I have found my beautiful, charming, and affectionate gopī friends, I have found my sister Candrāvalī, and all her friends. I have obtained my mother-in-law and Yaṣodā the queen of Vraja and I have also attained your pleasant company in the bowers of Vṛndāvana. What can be more pleasing to me than all these things?** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **10.36**

Having said this, she thought that perhaps this was an artificially produced Vṛndāvana:

*yā te līlā-rasa-parimalodgāri-vanyā parītā*  
*dhanyā kṣauṇī vilasati vṛtā māthurī mādhurībhiḥ \|*  
*tatrāsmābhiś caṭula-paśupī-bhāva-mugdhāntarābhiḥ*  
*saṁvītas tvaṁ kalaya vadanollāsi-veṇur vihāram \|\|*

**This fortunate earth, not far from Mathurā, spread with the forests giving the fragrance of your rāsa pastimes is surrounded by sweetness of trees, birds and animals. You, with flute in your mouth, should play here, surrounded by us foolish, unsteady women, identifying ourselves as wives of cowherd men.** ***Lalita-mādhava*** **10.38**

Mathurī means a place not far from the city of Mathurā or Mathurā. The rule is *adura-bhāvas ca:* a place is named after what is found near it. (Pāṇini 4.2.70) *Kṣauṇī* means the manifestation of Vṛndāvana. In the previous verse *yāmīyam* means Candrāvalī famous as her sister in order to avoid conflicts. They gave up hatred as co-wives. Previously Jaṭilā was the mother-in-law, but gave up her hostility to Kṛṣṇa. Now she was favorable. I have attained this Vṛndāvana. What to speak of attaining the real Vṛndāvana! Because the restrictions of place have disappeared here it is shown that all interference from others in meeting (*pāratantryā*) has disappeared. Association with you is pleasant, surrounded by all sorts of novelties. This shows the height of extreme enjoyment (*upabhogātirekha*). In this way the characteristics of *samṛddhimān* mentioned in the definition are fulfilled for the couple who had difficulty in meeting. What to speak of the happiness expressed in the second of the two verses.

Kṛṣṇa agreed with her. “My dear, may this come true!” To make this promise true, it should be understood that, because he appeared in Vṛndāvana, he accepted bodily expansions (*kāya-vyūha)* in Dvārakā Thus he associated with the forms of the queens in a suitable form in Dvārakā and associated with the *gopīs* in a suitable form in Vṛndāvana (within Dvārakā). However, the marriage with Rādhā and the women of Vraja was real, whereas all the other marriages previously to cowherd men were produced by *māyā.* This was revealed by Paurṇamāsī.

Therefore it is seen in the scriptures that in worship for seeing Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, the worship uses the names of Rukmiṇī and others, which are considered to be non-different from their Vraja counterparts. One should understand that the conclusions found in *Lalita-mādhava,* with such non-difference, take place in some occasional *kalpas.*

It is accepted by the *Bhāgavatam* that the arrangement in the normal *kalpa* is to have difference between Dvārakā and Vraja forms. There is, for instance, the description of *modana-bhāva* during the trip to Kurukṣetra.

*hanta stambha-karambitā bhuvi kuror bhadrā sarasvaty abhūd-*  
*bāṣpaṁ bhāskarajā mumoca tarasā satyābhraman narmadā \|*  
*bheje bhīṣma-sutā ca varṇa-vikṛtiṁ gāmbhīrya-bhāg apy asau*  
*kṛṣṇodanvati rādhikādbhuta-nadī-premormibhiḥ saṁvṛte \|\|177\|\|*

**When the astonishing river of Rādhā with its waves of** ***prema*** **entered the sea of Kṛṣṇa at Kurukṣetra, fluent (Sarasvatī) Bhadrā became stunned and could not speak, Kalindī (Yamunā) shed many tears, joking (Narmadā) Satyabhāmā became bewildered, and grave Rukmiṇī (Gaṅgā) turned white.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.177**

In *Uddhava-sandeśa* it is said:

*vindan vaṁśī-sphurita-vadano netra-vīthīm akasmād*  
*antarbādhā-kavalita-dhiyo dhātubhir dhūmalo 'ham*  
*krīḍā-kuñje luṭhita-vapuṣaḥ śrāntam ānanda-dhārā-*  
*kallolais te rahasi sahasotphullam ullāsayiṣye*

**Your mind is afflicted with inner pain and your body rolls on the ground of the pastime bower. I will suddenly appear to your eyes, the flute placed to my mouth, and my limbs decorated with mineral colors. In this secluded place I will make you, now exhausted, bloom with waves of bliss.**

In this version of the pastime (not the version in *Lalita-mādhava*), after the killing of Dantavakra, in order to resolve the great separation that previously took place, Kṛṣṇa returns to Gokula. This portion of the *Padma Purāṇa* stating this is quoted in the author’s *Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta* (5.482). His older brother also quoted this in *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.*

*kṛṣṇo’pi taṁ hatvā yamunām uttīrya nanda-vrajaṁ gatvā prāktanau pitarāv abhivādya āśvāsya tābhyāṁ sāśrukaṇṭham āliṅgitaḥ sakala-gopa-vṛddhān praṇamyāśvāsya ratnābharaṇādibhis tatrasthān santarpayāmāsa \|*

**Killing Dantavarka, Kṛṣṇa crossed the Yamunā River and arrived at Nanda-vraja. When he greeted his parents, who were shedding tears, they embraced him. He offered respects to all the elder cowherd men and comforted them. He satisfied them all with ornaments studded with many jewels and diamonds.** ***Padma Purāṇa*** **6.279.24-26**

*Bhāgavatam* agrees. Kṛṣṇa, who is glorified by the Vedas, must keep his promise.

*tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāṇe yadūttamaḥ*  
*sāntvayām asa sa-premair āyāsya iti dautyakaiḥ*

**As he departed, that best of the Yadus saw how the** ***gopīs,*** **were lamenting, and thus he consoled them by sending a messenger with this loving promise: “I will return.” SB 10.39.35**

*yāta yūyaṁ vrajaṁn tāta vayaṁ ca sneha-duḥkhitān*  
*jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṁ sukham*

**Now you should all return to Vraja, dear father. We shall come to see you, our dear relatives who suffer in separation from us, as soon as we have given some happiness to your well-wishing friends. SB 10.45.23**

The word *drastum* means “we will come so that you can see us” as in the following verse:

*tathāpi bhūman mahimāguṇasya te*  
*viboddhum arhaty amalāntar-ātmabhiḥ;*

**Nondevotees, however, cannot realize you in your full personal feature. Nevertheless, it may be possible for them to realize your expansion as the impersonal Supreme by cultivating direct perception of the self within the heart.**

The meaning of *viboddhum* is “to make you the object of understanding.” His promise is made explicit by Uddhava:

*āgamiṣyaty adīrgheṇa kālena vrajam acyutaḥ*  
*priyaṁ vidhāsyate pitror bhagavān sātvatāṁ patiḥ*

**Infallible Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the devotees, will soon return to Vraja to satisfy his parents. SB 10.46.34**

“Satisfying his parents” means he is always in the form cared for by his parents. His return is also clear in the words of the inhabitants of Dvārakā.

*yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra bho bhavān*  
*kurūn madhūn vātha suhṛd-didṛkṣayā*  
*tatrābda-koṭi-pratimaḥ kṣaṇo bhaved*  
*raviṁ vinākṣṇor iva nas tavācyuta*

**O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever you go away to Mathurā, Vṛndāvana or Hastināpura to meet your friends and relatives, every moment of your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun. SB 1.11.9**

The word *madhūn* means Mathurā according to Śrīdhara Svāmī. *Suhṛd* means the people of Vraja. It cannot mean the people of Mathurā because they were all transferred to Dvārakā: *tatra yoga-prabhāvena nītvā sarva-janaṁ hariḥ*: by the power of *yogamāyā* Kṛṣṇa transferred all the people of Mathurā to Dvārakā. (SB 10.50.51) That *suhṛd* means the people of Vraja is indicated in the following verse:

*balabhadraḥ kuru-śreṣṭha bhagavān ratham āsthitaḥ*  
*suhṛd-didṛkṣur utkaṇṭhaḥ prayayau nanda-gokulam*

**O best of the Kurus, once Lord Balarāma, eager to visit his well-wishing friends, mounted his chariot and traveled to Nanda Gokula. SB 10.65.1**

Kṛṣṇa returned to Vraja after killing Dantavakra. Kṛṣṇa says to the women of Vraja at Kurukṣetra:

*api smaratha naḥ sakhyaḥ svānām artha-cikīrṣayā*  
*gatāṁś cirāyitāñ chatru-pakṣa-kṣapaṇa-cetasaḥ*

**My dear girl friends, do you still remember me? It was for my relatives’ sake that I stayed away so long, intent on destroying my enemies. SB 10.82.42**

He set the limit of his return to Vraja as the killing of all the enemies, which ended with killing Dantavakra. The journey to Kurukṣetra was previous to killing Dantavakra. He killed Sālva and Dantavakra at the same time that the Pāndavas were exiled to the forest. After the Pāṇḍavas returned the Kurukṣetra war took place in which Bhīṣma was killed. Bhīṣma and others who were later killed also came to Kurukṣetra for the eclipse. Baladeva’s pilgrimage to holy places was before the Kurukṣetra war and was completed on the day that Duryodhana was killed. That journey to Kurukṣetra for the eclipse took place not much after the time Kaṁsa was killed. The order is as follows: going to Kurukṣetra for the eclipse, the assembly of Yudhiṣṭhira, killing of Śiṣupāla there, the gambling match between the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, killing of Śālva and Dantavakra, Pāṇḍavas going to the forest, Balarāma’s pilgrimage, Kurukṣetra war and killing of Duryodhana. 8 Vasudeva speaks to Kuntī during the journey to Kurukṣetra:

*kaṁsa-pratāpitāḥ sarve vayaṁ yātā diśaṁ diśam*  
*etarhy eva punaḥ sthānaṁ daivenāsāditāḥ svasaḥ*

**Harassed by Kaṁsa, we all fled in various directions, but by the grace of Providence we have now finally been able to return to our homes, my dear sister. SB 10.82.21**

Returning after killing of Dantavakra can be taken as an event of some *kalpas* or one can take explanations according to *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī.* Excluding some differences between *Bhāgavatam* and the *Padma Purāṇa* there should be agreement. According to *Bhāgavatam* after killing Dantavakra, Kṛṣṇa returned to Vraja. After the previous quotation from *Padma Purāṇa,* in the *Uttara-khanda* there are two verses:

*kālindyāḥ puline ramye puṇya-vṛkṣa-samāvṛte \|*  
*gopa-nārībhir aniśaṁ krīḍayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|\|*  
*ramya-keli-sukhenaiva gopa-veṣa-dharo hariḥ \|*  
*baddha-prema-rasenātra māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa played all day with the cowherd women on the charming bank of the Yamunā covered with pure trees. Wearing the dress of a cowherd he stayed two months absorbed in the** ***rasa*** **of** ***prema*** **filled with the happiness of pleasurable pastimes.** ***Padma Purāṇa*** **6.252.19-27**

The word *gopa-nārībhiḥ* means with women of cowherd birth rather than wives of the cowherd. In the Third Canto Śukadeva speaks of Devahūtī as *nṛpa-vadhū*, daughter of the king, rather than wife of the king. The word *aniśam* (incessantly) indicates that he married them after wandering as an *upapati.* He played continuously with millions of women in knowledge of all people, without restrictions. The happiness of the pastimes was pleasant *(ramya*). They were attractive to all people. If he were not married, these pastimes would be criticized by all, not attractive to all. Those pastimes nourished the *prema* of all people of Vraja (*baddha-prema*).

*atha tatrasthā nanda-gopādayaḥ sarve janāḥ putra-dārādi-sahitāḥ paśu-pakṣi-mṛgādayaś ca vāsudeva-prasādena divya-rūpadharā vimānam ārūḍhāḥ paramaṁ vaikuṇṭha-lokam avāpuḥ*  
*kṛṣṇas tu nanda-gopa-vrajaukasaḥ sarveṣāṁ paramaṁ nirāmayaṁ sva-padaṁ dattvā divi deva-gaṇam saṁstūyamāno dvāravatīṁ veveśa*

**All persons present in Vraja headed by Nanda, along with their wives and sons, cows, animals and birds, having brilliant forms by the mercy of Vāsudeva, mounted an airplane and went to the supreme Vaikuṇṭha planet. Having given his supreme, infallible abode to all the inhabitants of Vraja, and being praised by the** ***devatās,*** **Kṛṣṇa entered Dvārakā.** ***Padma Purāṇa*** **6.279.27**

The meaning is this. Nanda, along with his wife Yaśodā and his son Kṛṣṇa, went there. This means they all went together. They had *divya* forms. This means that out of joy their spiritual forms shone most brilliantly. Riding on airplanes to enter Vaikuṇṭha is mentioned only to cheat materialistic people. Actually they entered invisibly into a special manifestation of Vṛndāvana. It is shown in *Bṛhad-vāraha Purāna, Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* and *Gautamīya-tantra* that this abode has an eternal manifestation.

After Nanda returned from Varuṇa’s planet, Kṛṣṇa also showed the people of Vraja a special manifestation of his own planet Vṛndāvana but they were not taken by airplanes. This is known in the Tenth Canto.

*nandas tv atīndriyaṁ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam*  
*kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṁ teṣāṁ jñātibhyo vismito ’bravīt*

**Nanda Mahārāja had been astonished to see for the first time the great opulence of Varuṇa, the ruler of the ocean planet, and also to see how Varuṇa and his servants had offered such humble respect to Kṛṣṇa. Nanda described all this to his fellow cowherd men. SB 10.28.11**

*te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram*  
*api naḥ sva-gatiṁ sūkṣmām upādhāsyad adhīśvaraḥ*

**The cowherd men considered that Kṛṣṇa must be the Supreme Lord, and their minds, O King, were filled with eagerness. They thought, “Will the Supreme Lord bestow upon us His transcendental abode?”**

*iti svānāṁ sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam*  
*saṅkalpa-siddhaye teṣāṁ kṛpayaitad acintayat*

**Because he sees everything, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, automatically understood what the cowherd men were conjecturing. Wanting to show his compassion to them by fulfilling their desires, the Lord thought as follows.**

*jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ*  
*uccāvacāsu gatiṣu na veda svāṁ gatiṁ bhraman*

**Certainly people in this world are wandering among higher and lower destinations, which they achieve through activities performed according to their desires and without full knowledge. Thus people do not know their real destination.**

*iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ*  
*darśayām āsa lokaṁ svaṁ gopānāṁ tamasaḥ param*

**Thus deeply considering the situation, the all-merciful Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari revealed to the cowherd men his abode, which is beyond material darkness.**

*satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ yad brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam*  
*yad dhi paśyanti munayo guṇāpāye samāhitāḥ*

**Lord Kṛṣṇa revealed the indestructible spiritual effulgence, which is unlimited, conscious and eternal. Sages see that spiritual existence in trance, when their consciousness is free of the modes of material nature.**

*te tu brahma-hradam nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ*  
*dadṛśur brahmaṇo lokaṁ yatrākrūro ’dhyagāt purā*

**The cowherd men were brought by Lord Kṛṣṇa to the Brahma-hrada, made to submerge in the water, and then lifted up. From the same vantage point that Akrūra saw the spiritual world, the cowherd men saw the planet of the Absolute Truth.**

*nandādayas tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nivṛtāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ stūyamānaṁ su-vismitāḥ*

**Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherd men felt the greatest happiness when they saw that transcendental abode. They were especially amazed to see Kṛṣṇa himself there, surrounded by the personified Vedas, who were offering him prayers. SB 10.28.10-17**

Though Kṛṣṇa showed them his abode, he took them there later. He first took them to Brahma-hrada. He submerged them in the lake were Akrūra praised Kṛṣṇa and then raised them up and they saw the planet with Brahman in human form. Brahmaloka refers to the planet of the Lord, not that of Brahmā, since it is eternal *(sanātana*). It is very subtle, (*tamasaḥ param*). The words *na veda svāṁ gatim* and *kṛṣṇaṁ ca tatra* indicate the form of Gopāla. They did not see other associates there, only themselves. He was praised by the Vedas such as *Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad* as the form of Kṛṣṇa. That is the meaning of *kṛṣṇaṁ ca tatra.* They, who had attraction only for him, experienced supreme bliss. This caused them to lose awareness of even his planet. That is indicated by the phrase *jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ*. *Jana* means “his own people, the devotee” as in the following

*sālokya-sārṣṭi-sāmīpya- sārūpyaikatvam apy uta*  
*dīyamānaṁ na gṛhṇanti vinā mat-sevanaṁ janāḥ*

**A pure devotee does not accept any kind of liberation—sālokya, sārṣṭi, sāmīpya, sārūpya or ekatva—even though they are offered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. SB 3.29.13**

The following verse expresses the idea of “his own people” explicitly:

*tasmān mac-charaṇaṁ goṣṭhaṁ man-nāthaṁ mat-parigraham*  
*gopāye svātma-yogena so ‘yaṁ me vrata āhitaḥ*

**I must therefore protect the cowherd community by my transcendental potency, for I am their shelter, I am their master, and indeed they are my own family. After all, I have taken a vow to protect my devotees. SB 10.25.18**

They are included within himself. If the word *jana* means people in general, then he is merciful to all. He would show himself and the spiritual world to everyone. But that did not happen. Thus the word *jana* should be taken to mean “his own people.” My people in Vraja think that they are wandering around in the material world traveling in different species by karma caused by desire and ignorance without any goal. They do not know my form which I desire to show them. This is because they are under the influence of my pastimes as a human. They were not aware of his position or their position.

*eṣāṁ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṁ deva rāteti naś*  
*ceto viśva-phalāt phalaṁ tvad-aparaṁ kutrāpy ayan muhyati*  
*sad-veṣād iva pūtanāpi sa-kulā tvām eva devāpitā*  
*yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte*

**My mind becomes bewildered just trying to think of what reward other than you could be found anywhere. You are the embodiment of all benedictions, which you bestow upon these residents of the cowherd community of Vṛndāvana. You have already arranged to give yourself to Pūtanā and her family members in exchange for her disguising herself as a devotee. So what is left for you to give these devotees of Vṛndāvana, whose homes, wealth, friends, dear relations, bodies, children and very lives and hearts are all dedicated only to you? SB 10.14.35**

Thus Nanda acted as follows:

*nandas tv atīndriyaṁ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam*  
*kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṁ teṣāṁ jñātibhyo vismito ’bravīt*

**Nanda Mahārāja had been astonished to see for the first time the great opulence of Varuṇa, the ruler of the ocean planet, and also to see how Varuṇa and his servants had offered such humble respect to Kṛṣṇa. Nanda described all this to his fellow cowherd men. SB 10.28.11**

Therefore Kṛṣṇa who was their own family member showed them the planet and had them attain that planet. Using airplanes is insignificant for that attainment. However it is stated to cause astonishment in common people and to hide the real truth from them. This is the proper explanation, for concerning Vṛndāvana it is said *āvirbhāvas tirobāvo bhaven bhaven me ‘tra yuge yuge:* I appear and disappear in Vṛndāvana in every *yuga*. (*Gautamīya-tantra*)*Tejo-mayam idaṁ brahman adṛśyaṁ carma-cakṣuṣā:*  this place Vṛndāvana is effulgent, and not seen by the material eye. (*Gautamīya-tantra*)

The cowherd men then were returned to Vraja. This indicates their eternal position which is also indicated by the text *go-gopa-gopikā-saṅge yatra krīḍati kaṁsahā:* there Kṛṣṇa plays eternally with the cows, cowherds and *gopīs.*

The word *kaṁsa-hā* in the text should indicate the past. It is similar to *vṛtra-hā*. In this situation, the method by which the women of Vraja attained Kṛṣṇa (after he departed) should be considered. In going to Mathurā he promised he would return, though it would be after some time. (SB 10.39.35)

*dhārayanty ati-kṛcchreṇa prāyaḥ prāṇān kathañcana*  
*pratyāgamana-sandeśair ballavyo me mad-ātmikāḥ*

**Simply because I have promised to return to them, my fully devoted cowherd girlfriends struggle to maintain their lives somehow or other. SB 10.46.6**

Through Uddhava he sent a message:

*bhavatīnāṁ viyogo me na hi sarvātmanā kvacit*

**You are never actually separated from me, for I am the Soul of all creation. (SB 10.47.29)**

Being dissatisfied with this message, then repeated “me” three times to emphasize himself.

*mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛtsnaṁ vimuktāśeṣa-vṛtti yat*  
*anusmarantyo māṁ nityam acirān mām upaiṣyatha*

**Because your minds are totally absorbed in me and free from all other engagement, you remember me always, and so you will very soon have me again in your presence. SB 10.47.36**

Then at Kurukṣetra he instructed them.

*mayi bhaktir hi bhūtānām amṛtatvāya kalpate*  
*diṣṭyā yad āsīn mat-sneho bhavatīnāṁ mad-āpanaḥ*

**Rendering devotional service to e qualifies any living being for eternal life. But by your good fortune you have developed a special loving attitude toward me, by which you have obtained me. SB 10.82.44**

When they were dissatisfied they then pleaded:

*āhuś ca te nalina-nābha padāravindaṁ*  
*yogeśvarair hṛdi vicintyam agādha-bodhaiḥ*  
*saṁsāra-kūpa-patitottaraṇāvalambaṁ*  
*gehaṁ juṣām api manasy udiyāt sadā naḥ*

**Dear Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower, your lotus feet are the only shelter for those who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshiped and meditated upon by great mystic yogīs and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also be awakened within our hearts, although we are only ordinary persons engaged in household affairs. SB 10.82.48**

The meaning is this. O lotus navel lord! Your lotus feet should arise in your minds. “What is surprising about this from women with great anurāga?” The best of yogīs meditate in their heart on these feet, not us. They have deep intelligence, not disturbed even if they do not see you. We are not like that. As soon as we begin thinking of those feet we faint.

“By thinking of those lotus feet you should be free of the pain of separation just as the yogī becomes free of the pains of *saṁsāra.”* Those feet are the shelter of deliverance for those who have fallen in the well of *saṁsāra.* But we have drowned in the ocean of separation. When we think of those feet we simply experience further separation.

“Then come and look at my feet in Dvārakā, until I come to Vraja.” Worried that he will say this they say “Because we are women we are dependent on others in the house.” Therefore if they come and show us your feet constantly, we will be delivered.

Then what happened? Considering the anxiety of the listener at the end of the chapter Śukadeva then says:

*tathānugṛhya bhagavān gopīnāṁ sa gurur gatiḥ*  
*yudhiṣṭhiram athāpṛcchat sarvāṁś ca suhṛdo ’vyayam*

**Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa, the spiritual master of the gopīs and the very purpose of their life, showed them his mercy. He then met with Yudhiṣṭhira and all his other relatives and inquired from them about their welfare. SB 10.83.1**

As they desired, he showed mercy. As their guru, he instructed them what to do in order to attain their desire. What was the desire? Their desire was to attain him (*gatiḥ*), the highest result. Kṛṣṇa then inquired about Yudhiṣṭhira who was sitting at the door for a long time, and who could not be considered like an ordinary devotee, and then all other friends. Filled with great separation, they attained him.

In this manner, Kṛṣṇa speaks in the Eleventh Canto, Twelfth Chapter:

*rāmeṇa sārdhaṁ mathurāṁ praṇīte*  
*śvāphalkinā mayy anurakta-cittāḥ*  
*vigāḍha-bhāvena na me viyoga-*  
*tīvrādhayo ’nyaṁ dadṛśuḥ sukhāya*

**The residents of Vṛndāvana, headed by the** ***gopīs,*** **were always completely attached to me with deepest love. Therefore, when my uncle Akrūra brought my brother Balarāma and me to the city of Mathurā, the residents of Vṛndāvana suffered extreme mental distress because of separation from me and could not find any other source of happiness.**

*tās tāḥ kṣapāḥ preṣṭhatamena nītā*  
*mayaiva vṛndāvana-gocareṇa*  
*kṣaṇārdha-vat tāḥ punar aṅga tāsāṁ*  
*hīnā mayā kalpa-samā babhūvuḥ*

**Dear Uddhava, all of those nights that the gopīs spent with me, their most dearly beloved, in the land of Vṛndāvana seemed to them to pass in less than a moment. Bereft of my association, however, the gopīs felt that those same nights dragged on forever, as if each night were equal to a day of Brahmā. SB 11.12.10.11**

The verbs *dadṛṣuḥ* (they did not see anything for happiness) and *babhūvuḥ* (the nights became a *kalpa*) in the past tense indicate that those actions are completed. This means that in the present they see happiness, and the nights are not like a *kalpa.* Thus at the present, they have no separation. “It is not seen that they attained the Lord. Why do you say that they attained him?” They attained a special *aprakaṭa* manifestation of Vṛndāvana. That is stated:

*tā nāvidan mayy anuṣaṅga-baddha-*  
*dhiyaḥ svam ātmānam adas tathedam*  
*yathā samādhau munayo ’bdhi-toye*  
*nadyaḥ praviṣṭā iva nāma-rūpe*

**Their minds bound by constant association with me, they were not aware of their bodies, of this world or the next world, just as sages in** ***samādhi*** **are not aware of the world, and just as rivers, on entering the ocean, lose their names and forms. SB 11.12.12**

Those women (*tāḥ)* who were suffering great separation, whose minds were bound to me, which happened after I killed Dantavakra, did not know the self which is the object of possessiveness (*svam*) and *ahaṅkāra (ātmānam*) produced by karma, in the *prakaṭa* pastimes (*adaḥ*) and the *aprakaṭa* pastimes (*idam*). They knew the two as one with the self. An example is given to show the two types of pastimes becoming one with the self. The sages in *samādhi,* in the fourth state, overcome with this state, are not aware of the difference between the *ātmā* and the waking, sleeping and dreaming states.

An example is given to illustrate not seeing difference in the pastimes which are the object of possessiveness. The rivers do not distinguish difference between their coming from the earth or from a lake. Without regard for their origin they enter into the water of the ocean. Similarly the *gopīs* did not know difference in their position of *prakaṭa* and *aprakaṭa* pastimes, but entered into me. The examples of merging are applicable in that portion which illustrates lack of awareness of difference in pastimes, and not in all things. Their sense of identity is like that of the Lord being absorbed in his pastimes. *Lokavat tu līlā-kaivalyam*: the creation of the world is absorption of the Lord in one pastime, as in ordinary life. (*Vedānta-sutra* 2.1.33) *Nāma-rūpa* is a *samāhāra-dvandva.* The *gopīs* acted as if entering into a special *aprakaṭa* manifestation, with particular name and form, and also acted as if not entering. There is no difference between the *prakaṭa* and *aprakaṭa* manifestations for them. Their experience is similar to the experiences of the sixteen thousand maidens after their marriage to Kṛṣṇa.

In this way the author’s opinion has been shown to accord with the *Bhāgavatam.* The following should be further considered. In attaining the Lord in Vraja, was their love in married or unmarried form according to the author? It is recognized love of the *pati.* This is shown in another way in *Lalita-mādhava* to establish *rasa* (they marry in New Vṛndāvana within Dvārakā) and is also shown by the title of the last act, Fulfillment of Desires, in which marriage is accomplished.

(In terms of the *Bhāgavatam*) the marriages with the *gopīs* does not take place in Dvārakā, what to speak of earthly Vraja. There are no proofs of that Rādhā personally went to Dvārakā. What then would be the difference between Dvārakā and Vraja? And if Kṛṣṇa married them all and brought them all to Vraja with the permission of Rādhā, they would behave in the same way (with great longing) and not otherwise, even after being brought to Vṛndāvana, for, by the desire of the Lord, *rasa* is accomplished in Vraja.

When Kṛsṇa leaves for Mathurā this is their behaviour:

*nivārayāmaḥ samupetya mādhavaṁ*  
*kiṁ no ’kariṣyan kula-vṛddha-bāndhavāḥ*  
*mukunda-saṅgān nimiṣārdha-dustyajād*  
*daivena vidhvaṁsita-dīna-cetasām*
