**Let us directly approach Mādhava and stop him from going. What can our family elders and other relatives do to us? Now that fate is separating us from Mukunda, our hearts are already wretched, for we cannot bear to give up His association even for a fraction of a second. SB 10.39.28**

*evaṁ bruvāṇā virahāturā bhṛśaṁ*  
*vraja-striyaḥ kṛṣṇa-viṣakta-mānasāḥ*  
*visṛjya lajjāṁ ruruduḥ sma su-svaraṁ*  
*govinda dāmodara mādhaveti*

**After speaking these words, the ladies of Vraja, who were so attached to Kṛṣṇa, felt extremely agitated by their imminent separation from Him. They forgot all shame and loudly cried out, “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” SB 10.39.31**

Their behavior, their manifested *bhāvas* were like this from the beginning. And it will continue in this way in the future.

*tā man-manaskā tṛṣṭ-prāṇā mad-arthe tyakta-daihikāḥ*  
*mām eva dayitaṁ preṣṭham ātmānaṁ manasā gatāḥ*  
*ye tyakta-loka-dharmāś ca mad-arthe tān bibharmy aham*

**The minds of those** ***gopīs*** **are always absorbed in me, and their very lives are ever devoted to m. For my sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies, renouncing ordinary happiness in this life, as well as religious duties necessary for such happiness in the next life. I alone am their dearmost beloved and, indeed, their very self. Therefore I take it upon myself to sustain them in all circumstances. SB 10.46.4**

*iti gopyo hi govinde gata-vāk-kāya-mānasāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇa-dūte samāyāte uddhave tyakta-laukikāḥ*  
*gāyantyaḥ prīya-karmāṇi rudantyaś ca gata-hriyaḥ*  
*tasya saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya yāni kaiśora-bālyayoḥ*

**Thus speaking, the** ***gopīs,*** **whose words, bodies and minds were fully dedicated to Lord Govinda, put aside all their regular work now that Kṛṣṇa’s messenger, Śrī Uddhava, had arrived among them. Constantly remembering the activities their beloved Kṛṣṇa had performed in his childhood and youth, they sang about them and cried without shame. SB 10.47.9-10**

*āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ*  
*vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām*  
*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The** ***gopīs*** **of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the** ***gopīs*** **trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. SB 10.47.61**

*mātaraṁ pitaraṁ bhrātṝn patīn putrān svasṝn api*  
*yad-arthe jahima dāśārha dustyajān sva-janān prabho*

**For Kṛṣṇa’s sake, O descendant of Dāśārha, we abandoned our mothers, fathers, brothers, husbands, children and sisters, even though these family relations are difficult to give up. SB 10.65.11**

It became impossible to stop such *rati* in countless women. If they were married to other husbands through illusion in Vraja, the *rasa* produced would be transformed into something disgusting or into something most disagreeable. In the assembly of Parīkṣit filled with *jñana* and *aiśvarya*, just as *rasa* was established by rejecting *upapati* love through *jñāna* and *aiśvarya,* so in the assembly of Nanda filled with pastimes of people upholding *dharma, rasa* should be established, giving up *upapati* love through rules of *dharma*.

*bhagavān api tā rātṛīḥ śāradotphulla-mallikāḥ*  
*vīkṣya rantuṁ manaś cakre yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full in all opulences, yet upon seeing those autumn nights scented with blossoming jasmine flowers, he turned his mind toward loving affairs. To fulfill his purposes he employed his internal potency. SB 10.29.1**

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against him. SB 10.33.37**

Things manifest by the power of *yogamāyā.* She is the resolver. Just as she makes arrangements for novelty in the Lord’s pastimes and arranges so that hatred is avoided, so she arranges to that there is no slander of the pastimes, since their natures as *sakhīs* follows after the *aprakaṭa* pastimes. In *Brahma-saṁhitā* it is explained *nija-rūpatayā lakābhiḥ*: he accepts them as his own wives. They are married. In the *Gautamīya-tantra*, while explaining the ten syllable mantra, after explaining two meanings according to *māyā* and *aiśvarya,* a third and last explanation is given.

*aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnāṁ patir eva vā \|*  
*nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa is the husband of many cowherd women who are perfect in many appearances in the material world. He who is the son of Nanda, Nanda-nandana, increases the bliss of the three worlds.**

Considering this, the author has also considered the following verses:

*laghutvam atra yat proktaṁ tat tu prākṛta-nāyake \|*  
*na kṛṣṇe rasa-niryāsa-svādārtham avatārini \|\|*

**The** ***upapati*** **described in disparaging terms is the materialistic lover and does not apply to Kṛṣṇa, who appeared in the world to taste** ***madhura-rasa*** **in this way.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.21**

*neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā*  
*tad gokulāmbujadṛśāṁ kulam antarena \|*  
*āśāṁsayā rasavidher avatāritānāṁ*  
*kaṁsāriṇā rasikamaṇḍalaśekhareṇa*

**The lotus-eyed** ***gopīs*** **of Gokula descended to this material world to enjoy amorous pastimes with Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of those expert at relishing transcendental mellows, and the enemy of King Kaṁsa. Except for those** ***gopīs*****, learned scholars and philosophers do not consider amorous affairs between a married woman and a paramour to be good or auspicious.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **5.3**

Thus the author accepts the position that when the Lord comes as *avatāra,* he acts as *upapati* with others’ wives, while at other times he does not act in this way.

After saying *tā nāvidan mayy anuṣaṅga-baddha-dhiyā* (SB 11.12.12) Kṛṣna himself says:

*mat-kāmā ramaṇaṁ jāram asvarūpa-vido ’balāḥ*  
*brahma māṁ paramaṁ prāpuḥ saṅgāc chata-sahasraśaḥ*

**All those hundreds of thousands of** ***gopīs*****, desiring me, the supreme Brahman, not knowing my form of power, attained me, a lover and a husband, who gave them pleasure because of my association. SB 11.12.13**

The meaning of the verse is this. In the statement “He glances at great, attractive Bhīṣma (*bhīṣmam udāraṁ darśanīyam kaṭaṁ karoti*) the phrase *kaṭaṁ karoti*, formed of verb (*karoti)* and object *(kaṭam*) acts as a verb (*kaṭaṁ karoti*) with Bhīṣma as the object. Similarly *brahma prāpuḥ* should be taken as a verb (they attained Brahman) with *ramaṇaṁ jāram* as its object. Thus the meaning is “They attained the supreme Brahman who is the supremely attractive lover.” The order of words is significant also. The emphasis is on the first phrase *ramaṇaṁ jāram* as in a sentence like the following where the first phrase *pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ* has most importance:

*pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ sūpāntāḥ pāyasādayaḥ*  
*saṁyāvāpūpa-śaṣkulyaḥ sarva-dohaś ca gṛhyatām*

**Let many different kinds of food be cooked, from sweet rice to vegetable soups! Many kinds of fancy cakes, both baked and fried, should be prepared. And all the available milk products should be taken for this sacrifice. SB 10.24.26**

Or, another example is “He performs sacrifice. He cooks the pot of barley.”

The word *tā* is the subject from the previous verse. They attained Brahman, but not the impersonal Brahman, since *parama* can mean “he who possesses Lakṣmī.” According to the scriptural statement *brahmaṇo hi pratiṣtḥāham:* I am the source of Brahman (BG 14.27), Brahman means the form of Bhagavān. Similarly *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* (6.7.76) says *śubhāśrayasya cittasya sarvagasyācalātmanaḥ:* Viṣṇu is the shelter of all auspiciousness and the Brahman. To dispel the doubt that this Brahman may also appear at the time of Bhagavān’s appearance, the word *mām* is added. Similarly it is said *mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛtsnam*: absorbing your mind in me (SB 10.4.36) and *mayi bhaktir hi bhūtānām amṛtatvāya kalpate*: rendering devotional service to me qualifies any living being for eternal life. (SB 10.82.44)

They attained two different forms by having different *bhāvas* at different times. To give this understanding two descriptive terms are supplied to give particulars of their different realizations: *mat-kāmā ramaṇam* and *jāram.* The conventional meaning of *ramana* is a husband and *jāra* means an *upapati. Viśva-prakāśa* says *ramaṇa* means the root of *paṭola* and a dear person (*priya*). *Amara-koṣa* says dear person *(priya*) means a husband and *jāra* means *upapati*. They did not know my *svarūpa (asvarūpa-vidaḥ).* They did not know that I am their eternal beloved, since they were bewildered by my *līlā-śakti.* Being in that condition, they attained me as their *upapati (jāra)* and as their husband (*ramaṇam*), having love for me (*mat-kāmāḥ*)—thinking “Identifying anyone else as a husband should disappear as a dream” and “Kṛṣṇa should make his appearance (*prādurbhāva),* as if having him present in a waking state.” Śrīdhara Svāmī agrees with this: they thought of me as their *upapati*  According to the desire-- according to *tat-kratu-nyāya:* one attains the form upon which one meditates (*Vedānta-sūtra* 4.3.15), the Lord makes his appearance. *Ye yathā māṁ prapadyante*: according to your particular desire, I respond. (BG 4.11) Kṛṣṇa, having seen the *gopīs* himself, gave those examples of the yogī and the river.

The following should also be considered:

*yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṁ vane ’smin vraja āsthitāḥ*  
*alabdha-rāsāḥ kalyāṇyo māpur mad-vīrya-cintayā*

**Although some** ***gopīs*** **had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the** ***rāsa*** **dance to sport with me at night in the forest, they were nonetheless fortunate. Indeed, they attained me by thinking of my potent pastimes. SB 10.47.38**

They could not attain *upapati* love just by giving up their bodies and their husbands. My mercy is absolutely necessary to attain me as either *upapati* or husband. To indicate this, he uses the word *abalāḥ.* This means “without strength, helpless.” Without my help they did not attain me. But see the greatness of my eternal dear *gopīs.* Because of association with those eternal *gopīs* thousands of others still attained me.

This should also be considered:

*tāsāṁ nitya-priyāṇām avataraṇa-vaśād vismṛtātma-sthitīnām*  
*apy antaḥ sava-svabhāvād aghavijiti rati-śrī-bhṛtāṁ nitya-kānte*  
*viśvastānām amuṣmāt para-sadana-gati kleśa-bhājāṁ varītum*  
*taṁ tṛṣṇā sāpi na syād ahaha sahaphalā kaḥ pratpīyātamutra*

**The** ***gopīs,*** **his eternal beloveds, who forgot their positions when they appeared on earth, possessed within a wealth of love for their eternal lover Kṛṣṇa by their very natures and faithful to him, underwent suffering by being separated from him. Who will not believe that such thirst to marry him would be fulfilled in the next life?**

In *Gopāla-campu,* with the marriage, *samañjasa* takes place as in *Lalita-mādhava:*

*dampatyaa vraja-subhruvam aghajita yaj jatam etat paraa*  
*kavyasya prathitena nirvahaea-kat kia tv enu ragasya ca \| iti \|\|*  
*tad etad ākarṇya tu varṇyamāṇaṁ vivāha-vṛttaṁ cira-kāla-vṛttam \|*  
*tām eva sākṣād iva vīkṣya rātriṁ rahasy amū dhāmani dīvyataḥ sma \|\|*

**The exalted marriages that took place between the women of Vraja and Kṛṣṇa are not widely publicized by poets, but continued to produce great** ***rāga in*** **them. That** ***anurāga*** **in marriage is the abode of association without obstacles. Giving that up marriage as one’s shelter, one’s life becomes useless. 2.35.15-151**

*prāg-dūra-priyatā tato guru-jana-dhvasta-prayatnātmatā*  
*tat paścāc chruti-loka-laṅghi-rabhasād guptā priyāṅgīkṛtiḥ \|*  
*tasmād dūra-mahā-viyoga-ciratā tat-prāntam udvāhataḥ*  
*prāptaṁ cen mithunaṁ mitho hari-ramā-rūpaṁ sukhaṁ kiṁ param \|\|*

**First there was suffering in** ***pūrva-rāga*** **and then destruction of attempts to meet by the elders. Then they met by trespassing the norms of scripture and public opinion. Then they suffered great separation at a distance. If they then got married, how much happiness Kṛṣṇa and the** ***gopīs*** **would attain together!** ***Gopāla-campu*** **1.33.350**

*kṛṣṇaṁ kāntatayānupetya purataḥ svaṁ nitya-kāntaṁ tu tās*  
*tatrāpy anyakare nipatya ca balān nirvāhya dharmaṁ nijam \|*  
*tatrāpīṣṭam amuṁ kathañcana rahaḥ prāpyāpi viṣitāḥ*  
*puṇyāt taṁ patim etya śarma-valanāṁ saṁbhṛtya nṛtyaṁ vyadhuḥ \|\|*

**Not attaining their eternal husband Kṛṣṇa as their lover, the** ***gopīs*** **were forcibly married to others and maintained their** ***dharma*** **of chastity (by cheating them with** ***māyā*** **forms), but met him somehow privately. Then they were separated when he went to Mathurā, but by their good fortune attained him as their husband and gave happiness to the whole universe.** ***Gopāla-campu*** **2.37.203**

*namunaa sahajanuraga-vibhuta bhe-nirmita kia nu bher*  
*laighya syan na tu veti tat-prabalata-jianartham antau kata \|*  
*taj-jiataa nija-dharma-setu-dalanat tasyas tatha vismatis*  
*tadvad bhati yatha pareknita-vaco’py agre muhur dacyate \|\|*

**The attraction of the** ***gopīs*** **for Kṛṣṇa was not generated from fear but was their very nature. They had to overcome their fear to fulfill that attraction. That attraction was kept within so that no one would know its great strength. If fear arose from trespassing** ***dharma,*** **they forgot about it (after marriage), just as pure gold may be tested by fire, but remains the same.** ***Gopāla-campu*** **2.36.27**

*kaṁsārer akuto-bhayasya na bhayaṁ tad-bhakta-vṛndasya ca hrīḥ*  
*kintu asti samasta-sad-guṇa-maṇes tat-subhruvāḥ kiṁ punaḥ*  
*tatra hrīr duritodbhavā yadi tadā nindāspadaṁ yady asau*  
*gopyo narmaṇi gopana-sthiti-mayī puṣṇāty adas tarhi tu*

**There is no fear in Kṛṣṇa and his host of devotees. But there is shyness in the jewel of all good qualities Kṛṣṇa and his** ***gopīs.*** **If shyness were to produce sin then criticism would occur. But since Kṛṣṇa and the** ***gopīs*** **hide their feelings with joking, the situation is nourished.**

*anyāḥ santu sahasraśaḥ patiparā nāmūḥ stuve yā nijaṁ*  
*lokaṁ dharmam api śritā na hi punaḥ svaṁ svaṁ patiṁ kevalam \|*  
*gopīh staumi jana-prasiddham api yās taṁ taṁ vihāya sphuṭaṁ*

**Let there be thousands of chaste married women! I do not praise them for they took shelter of not only their husbands but of others’ opinions and rules of** ***dharma.*** **I instead praise the** ***gopīs*** **who gave up their fame as chaste wives following** ***dharma*** **and, discerning clearly, accepted Kṛṣṇa as their husband by the power of their conscious attraction to him.** ***Gopāla-campu*** **2.32.55**

*sāvitrī brahmaṇaḥ strī hima-giri-tanayā candra-maules tathā mā*  
*śrī-viṣṇor asya rukmiṇy api sumukhi bhaved bāḍham akṣṇāṁ sukhāya \|*  
*rūpaṁ svasyāpi vismāyaka-mayam abhitaḥ śobhayan svīyam āsīd*  
*rāse yāsāṁ rucā tā yadi na hi vivahed astu rādhā tu mūrdhni \|\|22\|\|*

**Brahmā’s wife is Sāvitrī, Śiva’s wife is Durgā, Viṣṇu’s wife is Lakṣmī and Kṛṣṇa’s wife is Rukmiṇī. These marriages give great happiness to the world. But if Kṛṣṇa were not to marry those women by whose beauty his own astonishing beauty spread everywhere in the** ***rāsa*** **dance, with the Rādhā at the chief, what use are those marriages?** ***Gopāla-campu*** **2.35.30**

Sometimes worship is seen in which pastimes occurring previous to killing of Kaṁsa are portrayed as if they were in the present, after the killing. (They may meditate on the following pastime.)

*evaṁ vihāraiḥ kaumāraiḥ kaumāraṁ jahatur vraje*  
*nilāyanaiḥ setu-bandhair markaṭotplavanādibhiḥ*

**In this way Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma passed their childhood age in Vrajabhūmi by engaging in activities of childish play, such as playing hide-and-seek, constructing a make-believe bridge on the ocean, and jumping here and there like monkeys. SB 10.11.59**

Though such pastimes took place in the past, like pastimes of other *avatāras* in the past*,* that worship reveals those pastimes, following after the special nature of *bhakti* and the devotee.

*tvaṁ bhakti-yoga-paribhāvita-hṛt-saroja*  
*āsse śrutekṣita-patho nanu nātha puṁsām*  
*yad-yad-dhiyā ta urugāya vibhāvayanti*  
*tat-tad-vapuḥ praṇayase sad-anugrahāya*

**O my Lord, your devotees can see you through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and you take our seat there. you are so merciful to your devotees that you manifest yourself in the particular eternal form of transcendence in which they always think of you. SB 3.9.11**

Thus it is seen that some householders worship Kṛṣṇa in his infant form, even after he killed Kaṁsa. Within the *sambhoga* pastimes at the *sampanna* level there is scope for such pastimes which follow individual desires, but not in *samṛddhimān.* It should be understood that these previous pastimes shown according to the devotee’s particular *bhakti* are lesser than the *sampanna* pastimes, what to speak of the *samṛddhimān* pastimes.

Practitioners of mantras following in *parampara* give an eternal status to some pastimes which are similar to pastimes in the *prakaṭa* manifestation. But not all *prakaṭa* pastimes can take on an eternal status since they would create a contradiction by producing great suffering, by mixing the eternal pastimes with inferior elements filled with impending disturbance. An example is Kṛṣṇa entering Kāliya’s lake. Thus it is said:

*yoga eva bhaved eṣa vicitraḥ ko’pi mādanaḥ \|*  
*yad-vilāsā virājante nitya-līlāḥ sahasradhā \|\|225\|\|*

**During union,** ***mādana*** **takes on unprecedented astonishing qualities, whose effects manifest as thousands of continuous pastimes.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **14.225**

In the above verse, it is stated that union alone gives happiness by showing thousands of pastimes. (Pastimes mixed with anxiety would not give such happiness.) Some devotees counter this idea. Let others practice the eternal pastimes which are like pictures, since they lack full pastimes. The worship using the pastimes on earth with pastimes is sequence of time produce the highest *rasa.* This is shown by the author in *Vidagdha-mādhava* where he depicts the absorption of previous exalted devotees in the appearances of the Lord.

As well it is said:

*rasika-jana sukhārthaṁ sādhayām āsa śaśvat*  
*kramam anu rasa-pūram sūdavat kṛṣṇa-candraḥ*  
*kramam anurasayan yaḥ pūrtiṁ āpnoti-pūrtyāṁ*  
*saphalam iha paraṁ sāt tatra vaidaghyam asya*

**Kṛṣṇa, like a cook, continually arranges step by step full** ***rasa*** **in order to give pleasure to the** ***rasikas.*** **The** ***rasikas,*** **tasting everything step by step, attains full satisfaction. The** ***rasika*** **attains success by that full satisfaction, and becomes an expert taster.** ***Gopāla-campu*** **2.37.235**

This is also stated in *Bhāgavatam:*

*prapañcaṁ niṣprapañco ’pi viḍambayasi bhū-tale*  
*prapanna-janatānanda-sandohaṁ prathituṁ prabho*

**My dear master, although you have nothing to do with material existence, you come to this earth and imitate material life just to expand the varieties of ecstatic enjoyment for your surrendered devotees. SB 10.14.35**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the previous example, a statue of Kṛṣṇa was thought to be Kṛṣṇa. In that verse also, the difficulty of the couple seeing each other--the control exerted by Rukmiṇī, was not clear. Therefore another example of *samṛddhimān* is given.

Seeing Rādhā directly after a long separation of great distance, with impossibility of seeing her for all that time, Kṛṣṇa speaks with choked voice, agitated by bliss. I have searched for some sign of you throughout the fourteen worlds. Searching for news of your *sakhīs,* your cloth or ornaments by means of Nārada and other wise men, now I have attained you. You proclaim the beauty in all the worlds and Vaikuṇṭha. Just as a woman is illuminated by a chief jewel on one of her limbs, so all the forests are illuminate by you situated in one place there. *Cañcatā* means wandering.

### Text 209

***atha gauṇa-sambhogaḥ***  
***channa-prakāśa-bhedena kaiścid eṣāṁ dvirūpatā \|***  
***iṣṭāpy atra na hi proktā nātyullāsakarī yataḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Secondary union: The four types of** ***sambhoga*** **are divided by some people into covered and uncovered types. Though approved, the two divisions are not described here because they do not give great bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Of the types of *sambhoga (eṣām),* there is a covered type that gives *rasa* to the wife. The two divisions are not described here.

### Text 210

***atha gauṇaḥ—***  
***svapne prāpti-viśeṣo’sya harer gauṇa itīryate \|***  
***svapno dvidhātra sāmānya-viśeṣatvena kīrtitaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Secondary Union: Attaining the Lord in dreams is called** ***gauṇa-sambhoga.*** **Dreams are of two types: general and particular.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

After the perfection of *rasa* in the whole work has been described in *samṛddhimān*, semblances of the four types of *sambhoga* are described. *Gauṇa* or secondary means it does not have the same significance as *mukhya-sambhoga.*

### Text 211-212

***sāmānyaḥ sa tu yaḥ pūrvaṁ kathito vyabhicāriṣu \|***  
***viśeṣaḥ khalu jāgaryā nirviśeṣo mahādbhutaḥ \|\|211\|\|***  
***bhāvautkaṇṭhye-mayo hy eṣa caturdhā pūrvavan mataḥ \|\|212\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**General dreams were described among the** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas.*** **Special dreams are those experienced in a state indistinguishable from waking state. These are most astonishing. Full of** ***autkaṇṭhya*** **among** ***vyabhicāri-bhāvas*****, this type is divided into** ***saṅkṣipta, saṅkīrṇa, sampanna*** **and** ***samṛddhimān*** **as previously.**

### Text 213

***tatra svapne saṅkṣipto, yathā—***  
***vihāraṁ kurvāṇas taraṇi-tanayā-tīra-vipine***  
***navāmbhoda-śreṇī-madhurima-viḍambi-dyuti-bharaḥ \|***  
***vidagdhānāṁ cūḍāmaṇir anudinaṁ cumbati mukhaṁ***  
***mama svapne ko’pi priya-sakhi balīyān nava-yuvā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Saṅkṣipta*** **dream: O dear** ***sakhī!*** **Every day in a dream an indescribable strong young man, whose bodily effulgence mocks the splendor of a host of fresh clouds, a most expert playboy, dallies in the forest on the bank of the Yamunā and kisses my mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā in *pūrva-rāga* speaks to Viśākhā.

### Text 214

***atha svapne saṅkīrṇo, yathā—***  
***sakhi kruddhā mā bhūr laghur api na doṣaḥ sumukhi me***  
***na mānāgni-jvālām aśamayam ahaṁ tām asamaye \|***  
***sa dhūrtas te svapne rasa-vṛṣṭiṁ mayi tathā***  
***yato vistīrṇāpi svayam iyam ayāsīd upaśamam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Saṅkīṛṇa*** **dream: O beautiful-faced friend! Do not be angry with me. I am not even slightly fault. I have not inappropriately extinguished the blazing fire of my anger. In my dream, your swindler friend showered nectar on me such that the widespread anger has disappeared on its own.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Asamaye* means “at the wrong time.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some *mugdhā sakhī* speaks to her friend. *Laghu* means small. The fire flame of anger indicates they have separated because of a quarrel.  *Samaye* means “at this moment, which is the wrong time.” The anger was widespread.

### Text 215

***atha svapne sampannaḥ, yathā haṁsadūte (105)—***  
***prayāto māṁ hitvā yadi kaṭhinacūḍāmaṇirasau***  
***paryātu svacchandaṁ mama samaya-dharmaḥ kila gatiḥ \|***  
***idaṁ soḍhuṁ kā vā prabhavati yataḥ svapnakapaṭād-***  
***ihāyāto vṛndāvanabhuvi balān māṁ ramayati \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Sampanna*** **dream, from** ***Haṁsadūta:*** **If that crest-jewel of all hard-hearted men had rejected me by going off, let him go as he wishes. Death should be my shelter. But who can tolerate this? On the pretext of a dream he comes to Vṛndāvana and forcibly enjoys me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Samaya-dharma* means “keeping his promise to come back.” *Amara-koṣa* says *samaya* means an oath, time, conclusion and agreement.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Lalitā. *Samaya-dharma* means death. According to *Amara-koṣa* the word *kāla-dharma* means death, and *kāla* and *samaya* have the same meaning. He comes on the pretext of a dream. I have a right to be angry since he went to Mathurā to enjoy the women there, rejecting me. What fault do I have? Being angry, I have not dressed up and against my will he enjoy me. One should not use force with an angry person. How can this be tolerated? One may argue that this is an example of *samṛddhimān,* not *sampanna*, since Kṛṣṇa has gone far away. However, the two of them are not both under others’ control (Kṛṣṇa is still unmarried, and when in Vṛndāvana identifies himself as he was previously). Thus it is *sampanna*. Instead of *yataḥ* sometimes *yadyapi* (even though) is seen. “In waking state, she knows that it was wrong for her to leave for Mathurā, but while dreaming I can enjoy with her as previously since she forgets that we are separated.” This is how he is thinking.

### Text 216

***atha svāpna-samṛddhimān, yathā lalita-mādhave (7.11)—***  
***cirād adya svapne mama vividha-yatnād upagate***  
***prapede govindaḥ sakhi nayanayor aṅgana-bhuvam \|***  
***gṛhītvā hā hanta tvaritam atha tasminn api rathaṁ***  
***kathaṁ pratyāsannaḥ sa khalu puruṣo rāja-puruṣaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Samṛddhimān*** **dream, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **After repeated attempts over a long time, Govinda finally appeared before me in a dream, but alas, then a cruel messenger of the king quickly put him on a chariot and departed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The first half of the verse should be understood to be *samṛddhimān.* There is extreme enjoyment (*upabhogātirekam*) and absence of fear arising from control of others. Others are a cause of not meeting in separation at a distance, but when they meet, the fear of others disappears. 9 Because it is possible to manifest strength of these characteristics in dreams sufficiently, it is *samṛddhimān.* The second half of the verse however is not *samṛddhimān.* It is *vipralambha.* *Ayam paruṣaḥ* means Akrūra in the future.

*yadā taṁ kārūṣam pathi katavatā kaṁsa-ripunā*  
*vraje pratyāyate pramada-patatā vyāptam akhilam*  
*tataḥ prāk yad rādhā vidhu-mukhi manorājya-kalitaṁ*  
*jajalpa svapnāntas tad idam udayat citrayati naḥ*

**“When Kṛṣṇa, having killed Dantavakra on the road, returned to Vraja, he spread joy to all.” When moon-faced Rādhā uttered this fanciful statement before the event took place, after a dream, it astonished us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While situated in Nava-vṛndāvana in Dvārakā, Rādhā tells Nava-vṛndā how she saw Kṛṣṇa in a dream. It is *samṛddhimān* because both parties have difficulty in seeing each other because of others. The second half of the verse refers to Akrūra.

### Text 217

***tulya-svarūpa evāyaṁ prodyan yūnor dvayor api \|***  
***ūṣā-niruddhayor yadvat kvacit svapno’py abādhitaḥ \|\|217\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes there are dreams in which the couple simultaneously dream of each other, as in the case of Ūṣā and Aniruddha.**

### Text 218

***ataeva hi siddhānāṁ svapne’pi paramādbhute \|***  
***prāptāni maṇḍanādīni dṛśyante jāgare’pi ca \|\|218\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes even perfected devotees in waking state have most astonishing dreams in which they obtain ornaments and other things.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

There are two types of dreams: a dream while awake and waking state resembling a dream. The first type has been demonstrated. The second type is now defined in verses 217 and 218.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“How can there be the quality of ‘difficulty in seeing each other’ in a dream with *samṛddhimān sambhoga*, since in the example only Rādhā has a dream?” This verse answers. Sometimes in dreams of both the hero and heroine at the same time, the same dream appears. When Rādhā had her dream in verse 216 and felt bliss, Kṛṣṇa also dreamed of bliss on seeing her while sleeping on his flower bed in a room in Dvārakā. When Ūṣā in Śoṇitapūra in the Bāṇa’s palace experienced pleasure with Aniruddha in a dream, Aniruddha in a bed in Dvārakā experienced bliss with Ūṣā. Verse 218 shows the how such dreams are frequent.

### Text 219

***vyatītya turyām api saṁśritānāṁ***  
***tāṁ pañcamīṁ prema-mayīm avasthām \|***  
***na sambhavaty eva hari-priyāṇāṁ***  
***svapno rajo-vṛtti-vijṛmbhito yaḥ \|\|219\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The beloved women of Kṛṣṇa, who are on the fifth level,** ***prema,*** **surpassing even the fourth state called** ***samādhi*****, cannot have dreams caused by** ***rajoguṇa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Both dream states cannot arise from *rajoguṇa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Since it is well known in scriptures that dreams arise from intelligence in *rajoguṇa*, it is impossible to have dreams about the Lord who is spiritual.” That is true for material persons, but not for persons with *prema.* They surpass *samādhi*, the fourth state, in which one realizes one’s *svarūpa,* and which is superior to the three states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep states.

### Text 220

***ity eṣa hari-bhāvasya vilāsaḥ ko’pi peśala \|***  
***citra-svapnam ivātanvan kṛṣṇaḥ saṅgamayaty alam \|\|220\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The pastimes of** ***prema*** **for Kṛṣṇa are inconceivably attractive. Kṛṣṇa produces something like astonishing dreams and then associates with his devotees in them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What type of dream is this? This verse answers. Kṛṣṇa associates in those pastimes appropriately, not showing the coming of Akrūra or other unsuitable pastimes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What type of dream is this? It is like an astonishing dream.

### Text 221

***athaiteṣu nirūpyante tad-viśeṣāḥ supeśalāḥ \|***  
***ye’nubhāva-daśām asyāḥ prāpnuvanti rateḥ sphuṭam \|\|221\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Now the most attractive excellences of the four types of** ***sambhoga*** **will be described. These excellences become distinct** ***anubhāvas*** **of** ***rati.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The different types of *sambhoga* were described. Now the differences in these four types will be described. In the four types described, excellences of them will now be described. These excellences are not *aṅgas* of *sambhoga*, but effects (*anubhāva*).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Among the four types like *saṁkṣipta,* there are specialties in the *sambhoga*. The word *rati* means also *prema* and other levels.

### Text 222-224

***te tu sandarśanaṁ jalpaḥ sparśanaṁ vartma-rodhanam \|***  
***rāsa-vṛndāvan-krīḍā-yamunādy-ambu-kelayaḥ \|\|222\|\|***  
***nau-khelā līlayā cauryaṁ ghaṭṭaḥ kuñjādi-līnatā \|***  
***madhu-pānaṁ vadhū-veśa-dhṛtiḥ kapaṭa-suptatā \|\|223\|\|***  
***dyūta-krīḍā paṭākṛṣṭiś cumbāśleṣau nakhārpaṇam \|***  
***bimbādhara-sudhā-pānaḥ samprayogādayo matāḥ \|\|224\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**These** ***anubhāvas*** **are seeing, speaking, touching, blocking the path,** ***rāsa*** **dance, pastimes in Vṛndāvana, playing in the Yamunā’s water, boat pastimes, stealing pastimes, the toll gate, hiding in a bower, drinking liquor, Kṛṣṇa dressing as a woman, pretending to sleep, gambling, pulling clothing, kissing, embracing, scratching, tasting the lips and amorous union.**

### Text 225

***tatra sandarśanaṁ, yathâ lalita-mādhave (2.26)***  
***calākṣi guru-lokataḥ sphurati tāvad antarbhayaṁ***  
***kula-sthitir alaṁ tu me manasi tāvad unmīlati \|***  
***calan-makara-kuṇḍala-sphurita-phulla-gaṇḍa-sthalaṁ***  
***na yāvad aparokṣatām idam apaiti vaktrāmbujam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Seeing, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **O restless-eyed girl! As long as Kṛṣṇa's lotus face, with full cheeks flashing with swinging** ***makara*** **earrings is not visible us, in my heart arises fear of my superiors and in my mind arises concern for family reputation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Kundalatā.

### Text 226

***atha jalpaḥ—***  
***jalpaḥ parasparaṁ goṣṭhī vitathoktiś ca kathyate \|\|226\|\|***

**Перевод:**

***Jalpa*** **refers to talking together and false words.**

### Text 227

***atra parasparaḥ goṣṭhī, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (42-43)***  
***dharṣaṇena kula-strīṇāṁ bhujaṅgeśaḥ kṣamaḥ katham \|***  
***yad etā daśanair eṣa daśan nāpnoti maṅgalam \|\|227\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Talking together, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **How can the king of lechers bear attacking women since he does not attain auspiciousness by biting them with his teeth?**

**How can the king of snakes tolerate attacking the wives of the mongoose, because it does not attain auspiciousness by biting them with his teeth?**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Two verses of conversation are given. How can the king of lechers bear attacking women since he does not attain auspiciousness by biting them with his teeth? The other meaning is “How can the king of snakes tolerate attacking the wives of the mongoose, because it does not attain auspiciousness by biting them with his teeth?” In terms of accusation, the meaning is “How can the king of lechers not tolerate attacking women, since he gains auspiciousness by biting them with his teeth?”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rādhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa who prevents her passage at the toll gate. How can the king of lechers bear attacking women? It is not suitable for him to do so. It is not auspicious for him since the husbands or the king will punish him and his next life will be miserable. There is another meaning. The mongoose is the enemy of the snake. How can the best of snakes tolerate attacking the wives of the mongoose? He cannot. Why? He does not attain auspiciousness because by the mongooses’ counter-bites the snake will immediately die.

If he is the king of lechers, why would he not tolerate attacking the chaste women since he attains happiness concerning his prowess by biting them? Other young girls have fallen into his hands. And there is another meaning. How can the king of snakes not tolerate attacking the wives of the mongoose? Let other snakes not tolerate, but the king of snakes can, because he gets happiness from showing his prowess.

### Text 228

***aprauḍha-dvija-rāja-rājad-alikā labdhā vibhūtiṁ rucāṁ***  
***navyām ātmani kṛṣṇa-vartma-vilasad-dṛṣṭir viśākhāñcitā \|***  
***kandarpasya vidagdhatāṁ vidadhatī netrāñcalasya tviṣā***  
***tvaṁ rādhe śiva-mūrtir ity urasi māṁ bhogīndram aṅgīkuru \|\|228\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: O Rādhā! You are the form of Lord Śiva. The crescent moon shines on in your forehead, and you have the fresh luster of ashes. Your eyes are like fire. You are worshipped by Kārtikeya. You burn Cupid to ashes from the corner of you eye. Please place me on your chest as the king of snakes.**

**Your forehead shines like the fresh moon. You have attained a wealth of praiseworthy beauty. Your eyes playfully gaze at Kṛṣṇa. You are worshipped by Viśākhā. By the beauty of your glance you defeat Cupid. You have an auspicious form. Place my the king of playboys, on your chest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

On your forehead shines the moon slightly decreased *(aprauḍha*), or your forehead shines like the fresh moon. You have glorious ashes on your body, or you have attained a wealth of praiseworthy beauty in your body. Your eyes are fire or your eyes playfully gaze at Kṛṣṇa. You are worshipped by Kārtikeya or you are worshipped by Viśākhā. By the intense effulgence of your gaze you burn up Cupid, or by the beauty of your glance you defeat Cupid. You are Śiva, or you have an auspicious form. Place me, the king of snakes, on your chest, or place me, the king of lechers, on your chest.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Accepting the two meanings to the word *bhujaṅga,* Kṛṣṇa replies to her accusations. O Rādhā! You are Śiva, or you have an auspicious form, because your forehead shines with the crescent moon, or because your forehead is as beautiful as the moon in its second phase. You have ashes praised (*navyām*) by beautiful women.  *Nu* means to praise. Or you have a wealth of new beauty.  *Bhūti* means ashes or wealth according to *Amara-koṣa.* Your third eye shines with fire, or your eyes wander on the path where Kṛṣṇa will come, or your eyes are beautiful with black eye lashes. *Vartma* means the eye lid or a path according to *Amara-koṣa.* You are worshipped by Kārtikeya or by Viśākhā. You burn up Cupid by the fire (*tviṣā*) of the third eye on your forehead. Or you cause great misery to Cupid by the beauty of your side glance. Place me, Vāsuki, the ornament on Śiva’s chest, on your chest. Or place me, the king of material enjoyment, on your chest.

### Text 229

***vitathoktiḥ, yathā tatraiva (44)—***  
***asminn adrau kati na hi mayā hanta hārādi-vittaṁ***  
***hāraṁ hāraṁ hariṇa-nayanā grāhitā jaina-dīkṣām \|***  
***yāḥ kākūkti-sthagita-vadanāḥ patra-dānena dīnās***  
***tūrṇaṁ dūrād anujagṛhire prauḍha-vallī-sakhībhiḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**False words, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī:*** **How many times have I not taken all the necklaces from young girls on Govardhana Hill? These poor doe-eyed girls, made naked, with pleading voices, became choked in shyness, and were quickly shown mercy by friendly mature creepers which, from far off, gave them leaves to cover themselves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Jaina-dīkṣām* means “leaving them devoid of clothing.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vitathokti* means false statements. Kṛṣṇa at the toll gate speaks to Rādhā and others to frighten them. *Hāraṁ hāram* means taking away. *Jaina-dīkṣām* means making them naked.

### Text 230

***atha sparśanam, yathā—***  
***na kuru śapatham asya sparśato dūṣitoccair***  
***asi bhuja-bhujagena tvaṁ bhujaṅgādhipasya \|***  
***tanur anupama-kampā svedam abhyudgirantī***  
***kapaṭini paritas te paśya romāñcitāsti \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Touching: You are extremely contaminated from being touched by the snake-like arms of the king of lechers. Deceitful girl! Do not swear that you are not. Just see! Your body is trembling to the extreme and you are perspiring. Your hairs are standing on end.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

An *adhika-prauḍha gopī* forbids Kṛṣṇa to touch a *mugdha-laghu,* an innocent girl. Kṛṣṇa touches her and she does not mind his touch. Calling Kṛṣṇa the king of lechers, she then jokes with the innocent girl.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *laghu-prakharā* leader of a group speaks to an *adhika-mṛdvī* friend and reveals great *rasa.*

### Text 231

***atha vartma-rodhanaṁ, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.19)—***  
***parītaṁ śṛṅgeṇa sphuṭatara-śilā-śyāmala-rucaṁ***  
***valad-vetraṁ vaṁśa-vyatikara-lasan-mekhalam amum \|***  
***atikramyottuṅgaṁ dharaṇi-dharam agre katham itas***  
***tvayā gantuṁ śakyā taraṇi-duhitus tīra-saraṇī \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Blocking the path, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava*****: Leaving the tall mountain Govardhana, spread with sharp points, shining with black rocks, covered with reeds and with a mixture of bamboos on its gleaming base, you can go by the path that goes by the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Leaving tall Kṛṣṇa, filled with poison, shining with the luster of sapphires, holding a stick and a flute in his belt, you should take the path by the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Śṛṅgam* is a peak or a snake. *Mekhalā* is a belt or part of the base of the mountain.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā, blocking her path, telling her to give up the path going to the sun temple. *Śṛṅgena* means “by the peak” or “by poison.” The mountain is shining black with rocks, or with a complexion like black jewels. *Vetra* is reeds or a stick. *Vaṁsa* is bamboo or the flute.  *Mekhalā* is the base of the mountain or small bells. *Dharaṇi-dharam* is a mountain or Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 232

***atha rāso, yathā—***  
***harir nava-ghanākṛtiḥ prati-vadhū-dvayaṁ madhyatas***  
***tad-aṁsa-vilasad-bhujo bhramati citram eko’py asau \|***  
***vadhūś ca taḍid-ujjvalā prati-hari-dvayaṁ madhyataḥ***  
***sakhī-dhṛta-karāmbujā naṭati paśya rāsotsave \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Rāsa dance: Look! There is one Kṛṣṇa, his complexion like a dark cloud, amazingly moving about with his shining arms on the shoulders of two gopī leaders. A gopī bright as lightning dances between two Kṛṣṇa’s, her lotus hand held by a sakhī, dances in the rāsa festival.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *devatā* woman in her airplane speaks to someone. Kṛṣṇa is between two *gopīs*. The word *vadhū* means a leader of a group. She has her right hand on Kṛṣṇa’s back and her left hand held by a *sakhī*. On Kṛṣṇa’s left is the group leader and on his right is her chief *sakhī.* In this way the fault of having two Kṛṣṇa’s putting their hands on one leader is avoided. *Bhāgavatam* says *tāsāṁ madhye dvayor dvayoḥ praviṣṭena gṛhītānāṁ kaṇṭhe*: he entered between two of them, and placed his arms on their necks. (SB 10.33.3) This shows one Kṛṣṇa placing his arms on two *gopīs’* necks, not two Kṛṣṇa’s. There should be *gopīs* of a friendly or neutral group on both sides of the group leader since this does not impede *rasa*. Or, in one group all the *sakhīs* of one group either as *nāyikās* or *sakhīs* would be situated on the left or right in each of the groups after the completion of suitable positioning, since they lacked the highest qualification. In this way all of the *gopīs* would be included in the *rāsa* circle by holding the two lotus hands of the *nitya-nāyikās.*

### Text 233

***atha vṛndāvana-krīḍā—***  
***sthala-kamalam alīnāṁ stauti gītaiḥ padaṁ te***  
***rada-tati-mati-namrā vandate kunda-rājī \|***  
***adharam anubhajantī lambate bimba-mālā***  
***vilasati tava vaśyā paśya vṛndāṭavīyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pastimes of Vṛndāvana: With the song of the bees, the land-growing lotus praises your feet. The rows of jasmines offer respects to your rows of teeth. The** ***bimba*** **fruits worship your lips. Look! This splendid Vṛndāvana forest shines under your control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Rādhā. *Sthala-kamalam* is the subject of the first sentence.

### Text 234

***yamunā-jala-keliḥ, yathā—***  
***vyātyukṣīyudhi rādhayā ghana-rasaiḥ paryukṣyamāṇasya te***  
***mālyaṁ bhaṅgam avāpa vīra tilako yātaḥ kilādṛśyatām \|***  
***vaktrendau pratimā-cchalena śaraṇaṁ labdhaḥ sakhīṁ kaustubhas***  
***tan mā bhūś cakito vimukta-cikuraṁ nārdaty asau tvad-vidham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Water play: O hero! In the water-splashing battle with Rādhā, your garland has become broken when you were splashed with water. Your** ***tilaka*** **has become invisible. The Kaustubha jewel has surrendered to my friend by reflecting her lotus face. Your hair has come undone. Don't be afraid. She cannot harm a person as you do.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Pratimām* means a reflection. *Nārdati* means “she does not afflict.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viśākhā speaks to Kṛṣṇa. *Vyātyūkṣī-yudhi* means a water fight between two people. This is modified by “with water.” The same phrase modifies *paryuksamānesya*, in the manner of a crow’s eyeball, which turns forwards and backwards. There is also a pun, for *ghana-rasaiḥ* means “with intense pleasure.” *Pratimā* means a reflection.  *Nārdati* means “she does not afflict.”

### Text 235

***yathā vā, padyāvalyāṁ (301)—***  
***jala-keli-tarala-karatala-***  
***mukta-punaḥ-pihita-rādhikā-vadanaḥ \|***  
***jagad avatu koka-yūnor***  
***vighaṭana-saṅghaṭana-kautukī kṛṣṇaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **May Kṛṣṇa, whose hands, like** ***cakravāka*** **birds uniting in the day and separating at night, covered and uncovered Rādhā’s face during water fights, protect the entire world!**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having described how Rādhā was victorious in a water fight, now Kṛṣṇa’s victory in a water fight is described. In the water fight he covered and uncovered Rādhā’s face with the palms of his hands. He uncovered her face to show her friends that she had been defeated. The *cakravākas* separate, fearing the night, on seeing her face which resembles the moon. When her face becomes invisible the *cakravākas* become blissful and thinking it is day, come together. This is the special feature of his hands.

### Text 236

***atha naukhelā, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (270)—***  
***muktā taraṅga-nivahena pataṅga-putrī***  
***navyā ca naur iti vacas tava tathyam eva \|***  
***śaṅkā-nidānam idam eva mamātimātraṁ***  
***tvaṁ cañcalo yad iha mādhava nāviko’si \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Boat pastimes, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **What you say is true. The Yamunā is free of waves and this boat is new. O Mādhava! I am afraid because you are the pilot and you are a lecher.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Muktā* means “without.”

### Text 237

***atha līlā-cauryam—***  
***līlā-cauryaṁ bhaved vaṁśī-vastra-puṣpādi-hāritā \|\|237\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Stealing as a pastime refers to stealing such things as the flute, clothing or flowers.**

### Text 238

***atha vaṁśī-cauryam, yathā padyāvalyāṁ (253)—***  
***nīcair nyāsād atha caraṇayor nūpura mūkayantī***  
***dhṛtvā dhṛtvā kataka-valayāny utkṣipantī bhujānte \|***  
***mudrām akṣṇoś cakitaṁ śaśvad ālokayantī***  
***smitvā smitvā harati muralīm aṅkato mādhavasya \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Stealing the flute, from** ***Padyāvalī:*** **Stepping softly with her feet and making her anklets noiseless, taking off her golden bracelets, looking around with fright with her contracted eyes, Rādhā stole the flute from Kṛṣṇa’s lap while slightly smiling.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sakhīs* relish among themselves Rādhā stealing Kṛṣṇa’s flute.

### Text 239

***atha vastra-cauryaṁ, yathā—***  
***chadāvali-vṛtaiva naḥ sapadi kācid ekā vrajaṁ***  
***praviśya jaratīr ihānayatu ghora-karmoddhatāḥ \|***  
***ayaṁ guṇa-nidhis taror upari tābhir abhyarcyatām***  
***umā-vrata-kumārikāpaṭala-cela-pāṭac-caraḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Stealing garments: One of us should cover herself with lotus leaves, go to Vraja, and return with elderly** ***gopīs*** **agitated by the narration of your horrible deeds. They should worship this storehouse of good qualities sitting in the tree, who has stolen the cloth from young girls performing vows for Pārvatī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The frightened *gopīs* standing in the water of the Yamunā speak to Kṛṣṇa after he would not give back their clothing by use of pleasant words. *Chadāvali* means a mass of lotus leaves. *Pātac-caraḥ* means a thief.

### Text 240

***atha puṣpa-cauryaṁ, yathā—***  
***ayi jñātaṁ jñātaṁ harasi hariṇākṣi pratidinaṁ***  
***tvam eva pracchannā mama sumanasāṁ mañjarim itaḥ \|***  
***cirād diṣṭyā cauri tvam iha vidhṛtādya svayam ato***  
***guhākārām ārāt praviśa vasatiṁ prauḍhibhir alam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Stealing flowers: O doe-eyed Rādhā! I have finally understood. Every day, secretly you steal my budding flowers from this place. Now, after a long time, by good fortune, I have caught you. Don’t be stubborn. From here, enter that cave dwelling.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Rādhā came alone to pick flowers in the garden, Kṛṣṇa, desiring to hold her, speaks.

### Text 241

***atha ghaṭṭaḥ, yathā dāna-keli-kaumudyām (64)—***  
***ghaṭṭādhirājam avamatya vivādam eva***  
***yūyaṁ yad ācaratha śulkam adityamānāḥ \|***  
***manye vidhitsatha tad atra gires taṭeṣu***  
***durgeṣu hanta viṣameṣu raṇābhiyogam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Collecting tolls, from** ***Dāna-keli-kaumudī*****: You disrespect the toll-collector, argue with him, and then refuse to pay the toll. I think you are enthusiastic for love battle in the rugged citadels of Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Situated at the toll gate, Kṛṣṇa speaks to Lalitā. *Viṣameṣu durgeṣu* means “in the rugged citadels.” But *viṣameṣuḥ* also means Cupid. Thus the phrase *viṣameṣu-rānābhiyogam* can mean “enthusiastic for a love battle.”

### Text 242

***atha kuñjādi-līnatā, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.25)—***  
***śaṅke saṅkulitāntarādya niviḍa-krīḍānubandhecchayā***  
***kuñje vañjula-śākhinaḥ śaśimukhī līnā varīvarti sā \|***  
***no ced eṣa tad-aṅghri-saṅgama-vinābhāvād akāle kathaṁ***  
***puṣpāmoda-nimantritāli-paṭalī-stotrasya pātrībhavet \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Hiding in a bower, from** ***Vidagdha-mādhava:*** **I think moon-faced Rādhā has entered this thick grove of** ***aśoka*** **trees with a desire to enjoy intense pastimes here. If this were not so, then why do the bees proclaim the glories of the fragrant** ***aśoka*** **flower out of season? It could not happen unless Rādhā had not touched them with her feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Vañjula* means *aśoka* tree. The poets say that by the touch of the foot of a beautiful woman the *aśoka* tree blossoms.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When searching for Rādhā who has disappeared, Kṛṣṇa reflects. *Vañjula* means *aśoka* tree.

### Text 243

***atha madhu-pānaṁ, yathā—***  
***mukha-vidhum uditaṁ madhu-dviṣo’sau***  
***madhu-caṣake madhuraṁ samīkṣya mugdhā \|***  
***adiśata dṛśam eva tatra pātuṁ***  
***na tu vadanaṁ muhur arthitāpi tena \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Drinking liquor: Rādhā became joyful on seeing the sweet moon of Kṛṣṇa's face reflected in the wine glass. Even though Kṛṣṇa repeatedly urged her to drink, she ordered her eyes to drink, not her mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Paurṇamāsī. She became filled with bewilderment in bliss (*mugdhā*) .She became beautiful by drinking the beauty of his face.

### Text 244

***atha vadhū-veśa-dhṛtiḥ, yathā uddhava-sandeśe (64)—***  
***keyaṁ śyāmā sphurati sarale gopakanyā kimarthaṁ***  
***prāptā sakhyaṁ tava mṛgayate nirmitāsau vayasyā \|***  
***āliṅgāmūṁ muhuriti tathā kurvatī māṁ viditvā***  
***nārīveśam hriyamupayayau māninī yatra rādhā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Wearing woman’s clothing, from** ***Uddhava-sandeśa*****: “Honest Viśākhā, who is this dark-complexioned girl?” Viśākhā replied, “She is a cowherd's daughter.” Rādhā said, “Why has she come here?” Viśākhā said, “She seeks your friendship since she is the same age. Embrace her repeatedly.” About to do this, Rādhā recognized it was me in a woman’s dress. Angry Rādhā became embarrassed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks to Uddhava to make him realize the sweetness of the questions and answers of angry Rādhā and Viśākhā. *Yatra* refers to the previous verse, meaning “in the conversation.”

### Text 245

***kapaṭa-suptatā, yathā karṇāmṛte (21)—***  
***stoka-stoka-nirudhyamāna-mṛdula-prasyandi-manda-smitaṁ***  
***premodbheda-nirargala-prasṛmara-pravyakta-romodgamam \|***  
***śrotuṁ śrotra-manoharaṁ vraja-vadhū-līlā-mitho jalpitaṁ***  
***mithyā-svāpam upāsmahe bhagavataḥ krīḍā-nimīlad-dṛśaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Feigned sleep, from** ***Kṛṣṇa-kārṇāmṛta:*** **We see the feigned sleep of Kṛṣṇa, endowed with all qualities, where he closes his eyes in jest, in order to hear the Vraja women’s conversation, attractive to the ear and mind, which causes Kṛṣṇa to break into a slight, soft smile which he cannot repress, and which causes his hairs to stand on end all over his body, irrepressible because of an outburst of** ***prema.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author quotes Bilvamaṅgala who tastes Kṛṣṇa’s pastime of feigned sleep for a cause. He had a slight smile appearing *(praspandi*) externally gently which he tried to suppress slightly *(stokam*). This indicates that the sweetness of the smile oozed out gradually, and that the women of Vraja began drinking it with the cups of their eyes. His hairs stood on end evidently, spreading out, because he could not suppress his *prema,* coming from a desire tree of *prema.* It is suggested that this fulfilled the desires of the minds and eyes of the women of Vraja.

### Text 246

***atha dyūta-krīḍā—***  
***jitvā dyūta-paṇaṁ daśaty aghahare gaṇḍaṁ mudā dakṣiṇaṁ***  
***sā vāmaṁ ca daśeti tatra rabhasād akṣaṁ kṣipanty abhyadhāt \|***  
***ājñāṁ sundari te yatheti hariṇā vāme ca daṣṭe tataḥ***  
***saṁrambhād iva sā bhujā-latikayā kaṇṭhe babandha priyam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Gambling: After Kṛṣṇa won at dice and bit Rādhā’s right cheek in bliss, she forcibly threw the dice saying “*****vāmaṁ ca daśa*****.” “O beautiful woman! I will do as you commanded.” Saying this he bit her left cheek. Rādhā in anger then bound him around the neck with her creeper-like arms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In some states they say *vāmaṁ ca daśa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Vṛndā speaks to Kundalatā. Biting the cheek was the prize in the game. Rādhā in saying *vāmaṁ ca daśa* knew the Bengali style of the game. In throwing the dice quickly she indicated her desire to win. Kṛṣṇa replied to her words. “You have ordered me to bite your left cheek. I must follow that order.”

### Text 247

***atha paṭṭākṛṣṭiḥ, yathā lalita-mādhave (6.31)—***  
***dhanyaḥ so’yaṁ maṇir avirala-dhvānta-puñje nikuñje***  
***smitvā smitvā mayi kuca-paṭīṁ kṛṣṭavaty unmadena \|***  
***gāḍhaṁ gūḍhākṛtir api tayā man-mukhākuta-vedī***  
***niṣṭhīvan yaḥ kiraṇa-laharīṁ hrepayāmāsa rādhām \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Pulling the cloth, from** ***Lalita-mādhava:*** **This jewel is very fortunate. When I passionately tugged at Rādhā’s bodice in the dense darkness of the bower with a smile, this jewel, whose form was hidden by Rādhā, understanding my wishes, by emitting waves of light, embarrassed Rādhā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Another version is *kiraṇa-laharīṁ hrepayāmāsa kīrṇīkurvanvas tām*: spreading light it embarrassed her.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks of the history of the jewel obtained from Jāmbavān, speaking to Madhumaṅgala when he recognizes it in Dvārakā. This jewel is fortunate. It was Śaṅkhacūḍa’s jewel (worn by Rādhā in Vraja, given to the sun god who gave it to Satrājit). This identifies it. I pulled at her bodice in great passion (*unmadena*). Rādhā became greatly frightened that the jewel would be revealed. Its form was covered but it knew my intentions (*samukhasyākūta-vedī).* It produced (*niṣṭīvan*) waves of light and made Rādhā embarrassed. It wanted to make me happy.

### Text 248

***atha cumbo, yathā—***  
***kapaṭa-caṭulita-bhruvaḥ samantān***  
***mukha-śaśinaḥ rabhasād vidhūyamānam \|***  
***danuja-ripur acumbad ambujākṣyāḥ***  
***kamalam ivānila-kampi cañcarīkaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Kissing: Moving her eyebrows with pretended anger, lotus-eyed Rādhā violently resisted the kissing of moon-faced Kṛṣṇa, who appeared like a bee resting on a lotus trembling in the breeze.**

**Kṛṣṇa kissed the lotus of moon faced Rādhā with lotus eyes and moving eyebrows, while she shook her head violently. He was like a bee on a lotus trembling in the wind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rūpa-mañjarī speaks to a friend. *Anilena kampi* means trembling in the wind, modifying *kamalam.*

### Text 249

***atha āśleṣo, yathā—***  
***nava-jāguḍa-varṇayopagūḍhaḥ***  
***sphurad-abhra-dyutir etayonmadena \|***  
***harati sma harir hiraṇya-vallī-***  
***parivītāṅga-tamāla-maṅgalāni \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Embraces: Embraced by impassioned Rādhā, the color of fresh** ***kuṁkuma,*** **Kṛṣṇa, with the complexion of a fresh cloud, stole the good qualities of a** ***tamāla*** **tree embraced by a golden creeper.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

According to *Trikāṇḍa-śeṣa* the word *jāguḍam* means *kuṁkuma.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A *sakhī* of Rādhā speaks. *Jāguḍa-varṇayā* means “with the color of *kuṁkuma*.” *Maṅgalāni* means fame.

### Text 250

***atha nakha-kṣataṁ, yathā—***  
***na kucāv imau gatijitā tayā hṛtaṁ***  
***gajataḥ prasahya sakhi kumbhayor yugam \|***  
***kṣatam atra nāga-damano yad arpayat***  
***param aṅgajāṅkuśa-vareṇa tat-kṣaṇam \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Nail scratching: friend! These are not breasts. They are the frontal lobes forcibly stolen from an elephant by your conquering gait. It is most suitable if an elephant driver injures them with the best of goads.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The subduer of the snake Kāliya should inflict wounds with his nails which are like elephant goads. The other meaning is the elephant driver (*nāga-damanaḥ*) should inflict a wound with his goad. That is suitable (*kṣamam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śyāmalā describes Rādhā in a joking way. *Gatijitā* means defeating an elephant’s gait.

*Nāga-damana* means subduer of Kāliya. He should scratch her with his nails, the goads of Cupid.

### Text 251

***atha bimbādhara-sudhā-pānaṁ, yathā—***  
***na hi sudhākara-bimba-sudhākaraṁ***  
***kuru mukhaṁ karabhoru karāvṛtam \|***  
***adhara-raṅgaṇam aṅga varāṅgane***  
***pibatu nīpa-vanī-bhramaras tava \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Drinking nectar of the lips: O Rādhā, whose thighs are as beautiful as elephant trunks! Do not cover the moon of your face, which makes the moon useless, with your hand. O Rādhā with a beautiful face! Let the bee called Kṛṣṇa wandering in this** ***kadamba*** **forest drink the** ***raṅgaṇa*** **flowers of your lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kṛṣṇa or a messenger speaks to Rādhā. Your face is a moon which makes the moon useless (*sudhākara-bimba*). Your lips are *raṅgaṇa* flowers. O woman with a beautiful face (*varānane*)!

### Text 252

***atha samprayogo, yathā—***  
***drāg-dor-maṇḍala-pīḍanoddhura-dhiyaḥ proddāma-vaijātyayā***  
***nirbandhād adharāmṛtāni pibataḥ sītkāra-pūrṇāsyayā \|***  
***kandarpotsava-paṇḍitasya maṇitair ākrānta-kuñjāntayā***  
***sārdhaṁ rādhikayā harer nidhuvana-krīḍā-vidhir vardhate \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Union: When Kṛṣṇa boldly decides to squeeze her suddenly with his arms she becomes most obstinate. When he drinks the nectar of her lips with persistence, she releases deep sighs. In this way, the pastimes of Nidhuvana increase between the expert of conjugal arts and Rādhā, overcome within the bower by murmurs of ecstasy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It should be understood that though *sambhoga* is not perceived as such by the author, it are considered the best by others. In the next verse his opinion will be expressed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When Kundalatā asks what happened in the bower, Vṛndā explains. *Drāk* means quickly. *Vaijātyam* means with *prāgalbhya.*  *Manita* is the sound of the woman during amorous union.

### Text 253

***vidagdhānāṁ mitho līlā-vilāsena yathā sukham \|***  
***na tathā samprayogeṇa syād evaṁ rasikā viduḥ \|\|253\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**The** ***rasikas*** **know that the great happiness experienced by the couple in** ***līlā-vilāsa*** **is not experienced in** ***samprayoga.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There are two types of enjoyment with women: *samprayoga* and *līla-vilāsa*. *Samprayoga* has been described above. The excellence of the second type is now explained.

### Text 254

***yathā—***  
***balena parirambhaṇe nakha-śikhābhir ullekhanaṁ***  
***haṭhād adhara-khaṇḍane bhuja-yugena bandha-kriyām \|***  
***dukūla-dalane hatiṁ kuvalayena kurvāṇayā***  
***ratād api sukhaṁ harer adhikam ādadhe rādhayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**An example of** ***līlā-vilāsa:*** **When Kṛṣṇa strongly embraced her, Rādhā scratched him with her nails. When he tried to kiss her, she blocked him with her arms. When Kṛṣṇa pulled her cloth, she struck him with a water lily. He obtained greater joy from this than from union.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sakhīs* who gazed through the lattice holes relish the *līlā-vilāsa* of the couple. Two verses are given as examples

### Text 255

***yathā vā—***  
***narmotseka-kalādṛgañcala-camatkārī bhruvor vibhramaḥ***  
***saṁvyānasya vikarṣaṇ caṭulatāṁ karṇotpalenāhatiḥ \|***  
***krīḍeyaṁ vraja-nāgarī-rati-guror gāndharvikāyās tathā***  
***bhūyiṣṭhaṁ suratotsavād api navāsvādaṁ vitene sukham \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Another example: When Kṛṣṇa showed his skills in joking, Rādhā moved her eyebrows. When he pulled her cloth with flattering words, she hit him with her ear ornament. This play between the Vraja women’s teacher of love and Rādhā spread fresher, tastier happiness than the ecstasy of amorous union.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having shown the later portion of *līlā-vilāsa,* now the first part will be shown. When the great *guru* Kṛṣṇa used his skills of joking on the Vraja women, Rādhā moved her eyebrows which astonished the tips of her eyes. When he pulled her cloth with flattery, she hit him with her ear ornament. This verse illustrates the first part of *līlā-vilāsa* and the previous verse shows the later part of *līlā-vilāsa.* Verse 252 illustrated *samprayoga*, union. The sequence of the pastimes and excellence is backwards from this verse to verse 252 (*samprayoga* being the best), according to the author, but the excellence is in forward sequence to the present verse according to others (the first part of *līlā-vilāsa* being the best). This is in disagreement with Jīva Gosvāmī’s comment on verse 252. 10

### Text 256

***ataeva śrī-gīta-govinde (12.10)—***  
***pratyūha-pulakāṅkureṇa niviḍa-leśa-nimeṣeṇa ca***  
***krīḍākūta-vilokite’dhara-sudhā-pāne kathā-kelibhiḥ \|***  
***ānandādhigamena manmatha-kalā-yuddhe’pi yasminn abhud***  
***udbhūtaḥ sa tayor babhūva suratārambhaḥ priyambhāvukaḥ \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**From** ***Gīta-govinda:*** **Though the goose bumps interrupted their embraces, the blinking of their eyes interrupted seeing the various pleasures, their playful words interrupted their kisses and eruptions of bliss interrupted the battle of Cupid, it all gave pleasure in the performance of love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Desiring to complete this work with a verse of Jayadeva, the best taster of the greatest *anubhāvas,* the author strengthens his opinion with that of Jayadeva. The performance of amorous pastimes, understood only by the experience of *rasika sakhīs,* made its appearance. In those pastimes, when they wanted to embrace, goose bumps created an obstacle. When they wanted to view the profusion of pastimes, blinking of the eyes was an obstacle. By not attaining embraces, seeing, kissing, and love battles, which were most desired, by the lack of pacifying that thirst, the *rasa* becomes even more relishable. In this way the excellence of *rasa* is established. It gave pleasure (*priyam-bhāvukaḥ*). It produced success.

### Text 257

***yathā—***  
***gokulānanda govinda goṣṭhendra-kula-candramaḥ \|***  
***prāṇeśa sundarottaṁsa nāgarāṇāṁ śikhāmaṇeḥ \|\|\|***  
***vṛndāvana-vidho goṣṭha-yuva-rāja manohara \|***  
***ity ādyā vraja-devīnāṁ preyasī praṇayoktayaḥ \|\|258\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**In conclusion: O bliss of Gokula! O Govinda! O moon arisen in the family of Vraja’s king! O master of our lives! O crown of all handsome men! O crest-jewel of lovers! O moon of Vṛndāvana! O handsome prince of Vraja! These are some of the names used by the women of Vraja to affectionately address their lover.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the conclusion, the author invokes auspiciousness by chanting the sweet names of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 258

***atalatvād apāratvād āpto’sau durvigāhatām \|***  
***spṛṣṭaḥ paraṁ taṭasthena rasābdhir madhuro mayā \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Because it is bottomless in depth and boundless in width, it is not completely understood.**

**By standing on the shore, I have merely touched the ocean of** ***madhura-rasa.***

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is bottomless because of its very nature and boundless because of quantity.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Madhura-rasa,* with its elements, has many unspoken qualities. How can one describe and taste what is unknown by ancient poets since it was not shown to them, and which has not been attained even by great devotees with *prema*? The author speaks with humility. The ocean of *madhura-rasa* cannot be understood. The subject of the verb is not mentioned but the meaning is “*Madhura-rasa* cannot be understood even by famous relishers of *rasa* like Śukadeva, ancient devotees like Bilvamaṅgala and Jayadeva, and all recent devotees.” The word *durvigāha* means “not understood in its entirety.” Two reasons are given. It is bottomless by nature and boundless in quantity. It is bottomless, because by type and quantity it is greater than the oceans of *dāsya* and other *rasas*. I cannot even submerge myself in it slightly (though other previous devotees have), and therefore I stand on the shore and touch it by putting one finger into it and lifting it up for tasting. In that way I have obtained a taste.

### Text 259

***ayam ujjvala-nīlamaṇir gahana-mahā-ghoṣa-sāgara-prabhavaḥ \|***  
***bhajatu tava makara-kuṇḍala-parisara-sevaucitīṁ deva \|\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**May** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,*** **arising from the deep ocean of Nanda’s Gokula, become qualified to serve your ear, next to your** ***makara*** **earring!**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This scripture (*ayam)* arises from the ocean of Nanda’s Vraja, from the women of Vraja, situated in one spot there. Or, it arises from the *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*, which was difficult to understand (*gahana*). May it become qualified to be heard (being next to the *makara* earring) by you, Kṛṣṇa. But the phrase also indicates the work should be the object of intense worship, and that it is most secret. Thus he has instructed that this topic should be studied by persons who have association with another person possessing this confidential *rasa*. No one should disregard following these most exalted teachers.

*kṛṣṇasya nirjana-vihāra-vikāśako’yaṁ*  
*svālokanāya rahasi prakaṭayya guptaḥ \|*  
*śrīmadbhir ujjvalamaṇis tad apīha daivād*  
*vyaktiḥ​​​​​ sa eṣa iti kasya samakṣam eva \|\|*

**This work,** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,*** **revealing Kṛṣṇa’s private pastimes, revealing the secret for his own viewing, being most confidential, by good fortune has nevertheless been revealed in this world by the great author Rūpa. Thus it is visible to some.**

### Text 260

***sanātana-samo yasya śrīmān jyāyān sanātanaḥ \|***  
***śrī-vallabho’nujaḥ so’sau śrī-rūpo jīva-sad-gatiḥ \|\|260\|\|***

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rūpa, eternal peace incarnate, identical in mood to Sanātana, his elder brother, and whose younger brother was Śrī Vallabha, is the means of my success and the good fortune of all the** ***jīvas.***

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The author expresses his aspiration for making his efforts successful. It is the object of hearing of Govinda-deva, whose lotus feet he serves. The name of the work is “The Sapphire of *Śṛṅgāra-rasa*.” It continually exists (*prabhavaḥ*) as the ocean of Nanda-vraja difficult to enter. *Ghoṣa* means a cowherd village according to *Amara-koṣa.* It is an ocean of *dāsya*, *sakhya, vātsalya* and *ujjvala rasas* because of its inhabitants Raktaka, Śrīdāmā, Nānda, Rādhā and others. Or the work arises from the *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,* ocean of *Nanda-vraja*, in which the twelve *rasas* take shelter by being described. This work should be received in service of Kṛṣṇa’s ear which is near (*parisara)* his earring. In terms of *rasa,* the ear, though not mentioned, should be understood. In terms of the scripture, the meaning is easily understood. In terms of gems, this spotless (*ujjvala*) gem, arising from the impenetrable ocean of great sound (*ghoṣa*), should be qualified for service localized (*parisara*) to Kṛṣṇa. This indicates the great secret nature of the work, since it is suitable for even Kṛṣṇa to hear, which to be taken up as the supreme, priceless object by his devotees, and hidden from other people.

May the commentary on *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* called *Ānanda-candrikā*, the moon of bliss, for those who understand *rasa,* for the benefit of the whole world, be pleasing to the upholder of the universe, Caitanya Mahāprabhu! I have consulted the verse in the commentary of Jīva Gosvāmī, namely:

*svecchayā likhitaṁ kiṁcit kiṁcid atra parecchayā \|*  
*yat pūrvāpara-sambaddhaṁ tat pūrvam aparaṁ param \|\|*

**Some portions I have written as my own opinions, and some portions are the opinions of others. What is consistent is my view and what is not consistent is the view of others.** ***Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*** **1.2**

As well I have considered his commentaries on *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi* 3.17 and 14.48. Taking all this into consideration, I have become rash in explaining the meaning of the text of this scripture, having briefly gone through it from the beginning, middle and end. Because I have received a particle of mercy dust from his lotus feet, you devotees who are oceans of mercy should tolerate my prattle.

This commentary *Ānanda-candrikā* has been completed on the fifth day of the waxing moon of Āśvina month, 1618 Śaka era.
